english_verse: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.
translation_verse: Komɛlbwa mumpar la, Korowii ta nyundua ne harɛ.

english_verse: The earth was barren, with no form of life; it was under a roaring ocean covered with darkness. But the Spirit of God was moving over the water. The First Day
translation_verse: A ɡɛ saŋ la dɛ harɛ ta mar dɔe, dɛ komɛlbwa toole o ta. Dɛ nee tɔ komɛlbwa ta asɛ bɔr bir kpirkpir ken, asɛ Korowii Doma do nee la sie dɛ la dɛɛ ba.

english_verse: God said, “I command light to shine!” And light started shining.
translation_verse: Belaa Korowii ŋɔ, <<Bɔ́r chaah.>> Asɛ bɔr chaah.

english_verse: God looked at the light and saw that it was good. He separated light from darkness
translation_verse: O na bochaah la kɛŋɔ o wer. Asɛ o pere bochaah la le biro la bini,

english_verse: and named the light “Day” and the darkness “Night.” Evening came, then morning—that was the first day. The Second Day
translation_verse: dɛ pa bochaah la sɔn <bɔrchaahna> asɛ dɛ pa biro la ɡe sɔn <bɔrjoe>. Asɛ bɔr jo dɛ chaah. Onee tɔpere waa tɔ sie.

english_verse: God said, “I command a dome to separate the water above it from the water below it.”
translation_verse: Korowii berɔ ŋɔ, <<Née la pere anɛ ásɛ ane kaa nyundua ásɛ ane ka harɛ.>>

english_verse: and named it “Sky.” Evening came, then morning—that was the second day. The Third Day
translation_verse: Asɛ o pa bɔr waa chɔ a baah ta la sɔn <nyundua>. Asɛ bɔr jo dɛ chaah. Onee tɔpere waa teŋa nɛɛ.

english_verse: God said, “I command the water under the sky to come together in one place, so there will be dry ground.” And that's what happened.
translation_verse: Belaa Korowii ŋɔ, <<Née la aa ka harɛ la ka chɔ bobeŋkpoŋ ásɛ a ka harɛpɛɛ chɔ.>> Asɛ a ɛ ɡɛ.

english_verse: God named the dry ground “Land,” and he named the water “Ocean.” God looked at what he had done and saw that it was good.
translation_verse: Asɛ o pa harɛpɛɛ la sɔn <harɛ>, dɛ pa nee la aa chɔ bobeŋkpoŋ la ɡe sɔn <mpo>, dɛ na kɛŋɔ a wer.

english_verse: God said, “I command the earth to produce all kinds of plants, including fruit trees and grain.” And that's what happened.
translation_verse: Dɛ ŋɔ, <<Hárɛ pɛɛ la le kpɔɡa ne daa bwa soo siwi. Anɔ la aa dɛ ɛ bie ne daa aa dɛ nɔnɛ dɛ dɔ bie a bini bwa.>> Asɛ a ɛ ɡɛ.

english_verse: The earth produced all kinds of vegetation. God looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: Harɛpɛɛ la le kpɔɡa ne daa bwa soo siwi. Anɔ la aa dɛ ɛ bie ne daa aa dɛ nɔnɛ dɛ dɔ bie a bini bwa. Asɛ Korowii na kɛŋɔ a wer.

english_verse: Evening came, then morning—that was the third day. The Fourth Day
translation_verse: Asɛ bɔr jo dɛ chaah, onee tɔpere waa teŋa tooro.

english_verse: God said, “I command lights to appear in the sky and to separate day from night and to show the time for seasons, special days, and years.
translation_verse: Asɛ Korowii ŋɔ, <<Kwáa chaah nyundua dɛ́ korɛ webaŋa le jwaana ta, dɛ́ baɡle tɔpera ne bene ne saŋ bɛla

english_verse: I command them to shine on the earth.” And that's what happened.
translation_verse: dɛ́ɛ chaah nyundua ne harɛ bwa.>> Asɛ a ɛ ɡɛ.

english_verse: God made two powerful lights, the brighter one to rule the day and the other to rule the night. He also made the stars.
translation_verse: Korowii ta konjena anɛ aa chaah. Anee wee ne korobie. Wee la kan dɛɛ chaah kohona bɔr chaahna saŋ, asɛ korobie waa do jeɡa la ɡe ɛɛ chaah jwaana. O ta weweela ɡe.

english_verse: Then God put these lights in the sky to shine on the earth,
translation_verse: O kpɔ ɡɛ kwaa nɔ bwa do nyundua asɛ aa chaah harɛ,

english_verse: to rule day and night, and to separate light from darkness. God looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: bɛl dɛ ɛ toma jwaana bɛl ɡee ɛ toma bɔr chaahna saŋ, dɛ pere biro le bochaah ta. Asɛ Korowii na kɛŋɔ a wer.

english_verse: Evening came, then morning—that was the fourth day. The Fifth Day
translation_verse: Asɛ bɔr jo dɛ chaah, onee tɔpere waa teŋa naarɛ.

english_verse: God said, “I command the ocean to be full of living creatures, and I command birds to fly above the earth.”
translation_verse: O berɔ ŋɔ, <<Pɛ́ŋa ne nee bini koŋkwaa su nee la ta pirim ásɛ jumbii ne koŋɡaahla do nyundua dɛɛ ɡah.>>

english_verse: So God made the giant sea monsters and all the living creatures that swim in the ocean. He also made every kind of bird. God looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: Korowii ta mpo bini oljena ne koŋkwaa bwa aa lɔ nee bini pirim, ne jumbii ne koŋɡaahla ɡɛ a bwa soo siwi aa doa. Asɛ o na kɛŋɔ a wer.

english_verse: Then he gave the living creatures his blessing—he told the ocean creatures to increase and live everywhere in the ocean and the birds to increase everywhere on earth.
translation_verse: Asɛ Korowii swee andɛɛɡa tɛa dɛ ŋɔ, <<Hé loɡle dɛ́ warɛ dɛ su neerare ne mpo, ásɛ jumbii la ɡe loɡle dɛ́ su harɛ.>>

english_verse: Evening came, then morning—that was the fifth day. The Sixth Day
translation_verse: Asɛ bɔr jo dɛ chaah, onee tɔpere waa teŋa nue.

english_verse: God said, “I command the earth to give life to all kinds of tame animals, wild animals, and reptiles.” And that's what happened.
translation_verse: Asɛ Korowii ŋɔ, <<Hweera kwaa bwa soo siwi ba harɛ ta, kpɔɡ bini olchɔɡa, ne kondɛɛra ne anɔ la aa dɛ tuuɡi tea ta ne anɔ la aa dɛ huuh, a bwa ne a soo siwi.>> Asɛ a ɛ ɡɛ.

english_verse: God made every one of them. Then he looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: Korowii ta a bini bɛlbwa soo siwi. Waa na kwaa waa taa la, o nao kɛŋɔ a wer.

english_verse: God said, “Now we will make humans, and they will be like us. We will let them rule the fish, the birds, and all other living creatures.”
translation_verse: Belaa Korowii ŋɔ, <<Yá ta nɛwɛnyina bá do kɛ yan, dɛ́ɛ di kpeɡri pɛŋa ne jumbii ne kondɛɛra ne kpɔɡ bini ola, anjena ne anjeɡre, dɛ hweera kwaa aa dɛ huuh dɛɛ tuuɡi tea ta bwa nɛ.>>

english_verse: So God created humans to be like himself; he made men and women.
translation_verse: Anomanta, o ta nɛwɛnyina, ɡɛ tenten waa doa laanee o ta ba. Baa ne haahnee o ta.

english_verse: God gave them his blessing and said: Have a lot of children! Fill the earth with people and bring it under your control. Rule over the fish in the ocean, the birds in the sky, and every animal on the earth.
translation_verse: Korowii swee andɛɛɡa tɛɛ ba dɛ ŋɔ, <<Hé loɡle dɛ́ su harɛ ta pirim, ásɛ dɛɛ di kpeɡri pɛŋa aa lɔ mpo ta, ne jumbii ne koŋɡaahla aa lɔ nyundua, dɛ hweera kwaa aa dɛ huuh dɛɛ tuuɡi tea ta bwa nɛ.>>

english_verse: And I have given the green plants as food for everything else that breathes, including animals, both wild and tame, and birds. And so it was.
translation_verse: dɛ kpɔ kpɔɡa ne papooni dɛ tɛ ola ne jumbii, ne kwaa aa dɛ tuuɡi tea ta ne anɔ la aa dɛ huuh, dɛ hweera kon te bɛlbwa ásɛ a ɛ a kondikwa.>> Asɛ a ɛ ɡɛ.

english_verse: God looked at what he had done. All of it was very good! Evening came, then morning—that was the sixth day.
translation_verse: Anɔ bwa habɔɔ la, Korowii nyiŋi kwaa waa taa la bwa dɛ na kɛŋɔ a bwa wer kɛrɛdɛ. Asɛ bɔr jo dɛ chaah, onee tɔpere waa teŋa numɛl.

english_verse: So the heavens and the earth and everything else were created. The Seventh Day
translation_verse: Gɛɛ a do Korowii ta nyundua ne harɛ, ne komɛlbwa aa lɔ a ta dɛ tonɛ.

english_verse: By the seventh day God had finished his work, and so he rested.
translation_verse: Tɔpenuanɛ te ne tela la, dɛ o tonɛ o toma bwa. Anomanta, o onɔ tɔpenuanɛ te la ta.

english_verse: That's how God created the heavens and the earth. The Garden of Eden When the Lord God made the heavens and the earth,
translation_verse: Kenii Korowii ta nyundua ne harɛ. Korowii aa ta nyundua ne harɛ la,

english_verse: no grass or plants were growing anywhere. God had not yet sent any rain, and there was no one to work the land.
translation_verse: dɛ konduula ne kpɔɡa ta harɛ la ta leɛ, dɛkalkɛŋɔ dɛ o ta ɡelɛ bwaala nɛ o ta mɔɔ. Dɛ nomɛlbwa ɡe toole dɛ́ parɛ harɛ la.

english_verse: But streams came up from the ground and watered the earth.
translation_verse: Nee yon le harɛ bini dɛɛ sɔɔh harɛ la.

english_verse: The Lord God took some soil from the ground and made a man. God breathed life into the man, and the man started breathing.
translation_verse: Asɛ Korowii kpɔ teera ma baa, dɛ hwee do o mebɔɔne bini, o dɔ mkpa dɛ so.

english_verse: The Lord made a garden in a place called Eden, which was in the east, and he put the man there.
translation_verse: A habɔɔ la, Korowii du daa bodɛɛɡe bobɛl baa yerɔ Eden wee leebɔr, dɛ kpɔ baa waa tao la ka so bela.

english_verse: The Lord God filled the garden with all kinds of beautiful trees and fruit trees. Two other trees were in the middle of the garden. One of these gave life—the other gave the wisdom to know the difference between right and wrong.
translation_verse: O ɡelɔ daa bwa soo siwi le bela dɛ do wer siwi ta a nɔna dɔ pɛla kɛŋɔ nɛn di. Daa anɛ ane cheɡɛ konduula la baah ta. Bɛl dɛ tɛ mkpa, bɛl ɡe ɡel nɛn ɛɛ jemɛ wedɛɛɡa ne anchɔɡa.

english_verse: From Eden a river flowed out to water the garden, then it divided into four rivers.
translation_verse: Moo bɛl nyu le Eden bodɛɛɡe bela dɛ palɛ dɛɛ kpɔ daa la baah dɛɛ sɔɔh harɛ la. Waa le bela la, o peɡri bɔre anaarɛ.

english_verse: The first one is the Pishon River that flows through the land of Havilah,
translation_verse: O kpale waa tɔ sie la sɔne Pesɔn Moo. O palɔ dɛ ɡoli kpɔ Havila harɛ ta bela suuɡaswɛm aa lole.

english_verse: where pure gold, rare perfumes, and precious stones are found.
translation_verse: Suuɡaswɛm tenten ne bwedɛɛɡa a yoɡ aa kpeɡa, ne konsɔɔhsoma a sɔɔh aa soma lɔ bela.

english_verse: The second is the Gihon River that winds through Ethiopia.
translation_verse: O kpal nɛɛte la sɔne Gehɔn Moo. O palɔ dɛ ɡoli kpɔ Kus harɛ ta.

english_verse: The Tigris River that flows east of Assyria is the third, and the fourth is the Euphrates River.
translation_verse: O kpal toorote la sɔne Tiɡris Moo. O palɔ dɛɛ kaa Asiiria harɛ wee leebɔr pera. Asɛ naarɛte la sɔne Yufretis Moo.

english_verse: The Lord God put the man in the Garden of Eden to take care of it and to look after it.
translation_verse: Korowii kpɔ baa waa tao la ka so Eden bodɛɛɡe bela waa du daa la dɛ ŋɔ, wɛ́ɛ parɛ o ta dɛɛ nyiŋi bela,

english_verse: But the Lord told him, “You may eat fruit from any tree in the garden,
translation_verse: asɛ dɛ jao ŋɔ, “Hɛɛ wonoo di daa la bɛlbwa sese nɔn.

english_verse: except the one that has the power to let you know the difference between right and wrong. If you eat any fruit from that tree, you will die before the day is over!”
translation_verse: Kɛ bɛ onɔ la waa dɛ tɛ liire dɛ́ ɡel nɛn jemɛ wedɛɛɡa ne anchɔɡa la te nɔn di. Awola haa di a ɡɛ daa la nɔn la bɛl la, sewaa hɛɛ ba sewa.”

english_verse: The Lord God said, “It isn't good for the man to live alone. I will make a suitable partner for him.”
translation_verse: Asɛ Korowii ŋɔ, “Aa were kɛŋɔ baa la ɡbo so. Mɛɛ kwaa o dɔŋee ja o nɛ, ásɛ wɛɛ chao.”

english_verse: So the Lord God made him fall into a deep sleep, and he took out one of the man's ribs. Then after closing the man's side,
translation_verse: Anomanta, o ɡelɔ baa la chɔ dom ka ɡarɛ, o laa o kuɡlambi beŋkpoŋ kpɔ dɛ kpɔ ol tɔ bela.

english_verse: the Lord made a woman out of the rib. The Lord God brought her to the man,
translation_verse: O kuɡlambi la waa kpɔa la, o kpɔɔ ka kwaa haah dɛ kpɔ ba tɛ baa la.

english_verse: and the man exclaimed, “Here is someone like me! She is part of my body, my own flesh and bones. She came from me, a man. So I will name her Woman!”
translation_verse: Asɛ baa la ŋɔ, “Yɔɔ! Taraken te, n ɡbaɡba hoɡ ne n bo-ol tentenee nɔ. O sɔne ‘haah’. Baa binii o le.”

english_verse: That's why a man will leave his own father and mother. He marries a woman, and the two of them become like one person.
translation_verse: A waa ɡela baa yon ɡel o nya ne mɛɛ, dɛ́ ka kpɔ haah ba yon pɛ so, dɛ́ ɛ beŋkpoŋ la.

english_verse: Although the man and his wife were both naked, they were not ashamed.
translation_verse: Dɛ baa la ne o haah la bwa dɛ valɛ mumɡbal, kɛ dɛ sihiih aa ban kpo.

english_verse: The snake was sneakier than any of the other wild animals that the Lord God had made. One day it came to the woman and asked, “Did God tell you not to eat fruit from any tree in the garden?”
translation_verse: Ola Korowii aa taa la bini la, dɛ harɛkon sie pilo ɡwaa a bwa. Harɛkon la baa pɛɛ haah la ŋɔ, “Kpelaa Korowii ŋɔ he bɛ daa nɔ bɛlbwa nɔn di naa?”

english_verse: The woman answered, “God said we could eat fruit from any tree in the garden,
translation_verse: Asɛ haah la chaŋo ŋɔ, “Dɛ́ ya won daa nɔ bɛlbwa nɔn dii.

english_verse: except the one in the middle. He told us not to eat fruit from that tree or even to touch it. If we do, we will die.”
translation_verse: Atane kɛŋɔ onɔ waa cheɡɛ bodɛɛɡe baa du daa nɔ baah tenten nɔ, Korowii ŋɔ ya bɛ o te leɡe a ba ɛ kɛŋɔ yaa di o nɔnee. Ya diu waa, yaa sewɔɔ.”

english_verse: “No, you won't!” the snake replied.
translation_verse: Belaa harɛkon la ŋɔ haah la be ŋɔ, “Nyosonee. Háa sewa ba.

english_verse: “God understands what will happen on the day you eat fruit from that tree. You will see what you have done, and you will know the difference between right and wrong, just as God does.”
translation_verse: Korowii jemɔ kɛŋɔ dɛ he di daa la nɔn aa, he sie dɛ ba pila, he jemɛ wedɛɛɡa ne anchɔɡa kɛ on ken. A waa o ŋɔ he bɛ di la.”

english_verse: The woman stared at the fruit. It looked beautiful and tasty. She wanted the wisdom that it would give her, and she ate some of the fruit. Her husband was there with her, so she gave some to him, and he ate it too.
translation_verse: Dɛ haah la nao kɛŋɔ daa la nɔn la ɡe wer siwi ta dɛ do wer ne dii, dɛɛ tɛ wejema ɡe ja. Anomanta, o haŋrɔ kahonɛ dɛ cha ane di, dɛ kpɔ ane ka tɛ o jaa ɡe o di.

english_verse: At once they saw what they had done, and they realized they were naked. Then they sewed fig leaves together to cover themselves.
translation_verse: Baa dia tonɛ la, buɡ la ta, ba bwa sie pilo, ba na kɛŋɔ ba cheɡɛ mumɡbal. Anomanta, ba nyin ɔɡ papooni dɛ nyara dɛ kpɔ li.

english_verse: Late in the afternoon, when the breeze began to blow, the man and woman heard the Lord God walking in the garden. So they hid behind some trees. Sin Brings a Curse
translation_verse: Awola jɔmɔra ne la, ba noɔ kɛŋɔ Korowii dɛ valɛ bodɛɛɡe baa du daa la bini, asɛ ba chwa ka sɔh baŋ pera daa la bini ásɛ o bɛ ban na.

english_verse: The Lord God called out to the man and asked, “Where are you?”
translation_verse: Anee Korowii yerɛ baa la ŋɔ, “Lee he dɔɔ?”

english_verse: The man answered, “I was naked, and when I heard you walking through the garden, I was frightened and hid!”
translation_verse: O sɛh dɛ ŋɔ, “N no he ɡbɔɡa daa la baah ta bela, asɛ n ɔmɛ dɛ ka sɔh dɛkalkɛ n cheɡɛ mumɡbal.”

english_verse: “How did you know you were naked?” God asked. “Did you eat any fruit from that tree in the middle of the garden?”
translation_verse: Anee Korowii pɛɛro ŋɔ, “Umee ŋɔ he be ŋɔ he cheɡɛ mumɡbal ɔ? He di daa la maa kaeh ŋɔ he bɛ o nɔn di la kɛɛ?”

english_verse: “It was the woman you put here with me,” the man said. “She gave me some of the fruit, and I ate it.”
translation_verse: Asɛ baa la ŋɔ, “Ɔɔh. Haah la haa kpɔɔ ja n nɛɛ la, onee tɛ mɛ bɛl n di.”

english_verse: The Lord God then asked the woman, “What have you done?” “The snake tricked me,” she answered, “and I ate some of that fruit.”
translation_verse: Belaa Korowii pɛɛ haah la ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ he ɛ ɡɛ nɔɔ?” Anee o chaŋe ŋɔ, “Harɛkon laanee neɡ mɛ asɛ n di.” Korowii taah baa ne haah dɛ harɛkon

english_verse: So the Lord God said to the snake: “Because of what you have done, you will be the only animal to suffer this curse— For as long as you live, you will crawl on your stomach and eat dirt.
translation_verse: Belaa Korowii ŋɔ harɛkon la be ŋɔ, “Gɛ haa ɛa nɔ nomanta, N taahne, ásɛ a do kpeɡri tɛɛ ɡwaa kpɔɡ bini ola ne kondɛɛra bwa. He tea taa hɛɛ ba tuuɡa, dɛɛ di teera ka tel he serewe bena.

english_verse: You and this woman will hate each other; your descendants and hers will always be enemies. One of hers will strike you on the head, and you will strike him on the heel.”
translation_verse: Mɛɛ kpɔ danchɔɡee ta he ne haah la baah ta, ásɛ he naanar ne o naanar hah dɔŋa dɛɛ la. Saŋ bɛlbwa waa nae la, wɛɛ paɡre he nyuu, ásɛ he ɡe choɡe o nalume.”

english_verse: Then the Lord God said to the woman, “You will suffer terribly when you give birth. But you will still desire your husband, and he will rule over you.”
translation_verse: Korowii ŋɔ haah la be ŋɔ, “Weweele binii hɛɛ ba tea kpoŋa, dɛ́ lolɛ bonyɛɡa bini. He sie ɛɛ beɡre he jaa nɛɛ, ásɛ o di kpeɡri he nɛ.”

english_verse: The Lord said to the man, “You listened to your wife and ate the fruit I told you not to eat. And so, the ground will be under a curse because of what you did. As long as you live, you will have to struggle to grow enough food.
translation_verse: Dɛ ŋɔ baa la be ŋɔ, “Haa no he haah nyoa dɛ di daa nɔn maa ŋɔa he bɛ di nomanta, N taah harɛ nɔ waa haa ɛa la wa, tomkpeɡaa hɛɛ ba ɛɛ dɛ́ kwee bɔwɔb mɔɔ dɛ́ di kwa he soɡa bini bwa.

english_verse: Your food will be plants, but the ground will produce thorns and thistles.
translation_verse: Sɔɔhne ne jabalnadaŋɛree dɛɛ ba harɛ la ta lee tɛɛ. Ásɛ hɛɛ di kpɔɡ bini kondikwa.

english_verse: You will sweat all your life to earn a living; you were made out of soil, and you will once again turn into soil.”
translation_verse: Hɛɛ kwee bɔwɔbee mɔɔ dɛ́ di kwa ka tel kɛŋɔ haa berɛ kaa teera maa kpɔa mae la bini, dɛkalkɛ teera hen, teera binii he berɛ dɛɛ ba kaala.”

english_verse: The man Adam named his wife Eve because she would become the mother of all who live.
translation_verse: Baa la sɔne Adam. O pa haah la ɡe sɔn Hawa dɛkalkɛŋɔ on dɛɛ ba nɛwɛnyina bwa nya ɛɛ.

english_verse: Then the Lord God made clothes out of animal skins for the man and his wife.
translation_verse: Korowii kpɔ ola tɔne tɛɛ ba ba kpɔ tɔ ba bwara. Korowii doŋi Adam ne Hawa le Eden bodɛɛɡe bela

english_verse: The Lord said, “They now know the difference between right and wrong, just as we do. But they must not be allowed to eat fruit from the tree that lets them live forever.”
translation_verse: Belaa Korowii lii kɛŋɔ, “Name baa la jemɛ wedɛɛɡa ne wechɔɡa kɛŋɔ yan. Yá nyiŋi kɛrɛdɛ o bɛ daa waa dɛ tɛ mkpa la te nɔn ba tor di dɛ́ do le saŋ bɛlbwa.”

english_verse: So the Lord God sent them out of the Garden of Eden, where they would have to work the ground from which the man had been made.
translation_verse: Anomanta, Korowii doŋu le Eden bodɛɛɡe bela waa du daa la, dɛ ɡel o kaa parɛ harɛ waa mao le o ta la ta.

english_verse: Then God put winged creatures at the entrance to the garden and a flaming, flashing sword to guard the way to the life-giving tree.
translation_verse: Waa doŋi baa la le bela habɔɔ la, o kpɔ Kerobim ne tokobii bɛl waa dɛ nyɛɡle kɛ ninlao dɛɛ beɡre bobɛlbwa, dɛ ka cheɡ Eden bodɛɛɡe wee leebɔr pera, ásɛ nomɛlbwa bɛ won di daa la nɔna.

english_verse: Adam and Eve had a son. Then Eve said, “I'll name him Cain because I got him with the help of the Lord.”
translation_verse: Adam la o haah Hawa be, asɛ o kpoŋe tea dɛ lolɛ bie, asɛ haah la lii o nyu bini ŋɔ, “Korowii alaworomɛ, n dɔ bibaa, dɛ pa o sɔn Keen.”

english_verse: Later she had another son and named him Abel. Abel became a sheep farmer, but Cain farmed the land.

translation_verse: Nomɛlbwa waa kpo o dɔŋ la, ɡɛɛ o dɔŋ bɛl ɡe ɛɛ ba o kpoe, dɛkalkɛ ɡɛ Korowii aa doa laanee o ta nɛwɛnyini.

english_verse: I want you and your descendants to have many children, so people will live everywhere on earth.
translation_verse: Hé loɡle bii, ásɛ dɛ ya warɛ kohona, ásɛ he naanar su harɛ nɔ ta bobɛlbwa.”

english_verse: Again, God said to Noah and his sons:
translation_verse: Anee Korowii ŋɔ Nowa ne o bii baa ja o nɛɛ la be ŋɔ,

english_verse: I am going to make a solemn promise to you and to everyone who will live after you.
translation_verse: “Taraken n ne hen, ne he naanar dɛ ba fɔo fɔwa,

english_verse: I promise every living creature that the earth and those living on it will never again be destroyed by a flood.
translation_verse: Waa aa lɔ n ne he fɔo nɔ ta laanee kɛŋɔ, saŋkama bɛlbwa toole mɛɛ ba ɡela nee su dɛ́ ba chɔɡ kontaala bɛlbwa kpa, ásɛ nee bɛlbwa ɡe aa won su kohona dɛ́ chɔɡ harɛ nɔ.”

english_verse: The rainbow that I have put in the sky will be my sign to you and to every living creature on earth. It will remind you that I will keep this promise forever.
translation_verse: Mɛɛ ɡeloo n bwaala deŋɡare do nyundua baama bini, dɛɛ baɡle fɔo n ne haa fɔwa harɛ nɔ ta la.

english_verse: When I send clouds over the earth, and a rainbow appears in the sky,
translation_verse: Dɛ baama baa tɔ bobɛlbwa, asɛ bwaala deŋɡare le a bini naa,

english_verse: I will remember my promise to you and to all other living creatures. Never again will I let floodwaters destroy all life.
translation_verse: a taa mɛ ba fɔo la n ne hen ne hweera kwaa bwa soo siwi aa fɔwa la nae. Aa won ba kɛ nee ɛɛ ba suu dɛ́ ba chɔɡ kontaale bɛlbwa kpa.

english_verse: When I see the rainbow in the sky, I will always remember the promise that I have made to every living creature.
translation_verse: Saŋ bɛlbwa, dɛ bwaala deŋɡare baa le baama bini naa, a taa mɛɛ ba nae dɛ́ lii fɔo la n ne hweera kwaa bwaa fɔwa harɛ nɔ ta la.”

english_verse: Noah and his sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth, left the boat. Ham later had a son named Canaan.
translation_verse: Nowa bibaala baa ja o nɛɛ dɛ le ɡbera la bini laanee Sɛm ne Ham dɛ Jafɛt. Dɛ Ham bibaa sɔne Keenan.

english_verse: All people on earth are descendants of Noah's three sons.
translation_verse: Banɔɔ Nowa bibaala batoro la, asɛ a che ba nɛɛ nɛwɛnyina warɛ harɛ nɔ ta la.

english_verse: Noah farmed the land and was the first to plant a vineyard.
translation_verse: Dɛ Nowa dɛ parɛ. Onee pa mun parɛ daa koo, dɛ du daa ane ba kpɔ a nɔna dɛɛ ɛ sen.

english_verse: One day he got drunk and was lying naked in his tent.
translation_verse: Waa kpɔ ane ɛ sen dɛ nyɔ la, o dɛɛrɔ dɛ ka chɔ mumɡbal o dea.

english_verse: Ham entered the tent and saw him naked, then went back outside and told his brothers.
translation_verse: Asɛ o bibaa Ham, waa ɛ Keenan mɛɛ la, na kɛ o mɛɛ chɔ mumɡbal, asɛ o le dɛ ka taa baɡle o bala banɛ la.

english_verse: Shem and Japheth put a robe over their shoulders and walked backwards into the tent. Without looking at their father, they placed it over his body.
translation_verse: Belaa Sɛm ne Jafɛt kpɔ yal, asɛ dɛ ka paɡri bɔle ba vaama ta, dɛ valɛ mumur, dɛ kpɔ yal la ka tɔ ba mɛɛ. Baa wola nyin kɛ ba siwi na ba mɛɛ mumɡbal la waa ba berɛ ba habɔɔ chaɡɔ dɛ kpɔ yal la ka tɔɔ la.

english_verse: he said, “I now put a curse on Canaan! He will be the lowest slave of his brothers.
translation_verse: Asɛ o ŋɔ, “Bwɛɛlɛ Keenan! Hɛɛ ɛ yomii, dɛ́ do he dɔɔranar lɔɡa.”

english_verse: I ask the Lord my God to bless Shem and make Canaan his slave.
translation_verse: Asɛ o berɛ ŋɔ, “Hé kpɛɛ Korowii Sɛm aa dɛ tomɔ, Keenan ɛɛ tomɛ Sɛmii.

english_verse: I pray God will give Japheth more and more land and let him take over the territory of Shem. May Canaan be his slave.”
translation_verse: Kórowii tɛ Jafɛt naanar kohona, ba ne Sɛm bwa pɛ so bobeŋkpoŋ! Keenan ɛɛ ɛ yomii do Jafɛt lɔɡa dɛɛ tomɔ.”

english_verse: and died at the age of
translation_verse: Waa baa sewɛ la, dɛ o di bene lafraanuanaarɛ fifraanue.

english_verse: After the flood Shem, Ham, and Japheth had many descendants. The Descendants of Japheth
translation_verse: Kenii Nowa bibaala Sɛm ne Ham dɛ Jafɛt waa do. Nee la aa sua dɛ hweeh la, ba bwa loɡle bibaala.

english_verse: At first everyone spoke the same language,
translation_verse: Wubwa la, dɛ nɛwɛnyina bwa fa ɛ beŋkpoŋ dɛɛ bol wobol beŋkpoŋ.

english_verse: but after some of them moved from the east and settled in Babylonia,
translation_verse: Ba iro dɛ ɡaaɡe wee leebɔr dɛ ka le Babelɔn tena deŋɡarere harɛ waa chɔa kaa ta, dɛ ka so bela.

english_verse: they said: Let's build a city with a tower that reaches to the sky! We'll use hard bricks and tar instead of stone and mortar. We'll become famous, and we won't be scattered all over the world.
translation_verse: Belaa ba yerɛ dɔŋa dɛ ŋɔ, “Amɔ hé ɡel ya pɛ nyoa, dɛ́ vɔrɔwe bwɛjen dɛ́ ma dejaŋ o ka tel nyundujaɡla, ásɛ a ɛ sɔn tɛ yaa ya bɛ lɔ peɡre harɛ nɔ ta.”

english_verse: But when the Lord came down to look at the city and the tower,
translation_verse: Asɛ Korowii tu ba harɛ dɛ ba na bwɛjen la ne dejaŋ nɛwɛnyina aa dɛ ma la ɡɛ waa kaa nyundua.

english_verse: he said: These people are working together because they all speak the same language. This is just the beginning. Soon they will be able to do anything they want.
translation_verse: Anee o ŋɔ, “Dɛ nɛnsiwi beŋkpoŋ ne wobol beŋkpoŋ nɛra soɡe harɛ nɔ ta, asɛ dɛ dɔ nyopɛo dɛ den won ɛ anɔ bwa ken tenaa, ate aa biɡri bɛlbwa komɛlbwa toole bá ŋɔ baa ɛɔ baa wola won ɛ.”

english_verse: Let's go down and confuse them! We'll make them speak different languages, and they won't be able to understand each other.
translation_verse: Korowii aa bera kaa nyundua la, o ŋɔ, “Amɔ hé ɡel ya tu kaa harɛ ta ásɛ dɛ ka beɡre ba wobol, ásɛ bane kapa bɛ ba dɔŋa wobol no kpa.”

english_verse: So the people had to stop building the city, because the Lord confused their language and scattered them all over the earth. That's how the city of Babel got its name. The Descendants of Shem
translation_verse: Gɛɛ a ɛ baa yerɛ bwɛjen la Babelɔn, o munii kɛŋɔ kooraŋkoora, dɛkalkɛŋɔ belaa Korowii ka koɡre nɛra wobol asɛ bɛlbwa dɔ o wobol korɛ, asɛ dɛ lɔ ba peɡre harɛ nɔ ta bobɛlbwa. Sem naanar wa

translation_verse: A habɔɔ la, o berɔ so bene lafraanue, dɛ lolɛ bibaala ne haahna bane ɡe.

translation_verse: A habɔɔ la, o berɔ so bene lafraanaarɛ dɛ atoro, dɛ lolɛ bibaala ne bihaahna bane ɡe.

translation_verse: A habɔɔ la, o berɔ so bene lafraanaarɛ fifraatoro, dɛ lolɛ bibaala ne bihaahna bane ɡe.

translation_verse: A habɔɔ la, o berɔ so bene lafraanɛ dɛ anuanaarɛ, dɛ lolɛ bibaala ne bihaahna bane ɡe.

english_verse: Reu had more children and died at the age of
translation_verse: A habɔɔ la, o berɔ so bene lafraanɛ dɛ anuanɛ, dɛ lolɛ bibaala ne bihaahna bane ɡe.

english_verse: Serug had more children and died at the age of
translation_verse: A habɔɔ la, o berɔ so bene lafraanɛ, dɛ lolɛ bibaala ne bihaahna bane ɡe.

english_verse: Nahor had more children and died at the age of
translation_verse: A habɔɔ, la o berɔ so bene lafa dɛ fi dɛ anuanaarɛ, dɛ lolɛ bibaala ne bihaahna bane ɡe.

english_verse: Terah decided to move from Ur to the land of Canaan. He took along Abram and Sarai and his grandson Lot, the son of Haran. But when they came to the city of Haran, they settled there instead.
translation_verse: Asɛ Tɛɛra kpɔ o bie Abram, ne o bibaa Haaran ɡe bibaa Lɔt, ne Sarai waa ɛ o hela dɛ ɛ o bibaa Abram haah la. Ba le Ur waa lɔ Kaldea harɛ ta la ŋɔ ba dɛ kaa Keenan harɛ ta. Baa bera ba tel Haran harɛ ta la, ba soɡe bela.

english_verse: The Lord said to Abram: Leave your country, your family, and your relatives and go to the land that I will show you.
translation_verse: Awola bɛl, Korowii ŋɔ Abram be ŋɔ, “Ir, dɛ́ le harɛ haa soɡe o ta la ta, ásɛ dɛ bɛ he nɛra dawɛ, bɛ he mɛɛ buse nɛra ɡe dawɛ, dɛ́ kaa harɛ maa dɛ ba he baɡla nɔ ta.

english_verse: I will bless you and make your descendants into a great nation. You will become famous and be a blessing to others.
translation_verse: Mɛɛ ɡeloo he mun ya, dɛ́ warɛ su harɛ ta bwa, ásɛ dɛ tɛɛ hɛɛra. Mɛɛ ɡeloo he sɔn le ásɛ a che he nɛɛ nɛwɛnyina dɔ andɛɛɡa.

english_verse: I will bless those who bless you, but I will put a curse on anyone who puts a curse on you. Everyone on earth will be blessed because of you.
translation_verse: Mɛɛ cha nɛra la baa soŋe andɛɛɡa dɛɛ tɛɛ la. Nomɛlbwa waa taahnee la, ɡɛɛ mɛɛ ba o ɡe taahna, ásɛ a che he nɛ nɛwɛnyini bwa dɔ andɛɛɡa.”

english_verse: Abram went as far as the sacred tree of Moreh in a place called Shechem. The Canaanites were still living in the land at that time,
translation_verse: Baa tel Keenan la, Abram ɡaaɡe harɛ la ta dɛ ka tel dajen bɛl mun More, o lɔ bwɛjen Sɛkem, dɛɛ nyin wɛɛ tomɛ Korowii bela. A ɡɛ saŋ baa tel bela la, dɛ Keenan tena soɡe harɛ la ta.

english_verse: but the Lord appeared to Abram and promised, “I will give this land to your family forever.” Abram then built an altar there for the Lord.
translation_verse: Belaa Korowii ba Abram be dɛ ba ŋɔ, “Harɛ nɔɔ mɛɛ ba kpɔe tɛ he naanar.” Anomanta, Abram pa bwea dawɛ dɔŋa nɛ bobɛl, dɛ kwaa saraha kon dɛ kpoo kwaa dɛɛ tɛ Korowii bela, kpɔe Korowii aa kpɔ o te baɡlo la wa.

english_verse: The crops failed, and there was no food anywhere in Canaan. So Abram and his wife Sarai went to live in Egypt for a while. But just before they got there, Abram said, “Sarai, you are really beautiful!
translation_verse: Baa dɛ kaa a ka tama ba tel Ijipt la, o ŋɔ o haah Sarai be ŋɔ “Gɛ haa wera tolo nɔ,

english_verse: When the Egyptians see you, they will murder me because I am your husband. But they won't kill you.
translation_verse: dɛ ya jo bwɛɛ nɔ ta ba na n ne hen, dɛ jemɛ kɛŋɔ he jaaree men naa, baa kpo mɛɛ dɛ́ ɡele.

english_verse: As soon as Abram and Sarai arrived in Egypt, the Egyptians noticed how beautiful she was.
translation_verse: Abram aa jo Ijipt harɛ ta la, ba na o haah la kɛ o wer kpela.

english_verse: The king was good to Abram because of Sarai, and Abram was given sheep, cattle, donkeys, slaves, and camels.
translation_verse: Kooro la koh o waa dɛ nyiŋi Abram kɛrɛdɛ, asɛ dɛ lawɛ boohna ne peera ne nae ne nyoɡmare ne yoma dɛ keeɡore tɛo.

english_verse: Because of Sarai, the Lord struck the king and everyone in his palace with terrible diseases.
translation_verse: Kɛ Korowii koh Sarai waa dɛ ɡel weechɔɡa ane ba le kooro la ne o dem tena bwa nɛ.

english_verse: Finally, the king sent for Abram and said to him, “What have you done to me? Why didn't you tell me Sarai was your wife?
translation_verse: Belaa kooro la aa na ɡɛ la, o tomɛ ba ka yerɛ Abram ba, asɛ o pɛɛro ŋɔ, “Bɔkwa waa he ɛɛ mɛ kenɔ? Ɛrɛɛ he ta n be ŋɔe ŋɔ he haahnee yɔ?

english_verse: Why did you make me believe she was your sister? Now I've married her. Take her and go! She's your wife.”
translation_verse: Ɛrɛɛ he ŋɔ he nimambiee dɛ ɡel n kpɔɔ ɛ n haah nɔɔ? He haahnee la. Ba lawɔ, ásɛ dɛ kpɔɔ le kaa.”

english_verse: So the king told his men to let Abram and Sarai take their possessions and leave.
translation_verse: Kooro la ŋɔ o bonɔɔna be asɛ ba lawɔ le o harɛ la ta. O ne haah la ne komɛlbwa waa dɔa bwa.

english_verse: Abram and Sarai took everything they owned and went to the Southern Desert. Lot went with them.
translation_verse: Asɛ Abram kpɔ o haah ne komɛlbwa waa dɔa le Ijipt harɛ weekaŋle nyunduabɔr, dɛ kaa Keenan harɛ weekaŋle harɛbɔr. O kpɔ Lɔt ja ba kaa.

english_verse: Abram was very rich. He owned many cattle, sheep, and goats, and had a lot of silver and gold.
translation_verse: Dɛ Abram nɔn bini wer, peera te kɛɛ, boohna kɛɛ nae ɔ? Suuɡapoŋa ne suuɡaswɛm bwa, dɛ o dɔa.

english_verse: Abram moved from place to place in the Southern Desert. And finally, he went north and set up his tents between Bethel and Ai,
translation_verse: Waa le bela la, o ɡaaɡɔ dɛ choɡ bwɛɛre ta ɡɛ naaa dɛ ba tel bela o fa aa baa choɡ mumpar bwa la. Bela lɔ Bɛtel ne Ai baah ta,

english_verse: where he had earlier camped and built an altar. There he worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: bela o fa aa pa bwea dawɛ dɔŋa nɛ dɛ kwaa kon dɛ kpo kwaa dɛɛ tɛ Korowii o ta la, dɛ tomɛ Korowii bela kɛrɛdɛ.

english_verse: Lot, who was traveling with him, also had sheep, goats, and cattle, as well as his own family and slaves.
translation_verse: Dɛ Lɔt ɡe dɔ kondɛɛra kɛŋɔ peera, boohna ne nae taeh, dɛ dɔ haah ne bii dɛ bonɔɔna ɡe.

english_verse: At this time the Canaanites and the Perizzites were still living in the same area, and so there wasn't enough pastureland left for Abram and Lot with all of their animals. Besides this, the men who took care of Abram's animals and the ones who took care of Lot's animals started quarreling.
translation_verse: A ɡɛ nomanta, naɡra chole Abram bonɔɔna baa dɛ nyiŋi o kondɛɛra ta la, ne Lɔt bonɔɔna baa dɛ nyiŋi o ɡe kwaa ta la baah. Gɛ saŋ dɛ Keenan harɛ tena ne nɛra bane baa dɛ yer ba Pɛrɛs tena ta soɡe harɛ la ta.

english_verse: Abram said to Lot, “We are close relatives. We shouldn't argue, and our men shouldn't be fighting one another.
translation_verse: Belaa Abram ŋɔ Lɔt be ŋɔ, “Nɛmbeŋkpoŋii n ne he bwa, anomanta, a ta chɛɛ kɛŋɔ n ne he yo, a ta chɛɛ kɛŋɔ n bonɔɔna ne he bonɔɔna ɡe yo.

english_verse: There is plenty of land for you to choose from. Let's separate. If you go north, I'll go south; if you go south, I'll go north.”
translation_verse: Anomanta, ya peɡri dɔŋa baah. Nyiŋi harɛ nɔ waa chɔa kaa nɔ bwa, ásɛ dɛ kpɔ baŋ bela bwa waa wera he be, ásɛ he do baŋ bɛl, ń ɡe do baŋ bɛl.”

english_verse: This happened before the Lord had destroyed the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah. And when Lot looked around, he saw there was plenty of water in the Jordan Valley. All the way to Zoar the valley was as green as the garden of the Lord or the land of Egypt.
translation_verse: Belaa Lɔt ha sie dɛ nyiŋi harɛ la, asɛ dɛ na ɡɛ Jɔɔdan Moo nyoa harɛ aa sɔna ka le Soar harɛ ta, dɛ do wer kɛŋɔ bela Korowii aa du daa Eden bodɛɛɡe ne Ijipt harɛ la ken. Gɛ waa nɔ chiɡo mɔɔ Korowii chɔɡ bwɛɛre ane baa dɛ yera Sodom ne Gomoora la.

english_verse: So Lot chose the whole Jordan Valley for himself, and as he started out toward the east, he and Abram separated.
translation_verse: Lɔt kpɔ deŋɡarere doa harɛ waa chɔa kaa Jɔɔdan Moo nyoa la te bwa, asɛ dɛ kpɔ sie chaɡɛ wee leebɔr pera. Gɛɛ a do ba nɛra banɛ la peɡri dɔŋa baah.

english_verse: Abram stayed in the land of Canaan. But Lot settled near the cities of the valley and put up his tents not far from Sodom,
translation_verse: Abram soɡe Keenan harɛ ta, asɛ Lɔt te ka baŋre o tɛnte deene deŋɡarere dor harɛ waa chɔa kaa Jɔɔdan Moo nyoa bwɛɛre ane baah ta dɛ bɛne Sodom.

english_verse: where the people were evil and sinned terribly against the Lord. Abram Moves to Hebron
translation_verse: A ɡɛ Sodom tena nɔ, dɛ ba nyubini kpeɡri ba wechɔɡa do kan Korowii be. Abram kaa so Hɛbrɔn

english_verse: After Abram and Lot had gone their separate ways, the Lord said to Abram: Look around to the north, south, east, and west.
translation_verse: Belaa Abram ne Lɔt aa peɡri dɔŋa baah la, asɛ Korowii ŋɔ Abram be ŋɔ, “Che bela haa lole nɔ, dɛ́ nyiŋi he sie ne habɔɔ, he diɡ ne ɡal.

english_verse: I will give you and your family all the land you can see. It will be theirs forever!
translation_verse: A ɡɛ harɛ nɔ bwaa mɛɛ ba kpɔe tɛ he ne he naanar ó den ɛ he kon saŋ bɛlbwa dɛɛ la.

english_verse: I will give you more descendants than there are specks of dust on the earth, and someday it will be easier to count those specks of dust than to count your descendants.
translation_verse: Mɛɛ ɡeloo he naanar warɛ kɛŋɔ hɛŋle ken, nomɛlbwa aa wola won jemɛ ba nyoa bwa.

english_verse: Now walk back and forth across the land, because I am going to give it to you.
translation_verse: Anomanta, ɡaaɡe harɛ la bwa ta, dɛ́ na ɡɛ waa doa dɛkalkɛŋɔ he nɔn taa mɛɛ ba kpɔe do.”

english_verse: Abram took down his tents and went to live near the sacred trees of Mamre at Hebron, where he built an altar in honor of the Lord.
translation_verse: Asɛ o ir bela waa soɡa la, dɛ ba so dajena ane mun Mamre, o bɛne bwɛɛ bɛl sɔne Hɛbrɔn. Asɛ o kwaa kon waa kpoo kwaa dɛɛ ɛ saraha o ta tɛ Korowii bela.

english_verse: About this time, King Amraphel of Babylonia, King Arioch of Ellasar, King Chedorlaomer of Elam, and King Tidal of Goiim
translation_verse: A kaa ba kɛŋɔ koranar banaarɛ banee lole. Ba sɔnaa nɔ. Amrafɛl waa ɛ Babelɔn kooro ne Areɔk waa ɛ Elasar kooro, ne Kedolaoma waa ɛ Elam kooro dɛ Tidal waa ɛ Goiim kooro.

english_verse: attacked King Bera of Sodom, King Birsha of Gomorrah, King Shinab of Admah, King Shemeber of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela, a city also known as Zoar.
translation_verse: Ba nyoa pɛo ba yo koranar banue bane. Banee nɔ. Sodom Kooro Bɛra, ne Gomoora Kooro Birsa ne Adma kooro Sinab ne Seboiim kooro Sɛmɛba dɛ Bɛla kooro. Bɛla nɔ sɔn bɛl ɡee Soar.

english_verse: King Chedorlaomer and his allies had ruled these last five kings for twelve years, but in the thirteenth year the kings rebelled and joined forces in Siddim Valley, which is now covered by the southern part of the Dead Sea.
translation_verse: Bene fi dɛ anɛ bwa dɛ ba lɔ kooro Kedolaoma lɔɡa dɛɛ tomɔ, asɛ bene fi dɛ atoro ta la, ba ɛɔ dɔm ŋɔ baa on tomɛ kpa.

english_verse: They also defeated the Horites in the hill country of Edom, as far as El-Paran, near the desert.
translation_verse: Ba yo nɛra bane ɡe baa dɛ yer ba Hɔr tena baa lɔ deŋɡarere harɛ Sɛɛ ta, dɛ kpɔ ka le bwɛɛ Ɛlparan waa bɛne pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ bɛl ta, dɛ pɔ ba nɛ.

english_verse: They went back to the city of Enmishpat, better known as Kadesh. Then they captured all the land that belonged to the Amalekites, and they defeated the Amorites who were living in Hazazon-Tamar.
translation_verse: Ba berɔ laa berɛ dɛ yo ba Kades, o sɔn bɛl ɡee Ɛn Mispat. Ba yoo dɛ lɛ Amalɛk tena harɛ bwa, asɛ dɛ pɔ Amɔre tena baa soɡe Hasasɔn Taama la ɡe nɛ.

english_verse: At Siddim Valley, the armies of the kings of Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, Zeboiim, and Bela fought the armies of King Chedorlaomer of Elam, King Tidal of Goiim, King Amraphel of Babylonia, and King Arioch of Ellasar. The valley
translation_verse: Elam Kooro Kedolaoma ne Goiim Kooro Tidal ne Sina Kooro Amrafɛl dɛ Elasar Kooro Areɔk. Koranar banue ne koranar banaarɛɛ yoa.

english_verse: was full of tar pits, and when the troops from Sodom and Gomorrah started running away, some of them fell into the pits. Others escaped to the hill country.
translation_verse: Dɛ Sidim Fɛlembɔjen la ɛ bɔɔne bɔɔne kootal su o bwa nomanta, Sodom kooro ne Gomoora kooro ne ba nɛra aa chwaa dɛɛ kaa la, ba bini bane kaa lee bɔɔne la bini asɛ koranar batoro la ɡe ne ba nɛra la chwa kaa bwejena la dor.

english_verse: Their enemies took everything of value from Sodom and Gomorrah, including their food supplies.
translation_verse: Belaa koranar banaarɛ la pa Sodom ne Gomoora tena laala bwa ne ba kondikwaare bwa dɛ kpɔ kaa.

english_verse: They also captured Abram's nephew Lot, who lived in Sodom. They took him and his possessions and then left.
translation_verse: Dɛ Abram nime bie Lɔt soɡe Sodom. Ba lawɔ dɛ pa o laala bwa ɡe ja.

english_verse: At this time Abram the Hebrew was living near the oaks that belonged to Mamre the Amorite. Mamre and his brothers Eshcol and Aner were Abram's friends. Someone who had escaped from the battle told Abram
translation_verse: A habɔɔ la, nɛra baa chwaa la bini bɛl ba Abram waa ɛ Hibru te la be, dɛ ba bol ɡɛ waa la o be. Dɛ o soɡe Mamre dajena ane aa lɔ Amɔre te bɛl harɛ ta la mune. Dɛ Mamre ne o nimanar Ɛskɔl ne Aner bwa ja Abram nɛ baa cha dɔŋa laa ta.

english_verse: that his nephew Lot had been taken away. Three hundred and eighteen of Abram's servants were fighting men, so he took them and followed the enemy as far north as the city of Dan.
translation_verse: Abram aa noa kɛŋɔ ba lawɛ o lole dɛɛ kaa o ne la, o kpɔ o dem bonɔɔna lafraatoro fi dɛ banuatoro baa dɔ laa wejema dɛ ti ba ka tel bwɛɛ bɛl baa dɛ yerɛ bela Dan.

english_verse: That night, Abram divided up his troops, attacked from all sides, and won a great victory. But some of the enemy escaped to the town of Hobah north of Damascus,
translation_verse: Bɔr aa joa la, Abram bɔne o bonɔɔna la bini kuore ta, asɛ ba ka yo nɛra la dɛ pɔ ba nɛ. Ba doŋ ba ɡɛ naaa dɛ ka tel bobɛl baa dɛ yerɛ bela Hoba waa lɔ Damaskɔs weekaŋle nyunduabɔr.

english_verse: and Abram went after them. He brought back his nephew Lot, together with Lot's possessions and the women and everyone else who had been captured. Abram Is Blessed by Melchizedek
translation_verse: Abram berɔ lɛ laala la bwa, ne o lole Lɔt ne o laala ne o haahna baa laɡ ba ja o nɛɛ la, dɛ nɛra bwa baa laɡ ba ja la, dɛ ba bane. Mɛlkesɛdɛk swee andɛɛɡa tɛ Abram

english_verse: Abram returned after he had defeated King Chedorlaomer and the other kings. Then the king of Sodom went to meet Abram in Shaveh Valley, which is also known as King's Valley.
translation_verse: Waa kaa yo Kooro Kedolaoma ne koranar baa ja o nɛɛ tonɛ la, o berɔ ba. O bala bini la, Sodom kooro kaa chemo fɛlembɔjen Savɛ ta. O sɔn bɛl ɡee Kooro Fɛlembɔjen.

english_verse: King Melchizedek of Salem was a priest of God Most High. He brought out some bread and wine
translation_verse: Belaa Salɛm Kooro Mɛlkesɛdɛk, waa ɛ Nemenɛ Korowii sɔfo la kpɔ paanoo ne sen ba tɛo,

english_verse: and said to Abram: “I bless you in the name of God Most High, Creator of heaven and earth.
translation_verse: dɛ soŋe andɛɛɡa tɛo ŋɔ, “Nemenɛ Korowii waa dɔ komɛlbwa kpeɡri dɛ ta nyundua ne harɛ la kwaa he kwaa tɛɛ.

english_verse: All praise belongs to God Most High for helping you defeat your enemies.” Then Abram gave Melchizedek a tenth of everything.
translation_verse: Nemenɛ Korowiirii dɔ jam kɛŋɔ waa ba he dɔma ne harɛ asɛ he tiɡri ba nɛɛ nɔ.” Asɛ Abram bɔne koŋkwaare waa kaa lɛ o dɔma la be la bini bɔre fi, dɛ kpɔ bɔrbeŋkpoŋ tɛ kooro Mɛlkesɛdɛk.

english_verse: The king of Sodom said to Abram, “All I want are my people. You can keep everything else.”
translation_verse: Belaa Sodom kooro ŋɔ Abram be ŋɔ, “Kpɔ n nɛra tɛ mɛ dɛ́ kpɔ laala la bwa.”

english_verse: Abram answered: The Lord God Most High made the heavens and the earth. And I have promised him
translation_verse: Anee Abram chaŋo ŋɔ, “N ŋwɛɛ ntam, Nemenɛ Korowii waa ta nyundua ne harɛ la sie kɛŋɔ,

english_verse: that I won't keep anything of yours, not even a sandal strap or a piece of thread. Then you can never say that you are the one who made me rich.
translation_verse: maa kapɛrɛ kɛɛ yakwara kɛɛ komɛlbwa waa ɛ he konee lɛ he be he ba ŋɔ, ‘Menee ɡela Abram dɔ kwa.’

english_verse: Let my share be the food that my men have eaten. But Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre went with me, so give them their share of what we brought back.
translation_verse: Maa sɛh lɛ komɛlbwa nemenɛ anɔ la bonɔɔna la aa dia la. Baala baa ja n nɛɛ dɛ la laanee chɛ kɛŋɔ he tɛɛ ba ba bɔr. Banee Aner ne Ɛskɔl dɛ Mamre.”

english_verse: Later the Lord spoke to Abram in a vision, “Abram, don't be afraid! I will protect you and reward you greatly.”
translation_verse: Waa la habɔɔ la, Korowii pili waane bini baɡle Abram dɛ ŋɔ, “Abram, bɛ ɔmɛ. Mɛɛ tɔe ɡbemɡbee dɛ́ tɛɛ kembɔr kohona.”

english_verse: But Abram answered, “Lord All-Powerful, you have given me everything I could ask for, except children. And when I die, Eliezer of Damascus will get all I own.
translation_verse: Anee Abram ŋɔ, “Nemenɛ Korowii, bɔkwa konee hɛɛ ba kpɔe tɛ mɛ ó ɡwaa kɛŋɔ maa wola bie lolɛ bwa nɔɔ? N bonɔɔ Eliesa waa le Damaskɔs laanee dɛɛ ba n kapɛrɛ dii.

english_verse: You have not given me any children, and this servant of mine will inherit everything.”
translation_verse: He nao kɛŋɔ he ta men bie tɛɛ anomanta, n bonɔɔna la bini bɛlee dɛ́ di n kapɛrɛ.”

english_verse: The Lord replied, “No, he won't! You will have a son of your own, and everything you have will be his.”
translation_verse: Belaa o berɛ no kɛŋɔ Korowii aa bol waa o be ja ŋɔ, “N dɛ ŋɔ he be ŋɔ a ɡɛ bonɔɔ nɔ laa dɛ́ di he kapɛrɛ, he ɡbaɡba biee dɛ́ di.”

english_verse: Then the Lord took Abram outside and said, “Look at the sky and see if you can count the stars. That's how many descendants you will have.”
translation_verse: O nao kɛŋɔ Korowii aa lawɔ le buse dɛ ka ŋɔ, “Ha sie nyiŋi nyundua, dɛ́ na ɡɛ weweela aa wara, hɛɛ won kura aa? Gɛɛ mɛɛ ba ɡela he naanar warɛ.”

english_verse: Abram believed the Lord, so the Lord was pleased with him and accepted him. The Lord Makes Another Promise to Abram
translation_verse: Belaa o yarada Korowii, asɛ Korowii che o yarada ta dɛ lɛo kɛ nɛndɛɛɡe o waa su o siwi.

english_verse: The Lord said to Abram, “I brought you here from Ur in Chaldea, and I gave you this land.”
translation_verse: O ŋɔ o be ja ŋɔ, “Menee Korowii, menee kpɔe le Ur waa lɔ Babelɔn harɛ ta, dɛ ba kpɔ harɛ nɔ tɛɛ o ɛ he ɡbabir kon saŋ bɛlbwa dɛɛ la.”

english_verse: Abram asked, “Lord God, how can I know the land will be mine?”
translation_verse: Belaa Abram bɔɔro ŋɔ, “Nemenɛ Korowii, ɛrɛɛ aa ba ɛɛ ń jemɛ kɛŋɔ n konee yɔ?”

english_verse: Then the Lord told him, “Bring me a three-year-old cow, a three-year-old female goat, a three-year-old ram, a dove, and a young pigeon.”
translation_verse: Anee Korowii chaŋo ŋɔ, “Lawɛ nao ne booh dɛ pebal, a bini bɛlbwa waa di bene atoro, ne borɔnoma ne kulukuku bie ba tɛ mɛ.”

english_verse: Abram obeyed the Lord. Then he cut the animals in half and laid the two halves of each animal opposite each other on the ground. But he did not cut the doves and pigeons in half.
translation_verse: Asɛ o lawɛ a ɡɛ kwaa waa baɡla la ba tɛo, dɛ pere a bɛlbwa bini anɛ, dɛ bila asɛ a peɡra la sie chaɡɛ dɔŋa. Kɛ jumbii la te, o ta a bini peɡre.

english_verse: And when birds came down to eat the animals, Abram chased them away.
translation_verse: Belaa kokosakire tu ba harɛ ŋɔ á ba di ola la, asɛ Abram doŋa.

english_verse: As the sun was setting, Abram fell into a deep sleep, and everything became dark and frightening.
translation_verse: Aa baa ka tama asɛ wee le harɛ la, Abram chɔ dom ka ɡarɛ. O dom chɔe bini la, bɔr biro kpirkpir ken ta o nɛ, asɛ ɔmee lawɔ kohona.

english_verse: Four generations later, your descendants will return here and take this land, because only then will the people who live here be so sinful that they deserve to be punished.
translation_verse: He naanar bele banaarɛ ɛɛ ba kaaloo mɔɔ, he naanar berɛ ba harɛ nɔ ta, dɛkalkɛŋɔ Amɔre tena wechɔɡa baa dɛ ɛ la ta tele kɛ bá dɔ deŋnetɛra mɔɔ.”

english_verse: Sometime after sunset, when it was very dark, a smoking cooking pot and a flaming fire passed between the two halves of each animal.
translation_verse: Wee aa joa asɛ bɔr bir la, kapɛla waa dɛ lawɛ nii ne vii bɛl soo siwi nii aa lɔ o ta wɛɛ le chuu deno ba kpɔ ola la baah.

english_verse: At that time the Lord made an agreement with Abram and told him: I will give your descendants the land east of the Shihor River on the border of Egypt as far as the Euphrates River.
translation_verse: Awolaa Korowii ne Abram fɔwɛ fɔo. Asɛ Korowii ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “He naanaree n kpɔ a ɡɛ harɛ nɔ dɛɛ tɛ. O le Ijipt harɛ jwɛh ta dɛ ba Yufretis Moo ta.

english_verse: They will possess the land of the Kenites, the Kenizzites, the Kadmonites,
translation_verse: Ken ne Kenis dɛ Kadmɔn tena harɛre bwa jao,

english_verse: the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Rephaites,
translation_verse: dɛ kpoŋe ka le Hiti ne Pɛrɛs dɛ Refa tena,

english_verse: the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Girgashites, and the Jebusites.
translation_verse: ne Amɔre ne Keenan ne Girɡasi dɛ Jebus tena harɛre ta bwa.”

english_verse: Abram's wife Sarai had not been able to have any children. But she owned a young Egyptian slave woman named Hagar,
translation_verse: Abram haah Sarai ta bie lolɛ tɛo. Dɛ o dɔ tolo bɛl waa ɛ Ijipt te baa yerɔ Heeɡa o do o sie,

english_verse: and Sarai said to Abram, “The Lord has not given me any children. Sleep with my slave, and if she has a child, it will be mine.” Abram agreed,
translation_verse: asɛ o ŋɔ Abram be ŋɔ, “Korowii ta ɡelɛ n lolɛ, anomanta, berɛ kpɔ n tolo nɔ. A ken ɛɛ che o nɛɛ n dɔ bie.” Asɛ o sɛh a ta.

english_verse: and Sarai gave him Hagar to be his wife. This happened after Abram had lived in the land of Canaan for ten years.
translation_verse: Anomanta, o lawɛ Heeɡa tɛo. Dɛ Abram soɡe Keenan harɛ bene fi mɔɔ a ɡɛ waa nɔ chiɡ.

english_verse: Later, when Hagar knew she was going to have a baby, she became proud and treated Sarai hatefully.
translation_verse: Abram lawɔ chɔ o kpoŋe tea. Heeɡa aa baa na kɛŋɔ o kpoŋe tea la, o hah Sarai dɛɛ nyiŋi o nyubaah.

english_verse: Then Sarai said to Abram, “It's all your fault! I gave you my slave woman, but she has been hateful to me ever since she found out she was pregnant. You have done me wrong, and you will have to answer to the Lord for this.”
translation_verse: Anee Sarai ŋɔ Abram be ŋɔ, “Henee ɡela Heeɡa dɛɛ ɛɛ mɛ la. Menee lawɛ n tolo tɛɛ, kɛ taraken waa bera jemɛ kɛŋɔ o kpoŋe tea la, o siwi aa men tɔɡɛ kpa. Korowiirii dɛ́ baɡle n ne hen naate waa ɛ wechɔɡa.”

english_verse: Abram said, “All right! She's your slave—do whatever you want with her.” Then Sarai began treating Hagar so harshly that she finally ran away.
translation_verse: Belaa Abram ŋɔ Sarai be ŋɔ, “He toloo, he dɔ o kpeɡri dɛ́ doo ɡɛ haa dɛ nyin.” Asɛ Sarai fiiɡu kohona o ba chwa le o be.

english_verse: Hagar stopped to rest at a spring in the desert on the road to Shur. While she was there, the angel of the Lord came to her
translation_verse: Waa dɛ kaa la, belaa Korowii nyundua torome bɛl ba o be. Dɛ o lɔ bobɛl nee aa dɛ bule pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ bɛl ta, dɛ do bwɛɛ Suur ŋwɛnɛ ta.

english_verse: and asked, “Hagar, where have you come from, and where are you going?” She answered, “I'm running away from Sarai, my owner.”
translation_verse: Korowii nyundua torome la bɔɔro ŋɔ, “Sarai tolo Heeɡa, leperaa hɛɛ kaalɔ?” Asɛ o ŋɔ, “Chwae n chwa le n nya Sarai be.”

english_verse: The angel said, “Go back to Sarai and be her slave.
translation_verse: Asɛ Korowii nyundua torome la ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Berɛ kaa o be dɛ́ kaa tomɔ.”

english_verse: I will give you a son, who will be called Ishmael, because I have heard your cry for help. And someday I will give you so many descendants that no one will be able to count them all.
translation_verse: Dɛ berɛ ŋɔ o be ja ŋɔ, “Bie lɔ he be. Hɛɛ lolɛ bibaalee dɛ́ pa o sɔn Ismael, dɛkalkɛ Korowii no he suna wii.

english_verse: But your son will live far from his relatives; he will be like a wild donkey, fighting everyone, and everyone fighting him.”
translation_verse: Kɛ he bibaa la ɛɛ do kɛŋɔ keeɡo kpaŋii o soɡa bini, ásɛ o ne nomɛlbwa aa somee do. Mɛɛ korɛ o soŋnibɔree dɛ́ le o lolanar bini.”

english_verse: Hagar thought, “Have I really seen God and lived to tell about it?” So from then on she called him, “The God Who Sees Me.”
translation_verse: Korowii aa bol waa Heeɡa be la nomanta, o pa bie la sɔn ŋɔ, “Korowii haa dɛ na mɛ,” dɛ ŋɔ, “Korowiirii n na dɛ ta so le nɔ naa?”

english_verse: That's why people call the well between Kadesh and Bered, “The Well of the Living One Who Sees Me.”
translation_verse: Anee ɡela nɛra ɛɛ yerɛ bule la Beɛ Lahae Rɔe, o munii kɛŋɔ, ‘Nɛn waa lole saŋ bɛlbwa dɛɛ na mɛ.’ O chɔ bwɛɛ Kades ne Bɛrɛd baah ta.

english_verse: I will keep my solemn promise to you and give you more descendants than can be counted.”
translation_verse: Mɛɛ ɡeloo n ne he baah fɔo la che, ásɛ he ne he naanar warɛ kohona.”

english_verse: Abram bowed with his face to the ground, and God said:
translation_verse: Belaa Abram kpɔ sie pi harɛ asɛ Korowii ŋɔ o be ŋɔ,

english_verse: I promise that you will be the father of many nations. So now I'm changing your name from Abram to Abraham.
translation_verse: Baa hen Abramee yerɛ kpa, kɛ baa dɛɛ yerɛ Abraham, dɛkalkɛŋɔ henee mɛɛ ba ɡela he ɛ nɛnfuuh bwa mɛɛ.

english_verse: I will give you a lot of descendants, and they will become great nations. Some of them will even be kings.
translation_verse: Mɛɛ ɡeloo he naanar ya taeh, ásɛ a che he nɛɛ nɛra warɛ harɛre ta, ásɛ ba bini bane ɛ koranar.

english_verse: I will always keep the promise I have made to you and your descendants, because I am your God and their God.
translation_verse: Mɛɛ ɡeloo n fɔo la do n ne hen ne he naanar baah saŋ bɛlbwa dɛɛ la, ásɛ n ɛ he ne he naanar baa ka ba la bwa Korowii haa dɛɛ tom mɛ.

english_verse: I will give you and them the land in which you are now a foreigner. I will give the whole land of Canaan to your family forever, and I will be their God.
translation_verse: Mɛɛ tɛ he ne he naanar Keenan harɛ haa ɛ hɔɔhra dɛ so o ta taraken nɔ bwaa, ásɛ o ɛ he kon saŋ bɛlbwa dɛɛ la, ásɛ n ɛ Korowii haa dɛɛ tom mɛ.”

english_verse: Abraham, you and all future members of your family must promise to obey me.
translation_verse: Korowii berɔ ŋɔ Abraham be ŋɔ, “He ɡe la, he ne he naanar baa ka ba la chɛ kɛŋɔ hé teŋɛ n fɔo nɔ ta.

english_verse: As the sign that you are keeping this promise, you must circumcise every man and boy in your family.
translation_verse: Penteŋa nɔɔ dɛ́ baɡle fɔo waa chɔ n ne he baah.

english_verse: Any man who isn't circumcised hasn't kept his part of the promise and cannot be one of my people.
translation_verse: Bɛlbwa waa wola o pen teŋe la ta n nɛra nɛɛ jae kpa, dɛkalkɛŋɔ o ta n fɔo la ta teŋɛ.”

english_verse: Abraham, from now on your wife's name will be Sarah instead of Sarai.
translation_verse: Korowii berɔ ŋɔ Abraham be ŋɔ, “He haah sɔn laa Sarai kpa. Le fini dɛɛ kaa o sɔne Saara.

english_verse: I will bless her, and you will have a son by her. She will become the mother of nations, and some of her descendants will even be kings.
translation_verse: Mɛɛ tɛo hɛɛraa, ásɛ o lolɛ bibaa tɛɛ. Mɛɛ ɡeloo o ɛ harɛre nɛra bwa naa, ásɛ ba bini bane ɛ koojena.”

english_verse: Then he asked God, “Why not let Ishmael inherit what you have promised me?”
translation_verse: Belaa o ŋɔ Korowii be ŋɔ, “N Naa Korowii, he fe ɡelɔ ɡɛ hɛɛra nɔ ba Ismael nɛɛ sɛ?”

english_verse: But God answered: No! You and Sarah will have a son. His name will be Isaac, and I will make an everlasting promise to him and his descendants.
translation_verse: Ate, Korowii ŋɔ, “N noɔ, kɛ Saara ɛɛ lolɛ bibaalee tɛɛ he pa o sɔn Aesek. Onee mɛɛ ba ɡela n fɔo la chɔ n ne o baah ta, dɛ́ chɔ tɛ n ne o ɡe naanar. Wɛɛ ɛ fɔo waa wola jaɡa dɔe bwa.

english_verse: However, I have heard what you asked me to do for Ishmael, and so I will also bless him with many descendants. He will be the father of twelve princes, and I will make his family a great nation.
translation_verse: N no Ismael haa soŋ mɛ o waa la wa. Mɛɛ tɛo hɛɛraa dɛ́ ɡel o bii ne o naanar warɛ kohona. Mɛɛ ɛo deene fi dɛ anɛ nomonome mɛɛ, ásɛ dɛ ɡel o naanar do kan ba harɛ ta.

english_verse: But your son Isaac will be born about this time next year, and the promise I am making to you and your family will be for him and his descendants forever.
translation_verse: Kɛ mɛɛ ɡeloo n fɔo la do n ne he bie Aesek Saara aa dɛ ba o lola benanyoa saŋ nɔ bɔr la baah.”

english_verse: God finished speaking to Abraham and then left.
translation_verse: Korowii aa bol waa Abraham be tonɛ la, o le o be dɛ kaa.

english_verse: On that same day Abraham obeyed God by circumcising Ishmael. Abraham was also circumcised, and so were all the other men and boys in his household, including his servants and slaves. He was
translation_verse: ne baala baa lɔ o dem, ne banɔ la baa ɛ o nɛndɔɔla dɛ bibaala baa lol ba o dem bwa.

english_verse: One hot summer afternoon while Abraham was sitting by the entrance to his tent near the sacred trees of Mamre, the Lord appeared to him.
translation_verse: Awola webaŋkpela bɛl, Abraham soɡe o tɛnte dea doonyoa Mamre dajena la bɔr, asɛ Korowii berɛ ba o be ja.

english_verse: Abraham looked up and saw three men standing nearby. He quickly ran to meet them, bowed with his face to the ground,
translation_verse: Abraham ha sie nyiŋi dɛ baala batoro banee ka cheɡa. Waa na ba la, o den ɛ warane dɛɛ chem ba, dɛ ɡuŋ ba harɛ dɛ kpɔ sie pi harɛ,

english_verse: and said, “Please come to my home where I can serve you.
translation_verse: dɛ ŋɔ, “Nomonome, dɛ men maa ɛ he bie chɛo kɛŋɔ hé choɡ mɛ naa, he bɛ men ɡarɛ ta kaa.

english_verse: I'll have some water brought, so you can wash your feet, then you can rest under a tree.
translation_verse: Hé ɡel n ba tɛ heyaa nee tama he sarame he nakpale, ásɛ dɛ ka onɛ daa nɔ mun bela.

english_verse: Let me get you some food to give you strength before you leave. I would be honored to serve you.” “Thank you very much,” they answered. “We accept your offer.”
translation_verse: Haa dɔa ba he bie be nɔ, hé ɡel n nyin kondikwaa tɛ heyaa he di, ásɛ he won dɔ bokpeɡfala dɛ́ kaa.” Anee ba sɛh ŋɔ o ɛ ɡɛ tɛɛ ba.

english_verse: Abraham went quickly to his tent and said to Sarah, “Hurry! Get a large sack of flour and make some bread.”

english_verse: But God said, “Abraham, don't worry about your slave woman and the boy. Just do what Sarah tells you. Isaac will inherit your family name,
translation_verse: Anee Korowii ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Bɛ ɡel he yomhaah Heeɡa ne o bie la waa hiaeh kwara. He te dɛɛ no Saara be dɛkalkɛ, Aesek luɡe taa hɛɛ ba he naanar maa baɡɛ nyoa la dɔe.

english_verse: but the son of the slave woman is also your son, and I will make his descendants into a great nation.”
translation_verse: He yomhaah bie la ɡe la, wɛɛ yao taeh, dɛ́ ɡe dɔ ba harɛ, dɛkalkɛ he bie o ɡe.”

english_verse: Early the next morning Abraham gave Hagar an animal skin full of water and some bread. Then he put the boy on her shoulder and sent them away. They wandered around in the desert near Beersheba,
translation_verse: Anomanta, Abraham iro chɔmbibii dɛ kpɔ kondikwaa ne oltɔn pur, dɛ do nee o bini o su dɛ kpɔ chɔŋɛ Heeɡa vaama ta. O lawɛ bie la ja o nɛ, dɛ ta ba ŋwɛnɛ ba kaa. Heeɡa aa lea kaa la, bobɛl waa ɛ pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ baa yerɔ Beɛseebaa o ka do dɛɛ ɡaaɡe.

english_verse: and after they had run out of water, Hagar put her son under a bush.
translation_verse: Pur bini nee la baa tonɛ o kpɔ bie la ka bil dajeɡa bɛl lɔɡa,

english_verse: Then she sat down a long way off, because she could not bear to watch him die. And she cried bitterly.
translation_verse: asɛ dɛ kaa ɡelo dɛ ɛ naɡale lafa del dɛ ka so. O lii o nyu bini ŋɔ, “Maa won che nyiŋi, ásɛ n bie sewɛ n siwi ta.” O soɡe bela dɛ wi kohona.

english_verse: When God heard the boy crying, the angel of God called out to Hagar from heaven and said, “Hagar, why are you worried? Don't be afraid. I have heard your son crying.
translation_verse: Belaa Korowii no bie la wii, asɛ o nyundua torome che nyundua ŋɔ Heeɡa be ŋɔ, “Heeɡa, bɔkwa waa dɛɛ hae nɔ? Bɛ ɔmɛ. Korowii no he bie la waa chɔ bela la wii.

english_verse: Help him up and hold his hand, because I will make him the father of a great nation.”
translation_verse: Anomanta, ir ka kpɔɔ dɛ́ ɡbɛɡbɛo. Mɛɛ ɡeloo o ya taeh o harɛ do kan.”

english_verse: Then God let her see a well. So she went to the well and filled the skin with water, then gave some to her son.
translation_verse: Belaa Korowii ɡel o sie chole bule bɛl ta, asɛ o la ka dɔ nee do oltɔn la bini, dɛ ka tɛ bie la ane o nyɔ.

english_verse: About this time Abimelech and his army commander Phicol said to Abraham, “God blesses everything you do!
translation_verse: A ɡɛ saŋ la, Kooro Abemɛlɛk kpɔ o laa tena nomoa Fekɔl dɛ la Abraham be dɛ ka ŋɔ, “He wobɛlbwa haa dɛ ɛ la, Korowii ja he nɛ.

english_verse: Now I want you to promise in the name of God that you will always be loyal to me and my descendants, just as I have always been loyal to you in this land where you have lived as a foreigner.”
translation_verse: Anomanta, ŋwɛɛ Korowii kɛŋɔ haa n ne n bii ne naanaree neɡre. Nyiŋi kɛrɛdɛ wedɛɛɡa maa ɛɛ la, ásɛ dɛ kpɔ ɡɛ ɛ n ne harɛ nɔ haa baa so o ta taraken dɛ ɛ hɔɔhra nɔ tena bwa.”

english_verse: And so, Abraham promised he would.
translation_verse: Asɛ o ŋɔ, “N ŋwɛɛrɔ kɛŋɔ mɛɛ ɛ ɡɛɛ.”

english_verse: One day, Abraham told Abimelech, “Some of your servants have taken over one of my wells.”
translation_verse: Belaa o bol o kɔlɔŋ bɛl Kooro Abemɛlɛk bonɔɔna aa kpɔ kpeɡri lɛ la waa baɡlo.

english_verse: “This is the first I've heard about it,” Abimelech replied. “Why haven't you said something before? I don't have any idea who did it.”
translation_verse: Asɛ o chaŋe ŋɔ, “Maa nɛra baa ɛ ɡɛ waa nɔ jemɛ bwa. Dɛ fini laa hɛɛ bola nɔ naa, n fe ta an noɛ bwa.”

english_verse: Abraham gave Abimelech some sheep and cattle, then the two men made a peace treaty.
translation_verse: Abraham kpɔ peera ne nae tɛo, asɛ ba che a ta dɛ fɔwɛ fɔo.

english_verse: Abraham separated seven female lambs from his flock of sheep,
translation_verse: Abraham berɔ chale peloni anuanɛ, dɛ le o peera bini dɛ kpɔa ka che baŋ bɛl.

english_verse: and Abimelech asked, “Why have you done this?”
translation_verse: Asɛ Kooro Abemɛlɛk bɔɔro ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ a mun ɛɛ chaɡle ɔ?”

english_verse: Abraham replied, “I want you to accept these seven lambs as proof that I dug this well.”
translation_verse: Anee o chaŋe ŋɔ, “Lɛ peloni anuanɛ nɔ, ásɛ a ɛ danseɛ kɛŋɔ he sɛoh kɛ menee kwi kɔlɔŋ nɔ.”

english_verse: So they called the place Beersheba, because they made a treaty there.
translation_verse: Ba pa bela sɔn Beɛseeba, dɛkalkɛŋɔ belaa ba nɛra banɛ la cheme dɛ fɔwɛ fɔo.

english_verse: When the treaty was completed, Abimelech and his army commander Phicol went back to the land of the Philistines.
translation_verse: Ba Beɛseeba fɔo nɔ habɔɔ la, Kooro Abemɛlɛk ne Fekɔl berɔ kaa Filisti tena harɛ ta.

english_verse: Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Beersheba and worshiped the eternal Lord God.
translation_verse: Asɛ Abraham chɔɔ daa bɛl Beɛseeba bela, dɛɛ tomɛ Korowii waa lole saŋ bɛlbwa la bela.

english_verse: Then Abraham lived a long time as a foreigner in the land of the Philistines.
translation_verse: Abraham soɡe Filisti tena harɛ ta bela biɡri.

english_verse: Some years later God decided to test Abraham, so he spoke to him. Abraham answered, “Here I am, Lord.”
translation_verse: Waa nɔ bwa habɔɔ la, Korowii daah Abraham dɛ́ na ɡɛ waa dɛ yaradao. O yerɔ, “Abraham,” asɛ o sɛh ŋɔ “N Naa Korowii, menee nɔ.”

english_verse: The Lord said, “Go get Isaac, your only son, the one you dearly love! Take him to the land of Moriah, and I will show you a mountain where you must sacrifice him to me on the fires of an altar.”
translation_verse: Belaa o ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Kpɔ he bibeŋkpoŋ Aesek haa dɛ nyin o waa la kaa Moria harɛ ta dɛ́ ka kpoo, dɛ́ fuuh ɛ saraha tɛ mɛ. Mɛɛ baɡlee bwejen bɛl haa ka ɛ saraha la o taa.”

english_verse: So Abraham got up early the next morning and chopped wood for the fire. He put a saddle on his donkey and set out with Isaac and two servants for the place where God had told him to go.
translation_verse: Tɔ aa per chɔmbibii la, o iro do o bone dɛ vɔwɛ dawɛ keeɡo nɛ. O kpɔ o bonɔɔna banɛ ne o bie Aesek, ne daa waa ka mar dɛ ɛ saraha la, asɛ ba chiɡ ŋwɛnɛ ta dɛɛ kaa bela Korowii aa baɡlo la.

english_verse: Three days later Abraham looked off in the distance and saw the place.
translation_verse: Tɔpetooro wee la, o ha sie nyiŋi dɛ na bela Korowii aa baɡlo la bojaŋ.

english_verse: He told his servants, “Stay here with the donkey, while my son and I go over there to worship. We will come back.”
translation_verse: O ŋɔ o bonɔɔna la be ŋɔ, “Hé ne keeɡo nɔ che bonɔ, ásɛ n ne bie nɔ ka soŋe Korowii dɛ́ berɛ ba.”

english_verse: Abraham put the wood on Isaac's shoulder, but he carried the hot coals and the knife. As the two of them walked along,
translation_verse: Ate, o laa daa baa ka mar la kpɔ choɡ Aesek, dɛ ɡe kpɔ kere ne nii kpoŋe baa kaa.

english_verse: Isaac said, “Father, we have the coals and the wood, but where is the lamb for the sacrifice?” “My son,” Abraham answered, “God will provide the lamb.” The two of them walked on, and
translation_verse: Asɛ Abraham chaŋe ŋɔ, “N bie, Korowii ɡbaɡbaa dɛ́ tɛ pee maa kpɔ ɛ saraha la.” Ba nɛra banɛ la bwa berɛ tɛr do dɛɛ kaa.

english_verse: when they reached the place that God had told him about, Abraham built an altar and placed the wood on it. Next, he tied up his son and put him on the wood.
translation_verse: Baa kaa tel bela Korowii aa chaɡle Abraham la, o kwaa kon baa dɛ fuh kwaa o ta dɛɛ jam Korowii la bɛl bela, asɛ dɛ pa daa darawe o ta. O vɔrɔwe o bie Aesek dɛ kpɔɔ dawɛ daa la doa.

english_verse: He then took the knife and got ready to kill his son.
translation_verse: Belaa o ha nɔn kpɔ kere la dɛ́ fee kpɔ kpo o bie la.

english_verse: But the Lord's angel shouted from heaven, “Abraham! Abraham!” “Here I am!” he answered.
translation_verse: Asɛ Korowii nyundua torome bɛl che nyundua yerɔ, “Abraham!” Anee o sɛh ŋɔ, “Menee nɔ.”

english_verse: “Don't hurt the boy or harm him in any way!” the angel said. “Now I know that you truly obey God, because you were willing to offer him your only son.”
translation_verse: Asɛ o ŋɔ, “Dɛɛ berɛ bie la wobɛlbwa ɛɛ. Namee n ta jemɛ kɛŋɔ he dɛ ɔmɛ Korowii, dɛkalkɛ he ta men he bibeŋkpoŋ nɔ kwaraa vɔmɛ.”

english_verse: Abraham looked up and saw a ram caught by its horns in the bushes. So he took the ram and sacrificed it instead of his son.
translation_verse: Abraham ha sie nyiŋi, asɛ dɛ na pebal o nyeɡlare aa karɛ kaɡra ane ta o che. Asɛ o ka lawɔ dɛ kpoo, dɛ kpɔ chiɡ o bie la naa ta, dɛ fuh ɛ saraha tɛ Korowii.

english_verse: Abraham named that place “The Lord Will Provide.” And even now people say, “On the mountain of the Lord it will be provided.”
translation_verse: Anomanta, o pa bela sɔn ‘Korowii Dɛɛ Tɛ.’ Dɛ ba le fini, ba dɛ bol bela waa ŋɔ, “Korowii ɛɛ tɛo o bwe la doa.”

english_verse: The Lord's angel called out from heaven a second time:
translation_verse: Belaa Korowii nyundua torome la che nyundua dɛ yerɛ nɛɛtena ja

english_verse: You were willing to offer your only son to the Lord, and so he makes you this solemn promise,
translation_verse: dɛ ŋɔ, “N ŋwɛɛ n ɡbaɡba kɛŋɔ waa nɔ haa ɛa he ta men he bibeŋkpoŋ kwaraa vɔmɛ nomanta,

english_verse: “I will bless you and give you such a large family, that someday your descendants will be more numerous than the stars in the sky or the grains of sand along the seashore. They will defeat their enemies and take over the cities where their enemies live.
translation_verse: mɛɛ tɛɛ hɛɛra tentenee. Mɛɛ ɡeloo he naanar warɛ kɛŋɔ weweela ne mpo nyoa hɛŋle. He naanar ɛɛ yoo lɛ ba dɔma bwɛɛre dɛɛ di a kpeɡri,

english_verse: You have obeyed me, and so you and your descendants will be a blessing to all nations on earth.”
translation_verse: ásɛ a che ba nɛɛ ń tɛ nɛwɛnyina bwa hɛɛra. Mɛɛ ɛ ɡɛɛ dɛkalkɛ, he ɛ waa maa dɛ nyin.”

english_verse: Abraham and Isaac went back to the servants who had come with him, and they returned to Abraham's home in Beersheba. The Children of Nahor
translation_verse: Belaa Abraham berɛ ba o bonɔɔna la be, asɛ ba ir ba Beɛseeba, Abraham so bela. Neehɔ bibaala wa

english_verse: Nahor also had another wife. Her name was Reumah, and she had four sons: Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah.
translation_verse: Dɛ o ne haah bɛl soɡo o ɛ o sɛno baa yerɔ Reuma. O ɡe bii waa lol ba laanee Teba ne Gaham ne Tahas dɛ Maaka.

english_verse: “I live as a foreigner in your land, and I don't own any property where I can bury my wife. Please let me buy a piece of land.”
translation_verse: “N ɛ hɔɔh dɛ ba pu heyaa so, bonɔ laa n le. Anomanta, hé tɛ mɛ harɛ asɛ n yawɛ dɛ huɡe n haah.”

english_verse: “Sir,” they answered, “you are an important man. Choose the best place to bury your wife. None of us would refuse you a resting place for your dead.”
translation_verse: “Nomoa, dɛɛ no, nomonjenii hen ya bini bonɔ. Yaa won vɔmɛ lalbɔɔ ŋɔ he bɛ he lale huɡe. He won o huɡa ya lalbɔɔne nɔ bɛlbwa he tea aa too o ta bini.”

english_verse: and replied, “If you are willing to let me bury my wife here, please ask Zohar's son Ephron
translation_verse: dɛ soŋ ba ŋɔ, “Dɛ he sɛoh ŋɔ n huɡe n nɛn tenaa, amɔ he no n be, dɛ́ soŋe Soha bie Efron tɛ mɛ

english_verse: to sell me Machpelah Cave at the end of his field. I'll pay what it's worth, and all of you can be witnesses.”
translation_verse: kɛŋɔ ó tɛ mɛ bwebɔɔ waa lɔ Makpɛla dɛ ɛ o kon dɛ chɔ o harɛ nyoa la. He ŋɔ o be ŋɔ ó yoɡu ɡɛ o yoɡ aa chɛa tɛ mɛ, ásɛ n dɔ lala huɡri bɔr he be bonɔ.”

english_verse: Ephron was sitting there near the city gate, when Abraham made this request, and he answered,
translation_verse: Anee Efron chaŋe Abraham o bala Hiti tena baa soɡe bwɛɛ la doonyoa la sie dɛ ŋɔ,

english_verse: “Sir, the whole field, including the cave, is yours. With my own people as witnesses, I freely give it to you as a burial place for your dead.”
translation_verse: “Akai, nomoa, dɛɛ no n be. N kpɔ harɛ la tɛɛ, dɛ kpɔ bwebɔɔ la ɡe tɛɛ. N nɛra nɔ bwa siwi taa n kpɔ harɛ la dɛɛ tɛɛ. Huɡe he nɛn o ta.”

english_verse: Once again, Abraham bowed down
translation_verse: Asɛ Abraham ba Hiti tena la harɛ ja,

english_verse: and said to Ephron, “In front of these witnesses, I offer you the full price, so I can bury my wife. Please accept my offer.”
translation_verse: dɛ ŋɔ Efron be nɛra la bwa sie ŋɔ, “Dɛɛ no, dɛ hɛɛ sɛoh tenaa, mɛɛ bɔe harɛ la kemee. N dɛ soŋe kɛ he lɛ, ásɛ n won huɡe n lale la bela.”

english_verse: Abraham accepted Ephron's offer and paid him the
translation_verse: dɛ do Abraham nɔn ta Hiti tena baa lɔ bwɛɛ doonyoa la ta la bwa sie.

english_verse: So Abraham buried his wife Sarah in Machpelah Cave that was in the field
translation_verse: A habɔɔ la, Abraham huɡe o haah Saara bwebɔɔ la ta. Belaa baa yerɛ Hɛbrɔn, o do Keenan harɛ ta la.

english_verse: Abraham was now a very old man. The Lord had made him rich, and he was successful in everything he did.
translation_verse: Abraham biɡro dɛ hwɛɛh ɡe kɛrɛdɛ. Dɛ Korowii tɛo hɛɛra o wobɛlbwa ta.

english_verse: One day, Abraham called in his most trusted servant and said to him, “Solemnly promise me
translation_verse: Asɛ o ŋɔ o bonɔɔna bwa nomoa waa dɛ nyiŋi o komɛlbwa ta dem bela la be ŋɔ, “Gɔɔ nɔɔra nyundua,

english_verse: in the name of the Lord, who rules heaven and earth, that you won't choose a wife for my son Isaac from the people here in the land of Canaan.
translation_verse: dɛ́ ŋwɛɛ Korowii waa lɔ nyundua ne harɛ bwa la, kɛŋɔ haa Keenan tena maa soɡe ba baah nɔ bihaahnee nyin tɛ n bie nɔ.

english_verse: Instead, go back to the land where I was born and find a wife for him from among my relatives.”
translation_verse: N ɡbaɡba harɛ ta ne n lolanar binii mɛɛ nyin kɛ he mo haah tɛ n bie Aesek.”

english_verse: But the servant asked, “What if the young woman I choose refuses to leave home and come here with me? Should I send Isaac there to look for a wife?”
translation_verse: Belaa o bonɔɔ la bɔɔro ŋɔ, “Dɛ haah maa nyin tɛo la ŋɔ waa won teŋɛ n nɛɛ dɛ́ ba harɛ nɔ ta naa, ń kpɔ he bie la berɛ kaa harɛ haa le o ta ba bonɔ la ta kɛɛ?”

english_verse: “No!” Abraham answered. “Don't ever do that, no matter what.
translation_verse: Asɛ o ɡe chaŋe ŋɔ, “Nyiŋi kɛrɛdɛ dɛ bɛ berɛ kpɔ n bie la kaa harɛ la ta kpa.”

english_verse: The Lord who rules heaven brought me here from the land where I was born and promised that he would give this land to my descendants forever. When you go back there, the Lord will send his angel ahead of you to help you find a wife for my son.
translation_verse: Dɛ berɛ ŋɔ, “Korowii Waa Dɛ Di Kora Nyundua laanee kpɔ mɛ le n mɛɛ dem ne harɛ baa lol mɛ o ta la ta, dɛ ŋwɛɛ baɡ mɛ kɛŋɔ n naanaree wɛɛ ba ɡɛ harɛ nɔ kpɔe tɛ. Wɛɛ ɡeloo o nyundua torome tɔ he sie, ásɛ he won ka dɔ haah ba tɛ n bie nɔ.

english_verse: If the woman refuses to come along, you don't have to keep this promise. But don't ever take my son back there.”
translation_verse: Kɛ dɛ haah la ta sɛɛh dɛ teŋɛ ba naa, amɔ dɛ he ta ŋwɛɛra haa ŋwɛɛra la ta toe. Kɛ nyiŋi kɛrɛdɛ kɛŋɔ ŋwɛnɛ bɛlbwa ta la haa n bie kpɔ kaa bela.”

english_verse: So the servant gave Abraham his word that he would do everything he had been told to do.
translation_verse: Asɛ Abraham bonɔɔ la ɡɔɔ nɔɔra nyundua o sie, asɛ dɛ ŋwɛɛ a ɡɛ ŋwɛɛra la baɡlo.

english_verse: Soon after that, the servant loaded ten of Abraham's camels with valuable gifts. Then he set out for the city in northern Syria, where Abraham's brother Nahor lived.
translation_verse: Belaa bonɔɔ la kpɔ o nomoa nyoɡmare fi, dɛ kpɔ nomoa la laaladɛɛɡa bwa soo siwi ja, dɛ chiɡ ŋwɛnɛ ta kaa Neehɔ bwɛ, Mɛsopoteemea harɛ ta.

english_verse: When he got there, he let the camels rest near the well outside the city. It was late afternoon, the time when the women came out for water.
translation_verse: Waa vala dɛ tel bwɛɛ la dahare awola bɛl la, dɛ bɔr dɛ jo haahna ɛɛ la jɔmɔrpoli, asɛ o ɡel nyoɡmare la ɡuŋi harɛ bule bɛl nyoa.

english_verse: The servant prayed: You, Lord, are the God my master Abraham worships. Please keep your promise to him and let me find a wife for Isaac today.
translation_verse: Ate, o soŋe Korowii ŋɔ, “N Naa Korowii n dɔɔ Abraham aa dɛ tomɛ, n dɛ soŋe, ɡel a chiɡ mɛ kɛrɛdɛ fini, dɛ́ teŋɛ nyoa haa baɡɛ n dɔɔ la ta.

english_verse: The young women of the city will soon come to this well for water,
translation_verse: Bule nɔ jwɛɛh bonɔ maa cheɡa nɔ, dɛ bwɛɛ nɔ toli balɔ ŋɔ bá ba dɔ ne aa,

english_verse: and I'll ask one of them for a drink. If she gives me a drink and then offers to get some water for my camels, I'll know she is the one you have chosen and that you have kept your promise to my master.
translation_verse: ɡel onɔ la maa ŋɔ ó choɡ o nee ásɛ n nyɔ ane la sɛh, dɛ́ berɛ ŋɔ wɛɛ tɛ n nyoɡmare nɔ ɡe anee á nyɔ la, ó ɛ haah haa dɛ ba kpɔe tɛ Aesek la. A taa mɛɛ ba cheɡa dɛ́ jemɛ kɛŋɔ he teŋɛ nyoa haa baɡɛ n nomoa la ta.”

english_verse: Abraham's servant ran to her and said, “Please let me have a drink of water.”
translation_verse: Asɛ bonɔɔ la chwa dɛ ka chemo dɛ ŋɔ, “N dɛ soŋe ɡel n nyɔ he nee nɔ tama ane.”

english_verse: “I'll be glad to,” she answered. Then she quickly took the jar from her shoulder and held it while he drank.
translation_verse: Anee o chaŋo ŋɔ, “N dɔɔ, nyɔ ane.” Asɛ o ɛ warane choɡ nee la dɛ kpoŋa nɔn ta dɛ ɡel o nyɔ.

english_verse: After he had finished, she said, “Now I'll give your camels all the water they want.” She quickly poured out water for them, and she kept going back for more, until his camels had drunk all they wanted.
translation_verse: O ɛ warane dɛ fuɡe nee la kar do kon kondɛɛra aa dɛ nyɔ o bini la ta, dɛ berɛ ɛ warane kaa bule la ta ja, dɛ ka dɔ ane ba tɛa a nyɔ vaɡre.

english_verse: Abraham's servant did not say a word, but he watched everything Rebekah did, because he wanted to know for certain if this was the woman the Lord had chosen.
translation_verse: Bonɔɔ la nyiŋu jeiih, o ta wobɛlbwa bolɛ dɛɛ lii kɛŋɔ o ŋwɛnɛ waa bao la, Korowii ɡelɔ wɛɛ ba hɛɛra dɔe kɛɛ?

english_verse: The servant had brought along an expensive gold ring and two large gold bracelets. When Rebekah had finished bringing the water, he gave her the ring for her nose and the bracelets for her arms.
translation_verse: Belaa nyoɡmare la aa nyɔ nee la tonɛ la, bonɔɔ la laa suuɡaswɛm noniseɡ baa kpɔa dɛɛ do mee o yoɡ do kpeɡri kohona do Rebɛka mee ta, dɛ berɛ kpɔ suuɡaswɛm nɔnloɡa do o nɔɔra.

english_verse: Then he said, “Please tell me who your father is. Does he have room in his house for me and my men to spend the night?”
translation_verse: Asɛ dɛ pɛɛro ŋɔ, “N poori, ume biee hen ɔ? Yaa dɔ chɔɔbɔr he mɛɛ deemii yaa.”

english_verse: She answered, “My father is Bethuel, the son of Nahor and Milcah.
translation_verse: Asɛ o ŋɔ, “Milka ne Neehɔ bie Bɛtoɛl bihaahnee men.”

english_verse: We have a place where you and your men can stay, and we also have enough straw and feed for your camels.”
translation_verse: Dɛ berɛ ŋɔ, “Ya dɔ kpɔɡa, ne kondɛɛra kondikwaa kohona, dɛ bela haa chɔ bwa.”

english_verse: Then the servant bowed his head and prayed,
translation_verse: Anee Abraham bonɔɔ la ɡuŋi harɛ dɛ kpɛɛ Korowii,

english_verse: “I thank you, Lord God of my master Abraham! You have led me to his relatives and kept your promise to him.”
translation_verse: dɛ ŋɔ, “Korowii n dɔɔ Abraham aa dɛ tomɛ, jam kɛŋɔ haa dɔ kasinteŋ dɛ teŋɛ dɛɛ nyin n dɔɔ nɔ. Asɛ dɛ kpɔ n naa andɛɛɡa ba n dɔɔ lolanar buse nɔ.”

english_verse: Her brother Laban heard her tell what the servant had said, and he saw the ring and the bracelets she was wearing. So Laban ran out to Abraham's servant, who was standing by his camels at the well.
translation_verse: dɛkalkɛŋɔ o na noniseɡ la aa lɔ o nime mee ta ne nɔnloɡa la aa lɔ o nɔɔra ta, dɛ no ɡɛ Rebɛka aa bol waa baa la aa bol o be la. O la baa la be, dɛ ka nao kɛŋɔ waa cheɡɛ o nyoɡmare jwɛɛh bule la ta.

english_verse: Then Laban said, “The Lord has brought you safely here. Come home with me. There's no need for you to keep on standing outside. I have a room ready for you in our house, and there's also a place for your camels.”
translation_verse: Asɛ dɛ jaamo dɛ ŋɔ, “Korowiirii kpɔ he naa la. Dɛɛ ba! Ɛrɛɛ he ba che dahara ɡɛ nɔɔ? Dea haa chɔ ne bela he nyoɡmare nɔ aa chɔ bwa lole.”

english_verse: Abraham's servant went home with Laban, where Laban's servants unloaded his camels and gave them straw and feed. Then they brought water into the house, so Abraham's servant and his men could wash their feet.
translation_verse: Belaa Laban kpɔ o ne nyoɡmare la kaa dem, dɛ ka laa laala nyoɡmare la aa cheɡa la pur. Dɛ tɛa kpɔɡa ne kondikwa. Asɛ dɛ tɛ baala baa teŋɛ o nɛɛ la nee ŋɔ bá sarame nakpale.

english_verse: After that, they brought in food. But the servant said, “Before I eat, I must tell you why I have come.” “Go ahead and tell us,” Laban answered.
translation_verse: Ba baa tɛɛ ba kondikwa, anee Abraham bonɔɔ la ŋɔ, “Maa di, nemenɛ maa bɔ me amaneɛ mɔɔ.” Asɛ Laban ŋɔ, “Amɔ bɔ he amaneɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: The servant explained: I am Abraham's servant.
translation_verse: Ate o ŋɔ, “Abraham bonɔɔnee men.

english_verse: The Lord has been good to my master and has made him very rich. He has given him many sheep, goats, cattle, camels, and donkeys, as well as a lot of silver and gold, and many slaves.
translation_verse: Korowii ɛ n dɔɔ andɛɛɡa kohona dɛ tɛo kondɔɔh. O tɛo peera ne nae ne suuɡapoŋa dɛ suuɡaswɛm, dɛ tɛo yombaala ne yomhaahna ne nyoɡmare dɛ keeɡore.

english_verse: Sarah, my master's wife, didn't have any children until she was very old. Then she had a son, and my master has given him everything.
translation_verse: N dɔɔ Abraham haah Saara lolɛ bibaa tɛo o hanjeni bini. Asɛ Abraham kpɔ o komɛlbwa waa dɔa tɛ bie la.

english_verse: I solemnly promised my master that I would do what he said. And he told me, “Don't choose a wife for my son from the women in this land of Canaan.
translation_verse: O ɡelɔ n ŋwɛɛ ntam ŋɔ, ‘Bɛ Keenan harɛ nɔ maa soɡe o ta nɔ haah mo tɛ n bie nɔ,

english_verse: I asked my master, “What if the young woman refuses to come with me?”
translation_verse: Belaa n pɛɛ n dɔɔ ŋɔ, ‘Aah dɛ haah la ŋɔ waa n nɛɛ teŋɛ ba sɛ?’

english_verse: My master answered, “I have always obeyed the Lord, and he will send his angel to help you find my son a wife from among my own relatives.
translation_verse: Anee o chaŋe ŋɔ, ‘Korowii maa dɛ tomɔ la ɛɛ tomɛ o nyundua toromee o ba ja he nɛɛ dɛ́ ɡel he dɔ hɛɛra, dɛ́ ka dɔ haah waa le ya dea ba tɛ n bie nɔ.

english_verse: But if they refuse to let her come back with you, then you are freed from your promise.”
translation_verse: Dɛ he la dea maa le o ta, dɛ ba ta hen haah la tɛɛ kwaraa ɡba aa, dɛ he ta ntam toe kpa.’

english_verse: When I came to the well today, I silently prayed, “You, Lord, are the God my master Abraham worships, so please lead me to a wife for his son
translation_verse: Maa tel bule la ta fini la, n ŋɔ, ‘Korowii n dɔɔ Abraham aa dɛ tomɛ, dɛ hɛɛ sɛoh waa, tɛ mɛ hɛɛra waa maa dɛ ba ba ɛ nɔ ta.

english_verse: while I am here at the well. When a young woman comes out to get water, I'll ask her to give me a drink.
translation_verse: Gel bule nɔ maa baa che o nyoa nɔ, tolo bɛlbwa waa ba dɛ́ ba dɔ nee ásɛ n soŋo ŋɔ ó tɛ mɛ nee tama ń nyɔ la,

english_verse: If she gives me a drink and offers to get some water for my camels, I'll know she is the one you have chosen.”
translation_verse: ásɛ o sɛh dɛ́ ŋɔ wɛɛ berɔɔ ka ɛ ane tɛ n nyoɡmare ɡe la, ɡel o ɛ haah hen Korowii aa kpɔɔ dɛɛ ba n dɔɔ bie la tɛɛ.’

english_verse: Even before I had finished praying, Rebekah came by with a water jar on her shoulder. When she had filled the jar, I asked her for a drink.
translation_verse: Maa dena soŋe a ɡɛ wesoŋa nɔ n nyu bini tonɛ, buɡ la ta, dɛ Rebɛka deno forɛ le, asɛ o polvii chɔŋɛ o vam ta, dɛ baa kaa bule la ta dɛ́ ka dɔ nee la. Asɛ n ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, ‘Tolo, n dɛ soŋe, tɛ mɛ nee nɔ ane n nyɔ.’
