english_verse: She quickly lowered the jar from her shoulder and said, “Have a drink. Then I'll get water for your camels.” So I drank, and after that she got some water for my camels.
translation_verse: Belaa o ɛ warane dɛ choɡ o nee la dɛ ŋɔ n nyɔ, asɛ n nyɔ. Asɛ o ka dɔ ane ba tɛ nyoɡmare la ɡe a nyɔ.

english_verse: I asked her who her father was, and she answered, “My father is Bethuel the son of Nahor and Milcah.” At once I put the ring in her nose and the bracelets on her arms.
translation_verse: Anee n pɛɛro ŋɔ, ‘Ume biee hen ɔ?’ Asɛ o ŋɔ, ‘Neehɔ ne Milka bie Bɛtoɛl biee men.’ Belaa n kpɔ noniseɡ do o mee ta, asɛ dɛ kpɔ nɔnloɡa ɡe do o nɔɔra.

english_verse: Then I bowed my head and gave thanks to the God my master Abraham worships. The Lord had led me straight to my master's relatives, and I had found a wife for his son.
translation_verse: Belaa n ɡuŋi dɛ jam Korowii, dɛ kpɛɛ n dɔɔ Abraham Korowii waa kpɔ n naa andɛɛɡa kɛŋɔ ń ka mo n dɔɔ nime bie ba tɛ o bie la.

english_verse: Now please tell me if you are willing to do the right thing for my master. Will you treat him fairly, or do I have to look for another young woman?
translation_verse: Taraken dɛ hɛɛ won cha n dɔɔ, ásɛ o yarada waa yarada heyaa la bɛ pɛɛ ɛ aa, hé di mɛ kasinteŋ. Ásɛ n jemɛ ɡɛ maa ɛ.”

english_verse: Laban and Bethuel answered, “The Lord has done this. We have no choice in the matter.
translation_verse: Belaa Laban ne Bɛtoɛl chaŋe ŋɔ, “Korowii bee waa nɔ bwa le, anomanta, ya ta liire bɛlbwa dɔe kpa.

english_verse: Take Rebekah with you; she can marry your master's son, just as the Lord has said.”
translation_verse: Rebɛkaa la, kpɔɔ kaa ásɛ o ka yalɛ he dɔɔ bie ɡɛ Korowii aa bola la.”

english_verse: Then he gave clothing, as well as silver and gold jewelry, to Rebekah. He also gave expensive gifts to her brother and her mother.
translation_verse: Asɛ bonɔɔ la laa kwaa baa kpɔ suuɡaswɛm ne suuɡapoŋ ɛa la ne yale tɛ Rebɛka, dɛ berɛ kpɔ laala a ɡe yoɡ aa kpeɡa tɛ haah la dɔɔ ne o nya.

english_verse: Abraham's servant and the men with him ate and drank, then spent the night there. The next morning they got up, and the servant told Rebekah's mother and brother, “I would like to go back to my master now.”
translation_verse: Awola ba hɔɔh o ne baala baa ja o nɛɛ la kɛrɛdɛ. Ba chɔ bela jwaana la ne. Asɛ tɔ aa pera chɔɔ la, o soŋ ba ŋwɛnɛ, dɛ́ berɛ kaa o dɔɔ be.

english_verse: “Let Rebekah stay with us for a week or ten days,” they answered. “Then she may go.”
translation_verse: Anee Rebɛka dɔɔ ne o nya chaŋe ŋɔ, “Gel haah la so ya be tama dɛ́ ɛ tɔpera fi mɔɔ dɛ́ kaa.”

english_verse: But he said, “Don't make me stay any longer. The Lord has already helped me find a wife for my master's son. Now let us return.”
translation_verse: Asɛ o ɡe berɛ ŋɔ, “He bɛ men lawɛ so bonɔ. Korowii aa dɔa ɡel n ŋwɛnɛ nɔ do wer tɛ mɛ nɔ, he tɛ mɛ ŋwɛnɛ, ásɛ n berɛ kaa n dɔɔ be.”

english_verse: They answered, “Let's ask Rebekah what she wants to do.”
translation_verse: Anee ba berɛ ŋɔ, “Gel ya yerɛ haah la ɡbabir ba dɛ́ ba bɔɔro.”

english_verse: They called her and asked, “Are you willing to leave with this man at once?” “Yes,” she answered.
translation_verse: Asɛ ba yerɔ dɛ pɛɛro ŋɔ, “He ne wɛɛ kaaloo kɛɛ?” Anee o ŋɔ, “Ɔɔh, n ne wɛɛ kaaloo.”

english_verse: So they agreed to let Rebekah and an old family servant woman leave immediately with Abraham's servant and his men.
translation_verse: Belaa ba ta Rebɛka ne haah waa kaa chao, ne Abraham bonɔɔ la ne o bala la bwa ŋwɛnɛ.

english_verse: They gave Rebekah their blessing and said, “We pray that God will give you many children and grandchildren and that he will help them defeat their enemies.”
translation_verse: Asɛ ba swee andɛɛɡa tɛ Rebɛka ŋɔ, “Ya nimambie, Korowii ɡel he ya kohona, he mun ya kohona aa wola nyoa dɔ, ásɛ he naanar yo lɛ ba dɔma bwɛɛre dɛɛ di a kpeɡri.”

english_verse: Afterwards, Rebekah and the young women who were to travel with her prepared to leave. Then they got on camels and left with Abraham's servant and his men.
translation_verse: Anee Rebɛka ne o toli ir, dɛ teeh so nyoɡmare la ta, dɛ teŋɛ bonɔɔ la nɛ. Asɛ dɛ chiɡ ŋwɛnɛ ta kaa. Kenii Abraham bonɔɔ la kpɔ Rebɛka kaa.

english_verse: At that time Isaac was living in the southern part of Canaan near a place called “The Well of the Living One Who Sees Me.”
translation_verse: Dɛ Aesek ɡe lɔ bobɛl baa dɛ yerɛ bela Beɛ Lahae Rɔe waa lɔ Nɛɡɛv harɛ ta.

english_verse: The servant told Isaac everything that had happened.
translation_verse: Bonɔɔ la bol wobɛlbwa waa kaa ɛ bwa chaɡle Aesek.

english_verse: Isaac took Rebekah into the tent where his mother had lived before she died, and Rebekah became his wife. He loved her and was comforted over the loss of his mother.
translation_verse: Asɛ Aesek kpɔ Rebɛka ba o nya tɛnte dea o fa aa lɔ o bini la bini, asɛ o ɛ o haah. Dɛ Aesek dɛ nyin Rebɛka kɛrɛdɛ. Anee ɡela o dɔ bolarawa o nya seo la habɔɔ.

english_verse: and they had six sons: Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah.
translation_verse: O ne on lolɛ Simran ne Joksan ne Medan ne Midian ne Esbak dɛ Suwa.

english_verse: Later, Jokshan became the father of Sheba and Dedan, and when Dedan grew up, he had three sons: Asshurim, Letushim, and Leummim.
translation_verse: Joksan ɡe bibaalaa Seeba ne Dedan. Dedan naanaree Assur ne Lɛtos dɛ Leum tena.

english_verse: Midian also had five sons: Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah.
translation_verse: Midian bibaalaa Efa ne Efar ne Hanɔk ne Abida dɛ Ɛldaa. Ketura naanaree banɔ bwa.

english_verse: While Abraham was still alive, he gave gifts to the sons of Hagar and Keturah. He also sent their sons to live in the east far from his son Isaac, and when Abraham died, he left everything to Isaac. The Death of Abraham
translation_verse: Waa soɡe le waa wola sewɛ mɔɔ la, o kɛ bii o ne o sɛnanar bane aa bera dɔ ja la koŋkwaare, asɛ dɛ ta ba ŋwɛnɛ ba kaa wee leebɔr pera dɛ le Aesek jwɛh.

english_verse: Abraham died at the ripe old age of
translation_verse: Dɛ o hwɛɛhrɔ kɛrɛdɛ, dɛ sewɛ dɛ ka pu o naawa.

english_verse: His sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him east of Hebron in Machpelah Cave that was part of the field Abraham had bought from Ephron son of Zohar the Hittite. Abraham was buried there beside his wife Sarah.
translation_verse: Gɛ harɛ Abraham aa yawa le Hiti tena be ba huɡe o haah Saara la, belaa ba huɡe o ɡe.

english_verse: God blessed Isaac after this, and Isaac moved to a place called “The Well of the Living One Who Sees Me.” Ishmael's Descendants
translation_verse: Abraham seo habɔɔ la, Korowii swee o bie Aesek andɛɛɡa. Asɛ o so Beɛ Lahae Rɔe jwɛh. Ismael bibaala wa

english_verse: Ishmael was the son of Abraham and Hagar, the slave woman of Sarah.
translation_verse: Kenii Abraham bie Ismael waa do. Onee Ijipt te Heeɡa waa ɛ Saara tolo lolɛ tɛ Abraham la.

english_verse: Ishmael had twelve sons, in this order: Nebaioth, Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,
translation_verse: Ismael bii waa lol ba la, kenii ba teŋɛ dɔŋa nɛ, Nɛbayɔt ne Keda ne Adbeel dɛ Mibsam,

english_verse: Mishma, Dumah, Massa,
translation_verse: ne Misma ne Duma dɛ Masa,

english_verse: Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah.
translation_verse: ne Hadad ne Tema ne Jetur ne Nafis dɛ Kedema.

english_verse: Each of Ishmael's sons was a tribal chief, and a village was named after each of them.
translation_verse: Banɔɔ Ismael bii. Ba sɔna nɔ cheɡɔɔ tɛ deene fi dɛ anɛ nomonome ne a bwɛɛre.

english_verse: Ishmael had settled in the land east of his brothers, and his sons settled everywhere from Havilah to Shur, east of Egypt on the way to Asshur. Ishmael was
translation_verse: O naanar soɡo dɛ le bwɛɛ Havila, dɛ ka le Suur waa bɛne Ijipt jwɛh ta dɛ kaa Asiiria. Ismael naanar ne Abraham bii baa kaa la naanar aa somɛ. Jekɔb ne Esɔ wa

english_verse: Isaac was the son of Abraham,
translation_verse: Kenii Abraham bibaa Aesek soɡa bini waa do.

english_verse: Rebekah still had no children. So Isaac asked the Lord to let her have a child, and the Lord answered his prayer.
translation_verse: Dɛ hambaraa. Asɛ Aesek soŋe Korowii o haah Rebɛka kpoŋe tea.

english_verse: Before Rebekah gave birth, she knew she was going to have twins, because she could feel them inside her, fighting each other. She thought, “Why is this happening to me?” Finally, she asked the Lord why her twins were fighting,
translation_verse: Kpara teaa o kpoŋe. Baa lɔ o tea bini la, dɛ ba dɛ lɔ dɔŋa. Anee o ŋɔ, “Bɔkwa ɡe waa nɔɔ.” Dɛ kpɔ ka bil Korowii sie dɛ́ jemɛ waa aa bala.

english_verse: and he told her: “Your two sons will become two separate nations. The younger of the two will be stronger, and the older son will be his servant.”
translation_verse: Anee Korowii ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Harɛre nɛra banɛ nomonomaa lɔ he tea bini. Ba baah dɛ́ ba doe kɛŋɔ kolmaala ken. Beŋkpoŋ ɛɛ dɔ kpeɡrii ɡwaa o dɔŋ, ásɛ nomoa la ɛɛ tomɛ bechala la.”

english_verse: The second baby grabbed on to his brother's heel, so they named him Jacob. Isaac was
translation_verse: Ba lola bini la, dɛ muŋkaa la lawɛ sitɔte la kpoŋe. A waa ba pa o sɔn Jekɔb. O munii kɛŋɔ nalume kpoŋri. Baa lol ba la, dɛ Aesek dɔ bene fifraanumɛl.

english_verse: As Jacob and Esau grew older, Esau liked the outdoors and became a good hunter, while Jacob lived the quiet life of a shepherd.
translation_verse: Bii la bwa baa kpeɡ. Asɛ Esɔ kpɔ o te ɛ kpɔɡ bini nɛn dɛɛ kpaah kɛrɛdɛ. Dɛ Jekɔb te dɛ so dem.

english_verse: Esau would take the meat of wild animals to his father Isaac, so Isaac loved him more, but Jacob was his mother's favorite son.
translation_verse: Dɛ Aesek dɛ nyin Esɔ dɛkalkɛ dɛ o kpaahnɔ baa tɛo wɛɛ di. Asɛ Rebɛka ɡe sie ɛɛ lɛ Jekɔb nɛ.

english_verse: One day, when Jacob was cooking some stew, Esau came home hungry
translation_verse: Awola bɛl, Jekɔb dɛ daa kondikwaa ane, dɛ lɔr lawɛ Esɔ taeh o le kpɔɡ bini ba.

english_verse: and said, “I'm starving to death! Here and now give me some of that red stew!” That's how Esau got the name “Edom.”
translation_verse: Belaa o ŋɔ Jekɔb be ŋɔ, “Ɛ warane dɛ́ tɛ mɛ he kondikonswɛɛma nɔ ane. Dɛkalkɛ lɔr dɛ kpo mɛ taeh. Anomanta, ba kpɔɔ dɛɛ yerɛ Edom. O munii kɛŋɔ konswɛm.”

english_verse: Jacob replied, “Sell me your rights as the first-born son.”
translation_verse: Anee Jekɔb ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Hɛɛ kpɔ he nomonomee charɛ tenaa, mɛɛ tɛɛ.”

english_verse: “I'm about to die,” Esau answered. “What good will those rights do me?”
translation_verse: Anee Esɔ chaŋe ŋɔ, “Sewaa mɛɛ ba sewa la, bɔkwaa nomonome dii ɡe ɛɛ ba wona ɛɛ mɛ nɔ?”

english_verse: But Jacob said, “Promise me your birthrights, here and now!” And that's what Esau did.
translation_verse: Asɛ o nime la ŋɔ, “Ŋwɛɛ kɛŋɔ hɛɛ kpɔ he nomonomee tɛ mɛ fini.” O ŋwɛɛ dɛ kpɔ tɛo.

english_verse: Jacob then gave Esau some bread and some of the bean stew, and when Esau had finished eating and drinking, he just got up and left, showing how little he thought of his rights as the first-born.
translation_verse: Ate, Jekɔb tɛ Esɔ paanoo ne kwaa waa daala la o di, dɛ nyɔ nee dawɛ dɛ ir chiɡ ŋwɛnɛ ta kaa o bɔr. Kenii Esɔ koh kondikwaa wa, dɛ kpɔ o nomonome ta.

english_verse: Once during Abraham's lifetime, the fields had not produced enough grain, and now the same thing happened. So Isaac went to King Abimelech of the Philistines in the land of Gerar,
translation_verse: Asɛ lɔr bɛl chole harɛ la ta. Gɛ lɔr nɔ korɛ Abraham saŋ lɔr la ta. Anee Aesek ir kaa Filisti tena Kooro Abemɛlɛk be Gerar.

english_verse: because the Lord had appeared to Isaac and said: Isaac, stay away from Egypt! I will show you where I want you to go.
translation_verse: Dɛ Korowii fa kpɔ o te baɡle Aesek dɛ ŋɔ, “Dɛɛ berɛ Ijipt laŋa kpa. So harɛ maa chaɡle nɔ ta.

english_verse: You will live there as a foreigner, but I will be with you and bless you. I will keep my promise to your father Abraham by giving this land to you and your descendants.
translation_verse: So bonɔ tama. Mɛɛ che he mun taa dɛ́ tɛɛ hɛɛra, dɛkalkɛŋɔ he ne he naanaree mɛɛ ba ń kpɔ harɛ nɔ bwa tɛ, ɡel n nyoa maa baɡɛ he mɛɛ Abraham la che kɛrɛdɛ.

english_verse: I will give you as many descendants as there are stars in the sky, and I will give your descendants all of this land. They will be a blessing to every nation on earth,
translation_verse: Mɛɛ ɡeloo he naanar warɛ kɛŋɔ weweela, dɛ́ kpɔ harɛre nɔ bwa tɛɛ ba. He naanar nɛɛ aa ba cheɡa harɛ nɔ ta nɛra bwa dɔ hɛɛra.

english_verse: Isaac moved to Gerar
translation_verse: Asɛ Aesek so Gerar.

english_verse: with his beautiful wife Rebekah. He was afraid that someone might kill him to get her, and so he told everyone that Rebekah was his sister.
translation_verse: Asɛ bela tena bɔɔro o haah wa, anee o chaŋ ba ŋɔ, “N nimambiee.” Dɛ o dɛ ɔmɛ kɛŋɔ o bol ŋɔ o haahnee. Gɛ laa aa, Rebɛka wer waa doo la nomanta, bela tena ɛɛ kpoo.

english_verse: After Isaac had been there a long time, King Abimelech looked out a window and saw Isaac hugging and kissing Rebekah.
translation_verse: Waa ba dɛ biɡri bela tama la, Filisti tena Kooro Abemɛlɛk cheɡɛ tokoro ta, dɛ na kɛŋɔ Aesek ne o haah dɛ hɛlɛ.

english_verse: Abimelech called him in and said, “Rebekah must be your wife! Why did you say she is your sister?” “Because I thought someone would kill me,” Isaac answered.
translation_verse: Anee kooro la yerɔ dɛ pɛɛro ŋɔ, “Tolo la, he haahnee. Aah ɛrɛɛ a ɛ asɛ he ŋɔ ya be ŋɔ he nimambiee yɔ?” Asɛ Aesek ŋɔ, “N liiro kɛŋɔ a ɡɛ ken ɛɛ ɡeloo n dɔ seo.”

english_verse: “Don't you know what you've done?” Abimelech exclaimed. “If someone had slept with her, you would have made our whole nation guilty!”
translation_verse: Belaa Kooro Abemɛlɛk ŋɔ, “Bɔkwaa he ɛ yaa ken? A ka tamaa ken ya bini bɛl fe nyin he haah nɔ, dɛ he fe ɡelɔ ya ɛ wechɔɡa dawɛ ya nɛ.”

english_verse: Then Abimelech warned his people that anyone who even touched Isaac or Rebekah would be put to death.
translation_verse: Ate, kooro la kah nɛra la bwa ŋɔ, bɛlbwa waa leɡe baa nɔ kɛɛ o haah la, a chɛ kɛ ba kpoo.

english_verse: Isaac planted grain and had a good harvest that same year. The Lord blessed him,
translation_verse: A bena la, Aesek parɔ dɛ dɔ kondikwaa kohona. Kwaa waa para la bele lafaa o dɔ dɛkalkɛ Korowii tɛo hɛɛra.

english_verse: and Isaac was so successful that he became very rich.
translation_verse: O teŋɔ dɔ kwaa ɡɛ naaa ka tel kɛŋɔ waa baa ɛ kondɔɔh tenten.

english_verse: In fact, the Philistines were jealous of the large number of sheep, goats, and slaves that Isaac owned,
translation_verse: O dɔ kondɛɛra ne bonɔɔna kohona, asɛ Filisti tena la sie beɡre o nɛ.

english_verse: and they stopped up the wells that Abraham's servants had dug before his death.
translation_verse: A cheɡɛ a ta ba che teera tɔɔɡe kɔlɔŋa o mɛɛ Abraham bonɔɔna aa kwia o bere saŋ la.

english_verse: Finally, Abimelech said, “Isaac, I want you to leave our country. You have become too powerful to stay here.”
translation_verse: Belaa Kooro Abemɛlɛk ŋɔ Aesek be ŋɔ, “Le ya harɛ nɔ ta. He berɔ dɔ he te kohona ɡwaa yaa.”

english_verse: Isaac left and settled in Gerar Valley,
translation_verse: Anee o ir dɛ kaa nenabɔjen Gerar ta, dɛ ka so bela.

english_verse: where he cleaned out those wells that the Philistines had stopped up. Isaac also gave each of the wells the same name that Abraham had given to them.
translation_verse: Asɛ o berɛ ka kwaa pili kɔlɔŋa la baa kwia o mɛɛ bere saŋ mɔɔ o sewɛ la, dɛ berɛ paa sɔna la o mɛɛ fa aa paa la.

english_verse: While his servants were digging in the valley, they found a spring-fed well.
translation_verse: Aesek bonɔɔna la kwi kɔlɔŋ nenabɔɔ la bini, asɛ dɛ ka pu ne.

english_verse: But the shepherds of Gerar Valley quarreled with Isaac's shepherds and claimed the water belonged to them. So this well was named “Quarrel,” because they had quarreled with Isaac.
translation_verse: A kaa ba kɛ nɛra bane baa dɛ nyiŋi kondɛɛra nɛ dɛ le Gerar balɔ, ba ne Aesek bonɔɔna baa dɛ nyiŋi o ɡe kondɛɛra ta la ɛɛ yo. Asɛ bela tena la baɡle ŋɔ, “Ya konee kɔlɔŋ la.” Anomanta, Aesek pa kɔlɔŋ la sɔn Esɛk. O munii webeɡra. Dɛkalkɛŋɔ ba beɡre o wa.

english_verse: Isaac's servants dug another well, and the shepherds also quarreled about it. So that well was named “Jealous.”
translation_verse: Belaa ba berɛ kwi onfale, asɛ ba yo o ɡe waa ja. Anee o pa o sɔn Sitna. O munii nɛn nɛɛ cheɡa.

english_verse: Finally, they dug one more well. There was no quarreling this time, and the well was named “Lots of Room,” because the Lord had given them room and would make them very successful.
translation_verse: O berɔ le bela kwara dɛ ka kwi onfale, kɛ o te la, o ne nomɛlbwa ta o waa beɡrɛ kpa. Asɛ o pa o sɔn Rɛhɔbɔt. O munii bɔr dɔe. Dɛ ŋɔ, “Taraken Korowii tɛ yaa bɔr ya so dɛ́ ya.”

english_verse: Isaac went on to Beersheba,
translation_verse: Asɛ Aesek ir bela dɛ berɛ kaa Beɛseeba ka so.

english_verse: where the Lord appeared to him that night and told him, “Don't be afraid! I am the God who was worshiped by your father Abraham, my servant. I will be with you and bless you, and because of Abraham I will give you many descendants.”
translation_verse: Awola jwaana la ne la, Korowii ba o be kɛŋɔ deera ta ken dɛ ŋɔ, “Menee Korowii he mɛɛ Abraham aa tomɔ la. Bɛ dɛɛ ɔmɛ, mɛɛ che he habɔɔ. Mɛɛ koh n bonɔndɛɛɡe Abraham waa dɛ́ tɛɛ hɛɛra dɛ́ ɡel he naanar warɛ.”

english_verse: Isaac built an altar there and worshiped the Lord. Then he set up camp, and his servants started digging a well.
translation_verse: Belaa Aesek ɛ kon baa ɛ saraha o ta dɛɛ tɛ Korowii bela dɛɛ tomɔ. O baŋre o tɛnte dea, asɛ o bonɔɔna la kwi kɔlɔŋ bela ja.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Abimelech had left Gerar and was taking his advisor Ahuzzath and his army commander Phicol to see Isaac.
translation_verse: Kooro Abemɛlɛk ne o nomoa Ahusat ne o laa tena nomoa Fekɔl le Gerar dɛ ba Aesek be.

english_verse: When they arrived, Isaac asked, “Why are you here? Didn't you send me away because you hated me?”
translation_verse: Asɛ Aesek bɔɔ ba ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛ waa he berɛ dɛɛ ba n be nɔɔ, kɛ he hah mɛ dɛ doŋ mɛ le he be nɔ?”

english_verse: They answered, “We now know for certain that the Lord is with you, and we have decided there needs to be a peace treaty between you and us. So let's make a solemn agreement
translation_verse: Ba chaŋo ŋɔ, “Ya nao kɛŋɔ Korowii teŋɛ he nɛ. Anomanta, ya liiro ŋɔ a chɛ kɛ ya ne he fɔwɛ fɔo. Gel ya ne he fɔwɛ fɔo,

english_verse: not to harm each other. Remember, we have never hurt you, and when we sent you away, we let you go in peace. The Lord has truly blessed you.”
translation_verse: ásɛ he bɛ yaa wechɔɡa bɛlbwa ɛ, ɡɛ ya fa aa wola hen hɔhɔrɔwa bɛlbwa ɛɛ, dɛ nyiŋi kɛrɛdɛ dɛ tae ŋwɛnɛ deŋnesɔɔhna ta he kaa la. Taraken ya nao kɛŋɔ Korowii tɛɛ hɛɛra.”

english_verse: Isaac gave a big feast for them, and everyone ate and drank.
translation_verse: Asɛ Aesek ɡel ba daa kondikwaa tɛɛ ba ba di, dɛ nyɔ sen lɛ ba sie.

english_verse: Early the next morning Isaac and the others made a solemn agreement, then he let them go in peace.
translation_verse: Tɔ aa pera chɔmbibi la, ba ŋwɛɛrɔ baɡle dɔŋa, asɛ ba fɔo la che, o ta ba ŋwɛnɛ deŋnesɔɔhna ta ba kaa.

english_verse: Later that same day Isaac's servants came and said, “We've struck water!”
translation_verse: Awola tɔpere la, Aesek bonɔɔna balɔ dɛ ba bol kɔlɔŋ baa kwiu la waa o be ŋɔ, “Ya pu ne.”

english_verse: So Isaac named the well Shibah, and the town is still called Beersheba. Esau's Foreign Wives
translation_verse: Asɛ baa yerɔ Seeba. Anomanta, dɛ ba le fini, ba dɛ yerɛ bwɛɛ la Beɛseeba.

english_verse: But these two women brought a lot of grief to Esau's parents Isaac and Rebekah.
translation_verse: Ba baa do Aesek ne Rebɛka bonyɛɡa ba bambile chɔɡ.

english_verse: Isaac was old and almost blind, when he called in his first-born son Esau, who asked him, “Father, what can I do for you?”
translation_verse: Aesek baa hwɛɛh dɛ nyoŋe. Awola bɛl, o yerɛ o binomoa Esɔ dɛ ŋɔ, “N bie.” O sɛh ŋɔ, “N mɛɛ men la.”

english_verse: Isaac replied, “I am old and might die at any time.
translation_verse: Belaa o ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Taraken n hwɛɛhrɔ, maa n seo tɔpere jemɛ.

english_verse: So go hunting with your bow and arrows and kill a wild animal.
translation_verse: Anomanta, kpɔ he laala, he hɛma ne to, dɛ́ kaa kpɔɡ bini ka nyin ol

english_verse: Cook some of that tasty food that I love so much and bring it to me. I want to eat it once more and give you my blessing before I die.”
translation_verse: dɛ́ ba daa n pɛla kondikwaa tɛ mɛ n di, ásɛ n soŋe andɛɛɡa le Korowii be tɛɛ mɔɔ dɛ́ sewɛ.”

english_verse: she said to Jacob, “I heard your father tell Esau
translation_verse: Rebɛka ŋɔ Jekɔb be ŋɔ, “Na, n noɔ kɛŋɔ he mɛɛ aa dɛ bol he dɔɔ be ŋɔ

english_verse: to kill a wild animal and cook some tasty food for him before he dies. Your father said this because he wants to bless your brother with the Lord as his witness.
translation_verse: ó kaa kpɔɡ bini ka nyin ol ba daa o pɛla kondikwaa ba tɛo ó di, ásɛ o soŋe Korowii andɛɛɡa tɛo mɔɔ dɛ sewɛ.

english_verse: Now, my son, listen carefully to what I want you to do.
translation_verse: Anomanta, n bie, cheɡ deŋne dɛ́ no waa maa dɛ ba he be bola nɔ dɛ́ ɛa.

english_verse: Go and kill two of your best young goats and bring them to me. I'll cook the tasty food that your father loves so much.
translation_verse: Ir la kondɛɛra la bini dɛ́ ka lawɛ bohloni anɛ aa wera ba tɛ mɛ, ásɛ n kpɔ daa he mɛɛ pɛla kondikwaa tɛo ɡɛ waa dɛ nyin.

english_verse: Then you can take it to him, so he can eat it and give you his blessing before he dies.”
translation_verse: Ásɛ he kpɔ ka tɛo o di, dɛ́ soŋe andɛɛɡa tɛɛ mɔɔ wɛɛ sewɔɔ waa o sewɛ.”

english_verse: “My brother Esau is a hairy man,” Jacob reminded her. “And I am not.
translation_verse: Anee Jekɔb ŋɔ o nya be ŋɔ, “N dɔɔ aa dɔ pona, n te aa wola pona dɔe nɔ,

english_verse: If my father touches me and realizes I am trying to trick him, he will put a curse on me instead of giving me a blessing.”
translation_verse: dɛ n mɛɛ kaa laɡ mɛ dɛ kpɔ nɔn valɛ n bwara aa, aa ka ɛ kɛŋɔ neɡraa mɛɛ neɡro wa aa? Taahna kwaraa wɛɛ ba n taahna, dɛ́ ɡel andɛɛɡa soŋa dɛ́ tɛ mɛ.”

english_verse: Rebekah insisted, “Let his curse fall on me! Just do what I say and bring me the meat.”
translation_verse: Belaa o nya chaŋo ŋɔ, “N bie, he te ka ɛ wobɛlbwa maa bola la, ásɛ a habɔɔ wobɛlbwa ba dawɛ n nɛ.”

english_verse: So Jacob brought the meat to his mother, and she cooked the tasty food that his father liked.
translation_verse: Ate, o la ka lawɛ boohna la ba tɛ o nya, asɛ o kpɔ ɛ kondikwaa aa do som ɡɛ o mɛɛ aa dɛ nyin.

english_verse: Then she took Esau's best clothes and put them on Jacob.
translation_verse: O kpɔ Esɔ bonɔnlaala ba do Jekɔb.

english_verse: She also covered the smooth part of his hands and neck with goatskins
translation_verse: O berɔ kpɔ boohna la tɔne bɔle o nɔɔra, ne o baŋa bela pona aa wola toole la.

english_verse: and gave him some bread and the tasty food she had cooked.
translation_verse: O kpɔ kondikonsoma la ne paanoo waa ɛa la do Jekɔb nɔn ta o ka tɛ o mɛɛ.

english_verse: Jacob went to his father and said, “Father, here I am.” “Which one of my sons are you?” his father asked.
translation_verse: Waa la kondikwaa la ne la, o yerɛ o mɛɛ, asɛ o sɛh dɛ pɛɛ ŋɔ, “Umee yɔ?”

english_verse: Jacob replied, “I am Esau, your first-born, and I have done what you told me. Please sit up and eat the meat I have brought. Then you can give me your blessing.”
translation_verse: Anee Jekɔb sɛh ŋɔ, “Menee he binomoa Esɔ, n ba ol la ne dɛ́ ba ɛ ɡɛ haa ŋɔa la. Ir so dɛ́ di kwaa la, ásɛ dɛ soŋe Korowii andɛɛɡa tɛ mɛ.”

english_verse: Isaac asked, “My son, how did you find an animal so quickly?” “The Lord your God was kind to me,” Jacob answered.
translation_verse: Asɛ Aesek ŋɔ, “N bie, he denɔ dɔ warane to.” Anee Jekɔb chaŋe ŋɔ, “Korowii haa dɛ tomɔ laanee tɛ mɛ hɛɛra.”

english_verse: “My son,” Isaac said, “come closer, where I can touch you and find out if you really are Esau.”
translation_verse: Anee Aesek ŋɔ Jekɔb be ŋɔ, “Tuuh ba ásɛ n lawɛ na kɛŋɔ Esɔɔ hen kpelaa?”

english_verse: Jacob went closer. His father touched him and said, “You sound like Jacob, but your hands feel hairy like Esau's.”
translation_verse: Asɛ o suuh tel o mɛɛ be o kpɔ o nɔn laɡro dɛ ŋɔ, “Taa nɔ te dɛ le Jekɔb taa, kɛ nɔɔra nɔ te le Esɔ nɔɔra.”

english_verse: Isaac asked, “Are you really my son Esau?” “Yes, I am,” Jacob answered.
translation_verse: O berɔ pɛɛro ja ŋɔ, “Esɔɔ hen kpelaa?” O ɡe sɛh ŋɔ, “Ɔɔh, menee.”

english_verse: So Isaac told him, “Serve me the wild meat, and I can give you my blessing.” Jacob gave him some meat, and he ate it. He also gave him some wine, and he drank it.
translation_verse: Anee Aesek ŋɔ, “N bie, kpɔ kondikwaa la tɛ mɛ, ásɛ n kpɔ ol la bɛl chwe, dɛ́ soŋe andɛɛɡa le Korowii be tɛɛ. Asɛ o kpɔ tɛo o di, dɛ kpɔ senfala ɡe tɛo o nyɔ ja.”

english_verse: While Jacob was kissing him, Isaac caught the smell of his clothes and said: “The smell of my son is like a field the Lord has blessed.
translation_verse: Asɛ o suuh tel o mɛɛ, dɛ ɡbaaro pɛl o bambile, dɛ mo o lwɛɛma. Waa no o bie Jekɔb laala la sɔɔh la, o soŋe andɛɛɡa Korowii be tɛo dɛ ŋɔ, “N bie sɔɔh do kɛŋɔ harɛ Korowii aa ɡela o ɛ harɛdɛɛɡe sɔɔh.

english_verse: God will bless you, my son, with dew from heaven and with fertile fields, rich with grain and grapes.
translation_verse: Kórowii pili nyundua dɛ́ nɛ bwaala, dɛ́ tɛɛ hɛɛra he konduula bwa do wer, he dɔ kondikwaa ne senfala kohona.

english_verse: Nations will be your servants and bow down to you. You will rule over your brothers, and they will kneel at your feet. Anyone who curses you will be cursed; anyone who blesses you will be blessed.”
translation_verse: Harɛre nɛra ɛɛ tomɛɛ, dɛ́ ɡuŋii harɛ. Hɛɛ ɛ nomoa he nya bii bwa nɛɛ, ásɛ ba ɡuŋi harɛ. Nomɛlbwa waa taahnee la, á berɛ ɡure o nyu ta, ásɛ nomɛlbwa waa soŋe andɛɛɡa tɛɛ la, ó ɡe dɔ andɛɛɡa.”

english_verse: Right after Isaac had given Jacob his blessing and Jacob had gone, Esau came back from hunting.
translation_verse: Aesek aa soŋe Korowii andɛɛɡa tɛ Jekɔb tonɛ asɛ o le kaa la, o dɔɔ Esɔ ɡe le kpaah bɔr ba.

english_verse: He cooked the tasty food, brought it to his father, and said, “Father, please sit up and eat the meat I have brought you, so you can give me your blessing.”
translation_verse: O ɡe daa kondikonsoma ba tɛo. Asɛ dɛ ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Ir so ásɛ dɛ di ol maa kaa kpoo ba ɛ kondikwaa ba tɛɛ nɔ, dɛ́ soŋe Korowii andɛɛɡa tɛ mɛ.”

english_verse: “Who are you?” Isaac asked. “I am Esau, your first-born son.”
translation_verse: Belaa o mɛɛ bɔɔ ŋɔ, “Umee hen ɔ?” O chaŋe ŋɔ, “Menee he binomoa Esɔ.”

english_verse: Isaac started trembling and said, “Then who brought me some wild meat right before you came in? I ate it and gave him a blessing that cannot be taken back.”
translation_verse: Anee o mɛɛ kpɔ bochechela dɛ bɔɔro ŋɔ, “Aah dɛ umee kpɔ kpɔɡ bini ol dɛ daa ba tɛ mɛ laɔ? Gɛ kondikwaa laanee n di tonɛ, dɛ soŋe Korowii andɛɛɡa tɛ naate, dɛ he ɡe deno baa jo la. Kasinteŋ, o wobɛlbwa ɛɛ do werii tɛo!”

english_verse: Esau replied, “My brother deserves the name Jacob, because he has already cheated me twice. The first time he cheated me out of my rights as the first-born son, and now he has cheated me out of my blessing.” Then Esau asked his father, “Don't you have any blessing left for me?”
translation_verse: Anee Esɔ ŋɔ, “O sɔn Jekɔb la maɡre o ne. O munii neɡra. Anɔɔ jaa nɛɛtena waa faah mɛ. O lɛ n nomonome, asɛ dɛ lɛ soŋa he fe aa soŋe tɛ mɛ la ɡe ja.” Dɛ berɛ bɔɔro ŋɔ, “Amɔ he ta wobɛlbwa dɔe dɛ́ soŋe Korowii andɛɛɡa tɛ mɛ kpa aa?”

english_verse: “My son,” Isaac answered, “I have made Jacob the ruler over you and your brothers, and all of you will be his servants. I have also promised him all the grain and grapes that he needs. There's nothing left that I can do for you.”
translation_verse: Belaa Aesek chaŋo ŋɔ, “N dɔɔ kpɔɔ ɛ he nomoa, dɛ kpɔ he lolanar bwa ɛ o bonɔɔna. N tɛo hɛɛra ásɛ o konduula bwa do wer o dɔ kondikwaa ne senfala kohona. Bɔkwaa kaa ń soŋe tɛɛ jaɔ?”

english_verse: “Father,” Esau asked, “don't you have more than one blessing? You can surely give me a blessing too!” Then Esau started crying again.
translation_verse: Esɔ toɔh marɛ o mɛɛ dɛ soŋo ŋɔ, “Amɔ wesoŋa beŋkpoŋ ɡboo he dɔ dɛ tɛ Jekɔb haa wola bɛlee dɔ tɛ n te kpa aa? Soŋe andɛɛɡa tɛ n ɡe.” Asɛ dɛ wi kohona.

english_verse: So his father said: “Your home will be far from that fertile land, where dew comes down from the heavens.
translation_verse: Belaa o mɛɛ Aesek ŋɔ, “Korowii aa nyundua pili dɛ́ nɛ bwaala tɛɛ, waa hen harɛdɛɛɡee tɛ he so dɛ́ dɔ kondikwa.

english_verse: You will live by the power of your sword and be your brother's slave. But when you decide to be free, you will break loose.”
translation_verse: Yoi ɡboo hɛɛ ba dɛɛ yoi mɔɔ dɛ́ dɔ kwaa di, dɛɛ tomɛ he nime. Kɛ he baa tomɔ la sie tama naa, hɛɛ yoo, dɛ́ berɛ won lɛ he te.” Jekɔb aa chwaa kaa Laban be

english_verse: Esau hated his brother Jacob because he had stolen the blessing that was supposed to be his. So he said to himself, “Just as soon as my father dies, I'll kill Jacob.”
translation_verse: Gɛ Jekɔb aa neɡre o mɛɛ o soŋe andɛɛɡa tɛo la, Esɔ haoh. O lii o nyu bini ŋɔ, “Aa biɡri bɛlbwa n mɛɛ sewɛ. Ba baa ɛ o lwe tonaa, ásɛ n kpo Jekɔb.”

english_verse: When Rebekah found out what Esau planned to do, she sent for Jacob and told him, “Son, your brother Esau is just waiting for a chance to kill you.
translation_verse: Waa dɛ kpɔ ɡɛ liire nɔ la, Rebɛka noɔ asɛ dɛ tomɛ ba ka yerɛ Jekɔb ba, dɛ ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “He dɔɔ Esɔ dɛ vɔrɔwe he vɔrɔwa kɛŋɔ wɛɛ kpoe.

english_verse: Now listen carefully and do what I say. Go to the home of my brother Laban in Haran
translation_verse: Taraken n bie, no n waa nɔ. N dɛ nyin kɛŋɔ he le bonɔ warane, dɛ́ kaa n dɔɔ Laban be Haran.

english_verse: and stay with him for a while. When Esau stops being angry
translation_verse: He laŋaa, he so bela tama ka tel kɛ he dɔɔ baah aa sɔɔhno mɔɔ.

english_verse: and forgets what you have done to him, I'll send for you to come home. Why should I lose both of my sons on the same day?”
translation_verse: He dɔɔ baa soh wobɛlbwa o baah sɔɔhnoo waa, mɛɛ tomɛ nɛra he bee ásɛ he berɛ ba. Maa won so nyiŋi n bii banɛ bwa serewe tɔpebeŋkpoŋ.”

english_verse: Rebekah later told Isaac, “Those Hittite wives of Esau are making my life miserable! If Jacob marries a Hittite woman, I'd be better off dead.”
translation_verse: Belaa Rebɛka ŋɔ Aesek be ŋɔ, “N sie aa Hiti bitoli nɔ nɛɛ lɛ. N kii ba kɔkɔkɔ. Dɛ Jekɔb ŋɔ wɛɛ mo ba bini bɛlee yaa, mɛɛ sewɔɔ hɛo.”

english_verse: Isaac called in Jacob, then gave him a blessing, and said: Don't marry any of those Canaanite women.
translation_verse: Belaa Aesek yerɛ Jekɔb dɛ swee andɛɛɡa tɛo dɛ berɛ ŋɔ, “Bɛ Keenan harɛ nɔ ta haahna nɔ bini bɛlbwa mo.

english_verse: Go at once to your mother's father Bethuel in northern Syria and choose a wife from one of the daughters of Laban, your mother's brother.
translation_verse: Ir dɛ́ kaa Mɛsopoteemea harɛ ta, dɛ ka mo haah le he nya mɛɛ Bɛtoɛl dem. Ka mo he naara Laban bihaahna la bini bɛl.

english_verse: I pray that God All-Powerful will bless you with many descendants and let you become a great nation.
translation_verse: Kórowii Waa ɛ Kpeɡri Bwa Dɔɔ la che he mun ta, dɛ́ swee andɛɛɡa tɛɛ he hahmor ta, ásɛ he lolɛ bii kohona á che a ta he ɛ harɛre nɛra ɡalɡa naa.

english_verse: May he bless you with the land he promised Abraham, so that you will take over this land where we now live as foreigners.
translation_verse: Onee dɛ́ che he ne he naanar mun ta, ɡɛ waa cheɡɛ Abraham mun ta la, ásɛ harɛ nɔ yaa ɛ hɔɔhra o ta Korowii kpɔ tɛ Abraham nɔ ɛ he kon.”

english_verse: Isaac then sent Jacob to stay with Rebekah's brother Laban, the son of Bethuel the Aramean. Esau Marries the Daughter of Ishmael
translation_verse: Belaa Aesek ta Jekɔb ŋwɛnɛ o kaa Mɛsopoteemea harɛ ta Bɛtoɛl bibaa Laban be. Rebɛka waa lolɛ Jekɔb ne Esɔ la dɔɔree. O ɛ Aram te.

english_verse: Esau found out that his father Isaac had blessed Jacob and had warned him not to marry any of the Canaanite women. He also learned that Jacob had been sent to find a wife in northern Syria
translation_verse: Esɔ nao kɛŋɔ Aesek swee andɛɛɡa tɛ Jekɔb, dɛ tao ŋwɛnɛ ŋɔ o kaa Mɛsopoteemea harɛ ka mo haah bela, dɛ ŋɔ o bɛ Keenan harɛ bihaah mo,

english_verse: and that he had obeyed his father and mother.
translation_verse: asɛ Jekɔb no o nya ne o mɛɛ deŋna wa dɛ kaa bela.

english_verse: Esau already had several wives, but he now realized how much his father hated the Canaanite women.
translation_verse: Esɔ ɡe nao kɛŋɔ Keenan harɛ haahna wa aa were o mɛɛ be kwaraa,

english_verse: So he married Ishmael's daughter Mahalath, who was the sister of Nebaioth and the granddaughter of Abraham. Jacob's Dream at Bethel
translation_verse: asɛ o chiɡ ŋwɛnɛ ta dɛ kaa Ismael waa ɛ Abraham bie la be dɛ ka mo o bihaah baa dɛ yerɔ Mahalat la ja o haahna la nɛ. O nime sɔne Nɛbayɔt. Jekɔb deera waa deera Bɛtel

english_verse: Jacob left the town of Beersheba and started out for Haran.
translation_verse: Belaa Jekɔb le Beɛseeba dɛ chiɡ ŋwɛnɛ ta dɛɛ kaa Haran.

english_verse: At sunset he stopped for the night and went to sleep, resting his head on a large rock.
translation_verse: Waa dɛ kaa la, o kaa tel bobɛl bɔr joo o chɔ, dɛ kpɔ nyu serɛ bwe bɛl.

english_verse: In a dream he saw a ladder that reached from earth to heaven, and God's angels were going up and down on it.
translation_verse: O chɔe bini la, o deero dɛ na kɛŋɔ sanjol le nyundua ba chiɡ harɛ, asɛ nyundua toroma teeh dɛ la dɛɛ ba.

english_verse: The Lord was standing beside the ladder and said: I am the Lord God who was worshiped by Abraham and Isaac. I will give to you and your family the land on which you are now sleeping.
translation_verse: Dɛ Korowii cheɡɛ o jwɛh dɛ ŋɔ, “Menee Korowii, menee he mɛɛ Abraham ne Aesek tomɛ la. Harɛ haa chɔ o ta nɔ, he ne he naanaree mɛɛ ba kpɔe tɛ.

english_verse: Your descendants will spread over the earth in all directions and will become as numerous as the specks of dust. Your family will be a blessing to all people.
translation_verse: He naanar ɛɛ warɔɔ kɛŋɔ harɛ nɔ ta teera, dɛ́ yɛɛ kaa harɛ nɔ ta bobɛlbwa. He ne he naanar nɛɛ aa ba cheɡa, ásɛ n swee andɛɛɡa tɛ harɛ nɔ ta nɛra bwa.

english_verse: Wherever you go, I will watch over you, then later I will bring you back to this land. I won't leave you—I will do all I have promised.
translation_verse: Berɛ lii kɛŋɔ mɛɛ teŋɛ he nɛɛ, dɛ́ tɔ he nɛɛ bobɛlbwa haa dɛ ba kaala, dɛ́ berɛ ba he ne harɛ nɔ ta ja. Maa hen ta bwa, nemenɛ n ɛ waa maa baɡɛ nyoa la.”

english_verse: Jacob woke up suddenly and thought, “The Lord is in this place, and I didn't even know it.”
translation_verse: Jekɔb aa ir dom ta la, o ŋɔ, “Amɔ Korowii lɔ bonɔ asɛ n ta jemɛ!”

english_verse: Then Jacob became frightened and said, “What a frightening place! It must be the house of God and the gateway to heaven.”
translation_verse: Asɛ ɔmee lawɔ o ŋɔ, “Bonɔ ɔma kɛrɛdɛ! Bonɔ ɛɛ ɛ Korowii demii. Bonɔ ɛ doonyoa baa kpɔ o ta dɛɛ kaa nyundua.”

english_verse: When Jacob got up early the next morning, he took the rock that he had used for a pillow and stood it up as a place of worship. Then he poured olive oil on the rock to dedicate it to God,
translation_verse: Tɔ aa pera chɔmbibi la, o kpɔ bwe waa kpɔ o nyu serɛ o ta la pa bela harɛ la ta, dɛ́ kpɔ dɛɛ lii bela, dɛ fuɡe noo ta o ta dɛ kpɔ do Korowii nɔn ta.

english_verse: and he named the place Bethel. Before that it had been named Luz.
translation_verse: Dɛ pa bela sɔn Bɛtel. Wubwa la dɛ o sɔne Lus.

english_verse: Jacob solemnly promised God, “If you go with me and watch over me as I travel, and if you give me food and clothes
translation_verse: Asɛ Jekɔb baɡɛ Korowii nyoa ŋɔ, “Dɛ hɛɛ ja n nɛɛ dɛ́ kpɔ nɔn tɔ n nɛɛ n ŋwɛnɛ maa dɛ kaa nɔ ta, dɛ́ tɛ mɛ kondikwaa ne yal maa tɔ,

english_verse: and bring me safely home again, you will be my God.
translation_verse: ásɛ n berɛ ba n mɛɛ dem deŋnesɔɔhna ne naa, hɛɛ ɛ Korowii maa dɛɛ tomɛɛ.

english_verse: This rock will be your house, and I will give back to you a tenth of everything you give me.”
translation_verse: Bwe maa kpɔa pa dɛ kpɔ dɛɛ liiri nɔɔ dɛɛ ba he torome bɔr ɛɛ. Ásɛ komɛlbwa ɡe haa tɛ mɛ la, bɔre fi bɛlbwa la, mɛɛ tɛɛ bɔrbeŋkpoŋii.”

english_verse: As Jacob continued on his way to the east,
translation_verse: Jekɔb ŋwɛnɛ waa valɔ la, o kpɔ sie chaɡɛ wee leebɔr dɛ kaa bela harɛ la ta.

english_verse: he looked out in a field and saw a well where shepherds took their sheep for water. Three flocks of sheep were lying around the well, which was covered with a large rock.
translation_verse: Waa kaa tel kpɔɡ bini bobɛl la, o na kɔlɔŋ, asɛ peera aa wara kuore atoro chɔ baro. Gɛ kɔlɔŋ nɔ taa ba dɔ nee tɛa aa nyɔ. Bwe baa kpɔa tɔ o nyoa la kan kɛrɛdɛ.

english_verse: Shepherds would roll the rock away when all their sheep had gathered there. Then after the sheep had been watered, the shepherds would roll the rock back over the mouth of the well.
translation_verse: Peera la bwa baa cheme kɔlɔŋ la ta naa, ɡɛɛ peteɡre la ɡbili bwe la le o nyoa, dɛ́ dɔ nee tɛa á nyɔ, ásɛ o berɛ ɡbili tɔ.

english_verse: Jacob asked the shepherds, “Where are you from?” “We're from Haran,” they answered.
translation_verse: Belaa Jekɔb pɛɛ peteɡra la ŋɔ, “Yabala, leperaa he leɔ?” Asɛ ba chaŋe ŋɔ, “Ya le Haran.”

english_verse: Then he asked, “Do you know Nahor's grandson Laban?” “Yes we do,” they replied.
translation_verse: O berɔ pɛɛ ba ŋɔ, “He jemɛ Neehɔ naa baa dɛ yerɔ Laban la aa?” Ba ɡe ŋɔ, “Ɔɔh, ya jemɔ.”

english_verse: “How is he?” Jacob asked. “He's fine,” they answered. “And here comes his daughter Rachel with the sheep.”
translation_verse: Anee Jekɔb bɔɔ ba ŋɔ, “O lea aa?” Ba ŋɔ, “O bwara kpeɡri.” Ba ŋɔ, “Nyiŋi na, o bihaah baa dɛ yerɔ Rakɛl la ne o peeraa dɛɛ ba la.”

english_verse: Jacob told them, “Look, the sun is still high up in the sky, and it's too early to bring in the rest of the flocks. Water your sheep and take them back to the pasture.”
translation_verse: Asɛ Jekɔb ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, “Wee ta nyɛɡre he ba boa peera nɔ nyoa la, hé tɛa nee a nyɔ dɛ berɛ kpɔa kaa dibɔr.”

english_verse: But they replied, “We can't do that until they all get here, and the rock has been rolled away from the well.”
translation_verse: Belaa ba chaŋe ŋɔ, “Yaa won ɛ ɡɛ, nemenɛ a bwa ba boa nyoa bonɔ, ásɛ ya ɡbili bwe nɔ le kɔlɔŋ nɔ nyoa mɔɔ dɛ́ tɛa nee a nyɔ.”

english_verse: While Jacob was still talking with the men, his cousin Rachel came up with her father's sheep.
translation_verse: O ne ba ta aa dɛ bol waa la dɛ Rakɛl ne o mɛɛ peera la ɡe balɔ dɛ ba jo. O te la, dɛ peera nɛɛ wɛɛ nyiŋi.

english_verse: When Jacob saw her and his uncle's sheep, he rolled the rock away and watered the sheep.
translation_verse: Jekɔb aa na o naara peera kɛ Rakɛl dɛ ba a ne la, o la kɔlɔŋ la ta dɛ ka ɡbili bwe la le o nyoa, dɛ dɔ nee tɛa a nyɔ.

english_verse: He then kissed Rachel and started crying because he was so happy.
translation_verse: Asɛ dɛ ka ɡbaa Rakɛl pɛl o bambile, dɛ mo o lwɛɛma dɛ wi.

english_verse: He told her that he was the son of her aunt Rebekah, and she ran and told her father about him.
translation_verse: Jekɔb ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “He mɛɛ lolee men, n nyaa Rebɛka.” Asɛ Rakɛl chwa dɛ ka ŋɔ o mɛɛ be.

english_verse: As soon as Laban heard the news, he ran out to meet Jacob. He hugged and kissed him and brought him to his home, where Jacob told him everything that had happened.
translation_verse: Laban aa no o manaara Jekɔb waa la, o chwao ka chemo dɛ ɡbaaro pɛl o te dɛ ba o ne dem. Asɛ Jekɔb bɔ o amaneɛ bwa.

english_verse: Laban said, “You are my nephew, and you are like one of my own family.” Jacob Marries Leah and Rachel After Jacob had been there for a month,
translation_verse: Asɛ Laban ŋɔ, “Kasinteŋii, n lole tentenee hen.” Asɛ Jekɔb so o be korobibir bwa. Jekɔb tomɛ o naara dɛ kpɔ o bihaahna mo

english_verse: Laban said to him, “You shouldn't have to work without pay, just because you are a relative of mine. What do you want me to give you?”
translation_verse: Belaa Laban ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Bɛ koh kɛŋɔ n lolee hen nomanta hɛɛ ɛ tomaa dɛɛ tɛ mɛ pɛɛ. Suuɡa aŋwɛnɛɛ hɛɛ nyin kɛ ń bɔ dɛɛ tɛɛ nɔ?”

english_verse: Laban had two daughters. Leah was older than Rachel, but her eyes didn't sparkle, while Rachel was beautiful and had a good figure.
translation_verse: Dɛ Lea sibie aa were kɛrɛdɛ, kɛ dɛ Rakɛl te wer tolo kohona.

english_verse: Since Jacob was in love with Rachel, he answered, “If you will let me marry Rachel, I'll work seven years for you.”
translation_verse: Bii la bwa bini la, dɛ Rakɛl nɛɛ Jekɔb sie ɛɛ lɛ, anomanta, o ŋɔ Laban be ŋɔ, “Hɛɛ tɛ mɛ Rakɛlee n mo te naa, mɛɛ ɛ he tomaa tɛɛ bene anuanɛ.”

english_verse: Laban replied, “It's better for me to let you marry Rachel than for someone else to have her. So stay and work for me.”
translation_verse: Anee Laban ŋɔ, “Dɛ he laa aa, maa on kpɔ tɛ nomɛlbwa. So n be.”

english_verse: Jacob worked seven years for Laban, but the time seemed like only a few days, because he loved Rachel so much.
translation_verse: Anomanta, Jekɔb koh Rakɛl waa dɛ ɛ toma tɛ Laban bene anuanɛ. Nyina waa dɛ nyin Rakɛl kohona la ɡelɔ bene anuanɛ la do kɛŋɔ tɔpera tamaa ane ken o be.

english_verse: Jacob said to Laban, “The time is up, and I want to marry Rachel now!”
translation_verse: Tɔpere la aa tela la, Jekɔb ŋɔ Laban be ŋɔ, “Bene anuanɛ la telo, tɛ mɛ n haah la ásɛ n mo name.”

english_verse: So Laban gave a big feast and invited all their neighbors.
translation_verse: Anomanta, Laban daa hanfalkondikwa dɛ yerɛ bwɛɛ la tena bwa ba cheme dɛ lɛ ba sie.

english_verse: But that evening he brought Leah to Jacob, who married her and spent the night with her.
translation_verse: Kɛ a jwaana la, Leaa Laban berɛ lawɛ ba tɛ Jekɔb asɛ o ne o ka chɔ.

english_verse: Laban also gave Zilpah to Leah as her servant woman.
translation_verse: Dɛ berɛ lawɛ tolo baa dɛ yerɔ Silpa la ba tɛ Lea ŋɔ ó do o sie.

english_verse: The next morning Jacob found out that he had married Leah, and he asked Laban, “Why did you do this to me? Didn't I work to get Rachel? Why did you trick me?”
translation_verse: Jekɔb ne haah la aa kaa chɔ la, bɔr chaahnɔ mɔɔ o ta na kɛŋɔ Leaa o ne o chɔ la. Belaa o la Laban be dɛ ka bɔɔro ŋɔ, “Bɔkwa waa he ɛɛ mɛ ken? Rakɛl waa laa n koh dɛ ɛ he toma aa? Aah ɛrɛ he berɛ neɡ mɛ ken nɔɔ?”

english_verse: Laban replied, “In our country the older daughter must get married first.
translation_verse: Asɛ Laban chaŋe ŋɔ, “Gɛ laa a do ya harɛ nɔ ta. Nomoaa ba lawɛ dɛɛ tɛ yal mɔɔ bechala.

english_verse: After you spend this week with Leah, you may also marry Rachel. But you will have to work for me another seven years.”
translation_verse: Gel hanfalwaa nɔ yawanyoa ba kaa, ásɛ n kpɔ Rakɛl ɡe tɛɛ. Dɛ hɛɛ berɔ tom mɛ bene anuanɛ jaa.”

english_verse: At the end of the week of celebration, Laban let Jacob marry Rachel, and he gave her his servant woman Bilhah. Jacob loved Rachel more than he did Leah, but he had to work another seven years for Laban.
translation_verse: Jekɔb lawɛ Rakɛl ɡe o ne o chɔ. Dɛ o dɛ nyinu dɛ ɡwaa Lea dɛ koh a waa dɛ tomɛ Laban bene anuanɛ ja. Jekɔb bii wa

english_verse: The Lord knew that Jacob loved Rachel more than he did Leah, and so he gave children to Leah, but not to Rachel.
translation_verse: Belaa Korowii aa naa kɛŋɔ o dɛ nyin Rakɛl waa dɛ ɡwaa Lea la, o tɛ Lea lol asɛ Rakɛl te ɛ hambara.

english_verse: Leah gave birth to a son and named him Reuben. Then she said, “The Lord has taken away my sorrow. Now my husband will love me more than he does Rachel.”
translation_verse: Lea kpoŋe tea dɛ lolɛ bibaa dɛ pa o sɔn Rubin. O munii kɛŋɔ Korowii na wahala maa lɔ a bini. “Name te n jaa ɛɛ dɛɛ nyin mɛɛ.”

english_verse: She had a second son and named him Simeon, because she said, “The Lord has heard that my husband doesn't love me.”
translation_verse: A habɔɔ, o berɔ kpoŋe tea dɛ lolɛ bibaa ja asɛ dɛ ŋɔ, “Korowii noɔ kɛŋɔ baa men nyin a waa o tɛ mɛ bie nɔ ja nɔ.” Dɛ pa o sɔn Simeon.

english_verse: When Leah's third son was born, she said, “Now my husband will hold me close.” So this son was named Levi.
translation_verse: O berɔ kpoŋe tea dɛ lolɛ bibaa ja. Dɛ ŋɔ, “Namee n jaa ɛɛ ba o bambile bwa kpɔe tɛ mɛ dɛkalkɛ n lolɛ bibaala batoro bwa tɛo.” Dɛ pa o sɔn Lewi.

english_verse: She had one more son and named him Judah, because she said, “I'll praise the Lord!”
translation_verse: O berɔ kpoŋe tea ja, waa baa lolɛ la, dɛ bibaalee ja, asɛ o ŋɔ, “Name te mɛɛ jam Korowiirii.” Asɛ dɛ pa o sɔn Juda. A habɔɔ o lol che.

english_verse: Rachel was very jealous of Leah for having children, and she said to Jacob, “I'll die if you don't give me some children!”
translation_verse: Rakɛl aa naa kɛŋɔ o ta bie lolɛ tɛ Jekɔb la, o mee Lea dɛ ŋɔ Jekɔb be ŋɔ, “Gel n lolɛ bii, dɛ ɡɛ laa aa, amɔ te mɛɛ sewɔɔ.”

english_verse: But Jacob became upset with Rachel and answered, “Don't blame me! I'm not God.”
translation_verse: Anee Jekɔb baah di o nɛ, o ŋɔ, “Bɛ n nɛɛ nya, n laa Korowii dɛ tɛɛ bii.”

english_verse: “Here, take my servant Bilhah,” Rachel told him. “Have children by her, and I'll let them be born on my knees to show that they are mine.”
translation_verse: Belaa Rakɛl ɡe chaŋe ŋɔ, “N tolo Bilhaa la, kpɔɔ ásɛ o lolɛ bie tɛ mɛ, á che o nɛɛ ń ɡe dɔ bii.”

english_verse: Then Rachel let Jacob marry Bilhah,
translation_verse: Anomanta, o lawɔ tɛ Jekɔb o mo.

english_verse: and they had a son.
translation_verse: Asɛ o kpoŋe tea dɛ lolɛ bibaa tɛ Jekɔb.

english_verse: Rachel named him Dan, because she said, “God has answered my prayers. He judged in my favor and has given me a son.”
translation_verse: Anee Rakɛl ŋɔ, “Korowii bol n waa tɛ mɛ. O no n wesoŋa dɛ tɛ mɛ bibaa, asɛ dɛ pa o sɔn Dan.”

english_verse: When Bilhah and Jacob had a second son,
translation_verse: Bilha berɔ kpoŋe tea dɛ lolɛ bibaa ja.

english_verse: Rachel said, “I've struggled hard with my sister, and I've won!” So she named the boy Naphtali.
translation_verse: Asɛ Rakɛl ŋɔ, “N ne n nahaah yoo taeh, kɛ n pɔ o nɛ.” Anomanta, o pa bie la sɔn Naftale, o munii yoi.

english_verse: When Leah realized she could not have any more children, she let Jacob marry her servant Zilpah,
translation_verse: Lea ɡe aa baa na kɛŋɔ o lol teŋo la, o lawɛ o tolo Silpa tɛ Jekɔb o mo.

english_verse: and they had a son.
translation_verse: Asɛ o lolɛ bibaa tɛo.

english_verse: “I'm really lucky,” Leah said, and she named the boy Gad.
translation_verse: Anee o ŋɔ, “N nyu wer,” asɛ dɛ pa bie la sɔn Gad.

english_verse: When they had another son,
translation_verse: Silpa berɔ lolɛ bibaa tɛ Jekɔb ja,

english_verse: Leah exclaimed, “I'm happy now, and all the women will say how happy I am.” So she named him Asher. Love Flowers
translation_verse: asɛ Lea ŋɔ, “N sie lɛo name. Taraken n bala ɛɛ dɛɛ yer mɛɛ nɛn waa na som.” Asɛ dɛ pa bie la sɔn Aasa.

english_verse: During the time of the wheat harvest, Reuben found some love flowers and took them to his mother Leah. Rachel asked Leah for some of them,
translation_verse: Rubin aa baa kpeɡ la, o la koo jaaɡe koma saŋ, dɛ ka kpɔ kwaane aa won ɡela baa ne haah ɛɛ nyin dɔŋa dɛ́ dɔ bii ba tɛ o nya Lea. Asɛ Rakɛl ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Tɛ mɛ he bie kwaa nɔ ane.”

english_verse: but Leah said, “It's bad enough that you stole my husband! Now you want my son's love flowers too.” “All right,” Rachel answered. “Let me have the flowers, and you can sleep with Jacob tonight.”
translation_verse: Asɛ Lea ŋɔ, “Lɛɛ haa lɛ n jaa nɔ ɡbo ta maɡra aa, he berɔ dɛɛ nyin he lɛ n bie kwaa nɔ o be ja aa?” Anee Rakɛl ŋɔ, “Dɛ hɛɛ tɛ mɛ he bie kwaa nɔ anee yaa, mɛɛ sɛoh dɛ tɛ he ne Jekɔb kalaŋre jwaana nɔ ne.”

english_verse: That evening when Jacob came in from the fields, Leah told him, “You're sleeping with me tonight. I hired you with my son's love flowers.” They slept together that night,
translation_verse: Belaa Jekɔb aa le koo dɛɛ ba jɔmɔra la, Lea ka chemo dɛ ŋɔ, “N ne henee dɛɛ ba chɔe fini jwaana nɔ ne, dɛkalkɛ n kpɔ n bie kwaa la ane lɛɛ le Rakɛl be.” Asɛ o ne o chɔ jwaana la ne.

english_verse: and God answered Leah's prayers by giving her a fifth son.
translation_verse: Korowii no o wesoŋa asɛ o kpoŋe tea ja dɛ lolɛ binuete tɛ Jekɔb.

english_verse: Leah shouted, “God has rewarded me for letting Jacob marry my servant,” and she named the boy Issachar.
translation_verse: Anee Lea ŋɔ, “Korowii tɛ mɛ n kembɔr, dɛkalkɛ n lawɛ n tolo tɛ n jaa asɛ o ne o chɔ.” Anomanta, o pa o sɔn Isaaka.

english_verse: When Leah had another son,
translation_verse: O berɔ kpoŋe binumɛlte tea, dɛ lolɛ bibaa tɛ Jekɔb.

english_verse: she exclaimed, “God has given me a wonderful gift, and my husband will praise me for giving him six sons.” So she named the boy Zebulun.
translation_verse: Asɛ o ŋɔ, “Korowii kɛ mɛ kondɛɛɡe. Name te n jaa ɛɛ dɛɛ duu mɛɛ, dɛkalkɛ n lolɛ bibaala banumɛl bwa tɛo.” Anomanta, o pa bie la sɔn Sebulon.

english_verse: Later, Leah had a daughter and named her Dinah.
translation_verse: A habɔɔ la, o lolɛ bihaah dɛ pa o sɔn Daena.

english_verse: Finally, God remembered Rachel—he answered her prayer by giving her a son. “God has taken away my disgrace,” she said.
translation_verse: Anomanta, o lolɛ bibaa dɛ ŋɔ, “Korowii tɛ mɛ bibaa dɛ laa sihiih kpɔ n sie.”

english_verse: “I'll name the boy Joseph, and I'll pray that the Lord will give me another son.” Jacob and Laban
translation_verse: O pa bie la sɔn Josef. Dɛ ŋɔ, “Korowii berɔ jaa mɛ bibaa.” Jekɔb kondɛɛra yae wa

english_verse: After Joseph was born, Jacob said to Laban, “Release me from our agreement and let me return to my own country.
translation_verse: Josef lola habɔɔ la, Jekɔb ŋɔ Laban be ŋɔ, “Tɛ mɛ ŋwɛnɛ ásɛ n berɛ kaa n bwɛ.

english_verse: You know how hard I've worked for you, so let me take my wives and children and leave.”
translation_verse: Gel n kpɔ n haahna ne bii maa ba he be dɛ ba ɛ toma dɔɔ ba la kaa. He ɡbabir na ɡɛ maa tomɛ.”

english_verse: But Laban told him, “If you really are my friend, stay on, and I'll pay whatever you ask. I'm sure the Lord has blessed me because of you.”
translation_verse: Gel n jemɛ kembɔr maa chɛ kɛ n kpɔ tɛɛ, ásɛ n nyin tɛɛ.”

english_verse: Jacob answered: You've seen how hard I've worked for you, and you know how your flocks and herds have grown under my care.
translation_verse: Belaa Jekɔb ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “He ɡbabir jemɛ ɡɛ maa tomɛ ka tel, ne ɡɛ maa nyiŋi he kondɛɛra ta a do wer nyiŋa maa nyiŋi a ta kɛrɛdɛ la wa.

english_verse: You didn't have much before I came, but the Lord has blessed everything I have ever done for you. Now it's time for me to start looking out for my own family.
translation_verse: A fa lɔ tamaa ken mɔɔ n ba, a berɔ ya kohona, asɛ Korowii tɛɛ hɛɛra bobɛlbwa maa dɛ la. Taraken, tɔpere telo kɛŋɔ n ɡbabir ɡe vɔrɔwe n dem.”

english_verse: “How much do you want me to pay you?” Laban asked. Then Jacob told him: I don't want you to pay me anything. Just do one thing, and I'll take care of your sheep and goats.
translation_verse: Anee Laban bɔɔro ŋɔ, “Aŋwɛnɛɛ hɛɛ nyin kɛ n bɔe nɔ?” Jekɔb ŋɔ, “Maa kembɔr bɛlbwa nyin. Dɛ he fe ɛɛ sɛh ɡɛ maa dɛ ba bola nɔ taa tɛ mɛ tenaa, he kondɛɛra la taa mɛɛ ba nyiŋa.

english_verse: Let me go through your flocks and herds and take the sheep and goats that are either spotted or speckled and the black lambs. That's all you need to give me.
translation_verse: Anee kɛŋɔ, ɡel n ka nyiŋi he kondɛɛra la bwa bini fini dɛ́ lawɛ pebie bɛlbwa waa ɛ ombiŋi ne bombiire aa lɛɡra kɛɛ dɛ peeɡe la. Anee ɛ kembɔr maa dɛ nyin.

english_verse: In the future you can easily find out if I've been honest. Just look and see if my animals are either spotted or speckled, or if the lambs are black. If they aren't, they've been stolen from you.
translation_verse: A ba ɡɛ naa, kerekere hɛɛ won jemɛ kɛŋɔ n ɛ nɛndɛɛɡe. Tɔpebɛl haa ba ŋɔ he nyiŋi n toma ɛɛ bini la, pebie bɛlbwa waa wola ombiŋi ɛɛ ne bombiire aa wola lɛɡrɛ kɛɛ dɛ peeɡe koo n kwaa ta naa, amɔ jemɛ kɛ dɛ ŋwɛɛ n ŋwɛ.”

english_verse: “I agree to that,” was Laban's response.
translation_verse: Anee Laban ŋɔ, “N sɛh ɡɛ. Yaa ɛ ɡɛ haa bola nɔɔ.”

english_verse: Before the end of the day, Laban had separated his spotted and speckled animals and the black lambs from the others and had put his sons in charge of them.
translation_verse: Awola tɔpere la, Laban lawɛ bombala aa lɛɡra ne anloni aa peeɡa kɛɛ anɔ la aa lɛɡre ampoŋa do o bii nɔn ta baa nyiŋi a ta. O lawɛ peera aa bira bwa ɡe jaa ba.

english_verse: Then Laban made Jacob keep the rest of the sheep and goats at a distance of three days' journey.
translation_verse: Asɛ dɛ ɡel tɔpera atoro ŋwɛnɛ ta o ne Jekɔb baah ta, asɛ Jekɔb ɡe ɛɛ nyiŋi kondɛɛra la kar ta.

english_verse: Jacob cut branches from some poplar trees and from some almond and evergreen trees. He peeled off part of the bark and made the branches look spotted and speckled.
translation_verse: Belaa Jekɔb teŋe daa ane kɛŋɔ sɛsɛ ne chɛnchɛne daa kpala, dɛ lɔ a pɛɡa peri ta, asɛ a to dɛ peeɡe.

english_verse: Then he put the branches where the sheep and goats would see them while they were drinking from the water trough. The goats mated there
translation_verse: O kpɔ daa la paaɡe kon aa dɛ nyɔ nee o bini la sie. Dɛkalkɛŋɔ belaa aa jwee.

english_verse: Some of the sheep that Jacob was keeping for Laban were already spotted. And when the others were ready to mate, he made sure that they faced in the direction of the spotted and black ones. In this way, Jacob built up a flock of sheep for himself and did not put them with the other sheep.
translation_verse: Jekɔb pere a bii la le anɔ la ta, dɛ ɡel anɔ la aa kaa la sie chaɡɛ Laban kwaa la waa paaɡe daa a sie la ne ambiŋere la be. Asɛ dɛ teɡɛ o ɡbabir kwaa la kaa baŋ bɛl, o ta an kpɔe koo Laban kwaa la ta.

english_verse: But he would not put out the branches when the weaker animals were mating. So Jacob got all of the healthy animals, and Laban got what was left.
translation_verse: Kɛ anɔ la a bwara aa wola kpeɡe la te, o ta daa la kpɔe paaɡe a sie. Labanee dɔ anɔ la aa wola kpeɡe la, asɛ Jekɔb ɡe dɔ anɔ la aa kpeɡa la.

english_verse: Jacob soon became rich and successful. He owned many sheep, goats, camels, and donkeys, as well as a lot of slaves.
translation_verse: A cheɡɛ a ta Jekɔb ba ɛ kondɔɔh dɛ dɔ kondɛɛra ne nɛndɔɔla ne nyoɡmare dɛ keeɡore kohona.

english_verse: Jacob heard that Laban's sons were complaining, “Jacob is now a rich man, and he got everything he owns from our father.”
translation_verse: Jekɔb noɔ kɛŋɔ Laban bibaala aa dɛ bol ŋɔ, “Jekɔb kpɔ ya mɛɛ kwaa waa dɔa la bwa. O kondɔɔh waa dɔa nɔ bwa le ya mɛɛ kwaa ta.”

english_verse: Jacob also noticed that Laban was not as friendly as he had been before.
translation_verse: Jekɔb nyiŋi Laban dɛ na kɛŋɔ ɡɛ o ne o fa aa doa wubwa la ta ɡɛ doe kpa.

english_verse: One day the Lord said, “Jacob, go back to your relatives in the land of your ancestors, and I will be with you.”
translation_verse: Belaa Korowii ŋɔ Jekɔb be ŋɔ, “Berɛ kaa he lolanar bini, he naawa harɛ la ta. Mɛɛ teŋɛ he nɛɛ.”

english_verse: Jacob sent for Rachel and Leah to meet him in the pasture where he kept his sheep,
translation_verse: Anomanta, o tomɔ ba ka yerɛ Rakɛl ne Lea ŋɔ bá chemo kpɔɡ bini bela o ne o kondɛɛra aa lole la.

english_verse: and he told them: Your father isn't as friendly with me as he used to be, but the God my ancestors worshiped has been on my side.
translation_verse: Asɛ o ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, “N nao kɛŋɔ n ne he mɛɛ ta ɡɛ ya fa aa doa wubwa la doe kpa. Kɛ Korowii n naawa aa tomɔ la ta teŋɛ n nɛ.

english_verse: years to buy your sheep and goats. During that time you kept changing my wages.
translation_verse: He bwa ɡe nao ɡɛ maa kpɔ n bokpeɡa bwa ɛ toma dɛ tɛ he mɛɛ.

english_verse: and that he keeps cheating me by changing my wages time after time. But God has protected me.
translation_verse: O ɡarɔ faah mɛ n kembɔr dɛ beɡra kera fi. Kɛ Korowii ta on ŋwɛnɛ tɛɛ asɛ o won ɛɛ mɛ wechɔɡa bɛlbwa.

english_verse: When your father said the speckled sheep would be my wages, all of them were speckled. And when he said the spotted ones would be mine, all of them were spotted.
translation_verse: Saŋ bɛlbwa waa ŋɔ, ‘Peera ne boohna aa lɛɡre laanee dɛ́ ɛ he kembɔr’ la, ɡɛɛ a bwa loɡle dɛ lɛɡre. O berɔ ŋɔ, ‘Pera ne boohna aa peeɡe laanee dɛ́ ɛ he kembɔr’ aa, ɡɛɛ a bwa loɡle dɛ peeɡe.

english_verse: That's how God has taken sheep and goats from your father and given them to me.
translation_verse: Gɛ ŋwɛnɛ nɔ taa a che Korowii ɡel n dɔ kondɛɛra le he mɛɛ kwaa ta.

english_verse: Once, when the flocks were mating, I dreamed that all the rams were either spotted or speckled.
translation_verse: Peera la teene kpoŋa saŋ la, n deero dɛ na kɛŋɔ bombala aa dɛ jweera la peeɡɔ dɛ lɛɡre.

english_verse: Then God's angel called me by name. I answered,
translation_verse: Belaa nyundua torome bɛl yer mɛ deera la ta dɛ ŋɔ, ‘Jekɔb’ asɛ n sɛh ŋɔ ‘Menee nɔ.’

english_verse: and he said, “Notice that all the rams are either spotted or speckled. I know everything Laban is doing to you,
translation_verse: Anee o ŋɔ, ‘Ha sie dɛ nyiŋi na, bombala bwa aa dɛ jwee la peeɡɔ dɛ lɛɡre. Dɛkalkɛ n na ɡɛ Laban aa dɛ ɛɛ bwa.

english_verse: and I am the God you worshiped at Bethel, when you poured olive oil on a rock and made a promise to me. Leave here at once and return to the land where you were born.”
translation_verse: Menee Korowii maa kpɔ n te baɡle Bɛtel asɛ he kpɔ bwe bɛl pa bela, dɛ fuɡe noo ta o ta, dɛ kpɔ dɛɛ lii mɛ, dɛ baɡ mɛ nyoa la. Ir dɛ́ kpɔ he te dɛ́ berɛ kaa harɛ baa lolɛ o ta la ta.’ ”

english_verse: He treats us like foreigners and has even cheated us out of the bride price that should have been ours.
translation_verse: O ɛ yaa kɛ nɛŋhɔɔhra dɛ yoɡ yaa. Suuɡa waa yoɡ yaa dɛ lɛ la ɡe, o di a bwa.

english_verse: So do whatever God tells you to do. Even the property God took from our father and gave to you really belongs to us and our children.
translation_verse: Kondɔɔh Korowii aa ɡela he dɔ le ya mɛɛ kwaa ta la berɛ ya ne ya bii kwa. Ɛ wobɛlbwa Korowii aa ŋɔa he ɛ.”

english_verse: Then Jacob, his wives, and his children got on camels and left
translation_verse: Belaa Jekɔb kpɔ o te, dɛ lawɛ o haahna ne bii so nyoɡmare ta, dɛ́ kaa Keenan o mɛɛ harɛ ta,

english_verse: northern Syria for the home of his father Isaac in Canaan. Jacob took along all his flocks, herds, and other property.
translation_verse: dɛ kpɔ o kondɛɛra waa dɔa Mɛsopoteemea harɛ ta bwa, ne komɛlbwa waa dɔa ɡe ja dɛɛ kaa o mɛɛ Aesek be Keenan harɛ ta.

english_verse: Before Rachel left, she stole the household idols while Laban was out shearing his sheep.
translation_verse: Laban kaa o peera pona fona, asɛ Rakɛl ŋwɛ ba dem voɡa aa lɔ o mɛɛ be.

english_verse: long years to earn your two daughters and another
translation_verse: Jekɔb ta ɡelɛ Laban jemɛ kɛŋɔ o dɛ kaa o bwɛ.

english_verse: When Jacob crossed the Euphrates River and headed for the hill country of Gilead, he took with him everything he owned. Laban Catches Up with Jacob
translation_verse: O kpɔ komɛlbwa dɛ ɛ warane dɛ le kaa. O kaa ɡale Yufretis Moo la, dɛ kpɔ sie pa Gelead deŋɡarere harɛ ta dɛɛ kaa. Laban ti Jekɔb

english_verse: Three days later Laban found out that Jacob had gone.
translation_verse: A tɔpetooro wee laanee ba ŋɔ Laban be ŋɔ Jekɔb chwao.

english_verse: So he took some of his relatives along and chased after Jacob for seven days, before catching up with him in the hill country of Gilead.
translation_verse: Belaa o kpɔ o lolanar bane ja o nɛɛ ba ti Jekɔb, dɛ ka puu Gelead deŋɡarere harɛ ta bela. Aa ɛ tɔpera anuanɛ ŋwɛnɛɛ.

english_verse: But God appeared to Laban in a dream that night and warned, “Don't say a word to Jacob. Don't make a threat or a promise.”
translation_verse: Korowii ba Laban be deera ta awola jwaana, dɛ ba ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Nyiŋi kɛrɛdɛ dɛ bɛ Jekɔb ba aah ŋwɛnɛ bɛlbwa ta.”

english_verse: Jacob had set up camp in the hill country of Gilead, when Laban and his relatives came and set up camp in another part of the hill country. Laban went to Jacob
translation_verse: Dɛ Jekɔb baŋre o tɛnte dea Gelead deŋɡarere harɛ ta, asɛ Laban ɡe ne o nɛra baŋre ba kon baŋ bɛl.

english_verse: and said: Look what you've done! You've tricked me and run off with my daughters like a kidnapper.
translation_verse: Laban la Jekɔb be dɛ ka ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ he ɛɛ mɛ ɡɛ nɔɔ? He neɡ mɛ dɛ kpɔ n bihaahna chwa kɛŋɔ haa kaa yo laa dɛ laɡ ba la.

english_verse: Why did you sneak away without telling me? I would have given you a going-away party with singing and with music on tambourines and harps.
translation_verse: Ɛrɛɛ he neɡ mɛ dɛ sɔh dɛ chwa he ta men amaneɛ ba bɔe nɔɔ? He ɡelɔ n deŋne no aa, n fe kpɔ janjela ne kwaa baa dɛ yiiɡa kɛŋɔ loŋa ba tae ŋwɛnɛ silɛɛ ne.

english_verse: You didn't even give me a chance to kiss my own grandchildren and daughters goodbye. That was really foolish.
translation_verse: He ta ɡelɛ n mo n bii ne naanar lwɛrɛme dɛ ta ba ŋwɛnɛ. Gɛnewaa he ɛ ɡɛ la!

english_verse: I could easily hurt you, but the God your father worshiped has warned me not to make any threats or promises.
translation_verse: N fe dɔ ŋwɛnɛ kɛŋɔ ń won ɛɛ wechɔɡa, kɛ dɛ jwaana ne la, Korowii he mɛɛ aa tomɔ la kah mɛ ŋɔ n bɛ hen aah ŋwɛnɛ bɛlbwa ta.

english_verse: I can understand why you were eager to return to your father, but why did you have to steal my idols?
translation_verse: N jemɔ kɛŋɔ he sie cheɡɛ chiŋ hɛɛ nyin bɔr dɛ́ kaa he bwɛ. Aah dɛ ɛrɛ waa he berɛ ŋwɛ n voɡa nɔɔ?”

english_verse: Jacob answered, “I left secretly because I was afraid you would take your daughters from me by force.
translation_verse: Belaa Jekɔb chaŋo ŋɔ, “Ɔmaa n ɔmɛ, n liiro ŋɔ he ken ɛɛ lɛ he bihaahna la n bee.

english_verse: If you find that any one of us has taken your idols, I'll have that person killed. Let your relatives be witnesses. Show me what belongs to you, and you can take it back.” Jacob did not realize that Rachel had stolen the household idols.
translation_verse: Nyiŋi, nomɛlbwa haa na voɡa la o be la, a chɛ kɛ bá kpoo. Ya nɛra nɔ ɡe lɔ bonɔ dɛ́ di yaa danseɛ, komɛlbwa waa ɛ he kon la, ásɛ he kpɔ.” Dɛ Jekɔb ta jemɛ kɛŋɔ Rakɛlee ŋwɛ o mɛɛ Laban voɡa la.

english_verse: Laban searched the tents of Jacob, Leah, and the two servant women, but did not find the idols. Then he went to Rachel's tent.
translation_verse: Laban kaa jo Jekɔb tɛnte dea bini dɛ ka ɡaaɡe, dɛ le ka jo Lea ne o toli la ɡe kon bini o ta voɡa la nae. Belaa o berɛ la Rakɛl ɡe kon bini.

english_verse: She had already hidden them in the cushion she used as a saddle and was sitting on it. Laban searched everywhere and did not find them.
translation_verse: Ajaah dɛ onee kpɔa do kon baa kpɔa dawɛ nyoɡma ta dɛɛ so o ta la lɔɡa dɛ so a ta. Dɛ Laban kaa nyiŋi o dea kɛ o ta an nae.

english_verse: Rachel said, “Father, please don't be angry with me for not getting up; I'm having my period.” Laban kept on searching, but still did not find the idols.
translation_verse: Asɛ Rakɛl ŋɔ o mɛɛ be ŋɔ, “N poori n mɛɛ, bɛ ɡel he baah di. Maa won ir che he sie, dɛkalkɛ n le dahara.” Laban nyiŋi o tɛnte dea bini kɛ wɛɛ na voɡa laanee, kɛ o ta an nae.

english_verse: Jacob became very angry and said to Laban: What have I done wrong? Have I committed some crime? Is that why you hunted me down?
translation_verse: Belaa Jekɔb kpɔ bandia dɛ bɔɔro ŋɔ, “Bɔkwa wechɔɡaa n ɛɔ? Mmara besoo n koni asɛ he ti mɛ kɛŋɔ nɛnchɔɡe nɔɔ?

english_verse: After searching through everything I have, did you find anything of yours? If so, put it here, where your relatives and mine can see it. Then we can decide what to do.
translation_verse: Haa nyiŋi n bone bwa bini nɔ, he dem kon besoo he na nɔ? Kpɔ bil n ne he nɛra baa lɔ bonɔ nɔ sie, ásɛ ba pa bole.

english_verse: If a wild animal killed one of your sheep or goats, I paid for it myself. In fact, you demanded the full price, whether the animal was killed during the day or at night.
translation_verse: Anɔ la konchɔɡa aa dɛ kpoora bwa la, n ɡbabirii dɛɛ bɔe a kem. Anɔ la baa dɛ ŋwɛa webaŋa ne jwaana ɡe bwa la, he ɡelɔ mɛɛ bɔe a kem.

english_verse: I sweated every day, and I couldn't sleep at night because of the cold.
translation_verse: Dɛ n dɛ na wahala, webaŋa wee dɛ kpo mɛ jwaana waa ɛɛ kpo mɛ, dɛ maa won dom chɔ.

english_verse: If the fearsome God worshiped by Abraham and my father Isaac had not been on my side, you would have sent me away without a thing. But God saw my hard work, and he knew the trouble I was in, so he helped me. Then last night he told you how wrong you were. Jacob and Laban Make an Agreement
translation_verse: Korowii n nabaa Abraham ne n mɛɛ Aesek aa tomɔ la laa teŋɛ n nɛɛ aa, he fe ɡelɔ n kpɔ nɔŋɡbala kaa. Kɛ Korowii na n wenaale ne n toma maa ɛa, a waa dɛ jwaana ne o ba pa bole la.” Jekɔb ne Laban fɔo fɔwa

english_verse: Laban said to Jacob, “Leah and Rachel are my daughters, and their children belong to me. All these sheep you are taking are really mine too. In fact, everything you have belongs to me. But there is nothing I can do to keep my daughters and their children.
translation_verse: Ate, Laban chaŋe ŋɔ, “N biirii haahna nɔ, ba bii ɡe n kwaa, asɛ kondɛɛra nɔ bwa ɡe ɛ n kwa. Komɛlbwa aa lɔ bonɔ ɛ n kon. Kɛ n bihaahna nɔ ne ba ɡe bii nɔ, maa won kpoŋ ba.

english_verse: So I am ready to make an agreement with you, and we will pile up some large rocks here to remind us of the agreement.”
translation_verse: Taraken n sɛoh kɛŋɔ n ne he fɔwɛ fɔo. Gel ya pa bwea dawɛ dɔŋa nɛ á baɡle ya fɔo la.”

english_verse: After Jacob had set up a large rock,
translation_verse: Asɛ Jekɔb kpɔ bwe bɛl pa bela ŋɔ bá kpɔ dɛɛ lii ba fɔo la.

english_verse: he told his men to get some more rocks and pile them up next to it. Then Jacob and Laban ate a meal together beside the rocks.
translation_verse: Jekɔb ɡelɔ o bonɔɔna pa bwea a daŋɛ chɔ, asɛ Jekɔb ne Laban dɛ bonɔɔna la bwa pɛ so a jwɛh, dɛ di kwa.

english_verse: Laban named the pile of rocks Jegar Sahadutha. But Jacob named it Galeed.
translation_verse: Laban pa bela sɔn Jeɡar Sahaduta, asɛ Jekɔb ɡe pa o sɔn Galiid.

english_verse: Laban said to Jacob, “This pile of rocks will remind us of our agreement.” That's why the place was named Galeed.
translation_verse: Belaa Laban ŋɔ Jekɔb be ŋɔ, “Bwea nɔ aa darawe dɔŋa nɛɛ nɔɔ dɛ́ lii ya nɛra banɛ nɔ fɔo la.” A waa ba pa bela sɔn Galiid, o munii danseɛ bwea la.

english_verse: Laban also said, “This pile of rocks means that the Lord will watch us both while we are apart from each other.” So the place was also named Mizpah.
translation_verse: Dɛ ŋɔ, “Yaa dɛ peɡri dɔŋa baah nɔ, Korowii nyiŋi ya nɛ.” Asɛ dɛ pa bela sɔn Mispa.

english_verse: Then Laban said: If you mistreat my daughters or marry other women, I may not know about it, but remember, God is watching us!
translation_verse: Dɛ berɛ ŋɔ, “Dɛ he ka dɛ fiiɡi n bihaahna nɔ kɛɛ dɛ ka mo haahna ja ba nɛ aa, a lole kɛŋɔ maa belaa do te, kɛ Korowii te ɛɛ nao.

english_verse: Both this pile of rocks and this large rock have been set up between us as a reminder. I must never go past them to attack you, and you must never come past them to attack me.
translation_verse: Bwea aa darawe dɔŋa nɛɛ nɔ ne onɔ maa kpɔa pa nɔɔ dɛɛ ba chɔe dɛ lii yaa. Maa bwea nɔɔ ɡale dɛ́ ba yoi, hé ɡe bɛ an ɡale dɛ́ ba yoo mɛ.

english_verse: My father Nahor, your grandfather Abraham, and their ancestors all worshiped the same God, and he will make sure that we each keep the agreement. Then Jacob made a promise in the name of the fearsome God his father Isaac had worshiped.
translation_verse: Korowii ya nabaa Abraham ne Neehɔ aa tomɔ laanee dɛ́ bol ya baah waa dɛ́ pa bole.” Anomanta, Jekɔb ŋwɛɛ Korowii o mɛɛ Aesek aa ɔmɔ dɛ tomɔ la kɛŋɔ wɛɛ teŋɛ waa waa bola la taa.

english_verse: Jacob killed an animal and offered it as a sacrifice there on the mountain, and he invited his men to eat with him. After the meal they spent the night on the mountain.
translation_verse: O ɛ saraha deŋɡarere harɛ baa soɡa la ta, dɛ yerɛ o lolanar la ba ba di kondikwaa la. Baa dia tonɛ la, ba chɔ bela awola jwaana.

english_verse: Early the next morning, Laban kissed his daughters and his grandchildren goodbye, then he left to go back home.
translation_verse: Tɔ aa pera chɔmbibi la, Laban mo o bihaahna ne o naanar la lwɛrɛme, dɛ swee andɛɛɡa tɛɛ ba dɛ berɛ kaa o bwɛ.

english_verse: As Jacob was on his way back home, some of God's angels came and met him.
translation_verse: Jekɔb chiɡ ŋwɛnɛ ta dɛɛ kaa, asɛ nyundua toroma ba chemo.

english_verse: When Jacob saw them, he said, “This is God's camp.” So he named the place Mahanaim.
translation_verse: Waa na ba la, anee o ŋɔ, “Korowii soŋnibɔree bonɔ.” Asɛ dɛ pa bela sɔn Mahanaim.

english_verse: Jacob sent messengers on ahead to Esau, who lived in the land of Seir, also known as Edom.
translation_verse: Belaa Jekɔb tomɛ toroma ŋɔ bá tɔ o sie dɛ́ kaa o dɔɔ Esɔ be. Dɛ Esɔ soɡe harɛ bɛl baa dɛ yerɛ bela Edom.

english_verse: Jacob told them to say to Esau, “Master, I am your servant! I have lived with Laban all this time,
translation_verse: Jekɔb do toroma la ŋɔ bá ka ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “He bonɔɔ Jekɔb ŋɔ, o kaa so Laban be, belaa o do dɛ ba le fini,

english_verse: and now I own cattle, donkeys, and sheep, as well as many slaves. Master, I am sending these messengers in the hope that you will be kind to me.”

translation_verse: Gɛ tentenee o ŋɔ nɛn nɛɛte, ne toorote, ne banɔ la bwa waa kpɔ kondɛɛra do ba nɔn ta la be ŋɔ, “Dɛ he cheme Esɔ aa, hé bwa ɡe ŋɔ o be ɡɛ.

english_verse: Jacob's men took the gifts on ahead of him, but he spent the night in camp. Jacob's Name Is Changed to Israel
translation_verse: Ba kpɔ koŋkɛɛla la tɔ sie dɛ kaa asɛ o te berɛ chɔ bela waa choɡa la. Jekɔb ne nyundua torome jwiira wa

english_verse: Jacob got up in the middle of the night and took his wives, his eleven children, and everything he owned across to the other side of the Jabbok River for safety.
translation_verse: Waa kpɔ ba le nee la tonɛ la, o berɛ ba kpɔ komɛlbwa ɡe waa dɔa la ɡe le,

english_verse: Afterwards, Jacob went back and spent the rest of the night alone. A man came and fought with Jacob until just before daybreak.
translation_verse: asɛ dɛ ɡbo ka baŋ bela. Belaa baa bɛl ba jwiiru, ba kpoŋe dɔŋa bini awola jwaana la ne, dɛ ka tel kɛŋɔ aa baa ka tama ásɛ bɔr chaah.

english_verse: When the man saw that he could not win, he struck Jacob on the hip and threw it out of joint.
translation_verse: Baa la aa baa na kɛŋɔ waa won ɡo Jekɔb la, o kpɔ nɔn lɔ Jekɔb kɛɡra asɛ o sor.

english_verse: They kept on wrestling until the man said, “Let go of me! It's almost daylight.” “You can't go until you bless me,” Jacob replied.
translation_verse: Baa la ŋɔ, “Kpɔ mɛ ta n kaa, bɔr dɛ chaah.” Asɛ Jekɔb ŋɔ, “Maa hen ta, nemenɛ haa swee andɛɛɡa tɛ mɛ mɔɔ.”

english_verse: Then the man asked, “What is your name?” “Jacob,” he answered.
translation_verse: Baa la bɔɔro ŋɔ, “He sɔne ɛrɔɔ?” Anee o ŋɔ, “N sɔne Jekɔb.”

english_verse: The man said, “From now on, your name will no longer be Jacob. You will be called Israel, because you have wrestled with God and with men, and you have won.”
translation_verse: Asɛ baa la berɛ ŋɔ, “He sɔne laa Jekɔb kpa. He ne Korowii ne nɛwɛnyina yoo, ba ta wone pɔ he nɛ, anomanta, he sɔne Israel.”

english_verse: Jacob said, “Now tell me your name.” “Don't you know who I am?” he asked. And he blessed Jacob.
translation_verse: Jekɔb ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “N poori, chaɡ mɛ he sɔn.” Anee o chaŋe ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛ waa hɛɛ nyin dɛ́ jemɛ n sɔn nɔɔ?” Asɛ o swee andɛɛɡa tɛo bela.

english_verse: The sun was coming up as Jacob was leaving Peniel. He was limping because he had been struck on the hip,
translation_verse: Jekɔb aa le Pɛneɛl dɛɛ kaa la dɛ wee leɔ. O kɛɡra la aa sora nomanta, dɛ o dɛ chole o ta.

english_verse: and the muscle on his hip joint had been injured. That's why even today the people of Israel don't eat the hip muscle of any animal.
translation_verse: Dɛ kpoŋe ba le fini Israel tena aa ol kɛɡra di. Baa la aa kpɔ nɔn lɔ Jekɔb kɛɡra ta o sor la nomanta.

english_verse: The two servant women, Zilpah and Bilhah, together with their children went first, followed by Leah and her children, then by Rachel and Joseph.
translation_verse: O ɡelɔ o toli la lawɛ ba bii tɔ sie mɔɔ Lea ne o bii teŋɛ, asɛ Rakɛl ne Josef ka mun ta.

english_verse: Jacob himself walked in front of them all, bowing to the ground seven times as he came near his brother.
translation_verse: Jekɔb berɔ ka tɔ ba bwa sie, asɛ waa dɛ bɛne Esɔ la, o ba harɛ kera anuanɛ mɔɔ dɛ tel o be.

english_verse: But Esau ran toward Jacob and hugged and kissed him. Then the two brothers started crying.
translation_verse: Esɔ aa nao la, o chwao dɛ ka ɡbaaro pɛl o te dɛ kpɔ o nɔɔra dawɛ o vaama ta dɛ mo o lwɛɛma, ba bwa berɛ wi.

english_verse: When Esau noticed the women and children he asked, “Whose children are these?” Jacob answered, “These are the children the Lord has been kind enough to give to me, your servant.”
translation_verse: Esɔ na haahna la ne bechale la, dɛ pɛɛro ŋɔ, “Aah bamewa ɡee ja he nɛɛ nɔɔ?” Asɛ Jekɔb chaŋe dɛ ŋɔ, “A ɡɛ bii nɔ, Korowiirii sune n nɛɛ dɛ kpɔ ba tɛ mɛ.”

english_verse: Then the two servant women and their children came and bowed down to Esau.
translation_verse: Anee o toli la ne ba bii ba ɡuŋi Esɔ harɛ,

english_verse: Next, Leah and her children came and bowed down; finally, Joseph and Rachel also came and bowed down.
translation_verse: asɛ Lea ɡe ne o bii ba ɡuŋu, asɛ Josef ne Rakɛl ɡe ka mun dɛ ba ɡuŋu harɛ.

english_verse: Esau asked Jacob, “Why did you send those herds I met along the road?” “Master,” Jacob answered, “I sent them so you would be friendly to me.”
translation_verse: Esɔ bɔɔro ŋɔ, “Nɛra maa chem ba ba kpɔ kondɛɛra damanta dɛɛ kaa la ɡe sɛ?” Anee Jekɔb chaŋe ŋɔ, “N kpɔa dɛɛ ba ba tɛɛ ásɛ he sie lɛ n nɛ.”

english_verse: “But, brother, I already have plenty,” Esau replied. “Keep them for yourself.”
translation_verse: Belaa Esɔ ŋɔ, “N nime dɛɛɡe, anɔ la n ɡbabir aa dɔa warɔ. Gel a che tɛɛ.”

english_verse: “No!” Jacob said. “Please accept them as a sign of your friendship for me. When you welcomed me and I saw your face, it was like seeing the face of God.
translation_verse: Anee Jekɔb ɡe ŋɔ, “Akai, n dɛ soŋe dɛ he sie lɛ n nɛɛ tenaa he kpɔ. Taraken maa nae nɔ, a denɔ ɛɛ mɛ kɛŋɔ maa na Korowii ken.

english_verse: Please accept these as gifts I brought to you. God has been good to me, and I have everything I need.” Jacob kept insisting until Esau agreed.
translation_verse: N poori, sɛh dɛ́ lɛ kwaa maa kpɔa dɛɛ tɛɛ nɔ. Korowii cha mɛ kohona dɛ sune n nɛɛ asɛ dɛ tɛ mɛ komɛlbwa.” Ba bolɔ la sie kɛrɛdɛ mɔɔ Esɔ ta ba lɛ.

english_verse: “Let's get ready to travel,” Esau said. “I'll go along with you.”
translation_verse: Asɛ Esɔ ŋɔ, “Ya kaa. Kɛ mɛɛ tɔ he siee.”

english_verse: But Jacob answered, “Master, you know traveling is hard on children, and I have to look after the sheep and goats that are nursing their young. If my animals travel too much in one day, they will all die.
translation_verse: Jekɔb ɡe berɔ ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “He nao kɛŋɔ n bii nɔ nɔn kao, asɛ n peera ne nae ne a bii aa dɛ ɔr la bwa ɡe waa hiah mɛ. Maa won kpɔa valɛ kohona tɔpebir a ba serewe.

english_verse: Why don't you go on ahead and let me travel along slowly with the children, the herds, and the flocks. We can meet again in the country of Edom.”
translation_verse: Amɔ tɔ sie ásɛ n ɡe ne n nae nɔ ne n bii nɔ valɛ tama tama ka tel kɛŋɔ yaa ba he be Edom.”

english_verse: Esau replied, “Let me leave some of my men with you.” “You don't have to do that,” Jacob answered. “I am happy, simply knowing that you are friendly to me.”
translation_verse: Anee Esɔ ŋɔ, “Amɔ mɛɛ ɡel n bonɔɔna nɔ bini banee tɛɛ he ne baa ba.” Asɛ Jekɔb ŋɔ, “Bonɔɔna la ɡela dɛ tɛ mɛ te waa ta hiaeh. Nyinaa mɛɛ nyin kɛŋɔ he sie lɛ n nɛ.”

english_verse: But Jacob went to Succoth, where he built a house for himself and set up shelters for his animals. That's why the place is called Succoth. Jacob Arrives at Shechem
translation_verse: Kɛ Jekɔb te kaa Sukot harɛ ta, dɛ ka do o dea, asɛ dɛ do patare tɛ o kondɛɛra ɡe. A waa ba pa bela sɔn Sukot la. O munii patare.

english_verse: After leaving northern Syria, Jacob arrived safely at Shechem in Canaan and set up camp outside the city.
translation_verse: Waa le Mɛsopoteemea la, o kaa bwɛjen Sɛkem waa lɔ Keenan harɛ ta, dɛ ka baŋre o tɛnte dea bɛne bwɛjen la.

english_verse: The land where he camped was owned by the descendants of Hamor, the father of Shechem. So Jacob paid them
translation_verse: O yawɛ harɛ waa baŋre o tɛnte dea o ta la suuɡapoŋa lafa le Sɛkem mɛɛ Hamɔ bii be.

english_verse: then he set up his tents and built an altar there to honor the God of Israel.
translation_verse: O ɛ kon baa ɛ saraha o ta dɛɛ tɛ Korowii bela, asɛ dɛ pa o sɔn ‘Korowii Israel tena aa dɛ tomɔ’.

english_verse: Dinah, the daughter of Jacob and Leah, went to visit some of the women who lived nearby.
translation_verse: Awola bɛl, Jekɔb ne o haah Lea bihaah Daena iro ŋɔ o dɛ la ka chɔɔ Keenan haahna bane.

english_verse: She was seen by Hamor's son Shechem, the leader of the Hivites, and he grabbed her and raped her.
translation_verse: Hivi tena Kooro Hamɔ bibaa Sɛkem nao dɛ lawɔ, dɛ ɡuɡru o ne o chɔ.

english_verse: But Shechem was attracted to Dinah, so he told her how much he loved her.
translation_verse: Dɛ o sie lɛ bitolo la nɛɛ kɛrɛdɛ, asɛ o bambile lawɔ wɛɛ di o deŋna.

english_verse: Shechem even asked his father to arrange for him to marry her.
translation_verse: Sɛkem ŋɔ o mɛɛ be ŋɔ, “N mɛɛ, n dɛ nyin kɛŋɔ he ka nyin Daena tɛ mɛ ń mo.”

english_verse: Meanwhile, Jacob heard what had happened. But his sons were out in the fields with the cattle, so he did not do anything at the time.
translation_verse: Dɛ Jekɔb noɔ kɛŋɔ Sɛkem ɡuɡri o bihaah Daena o ne o chɔ, kɛ bela la, o ta wobɛlbwa chaŋɛ, dɛkalkɛ dɛ o bibaala la kaa nae ne dibɔr ba ta balɛ mɔɔ.

english_verse: just as Jacob's sons were coming in from work. When they learned that their sister had been raped, they became furiously angry, because nothing is more disgraceful than rape, and it must not be tolerated.
translation_verse: dɛ Jekɔb bii la ɡe denɔ le kpɔɡ bini ba. Baa baa no waa la la, a we ba nɛ, asɛ ba baah di kohona kɛŋɔ Sɛkem aa ɛ wedoŋa dɛ nyiŋi Israel tena nyubaah kɛŋɔ waa ɡuɡri ba nimambie o ne o chɔ la.

english_verse: Hamor said to Jacob and his sons: My son Shechem really loves Dinah. Please let him marry her.
translation_verse: Belaa Kooro Hamɔ ŋɔ Jekɔb be ŋɔ, “N bie Sɛkem dɛ nyin he bie Daena. N poori, kpɔɔ tɛ mɛ n tɛo ó mo.

english_verse: Why don't you start letting your families marry into our families and ours marry into yours?
translation_verse: Gel ya nyoa pɛ yaa mo he bihaahna, ásɛ he ɡe ɛɛ mo ya kwa.

english_verse: You can share this land with us. Move freely about until you find the property you want; then buy it and settle down here.
translation_verse: Hɛɛ won so ya be bonɔ, harɛ ɡee dena chɔ kaa la. Hɛɛ won ka so bobɛlbwa haa dɛ nyin, dɛɛ di bona dɛ́ dɔ kwa.”

english_verse: Shechem added, “Do this favor for me, and I'll give whatever you want.
translation_verse: Asɛ Sɛkem ŋɔ Daena mɛɛ ne o dɔɔranar be ŋɔ, “Hɛ́ɛ sɛoh dɛ́ ɛ ɡɛ tɛ mɛ naa, komɛlbwa haa lɛ la, mɛɛ tɛ heyaa.

english_verse: Jacob's sons wanted to get even with Shechem and his father because of what had happened to their sister.
translation_verse: Sɛkem aa ɡuɡri ba nimambie Daena o ne o chɔ nomanta, Jekɔb bii la neɡre o ne o mɛɛ Hamɔ.

english_verse: So they tricked them by saying: You're not circumcised! It would be a disgrace for us to let you marry Dinah now.
translation_verse: Ba ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, “Yaa won ɛ ɡɛ. Yaa sɛh ya nimambie yalɛ baa waa wola o pen teŋe. A ɡɛ waa nɔ ɛ sihihwa dɛ tɛ yaa.

english_verse: But we will let you marry her, if you and the other men in your tribe agree to be circumcised.
translation_verse: Waa aa ɡel ya sɛh laanee kɛŋɔ, hé ɡel he bibaala bwa teŋni ba pena kɛ yan.

english_verse: Then your families can marry into ours, and ours can marry into yours, and we can live together like one nation.
translation_verse: Ate naa, aa maɡroo kɛŋɔ ya mo dɔŋa bihaahna. Ya ne hɛɛ pɛo so dɛ́ ɛ nɛmbeŋkpoŋ.

english_verse: But if you don't agree to be circumcised, we'll take Dinah and leave this place.
translation_verse: Dɛ he ta penteŋ la ta sɛɛh tenaa, yaa kpɔ ya nimambiee dɛ́ ir harɛ nɔ ta kaa.”
