english_verse: Hamor and Shechem liked what was said.
translation_verse: Waa baa bola la wer dɛ tɛ Hamɔ ne o bie Sɛkem.

english_verse: Shechem was the most respected person in his family, and he was so in love with Dinah that he hurried off to get everything done.
translation_verse: Sɛkem aa dɛ nyin tolo la kohona nomanta, o ta waa la kpɔe tuuɡi harɛ. Dɛ o waa dɔ nyɛl ɡwaa nɛra baa lɔ o mɛɛ dem bela bwa.

english_verse: The two men met with the other leaders of their city and told them:
translation_verse: Kooro Hamɔ ne o bie Sɛkem la ba bwɛɛ la doonyoa baa soɡa dɛɛ bol waa la, dɛ ka cheme bwɛɛ la tena dɛ ŋɔ,

english_verse: These people really are friendly. Why not let them move freely about until they find the property they want? There's enough land here for them and for us. Then our families can marry into theirs, and theirs can marry into ours.
translation_verse: “Ya ne nɛra la som, hé ɡel ba so dɛɛ ɛ ba toma. Harɛ la kan ba dɔ bɔr dɛ so. Yaa wonoo mo ba bii, ásɛ ba ɡe mo ya kwa.

english_verse: We have to do only one thing before they will agree to stay here and become one nation with us. Our men will have to be circumcised just like theirs.
translation_verse: Dɛ yaa ɛ waa baa kpɔ bil ya sie yaa, anee dɛ́ ɡel ba sɛh ya ne ba so. Anee kɛ yaa teŋe ya pena kɛ ban.

english_verse: Just think! We'll get their property, as well as their flocks and herds. All we have to do is to agree, and they will live here with us.
translation_verse: A ba ɡɛ naa, ba kondɛɛra ne komɛlbwa aa ya kwaa ɛa? Hé ɡel ya sɛh ásɛ ya ne ba so.”

english_verse: Every grown man followed this advice and got circumcised. Dinah's Brothers Take Revenge
translation_verse: Bwɛɛ la tena bwa sɛh waa Hamɔ ne o bie Sɛkem aa bola la ta, asɛ ba teŋni bwɛɛ la baala bwa pena.

english_verse: Three days later the men who had been circumcised were still weak from pain. So Simeon and Levi, two of Dinah's brothers, attacked with their swords and killed every man in the town,
translation_verse: Baa teŋni ba pena tɔpetooro wee a ta ɛɛ wee ba la, Jekɔb bibaala banɛ baa dɛ yer ba Simeon ne Lewi, ba ne Daena aa pɛ nya la iro kpɔ ba tokobie, asɛ dɛ piɡri bwɛɛ la tena dɛ jo ba bini dɛ kpoo ba baala te bwa.

english_verse: including Hamor and Shechem. Then they took Dinah and left.
translation_verse: Ba kpo Kooro Hamɔ ne o bie Sɛkem ɡe, dɛ lawɛ Daena le Sɛkem dem bela dɛ kpɔɔ kaa.

english_verse: Jacob's other sons came and took everything they wanted. All this was done because of the horrible thing that had happened to their sister.
translation_verse: Baa kpoo ba tonɛ la, Jekɔb bibaala baa kaa la jo bwɛɛ la bini dɛ pa ba komɛlbwa dɛ kpɔ tɔ ɡuɡra baa ɡuɡri ba nimambie dɛ lawɔ chɔ la wel.

english_verse: They took sheep, goats, donkeys, and everything else that was in the town or the countryside.
translation_verse: Ba larawe peera ne nae, keeɡore ne kwaa aa lɔ bwɛɛ la ta, dɛ ka pa ba kooni kwaa bwa ɡe,

english_verse: After taking everything of value from the houses, they dragged away the wives and children of their victims.
translation_verse: ne kondɔɔhkwaa te bwa ne haahna ne bechale, asɛ dɛ pa ba deene bini laala bwa dɛ chea kaa.

english_verse: Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, “Look what you've done! Now I'm in real trouble with the Canaanites and Perizzites who live around here. There aren't many of us, and if they attack, they'll kill everyone in my household.”
translation_verse: Asɛ Jekɔb ŋɔ Simeon ne Lewi be ŋɔ, “He nyin waa dɛ ba dawɛ n nɛ, dɛ ɡel dɔm ba chɔ n ne Keenan ne Pɛrɛs tena baa soɡe harɛ nɔ ta la baah ta. Yaa wola kanɛ nɔ, dɛ ɡɛ nɛra nɔ kaa pɛ nyoa ŋɔ bá ba yoo mɛ naa, amɔ dɛ ya bwaa dena dɛɛ ba hee laɔ.”

english_verse: They answered, “Was it right to let our own sister be treated that way?”
translation_verse: Anee ba chaŋe ŋɔ, “Yaa won so nyiŋi ba ɛ ya nimambie kɛŋɔ hanjwamane.”

english_verse: God told Jacob, “Return to Bethel, where I appeared to you when you were running from your brother Esau. Make your home there and build an altar for me.”
translation_verse: Anee Korowii ŋɔ Jekɔb be ŋɔ, “Ir kaa Bɛtel ásɛ dɛ ka so bela. Dɛ́ ɛ kon baa dɛ ɛ saraha o ta la tɛ men Korowii maa kpɔ n te baɡle ɡɛ saŋ haa chwaa dɛ le he dɔɔ Esɔ be la.”

english_verse: Jacob said to his family and to everyone else who was traveling with him: Get rid of your foreign gods! Then make yourselves acceptable to worship God and put on clean clothes.
translation_verse: Anomanta, Jekɔb ŋɔ o haahna ne o bii ne nɛra baa ja o nɛɛ la be ŋɔ, “Hé kpɔ harɛfala voɡa haa dɔa la bwa ta, dɛ́ sɔ he doŋa bɛlbwa ta, dɛ́ charɛ he laala.

english_verse: Afterwards, we'll go to Bethel. I will build an altar there for God, who answered my prayers when I was in trouble and who has always been at my side.
translation_verse: Ya dɛ ba bonɔ ira dɛ́ kaa Bɛtel ka so. Mɛɛ ɛ kon baa dɛ ɛ saraha o taa dɛɛ tɛ Korowii waa cha mɛ ɡɛ saŋ waa puu mɛ dɛ ja n nɛɛ bobɛlbwa maa laŋa la.”

english_verse: So everyone gave Jacob their idols and their earrings, and he buried them under the oak tree near Shechem.
translation_verse: Anomanta, ba pa ba voɡa aa lɔ ba be la bwa ne deŋna kwaa baa doa la tɛ Jekɔb. Asɛ o huɡe a ɡɛ laala la bwa dajen bɛl waa cheɡa bɛne bwɛjen Sɛkem la mun.

english_verse: While Jacob and his family were traveling through Canaan, God terrified the people in the towns so much that no one dared bother them.
translation_verse: Jekɔb ne o bii aa dɛ ba bela ira la, Korowii ɡelɔ ɔmee kohona chole nɛra baa lɔ bwɛɛre aa bɛne bela tena bwa nɛ ba ta wone ti ba dɛ ɛɛ ba wobɛlbwa.

english_verse: Jacob built an altar there and called it “God of Bethel,” because that was the place where God had appeared to him when he was running from Esau.
translation_verse: Asɛ dɛ ɛ kon baa dɛ ɛ saraha o ta tɛ Korowii bela, dɛ pa bela sɔn El Bɛtel. O munii Bɛtel Korowii. Dɛkalkɛ Korowii kpɔ o te baɡlo ŋwɛnɛ ta ɡɛ saŋ waa chwaa dɛɛ le o dɔɔ be la.

english_verse: While they were there, Rebekah's personal servant Deborah died. They buried her under an oak tree and called it “Weeping Oak.” God Blesses Jacob at Bethel
translation_verse: Dɛbora waa dɛɛ Rebɛka o bechale saŋ sewɔ, asɛ ba huɡo dajen bɛl mun Bɛtel. Anomanta, o pa bela sɔn Alɔn Bakut.

english_verse: I will give you the land that I promised Abraham and Isaac, and it will belong to your family forever.
translation_verse: Harɛ maa kpɔa baɡɛ he nabaa Abraham ne he mɛɛ Aesek nyoa la, he ne he naanar baa ka ba habɔɔ laanee mɛɛ ba kpɔe tɛ.”

english_verse: After God had gone,
translation_verse: Asɛ Korowii ɡelo bela dɛ kaa.

english_verse: Jacob set up a large rock, so that he would remember what had happened there. Then he poured wine and olive oil on the rock to show that it was dedicated to God,
translation_verse: Jekɔb kpɔ bwe bɛl pa bela dɛ kpɔ lii o ne Korowii waa baa ɛa, dɛ fuɡe sen ɛ saraha bwe la ta, dɛ berɛ fuɡe noo ɛ o ta tɛ Korowii.

english_verse: and he named the place Bethel. Benjamin Is Born
translation_verse: Dɛ pa bela sɔn Bɛtel. Rakɛl ne Aesek seo wa

english_verse: Jacob and his family had left Bethel and were still a long way from Ephrath, when the time came for Rachel's baby to be born.
translation_verse: Asɛ ba ir Bɛtel dɛ kaa. Baa dɛ kaa a ka tama ba tel bobɛl baa dɛ yerɛ bela Efrat la, loltea lɔ Rakɛl. Asɛ a do kpeɡri.

english_verse: She was having a rough time, but the woman who was helping her said, “Don't worry! It's a boy.”
translation_verse: O lola bini aa dɛ do kpeɡri la, haah waa dɛ lɛo lol la ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Bɛ ɔmɛ, bibaalee hɛɛ ba lola ja.”

english_verse: Rachel was at the point of death, and right before dying, she said, “I'll name him Benoni.” But Jacob called him Benjamin.
translation_verse: Dɛ Rakɛl dɛ ba sewa, anomanta, o pa bie la sɔn Bɛn Oni. Bɛn Oni munii n wenaale bie. Asɛ o mɛɛ ɡe pa o sɔn Bɛnjamen. Bɛnjamen munii n nɔndiɡ bie.

english_verse: Rachel was buried beside the road to Ephrath, which is also called Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Rakɛl aa sewa la, ba huɡo bwɛɛ Efrat la ŋwɛnɛ nyoa. Ba berɔ dɛɛ yerɔ Bɛtlɛham.

english_verse: Jacob set up a tombstone over her grave, and it is still there.
translation_verse: Jekɔb kpɔ bwe bɛl pa Rakɛl ŋwam la ta o ta do le ba le fini.

english_verse: Jacob, also known as Israel, traveled to the south of Eder Tower, where he set up camp.
translation_verse: Jekɔb berɔ ir dɛ ka baŋre o tɛnte dea bobɛl baa dɛ yerɛ bela Ida Dejaŋ bɛl baŋ.

english_verse: During their time there, Jacob's oldest son Reuben slept with Bilhah, who was one of Jacob's other wives. And Jacob found out about it. Jacob's Twelve Sons
translation_verse: Waa kaa so harɛ la ta la, Rubin kaa lawɛ tolo baa dɛ yerɔ Bilha baa lawa tɛ o mɛɛ o ɛ o sɛno la chɔ, asɛ Jekɔb no. Bii fi dɛ banɛɛ Jekɔb lolɛ.

english_verse: Jacob went to his father Isaac at Hebron, also called Mamre or Kiriath-Arba, where Isaac's father Abraham had lived as a foreigner.
translation_verse: Asɛ Jekɔb la o mɛɛ Aesek be Mamre, waa bɛne Hɛbrɔn bela Abraham ne Aesek fa aa soɡa ka la.

english_verse: Isaac died at the ripe old age of
translation_verse: mɔɔ dɛ sewɛ. Asɛ o bii Esɔ ne Jekɔb huɡo.

english_verse: Esau, also known as Edom, had many descendants.
translation_verse: Kenii Esɔ baa bera dɛɛ yerɔ Edom la bii ne o naanar waa do.

english_verse: He married three Canaanite women: The first was Adah, the daughter of Elon the Hittite; the second was Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah and the granddaughter of Zibeon the Hivite;
translation_verse: Esɔ mo haahna batoro baa ɛ Keenan tena. Bɛl sɔne Ada, o mɛɛ ɛ Hiti te baa yerɔ Ɛlɔn, hanɛɛte ɡe sɔne Oholibama, o mɛɛ sɔne Ana. O nabaa sɔne Sibeon o ɛ Hivi te.

english_verse: the third was Basemath, who was Ishmael's daughter and Nebaioth's sister.
translation_verse: O hantoorote sɔne Basemat, o mɛɛ sɔne Ismael, o nimambie sɔne Nɛbayɔt.

english_verse: Esau and his three wives had five sons while in Canaan. Adah's son was Eliphaz; Basemath's son was Reuel; Oholibamah's three sons were Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
translation_verse: Oholibama lolɛ bibaala batoro baa yer ba Jeyus ne Jalam dɛ Kora. Bii Esɔ aa lol ba Keenan harɛ ta laanee la.

english_verse: Esau took his children and wives, his relatives and servants, his animals and possessions he had acquired while in Canaan, and moved far from Jacob.
translation_verse: Esɔ kpɔ o haahna ne bibaala ne bihaahna, o dem tena bwa ne o kondɛɛra, ne komɛlbwa waa dɔa Keenan harɛ la ta bwa le o nime Jekɔb jwɛh dɛ kaa harɛfale bɛl ta ka so.

english_verse: He did this because the land was too crowded and could not support him and his brother with their flocks and herds.
translation_verse: Dɛkalkɛ dɛ harɛ o ne Jekɔb aa soɡe o ta la aa kanɛ tɛɛ ba. Ba dɔ kondɛɛra asɛ a ya, anomanta, dɛ a chɛ kɛ bɛlbwa nyin bofale dɛ́ ka so o kwaa ne.

english_verse: That's why Esau made his home in the hill country of Seir.
translation_verse: Asɛ Esɔ ka so Edom harɛ ta deŋɡarere ta.

english_verse: Esau and Adah's oldest son was Eliphaz, and the clans that descended from him were Teman, Omar, Zepho, Kenaz,
translation_verse: Gɛ nɛra nɔ aa teŋa nɔ ɛ koranar Esɔ naanar bini. Esɔ biloɡle Elifas bibaala waa lol ba laanee, Teman ne Omar ne Sefo dɛ Kenas,

english_verse: Korah, Gatam, and Amalek. These and Esau's other descendants lived in the land of Edom.
translation_verse: ne Kora ne Gatam dɛ Amalɛk. Banɔɔ ɛ Elifas naanar dɛ ɛ koranar dɛ so Edom. Ba berɔ ɛ Ada ɡe naanar.

english_verse: The clans that descended from Esau and Basemath's son Reuel were Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah.
translation_verse: Esɔ bibaa Ruwɛl bibaala waa lol ba laanee, Nahat ne Sɛra ne Samaa dɛ Misa. Banɔɔ ɛ Esɔ haah Basemat naanar dɛ ɛ koranar dɛ so Edom.

english_verse: The clans that descended from Esau and Oholibamah the daughter of Anah were Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
translation_verse: Esɔ haah Oholibama bibaala waa lol ba laanee, Jeyus ne Jalam dɛ Kora. Banɔɔ ɛ Esɔ haah Oholibama naanar dɛ ɛ koranar. Oholibama nya sɔne Ana.

english_verse: All of these clans descended from Esau, who was known as Edom.
translation_verse: Dɛ a ɡɛ nɛra nɔ bwa ɛ Esɔ bibaala, dɛ bwa ɛ koranar.

english_verse: Seir was from the Horite tribe that had lived in Edom before the time of Esau. The clans that had descended from him were Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,
translation_verse: Sɛɛ waa ɛ Hɔr te bibaala waa lol ba asɛ ba so Edom laanee, Lotan ne Sobal ne Sibeon dɛ Ana,

english_verse: Lotan's sons were Hori and Heman; his sister was Timna.
translation_verse: Lotan ɡe bibaalaa, Hɔr ne Homam. Dɛ Lotan nimambie sɔne Timna.

english_verse: Shobal's sons were Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, and Onam.
translation_verse: Sobal ɡe bibaalaa, Alvan ne Manahat ne Ebal ne Sɛfo dɛ Onam.

english_verse: Zibeon's sons were Aiah and Anah—the same Anah who found an oasis in the desert while taking the donkeys of his father out to pasture.
translation_verse: Sibeon ɡe bibaalaa, Aeya ne Ana. A ɡɛ Ana nɔ kaa na newɔb a bule dɛɛ le pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta, ɡɛ saŋ dɛ o dɛ nyiŋi o mɛɛ Sibeon keeɡore ta.

english_verse: Dishon's sons were Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.
translation_verse: Dison ɡe ir dɛ lolɛ, o bibaalaa, Hɛmdan ne Ɛsban ne Itran dɛ Keran.

english_verse: Ezer's sons were Bilhan, Zaavan, and Akan.
translation_verse: Asɛ Esa ɡe bibaalaa, Bilhan ne Saavan dɛ Akan.

english_verse: Dishan's sons were Uz and Aran.
translation_verse: Disan ɡe ir dɛ lolɛ, bibaalaa nɔ, Us ne Aran.

english_verse: The clans of the Horites were Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,
translation_verse: Hɔr tena koranaree, Lotan ne Sobal ne Sibeon dɛ Ana,

english_verse: Before there were kings in Israel, the following kings ruled Edom one after another: Bela son of Beor from Dinhabah; Jobab son of Zerah from Bozrah; Husham from the land of Teman; Hadad son of Bedad from Avith ; Samlah from Masrekah; Shaul from the city of Rehoboth on the Euphrates River; Baalhanan son of Achbor; Hadar from the city of Pau .
translation_verse: Kooro Baal Hanan ɡe aa baa sewɛ la, Hadad chiɡ o naa ta, dɛ di kora. Dɛ o bwɛjen sɔne Pau. O haah ɡe sɔne Mɛhetabɛl, o ɛ Matrɛd bihaah. Matrɛd ɡe nya sɔne Mɛsahab.

english_verse: The clans that descended from Esau took their names from their families and the places where they lived. They are Timna, Alvah, Jetheth,
translation_verse: Gɛɛ koranar baa le Esɔ be pera ɡe waa do. Ba sɔna ne ba deene ta ne ɡɛ baa soɡaa nɔ. Timna ne Alva dɛ Jetɛt,

english_verse: Oholibamah, Elah, Pinon,
translation_verse: ne Oholibama ne Ɛla dɛ Penɔn

english_verse: Kenaz, Teman, Mibzar,
translation_verse: ne Kenas ne Teman dɛ Mibsar

english_verse: Magdiel, and Iram. These clans descended from Esau, who was known as Edom, the father of the Edomites. They took their names from the places where they settled.
translation_verse: ne Maɡdiel dɛ Iram. Banee di kora Edom. Gɛ baa sosoɡa ba harɛre ta ne ɡɛ bɛlbwa wobol baa dɛ bol laanee la. Esɔ ɛ ba bwa naa.

english_verse: Jacob lived in the land of Canaan, where his father Isaac had lived,
translation_verse: Jekɔb soɡe Keenan harɛ ta, bela o mɛɛ fa aa soɡa la.

english_verse: “They're not here anymore,” the man replied. “I overheard them say they were going to Dothan.” Joseph left and found his brothers in Dothan.
translation_verse: Baa la chaŋo ŋɔ, “Ba le bonɔ. N noɔ kɛŋɔ baa dɛ bol dɔŋa be ŋɔ ba kaa Dotan.” Anomanta, o ti o dɔɔranar la dɛ ka na ba Dotan bela.

english_verse: Jacob loved Joseph more than he did any of his other sons, because Joseph was born when Jacob was very old. Jacob had even given Joseph a fancy coat
translation_verse: Dɛ Josef ɛ Jekɔb banjenbie, anomanta, dɛ o dɛ nyin o waa ɡwaa o bii la bwa. Asɛ o nyarɛ batakaarejaŋ ondɛɛɡe bɛl baa di ɡwini dawɛ o ta tɛo.

english_verse: which showed that Joseph was his favorite son, and so Joseph's brothers hated him and would not be friendly to him.
translation_verse: O dɔɔranar aa baa na kɛŋɔ o mɛɛ dɛ nyin o waa dɛ ɡwaa ba la, ba haoh, baa on sie tɛ kwaraa.

english_verse: One day, Joseph told his brothers what he had dreamed, and they hated him even more.
translation_verse: Awola jwaana bɛl Jekɔb deero dɛ taa baɡle o dɔɔranar. A taa ba haoh kohona kwara.

english_verse: Joseph said, “Let me tell you about my dream.
translation_verse: O ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, “Hé cheɡ deŋne dɛ́ no n deera nɔ.

english_verse: We were out in the field, tying up bundles of wheat. Suddenly my bundle stood up, and your bundles gathered around and bowed down to it.”
translation_verse: Ya dɛ vɔwɛ jaaɡe koo ta, asɛ bɛlbwa bil o kwaa dɛɛ korɛ. Belaa n kwaa maa vɔwa la ir che, asɛ he kwaa la ba bar n kwaa la cheme dɛɛ ɡuŋa.”

english_verse: His brothers asked, “Do you really think you are going to be king and rule over us?” Now they hated Joseph more than ever because of what he had said about his dream.
translation_verse: Asɛ o dɔɔranar la bɔɔro ŋɔ, “Amɔ he dɛ lii kɛ he dɛ ba bá di kora dɛ́ nyiŋi ya nɛɛ kɛɛ?” Belaa o haeh la berɛ ɡwaa kohona kwara.

english_verse: Joseph later had another dream, and he told his brothers, “Listen to what else I dreamed. The sun, the moon, and eleven stars bowed down to me.”
translation_verse: O berɔ dee anfala ja dɛ taa baɡle o dɔɔranar la ŋɔ, “Hé no, n deero asɛ wee ne korobie dɛ weweela fi dɛ beŋkpoŋ ɛɛ ɡuŋ mɛ.”

english_verse: When he told his father about this dream, his father became angry and said, “What's that supposed to mean? Are your mother and I and your brothers all going to come and bow down to you?”
translation_verse: Josef aa taa ɡɛ waa nɔ o mɛɛ ne o dɔɔranar be la, o mɛɛ kaoh dɛ ŋɔ, “Bɔkwa ɡe deeraa do ken? Amɔ n ne he nya ne he dɔɔranar ɛɛ bao dɛ́ ba ɡuŋi kɛɛ?”

english_verse: Joseph's brothers were jealous of him, but his father kept wondering about the dream. Joseph Is Sold and Taken to Egypt
translation_verse: Ate, o dɔɔranar la bwaawee ir o nɛɛ kɛrɛdɛ, kɛ o mɛɛ te kpɔ waa la do o nyu bini. Josef dɔɔranar yoɡu

english_verse: One day when Joseph's brothers had taken the sheep to a pasture near Shechem,
translation_verse: Awola bɛl, o dɔɔranar la kpɔ o mɛɛ kondɛɛra la kaa dibɔr Sɛkem pera,

english_verse: his father Jacob said to him, “I want you to go to your brothers. They are with the sheep near Shechem.” “Yes, sir,” Joseph answered.
translation_verse: asɛ Jekɔb ŋɔ Josef be ŋɔ, “He dɔɔranar kpɔ kondɛɛra kaa dibɔr Sɛkem pera, n dɛ́ tomɛ ba be.” Asɛ o chaŋe ŋɔ, “N mɛɛ, mɛɛ lao.”

english_verse: His father said, “Go and find out how your brothers and the sheep are doing. Then come back and let me know.” So he sent him from Hebron Valley. Joseph was near Shechem
translation_verse: O mɛɛ ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “La dɛ́ ka na he dɔɔranar ne ɡɛ kondɛɛra la aa doa, ásɛ dɛ ba bol n be.” O tomɔ le Hɛbrɔn Fɛlembɔjen bɔr pera dɛ kaa Sɛkem.

english_verse: Joseph answered, “I'm looking for my brothers who are watching the sheep. Can you tell me where they are?”
translation_verse: Asɛ o chaŋo ŋɔ, “N dɔɔranar ne ba kondɛɛra bɔree mɛɛ ɡaaɡe. N poori, hɛɛ won chaɡ mɛ bela baa lole naa?”

english_verse: But before he got there, they saw him coming and made plans to kill him.
translation_verse: Waa dɛ tel bela la, o dɔɔranar la te tɔ sie nao kɛŋɔ o taa lɔ bojaŋ. O ne bela tela la, dɛ ba te vɔrɔwɔ tonɛ kɛŋɔ ba kpoo.

english_verse: They said to one another, “Look, here comes the hero of those dreams!
translation_verse: Ba ŋɔ dɔŋa be ŋɔ, “Deera te laanee ka dɛ ba la.

english_verse: Reuben heard this and tried to protect Joseph from them. “Let's not kill him,” he said.
translation_verse: Rubin takapɔ kɛŋɔ o fee lɛo ta, dɛ ŋɔ, “He bɛ ɡel ya kpoo.”

english_verse: “Don't murder him or even harm him. Just throw him into a well out here in the desert.” Reuben planned to rescue Joseph later and take him back to his father.
translation_verse: Dɛ berɛ ŋɔ, “He bɛ on kpo. Hé kpɔɔ ta kɔlɔŋ nɔ bɛl bini.” Gɛ aa ɛ o won lɛo le ba nɔn ta, dɛ́ kpɔɔ ka tɛ ba mɛɛ la waa o bol ɡɛ.

english_verse: When Joseph came to his brothers, they pulled off his fancy coat
translation_verse: Josef aa tel o dɔɔranar la be la, ba laa o batakaarejaŋ ondɛɛɡe baa di ɡwini dawɛ o ta la wur,

english_verse: and threw him into a dry well.
translation_verse: dɛ kpɔɔ ka ta kɔlɔŋ la bini. Dɛ nee bɛlbwa toole o bini.

english_verse: As Joseph's brothers sat down to eat, they looked up and saw a caravan of Ishmaelites coming from Gilead. Their camels were loaded with all kinds of spices that they were taking to Egypt.
translation_verse: Ba soɡo dɛɛ di kwa, belaa ba ha sie nyiŋi, dɛ na Ismael bonadiire ne ba nyoɡmare aa cheɡɛ konsɔɔhsoma baa dɛ fuah, ne dapɛɡa ane baa dɛ ɛ ane tɛɛɡa, ne korobo le Gelead harɛ baa kaa Ijipt harɛ.

english_verse: So Judah said, “What will we gain if we kill our brother and hide his body?
translation_verse: Anee Juda ŋɔ o bala la be ŋɔ, “Dɛ ya kpo ya nime nɔ dɛ tɔ a ta naa, bɔkwa tɔnɔɔ yaa ba dɔe yɔ?

english_verse: Let's sell him to the Ishmaelites and not harm him. After all, he is our brother.” And the others agreed.
translation_verse: Hé ɡel ya yoɡu tɛ Ismael tena nɔ dɛ bɛ o haakɛ lɛ, o ɛ ya nime, ya bini bɛlee.” Asɛ ba sɛh ɡɛ waa bola la ta.

english_verse: When the Midianite merchants came by, Joseph's brothers took him out of the well, and for
translation_verse: Bonadiire la aa tel ba be la, o dɔɔranar la lawɔ le kɔlɔŋ la bini, dɛ yoɡu tɛɛ ba suuɡapoŋa fifraanɛ, asɛ ba kpɔɔ kaa Ijipt harɛ ta.

english_verse: When Reuben returned to the well and did not find Joseph there, he tore his clothes in sorrow.
translation_verse: Rubin aa bera la kɔlɔŋ la ta dɛ ka na kɛŋɔ o toole bela la, asɛ o laa o batakaare kɛɛ, a baɡle kɛŋɔ o loo kuu.

english_verse: Then he went back to his brothers and said, “The boy is gone! What am I going to do?”
translation_verse: O berɔ ba o bala la be dɛ ba ŋɔ, “N nime la toole bela! Ɛrɛɛ mɛɛ ba ɛɛ yɔ?”

english_verse: Joseph's brothers killed a goat and dipped Joseph's fancy coat in its blood.
translation_verse: Anee ba kpo booh la bɛl, dɛ kpɔ Josef batakaare la mili o chal la,

english_verse: After this, they took the coat to their father and said, “We found this! Look at it carefully and see if it belongs to your son.”
translation_verse: asɛ dɛ kpɔ ka chaɡle ba mɛɛ dɛ ŋɔ, “Batakaare nɔɔ ya na, nyiŋi na kɛŋɔ he bie la kon laanee kɛɛ?”

english_verse: Jacob knew it was Joseph's coat and said, “It's my son's coat! Joseph has been torn to pieces and eaten by some wild animal.”
translation_verse: Waa nyiŋa na la, o jemɔ asɛ dɛ chaŋe ŋɔ, “N bie batakaaree kpela! Olchɔɡe bɛl lawɔ chwe, o ka toɡri o bini.”

english_verse: Jacob mourned for Joseph a long time, and to show his sorrow he tore his clothes and wore sackcloth.
translation_verse: Belaa Jekɔb loo ku o laa o batakaare kɛɛ, dɛ kpɔ lweyal tɔ dɛ ɛ o bie la lwe dɛ la sie.

english_verse: All of Jacob's children came to comfort him, but he refused to be comforted. “No,” he said, “I will go to my grave, mourning for my son.” So Jacob kept on grieving.
translation_verse: Asɛ o bii ne o lolanar bwa ba dɛ ba larawe o bwara. Kɛ o ta larawa la noɛ dɛ ŋɔ, “N wii nɔɔ dɛ́ kpɔ mɛ kaa n bie be lalabwɛ.” Anomanta, o wi o bie la kɛrɛdɛ.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the Midianites had sold Joseph in Egypt to a man named Potiphar, who was the king's official in charge of the palace guard.
translation_verse: Ismael bonadiire la ɡe yoɡ Josef tɛ Ijipt te Pɔtefa. O ɛ Ijipt harɛ ta kooro laa tena baa dɛ daah o dem la bwa nomoa.

english_verse: About that time Judah left his brothers in the hill country and went to live near his friend Hirah in the town of Adullam.
translation_verse: A ɡɛ saŋ la, Juda ɡel o bala la, dɛ ka so Hira be, bwɛɛ Adulam ta.

english_verse: While there he met the daughter of Shua, a Canaanite man. Judah married her,
translation_verse: Waa kaa so bela la, o na bihaah bɛl dɛ moo, o mɛɛ ɛ Keenan te baa yerɔ Sua.

english_verse: and they had three sons. He named the first one Er;
translation_verse: Juda ne haah la kpoŋe tea dɛ lolɛ bibaa baa yerɔ Ɛr.

english_verse: The third one was born when Judah was in Chezib, and she named him Shelah.
translation_verse: O berɔ lolɛ bibaa ja, asɛ dɛ pa o sɔn Seela. Gɛ saŋ baa lolɔ la, dɛ ba soɡe bwɛɛ bɛl baa dɛ yerɔ Kesib.

english_verse: Later, Judah chose Tamar as a wife for Er, his oldest son.
translation_verse: Baa lɔ bela la, Juda mo haah tɛ o binomoa Ɛr. Haah la sɔne Taama.

english_verse: But Er was very evil, and the Lord took his life.
translation_verse: Dɛ Ɛr ɛ wechɔɡ-ɛɛ Korowii be, asɛ Korowii kpoo.

english_verse: So Judah told Onan, “It's your duty to marry Tamar and have a child for your brother.”
translation_verse: Anee Juda ŋɔ Onan be ŋɔ, “Kpɔ he dɔɔ haah mo, dɛ́ lolɛ bii tɛo o mun bɛ he.”

english_verse: Onan knew the child would not be his, and when he had sex with Tamar, he made sure that she would not get pregnant.
translation_verse: Dɛ Onan jemɔ kɛŋɔ a ɡɛ bii la aa won ɛ o kwa, anomanta, o ne haah la chɔɔ waa, o bane aa dɛ ba la, ɡɛɛ o ɡel a ba ta harɛ, ásɛ o bɛ won kpoŋe tea, dɛ́ lolɛ bii ba ɛ o dɔɔ kwa.

english_verse: The Lord wasn't pleased with Onan and took his life too.
translation_verse: Korowii be la, dɛ a ɡɛ liire nɔ ɛ wechɔɡa, asɛ dɛ kpo o ɡe.

english_verse: Judah did not want the same thing to happen to his son Shelah, and he told Tamar, “Go home to your father and live there as a widow until my son Shelah is grown.” So Tamar went to live with her father.
translation_verse: Belaa Juda ŋɔ o hela Taama be ŋɔ, “Kaa ka so doŋa ta he mɛɛ dem, dɛ́ ka tel kɛŋɔ n bie Seela aa baa kpeɡ.” O liiro kɛŋɔ o ɡe ken ɛɛ ba sewɔɔ kɛŋɔ o dɔɔranar. Asɛ haah la kaa o mɛɛ dem dɛ ka so.

english_verse: Some years later Judah's wife died, and he mourned for her. He then went with his friend Hirah to the town of Timnah, where his sheep were being sheared.
translation_verse: Aa baa la sie la, Juda haah sewɔ. Waa baa dɔ bolarawa tonɛ la, o ne o dam Hira waa le Adulam la Temna, bela baa dɛ fonɛ o peera pona.

english_verse: Tamar found out that her father-in-law Judah was going to Timnah to shear his sheep.
translation_verse: Belaa nomɛl ŋɔ Taama be ŋɔ, “He helabaa dɛ ba ba kaa Temna dɛ ka fonɛ o peera pona.”

english_verse: She also realized that Shelah was now a grown man, but she had not been allowed to marry him. So she decided to dress in something other than her widow's clothes and to cover her face with a veil. After this, she sat outside the town of Enaim on the road to Timnah.
translation_verse: Asɛ o foo o laala waa doa so doŋa ta la bil, dɛ kpɔ kon waa chaahna bɔle nyu, dɛ ka so bwɛɛ Enaem doonyoa, Temna ŋwɛnɛ ta. Dɛkalkɛ dɛ o nao kɛŋɔ Seela kpeɡo, asɛ ba ɡe ta on kpɔe tɛo ŋɔ o yalɔ.

english_verse: When Judah came along, he did not recognize her because of the veil. He thought she was a prostitute
translation_verse: Juda aa fɛra baa kaa Timna la, o nao kɛŋɔ waa kpɔ kon bɔle o nyu dɛ so, dɛ liiru hanjwamane bɛl.

english_verse: “One of my young goats,” he answered. “What will you give me to keep until you send the goat?” she asked.
translation_verse: Asɛ Juda ŋɔ, “Mɛɛ ɡeloo ba lawɛ bombie ba tɛɛ.” Anee haah la ŋɔ, “Bɔkwaa hɛɛ ba kpɔe tɛ mɛ ń cheɡ ka tel saŋ haa ba o ne nɔ?”

english_verse: “What do you want?” he asked in return. “The ring on that cord around your neck,” was her reply. “I also want the special walking stick you have with you.” He gave them to her, they slept together, and she became pregnant.
translation_verse: Anee Juda ɡe bɔɔro ŋɔ, “Bɔkwa konee hɛɛ nyin kɛŋɔ n kpɔ tɛɛ he cheɡ ɔ?” O ŋɔ, “He noniseɡ he sɔn aa dawɛ o ta ne he daŋɡbala.” Ate, o kpɔa tɛo mɔɔ o ne o ta chɔ, asɛ o kpoŋe tea.

english_verse: After returning home, Tamar took off the veil and dressed in her widow's clothes again.
translation_verse: Baa chɔa tonɛ la, haah la iro dɛ ka laa kon waa kpɔa bɔle o nyu la kpɔ bil, dɛ kpɔ laala waa kpɔa so doŋa ta la do.

english_verse: Judah asked his friend Hirah take a goat to the woman, so he could get back the ring and walking stick, but she wasn't there.
translation_verse: Juda aa kaala la, o kaa kpɔ bombie la tomɛ o dam Hira waa ɛ Adulam te la ŋɔ, ó kpɔ ba tɛ haah la dɛ́ lɛ kwaa waa kpɔa tɛo o cheɡ la ba. Waa laŋa la, o ta haah la ka pue bela.

english_verse: Hirah asked the people of Enaim, “Where is the prostitute who sat along the road outside your town?” “There's never been one here,” they answered.
translation_verse: O kaa pu baala bane bela asɛ dɛ bɔɔ ba ŋɔ, “Leperaa hanjwamane bɛl o fa aa soɡe Enaem doonyoa bonɔ la dɔɔ?” Asɛ ba chaŋo ŋɔ, “Hanjwamane bɛlbwa toole bonɔ.”

english_verse: Hirah went back and told Judah, “I couldn't find the woman, and the people of Enaim said no prostitute had ever been there.”
translation_verse: Asɛ o berɛ la Juda be dɛ ka ŋɔ, “Maa laŋa la, n ta on nae, asɛ dɛ bɔɔ baala bane baa lɔ bela o wa, ba ɡe ŋɔ hanjwamane bɛlbwa toole bela.”

english_verse: “If you couldn't find her, we'll just let her keep the things I gave her,” Judah answered. “And we'd better forget about the goat, or else we'll look like fools.”
translation_verse: Belaa Juda chaŋe ŋɔ, “Gel laala la do o be. Ya bɛ a waa ta teŋɛ nɛra ba na dɛ mamɛ yaa. N lawɛ bombie tɛɛ ŋɔ he ka tɛo he ta on pue yaa, anee ɡɛ.”

english_verse: About three months later someone told Judah, “Your daughter-in-law Tamar has behaved like a prostitute, and now she's pregnant!” “Drag her out of town and burn her to death!” Judah shouted.
translation_verse: Dɛ ɛ korobie atoro habɔɔ nomɛl ba ŋɔ Juda be ŋɔ, “He helahaah kaa bɔ jwamane dɛ kpoŋe tea.” Belaa o ŋɔ, “He lawɔ le dɛ́ ka fuuh!”

english_verse: As Tamar was being dragged off, she sent someone to tell her father-in-law, “The man who gave me this ring, this cord, and this walking stick is the one who got me pregnant.”
translation_verse: Baa lawɔ dɛɛ le la, anee o ŋɔ bá ka ŋɔ o helabaa Juda be ŋɔ, “Naate waa dɔ a ɡɛ noniseɡ ne daŋɡbala nɔ laanee do mɛ tea la.” Dɛ berɛ ŋɔ ba nyiŋi kwaa la dɛ́ na naate aa ɛ o kwa.

english_verse: “Those are mine!” Judah admitted. “She's a better person than I am, because I broke my promise to let her marry my son Shelah.” After this, Judah never slept with her again.
translation_verse: Juda ɡe nao kɛŋɔ onee, asɛ dɛ ŋɔ, “Haah la waa toɡrɔ ɡwaa mɛ. N na n wechɔɡa maa ɛa kɛŋɔ maa wola ɡelɛ o yalɛ n bibaa Seela la.” A habɔɔ la, o ta o be laŋɛ kpa.

english_verse: Tamar later gave birth to twins. But before either of them was born, one of them stuck a hand out of her womb. The woman who was helping tied a red thread around the baby's hand and explained, “This one came out first.”
translation_verse: Waa dɛ ba lola la, bii la bɛl tɔ sie kpɔ o nɔn le, asɛ haah waa dɛ lɛo lol la kpɔ jiseswɛm vɔwɛ o nɔn la ta dɛ ŋɔ “Onɔɔ tɔ sie.”

english_verse: At once his hand went back in, and the other child was born first. The woman then said, “What an opening you've made for yourself!” So they named the baby Perez.
translation_verse: Waa kpɔ jiseswɛm la vɔwɛ o nɔn tonɛ la, bie la berɔ kpɔ jo, asɛ nɛɛte la berɛ tɔ sie ba. Asɛ haah waa dɛ lɛo lol la ŋɔ, “Amɔ ŋwɛnɛ haa kpɔ o ta dɛ ba laanee nɔ kenɛ?” Asɛ o pa o sɔn Pɛrɛs.

english_verse: When the brother with the red thread was born, they named him Zerah.
translation_verse: Dɛ berɛ lolɛ onɔ la jiseswɛm aa vɔwɛ o nɔn la. Asɛ ba pa o sɔn Sɛra.

english_verse: The Ishmaelites took Joseph to Egypt and sold him to Potiphar, the king's official in charge of the palace guard.
translation_verse: Ismael tena la kpɔ Josef kaa Ijipt, dɛ ka yoɡu tɛ Pɔtefa waa ɛ Ijipt kooro nɛra baa dɛ daahno la nomonome la bɛl.

english_verse: So Joseph lived in the home of Potiphar, his Egyptian owner. Soon Potiphar realized that the Lord was helping Joseph to be successful in whatever he did.
translation_verse: O nomoa la ɡe nao kɛŋɔ Korowii teŋɛ o nɛ dɛ ɡel o wobɛlbwa do wer tɛo.

english_verse: Potiphar liked Joseph and made him his personal assistant, putting him in charge of his house and all of his property.
translation_verse: Anomanta, Pɔtefa sie lɛ o nɛ asɛ dɛ kpɔɔ ɛ o bonɔɔ, dɛ ɡel wɛɛ nyiŋi o dem ne o komɛlbwa waa dɔa ta.

english_verse: Potiphar left everything up to Joseph, and with Joseph there, the only decision he had to make was what he wanted to eat. Joseph was well-built and handsome,
translation_verse: Pɔtefa kpɔ komɛlbwa do o nɔn ta dɛ laa liire kpɔ a ta. Kwaa waa dɛ lii a waa kondikwa waa di ɡbo. Dɛ Josef mao kɛrɛdɛ dɛ do wer bonɔɔ ɡe.

english_verse: and Potiphar's wife soon noticed him. She asked him to make love to her,
translation_verse: Aa ba dɛ la sie la, Pɔtefa haah pɛla lawɛ Josef dɛ ŋɔ o ne o chɔ.

english_verse: but he refused and said, “My master isn't worried about anything in his house, because he has placed me in charge of everything he owns.
translation_verse: Kɛ Josef ta sɛɛh, asɛ dɛ ŋɔ o nomoa haah la be ŋɔ, “N dɔɔ aa dɛ yarada mɛ kohona nomanta, o kpɔ komɛlbwa waa lɔ o dem bonɔ, ne o komɛlbwa waa dɔa do n nɔn ta, waa wola a waa lii kpa.

english_verse: No one in my master's house is more important than I am. The only thing he hasn't given me is you, and that's because you are his wife. I won't sin against God by doing such a terrible thing as this.”
translation_verse: Nomɛlbwa toole dɛ dɔ kpeɡri n nɛɛ dem bonɔ nemenɛ on. O ta komɛlbwa ɡe waa lɔ dem bonɔ kpɔe sɔɔh mɛ, nemenɛ he ɡbosoroo dɛkalkɛ o haahnee hen. Ɛrɛɛ mɛɛ ba wona ɛ a ɡɛ wechɔɡa nɔ dɔŋa dɛ́ jo Korowii nɛɔ?”

english_verse: She kept begging Joseph day after day, but he refused to do what she wanted or even to go near her.
translation_verse: Dɛ tɔperee bwaa o swe dɛɛ marɛ Josef nɛɛ ŋɔ o ne o chɔ asɛ o yon vɛh, hale waa o jwɛɛh kwaraa la.

english_verse: One day, Joseph went to Potiphar's house to do his work, and none of the other servants were there.
translation_verse: Awola bɛl, Josef lɔ dem bela dɛɛ ɛ o toma. Dɛ dem bela bonɔɔna la bɛlbwa toole.

english_verse: Potiphar's wife grabbed hold of his coat and said, “Make love to me!” Joseph ran out of the house, leaving his coat there in her hands.
translation_verse: Belaa haah la ta lawɛ o yal kpoŋe dɛ ŋɔ, “Gel n ne he chɔ.” O ta sɛɛh, dɛ yo lɛ o te dɛ chwa le buse, asɛ a ka o yal la do haah la nɔn ta.

english_verse: she called in her servants and said, “Look! This Hebrew has come just to make fools of us. He tried to rape me, but I screamed for help.
translation_verse: o yerɛ bonɔɔna baa lɔ dem bela la dɛ ŋɔ, “Hé no waa nɔ. Hibru te nɔ n jaa aa kaa lawɛ ba dem bonɔ nɔ dɛ ɛ yaa sisawa. O baa jo n be dea ŋɔ o fee paɡ mɛ, asɛ n do lɔŋɔ kohona.

english_verse: And when he heard me scream, he ran out of the house, leaving his coat with me.”
translation_verse: Maa dɛ dooɡe lɔŋɔre ɡɛ la, o chwao le a ka o yal chɔ n jwɛh.”

english_verse: Potiphar's wife kept Joseph's coat until her husband came home.
translation_verse: Haah la kpɔ yal la cheɡ, dɛ ka tel kɛŋɔ Pɔtefa aa bala.

english_verse: But when I screamed for help, he left his coat and ran out of the house.”
translation_verse: Kɛ maa do lɔŋɔ la, o chwao le buse warane dɛ ɡel o yal.”

english_verse: Potiphar became very angry
translation_verse: Pɔtefa aa no ɡɛ la, o baah diu

english_verse: and threw Joseph in the same prison where the king's prisoners were kept. While Joseph was in prison,
translation_verse: dɛ ɡel ba ka lawɛ Josef ba do dea, bela kooro aa lawɛ nɛra dɛɛ do la, asɛ o chɔ bela.

english_verse: the Lord helped him and was good to him. He even made the jailer like Joseph so much that
translation_verse: Kɛ Korowii teŋɛ o nɛ, dɛ tɛo jirima dɛ ɛo kɛrɛdɛ, dɛ ɡel nomoa waa dɛ nyiŋi ba nɛɛ dea bela la sie lɛ o nɛ.

english_verse: he put him in charge of the other prisoners and of everything that was done in the jail.
translation_verse: Anomanta, o kpɔɔ ɛ o bala baa do ba dea la bwa nomoa, asɛ wɛɛ nyiŋi ba wobɛlbwa baa dɛ ɛa bela ta.

english_verse: The jailer did not worry about anything, because the Lord was with Joseph and made him successful in all that he did.
translation_verse: Korowii aa dɛ nyin Josef waa dɛɛ nyin kɛ o wobɛlbwa do wer tɛo la nomanta, o ɡelɔ nomoa waa dɛ nyiŋi ba nɛɛ la laa o sie kpɔ waa Josef aa chɔ a nyoa la ta.

english_verse: While Joseph was in prison, both the king's personal servant and his chief cook made the king angry. So he had them thrown into the same prison with Joseph.
translation_verse: asɛ dɛ laɡ ba do dea. Nomoa waa chɔ nɛra baa dɛ daah kooro dem la, o deemii o kpɔ ba do. A ɡɛ dea la binii ba lawɛ Josef ɡe do.

english_verse: They spent a long time in prison, and the official in charge of the palace guard, made Joseph their servant.
translation_verse: Ba chɔ bela biɡri, asɛ nomoa la kpɔ wobɛlbwa do Josef nɔn ta wɛɛ nyiŋi ba nɛ.

english_verse: One night each of the two men had a dream, but their dreams had different meanings.
translation_verse: Jwaana bɛl baa chɔ dea la bini la, kooro nomonome la deero. Bɛlbwa deera waa deera la ɡe korɔ.

english_verse: The next morning, when Joseph went to see the men, he could tell they were upset,
translation_verse: Tɔ aa pera chɔɔ la Josef ba ba be, waa baa na ba la, o nao kɛŋɔ ba liire chɔɡɔ.

english_verse: and he asked, “Why are you so worried today?”
translation_verse: Asɛ o bɔɔ ba ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ he so sum ne ɡɛ nɔɔ?”

english_verse: “We each had a dream last night,” they answered, “and there is no one to tell us what they mean.” Joseph replied, “Doesn't God know the meaning of dreams? Now tell me what you dreamed.”
translation_verse: Anee ba chaŋe ŋɔ, “Ya deero, kɛ bɛlbwa deera waa deera la ɡe korɔ, ya ta nomɛlbwa dɔe ó baɡle yaa a mun bonɔ yaa lole nɔ.” Ate Josef ŋɔ, “Korowiirii dɛɛ tɛ nɛn wejema ó won baɡle nɛn deera mun. Hé baɡle ásɛ n no.”

english_verse: with three branches. As soon as it budded, it blossomed, and its grapes became ripe.
translation_verse: asɛ kpala atoro do o ta. Waa moɡɛ papooni la, dɛ fee ɡe deno do a ta. Dɛ nɔna ba a ta a den be ɡe.

english_verse: I held the king's cup and squeezed the grapes into it, then I gave the cup to the king.”
translation_verse: Dɛ n kpoŋe kooro numol dɛ harame daa la nɔna nee dɛɛ do o bini dɛ́ kpɔ tɛo.”

english_verse: Joseph said: This is the meaning of your dream. The three branches stand for three days,
translation_verse: Anee Josef ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Kenii he deera la mun ɛɛ baɡle. Daa kpala atoro la cheɡɔɔ tɛ tɔpera atoro.

english_verse: and in three days the king will pardon you. He will make you his personal servant again, and you will serve him his wine, just as you used to do.
translation_verse: Tɔpetooro wee la, kooro ɛɛ lee dɛ́ berɛ kaa he ne he tombena ta. Ásɛ he kpɔ kooro numol do o nɔn ta kɛŋɔ he fa aa dɛ doo sen la.

english_verse: But when these good things happen, please don't forget to tell the king about me, so I can get out of this place.
translation_verse: Kɛ dɛ wobɛlbwa ba dɛ kaa kɛrɛdɛ dɛɛ tɛɛ naa, lii n wa. Berɛ takapɔ na n sum, dɛ́ bol n waa baɡle kooro, ásɛ o lee mɛ dea maa chɔa nɔ.

english_verse: I was kidnapped from the land of the Hebrews, and here in Egypt I haven't done anything to deserve being thrown in jail.
translation_verse: Kpeɡri nee ba kpɔ mɛ le Hibru tena harɛ ta, dɛ ba n ne Ijipt bonɔ. Maa lɔ bonɔ ɡe nɔ, n ta waa maa ɛa a chɛ kɛ ba do mɛ dea nae.”

english_verse: When the chief cook saw that Joseph had given a good meaning to the dream, he told Joseph, “I also had a dream. In it I was carrying three breadbaskets stacked on top of my head.
translation_verse: Paanowɔɔra nomoa la aa noa kɛŋɔ Josef wono baɡle o dɔŋ la deera la mun tɛo a do som la, o bol o be ŋɔ, “N ɡe deero dɛ che paanoo wɛɡrɛre atoro.

english_verse: The top basket was full of all kinds of baked things for the king, but birds were eating them.”
translation_verse: Dɛ paanoo bwa soo siwi aa ɛ Ijipt kooro kwaa su wɛɡrɛ waa chɔŋɛ nyundua tenten la bini, asɛ jumbii ɛɛ dia.”

english_verse: Joseph said: This is the meaning of your dream. The three baskets are three days,
translation_verse: Belaa Josef chaŋe dɛ ŋɔ, “Kenii he deera la mun ɛɛ baɡle. Wɛɡrɛre atoro la cheɡɔɔ tɛ tɔpera atoro.

english_verse: and in three days the king will cut off your head. He will hang your body on a pole, and birds will come and peck at it.
translation_verse: Tɔpetooro wee la, kooro ɛɛ teŋe he nyuu, dɛ́ kpɔe ka saɡɛ daa ta, ásɛ jumbii ba di he ola.”

english_verse: Three days later, while the king was celebrating his birthday with a dinner for his officials, he sent for his personal servant and the chief cook.
translation_verse: A habɔɔ tɔpetooro wee la, kooro la dɛ di o lola tɔpere, asɛ dɛ yerɛ o nomonome bwa. O le o sendoola nomoa la ne paanowɔɔra nomoa la, dɛ kpɔ ba ba o nɛra la sie.

english_verse: He put the personal servant back in his old job
translation_verse: O berɛ sendoola nomoa la toma tɛo

english_verse: and had the cook put to death. Everything happened just as Joseph had said it would,
translation_verse: asɛ dɛ teŋe paanowɔɔra nomoa la nyu ɡɛ Josef aa bola la.

english_verse: Two years later the king of Egypt dreamed he was standing beside the Nile River.
translation_verse: Bene anɛ habɔɔ la, awola bɛl, Ijipt harɛ ta kooro deero, dɛ o cheɡɛ Nael Moo nyoa o harɛ ta bela,

english_verse: Suddenly, seven fat, healthy cows came up from the river and started eating grass along the bank.
translation_verse: o na nae anuanɛ aa do bwara, dɛ le moo la ta dɛ baa chwe kpɔɡa o nyoa.

english_verse: Then seven ugly, skinny cows came up out of the river and
translation_verse: Belaa nae anuanɛ ane ɡe le moo la ta ba. Dɛ ate ɡwaŋrɔ dɛ doŋ dɛ ka che anɔ la jwɛh,

english_verse: ate the fat, healthy cows. When this happened, the king woke up.
translation_verse: asɛ nae aa ɡwaŋra la lawɛ anɔ la aa do bwara la liɡli, asɛ o den har dom ta.

english_verse: The king went back to sleep and had another dream. This time seven full heads of grain were growing on a single stalk.
translation_verse: O berɔ chɔ dom, dɛ dee ja asɛ boyu anuanɛ sɛɡle daa beŋkpoŋ ta dɛ ta pure. A bwa ɡe mao kɛrɛdɛ.

english_verse: Later, seven other heads of grain appeared, but they were thin and scorched by a wind from the desert.
translation_verse: Asɛ anfala anuanɛ ɡe berɛ sɛɡle daa la bampera. Peuwɔb bɛl tao le wee leebɔr dɛ ba chɔɡ a te, a ta wone ta pure.

english_verse: The thin heads of grain swallowed the seven full heads. Again the king woke up, and it had only been a dream.
translation_verse: Boyu aa wola wone ta pure la kpɔ anɔ la aa ta pure la liɡli, asɛ kooro la har dom ta.

english_verse: The next morning the king was upset. So he called in his magicians and wise men and told them what he had dreamed. None of them could tell him what the dreams meant.
translation_verse: Tɔ aa pera chɔɔ la, dɛ o liire chɔɡɔ, anomanta, o yerɛ dobodobo tena ne wejerema baa lɔ harɛ la ta ba o be. O taa o deera la ba be, kɛ bɛlbwa ta wone baɡle a mun.

english_verse: The king's personal servant said: Now I remember what I was supposed to do.
translation_verse: Belaa sendoola nomoa la ŋɔ kooro be ŋɔ, “N dɛ nyin ń bol fini kɛŋɔ n ɛ wechɔɡa.

english_verse: When you were angry with me and your chief cook, you threw us both in jail in the house of the captain of the guard.
translation_verse: He baah fa di n ne paanowɔɔra nomoa nɛ, a che a ta he lawɛ yaa do dea nɛra baa dɛ daahne la nomoa dem.

english_verse: One night we both had dreams, and each dream had a different meaning.
translation_verse: Awola bɛl, n ne paanowɔɔra nomoa la deero asɛ a mune koɡre.

english_verse: A young Hebrew, who was a servant of the captain of the guard, was there with us at the time. When we told him our dreams, he explained what each of them meant,
translation_verse: Dɛ ya ne Hibru te bonɔɔ bɛlee ba pɛ do dea. Dɛ o ɛ nomoa la waa dɛ daah yaa la bonɔɔ. Yaa bol ya deera la baɡlo la, o wono baɡle yaa a mun.

english_verse: and everything happened just as he said it would. I got my job back, and the cook was put to death.
translation_verse: Gɛ waa baɡle ya deera la mun la a ɛ ɡɛ. He berɔ kpɔ n toma do n nɔn ta, asɛ dɛ kpo paanowɔɔra nomoa la.”

english_verse: The king sent for Joseph, who was quickly brought out of jail. He shaved, changed his clothes, and went to the king.
translation_verse: Belaa kooro tomɛ ŋɔ bá ka kpɔ Josef ba. Ba kaa lawɔ le dea warane, dɛ fonɛ o nyu ne o tampona, dɛ kpɔ laalafala doo, dɛ ba o ne kooro sie.

english_verse: The king said to him, “I had a dream, yet no one can explain what it means. I am told that you can interpret dreams.”
translation_verse: Kooro ŋɔ Josef be ŋɔ, “N deero, kɛ nomɛlbwa toole dɛ baɡ mɛ a mun, n no he waa kɛŋɔ he won deera mun baɡla.”

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” Joseph answered, “I can't do it myself, but God can give a good meaning to your dreams.”
translation_verse: Anee Josef ŋɔ, “N naa, n laa dɛ́ baɡle deera nɔ mun. Korowiirii dɛ́ won baɡle a mun tɛɛ.”

english_verse: The king told Joseph: I dreamed I was standing on the bank of the Nile River.
translation_verse: Asɛ kooro ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “N deero dɛ che Nael Moo nyoa,

english_verse: I saw seven fat, healthy cows come up out of the river, and they began feeding on the grass.
translation_verse: belaa n na nae anuanɛ aa do bwara dɛ do wer, dɛ le nee la ta baa chwe kpɔɡa o nyoa.

english_verse: Next, seven skinny, bony cows came up out of the river. I have never seen such terrible looking cows anywhere in Egypt.
translation_verse: A habɔɔ, nae anuanɛ ane ɡe le nee la ta ba. Dɛ a te ɡwaŋrɔ dɛ doŋ kɛrɛdɛ. N ta nae aa doŋa ɡɛ nae Ijipt harɛ nɔ ta bobɛlbwa bwa.

english_verse: But you couldn't tell it, because these skinny cows were just as skinny as they were before. At once, I woke up.
translation_verse: Aa lawɛ a bala la liɡli tonɛ la, aa jemɛ kɛŋɔ a di kwaane kwara. Dɛ a ta doŋo ɡɛ aa doa la. N den har dom ta.

english_verse: I also dreamed that I saw seven heads of grain growing on one stalk. The heads were full and ripe.
translation_verse: N berɔ chɔ dom dɛ dee ja, asɛ boyu anuanɛ sɛɡle daa beŋkpoŋ ta dɛ ta pure, a bwa ɡe mao kɛrɛdɛ.

english_verse: Then seven other heads of grain came up. They were thin and scorched by a wind from the desert.
translation_verse: Asɛ anfala anuanɛ ɡe berɛ sɛɡle daa la bampera. Peuwɔb bɛl tao le wee leebɔr dɛ ba chɔɡ a te, a ta wone ta pure.

english_verse: These heads of grain swallowed the full ones. I told my dreams to the magicians, but none of them could tell me the meaning of the dreams.
translation_verse: Anɔ la aa wola wone ta pure la kpɔ anuanɛ aa ta pure la liɡli. Maa taara baɡle dobodobo tena la, bɛlbwa ta wone baɡ mɛ a mun.”

english_verse: Joseph replied: Your Majesty, both of your dreams mean the same thing, and in them God has shown what he is going to do.
translation_verse: Belaa Josef ŋɔ Ijipt kooro be ŋɔ, “N naa kooro, he deera anɛ la bwa dɛ baɡle webeŋkpoŋ. Korowii ɡelɔ he na waa waa dɛ ba ɛɛ.

english_verse: The seven good cows stand for seven years, and so do the seven good heads of grain.
translation_verse: Nae anuanɛ aa do bwara la cheɡɔ tɛ bene anuanɛ, asɛ boyu anuanɛ aa ta pure kɛrɛdɛ la ɡe che tɛ bene anuanɛ. Webeŋkpoŋii a bwa ɛɛ baɡle.

english_verse: The seven skinny, ugly cows that came up later also stand for seven years, as do the seven bad heads of grain that were scorched by the desert wind. The dreams mean there will be seven years when there won't be enough grain.
translation_verse: Asɛ naɡwaŋre anuanɛ aa doŋa dɛ ka mun le nee la ta ba la, ne boyu waa sɛɡla anuanɛ peuwɔb le wee leebɔr ba chɔɡa a ta wone ta pure la, ɡe cheɡɔ tɛ kɛŋɔ lɔr ɛɛ bao bene anuanɛ.

english_verse: It is just as I said—God has shown what he intends to do.
translation_verse: N naa kooro, ɡɛ n fa aa bol he be la, waa Korowii aa dɛ nyin ɛɛ laanee o ɡel he na la.

english_verse: For seven years Egypt will have more than enough grain,
translation_verse: Kondikwa ɛɛ ba Ijipt harɛ nɔ ta bobɛlbwaa taeh bene anuanɛ.

english_verse: when the king made him governor, and he went everywhere for the king.
translation_verse: A habɔɔ la, lɔr ɛɛ chiɡ harɛ nɔ taa bene anuanɛ, ásɛ nɛn soh kɛŋɔ kondikwaa fa balɔ ka. Dɛkalkɛ lɔr la ɛɛ chɔɡ harɛ nɔɔ.

english_verse: The famine will be so bad that no one will remember that once there had been plenty.
translation_verse: Lɔr la kpeɡri waa dɛ ba doe harɛ nɔ ta kohona nomanta, nɛn dɛ ba soeh kɛŋɔ kondikwaa fa lɔ harɛ nɔ ta taeh.

english_verse: God has given you two dreams to let you know that he has definitely decided to do this and that he will do it soon.
translation_verse: He deera bele anɛ la dɛ baɡle kɛŋɔ Korowii ɡbaɡbaa ɛa ɡɛ, kɛ waa ɡel a biɡri ásɛ a chiɡ.

english_verse: Your Majesty, you should find someone who is wise and will know what to do, so that you can put him in charge of all Egypt.
translation_verse: Anomanta, n naa kooro, nyin nɛn waa ɛ wejereme dɛɛ no waa mun, dɛ́ kpɔ Ijipt harɛ nɔ do o nɔn ta.

english_verse: Then appoint some other officials to collect one fifth of every crop harvested in Egypt during the seven years when there is plenty.
translation_verse: A chɛ kɛ he nyin nomonome bane ɡe, ba nyiŋi dɛɛ lɛ kondikwaare bene anuanɛ la ta, ɡɛ saŋ kondikwa aa ba warɛ harɛ nɔ ta kohona la. Bá bɔne a bini bɔre anue dɛ́ lɛ bɔrbeŋkpoŋ.

english_verse: Give them the power to collect the grain during those good years and to store it in your cities.
translation_verse: Gel ba lɛ boyu a ɡɛ bene la ta bwɛjena ta cheɡ he sɔn ta.

english_verse: It can be stored until it is needed during the seven years when there won't be enough grain in Egypt. This will keep the country from being destroyed because of the lack of food. Joseph Is Made Governor over Egypt
translation_verse: Anee dɛ́ ba ɛ kondikwa bene anuanɛ lɔr waa dɛ ba bala harɛ nɔ ta la. Ásɛ lɔr bɛ harɛ nɔ ba chɔɡ.”

english_verse: The king and his officials liked this plan.
translation_verse: Kooro ne o nomonome bwa sɛh ɡɛ waa la ta.

english_verse: So the king said to them, “Who could possibly handle this better than Joseph? After all, the Spirit of God is with him.”
translation_verse: Asɛ kooro ŋɔ o nomonome la be ŋɔ, “Dɛ Josef laa, nomɛlbwa toole, o nɛɛ Korowii Doma so, onee dɛ́ won nyiŋi kondikwaa nɔ ta.”

english_verse: The king told Joseph, “God is the one who has shown you these things. No one else is as wise as you are or knows as much as you do.
translation_verse: Belaa kooro ŋɔ Josef be ŋɔ, “Korowiirii baɡle anɔ bwa, anomanta, ya bwa nao kɛŋɔ he dɔ wejema dɛɛ no waa mun dɛ ɡwaa nomɛlbwa.

english_verse: I'm putting you in charge of my palace, and everybody will have to obey you. No one will be over you except me.
translation_verse: Mɛɛ kpɔe he chɔ n harɛ nɔ bwa nyoa, ásɛ nomɛlbwa ɛɛ teŋɛ he waa ta. Kora nɔ ɡbo taa n ɡwaale.”

english_verse: Then the king took off his royal ring and put it on Joseph's finger. He gave him fine clothes to wear and placed a gold chain around his neck.
translation_verse: Kooro laa o noniseɡ o nyanyini kon aa dawɛ o ta la foo do Josef, dɛ kpɔ yapondɛɛɡe batakaare ɡe doo, dɛ kpɔ suuɡaswɛm jɔɡrɔre baŋa kwaa ɡe do o baŋa.

english_verse: He also let him ride in the chariot next to his own, and people shouted, “Make way for Joseph!” So Joseph was governor of Egypt.
translation_verse: O ɡelɔ o so o koo kon waa do kɛ torɔɡo bini, asɛ nɛra tɔ o sie dɛɛ ŋɔ, “Hé tɛ ŋwɛnɛ! Hé tɛ ŋwɛnɛ!” Gɛɛ a do ba kpɔ Josef cheɡ ŋɔ wɛɛ nyiŋi Ijipt harɛ la bwa ta.

english_verse: The king told Joseph, “Although I'm king, no one in Egypt is to do anything without your permission.”
translation_verse: Asɛ kooro la ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Menee kooro te, kɛ nomɛlbwa ta ŋwɛnɛ dɔe kɛ o ɛ wobɛlbwa dɛ le he habɔɔ.”

english_verse: He gave Joseph the Egyptian name Zaphenath Paneah. And he let him marry Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, a priest in the city of Heliopolis. Joseph traveled all over Egypt.
translation_verse: O kpɔ Ijipt harɛ sɔn pao ŋɔ baa yerɔ Safenat Panea, dɛ mo haah ɡe tɛo. O haah la sɔne Asenat. Sɔfo Pɔtefɛra bihaahnee. Dɛ sɔfo nɔ soɡe bwɛjen On, o sɔn bɛl ɡee Hɛleopɔles. Asɛ Josef ka ɡaaɡe Ijipt harɛ ta bwa.

english_verse: For seven years there were big harvests of grain.
translation_verse: Bene anuanɛ kondikwa aa ɛa kohona la, koo kwaa ɛo kohona harɛ la ta,

english_verse: Joseph collected and stored up the extra grain in the cities of Egypt near the fields where it was harvested.
translation_verse: asɛ Josef ɡel ba boa kondikwaa aa bala bene anuanɛ la ta la nyoa cheɡ bwɛjena ta. Bwɛɛre aa bar bwɛjen bɛlbwa kondikwaa la, ba dɛ cheɡa bwɛjen la ta.

english_verse: In fact, there was so much grain that they stopped keeping record, because it was like counting the grains of sand along the beach.
translation_verse: Josef ɡelɔ ba lɛ kondikwaa cheɡ a warɛ kɛŋɔ mpo nyoa hɛŋle ken, anomanta, o berɔ ɡel a maɡa.

english_verse: Joseph and his wife had two sons before the famine began.
translation_verse: Sɔfo Pɔtefɛra waa le bwɛjen On bihaah Asenat lolɛ bibaala banɛ tɛ Josef mɔɔ lɔrchɔɡe la ba.

english_verse: Their first son was named Manasseh, which means, “God has let me forget all my troubles and my family back home.”
translation_verse: Josef pa o binomoa la sɔn Manasɛ. O munii Korowii ɡelɔ n soh n wenaale ne n mɛɛ lolanar bwa wa.

english_verse: His second son was named Ephraim, which means “God has made me a success in the land where I suffered.”
translation_verse: O pa binɛɛte la ɡe sɔn Efrem. O munii Korowii tɛ mɛ bii harɛ maa na wahala o ta la ta.

english_verse: Egypt's seven years of plenty came to an end,
translation_verse: Bene anuanɛ kondikwaa aa bu Ijipt harɛ ta la ba a jaɡa,

english_verse: and the seven years of famine began, just as Joseph had said. There was not enough food in other countries, but all over Egypt there was plenty.
translation_verse: asɛ bene anuanɛ lɔr Josef aa bol o waa la ɡe pa mun. Lɔr chole harɛre bwa ta, kɛ dɛ kondikwaa bu Ijipt te.

english_verse: When the famine finally struck Egypt, the people asked the king for food, but he said, “Go to Joseph and do what he tells you to do.”
translation_verse: Lɔr aa baa pa mun Ijipt harɛ ta bwa ɡe la, bela tena wio no kooro la ŋɔ ó tɛɛ ba kondikwa. Asɛ o ŋɔ bá la Josef be, ásɛ ɡɛ bwa waa ŋɔ la, bá ɛ.

english_verse: The famine became bad everywhere in Egypt, so Joseph opened the storehouses and sold the grain to the Egyptians.
translation_verse: Lɔr la aa chole Ijipt harɛ la ta o nyoa do kpeɡri la, Josef ɡelɔ ba pili deene baa kwaa boyu cheɡ a bini la bwa, dɛ yoɡ dɛɛ tɛ Ijipt tena.

english_verse: People from all over the world came to Egypt to buy grain, because the famine was so severe in their countries.
translation_verse: Nɛra le harɛre ta dɛ la Josef be Ijipt harɛ, dɛ kaa yawɛ boyu, dɛkalkɛ dɛ lɔr la nyoa kpeɡri bobɛlbwa.

english_verse: When Jacob found out there was grain in Egypt, he said to his sons, “Why are you just sitting here, staring at one another?
translation_verse: Jekɔb noɔ kɛŋɔ boyu lɔ Ijipt harɛ ta, asɛ o bɔɔ o bibaala la ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ he so dɛɛ nyiŋi dɔŋa sie ta nɔɔ?

english_verse: I have heard there is grain in Egypt. Go down and buy some, so we won't starve to death.”
translation_verse: N noɔ kɛŋɔ kondikwaa lɔ Ijipt harɛ ta, hé la bela ka yawɛ ane ba, ásɛ lɔr bɛ yaa kpo ya serewe.”

english_verse: Ten of Joseph's brothers went to Egypt to buy grain.
translation_verse: Belaa Josef dɔɔranar fi la ir la Ijipt harɛ, dɛ́ ka yawɛ boyu la.

english_verse: But Jacob did not send Joseph's younger brother Benjamin with them; he was afraid that something might happen to him.
translation_verse: Jekɔb ta ɡelɛ Bɛnjamen waa ɛ Josef nime pɔrɔdɔ la ja ba nɛɛ dɛ la. Dɛ o dɛ ɔmɛ kɛŋɔ waane ken ɛɛ ka ɛɔ.

english_verse: So Jacob's sons joined others from Canaan who were going to Egypt because of the terrible famine.
translation_verse: Jekɔb bii la ne Keenan harɛ ta tena banee pɛa la, dɛ ka yawɛ boyu la, dɛ harɛ la ta bwaa lɔr la do.

english_verse: Since Joseph was governor of Egypt and in charge of selling grain, his brothers came to him and bowed with their faces to the ground.
translation_verse: Dɛ Josef ɛ Ijipt harɛ la nomoa ne nɛn waa yoɡ boyu dɛɛ tɛ harɛre bwa nɛra. Anomanta, o dɔɔranar la aa bala la, ba kaa ɡuŋi o sie, dɛ kpɔ sie piiɡi harɛ.

english_verse: Joseph remembered what he had dreamed about them and said, “You're spies! You've come here to find out where our country is weak.”
translation_verse: Belaa o lii deera o fa aa dee ba la wa, dɛ ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, “He balɔ dɛ́ ba sɔh nyiŋi ya harɛ nɔ dɛ́ na kɛ ya chɔ pɛɛ.”

english_verse: “No sir,” they replied. “We're your servants, and we have only come to buy grain.
translation_verse: Anee ba ŋɔ, “Akai, nomoa, boyuu he bonɔɔna, yaa ba dɛ́ ba yawɛ.

english_verse: We're honest men, and we come from the same family—we're not spies.”
translation_verse: Babeŋkpoŋ biirii yan, ya ne ya tepoŋee. Ya ta balɛ dɛ́ ba sɔh nyiŋi harɛ nɔ.”

english_verse: “That isn't so!” Joseph insisted. “You've come here to find out where our country is weak.”
translation_verse: Ate, o ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, “Nyosone. He balɔ dɛ́ ba sɔh nyiŋi na kɛŋɔ harɛ nɔ chɔ pɛɛ.”

english_verse: But they explained, “Sir, we come from a family of twelve brothers. The youngest is still with our father in Canaan, and one of our brothers is dead.”
translation_verse: Ba ɡe ŋɔ, “Nomoa, he bonɔɔna, ya lɔ bii fi dɛ banɛ, dɛ ɛ babeŋkpoŋ bii, dɛ le Keenan harɛ ta. Ya bini bechala te lɔ ya mɛɛ be dem, asɛ ya bini beŋkpoŋ ɡe toole.”

english_verse: and I'm going to find out the truth. I swear by the life of the king that you won't leave this place until your youngest brother comes here.
translation_verse: Kenii mɛɛ ba ɛɛ dɛ́ jemɛ he kasinteŋ. N ŋwɛɛ Ijipt kooro kɛŋɔ he bini bɛlbwa aa bɔree dɔ kaa, nemenɛ he nime bechala la ba bonɔ mɔɔ.

english_verse: Choose one of you to go after your brother, while the rest of you stay here in jail. That will show whether you are telling the truth. But if you are lying, I swear by the life of the king that you are spies!
translation_verse: Hé ɡel he bini bɛl la ka kpɔ he nime la ba, ásɛ ba do he kar ɡe dea ka tel kɛŋɔ yaa na waa haa bola nɔ kasinteŋ. Dɛ ɡɛ laa tenaa, n ŋwɛɛ kooro kɛŋɔ he ɛ nɛra haa dɛ ba ba sɔh nyiŋi harɛ nɔ.”

english_verse: Joseph kept them all under guard for three days,
translation_verse: Asɛ dɛ laɡ ba do dea tɔpera atoro.

english_verse: before saying to them: Since I respect God, I'll give you a chance to save your lives.
translation_verse: Tɔpetooro wee la, Josef ŋɔ o dɔɔranar la be ŋɔ, “N te, n ɛ nɛn maa dɛ ɔmɛ Korowii, dɛ mɛɛ ɡel heyaa yaa, aa che webeŋkpoŋ taa.

english_verse: If you are honest men, one of you must stay here in jail, and the rest of you can take the grain back to your starving families.
translation_verse: He ɛ nɛndɛɛɡa aa, he ɡel he bini beŋkpoŋ ka dea bonɔ, ásɛ he kabora la ka kpɔ boyu la ka tɛ he lolanar lɔr aa dɛ kpo ba la.

english_verse: But you must bring your youngest brother to me. Then I'll know that you are telling the truth, and you won't be put to death. Joseph's brothers agreed
translation_verse: Ásɛ dɛ kpɔ he nime la ba tɛ mɛ, á baɡle kɛ he waa la ɛ kasinteŋ, ásɛ n bɛ ɡel ba kpoo heya.” Ate, ba sɛh waa waa bola la ta.

english_verse: and said to one another, “We're being punished because of Joseph. We saw the trouble he was in, but we refused to help him when he begged us. That's why these terrible things are happening.”
translation_verse: Dɛ ba dɛ bol dɔŋa be ŋɔ, “Taraken waa yaa dɛ na nɔ bwa le waa ya fa aa kpɔa ɛ ya nime Josef la. Ya na wenaale waa lɔ a ta dɛ soŋe yaa, kɛ ya ta noɛ. Anee ɡela ya ɡee na ɡɛ waa nɔ taraken la.”

english_verse: Reuben spoke up, “Didn't I tell you not to harm the boy? But you wouldn't listen, and now we have to pay the price for killing him.”
translation_verse: Belaa Rubin ŋɔ, “N te ŋɔ he be ŋɔ he bɛ bie la wobɛlbwa ɛ, kɛ he ta noɛ. Taraken, kpoe yaa kpoo laanee ɡure ya nyu ta la.”

english_verse: They did not know that Joseph could understand them, since he was speaking through an interpreter.
translation_verse: Baa cheɡɛ nomɛl nɛɛ dɛ bol waa dɛɛ tɛ Josef nomanta, dɛ baa jemɛ kɛ o dɛ no ba wobol la.

english_verse: Joseph turned away from them and cried, but soon he turned back and spoke to them again. Then he had Simeon tied up and taken away while they watched. Joseph's Brothers Return to Canaan
translation_verse: Belaa Josef le ba be bela dɛ ka wi. Dɛ berɛ ba ba be ja o ne ba bol wa, asɛ o lawɛ Simeon le ba bini dɛ ɡel ba vɔrɔwo ba siwi ta. Josef dɔɔranar berɔ kaa Keenan harɛ

english_verse: Joseph gave orders for his brothers' grain sacks to be filled with grain and for their money to be put in their sacks. He also gave orders for them to be given food for their journey home. After this was done,
translation_verse: Asɛ Josef ɡel ba do boyu o dɔɔranar la bɔɡtɔre bini a suuɡi, dɛ berɛ kpɔ ba suuɡare do a bini tɛɛ ba. Dɛ berɛ tɛɛ ba kondikwaa baa ka dia ŋwɛnɛ ta. Asɛ ba ɛ ɡɛ tɛɛ ba,

english_verse: they each loaded the grain on their donkeys and left.
translation_verse: ba kpɔ ba boyu la dawɛ ba keeɡore ta dɛ kaa.

english_verse: When they stopped for the night, one of them opened his sack to get some grain for his donkey, and at once he saw his moneybag.
translation_verse: Baa dɛ kaa la, bɔr kaa joo ba ŋwɛnɛ ta asɛ ba chɔ bela, asɛ ba bini bɛl ŋɔ ó pur o bɔɡtɔ dɛ́ tɛ o keeɡo kondikwa, asɛ dɛ na kɛŋɔ baa vɔwɛ suuɡa o pur la nyoa.

english_verse: “Here's my money!” he told his brothers. “Right here in my sack.” They were trembling with fear as they stared at one another and asked themselves, “What has God done to us?”
translation_verse: Anee o ŋɔ o bala la be ŋɔ, “Ba berɛ n suuɡa tɛ mɛ. Anee lɔ n bɔɡtɔ bini la.” Ba bwara yɔrɔ, asɛ ba kpɔ bochela dɛ ŋɔ dɔŋa be ŋɔ, “Bɔkwa waa Korowii ɛ yaa ken?”

english_verse: When they returned to the land of Canaan, they told their father Jacob everything that had happened to them:
translation_verse: Baa la ba mɛɛ Jekɔb be Keenan harɛ ta la, ba bol waa aa puu ba bwa baɡlo dɛ ŋɔ,

english_verse: But we told him, “We're honest men, not spies.
translation_verse: Asɛ ya ŋɔ, “Ya ne ya tepoŋee, ya ta balɛ dɛ́ ba sɔh nyiŋi harɛ la.

english_verse: We come from a family of twelve brothers. The youngest is still with our father in Canaan, and the other is dead.”
translation_verse: Ya lɔ bibaala fi dɛ banɛ, dɛ ɛ babeŋkpoŋ bii, ya bini beŋkpoŋ toole, asɛ ya bini bechala ɡe lɔ ya mɛɛ be taraken Keenan harɛ ta.”

english_verse: Then the governor of Egypt told us, “I'll find out if you really are honest. Leave one of your brothers here with me, while you take the grain to your starving families.
translation_verse: Belaa nomoa waa dɛ nyiŋi bela harɛ ta la ŋɔ, waa waa dɛ ba ɛɛ dɛ jemɛ ya kasinteŋ laanee kɛŋɔ, yá ɡel ya bini beŋkpoŋ o be, dɛ́ kpɔ boyu la ba tɛ ya dem tena lɔr aa dɛ kpo ba la.

english_verse: But bring your youngest brother to me, so I can be certain that you are honest men and not spies. After that, I'll let your other brother go free, and you can stay here and trade.”
translation_verse: Ásɛ dɛ kpɔ ya nime bechala la ba tɛo, ásɛ o jemɛ kɛŋɔ ya ta nɛra yaa laŋa dɛ́ ka sɔh nyiŋi harɛ la ɛɛ, kɛ ya ɛ nɛndɛɛɡa. Ásɛ o le ya dɔŋ la tɛ yaa, yaa di harɛ la ta bona.

english_verse: When the brothers started emptying their sacks of grain, they found their moneybags in them. They were frightened, and so was their father Jacob,
translation_verse: Baa dɛ pur ba bone la, bɛlbwa nao kɛŋɔ suuɡa vɔwɛ o bɔɡtɔ nyoa, asɛ ɔmee lawɛ ba ne ba mɛɛ bwa.

english_verse: who said, “You have already taken my sons Joseph and Simeon from me. And now you want to take away Benjamin! Everything is against me.”
translation_verse: Ate, ba mɛɛ Jekɔb ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, “Hé dɛ nyin kɛ n paŋɛ n bii bwa kɛɛ? Josef toole, Simeon ɡe kao. Hé berɔ dɛɛ nyin kɛ he kpɔ Bɛnjamen ɡe kaa. Menee dɛɛ ba waa nae!”

english_verse: Reuben spoke up, “Father, if I don't bring Benjamin back, you can kill both of my sons. Trust me with him, and I'll bring him back.”
translation_verse: Asɛ Rubin ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Dɛ n ta Bɛnjamen ne balɛ ba tɛɛ naa, he kpoo n bibaala banɛ nɔ. Kpɔ o waa do n nɔn ta, mɛɛ berɔɔ ba o ne ba tɛɛ.”

english_verse: But Jacob said, “I won't let my son Benjamin go down to Egypt with the rest of you. His brother is already dead, and he is the only son I have left. I am an old man, and if anything happens to him on the way, I'll die from sorrow, and all of you will be to blame.”
translation_verse: Ate Jekɔb ŋɔ, “Maa sɛh he kpɔ n bie nɔ kaa, o dɔɔ toole, o ɡboo kaa. N ɡe hwɛɛhrɔ tonɛ. Wobɛlbwa kaa ɛo ŋwɛnɛ ta bela haa dɛ kaa nɔ naa, n ne n tebinichɔɡee dɛɛ ba sewa.”

english_verse: The famine in Canaan got worse,
translation_verse: Lɔr la nyoa baa do kpeɡri Keenan harɛ la ta,

english_verse: until finally, Jacob's family had eaten all the grain they had bought in Egypt. So Jacob said to his sons, “Go back and buy some more grain.”
translation_verse: Jekɔb ne o bii aa di boyu baa kaa yawɛ le Ijipt harɛ ta ba tonɛ la, o ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, “Hé berɛ la ka yawɛ boyu la tama ba ja.”

english_verse: Judah replied, “The governor strictly warned us that we would not be allowed to see him unless we brought our youngest brother with us. If you let us take Benjamin along, we will go and buy grain. But we won't go without him!”
translation_verse: Kɛ dɛ haa sɛh tenaa, yaa la. Baa la ɡelɔ ya jemɛ kɛŋɔ dɛ ya ta ya nime la ne balaa, waa ya siwi nyin dɛ na kwara.”

english_verse: Jacob asked, “Why did you cause me so much trouble by telling the governor you had another brother?”
translation_verse: Anee Jekɔb ŋɔ, “Bɔkwaa dɔ baa nɔ be ŋɔe ŋɔ he dɔ nime bɛl dɛ kpɔ waa nɔ ba ta n nɛɛ ken?”

english_verse: They answered, “He asked a lot of questions about us and our family. He wanted to know if you were still alive and if we had any more brothers. All we could do was answer his questions. How could we know he would tell us to bring along our brother?”
translation_verse: Asɛ ba ɡe chaŋe ŋɔ, “O teŋɔ dɛɛ bɔɔ ya ne ya lolanar wa. Dɛ́ ya mɛɛ ta soɡe le naa? Ya dɔ nime bɛl dɛ ja ya nɛ aa? Waa waa bɔɔra laanee ya ɡe chaŋe. N mɛɛ, dɛ ya ta jemɛ kɛŋɔ wɛɛ ŋɔɔ ya kpɔ ya nime la ba.”

english_verse: Then Judah said to his father, “Let Benjamin go with me, and we will leave at once, so that none of us will starve to death.
translation_verse: Belaa Juda ŋɔ o mɛɛ be ŋɔ, “Kpɔ Bɛnjamen do n nɔn ta n ne o kaa warane, ásɛ lɔr bɛ yaa kpo ya ba serewe.

english_verse: I promise to bring him back safely, and if I don't, you can blame me as long as I live.
translation_verse: Mɛɛ cheo tɛ wobɛlbwa. Dɛ n ta o ne balɛ ba tɛɛ naa, bɔɔ mɛ. Dɛ n ta o ne balɛ sɔnɔnɔɔ ba tɛɛ naa, n nɛɛ wobɛlbwa dawɛ.

english_verse: If we had not wasted all this time, we could already have been there and back twice.”
translation_verse: Ken laa ya do waa nɔ ta dɛɛ tɛɡre aa, ya fe la kera anɛ ba.”

english_verse: Their father said: If Benjamin must go with you, take the governor a gift of some of the best things from our own country, such as perfume, honey, spices, pistachio nuts, and almonds.
translation_verse: Ba mɛɛ ɡe ŋɔ, “Dɛ ɡɛɛ tenaa, hé kpɔ ya harɛ nɔ ta kwaa kɛŋɔ, noo tama ne tooh tama ne konsɔɔhsoma, ne korobo ne daa nɔna aa dɔ pɛla do he pure bini ka tɛ nomoa la.

english_verse: Also take along twice the amount of money for the grain, because there must have been some mistake when the money was put back in your sacks.
translation_verse: Bɛ́lbwa kpɔ suuɡa bele anɛ, anɔ la haa naa he bɔɡtɔre nyoo la ken ɛ soohla.

english_verse: Take Benjamin with you and leave at once.
translation_verse: Hé lawɛ he nime Bɛnjamen, he ne o kaa baa la be warane.

english_verse: When you go in to see the governor, I pray that God All-Powerful will be good to you and that the governor will let your other brother and Benjamin come back home with you. But if I must lose my children, I suppose I must.
translation_verse: Kórowii Waa Ɛ Kpeɡri Bwa Dɔɔ la ja he nɛɛ dɛ́ ɡel nomoa la na he sum, dɛ́ kpɔ Simeon ne Bɛnjamen tɛ heya he ba tɛ mɛ. Dɛ baa le n nɔn taa yaa, ba den le n nɔn ta.”

english_verse: The brothers took the gifts, twice the amount of money, and Benjamin. Then they hurried off to Egypt. When they stood in front of Joseph,
translation_verse: Kɛ ane a bwa, ba kpɔ koŋkɛɛla la ne suuɡa bele anɛ la ne Bɛnjamen, dɛ chiɡ ŋwɛnɛ ta kaa Ijipt harɛ ta warane, dɛ kpɔ ba te ka chaɡle Josef.

english_verse: he saw Benjamin and told the servant in charge of his house, “Take these men to my house. Slaughter an animal and cook it, so they can eat with me at noon.”
translation_verse: Josef aa naa kɛ Bɛnjamen ja ba bini la, o ŋɔ o bonɔɔ waa dɛ nyiŋi o dem la be ŋɔ, “Kpɔ nɛra nɔ kaa n dem, dɛ́ ka kpo kon ɛ kondikwa, n dɛ́ ba n ne bá di kondikwa webaŋa nɔ ne.”

english_verse: The servant did as he was told and took the brothers to Joseph's house.
translation_verse: Bonɔɔ la ɛ ɡɛ Josef aa doo la, asɛ dɛ lawɛ nɛra la kaa o dem.

english_verse: But on the way they got worried and started thinking, “We are being taken there because of the money that was put back in our sacks last time. He will arrest us, make us his slaves, and take our donkeys.”
translation_verse: Waa kpɔ ba dɛɛ kaa dem la, dɛ ba dɛ ɔmɛ, asɛ dɛɛ bol dɔŋa be ŋɔ, “Suuɡa la baa bera do ya bone bini la waa baa ba ya ne dem bonɔ la. Baa ɡuɡri yaa, dɛ́ lawɛ yaa yoma, dɛ́ kpɔ ya keeɡore.”

english_verse: So when they arrived at Joseph's house, they said to the servant in charge,
translation_verse: Anomanta, baa tel dem la doonyoa la, ba ŋɔ bonɔɔ la be ŋɔ,

english_verse: “Sir, we came to Egypt once before to buy grain.
translation_verse: “Nomoa, ya fa ba bonɔ dɛ ba yawɛ kondikwa,

english_verse: But when we stopped for the night, we each found in our grain sacks the exact amount we had paid. We have brought that money back,
translation_verse: yaa chiɡ ŋwɛnɛ ta bɔr jo ya ka chɔ bobɛl la, ya pur ya bɔɡtɔre nyoo, dɛ na kɛŋɔ ya suuɡare yaa kpɔa ba yawɛ kondikwaa la lɔ a bini. Anomanta, ya berɔ ba a ne, anee la.

english_verse: together with enough money to buy more grain. We don't know who put the money in our sacks.”
translation_verse: Ya berɔ ba suuɡa ne, dɛ́ ba yawɛ kondikwaa ja. Ya ta wone jemɛ naate waa kpɔ anɔ la do ya bɔɡtɔre la bini.”

english_verse: “It's all right,” the servant replied. “Don't worry. The God you and your father worship must have put the money there, because I received your payment in full.” Then he brought Simeon out to them.
translation_verse: Anee bonɔɔ la chaŋe ŋɔ, “He bɛ ɡel a hiah heya hɛɛ ɔmɛ. Korowii he ne he nimanar aa dɛ tomɔ laanee ken kpɔa do he bone bini la. Gɛ suuɡa la tel n be.” Asɛ o le Simeon tɛɛ ba.

english_verse: The servant took them into Joseph's house and gave them water to wash their feet. He also tended their donkeys.
translation_verse: Ate, o laɡ ba jo dem dɛ tɛɛ ba nee ba sarame ba nakpale, dɛ tɛ ba keeɡore ɡe kwaa a di.

english_verse: The brothers got their gifts ready to give to Joseph at noon, since they had heard they were going to eat there.
translation_verse: Ba noɔ kɛŋɔ baa di webaŋkwaa dem belaa, anomanta, ba kwaa ba koŋkɛɛla la cheɡ dɛɛ kpa Josef bala webaŋa la ne.

english_verse: When Joseph came home, they gave him the gifts they had brought, and they bowed down to him.
translation_verse: Josef aa ba dem la, ba kpɔ koŋkɛɛla la ka ɡuŋi o sie dɛ kpɔ tɛo.

english_verse: After Joseph had asked how they were, he said, “What about your elderly father? Is he still alive?”
translation_verse: Asɛ o bɔɔ ba ɡɛ ba bwara aa doa dɛ berɛ ŋɔ, “Hé fa bol he mɛɛ wa n be. Ɛrɛɛ o bwara doɔ? O ta soɡe le o bwara do kpeɡri aa?”

english_verse: They answered, “Your servant our father is still alive and well.” And again they bowed down to Joseph.
translation_verse: Anee ba chaŋe ŋɔ, “Nomoa, he bonɔɔ waa ɛ ya mɛɛ la ta soɡe le o bwara do kpeɡri.” Asɛ ba ɡuŋi o sie dɛ kpɔ ba sie piiɡi harɛ.

english_verse: When Joseph looked around and saw his brother Benjamin, he said, “This must be your youngest brother, the one you told me about. God bless you, my son.”
translation_verse: Josef aa nyiŋa dɛ na Bɛnjamen waa ɛ o nyabie pɔrɔdɔ la, o ŋɔ, “Hé nime haa bol o waa n be laanee nɔ naa? Korowii chae, n bie.”

english_verse: Then, because of his love for Benjamin, he rushed off to his room and cried.
translation_verse: Nyina Josef aa dɛ nyin o nime la kohona nomanta, o haŋrɔ kahonɛ, dɛ le bela warane, dɛ ka jo o dea dɛ wi.

english_verse: After washing his face and returning, he was able to control himself and said, “Serve the meal!”
translation_verse: Waa tona la, o samɛ o sie dɛ le buse dɛ kwaa sie do, asɛ dɛ ŋɔ bá kpɔ kondikwaa la le ba bá di.

english_verse: Joseph was served at a table by himself, and his brothers were served at another. The Egyptians sat at yet another table, because Egyptians felt it was disgusting to eat with Hebrews.
translation_verse: Ba kpɔ Josef kwaa cheɡo korɛ, asɛ o dɔɔranar la ɡe kwaa korɛ. Dɛ Ijipt tena bane jao dɛ ɡee di kwaa la ane. Dɛ Ijipt tena kii ba ne Hibru tena nɔn pɛɛ dɛ́ di kwa, anomanta, ba korɛ ba kwa.

english_verse: To the surprise of Joseph's brothers, they were seated in front of him according to their ages, from the oldest to the youngest.
translation_verse: Josef dɔɔranar ne o nime la soɡo ba sie pa dɔŋa nɛ. O ɡelɔ ba so teŋɛ dɔŋa nɛɛ le ba nomonome bini kaa bechale ta. Baa na ɡɛ baa soɡa teŋɛ dɔŋa nɛɛ la, ba nyoa kpoo.

english_verse: They were served food from Joseph's table, and Benjamin was given five times as much as each of the others. So Joseph's brothers ate and drank with him and had a good time.
translation_verse: Ba kpɔ Josef kondikwaa la ane ba bɔne ba. Ba tɛ Bɛnjamen bɔre anue, dɛ ɡwaa ɡɛ baa tɛ ba kar la. Ba di kondikwaa la dɛ vaɡre, dɛ nyɔ sen lɛ ba sie.

english_verse: Early the next morning, the men were sent on their way with their donkeys.
translation_verse: Tɔ aa pera chɔmbibi la, ba ta ba ŋwɛnɛ ba ne ba keeɡore kaa.

english_verse: But they had not gone far from the city when Joseph told the servant, “Go after those men! When you catch them, say, ‘My master has been good to you. So why have you stolen his silver cup?
translation_verse: Baa dɛ kaa baa wola bobɛlbwa tele mɔɔ la, Josef ŋɔ bonɔɔ waa dɛ nyiŋi dem bela la be ŋɔ, “Ɛ warane dɛ́ ti baala la. He kaa puu ba aa, hé bɔɔ ba ŋɔ, ‘Ɛrɛɛ he kpɔ wechɔɡa bɔ wedɛɛɡa kem nɔɔ?

english_verse: Not only does he drink from his cup, but he also uses it to learn about the future. You have done a terrible thing.’ ”
translation_verse: Ɛrɛ waa he ŋwɛ n dɔɔ suuɡapoŋ numol nɔɔ? O nee wɛɛ nyɔ ne, dɛ che o ta dɛɛ jemɛ kerekere wa. Gɛ haa ɛa nɔ ɛ wechɔɡa kohona.’ ”

english_verse: When the servant caught up with them, he said exactly what Joseph had told him to say.
translation_verse: Waa ti ba dɛ ka puu ba la, ɡɛ waa laanee o bol ba be.

english_verse: But they replied, “Sir, why do you say such things? We would never do anything like that!
translation_verse: Asɛ ba chaŋo ŋɔ, “Nomoa, ɛrɛɛ hɛɛ nyin he chaɡle nɔɔ? Korowii ɛɛ kisi yaa, yaa ɡɛɛ ɛ.

english_verse: We even returned the money we found in our grain sacks when we got back to Canaan. So why would we want to steal any silver or gold from your master's house?
translation_verse: Ya ta suuɡa yaa naa ya bone bini Keenan harɛ la berɛ ba tɛ heya aa? Ɛrɛɛ yaa ba wona ŋwɛ suuɡapoŋ kɛɛ suuɡaswɛm he nomoa dem ɔ?

english_verse: If you find that one of us has the cup, then kill him, and the rest of us will become your slaves.”
translation_verse: Nomoa, ya bini bɛlbwa haa nao o be la, bá kpoo, ásɛ ya kar ɡe ɛ he yoma.”

english_verse: “Good!” the man replied, “I'll do what you have said. But only the one who has the cup will become my slave. The rest of you can go free.”
translation_verse: Asɛ o sɛh ɡɛ baa bola la dɛ ŋɔ, “A wer, kɛ naate maa nao o be la ɡboo dɛ́ berɛ n yom, ásɛ he kabora te kaa.”

english_verse: Each of the brothers quickly put his sack on the ground and opened it.
translation_verse: Belaa bɛlbwa ɛ warane dɛ choɡ o bone cheɡ, dɛ laa a nyoa pur.

english_verse: Joseph's servant started searching the sacks, beginning with the one that belonged to the oldest brother. When he came to Benjamin's sack, he found the cup.
translation_verse: Ate, Josef bonɔɔ la nyiŋi ba bone la bini. O pa mun le ba bini nomoa be dɛ ba tonɛ bechala la be, asɛ dɛ na numol la Bɛnjamen waa ɛ bechala la be.

english_verse: This upset the brothers so much that they began tearing their clothes in sorrow. Then they loaded their donkeys and returned to the city.
translation_verse: A we ba nɛ, ba laa ba laala kɛɛ, a baɡle kɛ ba tea bini chɔɡɔ, dɛ kwaa vɔwɛ ba bone choɡ keeɡore la, dɛ laa berɛ ba bwɛjen la ta.

english_verse: When Judah and his brothers got there, Joseph was still at home. So they bowed down to Joseph,
translation_verse: Juda ne o bala aa tel Josef dem la, dɛ o ta lole, asɛ ba ka ɡuŋu harɛ.

english_verse: who asked them, “What have you done? Didn't you know I could find out?”
translation_verse: O bɔɔ ba ŋɔ, “Bɔkwa waa he ɛ ken? Haa jemɛ kɛŋɔ n won chaahna nae, dɛ́ jemɛ waa aa dɛ ba chiɡa kerekere kɛɛ?”

english_verse: “Sir, what can we say?” Judah replied. “How can we say we are innocent, when God has shown we are guilty? And now all of us are your slaves, especially the one who had the cup.”
translation_verse: Anee Juda chaŋe ŋɔ, “N dɔɔ, ɛrɛɛ yaa ba he be bola ɔ? Ɛrɛɛ yaa ba wona tɔŋle ŋɔ ya laa ɔ? Ɛrɛɛ yaa ba wona ŋɔ ya waa dɔ kasinteŋ kpa ɔ? Korowii le ya mun ne. Taraken naate baa na numol nɔ o be ɡbo laa dɛ́ ɛ he yom, ya bwa ɛɛ ɛ he yomaa.”

english_verse: Joseph told them, “I would never punish all of you. Only the one who was caught with the cup will become my slave. The rest of you are free to go home to your father.” Judah Pleads for Benjamin
translation_verse: Anee Josef ŋɔ, “Akai, maa an ɡɛɛ ɛ bwa. Nemenɛ naate baa na numol la o be la ɡboo dɛ́ ɛ n yom. He kabora la te ɛɛ won kaa he mɛɛ be deŋnesɔɔhna ne.”

english_verse: Judah went over to Joseph and said: Sir, you have as much power as the king himself, and I am only your slave. Please don't get angry if I speak.
translation_verse: Ate, Juda suuh tel Josef, dɛ ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Nomoa, bɛ ɡel he baah di n nɛ. He do kɛŋɔ Ijipt kooro ɡbaɡba ken, kɛ n dɛ nyin kɛŋɔ he tɛ mɛ ŋwɛnɛ n ne he won bol wa.

english_verse: You asked us if our father was still alive and if we had any more brothers.
translation_verse: Nomoa, he fa ta yaa bɔɔrɛ kɛ ya dɔ mɛɛ kɛɛ nime bɛl a?

english_verse: So we told you, “Our father is a very old man. In fact, he was already old when Benjamin was born. Benjamin's brother is dead. Now Benjamin is the only one of the two brothers who is still alive, and our father loves him very much.”
translation_verse: Asɛ ya chaŋe ŋɔ ya dɔ mɛɛ o hwɛɛh dɛ dɔ nime bɛl ɡe. Ya mɛɛ aa hwɛɛhra la taa o lolɔ, asɛ o dɔɔ o ne waa pɛ nya la sewɛ a ka o ɡbo, anomanta, o mɛɛ dɛ nyin o waa taeh.

english_verse: You ordered us to bring him here, so you could see him for yourself.
translation_verse: He ŋɔ ya be ŋɔ ya la ka kpɔɔ ba he nao,

english_verse: We told you that our father would die if Benjamin left him.
translation_verse: asɛ ya ŋɔ bie la aa won le o mɛɛ jwɛh, dɛkalkɛ o le o jwɛh aa, o mɛɛ la ɛɛ sewɔɔ.

english_verse: But you warned us that we could never see you again, unless our youngest brother came with us.
translation_verse: Asɛ he berɛ ŋɔ ya be ŋɔ haa nyin kɛ he na yaa dɛ ya nime la ta jae.

english_verse: So we returned to our father and reported what you had said.
translation_verse: Nomoa, yaa bera kaa ya mɛɛ be la, ya kaa bol waa bwa haa bola la o be.

english_verse: Later our father sent us back here to buy more grain.
translation_verse: O berɔ ŋɔ ya be ŋɔ ya berɛ ba dɛ́ ba yawɛ kondikwaa tama.

english_verse: But we told him, “We can't go back to Egypt without our youngest brother. We will never be let in to see the governor, unless he is with us.”
translation_verse: Asɛ ya chaŋo ŋɔ yaa won la. Ya ɡbo laŋɔ dɛ ya nime nɔ ta ya nɛɛ jae yaa, yaa won la o sie. Dɛ ya nime la ɛɛ lao tenaa, ya ɡee lao.

english_verse: Sir, our father then reminded us that his favorite wife had given birth to two sons.
translation_verse: Anee ya mɛɛ ŋɔ ya be ŋɔ ya ɡbabir jemɔ ŋɔ bibaala banɛ ɡboo Rakɛl lolɛ tɛo.

english_verse: One of them was already missing and had not been seen for a long time. My father thinks the boy was torn to pieces by some wild animal,
translation_verse: Beŋkpoŋ te le o nɔn ta. O jemɔ kɛŋɔ kpɔɡ bini ola ka toɡri o bini, o ta on nae kpa ba le fini.

english_verse: and he said, “I am an old man. If you take Benjamin from me, and something happens to him, I will die of a broken heart.”
translation_verse: Ya berɔ kpɔ onɔ le o nɔn ta taraken asɛ waane ka ɛɔ waa, waa hwɛɛhra tonɛ nɔ, tebinichɔɡ ɡboo dɛɛ ba o kpoe.”

english_verse: That's why Benjamin must be with us when I go back to my father. He loves him so much
translation_verse: “Nomoa, taraken n berɔ kaa n mɛɛ be dɛ ya nime nɔ ta jae yaa, wɛɛ sewɔɔ. O dɛ nyinu kohona,

english_verse: that he will die if Benjamin doesn't come back with me.
translation_verse: ɡɛ waa hwɛɛhra la, dɛ o ta ya nɛɛ jae yaa, sum ɡbo ɛɛ kpoo.
