english_verse: I promised my father that I would bring him safely home. If I don't, I told my father he could blame me the rest of my life.
translation_verse: Anɔ la aa jaa laanee kɛŋɔ, n lɛ bie nɔ waa dawɛ n nɛ. N baɡɛ n mɛɛ nyoa kɛŋɔ dɛ n ta o ne balaa, menee waa dawɛ n nɛ n soɡa bini bwa.

english_verse: Sir, I am your slave. Please let me stay here in place of Benjamin and let him return home with his brothers.
translation_verse: Anomanta, nomoa, n dɛ́ soŋe, mɛɛ chiɡ bie nɔ naa taa, dɛ́ so dɛ́ ɛ he yom, ásɛ o pu o dɔɔranar kaa.

english_verse: How can I face my father if Benjamin isn't with me? I couldn't bear to see my father in such sorrow.
translation_verse: Dɛ bie nɔ ta n nɛɛ teŋaa, ɛrɛɛ mɛɛ ba ɛɛ dɛ́ won la n mɛɛ be nɔ? Maa won ka na wechɔɡa aa dɛ ba n mɛɛ nɛɛ bala.”

english_verse: Since Joseph could no longer control his feelings in front of his servants, he sent them out of the room. When he was alone with his brothers, he told them, “I am Joseph.”
translation_verse: Josef ta wone lawɛ o te o bonɔɔna la sie, o kpɔ takpeɡ ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ nomɛlbwa le buse, asɛ dɛ kpɔ o te baɡle o dɔɔranar la.

english_verse: Then he cried so loudly that the Egyptians heard him and told about it in the king's palace.
translation_verse: O wio kohona, asɛ Ijipt harɛ tena la no, kooro dem tena la bwa no.

english_verse: Joseph asked his brothers if his father was still alive, but they were too frightened to answer.
translation_verse: A habɔɔ la, Josef ŋɔ o dɔɔranar la be ŋɔ, “Menee Josef. N mɛɛ ta lole naa?” Waa bɔɔ ba ɡɛ la, ba ta wone chaŋe wobɛlbwa, dɛkalkɛ ɔmee laɡ ba.

english_verse: Joseph told them to come closer to him, and when they did, he said: Yes, I am your brother Joseph, the one you sold into Egypt.
translation_verse: Anee o ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, “N poo heya, hé suuh tel mɛ.” Baa suuhna telo la, asɛ o ŋɔ, “Menee he nime Josef haa yoɡ mɛ tɛ Ijipt tena la.

english_verse: Don't worry or blame yourselves for what you did. God is the one who sent me ahead of you to save lives.
translation_verse: He bɛ ɡel a we he nɛ, he bɛ he te pwah kɛŋɔ haa yoɡ mɛ. Korowiirii cheɡa ɡɛ dɛ lee mɛ, n tɔ he sie dɛ́ ba lɛ nɛra mkpa.

english_verse: There has already been a famine for two years, and for five more years no one will plow fields or harvest grain.
translation_verse: Lɔr nɔ bene anɛɛ la. A ta ka bene anue nomɛlbwa aa wola won du kwaa a ba ɛ kɛŋɔ wɛɛ dɔ kondikwaa.

english_verse: But God sent me on ahead of you to keep your families alive and to save you in this wonderful way.
translation_verse: Korowiirii cheɡa ɡɛ, dɛ lee mɛ ŋɔ n tɔ he sie, dɛ́ ba lɛ heyaa ɡɛ nyokpoa ŋwɛnɛ nɔ ta, ásɛ he ne he naanar dɔ mkpa.

english_verse: After all, you weren't really the ones who sent me here—it was God. He made me the highest official in the king's court and placed me over all Egypt.
translation_verse: He laa ba n ne bonɔ, Korowiirii ba n ne. Onee ɛɛ mɛ nomonjen n ja kooro nɛɛ dɛɛ nyiŋi o dem tena ne Ijipt harɛ bwa ta.

english_verse: Now hurry back and tell my father that his son Joseph says, “God has made me ruler of Egypt. Come here as quickly as you can.
translation_verse: He ɛ warane ka ŋɔ n mɛɛ be ŋɔ men o bie Josef ŋɔ, ‘Korowii ɛɛ mɛ nomonjen Ijipt harɛ bwa ta.’ Ó ba n be warane.

english_verse: You will live near me in the region of Goshen with your children and grandchildren, as well as with your sheep, goats, cattle, and everything else you own.
translation_verse: Ó ba, dɛ́ ba so Gosen waa lɔ Ijipt harɛ nɔ ta dɛ́ bɛn mɛ. Ó kpɔ o bii ne o naanar ne peera ne boohna, ne o nae dɛ komɛlbwa waa dɔa ba.

english_verse: I will take care of you there during the next five years of famine. But if you don't come, you and your family and your animals will starve to death.”
translation_verse: O baa so Gosen aa, anee mɛɛ ba wona nyiŋu. Lɔr nɔ ta ka bene anue, anomanta, maa nyin kɛŋɔ lɔr kpo o ne o bii ne kondɛɛra.”

english_verse: All of you, including my brother Benjamin, can tell by what I have said that I really am Joseph.
translation_verse: O berɔ ŋɔ, “Taraken, he ne Bɛnjamen bwa nao kɛŋɔ menee dɛɛ bol waa he be la.

english_verse: Tell my father about my great power here in Egypt and about everything you have seen. Hurry and bring him here.
translation_verse: He ka ŋɔ n mɛɛ be n kpeɡri maa dɔɔ Ijipt harɛ ta bonɔ, ne wobɛlbwa haa naa bonɔ bwa, ásɛ dɛ ɛ warane, dɛ́ kpɔɔ ba n be bonɔ.”

english_verse: Joseph was still crying as he kissed each of his other brothers. After this, they started talking with Joseph.
translation_verse: O mo o dɔɔranar la lwɛrɛme dɛ wi. Asɛ a habɔɔ o ne ba bol wa.

english_verse: When it was told in the palace that Joseph's brothers had come, the king and his officials were happy.
translation_verse: Baa no koodem kɛŋɔ Josef dɔɔranar balɔ la, kooro ne o nomonome bwa sie lɛo.

english_verse: So the king said to Joseph: Tell your brothers to load their donkeys and return to Canaan.
translation_verse: Asɛ kooro ŋɔ Josef be ŋɔ ó ŋɔ o dɔɔranar la be ŋɔ bá kpɔ ba bone la dawɛ keeɡore la ta, ásɛ dɛ berɛ kaa Keenan harɛ ta,

english_verse: Tell them to bring their father and their families here. I will give them the best land in Egypt, and they can eat and enjoy everything that grows there.
translation_verse: dɛ́ ka kpɔ ba mɛɛ ne ba bii ne ba dem tena bwa ba Ijipt harɛ ta. Dɛ́ wɛɛ tɛɛ baa bela waa wera Ijipt harɛ ta bonɔɔ, ásɛ ba dɔ komɛlbwa baa dɛ nyin.

english_verse: Also tell your brothers to take some wagons from Egypt for their wives and children to ride in. And be sure they bring their father.
translation_verse: Berɛ ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ bá kpɔ kwaa aa dɔ tɔre baa taɡa kɛ torɔɡo ba vɔwɛ pɛl jaɡre, dɛ́ ka kpɔ ba haahna ne bii, dɛ́ kpɔ ba mɛɛ ɡe ba.

english_verse: They can leave their possessions behind, because they will be given the best of everything in Egypt.
translation_verse: Ba bɛ komɛlbwa waa lii a we ba nɛ. Kondɛɛɡa aa lɔ Ijipt harɛ ta la bwa ɛ ba kwa.

english_verse: Jacob's sons agreed to do what the king had said. And Joseph gave them wagons and food for their trip home, just as the king had ordered.
translation_verse: Anomanta, Jekɔb bii la ɛ ɡɛ baa bol ba be la bwa. Josef kpɔ torɔɡore baa vɔwa pɛl jaɡre la ane tɛɛ ba ɡɛ kooro aa bola la. Asɛ dɛ tɛɛ ba kondikwaa baa di ŋwɛnɛ ta ɡe ja.

english_verse: Joseph gave some new clothes to each of his brothers, but to Benjamin he gave five new outfits and
translation_verse: O berɔ tɛ ba bini bɛlbwa laalafala, dɛ tɛ Bɛnjamen te suuɡapoŋa lafraatoro ne laalafala bele anue.

english_verse: To his father he sent ten donkeys loaded with the best things in Egypt, and ten other donkeys loaded with grain and bread and other food for the return trip.
translation_verse: Dɛ kpɔ Ijipt harɛ laala aa wera kohona tɛ ŋɔ ba ka tɛ o mɛɛ, keeɡore fii cheɡaa, asɛ keeɡoneenanar fi ɡe che boyu ne kondikwaa bwa soo siwi waa di ŋwɛnɛ ta dɛ́ berɛ ba.

english_verse: Then he sent his brothers off and told them, “Don't argue on the way home!”
translation_verse: O kaa do o dɔɔranar ŋwɛnɛ asɛ baa dɛ kaa la, o ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, “Hɛɛ berɛ ka yoi ŋwɛnɛ ta noo!”

english_verse: Joseph's brothers left Egypt, and when they arrived in Canaan,
translation_verse: Ba le Ijipt harɛ ta dɛ ba Keenan harɛ ta ba mɛɛ be.

english_verse: they told their father that Joseph was still alive and was the ruler of Egypt. But their father was so surprised that he could not believe them.
translation_verse: Baa tel ba mɛɛ be dem la, ba bol o be ŋɔ, “Josef ta lole! Onee dɛɛ nyiŋi Ijipt harɛ ta.” Baa bol ɡɛ o mɛɛ be la, o nyoa kpoo, o ta ɡɛ waa ɛ nae.

english_verse: and said, “Now I can believe you! My son Joseph must really be alive, and I will get to see him before I die.”
translation_verse: Asɛ o ŋɔ, “Anɔɔ mɛɛ nyin dɛ́ no. N bie Josef ta lole! Mɛɛ lao ka nao mɔɔ dɛ́ sewɛ.”

english_verse: Jacob packed up everything he owned and left for Egypt. On the way he stopped near the town of Beersheba and offered sacrifices to the God his father Isaac had worshiped.
translation_verse: Jekɔb kpɔ kwaa waa dɔa bwa, dɛ chiɡ ŋwɛnɛ ta, dɛ ba tel Beɛseeba. O kpoo kwaa ɛ saraha tɛ Korowii o mɛɛ Aesek aa tomɔ la bela.

english_verse: That night, God spoke to him in a dream and said, “Jacob! Jacob!” “Here I am,” Jacob answered.
translation_verse: Korowii kpɔ o te baɡlo bela deera ta jwaana dɛ yerɔ ŋɔ, “Jekɔb.” Asɛ o sɛh dɛ ŋɔ, “Menee la.”

english_verse: God said, “I am God, the same God your father worshiped. Don't be afraid to go to Egypt. I will give you so many descendants that one day they will become a nation.
translation_verse: Belaa Korowii ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Menee Korowii he mɛɛwa aa tom mɛ la. Bɛ ɔmɛ kɛŋɔ he dɛ kaa Ijipt harɛ ta. Mɛɛ ɡeloo he mun ya bela taeh.

english_verse: I will go with you to Egypt, and later I will bring your descendants back here. Your son Joseph will be at your side when you die.”
translation_verse: Mɛɛ teŋɛ he nɛɛ kaa bela, ásɛ dɛ berɛ ba he naanar ne a ɡɛ Keenan harɛ nɔ ta. He dɛ ba sewaa, Josef ɛɛ lawɛɛ he sewɛ.”

english_verse: When Jacob went to Egypt, his children who were born in northern Syria also went along with their families. Jacob and his wife Leah had a total of
translation_verse: A ɡɛ bibaala nɔɔ Lea lolɛ tɛ Jekɔb ɡɛ saŋ baa soɡe Mɛsopoteemea harɛ ta Daena waa ɛ o bihaah la habɔɔ. Dɛ o bihaahna ne bibaala dɛ naanar o ne Lea aa dɔa la bwa lɔ fifraatoro dɛ batoro.

english_verse: The king will call you in and ask what you do for a living.
translation_verse: Dɛ Kooro baa yerɛ heya dɛ bɔɔ toma haa dɛ ɛ wa aa,

english_verse: Jacob and Zilpah, the servant woman Laban had given his daughter Leah, had a total of
translation_verse: A ɡɛ bibaala fi dɛ banumɛl nɔɔ Silpa waa ɛ Lea tolo la lolɛ ba ɛ o ne Jekɔb naanar. Onee Laban lawɛ tɛ o bihaah Lea tolo la.

english_verse: Jacob and Bilhah, the servant woman Laban had given his daughter Rachel, had seven children and grandchildren. Their son Dan took his son Hushim. Their son Naphtali took his sons Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer, and Shillem.
translation_verse: A ɡɛ bibaala banuanɛ nɔɔ Bilha waa ɛ tolo Laban aa lawa tɛ o bihaah Rakɛl la lolɛ, ba ɛ Jekɔb bibaala ne naanar.

english_verse: Sixty-six members of Jacob's family went to Egypt with him, not counting his daughters-in-law.
translation_verse: Jekɔb naanar baa teŋɛ o nɛɛ dɛ la Ijipt la lɔ fifraanumɛl dɛ banumɛl. O bibaala haahna te ta jae.

english_verse: Jacob's two grandsons who were born there made it a total of
translation_verse: Josef lolɛ bibaala banɛ Ijipt. Anomanta, dɛ ba jao waa, dɛ Jekɔb ne o bii dɛ o naanar baa la Ijipt la lɔ fifraanuanɛ.

english_verse: Jacob had sent his son Judah ahead of him to ask Joseph to meet them in Goshen.
translation_verse: Baa dɛ tel Ijipt la, Jekɔb tomɛ Juda ŋɔ ó la ka ŋɔ Josef be ŋɔ ó ba tɔ o sie dɛ́ kaa o ne Gosen harɛ. Baa tel bela la,

english_verse: So Joseph got in his chariot and went to meet his father. When they met, Joseph hugged his father around the neck and cried for a long time.
translation_verse: Josef jo o kon waa do kɛŋɔ torɔɡo la bɛl bini, asɛ dɛ ka cheme o mɛɛ. Baa chema la, Josef ɡbaaro pɛl o te dɛ wi taeh.

english_verse: Jacob said to Joseph, “Now that I have seen you and know you are still alive, I am ready to die.”
translation_verse: Belaa Jekɔb ŋɔ Josef be ŋɔ, “Taraken maa nae dɛ jemɛ kɛŋɔ he ta soɡe le nɔ, mɛɛ won sewɛ name.”

english_verse: Then Joseph said to his brothers and to everyone who had come with them: I must go and tell the king that you have arrived from Canaan.
translation_verse: Asɛ Josef ŋɔ o dɔɔranar ne o mɛɛ lolanar baa kaa la be ŋɔ, “A chɛ kɛ ń la ka ŋɔ kooro be ŋɔ n dɔɔranar ne n mɛɛ lolanar bwa baa soɡe Keenan harɛ ta la ba n be.

english_verse: I will tell him that you are shepherds and that you have brought your sheep, goats, cattle, and everything else you own.
translation_verse: Mɛɛ ŋɔ o bee ŋɔ he ɛ peteɡra dɛɛ nyiŋi kondɛɛra ta, anomanta, he ba he kondɛɛra ne he kwaa haa dɔa bwa ne.

english_verse: When he does, be sure to say, “We are shepherds. Our families have always raised sheep.” If you tell him this, he will let you settle in the region of Goshen. Joseph wanted them to say this to the king, because the Egyptians did not like to be around anyone who raised sheep.
translation_verse: hé nyiŋi kɛrɛdɛ dɛ́ ŋɔ o be ŋɔ haa ira bwa, kondɛɛra ta nyiŋa toma ɡboo hɛɛ ɛ ɡɛ ya naawa aa ɛa wubwa la. O no ɡɛ naa, wɛɛ ɡeloo he so Gosen harɛ bonɔ.” Dɛ Ijipt tena kii peteɡra, a waa Josef ŋɔ ba ŋɔ ɡɛ la.

english_verse: who asked them, “What do you do for a living?” “Sir, we are shepherds,” was their answer. “Our families have always raised sheep.
translation_verse: Belaa kooro bɔɔ ba ŋɔ, “Bɔkwa tomaa hɛɛ ɛɔ?” Asɛ ba chaŋe ŋɔ, “Nomoa, ya ɛ peteɡra kɛŋɔ ya naawa fa aa ɛa la.

english_verse: But in our country all the pastures are dried up, and our sheep have no grass to eat. So we, your servants, have come here. Please let us live in the region of Goshen.”
translation_verse: Ya balɔ dɛ́ ba so harɛ nɔ ta, dɛkalkɛ lɔr chole Keenan harɛ ta taeh, kondikwaa toole ya kondɛɛra kwaraa di. Nomoa, ya dɛ soŋe kɛ he tɛ yaa bɔr ya so Gosen harɛ ta.”

english_verse: The king said to Joseph, “It's good that your father and brothers have arrived.
translation_verse: Ate, kooro ŋɔ Josef be ŋɔ, “Taraken he mɛɛ ne he dɔɔranar aa bala nɔ,

english_verse: I will let them live anywhere they choose in the land of Egypt, but I suggest that they settle in Goshen, the best part of our land. I would also like for your finest shepherds to watch after my own sheep and goats.”
translation_verse: Ijipt harɛɛ chɔa kaa la. Harɛ la bela waa wera la, kpɔ he mɛɛ ne he dɔɔranar ka so o ta. Dɛ he nyiŋi ba bini dɛ na kɛŋɔ bane ɛɛ won nyiŋi kondɛɛra ta kɛrɛdɛ naa, kpɔ n ɡbaɡba kondɛɛra la do ba nɔn ta.”

english_verse: Then Joseph brought his father Jacob and introduced him to the king. Jacob gave the king his blessing,
translation_verse: Belaa Josef ka kpɔ o mɛɛ Jekɔb ba baɡle kooro la, asɛ Jekɔb swee andɛɛɡa tɛ kooro,

english_verse: and the king asked him, “How old are you?”
translation_verse: asɛ kooro la bɔɔ Jekɔb ŋɔ, “He di bene aŋwɛnɛ ɔ?”

english_verse: Then Jacob gave the king his blessing once again and left.
translation_verse: Asɛ Jekɔb swee andɛɛɡa tɛ kooro ja dɛ kpɔ kalo.

english_verse: Joseph obeyed the king's orders and gave his father and brothers some of the best land in Egypt near the city of Rameses.
translation_verse: Josef kpɔ o mɛɛ ne o dɔɔranar ka so harɛ la ta, bela waa wera ŋɔ ó ɛ ba kon, ɡɛ kooro aa bola la. Dɛ bela bɛne bwɛjen Rameses, Gosen bela.

english_verse: The famine was bad everywhere in Egypt and Canaan, and the people were suffering terribly.
translation_verse: Lɔr bɛl baa chole Ijipt harɛ ta dɛ o nyoa kpeɡri kohona. Anomanta, kondikwaa toole bobɛlbwa kpa dɛ ɡwɛɡre Ijipt ne Keenan tena bwa.

english_verse: So Joseph sold them the grain that had been stored up, and he put the money in the king's treasury.
translation_verse: Nɛra baa yawɛ boyu aa, ɡɛɛ Josef kpɔ suuɡa la kaa koodem ka cheɡ.

english_verse: But when everyone had run out of money, the Egyptians came to Joseph and demanded, “Give us more grain! If you don't, we'll soon be dead, because our money's all gone.”
translation_verse: Ijipt tena ne Keenan tena baa di ba suuɡare tonɛ, asɛ Ijipt tena ba Josef be dɛ ba ŋɔ, “Lɔr kpo yaa yaa ba serewa. Ya suuɡare bwa tonɔ. Tɛ yaa kondikwa.”

english_verse: “If you don't have any money,” Joseph answered, “give me your animals, and I'll let you have some grain.”
translation_verse: Belaa Josef chaŋe dɛ ŋɔ, “Dɛ he suuɡa tonɔ aa, hé ka lawɛ kondɛɛra ba charɛ kondikwa.”

english_verse: Then the people came to him and said: Sir, there's no way we can hide the truth from you. We are broke, and we don't have any more animals. We have nothing left except ourselves and our land.
translation_verse: Benanyoa aa chema la, ba berɔ ba o be dɛ ba ŋɔ, “Nomoa, yaa ya wobɛlbwaa kpɔ sɔeh. Ya suuɡare bwa tonɔ, asɛ ya kondɛɛra bwa ɡe ɛ he kwa. Taraken komɛlbwa toole ya be ka ja ya bwadabii ne ya harɛre ta.

english_verse: Don't let us starve and our land be ruined. If you'll give us grain to eat and seed to plant, we'll sell ourselves and our land to the king. We'll become his slaves.
translation_verse: Bɛ ɡel ya serewe! Bɛ ɡel ya harɛ chɔ pɛɛ. Yawɛ ya ne ya harɛre, dɛ́ tɛ yaa kondikwa. Yaa ɛ kooro bonɔɔnaa, ásɛ o kpɔ ya harɛre ɡe ja. Tɛ yaa kondikwaa ya ka di dɛ́ dɔ mkpa, dɛ́ tɛ yaa kondwee yá kpɔ ka du ya harɛ ta, ásɛ dɛ bɛ serewe.”

english_verse: The famine became so severe that Joseph finally bought every piece of land in Egypt for the king
translation_verse: Anomanta, Josef yawɛ Ijipt harɛ bwa, dɛ kpɔ tɛ kooro. Lɔr la nyoa aa kana kohona nomanta, nomɛlbwa waa lɔ Ijipt yoɡ o harɛ, asɛ a bwa ba do kooro lɔɡa.

english_verse: and made everyone the king's slaves,
translation_verse: Josef kpɔ nɛra baa lɔ Ijipt harɛ ta bwa ɛ o nɛndɔɔla.

english_verse: except the priests. The king gave the priests a regular food allowance, so they did not have to sell their land.
translation_verse: Sɔfore ɡbo harɛɛ kaa ba ta yawɛ. Ba te ta ba harɛ yoɡe, dɛkalkɛ dɛ kooro tɛɛ ba kondikwaa baa di.

english_verse: Then Joseph said to the people, “You and your land now belong to the king. I'm giving you seed to plant,
translation_verse: Josef ŋɔ nɛra la be ŋɔ, “He nao maa yawɛ he ne he harɛre dɛ tɛ kooro kenɛ? Kondwee laanee la, hé kpɔ dɛ́ ka du harɛ la ta.

english_verse: but one fifth of your crops must go to the king. You can keep the rest as seed or as food for your families.”
translation_verse: A ɡɛ saŋ a koma aa ba tel la, a chɛ kɛ he bɔne a bini bɔre anue, dɛ́ kpɔ bɔrbeŋkpoŋ ba tɛ kooro. Ásɛ dɛ ɡe kpɔ a kar, dɛ́ kpɔ ane ɛ dwee cheɡ, ásɛ he ne he dem tena ɡe di a kabora.”

english_verse: “Sir, you have saved our lives!” they answered. “We are glad to be slaves of the king.”
translation_verse: Asɛ ba chaŋe ŋɔ, “Nomoa, he lɛ ya nyu dɛ nyiŋi yaa kɛrɛdɛ. Yaa ɛ kooro bonɔɔnaa.”

english_verse: Then Joseph made a law that one fifth of the harvest would always belong to the king. Only the priests did not lose their land. Jacob Becomes an Old Man
translation_verse: Anomanta, Josef ɛ mmara harɛ la ta kɛŋɔ nomɛlbwa komɛ o koo kwa aa, ó bɔne a bini bɔre anue, dɛ́ kpɔ bɔrbeŋkpoŋ ba tɛ kooro. A ɡɛ mmara la ta lɔ Ijipt harɛ ta ba le fini. Nemenɛ harɛ waa ɛ sɔfore kon la ɡboo wola jae.

english_verse: The people of Israel made their home in the land of Goshen, where they became prosperous and had large families.
translation_verse: Israel tena soɡe Ijipt harɛ Gosen pera, dɛ dɔ kondɔɔh asɛ ba mun ɡe ya kohona.

english_verse: When Jacob knew he did not have long to live, he called in Joseph and said, “If you really love me, you must make a solemn promise not to bury me in Egypt.
translation_verse: O seo tɔpere aa dɛ tel la, o yerɛ Josef dɛ ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Kpɔ nɔn do n hwie baah dɛ́ ŋwɛɛ kɛŋɔ nyina haa dɛ nyin mɛ ne kasinteŋ haa dɔa kohona tɛ mɛ nomanta, n sewaa, haa men Ijipt harɛ taa huɡe.

english_verse: Instead, bury me in the place where my ancestors are buried.” “I will do what you have asked,” Joseph answered.
translation_verse: N dɛ nyin kɛ he ka huɡ mɛ bela baa huɡe n mɛɛwa. Kaa n ne bela ka huɡe.” Asɛ Josef sɛh ŋɔ, “Mɛɛ ɛ ɡɛɛ.”

english_verse: “Will you give me your word?” Jacob asked. “Yes, I will,” Joseph promised. After this, Jacob bowed down and prayed at the head of his bed.
translation_verse: Anee Jekɔb ŋɔ, “Ŋwɛɛ kɛŋɔ hɛɛ ɛ ɡɛɛ.” Asɛ o ɡe ŋwɛɛ, asɛ Jekɔb ɡuŋi mpa ta dɛ jam Korowii.

english_verse: Joseph was told that his father Jacob had become very sick. So Joseph went to see him and took along his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim.
translation_verse: Awola bɛl, ba baa ŋɔ Josef be ŋɔ o mɛɛ bwara dɛ weo. Belaa o kpɔ o bibaala banɛ, Manasɛ ne Efrem asɛ ba ka nao.

english_verse: When Joseph arrived, someone told Jacob, “Your son Joseph has come to see you.” Jacob sat up in bed, but it took almost all his strength.
translation_verse: Jekɔb aa noa kɛŋɔ o bie Josef balɔ dɛ́ ba nao la, o takapɔ dɛ ir so mpa ta.

english_verse: Jacob told Joseph: God All-Powerful appeared to me at Luz in the land of Canaan, where he gave me his blessing
translation_verse: Jekɔb ŋɔ Josef be ŋɔ, “Korowii Waa Ɛ Kpeɡri Bwa Dɔɔ la kpɔ o te baɡ mɛ Bɛtel baa bera dɛɛ yerɔ Lus, Keenan harɛ ta dɛ swee andɛɛɡa tɛ mɛ.

english_verse: and promised, “I will give you a large family with many descendants that will grow into a nation. And I am giving you this land that will belong to you and your family forever.”
translation_verse: O baɡ mɛ nyoa ŋɔ, ‘Mɛɛ ɡeloo he mun ya, ásɛ he naanar warɛ kohona. Mɛɛ kpɔ harɛ nɔɔ tɛ he naanar ó ɛ ba kon saŋ bɛlbwa dɛɛ la.’ ”

english_verse: Then Jacob went on to say: Joseph, your two sons Ephraim and Manasseh were born in Egypt, but I accept them as my own, just as Reuben and Simeon are mine.
translation_verse: Jekɔb berɔ ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “He bibaala banɛ, Manasɛ ne Efrem haa lol ba Ijipt mɔɔ n ba la bwa ɛ n kwa, kɛŋɔ n bibaala Rubin ne Simeon.

english_verse: Any children you have later will be considered yours, but their inheritance will come from Ephraim and Manasseh.
translation_verse: Dɛ he dɔ bii bane ja kwaraa naa, n kwaa laa ba te. Ba kapɛrɛ diile ɛɛ le Manasɛ ne Efrem luɡe taa.

english_verse: Unfortunately, your mother Rachel died in Canaan after we had left northern Syria and before we reached Bethlehem. And I had to bury her along the way.
translation_verse: He nya Rakɛl waa mɛɛ ɛ ɡɛ la. Maa le Mɛsopoteemea harɛ ta dɛɛ ba la, o baa sewɛ Keenan harɛ ta. Bela lɔ Efrat ŋwɛnɛ nyoa asɛ n huɡo bela.” Ba berɔ dɛɛ yerɛ Efrat la, Bɛtlɛham fini.

english_verse: Jacob turned to Joseph and told him, “For many years I thought you were dead and that I would never see you again. But now God has even let me live to see your children.”
translation_verse: Anee Jekɔb ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “N ta liire ŋɔ mɛɛ nae kpa. Kɛ Korowii ɡelɔ n nae, hale dɛ berɛ na he bii ɡe.”

english_verse: Then Joseph made his sons move away from Jacob's knees, and Joseph bowed down in front of him with his face to the ground.
translation_verse: Belaa Josef ɡɔɔ ba le o mɛɛ nakpale ta, asɛ dɛ kpɔ sie pi harɛ o sie.

english_verse: But before Jacob gave them his blessing, he crossed his arms, putting his right hand on the head of Ephraim and his left hand on the head of Manasseh.
translation_verse: kɛ Jekɔb aa dɛ ba soŋa tɛɛ ba la, o ɡaɡre nɔɔra dɛ kpɔ nɔndiɡ dawɛ Efrem waa ɛ bechala la nyu ta, asɛ dɛ kpɔ nɔŋɡal dawɛ Manasɛ waa ɛ nomoa la ɡe nyu ta.

english_verse: Then he gave Joseph his blessing and said: My grandfather Abraham and my father Isaac worshiped the Lord God. He has been with me all my life,
translation_verse: Asɛ o soŋe tɛ Josef ŋɔ, “Korowii n mɛɛ Abraham ne Aesek aa tomɔ la swee bii nɔ andɛɛɡa. Korowii waa dɛ nyiŋi n nɛɛ, dɛ ba le fini tɔpere nɔ swee ba andɛɛɡa.

english_verse: and his angel has kept me safe. Now I pray that he will bless these boys and that my name and the names of Abraham and Isaac will live on because of them. I ask God to give them many children and many descendants as well.
translation_verse: Korowii torome waa lee mɛ le n wenaale bwa ta la swee bii nɔ andɛɛɡa. Korowii ɡel n sɔn ne n mɛɛ Abraham ne Aesek sɔn teŋɛ ba nɛ. Korowii ɡel ba dɔ bii ne naanar kohona.”

english_verse: Joseph did not like it when he saw his father place his right hand on the head of the younger son. So he tried to move his father's right hand from Ephraim's head and place it on Manasseh.
translation_verse: Josef aa naa kɛŋɔ o mɛɛ kpɔ nɔn diɡ dawɛ Efrem nyu ta la, a ta o som doe. Anomanta, o laa o mɛɛ nɔn kpɔ Efrem nyu ta, dɛ kpɔ ba dawɛ Manasɛ nyu ta.

english_verse: Joseph said, “Father, you have made a mistake. This is the older boy. Put your right hand on him.”
translation_verse: Asɛ dɛ ŋɔ, “N mɛɛ, Manasɛɛ binomoa, kpɔ he nɔndiɡ dawɛ o nyu ta.”

english_verse: But his father said, “Son, I know what I am doing. It's true that Manasseh's family will someday become a great nation. But Ephraim will be even greater than Manasseh, because his descendants will become many great nations.”
translation_verse: O mɛɛ ta sɛɛh dɛ ŋɔ, “N jemɔ, n bie. Manasɛ naanar ɡe ɛɛ warɔɔ dɛ́ ɛ nɛnjena. Kɛ o nime ɛɛ ba ɛ nɛnjenii ɡwaalo, ásɛ o naanar ɡe warɛ kohona.”

english_verse: Jacob told him that in the future the people of Israel would ask God's blessings on one another by saying, “I pray for God to bless you as much as he blessed Ephraim and Manasseh.” Jacob put Ephraim's name first to show that he would be greater than Manasseh.
translation_verse: Anomanta, o swee andɛɛɡa tɛɛ ba awola tɔpere la dɛ ŋɔ, “Israel tena dɛ ba andɛɛɡa sweeraa, baa ŋɔɔ, ‘Korowii ɡel he do kɛŋɔ Efrem ne Manasɛ.’ ” A waa o kpɔ Efrem sɔn tɔ Manasɛ sie la.

english_verse: After that, Jacob said, “Joseph, you can see that I won't live much longer. But God will be with you and will lead you back to the land he promised our family long ago.
translation_verse: Jekɔb ŋɔ Josef be ŋɔ, “Taraken n seo telo, kɛ Korowiirii dɛ́ teŋɛ he nɛ, dɛ́ berɛ kpɔ heyaa ba Keenan, waa ɛ he naawa harɛ ta.

english_verse: Jacob called his sons together and said: My sons, I am Jacob, your father Israel.
translation_verse: Jekɔb yerɛ o bibaala asɛ dɛ ŋɔ, “Hé bwa ba cheme, ásɛ n baɡle heyaa waa aa dɛ ba he nɛɛ bala kerekere.

english_verse: Come, gather around, as I tell your future.
translation_verse: Hé bwa ba cheme dɛ no. Hé ba no he mɛɛ Jekɔb wa.

english_verse: Reuben, you are my oldest, born at the peak of my powers; you were an honored leader.
translation_verse: Rubin haa ɛ n binyoa nɔ, henee n kpeɡri. Henee n tɔ sie lolɛ n bonɔɔne saŋ, dɛ dɔ jirima ne bokpeɡa ɡwaa n bii bwa.

english_verse: Uncontrollable as a flood, you slept with my wife and disgraced my bed. And so you no longer deserve the place of honor.
translation_verse: He we-ɛɛla do kɛŋɔ nehɛma, he jirima tonɔ. Dɛkalkɛ he lawɛ n hanɛɛte chɔ n chɔɔbɔr, dɛ kpɔ doŋa kah mɛ.

english_verse: Simeon and Levi, you are brothers, each a gruesome sword.
translation_verse: Simeon ne Lewi ɛ nimanar. Ba kpɔ ba dɔmkwaa dɛɛ ba yoi ne.

english_verse: I never want to take part in your plans or deeds. You slaughtered people in your anger, and you crippled cattle for no reason.
translation_verse: Maa ba nɛɛ ja ba wobɛlbwa baa vɔrɔwe ta. Ba baah diu waa, ba dɛ kpoo nɛra, dɛɛ ŋwɛne nae ɡe nakpale pɛɛpɛɛ á bɛ won valɛ.

english_verse: Now I place a curse on you because of your fierce anger. Your descendants will be scattered among the tribes of Israel.
translation_verse: Ba bandia ne ba nyubinikpeɡ nomanta, bá bwɛɛlɛ! Mɛɛ lɔ ba naanaree peɡre Israel harɛ bwa. Dɛ laɡ ba le ba nɛra bini.

english_verse: Judah, you will be praised by your brothers; they will bow down to you, as you defeat your enemies.
translation_verse: Juda, he dɔɔranar ɛɛ duurii, ásɛ he nɔn dawɛ he dɔma nɛ. He dɔɔranar ɛɛ ba ɡuŋi he siee.

english_verse: My son, you are a lion ready to eat your victim! You are terribly fierce; no one will bother you.
translation_verse: Juda do kɛŋɔ nyujente ken. Kpaahna taa he che dɛ kpeɡ. O chɔ harɛ kɛ nyujente aa, umee dɛ wonu wɔ?

english_verse: You will have power and rule until nations obey you and come bringing gifts.
translation_verse: Koodaŋɡbala aa o nɔn ta lee ba, mmarare doe ɡe aa o habɔɔ le, ásɛ harɛre nɛra kpɔ koŋkɛɛla baa tɛo, dɛ́ ba ɡuŋi o sie dɛɛ duuru.

english_verse: You will tie your donkey to a choice grapevine and wash your clothes in wine from those grapes.
translation_verse: Daa baa kpɔ o nɔna dɛɛ ɛ sen la taa wɛɛ ba o keeɡo bie lawa vɔwɛ. A sen nee wɛɛ ba o laala chɛɡa.

english_verse: Your eyes are darker than wine, your teeth whiter than milk.
translation_verse: Sen ɛɛ ɡeloo o sibie swɛɛ, ásɛ na-elne kohona ɡe ɡel o nyena to.

english_verse: Zebulun, you will settle along the seashore and provide safe harbors as far north as Sidon.
translation_verse: Sebulon sobɔree mpo nyoa, o jwɛh ka tel Sidon, ásɛ stiimaere che bela wobɛlbwa aa wola an ɛ.

english_verse: Issachar, you are a strong donkey resting in the meadows.
translation_verse: Isaaka do kɛŋɔ keeɡo ɡwaŋe, dɛ chɔ o bone baah ta,

english_verse: You found them so pleasant that you worked too hard and became a slave.
translation_verse: o nao kɛŋɔ bela waa dɛ ba ona la ɛ bodɛɛɡe asɛ silɛɛ do bela aa, wɛɛ kpɔ vaamaa lɛa, dɛ́ kpɔ o te tɛ tomkpeɡa.

english_verse: Dan, you are the tribe that will bring justice to Israel.
translation_verse: Dan ɛɛ ba nyiŋi o nɛra nɛɛ. Baa doo kɛŋɔ Israel deene aa kaa la.

english_verse: You are a snake that bites the heel of a horse, making its rider fall.
translation_verse: Wɛɛ ɛɔ kɛŋɔ domkpule, dɛ́ chɔ ŋwɛnɛ nyoa, dɛ́ choɡe jaaɡɔ nakpala, ásɛ nɛn waa soɡe o ta la ka le habɔɔ.

english_verse: Our Lord, I am waiting for you to save us.
translation_verse: N Naa Korowii, n soɡoo dɛɛ kpa kɛŋɔ he ba dɛ́ ba lɛ yaa.

english_verse: Gad, you will be attacked, then attack your attackers.
translation_verse: Ŋwɛɛra ɛɛ bao dɛ́ ba yo Gad. Kɛ o ɡe ɛɛ berɔ teŋɛ ba nɛɛ dɛ́ yoo ba.

english_verse: Asher, you will eat food fancy enough for a king.
translation_verse: Aasa harɛ ɛɛ ɛ kondikondɛɛɡaa, wɛɛ kpɔ anɔ la aa dɔ pɛlaa ka tɛ kooro.

english_verse: Naphtali, you are a wild deer with lovely fawns.
translation_verse: Naftale ɡe ɛɛ doo kɛŋɔ welo waa kpaŋa dɛ chwa dɛɛ kaa. Wɛɛ lolɛ bii ba do wer.

english_verse: Joseph, you are a fruitful vine growing near a stream and climbing a wall.
translation_verse: Josef ɡe do kɛŋɔ daa waa won nɔna kohona, dɛ che nee nyoa, o kpala ɛɛ teeh danjwɛɛ.

english_verse: Enemies attacked with arrows, refusing to show mercy.
translation_verse: O dɔma ɛɛ ba yoo á do kpeɡri, dɛ́ teŋɛ o nɛɛ dɛɛ tao hɛma.

english_verse: But you stood your ground, swiftly shooting back with the help of Jacob's God, the All-Powerful One— his name is the Shepherd, Israel's mighty rock.
translation_verse: Nemenɛ Korowii, o mɛɛ Jekɔb Kpeɡnɛn waa tomɔ nomanta, wɛɛ do kpeɡrii dɛ́ kpoŋe o to bini kiŋkiŋ. Peteɡre waa dɛ lɛ Israel tena, dɛ do kɛ Bwetal laanee dɛ́ chao.

english_verse: Your help came from the God your father worshiped, from God All-Powerful. God will bless you with rain and streams from the earth; he will bless you with many descendants.
translation_verse: Korowii he mɛɛ aa tomɔ laanee dɛ́ chae. Korowii Waa Ɛ Kpeɡri Bwa Dɔɔ sweere andɛɛɡa dɛ́ pili nyundua bwaala nɛ tɛɛ, dɛ́ tɛɛ nee aa le harɛ bini. Onee dɛ́ tɛɛ kondɛɛra ne naanar kohona.

english_verse: My son, the blessings I give are better than the promise of ancient mountains or eternal hills. Joseph, I pray these blessings will come to you, because you are the leader of your brothers.
translation_verse: He naawa sweera baa sweera tɛ he mɛɛ la ɡwaa kondɛɛɡa haa dɛ naa deŋɡarere dor. Korowii le Josef cheɡ dɛ tɛo a ɡɛ hɛɛra nɔ a dawɛ o tile ta, dɛkalkɛ o ɡwaa o dɔɔranar.

english_verse: Benjamin, you are a fierce wolf, destroying your enemies morning and evening.
translation_verse: Bɛnjamen do kɛŋɔ noniete o sie aa beɡre ol lawa dɛ́ di. Chɔɔ ne jɔmɔra bwaa o te ɛɛ kpoo ola dɛɛ dia.”

english_verse: These are the twelve tribes of Israel, and this is how Jacob gave each of them their proper blessings. Jacob's Death
translation_verse: Gɛɛ Israel deene fi dɛ anɛ la waa do. Gɛɛ ba mɛɛ Jekɔb bol ɡɛ saŋ waa sweera tɛɛ ba la. Jekɔb seo ne o huɡa wa

english_verse: Both the cave and the land that goes with it were bought from the Hittites.
translation_verse: Koo la ne bwebɔɔ waa lɔ o ta la, yawaa n naa Abraham yawɔ le Hiti tena be. Hé huɡ mɛ bela.”

english_verse: When Jacob had finished giving these instructions to his sons, he lay down on his bed and died.
translation_verse: Jekɔb aa bol o waa bwa tonɛ o bii la be la, o kpɔ o nyu bil kapuri ta dɛ sewɛ.

english_verse: Joseph started crying, then leaned over to hug and kiss his father.
translation_verse: Josef kaa pi o mɛɛ nɛ, dɛ wi dɛ mo o lwɛɛma.

english_verse: Joseph gave orders for Jacob's body to be embalmed,
translation_verse: Josef ɡelɔ ba kpɔ tɛɛɡa ka fɔɡle o mɛɛ bwara o bɛ pɔh warane.

english_verse: When the time of mourning was over, Joseph said to the Egyptian leaders, “If you consider me your friend, please speak to the king for me.
translation_verse: A ɡɛ tɔpera la aa baa kaa la, Josef ŋɔ o nomondɔŋa be ŋɔ, “N poo heya, hé ka ŋɔ kooro be tɛ mɛ.

english_verse: Just before my father died, he made me promise to bury him in his burial cave in Canaan. If the king will give me permission to go, I will come back here.”
translation_verse: N mɛɛ aa dɛ ba sewa la, o ɡelɔ n ŋwɛɛ baɡlo kɛŋɔ mɛɛ huɡoo bwebɔɔ waa kwaaro o do Keenan harɛ ta laanee. Anomanta, n dɛ soŋe, ó ɡel ń la ka huɡe n mɛɛ, ásɛ dɛ berɛ ba.”

english_verse: The king answered, “Go to Canaan and keep your promise to your father.”
translation_verse: Baa laŋa dɛ́ ka bol kooro be la, o chaŋɔ ŋɔ, “Kaa dɛ ka huɡe he mɛɛ ɡɛ haa ŋwɛɛra baɡlo la.”

english_verse: When Joseph left Goshen with his brothers, his relatives, and his father's relatives to bury Jacob, many of the king's highest officials and even his military chariots and cavalry went along. The Israelites left behind only their children, their cattle, and their sheep and goats.
translation_verse: Baala baa soɡe kwaa aa do kɛŋɔ torɔɡo ba vɔwa pɛl jaɡre, ne nɛra baa soɡe jaɡre ta ɡe bwa jao dɛ teŋɛ la bɛl. Nɛnlaa tentenee laŋa.

english_verse: After crossing the Jordan River, Joseph stopped at Atad's threshing place, where they all mourned and wept seven days for Jacob.
translation_verse: Ba baa tel Atad mea lɔbɔr. O lɔ Jɔɔdan Moo wee leebɔr, asɛ ba wi bela kohona. Josef ɛ o mɛɛ lwe tɔpera anuanɛ.

english_verse: The Canaanites saw this and said, “The Egyptians are in great sorrow.” Then they named the place “Egypt in Sorrow.”
translation_verse: Keenan tena baa soɡa bɛne bela la aa no ɡɛ baa dɛ wi Atad pɛla ta la, ba ŋɔ, “Ijipt tena lwejen tentenee nɔ.” Anomanta, ba pa bela sɔn Ebel Misraim. O munii Israel tena lwe ɛɛ.

english_verse: So Jacob's sons did just as their father had instructed.
translation_verse: Kenii a ɛ Jekɔb bibaala ɛ ɡɛ waa do ba ŋɔ ba ɛ la.

english_verse: They took him to Mamre in Canaan and buried him in Machpelah Cave, the burial place Abraham had bought from Ephron the Hittite.
translation_verse: Ba cheɡɔɔ kaa Keenan harɛ ta, dɛ ka huɡo bwebɔɔ waa lɔ Makpɛla. O bɛne Mamre wee leebɔr koo Abraham aa yawɔ le Hiti te Efron be dɛ kpɔ ɛ huɡri bɔr la.

english_verse: After the funeral, Joseph, his brothers, and everyone else returned to Egypt. Joseph's Promise to His Brothers
translation_verse: Josef aa huɡe o mɛɛ tonɛ la, o ne o dɔɔranar ne nɛra baa kaa doo la bwa berɔ ba Ijipt harɛ ta. Josef kpɔ o dɔɔranar wechɔɡa kɛ ba

english_verse: After Jacob died, Joseph's brothers said to each other, “What if Joseph still hates us and wants to get even with us for all the cruel things we did to him?”
translation_verse: Josef mɛɛ aa sewa la, o dɔɔranar la ŋɔ, “Dɛ Josef ŋɔ wɛɛ hah yaa dɛ́ bɔ yaa ya wechɔɡa yaa ɛo la kem sɛ?”

english_verse: So they sent this message to Joseph: Before our father died,
translation_verse: Anomanta, ba tomɛ nɛn Josef be ŋɔ, “Ya mɛɛ aa dɛ ba sewa la,

english_verse: he told us, “You did some cruel and terrible things to Joseph, but you must ask him to forgive you.” Now we ask you to please forgive the terrible things we did. After all, we serve the same God that your father worshiped. When Joseph heard this, he started crying.
translation_verse: o ŋɔ ya ŋɔ he be ŋɔ, ‘Hé kpɔ ya wechɔɡa yaa ɛɛ la bwa kɛ yaa. Ya dɛ soŋe, kpɔ ya wechɔɡa kɛ yaa. Kpɔ Korowii he mɛɛ aa tomɔ la bonɔɔna wechɔɡa kɛ yaa.’ ” Waa la aa tel o be la, o wio.

english_verse: Right then, Joseph's brothers came and bowed down to the ground in front of him and said, “We are your slaves.”
translation_verse: Belaa o dɔɔranar la ɡbabir la dɛ ka ɡuŋi o sie dɛ ŋɔ, “Kpɔ yaa ɛ he bonɔɔna.”

english_verse: But Joseph told them, “Don't be afraid! I have no right to change what God has decided.
translation_verse: Asɛ Josef ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, “He bɛ ɔmɛ, n laa Korowii.

english_verse: You tried to harm me, but God made it turn out for the best, so that he could save all these people, as he is now doing.
translation_verse: He te la, he lii n ne wechɔɡa, kɛ Korowii ɡelɔ a berɛ wedɛɛɡa, ɡɛ aa ɛ ó won lɛ nɛndamanta mkpa ɡɛ waa ɛa fini nɔ.

english_verse: Don't be afraid! I will take care of you and your children.” After Joseph said this, his brothers felt much better. Joseph's Death
translation_verse: A ta chɛ kɛ he ɔmɛ. Mɛɛ nyiŋi he ne he bii bwaa.” O bol anɔ dɛ kpɔ larawe ba bwara ba baah sɔɔh. Josef seo wa

english_verse: Joseph lived in Egypt with his brothers until he died at the age of
translation_verse: Josef ne o mɛɛ lolanar soɡe Ijipt harɛ ta. Waa baa sewɛ la, dɛ o dɔ bene lafa dɛ fi.

english_verse: Joseph lived long enough to see Ephraim's children and grandchildren. He also lived to see the children of Manasseh's son Machir, and he welcomed them into his family.
translation_verse: O soɡo dɛ na Efrem bii ne o naanar. Manasɛ bibaa Makir ɡe bii waa lol ba la, o naa taa ba lol ba dawɛ.

english_verse: Before Joseph died, he told his brothers, “I won't live much longer. But God will take care of you and lead you out of Egypt to the land he promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
translation_verse: Josef ŋɔ o dɔɔranar la be ŋɔ, “N dɛ́ ba sewa, kɛ Korowii ɛɛ nyiŋi he nɛɛ ásɛ dɛ kpɔ heyaa le harɛ nɔ ta kaa harɛ waa baɡɛ Abraham ne Aesek ne Jekɔb nyoa la ta.”

english_verse: Now promise me that you will take my body with you when God leads you to that land.”
translation_verse: Asɛ Josef berɛ ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, “Hé ŋwɛɛ baɡ mɛ kɛŋɔ Korowii tɔ he sie dɛ kaa he ne harɛ la ta naa, hɛɛ kpɔ n lalee kaa.”

english_verse: After Joseph, his brothers, and everyone else in that generation had died,
translation_verse: Aa ba dɛ la sie la, Josef ne o dɔɔranar ne nimanar ne ba bii la te kapa baa serewe,

english_verse: the people of Israel became so numerous that the whole region of Goshen was full of them.
translation_verse: kɛ ba bii baa lola la baa warɛ, dɛ ɡel Israel tena mun ya kohona, dɛ su Ijipt harɛ bwa ta.

english_verse: Many years later a new king came to power. He did not know what Joseph had done for Egypt,
translation_verse: Belaa koofale bɛl waa wola Josef waa jemɛ ba di kara Ijipt harɛ ta.

english_verse: and he told the Egyptians: There are too many of those Israelites in our country, and they are becoming more powerful than we are.
translation_verse: Awola bɛl, kooro la iro dɛ ŋɔ o nɛra la be ŋɔ, “Israel tena baa lɔ ya harɛ nɔ ta berɔ dɛɛ warɛ kohona, dɛ́ ba di kpeɡri ya nɛɛ tɔpetooro bɛl.

english_verse: If we don't outsmart them, their families will keep growing larger. And if our country goes to war, they could easily fight on the side of our enemies and escape from Egypt.
translation_verse: Hé ɡel ya kpɔ liire ɡɛ yaa ɛ ásɛ ba bɛ won warɛ ya harɛ nɔ ta kohona kpa. Gɛ laa dɛ laa baa chole harɛ nɔ ta naa, baa ja ya dɔma nɛɛ dɛ́ yo yaa dɛ́ chwa le harɛ nɔ ta kaa.”

english_verse: The Egyptians put slave bosses in charge of the people of Israel and tried to wear them down with hard work. Those bosses forced them to build the cities of Pithom and Rameses, where the king could store his supplies.
translation_verse: Anomanta, ba le nomonome ba chɔ ba nyoa, dɛ do ba baa ɛ tomkpeɡa. Dɛ ɡel ba do bwɛjena Petɔm ne Rameses, dɛɛ cheɡ kondikwaa a bini dɛɛ tɛ kooro.

english_verse: But even though the Israelites were mistreated, their families grew larger, and they took over more land. Because of this, the Egyptians feared them worse than before
translation_verse: Kɛ Ijipt tena la aa dɛ fiɡ ba kohona la, dɛ nae ba ɡe na dɛɛ ya kwara dɛɛ perɛ harɛ la bwa ta. Asɛ Ijipt tena berɛ dɛɛ ɔmɛ Israel tena la kohona.

english_verse: that their lives were miserable. The Egyptians were cruel to the people of Israel and forced them to make bricks and to mix mortar and to work in the fields.
translation_verse: Ba ɡelɔ baa teŋe berekese, dɛɛ ma Ijipt tena deene, dɛɛ ɛ ba kooni toma te bwa soo siwi. Ba ta ba nɛɛ sune, ba fiɡ ba taeh.

english_verse: Finally, the king called in Shiphrah and Puah, the two women who helped the Hebrew mothers when they gave birth.
translation_verse: Dɛ haahna bane lole baa yer ba Sifra ne Pua baa dɛ lɛ Hibru haahna lol. Awola bɛl, Ijipt kooro la ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ,

english_verse: He told them, “If a Hebrew woman gives birth to a girl, let the child live. If the baby is a boy, kill him!”
translation_verse: “Dɛ he dɛ lɛ Hibru haahna lol dɛ na kɛŋɔ bibaalaa yaa, hé kpoo ba, kɛ dɛ bihaahnaa tenaa, hé ɡel ba.”

english_verse: But the two women were faithful to God and did not kill the boys, even though the king had told them to.
translation_verse: Haahna la baa dɛ lɛ haahna lol la dɛ ɔmɛ Korowii, anomanta, ba ta ɡɛ Ijipt kooro aa ŋɔ ba be la ta teŋɛ. Ba ɡelɔ bii la do le.

english_verse: The king called them in again and asked, “Why are you letting those baby boys live?”
translation_verse: Belaa Ijipt kooro la yer ba dɛ bɔɔ ba ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ hɛɛ ɡel bii la haa wola ban kpoo nɔɔ?”

english_verse: They answered, “Hebrew women have their babies much quicker than Egyptian women. By the time we arrive, their babies are already born.”
translation_verse: Anee ba chaŋo dɛ ŋɔ, “Hibru haahna lola aa kpeɡe kɛŋɔ Ijipt haahna. Ba lola aa kpeɡri doe dɛɛ tɛɛ ba. Ba lolɛ ba bii dɛɛ tonɛ mɔɔ ya yon tel bela.”

english_verse: God was good to the two women because they truly respected him, and he blessed them with children of their own. The Hebrews kept increasing
translation_verse: Haahna baa dɛ lɛ lol la aa ɛ ɡɛ nomanta, Korowii ɛɛ ba andɛɛɡa dɛ ɡel ba dɔ bii.

english_verse: until finally, the king gave a command to everyone in the nation, “As soon as a Hebrew boy is born, throw him into the Nile River! But you can let the girls live.”
translation_verse: Ate, Ijipt kooro la ŋɔ nɛra bwa be ŋɔ, “Bibaa bɛlbwa Hibru te haah naa lolɔ la, hé lɛo dɛ́ kpɔɔ ka ta Nael Moo ta. Kɛ dɛ bihaahnee te naa, hé ɡel ó do le.”

english_verse: A man from the Levi tribe married a woman from the same tribe,
translation_verse: A ɡɛ saŋ baa dɛ kpoo Hibru bibaala ɡɛ la, baa bɛl le Lewi dea, dɛ mo a ɡɛ dea la haah,

english_verse: and she later had a baby boy. He was a beautiful child, and she kept him inside for three months.
translation_verse: asɛ o haah la kpoŋe tea dɛ lolɛ bibaa. Haah la aa naa kɛ bie la wer kohona la, o kpɔɔ sɔh korobie atoro.

english_verse: But when she could no longer keep him hidden, she made a basket out of reeds and covered it with tar. She put him in the basket and placed it in the tall grass along the edge of the Nile River.
translation_verse: Waa baa na kɛ waa won sɔɔh la sie bɛlbwa kpa la, o nyin komɛl baa kpɔ kpɔɡa sɔɔh kɛŋɔ fufu ken, o ne o tɔ dɛ kpɔ kootal maa o habɔɔ ásɛ nee bɛ won jo o bini. Dɛ kpɔ bie la do o bini ka cheɡ kpɔɡjaŋa ane aa cheɡɛ Nael Moo nyoa.

english_verse: The baby's older sister stood off at a distance to see what would happen to him.
translation_verse: Asɛ bie la nahaah ka che sie tama dɛɛ nyiŋi waa aa chiɡ bie la nɛ.

english_verse: About that time one of the king's daughters came down to take a bath in the river, while her servant women walked along the river bank. She saw the basket in the tall grass and sent one of them to pull it out of the water.
translation_verse: Belaa Ijipt kooro la bihaah la moo la ta ŋɔ o ka sɔ ne, dɛ o ne o tolii laŋa, asɛ ba kaa valɛ nee la nyoa. O baa ŋɔ o nyiŋi dɛ na fufu kpɔɡjaŋa la baah, asɛ dɛ tomɛ o toli la bɛl ŋɔ ó ka kpɔ ba.

english_verse: When the king's daughter opened the basket, she saw the baby crying and felt sorry for him. She said, “This must be one of the Hebrew babies.”
translation_verse: Waa ba o ne ba tɛo la, o pilu dɛ na bechasɔɔhna o bini. Dɛ bie la dɛ wi asɛ o waa do o sum. Anee o ŋɔ, “Hibru tena bii la bɛlee nɔ.”

english_verse: At once the baby's older sister came up and asked, “Do you want me to get a Hebrew woman to take care of the baby for you?”
translation_verse: Anee bie la nahaah la ŋɔ Ijipt kooro bihaah la be ŋɔ, “Amɔ ń la ka yerɛ Hibru haah ó ba ɔro tɛɛ kɛɛ?”

english_verse: “Yes,” the king's daughter answered. So the girl brought the baby's mother,
translation_verse: Asɛ o chaŋe ŋɔ, “Ɔɔh, la dɛ́ ka yerɛ bɛl ba.” Asɛ o la dɛ ka kpɔ bie la nya ɡbaɡba ba.

english_verse: and the king's daughter told her, “Take care of this child, and I will pay you.” The baby's mother carried him home and took care of him.
translation_verse: Belaa Ijipt kooro bihaah la ŋɔ haah la be ŋɔ, “Kpɔ bie nɔ, dɛ́ ka dɛɛro tɛ mɛ ásɛ n bɔe kem.” Asɛ o kpɔ bie la dɛ kaa.

english_verse: And when he was old enough, she took him to the king's daughter, who adopted him. She named him Moses because she said, “I pulled him out of the water.” Moses Escapes from Egypt
translation_verse: Bie la aa baa kpeɡ tama la, o kpɔɔ ka tɛ Ijipt kooro bihaah la o berɛ o bie. O ŋɔ, “O sɔne Mosis, dɛkalkɛ nee taa n kpɔɔ le.” Mosis chwae kaa Midian harɛ ta wa

english_verse: After Moses had grown up, he went out to where his own people were hard at work, and he saw an Egyptian beating one of them.
translation_verse: Mosis aa kpeɡa la, awola bɛl, o iro dɛ ka chɔɔ o bala Hibru tena, dɛ na ɡɛ baa do ba baa ɛ tomkpeɡa. Asɛ Mosis na Ijipt te kɛŋɔ waa dɛ lɔɔ o bwɛɛ Hibru te.

english_verse: Moses looked around to see if anyone was watching, then he killed the Egyptian and hid his body in the sand.
translation_verse: Waa nyiŋa bar o ta nomɛlbwa nae la, o kpo Ijipt te la dɛ ɡbaa hɛŋle tɔ o nɛ.

english_verse: When Moses went out the next day, he saw two Hebrews fighting. So he went to the man who had started the fight and asked, “Why are you beating up one of your own people?”
translation_verse: Tɔ aa pera la, o laŋɔ ŋɔ ó ka chɔɔ o bala la ja dɛ na Hibru tena baala banɛ aa dɛ yo. Belaa o bɔɔ onɔ la o kon aa wola maɡrɛ la ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ hɛɛ lɔɔ he dɔŋ nɔɔ?”

english_verse: The man answered, “Who put you in charge of us and made you our judge? Are you planning to kill me, just like you killed that Egyptian?” This frightened Moses because he was sure that people must have found out what had happened.
translation_verse: Anee o chaŋe ŋɔ, “Umee cheɡe kora ta ŋɔ hé baa nyiŋi ya nɛɛ dɛ́ bol ya waa dɛɛ pa bole ɔ? He dɛ nyin he kpo mɛ ɡɛ haa kpo Ijipt te la kɛɛ?” Ate, Mosis ɔmɛ, dɛ lii kɛŋɔ, “Jamɔ nɛra na n waa maa ɛa la.”

english_verse: When the king heard what Moses had done, he wanted to kill him. But Moses escaped and went to the land of Midian. One day, when Moses was sitting by a well,
translation_verse: Ijipt kooro baa no waa la, dɛɛ nyin ŋwɛnɛre waa kpɔ a ta dɛ́ kpo Mosis, asɛ o chwa le bela dɛ ka so Midian harɛ ta.

english_verse: When Jethro's daughters returned home, their father asked, “Why have you come back so early today?”
translation_verse: Bihaahna la aa bera la dem ba mɛɛ be la, o bɔɔ ba ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ fini te he ba warane ken?”

english_verse: They answered, “An Egyptian rescued us from the shepherds, and he even watered our sheep and goats.”
translation_verse: Anee ba chaŋe ŋɔ, “Ijipt te bɛlee lɛ yaa ta peteɡra bane nɔn ta. O ɡbabirii dɔ ya nee tɛ yaa dɛ tɛ kondɛɛra la ɡe ane a nyɔ.”

english_verse: “Where is he?” Jethro asked. “Why did you leave him out there? Invite him to eat with us.”
translation_verse: Belaa o bɔɔ ba ŋɔ, “Leperaa o dɔɔ? Ɛrɛ waa he ɡelo bela nɔɔ? He la ka yerɔ ó ba ya di kwa.”

english_verse: And when she had a son, Moses said, “I will name him Gershom, since I am a foreigner in this country.”
translation_verse: Ba lolɛ bibaa, asɛ Mosis ŋɔ, “O sɔne Gɛɛsɔm dɛkalkɛŋɔ, hɔɔhree men harɛ nɔ ta.”

english_verse: After the death of the king of Egypt, the Israelites still complained because they were forced to be slaves. They cried out for help,
translation_verse: A biɡro tama, asɛ Ijipt kooro la ba sewɛ. Kɛ dɛ Israel tena ta dɛ ɛ ba tomkpeɡa la, dɛ wi dɛɛ yerɛ Korowii ŋɔ ó ba lɛɛ ba.

english_verse: and God heard their loud cries. He did not forget the promise he had made to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob,
translation_verse: Korowii no ba wii, dɛ lii fɔo o ne Abraham ne Aesek dɛ Jekɔb aa fɔwa la wa.

english_verse: and because he knew what was happening to his people, he felt sorry for them.
translation_verse: Korowii na Israel tena wenaale, asɛ ba waa we o nɛɛ kohona.

english_verse: One day, Moses was taking care of the sheep and goats of his father-in-law Jethro, the priest of Midian, and Moses decided to lead them across the desert to Sinai, the holy mountain.
translation_verse: Awola bɛl, Mosis kpɔ o helabaa Jetro waa ɛ Midian sɔfo la kondɛɛra kaa di bɔr. O teɡa ka ɡarɛ pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta, dɛ ka le bwe waa do ɡoroŋ baa yerɔ Sinai la ta.

english_verse: There an angel of the Lord appeared to him from a burning bush. Moses saw that the bush was on fire, but it was not burning up.
translation_verse: Belaa Korowii nyundua torome bɛl kpɔ o te baɡlo dawii ane aa dɛ lawɛ nii baah ta. Mosis nao kɛŋɔ nii dɛ le bela, kɛ dɛ dawii la ɡe aa fuh.

english_verse: “This is strange!” he said to himself. “I'll go over and see why the bush isn't burning up.”
translation_verse: Anomanta, o lii o nyu bini ŋɔ, “Waa nɔ te ɔma. Mɛɛ suuhnu tel, dɛ́ na ɡɛ aa ɛa dawii nɔ aa wola fuh nɔ.”

english_verse: When the Lord saw Moses coming near, he called him by name from the bush, and Moses answered, “Here I am.”
translation_verse: Korowii aa naa kɛŋɔ o ba sie dɛ́ ba na la, o yerɔ dawii la bini ŋɔ, “Mosis! Mosis!” Asɛ o chaŋe ŋɔ, “N Naa Korowii, menee nɔ.”

english_verse: God replied, “Don't come any closer. Take off your sandals—the ground where you are standing is holy.
translation_verse: Anee Korowii ŋɔ, “Bɛ suuh tel. Foo he naŋɡawa, dɛkalkɛ bela haa cheɡa la ɛ boɡoroŋ.

english_verse: I am the God who was worshiped by your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.” Moses was afraid to look at God, and so he hid his face.
translation_verse: Menee Korowii he nabaala Abraham ne Aesek dɛ Jekɔb aa tom mɛ la.” Belaa Mosis kpɔ sie sɔh dɛkalkɛ dɛ o dɛ ɔmɛ kɛ ó nyiŋi Korowii.

english_verse: The Lord said: I have seen how my people are suffering as slaves in Egypt, and I have heard them beg for my help because of the way they are being mistreated. I feel sorry for them,
translation_verse: Anee Korowii ŋɔ, “N na sibeɡra kohona baa dɛ do n nɛra baa lɔ Ijipt. N no ba wii, dɛ le ba dɔɔranar tonchɔɡa baa dɛ do ba la ta, anomanta, ba waa hiah mɛ kohona.

english_verse: and I have come down to rescue them from the Egyptians. I will bring my people out of Egypt into a country where there is a lot of good land, rich with milk and honey. I will give them the land where the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites now live.
translation_verse: N tuo ba dɛ́ ba lɛɛ ba le Ijipt tena nɔn ta, ásɛ dɛ berɛ kpɔ ba ba harɛpare ondɛɛge ta. O do som Keenan ne Hiti ne Amɔre ne Pɛrɛs ne Hivi dɛ Jebus tena harɛ baa soɡe o ta la ta.

english_verse: My people have begged for my help, and I have seen how cruel the Egyptians are to them.
translation_verse: Taraken Israel tena wii la tel n be, asɛ n na ɡɛ Ijipt tena la aa dɛ ɛɛ ba hɔhɔrɔwa.

english_verse: Now go to the king! I am sending you to lead my people out of his country.
translation_verse: N dɛ tomɛ Ijipt kooro be, ásɛ he tɔ n nɛra sie ba won le o harɛ la ta.”

english_verse: But Moses said, “Who am I to go to the king and lead your people out of Egypt?”
translation_verse: Anee Mosis ŋɔ Korowii be ŋɔ, “Umee n ɡe kɛŋɔ ń won la Ijipt kooro be dɛ́ ka ŋɔ ń kpɔ Israel tena le o harɛ ta bela ɔ?”

english_verse: God replied, “I will be with you. And you will know that I am the one who sent you, when you worship me on this mountain after you have led my people out of Egypt.”
translation_verse: Asɛ Korowii chaŋo ŋɔ, “Mɛɛ ja he nɛɛ, ásɛ dɛ he baa kpɔ n nɛra le Ijipt harɛ ta ba naa, bá baa tom mɛ bwejen nɔ ta. Anee dɛɛ ba baɡla kɛŋɔ menee tomɛ.”

english_verse: Moses answered, “I will tell the people of Israel that the God their ancestors worshiped has sent me to them. But what should I say, if they ask me your name?”
translation_verse: Belaa Mosis chaŋo dɛ ŋɔ, “Amɔ dɛ n la Israel tena be dɛ ka ŋɔ, Korowii ba naawa aa tomɔ laanee tom mɛ ba be, asɛ ba bɔɔ mɛ o sɔn aa, bɔkwa waa ń bol ba be nɔ?”

english_verse: God said to Moses: I am the eternal God. So tell them that the Lord, whose name is “I Am,” has sent you. This is my name forever, and it is the name that people must use from now on.
translation_verse: Korowii berɔ ŋɔ Mosis be ŋɔ, “Ŋɔ Israel tena be ŋɔ, ‘Men Korowii ba nabaala Abraham ne Aesek dɛ Jekɔb aa tomɔ laanee tomɛ ba be.’ A ɡɛ sɔn nɔɔ dɛ́ ɛ n sɔn saŋ bɛlbwa dɛɛ la. Ásɛ naanar baa ka ba bwa ɡe ɛɛ yer mɛ ɡɛ.

english_verse: Call together the leaders of Israel and tell them that the God who was worshiped by Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob has appeared to you. Tell them I have seen how terribly they are being treated in Egypt,
translation_verse: La ka cheme Israel nomonome dɛ́ ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, ‘Korowii he naawa Abraham ne Aesek ne Jekɔb aa tomɔ la ba n be dɛ ba ŋɔ, o nyiŋo, dɛ na ɡɛ baa dɛ ɛ heyaa hɔhɔrɔwa Ijipt harɛ.

english_verse: and I promise to lead them out of their troubles. I will give them a land rich with milk and honey, where the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites now live.
translation_verse: Anomanta, o ŋɔ, wɛɛ lawɛ heyaa le Ijipt harɛ bela baa dɛ ɛ heyaa hɔhɔrɔwa kohona la, dɛ́ kaa he ne harɛpare ondɛɛɡe ta. Bela Keenan ne Hiti ne Amɔre ne Pɛrɛs ne Hivi dɛ Jebus tena aa soɡa la.’

english_verse: The leaders of Israel will listen to you. Then you must take them to the king of Egypt and say, “The Lord God of the Hebrews has appeared to us. Let us walk three days into the desert, where we can offer a sacrifice to him.”
translation_verse: Nomonome la ɛɛ no he waa haa bol ba be laanee, ásɛ he ne ba la Ijipt kooro be dɛ́ ka ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, ‘Korowii Hibru tena aa dɛ tomɔ la kpɔ o te chaɡle yaa. Anomanta, tɛ yaa ŋwɛnɛ yá ka ɡaaɡe tɔpera atoro pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta, dɛ́ ka kpoo kwaa ɛ saraha tɛ Korowii yaa dɛ tomɔ.’

english_verse: But I know that the king of Egypt won't let you go unless something forces him to.
translation_verse: N jemɔ kɛŋɔ Ijipt kooro aa sɛh ŋɔ he kaa nemenɛ wekpeɡa ane aa puu mɔɔ.

english_verse: So I will use my mighty power to perform all kinds of miracles and strike down the Egyptians. Then the king will send you away.
translation_verse: Anomanta, mɛɛ che n kpeɡri taa dɛ́ ɡel Ijipt tena na n nyokpowe-ɛɛla maa dɛ́ ba ɛɛ ba bini la, mɔɔ ó ɡel he kaa.

english_verse: Every Israelite woman will go to her Egyptian neighbors or to any Egyptian woman living with them and ask them for gold and silver jewelry and for their finest clothes. The Egyptians will give them to you, and you will put these fine things on your sons and daughters. Carry all this away when you leave Egypt.
translation_verse: Israel haah bɛlbwa la o dɔŋ Ijipt handɔŋ be, ne banɔ la bane baa pɛa so deremi ta ka soŋe kwaa baa kpɔ suuɡaswɛm ne suuɡapoŋa ɛa dɛ yale, dɛ́ kpɔ do he bibaala ne bihaahna. Ásɛ ba laala la berɛ kwaa haa kaa paa laa ta.”

english_verse: Moses asked the Lord, “Suppose everyone refuses to listen to my message, and no one believes that you really appeared to me?”
translation_verse: Anee Mosis chaŋe Korowii ŋɔ, “Dɛ ba ta men yaradae dɛ cheɡ deŋne no n be, dɛ ŋɔ he ta he te kpɔe baɡ mɛ naa, n ŋɔ ɛrɔɔ?”

english_verse: The Lord answered, “What's that in your hand?” “A walking stick,” Moses replied.
translation_verse: Belaa Korowii bɔɔro ŋɔ, “Bɔkwaa lɔ he nɔn ta nɔɔ?” Anee o chaŋe ŋɔ, “Daŋɡbalaa lɔ n nɔn ta.”

english_verse: “Throw it down!” the Lord commanded. So Moses threw the stick on the ground. It immediately turned into a snake, and Moses jumped back.
translation_verse: Asɛ Korowii ŋɔ, “Kpɔ ta harɛ.” Mosis aa kpɔa ta harɛ la, o berɛ harɛkon, asɛ o chwa le o jwɛh.

english_verse: “Pick it up by the tail!” the Lord told him. And when Moses did this, the snake turned back into a walking stick.
translation_verse: Ate, Korowii berɛ ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Tɛr nɔn lawɛ o din.” Waa lawɔ la, asɛ o berɛ daŋɡbala do o nɔn ta.

english_verse: “Do this,” the Lord said, “and the Israelites will believe that you have seen me, the God who was worshiped by their ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.”
translation_verse: Asɛ o berɛ ŋɔ, “Gɛ aa ɛ ásɛ ba yarada kɛŋɔ Korowii ba naawa Abraham ne Aesek ne Jekɔb aa tomɔ la kpɔ o te baɡle laanee la.”

english_verse: Next, the Lord commanded Moses, “Put your hand inside your shirt.” Moses obeyed, and when he took it out, his hand had turned white as snow—like someone with leprosy.
translation_verse: O berɔ ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Kpɔ he nɔn do he batakaare bini,” asɛ o ɛ ɡɛ. Waa laa nɔn kpɔ la, dɛ o lɛɡrɔ kɛŋɔ bwadabii weechɔɡa yon lawɛ nɛn la ken.

english_verse: “Put your hand back inside your shirt,” the Lord told him. Moses did so, and when he took it out again, it was as healthy as the rest of his body.
translation_verse: Asɛ Korowii ŋɔ, “Berɛ kpɔ he nɔn la do.” Asɛ o ɛ ɡɛ. Waa bera laa nɔn kpɔ la, dɛ o bwa kwaarɔ dɛ do kɛŋɔ o fa aa doa wubwa la.

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “If no one believes either of these miracles, take some water from the Nile River and pour it on the ground. The water will immediately turn into blood.”
translation_verse: Kɛ dɛ ba ta hen yaradae nyokpowe-ɛɛla nɔ bwa ta, kɛɛ dɛ taŋ deŋne aa, ka ɛ nee le Nael Moo ta dɛ́ fuɡa ta harɛ. Nee la ɛɛ berɛ chalee dawɛ harɛ la sie.”

english_verse: Moses replied, “I have never been a good speaker. I wasn't one before you spoke to me, and I'm not one now. I am slow at speaking, and I can never think of what to say.”
translation_verse: Asɛ Mosis ŋɔ Korowii be ŋɔ, “N Naa Korowii, n nyoa aa kpɛlɛ ń won bol waa a do som. Dɛ le n bechale saŋ ne ɡɛ saŋ haa kpɔ he te baɡ mɛ bwaa n nyoa aa wola kpɛlɛ ne wobol.”

english_verse: But the Lord answered, “Who makes people able to speak or makes them deaf or unable to speak? Who gives them sight or makes them blind? Don't you know that I am the one who does these things?
translation_verse: Belaa Korowii ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Umee tɛ nɛn nyoa o kpɔ dɛɛ bol waɔ? Kɛɛ umee dɛɛ ɛ nɛn amumu ne deŋneɡbeŋa te, kɛɛ nɛn waa dɛ na ne onɔ la waa wola na nɔ? Men Korowii laa aa?

english_verse: Now go! When you speak, I will be with you and give you the words to say.”
translation_verse: Ir kaa, mɛɛ chae he bol wa, dɛ́ baɡle ɡɛ bwa haa bol.”

english_verse: Moses begged, “Lord, please send someone else to do it.”
translation_verse: Asɛ Mosis ŋɔ, “N Naa Korowii, n dɛ soŋe amɔ he fe tomɛ nɛnfale bɛl sɛ?”

english_verse: The Lord became angry with Moses and said: What about your brother Aaron, the Levite? I know he is a good speaker. He is already on his way here to visit you, and he will be happy to see you again.
translation_verse: Belaa Korowii baah di o nɛɛ kohona asɛ dɛ ŋɔ, “He dɔɔ baa dɛ yerɔ Arɔn o ɛ Lewi dea te la sɛ? N jemɔ kɛŋɔ o te ɛɛ won bol waa kɛrɛdɛ. Hale o lɔ ŋwɛnɛ ta taraken dɛɛ ba dɛ́ ba cheme. O balɔ ba nae naa, o sie ɛɛ lɛo taeh.

english_verse: Aaron will speak to the people for you, and you will be like me, telling Aaron what to say. I will be with both of you as you speak, and I will tell each of you what to do.
translation_verse: Arɔn ɛɛ dɛɛ bol waa nɛra la bee, ásɛ a ɛ kɛŋɔ henee dɛɛ bol. Aa ka ɛɔ kɛŋɔ henee ɛ Korowii, asɛ o bol he waa nɛra la be dɛɛ tɛɛ.

english_verse: Now take this walking stick and use it to perform miracles. Moses Returns to Egypt
translation_verse: Kɛ kpɔ daŋɡbala nɔ kpoŋe, onee hɛɛ ba wona kpɔ dɛɛ ɛ nyokpowa.” Mosis bera dɛ́ kaa Ijipt harɛ ta

english_verse: Moses went to his father-in-law Jethro and asked, “Please let me return to Egypt to see if any of my people are still alive.” “All right,” Jethro replied. “I hope all goes well.”
translation_verse: Belaa Mosis berɛ kaa o helabaa Jetro be dɛ ka ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “N dɛ soŋe, ɡel ń berɛ kaa n lolanar be Ijipt dɛ́ ka na kɛŋɔ ba ta lole kɛɛ.” Anee o sɛh dɛ tao ŋwɛnɛ deŋnesɔɔhna ta o kaa.

english_verse: But even before this, the Lord had told Moses, “Leave the land of Midian and return to Egypt. Everyone who wanted to kill you is now dead.”
translation_verse: Mosis taa lɔ Midian harɛ ta la, Korowii ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Berɛ kaa Ijipt harɛ ta, dɛkalkɛ nɛra la ba fa aa dɛ nyini dɛ́ kpo la bwa serewɔ.”

english_verse: So Moses put his wife and sons on donkeys and headed for Egypt, holding the walking stick that had the power of God.
translation_verse: Anomanta, o kpɔ o haah ne bibaala so keeɡo ta, dɛ berɛ dɛɛ kaa Ijipt harɛ, dɛ kpɔ daŋɡbala Korowii aa bol o waa o be la kpoŋe.

english_verse: On the way the Lord said to Moses: When you get to Egypt, go to the king and work the miracles I have shown you. But I will make him so stubborn that he will refuse to let my people go.
translation_verse: Belaa Korowii berɛ ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Haa bera dɛɛ kaa Ijipt harɛ ta nɔ, na kɛŋɔ kpeɡri maa tɛɛ he kpɔ dɛɛ ɛ nyokpowaa la, hɛɛ ɛa Ijipt kooro siwi taa. Kɛ mɛɛ ɡeloo o deŋne do kpeɡri, waa wola ɡel n nɛra la kaa.

english_verse: Then tell him that I have said, “Israel is my first-born son,
translation_verse: Ásɛ he ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, Israel tena do kɛŋɔ n bibanloɡle ken,

english_verse: and I commanded you to release him, so he could worship me. But you refused, and now I will kill your first-born son.” Zipporah's Son Is Circumcised
translation_verse: asɛ n ŋɔ he be ŋɔ, he tɛ n bibaa ŋwɛnɛ ásɛ o ka tom mɛ. Kɛ he vɛoh, anomanta, mɛɛ kpo he ɡe bibanloɡlee.”

english_verse: One night while Moses was in camp, the Lord was about to kill him.
translation_verse: Baa dɛ kaa la, Korowii baa cheme Mosis Ijipt ŋwɛnɛ ta, bobɛl hɔɔhra tel bela ba yon chɔ la, dɛ fe ɛɛ nyin o kpoe.

english_verse: But Zipporah circumcised her son with a flint knife. She touched his legs with the skin she had cut off and said, “My dear son, this blood will protect you.”
translation_verse: Belaa o haah Sepora kpɔ bwepɛla o nyoa aa do kɛŋɔ kere teŋe o bie la pen, dɛ kpɔ chal la ka leɡe Mosis napaala dɛ ŋɔ, “Gɛ maa ɛa nɔ dɛ baɡle kɛŋɔ n ne he ɛ beŋkpoŋ ya soɡa nɔ bini.”

english_verse: The Lord sent Aaron to meet Moses in the desert. So Aaron met Moses at Mount Sinai and greeted him with a kiss.
translation_verse: Anee Korowii ŋɔ Arɔn be ŋɔ, “Ir la pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta, dɛ́ ka cheme Mosis.” Asɛ o ir dɛ la ka chemo Korowii bwe waa do ɡoroŋ ta dɛ jaamo.

english_verse: Moses told Aaron what God had sent him to say; he also told him about the miracles God had given him the power to perform.
translation_verse: Belaa Mosis bol wobɛlbwa Korowii aa tomɔ ŋɔ ó ka bol, ne nyokpowe-ɛɛla la bwa waa doo ŋɔ ó ɛ la bwa chaɡle Arɔn.

english_verse: Later they brought together the leaders of Israel,
translation_verse: Anomanta, o ne Arɔn bwa la Ijipt dɛ ka boa Israel nomonome la bwa nyoa,

english_verse: and Aaron told them what the Lord had sent Moses to say. Then Moses worked the miracles for the people,
translation_verse: asɛ Arɔn chaɡle wobɛlbwa Korowii aa bola baɡle Mosis la ba be. Mosis berɔ ɛ nyokpowe-ɛɛla la ba siwi ta,

english_verse: and everyone believed. They bowed down and worshiped the Lord because they knew that he had seen their suffering and was going to help them.
translation_verse: asɛ ba yaradao. Baa noa kɛŋɔ Korowii na ɡɛ baa dɛ ɛɛ ba hɔhɔrɔwa asɛ ba waa hiaoh kohona la, ba ɡuŋo dɛ duuru.

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the king of Egypt and told him, “The Lord God says, ‘Let my people go into the desert, so they can honor me with a celebration there.’ ”
translation_verse: A habɔɔ la, Mosis ne Arɔn la kooro la be dɛ ka ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Korowii Israel tena aa dɛ tomɔ la ŋɔ, ‘Tɛ n nɛra ŋwɛnɛ ba kaa, ásɛ dɛ ka di Tɔpejen tɛ mɛ pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ la ta.’ ”

english_verse: “Who is this Lord and why should I obey him?” the king replied. “I refuse to let you and your people go!”
translation_verse: Anee kooro la ŋɔ, “Umee Korowii n duuru, dɛ́ tɛ Israel tena ŋwɛnɛ ba kaalɔ? Maa Korowii bɛlbwa jemɛ, anomanta, maa ban ŋwɛnɛɛ tɛ ba kaa.”

english_verse: They answered, “The Lord God of the Hebrews has appeared to us. Please let us walk three days into the desert where we can offer sacrifices to him. If you don't, he may strike us down with terrible troubles or with war.”
translation_verse: Asɛ Mosis ne Arɔn chaŋe ŋɔ, “Korowii Hibru tena aa dɛ tomɛ la ba ya be, anomanta, tɛ yaa ŋwɛnɛ ya ka ɡaaɡe tɔpera atoro pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta, dɛ́ ka kpoo kwaa ɛ saraha tɛ Korowii yaa dɛ tomɔ. Dɛ ɡɛ laa, wɛɛ kpɔ laa kɛɛ weechɔɡaa ba kpoo yaa.”

english_verse: The king said, “Moses and Aaron, why are you keeping these people from working? Look how many you are keeping from doing their work. Now everyone get back to work!”
translation_verse: A ɡɛ nɛra nɔ warɔ ɡwaa Ijipt tena harɛ nɔ ta, asɛ he berɛ dɛɛ nyin ba ɡel toma ɛɛ la!”

english_verse: That same day the king gave orders to his Egyptian slave bosses and to the Israelite men directly in charge of the Israelite slaves. He told them:
translation_verse: Awola tɔpere la tenten la, kooro do Ijipt tena baa dɛ nyiŋi Hibru tena baa ɛ yoma dɛ chɔ ba bala nyoa la be ŋɔ,

english_verse: Don't give the slaves any more straw to put in their bricks. Force them to find their own straw wherever they can,
translation_verse: “He bɛ kpɔɡhola nɛra la aa kpɔa dɛɛ teŋe berekese la tɛ kpa. Hé ɡel ba ɡbabir kaa nyin ba kpɔɡa,

english_verse: but they must make the same number of bricks as before. They are lazy, or else they would not beg me to let them go and sacrifice to their God.
translation_verse: kɛ dɛ ta ɛɛ teŋe ɡɛ tenten baa dɛ teŋe wubwa la. He bɛ ane laa kpɔ a ta. Ba ɛ nɛra ba sie aa dɛ hwah toma ɛɛ, a waa baa wi ŋɔ, ń ɡel ba la ka kpoo kwaa ɛ saraha tɛ Korowii baa dɛ tomɔ la.

english_verse: Make them work so hard that they won't have time to listen to these lies.
translation_verse: Hé tɛɛ ba tomkpeɡa aa ɡwaa wubwa kwaa la, ásɛ ba bɛ bɔr dɔ dɛɛ no nyosonteŋna wobol.”

english_verse: The slave bosses and the men in charge of the slaves went out and told them, “The king says he will not give you any more straw.
translation_verse: Belaa Ijipt tena baa dɛ nyiŋi tom-ɛɛra la nɛ, ne Hibru tena baa chɔ ba bala nyoa la le dɛ ka ŋɔ nɛra la be kɛŋɔ kooro ŋɔ, “Maa heyaa kpɔɡholee tɛ kpa.

english_verse: Go and find your own straw wherever you can, but you must still make as many bricks as before.”
translation_verse: Hé ɡbabir ka ɡaaɡe nyin he kpɔɡa. Kɛ ɡɛ tenten maa maɡa tɛ heyaa wubwa laanee hɛɛ ba ɛɛ.”

english_verse: The slaves went all over Egypt, looking for straw.
translation_verse: Asɛ ba lɔ jo Ijipt harɛ ta bwa dɛ ka nyin kpɔɡa la.

english_verse: But the slave bosses were hard on them and kept saying, “Each day you have to make as many bricks as you did when you were given straw.”
translation_verse: Dɛ Ijipt tena baa dɛ nyiŋi tom-ɛɛra la nɛɛ la teŋɔ dɛɛ do ba ŋɔ, “Hé do sie dɛ́ ɛ toma ɡɛ wubwa yaa dɛ tɛ heyaa kpɔɡa hɛɛ ɛ tɔpere bɛlbwa la.”

english_verse: The bosses beat the men in charge of the slaves and said, “Why didn't you force the slaves to make as many bricks yesterday and today as they did before?”
translation_verse: Asɛ Ijipt nomonome la lɔɔ Hibru tena baa ɡela ba chɔ ba bala la nyoa la. Dɛ bɔɔ ba ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ he ta wone ɛ toma ɡɛ he fa aa dɛ ɛ wubwa la nɔɔ?”

english_verse: Finally, the men in charge of the slaves went to the king and said, “Why are you treating us like this?
translation_verse: Anee Israel tena baa ɡela ba chɔ ba bala nyoa la la Ijipt kooro be dɛ ka ŋɔ, “N naa kooro, ɛrɛɛ he ɛ yaa ɡɛ nɔɔ?

english_verse: No one brings us any straw, but we are still ordered to make the same number of bricks. We are beaten with whips, and your own people are to blame.”
translation_verse: Ba ta yaa kpɔɡa bɛlbwa tɛɛ, kɛ dɛ ɡe teŋɛ dɛɛ ŋɔ ya teŋe berekese ɡɛ baa maɡa tɛ yaa wubwa la, dɛɛ lɔɔ yaa kɛ dɛ he ɡbabir nɛra la bee a le.”

english_verse: The king replied, “You are lazy—nothing but lazy! That's why you keep asking me to let you go and sacrifice to your Lord.
translation_verse: Anee Ijipt kooro la ŋɔ, “Bɔhwaahra bane le! A waa laa hɛɛ bol ŋɔ, n ɡel hé la ka kpoo kwaa ɛ saraha tɛ Korowii haa dɛ tomɔ nɔ naa?

english_verse: Get back to work! You won't be given straw, but you must still make the same number of bricks.”
translation_verse: Hé berɛ kaa toma ta. Nomɛlbwa aa heya kpɔɡa tɛɛ ba, kɛ he ɡee teŋe berekese laanee kɛ wubwa la.”

english_verse: The men knew they were in deep trouble when they were ordered to make the same number of bricks each day.
translation_verse: Hibru tena baa chɔ ba bala nyoa la aa noa kɛŋɔ baa dɛɛ teŋe berekese ɡɛ tɔpere bɛlbwa baa maɡa tɛɛ ba wubwa la, belaa ba na kɛŋɔ taraken te waa puu ba.

english_verse: After they left the king, they went to see Moses and Aaron, who had been waiting for them.
translation_verse: Baa le Ijipt kooro be dɛɛ kaa la, ba kaa pu Mosis ne Arɔn dɛ ba cheɡɔ dɛɛ kpaa ba.

english_verse: Then the men said, “We hope the Lord will punish both of you for making the king and his officials hate us. Now they even have an excuse to kill us.” The Lord's Promise to Moses
translation_verse: Asɛ ba ŋɔ Mosis wa be ŋɔ, “Korowiirii dɛ tɛr he deŋne kɛŋɔ haa ɡela kooro ne o nomonome hah yaa la. A deno do kɛŋɔ haa kpɔ keri do ba nɔɔra ta ŋɔ bá kpoo yaa ken.” Mosis naɡre Korowii wa

english_verse: Moses left them and prayed, “Our Lord, why have you brought so much trouble on your people? Is that why you sent me here?
translation_verse: Belaa Mosis berɛ ka bɔɔ Korowii ŋɔ, “N Naa Korowii, ɛrɛɛ hɛɛ do he ɡbabir nɛra hɔhɔrɔwa ta ken? Anɔ waa he tom mɛ ba be kɛɛ?

english_verse: Ever since you told me to speak to the king, he has caused nothing but trouble for these people. And you haven't done a thing to help.”
translation_verse: Le a ɡɛ saŋ maa cheɡɛ he sɔn ta dɛ ka bol waa la Ijipt kooro be la, teŋaa ba teŋɛ dɛɛ na wahala, asɛ he ɡe den vɛh ba lɛɛ kwara.”

english_verse: The Lord God told Moses: Soon you will see what I will do to the king. Because of my mighty power, he will let my people go, and he will even chase them out of his country.
translation_verse: Belaa Korowii ŋɔ Mosis be ŋɔ, “Taraken n dɛ ba ɡela he jemɛ waa maa dɛ ba kpɔe ɛ Ijipt kooro la. Aa che n kpeɡri taa ó tɛ n nɛra la ŋwɛnɛ bá kaa. Hale dɛ́ ɡel ó doŋ ba le o harɛ ta.” Korowii yerɛ Mosis

english_verse: My name is the Lord.
translation_verse: Korowii berɔ ŋɔ Mosis be ŋɔ, “Menee Korowii.

english_verse: But when I appeared to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, I came as God All-Powerful and did not use my name.
translation_verse: Men kpɔ n te baɡle Abraham ne Aesek dɛ Jekɔb kɛ Menee Kpeɡri Bwa Dɔɔ la. Kɛ n ta ɡelɛ ba jemɛ n sɔn waa do ɡoroŋ la te.

english_verse: I made an agreement and promised them the land of Canaan, where they were living as foreigners.
translation_verse: Asɛ n ne ba fɔwɛ fɔo kɛŋɔ mɛɛ kpɔ Keenan harɛ baa soɡe o ta kɛŋɔ hɔɔhra laanee tɛɛ ba ó ɛ ba kon.

english_verse: Now I have seen how the people of Israel are suffering because of the Egyptians, and I will keep my promise.
translation_verse: N na wahala Israel tena aa dɛ na Ijipt tena nɔn ta baa ɛɛ ba kɛ yoma la, dɛ lii n ne ba fɔo yaa fɔwa la.

english_verse: Here is my message for Israel: “I am the Lord! And with my mighty power I will punish the Egyptians and free you from slavery.
translation_verse: Anomanta, ŋɔ Israel tena be ŋɔ, ‘Menee Korowii. Mɛɛ lɛ heyaa le Ijipt tena hɔhɔrɔwa baa dɛ ɛ heyaa la taa. Mɛɛ che n kpeɡri ne n nyokpowe-ɛɛla taa, dɛ́ tɛr ba deŋne ásɛ dɛ lɛ heya.

english_verse: I will accept you as my people, and I will be your God. Then you will know that I was the one who rescued you from the Egyptians.
translation_verse: Mɛɛ kpɔ heyaa ɛ n nɛra, ásɛ n ɡe ɛ Korowii haa dɛ tom mɛ. Anee dɛ́ ɡel he jemɛ kɛŋɔ menee Korowii haa dɛ tomɛ n lɛ heyaa le Ijipt tena nɔn ta.

english_verse: I will bring you into the land that I solemnly promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and it will be yours. I am the Lord!”
translation_verse: N baɡɛ Abraham ne Aesek dɛ Jekɔb nyoa kpeɡri nɛ harɛ maa ŋɔa mɛɛ kpɔɔ tɛɛ ba la wa. Mɛɛ kpɔɔ tɛ heya ó ɛ he kon pi. Men Korowii bola.’ ”

english_verse: When Moses told this to the Israelites, they were too discouraged and mistreated to believe him.
translation_verse: Mosis bol ɡɛ waa nɔ baɡle Israel tena la kɛ, bambichɔɡ kohona ne ba dochɔɡa la nomanta, ba ta noɛ.

english_verse: Then the Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Belaa Korowii ŋɔ Mosis be ŋɔ,

english_verse: to demand that the king of Egypt let the Israelites leave.
translation_verse: “La ka ŋɔ Ijipt kooro la be ŋɔ ó ɡel Israel tena la le o harɛ la ta.”

english_verse: But Moses replied, “I'm not a powerful speaker. If the Israelites won't listen to me, why should the king of Egypt?”
translation_verse: Asɛ Mosis ŋɔ Korowii be ŋɔ, “Israel tena ɡba aa wola a mun noɛ nɔ, ɛrɛɛ kooro te ɛɛ ba a mun noe yɔ? N nyoa aa kpɛlɛ ń won bol waa á do som.”

english_verse: But the Lord sent Aaron and Moses with a message for the Israelites and for the king. He also ordered Aaron and Moses to free the people from Egypt. Family Record of Aaron and Moses
translation_verse: Korowii berɔ bol Israel tena ne Ijipt kooro waa baɡle Mosis ne Arɔn, dɛ do ba ŋɔ bá ka kpɔ Israel tena le Ijipt harɛ ta. Mosis ne Arɔn naawa wa

english_verse: The following men were the heads of their ancestral clans: The sons of Reuben, Jacob's oldest son, were Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
translation_verse: Rubin waa ɛ Jekɔb bibanloɡle la bibaalaa Hanɔk ne Palu ne Hɛsrɔn dɛ Kaami. Ba sɔna nɔ cheɡɔ tɛ Rubin dea sɔna.

english_verse: The sons of Simeon were Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul, the son of a Canaanite woman.
translation_verse: Simeon ɡe bibaalaa Jɛmoɛl ne Jamin ne Ohad ne Jakin ne Soha dɛ Swaul o nya aa ɛ Keenan te. Simeon dea bii sɔnaa.

english_verse: Gershon's sons were Libni and Shimei.
translation_verse: Asɛ Gɛsɔn bibaalaa Libni ne Simee. Ba dea sɔnaa.

english_verse: Merari's sons were Mahli and Mushi. All of the above were from the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: Merari ɡe bibaalaa Maali ne Musi. Gɛɛ Lewi naanar teŋɛ dɔŋa nɛɛ dɛ le o dea.

english_verse: Izhar's sons were Korah, Nepheg, and Zichri.
translation_verse: Isiha ɡe bibaalaa Kora ne Nɛfɛɡ dɛ Sikri.

english_verse: Uzziel's sons were Mishael, Elzaphan, and Sithri.
translation_verse: Asɛ Usiel ɡe bibaala waa lol ba laanee Mesael ne Ɛlsafan dɛ Sitri.

english_verse: Aaron married Elisheba. She was the daughter of Amminadab and the sister of Nahshon; they had four sons, Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
translation_verse: Arɔn ɡe mo haah. O sɔne Eliseba. Dɛ Aminadab bihaahnee o ɛ Naasɔn nimambie. Bibaala baa lola laanee Nadab ne Abihu ne Eliasa dɛ Itama.

english_verse: Korah's sons were Assir, Elkanah, and Abiasaph.
translation_verse: Kora ɡe bibaalaa Asir ne Ɛlkana dɛ Abiasaf. Banee Kora dea sɔna.

english_verse: Aaron's son Eleazar married one of Putiel's daughters, and their son was Phinehas. This ends the list of those who were the heads of clans in the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: Arɔn bibaa Eliasa mo Putiel bihaah bɛl, asɛ dɛ lolɛ Fenehas. Banɔɔ le Lewi luɡe ta dɛ chɔ ba deene nyoo.

english_verse: The Lord had commanded Aaron and Moses to lead every family and tribe of Israel out of Egypt,
translation_verse: A ɡɛ Arɔn nɔ ne Mosisii Korowii ŋɔ bá ka kpɔ Israel tena le Ijipt harɛ ta la.

english_verse: and so they told the king of Egypt to set the people of Israel free. The Lord Commands Moses and Aaron To Speak to the King
translation_verse: Ba tentenee ŋɔ kooro be ŋɔ ó tɛ Israel tena ŋwɛnɛ bá kaa la. Arɔn cheɡɛ Mosis naa ta dɛɛ bol wa

english_verse: When the Lord spoke to Moses in the land of Egypt,
translation_verse: Korowii aa bol waa Mosis be Ijipt harɛ ta la,

english_verse: he said, “I am the Lord. Tell the king of Egypt everything I say to you.”
translation_verse: o ŋɔ, “Menee Korowii. Bol wobɛlbwa maa bol he be baɡle Ijipt kooro la.”

english_verse: But Moses answered, “You know I am a very poor speaker, and the king will never listen to me.”
translation_verse: Anee Mosis chaŋe ŋɔ, “N nyoa aa wola kpɛlɛ n won bol waa a do som nɔ, wɛɛ no a munii yaa?”

english_verse: The Lord said: I am going to let your brother Aaron speak for you. He will tell your message to the king, just as a prophet speaks my message to the people.
translation_verse: Asɛ Korowii ŋɔ Mosis be ŋɔ, “Dɛɛ no. N dɛ ba ɡela he do kɛŋɔ men Korowii ken Ijipt tena kooro sie, ásɛ he dɔɔ Arɔn ɛ keame dɛɛ bol waa o be.

english_verse: Tell Aaron everything I say to you, and he will order the king to let my people leave his country.
translation_verse: Ka ŋɔ wobɛlbwa maa dɛ bol he be nɔ baɡle Arɔn ó ŋɔ kooro be ó tɛ Israel tena la ŋwɛnɛ ba le o harɛ ta.

english_verse: But I will make the king so stubborn that he won't listen to you. He won't listen even when I do many terrible things to him and his nation. Then I will bring a final punishment on Egypt, and the king will let Israel's families and tribes go.
translation_verse: Waa wola he bee no nomanta, mɛɛ kpɔ deŋnetɛraa ba harɛ la ta dɛ́ do ba sibeɡra kohona dɛ́ lawɛ n nɛra Israel tena bwa le bela.

english_verse: When this happens, the Egyptians will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Mɛɛ baɡle n kpeɡri Ijipt harɛɛ, dɛ́ chɔɡ ba, dɛ́ lawɛ n nɛra Israel tena le, ásɛ Ijipt tena bwa jemɛ kɛŋɔ menee Korowii.”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron obeyed the Lord
translation_verse: Asɛ Mosis ne Arɔn ɛ ɡɛ Korowii aa bol ba be bwa.

english_verse: The Lord said, “Moses, when the king asks you and Aaron to perform a miracle, command Aaron to throw his walking stick down in front of the king, and it will turn into a snake.”
translation_verse: “Dɛ Ijipt kooro dɛ nyin kɛ he ɛ nyokpo waane o na naa, he ŋɔ Arɔn be ŋɔ ó kpɔ o daŋɡbala ta kooro sie. Wɛɛ berɛ harɛkonee.”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the king and his officials and did exactly as the Lord had commanded—Aaron threw the stick down, and it turned into a snake.
translation_verse: Anee ba la Ijipt kooro be dɛ ka ɛ ɡɛ Korowii aa ŋɔa ba ɛ la bwa. Asɛ Arɔn kpɔ o daŋɡbala la ta kooro ne o nomonome sie o berɛ harɛkon.

english_verse: Then the king called in the wise men and the magicians, who used their secret powers to do the same thing—
translation_verse: Ijipt kooro yerɛ Ijipt wejerema ne dobodobo tena cheme, asɛ dobodobo tena ɡe ɛ ba wa.

english_verse: they threw down sticks that turned into snakes. But Aaron's snake swallowed theirs.
translation_verse: Bɛlbwa kpɔ o daŋɡbala ta harɛ o berɛ harɛkon, kɛ Arɔn kon la wono lawɛ ba kwaa la liɡli.

english_verse: The king behaved just as the Lord had said and stubbornly refused to listen. The Nile River Turns into Blood
translation_verse: Anɔ bwa habɔɔ, dɛ Ijipt kooro deŋne ta kpeɡri o ŋɔ waa ba waa la munii no ɡɛ Korowii aa bola la. Nael Moo ne neerare bwa chal bera wa

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: The Egyptian king stubbornly refuses to change his mind and let the people go.
translation_verse: Belaa Korowii ŋɔ Mosis be ŋɔ, “Ijipt Kooro deŋne kpeɡri o vɛh nɛra la ŋwɛnɛ tae ba kaa kenɛ?

english_verse: Tomorrow morning take the stick that turned into a snake, then wait beside the Nile River for the king.
translation_verse: La o be chɔɔbɔr, hɛɛ nao kɛŋɔ waa dɛ kaa Nael Moo ta. Ka che nee la nyoa kpao dɛ́ kpɔ daŋɡbala o fa aa berɛ harɛkon la kpoŋe.”

english_verse: Tell him, “The Lord God of the Hebrews sent me to order you to release his people, so they can worship him in the desert. But until now, you have paid no attention.
translation_verse: Kenii chɛ kɛ he ŋɔ o be, “Korowii Hibru tena aa dɛ tomɔ laanee tom mɛ he be ŋɔ he ta o nɛra Israel tena ŋwɛnɛ bá kaa, dɛ́ won ka tomɔ pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta. Kɛ, ba le saŋ nɔ he ta o be noɛ.”

english_verse: “The Lord is going to do something to show you that he really is the Lord. I will strike the Nile with this stick, and the water will turn into blood.
translation_verse: Anomanta, o ŋɔ, “Anɔɔ hɛɛ ba kpɔe dɛ́ jemɛ kɛŋɔ onee Korowii. N dɛ ba daŋɡbala nɔ kpɔe lɔ nee nɔ sie, ásɛ o bwa berɛ chal.

english_verse: The fish will die, the river will stink, and none of you Egyptians will be able to drink the water.”
translation_verse: Pɛŋa aa lɔ o bini bwa ɛɛ serewoo, ásɛ o do sɔɔh kohona Ijipt te bɛlbwa aa wola won nyɔ o ne.”

english_verse: Moses, then command Aaron to hold his stick over the water. And when he does, every drop of water in Egypt will turn into blood, including rivers, canals, ponds, and even the water in buckets and jars.
translation_verse: Korowii berɔ ŋɔ Mosis be ŋɔ, “Ŋɔ Arɔn be ó tɛr o daŋɡbala dɛ́ kpɔ pa Ijipt neerare bwa ta, nenabɔɔne ne taama dɛ buli bwa, ásɛ a berɛ chal. Chal ɛɛ perɛ harɛ la ta bobɛlbwaa. Hale komɛlbwa nee aa lɔ o bini bwa.”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron obeyed the Lord. Aaron held out his stick, then struck the Nile, as the king and his officials watched. The river turned into blood,
