translation_verse: Asɛ Mosis ne Arɔn ɛ ɡɛ Korowii aa do ba la. Arɔn kpɔ o daŋɡbala la lɔ nee la Ijipt kooro ne o nomonome sie, asɛ nee la bwa berɛ chal.

english_verse: the fish died, and the water smelled so bad that none of the Egyptians could drink it. Blood was everywhere in Egypt.
translation_verse: Pɛŋa aa lɔ Nael Moo ta bwa serewɔ, dɛ do sɔɔh kohona Ijipt te bɛlbwa ta wone nyɔ o ne. Asɛ chal perɛ harɛ la ta bwa.

english_verse: But the Egyptian magicians used their secret powers to do the same thing. The king did just as the Lord had said—he stubbornly refused to listen.
translation_verse: Belaa Ijipt dobodobo tena ba ɛ ba wa dɛ ɡe ɛ ɡɛ tenten. Dɛ kooro ta lɔ o deŋnekpeɡ la ta, o ta ba waa la ta noɛ ɡɛ Korowii aa bola la.

english_verse: Then he went back to his palace and never gave it a second thought.
translation_verse: O berɔ kaa o koodem, dɛ ka laa o liire kpɔ waa waa naa la bwa ta.

english_verse: The Egyptians had to dig holes along the banks of the Nile for drinking water, because water from the river was unfit to drink. Frogs
translation_verse: Ijipt tena bwa ka dɛ kwi bɔɔne Nael Moo nyoa dɛɛ nyin nee ba nyɔ, dɛkalkɛ dɛ baa won ba nee la nyɔ kpa. Sapone ane wa

english_verse: Seven days after the Lord had struck the Nile,
translation_verse: Korowii aa ɡela nee la berɛ chal la, a yawanyoa habɔɔ o berɛ bol waa Mosis be.

english_verse: he said to Moses: Go to the palace and tell the king of Egypt that I order him to let my people go, so they can worship me.
translation_verse: Belaa Korowii bol waa Mosis be ŋɔ, “La Ijipt tena kooro be, dɛ́ ka ŋɔ n ŋɔ o tɛ n nɛra ŋwɛnɛ, ásɛ ba kaa tom mɛ.

english_verse: If he refuses, I will cover his entire country with frogs.
translation_verse: Dɛ o ta sɛɛh dɛ ɡel ba kaa laa, mɛɛ ɡeloo sapone ba su harɛ nɔ bwa ta.

english_verse: Warn the king that the Nile will be full of frogs, and from there they will spread into the royal palace, including the king's bedroom and even his bed. Frogs will enter the homes of his officials and will find their way into ovens and into the bowls of bread dough.
translation_verse: Aa su Nael Moo bwaa dɛ́ ba le koodem ne o dea ne o chɔɔbɔr bwa. O nomonome ne o nɛra bwa deremi, ne bela baa dɛ ɛ kondikwaare, ne bela baa dɛ wɔɔ paanoo, dɛ kwaa baa dɛ charame paanoo a bini bwa taa aa ba sui.

english_verse: Frogs will be crawling on everyone—the king, his officials, and every citizen of Egypt.
translation_verse: O ne o nomonome ne harɛ la ta tena bwa nɛɛ sapone la ɛɛ ba jaeh dɛɛ teeh.”

english_verse: Moses, now command Aaron to hold his stick over the water. Then frogs will come from all rivers, canals, and ponds in Egypt, and they will cover the land.
translation_verse: Korowii ɡelɔ Mosis ŋɔ Arɔn be ŋɔ, “Tɛr he daŋɡbala pa buli ne taama dɛ neerare ta, ásɛ sapone le ba su Ijipt harɛ bwa ta.”

english_verse: Aaron obeyed, and suddenly frogs were everywhere in Egypt.
translation_verse: Asɛ Arɔn tɛr pa neerare la ta, asɛ sapone la ba tɔ harɛ la bwa ta.

english_verse: But the magicians used their secret powers to do the same thing.
translation_verse: Dobodobo tena la ɡe ɛ ba we-ɛɛla dɛ ɡel sapone ba harɛ la ta.

english_verse: The king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “If you ask the Lord to take these frogs away from me and my people, I will let your people go and offer sacrifices to him.”
translation_verse: Belaa Ijipt kooro yerɛ Mosis ne Arɔn dɛ ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, “Hé soŋe Korowii ásɛ o laa sapone nɔ kpɔ n ne n nɛra nɛ, ásɛ n tɛ he nɛra ŋwɛnɛ bá ka kpoo kwaa tɛ Korowii.”

english_verse: “All right,” Moses answered. “You choose the time when I am to pray for the frogs to stop bothering you, your officials, and your people, and for them to leave your houses and be found only in the river.”
translation_verse: Anee Mosis ŋɔ, “A wer ɡa, mɛɛ soŋoo tɛɛ. Kɛ n poori, baɡle tɔpere haa dɛ nyin, ásɛ n soŋe tɛ he ne he nomonome ne he nɛra á le he nɛ, a ka Nael Moo kwaa la ɡbo.”

english_verse: “Do it tomorrow!” the king replied. “As you wish,” Moses agreed. “Then everyone will discover that there is no god like the Lord,
translation_verse: Asɛ Ijipt kooro chaŋo ŋɔ, “Soŋe tɛ mɛ kere.” Anee Mosis ŋɔ, “N noɔ, mɛɛ ɛ ɡɛ haa ŋɔa nɔɔ, ásɛ he jemɛ kɛŋɔ Korowii yaa dɛ tomɔ nɔ dɔŋ toole.

english_verse: and frogs will no longer be found anywhere, except in the Nile.”
translation_verse: Sapone la ɛɛ le he ne he nomonome ne nɛra ne he deremi taa, ásɛ a ka Nael Moo kwaa la ɡbo.”

english_verse: After Moses and Aaron left the palace, Moses begged the Lord to do something about the frogs he had sent as punishment for the king.
translation_verse: Ba le Ijipt kooro be bela, asɛ Mosis wi no Korowii ŋɔ ó laa sapone waa kpɔa ba ta kooro nɛɛ la kpɔ o nɛ.

english_verse: The Lord listened to Moses, and the frogs died everywhere—in houses, yards, and fields.
translation_verse: Asɛ Korowii no o wesoŋa la, dɛ ɡel sapone aa lɔ deene ne dembaahna ne kooni bwa serewe.

english_verse: The dead frogs were placed in piles, and the whole country began to stink.
translation_verse: Anee ba boa a nyoa a dadaŋɛ chɔ, bobɛlbwa taŋre.

english_verse: But when the king saw that things were now better, he again did just as the Lord had said he would and stubbornly refused to listen to Moses and Aaron. Gnats
translation_verse: Bosɔɔhna aa bala la, kooro berɔ ɛ deŋnekpeɡ dɛ vɛh Mosis ne Arɔn waa la ta teŋa ɡɛ Korowii aa bola la. Konjeɡre ane wa

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Command Aaron to strike the ground with his walking stick, and everywhere in Egypt the dust will turn into gnats.”
translation_verse: Asɛ Korowii ŋɔ Mosis be ŋɔ, “Ŋɔ Arɔn be ó kpɔ daŋɡbala la lɔ harɛ, ásɛ konjeɡre fuɡe le Ijipt harɛ bwa ta.

english_verse: They obeyed, and when Aaron struck the ground with the stick, gnats started swarming on people and animals. In fact, every speck of dust in Egypt turned into a gnat.
translation_verse: Anee Arɔn kpɔ daŋɡbala la lɔ harɛ asɛ bomboɡ aa lɔ Ijipt harɛ ta bwa berɛ konjeɡre tɔ nɛra ne ola nɛ.”

english_verse: When the magicians tried to use their secret powers to do this, they failed, and gnats stayed on people and animals.
translation_verse: Dobodobo tena la ɛ ba we-ɛɛla bwa baa ɛ dɛ ɡe ɡel konjeɡre ba kahonɛ. Dɛ konjeɡre la tɔ nɛra ne ola bwa nɛ.

english_verse: The magicians told the king, “God has done this.” But, as the Lord had said, the king was too stubborn to listen. Flies
translation_verse: Anee dobodobo tena la ŋɔ kooro la be ŋɔ, “Korowii we-ɛɛlaa nɔ noo!” Kɛ ane a bwa, dɛ Ijipt kooro deŋne ta kpeɡri o vɛh waa la noe, ɡɛ Korowii aa bola la. Chwɛɛhne ane wa

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: Early tomorrow morning, while the king is on his way to the river, go and say to him, “The Lord commands you to let his people go, so they can worship him.
translation_verse: Korowii ŋɔ Mosis be ŋɔ, “Kere chɔmbibii he ir. Kooro ɛɛ iruu dɛɛ kaa nee la ta, ásɛ he la o be dɛ́ ka ŋɔ kenii men Korowii ŋɔ, ‘Tɛ n nɛra ŋwɛnɛ ba kaa dɛ́ kaa tom mɛ.

english_verse: If you don't, he will send swarms of flies to attack you, your officials, and every citizen of your country. Your houses will be full of flies, and the ground will crawl with them.
translation_verse: He vɛh n nɛra ŋwɛnɛ tɛɛ ba kaa laa, mɛɛ ɡeloo chwɛɛhne fuɡe le he ne nɛra ne nomonome nɛ, dɛ deene bwa bini. Ijipt tena deene ne harɛ la bwa ɛɛ su chwɛɛhnee.

english_verse: “The Lord's people in Goshen won't be bothered by flies, but your people in the rest of the country will be tormented by them. That's how you will know that the Lord is here in Egypt. This miracle will happen tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Mɛɛ ɡeloo he jemɛ kɛŋɔ n nɛra korɛ he nɛra bini. Kere ɡbosoroo a ɡɛ nyokpowaa nɔ ɛɛ ba ɛɛ.’ ”

english_verse: The Lord kept his promise—the palace and the homes of the royal officials swarmed with flies, and the rest of the country was infested with them as well.
translation_verse: Asɛ Korowii ɛ ɡɛ, dɛ ɡel chwɛɛhne fuɡe le, dɛ ba su koodem ne o nomonome deremi, dɛ chɔɡ harɛ la bwa.

english_verse: Then the king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “Go ahead and sacrifice to your God, but stay here in Egypt.”
translation_verse: Belaa Ijipt kooro yerɛ Mosis ne Arɔn dɛ ŋɔ, “Hé ir kaa dɛ́ ka kpoo kwaa tɛ Korowii n harɛ ta bonɔ.”

english_verse: “That's impossible!” Moses replied. “Any sacrifices we offer to the Lord our God would disgust the Egyptians, and they would stone us to death.
translation_verse: Anee Mosis chaŋe ŋɔ, “A ta maɡrɛ kɛ ya ɛa bonɔ. Kwaa yaa kpɔ tɛ Korowii la ɛ kwaa haa kia. Dɛ ya ŋɔ ya ɛa he siwi ta naa, he nɛra aa yaa bwea foɡre kpo aa?

english_verse: No indeed! The Lord has ordered us to walk three days into the desert before offering sacrifices to him, and that's what we have to do.”
translation_verse: Gɛ Korowii yaa dɛ tomɔ aa ŋɔ ya be la, a chɛ kɛ yá valɛ tɔpera atoro ŋwɛnɛ pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta, dɛ́ ka kpoo kwaa tɛo.”

english_verse: Then the king told him, “I'll let you go into the desert to offer sacrifices, if you don't go very far. But in the meantime, pray for me.”
translation_verse: Anee Ijipt kooro ŋɔ, “Mɛɛ tɛ ŋwɛnɛɛ he la ka kpo kwaa tɛ Korowii haa dɛ tomɔ la pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta, kɛ he bɛ bojaŋ kaa. Hé soŋe Korowii tɛ mɛ mɔɔ.”

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” Moses replied, “I'll pray for you as soon as I leave, and by tomorrow the flies will stop bothering you, your officials, and the citizens of your country. Only make sure that you're telling the truth this time and that you really intend to let our people offer sacrifices to the Lord.”
translation_verse: Asɛ Mosis chaŋe ŋɔ, “Dɛ n le bonɔ naa, mɛɛ ka soŋe Korowii, ásɛ kere ɡbosoroo chwɛɛhne la le he ne nomonome ne he nɛra bwa nɛ. Kɛ na kɛŋɔ haa nyosonee teŋe kpa, haa wola ɡel Korowii nɛra la bɛ ŋwɛnɛ dɔ ka kpoo kwaa tɛo.”

english_verse: After leaving the palace, Moses prayed,
translation_verse: Belaa Mosis le Ijipt kooro be bela dɛ ka soŋe Korowii tɛo.

english_verse: and the Lord answered his prayer. Not a fly was left to pester the king, his officials, or anyone else in Egypt.
translation_verse: Asɛ Korowii ɛ ɡɛ waa soŋa la. O ɡelɔ chwɛɛhne la bwa le kooro ne o nomonome ne o nɛra bwa nɛ, beŋkpoŋ kwaraa ta kae.

english_verse: But the king turned stubborn again and would not let the people go.
translation_verse: Kɛ Ijipt kooro berɔ ɛ deŋnekpeɡ anɔ ɡe ta ja, o ta ɡelɛ nɛra la kaa.

english_verse: The Lord sent Moses with this message for the king of Egypt: The Lord God of the Hebrews commands you to let his people go, so they can worship him.
translation_verse: Belaa Korowii ŋɔ Mosis be ŋɔ ó la Ijipt kooro la be dɛ́ ka ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Kenii men Korowii Hibru tena aa dɛ tom mɛ la ɛɛ bol. N ŋɔ, tɛ n nɛra ŋwɛnɛ ásɛ ba ka tom mɛ.

english_verse: he will bring a terrible disease on your horses and donkeys, your camels and cattle, and your sheep and goats.
translation_verse: Korowii ŋɔ wɛɛ kpɔ weechɔɡaa ba ta he kondɛɛra bwa nɛ. He jaɡre ne keeɡore ne nyoɡmare ne nae ne boohna dɛ peera bwa ɛɛ we weelaa.

english_verse: But the Lord will protect the animals that belong to the people of Israel, and none of theirs will die.
translation_verse: Kɛ Korowii ɛɛ kpɔ nɔnee tɔ Israel tena kondɛɛra nɛɛ ásɛ a te bɛ serewe á baɡle kɛ o nɛra korɔ.”

english_verse: Tomorrow is the day the Lord has set to do this.
translation_verse: Asɛ Korowii do tɔpere dɛ ŋɔ, “Keree men Korowii ɛɛ ba ɡɛ waa nɔ ɛɛ harɛ nɔ ta.”

english_verse: It happened the next day—all of the animals belonging to the Egyptians died, but the Israelites did not lose even one.
translation_verse: Tɔ aa pera la, Korowii ɛ ɡɛ waa bola la. Kondɛɛra aa ɛ Ijipt tena kwaa la bwa serewɔ. Kɛ anɔ la aa ɛ Israel tena kwaa la te, beŋkpoŋ kwaraa ta sewɛ.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses and Aaron: Take a few handfuls of ashes from a stove and you, Moses, throw them into the air. Be sure the king is watching.
translation_verse: Anee Korowii ŋɔ Mosis ne Arɔn be ŋɔ, “Hé ɛ tɔɔ nɔn dela le nimar bɔr, ásɛ Mosis ka che Ijipt kooro sie dɛ́ taa nyundua.

english_verse: The ashes will blow across the land of Egypt, causing sores to break out on people and animals.
translation_verse: Aa berɛ tutuɡii dɛ́ tɔ Ijipt harɛ bwa, ásɛ ɔɡra chole kondɛɛra ne nɛra baa lɔ harɛ la ta bwa nɛ dɛ́ pili ŋwɛra.”

english_verse: So they took a few handfuls of ashes and went to the king. Moses threw them into the air, and sores immediately broke out on the Egyptians and their animals.
translation_verse: Mosis ne Arɔn ɛ tɔɔ la, dɛ ka che kooro sie. Asɛ Mosis taa nyundua, asɛ ɔɡra chole lee nɛra ne kondɛɛra nɛ, dɛ pili ŋwɛra.

english_verse: The magicians were suffering so much from the sores, that they could not even come to Moses.
translation_verse: Anɔ te la, dobodobo tena la ta wone ba che Mosis sie kpa, dɛkalkɛ dɛ ɔɡra la ɔɡre ba ne ba bwɛɛ la tena bwa.

english_verse: Everything happened just as the Lord had told Moses—he made the king too stubborn to listen to Moses and Aaron. Hailstones
translation_verse: Kɛ Korowii ɡelɔ Ijipt kooro deŋne do kpeɡri o ta Mosis ne Arɔn be noɛ ɡɛ waa bola la. Dombwea ane wa

english_verse: The Lord told Moses to get up early the next morning and say to the king: The Lord God of the Hebrews commands you to let his people go, so they can worship him!
translation_verse: Asɛ Korowii ŋɔ Mosis be ŋɔ, “Ir kere chɔmbibi dɛ́ la Ijipt kooro be dɛ́ ka ŋɔ ‘Kenii men Korowii Hibru tena aa dɛ tom mɛ la ŋɔ. Tɛ n nɛra ŋwɛnɛ ásɛ ba kaa tom mɛ,

english_verse: If you don't, he will send his worst plagues to strike you, your officials, and everyone else in your country. Then you will find out that no one can oppose the Lord.
translation_verse: A laa ɡe aa, mɛɛ tɛr he ne he nomonome ne he nɛra deŋnee á ɡwaa kohona, ásɛ he jemɛ kɛŋɔ nomɛlbwa toole dɛ do kɛŋɔ men harɛ nɔ bwa ta.

english_verse: In fact, he could already have sent a terrible disease and wiped you from the face of the earth.
translation_verse: Dɛ n fe dɛ nyin aa, n fe kpɔ serewe weela ba kpoo he bwa.

english_verse: But he has kept you alive, just to show you his power and to bring honor to himself everywhere in the world.
translation_verse: Kɛ n ɡelɔ he do le, ásɛ he na ɡɛ maa dɔ kpeɡri, ásɛ nɛwɛnyina bwa che he nɛɛ dɛɛ yerɛ n sɔn harɛ nɔ ta bobɛlbwa.

english_verse: You are still determined not to let the Lord's people go.
translation_verse: Kɛ ane a bwa, he ta dɛ maŋkura he te dɛɛ tɔ n nɛra nɛɛ ŋɔ haa ɡel ba kaa.

english_verse: All right. At this time tomorrow, he will bring on Egypt the worst hailstorm in its history.
translation_verse: Anomanta, n dɛ ba ɡela dombwea aa tɔɡa lee kere saŋ nɔ bɔr. Le saŋ la baa vɔrɔwe Ijipt bwa ɡɛ dombwea nɔ dɔŋa ta o ta leere mɔɔ.

english_verse: You had better give orders for every person and every animal in Egypt to take shelter. If they don't, they will die.
translation_verse: Gel ba ka teɡɛ kondɛɛra bɛlbwa aa lɔ dibɔr ba do deene. Dombwea la dɛ ba leera dɛ́ kpoo nɛra ne kondɛɛra aa lɔ kooni ta, ne komɛlbwa kon aa wola o nɛɛ tɔe.’ ”

english_verse: Some of the king's officials were frightened by what the Lord had said, and they hurried off to make sure their slaves and animals were safe.
translation_verse: Kooro nomonome baa ɔmɛ Korowii waa la ɛ warane kpɔ ba nɛndɔɔla ne kondɛɛra ba dem.

english_verse: But others paid no attention to his threats and left their slaves and animals out in the open.
translation_verse: Kɛ banɔ la baa taŋ deŋne Korowii waa la ta la te ɡel ba nɛndɔɔla ne ba kondɛɛra kooni ta.

english_verse: Then the Lord told Moses, “Stretch your arm toward the sky, so that hailstones will fall on people, animals, and crops in the land of Egypt.”
translation_verse: Belaa Korowii ŋɔ Mosis be ja ŋɔ, “Tɛr he nɔn pa nyundua, ásɛ dombwea lee nɛra ne kondɛɛra ne koo kondikwa, dɛ komɛlbwa aa lɔ Ijipt harɛ bwa ta.”

english_verse: Moses pointed his walking stick toward the sky, and hailstones started falling everywhere. Thunder roared, and lightning flashed back and forth, striking the ground. This was the worst storm in the history of Egypt.
translation_verse: A leero asɛ bwaala ɛɛ nyɛɡle bobɛlbwa pelɔpelɔ ken dɛɛ kɔɡre dɛ do ɔma. A dɔŋa ta Ijipt harɛ ta chiɡe bwa.

english_verse: People, animals, and crops were pounded by the hailstones, and bark was stripped from trees.
translation_verse: A chɔɡ kwaa komɛlbwa aa wola o ta tɔe. Le nɛra nɛɛ ba le kondɛɛra ta. Hale koo kwa ne daa bwa.

english_verse: Only Goshen, where the Israelites lived, was safe from the storm.
translation_verse: Gosen harɛ, bela Israel tena aa soɡa la ɡboo a ta leere.

english_verse: The king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “Now I have really sinned! My people and I are guilty, and the Lord is right.
translation_verse: Belaa Ijipt kooro yerɛ Mosis ne Arɔn dɛ ŋɔ, “Taraken n nao kɛŋɔ n ɛ wechɔɡa, Korowii waa toɡra. N ne n nɛra sɛh chɔɡre.

english_verse: We can't stand any more of this thunder and hail. Please ask the Lord to make it stop. Your people can go—you don't have to stay in Egypt any longer.”
translation_verse: Soŋe Korowii tɛ yaa. Bwaala kɔɡra ne dombwea la ɡwaalɔ to. Mɛɛ ɡeloo he kaa, maa heyaa lawɛ so kpa.”

english_verse: Moses answered, “As soon as I leave the city, I will lift my arms in prayer. When the thunder and hail stop, you will know that the earth belongs to the Lord.
translation_verse: Ate, Mosis chaŋe dɛ ŋɔ, “N baa le bwɛɛ nɔ ta naa, mɛɛ ɡɔɔ n nɔɔra nyunduaa dɛ́ soŋe Korowii. Bwaala kɔɡra la ɛɛ ɡeloo, dombwea la ɡe ɡel leera, ásɛ he jemɛ kɛŋɔ Korowiirii dɔ harɛ bwa.

english_verse: But I am certain that neither you nor your officials really fear the Lord God.”
translation_verse: Kɛ ane a bwa, n jemɔ kɛŋɔ he ne he nomonome deŋne ta kpeɡri haa Korowii ɔmɛ dɛ ba le fini.”

english_verse: Meanwhile, the flax and barley crops had been destroyed by the storm because they were ready to ripen.
translation_verse: Dombwea la chɔɡ koo kwaa aa kpɔ bie bwa.

english_verse: But the wheat crops ripen later, and they were not damaged.
translation_verse: Koo kwaa aa ka mun a ta bie kpɔe mɔɔ la te ta chɔɡɛ.

english_verse: After Moses left the royal palace and the city, he lifted his arms in prayer to the Lord, and the thunder, hail, and drenching rain stopped.
translation_verse: Mosis aa le Ijipt kooro be dɛ le bwɛɛ la ta la, o ɡɔɔ nɔɔra nyundua dɛ soŋe Korowii. Belaa bwaala kɔɡra, ne dombwea leera dɛ bwaala la bwa ɡel.

english_verse: When the king realized that the storm was over, he disobeyed once more. He and his officials were so stubborn
translation_verse: Kooro aa na ɡɛ la, o berɔ ɛ wechɔɡa ja. Anee kɛ o ne o nomonome la berɔ ɛ ba deŋnekpeɡ la ja.

english_verse: that he refused to let the Israelites go. This was exactly what the Lord had said would happen.
translation_verse: Ba vɛh Israel tena ŋwɛnɛ tɛɛ bá kaa, ɡɛ Korowii aa ŋɔ Mosis be la.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: Go back to the king. I have made him and his officials stubborn, so that I could work these miracles.
translation_verse: Belaa Korowii ŋɔ Mosis be ŋɔ, “La Ijipt kooro be, n ɡelɔ o ne o nomonome deŋne do kpeɡri ɡɛ aa ɛ ń won ɡel ba na n nyokpowe-ɛɛla ba baah,

english_verse: I did this because I want you to tell your children and your grandchildren about my miracles and about my harsh treatment of the Egyptians. Then all of you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: ásɛ kerekere he bol baɡle he bii ne naanar ɡɛ maa do Ijipt tena sibeɡra dɛ ɛ nyokpowe-ɛɛla la, ásɛ ba jemɛ kɛŋɔ menee Korowii.”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the king and told him that the Lord God of the Hebrews had said: How long will you stubbornly refuse to obey? Release my people so they can worship me.
translation_verse: Anomanta, Mosis ne Arɔn la Ijipt kooro be dɛ ka ŋɔ kenii Korowii Hibru tena aa dɛ tomɔ la ŋɔ, “Saŋ besoo hɛɛ ba he liire ne harɛ bala dɛ́ ɡel he deŋnekpeɡ nɔɔ? Gel n nɛra kaa dɛ́ kaa tom mɛ.

english_verse: Do this by tomorrow, or I will cover your country with so many locusts
translation_verse: He vɛoh he ta ɡelɛ ba kaa laa, kere mɛɛ ɡeloo tontombɛ ba harɛ nɔ ta.

translation_verse: Aa su he dem ne he nomonome deremi ne Ijipt te bɛlbwa demii. A ɡɛ waa nɔ ɛ waa he naawa aa wola a dɔŋa nae ka.” Mosis aa tona la, o le kooro be kaa.

english_verse: The king had Moses and Aaron brought back, and he said, “All right, you may go and worship the Lord your God. But first tell me who will be going.”
translation_verse: Belaa ba yerɛ Mosis ne Arɔn ba kooro be ja, asɛ o ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, “Hé kaa dɛ́ ka tomɛ he Korowii haa dɛ tomɔ la. Aah he bini bamewa tenee dɛɛ kaa nɔɔ?”

english_verse: “Everyone, young and old,” Moses answered. “We will even take our sheep, goats, and cattle, because we want to hold a celebration in honor of the Lord.”
translation_verse: Asɛ Mosis chaŋe ŋɔ, “Ya bwaa dɛɛ ba kaala. Bechale ne hanjeni ne banjeni, ne bibaala ne bihaahna dɛ ya kondɛɛra bwa, dɛkalkɛ ya dɛ la ka di tɔpejen bɛl Korowii sɔn ta.”

translation_verse: Kooro la ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “N ŋwɛɛ he Korowii la kɛŋɔ maa ɡel he kpɔ he haahna ne bechale la kaa. Liichɔɡaa lɔ he nyu bini ɡɛ la.

translation_verse: Aa ɡɛɛ maɡre, hé ɡel baala la ɡbo kaa dɛ́ ka tomɛ he Korowii la. Gɛɛ he ŋɔ la.” Asɛ ba doŋi Mosis ne Arɔn le kooro sie bela.

translation_verse: Korowii ŋɔ Mosis be ŋɔ, “Tɛr he nɔn pa Ijipt harɛ ta, ásɛ tontombɛ fuɡe le dɛ́ ba di koo kwaa aa kaa ne komɛlbwa dombwea la aa wola wone chɔɡ la.”

english_verse: Moses held out his walking stick, and the Lord sent an east wind that blew across Egypt the rest of the day and all that night. By morning, locusts
translation_verse: Asɛ o tɛr o daŋɡbala laa lɔ o nɔn ta la pa harɛ la ta, asɛ Korowii ɡel peu bɛl le wee leebɔr, dɛ ta harɛ la ta awola tɔpere la ne o jwaana bwa. Tɔ aa pera chɔɔ la, dɛ peu la kpɔ tontombɛ la ba.

english_verse: The ground was black with locusts, and they ate everything left on the trees and in the fields. Nothing green remained in Egypt—not a tree or a plant.
translation_verse: A balɔ warɛ dɛ tɔ harɛ la sie bwa o bir ken. A di kwaa dombwea la aa wola chɔɡɛ la bwa. Kwaa aa lɔ koo ne daa nɔna bwa. Konduuli bɛlbwa toole dɛ ka. Komɛlbwa ta Ijipt harɛ ta kae.

english_verse: At once the king sent for Moses and Aaron. He told them, “I have sinned against the Lord your God and against you.
translation_verse: Belaa Ijipt kooro ɛ warane dɛ ɡel ba yerɛ Mosis ne Arɔn tɛo dɛ soŋ ba ŋɔ, “N ɛ Korowii haa dɛ tomɔ la ne he bwa wechɔɡa.

english_verse: Forgive me one more time and ask the Lord to stop these insects from killing every living plant.”
translation_verse: Hé kpɔ n wechɔɡa kɛ mɛ ja dɛ́ soŋe Korowii haa dɛ tomɔ la o laa serewe waa nɔ kpɔ n nɛ.”

english_verse: Moses left the palace and prayed.
translation_verse: Ate, Mosis le kooro be bela dɛ ka soŋe Korowii.

translation_verse: Korowii beɡre peu la o ta kpeɡri nɛɛ le wee cholibɔr dɛ kpɔ tontombɛ la ka ta Mposwɛm ta. Beŋkpoŋ kwaraa ta harɛ la ta kae kpa.

translation_verse: Kɛ Korowii ɡelɔ kooro la bambile ta do kpeɡri o vɛh Israel tena la ŋwɛnɛ tɛɛ bá kaa. Biro tenten wa

english_verse: During that time, the Egyptians could not see each other or leave their homes, but there was light where the Israelites lived.

translation_verse: Belaa kooro yerɛ Mosis dɛ ŋɔ, “Hé kaa ásɛ dɛ ka tomɛ he Korowii la. Hé kpɔ haahna ne bechale kaa dɛ́ ɡel kondɛɛra la te.”

english_verse: “No!” Moses replied. “You must let us offer sacrifices to the Lord our God,
translation_verse: Asɛ Mosis chaŋe ŋɔ “A chɛ kɛ yá kpɔ kondɛɛra yaa ka kpoo ɛ saraha dɛ́ fuh ane tɛ Korowii yaa dɛ tomɔ la.

english_verse: and we won't know which animals we will need until we get there. That's why we can't leave even one of them here.”
translation_verse: A chɛ kɛ yá kaa ya kondɛɛra ɡe bwa ne beŋkpoŋ kwaraa aa wola ka. A bini anee yaa ba kpɔe ɛ saraha tɛ Korowii yaa dɛ tomɔ la, kɛ dɛ ya ta bela telaa, yaa won jemɛ anɔ la yaa lawɛ ɛ.”

english_verse: This time the Lord made the king so stubborn
translation_verse: Korowii ɡelɔ Ijipt kooro deŋne ta do kpeɡri, o ta ɡelɛ ba kaa.

english_verse: that he said to Moses, “Get out and stay out! If you ever come back, you're dead!”
translation_verse: Asɛ o ŋɔ Mosis be ŋɔ, “Le n sie bonɔ kaa! Dɛɛ berɛ n sie bonɔ bala kpa. Awola haa ba n sie bonɔ la, dɛ he sewee.”

english_verse: “Have it your way,” Moses answered. “You won't see me again.”
translation_verse: Anee o chaŋo ŋɔ, “Kasinteŋii, maa he sie bonɔɔ ba kpa.”

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: I am going to punish the king of Egypt and his people one more time. Then the king will gladly let you leave his land. In fact, he will even chase you out.
translation_verse: Asɛ Korowii berɛ ŋɔ Mosis be ŋɔ, “N dɛ ba deŋnetɛra beŋkpoŋ kpɔe ba ta Ijipt kooro la ne o nɛra nɛɛ ja. A habɔɔ la, wɛɛ ɡeloo he kaa. Doŋa kwaraa wɛɛ ba heyaa doŋa.

english_verse: Now go and tell my people to ask their Egyptian neighbors for gold and silver jewelry.
translation_verse: Berɛ ɡel Israel tena no kɛŋɔ, ba baala ne haahna bwa soŋe ba bala Ijipt tena suuɡaswɛm ne suuɡapoŋa kwa.”

english_verse: So the Lord made the Egyptians greatly respect the Israelites, and everyone, including the king's officials, considered Moses an important leader.
translation_verse: Korowii ɡelɔ Ijipt tena sie lɛ Israel tena la nɛ, asɛ kooro ne o nomonome ne harɛ la ta nɛra bwa kpɔ Mosis ɛ nɛnjen.

english_verse: Moses went to the king and said: I have come to let you know what the Lord is going to do. About midnight he will go through the land of Egypt,
translation_verse: Belaa Mosis ŋɔ Ijipt kooro be ŋɔ, “Kenii Korowii ɛɛ bol, dɛ wɛɛ valɛ harɛ nɔ bwa ta harambaŋaa,

english_verse: and wherever he goes, the first-born son in every family will die. Your own son will die, and so will the son of the lowest slave woman. Even the first-born males of your cattle will die.
translation_verse: ásɛ dɛ kpoo Ijipt tena bibanloɡla bwa. Dɛ́ le kooro waa soɡe kara ta bibanloɡle nɛ, dɛ́ ba le yomhaah waa lɔ nam ta bibanloɡle nɛ dɛ nae biloɡla.

english_verse: Everywhere in Egypt there will be loud crying. Nothing like this has ever happened before or will ever happen again.
translation_verse: Nɛra ɛɛ dɛɛ dooɡe lɔŋɔree dɛɛ wi kohona harɛ la ta a dɔŋa aa wola chiɡ bwa. A dɔŋa ɡe aa chiɡ kpa bwa.

english_verse: But there won't be any need for the Israelites to cry. Things will be so quiet that not even a dog will be heard barking. Then you Egyptians will know that the Lord is good to the Israelites, even while he punishes you.
translation_verse: Kɛ Israel tena te bini la, nyoate aa nɛn kɛɛ kondɛɛre kwaraa wor. Anee dɛ́ ɡel he jemɛ kɛŋɔ Korowii dɛ nyin o nɛra Israel tena dɛ ɡel ba korɛ Ijipt tena bini.

english_verse: Your leaders will come and bow down, begging me to take my people and leave your country. Then we will leave. Moses was very angry; he turned and left the king.
translation_verse: He nomonome nɔ bwa ɛɛ berɔɔ ba n be, dɛ́ ba ɡuŋ mɛ dɛ́ ŋɔ ń kaa, n ne n nɛra bwa baa teŋɛ n nɛ. Ásɛ mɔɔ ń kaa.” Belaa Mosis kpɔ bandia kohona le kooro sie kaa.

english_verse: What the Lord had earlier said to Moses came true. He had said, “The king of Egypt won't listen. Then I will perform even more miracles.”
translation_verse: Korowii fa bol Mosis be ŋɔ, “Ijipt kooro ɛɛ ɛ deŋnekpeɡii dɛ́ vɛh he be noe, ásɛ n nyokpowaa maa ɛ Ijipt harɛ la do kan.”

english_verse: So the king of Egypt saw Moses and Aaron work miracles, but the Lord made him stubbornly refuse to let the Israelites leave his country.
translation_verse: Mosis ne Arɔn ɛ nyokpowe-ɛɛla nɔ bwa kooro sie. Korowii ɡelɔ o deŋne ta do kpeɡri o ta ɡelɛ Israel tena la le o harɛ ta kaa.

english_verse: Some time later the Lord said to Moses and Aaron:
translation_verse: Korowii bol waa baɡle Mosis ne Arɔn Ijipt harɛ ta ja,

english_verse: Tell the people of Israel that on the tenth day of this month the head of each family must choose a lamb or a young goat for his family to eat.
translation_verse: Hé ŋɔ Israel tena be ŋɔ a ɡɛ korobie nɔ tɔpera fi ta la, bɛlbwa lawɛ pebie ó che tɛ o ne o dem tena. Dem te bɛlbwa lawɛ pebie beŋkpoŋ.

english_verse: If any family is too small to eat the whole animal, they must share it with their next-door neighbors. Choose either a sheep or a goat, but it must be a one-year-old male that has nothing wrong with it. And it must be large enough for everyone to have some of the meat.
translation_verse: Kondɛɛre ombal waa wola kirihiah bɛlbwa dii, dɛ di benanyoa laanee chɛ kɛ hé lawɛ ba ɛ ɡɛ waa nɔ. He ta pebie dɔe yaa, bohnee chɛ kɛ hé lawɛ.

english_verse: Each family must take care of its animal until the evening of the fourteenth day of the month, when the animals are to be killed.
translation_verse: Hé nyiŋa dɛ ka tel korobie nɔ tɔpera fi dɛ anaarɛ ta, a ɡɛ saŋee Israel tena ɛɛ ba a kpoora jɔmɔra.

english_verse: Some of the blood must be put on the two doorposts and above the door of each house where the animals are to be eaten.
translation_verse: Ásɛ ba kpɔ a chale la ane ɛ ba doonyoo daa nyundua, ne a keŋkeŋni dem bela baa dɛ ba ola la chwee la.

english_verse: That night the animals are to be roasted and eaten, together with bitter herbs and thin bread made without yeast.
translation_verse: Awola jwaana la tenten la, bá wɔɔ ola la, dɛ́ kpɔ papooni aa kpela ne paanoo baa wola iisi a ta doe la ja a ta dɛ́ di.

english_verse: Don't eat the meat raw or boiled. The entire animal, including its head, legs, and insides, must be roasted.
translation_verse: He bɛ ola la an lwɛɛ kɛɛ an daala chwe. Hé wɔɔ ane a nyuune ne nakpale ne a tea bini kwaa te bwa.

english_verse: Eat what you want that night, and the next morning burn whatever is left.
translation_verse: He bɛ di a ka tɔɔ per a ta. Anɔ la aa ka la bwa chɛ kɛ hé fuah.

english_verse: When you eat the meal, be dressed and ready to travel. Have your sandals on, carry your walking stick in your hand, and eat quickly. This is the Passover Festival in honor of me, your Lord.
translation_verse: Gɛ haa dia laanee nɔ. Hé bini bɛlbwa kpɔ o batakaarejaŋ dɛ́ kpɔ kiriso vɔwɛ o ta, dɛ́ do naŋɡawa ásɛ dɛ kpoŋe o daŋɡbala kɛŋɔ waa dɛ ba ŋwɛnɛ bɛl kaala. Warane ɡee chɛ kɛŋɔ hé dia. Anee ɛ Galekaa kondikwa haa dɛ ba dii n sɔn ta.

english_verse: That same night I will pass through Egypt and kill the first-born son in every family and the first-born male of all animals. I am the Lord, and I will punish the gods of Egypt.
translation_verse: Awola jwaana la tenten la, mɛɛ valɛ Ijipt harɛ ta bwaa, dɛ́ kpo bibanloɡle bɛlbwa waa ɛ binyoa, ne kondɛɛre bɛlbwa ɡe biloɡle ombal. Mɛɛ chɔɡ voɡa aa lɔ Ijipt harɛ ta bwaa. Menee Korowii.

english_verse: The blood on the houses will show me where you live, and when I see the blood, I will pass over you. Then you won't be bothered by the terrible disasters I will bring on Egypt.
translation_verse: Chal haa kpɔ ɛ he doonyoo laanee dɛ́ baɡle deene haa soɡe a bini. N teŋo baa kaa dɛ na chal laa, maa heyaa wobɛlbwaa ɛ, mɛɛ ɡale heyaa ta, ásɛ dɛ jo Ijipt tena la deremi dɛ́ tɛr ba deŋne.

english_verse: For seven days you must eat bread made without yeast. And on the first of these seven days, you must remove all yeast from your homes. If you eat anything made with yeast during this festival, you will no longer be part of Israel.
translation_verse: Hé di paanoo iisi aa wola toole a ta tɔpera anuanɛ. Tɔpere waa tɔ sie la, hé laa iisi bɛlbwa kpɔ he deene bini. Nomɛlbwa waa di paanoo iisi aa do o ta a ɡɛ tɔpera nɔ ta la, dɛ o ta n nɛra baa ɛ Israel tena la bini jae kpa.

english_verse: Meet together for worship on the first and seventh days of the festival. The only work you are allowed to do on either of these two days is that of preparing the bread.
translation_verse: Tɔpere waa tɔ sie ne tɔpenuanɛ wee la taa chɛ kɛ hé cheme dɛ́ tom mɛ. Nomɛlbwa ta chɛ kɛ ó ɛ toma bɛlbwa, nemenɛ kondikwaa waa ɛ dɛ́ di ɡbo.

english_verse: Celebrate this Festival of Thin Bread as a way of remembering the day that I brought your families and tribes out of Egypt. And do this each year.

english_verse: Moses called the leaders of Israel together and said: Each family is to pick out a sheep and kill it for Passover.

english_verse: Make a brush from a few small branches of a hyssop plant and dip the brush in the bowl that has the blood of the animal in it. Then brush some of the blood above the door and on the posts at each side of the door of your house. After this, everyone is to stay inside until morning.
translation_verse: Hé kpɔ hesɔp daa li ola la chal ta loɡbaa bini ɛ he doonyoo keŋkeŋna ne a nyundua daa la ta. He bini bɛlbwa bɛ buse le ka tel kɛ tɔɔ aa pera chɔɔ mɔɔ.

english_verse: During that night the Lord will go through the country of Egypt and kill the first-born son in every Egyptian family. He will see where you have put the blood, and he will not come into your house. His angel that brings death will pass over and not kill your first-born sons.

english_verse: After you have entered the country promised to you by the Lord, you and your children must continue to celebrate Passover each year.
translation_verse: He baa tel harɛ Korowii aa baɡɛ heyaa nyoa ŋɔ wɛɛ kpɔɔ tɛ heyaa la ta naa, hé teŋɛ tɔpejen nɔ dii waa ta dɛɛ ɛa.

english_verse: Your children will ask you, “What are we celebrating?”
translation_verse: Dɛ he bii baa bɔɔ heya ŋɔ, ‘Ɛrɛɛ a ɡɛ tɔpejen nɔ dii mun ɛɛ chaɡle aa,’

He killed the first-born sons of the Egyptians, but he spared our children from death.” After Moses finished speaking, the people of Israel knelt down and worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: hé ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, ‘Galekaa saraha taa Korowii kpoo Ijipt tena bibanloɡla bwa ba deremi ta, dɛ ɡale ya Israel tena deremi ta kaa.’ ” Mosis aa bol waa tonɛ la, Israel tena ɡuŋo dɛ tomɛ Korowii.

english_verse: Then they left and did what Moses and Aaron had told them to do. Death for the First-Born Sons
translation_verse: Asɛ ba la dɛ ka ɛ ɡɛ Korowii aa do Mosis ne Arɔn ŋɔ ba ɛ la.

english_verse: At midnight the Lord killed the first-born son of every Egyptian family, from the son of the king to the son of every prisoner in jail. He also killed the first-born male of every animal that belonged to the Egyptians.
translation_verse: Bɔr aa joa harambaŋa la, Korowii kpo Ijipt tena bibanloɡla bwa. O kpɔɔ le Ijipt kooro waa soɡe kara ta la bibanloɡle nɛ, dɛ ba nɛn baa lawɔ do dea bibanloɡle nɛ, dɛ kondɛɛra bwa ɡe biloɡla nɛ.

english_verse: That night the king, his officials, and everyone else in Egypt got up and started crying bitterly. In every Egyptian home, someone was dead. The People of Israel Escape from Egypt
translation_verse: Awola jwaana la, kooro ne o nomonome bwa ne Ijipt tena iro dɛɛ wi kohona harɛ la ta bobɛlbwa, dɛkalkɛ dɛ dem bɛlbwa toole nɛn aa wola o ta sewɛ.

translation_verse: Jwaana la tenten la, Ijipt kooro yerɛ Mosis ne Arɔn dɛ ŋɔ, “Hé kaa! He ne Israel tena bwa ir le harɛ nɔ ta. Hé kaa dɛ́ ka tomɛ Korowii ɡɛ haa soŋa la.

english_verse: Take your sheep, goats, and cattle, and get out. But ask your God to be kind to me.”
translation_verse: Hé kpɔ he peera ne boohna ne nae bwa kaa ɡɛ haa bola la, ásɛ dɛ soŋe andɛɛɡa le he Korowii be tɛ mɛ.”

english_verse: The Egyptians did everything they could to get the Israelites to leave their country as quickly as possible. They said, “Please hurry and leave. If you don't, we will all be dead.”
translation_verse: Ijipt tena la iro che ba nɛɛ ŋɔ, “Hé ɛ warane dɛ́ le ya harɛ nɔ ta.” Ba liiro ŋɔ dɛ ba ta ɡelɛ ba kaa laa, ba bwa ɛɛ serewoo.

english_verse: So the Israelites quickly made some bread dough and put it in pans. But they did not mix any yeast in the dough to make it rise. They wrapped cloth around the pans and carried them on their shoulders.
translation_verse: Anomanta, ba kpɔ men baa wola iisi a ta doe mɔɔ dɛ kpɔ ɛ paanoo do loɡa bini, dɛ kpɔ yale vɔrɔwa dɛ kpɔ chɔŋɛ ba vaama ta.

english_verse: The Israelites had already done what Moses had told them to do. They had gone to their Egyptian neighbors and asked for gold and silver and for clothes.
translation_verse: Ba ɛ ɡɛ Mosis aa do ba la, dɛ soŋe Ijipt tena la suuɡapoŋa ne suuɡaswɛm kwa dɛ yale.

english_verse: The Lord had made the Egyptians friendly toward the people of Israel, and they gave them whatever they asked for. In this way they carried away the wealth of the Egyptians when they left Egypt.
translation_verse: Korowii ɡelɔ Ijipt tena sie lɛ ba nɛ, dɛ ɡel ba tɛɛ ba komɛlbwa baa soŋ ba la. Anɔ taa a che ba che Ijipt kondɔɔh bwa kaa.

english_verse: The Israelites walked from the city of Rameses to the city of Succoth. There were about
translation_verse: Israel tena le Rameses waa lɔ Ijipt harɛ ta dɛ ba Sukot. Baala baa valɛ naa ta la ɡbo ɛɛ ɛ kaɡboŋa lafraanumɛlee. Haahna ne bechale te ta jae.

english_verse: Many other people went with them as well, and there were also a lot of sheep, goats, and cattle.
translation_verse: Nɛmpɛɛne warɔ dɛ ja ba nɛɛ kaa. Peera ne boohna dɛ nae kohona bwa ɡe jao.

english_verse: They left Egypt in such a hurry that they did not have time to prepare any food except the bread dough made without yeast. So they baked it and made thin bread.
translation_verse: Ba kpɔ men baa ɛa dɛ le ane Ijipt la ɛ paanoo iisi aa wola toole a ta. Dɛkalkɛ baa doŋ ba le bela la, ba ta bɔr dɔe dɛ́ ɛ ba kondikwa bɛlbwa.

english_verse: The Lord gave Moses and Aaron the following instructions for celebrating Passover: Only Israelites may eat the Passover meal.
translation_verse: Belaa Korowii ŋɔ Mosis ne Arɔn be ŋɔ, “Ŋwɛnɛre haa kpɔ a ta di Galekaa kondikwa laanee nɔ. A ta chɛ kɛŋɔ hɔɔh dia.

english_verse: Your slaves may eat the meal if they have been circumcised,
translation_verse: Yom bɛlbwa haa yawɔ ba teŋe o pen la ɛɛ won di,

english_verse: The entire meal must be eaten inside, and no one may leave the house during the celebration. No bones of the Passover lamb may be broken.
translation_verse: “Hé dɛ ba a dii yaa, dembeŋkpoŋ taa chɛ kɛŋɔ hé dia, dɛ bɛ ol la bɛlbwa kpɔ le fɔɡ. He bɛ a hoɡa ɡe paɡre.

english_verse: And all Israelites must take part in the meal.
translation_verse: Israel tena bwaa chɛ kɛ bá di a ɡɛ tɔpere nɔ.

english_verse: If anyone who isn't an Israelite wants to celebrate Passover with you, every man and boy in that family must first be circumcised. Then they may join in the meal, just like native Israelites. No uncircumcised man or boy may eat the Passover meal!
translation_verse: Nɛŋhɔɔh bɛlbwa waa baa so he bini dɛ nyin o di Galekaa kondikwaa nɔ Korowii sɔn ta naa, a chɛ kɛŋɔ ó teŋe o bibaala ne baala baa lɔ o dem bwa pena, ásɛ he ne ba bwa ɛ nɛnsiwi beŋkpoŋ mɔɔ dɛ́ won di ane. Bibaa te bɛlbwa baa wola o pen teŋe la ta chɛ kɛŋɔ ó di ane.

english_verse: This law applies both to native Israelites and to those foreigners who live among you.
translation_verse: Gɛ mmara nɔ chɔɔ tɛ harɛ nɔ ta bie ne nɛŋhɔɔhra baa soɡe o ta bwa.”

english_verse: The Israelites obeyed everything the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron to tell them.
translation_verse: Asɛ Israel tena la bwa ɛ ɡɛ Korowii aa do Mosis ne Arɔn ŋɔ ba ɛ la.

english_verse: And on that same day the Lord brought Israel's families and tribes out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Awola tɔpere la tentenee Korowii lawɛ o nɛra Israel tena bwa le Ijipt harɛ denaa ta.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Korowii ŋɔ Mosis be ŋɔ,

english_verse: “Dedicate to me the first-born son of every family and the first-born males of your flocks and herds. These belong to me.” The Festival of Thin Bread
translation_verse: “Le bibanloɡle bɛlbwa cheɡ tɛ mɛ ó ɛ n kon. Israel te bibanloɡle bɛlbwa ne kondɛɛre bɛlbwa ɡe biloɡle ombal bwa ɛ n kwa.”

english_verse: The Lord promised your ancestors that he would bring you into the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Hivites, and Jebusites. It is a land rich with milk and honey. Each year during the month of Abib, celebrate these events in the following way:
translation_verse: Dɛ Korowii baa kpɔ heyaa tel Keenan ne Hiti ne Amɔre ne Hivi, dɛ Jebus tena harɛ waa ŋwɛɛra baɡle he naawa ŋɔ wɛɛ kpɔɔ tɛ heya ó ɛ he kon la ta, harɛpare ondɛɛɡe ta naa, a chɛ kɛ hé di a ɡɛ tɔpere nɔ korobie nɔ ta. Dɛkalkɛ o ba he ne harɛ o taa soma ta.

english_verse: For seven days you are to eat bread made without yeast, and on the seventh day you are to celebrate a festival in honor of the Lord.
translation_verse: Tɔpera anuanɛɛ hɛɛ ba paanoo iisi aa wola toole a ta la dii. Kɛ tɔpenuanɛ wee la te, hé ɛo tɔpejen tɛ Korowii.

english_verse: During those seven days, you must not eat anything made with yeast or even have yeast anywhere near your homes.
translation_verse: Hé di paanoo iisi aa wola toole a ta tɔpera anuanɛ la ta. He bɛ ɡel komɛlbwa iisi aa lɔ o ta do he be. Hale he harɛ jwɛh ta bobɛlbwa kwara.

english_verse: Then on the seventh day you must explain to your children that you do this because the Lord brought you out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Awola haa dɛɛ di tɔpere la, hé ŋɔ he bii be ŋɔ, ‘Korowii kpeɡri ne bokpeɡa waa kpɔa lɛ yaa le Ijipt harɛ ta la waa yaa ɛ ɡɛ.’

english_verse: This celebration will be like wearing a sign on your hand or on your forehead, because then you will pass on to others the teaching of the Lord, whose mighty power brought you out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Gel tɔpere la dii do kɛŋɔ nɔnloɡ, kɛɛ komɛl haa kpɔ vɔwɛ he tile ta, dɛɛ liiri Korowii Mmara la ta teŋa. Dɛkalkɛ Korowii kpeɡri ne o bokpeɡaa o kpɔ lawɛ le Ijipt harɛ ta.

english_verse: Celebrate this festival each year at the same time.
translation_verse: Hé teŋɛ ɡɛ waa nɔ ta dɛɛ ɛa tɔpere waa chɛa ta bena bɛlbwa. Bibanloɡla wa

english_verse: The Lord will give you the land of the Canaanites, just as he promised you and your ancestors.
translation_verse: Korowii baa kpɔ heyaa ba Keenan harɛ ta, dɛ kpɔ tɛ heyaa ɡɛ waa ŋwɛɛra dɛ baɡɛ he ne he naawa nyoa la tonaa,

english_verse: From then on, you must give him every first-born son from your families and every first-born male from your animals, because these belong to him.
translation_verse: a chɛ kɛ hé kpɔ bibanloɡle bɛlbwa tɛo. Kondɛɛre bɛlbwa ɡe biloɡle ombal ɛ Korowii kon.

english_verse: You can spare the life of a first-born donkey by sacrificing a lamb; if you don't, you must break the donkey's neck. You must spare every first-born son.
translation_verse: Keeɡo biloɡle bɛlbwa chɛ kɛŋɔ hé kpɔ pee charɔ. Kɛ dɛ haa on charaa, hé ku o baŋa. Hɛɛ won charɛ bibanloɡle bwa ɡe nyu.

english_verse: In the future your children will ask what this ceremony means. Explain it to them by saying, “The Lord used his mighty power to rescue us from slavery in Egypt.
translation_verse: Tɔpebɛl dɛ he bibaa bɔɔre ŋɔ ɛrɛɛ ɡɛ waa nɔ ɛɛ chaɡle aa, he ŋɔ, ‘Korowii kpeɡri ne o bokpeɡaa o kpɔ lawɛ yaa le somanjiri dii ta Ijipt harɛ.

english_verse: The king stubbornly refused to set us free, so the Lord killed the first-born male of every animal and the first-born son of every Egyptian family. This is why we sacrifice to the Lord every first-born male of every animal and save every first-born son.”
translation_verse: Ijipt kooro aa ɛ deŋnekpeɡ dɛ vɛh yaa ŋwɛnɛ tɛɛ ya kaa la, Korowii kpoo nɛra bii baa ɛ bibanloɡla ne kondɛɛre bɛlbwa biloɡle Ijipt harɛ ta. Anee ɡela n kpɔ n kondɛɛra biloɡla ambala dɛɛ tɛ Korowii, dɛ́ berɛ charɛ n bibanloɡle nyu la.’

english_verse: This ceremony will serve the same purpose as a sign on your hand or on your forehead to tell how the Lord's mighty power rescued us from Egypt. The Lord Leads His People
translation_verse: Gɛ waa nɔ do kɛŋɔ nɔnloɡ kɛɛ kon yaa kpɔ vɔwɛ tili ta aa lii yaa Korowii kpeɡri, ne o bokpeɡa waa kpɔa lawɛ yaa le Ijipt harɛ ta la.” Korowii tɔ Israel tena sie ba ɡale Mposwɛm

english_verse: After the king had finally let the people go, the Lord did not lead them through Philistine territory, though that was the shortest way. God had said, “If they are attacked, they may decide to return to Egypt.”
translation_verse: Ijipt kooro tɛ nɛra la ŋwɛnɛ ŋɔ bá kaa, kɛ Korowii ta ba sie tɔe ba kpɔ ŋwɛnɛ waa chɔa kaa Filisti tena harɛ ta la, dɛ onee fe bora. Asɛ Korowii lii ŋɔ, “Dɛ ba kaa cheme laa laa, baa charɛ ba liiree dɛ́ berɛ kaa Ijipt harɛ ta.”

english_verse: So he led them around through the desert and toward the Red Sea. The Israelites left Egypt, prepared for battle.
translation_verse: Anomanta, o kpɔ ba bar kpɔ ŋwɛnɛ waa chɔa kaa pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta, Mposwɛm pera. Dɛ Israel tena vɔwɛ ntoa, dɛ le Ijipt harɛ dɛɛ ba ba yo.

english_verse: Moses had them take the bones of Joseph, whose dying words had been, “God will come to your rescue, and when he does, be sure to take my bones with you.”
translation_verse: Mosis aa dɛ kaa la, o pa Josef hoɡa dɛkalkɛ Josef ɡelɔ Jekɔb bii fa ŋwɛɛ baɡlo. O ŋɔ, “Korowii ɛɛ ba lɛ heyaa, anomanta, a chɛ kɛ hé kpɔ n chɔɔ le bonɔ harɛ nɔ ta.”

english_verse: The people of Israel left Succoth and camped at Etham at the border of Egypt near the desert.
translation_verse: Baa le Sukot la, ba kaa baŋre ba tɛnte deene Etaam. O chɔ pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta nyoa bobɛl.

english_verse: At Etham the Lord said to Moses:
translation_verse: Ate, Korowii ŋɔ Mosis be ŋɔ,

english_verse: Tell the people of Israel to turn back and camp across from Pi-Hahiroth near Baal-Zephon, between Migdol and the Red Sea.
translation_verse: “Ŋɔ Israel tena be ŋɔ ba berɛ ba baŋre ba tɛnte deene Pi Haherɔt jwɛh waa lɔ Miɡdol ne Mposwɛm baah ta la. Bá so mpo nyoa ásɛ Baal Sefon ɡe do baŋ bɛl.

english_verse: The king will think you were afraid to cross the desert and that you are wandering around, trying to find another way to leave the country.
translation_verse: Ijipt kooro ɛɛ liiruu kɛŋɔ Israel tena nyoɡre pua waa ɛ hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta belaa dɛɛ ɡaaɡe ba bɔr.

english_verse: I will make the king stubborn again, and he will try to catch you. Then I will destroy him and his army. People everywhere will praise me for my victory, and the Egyptians will know that I really am the Lord. The Israelites obeyed the Lord and camped where he told them.
translation_verse: Mɛɛ ɡeloo o deŋne do kpeɡri o ŋɔ wɛɛ ti baa. Mɛɛ pɔ o ne o laa tena nɛɛ dɛ́ dɔ jirima. Ásɛ Ijipt tena bwa jemɛ kɛŋɔ menee Korowii kpela.” Anomanta, ɡɛɛ Israel tena ɛ.

english_verse: When the king of Egypt heard that the Israelites had finally left, he and his officials changed their minds and said, “Look what we have done! We let them get away, and they will no longer be our slaves.”
translation_verse: Baa baa bol Ijipt kooro be ŋɔ nɛra la chwao la, o ne o nomonome charɛ ba liire dɛ ŋɔ, “Bɔkwa waa ya ɛ ken ɔ? Ya ɡelɔ Israel tena la kaa yaa wola ban dɔ ba ɛ ya tomare kpa.”

english_verse: The Lord made the king so stubborn that he went after them, while the Israelites proudly went on their way.
translation_verse: Korowii ɡelɔ Ijipt kooro la deŋne do kpeɡri, asɛ o ti Israel tena baa kpɔ silɛɛ le dɛɛ kaa la.

english_verse: But the king's horses and chariots and soldiers caught up with them while they were camping by the Red Sea near Pi-Hahiroth and Baal-Zephon.
translation_verse: Kooro kwaa aa do kɛ torɔɡore la bwa, ne nɛra baa soɡe jaɡre ta, dɛ laa tena la ti Israel tena, dɛ ka bɛn ba bela baa baŋre tɛnte deene Mposwɛm nyoa la. Bela bɛne Pi Haherɔt asɛ Baal Sefon ɡe do baŋ bɛl.

english_verse: When the Israelites saw the king coming with his army, they were frightened and begged the Lord for help.
translation_verse: Kooro ne o laa tena aa dɛ bɛn ba asɛ Israel tena ke nyiŋi la, ba nao kɛŋɔ Ijipt tena puu ba tonɛ. Asɛ ɔmee kohona nomanta, ba wi dɛɛ yerɛ Korowii ŋɔ ó ba cha ba.

english_verse: They also complained to Moses, “Wasn't there enough room in Egypt to bury us? Is that why you brought us out here to die in the desert? Why did you bring us out of Egypt anyway?
translation_verse: Dɛ bɔɔ Mosis ŋɔ, “Lalbɔɔnee wola toole Ijipt harɛ ta waa he ba ya ne pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta ŋɔ yá ba serewe nɔ kɛɛ? Bɔkwa waa he ɛ yaa ken?

english_verse: While we were there, didn't we tell you to leave us alone? We'd rather be slaves in Egypt than die in this desert!”
translation_verse: Ya ta he be bolɛ Ijipt ŋɔ he ɡel ya so dɛɛ tom ba aa? A wer kɛŋɔ ya fe aa lɔ bela dɛɛ tom ba, ɡwaa kɛŋɔ yaa lɔ pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta bonɔ dɛɛ ba serewa nɔ.”

english_verse: But Moses answered, “Don't be afraid! Be brave, and you will see the Lord save you today. These Egyptians will never bother you again.
translation_verse: Asɛ Mosis chaŋ ba ŋɔ, “He bɛ ɔmɛ, hé che kiŋkiŋ dɛ na lɛɛ Korowii aa dɛ ba heyaa lɛɛ fini. Ijipt tena haa dɛ na ba fini nɔ, haa ban na kpa bwa.

english_verse: The Lord will fight for you, and you won't have to do a thing.”
translation_verse: Korowiirii dɛ́ yo tɛ heya, hé te hel.”

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Why do you keep calling out to me for help? Tell the Israelites to move forward.
translation_verse: Anee Korowii ŋɔ Mosis be ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ he wi dɛɛ yer mɛ nɔɔ? He te ŋɔ Israel tena la be ŋɔ bá pa sie dɛɛ la.

english_verse: Then hold your walking stick over the sea. The water will open up and make a road where they can walk through on dry ground.
translation_verse: Tɛr he daŋɡbala la pa Mposwɛm la ta, ásɛ o bini pere Israel tena la won valɛ o bini le kɛŋɔ harɛpɛɛ ta.

english_verse: I will make the Egyptians so stubborn that they will go after you. Then I will be praised because of what happens to the king and his chariots and cavalry.
translation_verse: Mɛɛ ɡeloo Ijipt tena deŋne do kpeɡri, ásɛ ba ti heya. Belaa mɛɛ ba n jirima dɔe dɛ́ le Ijipt kooro ne o laa tena ne kwaa aa do kɛ torɔɡore, dɛ nɛra baa dɛ so jaɡre ta la bwa nɛ.

english_verse: The Egyptians will know for sure that I am the Lord.”
translation_verse: Maa ba pɔ kooro ne o nɛra nɛɛ la, anee baa ba jema kɛŋɔ menee Korowii.”

english_verse: All this time God's angel had gone ahead of Israel's army, but now he moved behind them. A large cloud had also gone ahead of them,
translation_verse: Korowii torome waa tɔ Israel tena sie o ne baa valɛ la le ba sie dɛ ba che ba habɔɔ. Bam la waa tɔ ba sie la ɡe le ba sie dɛ ba che ba habɔɔ,

english_verse: but now it moved between the Egyptians and the Israelites. The cloud gave light to the Israelites, but made it dark for the Egyptians, and during the night they could not come any closer.
translation_verse: dɛ do Ijipt laa tena ne Israel laa tena baah ta. Awola jwaana la, bam la baa tɔ baŋ bɛl, baŋ bɛl tena do biro ta asɛ bɔr chaah baŋ bɛl tena ɡe be. Anomanta, bɛlbwa ta wone la o dɔŋ be awola jwaana la bwa.

english_verse: Moses stretched his arm over the sea, and the Lord sent a strong east wind that blew all night until there was dry land where the water had been. The sea opened up,
translation_verse: Mosis tɛr daŋɡbala waa lɔ o nɔn ta la pa mpo la ta, asɛ awola jwaana la bwa Korowii ɡel peujen bɛl ta le wee leebɔr, dɛ taɡɛ nee la kaa habɔɔ o berɛ harɛpɛɛ dɛ hol chɔ. Mpo la bini pero,

english_verse: and the Israelites walked through on dry land with a wall of water on each side.
translation_verse: asɛ Israel tena valɛ harɛpɛɛ waa hola ta dɛ le o baŋ. Nee la pero che kɛŋɔ danjwɛ dɛ do ba diɡ ne ɡal,

english_verse: But before daylight the Lord looked down at the Egyptian army from the fiery cloud and made them panic.
translation_verse: Aa baa ka tama bɔr chaah la, Korowii cheɡɛ bam waa do jaŋne kaa nyundua la ne nii waa tɛra kaa nyundua la ta dɛ nyiŋi Ijipt laa tena dɛ chɔɡ ba liire.

english_verse: Their chariot wheels got stuck, and it was hard for them to move. So the Egyptians said to one another, “Let's leave these people alone! The Lord is on their side and is fighting against us.”
translation_verse: O ɡelɔ kwaa aa do kɛŋɔ torɔɡore la nakpale chɔɡ a tɛɡra do kpeɡri. Asɛ Ijipt tena la ŋɔ, “Hé ɡel ya ɡel Israel tena nɔ nɛɛ teŋa oo! Korowiirii cha ba dɛɛ yo yaa la.”

english_verse: The Lord told Moses, “Stretch your arm toward the sea—the water will cover the Egyptians and their cavalry and chariots.”
translation_verse: Ate, Korowii ŋɔ Mosis be ŋɔ, “Tɛr daŋɡbala waa lɔ he nɔn ta la pa mpo la ta, ásɛ o palɛ tɔ Ijipt tena ne kwaa aa do kɛ torɔɡore dɛ nɛra baa soɡe jaɡre ta la bwa nɛ.”

english_verse: Moses stretched out his arm, and at daybreak the water rushed toward the Egyptians. They tried to run away, but the Lord drowned them in the sea.
translation_verse: Asɛ Mosis tɛr pa mpo la ta, bɔr chaahna bini la, o berɛ ba che o buɡ ta. Dɛ Ijipt tena chwao dɛ fe ɛɛ ba lee, asɛ Korowii taɡ ba do mpo la bini.

english_verse: The water came and covered the chariots, the cavalry, and the whole Egyptian army that had followed the Israelites into the sea. Not one of them was left alive.
translation_verse: Nee la palɔ dɛ ba tɔ o laa tena la bwa nɛ. Kwaa aa do kɛŋɔ torɔɡo ne nɛra baa soɡe jaɡre ta dɛɛ ti Israel tena la bwa ka mpo la bini, beŋkpoŋ kwaraa ta kae.

english_verse: But the sea had made a wall of water on each side of the Israelites, so they walked through on dry land.
translation_verse: Kɛ Israel tena la te valɛ harɛpɛɛ waa hola ta mpo la bini, nee la pere kɛŋɔ danjwɛ dɛ do ba diɡ ne ɡal ta ba le o baŋ.

english_verse: On that day, when the Israelites saw the bodies of the Egyptians washed up on the shore, they knew that the Lord had saved them.
translation_verse: Kenii Korowii lɛ Israel tena le Ijipt tena nɔn ta awola tɔpere, asɛ Israel tena na ba kɛ baa serewa dɛ chɔ Mpo la nyoa.

english_verse: Because of the mighty power he had used against the Egyptians, the Israelites worshiped him and trusted him and his servant Moses.
translation_verse: Israel tena aa na Korowii kpeɡri kohona waa kpɔa chɔɡ Ijipt tena la, ba ɔmɔ asɛ dɛ yarada Korowii ne o bonɔɔ Mosis.

english_verse: Moses and the Israelites sang this song in praise of the Lord: I sing praises to the Lord for his great victory! He has thrown the horses and their riders into the sea.
translation_verse: Belaa Mosis ne Israel tena la ɡo yel kpɛɛ Korowii ŋɔ, “Mɛɛ ɡo yelee kpɛɛ Korowii, dɛkalkɛ o lɛ sɔn kohona. O kpɔ jaɡre ne nɛra baa soɡe a ta bwa ka do mpo bini.

english_verse: The Lord is my strength, the reason for my song, because he has saved me. I praise and honor the Lord— he is my God and the God of my ancestors.
translation_verse: Korowiirii n bokpeɡa, o sɔn ber mɛ yel mɛɛ ɡo, onee n Lɛɛ, onee mɛɛ tomɛ dɛɛ kpɛɛro, Korowii n naa wa aa tomɔ laanee on, o sɔnee mɛɛ ba yera dɛɛ tomɔ.

english_verse: The Lord is his name, and he is a warrior!
translation_verse: Korowiirii yoa dɛɛ tɛ yaa, Korowiirii o sɔn.

english_verse: He threw the chariots and army of Egypt's king into the Red Sea, and he drowned the best of the king's officers.
translation_verse: Ijipt kooro kwaa baa vɔwa pɛl jaɡre ne o laa tena, o taɡɛ a bwa do mpo bini, Kooro nomonome tenten bwa sirimi mpo la bini.

english_verse: They sank to the bottom just like stones.
translation_verse: Vil tentenee bɔle ba nɛ, ba chɔ vil la mun ta kɛŋɔ bwe ken.

english_verse: With the tremendous force of your right arm, our Lord, you crushed your enemies.
translation_verse: N Naa Korowii, he nɔn diɡ dɔ jirima kpeɡri do o ta, he kpɔ chɔɡ ya dɔma.

english_verse: What a great victory was yours, when you defeated everyone who opposed you. Your fiery anger wiped them out, as though they were straw.
translation_verse: He kpeɡri ne he jirimaa he kpɔ taɡɛ he dɔma ta. He ɡelɔ he bandia kohona ba fuuh ba kɛŋɔ kpɔɡa ken.

english_verse: You were so furious that the sea piled up like a wall, and the ocean depths curdled like cheese.
translation_verse: He nyoa peu ɡbo ɡelɔ mpo bini pere, dɛ che diɡ ne ɡal kɛŋɔ danjwɛ, o holɔ vile aa lɔ o baah ta chɔ pɛɛ.

english_verse: Your enemies boasted that they would pursue and capture us, divide up our possessions, treat us as they wished, then take out their swords and kill us right there.
translation_verse: Ya dɔma tamanɔ dɛ ŋɔ, ‘Mɛɛ ti baa dɛ́ ka pɔ ba nɛ. Ba kondɔɔh bwaa mɛɛ ba pae ɡɛ maa dɛ nyin. Mɛɛ tɛr n kere ba nɛɛ dɛ́ chɔɡ ba bwa.’

english_verse: But when you got furious, they sank like lead, swallowed by ocean waves.
translation_verse: Kɛ haa hweera kerabeŋkpoŋ ɡbo la, a ɡelɔ mpo nee bɔle banɛ. Ba sirimo kɛŋɔ kpana aa sirimi vil bini la ken.

english_verse: Our Lord, no other gods compare with you— Majestic and holy! Fearsome and glorious! Miracle worker!
translation_verse: N Naa Korowii, voɡ bisoo do kɛ hen ɔ? He do ɡoroŋ ɡa, he jirima do kan kohona. Umee won nyokpowaa ɛɛ kɛ he nɔ?

english_verse: When you signaled with your right hand, your enemies were swallowed deep into the earth.
translation_verse: He tɛr he nɔndiɡ, asɛ harɛ kpɔ ya dɔma lile.

english_verse: The leaders of Edom and of Moab were terrified. Everyone in Canaan fainted,
translation_verse: Ɔmee ɛɛ lawɛ Edom koranaree kohona, Moab nomonome bwara yɔr baa chel, Keenan tena ɡe bwa ɛɛ heo kwara.

english_verse: struck down by fear. Our Lord, your powerful arm kept them still as a rock until the people you rescued to be your very own had marched by.
translation_verse: Ɔmee kohona ɛɛ chole ba nɛɛ, á che he kpeɡri ta bá ka che bobeŋkpoŋ kɛŋɔ bwe ken, dɛ́ ka tel kɛŋɔ he nɛra aa teŋe ba kaa mɔɔ. N Naa Korowii, nemenɛ he nɛra haa lɛɛ ba le Ijipt harɛ ta la teŋe ba kaa mɔɔ.

english_verse: You will let your people settle on your own mountain, where you chose to live and to be worshiped.
translation_verse: He kpɔ ba ka so he be bwe doa, bwe la doa waa ɛ he soŋnibɔr la, he ɡbaɡba Dea waa do ɡoroŋ he che he kpeɡri ta cheɡo la.

english_verse: Our Lord, you will rule forever! The Song of Miriam
translation_verse: N Naa Korowii, hɛɛ di kora saŋ bɛlbwaa dɛɛ la.”

english_verse: Miriam the sister of Aaron was a prophet. So she took her tambourine and led the other women out to play their tambourines and to dance.
translation_verse: Belaa Arɔn nimambie Miriam waa ɛ Korowii keame kpɔ loŋ, asɛ haahna la bwa ɡe ja dɛ kpoŋe ane ba yiiɡa dɛ sa teŋɛ dɔŋa nɛ.

english_verse: Then she sang to them: “Sing praises to the Lord for his great victory! He has thrown the horses and their riders into the sea.” Bitter Water at Marah
translation_verse: Asɛ Miriam ɡo yel dɛ ŋɔ, “Hé ɡo yela kpɛɛ Korowii. O lɛ sɔn kohona ɡa. O kpɔ jaɡre ne nɛra baa soɡe a ta bwa ka ta mpo bini.” Neerare ane aa lɔ Mara ne Elim wa

english_verse: After the Israelites left the Red Sea, Moses led them through the Shur Desert for three days, before finding water.
translation_verse: Ate, Mosis tɔ Israel tena la sie le Mposwɛm la nyoa, dɛ kpɔ ba kaa pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta bobɛl baa dɛ yerɔ Suur. Ba ɡaaɡe harɛ la ta tɔpera atoro dɛ ba ta nee nae.

english_verse: They did find water at Marah, but it was bitter, which is how that place got its name.
translation_verse: Ba baa tel bobɛl baa yerɔ Mara dɛ na nee bɛl. Ba ta wone nyɔɔ, dɛkalkɛ dɛ o kpeli. Gɛɛ a do baa yerɛ bela Mara. O munii kpeli.

english_verse: The people complained and said, “Moses, what are we going to drink?”
translation_verse: Anomanta, nɛra la naɡre wa dɛ pɛɛ Mosis ŋɔ, “Leperaa ya dɔ nee dɛ́ nyɔɔ?”

english_verse: Moses asked the Lord for help, and the Lord told him to throw a certain piece of wood into the water. Moses did so, and the water became fit to drink. At Marah the Lord tested his people and also gave them some laws and teachings.
translation_verse: Ate, Mosis wi no Korowii asɛ o baɡlo daa bɛl. O kpɔ ta nee la ta nee la do som ba bwa nyɔ. Bela la, Korowii do Mmarare tɛɛ ba asɛ dɛ kpɔ daah ba na.

english_verse: Then he said, “I am the Lord your God, and I cure your diseases. If you obey me by doing right and by following my laws and teachings, I won't punish you with the diseases I sent on the Egyptians.”
translation_verse: Korowii bol ba be ŋɔ, “Dɛ hɛɛ cheɡ deŋnee dɛɛ no men Korowii haa dɛ tom mɛ nɔ dɛɛ ɛ anɔ la aa toɡra n be, dɛ́ swɛɛ siwi dɛɛ teŋɛ me Mmarare bwa ta ɡɛ naa, ate maa weela maa kpɔa ba ta Ijipt tena nɛɛ la bɛlbwaa kpɔ ba he nɛ. Menee Korowii maa dɛ chah heya weela.”

english_verse: On the fifteenth day of the second month after the Israelites had escaped from Egypt, they left Elim and started through the western edge of the Sinai Desert in the direction of Mount Sinai.
translation_verse: Israel tena bwa iro le Elim, dɛ ba pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta bobɛl baa dɛ yerɔ Sen, baa le Ijipt harɛ ta korobie anɛ tɔpera fi dɛ anue habɔɔ. Bela lɔ Elim ne Sinai baah ta.

english_verse: There in the desert they started complaining to Moses and Aaron,
translation_verse: Baa lɔ bela la, dɛ ba dɛ naɡre Mosis ne Arɔn wa,

english_verse: “We wish the Lord had killed us in Egypt. When we lived there, we could at least sit down and eat all the bread and meat we wanted. But you have brought us out here into this desert, where we are going to starve.”
translation_verse: dɛ ŋɔ, “Korowii fe den kpoo yaa Ijipt harɛ ta kwaraa naa, a fe bɔ. Yaa lɔ bela dɛ ola su viine, yaa di kondikwa ɡɛ yaa dɛ nyin. Dɛ a bɛlbwa ta yaa nyae, asɛ he kpɔ yaa ba ta pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta bonɔ lɔr kpo yaa ya bwa ɛɛ ba serewa nɔ.”

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “I will send bread down from heaven like rain. Tell the people to go out each day and gather only enough for that day. That's how I will see if they obey me.
translation_verse: Ate, Korowii ŋɔ Mosis be ŋɔ, “Mɛɛ ɡeloo kondikwa le nyundua lee kɛŋɔ bwaala tɛ heya. Gel nɛra la le tɔpere bɛlbwa dɛ́ ka tɔɔ tɔpebeŋkpoŋ kwaa aa tel ba. Anee ń kpɔ daah ba na kɛŋɔ baa dɛɛ teŋɛ n webaɡla taa kɛɛ baa teŋɔɔ?

english_verse: But on the sixth day of each week they must gather and cook twice as much.”
translation_verse: Tɔpenumɛl wee kwaa haa ka tɔɔ la te, hé tɔɔra ɡɛ haa dɛ tɔɔ tɔpebeŋkpoŋ kwaa la bele anɛ cheɡ.”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron told the people, “This evening you will know that the Lord was the one who rescued you from Egypt.
translation_verse: Asɛ Mosis ne Arɔn ŋɔ Israel tena la bwa be ŋɔ, “Jɔmɔra nɔ ne, hɛɛ jemɔɔ kɛŋɔ Korowiirii kpɔ heyaa le Ijipt harɛ ta,

english_verse: And in the morning you will see his glorious power, because he has heard your complaints against him. Why should you grumble to us? Who are we?”
translation_verse: ásɛ tɔɔ perɔ chɔɔ ɡe aa, he na Korowii jirima chaahna, dɛkalkɛ o noɔ kɛŋɔ haa dɛ naɡre o wa. Ya ɡee bamewa hɛɛ naɡre ya waɔ?”

english_verse: Then Moses continued, “You will know it is the Lord when he gives you meat each evening and more than enough bread each morning. He is really the one you are complaining about, not us—we are nobodies—but the Lord has heard your complaints.”
translation_verse: Anee Mosis berɛ ŋɔ, “Hɛ́ɛ jemɔɔ kɛŋɔ Korowiirii dɛ́ tɛ heya ola he chwe jɔmɔra, ne kondikwa bɛlbwa haa dɛ nyin dɛ́ di chɔɔ, dɛkalkɛ o na ɡɛ haa dɛ naɡre o wa kohona. Ya ɡee bamewa hɛɛ naɡre ya waɔ? Ya waa laa hɛɛ naɡre la, Korowii waa hɛɛ naɡre.”

english_verse: Moses turned to Aaron and said, “Bring the people together, because the Lord has heard their complaints.”
translation_verse: Ate, Mosis ŋɔ Arɔn be ŋɔ, “Ŋɔ Israel tena la bwa be ŋɔ bá ba Korowii sie, dɛkalkɛ o no naɡra baa dɛ naɡre o waa la bwa.”

english_verse: Aaron was speaking to them, when everyone looked out toward the desert and saw the bright glory of the Lord in a cloud.
translation_verse: Arɔn aa dɛ bol waa la Israel tena bwa be la, ba nyiŋo dɛ na pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta bela kɛŋɔ Korowii jirima aa chaahna le bam bɛl ta nyundua.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Asɛ Korowii ŋɔ Mosis be ŋɔ,

english_verse: “I have heard my people complain. Now tell them that each evening they will have meat and each morning they will have more than enough bread. Then they will know that I am the Lord their God.”
translation_verse: “N no Israel tena naɡra baa dɛ naɡre n waa la bwa. Ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ baa chwe ola jɔmɔraa, dɛ́ di kondikwaa chɔɔ dɛ́ vaɡɛ ɡɛ baa dɛ nyin, ásɛ dɛ jemɛ kɛŋɔ menee Korowii baa dɛ tom mɛ la.”

english_verse: That evening a lot of quails came and landed everywhere in the camp, and the next morning dew covered the ground.
translation_verse: Awola jɔmɔra la, chayambwibwi balɔ ba tɔ bela baa soɡa la bwa. Tɔ aa pera chɔɔ la, mɛn leo dɛ bar bela baa baŋre ba tɛnte deene la dɛ pwe harɛ la bwa.

english_verse: After the dew had gone, the desert was covered with thin flakes that looked like frost.
translation_verse: Mɛn la aa baa le la, dɛ kwaa ane aa do pɛlɛpɛlɛ kɛŋɔ pɛŋe pɛɡa chɔ harɛ la ta bobɛlbwa.

english_verse: The people had never seen anything like this, and they started asking each other, “What is it?” Moses answered, “This is the bread that the Lord has given you to eat.
translation_verse: Israel tena laa naa la, ba bɔɔ dɔŋa ŋɔ, “Bɔkwa ɡee nɔɔ, dɛkalkɛ dɛ baa a konsoo jemɛ.” Anee Mosis ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, “Kondikwaa Korowii aa kpɔa tɛ heyaa ŋɔ hé di laanee.

english_verse: And he orders you to gather about two liters for each person in your family—that should be more than enough.”
translation_verse: Anɔɔ Korowii do heya ŋɔ he bɛlbwa tɔɔ ɡɛ del aa maɡre o ne la. Aa ɛ kuruwa beŋkpoŋii dɛ maɡre nomɛlbwa ne dem bɛlbwa ta.”

english_verse: They did as they were told. Some gathered more and some gathered less.
translation_verse: Israel tena la ɛ ɡɛ baa bol ba be la bwa. Ba bini bane tɔɔ kohona, bane ɡe tɔɔ tamaa ken.

english_verse: Moses told them not to keep any overnight.
translation_verse: Asɛ Mosis ŋɔ, “Bɛ́lbwa bɛ ɡel tɔɔ per o kwaa ta.”

english_verse: Some of them disobeyed, but the next morning what they kept was stinking and full of worms, and Moses was angry.
translation_verse: Ba bini bane ta o waa la kpɔe dɛ kwaa ane cheɡ. Tɔ aa pera la, dɛ dudule lɛ a bwa a do sɔɔh. Anomanta, Mosis baah di ba nɛ.

english_verse: Each morning everyone gathered as much as they needed, and in the heat of the day the rest melted.
translation_verse: Tɔɔ perɔ chɔɔ bɛlbwa naa, bɛlbwa ka dɛ tɔɔ ɡɛ del aa maɡre o ne, asɛ wee baa baŋɛ aa, anɔ la aa kaa dɛ chɔ la bwa yon mwɛɛ.

english_verse: However, on the sixth day of the week, everyone gathered enough to have four liters, instead of two. When the leaders reported this to Moses,
translation_verse: Tɔpenumɛl wee la, ba dɛ tɔɔra bele anɛnɛ ɡɛ aa maɡre bɛlbwa ne, nɛmbeŋkpoŋ bɛlbwa dɛ dɔ dɛ ɛ kuruwa dela anɛ. Asɛ nomonome la ba Mosis be dɛ ba taa baɡlo.

english_verse: he told them that the Lord had said, “Tomorrow is the Sabbath, a sacred day of rest in honor of me. So gather all you want to bake or boil, and make sure you save enough for tomorrow.”
translation_verse: O ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, “Waa Korowii aa dɛ do heya a ta laanee nɔ, kere ɛ Ona Tɔpere, o ɛ tɔpere waa do ɡoroŋ dɛ tɛ Korowii. Anomanta, hé wɔɔ paanoo haa dɛ nyin wɔɔra, dɛ́ daa anɔ la haa dɛ nyin daala fini. Anɔ la haa di a ka la, he kwaa cheɡ tɔɔ per a ta.”

english_verse: “You may eat the food,” Moses said. “Today is the Sabbath in honor of the Lord, and there won't be any of this food on the ground today.
translation_verse: Ate, Mosis ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, “Hé dia fini, dɛkalkɛ fini ɛ Ona Tɔpere dɛ tɛ Korowii. Kondikwaa bɛlbwa toole he na harɛ la ta bobɛlbwa dɛ tɔɔra fini.

english_verse: You will find it there for the first six days of the week, but not on the Sabbath.”
translation_verse: Tɔpera anumɛlee chɛ kɛ hé kpɔ tɔɔ kondikwa la, kɛ tɔpenuanɛ wee waa ɛ Ona Tɔpere la te, kondikwaa bɛlbwa aa lee he tɔɔ.”

english_verse: A few of the Israelites did go out to look for some, but there was none.
translation_verse: Ane a bwa, tɔpenuanɛ wee la, nɛra la bane leɔ ŋɔ ba fee ka tɔɔ kondikwaa la ane, kɛ ba ta ane dɔe.

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “Moses, how long will you people keep disobeying my laws and teachings?
translation_verse: Belaa Korowii ŋɔ Mosis be ŋɔ, “Dɛ ka tel saŋ besoo hɛɛ nyin he vɛh waa maa do heyaa ta teŋa ɔ?

english_verse: Remember that I was the one who gave you the Sabbath. That's why on the sixth day I provide enough bread for two days. Everyone is to stay home and rest on the Sabbath.”
translation_verse: Hé jemɛ kɛŋɔ Korowii tɛ heyaa tɔpere haa onɛ o ta. A waa tɔpenumɛl wee ta wɛɛ tɛ heya tɔpenuanɛ wee kondikwa dɛɛ ja la. Bɛlbwa chɛ kɛ ó so o buɡ ta tɔpenuanɛ wee la ta, dɛ bɛ le kaa bobɛlbwa.”

english_verse: And so they rested on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Anomanta, nomɛlbwa onɛ tɔpenuanɛ wee la ta.

english_verse: The Israelites called the bread manna. It was white like coriander seed and delicious as wafers made with honey.
translation_verse: Israel tena la ŋɔ kondikwaa la sɔne ‘maana’. A do kɛŋɔ boyubi dɛ to. He dia aa, o som kɛŋɔ baa kpɔ tooh do biskeeti ta la ken.

english_verse: Moses told the people that the Lord had said, “Store up two liters of this manna, because I want future generations to see the food I gave you during the time you were in the desert after I rescued you from Egypt.”
translation_verse: Asɛ Mosis ŋɔ, “Waa Korowii aa do yaa a ta laanee kɛŋɔ, ‘Hé ɡel maana dɛ ɛ kuruwa del cheɡ, ásɛ he naanar baa ka ba la jemɛ kondikwaa la soo maa tɛ heya he di pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta, ɡɛ saŋ maa lawɛ heyaa le Ijipt harɛ ta la.’ ”

english_verse: Then Moses told Aaron, “Put some manna in a jar and store it in the place of worship for future generations to see.”
translation_verse: Anomanta, Mosis berɔ ŋɔ Arɔn be ŋɔ, “Kpɔ vii dɛ́ fuɡe maana kuruwa del do o bini, ásɛ dɛ kpɔ cheɡ Korowii sie á che tɛ ya naanar baa ka ba la.”

english_verse: Aaron followed the Lord's instructions and put the manna in front of the sacred chest for safekeeping.
translation_verse: Arɔn kpɔ maana la cheɡ Korowii Ne Nɛwɛnyina Fɔo Daka la sie, asɛ ba kwaa cheɡ ɡɛ Korowii aa do Mosis la.

english_verse: The Israelites left the desert and moved from one place to another each time the Lord ordered them to. Once they camped at Rephidim, but there was no water for them to drink.
translation_verse: Israel tena bwa iro le Sen pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta dɛɛ ɡaaɡe, dɛ so dɛɛ ir ɡɛ Korowii aa dɛ do ba la. Ba ɡaaɡɔ dɛ ka baŋre ba tɛnte deene so bobɛl ɡe baa dɛ yerɔ Refidim. Dɛ nee toole harɛ la ta bá nyɔ.

english_verse: The people started complaining to Moses, “Give us some water!” Moses replied, “Why are you complaining to me and trying to put the Lord to the test?”
translation_verse: Anomanta, ba ne Mosis naɡrɔ, asɛ ba ŋɔ, “Tɛ́ yaa nee yá nyɔ.” Asɛ o chaŋe ŋɔ, “N ne he naɡra munii ame o? Ɛrɛɛ hɛɛ nyin he daah Korowii dɛ́ na nɔɔ?”

english_verse: But the people were thirsty and kept on complaining, “Moses, did you bring us out of Egypt just to let us and our families and our animals die of thirst?”
translation_verse: Nyɔɡre kohona nomanta, ba teŋɔ naɡre Mosis waa bela. Ba ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ he lawɛ yaa le Ijipt harɛ ta, dɛ ɡel nyɔɡre baa kpo ya ne ya bii ne kondɛɛra ya bwa serewe nɔɔ?”

english_verse: Then Moses prayed to the Lord, “What am I going to do with these people? They are about to stone me to death!”
translation_verse: Ate, Mosis soŋe Korowii ŋɔ, “N Naa Korowii, ɛrɛɛ yaa ba wona ɛ tɛ nɛra nɔ te nɔ? Ba dɛ nyin kɛ ba foɡ mɛ bwea kpo kwara.”

english_verse: The Lord answered, “Take some of the leaders with you and go ahead of the rest of the people. Also take along the walking stick with which you struck the Nile River.
translation_verse: Anee Korowii chaŋe Mosis ŋɔ, “Tɔ nɛra la sie. Kpɔ nomonome la bini bane ja he nɛ, dɛ́ kpɔ daŋɡbala la haa kpɔa lɔ Nael Moo sie la ɡe kpoŋe kaa.

english_verse: When you get to the rock at Mount Sinai, I will be there with you. Strike the rock with the stick, and water will pour out for the people to drink.” Moses did this while the leaders watched.
translation_verse: Mɛɛ ka che bwe bɛl jwɛɛh Sinai Bwejen ta belaa dɛɛ kpa heya. Dɛ he tel belaa, kpɔ daŋɡbala la lɔ bwe la, nee ɛɛ le o taa ba, ásɛ nɛra la dɔ nyɔ.” Asɛ Mosis ɡe ɛ ɡɛ waa nɔ bwa Israel nomonome la siwi ta.

english_verse: The people had complained and tested the Lord by asking, “Is the Lord really with us?” So Moses named that place Massah, which means “testing” and Meribah, which means “complaining.” Israel Defeats the Amalekites
translation_verse: Mosis pa bela sɔn Maasa ne Mɛreba, dɛkalkɛ Israel tena la naɡre wa dɛ daah Korowii na dɛɛ bɔɔ ŋɔ, “Korowii ja ya nɛɛ kɛɛ o ta ya nɛɛ jae yɔ?” Israel tena yo Amalɛk tena

english_verse: When the Israelites were at Rephidim, they were attacked by the Amalekites.
translation_verse: Amalɛk tena balɔ ba lɔ tɔ Israel tena nɛ Refidim dɛ yoo ba.

english_verse: So Moses told Joshua, “Have some men ready to attack the Amalekites tomorrow. I will stand on a hilltop, holding this walking stick that has the power of God.”
translation_verse: Anee Mosis ŋɔ Josua be ŋɔ, “Le ya baala nɔ bini bane, ásɛ he ka yoo ba. Kere mɛɛ ka che deŋɡare bɛl doa belaa dɛ́ kpoŋe Korowii daŋɡbala la.”

english_verse: Joshua led the attack as Moses had commanded, while Moses, Aaron, and Hur stood on the hilltop.
translation_verse: Anomanta, Josua leɔ dɛ kaa yo Amalɛk tena la ɡɛ Mosis aa doo la, asɛ Mosis ne Arɔn dɛ Hur kaa deŋɡare la doa.

english_verse: The Israelites out-fought the Amalekites as long as Moses held up his arms, but they started losing whenever he lowered them.
translation_verse: Mosis baa ir o nɔɔra aa, dɛ Israel tena dɛ pɔ ba nɛ. O ba nɔɔra ne harɛ naa, dɛ Amalɛk tena ɡe berɔ dɛɛ pɔ Israel tena nɛ.

english_verse: After a while, his arms were so tired that Aaron and Hur got a rock for him to sit on. Then they stood beside him and supported his arms in the same position until sunset.
translation_verse: O nɔɔra aa baa koh la, Arɔn ne Hur kpɔ bwe ba bil Mosis o so o ta. Bɛl lɔ o ɡal asɛ bɛl ɡe do o diɡ, asɛ ba ɡɔɔ o nɔɔra nyundua, ásɛ o nɔɔra won che dɛ́ ka tel kɛŋɔ wee aa baa jo.

english_verse: Afterwards, the Lord said to Moses, “Write an account of this victory and read it to Joshua. I want the Amalekites to be forgotten forever.”
translation_verse: Asɛ Korowii ŋɔ Mosis be ŋɔ, “Chwerɛ ɡɛ waa nɔ do tɔn bini á ɛ waa aa chɔ kerekere. Gel Josua no dɛkalkɛ n dɛ ba Amalɛk tena chɔɡa baa wola ba waa no harɛ nɔ ta bobɛlbwa kpa.”

english_verse: Moses built an altar and named it “The Lord Gives Me Victory.”
translation_verse: Mosis ɛ kon waa ɛ saraha o ta dɛɛ tɛ Korowii bela, dɛ pa o sɔn ŋɔ, “Korowiirii yoa dɛɛ tɛ mɛ.”

english_verse: Then Moses explained, “This is because I depended on the Lord. But in future generations, the Lord will fight the Amalekites again and again.”
translation_verse: Dɛ berɛ ŋɔ, “Korowii nɛɛ n kpɔ sie dawɛ o yo dɛɛ tɛ mɛ. Korowii ɛɛ teŋɔɔ yo Amalɛk tena saŋ bɛlbwa dɛɛ la!”

english_verse: While Israel was camped in the desert near Mount Sinai, Jethro sent Moses this message: “I am coming to visit you, and I am bringing your wife and two sons.”
translation_verse: Dɛ Jetro tɔ sie kpɔ kala tɛ Mosis ŋɔ, “Men maa ɛ he helabaa, ne he haah dɛ he bibaala banɛ la dɛ ba he be.”

english_verse: You saw what I did in Egypt, and you know how I brought you here to me, just as a mighty eagle carries its young.
translation_verse: “Hé ɡbabir na ɡɛ maa ɛa Ijipt harɛ ta, ne ɡɛ maa kpɔ heyaa kɛŋɔ kee yon kpɔ o bii o kena ta dɛ ba he ne n be.

translation_verse: Anee Korowii ŋɔ Mosis be ŋɔ, “La nɛra la be dɛ́ ka ŋɔ ba le fini ne kere dɛ́ sɔ ba doŋa bwa ta, dɛ́ do ɡoroŋ n be pera. Bá chɛɡɛ ba laala,

translation_verse: Dɛ ba ta cheɡɛ bojaŋ, asɛ Mosis ɡe ka bɛne bam waa bira kpirkpir bela Korowii aa lole la. Voɡa ne kwaa baa dɛ ɛ saraha a ta

translation_verse: He bɛ ɡel he sie beɡre he dɔŋa deremi. He bɛ ɡel he dɔŋa haahna pɛla dɔ heya. He bɛ ɡel he sie beɡre he dɔŋa bonɔɔna kɛɛ toli, ba nae ne keeɡore, dɛ komɛlbwa aa ɛ ba kwa.”

translation_verse: Nɛra la aa na bwaala nyɛɡla dɛ no o kɔɡra, ne bɛla la sii dɛ na chuu tɔ bwe la ta la, ɔmee laɡ ba dɛ kpɔ bochechela ta ba nɛ ba ka che bojaŋ.
