english_verse: The Lord gave Moses and Aaron the following law: The people of Israel must bring Moses a reddish-brown cow that has nothing wrong with it and that has never been used for plowing.
translation_verse: “Mmara maa dɛ nyin n do Israel tena a ta laanee kɛŋɔ, bá lawɛ naneswɛm waa wola kirihiah bɛlbwa dii, baa wola daa kpɔe dawɛ o nɛɛ dɛ kpɔɔ parɛ ka ba tɛ mɛ.

english_verse: Moses will give it to Eleazar the priest, then it will be led outside the camp and killed while Eleazar watches.
translation_verse: Hé lawɔ tɛ sɔfo Eliasa, ásɛ o le o ne he bini kaa dahara dɛ́ ka kpoo n siwi ta.

english_verse: He will dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times in the direction of the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Ásɛ sɔfo Eliasa kpɔ nonii leɡe nao la chal, dɛ́ kpɔ sie chaɡɛ n Dea Cheremibɔr, dɛ́ ka ɛ merɛ bela kera anuanɛ.

english_verse: Then the whole cow, including its skin, meat, blood, and insides must be burned.
translation_verse: Wɛɛ cheo nyiŋi bá fuh nabir la. O tɔn ne o ol, ne o chal dɛ o tea bini kwaa bwa.

english_verse: A priest is to throw a stick of cedar wood, a hyssop branch, and a piece of red yarn into the fire.
translation_verse: Sɔfo Eliasa chɛ kɛ ó kpɔ peleme daa ane, ne hesɔp ne pee pona baa doa konswɛɛma ta nao waa dɛ fuh la nɛ.

english_verse: After the ceremony, the priest is to take a bath and wash his clothes. Only then can he go back into the camp, but he remains unclean and unfit for worship until evening.
translation_verse: Waa ɛ ɡɛ tonɛ la, ó sɔ ne, dɛ́ chɛɡɛ o laala mɔɔ dɛ́ won berɛ ba bela baa baŋre ba tɛnte deene la. Kɛ o doŋa ɛɛ do o nɛɛ ka tel jɔmɔra.

english_verse: The man who burned the cow must also wash his clothes and take a bath, but he is also unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Naate waa fuh nao la ɡe chɛ kɛŋɔ o sɔ ne dɛ chɛɡɛ o laala. O ɡe kah doŋa ka tel jɔmɔra mɔɔ o doŋa le o nɛ.

english_verse: A man who isn't unclean must collect the ashes of the burnt cow and store them outside the camp in a clean place. The people of Israel can mix these ashes with the water used in the ceremony to wash away sin.
translation_verse: Nɛn waa wola doŋa kaeh laanee chɛ kɛ ó pa nao la tɔɔ ka ta bela doŋa bɛlbwa aa wola toole tɛnte deene la dahara. Israel tena la kwaara cheɡ, ásɛ dɛ ba dɛ nyin dɛ sɔ nɛn waa kah doŋa ne aa, bá doa nee ta dɛ́ kpɔ sɔɔ. Anee dɛ́ baɡle kɛ o wechɔɡa bwa le o nɛ.

english_verse: The man who collects the ashes must wash his clothes, but will remain unclean until evening. This law must always be obeyed by the people of Israel and the foreigners living among them. What Must Be Done after Touching a Dead Body The Lord said:
translation_verse: Naate waa pa nao la tɔɔ ka cheɡ la ɡe chɛ kɛŋɔ ó sɔ nee dɛ́ chɛɡɛ o laala. O ɡe kah doŋa ka tel jɔmɔra mɔɔ o doŋa le o nɛ. Gɛ waa nɔ chɔ le saŋ bɛlbwa dɛ tɛ Israel tena ne hɔɔhra baa soɡe ba bini bwa.

english_verse: If you touch a dead body, you will be unclean for seven days.
translation_verse: Nomɛlbwa waa leɡe nɛn waa sewa la kah doŋa tɔpera anuanɛ.

english_verse: But if you wash with the water mixed with the cow's ashes on the third day and again on the seventh day, you will be clean and acceptable for worship. You must wash yourself on those days; if you don't, you will remain unclean.
translation_verse: Naate chɛ kɛŋɔ ó kpɔ nee la ane sɔ tɔpetooro wee waa kah doŋa la, ne tɔpenuanɛ wee mɔɔ dɛ́ le o doŋa waa kaah la ta. Kɛ dɛ o ta o doŋa sɔe ta tɔpetooro wee ne tɔpenuanɛ wee la aa, o ta kah doŋa.

english_verse: Suppose you touch a dead body, but refuse to be made clean by washing with the water mixed with ashes. You will be guilty of making my sacred tent unclean and will no longer belong to the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Nomɛlbwa waa leɡe nɛn waa sewa dɛ vɛh o doŋa sɔe dɛ ta la kpɔ doŋa kah n Tɛnte Dea la. A ta chɛ kɛ bá kuro ja Israel tena bini. Baa wola nee aa laa nɛn doŋa dɛɛ kpɔ o nɛɛ Tɛnte la ɛɛ merɛ naate nɛɛ nomanta, o kah doŋa. O doŋa ta lɔ o nɛ.

english_verse: If someone dies in a tent while you are there, you will be unclean for seven days. And anyone who later enters the tent will also be unclean.
translation_verse: Mmara waa lole dɛ tɛ nomɛl waa sewɛ tɛnte dea bini laanee nɔ. Nomɛlbwa waa lɔ ɡɛ tɛnte dea la bini, ne nomɛlbwa waa ka jo bela bwa kah doŋa tɔpera anuanɛ.

english_verse: Any open jar in the tent is unclean.
translation_verse: Komɛlbwa waa dɔ tɔ baa wola o ta tɔe ɡɛ saŋ la ɡe kah doŋa.

english_verse: If you touch the body of someone who died or was killed, or if you touch a human bone or a grave, you will be unclean for seven days.
translation_verse: Nomɛlbwa waa leɡe nɛn baa kpoo, kɛɛ nɛn waa sewɛ ɡɛ nɛra bwa aa dɛ sewɛ, kɛɛ o hoɡ, kɛɛ dɛ o ŋwamee yaa, o kah doŋa ka tel tɔpera anuanɛ.

english_verse: Before you can be made clean, someone who is clean must take some of the ashes from the burnt cow and stir them into a pot of spring water. That same person must dip a hyssop branch in the water and ashes, then sprinkle it on the tent and everything in it, including everyone who was inside. If you have touched a human bone, a grave, or a dead body, you must be sprinkled with that water.
translation_verse: Naate waa wola doŋa kaeh chɛ kɛ ó kpɔ hesɔp daa su nee la ne tɔɔ la ta, dɛ́ ɛ merɛ tɛnte dea nɛn aa sewɛ o bini la ta, ne nɛra baa lɔ o bini, dɛ o laala bwa ta. Dɛ nomɛl leɡe nɛn waa sewa hoɡ kɛɛ ŋwam, kɛɛ nɛn baa kpoo, kɛɛ dɛ sewɛ ɡɛ nɛra bwa aa dɛ sewɛ aa, ó ɛ nee la merɛ o ɡe nɛɛ ɡɛ.

english_verse: If this is done on the third day and on the seventh day, you will be clean. Then after you take a bath and wash your clothes, you can worship that evening.
translation_verse: Naate waa wola doŋa kaeh la kpɔ hesɔp daa la su nee la ta, dɛ́ ɛ merɛ naate waa kah doŋa la nɛ tɔpetooro wee ne tɔpenuanɛ wee la ta. Tɔpenuanɛ wee la, ó laa doŋa kpɔ doŋa te la nɛ. Naate baa laa doŋa kpɔ o nɛɛ la chɛɡɛ o laala dɛ́ sɔ ne, ásɛ awola jɔmɔra la, dɛ o le doŋa ta.

english_verse: If you are unclean and refuse to be made clean by washing with the water mixed with ashes, you will be guilty of making my sacred tent unclean, and you will no longer belong to the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Dɛ nomɛl kah doŋa dɛ vɛh a sɔe dɛ ta aa, a chɛ kɛŋɔ bá sɔɔ lola, dɛkalkɛŋɔ o kpɔ doŋa kah n Tɛnte Dea la. Ba ta doŋa laa kpɔ o nɛ, o ta kah doŋa.

english_verse: These laws will never change. The man who sprinkled the water and the ashes on you when you were unclean must also wash his clothes. And whoever touches this water is unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Mmara nɔ chɔ le tɛɛ ba saŋ bɛlbwa. Naate waa ɛ nee la dɛɛ merɛ la ɡe chɛ kɛ ó chɛɡɛ o laala. Nomɛlbwa waa leɡe nee la ɡba ɡe kah doŋa ka tel jɔmɔra.

english_verse: When you are unclean, everything you touch becomes unclean, and anyone who touches you will be unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Komɛlbwa naate waa kah doŋa aa leɡo la ɡe kah doŋa. Nomɛlbwa waa leɡo la ɡe kah doŋa ka tel jɔmɔra.”

english_verse: The people of Israel arrived at the Zin Desert during the first month and set up camp near the town of Kadesh. It was there that Miriam died and was buried.
translation_verse: Israel tena la bwa tel Sin pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ korobiloɡle ta, dɛ bwa baŋre ba tɛnte deene dɛ so Kades. Belaa Miriam sewɛ ba huɡo.

english_verse: The Israelites had no water, so they went to Moses and Aaron
translation_verse: Dɛ nee toole bela bá nyɔ, asɛ ba bwa ɛɛ naɡre Mosis ne Arɔn wa.

english_verse: and complained, “Moses, we'd be better off if we had died along with the others in front of the Lord's sacred tent.
translation_verse: Ba ŋɔ Mosis be ŋɔ, “Ya ne yabala la bwa fe pɛo sewɛ Korowii sie bela fe bɔ.

english_verse: You brought us into this desert, and now we and our livestock are going to die!
translation_verse: Bɔkwa waa he ba ya ne pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ nɔ ta ya ne ya kondɛɛra bwa ɛɛ ba serewa nɔɔ?

english_verse: Egypt was better than this horrible place. At least there we had grain and figs and grapevines and pomegranates. But now we don't even have any water.”
translation_verse: Bɔkwa waa he le ya ne Ijipt harɛ ta, dɛ kpɔ yaa ba ta bochɔɡe nɔ ta ken? Harɛ yaa wola won parɛ komɛlbwa. Mea kɛɛ fiɡ daa nɔna kɛɛ ɡrepore kɛɛ pɔmeɡranet nɔna toole. Nee kwaraa toole ya nyɔ.”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the entrance to the sacred tent, where they bowed down. The Lord appeared to them in all of his glory
translation_verse: Ate, Mosis ne Arɔn le nɛra la bwa be, dɛ la Korowii Dea Cheremibɔr doonyoa bela, dɛ ka kpɔ sie pi harɛ dɛ soŋe Korowii, asɛ Korowii jirima ba ba nɛ.

english_verse: and said, “Moses, get your walking stick. Then you and Aaron call the people together and command that rock to give you water. That's how you will provide water for the people of Israel and their livestock.”
translation_verse: “Kpɔ daŋɡbala la ásɛ he ne Arɔn ka cheme nɛra la bwa. Bol wa, nee ɛɛ le bwe la taa, ásɛ nɛra la ne ba kondɛɛra bwa nyɔ.”

english_verse: Moses obeyed and took his stick from the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Anee Mosis kpɔ daŋɡbala la le Korowii Dea Cheremi Bɔr doonyoa bela, dɛ ka ɛ ɡɛ Korowii aa doo la.

english_verse: After he and Aaron had gathered the people around the rock, he said, “Look, you rebellious people, and you will see water flow from this rock!”
translation_verse: O ne Arɔn yerɛ nɛra la bwa cheme bwe la jwɛh, dɛ ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, “Lwɛmkpeɡ tena, a chɛ kɛ yá dɔ nee le bwe nɔ ta tɛ heya aa?”

english_verse: He raised his stick in the air and struck the rock two times. At once, water gushed from the rock, and the people and their livestock had water to drink.
translation_verse: Ate, o ɡɔɔ daŋɡbala la lɔ bwe la kera anɛ, asɛ nee palɛ le bwe la ta yɔɔ ken, ba ne ba kondɛɛra bwa nyɔ.

english_verse: But the Lord said to Moses and Aaron, “Because you refused to believe in my power, these people did not respect me. And so, you will not be the ones to lead them into the land I have promised.”
translation_verse: Belaa Korowii ŋɔ Mosis ne Arɔn be ŋɔ, “Haa wola men yaradae, dɛ kpɔ jirima tɛ mɛ kɛ n do ɡoroŋ Israel tena siwi ta nɔ, haa ba sie tɔ dɛ́ kpɔ ba ka jo harɛ maa baɡ ba nyoa la ta.”

english_verse: The Israelites had complained against the Lord, and he had shown them his holy power by giving them water to drink. So they named the place Meribah, which means “Complaining.” Israel Isn't Allowed To Go through Edom
translation_verse: Ba pa bela sɔn Mɛreba, dɛkalkɛ belaa Israel tena naɡre Korowii wa, asɛ o baɡ ba kɛŋɔ o do ɡoroŋ. Edom tena ŋɔ Israel tena bɛ ba harɛ ta kpɔ

english_verse: Moses sent messengers from Israel's camp near Kadesh with this message for the king of Edom: We are Israelites, your own relatives, and we're sure you have heard the terrible things that have happened to us.
translation_verse: Kades belaa Mosis tomɛ toroma Edom kooro be ŋɔ, “He lolanar Israel tenaa yaa, he jemɛ ya wenaale yaa lɔ a ta wubwa la.

english_verse: Our ancestors settled in Egypt and lived there a long time. But later the Egyptians were cruel to us,
translation_verse: Gɛ ya naawa aa kaa Ijipt harɛ ta, asɛ ya ka bela biɡri, Ijipt tena fiiɡi yaa,

english_verse: and when we begged our Lord for help, he answered our prayer and brought us out of that land. Now we are camped at the border of your territory, near the town of Kadesh.
translation_verse: asɛ ya wi no Korowii o no yaa, dɛ ɡel nyundua torome ba kpɔ yaa le Ijipt harɛ ta. Taraken ya lɔ Kades, bwɛɛ waa lɔ he harɛ jwɛh ta.

english_verse: Please let us go through your country. We won't go near your fields or vineyards, and we won't drink any water from your wells. We will stay on the main road until we leave your territory.
translation_verse: N poori tɛ yaa ŋwɛnɛ yá kpɔ he harɛ ta ba kaa. Yaa kooni ne daa kooni taa kpɔ. Yaa bule bɛlbwa nee nyɔ, yaa kpɔ ŋwɛnɛjen la taa ba kaa yaa wola bobɛlbwaa bɛɡɛ dɛ́ ka tel kɛŋɔ yaa le he harɛ ta.”

english_verse: But the king of Edom answered, “No, I won't let you go through our country! And if you try, we will attack you.”
translation_verse: Anee Edom kooro ŋɔ, “Akai! Dɛɛ berɛ n harɛ ta kpɔe, dɛ he hɛlɛ ɡɛ naa, yáa cheme heyaa laa nee.”

english_verse: Moses sent back this message: “We promise to stay on the main road, and if any of us or our livestock drink your water, we will pay for it. We just want to pass through.”
translation_verse: Asɛ Israel tena la ŋɔ, “Ŋwɛnɛjen la taa yaa ba kpɔe ba kaa. Dɛ ya bɛlbwa nyɔ he ne, hale ya kondɛɛra kwaraa naa, yaa bɔ a kemee, wobɛlbwa ta jae kpa.”

english_verse: But the king insisted, “You can't go through our land!” Then Edom sent out its strongest troops
translation_verse: Asɛ Edom tena la berɛ ŋɔ, “Hɛɛ berɛ ya harɛ ta kpɔe.” Ate, dɛ le laa tena baa wara dɛ do kpeɡri ba la ka chem ba.

english_verse: to keep Israel from passing through its territory. So the Israelites had to go in another direction. Aaron Dies
translation_verse: Edom tena aa wola sɛɛh kɛŋɔ Israel tena kpɔ ba harɛ ta la, ba barɔ kpɔ baŋ bɛl kaa. Arɔn seo wa

english_verse: After the Israelites had left Kadesh and had gone as far as Mount Hor
translation_verse: Israel tena la bwa le Kades, dɛ ka tel Hɔr Bwejen ta.

english_verse: “Aaron, this is where you will die. You and Moses disobeyed me at Meribah, and so you will not enter the land I promised the Israelites.
translation_verse: “Arɔn ɛɛ sewɔɔ ka pu o naawa. Waa harɛ maa baɡɛ Israel tena nyoa la taa tel. He nɛra banɛ nɔ ɛ lwɛmkpeɡ waa maa do heyaa a ta Mɛreba la.

english_verse: Moses, go with Aaron and his son Eleazar to the top of the mountain.
translation_verse: Mosis, kpɔ Arɔn ne o bibaa Eliasa he ne ba kaa Hɔr Bwejen nɔ doa.

english_verse: Then take Aaron's priestly robe from him and place it on Eleazar. Aaron will die there.”
translation_verse: Ka foo Arɔn sɔfo laala la dɛ́ kpɔ do o bibaa Eliasa. Arɔn ɛɛ sewɛ belaa ka pu o naawa.”

english_verse: Moses obeyed, and everyone watched as he and Aaron and Eleazar walked to the top of Mount Hor.
translation_verse: Ate, Mosis ɛ ɡɛ Korowii aa doo la. Ba teehnɔ kaa bwejen la doa Israel tena la bwa siwi ta.

english_verse: Moses then took the priestly robe from Aaron and placed it on Eleazar. Aaron died there. When Moses and Eleazar came down,
translation_verse: Asɛ Mosis foo Arɔn laala la, dɛ kpɔ do Eliasa, asɛ Arɔn den sewɛ bwejen la doa bela. Asɛ Mosis ne Eliasa tu le bwe la doa.

english_verse: the people knew that Aaron had died, and they mourned his death for
translation_verse: Israel tena la bwa aa naa kɛŋɔ Arɔn sewɔ la, ba ɛ o lwe tɔpera fifraatoro.

english_verse: The Israelites had to go around the territory of Edom, so when they left Mount Hor, they headed south toward the Red Sea. But along the way, the people became so impatient
translation_verse: Israel tena le Hɔr Bwejen la bɔr dɛ kpɔ ŋwɛnɛ waa kaa Mposwɛm ta, dɛ bar kpɔ Edom tena harɛ nyoa. Baa dɛ kaa la ba ta bambile lawɛ,

english_verse: that they complained against God and said to Moses, “Did you bring us out of Egypt, just to let us die in the desert? There's no water out here, and we can't stand this awful food!”
translation_verse: dɛ bol waa yaɡɛ Korowii ne Mosis ŋɔ, “Bɔkwa waa he kpɔ yaa le Ijipt harɛ ta yaa ba ba serewe pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta ken? Kondikwaa tenten bɛlbwa toole bonɔ, nee ɡe kwaraa toole. Yaa maana nɔ ɡe nyin kpa.”

english_verse: Then the Lord sent poisonous snakes that bit and killed many of them.
translation_verse: Belaa Korowii ɡel harɛkonchɔɡa ba ba baah, dɛ choɡri ba ɡalɡa ba serewe.

english_verse: Some of the people went to Moses and admitted, “It was wrong of us to insult you and the Lord. Now please ask him to make these snakes go away.” Moses prayed,
translation_verse: Israel tena la berɔ ba Mosis be, dɛ ba sɛh ba chɔɡre dɛ ŋɔ, “Ya ɛ wechɔɡa kɛ yaa bol waa yaɡɛ Korowii ne hen. Soŋe Korowii tɛ yaa, ásɛ o le harɛkwaare nɔ ne tɛ yaa.” Asɛ Mosis soŋe Korowii tɛɛ ba.

english_verse: and the Lord answered, “Make a snake out of bronze and place it on top of a pole. Anyone who gets bitten can look at the snake and be saved from death.”
translation_verse: Anee Korowii ŋɔ Mosis be ŋɔ, “Kpɔ ayaawa ɛ harɛkon, dɛ́ kpɔ saɡɛ dajaŋ ta, ásɛ nomɛlbwa harɛkon la bɛl aa choɡo la nyiŋi dajaŋ kon la dɛ́ dɔ o nyu.”

english_verse: Moses obeyed the Lord. And all of those who looked at the bronze snake lived, even though they had been bitten by the poisonous snakes. Israel's Journey to Moab
translation_verse: Asɛ Mosis kpɔ ayaawa ɛ harɛkon la bɛl, dɛ kpɔ saɡɛ dajaŋ ta. Dɛ harɛkon choɡe ba bini bɛlbwa o nyiŋi dajaŋ kon la aa, dɛ o dɔ o nyu. Moab harɛ ta kaala

english_verse: As the Israelites continued their journey to Canaan, they camped at Oboth,
translation_verse: Israel tena la iro, dɛ ka baŋre ba tɛnte deene Ɔbɔt, dɛ so bela.

english_verse: and then in the Zered Gorge.
translation_verse: Ba berɔ le lye Abarim ɡe, dɛ ka so Sɛrɛd Fɛlembɔjen ta.

english_verse: After that, they crossed the Arnon River gorge and camped in the Moabite desert bordering Amorite territory. The Arnon was the border between the Moabites and the Amorites.
translation_verse: Dɛ berɛ le Sered Fɛlembɔjen ta bela, dɛ ka so Aanɔn Moo nyoa. Gɛ moo la chɔ pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta dɛɛ kaa Amɔre tena harɛ ta. Aanɔn Moo la chɔ Moab tena ne Amɔre tena baah ta, dɛ ɛ ba jwɛh.

english_verse: A song in The Book of the Lord's Battles mentions the town of Waheb with its creeks in the territory of Suphah. It also mentions the Arnon River,
translation_verse: A waa ɡela Korowii Laa Waa Yoa Tɔn ɛɛ baɡle ŋɔ, ‘Wahab bwɛɛ ne o nenabɔɔne aa lɔ Sufa harɛ ta. Dɛ berɛ baɡle Aanɔn Moo la

english_verse: with its valleys that lie alongside the Moabite border and extend to the town of Ar.
translation_verse: ne o felembɔjena aa le Moab tena jwɛh ta, dɛ wili kaa bwɛɛ bɛl baa dɛ yerɔ Ar.’

english_verse: From the Arnon, the Israelites went to the well near the town of Beer, where the Lord had said to Moses, “Call the people together, and I will give them water to drink.”
translation_verse: Israel tena le Aanɔn Moo ta, dɛ kaa bwɛɛ bɛl baa dɛ yerɔ Beɛ, belaa kɔlɔŋ bɛl do, asɛ Korowii ŋɔ Mosis be ŋɔ, “Gel nɛra la bwa cheme, ásɛ n tɛɛ ba nee ba nyɔ.”

english_verse: That's also the same well the Israelites sang about in this song: Let's celebrate! The well has given us water.
translation_verse: Asɛ Israel tena ɡo yel ŋɔ, “Kɔlɔŋ, ɡel nee ba! Hé ɡo yel ŋɔ,

english_verse: With their royal scepters, our leaders pointed out where to dig the well. The Israelites left the desert and camped near the town of Mattanah,
translation_verse: kɔlɔŋ koobii aa kwiu. Harɛ nɔ ta nomonjena aa kwiu, ba kpɔ ba koodaŋɡbale ne daŋɡbale kwiu.” Ba le pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta dɛ kaa Matana,

english_verse: then at Nahaliel, and then at Bamoth.
translation_verse: dɛ le Matana kaa Nahaleɛl, dɛ le Nahaleɛl kaa Bamɔt,

english_verse: Finally, they reached Moabite territory, where they camped near Mount Pisgah in a valley overlooking the desert north of the Dead Sea. Israel Defeats King Sihon the Amorite (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: dɛ le Bamɔt dɛ kaa fɛlembɔjen waa lɔ Moab, Pesɡa Bwejen o sie aa chaɡɛ pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ waa chɔa kaa Yar Mpo ta la ta. Kooro Sihon ne Kooro Ɔɡ nɛɛ pɔe

english_verse: King Sihon had ruled from Heshbon, after defeating the Moabites and taking over their land north of the Arnon River gorge.
translation_verse: Dɛ Hɛsbɔn fa ɛ Amɔre Kooro Sihon bwɛjen waa soɡe o ta, o ne Moab kooro bɛl yo laa, asɛ Kooro Sihon lɛ o harɛ bwa ka jaɡɛ Aanɔn Moo ta.

english_verse: The Israelites sent this message to King Sihon of the Amorites:
translation_verse: Israel tena tomɛ nɛra Amɔre Kooro Sihon be ŋɔ,

english_verse: Please let us pass through your territory. We promise to stay away from your fields and vineyards, and we won't drink any water from your wells. As long as we're in your land, we'll stay on the main road.
translation_verse: “Tɛ yaa ŋwɛnɛ ya kpɔ he harɛ ta ba kaa, yaa bɛɡɛ kpɔ kooni kɛɛ daa kooni ta. Yaa kɔlɔŋ bɛlbwa nee nyɔ. Yaa kpɔ ŋwɛnɛjen la taa, dɛ́ kpɔ he harɛ la ta ba kaa.”

english_verse: But Sihon refused to let Israel travel through his land. Instead, he called together his entire army and marched into the desert to attack Israel near the town of Jahaz.
translation_verse: Kooro Sihon ta Israel tena ŋwɛnɛ tɛɛ ba kpɔ o harɛ ta. Kɛ dɛ yerɛ o laa tena bwa ba ka pu Israel tena pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta, dɛ́ yoo ba. O kaa puu ba Jahas, asɛ o ne ba yo.

english_verse: Israel defeated them and took over the Amorite territory from the Arnon River gorge in the south to the Jabbok River gorge in the north. Beyond the Jabbok was the territory of the Ammonites, who were much stronger than Israel.
translation_verse: Israel tena kpo Kooro Sihon kere ne, dɛ lɛ o harɛ la dɔɔh. Le Aanɔn Moo ta dɛ kaa Jabɔk Moo ta, dɛ kpoŋe kaa Amɔn tena jwɛh ta. Dɛ Amɔn tena cheɡɛ ba jwɛh ta dɛ do kpeɡri.

english_verse: The Israelites settled in the Amorite towns, including the capital city of Heshbon with its surrounding villages.
translation_verse: Israel tena lɛ Amɔre tena bwɛjena bwa dɔɔh, dɛ so a ta. Hɛsbɔn ne bwɛɛre aa baro bwa jao.

english_verse: That's why the Amorites had written this poem about Heshbon: Come and rebuild Heshbon, King Sihon's capital city!
translation_verse: A waa ba bol wobobeela kɛŋɔ, “Hé ba Hɛsbɔn dɛ́ ba kwaa mao, hé ba vɔrɔwe Kooro Sihon bwɛjen ó berɛ do ɡɛ o fa aa doa.

english_verse: His armies marched out like fiery flames, burning down the town of Ar and destroying the hills along the Arnon River.
translation_verse: Kooro Sihon laa tena le Hɛsbɔn kɛ nii ken, kɛŋɔ ninlao dɛ le Kooro Sihon bwɛjen ta, dɛ ba chɔɡ Moab harɛ bwɛjen Ar, dɛ ka chɔɡ nɛra baa lɔ Aanɔn Moo deŋɡarere ta.

english_verse: You Moabites are done for! Your god Chemosh deserted your people; they were captured, taken away by King Sihon the Amorite.
translation_verse: Moab tena, hé bwɛɛlɛ! Voɡ Kemɔs toroma chɔɡɔ! Voɡ la ɡelɔ ba lawɛ o bibaala laa ta kaa, ba lawɛ o bihaahna tɛ Amɔre tena Kooro Sihon.

english_verse: We completely defeated Moab. The towns of Heshbon and Dibon, of Nophah and Medeba are ruined and gone.
translation_verse: Ya pɔ Hɛsbɔn tena nɛ, ya chɔɡ ba dɛ kpoŋe ka le Debɔn, dɛ ka tel Nɔfa kaa Medeba bwa.”

english_verse: After the Israelites had settled in the Amorite territory,
translation_verse: Gɛɛ a do Israel tena so Amɔre tena harɛ ta.

english_verse: Moses sent some men to explore the town of Jazer. Later, the Israelites captured the villages surrounding it and forced out the Amorites who lived there. Israel Defeats King Og of Bashan (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: A habɔɔ la, Mosis tomɛ nɛra ba ka sɔh nyiŋi Jasa, asɛ dɛ yo bela tena, dɛ pɔ ba nɛ. Asɛ Israel tena ka lɛ bwɛjeɡre aa baro cheme dɔɔh, dɛ doŋi Amɔre tena baa lɔ bela.

english_verse: The Israelites headed toward the region of Bashan, where King Og ruled, and he led his entire army to Edrei to meet Israel in battle.
translation_verse: Ba berɛ kpɔ sie chaɡɛ ŋwɛnɛ waa kaa Basan harɛ ta, asɛ Basan Kooro Ɔɡ kpɔ o laa tena bwa, dɛ ka cheme Israel tena Edrei dɛ yoo ba.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Don't be afraid of Og. I will help you defeat him and his army, just as you did King Sihon who ruled in Heshbon. Og's territory will be yours.”
translation_verse: Anee Korowii ŋɔ Mosis be ŋɔ, “Bɛ Kooro Ɔɡ ɔmɛ, n kpɔ o ne o laa tena ne harɛ la bwa do he nɔn ta. Ɛo ɡɛ haa ɛ Amɔre Kooro Sihon waa di kora Hɛsbɔn la.”

english_verse: So the Israelites wiped out Og, his family, and his entire army—there were no survivors. Then Israel took over the land of Bashan.
translation_verse: Ate, Israel tena kpo Kooro Ɔɡ ne o bibaala, dɛ o laa tena la bwa dɛ lɛ harɛ la. Ba ta nomɛlbwa ɡelɛ, asɛ dɛ so harɛ la ta.

english_verse: Israel moved from there to the hills of Moab, where they camped across the Jordan River from the town of Jericho. King Balak of Moab Hires Balaam To Curse Israel
translation_verse: Israel tena berɔ ir dɛ ka baŋre ba tɛnte deene, dɛ so Moab harɛpɛɛ waa chɔa kaa Jɔɔdan Moo nyoa, asɛ Jeriko do baŋ bɛl.

english_verse: They said to the Midianite leaders, “That huge mob of Israelites will wipe out everything in sight, like a bull eating grass in a field.” So King Balak
translation_verse: Belaa Moab tena ka ŋɔ Midian nomonome be ŋɔ, “Nɛnlaa tenten dɛ́ ba dɛ́ ba chɔɡ ya ne ya komɛlbwa kwaraa kɛŋɔ nao aa dɛ chwe kpɔɡa.” Ate, Sepɔ bibaa Kooro Balak

english_verse: sent a message to Balaam son of Beor who lived among his relatives in the town of Pethor near the Euphrates River. It said: I need your help. A large group of people has come here from Egypt and settled near my territory.
translation_verse: tomɛ toroma ba ka kpɔ Beɔ bibaa Balam. Dɛ o lɔ bwɛɛ bɛl baa dɛ yerɔ Pɛtɔ, o bɛne Yufretis Moo nyoa. Kooro Balak ŋɔ, “Nɛra bane warɔ pirim dɛ le Ijipt harɛ ta, dɛ ba su bɔr bwa dɛɛ ba dɛ́ ba lɛ n harɛ.

english_verse: They are too powerful for us to defeat, so would you come and place a curse on them? Maybe then we can run them off. I know that anyone you bless will be successful, but anyone you curse will fail.
translation_verse: Ba kpeɡri ɡwaa mɛ, anomanta, ba tomɛ ba toma tɛ mɛ, n ken ɛɛ wonoo pɔ ba nɛɛ dɛ́ doŋ ba le n harɛ nɔ ta. N jemɔ kɛŋɔ nomɛlbwa haa sweero andɛɛɡa la, dɛ́ dɔ wedɛɛɡa. Banɔ la ɡe haa taah ba dɛ́ na a wa.”

english_verse: The leaders of Moab and Midian left and took along money to pay Balaam. When they got to his house, they gave him Balak's message.
translation_verse: Ate, Moab nomonome ne Midian nomonome la kpɔ suuɡa baa kpɔ ka tomɛ toma la kaa. Baa la Balam be la, ba bol waa Kooro Balak aa ŋɔa la.

english_verse: “Spend the night here,” Balaam replied, “and tomorrow I will tell you the Lord's answer.” So the officials stayed at his house.
translation_verse: Asɛ Balam ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, “Hé chɔ ásɛ n ɛ dɛ́ bol he be waa Korowii aa ŋɔ n be.” Ate, nomonome la so Balam be.

english_verse: During the night, God asked Balaam, “Who are these people at your house?”
translation_verse: Jwaana la ne, Korowii bɔɔ Balam ŋɔ, “Nɛn besooree lɔ he be nɔɔ?”

english_verse: “They are messengers from King Balak of Moab,” Balaam answered. “He sent them
translation_verse: Anee Sepɔ bibaa Balam chaŋe ŋɔ, “Balak waa ɛ Moab harɛ ta kooro laanee tom ba n be ŋɔ,

english_verse: to ask me to go to Moab and put a curse on the people who have come there from Egypt. They have settled everywhere around him, and he wants to run them off.”
translation_verse: ‘Nɛra bane baa wara pirim dɛ le Ijipt harɛ ta, baa su bɔr bwa ken. Dɛ he ba, dɛ́ ba tomɛ ba toma tɛo, o ken ɛɛ won yoo ba dɛ́ doŋ ba.’ ”

english_verse: But God replied, “Don't go with Balak's messengers. I have blessed those people who have come from Egypt, so don't curse them.”
translation_verse: Korowii ŋɔ Balam be ŋɔ, “Bɛ ban pu kaa, bɛ nɛra la ɡe toma tomɛ. Israel tena ɛ nɛra maa swee andɛɛɡa tɛɛ ba.”

english_verse: The next morning, Balaam said to Balak's officials, “Go on back home. The Lord says I cannot go with you.”
translation_verse: Tɔɔ aa pera chɔɔ la, Balam ŋɔ Kooro Balak nomonome la be ŋɔ, “Hé berɛ kaa he harɛ ta, Korowii ta sɛɛh kɛ n ne he kaa.”

english_verse: The officials left and told Balak that Balaam refused to come.
translation_verse: Ate, nomonome la berɛ kaa Kooro Balak be dɛ ka ŋɔ, “Balam ta sɛɛh kɛ ya ne ó ba.”

english_verse: Then Balak sent a larger group of officials, who were even more important than the first ones.
translation_verse: Asɛ Balak berɛ tomɛ o nomonome baa dɔ sɔna dɛ warɛ ɡwaa banɔ la.

english_verse: They went to Balaam and told him that Balak had said, “Balaam, if you come to Moab,
translation_verse: Ba la Balam be dɛ kpɔ kala la ka tɛo ŋɔ, “Bɛ ɡel wobɛlbwa tɔe ŋwɛnɛ n be bala.

english_verse: I'll pay you very well and do whatever you ask. Just come and place a curse on these people.”
translation_verse: Mɛɛ bɔe kemee kɛrɛdɛ, ásɛ wobɛlbwa ɡe haa bol la, mɛɛ ɛo. Ba tomɛ ba toma tɛ mɛ.”

english_verse: Balaam answered, “Even if Balak offered me a palace full of silver or gold, I wouldn't do anything to disobey the Lord my God.
translation_verse: Anee Balam ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, “Hale Kooro Balak kpɔ o kara mun suuɡapoŋa ne suuɡaswɛm bwa tɛ mɛ naa, maa won ɛ wobɛlbwa Korowii aa do mɛ ŋɔ n bɛ ɛ la. Hale kohona kɛɛ tama bɛlbwa.

english_verse: You are welcome to spend the night here, just as the others did. I will find out if the Lord has something else to say about this.”
translation_verse: He ɡe chɔ bonɔ fini ɡɛ banɔ la aa chɔa la, ásɛ n no waa Korowii aa dɛ ba n be bola.”

english_verse: That night, God said, “Balaam, I'll let you go to Moab with Balak's messengers, but do only what I say.”
translation_verse: Awola jwaana la, Korowii ŋɔ Balam be ŋɔ, “Nɛra nɔ aa bala dɛɛ ba dɛ́ ba kpɔe nɔ, kpɔ he te he ne ba kaa, kɛ ka ɛ anɔ la maa ŋɔ he ɛ ɡbo.” Balam ne o keeɡo

english_verse: So Balaam got up the next morning and saddled his donkey, then left with the Moabite officials. Balaam and His Donkey Meet an Angel
translation_verse: Tɔɔ aa pera chɔɔ la, Balam iro dɛ pa yale dawɛ o keeɡo ta dɛ teeh so o ta, o ne Moab nomonome la chiɡ ŋwɛnɛ ta dɛ kaa.

english_verse: Balaam was riding his donkey to Moab, and two of his servants were with him. But God was angry that Balaam had gone, so one of the Lord's angels stood in the road to stop him.
translation_verse: Waa dɛ kaa la, Korowii baah diu, asɛ o ɡel o nyundua torome ba che ŋwɛnɛ la baah ta dɛ tɔɔ ŋwɛnɛ. Dɛ Balam soɡe o keeɡo la ta, o bonɔɔna banɛ ja o nɛ.

english_verse: When Balaam's donkey saw the angel standing there with a sword, it walked off the road and into an open field. Balaam had to beat the donkey to get it back on the road.
translation_verse: Keeɡo la na Korowii nyundua torome la kɛŋɔ waa pamɛ kere dɛ che ŋwɛnɛ la ta, asɛ o bɛɡɛ jo kpɔɡ bini. Asɛ Balam lɔɔ dɛ ɡel o ba chiɡ ŋwɛnɛ ta.

english_verse: Then the angel stood between two vineyards, in a narrow path with a stone wall on each side.
translation_verse: Asɛ Korowii nyundua torome la berɛ ka che daa kooni anɛ ane baah ta, asɛ danjwɛɛ do diɡ ne ɡal, ŋwɛnɛ chɔ a baah ta feelɔɔ ken.

english_verse: When the donkey saw the angel, it walked so close to one of the walls that Balaam's foot scraped against the wall. Balaam beat the donkey again.
translation_verse: Keeɡo la na Korowii nyundua torome la ja, dɛ kpɔ o te ka pɛl danjwɛɛ la, anee Balam nakpala seeɡe danjwɛɛ la. O berɛ lɔ keeɡo la ja.

english_verse: The angel moved once more and stood in a spot so narrow that there was no room for the donkey to go around.
translation_verse: Korowii nyundua torome la berɛ kaa sie, dɛ ka che bofeelɔɔ bobɛl keeɡo la aa wola won bɛɡɛ kpɔ diɡ kɛɛ ɡal.

english_verse: So it just lay down. Balaam lost his temper, then picked up a stick and whacked the donkey.
translation_verse: Keeɡo la aa na Korowii nyundua torome la, o chɔ harɛ, asɛ Balam baah di o kpɔ o daŋɡbala lɔɔ.

english_verse: When that happened, the Lord told the donkey to speak, and it asked Balaam, “What have I done that made you beat me three times?”
translation_verse: Asɛ Korowii ɡel keeɡo la bol waa ta Balam nɛɛ ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ n ɛɛ he lɔɔ mɛ kera atoro bwa ken?”

english_verse: “You made me look stupid!” Balaam answered. “If I had a sword, I'd kill you here and now!”
translation_verse: Anee Balam chaŋe keeɡo la ŋɔ, “Haa ɡela n di sihiih la waa! Dɛ n dɔ kere aa, n fe kpoe buɡ nɔ ta.”

english_verse: “But you're my owner,” answered the donkey, “and you've ridden me many times. Have I ever done anything like this before?” “No,” Balaam admitted.
translation_verse: Keeɡo la ŋɔ, “He laa dɔɔ mɛ hɛɛ so n nɛ tɔpere bɛlbwa ba le fini nɔ naa? N ɛɛ ken ka bwa naa?” Balam chaŋe ŋɔ, “Akai.”

english_verse: Just then, the Lord let Balaam see the angel standing in the road, holding a sword, and Balaam bowed down.
translation_verse: Ate, Korowii pili Balam sie, asɛ o na Korowii nyundua torome waa pamɛ kere che ŋwɛnɛ la ta. Asɛ Balam ba harɛ dɛ kpɔ sie pi harɛ.

english_verse: The angel said, “You had no right to treat your donkey like that! I was the one who blocked your way, because I don't think you should go to Moab.
translation_verse: Korowii nyundua torome la bɔɔro ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ he lɔɔ he keeɡo nɔ kera atoro bwa ken? Na, n balɔ dɛ́ ba tɔe ŋwɛnɛ dɛkalkɛŋɔ n ta hen ŋwɛnɛ tɛɛ kɛŋɔ he la Moab harɛ ta.

english_verse: If your donkey had not seen me and stopped those three times, I would have killed you and let the donkey live.”
translation_verse: Keeɡo la na mɛ kera atoro bwa dɛɛ kee mɛ. Dɛ o fe ta kee yaa, n fe kpoe dɛ ɡelo.”

english_verse: Balaam replied, “I was wrong. I didn't know you were trying to stop me. If you don't think I should go, I'll return home at once.”
translation_verse: Balam ŋɔ Korowii nyundua torome la be ŋɔ, “N ɛ wechɔɡa, n ta jemɛ kɛŋɔ he cheɡɛ ŋwɛnɛ ta dɛ tɔ mɛ ŋwɛnɛ. Dɛ he sie ta lɛɛ yaa, mɛɛ berɔɔ laa berɛ.”

english_verse: “It's all right for you to go,” the Lord's angel answered. “But you must say only what I tell you.” So Balaam went on with Balak's officials. King Balak Meets Balaam
translation_verse: Korowii nyundua torome la ŋɔ, “He ne nɛra la kaa, kɛ ka bol anɔ la maa bol he be.” Anee Balam ne Kooro Balak nomonome la kaa.

english_verse: When Balak heard that Balaam was coming, he went to meet him at the town of Ir on the Arnon River, which is the northern border of Moab.
translation_verse: Kooro Balak aa noa kɛŋɔ Balam dɛ ba la, o laŋɔ ka chemo Moab harɛ bwɛjen Ar waa chɔ Aanɔn Moo nyoa, bela ɛ o harɛ jwɛh ta.

english_verse: Balak asked, “Why didn't you come when I invited you the first time? Did you think I wasn't going to pay you?”
translation_verse: Kooro Balak ŋɔ Balam be ŋɔ, “N ta nɛra tomɛ ŋɔ ba ba kpɔe kɛ a hiah mɛ naa? Ɛrɛɛ haa wola balɔɔ? Maa won bɔe kem kɛrɛdɛ kɛɛ?”

english_verse: “I'm here now,” Balaam answered. “But I will say only what God tells me to say.”
translation_verse: Balam chaŋe ŋɔ, “Taraken n balɔ, kɛ maa won bol wobɛlbwa nemenɛ anɔ la Korowii aa ŋɔa n bol.”

english_verse: They left and went to the town of Kiriath-Huzoth,
translation_verse: Asɛ Kooro Balak ne Balam kaa bwɛɛ bɛl baa dɛ yerɔ Kiriat Hosɔt.

english_verse: where Balak sacrificed cattle and sheep and gave some of the meat to Balaam and the officials who were with him.
translation_verse: Kooro Balak kpo nae ne peera, dɛ kpɔ ane tɛ Balam ne nomonome baa ja o nɛɛ la.

english_verse: The next morning, Balak took Balaam to the town of Bamoth-Baal. From there, Balaam could see some of the Israelites.
translation_verse: Tɔ aa pera chɔɔ la, Kooro Balak kpɔ Balam kaa Bamɔt Baal ba ka che bela na Israel tena la bane.

english_verse: Balaam said to Balak, “Build seven altars here, then bring seven bulls and seven rams.”
translation_verse: Balam ŋɔ Kooro Balak be ŋɔ, “Ma kwaa baa dɛ ɛ saraha a ta anuanɛ, ásɛ dɛ nyin nabala anuanɛ ne pebala anuanɛ ba tɛ mɛ.”

english_verse: After Balak had done this, they sacrificed a bull and a ram on each altar.
translation_verse: Kooro Balak ɛ ɡɛ Balam aa ŋɔa la, ba nɛra banɛ la kpɔ nabal ne pebal ɛ saraha, saraha kon la bɛlbwa ta.

english_verse: Then Balaam said, “Wait here beside your offerings, and I'll go somewhere to be alone. Maybe the Lord will appear to me. If he does, I will tell you everything he says.” And he left.
translation_verse: Balam ŋɔ Kooro Balak be ŋɔ, “Che saraha kwaa la jwɛɛh ásɛ n le kɛrɛ, Korowii ken ɛɛ bol waa n bee. Wobɛlbwa waa pili a bini baɡ mɛ la, mɛɛ ŋɔ he bee.” Asɛ dɛ kaa deŋɡare bɛl doa.

english_verse: When God appeared to him, Balaam said, “I have built seven altars and have sacrificed a bull and a ram on each one.”
translation_verse: Asɛ Korowii ka chemo dɛ bol waa o be, asɛ Balam ŋɔ, “N ma kwaa baa dɛ ɛ saraha a ta anuanɛ, asɛ dɛ kpo nabal ne pebal a bɛlbwa ta.”

english_verse: The Lord gave Balaam a message, then sent him back to tell Balak.
translation_verse: Asɛ Korowii kpɔ waane tɛ Balam ŋɔ ó ka bol Kooro Balak be.

english_verse: When Balaam returned, he found Balak and his officials standing beside the offerings.
translation_verse: Ate, o la dɛ ka na kɛŋɔ Kooro Balak ne Moab nomonome la bwa cheɡɛ o saraha kwaa la jwɛh.

english_verse: Balaam said: “King Balak of Moab brought me from the hills of Syria to curse Israel and announce its doom.
translation_verse: Balam bol waa Korowii aa bola la dɛ ŋɔ, “Kooro Balak kaa kpɔ mɛ le Siiria harɛ ta, Moab harɛ ta wee leebɔr bwejena bɔr. Dɛ ŋɔ n ba tomɛ Israel tena toma tɛo, ba chɔɡ Israel tena tɛ mɛ.

english_verse: But I can't go against God! He did not curse or condemn Israel. *
translation_verse: Ɛrɛɛ mɛɛ ba wona chɔɡ nɛra Korowii aa swee ba andɛɛɡa ɔ? Ɛrɛɛ mɛɛ ba wona chɔɡ nɛra Korowii aa wola ban chɔɡɔ ɔ?

english_verse: They are living alone in peace. And though they are many, they don't bother the other nations. “I hope to obey God for as long as I live and to die in such peace.”
translation_verse: Umee dɛ́ won kure Israel tena ɔ? Dɛ he bɔne ba bini bɔre anaarɛ kwaraa naa, umee dɛ́ won jemɛ ba nyoa ɔ? N dɛ nyin n sewɛ kɛ nɛra ba wa aa toɡra, ɡel n seo do kɛ ban!”

english_verse: Balak said, “What are you doing? I asked you to come and place a curse on my enemies. But you have blessed them instead!”
translation_verse: Anee Kooro Balak ŋɔ Balam be ŋɔ, “Bɔkwa waa he ɛɛ mɛ ken? N kaa kpɔe ba ŋɔ hé ba tomɛ n dɔma toma, kɛ he ta wobɛlbwa ɛɛ, andɛɛɡaa he berɛ ŋɔ ba dɔ!”

english_verse: Balaam answered, “I can say only what the Lord tells me.” Balaam's Second Message
translation_verse: Ate Balam ŋɔ, “A chɛ kɛ ń bol waa Korowii aa ŋɔa n bol ɡbo.” Waa Korowii aa bol Balam be nɛɛtena

english_verse: Balak said to Balaam, “Let's go somewhere else. Maybe if you see a smaller part of the Israelites, you will be able to curse them for me.”
translation_verse: Kooro Balak ŋɔ Balam be ŋɔ, “Ba ya kaa bofale, bela haa dɛ ba wona na Israel tena la. Ba bini banee hɛɛ ba nae, ba bwa laa. Che bela tomɛ ba toma tɛ mɛ.”

english_verse: So he took Balaam to a field on top of Mount Pisgah where lookouts were stationed. Then he built seven altars there and sacrificed a bull and a ram on each one.
translation_verse: Dɛ kpɔɔ kaa kpɔɡ baah bobɛl baa dɛ yerɛ bela Sofim, Pesɡa Bwejen doa. O ma kwaa baa dɛ ɛ saraha a ta anuanɛ, dɛ kpɔ nabal ne pebal ɛ saraha bɛlbwa ta.

english_verse: “Wait here beside your offerings,” Balaam said. “The Lord will appear to me over there.”
translation_verse: Balam ŋɔ Kooro Balak be ŋɔ, “Che he saraha kwaa nɔ jwɛh ásɛ n ka na, Korowii ken ɛɛ bol waa n bee.”

english_verse: The Lord appeared to Balaam and gave him another message, then he told him to go and tell Balak.
translation_verse: Ate, Korowii bol waa Balam be ŋɔ, “Berɛ la Kooro Balak be dɛ́ ka ɡel o no.”

english_verse: Balaam went back and saw him and his officials standing beside the offerings. Balak asked, “What did the Lord say?”
translation_verse: Asɛ Balam berɛ la Kooro Balak be dɛ o ne Moab nomonome ta cheɡɛ saraha kwaa la jwɛh. Anee Kooro Balak bɔɔ Balam ŋɔ, “Bɔkwa waa Korowii bol ɔ?”

english_verse: God is no mere human! He doesn't tell lies or change his mind. God always keeps his promises.
translation_verse: Korowii ta nɛwɛnyini ɛɛ wɛɛ teŋe nyosone, kɛɛ nɛn dɛ́ charɛ o liire. O dɛ bol waa dɛ́ ɡel a ɛɛ yaa? Wɛɛ baɡɛ nyoa waa a taa teŋaa?

english_verse: “My command from God was to bless these people, and there's nothing I can do to change what he has done.
translation_verse: O do mɛ ŋɔ n swee andɛɛɡa tɛɛ ba. O swee andɛɛɡa tɛɛ ba maa wola won bera.

english_verse: Israel's king is the Lord God. He lives there with them and intends them no harm.
translation_verse: N ta wahala bɛlbwa nae Israel tena nɛ. N ta tebinichɔɡ nae ba bini. Korowii baa dɛ tomɔ ja ba nɛ. Ba kooroo on baa kpɛɛro.

english_verse: With the strength of a wild ox, God led Israel out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Korowii laɡ ba le Ijipt harɛ ta, dɛ yo dɛɛ tɛɛ ba kɛŋɔ kpɔɡ bini nao ken.

english_verse: No magic charms can work against them— just look what God has done for his people.
translation_verse: Sɔm we-ɛɛla aa won ɛ Israel tena wobɛlbwa, voɡre bɛlbwa ɡe aa ban wo. Taraken baa bol Israel tena waa ŋɔ, ‘He na waa Korowii aa ɛa tɛɛ ba.’

english_verse: They are like angry lions ready to attack; and they won't rest until their victim is gobbled up.”
translation_verse: Ba do kɛŋɔ nyujente nee ken, waa soɡe dɛɛ biɡri, dɛ o di ol waa kpoo. Waa so biɡri, dɛ o kpɛle kon waa kpoo chal bwa.”

english_verse: Balak shouted, “If you're not going to curse Israel, then at least don't bless them.”
translation_verse: Ate, Kooro Balak ŋɔ Balam be ŋɔ, “Dɛ haa ba tomaa tomɛ aa, bɛ andɛɛɡa ɡe swee tɛɛ ba.”

english_verse: “I've already told you,” Balaam answered. “I will say only what the Lord tells me.” Balaam's Third Message
translation_verse: Anee Balam chaŋo ŋɔ, “N ta he be ŋɔe ŋɔ waa Korowii aa bola laanee mɛɛ ba ɛɛ yaa?” Waa Korowii aa bol Balam be toorotena

english_verse: Balak said to Balaam, “Come on, let's try another place. Maybe God will let you curse Israel from there.”
translation_verse: Kooro Balak berɔ ŋɔ Balam be ŋɔ, “Ba ya kaa bofale, a ken ɛɛ too Korowii tea, ásɛ he won che bela tomɛ ba toma tɛ mɛ.”

english_verse: So he took Balaam to Mount Peor overlooking the desert north of the Dead Sea.
translation_verse: Asɛ Kooro Balak kpɔ Balam kaa Peɔ Bwejen doa, bela haa che dɛ́ na pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ la.

english_verse: Balaam said, “Build seven altars here, then bring me seven bulls and seven rams.”
translation_verse: Asɛ Balam ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Ma kwaa baa dɛ ɛ saraha a ta anuanɛ, dɛ́ kpɔ nabala anuanɛ ne pebala anuanɛ ba tɛ mɛ.”

english_verse: After Balak had done what Balaam asked, he sacrificed a bull and a ram on each altar.
translation_verse: Kooro Balak ɛ waa Balam aa ŋɔ o be la, dɛ kpɔ nabal beŋkpoŋ ne pebal beŋkpoŋ ɛ saraha kon la bɛlbwa ta.

english_verse: Balaam was sure that the Lord would tell him to bless Israel again. So he did not use any magic to find out what the Lord wanted him to do, as he had the first two times. Instead, he looked out toward the desert
translation_verse: Balam aa naa kɛŋɔ a too Korowii tea kɛŋɔ o swee andɛɛɡa tɛ Israel tena la, o ta laŋɛ ka voɡɛ ɡɛ o fa aa dɛ ɛ la. O berɛ sie chaɡɛ pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ la ta.

english_verse: and saw the tribes of Israel camped below. Just then, God's Spirit took control of him,
translation_verse: Balam ha sie dɛ na Israel tena la kɛŋɔ baa baŋre ba tɛnte deene dɛ so denaa ta. Korowii Doma baa so o nɛ,

english_verse: and Balaam said: “I am the son of Beor, and my words are true, so listen to my message!
translation_verse: asɛ o bol waa Korowii aa bol o be la ŋɔ, “Waa men Beɔ bibaa Balam aa noa le Korowii be, Waa waa naa chaahna ta kɛrɛdɛ ken,

english_verse: It comes from the Lord, the God All-Powerful. I bowed down to him and saw a vision of Israel.
translation_verse: nɛn waa dɛ no Korowii waa waa bola. Nɛn waa dɛ na waa Korowii Waa Ɛ Kpeɡri Bwa Dɔɔ aa pili a bini, dɛ chole chɔ harɛ o sie pili wɛɛ nyiŋi.

english_verse: “People of Israel, your camp is lovely.
translation_verse: He na ɡɛ he tɛnte deene aa wera, Israel tena, he sobɔra wer.

english_verse: It's like a grove of palm trees or a garden beside a river. You are like tall aloe trees that the Lord has planted, or like cedars growing near water.
translation_verse: A do kɛŋɔ fɛlembɔjena aa chɔa kaa, a wer kɛŋɔ bodɛɛɡa baa du daa a chɔ nee nyoa. A do kɛŋɔ Korowii aa du daa ane baa dɛ yera alore, ne peleme daa a cheɡɛ nee nyoa.

english_verse: You and your descendants will prosper like an orchard beside a stream. Your king will rule with power and be a greater king than Agag the Amalekite.
translation_verse: Bwaala ɛɛ nɛɔ taeh, ásɛ kwaa baa dua dɔ nee kohona. Ba kora ɛɛ do kanee ɡwaa Amalɛk Kooro Aɡaɡ. Ba harɛ do kan, dɛ́ dɔ jirima kohona.

english_verse: With the strength of a wild ox, God led you out of Egypt. You will defeat your enemies, shooting them with arrows and crushing their bones.
translation_verse: Korowii laɡ ba le Ijipt harɛ ta, dɛ yo dɛɛ tɛɛ ba kɛŋɔ kpɔɡ bini nao ken. Ba pɔ ba dɔma nɛɛ dɛ kuuɡi ba hoɡa, dɛ yaɡ ba hɛma ne.

english_verse: Like a lion you lie down, resting after an attack. Who would dare disturb you? “Anyone who blesses you will be blessed; anyone who curses you will be cursed.”
translation_verse: Ba do kɛŋɔ nyujente waa chɔa, nyujente nee chɔɔ waa, umee dɛ́ won lɔ bambile chumu wɔ? Nomɛlbwa waa swee andɛɛɡa tɛ Israel tena dɔ andɛɛɡa, nomɛlbwa waa taah ba la, á ɡure o ɡbaɡba nyu ta!”

english_verse: When Balak heard this, he was so furious that he pounded his fist against his hand and said, “I called you here to place a curse on my enemies, and you've blessed them three times.
translation_verse: Ate, Kooro Balak baah di Balam nɛ. O ume nɔɔra lɔ dɔŋa kohona dɛ ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “N dɔma taahna waa n ka kpɔe ba, kɛ he berɔ swee ba andɛɛɡa kera atoro bwa.

english_verse: Leave now and go home! I told you I would pay you well, but since the Lord didn't let you do what I asked, you won't be paid.”
translation_verse: Le warane kaa bela haa lea! N ŋɔ n fe ɛɛ bɔe kemee kɛrɛdɛ ɡa, kɛ Korowii tɔa ŋwɛnɛ.”

english_verse: that even if you offered me a palace full of silver or gold, I would still obey the Lord. And I explained that I would say only what he told me.
translation_verse: ‘Hale dɛ Kooro Balak kpɔ o kara mun suuɡapoŋa ne suuɡaswɛm bwa tɛ mɛ naa, maa won le Korowii habɔɔ dɛ́ ɛ n bambile wa, dɛ́ ɡel anɔ la Korowii aa do mɛ ŋɔ n bɛ ɛ la. A wer oo, aa were oo, a ta chɛ kɛ ń ɛ anɔ la Korowii aa bola ɡbo aa?’

english_verse: So I'm going back home, but I'm leaving you with a warning about what the Israelites will someday do to your nation.” Balaam's Fourth Message
translation_verse: Taraken n berɔ dɛɛ kaa n nɛra be, kɛ ɡel ń ŋɔ he be waa Israel tena aa dɛ́ ba kpɔe ɛ he nɛra kerekere.” Waa Korowii aa bol Balam be naarɛtena

english_verse: Balaam said: “I am the son of Beor, and my words are true, so listen to my message!
translation_verse: Ate, Balam bol waa aa le Korowii be ŋɔ, “Waa aa le men Beɔ bibaa Balam be, n na waa chaahna ta kɛrɛdɛ ken.

english_verse: My knowledge comes from God Most High, the Lord All-Powerful. I bowed down to him and saw a vision of Israel.
translation_verse: Nɛn waa dɛ no Korowii waa waa bola la, dɛ́ dɔ waa mun noe le Nemenɛ Korowii be. Nɛn waa na wepila le Korowii Waa Ɛ Kpeɡri Bwa Dɔɔ be, dɛ chole chɔ harɛ asɛ n sie pili wɛɛ nyiŋi.

english_verse: “What I saw in my vision hasn't happened yet. But someday, a king of Israel will appear like a star. He will wipe out you Moabites and destroy those tribes who live in the desert.
translation_verse: N na Israel tena wa aa dɛ ba bala kerekere, kɛ taraken laa. N nyiŋa, kɛ a ta men bɛnɛ. Kooro bɛl ɛɛ le Israel tena binii ba kɛŋɔ wewee ken. Nomoa bɛl ɛɛ ir ba binii, dɛ́ kpoŋe koodaŋɡbala. Wɛɛ kpoo Moab sitɔɔlaa, dɛ́ chɔɡ Sɛt naanar baa ɛ naɡrenyin tena.

english_verse: Israel will conquer Edom and capture the land of that enemy nation.
translation_verse: Israel tena ɛɛ pɔ Edom tena nɛɛ, baa pɔ ba dɔma Sɛɛ tena nɛɛ. Kɛ dɛ ta do kpeɡri kɛrɛdɛ.

english_verse: The king of Israel will rule and destroy the survivors of every town there.
translation_verse: Kooro la ɛɛ le Israel tena binii dɛ́ ba kpoo nɛra baa ka bwɛjen la ta bwa.” Waa aa ka mun Korowii bol Balam be

english_verse: “And I saw this vision about the Amalekites: Their nation is now great, but it will someday disappear forever.
translation_verse: Balam na Amalɛk tena wa chaahna ta dɛ bol ŋɔ, “Amalɛk tenaa fa kpeɡa harɛre bwa bini, kɛ a habɔɔ wɛɛ ba paɡroo kwara.”

english_verse: “And this is what I saw about the Kenites: They think they're safe, living among the rocks,
translation_verse: O na Ken tena ɡe wa dɛ ŋɔ, “He soɡe bwea baah ta, he sobɔr do wer.

english_verse: but they will be wiped out when Assyria conquers them.
translation_verse: Kɛ ane a bwa, baa pɔ he nɛɛ, ásɛ Asiiria tena lawɛ heyaa laa ta kaa.”

english_verse: “No one can survive if God plans destruction.
translation_verse: Balam berɔ ŋɔ, “Akwe, dɛ Korowii ɛ ken aa, umee dɛ́ dɔ o nyu ɔ?

english_verse: Ships will come from Cyprus, bringing people who will invade the lands of Assyria and Eber. But finally, Cyprus itself will be ruined.”
translation_verse: Stiimaere ɛɛ kpɔ nɛraa le Saepros harɛ taa ba, dɛ́ ba lɔ tɔ Asiiria tena ne Iba tena nɛ. Saepros tena ɡe kwara ɛɛ heo.”

english_verse: After Balaam finished, he started home, and Balak also left.
translation_verse: Balam aa tona la, o kaa o bwɛ. Kooro Balak ɡe kpɔ pera kaa.

english_verse: While the Israelites were camped at Acacia, some of the men had sex with Moabite women.
translation_verse: Israel tena aa baŋre ba tɛnte deene dɛ ta so Akaasia Fɛlembɔjen bini la, ba bini baala pa mun lawɛ Moab haahna dɛɛ chɔ.

english_verse: These women then invited the men to ceremonies where sacrifices were offered to their gods. The men ate the meat from the sacrifices and worshiped the Moabite gods.
translation_verse: Haahna la yerɛ Israel baala la dɛɛ la ba voɡa mune, dɛ ka kpoo kwaa dɛɛ tɛ ba voɡa, ba ne ba di dɛɛ ɡuŋi voɡa la harɛ.

english_verse: The Lord was angry with Israel because they had worshiped the god Baal Peor.
translation_verse: A cheɡɛ a ta Israel tena la ne Moab tena la bwa ɛɛ tomɛ voɡ Baal waa lɔ Peɔ la. Asɛ Korowii bwaawee ir ba nɛ.

english_verse: So he said to Moses, “Take the Israelite leaders who are responsible for this and have them killed in front of my sacred tent where everyone can see. Maybe then I will stop being angry with the Israelites.”
translation_verse: Korowii ŋɔ Mosis be ŋɔ, “Kpoo ɡɛ Israel nomonome la webaŋa n siwi ta tɛ mɛ, ásɛ n baah bɛ ba nɛɛ di kohona kpa.”

english_verse: Moses told Israel's officials, “Each of you must put to death any of your men who worshiped Baal.”
translation_verse: Ate, Mosis ŋɔ Israel tena sitɔɔla be ŋɔ, “A chɛ kɛ hé bini bɛlbwa kpo baa bɛlbwa waa kpɔ o te ka ja dɛɛ tomɛ voɡ Baal waa lɔ Peɔ la.”

english_verse: Later, Moses and the people were at the sacred tent, crying, when one of the Israelite men brought a Midianite woman to meet his family.
translation_verse: Mosis ne Israel tena la bwa aa cheme Korowii Dea Cheremibɔr la doonyoa dɛɛ wi ba te la, ba bwa siwi ta, Israel tena baala la bɛl lawɛ Midian haah ba jo o tɛnte dea, o ne o chɔ.

english_verse: Phinehas, the grandson of Aaron the priest, saw the couple and left the crowd. He found a spear
translation_verse: Asɛ sɔfo Arɔn naa Fenehas, waa ɛ Eliasa bibaa na ɡɛ dɛ le nɛra la bini dɛ ka kpɔ o lampea,

english_verse: and followed the man into his tent, where he ran the spear through the man and into the woman's stomach. The Lord immediately stopped punishing Israel with a deadly disease,
translation_verse: dɛ ka pu baa la tɛnte dea la bini dɛ yaɡɔ vah ka yaɡɛ haah la, ate weechɔɡa aa lɔ Israel tena la nyoa sɔɔh.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Korowii ŋɔ Mosis be ŋɔ,

english_verse: “In my anger, I would have wiped out the Israelites if Phinehas had not been faithful to me.
translation_verse: “Fenehas sie aa wola waa la ta lɛɛ la, a ɡelɔ n baah sɔɔh Israel tena nɛ. Anomanta, n ta ban hee.

english_verse: But instead of punishing them, I forgave them. So because of the loyalty that Phinehas showed, I solemnly promise that he and his descendants will always be my priests.”
translation_verse: Ásɛ a chɔ le tɛ o ne o naanar baa ka ba bwa, kɛ bá ɛ sɔfore saŋ bɛlbwa dɛɛ la, dɛkalkɛŋɔ o ta nomɛlbwa toma sɛɛh ka ja men Korowii waa dɛ tom mɛ nɛ, dɛ́ soŋe Israel tena bwa wechɔɡa tɛɛ ba.”

english_verse: The Israelite man that was killed was Zimri son of Salu, who was one of the leaders of the Simeon tribe.
translation_verse: Israel baa Fenehas aa kpo o ne Midian haah la sɔne Simri. Simeon dea nomoa Salu bibaalee.

english_verse: And the Midianite woman killed with him was Cozbi, the daughter of a Midianite clan leader named Zur.
translation_verse: Midian haah la ɡe sɔne Kosbi. Midian tena dea nomoa Sor bihaahnee.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses,
translation_verse: Korowii ŋɔ Mosis be ŋɔ,

english_verse: “The Midianites are now enemies of Israel, so attack and defeat them! They tricked the people of Israel into worshiping their god at Peor, and they are responsible for the death of Cozbi, the daughter of one of their own leaders.”
translation_verse: dɛkalkɛŋɔ ba kpɔ heyaa ɛ dɔma, dɛ neɡre heyaa he tomɛ ba voɡ Baal waa lɔ Peɔ. Midian nomoa bihaah Kosbi ɡe dɔ seo a ɡɛ weechɔɡa la ta.”

english_verse: After the Lord had stopped the deadly disease from killing the Israelites, he said to Moses and Eleazar son of Aaron,
translation_verse: Weechɔɡa la habɔɔ, Korowii ŋɔ Mosis ne sɔfo Arɔn bibaa Eliasa be ŋɔ,

english_verse: “I want you to find out how many Israelites are in each family. Then make a list of every man
translation_verse: “Hé kure Israel deene la bwa ne ba naanar baala baa baa di bene fifraanɛ ne a habɔɔ dɛ́ won la laa la.”

english_verse: years and older, just as Moses and their ancestors had done when they left Egypt.
translation_verse: Juda dea nɛraa teŋa nɔ, Seela ne o dea nɛra, ne Pɛrɛs ne o dea nɛra, dɛ Sɛra ne o dea nɛra.

english_verse: Israel was now camped in the hills of Moab across the Jordan River from the town of Jericho. Moses and Eleazar told them
translation_verse: Anomanta, ɡɛ saŋ Mosis ne sɔfo Eliasa dɛ Israel tena la aa lɔ Moab harɛ waa chɔa kaa Jɔɔdan Moo ta asɛ Jeriko do o baŋ la, ba ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ,

english_verse: Pallu was the father of Eliab
translation_verse: Palu bibaa sɔne Eliab,

english_verse: and the grandfather of Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram. These are the same Dathan and Abiram who had been chosen by the people, but who followed Korah and rebelled against Moses, Aaron, and the Lord.
translation_verse: o bibaalaa Nemoɛl ne Datan dɛ Abiram. Gɛ Datan nɔ ne Abiram fa ɛ Israel tena sitɔɔla, dɛ ka teŋɛ Kora ne o nɛra nɛɛ dɛ ɛ deŋnekpeɡ Mosis ne Arɔn dɛ Korowii nɛ.

english_verse: That's when the Lord made the earth open up and swallow Dathan, Abiram, and Korah. At the same time, fire destroyed
translation_verse: A che a ta harɛ pere ba ne Kora jo o bini, asɛ nii fuh Kora nɛra lafraanɛ fifraanue a ɛ waa chɔ tɛ nɛra bá hweli.

english_verse: But the Korahite clan wasn't destroyed.
translation_verse: Kɛ Kora luɡe nɛra te ta serewɛ.

english_verse: None of the people that Moses and Aaron had counted in the Sinai Desert were still alive,
translation_verse: Banɔ la Mosis ne sɔfo Arɔn fa aa kur ba Sinai pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta la bwa serewɔ, beŋkpoŋ bɛlbwa ta kae.

english_verse: Aaron was the father of Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
translation_verse: Arɔn lolɛ bibaala banaarɛ, banee Nadab ne Abihu, ne Eliasa dɛ Itama.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Asɛ Korowii ŋɔ Mosis be ŋɔ,

english_verse: “Divide the land of Canaan among these tribes, according to the number of people in each one,
translation_verse: “Bɔne Keenan harɛ la tɛ deene la ɡɛ bɛlbwa nɛra kan aa doa, ó ɛ ba kon.

english_verse: The total number of Israelite men listed was
translation_verse: Israel baala bwa baa kur ba la lɔ kaɡboŋa lafraanumɛl dɛ beŋkpoŋ, lafraanuanɛ fifraatoro.

english_verse: I will show you what land to give each tribe, and they will receive as much land as they need, according to the number of people in it.”
translation_verse: Che bie tae la ta dɛ́ bɔne tɛɛ ba, deene aa kana ne anɔ la aa wola kanɛ la bwa.”

english_verse: The tribe of Levi included the clans of the Gershonites, Kohathites, Merarites,
translation_verse: Lewi dea nɛraa teŋa nɔ. Gɛsɔn ne o dea nɛra, ne Kohat ne o dea nɛra, dɛ Merari ne o dea nɛra.

english_verse: as well as the clans of Libni, Hebron, Mahli, Mushi, and Korah. Kohath the Levite was the father of Amram,
translation_verse: Banɔ ɡee ɛ Lewi dea nɛra. Libni ne o dea nɛra, ne Hɛbrɔn ne o dea nɛra, ne Maali ne o dea nɛra, ne Musi bibaala ne o dea nɛra, dɛ Kora bibaala ne o dea nɛra. Amram nabaalee Kohat.

english_verse: the husband of Levi's daughter Jochebed, who was born in Egypt. Amram and Jochebed's three children were Aaron, Moses, and Miriam.
translation_verse: Amram haah sɔne Jɔkɛbɛd, Lewi naa. Ijipt harɛ taa ba lolɔ. Amram ne Jɔkɛbɛd lolɛ bibaala banɛ, banee Arɔn ne Mosis, ba nimambiee Miriam.

english_verse: But Nadab and Abihu had died when they offered fire that was unacceptable to the Lord.
translation_verse: Nadab ne Abihu kpɔ nii aa wola chɛ kɛ bá kpɔ do kon baa ɛ saraha o ta dɛɛ tɛ Korowii ta dɛ serewe.

english_verse: Moses and Eleazar counted the Israelites while they were camped in the hills of Moab across the Jordan River from Jericho.
translation_verse: Banɔɔ Israel tena Mosis ne sɔfo Eliasa aa kura Moab harɛ waa chɔa kaa Jɔɔdan Moo nyoa Jeriko do baŋ bɛl la.

english_verse: except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun. The Lord had said that everyone else would die there in the desert.
translation_verse: Dɛ Korowii ŋɔ ɡɛ Israel tena la be ŋɔ pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ la taa baa ba serewa. Beŋkpoŋ bɛlbwa ta kae, nemenɛ Jefune bibaa Kaleb ne Nun bibaa Josua.

english_verse: One day his daughters went to the sacred tent, where they met with Moses, Eleazar, and some other leaders of Israel, as well as a large crowd of Israelites. The young women said:
translation_verse: Awola bɛl, haahna nɔ kpɔɔ ka bil Mosis ne sɔfo Eliasa ne Israel nomonome dɛ Israel tena la bwa sie, Korowii Dea Cheremibɔr doonyoa dɛ ŋɔ,

english_verse: You know that our father died in the desert. But it was for something he did wrong, not for joining with Korah in rebelling against the Lord. Our father left no sons
translation_verse: “Ya mɛɛ aa sewɛ pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ la ta la, o ta bibaala dɔe. O ta Kora ne o bala baa pɛ nyoa dɛ ɛ deŋnekpeɡ Korowii nɛɛ la bini jae. O wechɔɡa sewee o sewɛ.

english_verse: to carry on his family name. But why should his name die out for that reason? Give us some land like the rest of his relatives in our clan, so our father's name can live on.
translation_verse: Ɛrɛɛ waa ɡela ya mɛɛ sɔn he Israel tena bini nɔɔ? Waa wola bibaala dɔe waa kɛɛ? Tɛ yaa harɛ ɡɛ haa tɛ o lolanar baa le ya dea la, ásɛ ya mɛɛ sɔn bɛ he.”

english_verse: Moses asked the Lord what should be done,
translation_verse: Ate, Mosis kpɔ waa la ka bil Korowii sie,

english_verse: and the Lord answered:
translation_verse: asɛ Korowii ŋɔ o be ŋɔ,

english_verse: Zelophehad's daughters are right. They should each be given part of the land their father would have received.
translation_verse: “Waa Selofehad bihaahna aa bola la ɛ kasinteŋ. A chɛ kɛŋɔ hé tɛɛ ba harɛ la pera.

english_verse: If he has no daughter, his brothers will inherit the land.
translation_verse: Dɛ o ta bihaah dɔe yaa, bá kpɔ harɛ la tɛ o nimanar.

english_verse: But if he has no brothers, his father's brothers will inherit the land.
translation_verse: O ta nimanar ɡe dɔe yaa, bá kpɔ tɛ o mɛɛ nimanar.

english_verse: And if his father has no brothers, the land must be given to his nearest relative in the clan. This is my law, and the Israelites must obey it. Joshua Is Appointed Israel's Leader (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: O mɛɛ ta nimanar dɔe yaa, bá kpɔ tɛ o lole tenten ba dea la ta. Waa nɔɔ Korowii do Mosis a ɛ mmara dɛ chɔ le tɛ Israel tena.” Josua chiɡ Mosis naa ta

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “One day you will go up into the Abarim Mountains, and from there you will see the land I am giving the Israelites.
translation_verse: Awola bɛl, Korowii ŋɔ Mosis be ŋɔ, “Teeh kaa Abarim Bwejena dor, dɛ́ ka na harɛ maa kpɔa tɛ Israel tena.

english_verse: After you have seen it, you will die, just like your brother Aaron,
translation_verse: Dɛ he kaa na harɛ la tonaa, he ɡee sewɔɔ ka ja he nɛra nɛɛ ɡɛ aa pu he dɔɔ Arɔn la.

english_verse: because both of you disobeyed me at Meribah near the town of Kadesh in the Zin Desert. When the Israelites insulted me there, you didn't believe in my holy power.”
translation_verse: He ne o bwaa fa vɛh n wa, he ta waa maa do heya a ta la ta teŋɛ dɛ yarada kpeɡri maa dɔa la.” Gɛ saŋee Israel tena la ɛ deŋnekpeɡ Mɛreba waa bɛne Kades dɛ do Sin pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta la.

english_verse: “You are the Lord God, and you know what is in everyone's heart. So I ask you to appoint a leader for Israel.
translation_verse: “Korowii haa dɛ tɛ mkpa, mɔɔ haa kpo mɛ la, n poori le nɛn waa nyiŋi nɛra nɔ nɛ.

english_verse: Your people need someone to lead them into battle, or else they will be like sheep wandering around without a shepherd.”
translation_verse: Naate waa kpɔ ba kaa dɛ berɛ ba ba ne, ásɛ he nɛra bɛ ɛ kɛŋɔ peera aa wola teɡre dɔe.”

english_verse: The Lord answered, “Joshua son of Nun can do the job. Place your hands on him to show that he is the one to take your place.
translation_verse: Anee Korowii ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Kpɔ Nun bibaa Josua, onee N Doma so o nɛ. Kpɔ nɔn dawɛ o nɛɛ dɛ swee andɛɛɡa tɛo.

english_verse: Then go with him and tell him to stand in front of Eleazar the priest and the Israelites. Appoint Joshua as their new leader
translation_verse: Kpɔɔ ka che sɔfo Eliasa ne nɛra la bwa sie, ásɛ dɛ kpɔ toma la do o nɔn ta.

english_verse: and tell them they must now obey him, just as they obey you.
translation_verse: Tɛo kpeɡri haa dɔa la pera, ásɛ nɛra la bwa ɛɛ no o be.

english_verse: Moses followed the Lord's instructions and took Joshua to Eleazar and the people,
translation_verse: Mosis no Korowii waa la, dɛ kpɔ Josua la sɔfo Eliasa ne Israel tena la bwa baah ta.

english_verse: then he placed his hands on Joshua and appointed him Israel's leader.
translation_verse: Mosis ɡbabir kpɔ nɔɔra dawɛ o nɛɛ dɛ kpɔ toma la do o nɔn ta, ɡɛ Korowii aa ŋɔ o be la.

english_verse: and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the young rams.
translation_verse: Pebali anuanɛ la bɛlbwa ɡe, hé kpɔ men la kuruwa beŋkpoŋ ja a ta.

english_verse: and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the young rams. The smell of the smoke from these sacrifices will please me.
translation_verse: Pebali anuanɛ la bɛlbwa ɡe la, hé kpɔ men baa nama a kper kɛrɛdɛ kuruwa del koo ɔleve noo ta. A ɛ saraha baa dɛ fuah aa sɔɔh ɛɛ do som Korowii be.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Korowii ŋɔ Mosis be ŋɔ

english_verse: to say to the people of Israel: Offer sacrifices to me at the appointed times of worship, so that I will smell the smoke and be pleased.
translation_verse: ó bol Israel tena la be ŋɔ, “Hé kpɔ mea aa chɛ kɛ hé kpɔ ba ɛ saraha saŋ aa chɛa ta, dɛ́ fuah a sɔɔh do som Korowii be.

english_verse: Each day offer two rams a year old as sacrifices to please me. The animals must have nothing wrong with them;
translation_verse: Kwaa haa kpɔ ba ɛ saraha dɛ́ fuah dɛɛ tɛo tɔpere bɛlbwa laanee, pebali anɛ bɛlbwa aa di benanyoa waa wola kirihiah bɛlbwa dii.

english_verse: Along with each of them, one kilogram of your finest flour mixed with a liter of olive oil must be offered as a grain sacrifice.
translation_verse: Hé kpɔ men baa nama a kper kɛrɛdɛ kuruwa del, dɛ́ kpɔ ɔleve noo pɛrɛntoa beŋkpoŋ ne fah koo men la ta ba ɛ mea saraha.

english_verse: Finally, along with each of these two sacrifices, a liter of wine must be poured on the altar as a drink offering.
translation_verse: Hé kpɔ sen pɛrɛntoa beŋkpoŋ ne tama ne loɡla pebale la, dɛ́ ba fuɡe sen la ta saraha kon la ta, ásɛ a ɛ sen saraha.

english_verse: On the first day of each month, bring to the altar two bulls, one full-grown ram, and seven rams a year old that have nothing wrong with them. Then offer these as sacrifices to please me.
translation_verse: Korobie bɛlbwa tɔpeloɡle ta la, hé kpɔ nabali anɛ ne pebal dɛ pebali anuanɛ a bɛlbwa aa di benanyoa, aa wola kirihiah bɛlbwa dii ɛ saraha tɛ Korowii.

english_verse: Three kilograms of your finest flour mixed with olive oil must be offered with each bull as a grain sacrifice. Two kilograms of flour mixed with oil must be offered with the ram,
translation_verse: Hé kpɔ men baa nama a kper kɛrɛdɛ kuruware atoro, dɛ́ kpɔ koo ɔleve noo ta ne nabal beŋkpoŋ la ta, á ɛ mea saraha. Ásɛ dɛ kpɔ men kuruware anɛ ja pebal la ta.

english_verse: Celebrate Passover in honor of me on the fourteenth day of the first month of each year.
translation_verse: Korobie waa tɔ sie tɔpera fi dɛ anaarɛ la ɛ Galekaa Tɔpejen dɛ tɛ Korowii, a chɛ kɛŋɔ hé diu.

english_verse: The following day will begin the Festival of Thin Bread, which will last for a week. During this time you must honor me by eating bread made without yeast.
translation_verse: Korobie la tenten tɔpera fi dɛ anue la ɛ tɔpejen haa lɛ sie o ta. Hé di paanoo iisi aa wola toole a ta la tɔpera anuanɛ.

english_verse: On the first day of this festival, you must rest from your work and come together for worship.
translation_verse: Tɔpejen la tɔpeloɡle la, hé cheme dɛ́ tomɛ Korowii, dɛ bɛ toma bɛlbwa ɛ.

english_verse: Bring to the altar two bulls, one full-grown ram, and seven rams a year old that have nothing wrong with them. And then offer these as sacrifices to please me.
translation_verse: Hé kpɔ nabali anɛ ne pebal ne pebali anuanɛ, a bɛlbwa aa dɔ benanyoa aa wola kirihiah bɛlbwa dii ba ɛ saraha, dɛ́ fuah tɛ Korowii.

english_verse: Three kilograms of your finest flour mixed with olive oil must be offered with each bull as a grain sacrifice. Two kilograms of flour mixed with oil must be offered with the ram,
translation_verse: Nabal bɛlbwa la, hé kpɔ men baa nama a kper kɛrɛdɛ kuruware atoro koo ɔleve noo ta. Pebal la ɡe la, hé kpɔ men baa nama a kper kɛrɛdɛ kuruware anɛ.

english_verse: and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the young rams.
translation_verse: Pebali la bɛlbwa ɡe, hé kpɔ men baa nama a kper kɛrɛdɛ la kuruwa ja.

english_verse: All of these are to be offered each day of the festival in additional to the regular sacrifices, and the smoke from them will please me.
translation_verse: Tɔpera anuanɛ la ta la, hɛ́ɛ ɛ mea saraha la tɔpere bɛlbwa, ásɛ a sɔɔh ɛɛ do Korowii som. Hé ɛa dɛɛ ja saraha haa ɛa tɔpere bɛlbwa dɛɛ fuah la, ne sen saraha la ta.

english_verse: Then on the last day of the festival, you must once again rest from work and come together for worship. The Sacrifices during the Harvest Festival (Leviticus
translation_verse: Tɔpenuanɛ ta, hé cheme dɛ́ tomɛ Korowii, dɛ bɛ toma bɛlbwa ɛ. Koo Kondikwaa Koma Tɔpejen dii

english_verse: On the first day of the Harvest Festival, you must rest from your work, come together for worship, and bring a sacrifice of new grain.
translation_verse: Awola haa kpɔ mefala dɛɛ ba dɛ́ ba tɛ Korowii la, a ɡɛ Koo Kondikwaa Koma Tɔpejen la dii ta, hé cheme dɛ́ tomɛ Korowii dɛ bɛ toma bɛlbwa ɛ.

english_verse: Offer two young bulls, one full-grown ram, and seven rams a year old as sacrifices to please me.
translation_verse: Hé kpɔ nabali anɛ ne pebal ne pebali anuanɛ a bɛlbwa aa di benanyoa, aa wola kirihiah bɛlbwa dii ba ɛ saraha, dɛ́ fuah tɛ Korowii a sɔɔh ɛɛ do som o be.

english_verse: Three kilograms of your finest flour mixed with olive oil must be offered with each bull as a grain sacrifice. Two kilograms of flour mixed with oil must be offered with the ram,
translation_verse: Nabal bɛlbwa la, hé ɛ mea saraha dɛ́ kpɔ men baa nama a kper kɛrɛdɛ kuruware atoro dɛ́ koo ɔleve noo a ta. Pebal la ɡe, hé kpɔ men kuruware anɛ ja.

english_verse: Also offer a goat as a sacrifice for sin.
translation_verse: Dɛ́ kpɔ bombal beŋkpoŋ ja ɛ saraha soŋe he wechɔɡa.

english_verse: On the first day of the seventh month, you must rest from your work and come together to celebrate at the sound of the trumpets.
translation_verse: Mosis berɔ ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, “Korobinuanɛ tɔpeloɡle ta, hé cheme dɛ́ tomɛ Korowii dɛ bɛ toma bɛlbwa ɛ. Hé hoh bɛle awola.

english_verse: Three kilograms of your finest flour mixed with olive oil must be offered with the bull as a grain sacrifice. Two kilograms of flour mixed with oil must be offered with the ram,
translation_verse: Hé ɛ mea saraha men baa nama a kper kɛrɛdɛ ne. Nabale la, hé kpɔ men kuruware atoro dɛ́ kpɔ ɔleve noo koo a ta. Pebal la ɡe, hé kpɔ men kuruware anɛ ja.

english_verse: and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the young rams.
translation_verse: Ásɛ pebali anuanɛ la ɡe, hé kpɔ men kuruwa beŋkpoŋ ja a bɛlbwa ta,

english_verse: You must also offer a goat as a sacrifice for sin.
translation_verse: dɛ́ kpɔ bombal ja ɛ wechɔɡa kpɔe dɛ kɛ saraha soŋe he wechɔɡa Korowii be.

english_verse: These sacrifices will be made in addition to the regular daily sacrifices and the sacrifices for the first day of the month. The smoke from these sacrifices will please me. The Sacrifices on the Great Day of Forgiveness (Leviticus
translation_verse: A ɡɛ sarahare nɔ ja korobie bɛlbwa ne saŋ bɛlbwa sarahare, ne a mea sarahare ne sen sarahare ɡɛ waa baɡla la ta. Á ɛ sarahare haa fuah baa tɛ Korowii a sɔɔh ɛɛ do som o be. Wechɔɡa Soŋa Korowii Be Ó Kpɔ Kɛ Tɔpejen

english_verse: and bring to the altar one young bull, one full-grown ram, and seven rams a year old that have nothing wrong with them. Then offer these as sacrifices to please me.
translation_verse: Hé kpɔ saraha kwaa haa fuah a sɔɔh ɛɛ do Korowii som la ba tɛo. Nabale beŋkpoŋ ne pebal ne pebali anuanɛ aa dɔ benanyoa, aa wola kirihiah bɛlbwa dii.

english_verse: Three kilograms of your finest flour mixed with olive oil must be offered with the bull as a grain sacrifice. Two kilograms of flour mixed with oil must be offered with the ram,
translation_verse: Hé ɛ mea saraha men baa nama a kper kɛrɛdɛ ne. Nabale la, hé kpɔ men kuruware atoro, dɛ́ kpɔ ɔleve noo koo a ta. Pebal la ɡe, men kuruware anɛ.

english_verse: and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the young rams.
translation_verse: Pebali la ɡe, hé kpɔ men la kuruwa beŋkpoŋ ja bɛlbwa ta.

english_verse: A goat must also be sacrificed for the sins of the people. You will offer these sacrifices in addition to the sacrifice to ask forgiveness and the regular daily sacrifices. The Sacrifices during the Festival of Shelters (Leviticus
translation_verse: Hé kpɔ bombal beŋkpoŋ ja ɛ wechɔɡa kpɔe dɛ kɛ saraha, dɛ́ ja sen la ne saraha kwaa haa dɛ fuah saŋ bɛlbwa la ta. Kukure Tɔpejen dii

english_verse: Beginning on the fifteenth day of the seventh month and continuing for seven days, everyone must celebrate the Festival of Shelters in honor of me.
translation_verse: Korobinuanɛ tɔpera fi dɛ anue ta, hé cheme dɛ́ tomɛ Korowii dɛ bɛ toma bɛlbwa ɛ. Hé di Kukure Tɔpejen tɔpera anuanɛ dɛ́ lɛ he sie dɛ́ tɛ Korowii.

english_verse: Three kilograms of your finest flour mixed with olive oil must be offered with each bull as a grain sacrifice. Two kilograms of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the rams,
translation_verse: Hé ɛ mea saraha men baa nama a kper kɛrɛdɛ ne. Nabali fi dɛ atoro la bɛlbwa, hé kpɔ men baa nama a kper kɛrɛdɛ kuruware atoro, dɛ́ kpɔ ɔleve noo koo a ta. Pebal la bɛlbwa ɡe, men kuruware anɛ.

english_verse: and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the young rams.
translation_verse: Pebali fi dɛ anaarɛ la bɛlbwa, hé kpɔ men kuruwa beŋkpoŋ ja a ta.

english_verse: You must also offer a goat as a sacrifice for sin. These are to be offered in addition to the regular daily sacrifices.
translation_verse: Hé kpɔ bombal ja ɛ wechɔɡa kpɔe dɛ kɛ saraha, dɛ́ ja mea sarahare ne sen sarahare haa dɛ fuah saŋ bɛlbwa la ta.

english_verse: For the next six days of the festival, you will sacrifice one less bull than the day before, so that on the seventh day, seven bulls will be sacrificed. The other sacrifices and offerings must remain the same for each of these days.
translation_verse: Dɛ́ kpɔ bombal ja ɛ wechɔɡa kpɔe dɛ kɛ saraha ja mea saraha ne sen saraha haa dɛ fuah saŋ bɛlbwa la ta.

english_verse: On the eighth day, you must once again rest from your work and come together for worship.
translation_verse: Tɔpenuatoro la, hé cheme dɛ́ tomɛ Korowii dɛ bɛ toma bɛlbwa ɛ.

english_verse: Bring to the altar one bull, one full-grown ram, and seven rams a year old that have nothing wrong with them. Then offer these as sacrifices to please me.
translation_verse: Hé kpɔ nabale ne pebal dɛ pebali anuanɛ aa dɔ benanyoa aa wola kirihiah bɛlbwa dii ɛ saraha dɛ fuah tɛ Korowii, a sɔɔh do o som.

english_verse: You must also offer the proper grain sacrifices and drink offerings of wine with each animal.
translation_verse: Nao la ne pebal dɛ pebali la, hé kpɔ ɛ mea sarahare ne a sen sarahare ɡɛ waa baɡla la.

english_verse: And offer a goat as the sacrifice to ask forgiveness for the people. These sacrifices are made in addition to the regular daily sacrifices.
translation_verse: Dɛ́ kpɔ bombal ja ɛ wechɔɡa kpɔe dɛ kɛ saraha ja mea saraha ne sen saraha haa dɛ fuah saŋ bɛlbwa la ta.

english_verse: You must offer all these sacrifices to me at the appointed times of worship, together with any offerings that are voluntarily given or given because of a promise.
translation_verse: Ŋwɛnɛ haa kpɔ a ta dɛ ɛ saraha kwaa haa dɛ fuah, ne mea sarahare ne sen sarahare, dɛ deŋnesɔɔhna sarahare tɛ Korowii he tɔpejena haa lea cheɡ, dɛ́ɛ dia ta laanee la. He nyobaɡa kwaa haa ba a ne ne kwaa aa le he bambili ta bwa jao.”

english_verse: Moses told the people of Israel everything the Lord had told him about the sacrifices.
translation_verse: Mosis bol Israel tena la be waa Korowii aa doo a ta bwa.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses to say to Israel's tribal leaders:
translation_verse: Mosis ŋɔ nomonome baa chɔ Israel deene nyoo la be ŋɔ waa Korowii aa do ba a ta laanee nɔ.

english_verse: When one of you men makes a promise to the Lord, you must keep your word.
translation_verse: “Dɛ nomɛlbwa baɡɛ Korowii nyoa kɛɛ dɛ ŋwɛɛ ntam waane ta naa, o bɛ ɡel a chɔ. Ó ɛ wobɛlbwa waa ŋɔa wɛɛ ɛo la.

english_verse: Suppose a young woman who is still living with her parents makes a promise to the Lord.
translation_verse: Dɛ haah baɡɛ Korowii nyoa kɛɛ dɛ ŋwɛɛ ntam waane ta o toli saŋ waa lɔ o mɛɛ dem,

english_verse: If her father hears about it and says nothing, she must keep her promise.
translation_verse: asɛ o mɛɛ no o nyobaɡa la, kɛɛ ŋwɛɛra la, o ta wobɛlbwa bolaa, a ta chɔ le.

english_verse: But if he hears about it and objects, then she no longer has to keep her promise. The Lord will forgive her, because her father did not agree with the promise.
translation_verse: O mɛɛ noɔ dɛ kaoh waa, a ta chɛ kɛ haah la teŋɛ a ta kpa. Korowii ɛɛ kpɔɔ kɛo dɛkalkɛ o mɛɛ ta sɛɛh.

english_verse: Suppose a woman makes a promise to the Lord and then gets married. If her husband later hears about the promise but says nothing, she must do what she said, whether she meant it or not.
translation_verse: asɛ o jaa no dɛ tɔ nyoa o ta wobɛlbwa haah la be bolaa, amɔ te ntam kɛɛ nyoa waa baɡa dɛ kpɔ vɔrɔwe o te la ta chɔ le.

english_verse: But if her husband hears about the promise and objects, she no longer has to keep it, and the Lord will forgive her.
translation_verse: Dɛ o jaa noɔ dɛ kaoh ŋɔ o kpɔ nyobaɡa kwaa la la naa, o bɛ ɡel a chɔ. Korowii ɛɛ kpɔɔ kɛo.

english_verse: Widows and divorced women must keep every promise they make to the Lord.
translation_verse: Luhaah kɛɛ haah o ne o jaa aa vɛh dɔŋa, o ŋwɛɛ ntam kɛɛ dɛ baɡɛ nyoa la, a dawɛ o nɛ.

english_verse: Suppose a married woman makes a promise to the Lord.
translation_verse: Dɛ haah yalɔ asɛ dɛ ŋwɛɛ ntam kɛɛ dɛ baɡɛ nyoa dɛ le waane ta,

english_verse: If her husband hears about the promise and says nothing, she must do what she said.
translation_verse: asɛ o jaa no o ta o haah kaeh yaa, dɛ ntam kɛɛ nyobaɡa la ta chɔ le.

english_verse: But if he hears about the promise and does object, she no longer has to keep it. The Lord will forgive her, because her husband would not allow her to keep the promise.
translation_verse: Dɛ o jaa la noɔ dɛ kaoh ŋɔ ó kpɔ ntam kɛɛ nyobaɡa kwaa la la, kɛ a ta chɛ kɛ ó ɡel a chɔ aa, Korowii ɛɛ kpɔɔ kɛo, dɛkalkɛŋɔ o jaa kaoh.

english_verse: Her husband has the final say about any promises she makes to the Lord.
translation_verse: O jaaree dɔ kpeɡri kɛŋɔ ó sɛh kɛɛ dɛ vɛh nyobaɡa kɛɛ ntam haah la aa ŋwɛɛra la.

english_verse: If her husband hears about a promise and says nothing about it for a whole day, she must do what she said—since he did not object, the promise must be kept.
translation_verse: Dɛ o jaa la ta wobɛlbwa bolɛ awola waa noa kɛŋɔ o baɡɛ nyoa la aa, amɔ te dɛ o sɛh haah la ntam ne nyobaɡa waa kpɔa vɔrɔwe o te la. A waa o ta wobɛlbwa bolɛ la.

english_verse: But if he waits until the next day to stop her from keeping her promise, he is the one who must be punished.
translation_verse: O jaa la noɔ mɔɔ dɛ kaoh waa, amɔ te haah la wechɔɡa dawɛ o jaa la nɛ.”

english_verse: These are the laws that the Lord gave Moses about husbands and wives, and about young daughters who still live at home.
translation_verse: A ɡɛ Mmarare laanee Korowii do Mosis ŋɔ a chɔ le tɛ baa ne o haah, dɛ baa ne o bihaah o taa soɡe o mɛɛ dem.

english_verse: “Before you die, make sure that the Midianites are punished for what they did to Israel.”
translation_verse: “Tɛr Midian tena deŋne waa baa kpɔa ɛ Israel tena la wa. Ásɛ mɔɔ dɛ́ chɔ he banɔn ta.”

english_verse: Then Moses told the people, “The Lord wants to punish the Midianites. So tell our men to prepare for battle.
translation_verse: Asɛ Mosis ŋɔ Israel tena la be ŋɔ, “Hé vɔwɛ baala la bane ntoa, bá ka pu Midian tena yo, dɛ́ tɛr ba deŋne bɔ kem tɛ Korowii.

english_verse: Twelve thousand men were picked from the tribes of Israel, and after they were prepared for battle,
translation_verse: Anomanta, baala kaɡboŋa fi dɛ banɛɛ vɔwɛ ntoa, dɛ́ ka yo. Baala kaɡboŋii le Israel deene la bɛlbwa ta.

english_verse: Moses sent them off to war. Phinehas the son of Eleazar went with them and took along some things from the sacred tent and the trumpets for sounding the battle signal.
translation_verse: Mosis ɡelɔ ba kaa laa la, asɛ sɔfo Eliasa bibaa Fenehas kpɔ laala aa do ɡoroŋ la ane, ne bɛle ba hoh dɛɛ baɡle laa la wa.

english_verse: The Israelites fought against the Midianites, just as the Lord had commanded Moses. They killed all the men,
translation_verse: Ba kaa yo Midian tena ɡɛ Korowii aa do Mosis la, dɛ kpoo baala bwa.

english_verse: The Israelites captured every woman and child, then led away the Midianites' cattle and sheep, and took everything else that belonged to them.
translation_verse: Israel tena la lawɛ Midian haahna ne bechale, dɛ lawɛ ba nae ne peera, dɛ kpɔ ba laala ɡe bwa kaa kɛŋɔ laa ta kwa.

english_verse: They also burned down the Midianite towns and villages.
translation_verse: Ba fuh Midian tena bwɛɛre ne bela baa kaa baŋre ba tɛnte deene dɛ so la bwa.

english_verse: Israel's soldiers gathered together everything they had taken from the Midianites, including the captives and the animals.
translation_verse: Ba pa laala dɛ larawe nɛra ne kondɛɛra bwa laa la ta

english_verse: Then they returned to their own camp in the hills of Moab across the Jordan River from Jericho, where Moses, Eleazar, and the other Israelite leaders met the troops outside camp.
translation_verse: Mosis ne sɔfo Eliasa dɛ nomonome baa chɔ Israel tena nyoa la bwa kaa cheme laa tena la bela baa baa baŋre ba tɛnte deene dɛ so la dahare.

english_verse: and said, “I can't believe you let the women live!
translation_verse: O bɔɔ ba ŋɔ, “Kɛ he ɡel Midian haahna la te nyu kɛ ba kenɛ?

english_verse: You must put to death every boy and all the women who have ever had sex.
translation_verse: Hé kpoo bibaala la bwa dɛ́ kpo haah bɛlbwa waa chɔ baa ka,

english_verse: But do not kill the young women who have never had sex. You may keep them for yourselves.”
translation_verse: dɛ́ ɡel toli baa wola baala chɔe ka la tɛ he te.

english_verse: Then Moses said to the soldiers, “If you killed anyone or touched a dead body, you are unclean and have to stay outside the camp for seven days. On the third and seventh days, you must go through a ceremony to make yourselves and your captives clean.
translation_verse: He bini bɛlbwa waa kpo nɛn kɛɛ dɛ leɡe nɛn waa sewa la chɛ kɛŋɔ ó so tɛnte deene la dahare tɔpera anuanɛ. Tɔpetooro wee ne tɔpenuanɛ wee la, hé sɔ he ne nɛra haa laɡ ba laa ta la doŋa bwa ta.

english_verse: Then wash your clothes and anything made from animal skin, goat's hair, or wood.”
translation_verse: Hé laa doŋa kpɔ yale ne kwaa baa kpɔ oltɔn ne booh pona ne daa ɛa bɛlbwa ta.”

english_verse: Eleazar then explained, “If you need to purify something that won't burn, such as gold, silver, bronze, iron, tin, or lead, you must first place it in a hot fire.
