english_verse: Manoah from the tribe of Dan lived in the town of Zorah. His wife was not able to have children,
translation_verse: Dɛ baa bɛl sɔne Manoa dɛ le bwɛɛ Sora, dɛ do Dan dea tena harɛ ta. Dɛ o haah ɛ hambara.

english_verse: but one day an angel from the Lord appeared to her and said: You have never been able to have any children, but very soon you will be pregnant and have a son. He will belong to God from the day he is born, so his hair must never be cut. And even before he is born, you must not drink any wine or beer or eat any food forbidden by God's laws. Your son will begin to set Israel free from the Philistines.
translation_verse: He tea haa dɛ ba kpoŋa la, bibaalee hɛɛ ba lola. Dɛ́ɛ berɛ o nyu fona bwa, dɛkalkɛ Korowii ɛɛ leo cheɡ ó ɛ Nasiri te dɛ́ le o lola saŋ bwa. Onee dɛɛ ba mun pae dɛ́ lɛ Israel tena le Filisti tena nɔn ta.”

english_verse: She went to Manoah and said, “A prophet who looked like an angel of God came and talked to me. I was so frightened, that I didn't even ask where he was from. He didn't tell me his name,
translation_verse: Asɛ haah la la o jaa be ka ŋɔ, “Korowii nɛn bɛl ba n be. O le Korowii nyundua torome, o ɔma kɛrɛdɛ. N ta on bɔɔrɛ bela waa lea, o ta men o sɔn ɡe baɡlɛ.

english_verse: but he did say that I'm going to have a baby boy. I'm not supposed to drink any wine or beer or eat any food forbidden by God's laws. Our son will belong to God for as long as he lives.”
translation_verse: O ŋɔ n be ŋɔ mɛɛ kpoŋe tea dɛ lolɛ bibaa. Anomanta, n bɛ seŋkpeɡa bɛlbwa nyɔ, kɛɛ dɛ di kii kon bɛlbwa, dɛkalkɛ Korowii le bie la cheɡ o lola saŋ bwa, ó ɛ Nasiri te ka tel o serewe wee.”

english_verse: Then Manoah prayed, “Our Lord, please send that prophet again and let him tell us what to do for the son we are going to have.”
translation_verse: Asɛ Manoa soŋe Korowii ŋɔ, “N Naa Korowii, n dɛ soŋe, ɡel he torome la ba ya be ja dɛ́ ba baɡle yaa ŋwɛnɛ yaa kpɔ o ta nyiŋi bie yaa dɛ́ ba o lola nɔ.”

english_verse: God answered Manoah's prayer, and the angel went back to Manoah's wife while she was resting in the fields. Manoah wasn't there at the time,
translation_verse: Korowii no Manoa wesoŋa la asɛ dɛ ɡel o nyundua torome ba haah la be ja, dɛ haah la lɔ kpɔɡ bini ɡɛ saŋ, dɛ o jaa ta o nɛɛ jae.

english_verse: so she found him and said, “That same man is here again! He's the one I saw the other day.”
translation_verse: Haah la ɛ warane dɛ ka ŋɔ o jaa be ŋɔ, “Baa la waa ba n be awola la balɔ ja!”

english_verse: Manoah went with his wife and asked the man, “Are you the one who spoke to my wife?” “Yes, I am,” he answered.
translation_verse: Ate, Manoa ir dɛ teŋɛ o haah nɛɛ ba kaa. Waa la baa la be la, o ŋɔ, “Henee bol waane n haah be la aa?” Anee baa la ŋɔ, “Menee.”

english_verse: Manoah then asked, “When your promise comes true, what rules must he obey and what will be his work?”
translation_verse: Belaa Manoa ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Dɛ he waa nɔ baa ɛ kpela aa, ɛrɛɛ bie la nyiŋa bini ne o toma ɛɛ bini ɛɛ ba doe yɔ?”

english_verse: “Your wife must be careful to do everything I told her,” the Lord's angel answered.
translation_verse: Korowii nyundua torome la ŋɔ, “A chɛ kɛ he haah ɛ ɡɛ bwa maa bol o be la.

english_verse: “She must not eat or drink anything made from grapes. She must not drink wine or beer or eat anything forbidden by God's laws. I told her exactly what to do.”
translation_verse: O bɛ ɡrepo nɔn komɛlbwa di, á ba ɛ kɛŋɔ wɛɛ nyɔ seŋkpeɡa bɛlbwa kɛɛ wɛɛ di kii konee. A chɛ kɛ ó ɛ anɔ la bwa maa doo la.”

english_verse: “Please,” Manoah said, “stay here with us for just a little while, and we'll fix a young goat for you to eat.”
translation_verse: Manoa ŋɔ Korowii nyundua torome la be ŋɔ, “Ya dɛ nyin kɛ he so ka tel kɛ yaa kpo bombie bɛl tɛɛ.”

english_verse: Manoah didn't realize that he was really talking to one of the Lord's angels. The angel answered, “I can stay for a little while, although I won't eat any of your food. But if you would like to offer the goat as a sacrifice to the Lord, that would be fine.”
translation_verse: O chaŋ ba ŋɔ, “Hé laɡ mɛ so ɡɛ bɛlbwa kwaraa naa, maa kondikwaa di. Dɛ hɛɛ fuh kwaa ɛ sarahaa te naa, hé ɛ tɛ Korowii.” Dɛ Manoa ta jemɛ kɛ Korowii nyundua toromee on.

english_verse: Manoah said, “Tell us your name, so we can honor you after our son is born.”
translation_verse: Manoa berɔ bɔɔro ja ŋɔ, “He sɔne ɛrɔɔ? Gɛ aa ɛ dɛ he waa haa bola nɔ baa ɛ kpela aa, yá tɛɛ duure.”

english_verse: “No,” the angel replied. “You don't need to know my name. And if you did, you couldn't understand it.”
translation_verse: Korowii nyundua torome la ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ hɛɛ bɔɔ mɛ n sɔn nɔɔ? A mun noe ɡwaa he liire ta.”

english_verse: So Manoah took a young goat over to a large rock he had chosen for an altar, and he built a fire on the rock. Then he killed the goat, and offered it with some grain as a sacrifice to the Lord. But then an amazing thing happened.
translation_verse: Asɛ Manoa kpo bombie dɛ kpɔ mea ja ɛ saraha tɛ Korowii bwetal bɛl ta. Korowii ɛ nyokpowaa Manoa ne o haah siwi ta bela.

english_verse: The fire blazed up toward the sky, and the Lord's angel went up toward heaven in the fire. Manoah and his wife bowed down low when they saw what happened.
translation_verse: Ninlao le kon baa dɛ ɛ saraha o ta la ta, dɛ hɔ dɛɛ kaa nyundua, asɛ Korowii nyundua torome la kpɔ ninlao la bini kaa nyundua. Manoa ne o haah aa na ɡɛ waa nɔ la, ba cholo dɛ kpɔ sie pi harɛ.

english_verse: Although the angel didn't appear to them again, they realized he was one of the Lord's angels.
translation_verse: Baa wola on nae kpa la, Manoa ne o haah jemɛ kɛŋɔ Korowii nyundua toromee kpela.

english_verse: Manoah said, “We have seen an angel. Now we're going to die.”
translation_verse: Manoa ŋɔ o haah be ŋɔ, “Serewaa yaa ba serewa, dɛkalkɛ ya na Korowii.”

english_verse: “The Lord isn't going to kill us,” Manoah's wife responded. “The Lord accepted our sacrifice and grain offering, and he let us see something amazing. Besides, he told us that we're going to have a son.”
translation_verse: Haah la ŋɔ o jaa be ŋɔ, “Korowii dɛ nyin ya kpoe yaa, o fe ta kwaa yaa fuah ɛ saraha nɔ ne mea nɔ lɛɛ. O fe ta ɡelɛ ya na nyokpowaa nɔ bwa, dɛ berɛ ŋɔ waa nɔ ya be nɔ.”

english_verse: Later, Manoah's wife did give birth to a son, and she named him Samson. As the boy grew, the Lord blessed him.
translation_verse: Haah la aa dɛ ba lola la, bibaalee o lolɛ, asɛ ba pa o sɔn Samsen. O kpeɡo asɛ Korowii sweero andɛɛɡa.

english_verse: Then, while Samson was staying at Dan's Camp between the towns of Zorah and Eshtaol, the Spirit of the Lord took control of him.
translation_verse: Korowii Doma ɡe baa so o nɛ, dɛ pa mun kpɔɔ dɛɛ ɛ toma ɡɛ saŋ waa lɔ bwɛɛ Mahane Dan, o lɔ Sora ne Ɛstaol baah ta.

english_verse: One day, Samson went to Timnah, where he saw a Philistine woman.
translation_verse: Awola bɛl, Samsen iro dɛ la Temna, dɛ ka na Filisti tolo bɛl.

english_verse: When he got back home, he told his parents, “I saw a Philistine woman in Timnah, and I want to marry her. Get her for me!”
translation_verse: Waa bera ba dem la, o ŋɔ o nya ne o mɛɛ be ŋɔ, “Maa la Temna la, n na Filisti tolo bɛl n sie lɛ o nɛ. N dɛ nyin kɛ hé ka moo tɛ mɛ.”

english_verse: His parents answered, “There are a lot of women in our clan and even more in the rest of Israel. Those Philistines are pagans. Why would you want to marry one of their women?” “She looks good to me,” Samson answered. “Get her for me!”
translation_verse: Anee ba chaŋo ŋɔ, “Haahna toole ya dea kɛɛ ya Israel tena bini hɛɛ la ka mo haah Filisti tena voɡtoroma nɔ bini naa?” Asɛ o ŋɔ o mɛɛ be ŋɔ, “Onee n bambile lawɛ, nyinu tɛ mɛ.”

english_verse: At that time, the Philistines were in control of Israel, and the Lord wanted to stir up trouble for them. That's why he made Samson desire that woman.
translation_verse: O mɛɛ ne o nya ta wone jemɛ kɛ Korowii bee a le wɛɛ nyin ŋwɛnɛ waa kpɔ o ta Samsen won ka yo Filisti tena. Gɛ saŋ dɛ banee dɛɛ nyiŋi Israel tena nɛ.

english_verse: As Samson and his parents reached the vineyards near Timnah, a fierce young lion suddenly roared and attacked Samson.
translation_verse: Samsen ne o nya ne o mɛɛ bwa pɛo la Temna. Baa dɛ tel bwɛɛ la daa kooni ta la, buɡ la ta, nyujente bie den le dɛ kɔɡre dɛɛ ba o be.

english_verse: But the Lord's Spirit took control of Samson, and with his bare hands he tore the lion apart, as though it had been a young goat. His parents didn't know what he had done, and he didn't tell them.
translation_verse: Korowii Doma den ba so Samsen nɛɛ kerabeŋkpoŋ dɛ tɛo kpeɡri, asɛ o lawɛ nyujente la dɛ kpɔ nɔn toɡru kɛŋɔ bombie ken. O ta o nya ne o mɛɛ be ɡɛ waa ɛa la bolɛ.

english_verse: When they got to Timnah, Samson talked to the woman, and he was sure that she was the one for him.
translation_verse: Samsen aa la Temna la, o kaa bol waa haah la be, o pɛla lawɔ.

english_verse: Later, Samson returned to Timnah for the wedding. And when he came near the place where the lion had attacked, he left the road to see what was left of the lion. He was surprised to see that bees were living in the lion's skeleton, and that they had made some honey.
translation_verse: Aa dɛ la sie la, o berɔ la ŋɔ ó ka nyin haah la, dɛ ka bɛɡɛ jo bela waa kpo nyujente la, dɛ na kɛ toohna aa do noo nyujente la lale ta.

english_verse: He scooped up the honey in his hands and ate some of it as he walked along. When he got back to his parents, he gave them some of the honey, and they ate it too. But he didn't tell them he had found the honey in the skeleton of a lion.
translation_verse: O kwɛɛ tohnoo la do o nɔɔra ta dɛ di dɛɛ kaa. Waa la o nya ne o mɛɛ be la, o tɛɛ ba ane ba di, kɛ o ta ba be bolɛ ŋɔ nyujente lale la taa o le a ne.

english_verse: While Samson's father went to make the final arrangements with the bride and her family, Samson threw a big party, as grooms usually did.
translation_verse: O mɛɛ laŋɔ ka na haah la. Samsen ɡelɔ ba ɛ kondikonjena ɡɛ hanfale jaa bɛlbwa aa dɛ ɛ la.

english_verse: When the Philistines saw what Samson was like, they told
translation_verse: Baa na Samsen la, ba tɛo bonɔɔna fifraatoro ba so o jwɛh.

english_verse: But if you can't tell me the answer, then each of you will have to give me a shirt and a full change of clothing.” “It's a bet!” the Philistines said. “Tell us the riddle.”
translation_verse: Dɛ he baɡ mɛ kahonɛ ɡe aa, mɛɛ lɛ heya yapondɛɛɡa fifraatoro ne yabele fifraatoroo.” Anee ba ŋɔ, “Bol waa la ya no.”

english_verse: Samson said: Once so strong and mighty— now so sweet and tasty! Three days went by, and the Philistine young men had not come up with the right answer.
translation_verse: Anee o ŋɔ, “Didii bee kondikwaa le, bokpeɡa te bee kontora do.” Tɔpera atoro bwa dɛ ba ta wone baɡle ɡɛ waa la mun.

english_verse: Finally, on the seventh day of the party they went to Samson's bride and said, “You had better trick your husband into telling you the answer to his riddle. Have you invited us here just to rob us? If you don't find out the answer, we will burn you and your family to death.”
translation_verse: Tɔpenaarɛ wee la, ba ŋɔ Samsen haah la be ŋɔ, “Yeraa he yerɛ yaa dɛ́ ba ŋwɛ yaa kɛɛ? Ta he jaa baradeɛ ó baɡle yaa waa nɔ mun. Gɛ la aa, yaa fuh he ne he mɛɛ dem tena bwaa.”

english_verse: Samson's bride went to him and started crying in his arms. “You must really hate me,” she sobbed. “If you loved me at all, you would have told me the answer to your riddle.” “But I haven't even told my parents the answer!” Samson replied. “Why should I tell you?”
translation_verse: Samsen haah la kpɔ wii la o be ka ŋɔ, “He hah mɛ, haa men nyin. He tɛ n nɛra wobobeele kɛ he ta men a mun baɡlɛ.” Anee o ŋɔ, “N ta n nya ne n mɛɛ ɡba baɡlɛ. Ɛrɛ waa mɛɛ baɡle he te nɔ?”

english_verse: For the entire seven days of the party, she had been whining and trying to get the answer from him. But that seventh day she put so much pressure on Samson that he finally gave in and told her the answer. She went straight to the young men and told them.
translation_verse: O wio tɔpera anuanɛ baa kpɔa dɛɛ ɛ hanfalwaa la bwa. Waa teŋa dɛɛ pɛɛro la, o sɛh dɛ baɡlo a mun tɔpenuanɛ wee la ta. Asɛ o ɡe ka bol o nɛra la be.

english_verse: Before sunset that day, the men of the town went to Samson with this answer: A lion is the strongest— honey is the sweetest! Samson replied, This answer you have given me doubtless came from my bride-to-be.
translation_verse: Wee aa dɛ ba joe la, nɛra la baɡle Samsen waa la mun ŋɔ, “Tohnoo som ɡwaa komɛlbwa. Nyujente bwara kpeɡri ɡwaa komɛlbwa.” Anee Samsen chaŋe ŋɔ, “N haah laa baɡle heya aa, he fe aa won jemɛ waa nɔ mun.”

english_verse: The father of the bride made Samson's wife marry one of the
translation_verse: Haah la mɛɛ berɔ kpɔ Samsen haah la tɛ o dam tɛnte waa soɡe o jwɛh hanfalkondikwaa la mun la.

english_verse: “When you left the way you did, I thought you were divorcing her. So I arranged for her to marry one of the young men who were at your party. But my younger daughter is even prettier, and you can have her as your wife.”
translation_verse: Haah la mɛɛ ŋɔ, “N ken ŋɔ he vɛoh, haa on nyin kpa. N kpɔɔ tɛ he daamanar baa ba he hanfalkondikwa mun la bɛl. O dɔ nime bɛl o do wer ɡwaalo kwara, amɔ kpɔɔ chiɡ o naa ta.”

english_verse: “This time,” Samson answered, “I have a good reason for really hurting some Philistines.” Samson Takes Revenge
translation_verse: Anee Samsen ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, “Taraken te n dɔ ŋwɛnɛ ń so Filisti tena nɛ, mɛɛ ɛɛ ba tomaa kɛrɛdɛ.”

english_verse: Then Samson took the foxes into the Philistine wheat fields that were ready to be harvested. He set the rags on fire and let the foxes go. The wheat fields went up in flames, and so did the stacks of wheat that had already been cut. Even the Philistine vineyards and olive orchards burned.
translation_verse: O choŋi nii do kapɛle la ta dɛ ɡel kalampoŋare la ta Filisti tena mea a taa cheɡɛ kooni ta, dɛ fuh mea ne daa kooni la bwa.

english_verse: Some of the Philistines started asking around, “Who could have done such a thing?” “It was Samson,” someone told them. “He married the daughter of that man in Timnah, but then the man gave Samson's wife to one of the men at the wedding.” The Philistine leaders went to Timnah and burned to death Samson's wife and her father.
translation_verse: Filisti tena la bɔɔrɔ ŋɔ, “Amɔ umee ɛ ken ɔ?” Asɛ ba bol ba be ŋɔ, “Samsen o helabaa aa ɛ Temna te laanee. O hela lɛ o haah la tɛ o dam bɛl.” Anomanta, Filisti tena la kaa fuh tolo la ne o mɛɛ bwa.

english_verse: When Samson found out what they had done, he went to them and said, “You killed them! And I won't rest until I get even with you.”
translation_verse: Anee Samsen ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, “Waa haa ɛa nɔ nomanta, maa ɡela ba, ka tel kɛŋɔ maa tɔ n wel he nɛ.”

english_verse: Then Samson started hacking them to pieces with his sword. Samson left Philistia and went to live in the cave at Etam Rock.
translation_verse: O kaa yoo ba sibeɡra ne dɛ kpoo ba ɡalɡa, dɛ ka so bwe Etam bɔɔ bini.

english_verse: But it wasn't long before the Philistines invaded Judah and set up a huge army camp at Jawbone.
translation_verse: Filisti laa tena kaa baŋre ba tɛnte deene Juda dea harɛ ta, dɛ ka yo bwɛɛ bɛl waa bɛne ba baa yerɔ Lehi.

english_verse: The people of Judah asked, “Why have you invaded our land?” The Philistines answered, “We've come to get Samson. We're going to do the same things to him that he did to our people.”
translation_verse: Asɛ Juda harɛ ta baala bɔɔ ba ŋɔ, “Bɔkwa waa hɛɛ ba ba yo yaa nɔɔ?” Anee ba ŋɔ, “Samsenee yaa ba bá lawɛ, dɛ́ ka ɛo ɡɛ waa ɛ yaa la bɔ kem.”

english_verse: Three thousand men from Judah went to the cave at Etam Rock and said to Samson, “Don't you know that the Philistines rule us, and they will punish us for what you did?” “I was only getting even with them,” Samson replied. “They did the same things to me first.”
translation_verse: Ate, Juda harɛ baala kaɡboŋa batoro la Samsen be Etam bwebɔɔ la bɔr dɛ ka ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Haa jemɛ kɛŋɔ Filisti tenaa dɛɛ di kpeɡri ya nɛɛ kɛɛ? Ɛrɛɛ he ɛ yaa ken nɔɔ?” Anee o chaŋ ba ŋɔ, “Gɛ baa ɛɛ mɛ la, ɡɛ ɡboo n ɡe ka ɛɛ ba.”

english_verse: “We came here to tie you up and turn you over to them,” said the men of Judah. “I won't put up a fight,” Samson answered, “but you have to promise not to hurt me yourselves.”
translation_verse: Ba ɡe ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Ya balɔ dɛ́ ba vɔrɔwe, dɛ́ kpɔe ka do Filisti tena nɔn ta.” Ate, Samsen ɡe ŋɔ, “Hé ŋwɛɛ baɡ mɛ kɛŋɔ he ɡbaɡba aa men kpo.”

english_verse: “We promise,” the men said. “We will only tie you up and turn you over to the Philistines. We won't kill you.” Then they tied up his hands and arms with two brand-new ropes and led him away from Etam Rock. When the Philistines saw that Samson was being brought to their camp at Jawbone, they started shouting and ran toward him. But the Lord's Spirit took control of Samson, and Samson broke the ropes, as though they were pieces of burnt cloth.
translation_verse: Waa dɛ bɛne Lehi la, Filisti tena la ɛɛ moo dɛ kpɔ sie pa o be dɛɛ ba. Buɡ la ta, Korowii Doma ba so o nɛ dɛ tɛo kpeɡri kohona. Asɛ ŋwɛɛra baa kpɔa vɔrɔwo la ɛ kɛŋɔ kwaa baa fuah ken dɛ le o nɔɔra ta.

english_verse: Samson tossed the jawbone on the ground and decided to call the place Jawbone Hill. It is still called that today.
translation_verse: Waa bol ɡɛ waa nɔ tonɛ la, o kpɔ keeɡo kaŋe hoɡ la viɡri, asɛ ba pa bela sɔn Ramat Lehi.

english_verse: Samson was so thirsty that he prayed, “Our Lord, you helped me win a battle against a whole army. Please don't let me die of thirst now. Those heathen Philistines will carry off my dead body.”
translation_verse: Dɛ nyɔɡre dɛ kpoo kohona, anomanta, o wio no Korowii ŋɔ, “N Naa Korowii, henee tɛ men maa ɛ he bonɔɔ kpeɡri n won ɛ wejena nɔ dɔŋ dɛ pɔ n dɔma nɛ, asɛ nyɔɡre ɛɛ kpo mɛ. Ń sewɛ voɡtoroma nɔ nɔn ta naa?”

english_verse: Samson was tired and weary, but God sent water gushing from a rock. Samson drank some and felt strong again. Samson named the place Caller Spring, because he had called out to God for help. The spring is still there at Jawbone.
translation_verse: Asɛ Korowii ɡel bɔɔ bɛl pili Lehi, asɛ nee le o bini. Samsen aa nyɔa la, o bwara berɔ ir o dɔ bokpeɡfala ja. Anomanta, ba pa bela nee aa bula le la sɔn Ɛn Hakore. O ta chɔ Lehi ba le fini.

english_verse: years, but the Philistines were still the rulers of Israel.
translation_verse: Samsen tɔ Israel tena sie bene fifraanɛ ɡɛ saŋ Filisti tena aa dɛ di kpeɡri ba nɛɛ la.

english_verse: The people who lived in Gaza found out he was there, and they decided to kill him at sunrise. So they went to the city gate and waited all night in the guardrooms on each side of the gate.
translation_verse: Asɛ nɛra bol bwɛɛ la tena be ŋɔ, “Samsen ba bonɔ!” Anomanta, ba bar bwɛɛ la cheme jwaana la ne dɛɛ kpao bwɛɛ la doonyoa. Ba ta bela leɛ jwaana la ne bwa dɛɛ bol ŋɔ, “Bɔr chaahna binii yaa ba o dɔe dɛ́ kpoo.”

english_verse: Some time later, Samson fell in love with a woman named Delilah, who lived in Sorek Valley.
translation_verse: A habɔɔ la, o pɛla lawɛ haah bɛl baa dɛ yerɔ Delaela. O soɡe fɛlembɔjen bɛl baa dɛ yerɔ Sorek bini.

english_verse: The Philistine rulers went to Delilah and said, “Trick Samson into telling you what makes him so strong and what can make him weak. Then we can tie him up so he can't get away. If you find out his secret, we will each give you
translation_verse: Filisti nomonome la la haah la be ŋɔ, “Takapɔ dɛ tao baradeɛre, ásɛ o baɡle o bokpeɡa kohona waa dɔa nɔ mun, ne ɡɛ yaa dɛ ba wona pɔ o nɛɛ dɛ́ won vɔrɔwo o sɔɔh. Ya bini bɛlbwa fe ɛɛ tɛɛ suuɡapoŋa kaɡboŋ dɛ lafaa.”

english_verse: The next time Samson was at Delilah's house, she asked, “Samson, what makes you so strong? How can I tie you up so you can't get away? Come on, you can tell me.”
translation_verse: Anomanta, Delaela ŋɔ Samsen be ŋɔ, “Baɡ mɛ he bokpeɡa kohona haa dɔa nɔ mun, ne ŋwɛnɛ yaa kpɔ o ta dɛ́ won vɔrɔwe he sɔɔh.”

english_verse: Samson answered, “If someone ties me up with seven new bowstrings that have never been dried, it will make me just as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: Anee Samsen chaŋo ŋɔ, “Dɛ nomɛlbwa kpɔ ol tɔnlwɛɛ ŋwɛɛra bele anuanɛ aa wola holɛ vɔɡ mɛ naa, mɛɛ ɡwɛɡroo dɛ do kɛ baa bɛlbwa aa doa.”

english_verse: The Philistine rulers gave seven new bowstrings to Delilah. They also told some of their soldiers to go to Delilah's house and hide in the room where Samson and Delilah were. If the bowstrings made Samson weak, they would be able to capture him. Delilah tied up Samson with the bowstrings and shouted, “Samson, the Philistines are attacking!” Samson snapped the bowstrings, as though they were pieces of scorched string. The Philistines had not found out why Samson was so strong.
translation_verse: Dɛ baala bane sɔh o be dea, asɛ o yerɔ takpeɡ ne ŋɔ, “Samsen, Filisti tena dɛ ba he nɛ!” O chaa ol tɔn ŋwɛɛra la kɛŋɔ jise baa choŋi nii leɡo ken. Anomanta, ba ta wone jemɛ o bokpeɡa waa dɔa la mun.

english_verse: “You lied and made me look like a fool,” Delilah said. “Now tell me. How can I really tie you up?”
translation_verse: Delaela ŋɔ Samsen be ŋɔ, “Gɛnee men hɛɛ neɡ mɛ naa? Name te, chaɡ mɛ ɡɛ baa ɛ dɛ́ won vɔrɔwe.”

english_verse: Samson answered, “Use some new ropes. If I'm tied up with ropes that have never been used, I'll be just as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: Samsen ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Dɛ ba vɔɡ mɛ kɛrɛdɛ ŋwɛnfala baa wola a ne wobɛlbwa ɛɛ mɔɔ ne naa, mɛɛ ɡwɛɡroo dɛ́ do kɛ baa bɛlbwa aa doa.”

english_verse: Delilah got new ropes, and again some Philistines hid in the room. Then she tied up Samson's arms and shouted, “Samson, the Philistines are attacking!” Samson snapped the ropes as if they were threads.
translation_verse: Anomanta, Delaela kpɔ ŋwɛnfala ba vɔrɔwo, dɛ baala bane sɔh dea. O yerɔ takpeɡ ne ŋɔ, “Samsen, Filisti tena dɛ ba he nɛ!” O berɔ chaa ŋwɛɛra la kɛŋɔ jise ken.

english_verse: “You're still lying and making a fool of me,” Delilah said. “Tell me how I can tie you up!” “My hair is in seven braids,” Samson replied. “If you weave my braids into the threads on a loom and nail the loom to a wall, then I will be as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: Delaela berɔ ŋɔ o be ja ŋɔ, “He kpɔ mɛ ɛ ɡɛne dɛ ba le saŋ nɔ dɛ ta na dɛɛ neɡ mɛ. Name te, den chaɡ mɛ ɡɛ baa vɔrɔwe.” Anee o chaŋo ŋɔ, “Dɛ he kpɔ n nyumpona baa pɛra anuanɛ dɛ do kokorowa kon ta dɛ sɔh pɛ, dɛ kpɔ dajeɡa la hama aa, mɛɛ ɡwɛɡroo dɛ́ do kɛ baa bɛlbwa aa doa.” Anomanta, waa baa chɔ dom la, Delaela ɛ ɡɛ. O lawɛ o nyumpona baa pɛra anuanɛ la dɛ sɔah ja jisere la ta, dɛ kpɔ dajeɡa la hama kiŋkiŋ ken.

english_verse: While Samson was asleep, Delilah wove his braids into the threads on a loom and nailed the loom to a wall. Then she shouted, “Samson, the Philistines are attacking!” Samson woke up and pulled the loom free from its posts in the ground and from the nails in the wall. Then he pulled his hair free from the woven cloth.
translation_verse: O yerɔ takpeɡ ne ja ŋɔ, “Samsen, Filisti tena la dɛ ba he nɛ!” O ir dom ta dɛ tɛr dajeɡa la ne kokorowa kon ne jisere la bwa le.

english_verse: “Samson,” Delilah said, “you claim to love me, but you don't mean it! You've made me look like a fool three times now, and you still haven't told me why you are so strong.”
translation_verse: Anee o ŋɔ Samsen be ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ he ŋɔ he dɛ nyin mɛ, dɛ haa he tea bini waa n be bol nɔɔ? Tooro tenaa he ta na dɛɛ ɛɛ mɛ ɡɛne, haa wola men he bokpeɡa haa dɔa kohona nɔ mun baɡlɛ la.”

english_verse: Delilah started nagging and pestering him day after day, until he couldn't stand it any longer.
translation_verse: Tɔpere bɛlbwaa haah la teŋɛ dɛɛ bɔɔro, a ba le o mee.

english_verse: Finally, Samson told her the truth. “I have belonged to God ever since I was born, so my hair has never been cut. If it were ever cut off, my strength would leave me, and I would be as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: Anomanta, Samsen bol o tea bini waa bwa chaɡlo ŋɔ, “Ba ta fon kpɔe fonɛ n nyu bwa. Nasiri tee men. Korowii lee mɛ cheɡ tɛ o te, dɛ le n lola saŋ bwa. Ba fonɛ n nyu aa, n bokpeɡa maa dɔa nɔ bwa dɛ ba tona n ɡwɛɡre kɛ baa bɛlbwa ken.”

english_verse: Delilah realized that he was telling the truth. So she sent someone to tell the Philistine rulers, “Come to my house one more time. Samson has finally told me the truth.” The Philistine rulers went to Delilah's house, and they brought along the silver they had promised her.
translation_verse: Delaela nao kɛŋɔ o bol o kasinteŋ bwa baɡlo, anomanta, o tomɛ nɛra ba ka ŋɔ Filisti tena nomonome la be ŋɔ, “Name te hé den ba kerabeŋkpoŋ. O baɡ mɛ o kasinteŋ bwa.” A ɡelɔ anɔ te, ba kpoŋe suuɡapoŋa la dɛ la.

english_verse: Delilah had lulled Samson to sleep with his head resting in her lap. She signaled to one of the Philistine men as she began cutting off Samson's seven braids. And by the time she was finished, Samson's strength was gone. Delilah tied him up
translation_verse: Haah la ɡbɛɡbɛ Samsen o chɔ dom dawɛ o nakpale ta. Asɛ o yerɛ baa bɛl o ba fonɛ o nyumpona baa pɛra anuanɛ la. Belaa o pa mun ɡwɛɡre, o bokpeɡa la bwa tonɛ.

english_verse: The Philistines grabbed Samson and poked out his eyes. They took him to the prison in Gaza and chained him up. Then they put him to work, turning a millstone to grind grain.
translation_verse: Filisti tena la lawɔ, dɛ foromi o sibie dɛ kaa o ne Gasa. Ba doo ayaawa jɔɡrɔre dɛ doo dea, dɛ ɡel wɛɛ namɛ kwa.

english_verse: But they didn't cut his hair any more, so it started growing back.
translation_verse: Baa fonɛ o nyu la habɔɔ, o nyumpona berɔ pa mun dɛɛ moɡɛ ja. Samsen seo

english_verse: The Philistine rulers threw a big party and sacrificed a lot of animals to their god Dagon. The rulers said: Samson was our enemy, but our god Dagon helped us capture him!
translation_verse: A balɔ kɛŋɔ Filisti tena nomonome chemo dɛ kpoo kwaa ɛ sarahajen tɛ ba voɡ baa dɛ yerɔ Daɡɔn dɛɛ lɛ ba sie. Ba ŋɔ, “Ya voɡ kpɔ Samsen waa ɛ ya dɔm la do ya nɔn ta.”

english_verse: Everyone there was having a good time, and they shouted, “Bring out Samson—he's still good for a few more laughs!” The rulers had Samson brought from the prison, and when the people saw him, this is how they praised their god: Samson ruined our crops and killed our people. He was our enemy, but our god helped us capture him. They made fun of Samson for a while, then they told him to stand near the columns that supported the roof.
translation_verse: Ba sie lɛo kohona, ba moo ŋɔ, “Hé ba Samsen ne ó ba lɛ ya sie.” Anomanta, ba kaa lawɔ le dea baa doo la bini, ó ba ɛ ɡɛ baa dɛ nyin bwa tɛɛ ba. Ba kpɔɔ ka che pilare ane baah ta,

english_verse: A young man was leading Samson by the hand, and Samson said to him, “I need to lean against something. Take me over to the columns that hold up the roof.”
translation_verse: asɛ Samsen ŋɔ bonɔɔ waa lawɛ o nɔn la be ŋɔ, “Kaa n ne pilare aa lawɛ voɡ dea nɔ kpoŋe nɔ jwɛh ásɛ n ka yala.”

english_verse: Samson prayed, “Please remember me, Lord God. The Philistines poked out my eyes, but make me strong one last time, so I can take revenge for at least one of my eyes!”
translation_verse: Belaa Samsen soŋe Korowii ŋɔ, “Nemenɛ Korowii, n dɛ soŋe, dɛɛ lii n wa. N Naa Korowii, n poori, ɡel n bokpeɡa berɛ ba kerabeŋkpoŋ ja, ásɛ n ɛ we-ɛɛle beŋkpoŋ dɛ́ kpɔ tɔ n wel Filisti tena baa foromi n sibie nɔ nɛ.”

english_verse: Samson was standing between the two middle columns that held up the roof. He felt around and found one column with his right hand, and the other with his left hand.
translation_verse: Anomanta, o suuhno bɛne baah ta pilare anɛ aa lawɛ dea la kpoŋe la. O kpɔ nɔndiɡ lawɛ bɛl asɛ dɛ kpɔ nɔŋɡal lawɛ nɛɛte, dɛ kpɔ o bokpeɡa bwa ta a ta

english_verse: Then he shouted, “Let me die with the Philistines!” He pushed against the columns as hard as he could, and the temple collapsed with the Philistine rulers and everyone else still inside. Samson killed more Philistines when he died than he had killed during his entire life.
translation_verse: dɛ ŋɔ, “N Naa Korowii, ɡel n ne Filisti tena nɔ pɛ serewe!” Asɛ o taɡɛ pilare la o bokpeɡa bwa ne, asɛ dea la chole pi Filisti nomonome ne nɛra baa lɔ o bini bwa nɛ. Gɛɛ a do nɛra o ne baa pɛa dɛ sewɛ la ɡwaa banɔ la ɡɛ saŋ o siwi aa lole o kpoo ba la.

english_verse: His brothers and the rest of his family went to Gaza and took his body back home. They buried him in his father's tomb, which was located between Zorah and Eshtaol. Samson was a leader of Israel for
translation_verse: Asɛ o dɔɔranar ne nimanar ne o mɛɛ nɛra bwa la ka kpɔ o lale, dɛ ba o ne dɛ ba pili bɔɔ baa huɡe o mɛɛ Manoa o bini la ta dɛ huɡo. Lalbɔɔ la lɔ bwɛɛre Sora ne Ɛstaol baah ta. Samsen tɔ Israel tena sie bene fifraanɛ.

english_verse: Micah returned the silver to his mother, and she said, “I give this silver to the Lord, so my son can use it to make an idol.” Turning to her son, she said, “Micah, now the silver belongs to you.” But Micah handed it back to his mother. She took
translation_verse: O kpɔ suuɡapoŋa la tɛ o nya, o ɡe kpɔ a bini lafraanɛ ka tɛ nɛn waa dɔ suuɡapoŋa kpɔe dɛ ɛ kwaa wejema, asɛ o kpɔ ɛ voɡ, ba kpɔ ka cheɡ Maeka dem.

english_verse: He had a shrine for worshiping God there at his home, and he had made some idols and a sacred priestly vest. Micah chose one of his own sons to be the priest for his shrine.
translation_verse: Dɛ Maeka nɔ dɔ voɡ dea, asɛ o ɛ batakaarebora kɛŋɔ sɔfo batakaare baa dɛ yerɔ efɔd la ken ne voɡa ane, dɛ kpɔ o bibaala la bɛl ɛ o kerekpoŋri.

english_verse: This was before kings ruled Israel, so all the Israelites did whatever they thought was right.
translation_verse: Gɛ saŋ dɛ Israel tena ta kooro dɔe, asɛ bɛlbwa ɛɛ ɛ waa waa dɛ nyin.

english_verse: One day a young Levite came to Micah's house in the hill country of Ephraim. He had been staying with one of the clans of Judah in Bethlehem, but he had left Bethlehem to find a new place to live where he could be a priest.
translation_verse: O le Bɛtlɛham dɛɛ la ka nyin bofale dɛ́ so. Waa chiɡ ŋwɛnɛ ta dɛɛ kaa la, o kaa le Maeka dem Efrem deŋɡarere harɛ la ta.

english_verse: “Where are you from?” Micah asked. “I am a Levite from Bethlehem in Judah,” the man answered, “and I'm on my way to find a new place to live.”
translation_verse: Anee Maeka bɔɔro ŋɔ, “Leperaa he leɔ?” Asɛ o ŋɔ, “N ɛ Lewi dea te, n le Bɛtlɛham Juda harɛ ta dɛɛ nyin bobɛl dɛ́ so.”

english_verse: Micah said, “Why don't you stay here with me? You can be my priest and tell me what God wants me to do. Every year I'll give you ten pieces of silver and one complete set of clothes, and I'll provide all your food.” The young man went for a walk,
translation_verse: Anee Maeka ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “So n be bonɔ dɛ berɛ n mɛɛ ne n kerekpoŋri, ásɛ benanyoa bɛlbwa mɛɛ tɛɛ suuɡapoŋa fi ne laala dɛ kondikwa.”

english_verse: Micah said, “I have a Levite as my own priest. Now I know that the Lord will be kind to me.”
translation_verse: Ate, Maeka ŋɔ, “Taraken maa dɔ Lewi dea te o ɛ n kerekpoŋri nɔ, n jemɔ kɛŋɔ Korowii ɛɛ ɡeloo n wobɛlbwa do wer tɛ mɛ.”

english_verse: These things happened before kings ruled Israel. The Tribe of Dan Takes Micah's Priest and Idols About this time, the tribe of Dan was looking for a place to live. The other tribes had land, but the people of Dan did not really have any to call their own.
translation_verse: Kooro toole Israel tena harɛ ta ɡɛ saŋ. Dɛ Dan dea tena ta harɛ dɔe o ɛ ba ɡbaɡba kon Israel harɛ ta, ba ɡaaɡe dɛɛ nyin bela baa so.

english_verse: The tribe chose five warriors to represent their clans and told them, “Go and find some land where we can live.” The warriors left the area of Zorah and Eshtaol and went into the hill country of Ephraim. One night they stayed at Micah's house,
translation_verse: Anomanta, Dan dea tena tomɛ laa tena banue le bwɛɛre Sora ne Ɛstaol ŋɔ bá ka sɔh ɡaaɡe harɛ la ta dɛ́ na ɡɛ waa doa. A ɡɛ laa tena nɔ cheɡɔ tɛ Dan dea tena bwa. Ba ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, “Hé ka ɡaaɡe harɛ la dɛ́ na ɡɛ waa doa.” Ba jo Efrem dea tena deŋɡarere harɛ ta, dɛ ka le Maeka dem dɛ chɔ bela.

english_verse: because they heard the young Levite talking, and they knew from his accent that he was from the south. They asked him, “What are you doing here? Who brought you here?”
translation_verse: Baa lɔ dem bela la, ba no Lewi bonɔɔ bɛl taa, dɛ la o be ka bɔɔro ŋɔ, “Umee ba he ne bonɔ nɔ? Bɔkwaa hɛɛ ɛ bonɔ nɔ? Bɔkwa waa he do bonɔ nɔ?”

english_verse: The Levite replied, “Micah hired me as his priest.” Then he told them how well Micah had treated him.
translation_verse: O ŋɔ ba be ɡɛ Maeka aa ɛa tɛo dɛ ŋɔ, “O kpɔ mɛ ɛ o voɡ kerekpoŋri dɛɛ bɔ mɛ kem.”

english_verse: “Please talk to God for us,” the men said. “Ask God if we will be successful in what we are trying to do.”
translation_verse: Ba ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Ya poori, bɔɔ Korowii na kɛ ya ŋwɛnɛ yaa dɛ kaa nɔ ɛɛ ka do werii tɛ yaa kɛɛ?”

english_verse: “Don't worry,” answered the priest. “The Lord is pleased with what you are doing.”
translation_verse: Anee kerekpoŋri la ŋɔ, “Hé kaa deŋnesɔɔhna ne. Korowii ja he nɛ.”

english_verse: The five men left and went to the town of Laish, whose people were from Sidon, but Sidon was too far away to protect them. Even though their town had no walls, the people thought they were safe from attack. So they had not asked anyone else for protection, which meant that the tribe of Dan could easily take over Laish.
translation_verse: Anomanta, baala banue la leɔ dɛ kaa Lais harɛ. Belaa ba ka na kɛŋɔ bela nɛra la soɡe deŋnesɔɔhna ta kɛŋɔ Sidon tena ken, dɛ so kɛrɛdɛ, dɛɛ lii kɛŋɔ wobɛlbwa aa ban pu. Komɛlbwa lɔ ba harɛ la ta, ba dɔ ba te. Ba ne Sidon tena baah jaŋne, ba ne nomɛlbwa aa chamene di.

english_verse: The five men went back to Zorah and Eshtaol, where their relatives asked, “Did you find any land?”
translation_verse: Nɛra banue la aa bera ba Sora ne Ɛstaol la, ba bala bɔɔ ba ŋɔ, “Bɔkwaa he ka na nɔ?”

english_verse: “Let's go!” the five men said. “We saw some very good land with enough room for all of us, and it has everything we will ever need. What are you waiting for? Let's attack and take it. You'll find that the people think they're safe, but God is giving the land to us.”
translation_verse: Hé laŋaa, hɛɛ pu nɛra baa wola lii kɛŋɔ waane ɛɛ pu baa. Harɛ la kan. Korowii kpɔɔ do he nɔn ta. Komɛlbwa ta o ta nyae.”

english_verse: Six hundred men from the tribe of Dan strapped on their weapons and left Zorah and Eshtaol with their families.
translation_verse: Anee baala lafraanumɛl le Dan dea dɛ vɔrɔwe laa le Sora ne Ɛstaol dɛɛ kaa ka yoo ba.

english_verse: One night they camped near Kiriath-Jearim in the territory of Judah, and that's why the place just west of Kiriath-Jearim is still known as Dan's Camp.
translation_verse: Baa dɛ kaa la, ba kaa baŋre ba tɛnte deene Kiriat Jearim, o lɔ Juda harɛ ta. A ɡɛ nomanta, ba dɛ yerɛ Kiriat Jearim wee cholibɔr Mahane Dan, dɛ ba le fini.

english_verse: Then they went into the hill country of Ephraim. When they came close to Micah's house,
translation_verse: Baa le bela la, ba kaa Efrem deŋɡarere harɛ ta, dɛ ka le Maeka dem.

english_verse: the five men who had been spies asked the other warriors, “Did you know that someone in this village has several idols and a sacred priestly vest? What do you think we should do about it?”
translation_verse: Baala banue baa laŋa ka sɔh nyiŋi Lais harɛ la ŋɔ ba bala laa tena la be ŋɔ, “Hé jemɔ kɛŋɔ batakaarebora waa do kɛŋɔ efɔd ne dem voɡare baa sɛah kɛɛ dɛ loɡa lɔ deremi nɔ bɛl ta naa? Ɛrɛɛ chɛ kɛ yá ɛɔ?”

english_verse: “Quiet!” the men said. “Keep your mouth shut and listen. Why don't you come with us and be our priest, so you can tell us what God wants us to do? You could stay here and be a priest for one man's family, but wouldn't you rather be the priest for a clan or even a whole tribe of Israel?”
translation_verse: Anee ba chaŋo ŋɔ, “Tɔ nyoa, bɛ nyoa pili bol wa. Ba ja ya nɛɛ dɛ́ ɛ ya mɛɛ ne nɛn waa dɛɛ ja yaa. Dɛ he tomɛ Israel dea bɛl nɛra kwaraa naa, a laa wera ɡwaa kɛŋɔ haa dɛ tomɛ nɛmbeŋkpoŋ ne o dem tena ɡbo naa?”

english_verse: The priest really liked that idea. So he took the vest and the idols and joined the others
translation_verse: Sɔfo la sɛoh silɛɛ ne dɛ pa batakaarebora waa do kɛ efɔd, ne voɡ baa sɛah ne deremi voɡa dɛ kwaa aa jaa bwa, dɛ teŋɛ nɛra la nɛɛ kaa.

english_verse: from the tribe of Dan. Then they turned and left, after putting their children, their cattle, and the rest of their other possessions in front.
translation_verse: Ba kpɔ ba bii ne ba laala dɛ teɡɛ ba kondɛɛra tɔ ba sie kaa.

english_verse: They had traveled for some time before Micah asked his neighbors to help him get his things back. He and his men caught up with the people of Dan
translation_verse: Baa vala le Maeka dem tel sie tama la, Maeka yerɛ nɛra o ne ba deremi aa bɛne dɔŋa la, dɛ ti Dan dea tena la dɛ ka puu ba.

english_verse: and shouted for them to stop. They turned to face him and asked, “What's wrong? Why did you bring all these men?”
translation_verse: Ba teŋɛ ba nɛɛ dɛ kpɔ takpeɡ dɛɛ yer ba, asɛ Dan dea tena la laa berɛ dɛ bɔɔ Maeka ŋɔ, “Bɔkwa waa yɔ? Ɛrɛɛ he yerɛ he nɛra bá ba yo yaa nɔɔ?”

english_verse: Micah answered, “You know what's wrong. You stole the gods I made, and you took my priest. I don't have anything left.”
translation_verse: Anee o chaŋ ba ŋɔ, “Haa jemɛ waa haa ɛa aa? He kpɔ n voɡa maa ɛa ne n Kerekpoŋri kaa. Bɔkwaa n dɔ jaɔ?”

english_verse: “We don't want to hear any more about it,” the people of Dan said. “And if you make us angry, you'll only get yourself and your family killed.”
translation_verse: Asɛ Dan dea tena la ŋɔ, “Bɛ yaa tɔŋle, ya bini bane baah aa biɡri dii. Ba baah diu waa, baa yo heyaa dɛ́ kpoo he ne he dem tena bwa.”

english_verse: After saying this, they turned and left. Micah realized there was no way he could win a fight with them, and so he went back home. The Tribe of Dan Captures Laish
translation_verse: Anomanta, Dan dea tena la kaalɔ, asɛ Maeka aa naa kɛŋɔ ba kpeɡri ɡwaalo la, o berɛ kaa dem.

english_verse: But they named it Dan, after one of Israel's sons, who was the ancestor of their tribe.
translation_verse: Ba kpɔ ba nabaa Dan sɔn pa bwɛɛ la, ba bwa nabaa Jekɔb aa lolɔ la. Dɛ ba fa dɛ yerɛ bwɛɛ la Lais.

english_verse: Before kings ruled Israel, a Levite was living deep in the hill country of the Ephraim tribe. He married a woman from Bethlehem in Judah,
translation_verse: A saŋ la, dɛ kooro toole Israel harɛ ta. Dɛ Lewi dea te bɛl soɡe bojaŋ bwɛɛ bɛl ta, Efrem deŋɡarere harɛ ta, dɛ ka kpɔ haah Bɛtlɛham waa lɔ Juda harɛ ta o ne wɛɛ di nyoa sɛm.

english_verse: but she was unfaithful and went back to live with her family in Bethlehem. Four months later
translation_verse: Haah la le baa la habɔɔ dɛ ka chɔ banfale be, dɛ berɛ le o sɛno la be dɛ kaa Bɛtlɛham ka so o mɛɛ dem korobie anaarɛ.

english_verse: her husband decided to try and talk her into coming back. So he went to Bethlehem, taking along a servant and two donkeys. He talked with his wife, and she invited him into her family's home. Her father was glad to see him
translation_verse: Banloɡle la la o be dɛ ka larawo ásɛ o berɛ ba. Keeɡore anɛɛ o kpɔ o ne o bonɔɔ bɛl kaa. Haah la kpɔ baa la la o mɛɛ dem, o mɛɛ ɡe lɛo silɛɛ ne.

english_verse: and did not want him to leave. So the man stayed three days, eating and drinking with his father-in-law.
translation_verse: Dɛ haah la mɛɛ aa nyin kɛ baa la kaa dɛ ŋɔ ó so bela tama. Anomanta, o soɡe bela tɔpera atoro, belaa wɛɛ di kwaa dɛɛ nyɔ sen dɛɛ chɔ ɡe.

english_verse: When everyone got up on the fourth day, the Levite started getting ready to go home. But his father-in-law said, “Don't leave until you have a bite to eat. You'll need strength for your journey.”
translation_verse: Tɔpenaarɛ wee la, ba felo ir asɛ o kpɔ o te dɛ fe ɛɛ kaa. Anee haah la mɛɛ ŋɔ, “Chɔɔ nyoa mɔɔ dɛ́ dɔ bokpeɡa dɛɛ la.”

english_verse: The two men sat down together and ate a big meal. “Come on,” the man's father-in-law said. “Stay tonight and have a good time.”
translation_verse: Anomanta, baala banɛ la soɡo dɛ pɛ di kwaa la. A habɔɔ la, haah la mɛɛ berɔ ŋɔ baa la be ŋɔ, “N dɛ soŋe, lɛ he sie dɛ chɔ.”

english_verse: The Levite tried to leave, but his father-in-law insisted, and he spent one more night there.
translation_verse: Baa la aa ira dɛɛ ba kaala la, o hela la ta sɛɛh, asɛ o berɛ chɔ bela awola tɔpere la.

english_verse: The fifth day, the man got up early to leave, but his wife's father said, “You need to keep up your strength! Why don't you leave right after lunch?” So the two of them started eating.
translation_verse: Tɔpenue wee waa ira chɔmbibii dɛɛ ba kaala la, o hela la ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “So dɛ́ di kwa, webaŋa mɔɔ dɛ kaa.” Asɛ ba nɛra banɛ la so dɛ di kwaa la.

english_verse: Finally, the Levite got up from the meal, so he and his wife and servant could leave. “Look,” his father-in-law said, “it's already late afternoon, and if you leave now, you won't get very far before dark. Stay with us one more night and enjoy yourself. Then you can get up early tomorrow morning and start home.”
translation_verse: Baa la ne o sɛno la ne bonɔɔ la aa ira dɛɛ ba kaala la, haah la mɛɛ ŋɔ ba be ja ŋɔ, “Taraken bɔr joɔ tonɛ, so lɛ he sie dɛ chɔ, ásɛ kere chɔmbibii, hé chiɡ ŋwɛnɛ ta kaa.”

english_verse: But the Levite decided not to spend the night there again. He had the saddles put on his two donkeys, then he and his wife and servant traveled as far as Jebus, which is now called Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Kɛ dɛ baa la aa nyin kɛ o chɔ bela jwaana kpa, dɛ pa kwaa baa paa dawɛ keeɡo ta dɛɛ so o ta la dawɛ keeɡore anɛ la ta, asɛ o ne o sɛno la kpɔ sie chaɡɛ Jebus waa ɛ Jerusalam.

english_verse: It was beginning to get dark, and the man's servant said, “Let's stop and spend the night in this town where the Jebusites live.”
translation_verse: Baa dɛ tel Jebus waa ɛ Jerusalam bɔr ɛɛ ba joe la, bonɔɔ la ŋɔ o dɔɔ be ŋɔ, “Nomoa, yá chɔ Jerusalam bonɔ, ásɛ kere chɔɔ dɛ́ kaa.”

english_verse: “No,” the Levite answered. “They aren't Israelites, and I refuse to spend the night there. We'll stop for the night at Gibeah,
translation_verse: Nomoa la ŋɔ, “Akai, yaa nɛŋhɔɔhra baa wola Israel tena ɛɛ bee chɔ. Yaa kaa Gebeaa.”

english_verse: They walked on and reached Gibeah in the territory of Benjamin just after sunset.
translation_verse: Ba kaalɔ ka bɛne Gebea waa lɔ Bɛnjamen dea harɛ ta, dɛ wee le harɛ.

english_verse: They left the road and went into Gibeah. But the Levite couldn't find a house where anyone would let them spend the night, and they sat down in the open area just inside the town gates.
translation_verse: Belaa ba choɡ ŋɔ bá chɔ. Ba kaa so bela bwɛɛ la tena aa dɛ cheme, kɛ nomɛlbwa ta ban kpɔe kaa dɛ́ ka tɛɛ ba bɔr bá chɔ.

english_verse: Soon an old man came in through the gates on his way home from working in the fields. Most of the people who lived in Gibeah belonged to the tribe of Benjamin, but this man was originally from the hill country of Ephraim.
translation_verse: Awola jɔmɔra la, dɛ banjena bɛl le koo dɛɛ ba. Dɛ o le Efrem deŋɡarere harɛ dɛ ba so Gebea bela, Bɛnjamen dea tena bwɛɛ.

english_verse: He noticed that the Levite was just in town to spend the night. “Where are you going?” the old man asked. “Where did you come from?”
translation_verse: Banjena la aa na hɔɔhra la bela bwɛɛ la tena aa dɛ cheme la, o bɔɔ ba ŋɔ, “Leperaa hɛɛ kaalɔ? Lee he leɔ?”

english_verse: “We've come from Bethlehem in Judah,” the Levite answered. “We went there on a visit. Now we're going to the place where the Lord is worshiped, and later we will return to our home in the hill country of Ephraim. But no one here will let us spend the night in their home.
translation_verse: Anee o ŋɔ, “Ya le Bɛtlɛham waa lɔ Juda harɛ ta dɛɛ kaa Efrem deŋɡarere harɛ bojaŋ, belaa n so. N dɛ kaa n bwɛ, kɛ nomɛlbwa ta yaa kpɔe kaa o dem yá ka chɔ.

english_verse: We brought food for our donkeys and bread and wine for ourselves, so we don't need anything except a place to sleep.”
translation_verse: Nomoa, ya dɔ kondikwaa dɛ́ tɛ ya keeɡore nɔ, dɛ dɔ ya ɡbaɡba kondikwaa ne sen. N ne n sɛno ne bonɔɔ nɔ dɔ komɛlbwa ya be.”

english_verse: The old man said, “You are welcome to spend the night in my home and to be my guest, but don't stay out here!”
translation_verse: Ate, banjena la ŋɔ, “Mɛɛ kaa he ne n demii. Mɛɛ tɛ heyaa komɛlbwa haa dɛ nyinii, kɛ waa aa hiah mɛɛ kɛ he bɛ bwɛɛ nɔ cheremibɔr bonɔ chɔ jwaana nɔ ne.”

english_verse: The old man brought them into his house and fed their donkeys. Then he and his guests washed their feet and began eating and drinking.
translation_verse: Anomanta, o kaa ba ne o dem, dɛ tɛ keeɡore la kwaa a di. O tɛ nɛra la nee ba sarame ba nakpale, dɛ tɛɛ ba kondikwaa ba di dɛ tɛɛ ba sen ɡe ba nyɔ.

english_verse: They were having a good time, when some worthless men of that town surrounded the house and started banging on the door and shouting, “A man came to your house tonight. Send him out, so we can have sex with him!”
translation_verse: Baa dɛ lɛ ba sie la, nɛnchɔɡa bane baa lɔ bwɛɛ la ta baa bar dem la cheme, dɛɛ lɔ dem la doonyoa ɡbera la, dɛɛ kɔɡre dem te la ŋɔ, “Le baa la waa ba he dem bonɔ la ne tɛ yaa yá lawɔ ka chɔ kɛ baa ne haah.”

english_verse: The old man went outside and said, “My friends, please don't commit such a horrible crime against a man who is a guest in my house.
translation_verse: Dem te la le buse dɛ ka ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, “Akai! Ya bala, he bɛ wedoŋa nɔ ɛ. N hɔɔhree, hɛɛ berɛ a ɡɛ sihihwaa nɔ ɛɛ.

english_verse: Let me send out my daughter instead. She's a virgin. And I'll even send out the man's wife. You can rape them or do whatever else you want, but please don't do such a horrible thing to this man.”
translation_verse: N bihaah waa wola baa jemɛ bwa lole, mɛɛ le o ne n hɔɔh nɔ sɛnoo tɛ heya, ásɛ he ne ba ka chɔ. Kɛ baa nɔ te, he bɛ on a ɡɛ sihihwaa nɔ ɛ.”

english_verse: The men refused to listen, so the Levite grabbed his wife and shoved her outside. The men raped her and abused her all night long. Finally, they let her go just before sunrise,
translation_verse: Nɛra la vɛh banjena la waa la. Anomanta, hɔɔh la lawɛ o sɛno la le buse tɛɛ ba, ba lawɔ dɛ ka ɡuɡru ba ne o chɔ jwaana la ne bwa. Bɔr aa dɛ chaah la, ba tao ŋwɛnɛ o kaa.

english_verse: and it was almost daybreak when she went back to the house where her husband was staying. She collapsed at the door and lay there until sunrise.
translation_verse: Bɔr aa dɛ chaah la, haah la berɔ kaa dem bela o dɔɔ aa lole la. O cholo chɔ dem la doonyoa ka tel kɛŋɔ bɔr aa chaahna.

english_verse: About that time, her husband woke up and got ready to leave. He opened the door and went outside, where he found his wife lying at the door with her hands on the doorstep.
translation_verse: Baa la aa ira chɔɔ ne la, o kaa ya dem la ɡbera dɛ le buse dɛ́ kaa, asɛ dɛ na ɡɛ o sɛno la aa chɔa o nɔɔra ba dawɛ doonyojoo ɡbera daa la ta.

english_verse: “Get up!” he said. “It's time to leave.” But his wife didn't move. He lifted her body onto his donkey and left.
translation_verse: Anee o ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Ir ya kaa!” Kɛ haah la ta on chaŋɛ, asɛ o na kɛŋɔ o sewɔ. Belaa o kpɔ o lale dawɛ keeɡo ta dɛɛ kaa o bwɛ.

english_verse: When he got home, he took a butcher knife and cut her body into twelve pieces. Then he told some messengers, “Take one piece to each tribe of Israel
translation_verse: Waa tel dem la, o kpɔ kere mɔne o sɛno la bini bɔre fi dɛ anɛ, dɛ kpɔ ka tɛ Israel deene fi dɛ anɛ la bwa.

english_verse: and ask everyone if anything like this has ever happened since Israel left Egypt. Tell them to think about it, talk it over, and tell us what should be done.” Everyone who saw a piece of the body said, “This is horrible! Nothing like this has ever happened since the day Israel left Egypt.”
translation_verse: Nomɛlbwa waa no ɡɛ waa nɔ la ŋɔ, “Dɛ le kɛŋɔ Israel tena aa le Ijipt harɛ ta ba la, ya ta waa nɔ dɔŋa nae bwa, ya ta a dɔŋa noɛ ɡe bwa. Ɛrɛɛ yaa ba ɛɛ yɔ? Yá nyiŋi a ta kɛrɛdɛ. A chɛ kɛ yá ɛ waane.”

english_verse: The husband of the murdered woman answered: My wife and I went into the town of Gibeah in Benjamin to spend the night.
translation_verse: Anee Lewi dea te baa kpo o sɛno la ŋɔ, “N ne n sɛnoo ba Gebea Bɛnjamen dea harɛ ta dɛ ba chɔ.

english_verse: It was a terrible thing for Israelites to do! So I cut up her body and sent the pieces everywhere in Israel.
translation_verse: N kpɔ o lale la dɛ ba mɔne o bini bɔne tɛ Israel deene fi dɛ anɛ la bɛlbwa, ásɛ a chaɡle wedoŋa ne waa baa kia ba ɛa Israel harɛ ta la.

english_verse: You are the people of Israel, and you must decide today what to do about the men of Gibeah.
translation_verse: Israel tena, he bwa aa chema nɔ, hé bol a waa dɛ́ baɡle ɡɛ aa chɛ kɛ yá ɛ.”

english_verse: The whole army was in agreement, and they said, “None of us will go home.
translation_verse: Nɛra la bwa pɛo dɛ ŋɔ, “Ya bini bɛlbwa toole dɛɛ ba dem kaala. Akai! Ya bini bɛlbwa aa o bwɛɛ kaa.

english_verse: Everyone agreed that Gibeah had to be punished.
translation_verse: Anomanta, Israel nɛra la bwa pɛo kɛ nɛmbeŋkpoŋ, dɛ́ ka yo Gebea tena.

english_verse: The tribes of Israel sent messengers to every town and village in Benjamin. And wherever the messengers went, they said, “How could those worthless men in Gibeah do such a disgusting thing?
translation_verse: Israel deene la tomɛ nɛra Bɛnjamen dea harɛ ta bobɛlbwa ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ he na wedoŋa baa ɛa he bini nɔ waɔ?

english_verse: We can't allow such a terrible crime to go unpunished in Israel! Hand the men over to us, and we will put them to death.” But the people of Benjamin refused to listen to the other Israelites.
translation_verse: Hé le Gebea nɛnchɔɡa nɔ tɛ yaa yá kpoo ba, ásɛ ɡɛ wedoŋa nɔ le Israel harɛ ta.” Kɛ Bɛnjamen dea tena la ta ba bala Israel tena waa la mun noɛ,

english_verse: Men from towns all over Benjamin's territory went to Gibeah and got ready to fight Israel.
translation_verse: dɛ ɡe le ba bwɛɛre ta ba cheme Gebea dɛ vɔrɔwe kɛ bá yo Israel tena.

english_verse: The other Israelite tribes organized their army and found they had
translation_verse: Israel tena dɔ laa tena kaɡboŋa lafraanaarɛ baa dɛ yo kɛrɛdɛ. Bɛnjamen dea tena ta ba nɛɛ jae.

english_verse: The next morning the Israelite army moved its camp to a place near Gibeah.
translation_verse: Tɔ aa pera chɔɔ la, Israel tena iro dɛ ka baŋre ba tɛnte deene bɛne Gebea,

english_verse: Then they left their camp and got into position to attack the army of Benjamin. The War Between Israel and Benjamin
translation_verse: dɛ kpɔ ba te dɛ́ ka yo Gebea tena la. Bɛlbwa kaa che bela waa che dɛ kpɔ o te dɛ́ yoo ba.

english_verse: Benjamin's soldiers came out of Gibeah and attacked, and when the day was over,
translation_verse: Bɛnjamen dea tena la le Gebea, dɛ ba kpoo Israel tena kaɡboŋa fifraanɛ dɛ banɛ laa la ta awola tenten.

english_verse: The people of Israel went to the place of worship at Bethel, where the sacred chest was being kept. They sat on the ground, crying and not eating for the rest of the day. Then about sunset, they offered sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask his blessing. Phinehas the priest then prayed, “Our Lord, the people of Benjamin are our relatives. Should we stop fighting or attack them again?” “Attack!” the Lord answered. “Tomorrow I will let you defeat them.”
translation_verse: Dɛ Eliasa bibaa Fenehas lɔ bela dɛɛ ɛ Korowii toma, o nabaalee Arɔn. Israel tena la bɔɔ Korowii ŋɔ, “Yá ka yo ya bala Bɛnjamen dea tena nɔ kɛɛ yá ɡelɔ?” Anee Korowii sɛh ŋɔ, “Hé kaa! Kere te mɛɛ kpɔ baa do he nɔn ta, ásɛ he pɔ ba nɛ.”

english_verse: The Israelites surrounded Gibeah, but stayed where they could not be seen.
translation_verse: Baa lea kaa la, ba kaa chɔ bar Gebea.

english_verse: The men of Benjamin headed down the road toward the desert, trying to escape from the Israelites. But the Israelites stayed right behind them, keeping up their attack. Men even came out of the nearby towns to help kill the men of Benjamin,
translation_verse: Ba chwao le Israel tena la be dɛ chaɡɛ pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ la ta, kɛ ba ta wone chwa le laa la ta. Israel tena la le bwɛɛ la ta dɛ ba kpoo ba bela.

english_verse: who were having to fight on all sides. The Israelite soldiers never let up their attack. They chased and killed the warriors of Benjamin as far as a place directly east of Gibeah,
translation_verse: Ba bar Bɛnjamen dea tena la, dɛ chwa teŋɛ ba nɛɛ dɛ ka puu ba Gebea wee leebɔr.

english_verse: Twenty-five thousand soldiers of Benjamin died that day, all of them experienced warriors.
translation_verse: Awola tɔpere la, Bɛnjamen dea laa tena kaɡboŋa fifraanɛ dɛ banue baa jemɛ yoi kɛrɛdɛ dɛ kpoŋe tokobiee serewa.

english_verse: The Israelites turned back and went to every town in Benjamin's territory, killing all the people and animals, and setting the towns on fire.
translation_verse: Israel tena la laa berɛ kaa Bɛnjamen dea tena harɛ ta, dɛ ka kpoo nɛra baa lɔ bwɛɛre la ta bwa, ne ba kondɛɛra, dɛ kon te bɛlbwa baa nao. Ba fuh bwɛɛre la bwa.

english_verse: When the Israelites had met at Mizpah before the war with Benjamin, they had made this sacred promise: “None of us will ever let our daughters marry any man from Benjamin.”
translation_verse: Israel tena la aa cheme Mispa la, ba ŋwɛɛrɔ kɛŋɔ ba bini bɛlbwa bɛ o bihaah kpɔ tɛ Bɛnjamen dea bie ó mo.

english_verse: After the war with Benjamin, the Israelites went to the place of worship at Bethel and sat there until sunset. They cried loudly and bitterly
translation_verse: Israel tena la Bɛtel dɛ ka so Korowii sie dɛ kpɔ takpeɡ wi noo kohona ka tel jɔmɔra.

english_verse: and prayed, “Our Lord, you are the God of Israel. Why did you let this happen? Now one of our tribes is almost gone.”
translation_verse: Ba wio ŋɔ, “Korowii ya Israel tena aa dɛ tomɛ, ɛrɛ taa a che ɡɛ waa nɔ pu yaa nɔɔ? Bɔkwa waa debeŋkpoŋ tena nyoɡre le ya bini fini nɔɔ?”

english_verse: Early the next morning, the Israelites built an altar and offered sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask his blessing.
translation_verse: Tɔ aa pera chɔmbibi la, nɛra la ɛ kon baa dɛ ɛ saraha o ta bela, dɛ ɛ saraha baa dɛ fuah ne deŋnesɔɔhna saraha o ta tɛ Korowii.

english_verse: Then they asked each other, “Did any of the tribes of Israel fail to come to the place of worship? We made a sacred promise that anyone who didn't come to the meeting at Mizpah would be put to death.”
translation_verse: Israel tena la bɔɔ dɔŋa ŋɔ, “Israel deene nɔ bwa bini, debesoo tenaa wola Korowii sie bonɔ balɔɔ?” Ba fa ŋwɛɛrɔ bil kɛŋɔ dea bɛlbwa waa wola Korowii sie Mispa bonɔ balɛ la, bá kpoo o nɛra.

english_verse: The Israelites were sad about what had happened to the Benjamin tribe, and they said, “One of our tribes was almost wiped out.
translation_verse: Israel tena la wio tɛ ba bala Bɛnjamen dea tena la ŋɔ, “Fini tɔpere nɔ, dea beŋkpoŋ nɛra toole ya bini.

english_verse: Only a few men of Benjamin weren't killed in the war. We need to get wives for them, so the tribe won't completely disappear. But how can we do that, after promising in the Lord's name that we wouldn't let them marry any of our daughters?”
translation_verse: Ɛrɛɛ yaa ba ɛɛ dɛ won dɔ haahna tɛ Bɛnjamen dea tena baa kaa nɔɔ? Ya ɡe dɔɔ ŋwɛɛ Korowii sɔn ta kɛŋɔ ya bɛ ya bihaahna kpɔ tɛɛ ba bá mo.”

english_verse: Again the Israelites asked, “Did any of the tribes stay away from the meeting at Mizpah?” After asking around, they discovered that no one had come from Jabesh in Gilead.
translation_verse: dɛkalkɛŋɔ baa kure nɛra baa ba bela la, ba nao kɛŋɔ Jabes Gelead harɛ ta te beŋkpoŋ kwaraa toole bela.

english_verse: The warriors attacked Jabesh in Gilead, and returned to their camp at Shiloh in Canaan with
translation_verse: Ba na toli lafraanaarɛ Jabes Gelead baa wola baala jemɛ bwa, asɛ ba laɡ ba kaa bela baa baŋre ba tɛnte deene Silo waa lɔ Keenan harɛ ta.

english_verse: The Israelites met and sent messengers to the men of Benjamin at Rimmon Rock, telling them that the Israelites were willing to make peace with them.
translation_verse: Nɛra baa cheme bela la bwa tomɛ nɛra Remɔn Bwe la ta bá ka larawe Bɛnjamen dea tena baa lɔ bela.

english_verse: So the men of Benjamin came back from Rimmon Rock, and the Israelites let them marry the young women from Jabesh. But there weren't enough women.
translation_verse: Anomanta, Bɛnjamen dea tena la berɔ ba ɡɛ saŋ, asɛ Israel tena la kpɔ haahna baa laɡ ba le Jabes Gelead baa wola ban kpoorɛ la tɛɛ ba ba mo, kɛ ba ta baala la nyoa tele.

english_verse: The Israelites were very sad, because the Lord had almost wiped out one of their tribes.
translation_verse: Israel tena la tea bini chɔɡɔ Bɛnjamen dea tena la wa, ɡɛ Korowii aa ɡela dea beŋkpoŋ tena aa wola toole ba bini la.

english_verse: Then their leaders said: All the women of the Benjamin tribe were killed. How can we get wives for the men of Benjamin who are left?
translation_verse: Nomonome baa lɔ nɛra baa cheme bela la ŋɔ, “Bɛnjamen dea haahna aa serewa nɔ, ɛrɛɛ yaa ba ɛɛ dɛ́ dɔ haahna tɛ baala baa kaa nɔɔ?”

english_verse: But we can't let the men of Benjamin marry any of our daughters. We made a sacred promise not to do that, and if we break our promise, we will be under our own curse.
translation_verse: Ya Israel tena aa ŋwɛɛ ntam nɔ, yáa won kpɔ ya bihaahna tɛɛ ba ba mo. Ya bini bɛlbwa waa ɡela o bihaah yalɛ Bɛnjamen dea bie la, nyotaahna ɛɛ lawɔɔ.

english_verse: Then someone suggested, “What about the Lord's Festival that takes place each year in Shiloh? It's held north of Bethel, south of Lebonah, and just east of the road that goes from Bethel to Shechem.”
translation_verse: Kɛ hé no! Ya dɛ ba tɔpejen bɛl dii Silo waa lɔ Bɛtel weekaŋle nyundua, ne ŋwɛnɛ waa lɔ Bɛtel ne Sɛkem wee leebɔr, ne Lɛbɔna weekaŋle harɛbɔr.”

english_verse: The leaders told the men of Benjamin who still did not have wives: Go to Shiloh and hide in the vineyards near the festival.
translation_verse: Israel tena la do Bɛnjamen dea tena la ŋɔ, “Hé ka sɔh ɡrepo daa kooni ta,

english_verse: Wait there for the young women of Shiloh to come out and perform their dances. Then rush out and grab one of the young women, then take her home as your wife.
translation_verse: dɛɛ nyiŋi. Hé na Silo bitoli ba baa sa aa, hé ɛ warane dɛ́ le daa kooni la baah, ásɛ bɛlbwa ka lawɛ bɛl kaa he Bɛnjamen dea tena harɛ ta ó ɛ he haah.

english_verse: If the fathers or brothers of these women complain about this, we'll say, “Be kind enough to let those men keep your daughter. After all, we couldn't get enough wives for all the men of Benjamin in the battle at Jabesh. And because you didn't give them permission to marry your daughters, you won't be under the curse we earlier agreed on.”
translation_verse: Ba mɛɛnanar kɛɛ ba dɔɔranar ba dɛ bol ba waa ya be naa, ya ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, ‘Hé takapɔ dɛ́ cha yaa, dɛkalkɛŋɔ ya ta haahna dɔe tɛɛ ba laa la nomanta. He kon som haa wola he bihaahna kpɔe tɛɛ ba la. Nyotaahna aa he nɛɛ ba.’ ”

english_verse: The men of Benjamin went to Shiloh and hid in the vineyards. The young women soon started dancing, and each man grabbed one of them and carried her off. Then the men of Benjamin went back to their own land and rebuilt their towns and started living in them again.
translation_verse: Anomanta, ɡɛɛ Bɛnjamen dea tena la ɛ. Haahna la aa ba dɛ sa la, asɛ bɛlbwa le ba lawɛ o kon dɛ kaa o ne, ó ɛ o haah. Ba berɔ kaa ka so ba harɛ ta, dɛ ka kwaa vɔrɔwe ba bwɛɛre dɛ so a ta.

english_verse: Afterwards, the rest of the Israelites returned to their homes and families. Israel Was Not Ruled by a King
translation_verse: Israel tena le bela dɛ berɛ kaa ba harɛ ta ba lolanar be ne ba bwɛɛre ta.

english_verse: In those days Israel wasn't ruled by a king, and everyone did what they thought was right.
translation_verse: Gɛ saŋ dɛ kooro toole Israel harɛ ta, asɛ bɛlbwa ɛɛ ɛ ɡɛ aa wera o be.

english_verse: Before Israel was ruled by kings, Elimelech from the clan of Ephrath lived in the town of Bethlehem. His wife was named Naomi, and their two sons were Mahlon and Chilion. But when their crops failed in Israel, they moved to the country of Moab. And while they were there,
translation_verse: Baa la sɔne Ɛlemɛlɛk, o haah ɡe sɔne Naomi. O bibaala la bɛl sɔne Maalɔn, asɛ nɛɛte la ɡe sɔne Keleɔn. Dɛ Efrat dea naanaree ban, ba le Bɛtlɛham waa lɔ Juda harɛ ta.

english_verse: Elimelech died, leaving Naomi with only her two sons.
translation_verse: Baa kaa so bela la, Ɛlemɛlɛk sewɔ, asɛ a ka Naomi ne bibaala banɛ la ɡbo.

english_verse: Later, Naomi's sons married Moabite women. One was named Orpah and the other Ruth. About ten years later,
translation_verse: Bibaala la mo Moab haahna. Bɛl sɔne Ɔpa, asɛ bɛl ɡe Rut. Baa soɡa bene fi habɔɔ la,

english_verse: Mahlon and Chilion also died. Now Naomi had no husband or sons.
translation_verse: Maalɔn ne Keleɔn baa sewɛ. Aa ba ɡɛ la a ka Naomi ɡbo.

english_verse: Naomi said to them, “Don't you want to go back home to your own mothers? You were kind to my husband and sons, and you've always been kind to me. I pray that the Lord will be just as kind to you.
translation_verse: Ŋwɛnɛ ta la, Naomi ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, “Hé berɛ kaa he nyawa be. Korowiirii dɛ́ cha heya, ɡɛ haa cha n ne n jaa ne n bii la.

english_verse: May he give each of you another husband and a home of your own.” Naomi kissed them. They cried
translation_verse: Korowiirii dɛ́ cha heya, ásɛ bɛlbwa berɛ dɔ jaa dɛ́ dɔ bodɛɛɡe so.” Belaa o ka mo ba lwɛɛma dɛ kal ba. Asɛ ba pa mun dɛɛ wi,

english_verse: and said, “We want to go with you and live among your people.”
translation_verse: dɛ ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Akai, ya ne henee dɛ́ kaa he nɛra be.”

english_verse: But she replied, “My daughters, why don't you return home? What good will it do you to go with me? Do you think I could have more sons for you to marry?
translation_verse: Anee Naomi chaŋe ŋɔ, “N bii, hé berɛ kaa he bwɛ. N ne he kaala mun ɔ? N lol tonɔ, mɛɛ won berɛ lolɛ bii bá kpɔ heyaa mo ja aa?

english_verse: You must go back home, because I am too old to marry again. Even if I got married tonight and later had more sons,
translation_verse: Hé berɛ kaa he bwɛ. Taraken bela maa tela nɔ, maa jaaree dɔ kpa. Dɛ hwɛɡa lole kɛŋɔ ń dɔ jaa aa, hale n ne o chɔɔ fini kwara naa, maa won den kpoŋe tea dɛ́ loɡle bibaala tɛ heya.

english_verse: would you wait for them to become old enough to marry? No, my daughters! Life is harder for me than it is for you, because the Lord has turned against me.”
translation_verse: Dɛ a ba ɡɛ kwara naa, hɛɛ won soŋni ka tel kɛŋɔ baa kpeɡ aa? Hɛɛ won so dɛ́ ŋɔ haa yalaa? Akai n bii, he ɡbabir jemɔ ŋɔ ɡɛ aa won maɡre. N nyuu wola were mɛɛ di suna, he te laa chɛ kɛŋɔ he di suna. Korowiirii ɛɛ mɛ ɡɛ.”

english_verse: They cried again. Orpah kissed her mother-in-law goodbye, but Ruth held on to her.
translation_verse: Asɛ ba berɛ wi anɔ ɡe ta ja. Belaa Ɔpa mo o lwɛɛma dɛ kalo. Kɛ Rut te ta lawɔ kpoŋe dɛ ŋɔ waa on ta.

english_verse: Naomi then said to Ruth, “Look, your sister-in-law is going back to her people and to her gods! Why don't you go with her?”
translation_verse: Anee Naomi ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Nyiŋi na, he nahaahnee bera dɛɛ kaa o harɛ ta ne ba voɡa bini la. He ɡe ka puu hé kaa.”

english_verse: Ruth answered, “Please don't tell me to leave you and return home! I will go where you go, I will live where you live; your people will be my people, your God will be my God.
translation_verse: Asɛ Rut chaŋo ŋɔ, “Bɛ n be ŋɔ n ɡele. Bobɛlbwa haa kaa ne bela haa so la, n ɡee so belaa. Mɛɛ kpɔ he nɛraa ɛ n nɛra, ásɛ Korowii haa dɛ tomɔ la, ń ɡee tomɔ.

english_verse: I will die where you die and be buried beside you. May the Lord punish me if we are ever separated, even by death!”
translation_verse: Bela haa sewɛ laanee n ɡee ba sewa, ásɛ ba huɡ mɛ bela. Dɛ seo laa aa, n ŋwɛɛrɔ kɛŋɔ wobɛlbwa aa won pere ya baah.”

english_verse: When Naomi saw that Ruth had made up her mind to go with her, she stopped urging her to go back.
translation_verse: Naomi aa naa kɛŋɔ Rut marɛ o nɛɛ kɛŋɔ o ne ó kaa la, o ta wobɛlbwa bolɛ kpa.

english_verse: They reached Bethlehem, and the whole town was excited to see them. The women who lived there asked, “Can this really be Naomi?”
translation_verse: Anomanta, haahna banɛ nɔ valɔ dɛ ba tel Bɛtlɛham, asɛ bwɛɛ la tena bwa lɔ kpu dɛɛ pɛɛ ŋɔ, “Naomii nɔ tenaa?”

english_verse: Then she told them, “Don't call me Naomi any longer! Call me Mara, because God has made my life bitter.
translation_verse: Asɛ o chaŋe ŋɔ, “He bɛ men Naomi yerɛ. Hɛɛ yer mɛ Mara dɛkalkɛ Korowii Waa Ɛ Kpeɡri Bwa Dɔɔ ta ɡelɛ n sie lɛ n soɡa bini.

english_verse: I had everything when I left, but the Lord has brought me back with nothing. How can you still call me Naomi, when God has turned against me and made my life so hard?”
translation_verse: Maa dɛ le bonɔ dɛ́ kaa la, dɛ n dɔ kwaa kohona. Kɛ Korowii ɡelɔ n valɛ nɔŋɡbala ba. Ɛrɛɛ Korowii Waa Ɛ Kpeɡri Bwa Dɔɔ ɛɛ mɛ nyuchɔɡe te dɛ ɡel mɛɛ na wahala nɔ, asɛ hɛɛ yer mɛ Naomi nɔɔ?”

english_verse: The barley harvest was just beginning when Naomi and Ruth, her Moabite daughter-in-law, arrived in Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Gɛɛ a do Naomi ne o helahaah Rut waa ɛ Moab te la ɛ dɛ ba Bɛtlɛham. Dɛ mea koma dɛ pa mun.

english_verse: When Boaz arrived from Bethlehem and went out to his field, he said to the harvest workers, “The Lord bless you!” They replied, “And may the Lord bless you!”
translation_verse: Baa lɔ bela la, Boas le dem ba, dɛ ba jam tom-ɛɛra la, dɛ ŋɔ, “Hé jam ne ɛɛ. Korowii dɛ kwaa he kwa.” Asɛ ba ɡe sɛh ŋɔ, “Korowii tɛɛ hɛɛra.”

english_verse: Then Boaz asked the man in charge of the harvest workers, “Who is that young woman?”
translation_verse: Belaa o bɔɔ tom-ɛɛra la nomoa ŋɔ, “Tolo besoo ɡee lɔ bela nɔɔ?”

english_verse: The man answered, “She is the one who came back from Moab with Naomi.
translation_verse: Anee o chaŋe ŋɔ, “Bitolo bɛl waa le Moab harɛ ta dɛ teŋɛ Naomi nɛɛ ba laanee.

english_verse: She asked if she could pick up grain left by the harvest workers, and she has been working all morning without a moment's rest.”
translation_verse: O baa soŋ mɛ ŋɔ ń ɡel ó teŋɛ tom-ɛɛra nɔ nɛ, ásɛ dɛɛ kuuh anɔ la aa leera la. Chɔɔ bwaa o le ɛ toma asɛ dɛ baa onɛ pata bini tama la.”

english_verse: Boaz went over to Ruth and said, “I think it would be best for you not to pick up grain in anyone else's field. Stay here with the women
translation_verse: Asɛ Boas suuh tel Rut dɛ ŋɔ, “Bɛ koo bɛlbwa ta la ka kuuh mea kpa ka ja koo nɔ ta. Dɛɛ teŋɛ haahna baa dɛ ɛ toma koo nɔ ta nɔ nɛ.

english_verse: and follow along behind them, as they gather up what the men have cut. I have warned the men not to bother you, and whenever you are thirsty, you can drink from their water jars.”
translation_verse: Dɛɛ do sie baala la nɛ, dɛɛ teŋɛ toli la nɛ. N ŋɔ baala la be ŋɔ ba bɛ hen panya. Nyɔɡre dɛ kpoe naa, ka nyɔ nee baa dɔa ba nɔ ane.”

english_verse: Ruth bowed down to the ground and said, “You know I come from another country. Why are you so good to me?”
translation_verse: Belaa Rut ɡuŋu harɛ dɛ ŋɔ, “Jam kɛŋɔ maa ɛ hɔɔh n ɡe waa hiaih ɡɛ nɔ.”

english_verse: Boaz answered, “I've heard how you've helped your mother-in-law ever since your husband died. You even left your own father and mother to come and live in a foreign land among people you don't know.
translation_verse: Asɛ Boas chaŋe ŋɔ, “He jaa seo habɔɔ la, n no waa bwa haa ɛa dɛ tɛ he helahaah. N no ɡɛ haa ɡel he nya ne he mɛɛ, ne harɛ haa le o ta, dɛ ba so nɛra haa wola ban jemɛ bwa bini nɔ.

english_verse: I pray that the Lord God of Israel will reward you for what you have done. And now that you have come to him for protection, I pray that he will bless you.”
translation_verse: Korowiirii dɛ́ tɛɛ he kembɔr he waa la haa ɛa la wa. Korowii Israel tena aa dɛ tomɔ he chwa ba marɔ nɔ, ó tɔ he nɛ kɛ jal yon kpɔ kena tɔ o bii nɛɛ la, dɛ́ kwaa he kwaa tɛɛ kohona.”

english_verse: Ruth replied, “Sir, it's good of you to speak kindly to me and make me feel so welcome. I'm not even one of your servants.”
translation_verse: Anee Rut ŋɔ, “N dɔɔ, a lole kɛŋɔ n ta he tom-ɛɛra la bɛl ɛɛ te, kɛ he nyin n waa kohona, dɛ larawe n bwara ɡe.”

english_verse: At mealtime Boaz said to Ruth, “Come, eat with us. Have some bread and dip it in the sauce.” At once she sat down with the workers, and Boaz handed her some roasted grain. Ruth ate all she wanted and had some left over.
translation_verse: Kondikwaa dii saŋ aa tela la, Boas ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Ba lɛ paanoo tama dɛ́ kpɔ li sennyɛɡa nɔ ta.” O ne tom-ɛɛra la aa soɡa dɛɛ di kwaa la, Boas berɛ kpɔ mea baa hala tɛo ja. O diu dɛ vaɡɛ asɛ ane ka.

english_verse: When Ruth left to start picking up grain, Boaz told his men, “Don't stop her, even if she picks up grain from where it is stacked.
translation_verse: Rut aa baa ir dɛ kuuh mea la la, Boas ŋɔ o bonɔɔna la be ŋɔ, “O ɡaaɡɔ dɛ ka kuuh anɔ la baa boa a nyoa bil la jwɛh kwaraa naa, he bɛ on panya.

english_verse: Be sure to pull out some stalks of grain from the bundles and leave them on the ground for her. And don't speak harshly to her!”
translation_verse: Hɛ́ɛ won tɛr ane le anɔ la haa boa a nyoa bil la ta, ásɛ o ba pa. He bɛ o nɛɛ nyɛɡ.”

english_verse: Ruth worked in the field until evening. Then after she had pounded the grain off the stalks, she had a large basket full of grain.
translation_verse: Anomanta, Rut ɡaaɡe koo la ta dɛ ka tel jɔmɔra. O lɔ mea waa dɔa la bwa asɛ a ɛ kuruware fi.

english_verse: She took the grain to town and showed Naomi how much she had picked up. Ruth also gave her the food left over from her lunch.
translation_verse: O cheɡaa ba dem asɛ o helahaah na ɡɛ del waa dɔa. Rut kpɔ kondikwaa waa dia a ka la ɡe tɛo.

english_verse: Naomi said, “Where did you work today? Whose field was it? God bless the man who treated you so well!” Then Ruth told her that she had worked in the field of a man named Boaz.
translation_verse: Asɛ Naomi bɔɔro ŋɔ, “Leperaa he ka ɡaaɡe fini nɔ? Ume koo taa he ka kuuh dɛ dɔ anɔ bwa ken? Korowiirii dɛ cha naate waa na he sum nɔ.” Anee Rut ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Boas koo taa n ka ɡaaɡe.”

english_verse: “The Lord bless Boaz!” Naomi replied. “He has shown that he is still loyal to the living and to the dead. Boaz is a close relative, one of those who is supposed to look after us.”
translation_verse: Naomi ŋɔ, “Korowiirii dɛ́ kwaa Boas kwaa tɛo. N nao kɛŋɔ Korowii ta teŋɔ dɛɛ nyin weera ne serewa.” Dɛ berɛ ŋɔ, “A ɡɛ baa la ɛ ya lole tenten. O ɛ nɛra baa chɛ kɛŋɔ báa nyiŋi ya nɛɛ la bini bɛl.”

english_verse: Ruth told her, “Boaz even said I could stay in the field with his workers until they had finished harvesting all his grain.”
translation_verse: Belaa Rut ŋɔ, “Silɛɛ wa aa jaa laanee kɛŋɔ, o ŋɔ ń teŋɛ o tom-ɛɛra nɛɛ dɛɛ kuuh mea ka tel kɛŋɔ baa teŋe tonɛ.”

english_verse: Naomi replied, “My daughter, it's good that you can pick up grain alongside the women who work in his field. Who knows what might happen to you in someone else's field!”
translation_verse: Naomi ɡe ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Kasinteŋii, a wer kɛŋɔ he ne toli la bwa pɛ dɛɛ ɛ toma Boas koo ta. He la nomɛl koo ta naa, ba ken ɛɛ panyae.”

english_verse: And so, Ruth stayed close to the women, while picking up grain in his field. Ruth worked in the fields until the barley and wheat were harvested. And all this time she lived with Naomi.
translation_verse: Gɛɛ a do o ne ba ɛ toma asɛ o kuuh mea la ka tel saŋ baa koma tonɛ. Asɛ o so o helahaah be.

english_verse: One day, Naomi said to Ruth: It's time I found you a husband, who will give you a home and take care of you.
translation_verse: Awola bɛl, Naomi ŋɔ Rut be ŋɔ, “N bie, a chɛ kɛ ń nyin jaa tɛɛ ásɛ he ne ó so.

english_verse: You have been picking up grain alongside the women who work for Boaz, and you know he is a relative of ours. Tonight he will be threshing the grain.
translation_verse: Baa n liire aa lɔ o nɛɛ laanee Boas he ne o toli aa pɛa dɛɛ ɛ toma la, o ɛ ya lole. Fini jwaana nɔ ne o dɛ ba mea lɔe.

english_verse: Now take a bath and put on some perfume, then dress in your best clothes. Go where he is working, but don't let him see you until he has finished eating and drinking.
translation_verse: Anomanta, sɔ ne dɛ́ fɔɡle nosɔɔhsoma dɛ́ do he laaladɛɛɡa dɛ́ kaa bela. Bɛ ɡel o nae ka tel kɛŋɔ waa di kondikwaa dɛ nyɔ sen tonɛ mɔɔ.

english_verse: Watch where he goes to spend the night, then when he is asleep, lift the cover and lie down at his feet. He will tell you what to do.
translation_verse: Pese bela waa chɔ, ásɛ waa ba chɔ dom la, hé ka laa yal kpɔ o nakpale ta, dɛ́ chɔ o naa bɔr. Wɛɛ ŋɔ he bee ɡɛ haa ɛ.”

english_verse: Ruth answered, “I'll do whatever you say.”
translation_verse: Asɛ Rut ŋɔ, “Mɛɛ ɛ wobɛlbwa haa bol n be nɔɔ.”

english_verse: She went out to the place where Boaz was working and did what Naomi had told her.
translation_verse: Anomanta, o la pɛla la ta jwaana la ne la, asɛ dɛ ka ɛ ɡɛ Naomi aa baɡlo la.

english_verse: After Boaz finished eating and drinking and was feeling happy, he went over and fell asleep near the pile of grain. Ruth slipped over quietly. She lifted the cover and lay down near his feet.
translation_verse: Boas aa di kondikwaa la dɛ nyɔ sen o sie lɛ la, o kaa chɔ mea baa boa a nyoa bil la jwɛh. Asɛ Rut ɛ bɔeeh dɛ ka laa yal kpɔ o nakpale ta dɛ chɔ bela.

english_verse: In the middle of the night, Boaz suddenly woke up and was shocked to see a woman lying at his feet.
translation_verse: Boas aa chɔa harambaŋa baah ta la, o jarɔ dɛ na kɛŋɔ haah chɔ o naa bɔr.

english_verse: “Who are you?” he asked. “Sir, I am Ruth,” she answered, “and you are the relative who is supposed to take care of me. So spread the edge of your cover over me.”
translation_verse: Anee o bɔɔ ŋɔ, “Umee nɔɔ?” Asɛ Rut chaŋe ŋɔ, “Menee he bitolo Rut. Haa ɛ n lole tenten nɔ, paɡri he yal la pera bɔle n nɛ.”

english_verse: Boaz replied: The Lord bless you! This shows how truly loyal you are to your family. You could have looked for a younger man, either rich or poor, but you didn't.
translation_verse: Asɛ Boas ŋɔ, “Korowii tɛɛ hɛɛra. He baɡle he nyina ɡwaa ɡɛ haa ɛa tɛ he helahaah la kwara. Bonɔɔna nɛɛ chɛ kɛ he fe ɛɛ pɛlɛ, hale ba dɔ suuɡa kɛɛ ba nyao. Kɛ he ta an ɡɛ ɛɛ.

english_verse: Don't worry, I'll do what you have asked. You are respected by everyone in town.
translation_verse: N bie, bɛ ɡel a hiaih. Mɛɛ ɛ wobɛlbwa haa dɛ nyinii tɛɛ, dɛkalkɛ nɛra baa lɔ bwɛɛ nɔ ta bwa jemɛ ɡɛ he wa aa do kaih.

english_verse: It's true that I am one of the relatives who is supposed to take care of you, but there is someone who is an even closer relative.
translation_verse: A ɛ kasinteŋ kɛŋɔ ya ɛ lolanar. Kɛ bɛl tɔ n sie mɔɔ n teŋɛ.

english_verse: Stay here until morning, then I will find out if he is willing to look after you. If he isn't, I promise by the living God to do it myself. Now go back to sleep until morning.
translation_verse: Chɔ n be bonɔ jwaana nɔ ne, ásɛ tɔɔ perɔ chɔɔ aa, ya na kɛŋɔ wɛɛ moe kɛɛ waa hen moɔ. O sɛoh ŋɔ wɛɛ kpɔe yaa, a fe wer kohona. Kɛ dɛ o ta sɛɛh yaa, n ŋwɛɛ Korowii waa lole saŋ bɛlbwa kɛŋɔ mɛɛ kpɔe. He te chɔ bonɔ ka tel kere chɔɔ.”

english_verse: Ruth lay down again, but she got up before daylight, because Boaz did not want anyone to know she had been there.
translation_verse: Anomanta, o chɔ o naa bɔr bela asɛ dɛ fel ir chɔmbibii bɛlbwa ta on nae, dɛkalkɛ Boas ŋɔ o be ŋɔ waa nyin kɛ nɛra jemɛ kɛŋɔ haah ba pɛla la ta.

english_verse: Then he told her to spread out her cape. And he filled it with grain and placed it on her shoulder. When Ruth got back to town,
translation_verse: Asɛ Boas ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Foo he batakaare ásɛ dɛ paɡru.” Waa paɡru la, asɛ o fuɡe mea dɛ ɛ kuruwa anue doo o kpɔ kaa dem.

english_verse: She also said, “Boaz gave me this grain, because he didn't want me to come back without something for you.”
translation_verse: O ŋɔ, “O tɛ mɛ mea nɔ ŋɔ ń kpɔ ba, dɛ ŋɔ a ta chɛɛ kɛŋɔ n valɛ nɔŋɡbala ba he be ɡɛ.”

english_verse: Naomi replied, “Just be patient and don't worry about what will happen. He won't rest until everything is settled today!”
translation_verse: Anee Naomi ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “N bie, lawɛ bambile dɛ́ na ɡɛ aa ka chiɡ. Dɛ Boas ta waa nɔ sie nae fini naa, o ta ona dɔe.”

english_verse: In the meanwhile, Boaz had gone to the meeting place at the town gate and was sitting there when the other close relative came by. So Boaz invited him to come over and sit down, and he did.
translation_verse: Boas la bwɛɛ la doonyoa baa soɡa dɛɛ kpɔ liire la, dɛ ka so bela. Belaa baa la Boas fa aa ŋɔa on tɔ sie o ɡe teŋɛ dɛ dɔ Rut nyiŋa la den baa kaa, asɛ o yerɔ dɛ ŋɔ, “N dam, ba so n be bonɔ tama.” Asɛ o ɡe la dɛ ka so o be bela.

english_verse: Then Boaz got ten of the town leaders and also asked them to sit down. After they had sat down,
translation_verse: Belaa Boas ka yerɛ bwɛɛ la nomonome fi ba ba ja o nɛ ba bwa soŋni, ba bwa aa baa soŋni la,

english_verse: he said to the man: Naomi has come back from Moab and is selling the land that belonged to her husband Elimelech.
translation_verse: o ŋɔ o lole la be ŋɔ, “Taraken Naomi aa le Moab harɛ ta dɛ ba nɔ, o dɛ nyin o yoɡ ya lole Ɛlemɛlɛk koo la,

english_verse: I'm telling you about this, since you are his closest relative and have the right to buy the property. If you want it, you can buy it now. These ten men and the others standing here can be witnesses. But if you don't want the property, let me know, because I am next in line. The man replied, “I'll buy it!”
translation_verse: mɛɛ nyin kɛ he ɡe jemɛ a wa. Dɛ he ɡbabir dɛ nyin koo la aa, n dɛ nyin kɛŋɔ he den yawɛ ya ne nomonome nɔ bwa sie bonɔ. Dɛ haa nyin ɡe aa, ɡel ya jemɛ, dɛkalkɛ dɛ nomɛlbwa ɛɛ won yawɛ aa, atane o tɔ sie nae mɔɔ ásɛ n ɡe teŋɛ.” Anee o sɛh ŋɔ “Mɛɛ yawɔɔ.”

english_verse: “If you do buy it from Naomi,” Boaz told him, “you must also marry Ruth. Then if you have a son by her, the property will stay in the family of Ruth's first husband.”
translation_verse: Asɛ Boas ŋɔ, “Gɛ wer, kɛ dɛ he yawɛ harɛ la le Naomi ne Rut waa ɛ Moab te la be tenaa, hɛɛ kpɔ ya lole waa sewa la luhaah Rut la ɡee ja, ásɛ he ne o dɔ bie ya lole la sɔn bɛ he harɛ la ta.”

english_verse: The man answered, “If that's the case, I don't want to buy it! That would make problems with the property I already own. You may buy it yourself, because I cannot.”
translation_verse: Belaa baa la chaŋe ŋɔ, “Mɛɛ yawɔɔ n bii aa harɛ la kpeɡrii ba dɔ tenaa, maa won. Hɛɛ wonoo waa, he yawɛ.”

english_verse: To make a sale legal in those days, one person would take off a sandal and give it to the other.
translation_verse: Dɛ a saŋ la Israel tena nawee waa kɛŋɔ dɛ nomɛl dɔ o komɛl dɛɛ nyin o yoɡ asɛ nɛra cheme ken aa, o dɛ foo o naŋɡawa, dɛ́ kpɔ tɛ nɛn waa dɛ yawɛ la á ɛ danseɛ.

english_verse: So after the man had agreed to let Boaz buy the property, he took off one of his sandals and handed it to Boaz.

english_verse: Boaz told the town leaders and everyone else: All of you are witnesses that today I have bought from Naomi the property that belonged to Elimelech and his two sons, Chilion and Mahlon.
translation_verse: Belaa Boas bol nomonome ne nɛra baa cheme bela la bwa no kɛŋɔ, “Heyaa ɛɛ mɛ danseɛ fini tɔpere nɔ, kɛŋɔ n yawɛ Ɛlemɛlɛk komɛlbwa ne o bibaala Keleɔn ne Maalɔn kwaa bwa le Naomi be.

english_verse: The town leaders and the others standing there said: We are witnesses to this. And we pray that the Lord will give your wife many children, just as he did Leah and Rachel, the wives of Jacob. May you be a rich man in the tribe of Ephrath and an important man in Bethlehem.

translation_verse: Anee haahna la ŋɔ Naomi be ŋɔ, “Korowii jam kɛŋɔ fini waa tɛɛ lole tenten wáa di he kwaa nɔ. Korowiirii dɛ́ ɡel o sɔn le Israel harɛ ta bwa!

english_verse: He will make you happy and take care of you in your old age, because he is the son of your daughter-in-law. And she loves you more than seven sons of your own would love you.
translation_verse: Wɛɛ tɛɛ silɛɛ, ásɛ dɛ lawɛ kpoŋe he hwɛɛhra bini. Dɛkalkɛ Rut waa dɛ nyini lolɛ bibeŋkpoŋ ɡwaa he be kɛŋɔ he fe aa lolɛ bibaala banuanɛ.”

english_verse: Naomi loved the boy and took good care of him.
translation_verse: Asɛ Naomi lɛ bie la dɛɛ nyiŋu.

english_verse: Elkanah lived in Ramah, a town in the hill country of Ephraim. His great-great-grandfather was Zuph, so Elkanah was a member of the Zuph clan of the Ephraim tribe. Elkanah's father was Jeroham, his grandfather was Elihu, and his great-grandfather was Tohu.
