translation_verse: Baa bɛlee fa lole baa yerɔ Ɛlkana, o le Efrem dea. Dɛ o soɡe Rama waa lɔ Efrem deŋɡarere harɛ ta. O mɛɛ sɔne Jɛroham, o nabaa ɡe sɔne Elihu. Elihu ɡe mɛɛ Tohu, asɛ Tohu ɡe mɛɛ sɔne Suf.

english_verse: Elkanah had two wives, Hannah and Peninnah. Although Peninnah had children, Hannah did not have any.
translation_verse: Dɛ Ɛlkana mo haahna banɛ. Bɛl sɔne Hana, asɛ nɛɛte ɡe Pɛnena. Pɛnena dɔ bii, asɛ Hana te ta bie dɔe.

english_verse: Once a year Elkanah traveled from his hometown to Shiloh, where he worshiped the Lord All-Powerful and offered sacrifices. Eli was the Lord's priest there, and his two sons Hophni and Phinehas served with him as priests.
translation_verse: Bena bɛlbwaa Ɛlkana yon le o bwɛɛ Rama kaa bwɛjen Silo, dɛ́ ka tomɛ Korowii Waa Ɛ Koranar Bwa Kooro dɛ kpoo kwaa ɛ saraha tɛo. Dɛ Eli ɛ sɔfo, dɛ dɔ bibaala banɛ bane ba ɡe aa ɛ sɔfore. Bɛl sɔne Hofni nɛɛte ɡe Fenehas.

english_verse: Whenever Elkanah offered a sacrifice, he gave some of the meat to Peninnah and some to each of her sons and daughters.
translation_verse: Saŋ bɛlbwa waa ka kpoo kwaa ɛ saraha la, o yon kpɔ o ola waa dɔa la ane ba tɛ Pɛnena, dɛ kpɔ ane ɡe tɛ bii la bɛlbwa.

english_verse: But he gave Hannah even more, because he loved Hannah very much, even though the Lord had kept her from having children of her own.
translation_verse: A lole kɛŋɔ dɛ Korowii ta ɡelɛ Hana dɔ bii te, dɛ Ɛlkana dɛ nyinu taeh, anomanta, o yon tɛo bɔre anɛ.

english_verse: Peninnah liked to make Hannah feel miserable about not having any children,
translation_verse: Waa wola bii dɔe nomanta, Penina waa ɛ o toŋre la yon dɛɛ ɛo sisawa dɛɛ muɡli o baah.

english_verse: especially when the family went to the house of the Lord each year. One day, Elkanah was there offering a sacrifice, when Hannah began crying and refused to eat.
translation_verse: Bena bɛlbwaa Penina na dɛɛ ɛo ɡɛ waa nɔ. Saŋ bɛlbwa baa la Korowii Dea kaa tomɔ la, o yon muɡli o baah ó wi, hale dɛ́ vɛh kondikwaa kwaraa dii.

english_verse: So Elkanah asked, “Hannah, why are you crying? Why won't you eat? Why do you feel so bad? Don't I mean more to you than ten sons?”
translation_verse: O jaa yon bɔɔro ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ hɛɛ wiɔ? Bɔkwa waa he ŋɔ haa kwaa diɔ? Saŋ bɛlbwa he bambile yon chɔɡ kohona ɡɛ nɔ wer aa? N ne he soɡa nɔ ta ɡwaalɛ kɛ he fe aa lolɛ bibaala fi aa?”

english_verse: When the sacrifice had been offered, and they had eaten the meal, Hannah got up and went to pray. Eli was sitting in his chair near the door to the place of worship.
translation_verse: Awola bɛl, ba di saraha kondikwaa bwɛjen Silo bela tonɛ, asɛ Hana ir dɛ kaa soŋe Korowii. Dɛ sɔfo Eli soɡe kara ta Korowii Dea doonyoa la jwɛh.

english_verse: Hannah was heartbroken and was crying as she prayed,
translation_verse: Dɛ o bambile chɔɡɔ kɛrɛdɛ, o wi dɛɛ soŋe Korowii.

english_verse: “Lord All-Powerful, I am your servant, but I am so miserable! Please let me have a son. I promise to give him to you for as long as he lives, and his hair will never be cut.”
translation_verse: Belaa Hana baɡɛ Korowii nyoa ŋɔ, “Nemenɛ Korowii, na n sum, bɛ n waa soh. No he tolo wa, dɛ́ tɛ mɛ bibaa, ásɛ n leo cheɡ tɛɛ o soɡa bini bwa, baa o nyumpon beŋkpoŋ kwaraa fonɛ bwa.”

english_verse: Hannah prayed silently to the Lord for a long time. But her lips were moving, and Eli thought she was drunk.
translation_verse: Dɛ o pili nyoa dɛɛ soŋe Korowii, kɛ dɛ wobol la aa baŋ le. A ɡelɔ sɔfo Eli lii kɛŋɔ o ken nyɔ sen dɛɛ,

english_verse: “How long are you going to stay drunk?” he asked. “Sober up!”
translation_verse: dɛ bɔɔro ŋɔ, “Haa won teŋɛ dɛ dɛɛ dɛɛ la ken. Gel sen nyɔe, dɛ́ ɡel he sie chɔ harɛ.”

english_verse: Eli replied, “Go home. Everything will be fine. The God of Israel will answer your prayer.”
translation_verse: Ate, sɔfo Eli ŋɔ, “Kaa deŋnesɔɔhna ne, Korowii Israel tena aa dɛ tomɔ la tɛɛ komɛlbwa haa dɛ nyin.”

english_verse: “Sir, thank you for being so kind to me,” Hannah said. Then she left, and after eating something, she felt much better. Samuel Is Born
translation_verse: Hana chaŋe ŋɔ, “N dɔɔ, ɡel he sie lɛ he bitolo nɛ.” Asɛ o le bela kaa, dɛ ka nyin kondikwaa di, asɛ bambichɔɡ la bwa kaa.

english_verse: Elkanah and his family got up early the next morning and worshiped the Lord. Then they went back home to Ramah. Later the Lord blessed Elkanah and Hannah
translation_verse: Tɔɔ aa pera chɔmbibii la, Ɛlkana ne o haahna ne bii iro dɛ ka tomɛ Korowii dɛ berɛ ba kaa Rama bela baa soɡa. Ɛlkana ne Hana chɔɔ, asɛ Korowii no o wesoŋa la.

english_verse: with a son. She named him Samuel because she had asked the Lord for him. Hannah Gives Samuel to the Lord
translation_verse: Gɛɛ a do o kpoŋe tea, dɛ lolɛ bibaa dɛ pa o sɔn Samoɛl, dɛ ŋɔ, “Korowiirii n soŋe o tɛ mɛ.”

english_verse: The next time Elkanah and his family went to offer their yearly sacrifice, he took along a gift that he had promised to give to the Lord.
translation_verse: Bena bɛl telo ja kɛŋɔ Ɛlkana ne o haahna ne bii kaa bwɛjen Silo ka ɛ benanyoa saraha tɛ Korowii, ásɛ dɛ ka chuɡri o nyobaɡa la ɡe.

english_verse: But Hannah stayed home, because she had told Elkanah, “Samuel and I won't go until he's old enough for me to stop nursing him. Then I'll give him to the Lord, and he can stay there at Shiloh for the rest of his life.”
translation_verse: Baa dɛ kaa la, Hana te ta bɛl jae dɛ́ la. Dɛ o tɔ sie ŋɔ o jaa be ŋɔ, “N baa teŋe bie la el aa, mɛɛ kpɔɔ kaa Korowii Dea ó den ka so bela kwaraa.”

english_verse: “You know what's best,” Elkanah said. “Stay here until it's time to stop nursing him. I'm sure the Lord will help you do what you have promised.” Hannah did not go to Shiloh until she stopped nursing Samuel.
translation_verse: Anee sɔfo Ɛlkana chaŋo ŋɔ, “A wer, ɛ ɡɛ bwa aa too he tea. So dem ka tel kɛŋɔ haa teŋe bie la el. Korowii sɛh he nyobaɡa la ta tɛɛ.” Anomanta, Hana soɡe dem ka tel kɛ waa baa teŋe bie la el.

english_verse: “Sir,” Hannah said, “a few years ago I stood here beside you and asked the Lord
translation_verse: asɛ Hana bɔɔ sɔfo Eli ŋɔ, “N poori, n dɔɔ, he dɛ lii mɛ naa? Menee he faa na n che bonɔ dɛɛ soŋe Korowii la.

english_verse: to give me a child. Here he is! The Lord gave me just what I asked for.
translation_verse: N kpɔɔ bil Korowii sie ŋɔ ó tɛ mɛ bie nɔ, asɛ o sɛh n nyoa dɛ tɛ mɛ.

english_verse: Now I am giving him to the Lord, and he will be the Lord's servant for as long as he lives.” Hannah Prays Elkanah worshiped the Lord there at Shiloh, and
translation_verse: Le fini dɛɛ kaa, n leo cheɡ tɛ Korowii, wɛɛ ɛ Korowii konee o soɡa bini bwa.” Asɛ ba tomɛ Korowii bela.

english_verse: Hannah prayed: You make me strong and happy, Lord. You rescued me. Now I can be glad and laugh at my enemies.
translation_verse: Anee Hana jam Korowii ŋɔ, “N Naa Korowii, he ɡelɔ n sie lɛ kohona, n sie lɛ waa haa ɛa wa! He ɡelɔ n sie lɛ mɛɛ mamɛ n dɔma, lɛɛ haa lɛɛ mɛ la wa.

english_verse: No other god is like you. And with you we are safer than on a high mountain.
translation_verse: Nomɛlbwa toole dɛ do ɡoroŋ kɛ hen Korowii, he habɔɔ nɛn toole, Lɛɛ bɛlbwa toole kɛ hen Korowii haa ɛ Bwetal yaa tomɛ nɔ.

english_verse: I can tell those proud people, “Stop your boasting! Nothing is hidden from the Lord, and he judges what we do.”
translation_verse: Gel mbarafo wobol bola, bɛ wobosale dɛɛ bol. Hen Korowii te, he jemɛ wobɛlbwa, he jemɛ wobɛlbwa nɛn aa dɛ ɛ, dɛɛ pa a bole.

english_verse: Our Lord, you break the bows of warriors, but you give strength to everyone who stumbles.
translation_verse: He kuuɡi banyoola tori, dɛ ɡel nɛra baa ɡwɛɡra dɔ bokpeɡa.

english_verse: People who once had plenty to eat must now hire themselves out for only a piece of bread. But you give the hungry more than enough to eat. A woman did not have a child, and you gave her seven, but a woman who had many was left with none.
translation_verse: Nɛra ba fa aa dɔ kondikwaa kohona la, ba ɛ toma tɛ ba bala mɔɔ dɛɛ di kwa, banɔ la ba fa aa dɛ chɔ lɔr ɡe dɔ dɛɛ di name. Hambara wono lolɛ bii banuanɛ, onɔ la waa dɔ bibaala kohona ɡe ta dɔe kpa.

english_verse: You take away life, and you give life. You send people down to the world of the dead and bring them back again.
translation_verse: Hen Korowiirii dɛɛ kpo, dɛ́ berɛ tɛ mkpa, henee ɡela nɛra sewɛ baa huɡ ba, dɛ́ berɛ ir dɛ́ dɔ mkpa.

english_verse: Our Lord, you are the one who makes us rich or poor. You put some in high positions and bring disgrace on others.
translation_verse: Henee ɡela nɛra ɛɛ nya, dɛ́ berɛ ɛ bane kondɔɔhna, dɛ́ lɔ nɛra harɛ dɛ́ berɛ ɡɔɔ bane ɡe.

english_verse: You lift the poor and homeless out of the garbage dump and give them places of honor in royal palaces. You set the world on foundations, and they belong to you.
translation_verse: He lawɛ nɛra baa nyaa le ba nyaa bini, dɛ lɛɛ ba dɛɛ le ba sum ta. He ɡelɔ nɛŋɡwɛɡra ne koranar pɛ dɛɛ so, dɛ ɡel baa dɔ jirima. Hen Korowii dɔ kwaa aa lawɛ harɛ nɔ kpoŋe kpeɡri, a taa he ma harɛ nɔ chɔŋɛ.

english_verse: You protect your loyal people, but everyone who is evil will die in darkness. We cannot win a victory by our own strength.
translation_verse: He dɛ tɔ he nɛra ba wa aa toɡra ɡbemɡbe, kɛ nyubinikpeɡ tena te, he dɛ kpoo ba. Nɛn aa won che o bokpeɡa ta ɛ wobɛlbwa.

english_verse: Our Lord, those who attack you will be broken in pieces when you fight back with thunder from heaven. You will judge the whole earth and give power and strength to your chosen king. Samuel Stays with Eli
translation_verse: Nɛra baa ɛ hen Korowii dɔm bwa ɛɛ serewoo, hɛɛ kɔro kɛŋɔ bwaala le nyundua, dɛ́ ba chɔɡ ba. Hen Korowiirii dɛ́ ba bol harɛ nɔ nɛra bwa waa dɛ́ pa bole. Hɛɛ tɛ he kooro haa leo cheɡ kpeɡrii ó pɔ o dɔma nɛ.”

english_verse: Elkanah and Hannah went back home to Ramah, but the boy Samuel stayed to help Eli serve the Lord. Eli's Sons
translation_verse: Belaa Ɛlkana ne Hana berɛ kaa Rama bela baa soɡa. Kɛ Samoɛl te soɡe Silo bela sɔfo Eli be, dɛɛ ɛ Korowii toma. Sɔfo Eli bibaala wa

english_verse: Eli's sons were priests, but they were dishonest and refused to obey the Lord. So, while people were boiling the meat from their sacrifices, these priests would send over a servant with a large, three-pronged fork.
translation_verse: Waa aa chɔ le tɛ nɛra baa ba kpo kwaa ɛ saraha a do bane sɔfore baah laanee kɛŋɔ, ol la taa chɔŋɛ nii ta la, sɔfo bonɔɔ waa lɔ o sie la yon kpɔ buni o nyoo aa ɛ atoro kpoŋe.

english_verse: The servant would stick the fork into the cooking pot, and whatever meat came out on the fork was taken back to Eli's two sons. That was how they treated every Israelite who came to offer sacrifices in Shiloh.
translation_verse: Wɛɛ taɡɔɔ su ola la bini, asɛ bɛlbwa waa le o ne la ɛ sɔfo la kon. Dɛ ɡɛɛ ba kpɔ dɛɛ ɛ Israel tena baa ba Silo bela baa ɛ saraha bwa.

english_verse: Sometimes, when people were offering sacrifices, the servant would come over, even before the fat had been cut off and sacrificed to the Lord. Then the servant would tell them, “The priest doesn't want his meat boiled! Give him some raw meat that he can roast!”
translation_verse: Mɔɔ baa fuh ol la noo la, sɔfo la bonɔɔ yon ba naate waa ba dɛ ɛ saraha la be ŋɔ, “Tɛ mɛ ol n ka wɔɔ tɛ sɔfo, waa ondaale nyin, atane onlwɛɛ.”

english_verse: Usually the people answered, “Take what you want. But first, let us sacrifice the fat to the Lord.” “No,” the servant would reply. “If you don't give it to me now, I'll take it by force.”
translation_verse: Dɛ nɛn waa baa ɛ saraha la ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Fuh ol la noo tonɛ mɔɔ, dɛ́ kpɔ onɔ la haa dɛ nyin” aa, bonɔɔ la ɛɛ chaŋoo ŋɔ, “Akai, kpɔ tɛ mɛ taraken, dɛ ɡɛ laa aa, amɔ te kpeɡri nee mɛɛ ba kpɔe.”

english_verse: Eli's sons did not show any respect for the sacrifices that the people offered. This was a terrible sin, and it made the Lord very angry. Hannah Visits Samuel
translation_verse: Sɔfo Eli bibaala wechɔɡa baa do kan Korowii sie. Dɛ ba ta ɡelɛ duure do kwaa baa kpɔa ba ɛ saraha dɛɛ tɛ Korowii la ta.

english_verse: The boy Samuel served the Lord and wore a special linen garment
translation_verse: Gɛ saŋ dɛ Samoɛl ta ɛ bechala dɛ do sɔfo batakaarebora efɔd baa kpɔ yapondɛɛɡe nyarɔ dɛɛ ɛ Korowii toma.

english_verse: and the clothes his mother made for him. She brought new clothes every year, when she and her husband came to offer sacrifices at Shiloh.
translation_verse: Bena bɛlbwa, o nya ne o mɛɛ dɛ́ la ka ɛ saraha tɛ Korowii Silo aa, o nya yon nyarɛ batakaarebora ka tɛo.

english_verse: Eli always blessed Elkanah and his wife and said, “Samuel was born in answer to your prayers. Now you have given him to the Lord. I pray that the Lord will bless you with more children to take his place.” After Eli had blessed them, Elkanah and Hannah would return home.
translation_verse: Sɔfo Eli yon swee andɛɛɡa tɛ Ɛlkana ne o haah ŋɔ, “Korowii ɡel he ne haah nɔ dɔ bii, bá ba chiɡ onɔ haa soŋo o waa dɛ kpɔ ba tɛo nɔ naa ta.” Ásɛ o ne haah la bwa yon berɛ kaa ba bwɛ.

english_verse: The Lord was kind to Hannah, and she had three more sons and two daughters. But Samuel grew up at the Lord's house in Shiloh. Eli Warns His Sons
translation_verse: Korowii na Hana sum dɛ tɛo bibaala batoro dɛ bihaahna banɛ. Samoɛl lɔ Silo bela Korowii sie dɛɛ tomɔ, dɛ ba kpeɡ.

english_verse: Eli was now very old, and he heard what his sons were doing to the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Sɔfo Eli baa hwɛɛh name, dɛ no waa o bibaala la aa kpɔa dɛɛ ɛ Israel tena bwa, ne ɡɛ baa lawɛ haahna baa dɛ ɛ toma Korowii Dea Cheremibɔr doonyoa bela dɛɛ chɔ.

english_verse: “Why are you doing these awful things?” he asked them. “I've been hearing nothing but complaints about you from all of the Lord's people.
translation_verse: Akai, n bii, he bwara wechɔɡa maa dɛ no Korowii nɛra nyoo la perɛ harɛ nɔ ta bwa.

english_verse: If you harm another person, God can help make things right between the two of you. But if you commit a crime against the Lord, no one can help you!” But the Lord had already decided to kill them. So he kept them from listening to their father. A Prophet Speaks to Eli
translation_verse: Nɛn ɛ o dɔŋ wechɔɡa aa, Korowiirii dɛ́ won kwaa ba baah. Kɛ dɛ nɛn ɛ Korowii wechɔɡa aa, nɛn toole dɛ́ cha naate kpa.” Bii la ta ba mɛɛ kaeh waa kah ba la noɛ, dɛ Korowiirii ɛa ɡɛ dɛ́ kpoo ba.

english_verse: Each day, as Samuel grew older, the Lord was pleased with him, and so were the people.
translation_verse: Samoɛl nao dɛ ɡee kpeɡ, o waa do wer Korowii ne nɛwɛnyini bwa be. Waa Korowii aa bola dɛ chɔɡ Eli ne o dem tena

english_verse: One day a prophet came to Eli and gave him this message from the Lord: When your ancestors were slaves of the king of Egypt, I came and showed them who I am.
translation_verse: Awola Korowii keame bɛl Korowii aa pili waane bini baɡlo ba sɔfo Eli be dɛ ba ŋɔ, “Waa Korowii aa dɛ bol laanee nɔ, ‘N fa ta n te kpɔe baɡle he naawa kɛrɛdɛ Ijipt harɛ ta ɡɛ saŋ baa lɔ Ijipt kooro lɔɡa la aa?

english_verse: Out of all the tribes of Israel, I chose your family to be my priests. I wanted them to offer sacrifices and burn incense to me and to find out from me what I want my people to do. I commanded everyone to bring their sacrifices here where I live, and I allowed you and your family to keep those that were not offered to me on the altar. But you honor your sons instead of me! You don't respect the sacrifices and offerings that are brought to me, and you've all grown fat from eating the best parts.
translation_verse: Ɛrɛɛ n saraha kwaa ne kwaa baa dɛ kpoora, n lea cheɡ ŋɔ bá kpɔ baa tɛ mɛ bela maa lole la, he nyiŋa dɛɛ vah nɔɔ? He duu he bibaala dɛɛ ɡwaa mɛ, saraha kwaa n nɛra Israel tena aa kpɔa baa tɛ mɛ la, he kpɔ a bodɛɛɡa bɔra la di dɛ je faɡra.’

english_verse: I am the Lord, the God of Israel. I promised to always let your family serve me as priests, but now I tell you that I cannot do this any longer! I honor anyone who honors me, but I put a curse on anyone who hates me.
translation_verse: Anomanta, men Korowii Israel tena aa dɛ tom mɛ fa baɡɛ heyaa nyoa kɛŋɔ, he dem nɛra ne he mɛɛ dem nɛraa dɛ́ do n sie, dɛ́ɛ tom mɛ kɛ sɔfore saŋ bɛlbwa dɛɛ la. Taraken te maa an ɡɛɛ ɛ kpa. Nɛra baa dɛ duu mɛ la, mɛɛ ɡeloo bá dɔ duure, nɛra baa nyiŋ mɛ dɛɛ vah la, n ɡee nyiŋ baa vah.

english_verse: The time will come when I will kill you and everyone else in your family. Not one of you will live to an old age.
translation_verse: Dɛɛ no, saŋ bɛl dɛ́ ba bala ásɛ n kpoo bonɔɔna baa le dea haa le o ta ne he lolanar bini, ásɛ bɛlbwa aa hwɛɛh he bini kpa.

english_verse: Your family will have a lot of trouble. I will be kind to Israel, but everyone in your family will die young.
translation_verse: Hɛɛ di suna bela maa lole laanee, ásɛ n swee andɛɛɡa tɛ Israel tena baa kaa la. Kɛ he lolanar bini te, bɛlbwa aa kpeɡ dɛ́ ba hwɛɛh bwa.

english_verse: If I let anyone from your family be a priest, his life will be full of sadness and sorrow. But most of the men in your family will die a violent death!
translation_verse: He naanar bini beŋkpoŋii mɛɛ ba ɡela o ɛ n sɔfo. Kɛ mɛɛ ɡeloo ó nyoŋe, o bambile chɔɡ, ásɛ he naanar baa kaa bwa piɡri serewe laa ta ba bonɔɔne saŋ.

english_verse: To prove to you that I will do these things, your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, will die on the same day.
translation_verse: Waa aa pu he bibaala banɛ Hofni ne Fenehas laanee kɛ, ba bwa ɛɛ pɛo sewɛ tɔpebeŋkpoŋ, ásɛ he jemɛ kɛŋɔ waa maa bola la ɛ kasinteŋ.

english_verse: I have chosen someone else to be my priest, someone who will be faithful and obey me. I will always let his family serve as priests and help my chosen king.
translation_verse: N ɡbaɡba ɛɛ le sɔfo o waa aa dɔ kasinteŋ dɛɛ ɛ n bambile bini waa tɛ n te, dɛ́ ɡel o dɔ naanar kohona, ásɛ baa tomɛ kooro maa leo cheɡ tɛ n te la.

english_verse: But if anyone is left from your family, he will come to my priest and beg for money or a little bread. He may even say to my priest, “Please let me be a priest, so I will at least have something to eat.”
translation_verse: Ásɛ nomɛlbwa waa kaa he lolanar bini la ba ɡuŋi sɔfo la sie, dɛ́ soŋo suuɡa ne kondikwa. Dɛ berɛ soŋo ŋɔ ó kpɔɔ sɔfore toma ta, ásɛ o won dɔ kondikwaa dɛɛ di.”

english_verse: and Samuel was sleeping on a mat near the sacred chest in the Lord's house. They had not been asleep very long
translation_verse: Dɛ kandea waa lɔ Korowii Dea Boɡoroŋ la ta dɛ chaah, asɛ Samoɛl chɔ bela Korowii Ne Nɛwɛnyina Fɔo Daka la aa cheɡa.

english_verse: when the Lord called out Samuel's name. “Here I am!” Samuel answered.
translation_verse: Asɛ Korowii yerɛ Samoɛl, o chaŋe ŋɔ, “N dɔɔ, menee la.”

english_verse: Then he ran to Eli and said, “Here I am. What do you want?” “I didn't call you,” Eli answered. “Go back to bed.” Samuel went back.
translation_verse: Ate, o chwa la Eli be ka ŋɔ, “N dɔɔ he yer mɛ, menee la.” Eli chaŋo ŋɔ, “N ta hen yerɛ, berɛ kaa ka chɔ.” Asɛ o berɛ kaa.

english_verse: Again the Lord called out Samuel's name. Samuel got up and went to Eli. “Here I am,” he said. “What do you want?” Eli told him, “Son, I didn't call you. Go back to sleep.”
translation_verse: A habɔɔ Korowii berɛ yerɔ ja, asɛ o ir dɛ la Eli be ka ŋɔ, “N dɔɔ, he yer mɛ, menee la.” Eli chaŋo ŋɔ, “N bie, n ta hen yerɛ, berɛ kaa ka chɔ.”

english_verse: The Lord had not spoken to Samuel before, and Samuel did not recognize the voice.
translation_verse: Dɛ Korowii ta waa Samoɛl be bolɛ bwa mɔɔ, anomanta, dɛ waa jemɛ kɛŋɔ onee dɛɛ yerɔ.

english_verse: When the Lord called out his name for the third time, Samuel went to Eli again and said, “Here I am. What do you want?” Eli finally realized that it was the Lord who was speaking to Samuel.
translation_verse: Korowii yerɔ toorotena, asɛ o berɛ ir la Eli be ŋɔ, “N dɔɔ, he yer mɛ, menee la.” Belaa Eli na kɛŋɔ Korowiirii dɛɛ yerɔ la.

english_verse: So he said, “Go back and lie down! If someone speaks to you again, answer, ‘I'm listening, Lord. What do you want me to do?’ ” Once again Samuel went back and lay down.
translation_verse: Ate, Eli ŋɔ Samoɛl be ŋɔ, “Berɛ kaa ka chɔ, he baa no kɛ ba dɛ yerɛ jaa, he ŋɔ, ‘N Naa Korowii, bol waa he bonɔɔ be, n dɛ no.’ ” Asɛ Samoɛl berɛ kaa o chɔɔbɔr bela ka chɔ.

english_verse: The Lord then stood beside Samuel and called out as he had done before, “Samuel! Samuel!” “I'm listening,” Samuel answered. “What do you want me to do?”
translation_verse: Korowii berɔ ba che o jwɛh dɛɛ yerɔ kɛ wubwa la ŋɔ, “Samoɛl! Samoɛl!” Asɛ o chaŋe ŋɔ, “N dɔɔ, bol waa he bonɔɔ be, n dɛ no.”

english_verse: The Lord said: Samuel, I am going to do something in Israel that will shock everyone who hears about it!
translation_verse: Anee Korowii ŋɔ Samoɛl be ŋɔ, “Na, n dɛ ba waane ɛɛ Israel tena bini ásɛ bɛlbwa waa no la, o bwara yɔr kohona dɛɛ chel.

english_verse: I will punish Eli and his family, just as I promised.
translation_verse: Awola tɔpere la, mɛɛ tɛr Eli ne o dem tena deŋnee ɡɛ aa chɛa, maa wola beŋkpoŋ kwaraa ta.

english_verse: He knew that his sons refused to respect me, and he let them get away with it, even though I said I would punish his family forever.
translation_verse: N tɔ sie ɡel o jemɛ kɛŋɔ mɛɛ tɛr o ne o dem tena deŋnee o bibaala waa baa bola yaɡ mɛ la wa, dɛkalkɛ o ta ban kasinteŋ dii.

english_verse: I warned Eli that sacrifices or offerings could never make things right! His family has done too many disgusting things.
translation_verse: Gɛ waa nɔ nomanta, n ŋwɛɛrɔ kɛŋɔ Eli ne o dem tena wechɔɡa baa ɛa la, hale kwaa kpoora kɛɛ saraha bɛlbwa ɛɛ aa won larawe tɛɛ ba.”

english_verse: The next morning, Samuel got up and opened the doors to the Lord's house. He was afraid to tell Eli what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Samoɛl chɔɔ asɛ tɔɔ per chɔmbibi o ir dɛ ka ya Korowii Dea ɡbeni la. Dɛ o dɛ ɔmɛ kɛ o bol waa waa noa le Korowii be la Eli be,

english_verse: But Eli told him, “Samuel, my boy, come here!” “Yes, sir!” Samuel answered.
translation_verse: kɛ Eli yerɔ dɛ ŋɔ, “N bie Samoɛl.” Asɛ o chaŋo ŋɔ, “N dɔɔ, menee la.”

english_verse: Eli said, “What did God say to you? Tell me everything. I'll ask God to punish you terribly if you don't tell me every word he said!”
translation_verse: Eli bɔɔro ŋɔ, “Bɔkwa waa Korowii bol he be nɔ? Bɛ wobɛlbwa kpɔ sɔɔh mɛ. Dɛ he kpɔ wobɛlbwa Korowii aa bol he be sɔɔh mɛ naa, ó tɛr he deŋne kohona.”

english_verse: Samuel told Eli everything. Then Eli said, “He is the Lord, and he will do what's right.” The Lord Helps Samuel
translation_verse: Anomanta, Samoɛl bol waa la bwa baɡlo, o ta bɛlbwa kpɔe sɔɔh. Ate Eli ŋɔ, “Onee Korowii, ɡel o ɛ waa aa too o tea.”

english_verse: As Samuel grew up, the Lord helped him and made everything Samuel said come true.
translation_verse: Korowii ja Samoɛl nɛ o ba kpeɡ, dɛ ɡel o wobɛlbwa ɡe waa dɛ bol la ɛ kasinteŋ.

english_verse: From the town of Dan in the north to the town of Beersheba in the south, everyone in the country knew that Samuel was truly the Lord's prophet.
translation_verse: Anomanta, Israel harɛ ta bwa, le Dan dea harɛ waa lɔ weekaŋle harɛbɔr, ka tel bwɛɛ Beɛseeba waa lɔ weekaŋle nyundua bwa jemɔ kɛŋɔ Samoɛl ɛ Korowii keame.

english_verse: The Lord often appeared to Samuel at Shiloh and told him what to say.
translation_verse: Korowii teŋɔ kpɔ o te baa baɡle Samoɛl Silo bela, dɛ baɡlo waa waa bol.

english_verse: Then Samuel would speak to the whole nation of Israel. The Philistines Capture the Sacred Chest One day the Israelites went out to fight the Philistines. They set up camp near Ebenezer, and the Philistines camped at Aphek.
translation_verse: Belaa Samoɛl bol waa Korowii aa kpɔa baɡlo la tɛ Israel tena bwa. Filisti tena kaa kpɔ Korowii Ne Nɛwɛnyina Fɔo Daka A balɔ kɛŋɔ Israel tena vɔrɔwɔ kɛŋɔ bá ka yo Filisti tena. Israel tena kaa baŋre ba tɛnte deene Ɛbɛneesa harɛ ta, asɛ Filisti tena ɡe do Afɛk.

english_verse: The Philistines made a fierce attack. They defeated the Israelites and killed about
translation_verse: Filisti tena laa tena lɔɔ ka tɔ Israel tena la nɛ, dɛ yoo ba dɛ pɔ ba nɛ. Ba kpoo ba nɛra kaɡboŋa banaarɛ.

english_verse: The army sent some soldiers to bring back the sacred chest from Shiloh, because the Lord All-Powerful has his throne on the winged creatures on top of the chest. As Eli's two sons, Hophni and Phinehas,
translation_verse: Anomanta, ba tomɛ baala ba la Silo, dɛ ka kpɔ Nemenɛ Korowii Ne Nɛwɛnyina Fɔo Daka le bela Korowii Waa Ɛ Koranar Bwa Kooro aa soɡe Kerobim la doa o kookara ta la ba. Eli bibaala banɛ, Hofni ne Fenehas, teŋɛ Daka la nɛɛ dɛ ba.

english_verse: The Israelite army returned to their camp, and the leaders said, “Why did the Lord let us lose to the Philistines today? Let's get the sacred chest where the Lord's agreement with Israel is kept. Then the Lord will help us and rescue us from our enemies.”
translation_verse: Israel laa tena baa kaa la aa bera ba bela baa baŋre ba tɛnte deene la, ba nomonome la bɔɔ ba ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ Korowii ɡel Filisti tena pɔ ya nɛɛ fini ken? Hé ɡel yá ka kpɔ Korowii Ne Nɛwɛnyina Fɔo Daka la le Silo ba, ásɛ ya ne wɛɛ valɛ ó lɛ yaa dɛɛ le ya dɔma nɔn ta.”

english_verse: brought the chest into camp, the army cheered so loudly that the ground shook.
translation_verse: Korowii Ne Nɛwɛnyina Fɔo Daka la aa ba bela baa baŋre ba tɛnte deene la, Israel tena la bwa moolo kohona silɛɛ ne, asɛ harɛ jiɡri.

english_verse: The Philistines heard the noise and said, “What are those Hebrews shouting about?” When the Philistines learned that the sacred chest had been brought into the camp,
translation_verse: Filisti tena la aa no Israel tena ɡbɔɡa la, ba ŋɔ, “Bɔkwa ɡe ɡbɔɡaa dɛɛ le Israel tena tɛnte deene bini ken?” Baa noa kɛŋɔ Korowii Ne Nɛwɛnyina Fɔo Daka la nee ba ba bela la,

english_verse: they were scared to death and said: The gods have come into their camp. Now we're in real trouble! Nothing like this has ever happened to us before.
translation_verse: ɔmee lawɛ Filisti tena la, asɛ ba ŋɔ, “Ba kpɔ voɡ ba cheɡ bela baa soɡa la. A dɔŋa ta chiɡe bwa, namete ya na wa!

english_verse: We're in big trouble! Who can save us from these powerful gods? They're the same gods who made all those horrible things happen to the Egyptians in the desert.
translation_verse: Ya bwɛɛlɛ! Umee dɛ́ lɛ yaa le voɡkpeɡa nɔ nɔn ta nɔ? Anee fa kpɔ weechɔɡa bwa soo siwi ta Ijipt tena nɛɛ pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta la.

english_verse: Philistines, be brave and fight hard! If you don't, those Hebrews will rule us, just as we've been ruling them. Fight and don't be afraid.
translation_verse: Filisti tena, hé dɔ bambile, dɛ́ che kiŋkiŋ kɛŋɔ baala, dɛ ɡɛ laa aa, hɛ́ɛ ka do Israel tena lɔɡaa ɡɛ ba fa aa lɔ ya lɔɡa la. Hé che kiŋkiŋ dɛ́ yo.”

english_verse: Hophni and Phinehas were killed, and the sacred chest was captured. Eli Dies
translation_verse: Filisti tena kpɔ Korowii Ne Nɛwɛnyina Fɔo Daka la, dɛ kpo sɔfo Eli bibaala Hofni ne Fenehas ɡe. Sɔfo Eli seo wa

english_verse: That same day a soldier from the tribe of Benjamin ran from the battlefront to Shiloh. He had torn his clothes and put dirt on his head to show his sorrow.
translation_verse: Awola tenten, baa bɛl waa le Bɛnjamen dea chwao le laa la ta dɛ ba Silo, dɛ o laala kɛɛrɔ asɛ teera do o nyu ta a baɡle kɛ o bambile chɔɡɔ.

english_verse: He went into town and told the news about the battle, and everyone started crying. Eli was afraid that something might happen to the sacred chest. So he was sitting on his chair beside the road, just waiting.
translation_verse: Waa bala la, dɛ Eli soɡe o kara ta ŋwɛnɛ nyoa dɛɛ nyiŋi, dɛkalkɛ ɔmee lawɔ Korowii Ne Nɛwɛnyina Fɔo Daka la wa. Baa la aa baa jo bwɛɛ la bini dɛ baɡle waa aa chiɡa la, ɔmee chole bɛlbwa nɛɛ baa wi bɔr bwa.

english_verse: “I escaped from the fighting today and ran here.” “Young man, what happened?” Eli asked.
translation_verse: Baa la ŋɔ Eli be ŋɔ, “Fini tɔpere tenten nɔɔ n chwa le laa ta dɛ ba la.” Asɛ Eli ŋɔ, “N bie, bɔkwa waa chiɡa ɔ?”

english_verse: “Israel ran away from the Philistines,” the soldier answered. “Many of our people were killed, including your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas. But worst of all, the sacred chest was captured.”
translation_verse: Ate, baa la ŋɔ, “Laa la ta la, Israel tena chwao, asɛ Filisti tena kpoo ba kohona. He bibaala Hofni ne Fenehas ɡe, ba kpoo ba, dɛ kpɔ Korowii Ne Nɛwɛnyina Fɔo Daka la ɡe kaa.”

english_verse: Eli was still sitting on a chair beside the wall of the town gate. And when the man said that the Philistines had taken the sacred chest, Eli fell backwards. He was a very heavy old man, and the fall broke his neck and killed him. He had been a leader of Israel for
translation_verse: Sɔfo Eli aa no Korowii Ne Nɛwɛnyina Fɔo Daka la waa la, o le o kara waa soɡe o ta la ta chole hanjala ɡbera jwɛh, asɛ o baŋa ku o sewɛ, dɛkalkɛ o hwɛɛhrɔ dɛ do tɔɡre. Bene fifraanaarɛ bwaa o tɔ Israel tena sie.

english_verse: The wife of Phinehas was about to give birth. And soon after she heard that the sacred chest had been captured and that her husband and his father had died, her baby came. The birth was very hard,
translation_verse: Gɛ saŋ dɛ o bibaa Fenehas haah kpoŋe tea a ka tama ó lolɛ. Waa no Korowii Ne Nɛwɛnyina Fɔo Daka la waa kɛŋɔ Filisti tena kpɔɔ kaa, asɛ o hela Eli ne o jaa sewɛ la, loltea piɡro lɔɔ o lolɛ, kɛ dɛ a ɡwaa o nɛ.

english_verse: and she was dying. But the women taking care of her said, “Don't be afraid—it's a boy!” She didn't pay any attention to them.
translation_verse: Aa ba dɛ ɡwaa kohona wɛɛ ba sewa la, haahna baa dɛ lawɔ lol la ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Bɛ ɡel he bambile chɔɡ, he lolɛ bibaa.” Kɛ dɛ waa no, á ba ɛ kɛŋɔ wɛɛ chaŋoo.

english_verse: Instead she kept thinking about losing her husband and her father-in-law. So she said, “My son will be named Ichabod, because the glory of Israel left our country when the sacred chest was captured.”
translation_verse: O ŋɔ, “Korowii jirima toole Israel tena nɛɛ kpa, Daka la Filisti tena aa kpɔa kaa la wa.”

english_verse: The Philistines took the sacred chest from near Ebenezer to the town of Ashdod.
translation_verse: Filisti tena la aa kpɔ Korowii Ne Nɛwɛnyina Fɔo Daka la, ba le o ne bwɛɛ Ɛbɛneesa, dɛ kaa ba bwɛjen Asdɔd ta.

english_verse: They brought it into the temple of their god Dagon and put it next to the statue of Dagon, which they worshiped.
translation_verse: Asɛ ba kpɔ ka cheɡ ba voɡ baa dɛ yerɔ Daɡɔn dea, o che voɡ la jwɛh.

english_verse: When the people of Ashdod got up early the next morning, they found the statue lying facedown on the floor in front of the sacred chest. They put the statue back where it belonged.
translation_verse: Tɔ aa pera chɔmbibi la, Asdɔd tena nao kɛŋɔ ba voɡ Daɡɔn la cholo o sie pi harɛ Korowii Ne Nɛwɛnyina Fɔo Daka la sie, asɛ ba ka kwaaro pa o buɡ ta.

english_verse: But early the next morning, it had fallen over again and was lying facedown on the floor in front of the chest. The body of the statue was still in one piece, but its head and both hands had broken off and were lying on the stone floor in the doorway.
translation_verse: Tɔ aa pera ja la, ba iro dɛ na kɛŋɔ voɡ la berɔ chole o sie pi harɛ Korowii Ne Nɛwɛnyina Fɔo Daka la sie, asɛ o nyu ne nɔɔra kuuɡi o chɔ doonyoa, a ka o kpul chɔ.

english_verse: This is why the priests and everyone else step over that part of the doorway when they enter the temple of Dagon in Ashdod.
translation_verse: A waa dɛ kpoŋe ba le fini, nɛra baa dɛ kpoŋe Daɡɔn kere kɛɛ bɛlbwa waa dɛ tomɔ dɛ ba dea la bini joe yaa, ba yon ɡale doonyoa bela mɔɔ dɛɛ jo la.

english_verse: The Lord caused a lot of trouble for the people of Ashdod and their neighbors. He made sores break out all over their bodies, and everyone was in a panic.
translation_verse: Korowii tɛr Asdɔd ne bwɛɛre aa baro cheme nɛra deŋne kɛrɛdɛ, dɛ kpɔ ɔmee kohona ta ba nɛ. O kpɔ ɔɡra ne ŋwɛra ta ba nɛ.

english_verse: Finally, they said, “The God of Israel did this. He is the one who caused all this trouble for us and our god Dagon. We've got to get rid of this chest.”
translation_verse: Asdɔd tena aa na waa aa dɛ chiɡ la, ba ŋɔ, “Korowii Israel tena aa dɛ tomɔ Ne Nɛwɛnyina Fɔo Daka la ta chɛ kɛ ó che ya be kpa, dɛkalkɛ o dɛ tɛr ya ne ya voɡ Daɡɔn deŋne.”

english_verse: The people of Ashdod invited all the Philistine rulers to come to Ashdod, and they asked them, “What can we do with the sacred chest that belongs to the God of Israel?” “Send it to Gath,” the rulers answered. But after they took it there,
translation_verse: Anomanta, ba yerɛ Filisti koranar baa dɛ nyiŋi ba harɛre ta bwa cheme dɛ bɔɔ ba ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ chɛ kɛ yá ɛ Korowii Israel tena aa dɛ tomɔ Ne Nɛwɛnyina Fɔo Daka nɔɔ?” Anee ba chaŋe ŋɔ, “Hé kpɔ kaa bwɛjen Gat ka cheɡ.” Gɛɛ a do ba kpɔ Korowii Israel tena aa dɛ tomɔ Fɔo Daka la le bela kaa.

english_verse: the Lord made sores break out on everyone in town. The people of Gath were frightened,
translation_verse: Baa kpɔ Daka la kaa Gat kwaraa la, Korowii tɛr bwɛjen Gat tena deŋne ɔmee kohona chole ba nɛ. O kpɔ ɔɡra ba ta bechale ne nomonome bwa nɛ.

english_verse: so they sent the sacred chest to Ekron. But before they could take it through the town gates, the people of Ekron started screaming, “They've brought the sacred chest that belongs to the God of Israel! It will kill us and our families too!” The Philistines Send Back the Sacred Chest
translation_verse: Ate, ba berɛ kpɔ Korowii Ne Nɛwɛnyina Fɔo Daka la kaa Ekron, dɛ o ɡe ɛ Filisti tena bwɛjena la bini bɛl. Bwɛjen la bini nɛra aa naa la, ba wio ŋɔ, “Ba kpɔ Israel tena Korowii baa dɛ tomɔ Ne Nɛwɛnyina Fɔo Daka la ba jo ya baah, dɛ́ ba kpoo yaa.”

english_verse: The people of Ekron called for another meeting of the Philistine rulers and told them, “Send this chest back where it belongs. Then it won't kill us.” Everyone was in a panic, because God was causing a lot of people to die,
translation_verse: Anomanta, ba yerɛ Filisti koranar la bwa cheme dɛ ŋɔ, “Hé berɛ kpɔ Korowii Israel tena aa dɛ tomɔ Ne Nɛwɛnyina Fɔo Daka la ka cheɡ o buɡ ta, ásɛ o bɛ ya ne ya bii ba kpoo.” Dɛ deŋnetɛra Korowii aa kpɔa ba ta ba nɛɛ la ɡelɔ sibeɡra chole ba nɛɛ kɛrɛdɛ bwɛjen la ta.

english_verse: and those who had survived were suffering from the sores. They all cried to their gods for help.
translation_verse: Banɔ la baa wola serewɛ la, ɔɡra ɔɡ ba ba wi dɛɛ yerɛ ba voɡa ŋɔ á ba lɛɛ ba.

english_verse: After the sacred chest had been in Philistia for seven months,
translation_verse: Korowii Ne Nɛwɛnyina Fɔo Daka la lɔ Filisti tena nɔn ta korobie anuanɛ,

english_verse: the Philistines called in their priests and fortunetellers, and asked, “What should we do with this sacred chest? Tell us how to send it back where it belongs!”
translation_verse: asɛ Filisti tena la yerɛ kerekpoŋra baa soɡe voɡa ta ne voɡra baa lɔ harɛ la ta bwa cheme dɛ bɔɔ ba ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ yá ɛ Korowii Ne Nɛwɛnyina Fɔo Daka nɔɔ? Hé baɡle ɡɛ yaa ɛ dɛ́ berɛ kaa o ne o buɡ ta.”

english_verse: “Don't send it back without a gift,” the priests and fortunetellers answered. “Send along something to Israel's God to make up for taking the chest in the first place. Then you will be healed, and you will find out why the Lord was causing you so much trouble.”
translation_verse: Anee ba chaŋe ŋɔ, “Hé kpɔ Korowii Israel tena aa dɛ tomɔ, Ne Nɛwɛnyina Fɔo Daka la berɛ dɛɛ kaa o buɡ ta tenaa, he bɛ o ne kaa pɛɛpɛɛ. Hé kpɔ bolchɔɡe dii saraha kwaa ja ka tɛ Korowii. Anee dɛɛ ba ɡela he dɔ chaeh, ásɛ he jemɛ he deŋnetɛra mun.”

english_verse: “What should we send?” the Philistines asked. The priests and fortunetellers answered: There are five Philistine rulers, and they all have the same disease that you have.
translation_verse: Filisti tena la bɔɔrɔ ja ŋɔ, “Bolchɔɡe dii saraha besoo yá kpɔ ka tɛo wɔ?” Ate, ba chaŋe ŋɔ, “Hé kpɔ suuɡaswɛm loɡɛ konɡuleɡule anue kɛŋɔ ɔɡra, dɛ́ kpɔ ane ɡe loɡɛ kwaane kɛŋɔ mari anue, ásɛ a che tɛ Filisti koranar banue la, dɛkalkɛ he ne ba bwaa weechɔɡa la lawɛ.

english_verse: So make five gold models of the sores and five gold models of the rats that are wiping out your crops. If you honor the God of Israel with this gift, maybe he will stop causing trouble for you and your gods and your crops.
translation_verse: Hé kpɔ suuɡaswɛm konɡuleɡule anue la ne mari anue la aa dɛ chɔɡ he ne he harɛre ta nɛra bwa la, ásɛ dɛ kpɔ duure tɛ Korowii Israel tena aa dɛ tomɔ la. O ken ɛɛ laa deŋnetɛra laanee kpɔ he ne he harɛ dɛ he voɡa bwa nɛ.

english_verse: Don't be like the Egyptians and their king. They were stubborn, but when Israel's God was finished with them, they had to let Israel go.
translation_verse: Ɛrɛɛ he deŋne do kpeɡri kɛŋɔ Ijipt kooro ne o nɛra nɔɔ? Hé lii ɡɛ Korowii fa aa tɛr ba deŋne kohona, dɛ ka tel kɛŋɔ baa tɛ Israel tena ŋwɛnɛ ba le Ijipt harɛ ta kaa la.

english_verse: Get a new cart and two cows that have young calves and that have never pulled a cart. Hitch the cows to the cart, but take the calves back to their barn.
translation_verse: Anomanta, hé kpɔ konfala aa do kɛŋɔ torɔɡo dɛ dɔ tɔre, dɛ́ lawɛ naneene anɛ a bii ta aa dɛ ɔra, baa wola ane parɛ bwa vɔwa, ásɛ dɛ pere a bii la le anɛ ka do leɡ bini.

english_verse: Then put the chest on the cart. Put the gold rats and sores into a bag and put it on the cart next to the chest. Then send it on its way.
translation_verse: Hé kpɔ Korowii Ne Nɛwɛnyina Fɔo Daka la ka chɔŋɛ torɔɡo la ta, dɛ́ kpɔ kwaa haa kpɔ suuɡaswɛm loɡa la bil o jwɛh. Hé kpɔ bolchɔɡe dii saraha kwaa la do dakajeɡa bɛl bini, ásɛ o che Daka la jwɛh a kpɔ dɛɛ kaa,

english_verse: Watch to see if the chest goes on up the road to the Israelite town of Beth-Shemesh. If it goes back to its own country, you will know that it was the Lord who made us suffer so badly. But if the chest doesn't go back to its own country, then the Lord had nothing to do with the disease that hit us—it was simply bad luck.
translation_verse: dɛɛ nyiŋi a kaala bini. Hé nao kɛŋɔ a kpɔ sie chaɡɛ bwɛɛ Bɛt Sɛmɛs pera dɛɛ kaa laa, amɔ dɛ Korowiirii kpɔ wahala kohona nɔ ba ta ya nɛ. A ta sie kpɔe chaɡɛ bela bɔr ɡe aa, yaa jemɔɔ kɛŋɔ Korowii be laa aa le, ya nyuchɔɡee ɡelaa a ba ɡɛ.”

english_verse: The Philistines followed their advice. They hitched up the two cows to the cart, but they kept their calves in a barn.
translation_verse: Anomanta, ba ɛ ɡɛ. Ba lawɛ naneene anɛ la, dɛ vɔwa pɛl kwaa aa do kɛŋɔ torɔɡo dɛ dɔ tɔre la nɛ, dɛ pere a bii la le a nɛ ka do leɡ bini.

english_verse: Then they put the chest on the cart, along with the bag that had the gold rats and sores in it.
translation_verse: Ba kpɔ Korowii Ne Nɛwɛnyina Fɔo Daka la ka chɔŋɛ o ta, dɛ kpɔ dakajeɡa baa kpɔ suuɡaswɛm kwaa la do o bini la ɡe ka cheɡ o jwɛh.

english_verse: The cows went straight up the road toward Beth-Shemesh, mooing as they went. The Philistine rulers followed them until they got close to Beth-Shemesh.
translation_verse: Nae la aa lea la, a den kpɔ sie pa Bɛt Sɛmɛs ŋwɛnɛ ta dɛɛ kaa, a ta bɛɡɛ kpɔ diɡ kɛɛ ɡal, dɛ si dɛɛ kaa. Filisti tena koranar banue la teŋɛ a nɛɛ ka tel Bɛt Sɛmɛs jwɛh ta.

english_verse: The people of Beth-Shemesh were harvesting their wheat in the valley. When they looked up and saw the chest, they were so happy that they stopped working and started celebrating.
translation_verse: Dɛ Bɛt Sɛmɛs tena lɔ fɛlembɔjen bɛl bini dɛɛ komɛ mea. Baa ha sie nyiŋi dɛ na Korowii Ne Nɛwɛnyina Fɔo Daka la, ba sie lɛo kɛrɛdɛ.

english_verse: When the five rulers of the Philistines saw what had happened, they went back to Ekron that same day.
translation_verse: Filisti tena koranar banue la na a ɡɛ waa nɔ bwa, dɛ berɛ kaa bwɛjen Ekron ta awola tenten.

english_verse: That is how the Philistines sent gifts to the Lord to make up for taking the sacred chest. They sent five gold sores, one each for their towns of Ashdod, Gaza, Ashkelon, Gath, and Ekron.
translation_verse: Gɛ kwaa aa do kɛŋɔ ɔɡra, ba kpɔ suuɡaswɛm ɛa Filisti tena la kpɔ ka ɛ bolchɔɡe dii saraha tɛ Korowii laanee la. Bɛlbwa cheɡɔ tɛ ba bwɛjena Asdɔd ne Gasa ne Askɛlɔn ne Gat dɛ Ekron.

english_verse: They also sent one gold rat for each walled town and for every village that the five Philistine rulers controlled. The huge stone where the Levites set the chest is still there in Joshua's field as a reminder of what happened. The Sacred Chest Is Sent to Kiriath-Jearim
translation_verse: Ba berɔ kpɔ mari anue baa kpɔ suuɡaswɛm ɛa la, a ɡe che tɛ Filisti koranar banue bwɛjena baa ma danjwɛjena bara ne a bwɛjeɡre. Bwe baa kpɔ Korowii Ne Nɛwɛnyina Fɔo Daka la chɔŋɛ o ta Josua waa le Bɛt Sɛmɛs koo ta la, o ta ɛ danseɛ kon ba le fini.

english_verse: Some of the men of Beth-Shemesh looked inside the sacred chest, and the Lord God killed
translation_verse: Korowii kpoo Bɛt Sɛmɛs baala fifraanuanɛ, nyiŋa baa kaa nyiŋi Korowii Ne Nɛwɛnyina Fɔo Daka la bini la wa. Bela tena la wii ba kohona, Korowii kpoe waa kpo ba la wa.

english_verse: and they started saying, “No other God is like the Lord! Who can go near him and stay alive? We'll have to send the chest away from here. But where can we send it?”
translation_verse: Anee Bɛt Sɛmɛs baala ŋɔ, “Umee dɛ́ won che Korowii o wa aa do ɡoroŋ nɔ sie nɔ? Leperaa ya kaa Daka nɔ ne ó le ya nɛɔ?”

english_verse: They sent messengers to tell the people of Kiriath-Jearim, “The Philistines have sent back the sacred chest. Why don't you take it and keep it there with you?”
translation_verse: Ba kpɔ kala tɛ Kiriat Jearim tena ŋɔ, “Filisti tena la berɔ kpɔ Korowii Ne Nɛwɛnyina Fɔo Daka la ba, hé ba dɛ́ ba kpɔ kaa he be.”

english_verse: The people of Kiriath-Jearim got the chest and took it to Abinadab's house, which was on a hill in their town. They chose his son Eleazar to take care of it,
translation_verse: Kiriat Jearim baala baa kpɔ Korowii Ne Nɛwɛnyina Fɔo Daka la, dɛ kaa o ne Abinadab dem deŋɡare bɛl doa. Ba sɔ o bibaa baa dɛ yerɔ Eliasa doŋa ta o do ɡoroŋ tɛ Korowii, dɛ ŋɔ wɛɛ nyiŋi Korowii Fɔo Daka la ta. Samoɛl nyiŋi Israel tena nɛ

english_verse: One day, Samuel told all the people of Israel, “If you really want to turn back to the Lord, then prove it. Get rid of your foreign idols, including the ones of the goddess Astarte. Turn to the Lord with all your heart and worship only him. Then he will rescue you from the Philistines.”
translation_verse: Asɛ Samoɛl ŋɔ Israel tena be ŋɔ, “Dɛ hɛɛ berɔɔ ba Korowii be dɛɛ nyinu he bambile bwa ne, dɛ́ laa he te kpɔ voɡa toma ne voɡhaahna Astɔrɛt nɛ, dɛ́ kpɔ he te tɛo dɛɛ tomɛ o ɡbo aa, wɛɛ lɛ heyaa le Filisti tena kpeɡri baa dɛ di he nɛɛ la taa.”

english_verse: The people got rid of their idols of Baal and Astarte and began worshiping only the Lord.
translation_verse: Anomanta, ba pa Baal ne voɡhaahna Astɔrɛt aa lɔ ba be ta, dɛɛ tomɛ Korowii ɡbo.

english_verse: Then Samuel said, “Tell everyone in Israel to meet together at Mizpah, and I will pray to the Lord for you.”
translation_verse: Asɛ Samoɛl berɛ ŋɔ, “Hé ŋɔ Israel tena be bá bwa cheme bwɛjen Mispa, ásɛ n soŋe andɛɛɡa le Korowii be tɛ heya.”

english_verse: The Israelites met together at Mizpah with Samuel as their leader. They drew water from the well and poured it out as an offering to the Lord. On that same day they went without eating to show their sorrow, and they confessed they had been unfaithful to the Lord. The Philistines Attack Israel
translation_verse: Ba bwa aa baa cheme Mispa la, ba dɔ nee dɛ fuɡe ta Korowii sie a baɡle wechɔɡa baa ɛa la saraha. Ba vɔwɛ nyoa tɔpebir la bwa, dɛ ŋɔ, “Ya ɛ wechɔɡa dɛ jo Korowii nɛ.” Mispa belaa Samoɛl do dɛ tɔ ba sie, dɛ bol bane ba bala waa dɛɛ tɛɛ ba.

english_verse: When the Philistine rulers found out about the meeting at Mizpah, they sent an army there to attack the people of Israel. The Israelites were afraid when they heard that the Philistines were coming.
translation_verse: Filisti tena la aa noa kɛŋɔ Israel tena cheme Mispa la, ba koranar banue la kpɔ ba laa tena dɛ́ ka yoo ba. Israel tena la no ba wa, asɛ ɔmee chole ba nɛ.

english_verse: Samuel begged the Lord to rescue Israel, then he sacrificed a young lamb to the Lord. Samuel had not even finished offering the sacrifice when the Philistines started to attack. But the Lord answered his prayer and made thunder crash all around them. The Philistines panicked and ran away.
translation_verse: Waa dɛ fuh saraha kon la, dɛ Filisti tena la kpɔ ba te dɛɛ ba ba puu ba yo. Asɛ Korowii ɡel bwaala kɔr kohona jo Filisti tena la bini, ɔmee chole ba nɛɛ ba wili, dɛ kpɔ bambiteŋa chwa le Israel tena sie.

english_verse: The men of Israel left Mizpah and went after them as far as the hillside below Beth-Car, killing every enemy soldier they caught.
translation_verse: Israel laa tena le Mispa dɛ ti ba, ba kpoo ba le ŋwɛnɛ bɛl waa chɔa kaa bwɛɛ Bɛt Kaa harɛbɔr.

english_verse: The Israelites were even able to recapture their towns and territory between Ekron and Gath. Israel was also at peace with the Amorites. Samuel Is a Leader in Israel
translation_verse: Israel harɛ bwɛjena ane kɛŋɔ le Ekron ka tel Gat Filisti tena aa lɛa le ba be la, ba bera tɛɛ ba ba dɔ ba harɛ bwa. Asɛ deŋnesɔɔhna ba ba ne Amɔre tena baah.

english_verse: Every year he would go around to the towns of Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah where he served as judge for the people.
translation_verse: Bena bɛlbwa, o dɛ ɡaaɡe ba nɛɛ le bwɛjena Bɛtel kaa Gelɡal ne Mispa bwa, dɛ bol nɛra waa dɛɛ pa bole.

english_verse: Then he would go back to his home in Ramah and do the same thing there. He also had an altar built for the Lord at Ramah.
translation_verse: O yon berɛ ba kaa Rama, bela waa soɡa. Bela ɡe, o bol Israel tena ne ba bala waa dɛɛ pa bole, asɛ o ma kon baa ɛ saraha o ta bela tɛ Korowii.

english_verse: Samuel had two sons. The older one was Joel, and the younger one was Abijah. When Samuel was getting old, he let them be leaders at Beersheba.
translation_verse: O bibaa waa tɔ sie sɔne Joel, nɛɛte la ɡe sɔne Abija. Dɛ ba ɛ sitɔɔla dɛ so Beɛseeba dɛɛ nyiŋi nɛra la nɛ.

english_verse: But they were not like their father. They were dishonest and accepted bribes to give unfair decisions.
translation_verse: Kɛ dɛ ba te ta doe kɛŋɔ ba mɛɛ. Dɛ ba sie beɡre suuɡa, anomanta, ba ɡelɔ nɛra ɛɛ yaɡ ba sen, baa waa aŋwɛnɛ ta bol.

english_verse: One day the nation's leaders came to Samuel at Ramah
translation_verse: Anomanta, Israel nomonome la bwa chemo dɛ la Samoɛl be Rama,

english_verse: and said, “You are an old man. You set a good example for your sons, but they haven't followed it. Now we want a king to be our leader, just like all the other nations. Choose one for us!”
translation_verse: dɛ ka ŋɔ, “Taraken he hwɛɛhrɔ, asɛ he bii la ɡe ta do kɛ hen, ba we-ɛɛla aa were. Nyin kooro tɛ yaa wɛɛ tɔ ya sie ɡɛ harɛre nɛra bwa aa dɔa la.”

english_verse: Samuel was upset to hear the leaders say they wanted a king, so he prayed about it.
translation_verse: Baa ŋɔ o be ŋɔ ó tɛɛ ba kooro wɛɛ tɔ ba sie la, a ta o som doe asɛ o soŋe Korowii a wa.

english_verse: The Lord answered: Samuel, do everything they want you to do. I am really the one they have rejected as their king.
translation_verse: Asɛ Korowii ŋɔ Samoɛl be ŋɔ, “No waa bwa nɛra la aa dɛ bol he be la, he laa ba vɛh kɛ ba kooro, men Korowiirii ba vɛh.

english_verse: Ever since the day I rescued my people from Egypt, they have turned from me to worship idols. Now they are turning away from you.
translation_verse: Gɛɛ ba ɛɛ mɛ dɛ le ɡɛ saŋ maa le ba ne Ijipt harɛ ta. Ba vɛɛh baa vɛɛh mɛ dɛ kaa tomɛ harɛre ane voɡa la taa ba ta do ba le fini, dɛ kpɔ dɛɛ ɛ he ɡe la.

english_verse: Do everything they ask, but warn them and tell them how a king will treat them.
translation_verse: Name cheɡ deŋne no waa baa bol, kɛ kah ba kɛrɛdɛ dɛ́ ɡel ba jemɛ ɡɛ ba koranar aa dɛ ba kpɔe dɛɛ ɛɛ ba.”

english_verse: Samuel told the people who were asking for a king what the Lord had said:
translation_verse: Samoɛl bol waa Korowii aa bol o be la bwa baɡle nɛra baa dɛ bɔɔ kooro dɔe waa la.

english_verse: If you have a king, this is how he will treat you. He will force your sons to join his army. Some of them will ride in his chariots, some will serve in the cavalry, and others will run ahead of his own chariot.
translation_verse: O ŋɔ, “He baa dɔ kooro aa, waa waa dɛ ba ɛɛ laanee nɔ. Wɛɛ kpɔ he bibaalaa ɛ o laa tena, bane so kwaa aa do kɛŋɔ torɔɡo ba vɔwɛ pɛl jaɡre la ta, ásɛ bane ɡe so jaɡre ta, bane ɡe chwa tɔ kwaa aa do kɛŋɔ torɔɡore ba kpɔ dɛɛ la laa la sie.

english_verse: Your daughters will have to make perfume or do his cooking and baking.
translation_verse: Wɛɛ ɡeloo he bihaahna ɛɛ ɛ konsɔɔhsoma, bane ɛɛ daa kondikwa ásɛ bane ɡe ɛɛ wɔɔ paanoo.

english_verse: The king will take your best fields, as well as your vineyards, and olive orchards and give them to his own officials.
translation_verse: Wɛɛ lɛ he harɛdɛɛɡa ne he daa koonii tɛ o nomonome.

english_verse: He will also take a tenth of your grain and grapes and give it to his officers and officials.
translation_verse: Wɛɛ bɔne he mea ne he daa kooni bini bɔre fii, dɛ́ kpɔ bɔrbeŋkpoŋ tɛ o nomonome ne bonɔɔna.

english_verse: The king will take your slaves and your best young men and your donkeys and make them do his work.
translation_verse: Dɛ́ kpɔ he bonɔɔna ne toli bwa, ne he nae aa wera ne keeɡore ɛ o kwa áa ɛ o toma.

english_verse: He will also take a tenth of your sheep and goats. You will become the king's slaves,
translation_verse: He peera ɡe la, wɛɛ bɔne a bini bɔre fii, dɛ́ kpɔ bɔrbeŋkpoŋ, ásɛ dɛ kpɔ heyaa berɛ o yoma.

english_verse: and you will finally cry out for the Lord to save you from the king you wanted. But the Lord won't answer your prayers.
translation_verse: Awola tɔpere la, hɛ́ɛ dɛɛ wiu, dɛɛ nyin kɛŋɔ he fe aa le kooro he ɡbabir aa leo la nɔn ta, kɛ Korowii aa heyaa chaŋe.”

english_verse: The people would not listen to Samuel. “No!” they said. “We want to be like other nations. We want a king to rule us and lead us in battle.”
translation_verse: Ásɛ ya dɔ kooro kɛŋɔ harɛre nɛra aa dɔa la, ó tɔ ya sie dɛɛ la ya ne laa.”

english_verse: Samuel listened to them and then told the Lord exactly what they had said.
translation_verse: Samoɛl aa no waa bwa baa bola la, o berɔ kpɔ bil Korowii sie ja.

english_verse: “Do what they want,” the Lord answered. “Give them a king.” Samuel told the people to go back to their homes.
translation_verse: Anee Korowii chaŋo ŋɔ, “No ba wesoŋa la tɛɛ ba, dɛ́ tɛɛ ba kooro.” Ate, Samoɛl ŋɔ Israel tena la be ŋɔ nomɛlbwa berɛ kaa o bwɛ.

english_verse: Kish was a wealthy man who belonged to the tribe of Benjamin. His father was Abiel, his grandfather was Zeror, his great-grandfather was Becorath, and his great-great-grandfather was Aphiah.
translation_verse: Baa bɛlee fa lole dɛ le Bɛnjamen dea baa yerɔ Kes. O mɛɛ sɔne Abiel, o nabaa sɔne Sɛrɔ. Sɛrɔ mɛɛ sɔne Bɛkɔrat, o ɡe mɛɛ Afiaa. Dɛ a ɡɛ Kes nɔ ɛ nɛnjen dɛ ɛ kondɔɔh.

english_verse: Kish had a son named Saul, who was better looking and more than a head taller than anyone else in all Israel.
translation_verse: Dɛ o dɔ bibaa bɛl baa yerɔ Sɔɔl. O wer bonɔɔ, dɛ kpeɡ kɛrɛdɛ o dɔŋ aa wola toole Israel harɛ ta.

english_verse: Kish owned some donkeys, but they had run off. So he told Saul, “Take one of the servants and go look for the donkeys.”
translation_verse: Awola bɛl, Sɔɔl mɛɛ Kes keeɡo neenanar baa nyoɡre, asɛ Kes ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Kpɔ n bonɔɔna la bini bɛl ja he nɛ ásɛ he la ka ɡaaɡe a bɔr.”

english_verse: Saul and the servant went through the hill country of Ephraim and the territory of Shalishah, but they could not find the donkeys. Then they went through the territories of Shaalim and Benjamin, but still there was no sign of the donkeys.
translation_verse: Baa lea la, ba kpɔ Efrem deŋɡarere harɛ ta, dɛ ka le Salisa harɛ ta, kɛ ba ta an nae. Ba ɡaaɡɔ ka le Saalim harɛ ta ɡe, ba ta an nae, dɛ berɛ le bela ka kpɔ Bɛnjamen dea harɛ ta, kɛ ba ta keeɡo beŋkpoŋ kwaraa nae.

english_verse: Finally they came to the territory where the clan of Zuph lived. “Let's go back home,” Saul told his servant. “If we don't go back soon, my father will stop worrying about the donkeys and start worrying about us!”
translation_verse: Ba ɡaaɡɔ dɛ ba tel Suf harɛ ta, asɛ Sɔɔl ŋɔ bonɔɔ waa ja o nɛɛ la be ŋɔ, “Yá berɛ kaa dem, ɡɛ laa aa, n mɛɛ sie ɛɛ berɔ beɡre ya wa, dɛ́ ɡwaa kɛ keeɡore nɔ aa nyoɡra nɔ.”

english_verse: “Wait!” the servant answered. “There's a man of God who lives in a town near here. He's amazing! Everything he says comes true. Let's talk to him. Maybe he can tell us where to look.”
translation_verse: Anee bonɔɔ la chaŋe ŋɔ, “Na, Korowii nɛn bɛl lɔ bwɛɛ nɔ ta. O wobɛlbwa waa bol dɛ ɛ kasinteŋ, baa duuru kohona ɡe. Gel ya la o be, o ken ɛɛ won baɡle yaa bela yaa kpɔ dɛ́ na keeɡore nɔ.”

english_verse: Saul said, “How can we talk to the prophet when I don't have anything to give him? We don't even have any bread left in our sacks. What can we give him?”
translation_verse: Ate, Sɔɔl bɔɔro ŋɔ, “Ya la baa la be naa, bɔkwaa yaa ba dɔe tɛo wɔ? Kondikwaa aa lɔ ya pure bini bwa tonɔ. Komɛlbwa toole yá dɔ ka tɛo.”

english_verse: “I have a small piece of silver,” the servant answered. “We can give him that, and then he will tell us where to look for the donkeys.”
translation_verse: Bonɔɔ la berɛ chaŋe ŋɔ, “N dɔ suuɡapoŋ jeɡaa bɛl n be, yá kpɔ ka tɛ Korowii nɛn waa dɛ na chaahna la, ásɛ o baɡle yaa bela yaa kpɔ dɛ́ naa.”

english_verse: “Great!” Saul replied. “Let's go to the man who can see visions!” He said this because in those days God would answer questions by giving visions to prophets. Saul and his servant went to the town where the prophet lived.
translation_verse: Anee Sɔɔl chaŋe ŋɔ, “A wer, ya kaa.” Asɛ ba chiɡ ŋwɛnɛ ta dɛ kaa bwɛɛ Korowii nɛn la aa lole la ta.

english_verse: As they were going up the hill to the town, they met some young women coming out to get water, and the two men said to them, “We're looking for the man who can see visions. Is he in town?”
translation_verse: Baa teeh deŋɡare bɛl dɛɛ kaa bwɛɛ la ta la, ba cheme bitoli bane baa dɛ ba bá dɔ ne. Asɛ ba bɔɔ ba ŋɔ, “Korowii nɛn bɛl waa dɛ na chaahna lɔ bonɔ naa?”

english_verse: “Yes, he is,” they replied. “He's in town today because there's going to be a sacrifice and a sacred meal at the place of worship. In fact, he's just ahead of you. Hurry
translation_verse: Ba chaŋe ŋɔ, “Ɔɔh, bɛl lole. O tɔ he sie, hé ɛ warane, finii o den ba ya bwɛɛ nɔ ta. Bwɛɛ la tena dɛ la ka kpoo kwaa bela baa dɛ ɛ saraha la.

english_verse: and you should find him right inside the town gate. He's on his way out to the place of worship to eat with the invited guests. They can't start eating until he blesses the sacrifice. If you go now, you should find him.”
translation_verse: Hé deno jo bwɛɛ la bini naa, hɛɛ nao mɔɔ dɛ́ kaa saraha la bɔr ka di kwa. Onee dɛ́ swee saraha kwaa ta tɛ nɛra la mɔɔ bá di, ásɛ mɔɔ nɛra baa ta nɔn yer ba la ɡe di. Hé kaa taraken, hɛ́ɛ ka nao.”

english_verse: They went to the town, and just as they were going through the gate, Samuel was coming out on his way to the place of worship.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl ne bonɔɔ la aa kaa jo bwɛɛ la ta ba den na Samoɛl o valɛ dɛɛ chem ba dɛ baa kaa saraha la bɔr.

english_verse: The day before Saul came, the Lord had told Samuel,
translation_verse: Tɔ aa per mɔɔ Sɔɔl ba la, dɛ Korowii pili waa la bini baɡle Samoɛl ŋɔ,

english_verse: “I've seen how my people are suffering, and I've heard their call for help. About this time tomorrow I'll send you a man from the tribe of Benjamin, who will rescue my people from the Philistines. I want you to pour olive oil on his head to show that he will be their leader.”
translation_verse: “Kere saŋ nɔ bɔr, mɛɛ tomɛ baa bɛlee le Bɛnjamen dea harɛ taa he be. O balaa, fuɡe noo do o nyu ta, dɛ́ ɛo n nɛra Israel tena sitɔɔ. Onee dɛ́ ba lɛɛ baa le Filisti tena nɔn ta. N na wenaale baa lɔ a ta, ba wii ɡe tel n be.”

english_verse: Samuel looked at Saul, and the Lord told Samuel, “This is the man I told you about. He's the one who will rule Israel.”
translation_verse: Samoɛl siwi aa dena dawɛ Sɔɔl nɛɛ la, Korowii ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Baa la maa bol o waa he be laanee la, onee dɛ́ ba nyiŋi n nɛra nɛ.”

english_verse: Saul went over to Samuel in the gateway and said, “A man who can see visions lives here in town. Could you tell me the way to his house?”
translation_verse: Sɔɔl kaa cheme Samoɛl doonyoa dɛ bɔɔro ŋɔ, “Leperaa Korowii nɛn waa dɛ na chaahna la dem doɔ?”

english_verse: “I am the one who sees visions!” Samuel answered. “Go on up to the place of worship. You will eat with me today, and in the morning I'll answer your questions.
translation_verse: Anee Samoɛl chaŋ ba ŋɔ, “Menee a ɡɛ nɛn la, hé tɔ n sie kaa saraha bɔr bela. Fini n ne heyaa dɛɛ ba kwaa dii, ásɛ tɔɔ perɔ chɔɔ aa, waa aa lɔ he be bwa la, ń bol baɡle heya, dɛ́ ta heyaa ŋwɛnɛ hé kaa.

english_verse: Don't worry about your donkeys that ran off three days ago. They've already been found. Everything of value in Israel now belongs to you and your family.”
translation_verse: Keeɡore aa nyoɡra tɔpera atoro bwaa nɔ la te, he bɛ ɡel a waa hiah heya, ba naa. Hen Sɔɔl nɛɛ Israel tena bwa sie dawɛ. Nomɛlbwa toole ka ja he ne he mɛɛ dem tena nɛ.”

english_verse: “Why are you telling me this?” Saul asked. “I'm from Benjamin, the smallest tribe in Israel, and my clan is the least important in the tribe.” Saul Eats with Samuel and Stays at His House
translation_verse: Ate, Sɔɔl chaŋe ŋɔ, “Bɛnjamen dea o nɛra aa wola kanɛ Israel deene bwa binii n le. N lolanar ɡe toole wobɛlbwa bini. Ɛrɛɛ hɛɛ bol ɡɛ waa nɔ n be nɔɔ?”

english_verse: Then Samuel told the cook, “I gave you the best piece of meat and told you to set it aside. Bring it here now.” The cook brought the meat over and set it down in front of Saul. “This is for you,” Samuel told him. “Go ahead and eat it. I had this piece saved especially for you, and I invited these guests to eat with you.” After Saul and Samuel had finished eating,
translation_verse: Asɛ o kpɔ ol la hwii ne o nakpala bwa ba cheɡ Sɔɔl sie. Ate, Samoɛl ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Ol maa kpɔa cheɡe laanee la. Chwe, dɛkalkɛ anee n kpɔ cheɡe, he ne nɛra maa ta nɔn yer ba nɔ pɛ di.” Sɔɔl ne Samoɛl pɛo di kondikwaa awola.

english_verse: they went down from the place of worship and back into town. A bed was set up for Saul on the flat roof of Samuel's house,
translation_verse: Baa le saraha bɔr bela dɛ ba bwɛɛ la ta la, Samoɛl ɡelɔ ba pa kalaŋ tɛ Sɔɔl o chɔ o saldoa, asɛ o la o ne o ka bol wa.

english_verse: and Saul slept there. About sunrise the next morning, Samuel called up to Saul on the roof, “Time to get up! I'll help you get started on your way.” Saul got up. He and Samuel left together
translation_verse: Ba iro bɔr chaahna saŋ, asɛ Samoɛl la Sɔɔl be saldoa bela dɛ ŋɔ, “Ir dɛ́ kpɔ he te, ásɛ n ka doe ŋwɛnɛ.” Asɛ o kpɔ o te ba bwa le kaa.

english_verse: and had almost reached the edge of town when Samuel stopped and said, “Tell your servant go on. Stay here with me for a few minutes, and I'll tell you what God has told me.” Samuel Tells Saul He Will Be King After the servant had gone,
translation_verse: Baa dɛ tel bwɛɛ la dahare la, Samoɛl ŋɔ Sɔɔl be ŋɔ ó ŋɔ bonɔɔ la be ásɛ wɛɛ tɔ sie, asɛ o ba tɔ ba sie dɛɛ kaa. O ŋɔ Sɔɔl be ŋɔ, “He te so bonɔ tama, ásɛ n bol waa aa le Korowii be baɡle.”

english_verse: Samuel took a small jar of olive oil and poured it on Saul's head. Then he kissed Saul and told him: The Lord has chosen you to be the leader and ruler of his people.
translation_verse: Belaa Samoɛl kpɔ ɔleve noo loŋbir dɛ fuɡe do Sɔɔl nyu ta, dɛ ɡbaaro pɛl bambile dɛ ŋɔ, “Korowii lee he ɛ o nɛra Israel tena sitɔɔ. Hɛɛ nyiŋi ba nɛɛ, dɛ́ lɛɛ ba le ba dɔma baa bar ba cheme nɔn ta. Anee dɛ́ baɡle kɛŋɔ Korowii lee he ɛ o nɛra Israel sitɔɔ.

english_verse: When you leave me today, you'll meet two men near Rachel's tomb at Zelzah in the territory of Benjamin. They'll tell you, “The donkeys you've been looking for have been found. Your father has forgotten about them, and now he's worrying about you! He's wondering how he can find you.”
translation_verse: He le n be bonɔ fini dɛɛ kaa laa, hɛɛ cheme baala banɛ bane Rakɛl ŋwam taa, o lɔ Sɛlsa ne Bɛnjamen dea harɛ jwɛh ta. Baa ŋɔ he bee ŋɔ, ‘Keeɡore aa nyoɡra hɛɛ ɡaaɡe a bɔr la, ba naa. A waa laa bera hiah he mɛɛ kpa, o dɛ bɔɔ bela waa nae.’

english_verse: Go on from there until you reach the big oak tree at Tabor, where you'll meet three men on their way to worship God at Bethel. One of them will be leading three young goats, another will be carrying three round loaves of bread, and the last one will be carrying a clay jar of wine.
translation_verse: He le bela dɛɛ kaa laa, hɛɛ ka tel dajen bɛl waa lɔ bwɛɛ Tabɔ munii. Hɛɛ ka pu baala batoro bane baa dɛ kaa bwɛjen Bɛtel ka ɛ saraha tɛ Korowii. Ba bini bɛl lawɛ bombiire atoro teŋɛ o nɛ, nɛɛte kpoŋe paanoo atoro, asɛ toorote la ɡe kpoŋe sen aa lɔ oltɔn pur bini.

english_verse: After they greet you, they'll give you two loaves of bread.
translation_verse: Baa jaamee, dɛ́ kpɔ paanoo anɛ baa ɡɔɔra nyundua tɛ Korowii tɛɛ, ásɛ he lɛ.

english_verse: Next, go to Gibeah, where the Philistines have an army camp. As you're going into the town, you'll meet a group of prophets coming down from the place of worship. They'll be going along prophesying while others are walking in front of them, playing small harps, small drums, and flutes.
translation_verse: A habɔɔ, hɛɛ ka tel Korowii deŋɡare waa lɔ Gebea la taa, belaa Filisti tena baŋre ba tɛnte deene dɛ so. Haa dɛɛ jo bwɛɛ la doonyojen bini la, hɛɛ cheme Korowii keamere baa le saraha bɔr deŋɡare la ta dɛ teŋɛ dɔŋa nɛɛ dɛɛ ba, dɛɛ lɔ janjela ne ɡboŋri, dɛɛ hoh kalipere. Baa bol Korowii waa.

english_verse: The Spirit of the Lord will suddenly take control of you. You'll become a different person and start prophesying right along with them.
translation_verse: Korowii Doma ɛɛ ba so he nɛɛ kpeɡri nɛɛ, dɛ́ beɡre nɛnfale, ásɛ he ne ba bwa ɛɛ bol Korowii waa aa dɛ́ ba bala kerekere.

english_verse: After these things happen, do whatever you think is right! God will help you.
translation_verse: Gɛ waa nɔ bwa ɛo waa, Korowii ɛɛ ba ja he nɛɛ he ɛ waa waa dɛ nyin kɛ he ɛ.

english_verse: Then go to Gilgal. I'll come a little later, so wait for me. It may even take a week for me to get there, but when I come, I'll offer sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask for his blessings. I'll also tell you what to do next. Saul Goes Back Home
translation_verse: Berɛ tɔ n sie dɛ kaa bwɛjen Gelɡal. Mɛɛ pui belaa dɛ́ ba fuh kwaa ɛ saraha ne deŋnesɔɔhna saraha. Kɛ so ka tel tɔpera anuanɛ mɔɔ ń ba baɡle waa haa ɛ.” Ba cheɡ Sɔɔl kora ta

english_verse: As Saul turned around to leave Samuel, God made Saul feel like a different person. That same day, everything happened just as Samuel had said.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl aa dɛ le Samoɛl be la, Korowii charɛ Sɔɔl liire asɛ waa Samoɛl aa bola la bwa ɛ ɡɛ.

english_verse: When Saul arrived at Gibeah, a group of prophets met him. The Spirit of God suddenly took control of him, and right there in the middle of the group he began prophesying.
translation_verse: Baa tel Gebea la, Korowii keamere teŋɛ dɔŋa nɛɛ ba chemo, asɛ Korowii Doma ba so o nɛɛ kpeɡri nɛ, o ka ja ba nɛ baa bol Korowii waa aa dɛ ba bala kerekere.

english_verse: Some people who had known Saul for a long time saw that he was speaking and behaving like a prophet. They said to each other, “What's happened? How can Saul be a prophet?”
translation_verse: Nɛra ba fa aa jemɛ Sɔɔl, dɛ na kɛ o berɔ ja Korowii keamere nɛɛ o ne baa bol Korowii waa ɡɛ la bɔɔ dɔŋa ŋɔ, “Bɔkwa waa ba Kes bibaa nɔ nɛɔ? O ɡe berɔ ɛ Korowii keame la bɛl kɛɛ?”

english_verse: “Why not?” one of them answered. “Saul has as much right to be a prophet as anyone else!” That's why everyone started saying, “How can Saul be a prophet?”
translation_verse: Anee baa bɛl waa soɡe bela bɔɔ ŋɔ, “Ba mɛɛnanaree bame waɔ?” Anomanta, ba kpɔɔ dɛɛ bol waa ŋɔ, “Sɔɔl ɡe ɛ Korowii keamere la bɛl kɛɛ?”

english_verse: After Saul stopped prophesying, he went to the place of worship.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl aa bol Korowii waa tonɛ la, o berɔ kaa saraha bɔr deŋɡare la ta.

english_verse: Later, Saul's uncle asked him, “Where have you been?” Saul answered, “Looking for the donkeys. We couldn't find them, so we went to talk with Samuel.”
translation_verse: Asɛ Sɔɔl mɛwee bɔɔ o ne o bonɔɔ la ŋɔ, “Leperaa he kaalɔ?” Sɔɔl ɡe chaŋo ŋɔ, “Keeɡore la bɔree ya kaa ɡaaɡe, asɛ yaa wola an na la ya kaa Samoɛl be.”

english_verse: “And what did he tell you?” Saul's uncle asked.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl mɛwee la ŋɔ, “Bol waa Samoɛl aa bol he be la baɡ mɛ.”

english_verse: Saul answered, “He told us the donkeys had been found.” But Saul didn't mention that Samuel had chosen him to be king. The Lord Shows Israel that Saul Will Be King
translation_verse: Anee Sɔɔl ŋɔ, “Samoɛl ɡelɔ ya jemɛ kɛŋɔ ba na keeɡore la.” Kɛ o ta kara dii waa Samoɛl aa bola la te baɡlɛ. Sɔɔl lɛɛ dɛ do kɛ kooro

english_verse: Samuel sent messengers to tell the Israelites to come to Mizpah and meet with the Lord.
translation_verse: Samoɛl cheme Israel tena la bwa Korowii sie Mispa,

english_verse: When everyone had arrived, Samuel said: The Lord God of Israel told me to remind you that he had rescued you from the Egyptians and from the other nations that abused you.
translation_verse: dɛ ŋɔ Korowii Israel tena aa dɛ tomɔ la ŋɔ, “Menee lawɛ heyaa le Ijipt harɛ ta, dɛ lɛ heyaa le Ijipt tena ne harɛfala nɛra baa dɛ fiiɡi heyaa nɔn ta.

english_verse: God has rescued you from your troubles and hard times. But you have rejected your God and have asked for a king. Now each tribe and clan must come near the place of worship so the Lord can choose a king.
translation_verse: Kɛ taraken he vɛh men Korowii haa dɛ tom mɛ, n lɛ heyaa le wahala ne wekpeɡa bwa ta la. He berɔ ŋɔ ń tɛ heyaa kooro wɛɛ tɔ he sie. Anomanta, he bwa ba cheme n sie deenaa ta.”

english_verse: Samuel brought each tribe, one after the other, to the altar, and the Lord chose the Benjamin tribe.
translation_verse: Samoɛl aa ɡela Israel deene bwa ba cheme la, Bɛnjamen dea tenaa Korowii lawɛ.

english_verse: Next, Samuel brought each clan of Benjamin there, and the Lord chose the Matri clan. Finally, Saul the son of Kish was chosen. But when they looked for him, he was nowhere to be found.
translation_verse: O berɔ ɡel Bɛnjamen dea nɛra ba o sie lolanar ta, asɛ Korowii lawɛ Matri lolanar. A habɔɔ la, Sɔɔl waa ɛ Kes bibaa laanee Korowii lawɛ, kɛ baa nyiŋa la dɛ Sɔɔl toole ba bini.

english_verse: The people prayed, “Our Lord, is Saul here?” “Yes,” the Lord answered, “he is hiding behind the baggage.”
translation_verse: Anee ba ka bɔɔ le Korowii be ŋɔ, “Sɔɔl ta bonɔ balɛ mɔɔ kɛɛ?” Asɛ Korowii ŋɔ, “O sɔh bone la habɔɔ.”

english_verse: The people ran and got Saul and brought him into the middle of the crowd. He was more than a head taller than anyone else.
translation_verse: Ate, ba chwa ka kpɔɔ ba, dɛ o cheɡɛ nɛra bini, dɛ kpeɡ ɡwaa ba bwa.

english_verse: “Look closely at the man the Lord has chosen!” Samuel told the crowd. “There is no one like him!” The crowd shouted, “Long live the king!”
translation_verse: Samoɛl ŋɔ nɛra la bwa be ŋɔ, “Kɛ he bwa na nɛn Korowii aa leo kenɛ? Ya bini bɛlbwa toole dɛ do kɛ on.” Anee nɛra la bwa moo ŋɔ, “Kórowii tɛ kooro mkpajaŋ!”

english_verse: Samuel explained the rights and duties of a king and wrote them all in a book. He put the book in one of the shrines where the Lord was worshiped. Then Samuel sent everyone home.
translation_verse: Samoɛl kure kara mun mmarare baɡle nɛra la. O chwera do tɔn bini dɛ kpɔ ka bil Korowii sie bela. Asɛ Samoɛl ta ba ŋwɛnɛ, bɛlbwa kaa bela waa lea ba.

english_verse: God had encouraged some young men to become followers of Saul, and when he returned to his hometown of Gibeah, they went with him.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl ɡe berɔ kaa Gebea bela waa soɡa. Korowii ɡelɔ laa tena baa kpeɡa sie lɛ o nɛ, asɛ ba teŋɛ o nɛɛ kaa.

english_verse: But some worthless fools said, “How can someone like Saul rescue us from our enemies?” They did not want Saul to be their king, and so they didn't bring him any gifts. But Saul kept calm.
translation_verse: Kɛ nɛnchɔɡa bane ɡe ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ nɛn waa do ken ɡe ɛɛ ba wona lɛ yaa ɔ?” Ba haoh dɛɛ nyiŋi o nyubaah, ba ta on koŋkɛɛla bɛlbwa ba tɛɛ. Sɔɔl ɡe ta ba waa la kpɔe ɛ wobɛlbwa.

english_verse: About this time, King Nahash of Ammon came with his army and surrounded the town of Jabesh in Gilead. The people who lived there told Nahash, “If you will sign a peace treaty with us, you can be our ruler, and we will pay taxes to you.”
translation_verse: Dɛ ɛ korobie beŋkpoŋ habɔɔ la, Amɔn Kooro Nahas tɔ o laa tena sie ba ka bar bwɛɛ Jabes waa lɔ Gelead harɛ ta dɛ́ yoo ba. Anee Jabes baala bwa ŋɔ Kooro Nahas be ŋɔ, “Gel ya ne he fɔwɛ fɔo, ásɛ ya do he lɔɡa.”

english_verse: Nahash answered, “Sure, I'll sign a treaty! But not before I insult Israel by poking out the right eye of every man who lives in Jabesh.”
translation_verse: Anee Kooro Nahas chaŋe ŋɔ, “N ne hɛɛ fɔwɛ fɔwee yaa, webeŋkpoŋ taa aa ba cheɡa. Atane n fome he bini bɛlbwa diɡ siwi, ásɛ a ɛ sihihwa tɛ Israel tena bwa.”

english_verse: The town leaders said, “Give us seven days so we can send messengers everywhere in Israel to ask for help. If no one comes here to save us, we will surrender to you.”
translation_verse: Belaa Jabes nomonome ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Tɛ yaa tɔpera anuanɛ ásɛ ya tomɛ nɛra Israel harɛ ta bwa, dɛ ya ta nomɛlbwa dɔe ó ba lɛ yaa aa, yáa kpɔ ya tenee do he lɔɡa.”

english_verse: Some of the messengers went to Gibeah, Saul's hometown. They told what was happening at Jabesh, and everyone in Gibeah started crying.
translation_verse: Toroma la aa tel Gebea bela Sɔɔl aa soɡa dɛ bol ɡɛ waa nɔ ba be la, ba wio kɛrɛdɛ.

english_verse: Just then, Saul came in from the fields, walking behind his oxen. “Why is everyone crying?” Saul asked. They told him what the men from Jabesh had said.
translation_verse: Buɡ la ta, dɛ Sɔɔl teŋɛ o nae baa kpɔa dɛɛ parɛ le koo ta dɛɛ ba. Waa no wii la, o bɔɔrɔ ŋɔ, “Bɔkwa waa chiɡa ɔ? Ɛrɛɛ bɛlbwa ɛɛ wi ɡɛ nɔɔ?” Asɛ ba bol waa Jabes baala la aa baa bol la ba be.

english_verse: Then the Spirit of God suddenly took control of Saul and made him furious.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl aa no waa nɔ la, Korowii Doma baa so o nɛɛ kpeɡri nɛ, asɛ o baah di kohona.

english_verse: Saul killed two of his oxen, cut them up in pieces, and gave the pieces to the messengers. He told them to show the pieces to everyone in Israel and say, “Saul and Samuel are getting an army together. Come and join them. If you don't, this is what will happen to your oxen!” The Lord made the people of Israel terribly afraid. So all the men came together
translation_verse: O lawɛ nabala anɛ kpo, dɛ chɛwa dɛ kpɔ tomɛ nɛra Israel harɛ ta bwa ŋɔ, “Nomɛlbwa waa wola Samoɛl ne Sɔɔl nɛɛ teŋɛ la, kenii baa ba o nae kpoe dɛ chɛwa.” Korowii ɡelɔ ɔmee kohona chole ba bwa nɛ, asɛ ba pɛ nyoa ba ja Samoɛl ne Sɔɔl nɛ.

english_verse: Saul and his officers sent the messengers back to Jabesh with this promise: “We will rescue you tomorrow afternoon.” The messengers went back to the people at Jabesh and told them that they were going to be rescued. Everyone was encouraged!
translation_verse: Sɔɔl ne o nomonome ŋɔ toroma baa le Jabes la be ŋɔ, “Hé ka ŋɔ he nɛra be kɛŋɔ, ‘Le kere wee ne ŋɔ o che nyufala dɛ he dɔ lɛɛ.’ ” Toroma la aa laŋa dɛ ka bol Jabes tena la be la, ba sie lɛo kohona,

english_verse: So they told the Ammonites, “We will surrender to you tomorrow, and then you can do whatever you want to.”
translation_verse: dɛ ŋɔ Amɔn tena la be ŋɔ, “Kere yaa kpɔ ya tenee ba do he lɔɡa, ásɛ he ɛ yaa ɡɛ bwa haa dɛ nyin.”

english_verse: The next day, Saul divided his army into three groups and attacked before daylight. They started killing Ammonites and kept it up until afternoon. A few Ammonites managed to escape, but they were scattered far from each other.
translation_verse: Tɔ aa pera la, Sɔɔl bɔne o laa tena bini kuore atoro, asɛ bɔr aa dɛ chaah la ba ka lɔ tɔ Amɔn tena la nɛ bela baa soɡa, dɛ kpoo ba ka tel webaŋa. Banɔ la baa kaa la ɡe lɔ peɡre, bɛlbwa chwa dɛɛ nyin o nyu. Sɔɔl lɛɛ dɛ do kɛ kooro

english_verse: The Israelite soldiers went to Samuel and demanded, “Where are the men who said they didn't want Saul to be king? Bring them to us, and we will put them to death!”
translation_verse: Ate, Israel tena la ŋɔ Samoɛl be ŋɔ, “Nɛn besooree ŋɔa ŋɔ Sɔɔl bɛ ya kooro ɛ laɔ? Le ba ne tɛ yaa ya kpoo ba.”

english_verse: “No you won't!” Saul told them. “The Lord rescued Israel today, and no one will be put to death.” Saul Is Accepted as King
translation_verse: Anee Sɔɔl ŋɔ, “Baa nomɛlbwa kpoe ba fini, fini tɔperee Korowii lɛ o nɛra Israel tena.”

english_verse: “Come on!” Samuel said. “Let's go to Gilgal and make an agreement that Saul will continue to be our king.”
translation_verse: Ate, Samoɛl ŋɔ Israel tena la be ŋɔ, “Hé ba ya bwa kaa Gelɡal dɛ́ ka che Sɔɔl mun ta dɛ́ lɛo do kɛ ya kooro kɛrɛdɛ.”

english_verse: Everyone went to the place of worship at Gilgal, where they agreed that Saul would be their king. Saul and the people sacrificed animals to ask for the Lord's blessing, and they had a big celebration.
translation_verse: Anomanta, nɛra la bwa la Gelɡal bela, Korowii sie, dɛ ka lɛo do kɛ ba kooro. Ba kpoo kwaa ɛ deŋnesɔɔhna saraha, asɛ Sɔɔl ne Israel tena la bwa di kondikonjena dɛ lɛ ba sie.

english_verse: Samuel told the Israelites: I have given you a king, just as you asked.
translation_verse: Samoɛl ŋɔ Israel tena la bwa be ŋɔ, “N no waa haa bɔɔra la, dɛ nyin kooro tɛ heya o tɔ he sie dɛɛ nyiŋi he nɛ.

english_verse: You have seen how I have led you ever since I was a young man. I'm already old. My hair is gray, and my own sons are grown. Now you must see how well your king will lead you.
translation_verse: Taraken he dɔ kooro o ɛ he sitɔɔ. N hwɛɛhrɔ n nyumpona to, asɛ n bibaala do he bini bonɔ. N bonɔɔne saŋ bwaa n le dɛ tɔ he sie dɛ ba le fini.

english_verse: Let me ask this. Have I ever taken anyone's ox or donkey or forced you to give me anything? Have I ever hurt anyone or taken a bribe to give an unfair decision? Answer me so the Lord and his chosen king can hear you. And if I have done any of these things, I will give it all back.
translation_verse: N cheɡɛ bonɔ fini, dɛ n ɛ nomɛl wechɔɡe bɛl aa, bɛlbwa bol Korowii ne nɛn waa leo cheɡ o ɛ kooro nɔ sie. N lɛ nomɛl keeɡo kɛɛ nao o be naa? N faah nomɛl kɛɛ dɛ fiiɡi nomɛl aa? Umee n ɡel o yaɡ mɛ sen ɔ? Dɛ n ɛ anɔ bini bɛlbwa naa, mɛɛ bɔ naate a kemee.”

english_verse: “No,” the Israelites answered. “You've never cheated us in any way!”
translation_verse: Ba ɡe chaŋe ŋɔ, “He ta yaa faahrɛ kɛɛ dɛ fiiɡi bɛlbwa, he ta komɛlbwa ɡe lɛɛ le nomɛlbwa be.”

english_verse: Samuel said, “The Lord and his chosen king are witnesses to what you have said.” “That's true,” they replied.
translation_verse: Anee Samoɛl ŋɔ, “Korowii ne kooro waa leo laanee ɛ he danseɛ fini kɛŋɔ he ta wechɔɡe bɛlbwa n nɛɛ nae.” Asɛ ba chaŋe ŋɔ, “Ɔɔh, Korowiirii ya danseɛ.”

english_verse: Then Samuel told them: The Lord brought your ancestors out of Egypt and chose Moses and Aaron to be your leaders.
translation_verse: Ate, Samoɛl berɛ ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, “Korowiirii le Mosis ne Arɔn ba ka lawɛ he naawa le Ijipt harɛ ta.

english_verse: Now the Lord will be your judge. So stand here and listen, while I remind you how often the Lord has saved you and your ancestors from your enemies.
translation_verse: Name, hé che bonɔ, ásɛ n ɡel Korowii bol he be hé jemɛ nyokpowe-ɛɛla waa ɛa dɛ́ lɛ he ne he naawa la.

english_verse: After Jacob went to Egypt, your ancestors cried out to the Lord for help, and he sent Moses and Aaron. They brought your ancestors out of Egypt and led them here to settle this land.
translation_verse: Jekɔb ne o bii aa kaa jo Ijipt harɛ ta asɛ baa fiɡ ba la, he naawa wio no Korowii ŋɔ ó cha ba. Asɛ o tomɛ Mosis ne Arɔn ba ba lawɛ he naawa le Ijipt harɛ ta, dɛ kpɔ ba ba so bonɔ.

english_verse: But your ancestors forgot the Lord, so he let them be defeated by the Philistines, the king of Moab, and Sisera, the commander of Hazor's army.
translation_verse: Kɛ ba soh Korowii baa dɛ tomɔ la wa, anomanta, o ɡelɔ Filisti tena ne Moab kooro dɛ Sisera waa ɛ laa sitɔɔ dɛ do bwɛjen Hasɔ ba yo he naawa dɛ pɔ ba nɛ.

english_verse: Again your ancestors cried out to the Lord for help. They said, “We have sinned! We stopped worshiping you, our Lord, and started worshiping Baal and Astarte. But now, if you rescue us from our enemies, we will worship you.”
translation_verse: Ba wio yerɛ Korowii ŋɔ, ‘Korowii, ya ɛɛ wechɔɡa dɛ vɛh he toma dɛ kaa tomɛ voɡa Baalre aa ɛ baala ne voɡhaahna Astɔrɛt. Name te lɛ yaa le ya dɔma nɔn ta ásɛ yaa tomɛ.’

english_verse: The Lord sent Gideon, Bedan, Jephthah, and Samuel to rescue you from your enemies, and you didn't have to worry about being attacked.
translation_verse: Korowii tomɛ Gedeɔn ne Barak ne Jɛfta dɛ men Samoɛl asɛ ya ba lɛ heyaa le he dɔma nɔn ta, he so deŋnesɔɔhna ta.

english_verse: Then you saw that King Nahash of Ammon was going to attack you. And even though the Lord your God is your king, you told me, “This time it's different. We want a king to rule us!”
translation_verse: Háa na Amɔn Kooro Nahas wɛɛ ba dɛ́ ba yo heyaa la, he le Korowii waa ɛ he kooro la habɔɔ, dɛ ŋɔ n be ŋɔ, ‘Ya dɛ nyin kooro wɛ́ɛ nyiŋi ya nɛ.’

english_verse: If you and your king want to be followers of the Lord, you must worship him and do what he says. Don't be stubborn!
translation_verse: Dɛ he dɛ ɔmɛ Korowii dɛɛ tomɔ dɛɛ teŋɛ o Mmarare ta, hale he ne he kooro bwa naa, he wobɛlbwa ɛɛ do werii tɛ heya.

english_verse: If you're stubborn and refuse to obey the Lord, he will turn against you and your king.
translation_verse: Kɛ dɛ haa duure kpɔe dɛɛ tɛo, dɛ vɛh o Mmarare ta teŋa aa, o baah ɛɛ di he ne he kooro nɛɛ ɡɛ o baah fa aa di he naawa nɛɛ la.

english_verse: Just stand here and watch the Lord show his mighty power.
translation_verse: Anomanta, hé che bela haa cheɡa, dɛ́ na wejena Korowii aa dɛ́ ba ɛɛ he siwi ta.

english_verse: Isn't this the dry season? I'm going to ask the Lord to send a thunderstorm. When you see it, you will realize how wrong you were to ask for a king.
translation_verse: Lɔmɔɡa saŋ laa nɔ naa? Mɛɛ soŋe Korowiirii ó ɡel bwaala nɛ dɛ kɔr. Anee hɛɛ ba nae kɛŋɔ kooro haa soŋa la ɛ wechɔɡa Korowii be.”

english_verse: Samuel prayed, and that same day the Lord sent a thunderstorm. Everyone was afraid of the Lord and of Samuel.
translation_verse: Anee Samoɛl soŋe Korowii awola, asɛ bwaala nɛ dɛ kɔr kohona. Asɛ ɔmee kohona lawɛ nɛra la bwa Korowii ne Samoɛl wa.

english_verse: They told Samuel, “Please, pray to the Lord your God for us! We don't want to die. We have sinned many times in the past, and we were very wrong to ask for a king.”
translation_verse: Ate, nɛra la bwa ŋɔ Samoɛl be ŋɔ, “Soŋe Korowii haa dɛ tomɔ la, ásɛ yan yaa ɛ he bonɔɔna nɔ bɛ serewe. Ya wechɔɡa la habɔɔ, ya berɔ ɛ wechɔɡa kɛŋɔ yaa ŋɔa ya dɛ nyin kooro la.”

english_verse: Samuel answered: Even though what you did was wrong, you don't need to be afraid. But you must always follow the Lord and worship him with all your heart.
translation_verse: Samoɛl ŋɔ, “A lole kɛŋɔ he ɛ wechɔɡa nɔ bwa te, kɛ hɛɛ berɛ ɔma, he bɛ habɔɔ berɛ kpo Korowii, hɛ́ɛ tomɔ bambile bwa ne.

english_verse: Don't worship idols! They don't have any power, and they can't help you or save you when you're in trouble.
translation_verse: Hé laa sie kpɔ voɡa ta. Wedɛɛɡa bɛlbwa toole a toma ta. Aa won lɛ heya, a wobɛlbwa ɛ wepuu.

english_verse: But the Lord has chosen you to be his own people. He will always take care of you so that everyone will know how great he is.
translation_verse: Korowii ŋwɛɛrɔ ŋɔ, waa o nɛraa vɛh. O sie lɛo kɛŋɔ ó kpɔ heyaa ɛ o nɛra.

english_verse: I would be disobeying the Lord if I stopped praying for you! I will always teach you how to live right.
translation_verse: Korowii ɛɛ la ane bojaŋ kɛŋɔ n ɛo wechɔɡa dɛ́ vɛh kɛ mɛɛ soŋo tɛ heya. Mɛɛ baɡle heyaa waa aa wera ne anɔ la aa toɡraa.

english_verse: You also must obey the Lord—you must worship him with all your heart and remember the great things he has done for you.
translation_verse: Hé nyiŋi kɛrɛdɛ dɛ́ɛ teŋɛ Korowii waa ta dɛ́ɛ tomɔ kasinteŋ ne bambile bwa ne, dɛ́ɛ lii wejena waa ɛa tɛ heya la.

english_verse: But if you and your king do evil, the Lord will wipe you out.
translation_verse: Kɛ dɛ he ta nao dɛɛ ɛ wechɔɡa aa, he ne he kooro bwa ɛɛ serewoo.”
