english_verse: The messengers then said to the people of Israel, “Saul has destroyed the Philistine army camp at Geba. Now the Philistines really hate Israel, so every town and village must send men to join Saul's army at Gilgal.”
translation_verse: Anomanta, Israel tena la bwa aa noa kɛŋɔ Sɔɔl kpo Filisti tena laa nomoa bela o ne o laa tena aa soɡa la, Filisti tena hah Israel tena kohona. Israel laa tena la bwa baa cheme, dɛ ka ja Sɔɔl nɛɛ Gelɡal.

english_verse: The Israelite army realized that they were outnumbered and were going to lose the battle. Some of the Israelite men hid in caves or in clumps of bushes, and some ran to places where they could hide among large rocks. Others hid in tombs or in deep dry pits.
translation_verse: Israel laa tena la aa naa kɛŋɔ a kpeɡri tɛɛ ba name la, ba chwao ka sɔh bwebɔɔne ne sɔɔhne bini, ne bwea ne bɔɔne dɛ kɔlɔŋa bini dɛ́ lɛ ba nyuune.

english_verse: Still others went to Gad and Gilead on the other side of the Jordan River. Saul stayed at Gilgal. His soldiers were shaking with fear,
translation_verse: Ba bini banɔ la baa kaa ɡe ɡale Jɔɔdan Moo, dɛ kaa Gad ne Gelead harɛre ta. Kooro Sɔɔl te ka Gelɡal, asɛ ɔmee chole laa tena baa ja o nɛɛ la nɛɛ kohona baa chel.

english_verse: and they were starting to run off and leave him. Saul waited there seven days, just as Samuel had ordered him to do, but Samuel did not come.
translation_verse: Kooro Sɔɔl soɡe bela ka tel tɔpera anuanɛ ɡɛ Samoɛl aa doo la. Kɛ Samoɛl ta wone ba o be Gelɡal ɡɛ waa doo la, asɛ Sɔɔl nɛra la pa mun dɛɛ peɡre.

english_verse: Finally, Saul commanded, “Bring me some animals, so we can offer sacrifices to please the Lord and ask for his help.” Saul killed one of the animals,
translation_verse: Kooro Sɔɔl ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, “Hé kpɔ saraha kwaa baa fuah ne deŋnesɔɔhna saraha kwaa ba.” Asɛ Kooro Sɔɔl kpɔ fuh ɛ saraha.

english_verse: and just as he placed it on the altar, Samuel arrived. Saul went out to welcome him.
translation_verse: Waa ɛ saraha la dɛɛ tonɛ la, buɡ la ta, Samoɛl ɡe den tel bela. Asɛ Kooro Sɔɔl le dɛ ba chemo.

english_verse: “What have you done?” Samuel asked. Saul answered, “My soldiers were leaving in all directions, and you didn't come when you were supposed to. The Philistines were gathering at Michmash,
translation_verse: Samoɛl bɔɔro ŋɔ, “Bɔkwa waa he ɛ nɔɔ?” Kooro Sɔɔl chaŋo ŋɔ, “Saŋ haa doa la aa baa kaa haa wola balɛ mɔɔ, asɛ nɛra la ɛɛ peɡre, asɛ Filisti tena ɡe baa cheme Mikmas la,

english_verse: and I was worried that they would attack me here at Gilgal. I hadn't offered a sacrifice to ask for the Lord's help, so I forced myself to offer a sacrifice on the altar fire.”
translation_verse: n liiro kɛ Filisti tena ɛɛ ba yoo mɛɛ Gelɡal, maa wola chae soŋɛ le Korowii be wa. Anomanta, n nao kɛ a chɛ kɛ ń fuh saraha kwaa tɛ Korowii.”

english_verse: “That was stupid!” Samuel said. “You didn't obey the Lord your God. If you had obeyed him, someone from your family would always have been king of Israel.
translation_verse: Samoɛl ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “He ɛ ɡɛnewa. He ta Korowii haa dɛ tomɔ doe waa doe la kpɔe ɛ toma ɡɛ aa chɛa. He fe teŋɛ ɡɛ waa doe la ta naa, o fe ɛɛ ɡeloo he ne he naanar di kora Israel harɛ saŋ bɛlbwa dɛɛ la.

english_verse: But no, you disobeyed, and so the Lord won't choose anyone else from your family to be king. In fact, he has already chosen the one he wants to be the next leader of his people.”
translation_verse: Taraken he kora aa lee do kpa. Korowii ɛɛ le nɛnfale o bambile aa lawaa, ásɛ o tɔ o nɛra sie. Dɛkalkɛ he ta o waa ta teŋɛ.”

english_verse: Then Samuel left Gilgal. Part of Saul's army had not deserted him, and he led them to Gibeah in Benjamin to join his other troops. Then he counted them and found that he still had
translation_verse: Samoɛl le Gelɡal dɛ kaa Gebea waa lɔ Bɛnjamen harɛ ta, asɛ Kooro Sɔɔl kure baala baa ja o nɛɛ la. Baa ɛ nɛra lafraanumɛlee.

english_verse: Saul, Jonathan, and their army set up camp at Geba in Benjamin. Jonathan Attacks the Philistines The Philistine army was camped at Michmash.
translation_verse: Kooro Sɔɔl ne o bibaa Jonatan ne baala baa ja ba nɛɛ la soɡe Gebea waa lɔ Bɛnjamen harɛ ta, asɛ Filisti tena la ɡe ka baŋre ba tɛnte deene dɛ so Mikmas.

english_verse: Each day they sent out patrols to attack and rob villages and then destroy them. One patrol would go north along the road to Ophrah in the region of Shual.
translation_verse: Filisti laa tena le bela baa soɡa, ba bɔne ba bini kuore atoro ba ka yo dɛ pa laala dɛɛ ba. Beŋkpoŋ kpɔ sie pa weekaŋle nyunduabɔr bwɛjen Ofra waa lɔ Sual harɛ ta,

english_verse: Another patrol would go west along the road to Beth-Horon. A third patrol would go east toward the desert on the road to the ridge that overlooks Zeboim Valley.
translation_verse: Bɛl ɡe kpɔ sie pa wee cholibɔr Bɛt Hɔrɔn pera. Banɔ la baa kaa la ɡe kpɔ sie chaɡɛ wee leebɔr pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ jwɛh ta, asɛ Seboim Fɛlembɔjen la sie chaɡɛ bela.

english_verse: The Philistines would not allow any Israelites to learn how to make iron tools. “If we allowed that,” they said, “those worthless Israelites would make swords and spears.”
translation_verse: Dɛ loɡre bɛlbwa toole Israel harɛ ta, dɛkalkɛ Filisti tena la ta sɛɛh kɛŋɔ Hibru tena la loɡɛ buni kon bɛlbwa. Gɛ laa aa, baa loɡɛ lampeare ne kerii.

english_verse: Whenever the Israelites wanted to get an iron point put on a cattle prod, they had to go to the Philistines. Even if they wanted to sharpen plow-blades, picks, axes, sickles, and pitchforks they still had to go to them. And the Philistines charged high prices.
translation_verse: Ba sar Israel tena la kwaa tɛɛ ba aa, ɡɛɛ ba lɛɛ ba yokpeɡ. Suuɡabwe jeɡaa ba lɛ dɛɛ sar kpanfɛre ne buni baa kpɔ lɔ nao o do sie parɛ, ne para nae aa dɛ parɛ ane ne para te bwa soo siwi la, suuɡabwea anɛɛ baa lɛ.

english_verse: So, whenever the Israelite soldiers had to go into battle, none of them had a sword or a spear except Saul and his son Jonathan.
translation_verse: Anomanta, dɛ laa baa chole aa, Israel te bɛlbwa aa kere kɛɛ lampea kpoŋe ka ja Kooro Sɔɔl ne o bibaa Jonatan nɛ.

english_verse: The Philistines moved their camp to the pass at Michmash,
translation_verse: Filisti tena le laa tena la bini bane, ba ka che ŋwɛnɛ waa chɔa kaa Mikmas dɛɛ daah bela.

english_verse: Jonathan decided to get to the Philistine camp by going through the pass that led between Shiny Cliff and Michmash to the north and Thornbush Cliff and Geba to the south.
translation_verse: Bwe la beŋkpoŋ cheɡɛ ŋwɛnɛ la weekaŋle nyunduabɔr o sie chaɡɛ Mikmas, asɛ nɛɛte la ɡe che weekaŋle harɛbɔr, o sie chaɡɛ Geba.

english_verse: Jonathan and the soldier who carried his weapons talked as they went toward the Philistine camp. “It's just the two of us against all those godless men,” Jonathan said. “But the Lord can help a few soldiers win a battle just as easily as he can help a whole army. Maybe the Lord will help us win this battle.”
translation_verse: Jonatan ŋɔ o bonɔɔ waa cheɡɛ o dɔmkwa la be ŋɔ, “Ba yá ɡale kaa Filisti tena baa wola Korowii tomɛ nɔ be. Korowii ken ɛɛ cha yaa. Komɛlbwa aa won tɔ Korowii ŋwɛnɛ yaa wola won pɔ ba nɛ, ya warɔ kɛɛ ya ta warɛ kwara noo.”

english_verse: “Do whatever you want,” the soldier answered. “I'll be right there with you.”
translation_verse: O bonɔɔ la ŋɔ, “Ɛ ɡɛ bwa haa dɛ nyin he ɛ, n cheɡɛ he habɔɔ kiŋkiŋ ken.”

english_verse: “This is what we will do,” Jonathan said. “We will go across and let them see us.
translation_verse: Anee Jonatan ŋɔ, “Ba yá ɡale ka kpɔ Filisti tena la sie ásɛ ba na yaa.

english_verse: If they agree to come down the hill and fight where we are, then we won't climb up to their camp.
translation_verse: Dɛ ba ŋɔ ya be ŋɔ, ‘Hé che bela ya ba pu heya aa,’ yaa che ya buɡ ta belaa.

english_verse: But we will go if they tell us to come up the hill and fight. That will mean the Lord is going to help us win.”
translation_verse: Kɛ dɛ ba ŋɔ, ‘Hé ba ya be bonɔ naa,’ yaa teehnoo kaa ba be, anee dɛ́ chaɡle kɛŋɔ Korowii kpɔ ba do ya nɔn ta.”

english_verse: Jonathan and the soldier stood at the bottom of the hill where the Philistines could see them. The Philistines said, “Look! Those worthless Israelites have crawled out of the holes where they've been hiding.” Then they yelled down to Jonathan and the soldier, “Come up here, and we will teach you a thing or two!” Jonathan turned to the soldier and said, “Follow me! The Lord is going to let us win.”
translation_verse: Ate, Filisti tena baa lɔ bela la nyɛɡ Jonatan ne o bonɔɔ la nɛɛ ŋɔ, “Hé ba ya be nyundua bonɔ, ásɛ ya baɡle heyaa waane.” Anee Jonatan ŋɔ o bonɔɔ la be ŋɔ, “Teŋɛ n nɛ dɛɛ ba, Korowii kpɔ ba do Israel tena nɔn ta.”

english_verse: Jonathan crawled up the hillside with the soldier right behind him. When they got to the top, Jonathan killed the Philistines who attacked from the front, and the soldier killed those who attacked from behind.
translation_verse: Jonatan kpɔ nakpale ne nɔɔra huuh dɛɛ kaa, asɛ o bonɔɔ la ɡe teŋɛ. Jonatan kaa yo Filisti tena la dɛ pɔ ba nɛ ba choɡli chɔ, asɛ o bonɔɔ la ɡe teŋɛ dɛɛ kpoo ba.

english_verse: I wish you had eaten some of the food the Philistines left behind. We would have been able to kill a lot more of them.”
translation_verse: Dɛ laa tena nɔ fe dɔ kondikwa baa paa laa ta le ba dɔma be nɔ ane di aa, ba bwara fe kpeɡri. Filisti tena baa kpoora fe ta ken ɡwaalaa?”

english_verse: Saul quickly called his army together, then led them to the Philistine camp. By this time the Philistines were so confused that they were killing each other.
translation_verse: Ate, Kooro Sɔɔl ne o laa tena la bwa cheme, dɛ kaa laa la ta. Ba kaa pu Filisti tena la kɛŋɔ ba wilo kohona, dɛ berɛ sie ta dɔŋa nɛɛ dɛɛ kpoo.

english_verse: The whole Philistine army panicked—those in camp, those on guard duty, those in the fields, and those on raiding patrols. All of them were afraid and confused. Then God sent an earthquake, and the ground began to tremble. Israel Defeats the Philistines
translation_verse: Belaa ɔmee kohona chole laa tena la bwa nɛɛ baa chel, banɔ la baa lɔ bela baa baŋre ba tɛnte deene ne banɔ la baa lɔ kpɔɡ bini, dɛ nɛra baa laŋa dɛɛ la ka yo bwa. Korowii ɡelɔ harɛ jiɡri ɔmee kohona chole ba nɛ.

english_verse: Saul's lookouts at Geba saw that the Philistine army was running in every direction, like melted wax.
translation_verse: Kooro Sɔɔl laa tena baa dɛ daahno dɛ do Bɛnjamen harɛ ta Gebea la na Filisti tena kɛŋɔ baa wila, dɛ chwa sibeɡra ne bobɛlbwa dɛɛ kaa.

english_verse: Saul told his officers, “Call the roll and find out who left our camp.” When they had finished, they found out that Jonathan and the soldier who carried his weapons were missing.
translation_verse: Anee o ŋɔ laa tena o ne baa lɔ bela la be ŋɔ, “Hé bwa ba boa nyoa dɛ́ na he bini banɔ la baa wola toole. Baa chema la, dɛ Jonatan ne o bonɔɔ waa dɛ che o dɔmkwaa laanee wola toole ba bini.”

english_verse: At that time, Ahijah was serving as priest for the army of Israel, and Saul told him, “Come over here! Let's ask God what we should do.”
translation_verse: Kooro Sɔɔl ŋɔ sɔfo Ahija be ŋɔ, “Ka kpɔ Korowii Ne Nɛwɛnyina Fɔo Daka la ba.” Gɛ saŋ dɛ Israel tena bee o do.

english_verse: Just as Saul finished saying this, he could see that the Philistine army camp was getting more and more confused, and he said, “Ahijah, never mind!”
translation_verse: O taa dɛ bol waa sɔfo la be la, dɛ name te kwaraa a ɡɛ bambiteŋa la ɡwaa Filisti tena la nɛ bela baa soɡa la. Anomanta, Kooro Sɔɔl ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Gel wobɛlbwa ɛɛ.”

english_verse: There were also some hired soldiers in the Philistine camp, who now switched to Israel's side and fought for Saul and Jonathan.
translation_verse: Hibru tena bane ba fa aa la Filisti tena be ba ne ba kaa ba soŋnibɔr la, berɔ kaa Israel tena baa ja Kooro Sɔɔl ne Jonatan nɛɛ la be.

english_verse: Many Israelites had been hiding in the hill country of Ephraim. And when they heard that the Philistines were running away, they came out of hiding and joined in chasing the Philistines.
translation_verse: Israel tena baa sɔh Efrem deŋɡarere ta aa noa kɛŋɔ Filisti tena la dɛ chwa la, ba kaa ja ba bala Israel tena la nɛɛ laa la ta, dɛ chwa ti ba dɛɛ yoo ba.

english_verse: So the Lord helped Israel win the battle that day. Saul's Curse on Anyone Who Eats Saul had earlier told his soldiers, “I want to get even with those Philistines by sunset. If any of you eat before then, you will be under a curse!” So he made them swear not to eat. By the time the fighting moved past Beth-Aven, the Israelite troops were weak from hunger.
translation_verse: Lɔr kpo Israel tena ba ɡwɛɡre awola, dɛkalkɛ dɛ Kooro Sɔɔl ŋwɛɛrɔ kɛŋɔ ba bini bɛlbwa waa di kondikwaa mɔɔ wee le la, nyotaahna lawɛ naate mɔɔ ó tɔ o dɔma wel. Anomanta, o laa tena la bɛlbwa ta kondikwaa dii.

english_verse: The army and the people who lived nearby had gone into a forest, and they came to a place where honey was dripping on the ground. But no one ate any of it, because they were afraid of being put under the curse.
translation_verse: Baa tel bela tohnoo la aa kora dɛɛ lee la, bɛlbwa ta ane kpɔe do nyoa, dɛkalkɛ ba ɔmɛ Kooro Sɔɔl nyotaahna la.

english_verse: Jonathan did not know about Saul's warning to the soldiers. So he dipped the end of his walking stick in the honey and ate some with his fingers. He felt stronger and more alert.
translation_verse: Kɛ dɛ Jonatan te ta noɛ kɛ o mɛɛ ŋwɛɛrɔ ŋɔ bɛlbwa bɛ ɡel kondikwaa leɡe o nyoa. O tɛr daŋɡbala do tohvaahna la ta dɛ di ane, buɡ la ta, o sie deŋu o dɔ bokpeɡa.

english_verse: Then a soldier told him, “Your father swore that anyone who ate food today would be put under a curse, and we agreed not to eat. That's why we're so weak.”
translation_verse: Belaa laa tena la bɛl ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “He mɛɛ ŋwɛɛrɔ dawɛ ya nɛɛ kɛŋɔ bɛlbwa di kwaa fini naa, nyotaahna lawɔ. A waa lɔr ɛɛ kpo yaa ya bwa ɡwɛɡre la.”

english_verse: Jonathan said, “My father has caused you a lot of trouble. Look at me! I ate only a little of this honey, but already I feel strong and alert.
translation_verse: Anee Jonatan ŋɔ, “N mɛɛ kpɔ waa aa wola were ba ta ya harɛ nɔ nɛra nɛ. Na ɡɛ n bwara bini aa chaah mɛ, tooh tama maa dia nɔ nomanta.

english_verse: By evening the Israelite army was exhausted from killing Philistines all the way from Michmash to Aijalon.
translation_verse: Awola tɔpere la, Israel tena kpoo Filisti tena le Mikmas ka tel bwɛjen Aejalɔn, dɛ ba bwa koɔh, lɔr ɡe kpo ba ba ɡwɛɡre.

english_verse: They grabbed the food they had captured from the Philistines and started eating. They even killed sheep and cows and calves right on the spot and ate the meat without draining the blood.
translation_verse: Buɡ la ta, ba den ka su kwaa baa paa laa ta le ba dɔma be la ta dɛɛ kama, peera ne nae ne a bii, ba kpoora dɛ chɛwa buɡ la ta bela, dɛ chwea ane chal ɡɛ.

english_verse: Someone told Saul, “Look! The army is disobeying the Lord by eating meat before the blood drains out.” “You're right,” Saul answered. “They are being unfaithful to the Lord! Hurry! Roll a big rock over here.
translation_verse: Anee nomɛl ka ŋɔ Kooro Sɔɔl be ŋɔ, “Na, laa tena la dɛ chwe ol lwɛɛ ne chal, dɛ jo Korowii nɛ.” Ate, Kooro Sɔɔl ŋɔ, “Hé ɛ nɛnchɔɡa kohona. Hé ɡbili bwejen ba tɛ mɛ bonɔ warane.”

english_verse: Then tell everyone in camp to bring their cattle and lambs to me. They can kill the animals on this rock, then eat the meat. That way no one will disobey the Lord by eating meat with blood still in it.” That night the soldiers brought their cattle over to the big rock and killed them there.
translation_verse: Asɛ o ŋɔ, “Hé jo ba bini dɛ́ ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, ‘Bɛlbwa lawɛ o nao ne pee dɛ́ ba kpoa bwe nɔ ta. He bɛ ol ne o chal di dɛ́ ba ɛ wechɔɡa jo Korowii nɛ.’ ” Anomanta, jwaana la ne, bɛlbwa ba o kon ne dɛ ba kpo bela.

english_verse: It was the first altar Saul had built for offering sacrifices to the Lord. The Army Rescues Jonathan
translation_verse: Kooro Sɔɔl ma kon baa ɛ saraha o ta tɛ Korowii bela. Onee ɛ saraha kon waa tɔ sie ma tɛ Korowii.

english_verse: Saul said, “Let's attack the Philistines again while it's still dark. We can fight them all night. Let's kill them and take everything they own!” The people answered, “We will do whatever you want.” “Wait!” Ahijah the priest said. “Let's ask God what we should do.”
translation_verse: Anee Kooro Sɔɔl ŋɔ, “Hé ɡel ya ti Filisti tena la jwaana nɔ ne, dɛ́ ka tel bɔr chaahna saŋ, dɛ́ ka yoo ba dɛ́ pa ba laala. Ya kpoo ba bwa, dɛ bɛ ba bini beŋkpoŋ kwaraa ɡel.” Anee ba chaŋo ŋɔ, “Ɛ ɡɛ bɛlbwa aa too he tea.” Kɛ sɔfo Ahija ɡe ŋɔ, “Hé ɡel ya bɔɔ le Korowii be ó baɡle ɡɛ yaa ɛ mɔɔ.”

english_verse: Saul asked God, “Should I attack the Philistines? Will you help us win?” This time God did not answer.
translation_verse: Anomanta, Kooro Sɔɔl bɔɔ Korowii ŋɔ, “Mɛɛ won la ka yo Filisti tena la kɛɛ? Yaa won pɔ ba nɛ aa?” Kɛ Korowii ta on chaŋɛ awola tɔpere.

english_verse: Saul called his army officers together and said, “We have to find out what sin has kept God from answering.
translation_verse: Kooro Sɔɔl yerɛ nomonome baa chɔ laa tena nyoa la bwa dɛ ŋɔ, “Hé ba ya cheme dɛ́ na wechɔɡa yaa ɛa fini.

english_verse: I swear by the living Lord that whoever sinned must die, even if it turns out to be my own son Jonathan.” No one said a word.
translation_verse: N ŋwɛɛ Korowii waa ɛ Israel tena Lɛɛ la kɛŋɔ, hale dɛ n bibaa Jonatan ɛ wechɔɡa ane kwaraa naa, a chɛ kɛ ó sewɛ.” Kɛ ba bini bɛlbwa ta waane bolɛ.

english_verse: Saul told his army, “You stand on that side of the priest, and Jonathan and I will stand on the other side.” Everyone agreed.
translation_verse: Anee Kooro Sɔɔl ŋɔ Israel tena la bwa be ŋɔ, “He bwa ka che le, ásɛ n ne n bibaa Jonatan ɡe che bonɔ.” Asɛ ba bwa ŋɔ, “Ɛ ɡɛ bwa aa too he tea.”

english_verse: Then Saul prayed, “Our Lord, God of Israel, why haven't you answered me today? Please show us who sinned. Was it my son Jonathan and I, or was it your people Israel?” The answer came back that Jonathan or Saul had sinned, not the army.
translation_verse: Kooro Sɔɔl soŋe Korowii Israel tena aa dɛ tomɔ la ŋɔ, “N Naa Korowii, ɡel n jemɛ waa nɔ kasinteŋ.” Asɛ ba bil daa a lawɛ o ne o bibaa Jonatan, asɛ nɛra la kar te, bie la ta ba tɔɔ.

english_verse: Saul told Ahijah, “Now ask the Lord to decide between Jonathan and me.” The answer came back that Jonathan had sinned.
translation_verse: Anee Kooro Sɔɔl ŋɔ sɔfo Ahija be ŋɔ, “Berɛ bil daa n ne n bibaa Jonatan nyu ta ja, dɛ́ na naate waa ɛ wechɔɡa la.” Asɛ a lawɛ Jonatan.

english_verse: “Jonathan,” Saul exclaimed, “tell me what you did!” “I dipped the end of my walking stick in some honey and ate a little. Now you say I have to die!”
translation_verse: Ate, Kooro Sɔɔl bɔɔ Jonatan ŋɔ, “Baɡ mɛ waa haa ɛa.” Asɛ o ŋɔ, “N daŋɡbala nyoa n kpɔ li tooh tama di, dɛɛ ba sewa taraken la.”

english_verse: “Yes, Jonathan. I swear to God that you must die.”
translation_verse: Anee Kooro Sɔɔl ŋɔ, “Dɛ hen Jonatan ta sewaa, Korowii bɛ men ɡel.”

english_verse: “No!” the soldiers shouted. “God helped Jonathan win the battle for us. We won't let you kill him. We swear to the Lord that we won't let you kill him or even lay a hand on him!” So the army kept Saul from killing Jonathan.
translation_verse: Kɛ nɛra la ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Jonatan aa cheɡɛ o nɛɛ Israel tena bwa dɔ lɛɛ nɔ chɛ kɛŋɔ ó sewaa? Akai, ya ŋwɛɛ Korowii waa lole saŋ bɛlbwa kɛŋɔ, nomɛlbwa aa won ɛo wobɛlbwa, dɛkalkɛ Korowiirii chao o won ɛ waa waa ɛa fini nɔ.” Gɛɛ a do nɛra la lɛ Jonatan ba ta on kpoe.

english_verse: Saul stopped hunting down the Philistines, and they went home. Saul Fights His Enemies
translation_verse: Belaa Kooro Sɔɔl ɡel Filisti tena la tii, ba bwa berɛ kaa ba harɛ ta.

english_verse: When Saul became king, the Moabites, the Ammonites, the Edomites, the kings of Zobah, the Philistines, and the Amalekites had all been robbing the Israelites. Saul fought back against these enemies and stopped them from robbing Israel. He was a brave commander and always won his battles. Saul's Family
translation_verse: O yoo bambile bwa ne, dɛ pɔ Amalɛk tena nɛ, dɛ lɛ Israel tena, nomɛlbwa ta wone ba yoo ba kpa. Kooro Sɔɔl haah ne o bii

english_verse: Saul was at war with the Philistines for as long as he lived. Whenever he found a good warrior or a brave man, Saul made him join his army.
translation_verse: Kooro Sɔɔl soɡa bini bwa, o ne Filisti tena yo laa taeh. Anomanta, o na banyoo bɛlbwa naa, ɡɛɛ o lawɔ ba ja o laa tena nɛ.

english_verse: One day, Samuel told Saul: The Lord told me to choose you to be king of his people, Israel. Now listen to this message from the Lord:
translation_verse: Samoɛl ŋɔ Kooro Sɔɔl be ŋɔ, “Menee Korowii tomɛ n fuɡe noo do he nyu ta, dɛ cheɡe kooro tɛ o nɛra Israel tena. Berɛ no waa aa le Korowii be taraken.

english_verse: “When the Israelites were on their way out of Egypt, the nation of Amalek attacked them. I am the Lord All-Powerful, and now I am going to make Amalek pay!
translation_verse: Nemenɛ Korowii ŋɔ, ‘Mɛɛ tɛr Amalɛk tena deŋnee, dɛkalkɛŋɔ ba naawa teŋe Israel tena ŋwɛnɛ, ɡɛ saŋ baa le Ijipt dɛɛ ba la.

english_verse: “Go and attack the Amalekites! Destroy them and all their possessions. Don't have any pity. Kill their men, women, children, and even their babies. Slaughter their cattle, sheep, camels, and donkeys.”
translation_verse: Hé kaa taraken dɛ́ ka yo Amalɛk tena la, dɛ́ chɔɡ kwaa baa dɔa bwa kwaraa. He bɛ ba sum na, hé kpoo baala ne haahna, ne bechale ne bechasɔɔhne, ne nae ne peera dɛ ba nyoɡmare ne keeɡore bwa.’ ”

english_verse: Saul sent messengers who told every town and village to send men to join the army at Telaim. There were
translation_verse: Anomanta, Kooro Sɔɔl yerɛ o laa tena la cheme Telaim dɛ kur ba. Ba lɔ nɛra kaɡboŋa lafraanɛ dɛ le Israel harɛ, asɛ kaɡboŋa fi ɡe le Juda harɛ ta.

english_verse: The Lord told Samuel,
translation_verse: Anee Korowii ŋɔ Samoɛl be ŋɔ,

english_verse: then led them to a valley near one of the towns in Amalek, where they got ready to make a surprise attack.
translation_verse: Kooro Sɔɔl ne o laa tena la Amalɛk tena bwɛjen bɛl ta, dɛ ka sɔh chɔ fɛlembɔjen bɛl bini bar bwɛɛ la.

english_verse: Some Kenites lived nearby, and Saul told them, “Your people were kind to our nation when we left Egypt, and I don't want you to get killed when I wipe out the Amalekites. So stay away from them.” The Kenites left,
translation_verse: O kah Ken tena ba ne baa soɡa la ŋɔ, “Hé le Amalɛk tena la bini kaa, ásɛ n bɛ pɛ kpo he ne ban. Israel tena aa le Ijipt harɛ ta dɛɛ ba la, hé nyin ba wa.” Asɛ Ken tena la le ba bini kaa.

english_verse: and Saul attacked the Amalekites from Havilah to Shur, which is just east of Egypt.
translation_verse: Asɛ Kooro Sɔɔl yo Amalɛk tena la le Havila harɛ ta ka tel Suur, o lɔ Ijipt wee leebɔr.

english_verse: Saul and his army let Agag live, and they also spared the best sheep and cattle. They didn't want to destroy anything of value, so they only killed the animals that were worthless or weak. The Lord Rejects Saul
translation_verse: Kooro Sɔɔl ne o laa tena la ɡel Kooro Aɡaɡ ne o peera ne nae ne nabali aa wera kohona, ne pebali ne nae bii dɛ koŋkwaa aa wera la te bwa. Kwaa aa wera dɛ dɔ tɔnɔ la te, ba ɡela, kɛ anɔ la aa wola were la, ba chɔɡa.

english_verse: “Saul has stopped obeying me, and I'm sorry that I made him king.” Samuel was angry, and he cried out in prayer to the Lord all night.
translation_verse: “A dɛ we n nɛɛ kɛ maa cheɡ Sɔɔl kooro, dɛkalkɛŋɔ o ta n waa ta teŋɛ dɛ vɛɛh mɛ.” Samoɛl liire chɔɡ ɡɛ waa nɔ waa kɛrɛdɛ, asɛ o wi no Korowii awola jwaana la bwa.

english_verse: Early the next morning he went to talk with Saul. Someone told him, “Saul went to Carmel, where he had a monument built so everyone would remember his victory. Then he left for Gilgal.”
translation_verse: Tɔ aa pera chɔmbibi la, Samoɛl iro la ka ɡaaɡe Kooro Sɔɔl bɔr, asɛ ba ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Ó kaa Kaamɛl. Asɛ o ma kon cheɡ bela o sɔn ta, dɛ kpɔ dɛɛ lii laa waa yoa dɛ pɔ nɛra nɛɛ la wa, dɛ berɛ kaa Gelɡal.”

english_verse: Samuel finally caught up with Saul, and Saul told him, “I hope the Lord will bless you! I have done what the Lord told me.”
translation_verse: Samoɛl aa tel o be la, Kooro Sɔɔl ŋɔ, “Korowii swee andɛɛɡa tɛɛ! N ɛ waa Korowii aa do mɛ ŋɔ ń ɛ la.”

english_verse: “Then why,” Samuel asked, “do I hear sheep and cattle?”
translation_verse: Anee Samoɛl ŋɔ, “Bɔkwa ɡe peera ne nae sii mɛɛ no ken?”

english_verse: “The army took them from the Amalekites,” Saul explained. “They kept the best sheep and cattle, so they could sacrifice them to the Lord your God. But we destroyed everything else.”
translation_verse: Anee Kooro Sɔɔl chaŋe ŋɔ, “Laa tena laanee le ane Amalɛk tena be ba. Ba ɡel peera aa wera kohona ne nae, dɛ́ ba kpoora ɛ saraha tɛ Korowii haa dɛ tomɔ la. Kɛ kwaa aa wola were la te, ba kpoo a bwa sekwaraa.”

english_verse: “Stop!” Samuel said. “Let me tell you what the Lord told me last night.” “All right,” Saul answered.
translation_verse: Ate, Samoɛl ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Gel, ásɛ n baɡle waa Korowii aa bol n be dɛ jwaana ne.” Anee Kooro Sɔɔl ŋɔ, “Bol ń no.”

english_verse: Samuel continued, “You may not think you're very important, but the Lord chose you to be king, and you are in charge of the tribes of Israel.
translation_verse: Samoɛl ŋɔ, “A lole kɛ he dɛ lii he te nɛnjeɡa, he laa bera ba ɛ Israel deene bwa nyu te nɔ naa? Korowii fuɡe noo do he nyu ta, dɛ cheɡe kora ta Israel.

english_verse: When the Lord sent you on this mission, he told you to wipe out those worthless Amalekites.
translation_verse: Waane le Korowii be ba he be kɛŋɔ, ‘Kaa dɛ́ ka chɔɡ Amalɛk nyubinikpeɡ tena la bwa sekwaraa. Yoo ba ka tel kɛŋɔ haa he ba bwa.’

english_verse: Why didn't you listen to the Lord? Why did you keep the animals and make him angry?”
translation_verse: Ɛrɛɛ haa wola Korowii waa noɔ? Ɛrɛɛ he la ka kam kwaa baa paa laa ta dɛ ɛ wechɔɡa Korowii sie ken?”

english_verse: “But I did listen to the Lord!” Saul answered. “He sent me on a mission, and I went. I captured King Agag and destroyed his nation.
translation_verse: Kooro Sɔɔl ŋɔ, “N teŋɛ Korowii waa la ta. Waa waa do mɛ a ta la, n ɛa. N chɔɡ Amalɛk tena la bwa kwaraa. Hale dɛ lawɛ ba Kooro Aɡaɡ nɔn ne, dɛ ba o ne.

english_verse: All the animals were going to be destroyed anyway. That's why the army brought the best sheep and cattle to Gilgal as sacrifices to the Lord your God.”
translation_verse: Laa tena la larawe ba peera ne nae aa wera kohona, dɛ lea cheɡ tɛ Korowii laa la ta, dɛ́ ba a ne Gelɡal, dɛ́ kpoora ɛ saraha tɛ Korowii haa dɛ tomɔ la.”

english_verse: “Tell me,” Samuel said. “Does the Lord really want sacrifices and offerings? No! He doesn't want your sacrifices. He wants you to obey him.
translation_verse: Kɛ Samoɛl chaŋo ŋɔ, “Korowii sie dɛ lɛ saraha baa fuah ne kwaa baa kpoora, ɡwaa kɛ haa no o deŋna wa aa? Korowii deŋna waa noe wer ɡwaa kɛ haa kpo pedɛɛɡe ɛ saraha tɛo.

english_verse: Rebelling against God or disobeying him because you are proud is just as bad as worshiping idols or asking them for advice. You refused to do what God told you, so God has decided that you can no longer be king.”
translation_verse: Dɛ he ɛ Korowii deŋnekpeɡ aa, a do kɛŋɔ haa dɛ tomɛ voɡa ken, bambikpeɡ ɡe do kɛŋɔ voɡa toma. Haa vɛh Korowii waa la nomanta, o ɡe vɛɛh kooro.”

english_verse: “I have sinned,” Saul admitted. “I disobeyed both you and the Lord. I was afraid of the army, and I listened to them instead.
translation_verse: Anee Kooro Sɔɔl ŋɔ Samoɛl be ŋɔ, “N ɛ wechɔɡa, n vɛh Korowii waa waa do mɛ a ta, ne waa haa ŋɔa n ɛ la. Ɔmaa n ɔmɛ nɛra la waa n teŋɛ waa baa dɛ nyin ta.

english_verse: Please forgive me and come back with me so I can worship the Lord.”
translation_verse: Taraken n dɛ soŋe kɛ he kpɔ n wechɔɡa kɛ mɛ, ásɛ n ne he berɛ kaa, ń kaa tomɛ Korowii.”

english_verse: “No!” Samuel replied, “You disobeyed the Lord, and I won't go back with you. Now the Lord has said that you can't be king of Israel any longer.”
translation_verse: Asɛ Samoɛl ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “N ne haa berɛ kaa. He vɛh waa Korowii aa bola he be, asɛ o vɛɛh kɛŋɔ he ɛ kooro Israel tena nɛ.”

english_verse: As Samuel turned to go, Saul grabbed the edge of Samuel's robe. It tore!
translation_verse: Samoɛl aa bera dɛɛ ba kaala la, Kooro Sɔɔl tao lawɛ o batakaare nyoa asɛ o kɛɛ.

english_verse: Samuel said, “The Lord has torn the kingdom of Israel away from you today, and he will give it to someone who is better than you.
translation_verse: Anee Samoɛl ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Korowii chɔɡ Israel kora la kɛŋɔ batakaare nɔ dɛ le he nɔn ta fini, dɛ kpɔ tɛ he dɔŋ o wa aa wera ɡwaale.

english_verse: Besides, the eternal God of Israel isn't a human being. He doesn't tell lies or change his mind.”
translation_verse: Korowii Israel tena aa dɛ tomɔ la dɔ jirima, waa nyosone teŋe, waa o liire ɡe charɛ. Nɛwɛnyini laa on ó charɛ o liire.”

english_verse: Saul said, “I did sin, but please honor me in front of the leaders of the army and the people of Israel. Come back with me, so I can worship the Lord your God.”
translation_verse: Ate, Kooro Sɔɔl chaŋe ŋɔ, “N ɛ wechɔɡa te, kɛ ɡel ń dɔ duure Israel tena bwa ne ba nomonome sie. Gel n ne he kaa, ásɛ n kaa tomɛ Korowii haa dɛ tomɔ la.”

english_verse: Samuel followed Saul back, and Saul worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: Gɛɛ a do Samoɛl ne Kooro Sɔɔl berɛ kaa o kaa tomɛ Korowii.

english_verse: Then Samuel shouted, “Bring me King Agag of Amalek!” Agag came in chains, and he was saying to himself, “Surely they won't kill me now.”
translation_verse: Samoɛl ŋɔ, “Hé ka kpɔ Amalɛk tena Kooro Aɡaɡ ba tɛ mɛ.” Anee Aɡaɡ lɔ bambile dɛ ba o be, dɛɛ lii ŋɔ, “N jemɔ taraken kɛ baa men kpo kpa.”

english_verse: But Samuel said, “Agag, you have snatched children from their mothers' arms and killed them. Now your mother will be without children.” Then Samuel chopped Agag to pieces at the place of worship in Gilgal.
translation_verse: Ate, Samoɛl berɛ ŋɔ, “Gɛ haa kpoo bechale ba nyare paŋɛ bii la, ɡɛɛ he nya ɡe ɛɛ ba bie paŋa.” Asɛ Samoɛl kpo Kooro Aɡaɡ Korowii sie Gelɡal bela.

english_verse: Samuel went home to Ramah, and Saul returned to his home in Gibeah.
translation_verse: Ate, Samoɛl le bela dɛ kaa Rama, kɛ Kooro Sɔɔl te berɔ kaa o bwɛ Gebea.

english_verse: Even though Samuel felt sad about Saul, Samuel never saw him again. The Lord Chooses David To Be King The Lord was sorry he had made Saul the king of Israel.
translation_verse: Samoɛl ta Kooro Sɔɔl nae kpa, dɛ ka tel o serewe wee. Dɛ o wio dɛɛ tɛo te. A we Korowii nɛɛ kɛ waa cheɡo kora Israel.

english_verse: One day he said, “Samuel, I've rejected Saul, and I refuse to let him be king any longer. Stop feeling sad about him. Put some olive oil in a small container and go visit a man named Jesse, who lives in Bethlehem. I've chosen one of his sons to be my king.”
translation_verse: Awola bɛl, Korowii ŋɔ Samoɛl be ŋɔ, “Saŋ besoo hɛɛ nyin he wi Sɔɔl ka tel, dɛ́ le vɛɛh maa vɛoh kɛ Israel kooro nɔɔ? Do noo pebal nyeɡle ta, ásɛ dɛ chiɡ ŋwɛnɛ ta ń tomɛ Jese be Bɛtlɛham. N le o bibaala la bini bɛl dɛ cheɡo kooro tɛ Israel tena.”

english_verse: Samuel answered, “If I do that, Saul will find out and have me killed.” “Take a calf with you,” the Lord replied. “Tell everyone that you've come to offer it as a sacrifice to me,
translation_verse: Anee Samoɛl ŋɔ, “Dɛ n laŋɔ Kooro Sɔɔl noɔ kɛ n ba bela aa, wɛɛ kpo mɛɛ.” Anee Korowii ŋɔ, “Lawɛ nalor ásɛ he laŋaa, he ŋɔ he dɛ ba ba kpo ɛ saraha tɛ men Korowii.”

english_verse: then invite Jesse to the sacrifice. When I show you which one of his sons I have chosen, pour the olive oil on his head.”
translation_verse: Yerɛ Jese ó ba saraha la bɔr. Mɛɛ baɡle ɡɛ haa ɛ. Bɛl la háa fuɡe noo do o nyu ta la, dɛ onee n le kooro.

english_verse: Samuel did what the Lord told him and went to Bethlehem. The town leaders went to meet him, but they were terribly afraid and asked, “Is this a friendly visit?”
translation_verse: Samoɛl ɛ ɡɛ Korowii aa baɡlo la bwa. Waa tel bwɛjen Bɛtlɛham la, bwɛɛ la nomonome ɔmɔ, dɛ kpɔ bochechela ka chemo dɛɛ bɔɔro ŋɔ, “Deŋnesɔɔhna nee he ba tenaa?”

english_verse: “Yes, it is!” Samuel answered. “I've come to offer a sacrifice to the Lord. Get yourselves ready to take part in the sacrifice and come with me.” Samuel also invited Jesse and his sons to come to the sacrifice, and he got them ready to take part.
translation_verse: Anee Samoɛl chaŋe ŋɔ, “Ɔɔh, deŋnesɔɔhna taa. N balɔ dɛ́ ba kpo kon ɛ saraha tɛ Korowii. Hé sɔ he doŋa bwa ta Korowii be pera, dɛ́ ba ja n nɛɛ saraha la mun.” Ate, o sɔ Jese ne o bibaala doŋa bwa ta dɛ ta nɔn yer ba saraha la mun.

english_verse: When Jesse and his sons arrived, Samuel noticed Jesse's oldest son, Eliab. “He has to be the one the Lord has chosen,” Samuel said to himself.
translation_verse: Baa tel bela la, Samoɛl na Eliab dɛ lii ŋɔ, “N jemɔ kɛrɛdɛ kɛŋɔ nɛn Korowii aa fuɡe noo do o nyu ta laanee cheɡɛ o sie bela nɔ.”

english_verse: But the Lord told him, “Samuel, don't think Eliab is the one just because he's tall and handsome. He isn't the one I've chosen. People judge others by what they look like, but I judge people by what is in their hearts.”
translation_verse: Kɛ Korowii ŋɔ Samoɛl be ŋɔ, “Bɛ o jaŋne ne o wer nyiŋi, o laa mɛɛ nyin, n vɛoh. Kwaa nɛwɛnyini aa dɛ nyiŋi la korɛ anɔ la Korowii aa dɛ nyiŋi ta. Nɛwɛnyini dɛ nyiŋi siebɔr, kɛ Korowii te, nɛn bambile binii wɛɛ nyiŋi.”

english_verse: Jesse told his son Abinadab to go over to Samuel, but Samuel said, “No, the Lord hasn't chosen him.”
translation_verse: Ate, Jese yerɛ Abinadab dɛ ɡel o valɛ kpɔ Samoɛl sie ba kaa. Asɛ Samoɛl ŋɔ, “Korowii ta onɔ ɡe leɛ.”

english_verse: Next, Jesse sent his son Shammah to him, and Samuel said, “The Lord hasn't chosen him either.”
translation_verse: Jese berɔ ɡel Samaa ɡe valɛ Samoɛl sie ba kaa. Anee Samoɛl ŋɔ, “Korowii ta onɔ ɡe leɛ.”

english_verse: One by one, Jesse told all seven of his sons to go over to Samuel. Finally, Samuel said, “Jesse, the Lord hasn't chosen any of these young men.
translation_verse: Jese ɡelɔ o bibaala banuanɛ bwa kpɔ Samoɛl sie ba kaa. Anee Samoɛl ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Korowii ta ba bini bɛlbwa leɛ.”

english_verse: Do you have any other sons?” “Yes,” Jesse answered. “My youngest son David is out taking care of the sheep.” “Send for him!” Samuel said. “We won't start the ceremony until he gets here.”
translation_verse: Samoɛl bɔɔ Jese ŋɔ, “He bibaala haa dɔa bwaa nɔ naa?” Anee o chaŋo ŋɔ, “Ba bini bechala ta lole, kɛ o dɛ teɡɛ peera.” Anee Samoɛl ŋɔ, “Tomɛ bá ka yerɔ ba. O ta balaa, ya ta saraha la ɛɛ.”

english_verse: Jesse sent for David. He was a healthy, good-looking boy with a sparkle in his eyes. As soon as David came, the Lord told Samuel, “He's the one! Get up and pour the olive oil on his head.”
translation_verse: Anomanta, o ɡelɔ ba ka yerɔ ba. O mao dɛ do wer bonɔɔ, o siwinyiŋi ɡe do wer kɛrɛdɛ. Anee Korowii ŋɔ, “Ir dɛ́ fuɡe noo do o nyu ta, onee ɛ nɛn maa leo.”

english_verse: Samuel poured the oil on David's head while his brothers watched. At that moment, the Spirit of the Lord took control of David and stayed with him from then on. Samuel returned home to Ramah. David Plays the Harp for Saul
translation_verse: Samoɛl kpɔ pebal nyeɡle noo aa lɔ o bini la fuɡe do Devid nyu ta ba siwi ta. Dɛ onee Korowii le. Le awola dɛɛ kaa la, Korowii Doma baa so o nɛɛ kpeɡri nɛ, asɛ Samoɛl berɛ kaa Rama. Devid lɔ Kooro Sɔɔl dem dɛɛ tomɔ

english_verse: The Spirit of the Lord had left Saul, and an evil spirit from the Lord was terrifying him.
translation_verse: Dɛ Korowii Doma la le Kooro Sɔɔl nɛ, asɛ o ɡel kwaa ir o nɛɛ dɛ ɡel o bwara ɛɛ nyɛɡ.

english_verse: “It's an evil spirit from God that's frightening you,” Saul's officials told him.
translation_verse: Kooro Sɔɔl bonɔɔna la ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Na ɡɛ kwaa aa ir he nɛɛ dɛɛ doe bonyɛɡa ta ɡɛ.

english_verse: “Your Majesty, let us go and look for someone who is good at playing the harp. He can play for you whenever the evil spirit from God bothers you, and you'll feel better.”
translation_verse: Ya naa kooro, tomɛ bonɔɔna bá ka nyin nɛn waa jemɛ janjela lɔe. O baa lɔ, ásɛ dɛ kwaa ir he nɛɛ aa, he bwara ɛɛ sɔɔhnee.”

english_verse: “All right,” Saul answered. “Find me someone who is good at playing the harp and bring him here.”
translation_verse: Anomanta, Kooro Sɔɔl tomɛ o bonɔɔna la ŋɔ, “Hé la ka nyin nɛn waa jemɛ janjela lɔe kɛrɛdɛ ba tɛ mɛ.”

english_verse: “A man named Jesse who lives in Bethlehem has a son who can play the harp,” one official said. “He's a brave warrior, he's good-looking, he can speak well, and the Lord is with him.”
translation_verse: Belaa bonɔɔna la bɛl chaŋe ŋɔ, “N na Jese bibaa bɛl, o lɔ Bɛtlɛham dɛ jemɛ janjela lɔe. O ɛ banyoo, o bambile ɡe do kpeɡri, o jemɛ wobol dɛ do wer bonɔɔ ɡe. Asɛ Korowii ja o nɛ.”

english_verse: Saul sent a message to Jesse: “Tell your son David to leave your sheep and come here to me.”
translation_verse: Kooro Sɔɔl tomɛ nɛra Jese be ŋɔ, “N dɛ soŋe, ɡel he bibaa Devid waa dɛ teɡɛ peera la ba n be.”

english_verse: Jesse loaded a donkey with bread and a goatskin full of wine, then he told David to take the donkey and a young goat to Saul.
translation_verse: Anomanta, Jese kpɔ keeɡo, dɛ kpɔ paanoo ne oltɔn pur sen aa suu, ne bombie ja ŋɔ Devid kpɔ ka tɛ Kooro Sɔɔl.

english_verse: David went to Saul and started working for him. Saul liked him so much that he put David in charge of carrying his weapons.
translation_verse: Devid la Kooro Sɔɔl be dɛ kaa tomɔ. Dɛ Kooro Sɔɔl sie dɛ lɛ o nɛɛ kɛrɛdɛ, dɛ ɡel wɛɛ che o dɔmkwa.

english_verse: Not long after this, Saul sent another message to Jesse: “I really like David. Please let him stay with me.”
translation_verse: Ate, Kooro Sɔɔl ɡel ba ka ŋɔ Jese be ŋɔ, “Gel Devid so n be dɛɛ tom mɛ, n sie dɛ lɛ o nɛ.”

english_verse: Whenever the evil spirit from God bothered Saul, David would play his harp. Saul would relax and feel better, and the evil spirit would go away.
translation_verse: Le bela dɛɛ kaa la, saŋ bɛlbwa kwa aa ba ir Sɔɔl nɛɛ la, ɡɛɛ Devid yon kpɔ o janjela lɔ, asɛ a le o nɛɛ o bwara sɔɔhno.

english_verse: The Philistines got ready for war and brought their troops together to attack the town of Socoh in Judah. They set up camp at Ephes-Dammim, between Socoh and Azekah.
translation_verse: A balɔ kɛŋɔ Filisti tena lawɛ ba laa tena cheme Soko waa lɔ Juda harɛ ta. Ba kaa baŋre ba tɛnte deene bobɛl baa dɛ yerɔ Efes Damim, o lɔ Soko ne Aseka baah ta.

english_verse: King Saul and the Israelite army set up camp on a hill overlooking Elah Valley, and they got ready to fight the Philistine army that was on a hill on the other side of the valley.
translation_verse: Filisti tena la cheɡɛ deŋɡare bɛl ta baŋ bɛl, asɛ Israel tena ɡe che bɛl ta, fɛlembɔjen la chɔ ba baah ta.

english_verse: The Philistine army had a hero named Goliath who was from the town of Gath and was about three meters tall.
translation_verse: Dɛ Filisti tena banyoo bɛl sɔne Goliat, o le Gat. O jaŋne ɡwaa naɡale anuanaarɛ, o le bela Filisti tena aa baŋre ba tɛnte deene la bini ba che.

english_verse: He wore a bronze helmet and had bronze armor to protect his chest and legs. The chest armor alone weighed about
translation_verse: Ayaawaa ba kpɔ ɛ kwaa bɔle o nakpale, asɛ ayaawa lampea saɡɛ o vam ta.

english_verse: When David came back from fighting Goliath, he was still carrying Goliath's head. Abner took David to Saul,
translation_verse: Devid aa kpo Goliat dɛ den baa jo la, Abna lawɔ dɛ ba o ne Kooro Sɔɔl sie dɛ o ta kpoŋe o nyu la.

english_verse: and his spear was so big that the iron spearhead alone weighed about seven kilograms. A soldier always walked in front of Goliath to carry his shield.
translation_verse: O lampea daa bare do kɛŋɔ yasɔɔh kokorowa ken, o nyoa buni tɔɡre ɡe lɔ suuɡapoŋa lafraanumɛl. Nɛn waa kpoŋe kon waa kpɔa dɛɛ tɔ o te ɡbemɡbe tɔ o sie.

english_verse: Goliath went out and shouted to the army of Israel: Why are you lining up for battle? I'm the best soldier in our army, and all of you are in Saul's army. Choose your best soldier to come out and fight me!
translation_verse: Goliat iro che, dɛ nyɛɡ Israel laa tena nɛɛ ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ hé ba che bonɔ dɛɛ nyin kɛ hé ba yo yaa nɔɔ? Filisti te laa men asɛ he ɡe ɛ Kooro Sɔɔl bonɔɔna aa? Hé le nɛmbeŋkpoŋ, ásɛ o ba puu mɛ yo.

english_verse: If he can kill me, our people will be your slaves. But if I kill him, your people will be our slaves.
translation_verse: Dɛ o wono yoo mɛ dɛ kpo mɛ naa, yaa ba do he lɔɡaa dɛɛ tomɛ heya. Kɛ dɛ menee pɔ o nɛɛ dɛ kpoo ɡe aa, hɛɛ ba do ya lɔɡaa dɛɛ tomɛ yaa.

english_verse: Saul and his men heard what Goliath said, but they were so frightened of Goliath that they couldn't do a thing. David Decides To Challenge Goliath
translation_verse: Baa no waa Filisti te la aa bola la, Kooro Sɔɔl ne Israel tena la bambile teŋo kɛrɛdɛ.

english_verse: David's father Jesse was an old man, who belonged to the Ephrath clan and lived in Bethlehem in Judah. Jesse had eight sons:
translation_verse: Devid mɛɛ sɔne Jese. O le Efrat waa lɔ Bɛtlɛham, Juda harɛ ta. Jese bibaala lɔ banuatoro. Gɛ saŋ Kooro Sɔɔl aa di kora Israel la, dɛ o hwɛɛhrɔ kɛrɛdɛ.

english_verse: He took care of his father's sheep, and he went back and forth between Bethlehem and Saul's camp.
translation_verse: kɛ Devid yon le Kooro Sɔɔl be kaa Bɛtlɛham dɛ́ ka teɡɛ o mɛɛ peera tama, dɛ́ yon berɛ ba.

english_verse: Goliath came out and gave his challenge every morning and every evening for
translation_verse: Tɔpera fifraanaarɛ, chɔɔ ne jɔmɔra bwaa Goliat waa ɛ Filisti te la yon le ba che, dɛɛ muɡli Israel tena la baah.

english_verse: and picked up his shepherd's stick. He went out to a stream and picked up five smooth rocks and put them in his leather bag. Then with his sling in his hand, he went straight toward Goliath. David Kills Goliath
translation_verse: O kpɔ o daŋɡbala kpoŋe, dɛ tɔɔ bwea a bwara aa loɡa anue le fɛlembɔjen bɛl bini, dɛ kpɔa do o pur bini, dɛ kpoŋe o vamtor, asɛ dɛ suuh dɛɛ tel Filisti te la.

english_verse: One day, Jesse told David, “Hurry and take this sack of roasted grain and these ten loaves of bread to your brothers at the army camp.
translation_verse: Awola bɛl, Jese ŋɔ Devid be ŋɔ, “Kpɔ boyuhala kuruware fi ne paanoo fi nɔ chwa warane ka tɛ he dɔɔranar bela baa baŋre ba tɛnte deene dɛ so la.

english_verse: And here are ten large chunks of cheese to take to their commanding officer. Find out how your brothers are doing and bring back something that shows that they're all right.
translation_verse: Kpɔ waɡasi fi nɔ ka tɛ ba laa nomoa la ɡe, ásɛ dɛ dɔ waane ba bol n be á baɡle kɛ he dɔɔranar ta waane doe.

english_verse: They're with Saul's army, fighting the Philistines in Elah Valley.”
translation_verse: Ba ne Kooro Sɔɔl ne laa tena la bwa lɔ Ɛla Fɛlembɔjen la bini, ba ne Filisti tena ɛɛ yo.”

english_verse: David obeyed his father. He got up early the next morning and left someone else in charge of the sheep; then he loaded the supplies and started off. He reached the army camp just as the soldiers were taking their places and shouting the battle cry.
translation_verse: Tɔ aa pera chɔmbibi la, Devid ɡel peera la tɛ peteɡre bɛl, dɛ kpɔ o bone chiɡ ŋwɛnɛ ta kaa, ɡɛ o mɛɛ aa ŋɔa la. Waa tel bela baa soɡa la, dɛ laa tena la ɡe deno le dɛɛ kaa bela baa dɛ la ka yo laa la, dɛɛ dooɡe laa lɔŋɔre.

english_verse: The army of Israel and the Philistine army stood there facing each other.
translation_verse: Israel laa tena la kaa che, asɛ Filisti laa tena ɡe ka che ba bɔr, ba bwa sie chaɡɛ dɔŋa.

english_verse: David left his things with the man in charge of supplies and ran up to the battle line to ask his brothers if they were well.
translation_verse: Devid kpɔ o kondikwaa ja nɛn waa dɛ nyiŋi ba laala ta la, dɛ chwa kaa o dɔɔranar be laa la ta, dɛ ka na ɡɛ baa doa.

english_verse: While David was talking with them, Goliath came out from the line of Philistines and started boasting as usual. David heard him.
translation_verse: Waa la ba be o ne baa bol waa la, Filisti tena kpeɡnɛn waa le Gat baa yerɔ Goliat la suuhno ba sie, dɛ kpɔ nyɛɡa dɛɛ muɡli ba baah, asɛ Devid no.

english_verse: When the Israelite soldiers saw Goliath, they were scared and ran off.
translation_verse: Israel tena la aa na Goliat la, ba jum jaoh dɛ bwa chwa le o sie.

english_verse: They said to each other, “Look how he keeps coming out to insult us. The king is offering a big reward to the man who kills Goliath. That man will even get to marry the king's daughter, and no one in his family will ever have to pay taxes again.”
translation_verse: Name dɛ Israel tena la dɛ bol ŋɔ, “Hé na ɡɛ baa nɔ aa naa dɛɛ ba ya be nɔ kenɛ? O balɔ dɛ baa muɡli ya Israel tena baah. Nomɛlbwa waa won kpo baa nɔ la, kooro ɛɛ tɛo kondɔɔh kohonaa. Wɛɛ berɔ lawɛ o bihaah tɛo ó mo, ásɛ dɛ ɡel naate mɛɛ nɛra ɡel toɔ bɔe Israel harɛ ta.”

english_verse: David asked some soldiers standing nearby, “What will a man get for killing this Philistine and stopping him from insulting our people? Who does that worthless Philistine think he is? He's making fun of the army of the living God!”
translation_verse: Anee Devid bɔɔ nɛra baa cheɡɛ o jwɛɛh la ŋɔ, “Dɛ nomɛl wono kpo Filisti baa nɔ dɛ le Israel tena sihiih nɔ ta naa, bɔkwaa wɛɛ ba dɔe yɔ? Umee Filisti te nɔ waa wola Korowii tomɛ, dɛ ɡe won dɛɛ muɡli Korowii waa lole saŋ bɛlbwa laa tena baah nɔɔ?”

english_verse: The soldiers told David what the king would give the man who killed Goliath.
translation_verse: Ba berɔ bol waa ba fa aa dɛ bol o be ŋɔ, “Gɛɛ baa ba ɛɛ tɛ nomɛlbwa waa dɛ ba wona kpo Goliat.”

english_verse: David's oldest brother Eliab heard him talking with the soldiers. Eliab was angry with him and said, “What are you doing here, anyway? Who's taking care of your little flock of sheep out in the desert? You spoiled brat! You came here just to watch the fighting, didn't you?”
translation_verse: Devid dɔɔ nomoa Eliab aa noa kɛŋɔ Devid ne baala la dɛ bol waa la, o baah di o nɛ, dɛ bɔɔro ŋɔ, “Bɔkwaa hɛɛ nyin bonɔ nɔ? Umee he kpɔ peera la kabora ja pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta bela wɛɛ nyiŋi a ta nɔ? N jemɛ ɡɛ haa dɛ ɡɔɔ he te, ne ɡɛ he bambile aa kpeɡa, he balɔ dɛ́ ba nyiŋi laa nɔ.”

english_verse: “Now what have I done?” David answered. “Can't I even ask a question?”
translation_verse: Devid ŋɔ, “Bɔkwa waa n ɛɔ? N bɛ waa ɡe bolaa?”

english_verse: Then he turned and asked another soldier the same thing he had asked the others, and he got the same answer.
translation_verse: O berɔ bɔɔ nɛnfala waa o fa aa bɔɔ baala la, asɛ ba chaŋo ɡɛ baa chaŋo wubwa la.

english_verse: Some soldiers overheard David talking, so they told Saul what David had said. Saul sent for David, and David came.
translation_verse: Baala bane no waa Devid aa bola la, dɛ la ka bol Kooro Sɔɔl be, asɛ o ɡel ba yerɛ Devid tɛo.

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” he said, “this Philistine shouldn't turn us into cowards. I'll go out and fight him myself!”
translation_verse: Asɛ Devid ŋɔ Kooro Sɔɔl be ŋɔ, “Bɛlbwa bɛ ɡel o bambile chɔɡ Filisti te nɔ wa, men maa ɛ he bonɔɔ nɔ ɛɛ lao dɛ́ ka yoo.”

english_verse: “You don't have a chance against him,” Saul replied. “You're only a boy, and he's been a soldier all his life.”
translation_verse: Kooro Sɔɔl chaŋo ŋɔ, “Bechalaa hen, haa won ka puu yo. O bonɔɔne saŋ bwaa o le dɛɛ yo.”

english_verse: But David told him: Your Majesty, I take care of my father's sheep. And when one of them is dragged off by a lion or a bear,
translation_verse: Kɛ Devid ŋɔ Kooro Sɔɔl be ŋɔ, “Dɛ he bonɔɔ dɛ teɡɛ o mɛɛ peera, dɛ nyujente kɛɛ sisire baa lawɛ bɛl dɛɛ kaa laa,

english_verse: I go after it and beat the wild animal until it lets the sheep go. If the wild animal turns and attacks me, I grab it by the throat and kill it.
translation_verse: n dɛ teŋɛ o nɛɛ dɛ́ yo, dɛ́ lɛo le o be. O berɛ sie dɛɛ ba n be naa, n dɛ hamɛ o baŋa dɛ́ lɔɔro kpo.

english_verse: Sir, I have killed lions and bears that way, and I can kill this worthless Philistine. He shouldn't have made fun of the army of the living God!
translation_verse: Gɛ Korowii aa ɡela he bonɔɔ won kpo nyujente ne sisire kwaraa la, ɡɛɛ mɛɛ ba Filisti te waa wola Korowii tomɛ nɔ ɡe ɛɛ, dɛkalkɛŋɔ o ɛ Korowii waa lole saŋ bɛlbwa la sisawa.

english_verse: The Lord has rescued me from the claws of lions and bears, and he will keep me safe from the hands of this Philistine. “All right,” Saul answered, “go ahead and fight him. And I hope the Lord will help you.”
translation_verse: Korowii waa lɛɛ mɛ le nyujente ne sisire nɔn ta la, wɛɛ lɛɛ mɛ le Filisti te nɔ nɔn ta.” Ate, Kooro Sɔɔl ŋɔ Devid be ŋɔ, “Kaa, Korowii ja he nɛ.”

english_verse: Saul had his own military clothes and armor put on David, and he gave David a bronze helmet to wear.
translation_verse: Asɛ Sɔɔl kpɔ o ɡbaɡba laa batakaare ne kwaa waa kpɔa dɛɛ yo do Devid, dɛ kpɔ o ayaawa ɡbɛrɛ piu.

english_verse: David strapped on a sword and tried to walk around, but he was not used to wearing those things. “I can't move with all this stuff on,” David said. “I'm just not used to it.” David took off the armor
translation_verse: Devid kpɔ o laa kere sɛɡle laa batakaare la ta, dɛ kpɔ valɛ bar tama, dɛkalkɛŋɔ dɛ ɡɛ laala ta on manɛ. O ŋɔ Kooro Sɔɔl be ŋɔ, “Maa won valɛ ane, n ta ane doe bwa,” anomanta, o foo laala la bil.

english_verse: When Goliath saw that David was just a healthy, good-looking boy, he made fun of him.
translation_verse: Waa na Devid la, o nyiŋu vah, dɛ na kɛ o jeɡa o siwi ta dɛ do wer bonɔɔ.

english_verse: “Do you think I'm a dog?” Goliath asked. “Is that why you've come after me with a stick?” He cursed David in the name of the Philistine gods
translation_verse: O bɔɔ Devid ŋɔ, “Nyoatee men he kpoŋe daa dɛɛ ba n be naa?” Asɛ o ŋwɛɛ voɡa ta Devid nɛɛ dɛ taahno.

english_verse: and shouted, “Come on! When I'm finished with you, I'll feed you to the birds and wild animals!”
translation_verse: “Ba bonɔ, mɛɛ kpoe ásɛ jumbii ne kpɔɡ bini ola di he ola!”

english_verse: David answered: You've come out to fight me with a sword and a spear and a dagger. But I've come out to fight you in the name of the Lord All-Powerful. He is the God of Israel's army, and you have insulted him too!
translation_verse: Anee Devid ŋɔ Goliat be ŋɔ, “Kere ne lampeaa he kpoŋe dɛɛ ba ba yoo mɛ, kɛ n te Korowii Waa Ɛ Koranar Bwa Kooro wɛɛ teŋɛ Israel laa tena nɛɛ he nyiŋu dɛɛ vah la sɔn nee mɛɛ ba dɛ́ ba yoi.

english_verse: Today the Lord will help me defeat you. I'll knock you down and cut off your head, and I'll feed the bodies of the other Philistine soldiers to the birds and wild animals. Then the whole world will know that Israel has a real God.
translation_verse: Fini tɔpere nɔ, Korowii ɛɛ kpɔe do n nɔn taa, ásɛ n kpoe dɛ́ teŋe he nyu. Ásɛ jumbii ne kpɔɡ bini ola ba di he ne Filisti laa tena bwa ola, ásɛ harɛre nɛra bwa jemɛ kɛŋɔ Korowii Israel tena aa dɛ tomɔ la lole.

english_verse: Everybody here will see that the Lord doesn't need swords or spears to save his people. The Lord always wins his battles, and he will help us defeat you.
translation_verse: Nɛra baa cheme bonɔ bwa ɛɛ jemɔɔ kɛŋɔ kere kɛɛ lampea ne laa Korowii ɛɛ lɛ nɛn, yoi la ɛ Korowii kon, wɛɛ kpɔ he bwaa do ya nɔn ta.”

english_verse: He put a rock in his sling and swung the sling around by its straps. When he let go of one strap, the rock flew out and hit Goliath on the forehead. It cracked his skull, and he fell facedown on the ground.
translation_verse: Devid do nɔn pur bini dɛ kpɔ bwe do vamtor la ta, dɛ kile o ka forɛ Goliat tile. Bwe la joɔ kaa bini, asɛ o chole kpɔ sie pi harɛ.

english_verse: David defeated Goliath with a sling and a rock. He killed him without even using a sword.
translation_verse: Gɛɛ a do, Devid kpo Goliat vamtor bwe ne, dɛ kere ne laa.

english_verse: David ran over and pulled out Goliath's sword. Then he used it to cut off Goliath's head. When the Philistines saw what had happened to their hero, they started running away.
translation_verse: Ate, Devid chwa kaa Goliat be, dɛ ka laa o kere pamɛ le o tɔɔ ta, dɛ teŋe o nyu. Filisti laa tena aa naa kɛŋɔ ba banyoo sewɔ la, ba berɔ, dɛ chwa kaa.

english_verse: But the soldiers of Israel and Judah let out a battle cry and went after them as far as Gath and Ekron. The bodies of the Philistines were scattered all along the road from Shaaraim to Gath and Ekron.
translation_verse: Name, Israel ne Juda tena laa tena moo teŋɛ Filisti tena nɛ ka tel Gat ne Ekron doonyoo. Filisti tena la sewɔ chɔ perɛ le bwɛjen Saaraim ŋwɛnɛ ta dɛ kaa Gat ne Ekron.

english_verse: When the Israelite army returned from chasing the Philistines, they took what they wanted from the enemy camp.
translation_verse: Israel tena la aa ti Filisti tena la dɛ berɛ ba la, ba la bela baa baŋre ba tɛnte deene dɛ so la, dɛ ka pa ba laala.

english_verse: David took Goliath's head to Jerusalem, but he kept Goliath's weapons in his own tent. David Becomes One of Saul's Officers
translation_verse: Devid kpɔ Goliat nyu ba Jerusalam, dɛ kpɔ o dɔmkwaa la ba bil o tɛnte dea bini.

english_verse: After King Saul had watched David go out to fight Goliath, Saul turned to the commander of his army and said, “Abner, who is that young man?” “Your Majesty,” Abner answered, “I swear by your life that I don't know.”
translation_verse: Gɛ saŋ Kooro Sɔɔl aa nyiŋi Devid o le dɛɛ la ka yo Goliat la, o bɔɔ Abna waa ɛ laa sitɔɔ la ŋɔ, “Ume bie bonɔɔ nɔɔ?” Ate, Abna chaŋe ŋɔ, “N dɔɔ, maa o wobɛlbwa jemɛ.”

english_verse: and Saul asked, “Who are you?” “I am David the son of Jesse, a loyal Israelite from Bethlehem.”
translation_verse: Kooro Sɔɔl bɔɔro ŋɔ, “Bonɔɔ, ume bie hen nɔ?” Anee Devid chaŋe ŋɔ, “N dɔɔ, he bonɔɔ Jese waa le Bɛtlɛham la biee men.”

english_verse: From that time on, Saul kept David in his service and would not let David go back to his own family.
translation_verse: Le awola tɔpere la, Kooro Sɔɔl ɡelɔ Devid do o sie dɛɛ tomɔ, o ta ɡelɛ o kaa o mɛɛ dem kpa.

english_verse: Jonathan liked David so much that they promised to always be loyal friends.
translation_verse: Jonatan ne Devid vɔwɛ darame fɔo, dɛkalkɛŋɔ dɛ o dɛ nyin o waa kɛ o ɡbaɡba.

english_verse: Jonathan took off the robe that he was wearing and gave it to David. He also gave him his military clothes, his sword, his bow and arrows, and his belt.
translation_verse: Jonatan foo o batakaare waa doa, ne o laa batakaare tɛ Devid, hale o kere ne o to, dɛ o kiriso.

english_verse: David was a success in everything that Saul sent him to do, and Saul made him a high officer in his army. That pleased everyone, including Saul's other officers. Saul Becomes David's Enemy
translation_verse: Kooro Sɔɔl tomɛ Devid ŋɔ ó ka ɛ wobɛlbwa naa, o dɛ ɛa kɛrɛdɛ. Anomanta, o ɛo o laa nomonjena la bini bɛl. Gɛ waa nɔ lɛ Kooro Sɔɔl nomonome ne o nɛra bwa sie.

english_verse: David had killed Goliath, the battle was over, and the Israelite army set out for home. As the army went along, women came out of each Israelite town to welcome King Saul. They were celebrating by singing songs and dancing to the music of tambourines and harps.
translation_verse: Devid aa kpo Goliat asɛ laa tena la berɛ dɛɛ kaa dem la, haahna le Israel bwɛɛre bwa ta ba cheme Kooro Sɔɔl. Ba yiiɡi loŋa, dɛ lɔ janjela silɛɛ ne dɛɛ sa.

english_verse: They sang: Saul has killed a thousand enemies; David has killed ten thousand!
translation_verse: Baa saa dɛɛ hɛɡre la, ba ɡo yela ŋɔ, “Kooro Sɔɔl kpo nɛra kaɡboŋa, Devid ɡe kpo nɛra kaɡboŋa fi.”

english_verse: This song made Saul very angry, and he thought, “They are saying that David has killed ten times more enemies than I ever did. Next they will want to make him king.”
translation_verse: Gɛ waa nɔ ta Kooro Sɔɔl som doe, o baah di dɛ ŋɔ, “Ba ŋɔ Devid kpo nɛra kaɡboŋa fi, asɛ n te kpo nɛra kaɡboŋ ɡbo. Onee baa ba lawa cheɡ kora ta.”

english_verse: The next day the Lord let an evil spirit take control of Saul, and he began acting like a crazy man inside his house. David came to play the harp for Saul as usual, but this time Saul had a spear in his hand.
translation_verse: Tɔ aa pera la, Korowii ɡelɔ kwaa ir Kooro Sɔɔl nɛɛ kpeɡri nɛ, o do dem dɛɛ bol waa kɛŋɔ choɡla te ken. Dɛ Devid ɡe soɡo dɛɛ lɔ o janjela kɛ wubwa la, anɔ te la dɛ Kooro Sɔɔl kpoŋe lampea.

english_verse: Saul thought, “I'll pin David to the wall.” He threw the spear at David twice, but David dodged and got away both times.
translation_verse: O ta lampea la dɛ ŋɔ, “Mɛɛ yaɡɛ Devid nɔɔ pɛl danjwɛ.” O ta lampea la kera anɛ, kɛ Devid ke o te, o ta on dɔe.

english_verse: Saul was afraid of David, because the Lord was helping David and was no longer helping him.
translation_verse: Dɛ Kooro Sɔɔl dɛ ɔmɛ Devid dɛkalkɛŋɔ Korowii ɡelo dɛ ka ja Devid nɛ.

english_verse: The Lord helped David, and he and his soldiers always won their battles.
translation_verse: Korowii aa ja Devid nɛɛ nomanta, wobɛlbwa waa ɛ́ la, dɛ a maɡrɔ tɛo.

english_verse: This made Saul even more afraid of David.
translation_verse: Kooro Sɔɔl aa naa kɛŋɔ o wobɛlbwa wer dɛɛ tɛo la, dɛ o dɛ ɔmɔ kɛrɛdɛ.

english_verse: But everyone else in Judah and Israel was loyal to David, because he led the army in battle.
translation_verse: Kɛ dɛ Israel ne Juda tena bwa dɛ nyin Devid wa, waa tɔ ba sie dɛ kpɔ ba dɛɛ la laa a maɡre dɛɛ tɛɛ ba la wa.

english_verse: One day, Saul told David, “If you'll be brave and fight the Lord's battles for me, I'll let you marry my oldest daughter Merab.” But Saul was really thinking, “I don't want to kill David myself, so I'll let the Philistines do it for me.”
translation_verse: Kooro Sɔɔl ŋɔ Devid be ŋɔ, “N lawɛ n bihanomoa baa dɛ yerɔ Merab dɛɛ tɛɛ hé mo. Dɛ hɛɛ dɛɛ tom mɛɛ, dɛ́ yo Korowii laa kasinteŋ ta dɛɛ tɛo tenaa.” Kooro Sɔɔl liiro kɛŋɔ anɔ taa aa ba cheɡa Filisti tena kpoo, kɛ o ɡbaɡba laa dɛ́ kpoo.

english_verse: David answered, “How could I possibly marry your daughter? I'm not very important, and neither is my family.”
translation_verse: Ate, Devid ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Umee n ɡeɔ? Israel dejen besoo taa n le dɛ́ ɛ kooro hela ɔ?”

english_verse: But when the time came for David to marry Saul's daughter Merab, Saul told her to marry Adriel from the town of Meholah.
translation_verse: Aa baa tel kɛ ba kpɔ Kooro Sɔɔl bihaah Merab tɛ Devid ó mo la, ba kpɔɔ tɛ Adreɛl waa le Mehola.

english_verse: Saul had another daughter. Her name was Michal, and Saul found out that she was in love with David. This made Saul happy,
translation_verse: Dɛ Kooro Sɔɔl bihaah bɛl ɡe baa dɛ yerɔ Mikal dɛ nyin Devid. Baa bol Kooro Sɔɔl be a waa la, o sie lɛo.

english_verse: and he thought, “I'll tell David he can marry Michal, but I'll set it up so that the Philistines will kill him.” He told David, “I'm going to give you a second chance to marry one of my daughters.”
translation_verse: Asɛ Kooro Sɔɔl lii ŋɔ, “Mɛɛ kpɔ Mikalee tɛo, dɛ́ kpɔ harɔ bel, ásɛ Filisti tena la dɔɔ kpo.” Anomanta, Kooro Sɔɔl ŋɔ Devid be ŋɔ, “He dɔ bɔr nɛɛtena name kɛ he ɛ n hela.”

english_verse: Saul ordered his officials to speak to David in private, so they went to David and said, “Look, the king likes you, and all of his officials are loyal to you. Why not ask the king if you can marry his daughter Michal?” “I'm not rich or famous enough to marry princess Michal!” David answered.
translation_verse: Ba kaa bol ɡɛ waa nɔ Devid be. Anee o ŋɔ, “Hé dɛ lii kɛ a ɛ wekokori kɛ nɛn ɛ kooro hela kɛɛ? Nyaaree men, n ɛ nɛŋɡwɛɡre.”

english_verse: The officials went back to Saul and told him exactly what David had said.
translation_verse: Kooro Sɔɔl nomonome la aa kaa bol waa Devid aa bola o be la,

english_verse: Saul was hoping that the Philistines would kill David, and he told his officials to tell David, “The king doesn't want any silver or gold. He only wants to get even with his enemies. All you have to do is to bring back proof that you have killed
translation_verse: o ŋɔ, “Hé ka ŋɔ Devid be ŋɔ kooro aa komɛlbwa nyin dɛ́ tɛ hanfale la ka ja Filisti tena lafa baa serewa pena tɔne, dɛ́ kpɔ bɔ ba kem.” Kooro Sɔɔl ɛ ɡɛ ásɛ Filisti tena la dɔ Devid kpo.

english_verse: The officials told David, and David wanted to marry the princess. King Saul had set a time limit, and before it ran out,
translation_verse: Nomonome la aa baa bol Devid be la, o sie lɛo kɛ ó ɛ kooro hela. Anomanta, mɔɔ hanfalwaa la tel la,

english_verse: King Saul knew that she loved David, and he also realized that the Lord was helping David.
translation_verse: Kooro Sɔɔl aa naa kɛŋɔ Korowii ja Devid nɛɛ, asɛ o bihaah la ɡe ɛɛ nyinu la,

english_verse: But knowing those things made Saul even more afraid of David, and he was David's enemy for the rest of his life.
translation_verse: dɛ name kwaraa Kooro Sɔɔl ɛɛ ɔmɔ kohona. O kpɔ Devid ɛ o dɔm o soɡa bini bwa.

english_verse: The Philistine rulers kept coming to fight Israel, but whenever David fought them, he won. He was famous because he won more battles against the Philistines than any of Saul's other officers.
translation_verse: Filisti laa nomonome teŋɔ kpɔ ba laa tena dɛɛ la laa, kɛ saŋ bɛlbwa ba ne Devid aa yo la, o dɛ pɔ ba nɛ. Devid lɛ sɔn kohona, dɛkalkɛ Kooro Sɔɔl laa nomonome bwa bini la, dɛ onee yo laa dɛ kpoo nɛra kohona.

english_verse: One day, Saul told his son Jonathan and his officers to kill David. But Jonathan and David were best friends,
translation_verse: Awola bɛl, Kooro Sɔɔl ŋɔ o bibaa Jonatan ne o nomonome be ŋɔ bá kpo Devid. Kɛ dɛ Jonatan dɛ nyin Devid waa taeh,

english_verse: and he warned David, “My father is trying to have you killed, so be very careful. Hide in a field tomorrow morning, and I'll bring him there. Then I'll talk to him about you, and if I find out anything, I'll let you know.”
translation_verse: N ne n mɛɛ ɛɛ ka che bela haa ka sɔh laanee, ásɛ n bol he waa baɡlo, ásɛ dɛ o bol waane aa, ń ba bol he be.”

english_verse: The next morning, Jonathan reminded Saul about the many good things David had done for him. Then he said, “Why do you want to kill David? He hasn't done anything to you. He has served in your army and has always done what's best for you. He even risked his life to kill Goliath. The Lord helped Israel win a great victory that day, and it made you happy.”
translation_verse: O sɛh seo dɛ ka pu Goliat yo dɛ kpoo. Korowiirii ɡela o yo tɛ he ne Israel tena bwa, asɛ he bwa sie lɛ. Ɛrɛɛ hɛɛ ba wona kpo nɛndɛɛɡe waa do ken pɛɛpɛɛ ɔ?”

english_verse: Saul agreed and promised, “I swear by the living Lord that I won't have David killed!”
translation_verse: Kooro Sɔɔl no o bibaa Jonatan waa la dɛ ŋwɛɛ Korowii ŋɔ, “Kasinteŋ, maa Devidii kpo.”

english_verse: Jonathan went to David and told him what Saul had said. Then he brought David to Saul, and David served in Saul's army just as he had done before.
translation_verse: Anomanta, Jonatan yerɛ Devid dɛ bol waa la bwa o be. O lawɔ ba Kooro Sɔɔl be asɛ o ne o so kɛ wubwa la.

english_verse: The next time there was a war with the Philistines, David fought hard and forced them to retreat. Michal Helps David Escape
translation_verse: Laa berɔ ba chole ja, asɛ Devid la dɛ ka yo Filisti tena la. O kpoo ba kɛrɛdɛ, ba kar bwa ɡe chwa kaa.

english_verse: One night, David was in Saul's home, playing the harp for him. Saul was sitting there, holding a spear, when an evil spirit from the Lord took control of him. Saul tried to pin David to the wall with the spear, but David dodged, and it stuck in the wall. David ran out of the house and escaped.
translation_verse: asɛ Kooro Sɔɔl fe ɛɛ nyin o yaɡɔ marɛ danjwɛɛ ta, asɛ o ke o te lampea la ka yaɡɛ danjwɛɛ la ta. Awola jwaana la, Devid chwao le dem bela.

english_verse: Saul sent guards to watch David's house all night and then to kill him in the morning. Michal, David's wife, told him, “If you don't escape tonight, they'll kill you tomorrow!”
translation_verse: Kooro Sɔɔl tomɛ bonɔɔna ŋɔ bá la Devid dem jwaana ka kpaahno, ásɛ bɔr ne chaahna la dɛ ba kpoo. Kɛ Devid haah Mikal kaoh ŋɔ, “Dɛ he ta bɔr nyine dɛ chwa jwaana nɔ ne naa, tɔɔ ne pera dɛ ba kpoe.”

english_verse: She helped David leave through a window and climb down to the ground. As David ran off,
translation_verse: Anomanta, Mikal cha Devid o kpɔ tokoro ta, dɛ tu bwɛɛ la dahara chwa kaa.

english_verse: Michal put a statue in his bed. She put goat hair on its head and dressed it in some of David's clothes.
translation_verse: Mikal kpɔ yal fɔrɔwe ba buse bela voɡ dɛ kpɔ bil mpa ta, dɛ kpɔ booh pona bil o nyu bɔr.

english_verse: The next morning, Saul sent guards to arrest David. But Michal told them, “David is sick.”
translation_verse: Kooro Sɔɔl aa tomɛ o bonɔɔna ŋɔ bá ka lawɛ Devid ba la, Mikal ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, “O bwara dɛ weo.”

english_verse: Saul sent the guards back and told them, “Bring David to me—bed and all—so I can kill him.”
translation_verse: Anee Kooro Sɔɔl berɛ tom ba Devid be ja ŋɔ, “Hé la ka kpɔɔ le o mpa ta ba tɛ mɛ, ásɛ n kpoo.”

english_verse: When the guards went in, all they found in the bed was the statue with the goat hair on its head.
translation_verse: Kɛ bonɔɔna la aa laŋa dɛ ka jo dea la, dɛ voɡ bɛl chɔ mpa la ta asɛ boohpona ane chɔ o nyu bɔr.

english_verse: “Why have you tricked me this way?” Saul asked Michal. “You helped my enemy get away!” She answered, “He said he would kill me if I didn't help him escape!” Samuel Helps David Escape
translation_verse: Anee Kooro Sɔɔl ŋɔ o bie Mikal be ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ he neɡ mɛ dɛ ɡel n dɔm dɔ bɔr chwa kaa ken?” Mikal chaŋe ŋɔ, “O ŋɔ n be ŋɔ n ta on chae o dɔ bɔr kaa laa, wɛɛ kpo mɛɛ.”

english_verse: Meanwhile, David went to Samuel at Ramah and told him what Saul had done. Then Samuel and David went to Prophets Village and stayed there.
translation_verse: Devid aa chwaa kaa la, o kaa Samoɛl be Rama dɛ ka bol ɡɛ Kooro Sɔɔl aa kpɔa ɛo bwa. Ate, o ne Samoɛl kaa Nayɔt, dɛ ka so bela.

english_verse: Someone told Saul, “David is at Prophets Village in Ramah.”
translation_verse: Belaa Kooro Sɔɔl aa noa kɛŋɔ, Devid lɔ Nayɔt waa lɔ Rama la,

english_verse: Saul sent a few soldiers to bring David back. They went to Ramah and found Samuel in charge of a group of prophets who were all prophesying. Then the Spirit of God took control of the soldiers and they started prophesying too.
translation_verse: o tomɛ o bonɔɔna ŋɔ bá la ka lawɔ. Baa laŋa la, ba nao kɛŋɔ Korowii keamere aa wara dɛɛ bol Korowii wa, asɛ Samoɛl tɔ ba sie. Belaa Korowii Doma ba so Sɔɔl bonɔɔna la nɛɛ kpeɡri nɛ, asɛ ba ɡe ɛɛ bol waa la ane dɛɛ sa.

english_verse: When Saul heard what had happened, he sent some more soldiers, but they prophesied just like the first group. He sent a third group of soldiers, but the same thing happened to them.
translation_verse: Ba kaa bol Kooro Sɔɔl be a wa, asɛ o berɛ tomɛ bonɔɔna la bane ja, ba ɡe ba bol Korowii waa la ane dɛɛ sa. Kooro Sɔɔl tomɛ bonɔɔna toorotena, ba ɡe ka bol Korowii waa dɛɛ sa.

english_verse: Finally, Saul left for Ramah himself. He went as far as the deep pit at the town of Secu, and he asked, “Where are Samuel and David?” “At Prophets Village in Ramah,” the people answered.
translation_verse: Anee Kooro Sɔɔl ɡbaɡba chiɡ ŋwɛnɛ ta kaa Rama, dɛ ka tel kɔlɔŋ bɛl waa lɔ bwɛɛ Seku. Asɛ o bɔɔ ŋɔ, “Leperaa Samoɛl ne Devid dɔɔ?” Ba chaŋe ŋɔ, “Ba lɔ Nayɔt waa lɔ Rama la.”

english_verse: Saul left for Ramah. But as he walked along, the Spirit of God took control of him, and he started prophesying. Then, when he reached Prophets Village,
translation_verse: Anomanta, Kooro Sɔɔl la Nayɔt waa lɔ Rama asɛ Korowii Doma ba so o ɡe nɛɛ kpeɡri nɛ, o valɛ bol Korowii waa la dɛɛ sa ka tel kɛŋɔ waa tel Nayɔt.

english_verse: he stripped off his clothes and prophesied in front of Samuel. He dropped to the ground and lay there naked all that day and night. That's how the saying started, “Is Saul now a prophet?”
translation_verse: O foo o laala dɛ ka che Samoɛl sie, dɛɛ bol Korowii waa la dɛɛ sa. O chɔ mumɡbal ɡɛ tɔpebir la bwa, webaŋa ne jwaana. A waa nɛra yon dɛɛ bɔɔ ŋɔ, “Kooro Sɔɔl ɡe ja Korowii keamere la nɛɛ kɛɛ?”

english_verse: David escaped from Prophets Village. Then he ran to see Jonathan and asked, “Why does your father Saul want to kill me? What have I done wrong?”
translation_verse: Anee Devid chwa le Nayɔt waa lɔ Rama dɛ la Jonatan be ka bɔɔro ŋɔ, “Bɔkwa waa n ɛɔ? N wechɔɡaa ame o? Bɔkwaa n ɛ he mɛɛ wɛɛ nyin mɛ dɛ́ kpo nɔɔ?”

english_verse: “My father can't be trying to kill you! He never does anything without telling me about it. Why would he hide this from me? It can't be true!”
translation_verse: Jonatan chaŋo ŋɔ, “Akai, Korowii ɛɛ la ane bojaŋ kɛ he sewɛ! Dɛ n mɛɛ ɛɛ ɛ wejena kɛɛ wejeɡa bɛlbwa kwaraa yaa, o ɡelɔ mɛɛ jemɛ a bini. Waa kpɔ sɔɔh mɛ. A ta kasinteŋ ɛɛ.”

english_verse: “Jonathan, I swear it's true! But your father knows how much you like me, and he didn't want to break your heart. That's why he didn't tell you. I swear by the living Lord and by your own life that I'm only one step ahead of death.”
translation_verse: Anee Devid ŋwɛɛ ŋɔ, “He mɛɛ jemɔ kɛŋɔ n dɛ nyin he wa, asɛ o lii o nyu bini ŋɔ, ‘Jonatan ta chɛ kɛ ó jemɛ ɡɛ waa nɔ, ɡɛ laa aa, o bambile ɛɛ chɔɡoo.’ N ŋwɛɛ Korowii waa lole saŋ bɛlbwa nɔ kɛŋɔ, n ne seo baah aa jaŋɛ kpa.”

english_verse: Then Jonathan said, “Tell me what to do, and I'll do it.”
translation_verse: Jonatan ŋɔ Devid be ŋɔ, “Komɛlbwa haa dɛ nyin kɛ ń ɛ la, mɛɛ ɛo tɛɛ.”

english_verse: David answered: Tomorrow is the New Moon Festival, and I'm supposed to eat dinner with your father. But instead, I'll hide in a field until the evening of the next day.
translation_verse: Ate Devid ŋɔ, “Keree Korobifale Tɔpejen, a chɛ kɛ n ne kooro di kwa. Kɛ ɡel ń chwa ka sɔh kpɔɡ bini ka tel kerele jɔmɔra.

english_verse: If Saul wonders where I am, tell him, “David asked me to let him go to his hometown of Bethlehem, so he could take part in a sacrifice his family makes there every year.”
translation_verse: Dɛ he mɛɛ ta men ba nae yaa, he ŋɔ, ‘Devid soŋ mɛ, n tɛo ŋwɛnɛ o ɛ warane kaa o bwɛɛ Bɛtlɛham, dɛkalkɛ o lolanar bwa dɛ ba kwaa kpoora ɛ benanyoa saraha.’

english_verse: If your father says it's all right, then I'm safe. But if he gets angry, you'll know he wants to harm me.
translation_verse: Dɛ o sɛoh waa, ate mɛɛ dɔ n nyuu. Kɛ dɛ o baah diu waa, dɛ he jemɔ kɛŋɔ o dɛ nyin mɛ dɛ́ kpo.

english_verse: Be kind to me. After all, it was your idea to promise the Lord that we would always be loyal friends. If I've done anything wrong, kill me yourself, but don't hand me over to your father.
translation_verse: He te sune men maa ɛ he bonɔɔ nɔ nɛ, ásɛ dɛ teŋɛ fɔo n ne haa fɔwa Korowii sie la ta. Dɛ n di bolchɔɡe aa, he ɡbabir den kpo mɛ. Ɛrɛɛ chɛ kɛŋɔ he kpɔ mɛ tɛ he mɛɛ ɔ?”

english_verse: “Don't worry,” Jonathan said. “If I find out that my father wants to kill you, I'll certainly let you know.”
translation_verse: Jonatan ŋɔ, “Akai, dɛ n noɔ tamaa bɛlbwa kɛŋɔ n mɛɛ siwi beɡrɔ wɛɛ nyini dɛ́ kpo aa, n fe ta he be bolaa?”

english_verse: “Let's go out to this field, and I'll tell you,” Jonathan answered. When they got there,
translation_verse: Jonatan ŋɔ, “Ba ya kaa kpɔɡ bini.” Asɛ ba bwa teŋɛ dɔŋa nɛɛ kaa.

english_verse: Jonathan said: I swear by the Lord God of Israel, that two days from now I'll know what my father is planning. Of course I'll let you know if he's friendly toward you.
translation_verse: Ate, Jonatan ŋɔ Devid be ŋɔ, “Korowii Israel tena aa dɛ tomɔ la ɛ ya bwa danseɛ. Kerele saŋ nɔ bɔr, mɛɛ bɔɔ n mɛɛ waa nɔɔ, dɛ o ta liichɔɡa bɛlbwa dɔe he nɛ aa, mɛɛ ɡeloo he no.

english_verse: But if he wants to harm you, I promise to tell you and help you escape. And I ask the Lord to punish me severely if I don't keep my promise. I pray that the Lord will bless you, just as he used to bless my father.
translation_verse: Dɛ n mɛɛ dɛ nyini dɛ́ kpoe naa, n ŋwɛɛrɔ kɛ dɛ n ta he be bolɛ dɛ ɡel he dɔ bɔr chwa aa, Kórowii tɛr n deŋne kohona. Korowiirii dɛ́ ja he nɛɛ ɡɛ waa ja he mɛɛ nɛɛ la.

english_verse: Someday the Lord will wipe out all of your enemies. Then if I'm still alive, please be as kind to me as the Lord has been. But if I'm dead, be kind to my family.
translation_verse: Baɡle ɡɛ nyina la n lolanar nɛ, ásɛ dɛ Korowii chɔɡ n dɔma bwa le harɛ nɔ ta kwaraa naa.

english_verse: Jonathan and David made an agreement that even David's descendants would have to keep. Then Jonathan said, “I pray that the Lord will take revenge on your descendants if they break our promise.”
translation_verse: Bɛ ɡel fɔo n ne haa fɔwa la chɔɡ. A ba ɡɛ naa Korowii ɛɛ tɛr he deŋnee.”

english_verse: Jonathan thought as much of David as he did of himself, so he asked David to promise once more that he would be a loyal friend.
translation_verse: Jonatan ɡelɔ Devid berɛ kwaa baɡɛ nyoa kɛ wɛɛ dɛɛ nyin o waa kohonaa, dɛkalkɛŋɔ o dɛ nyin Devid waa kɛŋɔ o ɡbaɡba ken.

english_verse: After this Jonathan said: Tomorrow is the New Moon Festival, and people will wonder where you are, because your place at the table will be empty.
translation_verse: Ate, Jonatan ŋɔ Devid be ŋɔ, “Korobifale Tɔpejen dii kere, baa hen na, he kara ɛɛ che pɛɛ.

english_verse: By the day after tomorrow, everyone will think you've been gone a long time. Then go to the place where you hid before and stay beside Going-Away Rock.
translation_verse: Le kere jɔmɔra bɔr la, berɛ kaa bela haa kaa sɔh ɡɛ saŋ waa nɔ aa pa mun la, dɛ́ sɔh Esel bwetal la jwɛh.

english_verse: I'll shoot three arrows at a target off to the side of the rock,
translation_verse: Mɛɛ ta hɛma atoroo yaɡɛ o keŋkeŋ kɛŋɔ maa dɛ nyin komɛl dɛ́ yaɡɛ ken.

english_verse: and send my servant to find the arrows. You'll know if it's safe to come out by what I tell him. If it is safe, I swear by the living Lord that I'll say, “The arrows are on this side of you! Pick them up!”
translation_verse: Mɛɛ tomɛ n bonɔɔnee dɛ́ ŋɔ, ‘La ka ɡaaɡe hɛma la bɔr.’ Dɛ n ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, ‘Na, hɛma la lɔ he baŋ bonɔ, kpɔa ba bonɔ naa,’ a dɛ baɡle kɛ he dɔ he nyu name, ásɛ he le ba. N ŋwɛɛ Korowii kɛŋɔ dɛ ɔmee bɛlbwa toole kpa.

english_verse: But if it isn't safe, I'll say to the boy, “The arrows are farther away!” This will mean that the Lord wants you to leave, and you must go.
translation_verse: Kɛ dɛ n ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, ‘Hɛma la lɔ he sideŋ bela aa,’ amɔ le kaa, dɛkalkɛŋɔ Korowii ŋɔa ŋɔ he kaa,

english_verse: But he will always watch us to make sure that we keep the promise we made to each other.
translation_verse: ásɛ he lii waa n ne haa bola la, Korowii ɛ ya bwa danseɛ, á do ya baah saŋ bɛlbwa dɛɛ la.”

english_verse: So David hid there in the field. During the New Moon Festival, Saul sat down to eat
translation_verse: Devid sɔh kpɔɡ bini bela asɛ Korobifale Tɔpejen la dii aa tela la, Kooro Sɔɔl ka so dɛɛ ba kwaa dii.

english_verse: by the wall, just as he always did. Jonathan sat across from him, and Abner sat next to him. But David's place was empty.
translation_verse: Kooro soɡo pɛl danjwɛ bela waa ɛ o soŋnibɔr, asɛ Jonatan so o sie chaɡɔ, Abna ɡe so teŋɛ Kooro Sɔɔl nɛ, kɛ dɛ Devid sobɔr la te chɔ pɛɛ.

english_verse: Saul didn't say anything that day, because he was thinking, “Something must have happened to make David unfit to be at the Festival. Yes, something must have happened.”
translation_verse: Awola tɔpere la, Kooro Sɔɔl ta wobɛlbwa bolɛ, dɛ o dɛ lii ŋɔ, “Waane ken ka chiɡ Devid nɛɛ dɛ ɡel o kah doŋa waa wola won ba Tɔpejen nɔ dii ta.”

english_verse: The day after the New Moon Festival, when David's place was still empty, Saul asked Jonathan, “Why hasn't that son of Jesse come to eat with us? He wasn't here yesterday, and he still isn't here today!”
translation_verse: Tɔ aa pera Korobifale Tɔpejen tɔpenɛɛte ta la, dɛ Devid sobɔr la chɔ pɛɛ ja. Anee Kooro Sɔɔl bɔɔ o bibaa Jonatan ŋɔ, “Bɔkwa waa bala Jese bibaa la aa wola kondikwaa nɔ bɔr balɛ dɛ ne fini bwa nɔɔ?”

english_verse: Jonathan answered, “The reason David hasn't come to eat with you is that he begged me to let him go to Bethlehem. He said, ‘Please let me go. My family is offering a sacrifice, and my brother told me I have to be there. Do me this favor and let me slip away to see my brothers.’ ”
translation_verse: O ŋɔ ń tɛo ŋwɛnɛ ó kaa, dɛkalkɛ o lolanar kpo kwaa dɛɛ ba saraha ɛɛ ba bwɛ, asɛ o dɔɔ wa ta nɔn yerɔ ŋɔ ó ba. Dɛ n nao kɛŋɔ n dɛ nyin o wa aa, n tɛo ŋwɛnɛ ó la ka na o lolanar. A waa haa wola on o sobɔr nae la.”

english_verse: Saul was furious with Jonathan and yelled, “You're no son of mine, you traitor! I know you've chosen to be loyal to that son of Jesse. You should be ashamed of yourself! And your own mother should be ashamed that you were ever born.
translation_verse: Ate, Kooro Sɔɔl baah di Jonatan nɛ dɛ ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Bie o nya deŋne aa kpeɡa o waa aa wola kasinteŋ dɔe kohona! N nao kɛŋɔ he ne Jese bibaa bwa nyoa pɛo dɛ́ kpɔ sihiih kpo he ɡbaɡba ne he nya.

english_verse: You'll never be safe, and your kingdom will be in danger as long as that son of Jesse is alive. Turn him over to me now! He deserves to die!”
translation_verse: Haa jemɛ kɛŋɔ Devid taa soɡe le nɔ, haa won ɛ kooro ya harɛ nɔ ta naa? Kaa taraken dɛ́ ka kpɔɔ ba bonɔ, a chɛ kɛ ó sewɛ.”

english_verse: “Why do you want to kill David?” Jonathan asked. “What has he done?”
translation_verse: Asɛ Jonatan bɔɔ o mɛɛ ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ chɛ kɛŋɔ bá kpoo wɔ? Bɔkwa waa o ɛɔ?”

english_verse: Saul threw his spear at Jonathan and tried to kill him. Then Jonathan was sure that his father really did want to kill David.
translation_verse: Ate, Kooro Sɔɔl ta o lampea ŋɔ, ó kpo Jonatan. A ɡelɔ o jemɛ kɛŋɔ o mɛɛ siwi beɡrɔ kɛ ó kpo Devid kpela.

english_verse: Jonathan was angry and hurt that his father had insulted David so terribly. He got up, left the table, and didn't eat anything all that day.
translation_verse: Jonatan iro o baah di kohona o le teebur ta, a ɡɛ Korobifale Tɔpejen la tɔpenɛɛte la ta. O ta kwaa dii, dɛkalkɛ a dɛ we o nɛ, sihihwaa o mɛɛ aa ɛa dɛ chɛɡre Devid la.

english_verse: In the morning, Jonathan went out to the field to meet David. He took a servant boy along
translation_verse: Tɔ aa pera chɔmbibi la, Jonatan kaa kpɔɡ bini dɛ ka cheme Devid, dɛ bechala bɛl ja o nɛ.

english_verse: and told him, “When I shoot the arrows, you run and find them for me.” The boy started running, and Jonathan shot an arrow so that it would go beyond him.
translation_verse: Asɛ o ŋɔ bie la be ŋɔ, “Chwa dɛ́ ka ɡaaɡe hɛma maa taa la bɔr.” Bie la aa chwaa dɛɛ kaa la, dɛ Jonatan tao dɛɛ ta o sie.

english_verse: When the boy got near the place where the arrow had landed, Jonathan shouted, “Isn't the arrow on past you?”
translation_verse: Bie la aa tel bela hɛm la aa kaa le la, Jonatan nyɛɡ o nɛɛ ŋɔ, “Hɛm la chɔ he sideŋ.”

english_verse: Jonathan shouted to him again, “Hurry up! Don't stop!” The boy picked up the arrows and brought them back to Jonathan,
translation_verse: Anee o kɔr bie la ŋɔ, “Ɛ warane kaa. Bɛ che!” Bie la kaa kpɔ hɛm la dɛ berɛ ba o nomoa be.

english_verse: but he had no idea about what was going on. Only Jonathan and David knew.
translation_verse: Dɛ bechala la aa waa nɔ bɛlbwa bini jemɛ, Jonatan ne Devid ɡboo jema.

english_verse: Jonathan gave his weapons to the boy and told him, “Take these back into town.”
translation_verse: Jonatan kpɔ o dɔmkwaa la choɡ bie la ŋɔ ó kpɔ kaa dem.

english_verse: After the boy had gone, David got up from beside the mound and bowed very low three times. Then he and Jonathan kissed each other and cried, but David cried louder.
translation_verse: Bie la aa kaala la, Devid iro le Esal bwetal o fa aa kaa sɔh o ta la ta, dɛ ba ɡuŋi Jonatan sie, dɛ kpɔ sie pi harɛ kera atoro. Asɛ ba ɡbaa dɔŋa pɛl ba te, dɛ bwa ɛɛ wi, kɛ Devid wii laanee ɡwaala.

english_verse: Jonathan said, “Take care of yourself. And remember, we each have asked the Lord to watch and make sure that we and our descendants keep our promise forever.” David left and Jonathan went back to town.
translation_verse: Jonatan ŋɔ Devid be ŋɔ, “Kaa deŋnesɔɔhna ne, ya bwa ŋwɛɛrɔ Korowii sɔn ta ŋɔ, ‘Korowii ɛ ya danseɛ dɛ́ chɔ le tɛ n ne hen, he naanar ne n ɡe naanar baah saŋ bɛlbwa dɛɛ la.’ ” Belaa Devid kaa asɛ Jonatan ɡe berɛ kaa bwɛɛ la ta.

english_verse: David went to see Ahimelech, a priest who lived in the town of Nob. Ahimelech was trembling with fear as he came out to meet David. “Why are you alone?” Ahimelech asked. “Why isn't anyone else with you?”
translation_verse: Devid la sɔfo Ahemɛlɛk be Nɔb. Sɔfo Ahemɛlɛk aa nao la, o leɔ ba chemo, dɛ o bwara dɛ sa, asɛ Ahemɛlɛk bɔɔro ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ he ɡbo ɛɛ valɛ nɔɔ? Bɔkwa waa nomɛlbwa ta he nɛɛ jae yɔ?”
