english_verse: “I'm on a mission for King Saul,” David answered. “He ordered me not to tell anyone what the mission is all about, so I ordered my soldiers to stay somewhere else.
translation_verse: Devid chaŋe sɔfo Ahemɛlɛk ŋɔ, “Kooro Sɔɔl tom mɛ waane ta dɛ ŋɔ n be ŋɔ, ‘Nomɛlbwa ta chɛ kɛ ó jemɛ waa haa koh a waa dɛɛ valɛ, ne anɔ la maa ŋɔa he ɛ.’ Kɛ laa tena baa ja n nɛɛ la te, n ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ bá chem mɛ bobɛl.

english_verse: Do you have any food you can give me? Could you spare five loaves of bread?”
translation_verse: Taraken, kondikwaa besoo lɔ he be nɔ? Tɛ mɛ paanoo anue kɛɛ kon te bɛlbwa haa dɔa.”

english_verse: “The only bread I have is the sacred bread,” the priest told David. “You can have it if your soldiers didn't sleep with women last night.”
translation_verse: Anee sɔfo la chaŋe Devid ŋɔ, “N ta paanoo pɛɛ bɛlbwa dɔe, atane onɔ la baa lea cheɡ tɛ Korowii la ɡbo. Dɛ he laa tena nɔ ta haahna chɔe baah nɔ ta tenaa, he lɛ tɛɛ ba.”

english_verse: “Of course we didn't sleep with women,” David answered. “I never let my men do that when we're on a mission. They have to be acceptable to worship God even when we're on a regular mission, and today we're on a special mission.”
translation_verse: Devid ŋɔ, “Kasinteŋ, n ne laa tena nɔ dɛ kaa wepɛɛ ta kwaraa naa, ba laa ba te dɛɛ kpɔ haahna chɔe ta, doŋa bɛlbwa le ba nɛ, ń baa bol waa aa hiah dɛ do ken nɔ.”

english_verse: The only bread the priest had was the sacred bread that he had taken from the place of worship after putting out the fresh loaves. So he gave it to David.
translation_verse: Anomanta, sɔfo la kpɔ paanoo baa lea cheɡ tɛ Korowii o do ɡoroŋ la tɛo, dɛkalkɛ dɛ paanoo bɛlbwa toole ka ja anɔ la baa kpɔa dɛɛ bil Korowii sie. O laa kpɔ teebur waa do ɡoroŋ la ta, dɛ kpɔ anɔ la aa wɔba ba chiɡ a naa ta.

english_verse: It so happened that one of Saul's officers was there, worshiping the Lord that day. His name was Doeg the Edomite, and he was the strongest of Saul's shepherds.
translation_verse: Dɛ Doeɡ waa le Edom, dɛ ɛ Kooro Sɔɔl peteɡre nomoa lɔ bela awola tɔpere la dɛɛ tomɛ Korowii.

english_verse: David asked Ahimelech, “Do you have a spear or a sword? I had to leave so quickly on this mission for the king that I didn't bring along my sword or any other weapons.”
translation_verse: Devid bɔɔ sɔfo Ahemɛlɛk ŋɔ, “He dɔ lampea kɛɛ kere he be bonɔ naa? N ta kere kɛɛ dɔmkon bɛlbwa ne bonɔ balɛ, dɛ kooro toma la waa hiaoh kohona, asɛ mɛɛ too nomanta, n ta wone kpɔ komɛlbwa.”

english_verse: The priest answered, “The only sword here is the one that belonged to Goliath the Philistine. You were the one who killed him in Elah Valley, and so you can take his sword if you want to. It's wrapped in a cloth behind the statue.” “It's the best sword there is,” David said. “I'll take it!” David Tries To Find Safety in Gath
translation_verse: Sɔfo la chaŋo ŋɔ, “Goliat waa ɛ Filisti te he kpoo Ɛla Fɛlembɔjen bini la kere lɔ n be bonɔ. Ba kpɔ yal fɔrɔwo o tel sɔfo batakaarebora efɔd la habɔɔ. He dɛ nyin aa, he ka kpɔ. Kere bɛlbwa toole bonɔ ka ja o nɛɛ kpa.” Ate Devid ŋɔ, “Keredɛɛɡe toole bobɛlbwa, kpɔ tɛ mɛ.” Devid la bwɛjen Gat

english_verse: David kept on running from Saul that day until he came to Gath, where he met with King Achish.
translation_verse: Awola tɔpere la, Devid chwao le Kooro Sɔɔl be dɛ kaa bwɛjen Gat Kooro Akis be.

english_verse: The officers of King Achish were also there, and they asked Achish, “Isn't David a king back in his own country? Don't the Israelites dance and sing, ‘Saul has killed a thousand enemies; David has killed ten thousand’?”
translation_verse: Anee Kooro Akis nomonome bɔɔ Devid ŋɔ, “Hen Devid nɔ laa ɛ kooro he harɛ ta la aa? He laa ba kpɔ ɡo yela dɛɛ sa ŋɔ, ‘Kooro Sɔɔl kpo nɛra kaɡboŋa, asɛ Devid ɡe kpo nɛra kaɡboŋa fi la aa?’ ”

english_verse: David thought about what they were saying, and it made him afraid of Achish.
translation_verse: Devid kpɔ ɡɛ waa nɔ do o nyu bini, dɛ koh a waa dɛɛ ɔmɛ bwɛjen Gat Kooro Akis kɛrɛdɛ.

english_verse: So right there in front of everyone, he pretended to be insane. He acted confused and started making scratches on the doors of the town gate, while drooling in his beard.
translation_verse: Anomanta, o saahnɔ dɛɛ ɛ kɛŋɔ waa dɛ we choɡla ken ba sie, o taa lɔ ba nɔn ta la, dɛ o we-ɛɛla bwa ɛ choɡla wa, dɛ kpɔ kon dɛɛ peeɡe ba doonyojen ɡbeni ta, asɛ dɛ ɡel nentane ɛɛ yɔɔ o tampona.

english_verse: “Look at him!” Achish said to his officers. “You can see he's crazy. Why did you bring him to me?
translation_verse: Kooro Akis ŋɔ o nomonome be ŋɔ, “Hé na baa la! O dɛ we choɡla! Bɔkwaa dɔ o ne n be bonɔ bala ɔ?

english_verse: I have enough crazy people without your bringing another one here. Keep him away from my palace!”
translation_verse: N nya choɡla tena asɛ he berɛ lawɛ onɔ ɡe ba n sie o baa ɛ anɔ bwa nɔ naa? Nɛn waa do ken chɛ kɛ ó ba dem bonɔ naa?”

english_verse: When David escaped from the town of Gath, he went to Adullam Cave. His brothers and the rest of his family found out where he was, and they followed him there.
translation_verse: Devid le bwɛjen Gat dɛ chwa ka sɔh bwɛjen Adulam bwebɔɔ bini. O dɔɔranar ne o mɛɛ dem tena aa no o waa la, ba la o be bela.

english_verse: A lot of other people joined him too. Some were in trouble, others were angry or in debt, and David was soon the leader of
translation_verse: Banɔ la baa dɛ fiɡ ba ne nɛra baa di kema, dɛ banɔ la ba bambile aa chɔɡa bwa baa teŋɛ o nɛ. Nɛra dɛ ɛ lafraanaarɛɛ baa cheme o sie, o ɛ ba nomoa.

english_verse: David left Adullam Cave and went to the town of Mizpeh in Moab, where he talked with the king of Moab. “Please,” David said, “let my father and mother stay with you until I find out what God will do with me.”
translation_verse: Devid le bela dɛ la Mispa waa lɔ Moab harɛ ta, dɛ ka ŋɔ bela kooro be ŋɔ, “Hɛɛ sɛoh dɛ́ ɡel n mɛɛ ne n nya ba so he be bonɔ ka tel saŋ maa na waa Korowii aa ɛ tɛ mɛ naa?”

english_verse: So he brought his parents to the king of Moab, and they stayed with him while David was in hiding.
translation_verse: Anomanta, o ɡelɔ ba so kooro la be ɡɛ saŋ waa kaa sɔh bwebɔɔ la bini la bwa.

english_verse: One day the prophet Gad told David, “Don't stay here! Go back to Judah.” David then left and went to Hereth Forest. Saul Kills the Priests of the Lord
translation_verse: Ate, Korowii keame baa dɛ yerɔ Gad ba ŋɔ Devid be kɛŋɔ, ó le bwebɔɔ la bini bela dɛ́ kaa Juda harɛ ta. Anomanta, Devid le bela dɛ kaa Hɛrɛt kɔne bini. Kooro Sɔɔl kpoo Nɔb sɔfore

english_verse: Saul was sitting under a small tree on top of the hill at Gibeah when he heard that David and his men had been located. Saul was holding his spear, and his officers were standing in front of him.
translation_verse: Awola bɛl, Kooro Sɔɔl baa no kɛŋɔ ba na Devid ne o laa tena. Dɛ Kooro Sɔɔl kpoŋe o lampea dɛ so dajen bɛl mun Gebea deŋɡare doa, asɛ o laa nomonome bwa che baro.

english_verse: He told them: Listen to me! You belong to the Benjamin tribe, so if that son of Jesse ever becomes king, he won't give you fields or vineyards. He won't make you officers in charge of thousands or hundreds as I have done.
translation_verse: Asɛ Kooro Sɔɔl ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, “N bala haa le Bɛnjamen dea, hé no! Jese bibaa nɔ ɛɛ won tɛ he bwa harɛre ne daa kooni aa? Wɛɛ won cheɡ heyaa nomonome he chɔ laa tena kaɡboŋa kɛɛ lafare nyoa aa?

english_verse: But you're all plotting against me! Not one of you told me that my own son Jonathan had made an agreement with him. Not one of you cared enough to tell me that Jonathan had helped one of my officers rebel. Now that son of Jesse is trying to ambush me.
translation_verse: Amɔ a waa he bwa sɔh dɛɛ vɔrɔwe n vɔrɔwa nɔ naa? Nomɛlbwa ta n be bolɛ ŋɔ n bie ne Jese bie fɔwɛ fɔo. Bɛlbwa waane laa n wa kɛɛ dɛ bol n be ŋɔ n bie ɡelɔ n bonɔɔ Devid ɛɛ vɔrɔwe n vɔrɔwa dɛ́ kpo mɛ, ɡɛ waa ɛa fini nɔ.”

english_verse: Doeg the Edomite was standing with the other officers and spoke up, “When I was in the town of Nob, I saw that son of Jesse. He was visiting the priest Ahimelech the son of Ahitub.
translation_verse: Ate, Edom te Doeɡ o ne Kooro Sɔɔl laa nomonome la aa cheɡa la ŋɔ, “N na Jese bibaa la o ba Nɔb, Ahitub bibaa sɔfo Ahemɛlɛk be.

english_verse: Ahimelech talked to the Lord for him, then gave him food and the sword that had belonged to Goliath the Philistine.”
translation_verse: Ahemɛlɛk kaa bɔɔ le Korowii be tɛo, dɛ berɛ kpɔ kondikwaa ne Goliat waa ɛ Filisti te kere tɛo.”

english_verse: Saul sent a message to Ahimelech and his whole family of priests at Nob, ordering them to come to him. When they came,
translation_verse: Belaa Kooro Sɔɔl tomɛ ŋɔ bá ka yerɛ Ahitub bibaa sɔfo Ahemɛlɛk ne o mɛɛ dem tena bwa baa ɛ sɔfore dɛ so Nɔb la, ásɛ ba bwa ba kooro be.

english_verse: Saul told them, “Listen to me, you son of Ahitub.” “Certainly, Your Majesty,” Ahimelech answered.
translation_verse: Kooro Sɔɔl ŋɔ, “Ahitub bibaa, dɛɛ no n be name.” Anee o chaŋe ŋɔ, “N naa, n dɛ no he be.”

english_verse: Saul demanded, “Why did you plot against me with that son of Jesse? You helped him rebel against me by giving him food and a sword, and by talking with God for him. Now he's trying to ambush me!”
translation_verse: Anee Kooro Sɔɔl ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ he ne Jese bibaa sɔh dɛɛ vɔrɔwe n vɔrɔwa, he tɛo kondikwa ne kere dɛ berɛ bɔɔ le Korowii be tɛo nɔɔ? A ɡelɔ o ɛɛ mɛ deŋnekpeɡ dɛɛ nyin mɛ dɛ́ kpo fini tɔpere.”

english_verse: “Your Majesty, none of your officers is more loyal than David!” Ahimelech replied. “He's your son-in-law and the captain of your bodyguard. Everyone in your family respects him.
translation_verse: Sɔfo Ahemɛlɛk chaŋe kooro ŋɔ, “He nomonome nɔ bwa bini ume waa dɔ kasinteŋ kɛ Devid waa ɛ he hela, dɛ berɛ chɔ nɛra baa dɛ daahne nyoa, dɛ dɔ duure kohona he dem ɔ?

english_verse: This isn't the first time I've talked with God for David, and it's never made you angry before! Please don't accuse me or my family like this. I have no idea what's going on!”
translation_verse: A ɡɛ tɔpere la ɡboo n bɔɔ waa le Korowii be tɛo waa? Akai, ɡɛ laa a do. N naa kooro, bɛ men maa ɛ he bonɔɔ nɔ ne n mɛɛ dem nɛra wechɔɡa bɛlbwa ɛ, he bonɔɔ aa waa nɔ wobɛlbwa jemɛ.”

english_verse: “Ahimelech,” Saul said, “you and your whole family are going to die.”
translation_verse: Anee Kooro la ŋɔ Ahemɛlɛk be ŋɔ, “Kasinteŋ, he ne he mɛɛ dem tena bwa ɛɛ serewoo.”

english_verse: Saul shouted to his bodyguards, “These priests of the Lord helped David! They knew he was running away, but they didn't tell me. Kill them!” But the king's officers would not attack the priests of the Lord.
translation_verse: Belaa kooro la ŋɔ nɛra baa dɛ daahno dɛ che o baŋ bɛl la be ŋɔ, “Hé berɛ he te dɛ́ kpoo Korowii sɔfore nɔ, dɛkalkɛ ba ɡe teŋɛ Devid nɛ. Ba jemɔ kɛ o dɛ chwa, kɛ ba ta n be bolɛ.” Kɛ dɛ nɛra baa dɛ daah kooro la aa nyin kɛ bá kpoo ba.

english_verse: Then he attacked the town of Nob, where the priests had lived, and he killed everyone there—men, women, children, and babies. He even killed their cattle, donkeys, and sheep. Only Abiathar Escapes from Nob
translation_verse: O ɡelɔ ba kpoo nɛra baa kaa dɛ do Nɔb waa ɛ sɔfore bwɛɛ la bwa, ne baala ne haahna, ne bechale ne bechasɔɔhne, ne nae ne keeɡore dɛ peera bwa.

english_verse: Ahimelech's son Abiathar was the only one who escaped. He ran to David
translation_verse: Kɛ Abiata waa ɛ sɔfo Ahemɛlɛk bibaala la bini bɛl chwao dɛ ka ja Devid nɛ.

english_verse: and told him, “Saul has murdered the Lord's priests at Nob!”
translation_verse: Abiata ŋɔ Devid be ŋɔ Kooro Sɔɔl kpoo Korowii sɔfore la bwa.

english_verse: David answered, “That day when I saw Doeg, I knew he would tell Saul! Your family died because of me.
translation_verse: Anee Devid ŋɔ Abiata be ŋɔ, “Awola Doeɡ aa lɔ bela la, dɛ n jemɔ kɛrɛdɛ kɛŋɔ wɛɛ bol Kooro Sɔɔl bee. N nɛɛ a che ba kpoo he mɛɛ dem nɛra bwa la.

english_verse: Stay here. Isn't the same person trying to kill both of us? Don't worry! You'll be safe here with me.”
translation_verse: So n be bonɔ, dɛɛ berɛ ɔma. Nɛn waa dɛ nyini dɛ́ kpo la, dɛ́ nyin n ɡe dɛ́ kpo. He lɔ n be bonɔ naa, hɛɛ dɔ he nyuu.”

english_verse: One day some people told David, “The Philistines keep attacking the town of Keilah and stealing grain from the threshing place.”
translation_verse: Devid baa no kɛŋɔ Filisti tena dɛ yo bwɛɛ Keila dɛ ŋwɛ mefala le o ta dɛɛ kaa.

english_verse: David asked the Lord, “Should I attack these Philistines?” “Yes,” the Lord answered. “Attack them and rescue Keilah.”
translation_verse: Asɛ o bɔɔ Korowii ŋɔ, “Ń ka yo Filisti tena nɔ naa?” Anee Korowii chaŋo ŋɔ, “Kaa ka yoo ba, dɛ́ lɛ Keila tena ta.”

english_verse: But David's men said, “Look, even here in Judah we're afraid of the Philistines. We will be terrified if we try to fight them at Keilah!”
translation_verse: Kɛ baala baa ja Devid nɛɛ la ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Juda harɛ ta bonɔ kwaraa yaa ɔmɛ nɔ. Ɛrɛɛ yaa ba wona la Keila dɛ́ ka pu Filisti laa tena yoo?”

english_verse: David asked the Lord about it again. “Leave at once,” the Lord answered. “I will give you victory over the Philistines at Keilah.”
translation_verse: Devid berɔ bɔɔ waa le Korowii be asɛ o chaŋo ŋɔ, “Kaa Keila dɛ́ ka puu ba yo, mɛɛ ɡeloo he pɔ Filisti tena la nɛ.”

english_verse: David and his men went there and fiercely attacked the Philistines. They killed many of them, then led away their cattle, and rescued the people of Keilah.
translation_verse: Anomanta, Devid ne o laa tena la Keila, dɛ ka yo Filisti tena dɛ larawe ba kondɛɛra bwa kaa. O kpo Filisti tena ɡalɡa dɛ lɛ Keila tena ta.

english_verse: David heard about Saul's plan to capture him, and he told Abiathar, “Let's ask God what we should do.”
translation_verse: Devid aa naa kɛŋɔ Kooro Sɔɔl dɛ vɔrɔwe o kpoe waa la, o ŋɔ sɔfo Abiata be ŋɔ, “Kpɔ sɔfo batakaarebora efɔd la ba tɛ mɛ, ásɛ ya bɔɔ le Korowii be ɡɛ yaa ɛ.”

english_verse: David prayed, “Lord God of Israel, I was told that Saul is planning to come here. What should I do? Suppose he threatens to destroy the town because of me.
translation_verse: Asɛ Devid ŋɔ, “N Naa Korowii Israel tena aa dɛ tomɛ, he bonɔɔ noɔ kɛrɛdɛ kɛŋɔ Kooro Sɔɔl koh n waa dɛɛ ba ba yo Keila tena dɛ́ chɔɡ bwɛɛ la.

english_verse: Would the leaders of Keilah turn me over to Saul? Or is he really coming? Please tell me, Lord.” “Yes, he will come,” the Lord answered.
translation_verse: Keila tena ɛɛ sɛoh dɛ́ kpɔ mɛ tɛo wa aa? Kooro Sɔɔl ɛɛ bao ɡɛ he bonɔɔ aa noa la aa? N Naa Korowii Israel tena aa dɛ tomɛ, ɡel he bonɔɔ jemɛ.” Anee Korowii chaŋe ŋɔ, “Kooro Sɔɔl ɛɛ bao.”

english_verse: David asked, “Would the leaders of Keilah hand me and my soldiers over to Saul?” “Yes, they would,” the Lord answered.
translation_verse: Devid berɔ bɔɔ ja ŋɔ, “Keila tena ɛɛ le n ne n laa tenaa tɛ yá do Kooro Sɔɔl lɔɡa kɛɛ?” Anee Korowii ŋɔ, “Baa le heyaa tɛo.”

english_verse: David stayed in hideouts in the hill country of Ziph Desert. Saul kept searching, but God never let Saul catch him.
translation_verse: Devid kaa sɔh Sif pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ne o deŋɡarere ta. Tɔpere bɛlbwaa Kooro Sɔɔl ɛɛ ɡaaɡe o bɔr, kɛ Korowii ta ɡelɛ o dɔ Devid lawɛ.

english_verse: One time, David was at Horesh in Ziph Desert. He was afraid because Saul had come to the area to kill him.
translation_verse: Waa lɔ bwɛɛ Hɔrɛs waa bɛne Sif pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta la, o noɔ kɛŋɔ Kooro Sɔɔl dɛ́ nyinu dɛ́ kpo.

english_verse: But Jonathan went to see David, and God helped him encourage David.
translation_verse: Asɛ Kooro Sɔɔl bibaa Jonatan la Devid be Hɔrɛs, dɛ ka doo ɡbemba kɛŋɔ Kórowii kpɔ nɔn tɔ o nɛ.

english_verse: “Don't be afraid,” Jonathan said. “My father Saul will never get his hands on you. In fact, you're going to be the next king of Israel, and I'll be your highest official. Even my father knows it's true.”
translation_verse: O ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Dɛɛ berɛ ɔma, n mɛɛ aa hen wobɛlbwa ɛɛ ba. Henee dɛɛ ba Israel kora dii, ásɛ he toole naa, menee dɛ́ teŋɛ. Hale n mɛɛ Kooro Sɔɔl ɡbabir jemɔ.”

english_verse: They both promised the Lord that they would always be loyal to each other. Then Jonathan went home, but David stayed at Horesh. David Escapes from Saul
translation_verse: Belaa ba nɛra banɛ la fɔwɛ fɔo Korowii sie, Jonatan berɛ kaa dem, asɛ Devid te so Hɔrɛs bela.

english_verse: Some people from the town of Ziph went to Saul at Gibeah and said, “Your Majesty, David has a hideout not far from us! It's near Horesh, somewhere on Mount Hachilah south of Jeshimon.
translation_verse: Sif tena la Kooro Sɔɔl be Gebea dɛ ka ŋɔ, “Devid sɔh ya baah nɔ ta, Hɔrɛs deŋɡarere ta Hakila Bwejen waa lɔ Jasimɔn weekaŋle harɛbɔr doa.

english_verse: Saul told them: You've done me a big favor, and I pray that the Lord will bless you.
translation_verse: Kooro Sɔɔl chaŋ ba ŋɔ, “Kórowii swee heyaa andɛɛɡa kɛ haa dɛ dawɛ n waa nɔ.

english_verse: Now please do just a little more for me. Find out exactly where David is, as well as where he goes, and who has seen him there. I've been told that he's very tricky.
translation_verse: Hé berɛ kaa dɛ́ ka nyiŋi a bini kɛrɛdɛ, dɛ́ na bela Devid aa lole, ne naate waa nao bela. Ba dɛ bol ŋɔ o keo taeh.

english_verse: Find out where all his hiding places are and come back when you're sure. Then I'll go with you. If he is still in the area, or anywhere among the clans of Judah, I'll find him.
translation_verse: Hé ka ɡaaɡe bɔra o yon kaa sɔh a ta la, dɛ́ berɛ ba bol kasinteŋ aa lɔ a ta n be. Ásɛ n ne he kaa, dɛ o lɔ bela ɡbosoroo tenaa, mɛɛ ɡaaɡe o bɔree, hale Juda harɛ bwa ta.”

english_verse: The people from Ziph went back ahead of Saul, and they found out that David and his men were still south of Jeshimon in the Maon Desert.
translation_verse: Anomanta, ba tɔ Kooro Sɔɔl sie dɛ kaa Sif. Dɛ Devid ne o laa tena lɔ Mayɔn pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ Jɔɔdan Fɛlembɔjen ta, Jesimɔn weekaŋle harɛbɔr.

english_verse: Saul and his army set out to find David. But David heard that Saul was coming, and he went to a place called The Rock, one of his hideouts in Maon Desert. Saul found out where David was and started closing in on him.
translation_verse: Kooro Sɔɔl ne o laa tena pa mun dɛɛ ɡaaɡe, asɛ Devid no kɛŋɔ ba dɛ ɡaaɡe o bɔr, asɛ o chwa ka so deŋɡare bɛl doa Mayɔn pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta. Kooro Sɔɔl ɡe aa noa kɛ o lɔ bela la, o tiu bela dɛ kaa ɡaaɡe o bɔr.

english_verse: Saul was going around a hill on one side, and David and his men were on the other side, trying to get away. Saul and his soldiers were just about to capture David and his men,
translation_verse: Kooro Sɔɔl ne o laa tena kpɔ bwejen la baŋ bɛl dɛɛ kaa, asɛ Devid ɡe ne o nɛra do o baŋ bɛl dɛ ɛ warane dɛɛ nyin ba le Kooro Sɔɔl ne o laa tena be. O ne o nɛra aa dɛ tel Devid ne o nɛra be dɛ laɡ ba la,

english_verse: when a messenger came to Saul and said, “Come quickly! The Philistines are attacking Israel and taking everything.”
translation_verse: dɛ torome bɛl deno ba Kooro Sɔɔl be dɛ ŋɔ, “N naa kooro, berɛ ɛ warane ba taraken! Filisti tena baa su harɛ la bwa dɛɛ ba o chɔɡa.”

english_verse: Saul stopped going after David and went back to fight the Philistines. That's why the place is called “Escape Rock.”
translation_verse: Ate, Kooro Sɔɔl den ɡel Devid bɔr ɡaaɡa dɛ berɛ kaa dɛ ka yo Filisti tena la. A waa ba pa bela sɔn Sela Hamalekɔt la.

english_verse: David left and went to live in the hideouts at En-Gedi.
translation_verse: Asɛ Devid le bela dɛ kaa Ɛn Gedi harɛ ta, bela waa chwaa ka sɔh la.

english_verse: When Saul got back from fighting off the Philistines, he heard that David was in the desert around En-Gedi.
translation_verse: Kooro Sɔɔl aa kaa ti Filisti tena dɛ berɛ ba la, ba ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Devid lɔ Ɛn Gedi pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta bela.”

english_verse: There were some sheep pens along the side of the road, and one of them was built around the entrance to a cave. Saul went into the cave to relieve himself. David and his men were hiding at the back of the cave.
translation_verse: Kooro Sɔɔl baa tel peera leɡa ane aa lɔ ŋwɛnɛ la nyoa bwebɔɔ bɛl bɔr, asɛ o jo o bini ka kwaa o te. Dɛ Devid ɡe ne o nɛra lɔ bwebɔɔ la jaɡa.

english_verse: They whispered to David, “The Lord told you he was going to let you defeat your enemies and do whatever you want with them. This must be the day the Lord was talking about.” David sneaked over and cut off a small piece of Saul's robe, but Saul didn't notice a thing.
translation_verse: Asɛ Devid nɛra la ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Fini tɔpere nɔ, Korowii dɛ bol he be ŋɔ, ‘Mɛɛ kpɔ he dɔmee do he nɔn ta he ɛo ɡɛ bɛlbwa haa dɛ nyin.’ ” Ate, Devid huuh dɛ sɔh ka mɔn Kooro Sɔɔl batakaare nyoa, dɛ waa jemɛ.

english_verse: Afterwards, David was sorry that he had even done that,
translation_verse: A habɔɔ la, Devid liire chɔɡɔ kɛ waa kaa mɔn Kooro Sɔɔl batakaare nyoa la.

english_verse: and he told his men, “Stop talking foolishly. We're not going to attack Saul. He's my king, and I pray that the Lord will keep me from doing anything to harm his chosen king.” Saul left the cave and started down the road.
translation_verse: Devid cheɡɛ waa nɔ ta dɛ kah o laa tena la, o ta ɡelɛ ba ka yo Kooro Sɔɔl. Ate, Kooro Sɔɔl le bwebɔɔ la bini dɛ kaa.

english_verse: Soon, David also got up and left the cave. “Your Majesty!” he shouted from a distance. Saul turned around to look. David bowed down very low
translation_verse: Belaa Devid ɡe le bwebɔɔ la bini dɛ yerɛ Kooro Sɔɔl ŋɔ, “N naa kooro.” Kooro Sɔɔl aa kea nyiŋu la, Devid ɡure nyu su, dɛ kpɔ sie pi harɛ.

english_verse: and said: Your Majesty, why do you listen to people who say that I'm trying to harm you?
translation_verse: O ŋɔ Kooro Sɔɔl be ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ he cheɡ deŋne dɛɛ no nɛra nyoa wobol kɛŋɔ n dɛ nyin hen waane ɛɛ nɔɔ?

english_verse: You can see for yourself that the Lord gave me the chance to catch you in the cave today. Some of my men wanted to kill you, but I wouldn't let them do it. I told them, “I will not harm the Lord's chosen king!”
translation_verse: He ɡbabir nao fini ɡɛ Korowii aa kpɔe do n nɔn ta bwebɔɔ la bini. Bane ŋɔ ń kpoe, kɛ n ɡele dɛ ŋɔ maa nɛn n dɔɔ Korowii aa fuɡe noo do o nyu ta, dɛ cheɡo kora ta la wechɔɡa bɛlbwaa ɛ ŋwɛnɛ bɛlbwa ta.

english_verse: Your Majesty, look at what I'm holding. You can see that it's a piece of your robe. If I could cut off a piece of your robe, I could have killed you. But I let you live, and that should prove I'm not trying to harm you or to rebel. I haven't done anything to you, and yet you keep trying to ambush and kill me.
translation_verse: N naa, nyiŋi na, he batakaare peraa n kpoŋe la! Menee baa laa mɔn, kɛ n ta hen kpoe. Jemɛ name kɛŋɔ maa he ne wechɔɡa lii, kɛɛ dɛ́ ɛɛ wechɔɡa bɛlbwa. N ta hen wobɛlbwa ɛɛ, kɛ he teŋɛ n nɛɛ dɛɛ nyin mɛ dɛ́ kpo.

english_verse: I'll let the Lord decide which one of us has done right. I pray that the Lord will punish you for what you're doing to me, but I won't do anything to you.
translation_verse: Korowiirii dɛ́ bol n ne he baah waa dɛ́ pa bole. Onee dɛ́ bɔe kem waa haa liira n nɛɛ la wa, kɛ n te maa hen waanee ɛ bwa.

english_verse: An old proverb says, “Only evil people do evil things,” and so I won't harm you.
translation_verse: Saŋ la tena bolɔ ŋɔ, ‘Wechɔɡ-ɛɛra bee dichɔɡa le,’ anomanta, maa n nɔnee kpɔ leɡe.

english_verse: Why should the king of Israel be out chasing me, anyway? I'm as worthless as a dead dog or a flea.
translation_verse: Umee Israel kooro ɛɛ nyin o bɔr dɛ́ kpo nɔɔ? Men maa do kɛ nyoate lale maa wola toole wobɛlbwa bini, kɛɛ koŋɡaahle nɔ naa?

english_verse: I pray that the Lord will help me escape and show that I am in the right.
translation_verse: Korowiirii dɛ́ bol n ne he baah waa dɛ́ na naate waa di bolchɔɡe. Onee dɛ́ nyiŋi waa nɔ ta ásɛ dɛ cha mɛ, dɛ́ lɛɛ mɛ le he nɔn ta.”

english_verse: and said: David, you're a better person than I am. You treated me with kindness, even though I've been cruel to you.
translation_verse: O ŋɔ, “He waa toɡrɔ dɛ ɡwaa mɛ. He te nyiŋi n nɛɛ kɛrɛdɛ, kɛ menee wola hen nyiŋe.”

english_verse: You've told me how you were kind enough not to kill me when the Lord gave you the chance.
translation_verse: Kooro Sɔɔl ŋɔ, “Namee he baɡle wedɛɛɡa haa ɛɛ mɛ bwa, Korowii kpɔ mɛ do he nɔn ta, kɛ he ta men kpoe.

english_verse: If you really were my enemy, you wouldn't have let me leave here alive. I pray that the Lord will give you a big reward for what you did today.
translation_verse: Dɛ nɛn dɔ o dɔm aa, o ɡelo wɛɛ kaa pɛɛpɛɛ aa? Korowiirii dɛ́ chae kohona wedɛɛɡa haa ɛa dɛ ɡel n kpoe nɔ wa.

english_verse: I realize now that you will be the next king, and a powerful king at that.
translation_verse: N jemɔ kɛrɛdɛ kɛŋɔ henee dɛ́ di kora Israel harɛ, dɛ harɛ la ɛɛ cheo kɛrɛdɛ naa, he bee aa ba lee.

english_verse: Promise me with the Lord as your witness, that you won't wipe out my descendants. Let them live to keep my family name alive.
translation_verse: Taraken nɔ, ŋwɛɛ Korowii kɛŋɔ haa n naanaree kpo kɛɛ haa n sɔnee fee le n mɛɛ lolanar bini.”

english_verse: So David promised, and Saul went home. David and his men returned to their hideout.
translation_verse: Anomanta, Devid ŋwɛɛrɔ baɡle Kooro Sɔɔl. Asɛ Kooro Sɔɔl berɛ kaa dem, kɛ Devid ne o laa tena la berɔ kaa bela ba fa aa kaa sɔh la.

english_verse: One day, Nabal was in Carmel where his servants were cutting the wool from his sheep. David was in the desert when he heard about it.
translation_verse: Devid taa lɔ pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta bela la, o noɔ kɛŋɔ Nabal dɛ fonɛ o peera pona bela.

english_verse: So he sent ten men to Carmel with this message for Nabal: I hope that you and your family are healthy and that all is going well for you.
translation_verse: Hé ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, ‘Kórowii tɛɛ mkpajaŋ! Ó tɛ he ne he dem tena ne he komɛlbwa haa dɔa bokpeɡa!

english_verse: I've heard that you are cutting the wool from your sheep. When your shepherds were with us in Carmel, we didn't harm them, and nothing was ever stolen from them.
translation_verse: N noɔ taraken kɛŋɔ peera pona fona saŋee la. He peteɡra fa aa lɔ ya be la, ya ta ban chɔɡre ɛɛ, ba komɛlbwa ɡe ta nyoɡrɛ ɡɛ saŋ baa lɔ Kaamɛl la bwa.

english_verse: Ask your shepherds, and they'll tell you the same thing. My servants are your servants, and you are like a father to me. This is a day for celebrating, so please be kind and share some of your food with us.
translation_verse: Bɔɔ he bonɔɔna la, bá bol waa aa lole. Anomanta, nyiŋi n bonɔɔna kɛrɛdɛ tɔpejen dii saŋ nɔ ta. N dɛ soŋe, tɛ he bonɔɔna ne he bibaa Devid kon te bɛlbwa haa dɔa.’ ”

english_verse: David's men went to Nabal and gave him David's message, then they waited for Nabal's answer.
translation_verse: Devid toroma la laŋɔ dɛ ka bol waa la Nabal be Devid sɔn ta. Asɛ ba so tama.

english_verse: This is what he said: Who does this David think he is? That son of Jesse is just one more slave on the run from his master, and there are too many of them these days.
translation_verse: Belaa Nabal chaŋ ba ŋɔ, “Umee a ɡɛ Devid nɔɔ, Jese bie ɛ? O ɛ bonɔɔna baa chwaa dɛɛ le ba nomonome be tɔpera anɛ nɔ bini bɛl kɛɛ?

english_verse: What makes you think I would take my bread, my water, and the meat that I've had cooked for my own servants and give it to you? Besides, I'm not sure that David sent you!
translation_verse: Ɛrɛɛ chɛ kɛ ń kpɔ n paanoo ne n ne, dɛ ola maa kpoora tɛ nɛra baa dɛ fonɛ n peera tɛ nɛra maa wola ba leebɔr jemɔɔ?”

english_verse: The men returned to their camp and told David everything Nabal had said.
translation_verse: Ate, Devid bonɔɔna la berɛ ba o be, dɛ ba bol wobɛlbwa Nabal aa bola la.

english_verse: He's a bully who won't listen to anyone. Isn't there something you can do? Please think of something! Or else our master and his family and everyone who works for him are all doomed.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ɡɛ waa nɔ liire, dɛ́ na ɡɛ haa dɛ ba wona ɛ, dɛkalkɛŋɔ wenaale dɛ ba n nomoa Nabal ne o dem tena bwa nɛ. O bambile kpeɡri kɛŋɔ nɛn bol waa ó no a mun.”

english_verse: and told her servants, “Take this on ahead, and I'll catch up with you.” She didn't tell her husband Nabal what she was doing.
translation_verse: Ate, o ŋɔ o bonɔɔna la be ŋɔ, “Hé tɔ sie, n ɡe teŋɔ dɛɛ ba.” Kɛ o ta o jaa Nabal be bolɛ a wa.

english_verse: Abigail was riding her donkey on the path that led around the hillside, when suddenly she met David and his men heading straight at her.
translation_verse: Abiɡel soɡe keeɡo ta dɛɛ teeh deŋɡare bɛl dɛ den cheme Devid ne o laa tena ba tu dɛɛ ba o be.

english_verse: David had just been saying, “I surely wasted my time guarding Nabal's things in the desert and keeping them from being stolen! I was good to him, and now he pays me back with insults.
translation_verse: Dɛ Devid fa liiro ŋɔ, “Bɔkwa waa bala n nyiŋi a ɡɛ nɛn nɔ kwaa ta tɛo pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta bela kwaraa te nɔ? N ta o komɛlbwa ŋwɛɛ ɡe. N kembɔree chɛɡa nɔ naa?

english_verse: Abigail quickly got off her donkey and bowed down in front of David.
translation_verse: Abiɡel aa na Devid la, o ɛ warane dɛ tu o keeɡo ta, dɛ ka ɡuŋu dɛ kpɔ sie pi harɛ,

english_verse: Don't pay any attention to that good-for-nothing Nabal. His name means “fool,” and it really fits him! I didn't see the men you sent,
translation_verse: N dɔɔ, laa sie kpɔ nyubinikpeɡ te Nabal nɔ nɛ. O deno do kɛŋɔ o sɔn aa doa baa yerɔ ɡɛne nɔ. Kɛ men maa ɛ he tolo te, n ta bonɔɔna haa tom ba la nae.

english_verse: Please forgive me if I say a little more. The Lord will always protect you and your family, because you fight for him. I pray that you won't ever do anything evil as long as you live.
translation_verse: N poori, kpɔ he tolo wechɔɡa kɛo. Korowii ɛɛ ɡeloo n dɔɔ kora che saŋ bɛlbwa dɛɛ la, dɛkalkɛ Korowii laalee hɛɛ yo. Bɛ ɡel wechɔɡa bɛlbwa do he waa bini he soɡa bini bwa.

english_verse: The Lord your God will keep you safe when your enemies try to kill you. But he will snatch away their lives quicker than you can throw a rock from a sling.
translation_verse: Hale dɛ nomɛl dɛ nyini dɛ́ kpo kwara naa, Korowii haa dɛ tomɔ la ɛɛ kpɔ nɔnee tɔ he nɛ, kɛŋɔ nomɛl aa dɛ nyiŋi kondɛɛɡe bɛl o waa hiah la ken. Kɛ he dɔma te, wɛɛ viɡ baa kɛŋɔ vamtor bwea ken.

english_verse: The Lord has promised to do many good things for you, even to make you the ruler of Israel. The Lord will keep his promises to you,
translation_verse: Dɛ Korowii ɛ wedɛɛɡe bɛlbwa waa baɡɛ nyoa la dɛ cheɡe kora ta Israel harɛ ta naa,

english_verse: and now your conscience will be clear, because you won't be guilty of taking revenge and killing innocent people. When the Lord does all those good things for you, please remember me.
translation_verse: he liire ɛɛ ba harɛɛ, ásɛ o baa swee andɛɛɡa tɛɛ naa, haa nɛra baa wola wobɛlbwa ɛɛ kpoo bɔ kem, dɛ́ di a bolchɔɡe kpa. N dɔɔ, n dɛ soŋe bɛ n waa soh.”

english_verse: David told her: I praise the Lord God of Israel! He must have sent you to meet me today.
translation_verse: Devid ŋɔ Abiɡel be ŋɔ, “Korowii Israel tena aa dɛ tomɔ la chɛ jam, kɛŋɔ waa tomɛ fini he ba chem mɛ nɔ.

english_verse: And you should also be praised. Your good sense kept me from taking revenge and killing innocent people.
translation_verse: Korowii jam, he liidɛɛɡa ne waa haa ɛa tɛ mɛ fini dɛ lɛɛ mɛ le nɛŋkpoa ta, n fee ka kpoo nɛra baa wola waane ɛɛ nɔ.

english_verse: If you hadn't come to meet me so quickly, every man and boy in Nabal's family and in his servants' families would have been killed by morning. I swear by the living Lord God of Israel who protected you that this is the truth.
translation_verse: Korowii Israel tena aa dɛ tomɔ laanee ɡela n ta hen wobɛlbwa ɛɛ la. Kɛ n ŋwɛɛrɔ kɛŋɔ dɛ he fe ta warane ɛɛ dɛ ba chem mɛ naa, tɔɔ ne pera Nabal dem baa te bɛlbwa fe aa ka.”

english_verse: David accepted the food Abigail had brought. “Don't worry,” he said. “You can go home now. I'll do what you asked.”
translation_verse: Belaa Devid sɛh, dɛ lɛ kwaa waa kpɔa ba tɛo la dɛ ŋɔ, “Berɛ kaa dem deŋnesɔɔhna ne, mɛɛ ɛ waa haa dɛ nyin laanee tɛɛ.”

english_verse: Abigail went back home and found Nabal throwing a party fit for a king. He was very drunk and feeling good, so she didn't tell him anything that night.
translation_verse: Abiɡel aa la Nabal be la, dɛ o lɔ o dem dɛɛ di kondikonjena dɛɛ lɛ o sie kɛŋɔ kooro ken. Dɛ o dɛɛrɔ o sie lɛ kɛrɛdɛ. Anomanta, o ta wobɛlbwa o be bolɛ ka tel kɛ tɔ aa pera chɔɔ.

english_verse: But when he sobered up the next morning, Abigail told him everything that had happened. Nabal had a heart attack, and he lay in bed as still as a stone.
translation_verse: Tɔ aa pera chɔɔ sen la le o sie la, o haah la bol waa aa chiɡa la bwa o be. O bambile teŋo kohona, asɛ o beŋri chɔ.

english_verse: Ten days later, the Lord took his life.
translation_verse: Dɛ ɛ tɔpera fi habɔɔ la, Korowii ɡelɔ Nabal sewɛ.

english_verse: She bowed down and said, “I would willingly be David's slave and wash his servants' feet.”
translation_verse: Ate, o ɡuŋi dɛ kpɔ sie pi harɛ dɛ ŋɔ, “O toloo men, mɛɛ tomɔɔ dɛɛ sarame o bonɔɔna nakpale.”

english_verse: Abigail quickly got ready and went back with David's messengers. She rode on her donkey, while five of her servant women walked alongside. She and David were married as soon as she arrived.
translation_verse: Abiɡel den ɛ warane ka so o keeɡo ta, asɛ o toli banue teŋɛ, bane Devid bonɔɔna la kaa o ka yalɛ Devid.

english_verse: David had earlier married Ahinoam from the town of Jezreel, so both she and Abigail were now David's wives.
translation_verse: Dɛ Devid tɔ sie mo Ahinoam waa le Jesreel la, ba bwa ɛ o haahna.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Saul had arranged for Michal to marry Palti the son of Laish, who came from the town of Gallim.
translation_verse: Kɛ dɛ Kooro Sɔɔl berɔ kpɔ o bihaah Mikal waa ɛ Devid haah la tɛ Laes bibaa Paltiel waa le Galim la ŋɔ ó moo.

english_verse: Once again, some people from Ziph went to Gibeah to talk with Saul. “David has a hideout on Mount Hachilah near Jeshimon out in the desert,” they told him.
translation_verse: Baala bane le bwɛjen Sif ta, dɛ la Kooro Sɔɔl be Gebea ka ŋɔ Devid sɔh Hakila Bwejen o sie aa chaɡɛ Juda pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta la nyoa.

english_verse: Saul set up camp on Mount Hachilah, which is across the road from Jeshimon. But David was hiding out in the desert. When David heard that Saul was following him,
translation_verse: Kooro Sɔɔl baŋre o tɛnte dea Hakila Bwejen ŋwɛnɛ nyoa, o sie chaɡɛ Jesimɔn pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ bela Devid aa soɡa la. Waa baa no kɛ Kooro Sɔɔl teŋɛ o nɛɛ dɛɛ nyin o bɔr la,

english_verse: he sent some spies to find out if it was true.
translation_verse: o tomɛ nɛra ba ka sɔh nyiŋi dɛ na kɛŋɔ Kooro Sɔɔl lɔ bela kpela.

english_verse: Then he sneaked up to Saul's camp. He noticed that Saul and his army commander Abner the son of Ner were sleeping in the middle of the camp, with soldiers sleeping all around them.
translation_verse: Ate, Devid kpɔ o te warane, dɛ kaa bela Kooro Sɔɔl ne Nɛr bibaa Abna waa ɛ Kooro Sɔɔl laa tena nomoa aa chɔa. Dɛ Kooro Sɔɔl chɔ tɛnte dea bini bela baa baŋre ba tɛnte deene la baah ta, asɛ laa tena chɔ ane bini, dɛ baro.

english_verse: David asked Ahimelech the Hittite and Joab's brother Abishai, “Which one of you will go with me into Saul's camp?” “I will!” Abishai answered.
translation_verse: Anee Devid bɔɔ Ahemɛlɛk waa ɛ Hiti te, ne Seruya bibaa Abisae waa ɛ Joab dɔɔ la ŋɔ, “He bini umee dɛ́ ja n nɛɛ la Kooro Sɔɔl be bela baa baŋre ba tɛnte deene dɛ so laɔ?” Asɛ Abisae ŋɔ, “N ne hɛɛ lao.”

english_verse: That same night, David and Abishai crept into the camp. Saul was sleeping, and his spear was stuck in the ground not far from his head. Abner and the soldiers were sound asleep all around him.
translation_verse: Anomanta, Devid ne Abisae la Kooro Sɔɔl ne o laa tena be jwaana, dɛ Kooro Sɔɔl chɔ dom bela baa soɡa la baah ta, asɛ lampea pa o nyu bɔr pera. Asɛ Abna ne laa tena la ɡe chɔ baro.

english_verse: Abishai whispered, “This time God has let you get your hands on your enemy! I'll pin him to the ground with one thrust of his own spear.”
translation_verse: Abisae den ŋɔ Devid be ŋɔ, “Korowii kpɔ he dɔm do he nɔn ta fini. Gel n kpɔ o ɡbaɡba lampea nɔ yaɡɔ marɛ harɛ kera beŋkpoŋ ɡbo, kera anɛ kwaraa laa.”

english_verse: “Don't kill him!” David whispered back. “The Lord will punish anyone who kills his chosen king.
translation_verse: Kɛ Devid ŋɔ, “Bɛ on kpo! Nomɛlbwa waa kpo nɛn Korowii aa fuɡe noo do o nyu ta dɛ cheɡo kora ta la ɛɛ di bolchɔɡee.”

english_verse: As surely as the Lord lives, the Lord will kill Saul, or Saul will die a natural death or be killed in battle.
translation_verse: Dɛ berɛ ŋwɛɛ ŋɔ, “Korowii aa lole nɔ, dɛ o seo tɔpere ta tele o sewɛ, kɛɛ o sewɛ laa ta naa, Korowii ɡbabirii dɛ́ kpoo.

english_verse: But I pray that the Lord will keep me from harming his chosen king. Let's grab his spear and his water jar and get out of here!”
translation_verse: Korowii ɛɛ la ane bojaŋ kɛ n kpo nɛn Korowii aa fuɡe noo do o nyu ta dɛ cheɡo kora ta. Gel ya kpɔ o lampea ne loŋ waa dɛ do nee o bini a che o nyu bɔr nɔ kaa.”

english_verse: David took the spear and the water jar, then left the camp. None of Saul's soldiers knew what had happened or even woke up—the Lord had made all of them fall sound asleep.
translation_verse: Anomanta, Devid kpɔ lampea ne loŋ waa dɛ do nee o bini o che o nyu bɔr la, asɛ ba kaa. Nomɛlbwa ta nae, bɛlbwa ɡe ta harɛ. Ba bwa chɔɔ ka ɡarɛ dɛkalkɛ Korowiirii ɡela a ba ɡɛ.

english_verse: David and Abishai crossed the valley and went to the top of the next hill, where they were at a safe distance.
translation_verse: Belaa Devid ɡale kaa fɛlembɔjen la baŋ bɛl dɛ ka chɔŋɛ deŋɡare la ta, o ne ba baah do jaŋne.

english_verse: “Abner!” David shouted toward Saul's army. “Can you hear me?” Abner shouted back. “Who dares disturb the king?”
translation_verse: Asɛ dɛ yerɛ laa tena ne Nɛr bibaa Abna ŋɔ, “Haa men chaŋe aa, Abna?” Ate, Abna chaŋe ŋɔ, “Umee kooro chɔ wɛɛ doo ɡbɔɡa ɡɛ nɔɔ?”

english_verse: “Abner, what kind of a man are you?” David replied. “Aren't you supposed to be the best soldier in Israel? Then why didn't you protect your king? Anyone who went into your camp could have killed him tonight.
translation_verse: Devid chaŋe ŋɔ, “Laa nomonjen laa hen Israel harɛ ta naa? Bɔkwa waa bala he ta kooro waa ɛ he nomoa la daahnɛ ɔ? A ta biɡre bɛlbwa nomɛl ba jo ŋɔ ó fe den ba kpo kooro.

english_verse: You're a complete failure! I swear by the living Lord that you and your men deserve to die for not protecting the Lord's chosen king. Look and see if you can find the king's spear and the water jar that were near his head.”
translation_verse: He ta he toma ɛɛ, Abna. N ŋwɛɛ Korowii waa lole saŋ bɛlbwa kɛŋɔ, a chɛ kɛ he bwa sewɛ, dɛkalkɛŋɔ he ta he dɔɔ Korowii aa cheɡo kora ta daahnɛ. Leperaa kooro lampea ne loŋ waa dɛ do nee o bini a che o nyu bɔr la dɔɔ?”

english_verse: Saul could tell it was David's voice, and he called out, “David, my son! Is that you?” “Yes it is, Your Majesty.
translation_verse: Kooro Sɔɔl jemɛ Devid taa dɛ ŋɔ, “Henee nɔ naa, n bibaa Devid?” Asɛ Devid chaŋe ŋɔ, “Menee, n naa kooro.”

english_verse: Why are you hunting me down? Have I done something wrong, or have I committed a crime?
translation_verse: Dɛ berɛ ŋɔ, “N dɔɔ, ɛrɛɛ n ɛɛ hɛɛ ti men maa ɛ he bonɔɔ ken te nɔ? Bɔkwa waa n ɛɔ? N ɛ wechɔɡa ane kɛɛ?

english_verse: Please listen to what I have to say. If the Lord has turned you against me, maybe a sacrifice will make him change his mind. But if some people have turned you against me, I hope the Lord will punish them! They have forced me to leave the land that belongs to the Lord and have told me to worship foreign gods.
translation_verse: N naa kooro, no men maa ɛ he bonɔɔ waa maa dɛ bol. Dɛ Korowiirii ɡela he fome siwi pa n nɛ aa, mɛɛ kpɔ saraha kwaa tɛo. Kɛ dɛ nɛwɛnyinii dɛɛ ɛ aa, Korowii nyotaahna laɡ ba. Dɛkalkɛ, ba doŋ mɛ le Korowii be o harɛ ta, n ka do harɛfale baa dɛ tomɛ voɡa ɡbo o ta.

english_verse: Don't let me die in a land far away from the Lord. I'm no more important than a flea! Why should the king of Israel hunt me down as if I were a bird in the mountains?”
translation_verse: Bɛ ɡel ba kpo mɛ harɛfale ta, maa wola Korowii sie do. Ɛrɛɛ chɛ kɛŋɔ Israel kooro le dɛ baa kpaah men maa do kɛŋɔ nyuhɔl kɛɛ jumbie nɔɔ?”

english_verse: “David, you had the chance to kill me today. But you didn't. I was very wrong about you. It was a terrible mistake for me to try to kill you. I've acted like a fool, but I'll never try to harm you again. You're like a son to me, so please come back.”
translation_verse: Anee Kooro Sɔɔl ŋɔ, “N bie Devid, n ɛ wechɔɡa, berɛ ba n be. Maa hen kpo kpa, dɛkalkɛ he dɔɔ mɛ he ta men kpoe jwaana nɔ ne. N ɛ ɡɛnewaa kohona ne waa aa wola were.”

english_verse: “Your Majesty, here's your spear! Let one of your soldiers come and get it.
translation_verse: Asɛ Devid chaŋe ŋɔ, “N naa kooro, he lampea laanee la, ɡel he bonɔɔna nɔ bini bɛl ba, dɛ́ ba lɛ.

english_verse: The Lord put you in my power today, but you are his chosen king and I wouldn't harm you. The Lord rewards people who are faithful and live right.
translation_verse: Nɛra baa dɛ di kasinteŋ Korowii waa ta ba waa toɡre la, Korowii dɛ bɔ ba kem. O kpɔe do n nɔn ta fini, kɛ waa lee cheɡ kora ta nomanta, n ta hen kpoe.

english_verse: I spared your life today, and I pray that the Lord will spare my life and keep me safe.”
translation_verse: Gɛ maa sune he nɛɛ n ta hen kpoe fini nɔ, Korowii cha mɛ ɡɛ tenten, dɛ́ lɛɛ mɛ le n wenaale bwa ta.”

english_verse: “David, my son, I pray that the Lord will bless you and make you successful!” David in Philistia Saul went back home. David also left,
translation_verse: Ate, Kooro Sɔɔl ŋɔ Devid be ŋɔ, “N bie, Korowii swee andɛɛɡa tɛɛ, ásɛ wobɛlbwa haa ɛ la, á chiɡi kɛrɛdɛ.” Asɛ Devid chiɡ ŋwɛnɛ ta kaa, Kooro Sɔɔl ɡe berɛ kaa o dem.

english_verse: but he thought to himself, “One of these days, Saul is going to kill me. The only way to escape from him is to go to Philistia. Then I'll be outside of Israel, and Saul will give up trying to catch me.”
translation_verse: Devid baa lii o nyu bini ŋɔ, “Tɔpebɛl Kooro Sɔɔl ɛɛ ba kpo mɛɛ. Chwae chɛ kɛ ń chwa kaa Filisti tena harɛ ta ka so. Anee dɛ́ ɡel ó ɡel n bɔr ɡaaɡa Israel harɛ ta bobɛlbwa, dɛ bɛ men dɔ lawɛ.”

english_verse: When Saul found out that David had run off to Gath, he stopped trying to catch him.
translation_verse: Baa bol Kooro Sɔɔl be kɛ Devid chwao ka so Gat la, o ta o bɔr ɡaaɡɛ kpa.

english_verse: One day, David was talking with Achish and said, “If you are happy with me, then let me live in one of the towns in the countryside. I'm not important enough to live here with you in the royal city.”
translation_verse: Devid ŋɔ Kooro Akis be ŋɔ, “Dɛ he sie lɛ n nɛ aa, ɡel ba tɛ mɛ he bwɛjeɡre nɔ bɛl ń ka so o ta. He ne he bonɔɔ aa won pɛ so bwɛjen beŋkpoŋ ta ɡɛ.”

english_verse: Achish gave David the town of Ziklag that same day, and Ziklag has belonged to the kings of Judah ever since.
translation_verse: Anomanta, awola tɔpere la, Kooro Akis kpɔ bwɛɛ Siklaɡ tɛo o ka so bela. Le ɡɛ saŋ dɛ kaa la, Siklaɡ ɛ Juda koranar bwɛɛre la bɛl.

english_verse: David was in Philistia for a year and four months.
translation_verse: Devid soɡe Filisti harɛ ta benanyoa beŋkpoŋ ne korobie anaarɛ.

english_verse: The Geshurites, the Girzites, and the Amalekites lived in the area from Telam to Shur and on as far as Egypt, and David often attacked their towns.
translation_verse: Devid ta aa soɡe Siklaɡ la, o ne o laa tena la kaa lɔ tɔ Gesur ne Girsi dɛ Amalɛk tena nɛ. Saŋ la dɛ a ɡɛ nɛra nɔ soɡe Suur harɛ dɛ kpoŋe ka le Ijipt harɛ ta.

english_verse: Whenever David and his men attacked a town, they took the sheep, cattle, donkeys, camels, and the clothing, and killed everyone who lived there. After he returned from a raid, David always went to see Achish,
translation_verse: Saŋ bɛlbwa Devid aa ka yo bobɛl tena la, waa baa kɛɛ haah bɛlbwa ɡel. O dɛ kpɔ peera ne nae ne keeɡore ne nyoɡmare dɛ yale bwa kaa. A habɔɔ la, o yon berɛ ba Kooro Akis be.

english_verse: who would ask, “Where did you attack today?” David would answer, “Oh, we attacked some desert town that belonged to the Judah tribe.” Sometimes David would say, “Oh, we attacked a town in the desert where the Jerahmeel clan lives” or “We attacked a town in the desert where the Kenites live.”
translation_verse: Kooro Akis bɔɔro ŋɔ, “Leperaa he ka yo dɛ pa laala fini naa,” ɡɛɛ Devid yon ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “N kaa yo Juda weekaŋle harɛbɔr tena” kɛɛ “Jeramiil dea harɛ tena,” kɛɛ “Ken harɛ tena.”

english_verse: That's why David killed everyone in the towns he attacked. He thought, “If I let any of them live, they might come to Gath and tell what I've really been doing.” David made these raids all the time he was in Philistia.
translation_verse: O ta baa kɛɛ haah bɛlbwa ɡelɛ o ka Gat. O liiro ŋɔ, “Baa ka bol waa n ne n laa tena aa ɛa laanee.” Devid aa soɡe Filisti tena harɛ ta la, dɛ waa waa dɛ ɛ laanee la.

english_verse: But Achish trusted David and thought, “David's people must be furious with him. From now on he will have to take orders from me.”
translation_verse: Kooro Akis yarada Devid, asɛ dɛ lii o nyu bini ŋɔ, “O nɛra Israel tena haoh kohona nomanta, wɛɛ so n bee dɛ́ tom mɛ dɛɛ la.”

english_verse: The Philistines went to Shunem and set up camp. Saul called the army of Israel together, and they set up their camp in Gilboa.
translation_verse: Filisti laa tena chemo dɛ ba baŋre ba tɛnte deene bwɛɛ Sunem, asɛ Kooro Sɔɔl ɡe boa Israel laa tena bwa nyoa ba baŋre ba tɛnte deene Gelboa Bwejen ta.

english_verse: Saul took one look at the Philistine army and started shaking with fear.
translation_verse: Kooro Sɔɔl aa na Filisti laa tena la, o ɔmɔ kohona.

english_verse: So he asked the Lord what to do. But the Lord would not answer, either in a dream or by a priest or a prophet.
translation_verse: O bɔɔrɔ le Korowii be dɛ na ɡɛ o fe aa ɛ, kɛ Korowii ta on chaŋɛ deera ta kɛɛ Urim ne Tumim waa ɛ komɛl baa cheɡɛ o ta dɛɛ jemɛ waa aa wera Korowii be, kɛɛ Korowii keamere be.

english_verse: Then Saul told his officers, “Find me a woman who can talk to the spirits of the dead. I'll go to her and find out what's going to happen.” His servants told him, “There's a woman at Endor who can talk to spirits of the dead.”
translation_verse: Kooro Sɔɔl ŋɔ o laa nomonome be ŋɔ, “Hé nyin haah waa voɡa dɛɛ yerɛ lala tɛ mɛ, ásɛ n la ka bɔɔ le o be.” Anee ba ŋɔ, “Bɛl lɔ bwɛɛ Ɛndɔr.”

english_verse: That night, Saul put on different clothing so nobody would recognize him. Then he and two of his men went to the woman, and asked, “Will you bring up the ghost of someone for us?”
translation_verse: Anomanta, Kooro Sɔɔl kpɔ laalafala do, ásɛ nomɛlbwa bɛ on jemɛ, asɛ dɛ kpɔ nɛra banɛ ja o nɛ, ba la haah la be jwaana la ne. Asɛ o ŋɔ haah la be ŋɔ, “Yerɛ lale maa yerɛ o sɔn tɛɛ nɔ tɛ mɛ.”

english_verse: The woman said, “Why are you trying to trick me and get me killed? You know King Saul has killed everyone who talks to the spirits of the dead!”
translation_verse: Asɛ haah la ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Kasinteŋ, he jemɛ waa Kooro Sɔɔl aa ɛa dɛ doŋi voɡra ne nɛra baa dɛ yerɛ lala le Israel harɛ nɔ ta. Ɛrɛɛ hɛɛ neɡ mɛ dɛ́ dɔɔ mɛ kpo nɔɔ?”

english_verse: Saul replied, “I swear by the living Lord that nothing will happen to you because of this.”
translation_verse: Ate, Kooro Sɔɔl ŋwɛɛ ŋɔ, “N ŋwɛɛ Korowii waa lole kɛŋɔ, haa deŋnetɛra bɛlbwa dɔe ba dɛ́ le ɡɛ waa nɔ ta.”

english_verse: “Who do you want me to bring up?” she asked. “Bring up the ghost of Samuel,” he answered.
translation_verse: Haah la bɔɔro ŋɔ, “Ume lalee hɛɛ nyin ń yerɛ tɛɛ nɔ?” Kooro Sɔɔl chaŋe ŋɔ, “Yerɛ Samoɛl lale tɛ mɛ.”

english_verse: When the woman saw Samuel, she screamed. Then she turned to Saul and said, “You've tricked me! You're the king!”
translation_verse: Haah la aa na Samoɛl la, o do lɔŋɔ kohona dɛ ŋɔ Sɔɔl be ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ he neɡ mɛ nɔɔ? Henee Sɔɔl.”

english_verse: “Don't be afraid,” Saul replied. “Just tell me what you see.” She answered, “I see a spirit rising up out of the ground.”
translation_verse: Anee Kooro Sɔɔl ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Bɔkwaa hɛɛ na nɔ, bɛ ɔmɛ?” Anee haah la ŋɔ, “N dɛ na komɛl waa do kɛŋɔ lale dɛ le lalabwɛɛ dɛɛ ba.”

english_verse: “What does it look like?” “It looks like an old man wearing a robe.” Saul knew it was Samuel, so he bowed down low.
translation_verse: Kooro Sɔɔl bɔɔro ŋɔ, “Bɔkwaa wɛɛ leɔ?” Haah la chaŋe ŋɔ, “O do kɛŋɔ banjena bɛl waa do batakaarejaŋ dɛɛ ba.” Ate, Kooro Sɔɔl jemɛ kɛŋɔ Samoɛlee, asɛ o kpɔ sie pi harɛ dɛ duuru.

english_verse: “Why are you bothering me by bringing me up like this?” Samuel asked. “I'm terribly worried,” Saul answered. “The Philistines are about to attack me. God has turned his back on me and won't answer any more by prophets or by dreams. What should I do?”
translation_verse: Samoɛl ŋɔ Kooro Sɔɔl be ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ he ta ɡelɛ n chɔ jeih asɛ he yer mɛ le baŋ nɔɔ?” Anee Kooro Sɔɔl ŋɔ, “N bambile chɔɡɔ kohona. Filisti tena dɛ yoo mɛ, asɛ Korowii berɛ habɔɔ kpo mɛ. Waa Korowii keamere kɛɛ deera ta cheɡɛ dɛɛ chaŋ mɛ kpa. A waa mɛɛ yerɛ he baɡ mɛ ɡɛ maa ɛ.”

english_verse: Samuel said: If the Lord has turned away from you and is now your enemy, don't ask me what to do.
translation_verse: Anee Samoɛl ŋɔ, “Dɛ Korowii berɛ habɔɔ kpoe dɛ ɛ he dɔm aa, ɛrɛɛ hɛɛ yer mɛ ŋɔ n ɛɔ?

english_verse: I've already told you: The Lord has sworn to take the kingdom from you and give it to David. And that's just what he's doing!
translation_verse: Korowii cheɡɛ n nɛɛ dɛ ɛ waa waa ŋɔa wɛɛ ɛɔ la. O lɛ harɛ la kpeɡri he be dɛ kpɔ tɛ he dɔŋ Devid.

english_verse: When the Lord was angry with the Amalekites, he told you to destroy them, but you didn't do it. That's why the Lord is doing this to you.
translation_verse: Haa wola waa Korowii aa doe a ta teŋɛ, he ta Amalɛk tena yoi dɛ kpoo ba kɛrɛdɛ la, a waa Korowii kpɔ waa nɔ ba ta he nɛɛ taraken la.

english_verse: Tomorrow the Lord will let the Philistines defeat Israel's army, then you and your sons will join me down here in the world of the dead.
translation_verse: Korowii ɛɛ kpɔ he ne Israel tena bwaa do Filisti tena nɔn ta, ásɛ kere he ne he bibaala bwa sewɛ ba n be. Korowii ɛɛ berɔɔ kpɔ Israel laa tena bwa ɡe do Filisti tena nɔn ta.”

english_verse: At once, Saul collapsed and lay stretched out on the floor, terrified at what Samuel had said. He was weak because he had not eaten anything since the day before.
translation_verse: Buɡ la ta, Kooro Sɔɔl den chole dɛ toɡre chɔ, ɔmee lawɔ kohona waa Samoɛl aa bola la wa. Dɛ o ɡwɛɡrɔ dɛkalkɛŋɔ o ta kondikwaa dii chɔɔ ne awola jwaana la bwa.

english_verse: The woman came over to Saul, and when she saw that he was completely terrified, she said, “Your Majesty, I listened to you and risked my life to do what you asked.
translation_verse: Haah la aa ba Kooro Sɔɔl be dɛ na o chɔ dɛɛ chel kohona la, o ŋɔ, “N naa, he toloo men, dɛ seo kwaraa yaa, n sɛoh dɛ ɛ wobɛlbwa haa ŋɔa n ɛ la.

english_verse: Now please listen to me. Let me get you a little something to eat. It will give you strength for your walk back to camp.”
translation_verse: Taraken, no he tolo wa ásɛ n tɛɛ kondikwa he di, dɛ́ dɔ bokpeɡfala dɛ́ won kaa bela haa dɛ kaa.”

english_verse: “No, I won't eat!” But his officers and the woman kept on urging Saul, until he finally agreed. He got up off the floor and sat on the bed.
translation_verse: O vɛoh dɛ ŋɔ, “Máa di.” Kɛ o nomonome banɛ la ja haah la nɛ ba soŋo o no ba waa la. Ate, o ir harɛ dɛ so karajaŋ ta.

english_verse: At once the woman killed a calf that she had been fattening up. She cooked part of the meat and baked some thin bread.
translation_verse: Dɛ haah la dɔ nabale bɛl waa do noo dem bela, asɛ o den kpoo buɡ la ta. O kpɔ men aa kpera kɛrɛdɛ dɛ kpɔ ɛ paanoo iisi aa wola toole a ta.

english_verse: Then she served the food to Saul and his officers, who ate and left before daylight.
translation_verse: Asɛ dɛ kpɔ cheɡ Kooro Sɔɔl ne o nomonome la sie ba di. Awola jwaana la tentenee ba ir dɛ kaa.

english_verse: The Philistine army commanders were angry and shouted: Send David back to the town you gave him. We won't have him going into the battle with us. He could turn and fight against us! Saul would take David back as an officer if David brought him the heads of our soldiers.
translation_verse: Kɛ Filisti tena laa nomonome la baah di Kooro Akis nɛ dɛ ŋɔ, “Gel o berɛ kaa ka so bwɛɛ haa kpɔa tɛo la ta. A ta chɛ kɛŋɔ yá ne o pɛ la laa, ɡɛ laa aa, o ken ɛɛ berɛ siee chaɡɛ ya nɛɛ dɛ́ kpoo yaa. Dɛ Devid wono kpoo ya laa tena dɛ dɔ ba nyuune ka tɛ Kooro Sɔɔl aa, o sie ɛɛ lɛ o nɛɛ ó berɛ lɛo.”

english_verse: The Israelites even dance and sing, “Saul has killed a thousand enemies; David has killed ten thousand!”
translation_verse: Devid nɔ laa haahna kpɔ ɡo yela dɛɛ sa ŋɔ, “Kooro Sɔɔl kpoo nɛra kaɡboŋa, asɛ Devid ɡe kpoo kaɡboŋa fi la aa?”

english_verse: Achish called David over and said: I swear by the living Lord that you've been honest with me, and I want you to fight by my side. I don't think you've done anything wrong from the day you joined me until this very moment. But the other Philistine rulers don't want you to come along.
translation_verse: Belaa Kooro Akis yerɛ Devid dɛ ŋɔ, “N ŋwɛɛ Korowii Israel tena aa dɛ tomɔ o do le saŋ bɛlbwa kɛŋɔ, he waa dɔ kasinteŋ tɛ mɛ. N sie fe ɛɛ lɛo kɛ he ja n nɛɛ dɛ́ ka yo laa nɔ. Dɛ le awola haa ba n be ba le fini, n ta he wechɔɡe bɛlbwa nae, kɛ koranar la bane sie ta he nɛɛ lɛɛ.

english_verse: Go on back home and try not to upset them.
translation_verse: Berɛ kaa deŋnesɔɔhna ne, bɛ wobɛlbwa ɛ ásɛ dɛ jo Filisti koranar la nɛ.”

english_verse: “But what have I done?” David asked. “Do you know of anything I've ever done that would keep me from fighting the enemies of my king?”
translation_verse: Anee Devid chaŋe ŋɔ, “N dɔɔ, ɛrɛɛ n ɛɔ? Wechɔɡ besoo he na men maa ɛ he bonɔɔ nɛɛ dɛ le tɔpere maa ba he be dɛ ba le fini nɔɔ? Ɛrɛɛ maa wola won ka yo n dɔɔ kooro dɔma ɔ?”

english_verse: Achish said: I believe that you're as good as an angel of God, but our army commanders have decided that you can't fight in this battle.
translation_verse: Kooro Akis ŋɔ, “N jemɔ kɛ he waa wer, wechɔɡa bɛlbwa toole he nɛɛ kɛ nyundua torome ken. Kɛ ane a bwa, koranar la bane ŋɔ haa won ja ya nɛɛ dɛ́ la laa.

english_verse: You and your troops will have to go back to the town I gave you. Get up and leave tomorrow morning as soon as it's light. I'm pleased with you, so don't let any of this bother you.
translation_verse: Anomanta, fel ir kere chɔɔ, he ne banɔ la haa le Kooro Sɔɔl be dɛ ba la bwa, ásɛ he le kaa bɔr chaahna saŋ.”

english_verse: David and his men got up early in the morning and headed back toward Philistia, while the Philistines left for Jezreel.
translation_verse: Asɛ Devid ne o baala baa ja o nɛɛ la fel ir chɔmbibii dɛ berɛ kaa Filisti tena harɛ ta, asɛ Filisti tena la ɡe kaa Jesreel.

english_verse: It took David and his men three days to reach Ziklag. But while they had been away, the Amalekites had been raiding in the desert around there. They had attacked Ziklag, burned it to the ground,
translation_verse: Tɔpetooro wee la, Devid ne o laa tena valɔ dɛ berɛ ba bwɛjen Siklaɡ. Dɛ Amalɛk tena baa yo Juda weekaŋle harɛbɔr bwɛɛre, dɛ ba pa ba laala dɛ fuh Siklaɡ,

english_verse: When David and his men came to Ziklag, they saw the burned-out ruins and learned that their families had been taken captive.
translation_verse: Devid ne o laa tena aa tel Siklaɡ la, ba nao kɛŋɔ Amalɛk tenaa fuh bwɛɛ la, dɛ lawɛ ba haahna ne bii bwa kaa.

english_verse: They started crying and kept it up until they were too weak to cry any more.
translation_verse: Devid ne o laa tena la wio kohona ka tel kɛŋɔ baa koah baa wola won wi kpa.

english_verse: David's two wives, Ahinoam and Abigail, had been taken captive with everyone else.
translation_verse: Ba lawɛ Devid haahna banɛ, Ahinoam waa le Jesreel, ne Abiɡel waa ɛ Nabal luhaah dɛ le Kaamɛl la kaa.

english_verse: David was desperate. His soldiers were so upset over what had happened to their sons and daughters that they were thinking about stoning David to death. But he felt the Lord God giving him strength,
translation_verse: Devid bambile chɔɡɔ kɛrɛdɛ, dɛkalkɛ dɛ a dɛ we o laa tena la nɛɛ kɛŋɔ baa lawɛ ba bii kaa la, asɛ dɛɛ nyin ba foɡre Devid bwea kpo. Kɛ Korowii waa dɛ tomɔ la doo ɡbemba.

english_verse: and he said to the priest, “Abiathar, let's ask God what to do.” Abiathar brought everything he needed to get answers from God, and he went over to David.
translation_verse: Ate, Devid ŋɔ Ahemɛlɛk bibaa Abiata waa ɛ sɔfo la be ŋɔ, “Kpɔ sɔfore batakaarebora efɔd la ba tɛ mɛ, ásɛ n bɔɔ le Korowii be.” Asɛ o kpɔ ba tɛo.

english_verse: Then David asked the Lord, “Should I go after the people who raided our town? Can I catch up with them?” “Go after them,” the Lord answered. “You will catch up with them, and you will rescue your families.”
translation_verse: Asɛ Devid bɔɔ le Korowii be ŋɔ, “Ń ti laa tena la kɛɛ? Mɛɛ puu baa yaa?” Korowii chaŋe ŋɔ, “Ti ba, hɛɛ ka puu baa dɛ́ lɛ nɛra baa laɡ ba dɛɛ kaa la ta.”

english_verse: Some of David's men found an Egyptian out in a field and took him to David. They gave the Egyptian some bread, and he ate it. Then they gave him a drink of water,
translation_verse: Ba na Ijipt te bɛl kpɔɡ bini bela dɛ lawɔ ba tɛ Devid. Ba tɛo nee ne kondikwaa o di,

english_verse: some dried figs, and two handfuls of raisins. This was the first time in three days he had tasted food or water. Now he felt much better.
translation_verse: ne fiɡ nɔna nɔndel tama, dɛ daa nɔna aa hola nɔndela anɛ. Waa dia tonɛ la, o berɔ dɔ bokpeɡa dɛkalkɛ dɛ o ta kondikwaa dii, o ta nee ɡe nyɔe tɔpera atoro la bwa.

english_verse: “Who is your master?” David asked. “And where do you come from?” “I'm from Egypt,” the young man answered. “I'm the servant of an Amalekite, but he left me here three days ago because I was sick.
translation_verse: Devid bɔɔro ŋɔ, “He dɔɔree ume ɔ? Leperaa he leɔ?” O chaŋe ŋɔ, “Ijipt tee men, n ɛ Amalɛk te bɛl yom. Tɔpera atoroo nɔ weela aa lɔ mɛ bil, asɛ n dɔɔ chwa kaa ɡel mɛ.

english_verse: We had attacked some towns in the desert where the Cherethites live, in the area that belongs to Judah, and in the desert where the Caleb clan lives. And we burned down Ziklag.”
translation_verse: Ya kaa yo Nɛɡɛv pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ bela nɛra bane baa dɛ yer ba Kɛrɛt tena baa lɔ Juda harɛ ta, dɛ pa ba laala, ne Kaleb dea lolanar ba ɡe aa soɡe bela, dɛ fuh bwɛjen Siklaɡ ɡe.”

english_verse: “Will you take me to those Amalekites?” David asked. “Yes, I will, if you promise with God as a witness that you won't kill me or hand me over to my master.”
translation_verse: Devid bɔɔ Ijipt te la ŋɔ, “Hɛɛ won tɔ n sie dɛ́ la n ne n laa tena nɔ be naa?” O chaŋe ŋɔ, “Ŋwɛɛ Korowii kɛŋɔ haa men kpo kɛɛ haa men le tɛ n dɔɔ, ásɛ n tɔ he sie la he ne ba be.”

english_verse: David attacked just before sunrise the next day and fought until sunset. Four hundred Amalekites rode away on camels, but they were the only ones who escaped.
translation_verse: Devid yoo ba le chɔmbibii ka tel tɔ aa pera jɔmɔra. Ba bini bɛlbwa ta wone dɔ bɔr chwa, nemenɛ bonɔɔna lafraanaarɛ baa soɡe nyoɡmare taa wona dɔ bɔr chwa kaa.

english_verse: David rescued his two wives and everyone else the Amalekites had taken from Ziklag.
translation_verse: Devid berɔ lɛ kwaa Amalɛk tena aa paa la bwa, dɛ kpɔ o haahna banɛ la bwa ja.

english_verse: No one was missing—young or old, sons or daughters. David brought back everything that had been stolen,
translation_verse: Komɛlbwa ta nyoɡrɛ, bechale kɛɛ nomonome, bibaala ne bihaahna, komɛlbwa baa paa laa ta kaa la, Devid berɔ ba a bwa ne.

english_verse: including their livestock. David also took the sheep and cattle that the Amalekites had with them, but he kept these separate from the others. Everyone agreed that these would be David's reward.
translation_verse: O lɛ peera ne nae Amalɛk tena aa paa kaa la, asɛ o bonɔɔna la teɡa tɔ ba sie dɛ ŋɔ, “Devid laa ta kwaa waa kaa pa laanee la.”

english_verse: Some of David's men were good-for-nothings, and they said, “Those men didn't go with us to the battle, so they don't get any of the things we took back from the Amalekites. Let them take their wives and children and go!”
translation_verse: Kɛ ba bini nyubinikpeɡ tena ne nɛnchɔɡa bwa baa ja Devid ne o laa tena nɛɛ la ŋɔ, “Baa wola ya nɛɛ jae ya ne ba ka yo nɔ, ya ne baa won bɔne kwaa yaa kaa paa laa ta nɔ. Kɛ bɛlbwa ɛɛ won kpɔ o haah ne bii te kaa.”

english_verse: But David said: My friends, don't be so greedy with what the Lord has given us! The Lord protected us and gave us victory over the people who attacked.
translation_verse: Devid chaŋe ŋɔ, “Akai, he bɛ laala Korowii aa kpɔa tɛ yaa la ɡɛ ɛ! O kpɔ nɔn tɔ ya nɛ dɛ ɡel ya yo, dɛ pɔ ba laa tena la nɛ.

english_verse: Who would pay attention to you, anyway? Soldiers who stay behind to guard the camp get as much as those who go into battle.
translation_verse: Nomɛlbwa toole dɛ́ no he waa nɔ mun. Bɛl la waa soɡa dɛɛ daah laala, ne bɛl la waa la laa bwa chɛ kɛ he bwa bɔna kɛrɛdɛ.”

english_verse: David made this a law for Israel, and it has been the same ever since.
translation_verse: Devid ɛ ɡɛ waa nɔ mmara dɛ tɛ Israel tena, a ta do le ba le fini.

english_verse: David went back to Ziklag with everything they had taken from the Amalekites. He sent some of these things as gifts to his friends who were leaders of Judah, and he told them, “We took these things from the Lord's enemies. Please accept them as a gift.”
translation_verse: Devid aa tel Siklaɡ la, o kpɔ laala la ane ka tɛ Juda nomonome baa ɛ o daamanar la dɛ ŋɔ, “Kwaa maa paa laa ta dɛ le Korowii dɔma be, dɛ kpɔ a bini ane dɛɛ ba ba tɛ heyaa laanee la.”

english_verse: Meanwhile, the Philistines were fighting Israel at Mount Gilboa. Israel's soldiers ran from the Philistines, and many of them were killed.
translation_verse: A kaa ba kɛ Filisti tena ne Israel tena cheme Gelboa Bwejen ta dɛ yo laa. Ba kpoo Israel tena ɡalɡa bela, asɛ ba kar ne Kooro Sɔɔl ne o bibaala chwa.

english_verse: The Philistines closed in on Saul and his sons, and they killed his sons Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua.
translation_verse: Filisti tena la chwao ti Kooro Sɔɔl ne o bibaala batoro, Jonatan ne Abinadab dɛ Malki Sua sibeɡra ne dɛ kpoo o bibaala la.

english_verse: The fighting was fierce around Saul, and he was badly wounded by enemy arrows.
translation_verse: Laa la baa do kpeɡri tɛ Kooro Sɔɔl, asɛ o dɔma la bɛl ta hɛm yaɡɔ dɛ doo bol kohona.

english_verse: Saul told the soldier who carried his weapons, “Kill me with your sword! I don't want these worthless Philistines to torture and make fun of me.” But the soldier was afraid to kill him. Saul then took out his own sword; he stuck the blade into his stomach, and fell on it.
translation_verse: Asɛ Kooro Sɔɔl ŋɔ o bonɔɔ waa dɛ che o dɔmkwaa la be ŋɔ, “Pamɛ he kere la, dɛ́ ba tɔɡ mɛ kpo, ásɛ nɛra baa wola Korowii tomɛ nɔ bɛ men ba kpo dɛ́ chɛɡ mɛ ja.” Kɛ dɛ bonɔɔ la dɛ ɔmɛ kɛ ó ɛ ɡɛ, anomanta, Kooro Sɔɔl pamɛ o ɡbaɡba kere dɛ chole o ta.

english_verse: When the soldier knew that Saul was dead, he killed himself in the same way.
translation_verse: Bonɔɔ la aa naa kɛ Kooro Sɔɔl sewɔ la, o ɡe chole o kon ta dɛ sewɛ ja o nɛ.

english_verse: Saul was dead, his three sons were dead, and the soldier who carried his weapons was dead. They and all his soldiers died on that same day.
translation_verse: Gɛɛ a do Kooro Sɔɔl ne o bibaala batoro ne o bonɔɔ dɛ o laa tena bwa sewɛ awola tenten.

english_verse: The Israelites on the other side of Jezreel Valley and the other side of the Jordan learned that Saul and his sons were dead. They saw that the Israelite army had run away. So they ran away too, and the Philistines moved into the towns the Israelites had left behind.
translation_verse: Israel tena baa lɔ Jesreel Fɛlembɔjen la baŋ bɛl, ne Jɔɔdan Moo wee leebɔr aa noa kɛŋɔ Israel laa tena la chwao, asɛ ba kpo Kooro Sɔɔl ne o bibaala ɡe la, ba chwao ɡel ba bwɛɛre. Asɛ Filisti tena la ba kpɔ dɛ so a ta.

english_verse: The day after the battle, when the Philistines returned to the battlefield to take the weapons of the dead Israelite soldiers, they found Saul and his three sons lying dead on Mount Gilboa.
translation_verse: Tɔ aa pera la, Filisti tena la laŋɔ dɛ ka pa laa tena baa kpoo ba la laala, asɛ dɛ na Kooro Sɔɔl ne o bibaala batoro la kɛ baa serewa chɔ Gelboa Bwejen ta.

english_verse: The people who lived in Jabesh in Gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul's body.
translation_verse: Bwɛjen Jabes waa lɔ Gelead harɛ tena la aa noa ɡɛ Filisti tena aa ɛ Kooro Sɔɔl la,

english_verse: So one night, some brave men from Jabesh went to Beth-Shan. They took down the bodies of Saul and his sons, then brought them back to Jabesh and burned them.
translation_verse: bansua tena baa lɔ bwɛɛ la ta kpɔ ba te, dɛ valɛ jwaana la bwa kaa bwɛjen Bɛt San. Ba laa Kooro Sɔɔl lale kpɔ danjwɛɛ la ta, dɛ kpɔ o bii la ja, dɛ ba ba ne Jabes dɛ ba fuuh ba.

english_verse: They buried the bones under a small tree in Jabesh, and for seven days, they went without eating to show their sorrow.
translation_verse: Ba pa ba hoɡa ka huɡe dajen bɛl waa lɔ Jabes mun, asɛ dɛ vɔwɛ nyoa tɔpera anuanɛ.

english_verse: Three days later, a soldier came from Saul's army. His clothes were torn, and dirt was on his head. He went to David and knelt down in front of him.
translation_verse: Tɔpetooro wee ta la, baa bɛl le bela Kooro Sɔɔl aa baŋre o tɛnte deene dɛ so la ba. Dɛ o kɛɛ o laala bwa, dɛ ɛ teera su o nyu ta a baɡle kɛ o loo kuu. O la Devid be, dɛ ka ba harɛ dɛ kpɔ duure tɛo.

english_verse: David asked, “Where did you come from?” The man answered, “From Israel's army. I barely escaped with my life.”
translation_verse: Anee Devid bɔɔro ŋɔ, “Leperaa he leɔ?” Asɛ o chaŋe ŋɔ, “Chwae n chwa le bela Israel tena aa baŋre ba tɛnte deene dɛ so la.”

english_verse: “Who won the battle?” David asked. The man said, “Our army turned and ran, but many were wounded and died. Even King Saul and his son Jonathan are dead.”
translation_verse: Devid berɛ bɔɔro ŋɔ, “Bɔkwa waa bala ɔ? Gel n jemɛ.” Asɛ o chaŋo ŋɔ, “Kooro Sɔɔl laa tena chwa laa la ta, asɛ ba kpo Filisti tena la ɡalɡa. Kooro Sɔɔl ne o bibaa Jonatan ɡe sewɔ.”

english_verse: David asked, “How do you know Saul and Jonathan are dead?”
translation_verse: Anee Devid bɔɔ bonɔɔ la ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ he ɛ jemɛ kɛŋɔ Kooro Sɔɔl ne o bie Jonatan sewɔ ɔ?”

english_verse: The young man replied: I was on Mount Gilboa and saw King Saul leaning on his spear. The enemy's war chariots and cavalry were closing in on him.
translation_verse: Ate, o chaŋe ŋɔ, “Dɛ n lɔ Gelboa Bwejen doa dɛ na Kooro Sɔɔl kɛŋɔ waa kpoŋe o lampea dɛ kpɔ o te dawɛ o ta, asɛ nɛra baa soɡe kwaa aa do kɛŋɔ torɔɡo ba vɔwɛ pɛl jaɡre, ne nɛra baa soɡe jaɡre ta siwi beɡre dɛɛ bɛno dɛ́ lawɔ.

english_verse: When he turned around and saw me, he called me over. I went and asked what he wanted.
translation_verse: Belaa Kooro Sɔɔl ke nyiŋi dɛ yer mɛ, asɛ n bɔɔro ŋɔ, ‘N naa, bɔkwa waa hɛɛ nyin ń ɛ tɛɛ nɔ?’

english_verse: Saul asked me, “Who are you?” “An Amalekite,” I answered.
translation_verse: O bɔɔ mɛ ŋɔ, ‘Umee hen ɔ?’ Asɛ n chaŋe ŋɔ, ‘Amalɛk tee men.’

english_verse: Then he said, “Kill me! I'm dying, and I'm in terrible pain.”
translation_verse: Belaa o ŋɔ, ‘Ba, dɛ́ ba kpo mɛ. Ba do mɛ bol kohona, mɛɛ ba sewa.’

english_verse: So I killed him. I knew he was too badly wounded to live much longer. Then I took his crown and his arm-band, and I brought them to you, Your Majesty. Here they are.
translation_verse: Anomanta, n laŋɔ dɛ ka kpoo, dɛkalkɛ n jemɔ kɛŋɔ waa dɔa ɡwɛɡre la, o chola bini la, dɛ o ne sewee. Ate, n laa o kooɡbɛrɛ ne o baŋe kpɔ ŋɔ ń kpɔ ba tɛɛ la, n dɔɔ.”

english_verse: At once, David and his soldiers tore their clothes in sorrow.
translation_verse: Belaa Devid ne laa tena baa ja o nɛɛ bwa kɛɛ ba laala a baɡle kɛ ba loo kuu.

english_verse: They cried all day long and would not eat anything. Everyone was sad because Saul, his son Jonathan, and many of the Lord's people had been killed in the battle.
translation_verse: Ba ɛ Kooro Sɔɔl ne Jonatan ne Israel tena baa ɛ Korowii nɛra la lwe dɛ wii ba, dɛ vɔwɛ nyoa ka tel jɔmɔra, dɛkalkɛ nɛra ɡalɡaa sewɛ laa la ta.

english_verse: David asked the young man, “Where is your home?” The man replied, “My father is an Amalekite, but we live in Israel.”
translation_verse: Ate, Devid bɔɔ baa o fa aa baa bol waa o be la ŋɔ, “Leperaa he leɔ?” O chaŋe ŋɔ, “N mɛɛ ɛ Amalɛk te ya so Israel harɛ ta.”

english_verse: David said to him, “Why weren't you afraid to kill the Lord's chosen king? And you even told what you did. It's your own fault that you're going to die!” Then David told one of his soldiers, “Come here and kill this man!” David Sings in Memory of Saul
translation_verse: Dɛ Devid fa bol baa la be ŋɔ, “He waa haa ɛa laanee ɡure he nyu ta la. Waa aa le he nyoa he ŋɔ henee kpo nɛn Korowii aa cheɡo kora ta laanee ɛ danseɛ.” Devid wi Kooro Sɔɔl ne Jonatan

english_verse: David sang a song in memory of Saul and Jonathan,
translation_verse: Devid taa ɡɛ wiile aa teŋa nɔ tɛ Kooro Sɔɔl ne o bibaa Jonatan,

english_verse: and he ordered his men to teach the song to everyone in Judah. He called it “The Song of the Bow,” and it can be found in The Book of Jashar. This is the song:
translation_verse: dɛ ŋɔ bá kpɔ baɡle Juda baala bá hweli. Ba chwera do tɔn bɛl baa dɛ yerɔ Jasar Tɔn bini ŋɔ,

english_verse: Israel, your famous hero lies dead on the hills, and your mighty warriors have fallen!
translation_verse: “Ya nomonome serewɔ Israel deŋɡarere dor. Na ɡɛ banyoola tenten aa serewa chɔ.

english_verse: Don't tell it in Gath or spread the news on the streets of Ashkelon. The godless Philistine women will be happy and jump for joy.
translation_verse: He bɛ an bol bwɛjena Gat tena be, kɛɛ Askɛlɔn fɔɡbaahna. He bɛ ɡel Filisti haahna no ba sie lɛ, á ba ɛ kɛŋɔ nɛra baa wola Korowii tomɛ bihaahna sie ɛɛ lɛo.

english_verse: Don't let dew or rain fall on the hills of Gilboa. Don't let its fields grow offerings for God. There the warriors' shields were smeared with mud, and Saul's own shield was left unpolished.
translation_verse: Mɛn kɛɛ bwaala bɛ Gelboa deŋɡarere ta nɛ, o harɛre bɛ won dɛɛ ɛ kondikwaa ɡe kpa! Banyoola kwaa baa kpɔa tɔ ba te ɡbemɡbe dɛɛ yo chɔ bela, baa noo kpɔe dɛɛ fɔɡɛ Kooro Sɔɔl kon waa kpɔa dɛɛ tɔ o te ɡbemɡbe wɛɛ nyɛɡle kpa.

english_verse: The arrows of Jonathan struck, and warriors died. The sword of Saul cut the enemy apart.
translation_verse: Jonatan ta o hɛma aa, a nyoa wɔrɔbe, Kooro Sɔɔl ɡe kere aa dawɛ dɛɛ kpo banyoola ne o dɔma.

english_verse: It was easy to love Saul and Jonathan. Together in life, together in death, they were faster than eagles and stronger than lions.
translation_verse: Kooro Sɔɔl ne Jonatan waa wer ba soɡa bini dɛ dɔ nyokpoa kohona, ba baah ta pere ba seo bini bwa. Ba ɡbaŋre ɡwaa kee bɛlbwa, dɛ do kpeɡri ɡwaa nyujentena.

english_verse: Women of Israel, cry for Saul. He brought you fine red cloth and jewelry made of gold.
translation_verse: Israel haahna, hé wi Kooro Sɔɔl, a do kɛ waa kpɔ yaswɛm dɛɛɡe tɔ heya, dɛ kpɔ kwaa baa kpɔ suuɡaswɛm ɛa do heya.

english_verse: Our warriors have fallen in the heat of battle, and Jonathan lies dead on the hills of Gilboa.
translation_verse: Na ɡɛ banyoola aa sewɛ laa ta! Jonatan sewɔ chɔ Gelboa bwejen doa.

english_verse: Jonathan, I miss you most! I loved you like a brother. You were truly loyal to me, more faithful than a wife to her husband.
translation_verse: N wio dɛɛ tɛɛ, n nime Jonatan, dɛ n fa dɛ nyin he waa taeh. He nyina he fa aa dɔa tɛ mɛ dɔ nyokpoa, a ɡwaa ɡɛ haah naa dɛ nyin o bii kɛɛ o jaa kwara.

english_verse: Our warriors have fallen, and their weapons are destroyed.
translation_verse: Na ɡɛ banyoola aa serewa, asɛ ba dɔmkwa chɔ pɛɛpɛɛ!”

english_verse: Later, David asked the Lord, “Should I go back to one of the towns of Judah?” The Lord answered, “Yes.” David asked, “Which town should I go to?” “Go to Hebron,” the Lord replied.
translation_verse: A habɔɔ la, Devid bɔɔ Korowii ŋɔ, “N Naa Korowii, mɛɛ won la ka so Juda bwɛɛre nɔ bɛl ta naa?” Anee Korowii chaŋo ŋɔ “Ɔɔh.” Asɛ Devid berɛ bɔɔ ŋɔ, “Bwɛ besoo ta nɔ?” Anee Korowii ŋɔ, “Ka so Hɛbrɔn.”

english_verse: David went to Hebron with his two wives, Ahinoam and Abigail. Ahinoam was from Jezreel, and Abigail was the widow of Nabal from Carmel.
translation_verse: Anomanta, Devid ne o haahna banɛ, Ahinoam waa le Jesreel, ne Abiɡel waa ɛ Nabal luhaah dɛ le Kaamɛl la iro, dɛ kaa Hɛbrɔn.

english_verse: David also told his men and their families to come and live in the villages near Hebron.
translation_verse: O berɔ kpɔ laa tena baa ja o nɛɛ la ne bɛlbwa haah ne o bii, asɛ ba ka so Hɛbrɔn ne bwɛɛre aa baro la ta.

english_verse: The people of Judah met with David at Hebron and poured olive oil on his head to show that he was their new king. Then they told David, “The people from Jabesh in Gilead buried Saul.”
translation_verse: Belaa Juda baala ba Hɛbrɔn bela, dɛ ba fuɡe noo do Devid nyu ta, dɛ cheɡo Juda harɛ ta kooro. Devid aa baa no kɛ Jabes Gelead baalaa huɡe Kooro Sɔɔl la,

english_verse: David sent messengers to tell them: The Lord bless you! You were kind enough to bury Saul your ruler,
translation_verse: o tomɛ toroma Jabes Gelead baala la be ŋɔ, “Korowii swee heyaa andɛɛɡa kɛ haa nyin he dɔɔ Kooro Sɔɔl dɛ huɡo nɔ.

english_verse: and I pray that the Lord will be kind and faithful to you. I will be your friend because of what you have done.
translation_verse: Kórowii sune he nɛ, dɛ́ cha heya. N ɡee sune he nɛɛ, dɛ́ cha heya waa haa ɛa nɔ wa.

english_verse: Saul is dead, but the tribe of Judah has made me their king. So be strong and have courage. Ishbosheth Becomes King of Israel
translation_verse: He bɛ ɔmɛ, hé che kiŋkiŋ, Kooro Sɔɔl waa ɛ he dɔɔ la sewɔ, asɛ Juda dea tena fuɡe noo do n nyu ta, dɛ cheɡ mɛ kora ta.” Ba cheɡ Esbɔsɛt kora Israel harɛ ta

english_verse: Abner the son of Ner had been the general of Saul's army. He took Saul's son Ishbosheth across the Jordan River to Mahanaim
translation_verse: Nɛr bibaa Abna waa ɛ Kooro Sɔɔl laa nomoa la lawɛ Kooro Sɔɔl bibaa baa dɛ yerɔ Esbɔsɛt ɡale Jɔɔdan Moo la, dɛ ba o ne Mahanaim.

english_verse: and made him king of Israel, including the areas of Gilead, Asher, Jezreel, Ephraim, and Benjamin.
translation_verse: Abna cheɡo kora ta wɛɛ nyiŋi Gelead ne Asuri ne Jesreel ne Efrem ne Bɛnjamen dɛ Israel harɛre bwa ta.

english_verse: and he ruled from Hebron for seven and a half years. The War between David and Ishbosheth
translation_verse: Kooro Devid di kora Hɛbrɔn Juda dea harɛ ta bene anuanɛ korobie anumɛl.

english_verse: One day, Abner and the soldiers of Ishbosheth left Mahanaim and went to Gibeon.
translation_verse: Awola bɛl, Nɛr bibaa Abna ne Esbɔsɛt nomonome iro le Mahanaim dɛ ba bwɛjen Gebeɔn ta.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Joab the son of Zeruiah was leading David's soldiers, and the two groups met at the pool in Gibeon. Abner and his men sat down on one side of the pool, while Joab and his men sat on the other side.
translation_verse: Asɛ Joab baa dɛ yerɛ o nya Seruya, ne Kooro Devid nomonome ir le ka chem ba tam bɛl waa chɔ Gebeɔn nyoa. Kooro Devid ne o nɛra soɡe tam la baŋ bɛl, asɛ banɔ la ɡe so o baŋ bɛl.

english_verse: Abner yelled to Joab, “Let's get some of our best soldiers to stand up and fight each other!” Joab agreed,
translation_verse: Belaa Abna ŋɔ Joab be ŋɔ, “Gel ya yerɛ bonɔɔna le baŋ bɛlbwa ta ba, bá yo ya siwi ta.” Ate, Joab chaŋe ŋɔ, “A wer.”

english_verse: and twelve of Ishbosheth's men from the tribe of Benjamin got up to fight twelve of David's men.
translation_verse: Ate, baala fi dɛ banɛ le Esbɔsɛt ne Bɛnjamen dea, ba ne baala fi dɛ banɛ ba ɡe aa le Devid be pera yo.

english_verse: They grabbed each other by the hair and stabbed each other in the side with their daggers. They all died right there! That's why the place in Gibeon is called “Field of Daggers.”
translation_verse: Bɛlbwa hamɛ o dɔŋ nyu kpoŋe, ba kpɔ keri tɔɡɛ dɔŋa baŋ bɛla, asɛ ba nɛra fifraanɛ dɛ banaarɛ la bwa chole dɛ serewe. Anomanta, ba dɛ yerɛ bela Hɛlkat Hasurim o do Gebeɔn harɛ ta.

english_verse: Then everyone started fighting. Both sides fought very hard, but David's soldiers defeated Abner and the soldiers of Israel.
translation_verse: Belaa laa chole sibeɡra ne awola, asɛ Kooro Devid baala la pɔ Abna ne Israel tena la nɛ.

english_verse: Zeruiah's three sons were there: Joab, Abishai, and Asahel. Asahel could run as fast as a deer in an open field,
translation_verse: Dɛ Seruya bibaala batoro lɔ bela. Banee Joab ne Abisae dɛ Asahɛl. Dɛ Asahɛl won chwae kɛŋɔ kweɡla ken.

english_verse: When Abner turned and saw him, he said, “Is that you, Asahel?” Asahel answered, “Yes it is.”
translation_verse: Abna baa ke nyiŋi dɛ nao, dɛ ŋɔ, “Henee nɔ naa, Asahɛl?” Asɛ o chaŋe ŋɔ, “Ɔɔh, menee.”

english_verse: Abner said, “There are soldiers all around. Stop chasing me and fight one of them! Kill him and take his clothes and weapons for yourself.” But Asahel refused to stop.
translation_verse: Belaa Abna berɛ ŋɔ, “Bɛ chwa teŋɛ n nɛ, chwa teŋɛ laa tena la bɛl nɛ dɛ́ ka lɛ o dɔmkwa.” Kɛ Asahɛl ta noɛ, dɛ ta chwa teŋɛ o nɛɛ ɡɛ.

english_verse: Abner said, “If you don't turn back, I'll have to kill you! Then I could never face your brother Joab again.”
translation_verse: Abna berɔ ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Bɛ chwa teŋɛ n nɛɛ ɡɛ. Bɛ ɡɛ ɛ, ásɛ n ba kpoe. A ba ɡɛ naa, ɛrɛɛ mɛɛ ba wona nyiŋi he dɔɔ Joab siwi ta nɔ?”

english_verse: But Asahel would not turn back, so Abner struck him in the stomach with the back end of his spear. The spear went all the way through and came out of his back. Asahel fell down and died. Everyone who saw Asahel lying dead just stopped and stood still.
translation_verse: Kɛ Asahɛl vɛoh dɛ ta teŋɛ o nɛ, asɛ Abna ta o lampea la habɔɔ, asɛ o mun daa la ka yaɡɛ o tea dɛ vah le o nyaŋ ta. Buɡ la ta, o chole chɔ dɛ sewɛ. Nomɛlbwa valɔ ba tel bela aa, o yon che dɛ́ nyiŋi.

english_verse: But Joab and Abishai went after Abner. Finally, about sunset, they came to the hill of Ammah, not far from Giah on the road to Gibeon Desert.
translation_verse: Kɛ Joab ne Abisae ti Abna, wee aa ba dɛ jo la, ba baa tel deŋɡare bɛl baa dɛ yerɔ Ama ta. O bɛne bwɛɛ bɛl baa dɛ yerɔ Gia ŋwɛnɛ, dɛ kaa Gebeɔn harɛpɛɛ waa chɔa kaa ta.

english_verse: Abner brought the men of Benjamin together in one group on top of a hill, and they got ready to fight.
translation_verse: Ate, Bɛnjamen dea baala ba bar Abna cheme. Ba boa ba nyoa, asɛ dɛ ka che deŋɡare bɛl doa.

english_verse: Abner shouted to Joab, “Aren't we ever going to stop killing each other? Don't you know that the longer we keep on doing this, the worse it's going to be when it's all over? When are you going to order your men to stop chasing their own relatives?”
translation_verse: Anee Abna ŋɔ Joab be ŋɔ, “A chɛ kɛ yá yo dɛɛ la ɡɛ naa? Haa jemɛ kɛŋɔ bambichɔɡa nee aa ba bala ba tɛ yaa aa? Harɛ beŋkpoŋ nɛraa yan, saŋ besoo hɛɛ ba ɡela he nɛra ɡel chwae dɛɛ ti yaa ɔ?”

english_verse: Joab shouted back, “I swear by the living God, if you hadn't spoken, my men would have chased their relatives all night!”
translation_verse: Anee Joab chaŋe ŋɔ, “N ŋwɛɛ Korowii waa lole saŋ bɛlbwa kɛŋɔ, dɛ ken laa he bol aa, n nɛra la fe ɛɛ ti heyaa ka tel kere chɔɔ.”

english_verse: Joab took his trumpet and blew the signal for his soldiers to stop chasing the soldiers of Israel. At once, the fighting stopped.
translation_verse: Belaa Joab hoh bɛla a baɡle kɛ o laa tena la ɡel Israel tena la tii, ba ta yoi kpa.

english_verse: Abner and his troops marched through the Jordan River valley all that night. Then they crossed the river and marched all morning until they arrived back at Mahanaim.
translation_verse: Awola jwaana la bwa Abna ne o laa tena la valɔ kpɔ Jɔɔdan Fɛlembɔjen bini, mɔɔ dɛ ɛɡɛ le o baŋ. Tɔ aa pera chɔɔ la, ba valɔ dɛ ba le Mahanaim.

english_verse: As soon as Joab stopped chasing Abner, he got David's troops together and counted them. There were
translation_verse: Joab aa ɡel Abna tii la, o boa o laa tena la bwa nyoa, dɛ na kɛŋɔ ba bini fi dɛ banuanaarɛ sewɔ dɛ ja Asahɛl nɛ.

english_verse: Joab and his troops carried Asahel's body to Bethlehem and buried him in the family burial place. Then they marched all night and reached Hebron before sunrise.
