translation_verse: Joab ne o laa tena kpɔ Asahɛl, dɛ ka huɡo ba lolanar bwebɔɔ waa lɔ Bɛtlɛham bini. Asɛ ba valɛ awola jwaana la bwa, dɛ ba tel Hɛbrɔn bɔr chaahna saŋ.

english_verse: As the war went on between the families of David and Saul, Abner was gaining more power than ever in Saul's family.
translation_verse: Kooro Sɔɔl ne o laa tena ne Kooro Devid ne o laa tena laa la ta la, dɛ nɛra baa teŋɛ Kooro Sɔɔl nɛɛ la dɛ nyin Abna waa taeh.

english_verse: He had even slept with a wife of Saul by the name of Rizpah the daughter of Aiah. But Saul's son Ishbosheth told Abner, “You shouldn't have slept with one of my father's wives!”
translation_verse: Dɛ Kooro Sɔɔl fa dɔ sɛno bɛl baa yerɔ Rispa, o nya sɔne Aeya. Anee Esbɔsɛt bɔɔ Abna ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ he lawɛ n mɛɛ haah chɔ nɔɔ?”

english_verse: Abner was very angry because of what Ishbosheth had said, and he told Ishbosheth: Am I some kind of worthless dog from Judah? I've always been loyal to your father's family and to his relatives and friends. I haven't turned you over to David. And yet you talk to me as if I've committed a crime with this woman.
translation_verse: Asɛ o baah di kohona waa waa bɔɔro la wa dɛ ŋɔ, “He dɛ lii kɛ n ɛ nyoatechɔɡe dɛ do Juda dea tena bini kɛɛ? Le fini dɛɛ kaa, n kpɔ n te do he mɛɛ Kooro Sɔɔl ne o lolanar dɛ o daamanar lɔɡa. N ta he bwara wechɔɡe bolɛ tɛ Kooro Devid, kɛ he dɛ bol ŋɔ n lawɛ he mɛɛ haah chɔ a ɛ waa aa wola were.

english_verse: I ask God to punish me if I don't help David get what the Lord promised him!
translation_verse: N ŋwɛɛrɔ kɛŋɔ dɛ n ta waa Korowii aa baɡɛ Kooro Devid nyoa la ɛɛ tɛo waa, ó tɛr n deŋne kohona,

english_verse: God said that he wouldn't let anyone in Saul's family ever be king again and that David would be king instead. He also said that David would rule both Israel and Judah, all the way from Dan in the north to Beersheba in the south.
translation_verse: dɛ́ berɛ kora waa lɔ Kooro Sɔɔl luɡe ta la, dɛ́ ɡel Kooro Devid kora che kɛrɛdɛ Israel ne Juda, dɛ́ le Dan waa lɔ weekaŋle nyundua dɛ́ ba kaa Beɛseeba waa lɔ weekaŋle harɛbɔr.”

english_verse: Ishbosheth was so afraid of Abner that he could not even answer.
translation_verse: Esbɔsɛt ta wone bɔɔ Abna wobɛlbwa kpa, dɛkalkɛ dɛ o dɛ ɔmɔ.

english_verse: Abner sent some of his men to David with this message: “You should be the ruler of the whole nation. If you make an agreement with me, I will persuade everyone in Israel to make you their king.”
translation_verse: Belaa Abna tomɛ toroma bá ka ŋɔ Kooro Devid be ŋɔ, “Umee dɔ harɛ nɔ kpeɡri ɔ? Gel n ne he fɔwɛ fɔo, ásɛ n chae dɛ́ ba Israel tena bwa ne he be.”

english_verse: David sent this message back: “Good! I'll make an agreement with you. But before I will even talk with you about it, you must get Saul's daughter Michal back for me.”
translation_verse: Ate, Kooro Devid sɛh ŋɔ, “A wer ɡa! N ne hɛɛ fɔwɛ fɔwee. Kɛ kombeŋkpoŋii n hiah dɛ́ le he be. Dɛ Kooro Sɔɔl bihaah Mikal ta he nɛɛ jae yaa, bɛ ɡel he naa tire n sie kwara.”

english_verse: David sent a few of his officials to Ishbosheth to give him this message: “Give me back my wife Michal! I killed
translation_verse: Belaa Kooro Devid tomɛ toroma Kooro Sɔɔl bibaa Esbɔsɛt be ŋɔ, “Kpɔ n haah Mikal maa kpɔ Filisti tena lafa pen nyoa tɔne ba ɛ o bwara waa dɛ dɔɔ la tɛ mɛ.”

english_verse: Ishbosheth sent some of his men to take Michal away from her new husband, Paltiel the son of Laish.
translation_verse: Anomanta, Esbɔsɛt ɡelɔ ba lawɛ Mikal le o jaa Paltiel waa ɛ Laes bibaa dea.

english_verse: Paltiel followed Michal and the men all the way to Bahurim, crying as he walked. But he went back home after Abner ordered him to leave.
translation_verse: Baa lawɔ dɛɛ kaa la, o jaa Paltiel wio teŋɛ o nɛɛ ka tel bwɛɛ Bahurim ta. Belaa Abna ŋɔ o be ŋɔ “Berɛ kaa dem!” Asɛ o berɛ kaa.

english_verse: Abner talked with the leaders of the tribes of Israel and told them, “You've wanted to make David your king for a long time now.
translation_verse: Abna fa la Israel nomonome be dɛ ka ŋɔ, “Saŋ la bwaa he le dɛɛ nyin hé cheɡ Devid he kooro.

english_verse: So do it! After all, God said he would use his servant David to rescue his people Israel from their enemies, especially from the Philistines.”
translation_verse: Saŋ laanee nɔ! Hé lii ɡɛ Korowii fa aa baɡɛ nyoa ŋɔ, ‘N bonɔɔ Devid nɛɛ mɛɛ ba cheɡa, dɛ́ lɛ n nɛra Israel tena le Filisti tena ne ba dɔma bwa nɔn ta.’ ”

english_verse: Soon after Abner had left Hebron, Joab and some of David's soldiers came back, bringing a lot of things they had taken from an enemy village.
translation_verse: A habɔɔ la, Kooro Devid laa tena tama bane ne Joab kaa le laa ta ba, ba pa laala pirim le laa la ta ba. Kɛ dɛ Abna toole Kooro Devid be Hɛbrɔn kpa, dɛ kooro dɔɔ tao ŋwɛnɛ deŋnesɔɔhna ne o kaa.

english_verse: Right after they arrived, someone told Joab, “Abner visited the king, and the king let him go. Abner even left without causing any trouble.”
translation_verse: Joab ne o laa tena bwa aa kaa ba la, ba ŋɔ o be ŋɔ Abna ba Kooro Devid be asɛ o tao ŋwɛnɛ deŋnesɔɔhna ne o kaa.

english_verse: Joab went to David and said, “What have you done? Abner came to you, and you let him go. Now he's long gone!
translation_verse: Anomanta, Joab la kooro be dɛ ka ŋɔ, “N naa kooro, bɔkwa waa he ɛ ken? Abna ba he be he berɛ tao ŋwɛnɛ o kaalaa? Taraken he ɡelɔ o dɔ bɔr kaa!

translation_verse: He ɡbabir jemɛ Abna, o balɔ dɛ́ ba neɡre, dɛ́ ba nyiŋi he ŋwɛnɛre, dɛ́ jemɛ waa bwa haa dɛ ɛ.”

english_verse: Joab left David, then he sent some messengers to catch up with Abner. They brought him back from the well at Sirah, but David did not know anything about it.
translation_verse: Ate, Joab le Kooro Devid be, dɛ ka tomɛ toroma ba chwa ti Abna dɛ ka lawɔ kɔlɔŋ bɛl waa chɔ bobɛl baa dɛ yerɔ Sira, dɛ ba o ne. Dɛ Kooro Devid te aa a wobɛlbwa jemɛ.

english_verse: When Abner returned to Hebron, Joab pretended he wanted to talk privately with him. So he took Abner into one of the small rooms that were part of the town gate and stabbed him in the stomach. Joab killed him because Abner had killed Joab's brother Asahel. Abner's Funeral
translation_verse: Abna aa bera ba Hɛbrɔn la, Joab lawɔ o ne o ka che bwɛjen la doonyojen keŋkeŋ, a do kɛŋɔ waa dɛ nyin kɛ o ne o ɡbo bol waane ken. Belaa o kpɔ kere tɔɡɛ o tea dɛ kpoo. Gɛɛ a do Joab kpo Abna bɔ kem, o nime Asahɛl o fa aa kpoo la wa.

english_verse: David heard how Joab had killed Abner, and he said, “I swear to the Lord that I am completely innocent of Abner's death!
translation_verse: A habɔɔ Kooro Devid aa baa no la, o ŋɔ, “N ne n harɛ nɔ ta nɛn bɛlbwa ta bolchɔɡe dii Korowii sie, Abna seo wa.

english_verse: Joab and his family are the guilty ones. I pray that Joab's family will always be sick with sores and other skin diseases. May they all be cowards, and may they die in war or starve to death.”
translation_verse: Korowiirii dɛ́ tɛr Joab ne o lolanar deŋne a wa. Kórowii kpɔ ŋwɛra kɛɛ bwadabii weechɔɡa, kɛɛ nɛn waa dɛ valɛ daa ne, kɛɛ laa ta seo, kɛɛ kondikwaa nyae, ba ta ba naanar baa ka ba bwa nɛ!”

english_verse: Joab and his brother Abishai killed Abner because he had killed their brother Asahel in the battle at Gibeon.
translation_verse: Gɛɛ a do Joab ne o nime Abisae kpo Abna bɔ kem, kpoe waa kpo ba nime Asahɛl laa ta Gebeɔn la wa.

english_verse: David told Joab and everyone with him, “Show your sorrow by tearing your clothes and wearing sackcloth! Walk in front of Abner's body and cry!” David walked behind the stretcher on which Abner's body was being carried.
translation_verse: Ate, Kooro Devid ŋɔ Joab ne nɛra baa ja o nɛɛ la be ŋɔ, “Hé kɛɛ he laala dɛ́ kpɔ lweyale tɔ á baɡle kɛŋɔ he loo kuu dɛ́ tɔ Abna lale sie.” Kooro Devid ɡbabir ɡe teŋɛ lale la nɛ.

english_verse: Abner was buried in Hebron, while David and everyone else stood at the tomb and cried loudly.
translation_verse: Ba huɡe Abna Hɛbrɔn asɛ kooro ne nɛra la bwa wiu kohona, o huɡribɔr bela.

english_verse: Then the king sang a funeral song about Abner: Abner, why should you have died like an outlaw?
translation_verse: Kooro Devid taa wiile nɔ tɛ Abna ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ a chɛ kɛ Abna sewɛ ɡɛne seo waa do ken nɔɔ?

english_verse: No one tied your hands or chained your feet, yet you died as a victim of murderers. Everyone started crying again.
translation_verse: Abna, ba ta he nɔɔra vɔrɔwɛ, kɛɛ dɛ do kwaa he nakpale. He sewɔ kɛŋɔ nɛn nɛnchɔɡa aa lawɔ ka kpo.” Asɛ nɛra la bwa berɛ wiu ja.

english_verse: Then they brought some food to David and told him he would feel better if he had something to eat. It was still daytime, and David said, “I swear to God that I won't take a bite of bread or anything else until sunset!”
translation_verse: Nɛra la bwa soŋe Kooro Devid ŋɔ ó nyin komɛl do nyoa mɔɔ wee le harɛ. Kɛ o ta sɛɛh dɛ ŋwɛɛ ŋɔ, “Dɛ n kpɔ komɛlbwa do nyoa mɔɔ wee le harɛ naa, Kórowii tɛr n deŋne kohona.”

english_verse: Everyone noticed what David did, and they liked it, just as they always liked what he did.
translation_verse: Nɛra la bwa sie lɛ waa kooro aa ɛa la ta, dɛ kpɔ do ba liire bini. Kasinteŋ, kooro wobɛlbwa waa ɛa lɛ nɛra la bwa sie.

english_verse: Now the people of Judah and Israel were certain that David had nothing to do with killing Abner.
translation_verse: Awola tɔpere la, nɛra la bwa ne Israel tena bwa nao kɛŋɔ kooro nɔn toole Abna seo ta.

english_verse: David said to his officials, “Don't you realize that today one of Israel's great leaders has died?
translation_verse: Belaa kooro ŋɔ o nomonome la be ŋɔ, “Haa jemɛ kɛŋɔ nomonjen tenten cholo fini Israel harɛ nɔ ta naa?

english_verse: I am the chosen king, but Joab and Abishai have more power than I do. So God will have to pay them back for the evil thing they did.”
translation_verse: Fini, Korowii fuɡe noo do n nyu ta dɛ lee mɛ cheɡ kɛ kooro te, kɛ n ɡwɛɡrɔ. Seruya bibaala nɔ kpeɡri ɡwaa n nɛ. Korowiirii dɛ́ bɔ nɛnchɔɡe waa ɛ ɡɛ nɔ kem ɡɛ aa chɛa.”

english_verse: Ishbosheth felt like giving up after he heard that Abner had died in Hebron. Everyone in Israel was terrified.
translation_verse: Kooro Sɔɔl bibaa Esbɔsɛt aa baa no kɛŋɔ Abna sewɛ Hɛbrɔn la, o ɔmɔ asɛ Israel tena bwa ɡe bambile teŋe.

english_verse: Ishbosheth had put the two brothers Baanah and Rechab in charge of the soldiers who raided enemy villages. Rimmon was their father, and they were from the town of Beeroth, which belonged to the tribe of Benjamin.
translation_verse: Dɛ Esbɔsɛt dɔ baala banɛ bane ba chɔ nɛra ba yon la ka lɔ tɔ bwɛɛre nɛra nɛɛ dɛ́ pa ba laala nyoa. Bɛl sɔne Baana, asɛ nɛɛte la ɡe Rekab. Remɔn waa le Beɛrɔt harɛ ta biirii ban, Bɛnjamen dea. Ba kpɔ Beɛrɔt nɔ ɛ Bɛnjamen dea harɛ pera,

english_verse: Saul's son Jonathan had a son named Mephibosheth, who had not been able to walk since he was five years old. It happened when someone from Jezreel told his nurse that Saul and Jonathan had died. She hurried off with the boy in her arms, but he fell and injured his legs.
translation_verse: Dɛ Kooro Sɔɔl bibaa Jonatan dɔ bie bɛl baa yerɔ Mɛfebɔsɛt, o ɛ boobi. Waa di bene anue taa a le Jesreel ba kɛŋɔ Kooro Sɔɔl ne Jonatan sewɔ. Haah waa dɛ nyiŋi o nɛɛ la aa noa la, o kpɔɔ chwa. Waa dɛ too nomanta, bie la le o nɔn ta le harɛ, a taa a che o ɛ boobi.

translation_verse: Remɔn bibaala Rekab ne Baana iro ŋɔ ba dɛ kaa Esbɔsɛt dem. Baa kaa tel bela la, dɛ wee cheɡɛ nyufala, asɛ Esbɔsɛt so dɛɛ onɛ.

translation_verse: Gɛ saŋ baa lɔ dea la bini la, dɛ Esbɔsɛt chɔ mpa ta. Baa tɔɡɔ o sewɛ tonɛ la, ba teŋe o nyu. Ba kpɔɔ valɛ awola jwaana la bwa Jɔɔdan Fɛlembɔjen bini dɛ kaa.

english_verse: Finally they turned west and went to Hebron. They went in to see David and told him, “Your Majesty, here is the head of Ishbosheth, the son of your enemy Saul who tried to kill you! The Lord has let you get even with Saul and his family.”
translation_verse: Ba kpɔ Esbɔsɛt nyu ba tɛ Kooro Devid Hɛbrɔn dɛ ŋɔ, “N naa, Esbɔsɛt nyuu la, o mɛɛ fa ɛɛ dɔm dɛɛ nyini dɛ́ kpo la. Fini Korowii ɡelɔ kooro tɔ o wel Kooro Sɔɔl ne o naanar nɛ.”

english_verse: David answered: I swear that only the Lord rescues me when I'm in trouble!
translation_verse: Ate, Kooro Devid chaŋe Remɔn bibaala Rekab ne Baana ŋɔ, “N ŋwɛɛ Korowii waa lole saŋ bɛlbwa dɛ lɛɛ mɛ le n wenaale bwa ta,

english_verse: When a man came to Ziklag and told me that Saul was dead, he thought he deserved a reward for bringing good news. But I grabbed him and killed him.
translation_verse: kɛŋɔ torome waa ba n be Siklaɡ dɛ ba bol Kooro Sɔɔl seo waa n be la, o liiro kɛŋɔ amanesoma nee o fe ɛɛ ba. N lawɔ dɛ kpoo, a ɛ amanesoma la kembɔr.

english_verse: You evil men have done something much worse than he did. You've killed an innocent man in his own house and on his own bed. I'll make you pay for that. I'll wipe you from the face of the earth!
translation_verse: Ɛrɛɛ mɛɛ ba nɛn waa wola wechɔɡa bɛlbwa ɛɛ dɛ chɔ o dea mpa ta nyubinikpeɡ tena ka kpoo waa bola ɔ? A ta chɛ kɛ o seo ɡure he nyu ta ń kpoo heyaa bɔ kem le harɛ nɔ ta naa?”

english_verse: Then David said to his troops, “Kill these two brothers! Cut off their hands and feet and hang their bodies by the pool in Hebron. But bury Ishbosheth's head in Abner's tomb near Hebron.” And they did.

english_verse: King Hiram of Tyre sent some officials to David. Carpenters and stone workers came with them, and they brought cedar logs so they could build David a palace.

translation_verse: Kooro Devid aa kaa yo Jerusalam dɛ pɔ o nɛra nɛɛ la, o kaa so bela dɛ pa o sɔn Kooro Devid Bwɛjen. O ma danjwɛkpeɡ baro dɛ le deŋɡare la wee leebɔr pera harɛ waa baro la ta.

english_verse: The Jebusites lived in Jerusalem, and David led his army there to attack them. The Jebusites did not think he could get in, so they told him, “You can't get in here! We could keep you out, even if we couldn't see or walk!”
translation_verse: Kooro Devid ne o laa tena kpɔ ba te kaa Jerusalam dɛ́ ka yo Jebus tena baa soɡe bela la. Belaa Jebus tena la ŋɔ kooro be ŋɔ, “Haa won ba ya be bonɔ, hale nyoŋa ne boobie kwaraa ɛɛ won doŋi he berɛ kaa.” Dɛ ba liire bwaa kɛŋɔ Kooro Devid aa won la bela.

english_verse: David became a great and strong ruler, because the Lord All-Powerful was on his side.
translation_verse: Kooro Devid teŋɔ di kpeɡri kohona dɛkalkɛ dɛ Korowii waa ɛ Koronar Bwa Kooro ja o nɛ.

english_verse: The Philistines heard that David was now king of Israel, and they came into the hill country to try and capture him. But David found out and went into his fortress.
translation_verse: Filisti tena aa noa kɛŋɔ ba fuɡe noo do Devid nyu ta dɛ cheɡo kora ta Israel harɛ bwa ta la, ba laa tena bwa iro dɛ kaa nyin o bɔr sibeɡra ne, asɛ Kooro Devid ɡe no ba wa, dɛ le ka chem ba bela waa soɡa danjwɛkpeɡ la ta.

translation_verse: Filisti tena la balɔ dɛ ba su Refaim Fɛlembɔjen bini bwa.

translation_verse: Belaa Kooro Devid ka bɔɔ le Korowii be ŋɔ, “N Naa Korowii, ń la ka yo Filisti tena nɔ naa? Hɛɛ kpɔ baa do n nɔn taa kɛɛ?” Asɛ Korowii chaŋo ŋɔ, “Ir kaa, mɛɛ kpɔ baa do he nɔn taa, ásɛ he pɔ ba nɛ.”

english_verse: David attacked the Philistines and defeated them. Then he said, “I watched the Lord break through my enemies like a mighty flood.” So he named the place “The Lord Broke Through.”
translation_verse: Anomanta, Kooro Devid iro, dɛ ka yoo ba Baal Pɛrasem, dɛ pɔ ba nɛ. Dɛ ŋɔ, “Gɛ nee yon su ba tɔ bobɛlbwa la, ɡɛɛ Korowii ba tɔ n dɔma nɛɛ n sie.” Anomanta, ba dɛ yerɛ bela Baal Pɛrasem.

english_verse: David and his troops also carried away the idols that the Philistines had left behind.
translation_verse: Filisti tena chwao ɡel ba voɡare bela, asɛ Kooro Devid ne o laa tena paa kaa.

english_verse: Some time later, the Philistines came back into the hill country and camped in Rephaim Valley.
translation_verse: Filisti tena la balɔ ba su Refaim Fɛlembɔjen bini ja,

english_verse: David asked the Lord what he should do, and the Lord answered: Don't attack them from the front. Circle around behind and attack from among the balsam trees.
translation_verse: asɛ Kooro Devid ka bɔɔ le Korowii be ja, asɛ o chaŋo ŋɔ, “Hɛɛ berɛ sie pae dɛ́ kaa ba be. Hé bar ba ka che ba habɔɔ dɛ́ yoo ba daa ane baa dɛ yera balsam sie bela.

translation_verse: Hé ba dɛ no ba naɡime sii daa la dor aa, hé pa mun dɛɛ yo, a dɛ baɡle kɛŋɔ men Korowiirii baa tɔ he sie, dɛ́ ka yo Filisti tena la dɛ́ pɔ ba nɛ.”

english_verse: David obeyed the Lord and defeated the Philistines. He even chased them all the way from Geba to the entrance to Gezer.
translation_verse: Gɛɛ Kooro Devid ɛ ɡɛ Korowii aa doo bwa, dɛ won doŋi Filisti tena le Gebeɔn ba Gɛsa.

english_verse: The people carrying the chest walked six steps, then David sacrificed an ox and a choice cow.
translation_verse: Baala baa cheɡɛ Daka la aa ta naɡale anumɛl la, Kooro ɡelɔ ba che asɛ o kpo nabal dɛ nao bie waa do noo kohona, dɛ ɛ saraha tɛ Korowii.

english_verse: He was dancing for the Lord with all his might, but he wore only a linen cloth.

english_verse: He and everyone else were celebrating by shouting and blowing horns while the chest was being carried along.
translation_verse: asɛ o ne Israel tena la bwa kpɔ silɛɛ lɔŋɔre dɛɛ hoh bɛle, dɛ kpɔ Daka la ba Jerusalam.

english_verse: Saul's daughter Michal looked out her window and watched the chest being brought into David's City. But when she saw David jumping and dancing for the Lord, she was disgusted.
translation_verse: Baa kpɔ Korowii Ne Nɛwɛnyina Fɔo Daka la dɛɛ jo Jerusalam Devid Bwɛjen la ta la, Kooro Sɔɔl bihaah Mikal aa cheɡɛ tokoro ta dɛ na Kooro Devid o sa dɛɛ hɛɡre la, o sie ta o nɛɛ lɛɛ, dɛ nyiŋu vah.

english_verse: They put the sacred chest on a new ox cart and started bringing it down the hill from Abinadab's house. Abinadab's sons Uzzah and Ahio were guiding the ox cart,
translation_verse: Ba kpɔ Korowii Ne Nɛwɛnyina Fɔo Daka la le Abinadab dem deŋɡare bɛl doa, dɛ kpɔ chɔŋɛ torɔɡofale bɛl ta nabala ɛɛ tɛro. Abinadab bibaala bane baa dɛ yer ba Ussa ne Ahio, banee ba le ŋɔ baa daah torɔɡo la,

english_verse: led them to Baalah in Judah, which was also called Kiriath-Jearim. They were going there to get the sacred chest and bring it back to Jerusalem. The throne of the Lord All-Powerful is above the winged creatures on top of this chest, and he is worshiped there.
translation_verse: O ne o laa tena la iro le bwɛjen Baala baa bera dɛɛ yerɔ Kiriat Jearim waa lɔ Juda harɛ ta, dɛ́ ka kpɔ Korowii Ne Nɛwɛnyina Fɔo Daka la le bela dɛ́ kaa Jerusalam. Nemenɛ Korowii sɔn dawɛ Daka la ta, asɛ o so o kookara ta, kena kwaa baa dɛ yera Kerobim la baah ta.

english_verse: Some of the people of Israel were playing music on small harps and other stringed instruments, and on tambourines, castanets, and cymbals. David and the others were happy, and they danced for the Lord with all their might.
translation_verse: Dɛ Kooro Devid ne Israel tena la bwa dɛ lɛ ba sie. Ba ɡo yela silɛɛ ne kohona, dɛɛ lɔ janjela dɛɛ hoh kalipere, dɛɛ lɔ kwaa anɛ ane baa kpɔ ayaawa ɛa, dɛɛ yiiɡi loŋa ɡe Korowii sie.

english_verse: But when they came to Nacon's threshing-floor, the oxen stumbled, so Uzzah reached out and took hold of the sacred chest.
translation_verse: Ba valɔ ba tel Nakɔn mea lɔ bɔr, asɛ nabala aa dɛ tɛɡre Korowii Ne Nɛwɛnyina Fɔo Daka la lɔ na, asɛ Ussa ta lawɛ Korowii Fɔo Daka la kpoŋe.

english_verse: The Lord God was very angry with Uzzah for doing this, and he killed Uzzah right there beside the chest.
translation_verse: Korowii baah di Ussa nɛɛ kohona, dɛkalkɛ o kono kɛ waa lawɛ Korowii Ne Nɛwɛnyina Fɔo Daka la kpoŋe la. Anomanta, Ussa sewɔ chɔ Korowii Fɔo Daka la keŋkeŋ.

english_verse: David got angry with God for killing Uzzah. He named that place “Bursting Out Against Uzzah,” and that's what it's still called.
translation_verse: Belaa Kooro Devid ɡe baah di, ɡɛ Korowii baah aa di Ussa nɛɛ dɛ tɛr o deŋne la wa. Anomanta, dɛ ba le fini ba dɛ yerɛ bela Pɛrɛs Ussa.

english_verse: David was afraid of the Lord and thought, “Should I really take the sacred chest to my city?”
translation_verse: Kooro Devid ɔmɛ Korowii awola tɔpere dɛ ŋɔ, “Dɛ n kpɔ Korowii Ne Nɛwɛnyina Fɔo Daka nɔ ba n be bonɔ naa, ɛrɛɛ mɛɛ ba wona nyiŋi o ta nɔ?”

english_verse: He decided not to take it there. Instead, he turned off the road and took it to the home of Obed Edom, who was from Gath.
translation_verse: Dɛ waa berɛ dɛɛ nyin ó ba Korowii Ne Nɛwɛnyina Fɔo Daka la ne o be Jerusalam kpa. O ɡelɔ ba kpɔ ba cheɡ Ɔbɛd Edom dem, o le bwɛjen Gat.

english_verse: The chest stayed there for three months, and the Lord greatly blessed Obed Edom, his family, and everything he owned. Then someone told King David, “The Lord has done this because the sacred chest is in Obed Edom's house.” At once, David went to Obed Edom's house to get the chest and bring it to David's City. Everyone was celebrating.
translation_verse: Kooro Devid baa no kɛŋɔ Korowii swee Ɔbɛd Edom ne o dem tena, dɛ komɛlbwa waa dɔa andɛɛɡa Korowii Ne Nɛwɛnyina Fɔo Daka la wa. Anomanta, o ne Israel tena bane la Ɔbɛd Edom dem silɛɛ ne, dɛ ka kpɔ Daka la ba Jerusalam waa ɛ Devid Bwɛjen la ta.

english_verse: They put the chest inside a tent that David had set up for it. David worshiped the Lord by sacrificing animals and burning them on an altar,
translation_verse: Israel tena la kpɔ Korowii Ne Nɛwɛnyina Fɔo Daka la ba cheɡ o chebɔr, tɛnte dea Kooro Devid aa baŋro la bini, asɛ dɛ kpɔ saraha kwaa baa fuah, ne deŋnesɔɔhna sarahare ba Korowii sie bela.

english_verse: then he blessed the people in the name of the Lord All-Powerful.
translation_verse: Kooro Devid aa kpoo kwaa dɛ fuh ɛ sarahare ne deŋnesɔɔhna sarahare tonɛ la, o soŋe andɛɛɡa Nemenɛ Korowii be tɛ nɛra la.

english_verse: He gave all the men and women in the crowd a small loaf of bread, some meat, and a handful of raisins, then everyone went home. Michal Talks to David
translation_verse: Belaa o kpɔ paanoo ne daa nɔna ane aa hola dɛ ɛ nɔndel, dɛ ɡrepo daa nɔna aa hola nɔndel tɛ Israel haah ne baa te bɛlbwa. Asɛ bɛlbwa berɛ kaa o dem.

english_verse: David went home so he could ask the Lord to bless his family. But Saul's daughter Michal went out and started yelling at him. “You were really great today!” she said. “You acted like a dirty old man, dancing around half-naked in front of your servants' slave-girls.”
translation_verse: A habɔɔ Kooro Devid aa kaa dem dɛ ka soŋe andɛɛɡa tɛ o dem tena la, Kooro Sɔɔl bihaah Mikal leɔ ba chemo dɛ ŋɔ, “Na ɡɛ Israel kooro aa lɛ sɔn tɛ o te fini ɡɛ. O ɛ o te kɛ ɡɛne dɛɛ sa o bitoli sie!”

english_verse: David told her, “The Lord didn't choose your father or anyone else in your family to be the leader of his people. The Lord chose me, and I was celebrating in honor of him.
translation_verse: Belaa Kooro Devid chaŋe ŋɔ, “Korowii siee mɛɛ sa. Onee cheɡ mɛ kora Israel harɛ ta, he mɛɛ kɛɛ he dem te bɛlbwa laa. Mɛɛ teŋɔɔ dɛɛ lɛ n sie Korowii wa, dɛɛ duuru.

english_verse: I'll show you just how great I can be! I'll even be disgusting to myself. But those slave-girls you talked about will still honor me!”
translation_verse: A lole kɛŋɔ he dɛ lii kɛ n sae la ɛ sihihwa, kɛ bitoli haa dɛ bol ba waa nɔ ɛɛ kpɔ duuree tɛ mɛ.”

english_verse: But I will never put an end to my agreement with him, as I put an end to my agreement with Saul, who was king before you.
translation_verse: Maa n nyinaa laa kpɔ o nɛ, kɛŋɔ maa le Kooro Sɔɔl ne dɛ ɡel he ba chiɡ o naa ta di kora la.

english_verse: Then one day, as David was talking with Nathan the prophet, David said, “Look around! I live in a palace made of cedar, but the sacred chest has to stay in a tent.”
translation_verse: Belaa o ŋɔ Korowii keame bɛl baa dɛ yerɔ Netan be ŋɔ, “N soɡe koodem baa kpɔ peleme daa kwaaro bini, asɛ Korowii Ne Nɛwɛnyina Fɔo Daka la te ta che tɛnte dea bini.”

english_verse: Nathan replied, “The Lord is with you, so do what you want!”
translation_verse: Anee Netan chaŋe ŋɔ, “Ɛ wobɛlbwa aa lɔ he liire bini, dɛkalkɛ Korowii ja he nɛ.”

english_verse: That night, the Lord told Nathan
translation_verse: Kɛ awola jwaana la, Korowii ŋɔ Netan be ŋɔ,

english_verse: to go to David and give him this message: David, you are my servant, so listen to what I say. Why should you build a temple for me?
translation_verse: ó ir la ka ŋɔ o bonɔɔ Devid be ŋɔ, “Henee dɛ́ do dea tɛ mɛ n ba so o bini naa?

english_verse: I didn't live in a temple when I brought my people out of Egypt, and I don't live in one now. A tent has always been my home wherever I have gone with them.
translation_verse: Le awola tɔpere maa kpɔ Israel tena le Ijipt harɛ ta ba le fini, n ta dea bini soɡe bwa. Tɛnte dea binii mɛɛ so ba kpɔ mɛ dɛɛ ɡaaɡe.

english_verse: I chose leaders and told them to be like shepherds for my people Israel. But did I ever say anything to even one of them about building a cedar temple for me?
translation_verse: Bobɛlbwa n ne Israel tena aa laŋa bwa, n ta ba sitɔɔla bɛlbwa maa do ba ŋɔ baa nyiŋi n nɛra nɛɛ kɛŋɔ peera be ŋɔe ŋɔ, ba ta peleme daa aa kpeɡa kpɔe kwaa dea tɛ mɛ.

english_verse: David, this is what I, the Lord All-Powerful, say to you. I brought you in from the fields where you took care of sheep, and I made you the leader of my people.
translation_verse: N bonɔɔ Devid, peeraa he teɡɛ dɛɛ la ane dibɔr n ka lawɛ dɛ ba cheɡe kora ta n nɛra Israel tena nɛ.

english_verse: Wherever you went, I helped you and destroyed your enemies right in front of your eyes. I have made you one of the most famous people in the world.
translation_verse: N ja he nɛ bobɛlbwa haa laŋa, dɛ yo he dɔma baa lɔ he sie dɛ pɔ ba nɛɛ tɛɛ. Mɛɛ ɡeloo he sɔn le kɛŋɔ harɛ nɔ ta nɛnjena ken.

english_verse: I have given my people Israel a land of their own where they can live in peace, and they won't have to tremble with fear any more. Evil nations won't bother them, as they did
translation_verse: Mɛɛ kpɔ harɛ waa ɛ n nɛra Israel tena ɡbaɡba konee tɛɛ ba, bá ka so o ta ba bwara sɔɔh ba. Nɛnchɔɡa aa ban fiiɡi kpa, ɡɛ a fa aa doa wubwa la,

english_verse: when I let judges rule my people. And I have kept your enemies from attacking you. Now I promise that you and your descendants will be kings.
translation_verse: ne ɡɛ maa ɛa dɛ le saŋ maa le sitɔɔla tɛ n nɛra Israel tena la. Mɛɛ berɔ tɛ heyaa bosɔɔhna le he dɔma bwa nɔn ta. Men Korowii, n bol he be ŋɔ he ne he naanaree dɛɛ ba koranar ɛɛ.

english_verse: I'll choose one of your sons to be king when you reach the end of your life and are buried in the tomb of your ancestors. I'll make him a strong ruler,
translation_verse: Haa ba sewɛ ka pu he naawa la, mɛɛ ɡeloo he ɡbabir bibaala la bini bɛl bá chiɡ he naa ta dɛ́ di kora, ásɛ o kora che kiŋkiŋ saŋ bɛlbwa dɛɛ la.

english_verse: and no one will be able to take his kingdom away from him. He will be the one to build a temple for me.
translation_verse: Onee dɛ́ do n Dea tɛ mɛ n sɔn ta, ásɛ n ɡel o kora che kiŋkiŋ saŋ bɛlbwa dɛɛ la.

english_verse: I will be his father, and he will be my son. When he does wrong, I'll see that he is corrected, just as children are corrected by their parents.
translation_verse: Mɛɛ ɛ o mɛɛ, ásɛ o ɛ n bie. O ɛ wechɔɡa aa, mɛɛ tɛr o deŋnee kɛŋɔ mɛɛ yon dɛɛ tɛr o bie deŋne o wechɔɡa waa la.

english_verse: After all, you really are Israel's God, the Lord All-Powerful. You've told me that you will let my descendants be kings. That's why I have the courage to pray to you like this, even though I am only your servant.
translation_verse: Koranar Bwa Kooro, Israel tena aa dɛ tomɛ, he pili waa nɔ bini baɡle men he bonɔɔ dɛ ŋɔ, ‘Mɛɛ ɡeloo he naanar ɛ koranar’

english_verse: David went into the tent he had set up for the sacred chest. Then he sat there and prayed: Lord All-Powerful, my family and I don't deserve what you have already done for us,
translation_verse: Belaa Kooro Devid ka jo Korowii Dea Cheremibɔr waa baŋro la bini, dɛ ka so Korowii sie dɛ ŋɔ, “Nemenɛ Korowii, umee n ɡe ne n lolanar, asɛ he ɛ ɡɛ waa nɔ dɔŋa bwa tɛ mɛ ken nɔɔ?

english_verse: I am your servant, and you know my thoughts, so there is nothing more that I need to say.
translation_verse: Bɔkwaa men Devid dɔ dɛ́ bol he be jaɔ? Nemenɛ Korowii, he ɡbabir jemɛ men maa ɛ he bonɔɔ wa.

english_verse: You have done this wonderful thing, and you have let me know about it, because you wanted to keep your promise.
translation_verse: N Naa Korowii, he cheɡɛ waa haa bola ne waa haa dɛ nyin ɛɛ ta dɛ ɛ wejena nɔ bwa, asɛ men maa ɛ he bonɔɔ jemɛ a wa.

english_verse: Lord All-Powerful, you are greater than all others. No one is like you, and you alone are God. Everything we have heard about you is true.
translation_verse: Nemenɛ Korowii, he kan kohona. Nomɛlbwa toole dɛ do kɛ hen, ya te jemɔ saŋ bɛlbwa kɛŋɔ he ɡboo Korowii.

english_verse: And there is no other nation on earth like Israel, the nation you rescued from slavery in Egypt to be your own. You became famous by using great and wonderful miracles to force other nations and their gods out of your land, so your people could live here.
translation_verse: Harɛ bɛlbwa nɛra toole dɛ do kɛŋɔ he nɛra Israel tena, harɛ beŋkpoŋ nɛra hen Korowii aa lɛɛ ba le wenaale ta Ijipt harɛ dɛ kpɔ ba ɛ he nɛra la. Wejena ne nyokpowe-ɛɛla haa ɛa tɛɛ ba la bwa ɡelɔ he dɔ sɔn harɛ nɔ ta bwa. He berɔ doŋi harɛre ane nɛra ne ba voɡa le ba sie.

english_verse: You have chosen Israel to be your people forever, and you have become their God.
translation_verse: He lɛ he nɛra Israel tena cheɡ saŋ bɛlbwa dɛɛ la, asɛ dɛ ɛ Korowii baa dɛ tomɛ.

english_verse: And now, Lord God, please do what you have promised me and my descendants.
translation_verse: N Naa Korowii, ɡel he nyobaɡa haa baɡɛ he bonɔɔ ne o naanar la do le saŋ bɛlbwa dɛɛ la. Ɛ ɡɛ haa ŋɔa la,

english_verse: Then you will be famous forever, and everyone will say, “The Lord God All-Powerful rules Israel, and David's descendants are his chosen kings.”
translation_verse: á che a ta he dɔ sɔn kohona saŋ bɛlbwa dɛɛ la. Ásɛ nɛra na dɛ ŋɔ, ‘Korowiirii Koranar Bwa Kooro dɛɛ nyiŋi Israel tena nɛ!’ Ásɛ men, he bonɔɔ Devid naanar che kiŋkiŋ dɛ́ do he sie saŋ bɛlbwa.

english_verse: Lord All-Powerful, you are God. You have promised me some very good things, and you can be trusted to do what you promise.
translation_verse: Nemenɛ Korowii, henee Korowii yaa dɛ tomɛ! He waa ɛ kasinteŋ kɛ yaa teŋɛ a ta, asɛ he kpɔ wedɛɛɡa aa do ken baɡɛ men maa ɛ he bonɔɔ nyoa nɔ.

english_verse: Please bless my descendants and let them always be your chosen kings. You have already promised, and I'm sure that you will bless my family forever.
translation_verse: N dɛ soŋe kɛ he swee n naanar andɛɛɡa, ásɛ baa di he laworomɛ saŋ bɛlbwa. Hen Nemenɛ Korowiirii baɡ mɛ a ɡɛ nyoa nɔ. Sweera haa sweera tɛ n naanar la ɛɛ do lee saŋ bɛlbwa dɛɛ la.”

english_verse: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was the commander of David's bodyguard. David's sons were priests.
translation_verse: Jehoiada bibaa Bɛnaya ɡe ɛ Kɛrɛt ne Pɛlet tena baa dɛ daah kooro la nomoa, asɛ Kooro Devid bibaala ɛɛ ja kooro o waa ta.

english_verse: David also defeated the Moabites. Then he made their soldiers lie down on the ground, and he measured them off with a rope. He would measure off two lengths of the rope and have those men killed, then he would measure off one length and let those men live. The people of Moab had to accept David as their ruler and pay taxes to him.
translation_verse: O berɔ ka yo Moab tena ɡe dɛ pɔ ba nɛ. O ɡelɔ nɛra baa laɡ ba laa la ta la chɔ harɛ bɔre atoro, asɛ o maɡ ba ŋwɛn ne. O kpoo nɛra baa chɔa teŋɛ nɛɛ la, dɛ ɡel banɔ la baa chɔa teŋɛ tooro la, o ta ban kpoorɛ. Gɛɛ a do Moab tena ba do Kooro Devid lɔɡa, dɛ kpɔ harɛ la kwaa baa tɛo.

english_verse: David set out for the Euphrates River to build a monument there. On his way, he defeated the king of Zobah, whose name was Hadadezer the son of Rehob.
translation_verse: Belaa Kooro Devid berɛ ka yo Rehob bibaa Soba Kooro Hadadesa, ɡɛ saŋ waa la Yufretis Moo nyoa dɛ ka lɛ bela harɛ ba do o lɔɡa ja la.

english_verse: When troops from the Aramean kingdom of Damascus came to help Hadadezer, David killed
translation_verse: Siiria tena baa le Damaskɔs balɔ dɛ ba cha Soba Kooro Hadadesa, asɛ Kooro Devid kpoo ba bini nɛra kaɡboŋa fifraanɛ dɛ banɛ.

english_verse: He left some of his soldiers in Damascus, and the Arameans had to accept David as their ruler and pay taxes to him. Everywhere David went, the Lord helped him win battles.
translation_verse: Kooro Devid bɔne laa tena la bini ba so kuore ta Damaskɔs harɛ ta, asɛ Siiria tena la do o lɔɡa dɛ kpɔ harɛ la kwaa baa tɛo. Korowii ja Kooro Devid nɛɛ dɛ ɡel bobɛlbwa waa la ka yo la, o pɔ ba nɛ.

english_verse: Hadadezer's officers had carried their arrows in gold cases hung over their shoulders, but David took these cases and brought them to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Kooro Devid kpɔ suuɡaswɛm kwaa Kooro Hadadesa nomonome aa kpɔa dɛɛ tɔ ba te ɡbemɡbe laa ta la, dɛ ba a ne Jerusalam.

english_verse: He also took a lot of bronze from the cities of Betah and Berothai, which had belonged to Hadadezer.
translation_verse: O berɔ pa ayaawa aa wara le Kooro Hadadesa bwɛjena Teba ne Bɛrɔtae ta.

english_verse: King Toi of Hamath and King Hadadezer had been enemies. So when Toi heard that David had attacked and defeated Hadadezer's whole army, he sent his son Joram to praise and congratulate David. Joram also brought him gifts made of silver, gold, and bronze.
translation_verse: o tomɛ o bibaa Hadoram Kooro Devid be, o ka jaamo yoi waa kaa yo Kooro Hadadesa dɛ pɔ o nɛɛ la wa. Dɛ o ne Kooro Tou nɔ yo laa ka. Hadoram kpɔ suuɡaswɛm ne suuɡapoŋa dɛ ayaawa kwaa bwa soo siwi ba tɛ Kooro Devid.

english_verse: David gave these to the Lord, just as he had done with the silver and gold that he had captured from
translation_verse: Kooro Devid kpɔ a ɡɛ kwaa nɔ dɛ lea cheɡ tɛ Korowii toma, ɡɛ o fa aa ɛ suuɡapoŋa ne suuɡaswɛm waa paa le harɛre waa kaa yo dɛ pɔ a nɛra nɛɛ la.

english_verse: Zadok the son of Ahitub, and Abiathar the son of Ahimelech, were the priests. Seraiah was the secretary.
translation_verse: asɛ Ahitub bibaala Sadɔk ne Abiata bibaala Ahemɛlɛk ɡe ɛ sɔfore, asɛ Seraya ɡe ɛ ba karake waa chwerɛ waa dɛɛ do tɔne bini.

english_verse: Joab the son of Zeruiah was the commander in chief of the army. Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud kept the government records.
translation_verse: Dɛ haah bɛl baa dɛ yerɔ Seruya bibaa Joab laanee chɔ laa tena nyoa, asɛ Ahilud bibaa Jehosafat ɡe chwerɛ waa aa chiɡa bwa dɛɛ bil,

english_verse: One day, David thought, “I wonder if any of Saul's family are still alive. If they are, I will be kind to them, because I made a promise to Jonathan.”
translation_verse: Awola bɛl, Kooro Devid bɔɔrɔ ŋɔ, “Nomɛl ta ka Kooro Sɔɔl dem ásɛ n koh Jonatan wa dɛ́ ɛo wedɛɛɡe aa?”

english_verse: David called in Ziba, one of the servants of Saul's family. David said, “So you are Ziba.” “Yes, Your Majesty, I am.”
translation_verse: Dɛ bonɔɔ bɛl lɔ Kooro Sɔɔl dem baa yerɔ Siba. Ba yerɔ ba kooro sie asɛ o bɔɔro ŋɔ, “Henee baa yerɛ Siba la aa?” O chaŋe ŋɔ, “N dɔɔ menee, he bonɔɔ.”

english_verse: David asked, “Are any of Saul's family still alive? If there are, I want to be kind to them.” Ziba answered, “One of Jonathan's sons is still alive, but he can't walk.”
translation_verse: Belaa kooro bɔɔro ŋɔ, “Nomɛl ta ka Kooro Sɔɔl dem ń nyin o wa ɡɛ maa baɡɛ Korowii nyoa la aa?” Anee Siba chaŋe ŋɔ, “Jonatan bibaa bɛl lole. O ɛ boobi.”

english_verse: “Where is he?” David asked. Ziba replied, “He lives in Lo-Debar with Machir the son of Ammiel.”
translation_verse: Asɛ kooro bɔɔ ŋɔ, “Leperaa o dɔɔ.” Anee Siba chaŋe ŋɔ, “O lɔ Ameɛl bibaa Makir dem Lo Debar.”

english_verse: David sent some servants to bring Jonathan's son from Lo-Debar. His name was Mephibosheth, and he was the grandson of Saul. He came to David and knelt down. David asked, “Are you Mephibosheth?” “Yes, I am, Your Majesty.”
translation_verse: Jonatan bibaa Mɛfebɔsɛt waa ɛ Kooro Sɔɔl naa aa ba Kooro Devid be la, o ɡuŋu dɛ kpɔ duure tɛo. Belaa Kooro Devid ŋɔ, “Mɛfebɔsɛt!” O chaŋe ŋɔ, “N naa menee, he bonɔɔ.”

english_verse: David said, “Don't be afraid. I'll be kind to you because Jonathan was your father. I'm going to give you back the land that belonged to your grandfather Saul. Besides that, you will always eat with me at my table.”
translation_verse: Kooro Devid ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Dɛɛ berɛ ɔma, mɛɛ koh he mɛɛ Jonatan waa dɛ́ nyini kɛrɛdɛ. Mɛɛ berɛ he naa Kooro Sɔɔl harɛ la bwaa tɛɛ, ásɛ n ne he pɛ nɔn dɛɛ di kwa saŋ bɛlbwa n dem.”

english_verse: Mephibosheth knelt down again and said, “Why should you care about me? I'm worth no more than a dead dog.”
translation_verse: Asɛ Mɛfebɔsɛt ɡuŋu ja dɛ ŋɔ, “Bɔkwaa men maa ɛ he bonɔɔ, maa wola toole wobɛlbwa bini kɛ nyoate lale, ɛɛ ba wona su he siwi ɔ?”

english_verse: David called in Ziba, Saul's chief servant, and told him, “Since Mephibosheth is Saul's grandson, I've given him back everything that belonged to your master Saul and his family.
translation_verse: Belaa Kooro Devid yerɛ Kooro Sɔɔl bonɔɔ Siba dɛ ŋɔ, “N kpɔ he nomoa komɛlbwa aa ɛ o ne o bii kwaa bwa tɛ o naa Mɛfebɔsɛt.

english_verse: When the kings who had been under Hadadezer's rule saw that Israel had beaten them, they made peace with Israel and accepted David as their ruler. The Arameans were afraid to help Ammon any more.
translation_verse: Koranar baa lɔ Kooro Hadadesa lɔɡa aa naa kɛŋɔ Israel tena pɔ ba nɛɛ la, ba ne Kooro Devid kaa fɔwɛ deŋnesɔɔhna fɔo, dɛ kpɔ ba te do o lɔɡa dɛɛ tomɔ. Gɛɛ a do Siiria tena ɔmɛ, ba ta Amɔn tena chae kpa.

english_verse: David said, “Nahash was kind to me, and I will be kind to his son.” So he sent some officials to the country of Ammon to tell Hanun how sorry he was that his father had died.
translation_verse: Anee Kooro Devid lii ŋɔ, “Mɛɛ kpɔ Kooro Nahas bibaa Hanun daramee, ɡɛ n ne o mɛɛ fa aa kpɔ darame la.” Anomanta, kooro tomɛ toroma o be ba ka bwɛɛlo o mɛɛ seo wa. Toroma la aa tel Kooro Hanun be Amɔn tena harɛ ta la,

english_verse: But Hanun's officials told him, “Do you really believe David is honoring your father by sending these people to comfort you? He probably sent them to spy on our city, so he can destroy it.”
translation_verse: anee Amɔn nomonjena ŋɔ Kooro Hanun be ŋɔ, “He dɛ lii kɛŋɔ duuree Kooro Devid kpɔ dɛɛ tɛ he mɛɛ dɛ tomɛ toroma ŋɔ bá ba bwɛɛle nɔ naa? Toma laa o tom ba ŋɔ bá ba sɔh nyiŋi ya harɛ nɔ, dɛ́ won ba yo yaa dɛ́ pɔ ya nɛ aa?”

english_verse: Hanun arrested David's officials and had their beards shaved off on one side of their faces. He had their robes cut off just below the waist, and then he sent them away.

english_verse: David called the rest of the army together and attacked Rabbah. He captured the city
translation_verse: Anomanta, Kooro Devid boa laa tena la bwa nyoa dɛ la ba ne Bwɛjen Raba dɛ ka yoo ba, dɛ kpɔ bwɛɛ la.

english_verse: David made the people of Rabbah tear down the city walls with iron picks and axes, and then he put them to work making bricks. He did the same thing with all the other Ammonite cities. David went back to Jerusalem, and the people of Israel returned to their homes.
translation_verse: asɛ dɛ lawɛ nɛra baa lɔ bwɛjen la ta, dɛ ɡel baa peɡri daa dɛɛ loɡɛ para ne kpanfɛre, dɛ ɡel baa teŋe berekese ɡe. Gɛɛ o ɛ Amɔn bwɛɛre la bwa ta, asɛ o ne o laa tena la bwa berɛ kaa Jerusalam.

english_verse: David had a beautiful daughter named Tamar, who was the sister of Absalom. She was also the half sister of Amnon, who fell in love with her.
translation_verse: A habɔɔ la, Kooro Devid bibaa Absalɔm dɔ nimambihaah bɛl waa wola yalɛ baa yerɔ Taama, asɛ Kooro Devid bibaa Amnɔn ɛɛ nyinu. Dɛ o wer tolo kɛrɛdɛ.

english_verse: But Tamar was a virgin, and Amnon could not think of a way to be alone with her. He was so upset about it that he made himself sick.
translation_verse: Dɛ Amnɔn sie dɛ lɛ Taama nɛɛ kohona, a ɡel a berɔ weela, dɛkalkɛ a kpeɡri kɛ o dɔɔ, dɛ waa baa bɛlbwa ɡe jemɛ mɔɔ.

english_verse: Amnon had a friend named Jonadab, who was the son of David's brother Shimeah. Jonadab always knew how to get what he wanted,
translation_verse: Kɛ dɛ Amnɔn dɔ dam bɛl baa dɛ yerɔ Jonadab. O mɛɛ sɔne Simea, onee nomoa ka tɛ Kooro Devid lola bini. Dɛ Jonadab keo taeh.

english_verse: and he said to Amnon, “What's the matter? You're the king's son! You shouldn't have to go around feeling sorry for yourself every morning.” Amnon said, “I'm in love with Tamar, my brother Absalom's sister.”
translation_verse: Awola bɛl, Jonadab bɔɔ Amnɔn ŋɔ, “He ɛ kooro bie, kɛ saŋ bɛlbwa n nae naa, a do kɛŋɔ he sie aa lɛ. Bɔkwa waa dɛɛ hae nɔ?” Anee o chaŋe ŋɔ, “N dɛ nyin Taama waa ɛ n dɔɔ Absalɔm nimambihaah la.”

english_verse: Jonadab told him, “Lie down on your bed and pretend to be sick. When your father comes to see you, ask him to send Tamar, so you can watch her cook something for you. Then she can serve you the food.”
translation_verse: Ate, Jonadab ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Saah ka chɔ mpa ta kɛŋɔ he bwara dɛ wee ken. He mɛɛ balɔ ba nae naa, he ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, ‘N dɛ́ soŋe, yerɛ n nimambihaah ó ba tɛ mɛ kondikwa ń di. Ó ba daa kondikwaa la n siwi ta bonɔ, dɛ́ kpɔ tɛ mɛ ń di.’ ”

english_verse: So Amnon went to bed and pretended to be sick. When the king came to see him, Amnon said, “Please, ask Tamar to come over. She can make some special bread while I watch, and then she can serve it to me.”
translation_verse: Anomanta, Amnɔn saahnɔ ka chɔ mpa ta kɛŋɔ o bwara aa dɛ weo ken. Kooro balɔ ba nao asɛ o ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “N dɛ soŋe, ɡel Taama ba dɛ́ ba ɛ n pɛla kondikwaa n siwi ta bonɔ tɛ mɛ, ásɛ n dɔ o nɔn ta kondikwaa di.”

english_verse: David told Tamar, “Go over to Amnon's house and fix him some food.”
translation_verse: Anomanta, Kooro Devid tomɛ nɛra Taama be o koodem bela ŋɔ, “La he dɔɔ Amnɔn be o dem dɛ́ ka daa kondikwaa tɛo.”

english_verse: When she got there, he was lying in bed. She mixed the dough, made the loaves, and baked them while he watched.
translation_verse: Asɛ Taama la Amnɔn be o dem dɛ o chɔɔ. O kpɔ men baa kpɔa dɛɛ ɛ paanoo la ane dɛ koora, dɛ ɛ o pɛla kondikwaa la o siwi ta.

english_verse: Then she took the bread out of the pan and put it on his plate, but he refused to eat it. Amnon said, “Send the servants out of the house.” After they had gone,
translation_verse: O kpɔ kondikwaa la do loɡ bini tɛo, o ŋɔ waa di. Belaa Amnɔn ŋɔ, “Gel nomɛlbwa le bonɔ kaa.” Asɛ nɛra baa lɔ bela bwa kaa.

english_verse: he said to Tamar, “Serve the food in my bedroom.” Tamar picked up the bread that she had made and brought it into Amnon's bedroom.
translation_verse: Belaa Amnɔn ŋɔ Taama be ŋɔ, “Kpɔ kondikwaa la ba tɛ mɛ n chɔɔbɔr, ásɛ n dɔ he nɔn ta kwaa di.” Asɛ o kpɔ kondikwaa la jo dea ka tɛ o dɔɔ Amnɔn.

english_verse: But as she was taking it over to him, he grabbed her and said, “Come to bed with me!”
translation_verse: Waa kpɔa jo ka tɛo la, o ɡuɡru dɛ ŋɔ, “N nimambihaah, ɡel n ne he chɔ.”

english_verse: She answered, “No! Please don't force me! This sort of thing isn't done in Israel. It's disgusting!
translation_verse: Asɛ o ŋɔ o dɔɔ be ŋɔ, “Akai, bɛ men ɡuɡri. A ɡɛ waa nɔ ta chɛ kɛ bá ɛa Israel harɛ nɔ ta! A ɛ wedoŋa kohona.

english_verse: Think of me. I'll be disgraced forever! And think of yourself. Everyone in Israel will say you're nothing but trash! Just ask the king, and he will let you marry me.”
translation_verse: Dɛ a ba ɡɛ naa, ɛrɛɛ mɛɛ ba wona ɡɔɔ nyu nɛra bini nɔ? He ɡe kwaraa la, sihiih ɛɛ kpoe Israel harɛ nɔ ta bwa. N poori, ka bol kooro be mɔɔ, waa sɛh ŋɔ n bɛ hen yalɛ.”

english_verse: But Amnon would not listen to what she said. He was stronger than she was, so he overpowered her and raped her.
translation_verse: Kɛ Amnɔn ta o waa la ta sɛɛh, o bokpeɡa aa ɡwaalo nomanta, o wono ɡuɡru o ne o chɔ.

english_verse: Then Amnon hated her even more than he had loved her before. So he told her, “Get up and get out!”
translation_verse: Belaa Amnɔn berɛ haoh kohona. Kasinteŋ, o haoh dɛ ɡwaa ɡɛ o fa aa dɛ nyinu la. Asɛ o ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Ir le kaa!”

english_verse: She said, “Don't send me away! That would be worse than what you have already done.” But Amnon would not listen.
translation_verse: Anee Taama ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Akai. He doŋ mɛ ŋɔ n le kaa laa, a ɛ wechɔɡa kohona dɛ ɡwaa waa haa kpɔa ɛɛ mɛ nɔ.” Kɛ Amnɔn ta sɛɛh.

english_verse: He called in his servant and said, “Throw this woman out and lock the door!”
translation_verse: O yerɛ o bonɔɔ bɛl dɛ ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Lawɛ haah nɔ le bonɔ kaa dɛ́ laa ɡbera karɛ habɔɔ.”

english_verse: The servant made her leave, and he locked the door behind her. The king's unmarried daughters used to wear long robes with sleeves.
translation_verse: Anomanta, bonɔɔ la lawɔ le dɛ laa ɡbera la laa karɛ habɔɔ. Dɛ o do batakaarejaŋ ondɛɛɡe bɛl. Dɛ ɡɛ batakaani laanee kooro bihaahna baa wola baala jemɛ bwa ɛɛ do.

english_verse: Tamar tore the robe she was wearing and put ashes on her head. Then she covered her face with her hands and cried loudly as she walked away. Absalom Kills Amnon
translation_verse: Taama ɛ tɔɔ do o nyu ta dɛ kɛɛ o batakaarejaŋ ondɛɛɡe la. Dɛ kpɔ nɔɔra dawɛ nyu dɛ wi kohona dɛɛ kaa.

english_verse: Tamar's brother Absalom said to her, “How could Amnon have done such a terrible thing to you! But since he's your brother, don't tell anyone what happened. Just try not to think about it.” Tamar soon moved into Absalom's house, but she was always sad and lonely.
translation_verse: Belaa o dɔɔ Absalɔm bɔɔro ŋɔ, “He dɔɔ Amnɔn la ɡelɔ he ne o chɔ kɛɛ? He te hel n nimambie, he dɔɔree on, bɛ nomɛlbwa be bol.” Asɛ Taama so o dɔɔ dem bela, bambichɔɡ ne.

english_verse: Absalom treated Amnon as though nothing had happened, but he hated Amnon for what he had done to his sister Tamar.
translation_verse: Absalɔm ɡe ta wedɛɛɡe kɛɛ wechɔɡe bɛlbwa bolɛ baɡle Amnɔn, kɛ dɛ o waa lɔ o bini o haoh, dɛkalkɛ o ɡelɔ sihiih kpo o nimambihaah Taama. Absalɔm kpo Amnɔn

english_verse: Two years later, Absalom's servants were cutting wool from his sheep in Baal-Hazor near the town of Ephraim, and Absalom invited all of the king's sons to be there.
translation_verse: Bene anɛ habɔɔ la, Absalɔm nɛra baa dɛ fonɛ o peera lɔ bwɛɛ bɛl baa dɛ yerɔ Baal Hasɔ. O bɛne Efrem dea harɛ jwɛh ta, asɛ o ta nɔn yerɛ kooro bibaala bwa ŋɔ bá ba bela.

english_verse: Then he went to David and said, “My servants are cutting the wool from my sheep. Please come and join us!”
translation_verse: Belaa Absalɔm la kooro be dɛ ka ŋɔ, “N naa, he bonɔɔ dɔ nɛra ba baa fonɛ o peera pona. N poori, he ne he nomonome ɛɛ won ba ja ya nɛ aa?”

english_verse: David answered, “No, my son, we won't go. It would be too expensive for you.” Absalom tried to get him to change his mind, but David did not want to go. He only said that he hoped they would have a good time.
translation_verse: Anee kooro chaŋe ŋɔ, “Akai, n bie, a ta chɛ kɛ ya bwa kaa ka dawɛ he nɛɛ ɡɛ.” Absalɔm soŋe kooro la sie kɛ o ta sɛɛh, kɛ o soŋe andɛɛɡa tɛo.

english_verse: Absalom said, “If you won't go, at least let my brother Amnon come with us.” David asked, “Why should he go with you?”
translation_verse: Ate, Absalɔm berɛ ŋɔ, “A wer, dɛ ɡɛɛ tenaa, tɛ n dɔɔ Amnɔn ŋwɛnɛ ó ba ja ya nɛ.” Asɛ kooro bɔɔro ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ chɛ kɛ ó ba ja he nɛɔ?”

english_verse: But Absalom kept on insisting, and finally David let Amnon and all his other sons go with Absalom. Absalom prepared a banquet fit for a king.
translation_verse: Dɛ Absalɔm ta teŋɔ dɛɛ soŋe, asɛ kooro tɛ Amnɔn ne o bibaala la kar ŋwɛnɛ ba kaa ka ja o nɛ. Absalɔm daa kondikonjena aa chɛ kooro,

english_verse: But he told his servants, “Keep an eye on Amnon. When he gets a little drunk from the wine and is feeling relaxed, I'll give the signal. Then kill him! I've commanded you to do it, so don't be afraid. Be strong and brave.”
translation_verse: dɛ ŋɔ o bonɔɔna be ŋɔ, “Hé ɡel he sie do Amnɔn be ɡɛ saŋ waa nyɔ sen dɛ dɛɛ la, mɛɛ lɔ sie he bee, ásɛ he kpoo. Hé te bɛ ɔmɛ. Mɛɛ lɛ wobɛlbwaa dawɛ n nɛ. He bɛ ɔmɛ, dɛ́ che kiŋkiŋ.”

english_verse: Absalom's servants killed Amnon, just as Absalom had told them. The rest of the king's sons quickly rode away on their mules to escape from Absalom.
translation_verse: Anomanta, o bonɔɔna la teŋɛ o waa waa baɡ ba la ta, dɛ kpo Amnɔn. Belaa kooro bibaala la bwa ir, dɛ kpɔ ba keeɡore dɛ chwa kaa.

english_verse: While they were on their way to Jerusalem, someone told David, “Absalom has killed all of your sons! Not even one is left.”
translation_verse: Ba ta aa lɔ ŋwɛnɛ ta dɛ waa la tɔ sie tel Kooro Devid be kɛŋɔ, “Absalɔm kpoo he bibaala la bwa, beŋkpoŋ kwaraa ta kae.”

english_verse: David got up, and in his sorrow he tore his clothes and lay down on the ground. His servants remained standing, but they tore their clothes too.
translation_verse: Belaa kooro ir che dɛ kɛɛ o laala, dɛ chole harɛ, a baɡle kɛ o loo kuu. O bonɔɔna baa ja o nɛɛ bela la ɡe kɛɛ ba laala.

english_verse: Then David's nephew Jonadab said, “Your Majesty, not all of your sons were killed! Only Amnon is dead. On the day that Amnon raped Tamar, Absalom decided to kill him.
translation_verse: Kɛ Kooro Devid dɔɔ Simea, o bibaa baa dɛ yerɔ Jonadab ŋɔ, “N naa kooro, he bibaala la bwa laa ba kpoo, Amnɔn ɡboo ɛ nɛn waa sewa. He ɡbabir ɛɛ won na kɛŋɔ le ɡɛ saŋ Amnɔn aa ɡuɡri Absalɔm nimambie Taama o ne o chɔ la bwaa o le dɛ dɔ ɡɛ liire nɔ o nyu bini.

english_verse: Don't worry about the report that all your sons were killed. Only Amnon is dead,
translation_verse: Anomanta, n dɔɔ, bɛ waa la yarada kɛŋɔ he bibaala la bwa serewɔ, Amnɔn ɡboo ɛ nɛn waa sewa.”

english_verse: and Absalom has run away.” One of the guards noticed a lot of people coming along the hillside on the road to Horonaim. He went and told the king, “I saw some men coming along Horonaim Road.”
translation_verse: Anɔ bwa la, dɛ Absalɔm chwao. Kooro nɛn waa dɛ daahno la nyiŋo dɛ na nɛra baa wara dɛ do ŋwɛnɛ ta o wee cholibɔr Horonaim pera, deŋɡare bɛl doa. Waa le belaa o la ka ŋɔ kooro be ŋɔ, “N na baala bane baa le deŋɡare la ta Horonaim pera dɛɛ ba.”

english_verse: Jonadab said, “Your Majesty, look! Here come your sons now, just as I told you.”
translation_verse: Anee Jonadab ŋɔ kooro be ŋɔ, “N naa, he bibaala laanee la, a deno ɛ ɡɛ he bonɔɔ aa bola la.”

english_verse: No sooner had he said it, than David's sons came in. They were weeping out loud, and David and all his officials cried just as loudly.
translation_verse: O nyoa aa dena dɛɛ chiɡ, dɛ Kooro Devid bibaala la ɡe deno baa jo dɛɛ wi kohona. Kooro ne o bonɔɔna la bwa ɡe wio kɛrɛdɛ.

english_verse: David still felt so sad over the loss of Amnon that he wanted to take his army there and capture Absalom.
translation_verse: Dɛ kooro bambile lawɔ kɛŋɔ ó la Absalɔm be ka nao, dɛkalkɛ o dɔ bolarawa le Amnɔn seo la ta.

english_verse: Joab knew that David couldn't stop thinking about Absalom,
translation_verse: Dɛ Seruya bibaa Joab na ɡɛ Kooro Devid aa dɛ lii o bibaa Absalɔm wa o bambile ta.

english_verse: The woman from Tekoa went to David. She bowed very low and said, “Your Majesty, please help me!”
translation_verse: Haah baa kaa kpɔɔ le Tekoa la aa la kooro be la, o ba harɛ dɛ kpɔ duure tɛo, dɛ ŋɔ, “N naa kooro, cha mɛ!”

english_verse: David asked, “What's the matter?” She replied: My husband is dead, and I'm a widow.
translation_verse: Belaa Kooro bɔɔro ŋɔ, “Bɔkwa waa dɛɛ hae nɔ?” O chaŋe ŋɔ, “N naa, luhaahnee men, n jaa sewɔ.

english_verse: I had two sons, but they got into a fight out in a field where there was no one to pull them apart, and one of them killed the other.
translation_verse: N naa kooro, men maa ɛ he tolo, dɛ n dɔ bibaala banɛ. Yoi chole ba baah ta awola bɛl kpɔɡ bini, nomɛlbwa toole dɛ larawe ba, asɛ bɛl kpo o dɔŋ.

english_verse: Now all of my relatives have come to me and said, “Hand over your son! We're going to put him to death for killing his brother.” But what they really want is to get rid of him, so they can take over our land. Please don't let them put out my only flame of hope! There won't be anyone left on this earth to carry on my husband's name.
translation_verse: Anomanta, dea bii la bwa cheɡɛ he tolo nɛɛ ŋɔ, ‘Le he bie la waa lɔ o dɔŋ kpo la tɛ yaa ásɛ ya kpoo, o dɔŋ la waa kpoo la wa.’ Ba ɛ ken aa, maa bie bɛlbwaa dɔ kpa. N hwɛɡa bwa ɡe dɛ ba tona, ásɛ n jaa ɡe aa bibaa bɛlbwaa dɔ o sɔn den he kwaraa.”

english_verse: “Go on home,” David told her. “I'll take care of this matter for you.”
translation_verse: Ate, kooro ŋɔ haah la be ŋɔ, “Kaa dem, mɛɛ nyiŋi waa la binii dɛ́ bol tɛɛ.”

english_verse: The woman said, “I hope your decision doesn't cause any problems for you. But if it does, you can blame me.”
translation_verse: Kɛ haah la ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “N naa kooro, ɡel sɔnchɔɡe la dawɛ n ne n mɛɛ lolanar nɛ, ásɛ he bɛ bolchɔɡe bɛlbwa di.”

english_verse: He said, “If anyone gives you trouble, bring them to me, and it won't happen again!”
translation_verse: Ate, kooro chaŋo ŋɔ, “Nomɛlbwa bol wobɛlbwa naa, he ba o ne n be, ásɛ o laa sie kpɔ he nɛ.”

english_verse: “Please,” she replied, “swear by the Lord your God that no one will be allowed to kill my son!” He said, “I swear by the living Lord that no one will touch even a hair on his head!”
translation_verse: Haah la ŋɔ, “Amɔ soŋe Korowii haa dɛ tomɔ, ásɛ n lole waa chɛ kɛ ó kpo nɛn waa kpo o dɔŋ bɔ kem la, o bɛ wechɔɡa kohona ba ɛ, n binɛɛte la kpoe wa.” Anee kooro chaŋe ŋɔ, “N ŋwɛɛ Korowii waa lole kɛŋɔ, wobɛlbwa aa he bie la ɛɛ ba.”

english_verse: The woman said: Haven't you been hurting God's people? Your own son had to leave the country. And when you judged in my favor, it was the same as admitting that you should have let him come back.
translation_verse: Anee haah la ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ he ɛ Korowii nɛra waa aa wola were ken nɔɔ? He ta ɡelɛ he ɡbaɡba bie baa lawɔ laa ta kaa bojaŋ harɛfale ta berɛ ba, anomanta, he ɡbaɡba nyoa wobol pae bolchɔɡe.

english_verse: We each must die and disappear like water poured out on the ground. But God doesn't take our lives. Instead, he figures out ways of bringing us back when we run away.
translation_verse: Ya bwa ɛɛ serewoo kɛŋɔ baa fuɡe nee ta aa palɛ harɛ, baa wola won berɛ boa a nyoa kpa la ken. Kɛ Korowii aa ɡel nɛn waa sewa berɛ ba mkpa ta, kɛ kooro fe ɛɛ won che ŋwɛnɛ bɛl ta, dɛ́ ɡel nɛn baa lawɔ laa ta kaa bojaŋ harɛfale ta berɛ ba o harɛ ta.

english_verse: Your Majesty, I came here to tell you about my problem, because I was afraid of what someone might do to me. I decided to come to you, because I thought you could help.
translation_verse: N balɔ taraken dɛ́ ba bol waa nɔ n naa kooro be, dɛkalkɛ aahraa nɛra la aah mɛ. He tolo liiro ŋɔ, ‘Mɛɛ ba ŋɔ kooro bee, o ken ɛɛ no n waa tɛ mɛ.

english_verse: In fact, I knew that you would listen and save my son and me from those who want to take the land that God gave us.
translation_verse: N naa kooro ken ɛɛ sɛoh dɛ́ lɛ o tolo le nɛn waa dɛ nyin o kpo n ne n bie le harɛ Korowii aa kpɔa tɛ yaa nɔ ta.’

english_verse: I can rest easy now that you have given your decision. You know the difference between right and wrong just like an angel of God, and I pray that the Lord your God will be with you.
translation_verse: N berɔ lii ja kɛŋɔ, hɛɛ ɡeloo n dɔ bosɔɔhna, dɛkalkɛŋɔ he do kɛŋɔ Korowii torome, he jemɛ wechɔɡa ne wedɛɛɡa. Korowii haa dɛ tomɔ la ja he nɛ.”

english_verse: Then David said to the woman, “Now I'm going to ask you a question, and don't try to hide the truth!” The woman replied, “Please go ahead, Your Majesty.”
translation_verse: Anee kooro chaŋe haah la ŋɔ, “N dɛ nyin n bɔɔre waane, ásɛ he ɡel ń jemɛ a kasinteŋ bwa.” Ate, o chaŋe ŋɔ, “N naa, wobɛlbwa haa dɔa la, bɔɔ mɛ.”

english_verse: David asked, “Did Joab put you up to this?” The woman answered, “Your Majesty, I swear by your life that no one can hide the truth from you. Yes, Joab did tell me what to say,
translation_verse: Asɛ kooro la bɔɔ ŋɔ, “Joab nɔn toole waa nɔ ta naa?” Anee o ŋɔ, “N naa kooro, n ŋwɛɛ Korowii waa lole kɛŋɔ, nomɛlbwa aa won kpɔ waa aa ɛ kasinteŋ sɔeh. Kpelaa, he bonɔɔ Joab, onee chaɡ mɛ ɡɛ maa ɛ, ne anɔ la maa bol bwa.

english_verse: but only to show you the other side of this problem. You must be as wise as the angel of God to know everything that goes on in this country.”
translation_verse: He bonɔɔ Joab ɛ ɡɛ dɛ́ fee berɛ waa nɔ sie. N dɔɔ, he dɔ wejema kɛŋɔ Korowii torome, dɛ jemɛ wobɛlbwa aa dɛ chiɡ harɛ nɔ ta bobɛlbwa.”

english_verse: David turned to Joab and said, “It seems that I have already given my decision. Go and bring Absalom back.”
translation_verse: A habɔɔ la, kooro ŋɔ Joab be ŋɔ, “A wer, mɛɛ ɛo. Kaa, dɛ́ ka kpɔ Absalɔm ba.”

english_verse: Joab bowed very low and said, “Your Majesty, I thank you for giving your permission. It shows that you approve of me.”
translation_verse: Belaa Joab chole dɛ kpɔ sie pi harɛ Kooro Devid sie, dɛ kpɔ duure tɛo, dɛ soŋe andɛɛɡa tɛ kooro! O ŋɔ, “N nao kɛŋɔ he sie lɛo, dɛkalkɛ he ɛ waa maa dɛ nyin tɛ mɛ.”

english_verse: Joab went to Geshur to get Absalom. But when they came back to Jerusalem,
translation_verse: Belaa Joab ir dɛ la Gesur ka kpɔ Absalɔm ba Jerusalam.

english_verse: David told Joab, “I don't want to see my son Absalom. Tell him to stay away from me.” So Absalom went to his own house without seeing his father. Absalom Was Handsome
translation_verse: Anee kooro ŋɔ, “A ta chɛ kɛ Absalɔm so koodem bonɔ, maa nyin kɛ n siwi nao, ó kaa o dem ka so.” Anomanta, Absalɔm kaa so o dem, o ta kooro sie laŋɛ.

english_verse: His hair grew so thick and heavy that when he got it cut once a year, it weighed over two kilograms.
translation_verse: Bena bɛlbwaa wɛɛ fonɛ o nyu, o nyumpona waa fona la ɡbo tɔɡre ɛɛ ɡwaa kilore anɛɛ, ɡɛ kooro aa maɡa bil harɛ la ta.

english_verse: Absalom had three sons. He also had a daughter named Tamar, who grew up to be very beautiful. Absalom Finally Sees David
translation_verse: Bibaala batoro ne bihaah beŋkpoŋii Absalɔm lolɛ. Bihaah la sɔne Taama. Dɛ o wer tolo kɛrɛdɛ.

english_verse: Absalom lived in Jerusalem for two years without seeing his father.
translation_verse: Absalɔm soɡe Jerusalam bene anɛ dɛ o siwi ta kooro nɛɛ dawɛ.

english_verse: He wanted Joab to talk to David for him. So one day he sent a message asking Joab to come over, but Joab refused. Absalom sent another message, but Joab still refused.
translation_verse: Belaa Absalɔm tomɛ ba ka yerɛ Joab, ásɛ o tomɔ kooro be. Kɛ o vɛoh, o ta balɛ. O berɔ tomɛ nɛɛtena ŋɔ bá ka yerɔ, o ta balɛ ja.

english_verse: Finally, Absalom told his servants, “Joab's barley field is right next to mine. Go set it on fire!” And they did.
translation_verse: Anomanta, Absalɔm ŋɔ o bonɔɔna be ŋɔ, “He nao kɛŋɔ Joab koo teŋɛ n kon ta asɛ o du mea. Hé la dɛ́ ka kpaa nii do o ta.” Anomanta, o bonɔɔna la laŋɔ dɛ ka kpaa nii do koo la ta.

english_verse: Joab went to Absalom's house and demanded, “Why did your servants set my field on fire?”
translation_verse: A habɔɔ, Joab la Absalɔm dem dɛ ka bɔɔro ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ he ɡel he bonɔɔna ka fuh n koo nɔɔ?”

english_verse: Absalom answered, “You didn't pay any attention when I sent for you. I want you to ask my father why he told me to come back from Geshur. I was better off there. I want to see my father now! If I'm guilty, let him kill me.”
translation_verse: Anee Absalɔm chaŋo ŋɔ, “N tomɔ ŋɔ bá ka ŋɔ he be ŋɔ he ba ásɛ n tomɛ kooro be, dɛ́ fee ka bɔɔro ŋɔ, ‘Bɔkwa waa n le Gesur ba bonɔ nɔ? A wer kɛ n fe ta aa soɡe bela!’ N dɛ nyin kɛŋɔ n la kooro sie, dɛ bolchɔɡe bɛlbwa kwaraa n di aa, he ɡel o kpo mɛ.”

english_verse: Joab went to David and told him what Absalom had said. David sent for Absalom, and Absalom came. He bowed very low, and David leaned over and kissed him.
translation_verse: Anomanta, Joab la Kooro Devid be dɛ ka bol waa nɔ baɡlo. Belaa o yerɛ Absalɔm o ba ɡuŋi o sie, asɛ kooro jaamo dɛ ɡbaaro pɛl o te.

english_verse: Some time later, Absalom got himself a chariot with horses to pull it, and he had
translation_verse: A habɔɔ la, Absalɔm nyin torɔɡo baa vɔwa dɛɛ pɛl jaɡre la bɛl ne jaɡre, dɛ baala fifraanue baa tɔ o sie.

english_verse: He would get up early each morning and wait by the side of the road that led to the city gate. Anyone who had a complaint to bring to King David would have to go that way, and Absalom would ask each of them, “Where are you from?” If they said, “I'm from a tribe in the north,”
translation_verse: Absalɔm yon fel ir chɔmbibi, dɛ́ ka che ŋwɛnɛ waa chɔa kaa bwɛjen la doonyoa la keŋkeŋ. Dɛ nomɛl ba waa ne dɛɛ nyin kooro nyiŋi a ta tɛo waa, o yon yerɛ naate dɛ́ bɔɔro bela waa lea. Dɛ naate chaŋo ŋɔ o le Israel deene la bɛl bini naa,

english_verse: Absalom would say, “You deserve to win your case. It's too bad the king doesn't have anyone to hear complaints like yours.
translation_verse: o yon ŋɔ naate be ŋɔ, “He waa la wer dɛ toɡre, kɛ kooro nachiɡnɛn bɛlbwa toole dɛ́ no he waa nɔ.”

english_verse: Whenever anyone came to Absalom and started bowing down, he would reach out and hug and kiss them.
translation_verse: Dɛ nomɛlbwa ba Absalɔm sie dɛ ba ɡuŋu waa, ó yon ha nɔn lawɛ naate dɛ́ ɡbaaro pɛl o te.

english_verse: That's how he treated everyone from Israel who brought a complaint to the king. Soon everyone in Israel liked Absalom better than they liked David.
translation_verse: Dɛ ɡɛɛ wɛɛ ɛ Israel tena bwa ba yon kpɔ ba waa ba kooro be ŋɔ ó nyiŋi a ta tɛɛ ba la, asɛ ba bwa berɛ dɛɛ nyin o wa.

english_verse: Four years later, Absalom said to David, “Please, let me go to Hebron. I have to keep a promise that I made to the Lord,
translation_verse: Bene anaarɛ habɔɔ la, Absalɔm ŋɔ Kooro Devid be ŋɔ, “Tɛ mɛ ŋwɛnɛ ń la Bwɛjen Hɛbrɔn, dɛ́ ka chuɡri n nyobaɡa maa baɡɛ Korowii.

english_verse: when I was living with the Arameans in Geshur. I promised that if the Lord would bring me back to live in Jerusalem, I would worship him in Hebron.”
translation_verse: Gɛ saŋ he bonɔɔ fa aa lɔ Gesur Siiria harɛ ta la, n baɡɛ nyoa ŋɔ, ‘Dɛ Korowii wono berɛ kpɔ mɛ ba Jerusalam aa, mɛɛ tomɔɔ Hɛbrɔn.’ ”

english_verse: David gave his permission, and Absalom went to Hebron.
translation_verse: Belaa kooro ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Kaa deŋnesɔɔhna ne.” Asɛ o kaa Hɛbrɔn.

english_verse: A messenger came and told David, “Everyone in Israel is on Absalom's side!”
translation_verse: Awola bɛl, torome bɛl baa ŋɔ Kooro Devid be ŋɔ, “Israel tena bwa bambile lawɛ Absalɔm waa dɛɛ teŋɛ o nɛ.”

english_verse: David's officials were in Jerusalem with him, and he told them, “Let's get out of here! We'll have to leave soon, or none of us will escape from Absalom. Hurry! If he moves fast, he could catch us while we're still here. Then he will kill us and everyone else in the city.”
translation_verse: Belaa Kooro Devid ŋɔ o nomonome baa ja o nɛɛ Jerusalam la be ŋɔ, “Hé dɛ nyin ya chwa le Absalɔm be tenaa, hé ɡel ya le warane! Dɛ ɡɛ laa aa, waa biɡri ba bonɔ ba yo yaa, dɛ́ kpoo nɛra yaa lɔ bwɛjen nɔ bini bwa.”

english_verse: The officials said, “Your Majesty, we'll do whatever you say.”
translation_verse: Anee nomonome la chaŋe ŋɔ, “N naa kooro, wobɛlbwa haa ŋɔa la, he bonɔɔna ɛɛ ɛo.”

english_verse: Then David stood there and watched while his regular troops and his bodyguards marched past. The last group was the
translation_verse: O nɛra la bwa baa ɡarɔ ta kaa sie, bane Kɛrɛt tena ne Pɛlet tena baa dɛ daahno dɛ Giti tena baa le Gat, dɛ nɛra lafraanumɛl baa teŋɛ o nɛɛ la bwa tɔ o sie baa kaa.

english_verse: David spoke to Ittai and said, “You're a foreigner from the town of Gath. You don't have to leave with us. Go back and join the new king!
translation_verse: Belaa Kooro Devid bɔɔ Itai, Giti te waa le Gat la ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ he teŋɛ ya nɛɔ? Berɛ ka so Kooro Absalɔm be. He ɛ hɔɔh haa le harɛfale ta dɛ ba so bonɔ.

english_verse: You haven't been with me very long, so why should you have to follow me, when I don't even know where I'm going? Take your soldiers and go back. I pray that the Lord will be kind and faithful to you.”
translation_verse: Dɛ tɔpere nɔ ɡbosoroo he den ba. Maa wola jemɛ bela maa dɛ kaa nɔ, ɛrɛɛ mɛɛ ba wona ɡel he teŋɛ ya nɛɛ dɛɛ ɡaaɡe ɔ? Berɛ kaa ka tɔ he nɛra sie. Kórowii sune he nɛ, dɛ́ chae.”

english_verse: Ittai answered, “Your Majesty, just as surely as you and the Lord live, I will go where you go, no matter if it costs me my life.”
translation_verse: Anee Itai chaŋe kooro ŋɔ, “N ŋwɛɛ Korowii waa lole saŋ bɛlbwa ne n dɔɔ kooro o ta aa soɡe le kɛŋɔ, bobɛlbwa n dɔɔ kooro aa kaa, dɛ sewee kɛɛ mkpaa yoo, belaa men maa ɛ o bonɔɔ ɡe ɛɛ ba doe.”

english_verse: “Then come on!” David said. So Ittai and all his men and their families walked on past David. David Sends the Sacred Chest Back to Jerusalem
translation_verse: Kooro Devid ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “A wer, he te pa sie dɛɛ la.” Anomanta, Itai Giti te waa le Gat la ne baala la, dɛ o lolanar baa ja o nɛɛ bwa pa sie kaa.

english_verse: The people of Jerusalem were crying and moaning as David and everyone with him passed by. He led them across Kidron Valley and along the road toward the desert.
translation_verse: Nɛra la bwa aa teŋa baa kaa ɡɛ la, bwɛɛ la tena bwa wio kɛrɛdɛ. Kooro ɡe ɛɡɛ Kedrɔn Fɛlembɔjen la le, asɛ o nɛra la bwa kpɔ sie pa pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta dɛ kaa.

english_verse: Zadok and Abiathar the priests were there along with several men from the tribe of Levi who were carrying the sacred chest. They set the chest down, and left it there until David and his followers had gone out of the city.
translation_verse: Dɛ sɔfo Sadɔk lɔ bela, asɛ Lewi dea tena bwa baa ja o nɛɛ la che Korowii Ne Nɛwɛnyina Fɔo Daka la. Ba kpɔɔ cheɡ harɛ, asɛ sɔfo Abiata kpoo kwaa ɛ saraha ka tel kɛŋɔ Kooro Devid ne o nɛra la bwa aa le bwɛjen la ta.

english_verse: Then David said: Zadok, take the sacred chest back to Jerusalem. If the Lord is pleased with me, he will bring me back and let me see it and his tent again.
translation_verse: Belaa Kooro Devid ŋɔ sɔfo Sadɔk be ŋɔ, “Berɛ kpɔ Korowii Ne Nɛwɛnyina Fɔo Daka la kaa bwɛjen la ta. Dɛ Korowii sie lɛ n nɛ aa, wɛɛ berɔɔ kpɔ mɛ ba, dɛ́ ɡel n nao ne bela waa cheɡa bwa.

english_verse: But if he says he isn't pleased with me, then let him do what he knows is best.
translation_verse: Kɛ o sie ta n nɛɛ lɛɛ yaa, ó ɛ ɡɛ bwa aa too o tea.”

english_verse: Zadok, you are a good judge of things, so return to the city and don't cause any trouble. Take your son Ahimaaz with you. Abiathar and his son Jonathan will also go back.
translation_verse: Kooro Devid berɔ ŋɔ sɔfo Sadɔk be ŋɔ, “He dɛ no waa mun. Lawɛ he bibaa Ahimas ne Abiata bibaa Jonatan, ásɛ he berɛ kaa bwɛjen la ta deŋnesɔɔhna ta.

english_verse: I'll wait at the river crossing in the desert until I hear from you.
translation_verse: Mɛɛ dɛɛ kpa leebɔɔ baa cheɡɛ o ta le dɛɛ kaa pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta belaa, ka tel kɛŋɔ maa no waane le he be.”

english_verse: Zadok and Abiathar took the sacred chest back into Jerusalem and stayed there.
translation_verse: Anomanta, Sadɔk ne Abiata baa ɛ sɔfore berɔ kpɔ Korowii Ne Nɛwɛnyina Fɔo Daka la kaa Jerusalam dɛ ka so bela.

english_verse: David went on up the slope of the Mount of Olives. He was barefoot and crying, and he covered his head to show his sorrow. Everyone with him was crying, and they covered their heads too.
translation_verse: Kooro Devid teŋɔ teeh kaa Ɔlevere Bwejen la doa dɛ kaa wi, o kpɔ kon bɔle nyu dɛɛ valɛ nakpapɛɛ, a baɡle kɛ o loo kuu. Nɛra baa ja o nɛɛ la bwa ɡe kpɔ kwaa tɔ nyuune dɛ wi teŋɛ, dɛ teeh dɛɛ kaa.

english_verse: Someone told David, “Ahithophel is helping Absalom plot against you!” David said, “Please, Lord, keep Ahithophel's plans from working!” David Sends Hushai Back as a Spy
translation_verse: Dɛ ba ŋɔ Kooro Devid be kɛŋɔ Ahetofɛl ja Absalɔm nɛra o ne baa dɛ vɔrɔwe waa la nɛ. Anomanta, Kooro soŋɔ ŋɔ, “N Naa Korowii, ɡel Ahetofɛl liire bwa berɛ wepuu.”

english_verse: When David reached the top of the Mount of Olives, he met Hushai the Archite at a place of worship. Hushai's robe was torn, and dust was on his head.
translation_verse: Kooro Devid aa tel bwe la doa, bela nɛra yon dɛɛ tomɛ Korowii la, dɛ Husai waa ɛ Aaki te lɔ bela, dɛ ba chemo. Dɛ o batakaare kɛɛrɔ, asɛ teera su o nyu bwa.

english_verse: David told him: If you come with me, you might slow us down.
translation_verse: Anee Kooro Devid ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “He ŋɔ hɛɛ teŋɛ n nɛɛ kaa laa, aa tɔnɔ bɛlbwaa dɔ tɛ mɛ.

english_verse: Go back into the city and tell Absalom, “Your Majesty, I am your servant. I will serve you now, just as I served your father in the past.” Hushai, if you do that, you can help me ruin Ahithophel's plans.
translation_verse: Waa haa ɛ á won cha mɛ laanee kɛ, he berɛ kaa bwɛjen la ta, dɛ́ ka ŋɔ Absalɔm be kɛŋɔ taraken te hɛɛ berɔ tomɔ kasinteŋ ne, ɡɛ haa tomɛ o mɛɛ la. Ásɛ he takapɔ kɛŋɔ Ahetofɛl liire bɛlbwa waa ba a ne la, hɛɛ lɔɔ ta.

english_verse: Zadok and Abiathar the priests will be there with you, and you can tell them everything you hear in the palace.
translation_verse: Sadɔk ne Abiata baa ɛ sɔfore bwa ɛɛ do he be belaa, wobɛlbwa haa no kooro dem bela la, bol ba be.

english_verse: Then they can send their sons Ahimaaz and Jonathan to tell me what you've heard.
translation_verse: Dɛ sɔfo Sadɔk bibaa Ahimas ne Sɔfo Abiata bibaa Jonatan ja ba nɛɛ bela. He dɔ wobɛlbwa naa, hɛɛ won tom ba n be ba ba bol.”

english_verse: David's advisor Hushai slipped back into Jerusalem, at just about the same time Absalom was coming in.
translation_verse: Gɛɛ a do, asɛ Kooro Devid dam Husai berɛ kaa bwɛjen Jerusalam, dɛ namee Absalɔm ɡe den dɛɛ jo bwɛɛ la bini.

english_verse: David had started down the other side of the Mount of Olives, when he was met by Ziba, the chief servant of Mephibosheth. Ziba had two donkeys that were carrying
translation_verse: Kooro Devid aa kaa sie tama bwe la doa la, Mɛfebɔsɛt bonɔɔ Siba den le bela ba chemo. Dɛ o dɔ keeɡore ane, dɛ kpɔ paanoo lafraanɛ ne ɡrepo daa nɔna aa hola nɔndela lafa, ne fiɡ daa nɔna aa hola nɔndela lafa, dɛ sen oltɔn pur del.

english_verse: “What's all this?” David asked. Ziba said, “The donkeys are for your family to ride. The bread and fruit are for the people to eat, and the wine is for them to drink in the desert when they are tired out.”
translation_verse: Asɛ Kooro Devid bɔɔ Siba ŋɔ, “Bɔkwaa hɛɛ la ka ɛ anɔ bwa ne nɔ?” Ate, o chaŋe ŋɔ, “N naa kooro, keeɡore nɔ ɛ hen n naa kooro ne he haahna, ne bii bwa kwa, ásɛ baa so a ta. Paanoo la ne daa nɔna nɔ ɡe ɛ kwaa baala nɔ aa di, asɛ sen la ɡe, banɔ la baa ka ɡwɛɡre pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta la nyɔ dɛ́ do kpeɡri.”

english_verse: “And where is Mephibosheth?” David asked. Ziba answered, “He stayed in Jerusalem, because he thinks the people of Israel want him to rule the kingdom of his grandfather Saul.”
translation_verse: Belaa kooro bɔɔ ŋɔ, “Leperaa he nomoa naa Mɛfebɔsɛt la dɔɔ?” Anee Siba chaŋo ŋɔ, “O soɡe Jerusalam dɛkalkɛ o liiro ŋɔ, ‘Fini Israel tena ɛɛ berɔ kpɔ mɛ cheɡ n nabaa Kooro Sɔɔl naa ta, ń di kora.’ ”

english_verse: David then told him, “Everything that used to belong to Mephibosheth is now yours.” Ziba said, “Your Majesty, I am your humble servant, and I hope you will be pleased with me.” Shimei Curses David
translation_verse: Ate, kooro ŋɔ Siba be ŋɔ, “N dɛ ŋɔ he be kɛŋɔ komɛlbwa aa ɛ Mɛfebɔsɛt kwaa la ɛ he kwaa taraken.” Asɛ Siba ŋɔ, “N dɛ duuri, N naa kooro, ɡel he sie lɛ men maa ɛ he bonɔɔ nɛ.” Simei taah Kooro Devid

english_verse: David was near the town of Bahurim when a man came out and started cursing him. The man was Shimei the son of Gera, and he was one of Saul's distant relatives.
translation_verse: Kooro Devid aa baa tel bwɛɛ Bahurim la, Gɛra bibaa Simei waa le dea Kooro Sɔɔl aa le o ta balɔ ba chemo. Waa lea dɛɛ ba dɛ o dɛ taahno.

english_verse: He threw stones at David, at his soldiers, and at everyone else, including the bodyguards who walked on each side of David.
translation_verse: Dɛ a lole kɛŋɔ Kooro laa tena ne nɛra baa dɛ daahno bwa baro cheme te, kɛ dɛ Simei dɛ foɡre o ne o nomonome bwa bwea,

english_verse: Shimei was yelling at David, “Get out of here, you murderer! You good-for-nothing,
translation_verse: Simei taahno dɛ ŋɔ, “Le bonɔ kaa! Le bonɔ kaa! Nɛŋkpoa nɛn bɛl le! Wechɔɡ-ɛɛ kohona!

english_verse: the Lord is paying you back for killing so many in Saul's family. You stole his kingdom, but now the Lord has given it to your son Absalom. You're a murderer, and that's why you're in such big trouble!”
translation_verse: Korowiirii bɔe kem Kooro Sɔɔl dem nɛra haa kpoora dɛ ba so o buɡ ta la. Korowii kpɔ he kora la tɛ he bibaa Absalɔm. He kora chɔɡɔ, nyubinikpeɡ haa ɛa kohona dɛ kpoo nɛra la wa.”

english_verse: Abishai said, “Your Majesty, this man is as useless as a dead dog! He shouldn't be allowed to curse you. Let me go over and chop off his head.”
translation_verse: Belaa Abisae baa dɛ yerɛ o nya Seruya la ŋɔ kooro be ŋɔ, “N naa, ɛrɛɛ he ɡel nɛn waa wola toole wobɛlbwa bini kɛ nyoate lale ɡe ɛɛ taahne ken? Gel n la ka teŋe o nyu le bela!”

english_verse: David replied, “What will I ever do with you and your brother Joab? If Shimei is cursing me because the Lord has told him to, then who are you to tell him to stop?”
translation_verse: Ate, kooro ŋɔ, “Abisae ne Joab, bɔkwa waa n ne he dɔ ɛɛ yɔ? Dɛ Korowiirii ŋɔa Abisae taah men Devid aa, umee dɛ́ won bɔɔ ŋɔ ɛrɛ waa wɛɛ ɛ ken ɔ?”

english_verse: Then David said to Abishai and all his soldiers: My own son is trying to kill me! Why shouldn't this man from the tribe of Benjamin want me dead even more? Let him curse all he wants. Maybe the Lord did tell him to curse me.
translation_verse: Belaa Kooro Devid ŋɔ Abisae ne o nomonome la bwa be ŋɔ, “N bilole ɡbabir dɛ nyin mɛ dɛ́ kpo, ɛrɛɛ he ɡel Bɛnjamen dea nɛn nɔ wa ɛɛ ɛɛ nyokpoa ɔ? Hé ɡelo wɛɛ taah, Korowiirii tɛo ŋwɛnɛ.

english_verse: But if the Lord hears these curses and sees the trouble I'm in, maybe he will have pity on me instead.
translation_verse: Korowii ken ɛɛ na n suna maa dɛ di nɔɔ, dɛ́ kpɔ wedɛɛɡa ba chiɡ taahna aa dɛ ba n nɛɛ fini nɔ naa ta.”

english_verse: David and the others went on down the road. Shimei went along the hillside by the road, cursing and throwing rocks and dirt at them.
translation_verse: Kooro Devid ne o nɛra kpɔ ŋwɛnɛ la ta dɛɛ kaa, asɛ Simei ɡe kpɔ deŋɡare la ta ba baŋ bɛl dɛɛ taah, dɛɛ foɡ ba bwea, dɛ ɡo tee dɛɛ ta ba nɛ.

english_verse: When David and those with him came to the Jordan River, they were tired out. But after they rested, they felt much better. Hushai Meets Absalom
translation_verse: Kooro ne nɛra baa ja o nɛɛ la bwa koɔh ken ɡɛ saŋ baa kaa tel Jɔɔdan Moo ta, asɛ dɛ onɛ. Absalɔm la Jerusalam

english_verse: By this time, Absalom, Ahithophel, and the others had reached Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Absalɔm ne Israel tena bwa ba Jerusalam, dɛ Ahetofɛl ja ba bini.

english_verse: David's friend Hushai came to Absalom and said, “Long live the king! Long live the king!”
translation_verse: Belaa Husai waa ɛ Aaki te, Kooro Devid dam la, la Absalɔm be dɛ ka ŋɔ, “Korowii tɛ kooro mkpajaŋ! Korowii tɛ kooro mkpajaŋ!”

english_verse: But Absalom asked Hushai, “Is this how you show loyalty to your friend David? Why didn't you go with him?”
translation_verse: Anee Absalɔm bɔɔ Husai ŋɔ, “He nyina haa dɛ chaɡle he dam Kooro Devid nɛɛ nɔ naa? Ɛrɛɛ he ne waa wola kaalɛ ɔ?”

english_verse: Hushai answered, “The Lord and the people of Israel have chosen you to be king. I can't leave. I have to stay and serve the one they've chosen.
translation_verse: Ate, Husai ɡe ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Akai, nɛn Korowii ne Israel tena nɔ bwa aa leo la, o nɛɛ mɛɛ ba teŋa n ne ó do le.

english_verse: Besides, it seems right for me to serve you, just as I served your father.” Ahithophel's Advice
translation_verse: Dɛ Absalɔm laa ń tomaa, umee ń tomɛ jaɔ? Gɛ maa tomɛ he mɛɛ la, ɡɛɛ mɛɛ ba he ɡe toma.”

english_verse: Absalom turned to Ahithophel and said, “Give us your advice! What should we do?”
translation_verse: Ate, Absalɔm ŋɔ Ahetofɛl be ŋɔ, “Yaa lɔ bonɔ nɔ, baɡle yaa ɡɛ yaa ɛ.”

english_verse: Ahithophel answered, “Some of your father's wives were left here to take care of the palace. You should have sex with them. Then everyone will find out that you have publicly disgraced your father. This will make you and your followers even more powerful.”
translation_verse: Anee Ahetofɛl chaŋe ŋɔ, “La ka lawɛ he mɛɛ sɛnanar waa ɡel ba habɔɔ baa daah koodem la he ne ba chɔ. Anee dɛ́ ɡel Israel tena bwa no kɛŋɔ he ɛ he mɛɛ dɔm kɛrɛdɛ, dɛ́ ɡel nɛra baa ja he nɛɛ la bwara do kpeɡri name.”

english_verse: Absalom had a tent set up on the flat roof of the palace, and everyone watched as he went into the tent with his father's wives.
translation_verse: Anomanta, ba baŋre tɛnte dea koodem bela saldoa tɛ Absalɔm, asɛ o lawɛ o mɛɛ sɛnanar la chɔ Israel tena la bwa siwi ta.

english_verse: Ahithophel gave such good advice in those days that both Absalom and David thought it came straight from God.
translation_verse: Saŋ la, dɛ Ahetofɛl bol wobɛlbwa naa, Kooro Devid ne Absalɔm dɛ yaradao kɛŋɔ a ɛ waa waa bɔɔra le Korowii be.

english_verse: and we will all go to fight David wherever he is. We will fall on him just as dew falls and covers the ground. He and all his soldiers will die!
translation_verse: Ásɛ bobɛlbwa Kooro Devid aa lole la, yaa ɡaaɡe o bɔree dɛ́ nao, o ne jara dɛ ya kaa yoo. O ne o laa tena la bini bɛlbwa toole dɛ́ ka.

english_verse: while he is tired and discouraged. He will panic, and everyone with him will run away. I won't kill anyone except David,
translation_verse: Mɛɛ lao ka lɔ tɔ o nɛ ɡɛ saŋ waa koah dɛ ɡwɛɡre. A ba ɡɛ naa, ɔmee ɛɛ chole o nɛɛ, ásɛ o nɛra baa ja o nɛɛ la bwa chwa kaa. Mɛɛ kpo Kooro Devid ɡboo,

english_verse: since he's the one you want to get rid of. Then I'll bring the whole nation back to you like a bride coming home to her husband. This way there won't be a civil war. Hushai Fools Absalom
translation_verse: dɛ́ berɛ lawɛ nɛra la bwa ba tɛɛ. Naate haa dɛ nyinu la sewaa, anee dɛ́ baɡle kɛ nɛra la bwa berɔ ba he be, wobɛlbwa toole dɛ́ ba ba nɛ.”

english_verse: Absalom and all the leaders of the tribes of Israel agreed that Ahithophel had a good plan.
translation_verse: Absalɔm ne Israel nomonome la bwa lii a ɡɛ waa nɔ kɛŋɔ a ɛ wedɛɛɡa.

english_verse: Then Absalom said, “Bring in Hushai the Archite. Let's hear what he has to say.”
translation_verse: Anee Absalɔm ŋɔ, “Yerɛ Husai Aaki te la, ásɛ ya no waa waa dɔa dɛ bol.”

english_verse: Hushai came in, and Absalom told him what Ahithophel had planned. Then Absalom said, “Should we do what he says? And if we shouldn't, can you come up with anything better?”
translation_verse: Husai aa bala la, Absalɔm ŋɔ, “Waa Ahetofɛl aa baɡle yaa laanee nɔ. Yá teŋɛ a ta naa? Dɛ ɡɛ laa aa, ɛrɛɛ he liire ɔ?”

english_verse: Hushai said: This time Ahithophel's advice isn't so good.
translation_verse: Anee Husai chaŋo ŋɔ, “Waa Ahetofɛl aa baɡla la aa were tɛ yaa taraken.

english_verse: You know that your father and his followers are real warriors. Now they are as fierce as a mother bear whose cubs have just been killed. Besides, your father has a lot of experience in fighting wars, and he won't be spending the night with the others.
translation_verse: He ɡbabir jemɛ ɡɛ he mɛɛ ne o laa tena aa kpeɡa dɛ won yoi. Ba kpeɡri dɛ do ɔma kɛŋɔ sisire hansɔɔh baa pa o bii kaa ken. He mɛɛ jemɛ yoi waa kɛrɛdɛ, waa sɛh so o ne o laa tena so jwaana beŋkpoŋ ɡba.

english_verse: He has probably already found a hiding place in a cave or somewhere else. As soon as anyone hears that some of your soldiers have been killed, everyone will think your whole army has been destroyed.
translation_verse: Maa dɛ ŋɔ nɔ, o ka sɔh bwebɔɔ bɛl bini kɛɛ bobɛl kwara. O tɔ sie kpɔ o laa tena ba yoi asɛ nomɛlbwa no a wa aa, wɛɛ ŋɔɔ o pɔ he nɛ.

english_verse: Then even those who are as brave as a lion will lose their courage. All Israel knows what a great warrior your father is and what brave soldiers he has.
translation_verse: Hale banyoola baa do ɔma kɛŋɔ nyujente ɡba la dɛ ɔmɔ, dɛkalkɛ nomɛlbwa waa lɔ Israel harɛ ta jemɔ kɛ he mɛɛ ɛ banyoo tenten, o laa tena ɡe do kpeɡri.

english_verse: My advice is to gather all the fighting men of Israel from the town of Dan in the north down to the town of Beersheba in the south. You will have more soldiers than there are grains of sand on the seashore. Absalom, you should lead them yourself,
translation_verse: Anomanta, waa maa dɛ bol laanee kɛŋɔ, he boa Israel tena nyoa le Dan dea waa lɔ weekaŋle nyundua pera, dɛ́ ba kaa Beɛseeba waa lɔ weekaŋle harɛbɔr baa wara kɛŋɔ mpo nyoa hɛŋle dɛ do harɛ la bobɛlbwa, ásɛ he ɡbaɡba tɔ ba sie la ba ne laa.
