english_verse: If they go into a walled town, we will put ropes around that town and drag it into the river. We won't leave even one small piece of a stone.
translation_verse: Dɛ o berɔ ba jo bwɛjen la bini naa, Israel tena bwa ɛɛ kpɔ ŋwɛɛraa ba tɛɡre danjwɛkpeɡ la ó kuuɡi chɔ fɛlembɔjen la bini, ka tel kɛŋɔ nɛn aa wola bwe beŋkpoŋ kwaraa na bela kpa.”

english_verse: Absalom and the others liked Hushai's plan better than Ahithophel's plan. This was because the Lord had decided to keep Ahithophel's plan from working and to cause trouble for Absalom. Jonathan and Ahimaaz Tell David the News
translation_verse: Belaa Absalɔm ne Israel tena la bwa ŋɔ, “Husai waa ɛ Aaki te waa waa dɛ baɡle la ɡwaa anɔ la Ahetofɛl aa bola la.” Korowii ɡbabirii ɛa kɛŋɔ wedɛɛɡa Ahetofɛl aa bola la, ba bɛ a ta teŋɛ, ásɛ a ba wenaale ne ba ta Absalɔm nɛ.

english_verse: At once, Hushai went to Zadok and Abiathar. He told them what advice Ahithophel had given to Absalom and to the leaders of Israel. He also told them about the advice he had given.
translation_verse: Anee Husai ŋɔ Sadɔk ne Abiata baa ɛ sɔfore la be ŋɔ, “Ahetofɛl baɡle Absalɔm ne Israel nomonome ŋɔ bá ɛ ken ne ken, kɛ n ja ba ŋɔ ba bɛ anɔ ɛ.”

english_verse: Then he said, “Hurry! Send someone to warn David not to spend the night on this side of the Jordan. He must get across the river, so he and the others won't be wiped out!”
translation_verse: Husai berɔ ŋɔ, “Tomɛ nɛra Kooro Devid be warane ŋɔ, ‘Dɛɛ berɛ leebɔɔ ŋwɛnɛ waa chɔa kaa pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta bela chɔe jwaana, hé ɛɡɛ Jɔɔdan Moo la le warane, ɡɛ aa ɛ ásɛ ba bɛ kooro ne o laa tena bwa lawɛ dɛ́ kpoo ba.’ ”

english_verse: Jonathan and Ahimaaz had been waiting at Rogel Spring because they did not want to be seen in Jerusalem. A servant girl went to the spring and gave them the message for David.
translation_verse: Dɛ sɔfo Abiata bibaa Jonatan ne sɔfo Sadɔk bibaa Ahimas lɔ Jerusalam dahare, bule waa chɔ bobɛl baa dɛ yerɔ Ɛn Roɡel ta, dɛkalkɛ dɛ baa nyin kɛ nomɛl na ba báa jo bwɛjen la bini. Dɛ bitolo bɛlee lɔ bela dɛ yon la ba be dɛ kaa bol waa aa dɛ chiɡ, ásɛ ba ɡe berɛ ka bol kooro be.

english_verse: But a young man saw them and went to tell Absalom. So Jonathan and Ahimaaz left and hurried to the house of a man who lived in Bahurim. Then they climbed down into a well in the courtyard.
translation_verse: Kɛ awola bɛl, bonɔɔ bɛl na ba asɛ dɛ ŋɔ Absalɔm be, anomanta, ba nɛra banɛ la ɛ warane chwa ka sɔh baa bɛl waa lɔ Bahurim dem. O dɔ kɔlɔŋ bɛl o dembaah, asɛ ba ka jo o bini.

english_verse: The man's wife put the cover on the well and poured grain on top of it, so the well could not be seen.
translation_verse: Baa la haah paɡri kon bɔle kɔlɔŋ la nyoa, dɛ kpɔ boyu yaa o ta, nomɛlbwa ta jemɛ kɛ ba lɔ o bini.

english_verse: Absalom's soldiers came to the woman and demanded, “Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?” The woman answered, “They went across that stream.” The soldiers went off to look for the two men. But when they did not find the men, they went back to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Absalɔm nɛra la ba dem bela dɛ ba bɔɔ haah la ŋɔ, “Leperaa Ahimas ne Jonatan dɔɔ?” O chaŋe ŋɔ, “Ba ɛɡɛ nenabɔɔ la le kaa.” Baala la nyin ba bɔr, ba ta ban nae, dɛ berɛ kaa Jerusalam.

english_verse: After the soldiers had gone, Jonathan and Ahimaaz climbed out of the well. They went to David and said, “Hurry! Get ready to cross the river!” Then they told him about Ahithophel's plan.
translation_verse: Baala la aa kaala habɔɔ la, Ahimas ne Jonatan le kɔlɔŋ la bini, dɛ kpɔ ba te ka baɡle Kooro Devid. Ba ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Kpɔ he te, dɛ́ ɛ warane ka ɛɡɛ nee la le, dɛ́ chwa kaa. Ahetofɛl dɛ vɔrɔwe he vɔrɔwa.”

english_verse: David and the others got ready and started crossing the Jordan River. By sunrise all of them were on the other side. Ahithophel Kills Himself
translation_verse: Anomanta, Kooro Devid ne o nɛra baa ja o nɛɛ la bwa kpɔ ba te, dɛ ka ɛɡɛ Jɔɔdan Moo la kaa o baŋ. Tɔɔ ne pera dɛ ba bwa ɡalɔ kaa.

english_verse: When Ahithophel saw that Absalom and the leaders of Israel were not going to follow his advice, he saddled his donkey and rode back to his home in Gilo. He told his family and servants what to do. Then he hanged himself, and they buried him in his family's burial place. Absalom Puts Amasa in Charge of the Army
translation_verse: Ahetofɛl aa naa kɛŋɔ ba ta o waa la ta teŋɛ la, o pa laala dawɛ o keeɡo ta dɛ kpɔ sie pa o bwɛɛ dɛ kaa. O baa kwaa o dem wobɛlbwa tonɛ dɛ ka saɡɛ o te. Waa sewa la, o mɛɛwa huɡri bɔree ba ka huɡo.

english_verse: David went to the town of Mahanaim, and Absalom crossed the Jordan River with the army of Israel.
translation_verse: Kooro Devid la bwɛɛ bɛl baa dɛ yerɔ Mahanaim asɛ Absalɔm ne Israel laa tena la bwa ɛɡɛ Jɔɔdan Moo la.

english_verse: Absalom put Amasa in Joab's place as commander of the army. Amasa's father was Ithra from the family of Ishmael, and his mother was Abigal, the daughter of Nahash and the sister of Joab's mother Zeruiah.
translation_verse: Dɛ Absalɔm le Amasa o chiɡ Joab naa ta dɛ chɔ laa tena la nyoa. Amasa mɛɛ sɔne Jɛta, o le Israel harɛ ta. O nya sɔne Abiɡel. Abiɡel ɡe nya sɔne Nahas asɛ o nahaah ɛ Joab nya baa dɛ yerɔ Seruya la.

english_verse: The Israelites under Absalom's command set up camp in the region of Gilead. Friends Bring Supplies to David
translation_verse: Israel tena la ne Absalɔm baŋre ba tɛnte deene Gelead harɛ ta.

english_verse: After David came to the town of Mahanaim, Shobi the son of Nahash came from Rabbah in Ammon, Machir the son of Ammiel came from Lo-Debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite came from Rogelim.
translation_verse: Kooro Devid aa tel Mahanaim la, Nahas bibaa Sobi waa le bwɛjen Raba waa lɔ Amɔn harɛ laanee baa chemo, dɛ Ameɛl bibaa Makir waa le Lo Debar, ne Baasilai waa le Roɡelim dɛ do Gelead harɛ ta,

english_verse: Here is a list of what they brought: sleeping mats, blankets, bowls, pottery jars, wheat, barley, flour, roasted grain, beans, lentils, honey, yogurt, sheep, and cheese. They brought the food for David and the others because they knew that everyone would be hungry, tired, and thirsty from being out in the desert.
translation_verse: ne tohno ne peera dɛ waɡasi ba tɛ kooro ne o nɛra ba di. Ba liiro ŋɔ lɔr ne nyɔɡre ɛɛ kpo Kooro Devid ne o nɛra laanee, ásɛ ba koh pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta bela.

english_verse: He sent out one third of his army under the command of Joab, another third under the command of Abishai the son of Zeruiah, and the rest under the command of Ittai from Gath. He told the soldiers, “I'm going into battle with you.”
translation_verse: O bɔne laa tena la bini kuore atoro dɛ tom ba. Joab chɔ bɔrbeŋkpoŋ nyoa, asɛ Seruya bibaa Abisae waa ɛ Joab nime la chɔ nɛɛte nyoa, asɛ Itai waa ɛ Gat te la ɡe chɔ toorote nyoa. O ŋɔ o laa tena la be ŋɔ, “N ne heyaa dɛɛ ba kaala.”

english_verse: But the soldiers said, “No, don't go into battle with us! It won't matter to our enemies if they make us all run away, or even if they kill half of us. But you are worth
translation_verse: Anee ba chaŋo ŋɔ, “N naa, a ta chɛ kɛ he ja ya nɛɛ kaa ɡɛ. A kaa ba kɛ ya dɔma sii ya nɛɛ yaa chwa aa, a ta waane ɛɛ. Ya pera kwaraa serewɔ aa, aa ban waanee ɛ. He ɡwaa yaa nɛra kaɡboŋa fi, a wer kɛŋɔ he te so bwɛjen nɔ bini, ásɛ ya hiah chae bɛl aa, he ba cha yaa.”

english_verse: and one of them went and told Joab, “I saw Absalom hanging in a tree!”
translation_verse: Kooro Devid laa tena la bɛl nao dɛ ŋɔ Joab be ŋɔ, “Nomoa, n na Absalɔm o saɡɛ dajen bɛl ta.”

english_verse: Battles were being fought all over the forest, and David's soldiers were winning. Twenty thousand soldiers were killed that day, and more of them died from the dangers of the forest than from the fighting itself.
translation_verse: Laa la yɛɛrɔ kaa bwɛɛ la dahare bwa, asɛ nɛra serewe kɔr la bini dɛ ɡwaa banɔ la baa sewɛ laa la ta.

english_verse: Absalom was riding his mule under a huge tree when his head caught in the branches. The mule ran off and left Absalom hanging in midair. Some of David's soldiers happened by,
translation_verse: Absalɔm soɡe keeɡo bie ta dɛ den cheme kooro laa tena la, dɛ keeɡo la dɛ jo dajen bɛl lɔɡa, asɛ Absalɔm nyu ka karɛ daa la kpala ta. O saɡɛ daa la ta, asɛ keeɡo la na tɛr do dɛɛ kaa.

english_verse: Joab said, “You saw Absalom? Why didn't you kill him? I would have given you ten pieces of silver and a special belt.”
translation_verse: Belaa Joab chaŋe ŋɔ, “Haa nao ɡɛ la, ɛrɛɛ he ta on kpoe buɡ ta nɔ? N ɡbabir fe ɛɛ tɛɛ suuɡapoŋa fi ne banyoo kiriso waa dɛ yo o ne laalee.”

english_verse: He always finds out what's going on. I would have been risking my life to kill Absalom, because you would have let me take the blame.”
translation_verse: Dɛ n vɛh kooro waa la dɛ fee kpo Absalɔm aa, o fe no a wa, wobɛlbwa toole waa wola no. He fe aa n habɔɔ cheɡa ba, ásɛ n fee di a bolchɔɡe.”

english_verse: Joab said, “I'm not going to waste any more time on you!” Absalom was still alive, so Joab took three spears and stuck them through Absalom's chest.
translation_verse: Ate, Joab ŋɔ, “Maa ŋɔ n dɛ che dɛ biɡri kpa.” Anomanta, o kpɔ lampeare atoro dɛ yaɡɛ Absalɔm bambile ta, o siwi ta aa lole o saɡɛ dajen la ta la.

english_verse: Ten of Joab's bodyguards came over and finished him off.
translation_verse: Asɛ Joab laa tena la fi den ba lɔ tɔ Absalɔm nɛ dɛ kpoo.

english_verse: Then Joab blew a trumpet to signal his troops to stop chasing Israel's soldiers.
translation_verse: Belaa Joab hoh bɛla, asɛ Kooro Devid laa tena la ɡel Israel tena nɛɛ teŋa dɛ yoo ba.

english_verse: They threw Absalom's body into a deep pit in the forest and put a big pile of rocks over it. Meanwhile, the people of Israel had all run back to their own homes.
translation_verse: Ba kpɔ Absalɔm chɔɔ la ta bɔluŋ bɛl bini kɔr la bini, dɛ pa bwea dawɛ o nɛ a daŋɛ kohona. Asɛ Israel tena la bwa chwa kaa ba deremi.

english_verse: When Absalom was alive, he had set up a stone monument for himself in King's Valley. He explained, “I don't have any sons to keep my name alive.” He called it Absalom's Monument, and that is the name it still has today. Ahimaaz Wants To Tell David
translation_verse: Absalɔm fa aa soɡe le la, o ma komɛl dɛ kpɔ tɛ o te ba kpɔ dɛɛ liiru bobɛl baa dɛ yerɔ Kooro Fɛlembɔjen ta. O liiro ŋɔ, “N ta bibaa lolɛ á che o nɛɛ ń dɔ sɔn.” O kpɔ kon la sɔn pa o te, anomanta, ba le fini ba dɛ yerɛ kon la Absalɔm Kon Baa Kpɔ Dɛɛ Liiru. Kooro Devid wi o bie Absalɔm

english_verse: Ahimaaz the son of Zadok said, “Joab, let me run and tell King David that the Lord has rescued him from his enemies.”
translation_verse: Belaa sɔfo Sadɔk bibaa Ahimas ŋɔ Joab be ŋɔ, “Gel n chwa la ka ŋɔ kooro be ŋɔ Korowii lɛo le o dɔma nɔn ta.”

english_verse: Joab answered, “You're not the one to tell the king that his son is dead. You can take him a message some other time, but not today.”
translation_verse: Belaa Joab ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Akai, he laa dɛ́ la kala nɔ ne fini. Gel tɔpebɛl wee mɔɔ, fini te laa, dɛkalkɛ kooro bibaa sewɔ.”

english_verse: Someone from Ethiopia was standing there, and Joab told him, “Go and tell the king what you have seen.” The man knelt down in front of Joab, then got up and started running.
translation_verse: Belaa Joab ŋɔ o bonɔɔ bɛl waa le Itiopia harɛ be ŋɔ, “La dɛ́ ka baɡle waa haa naa kooro be.” Ate, o ɡuŋi Joab dɛ chwa kaa.

english_verse: Ahimaaz spoke to Joab again, “No matter what happens, I still want to go. And besides, the Ethiopian has already left.” Joab said, “Why should you go? You won't get a reward for the news you have!”
translation_verse: Anee sɔfo Sadɔk bibaa Ahimas ŋɔ Joab be ŋɔ, “Gɛ bɛlbwa aa do, ɡel n chwa teŋɛ he bonɔɔ nɔ nɛ.” Kɛ Joab chaŋo ŋɔ, “N bie, bɔkwa waa he siwi beɡre kɛ he la bɛl nɔɔ? Komɛlbwa toole he dɔ le a ta.”

english_verse: “I'll run no matter what!” Ahimaaz insisted. “All right then, run!” Joab said. Ahimaaz took the road through the Jordan Valley and outran the Ethiopian.
translation_verse: Ahimas berɛ ŋɔ, “Gɛ aa doa bwa, mɛɛ chwao teŋɛ.” Anomanta, Joab ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Kpɔ chwae kaa!” Belaa Ahimas chwa kpɔ deŋɡarere dor harɛ waa chɔa kaa Jɔɔdan Moo pera la ta, dɛ tɔ Itiopia bonɔɔ la sie.

english_verse: Meanwhile, David was sitting between the inner and outer gates in the city wall. One of his soldiers was watching from the roof of the gate-tower. He saw a man running toward the town
translation_verse: Dɛ Kooro Devid ta soɡe bwɛjen la bini doonyoa ne baŋ kon la baah ta, nɛn waa dɛ daah bela la teehnɔ kaa danjwɛɛ la kaa ka che o doa, dɛ ka pɛl o doonyoa. Waa dɛ nyiŋi la o na baa bɛl waa dɛ chwa.

english_verse: and shouted down to tell David. David answered, “If he's alone, he must have some news.” The runner was getting closer,
translation_verse: Belaa o yerɛ kooro dɛ ŋɔ o be. Asɛ kooro ŋɔ, “Dɛ o ɡboo tenaa, o ken dɛ ba amanesoma ne.” Dɛ balaa baa la ɡe na dɛɛ ba.

english_verse: when the soldier saw someone else running. He shouted down to the gate, “Look! There's another runner!” David said, “He must have some news too.”
translation_verse: Nɛn waa dɛ daah bela la berɔ na baa bɛl ɡe o ɡbo aa dɛ chwa, asɛ o yerɛ nɛn waa dɛ daah doonyoa la ŋɔ, “Nyiŋi na, baa bɛl ɡe ɡbo chwao dɛɛ ba.” Anee kooro ŋɔ, “Amanesoma nee o ken ɛɛ ba.”

english_verse: The soldier on the roof shouted, “The first one runs just like Ahimaaz the son of Zadok.” This time David said, “He's a good man. He must have some good news.”
translation_verse: Belaa nɛn waa dɛ daah bela la ŋɔ, “N dɛ na kɛŋɔ baa waa tɔ sie la dɛ le sɔfo Sadɔk bibaa Ahimas.” Asɛ kooro ŋɔ, “O ɛ nɛndɛɛɡe. Amanesoma nee wɛɛ ba.”

english_verse: Ahimaaz called out, “We won! We won!” Then he bowed low to David and said, “Your Majesty, praise the Lord your God! He has given you victory over your enemies.”
translation_verse: Ate, Ahimas kpɔ silɛɛ yerɛ kooro ŋɔ, “Wobɛlbwa maɡrɔ.” O ɡuŋi kooro sie dɛ kpɔ duure tɛo dɛ ŋɔ, “Korowii haa dɛ tomɔ laanee dɔ jam! O ɡelɔ he pɔ nɛra baa ɛɛ dɔm la nɛ!”

english_verse: “Is my son Absalom all right?” David asked. Ahimaaz said, “When Joab sent your personal servant and me, I saw a noisy crowd. But I don't know what it was all about.”
translation_verse: Belaa kooro bɔɔ bonɔɔ la ŋɔ, “Absalɔm le a nyoa aa?” Anee Ahimas chaŋe ŋɔ, “N naa, Joab aa dɛ ba men toma la, n na wesaɡasaɡare ane, kɛ men he bonɔɔ aa a ɡɛ waa la bɛlbwa bini jemɛ.”

english_verse: David told him, “Stand over there and wait.” Ahimaaz went over and stood there.
translation_verse: Ate, kooro ŋɔ, “Kaa ka che baŋ bɛl dɛɛ kpa.” Anomanta, o kaa che baŋ bɛl dɛɛ kpa.

english_verse: The Ethiopian came and said, “Your Majesty, today I have good news! The Lord has rescued you from all your enemies!”
translation_verse: Belaa Itiopia bonɔɔ la ba dɛ ŋɔ, “N naa kooro, dɛɛ no amanesoma nɔ! Korowii lɛɛ le he dɔma baa cheɡɛ he nɛɛ nɔn ta fini.”

english_verse: “Is my son Absalom all right?” David asked. The Ethiopian replied, “I wish that all Your Majesty's enemies and everyone who tries to harm you would end up like him!” David Cries for Absalom
translation_verse: Anee Kooro bɔɔro ŋɔ, “N bibaa Absalɔm dɔ o nyu tenaa?” Asɛ Itiopia te la chaŋe ŋɔ, “N naa, n dɛ nyin kɛŋɔ anɔ la aa puu la, ɡe pu he dɔma bwa.”

english_verse: David started trembling. Then he went up to the room above the city gate to cry. As he went, he kept saying, “My son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom! I wish I could have died instead of you! Absalom, my son, my son!”
translation_verse: Ate, dɛ kooro soɡo dɛɛ chel. O cheɡɛ doonyoa la nyundua dɛ kaa dea dɛ ka wi. Waa dɛ kaa la, dɛ o dɛ wi ŋɔ, “N bidɛɛɡe, Absalɔm, menee fe sewa sɛ?”

english_verse: Someone told Joab, “The king is crying because Absalom is dead.”
translation_verse: Joab baa no kɛŋɔ Kooro Devid dɛ wi o bibaa Absalɔm waa sewa la kohona.

english_verse: David's army found out he was crying because his son had died, and their day of victory suddenly turned into a day of sadness.
translation_verse: Anomanta, silɛɛ waa lole dɛ le yoi baa kaa yo dɛ pɔ ba dɔma nɛɛ awola tɔpere la berɛ laa tena la bwa bambichɔɡa, dɛkalkɛ ba noɔ kɛŋɔ kooro dɛ wi o bie waa sewa la.

english_verse: The troops were sneaking into Mahanaim, just as if they had run away from a battle and were ashamed.
translation_verse: Laa tena la ba dɛ jo bwɛjen la bini sum ne kɛŋɔ, baa pɔ ba nɛɛ laa ta ba kpɔ sihiih chwa la ken.

english_verse: David covered his face with his hands and kept on crying loudly, “My son, Absalom! Absalom, my son, my son!”
translation_verse: Kooro kpɔ nɔɔra tɔ sie dɛ do lɔŋɔ kohona ŋɔ, “N bidɛɛɡe Absalɔm, n bidɛɛɡe kohona.”

english_verse: Joab went to the house where David was staying and told him: You've made your soldiers ashamed! Not only did they save your life, they saved your sons and daughters and wives as well.
translation_verse: Belaa Joab jo kooro dem bela dɛ ka ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “N naa, he ɡelɔ sihiih kpo he laa tena baa lɛ he ne he bibaala, ne bihaahna ne haahna dɛ he sɛnanar la nyu.

english_verse: You're more loyal to your enemies than to your friends. What you've done today has shown your officers and soldiers that they don't mean a thing to you. You would be happy if Absalom was still alive, even if the rest of us were dead.
translation_verse: He dɛ nyin nɛra baa haeh, dɛ hah nɛra baa dɛ nyin he wa! He berɔ ɡel ya jemɛ fini kɛŋɔ laa tena ne nomonome baa chɔ ba nyoa la ta komɛlbwa ɛɛ he be. N nao kɛŋɔ he sie ɛɛ lɛo kɛŋɔ Absalɔm fe aa lole ásɛ ya bwa serewe.

english_verse: Now get up! Go out there and thank them for what they did. If you don't, I swear by the Lord that you won't even have one man left on your side tomorrow morning. You may have had a lot of troubles in the past, but this will be the worst thing that has ever happened to you!
translation_verse: Ir le ka larawe he laa tena la bwara. N ŋwɛɛ Korowii o sɔn aa kana la kɛŋɔ dɛ he ta leɛ kaa laa, bɔr ne joe nɛmbeŋkpoŋ kwara aa he bee ka. Dɛ a fe ɛ wedoŋa dɛ ɡwaa anɔ la bwa haa naa le he bonɔɔne saŋ ba le fini.”

english_verse: David got up and went to the town gate and sat down. When the people heard that he was sitting there, they came to see him. Israel and Judah Want David Back After Israel's soldiers had all returned home,
translation_verse: Ate, kooro ɡel wii dɛ ir dɛ ka so bwɛjen la doonyojen la jwɛh. O laa tena la noɔ kɛŋɔ o leɔ dɛ ba so bela, asɛ ba la ka che baro. Kooro Devid berɔ ba Jerusalam Anɔ bwa aa dɛ ɛ la, dɛ Israel tena la bwa berɔ kaa ba deremi.

english_verse: everyone in Israel started arguing. They were saying to each other, “King David rescued us from the Philistines and from our other enemies. But then we chose Absalom to be our new leader, and David had to leave the country to get away. Absalom died in battle, so why hasn't something been done to bring David back?”
translation_verse: Absalɔm ɡe yaa fuɡe noo do o nyu ta dɛ cheɡo ŋɔ ó ɛ ya kooro la ɡe ka laa ta. Ɛrɛɛ haa wola Kooro Devid ka kpɔe ba te waa bol kpa nɔɔ?”

english_verse: When David found out what they were saying, he sent a message to Zadok and Abiathar the priests. It said: Say to the leaders of Judah, “Why are you the last tribe to think about bringing King David back home?
translation_verse: Kooro Devid no waa Israel tena la aa dɛ bol la, anomanta, o tomɛ Sadɔk ne Abiata baa ɛ sɔfore la ŋɔ bá ka bɔɔ Juda harɛ nomonome ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ he ɛ nɛra haa ka mun dɛɛ ba men kooro ne n koodem nɔɔ?

english_verse: He is your brother, your own relative! Why haven't you done anything to bring him back?”
translation_verse: He ɛ n lolanar, ya bwa ɛ nɛmbeŋkpoŋ. Ɛrɛɛ he ta sie tɔe dɛ berɛ ka mun, n kpɔe dɛ ba n koodem nɔɔ?”

english_verse: And tell Amasa, “You're my nephew, and with God as a witness, I swear I'll make you commander of my army instead of Joab.”
translation_verse: Kooro berɔ ŋɔ ba bɔɔ Amasa ŋɔ, “N lole laa hen ya bwa ɛ nɛmbeŋkpoŋ aa? Le fini dɛɛ kaa dɛ he laa dɛ́ ɛ nomoa dɛ́ chiɡ Joab naa ta, dɛ́ chɔ n laa tena nyoa aa, amɔ te Kórowii tɛr n deŋne kohona.”

english_verse: Soon the tribe of Judah again became followers of David, and they sent him this message: “Come back, and bring your soldiers with you.” David Starts Back for Jerusalem
translation_verse: Juda harɛ laa tena bwa bambile lawɛ Kooro Devid waa la, asɛ ba bwa nyoa pɛ, dɛ kpɔ kala tɛo ŋɔ o ne o laa tena la bwa berɛ ba.

english_verse: Shimei the son of Gera was there with them. He had hurried from Bahurim to meet David. Shimei was from the tribe of Benjamin, and
translation_verse: Gɛ saŋ la tenten Gɛra bibaa Simei waa le Bahurim dɛ le Bɛnjamen dea, ɡe ɛ warane kaa Jɔɔdan Moo nyoa dɛ́ ka cheme Kooro Devid.

english_verse: I know I was wrong. That's why I wanted to be the first one from the northern tribes to meet you.”
translation_verse: Men maa ɛ he bonɔɔ jemɔ kɛŋɔ n ɛ wechɔɡa, kɛ fini n balɔ kɛŋɔ nɛn waa tɔ sie dɛ le Josef dem dɛ ba cheme n dɔɔ kooro.”

english_verse: Then they brought David's family and servants back across the river, and they did everything he wanted them to do. Shimei Meets with David Shimei crossed the Jordan River and bowed down in front of David.
translation_verse: Ba cheɡɛ leebɔɔ la ta, dɛ́ ka kpɔ kooro ne o dem nɛra ɛɡɛ le, dɛ́ ɛ wobɛlbwa waa dɛ nyin tɛo. Belaa Simei aa ɛɡɛ Jɔɔdan Moo la le la, o baa chole chɔ kooro sie,

english_verse: He said, “Your Majesty, I beg you not to punish me! Please, forget what I did when you were leaving Jerusalem. Don't even think about it.
translation_verse: dɛ ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “N dɔɔ, Korowii bɛ ɡel he pa mɛ bolchɔɡe kpa. Bɛ wechɔɡa maa ɛa awola haa dɛ le Jerusalam la lii. N dɛ soŋe kɛ he laa kpɔ he nyu bini.

english_verse: David said, “Abishai, what will I ever do with you and your brother Joab? Is it your job to tell me who has done wrong? I've been made king of all Israel today, and no one will be put to death!”
translation_verse: Anee Kooro Devid chaŋe ŋɔ, “Seruya bii, bɔkwa waa n ne he dɔ ɛɛ yɔ? He nyin wa ba dawɛ n nɛ, dɛ berɛ n dɔma! A chɛ kɛ bá lawɛ nɛn kpo Israel harɛ ta fini ɡɛ naa? N laa kooro Israel harɛ ta taraken nɔ naa?”

english_verse: Then David promised Shimei that he would not be killed. Mephibosheth Meets with David
translation_verse: Asɛ kooro ŋɔ Simei be ŋɔ, “N ŋwɛɛrɔ kɛŋɔ a ta chɛ kɛŋɔ bá kpoe.”

english_verse: He answered, “Your Majesty, you know I can't walk. I told my servant to saddle a donkey for me so I could go with you. But my servant left without me, and
translation_verse: O chaŋe ŋɔ, “N naa kooro, maa ɛ boobi nomanta, n ŋɔ n bonɔɔ Siba be ŋɔ ó kpɔ kon ba dawɛ n keeɡo ta, ásɛ n so o ta n ne he kaa, kɛ o ta waa maa bola la ta teŋɛ.

english_verse: then he lied about me. You're as wise as an angel of God, so do what you think is right.
translation_verse: O teŋe nyosone dawɛ n nɛɛ tɛ hen n dɔɔ kooro. N dɔɔ, he do kɛŋɔ Korowii torome ken anomanta, ɛ wobɛlbwa aa too he tea.

english_verse: After all, you could have killed my whole family and me. But instead, you let me eat at your own table. Your Majesty, what more could I ask?”
translation_verse: N nabaa naanar bwa chɛ kɛ n naa kooro kpoo ba, kɛ he tɛ mɛ ŋwɛnɛ n ne he pɛ nɔn di kwa. N ta ŋwɛnɛ dɔe kɛ ń berɛ soŋe waane le hen n naa kooro be kpa.”

english_verse: David answered, “You've said enough! I've decided to divide the property between you and Ziba.”
translation_verse: Belaa Kooro chaŋe ŋɔ, “A ta chɛ kɛ he bol waane kpa. He ne Siba la ka bɔne Kooro Sɔɔl kondɔɔh.”

english_verse: Mephibosheth replied, “He can have it all! I'm just glad you've come home safely.” Barzillai Returns Home
translation_verse: Anee Mɛfebɔsɛt ŋɔ kooro be ŋɔ, “N naa kooro aa dɛ ba dem deŋnesɔɔhna ta nomanta, ɡel Siba kpɔ o komɛlbwa.”

english_verse: Barzillai came from Rogelim in Gilead to meet David at the Jordan River and go across with him.
translation_verse: Belaa Baasilai le Roɡelim Gelead harɛ ba, dɛ ba kpɔ kooro ɛɡɛ Jɔɔdan Moo la le, asɛ o kaa.

english_verse: David said to him, “Cross the river and go to Jerusalem with me. I will take care of you.”
translation_verse: Belaa kooro ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Ir ja n nɛɛ yá kaa Jerusalam he ka puu mɛ so, ásɛ mɛɛ nyiŋi he nɛ.”

english_verse: Barzillai answered: Your Majesty, why should I go to Jerusalem? I don't have much longer to live.
translation_verse: Ate, o chaŋe kooro ŋɔ, “Bene aŋwɛnɛɛ ka mɛ jaɔ? N naa kooro, a ta chɛ kɛ n ne he kaa Jerusalam ka so.

english_verse: I'll cross the river with you, but I'll only go a little way on the other side. You don't have to be so kind to me.
translation_verse: Men maa ɛ he bonɔɔ ta ɡɛ waa nɔ chɛɛ. Mɛɛ teŋɛ he nɛɛ ka ɡale Jɔɔdan Moo tama. Bɔkwa waa n ɛ tɛɛ hɛɛ tɛ mɛ a kembɔr ɔ?

english_verse: Just let me return to my hometown, where I can someday be buried near my father and mother. My servant Chimham can go with you, and you can treat him as your own.
translation_verse: Gel he bonɔɔ berɛ ba kaa dem dɛ́ ka sewɛ bɛne n lolanar huɡribɔr. N bibaa Kimham ɡee nɔ, kpɔɔ kaa ó kaa tomɛ. N naa kooro, ɛ ɡɛ bɛlbwa aa too he tea tɛo.”

english_verse: David said, “I'll take Chimham with me, and whatever you ask me to do for him, I'll do. And if there's anything else you want, I'll also do that.”
translation_verse: Asɛ kooro ŋɔ, “N ne Kimham ɛɛ kaaloo ka ɛɡɛ moo le kaa, ásɛ n ɛ wobɛlbwa haa dɛ nyin tɛo. He bɔɔ mɛ komɛlbwa ɡe aa, mɛɛ ɛo tɛɛ.”

english_verse: David's soldiers went on across the river, while he stayed behind to tell Barzillai goodbye and to wish him well. Barzillai returned home, but
translation_verse: Anomanta, nɛra la bwa ɛɡɛ Jɔɔdan Moo la le asɛ Kooro Devid ɡe teŋɛ. Asɛ kooro kal Baasilai dɛ ɡbaaro pɛl o te, dɛ swee andɛɛɡa tɛo, asɛ Baasilai berɛ kaa dem.

english_verse: Chimham crossed the river with David. Israel and Judah Argue All of Judah's army and half of Israel's army were there to help David cross the river.
translation_verse: Kooro aa kaa ɛɡɛ Jɔɔdan Moo le dɛ kaa Gelɡal la, dɛ Kimham ja o nɛ. Dɛ Juda laa tena bwa ne Israel laa tena pera bwa teŋɛ o nɛ dɛ kpɔɔ ɡale.

english_verse: The soldiers from Israel came to him and said, “Why did our relatives from Judah secretly take you and your family and your soldiers across the Jordan?”
translation_verse: Belaa Israel tena la bwa ba kooro be dɛ ba ŋɔ, “N naa kooro, ɛrɛɛ Juda tena baa ɛ ya lolanar ŋwɛ kooro ne o dem tena, dɛ o laa tena bwa, dɛ kpɔ ba ɛɡɛ Jɔɔdan Moo la kaa nɔɔ?”

english_verse: The people of Judah answered, “Why are you so angry? We are the king's relatives. He didn't give us any food, and we didn't take anything for ourselves!”
translation_verse: Belaa Juda laa tena la bwa chaŋe Israel laa tena la ŋɔ, “Ya ne kooro bwa ɛ nɛmbeŋkpoŋ waa ya ɛ ɡɛ la. Ɛrɛɛ chɛ kɛŋɔ he baah diɔ? Ya kpɔ kooro kwaane di kɛɛ? Ya kpɔ o komɛl ɡe kɛɛ?”

english_verse: Those from Israel said, “King David belongs to us ten times more than he belongs to you. Why didn't you think we were good enough to help you? After all, we were the first ones to think of bringing him back!” The people of Judah argued more strongly than the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Asɛ Israel laa tena la chaŋ ba ŋɔ, “Ya dɔ kooro baŋne fi bwa. A habɔɔ ya ne o pɛo ɡwaa kɛ he ne waa doa. Ɛrɛ waa hɛɛ nyiŋi ya nyubaahna nɔɔ? Ya laa tɔ sie bol kooro ka kpɔe dɛ́ ba wa aa?” Kɛ Juda laa tena la chaŋɔ bandia kohona ne, dɛ ɡwaa Israel baala la kwara.

english_verse: A troublemaker from the tribe of Benjamin was there. His name was Sheba the son of Bichri, and he blew a trumpet to get everyone's attention. Then he said, “People of Israel, David the son of Jesse doesn't belong to us! Let's go home.”
translation_verse: A balɔ kɛŋɔ Bikri bibaa Seeba lɔ Gelɡal harɛ, o le Bɛnjamen dea. Dɛ o dɔ dichɔɡa o nyu bini. O hoh bɛla dɛ ŋɔ, “Ya ta dibɔr bɛlbwa dɔe Kooro Devid be, yaa Jese bibaa nɛɛ teŋɛ! Israel baa bɛlbwa berɛ kaa dem.”

english_verse: So they stopped following David and went off with Sheba. But the people of Judah stayed close to David all the way from the Jordan to Jerusalem. David's Ten Wives
translation_verse: Anomanta, Israel laa tena la bwa le Kooro Devid habɔɔ, ba ne Seeba kaa. Kɛ Juda laa tena la teŋɛ Kooro Devid nɛɛ le Jɔɔdan Moo la ta dɛ ba Jerusalam.

english_verse: David had left ten of his wives in Jerusalem to take care of his palace. But when he came back, he had them taken to another house, and he placed soldiers there to guard them. He gave them whatever they needed, but he never slept with any of them again. They had to live there for the rest of their lives as if they were widows. The Army Goes after Sheba
translation_verse: Kooro Devid aa bera kaa o koodem Jerusalam la, o lawɛ o sɛnanar fi baa dɛ daah koodem la do dea, baa daah ba. Dɛ o dɛ tɛɛ ba komɛlbwa kɛ dɛ o ne baa chɔ. Ba chɔ dea ka tel ba serewe wee, kɛŋɔ luhaahna ken.

english_verse: David said to Amasa, “Three days from now I want you and all of Judah's army to be here!”
translation_verse: Belaa kooro ŋɔ Amasa be ŋɔ, “Yerɛ Juda laa tena la bwa, he ne ba ba cheme n sie tɔpera atoro nɔ ta.”

english_verse: Amasa started bringing the army together, but it was taking him more than three days.
translation_verse: Amasa laŋɔ ka yerɛ Juda laa tena la cheme, kɛ o berɔ biɡri asɛ saŋ kooro aa doo la ɡarɛ.

english_verse: So David said to Abishai, “Sheba will hurt us more than Absalom ever did. Take my best soldiers and go after him. We don't want him to take over any walled cities and get away from us.” Joab Kills Amasa
translation_verse: Belaa kooro ŋɔ Abisae be ŋɔ, “Seeba nɔ ɛɛ ba waa nee ba ta ya nɛ ɡwaa Absalɔm. Kpɔ he dɔɔ laa tena la dɛ ti ba, o ken ɛɛ ka nyin bwɛjena baa ma danjwɛjena bara la bɛl binii ka sɔh, dɛ́ chwa yaa.”

english_verse: Abishai left Jerusalem to try and capture Sheba. He took along Joab and his soldiers, as well as David's bodyguard and best troops.
translation_verse: Anomanta, Abisae kpɔ Joab ne o laa tena la ne kooro nɛra baa dɛ daahno, dɛ laa tena baa ka Jerusalam bwa le, ba ne o ti Seeba.

english_verse: They had gone as far as the big rock at Gibeon when Amasa caught up with them. Joab had a dagger strapped around his waist over his military uniform, but it fell out as he started toward Amasa.
translation_verse: Ba tel bwe bɛl waa lɔ Gebeɔn ta, asɛ Amasa ba chem ba. Dɛ Joab do o laa batakaare, dɛ vɔwɛ kiriso asɛ kerejeɡa do o tɔɔ bini dɛ sɛɡle o ta. Waa dɛ tel o be la, kere la le o tɔɔ bini le harɛ.

english_verse: Joab said, “Amasa, my cousin, how are you?” Then Joab took hold of Amasa's beard with his right hand, so that he could greet him with a kiss.
translation_verse: Joab bɔɔ Amasa ŋɔ, “N dam, ɛrɛɛ he bwara doɔ?” Belaa Joab kpɔ nɔndiɡ lawɛ Amasa tampona dɛ ɡbaaro pɛl o te.

english_verse: Amasa did not see the dagger in Joab's other hand. Joab stuck it in Amasa's stomach, and his insides spilled out on the ground. Joab only struck him once, but Amasa was dying. Joab and his brother Abishai went off to chase Sheba.
translation_verse: Dɛ Amasa aa jemɛ kɛŋɔ Joab kpoŋe kere o nɔn bɛl la ta, asɛ Joab kpɔ yaɡɛ o tea o looni le dɛ ba le harɛ. O sewɛ buɡ ta, anomanta, o ta on wobɛlbwa ɛɛ kpa. Belaa Joab ne o nime Abisae ti Seeba ɡe.

english_verse: One of Joab's soldiers stood by Amasa and shouted, “If any of you are for Joab and David, then follow Joab!”
translation_verse: Joab laa tena la bɛl cheɡɛ Amasa chɔɔ la jwɛh dɛ ŋɔ, “Nomɛlbwa waa dɛ nyin Joab wa dɛɛ teŋɛ Kooro Devid nɛɛ la, ó teŋɛ Joab nɛ!”

english_verse: Amasa was still rolling in his own blood in the middle of the road. The soldier who had shouted noticed that everyone who passed by would stop, so he dragged Amasa off the road and covered him with a blanket.
translation_verse: Chal tɔ Amasa chɔɔ la o chɔ ŋwɛnɛ baah. Baa la nao kɛŋɔ laa tena la bɛlbwa tel belaa o dɛ che. Waa na ɡɛ la, o tuuɡu le ŋwɛnɛ la ta ka ta kpɔɡ bini dɛ kpɔ yal tɔ o nɛ.

english_verse: After this, no one else stopped. They all walked straight past him on their way to help Joab capture Sheba. Sheba Hides Out in the Town of Abel
translation_verse: Waa laa Amasa chɔɔ la laa kpɔ ŋwɛnɛ la ta tonɛ la, laa tena la bwa teŋɛ Joab nɛ ba ka ti Seeba.

english_verse: Sheba had gone through all of the tribes of Israel when he came to the town of Abel Beth-Maacah. All of his best soldiers met him there and followed him into the town.
translation_verse: Seeba kpɔ Israel deene harɛre bwa ta ka le bwɛjen bɛl baa dɛ yerɔ Ebel Bɛt Maaka, asɛ Bɛr dea tena bwa cheme dɛ teŋɛ o nɛɛ ba jo o ta.

english_verse: Joab and his troops came and surrounded Abel, so that no one could go in or come out. They made a dirt ramp up to the town wall and then started to use a battering ram to knock the wall down. A Wise Woman Saves the Town
translation_verse: Joab laa tena la bwa balɔ dɛ ba chɔ bar Ebel Bɛt Maaka, dɛ ba noɔ kɛŋɔ Seeba lɔ bela. Ba ma kwaa báa kpɔ a ta jo bwɛjen la ta, a pɛl danjwɛkpeɡa baa maa bar bwɛjen la. Baa kpɔ bune dɛɛ chuɡe danjwɛɛ la dɛɛ kuuɡu la,

english_verse: A wise woman shouted from the top of the wall, “Listen to me! Listen to me! I have to talk to Joab! Tell him to come here!”
translation_verse: haah bɛl waa jemɛ waa baa che bwɛɛ la danjwɛkpeɡ doa dɛ do lɔŋɔ ŋɔ, “Hé yerɛ Joab tɛ mɛ bonɔ, ń bol waane o be.”

english_verse: When he came, the woman said, “Are you Joab?” “Yes, I am,” he answered. She said, “Please, listen to what I have to say.” “All right,” he said. “I'll listen.”
translation_verse: Ate, Joab ba asɛ haah la bɔɔro ŋɔ, “Henee Joab la aa?” Asɛ o chaŋe ŋɔ, “Ɔɔh, menee.” Asɛ haah la ŋɔ, “Nomoa, cheɡ deŋne dɛ́ no men maa ɛ he tolo be.” Ate, o chaŋe ŋɔ, “N dɛ no he be.”

english_verse: She said, “Long ago people used to say, ‘If you want good advice, go to the town of Abel to get it.’ The answers they got here were all that was needed to settle any problem.
translation_verse: Haah la ŋɔ, “Saŋ la ba yon ŋɔ, ‘He dɛ nyin wejema aa, la bwɛjen Ebel,’ dɛ ɡɛɛ baa ɛ.

english_verse: We are Israelites, and we want peace! You can trust us. Why are you trying to destroy a town that's like a mother in Israel? Why do you want to wipe out the Lord's people?”
translation_verse: Nɛra yaa soɡe bwɛjen nɔ ta waa dɔ deŋnesɔɔhna kohona ne kasinteŋ Israel harɛ, asɛ hɛɛ nyin he chɔɡ bwɛjen Ebel. Ɛrɛɛ hɛɛ nyin he chɔɡ Korowii kapɛrɛ kwaa nɔɔ?”

english_verse: Joab answered, “No, no! I'm not trying to wipe you out or destroy your town!
translation_verse: Anee Joab chaŋe ŋɔ, “Akai, Korowii ɛɛ la ane bojaŋ kɛŋɔ ń ba chɔɡ bwɛjen nɔ.

english_verse: That's not it at all. There's a man in your town from the hill country of Ephraim. His name is Sheba, and he is the leader of a rebellion against King David. Turn him over to me, and we will leave your town alone.” The woman told Joab, “We will throw his head over the wall.”
translation_verse: Gɛ laa waa la do. Bikri bibaa Seeba waa le Efrem deŋɡarere harɛ ta laanee ɛ Kooro Devid deŋnekpeɡ. Hé le Seeba ɡbo ne tɛ mɛ, ásɛ n ɡel wobɛlbwa dɛ́ berɛ kaa.” Belaa haah la ŋɔ Joab be ŋɔ, “Yaa kpoo dɛ́ kpɔ o nyu ba che danjwɛɛ ta viɡri tɛɛ.”

english_verse: She went to the people of the town and talked them into doing it. They cut off Sheba's head and threw it to Joab. Joab blew a signal on his trumpet, and the soldiers returned to their homes. Joab went back to David in Jerusalem. Another List of David's Officials
translation_verse: Ate, haah la kpɔ o liire waa ba a ne la tɛ nɛra la bwa, asɛ ba sɛh dɛ teŋe Seeba nyu dɛ kpɔ viɡru. Belaa o hoh bɛla la, asɛ o laa tena la bwa peɡre le bwɛjen la ta, asɛ bɛlbwa kaa o dem. Asɛ Joab ɡe berɛ kaa kooro be Jerusalam.

english_verse: Joab was the commander of Israel's entire army. Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was in command of David's bodyguard.
translation_verse: Dɛ Joab, onee chɔ Israel laa tena bwa nyoa, asɛ Jehoiada bibaa Bɛnaya chɔ Pɛlet ne Kɛrɛt tena baa dɛ daah kooro la nyoa,

english_verse: Adoram was in charge of the slave-labor force. Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud kept government records.
translation_verse: asɛ Adoniram chɔ nɛra baa dɛ do ba tomkpeɡa ta nyoa, Ahilud bibaa Jehosafat ɡe chɔ waa aa chiɡa ba chwera dɛɛ bil dɛ́ kwaa cheɡ nyoa.

english_verse: Sheva was the secretary. Zadok and Abiathar were the priests.
translation_verse: Sɛva ɛ kɔɔto karake, asɛ Sadɔk ne Abiata ɛ sɔfore,

english_verse: The Gibeonites were not Israelites; they were descendants of the Amorites. The people of Israel had promised not to kill them, but Saul had tried to kill them because he wanted Israel and Judah to control all the land. David had the Gibeonites come, and he talked with them.
translation_verse: Kooro yerɛ Gebeɔn tena baa kaa la, dɛ bol waa baɡ ba. Dɛ Gebeɔn tena la ta Israel tena ɛɛ. Ba ɛ Amɔre tena bane Israel tena aa baɡ ba nyoa ŋɔ baa ban kpoo. Kɛ Kooro Sɔɔl siwi beɡrɔ wɛɛ nyin ba dɛ́ kpo, Israel ne Juda tena wa.

english_verse: He said, “What can I do to make up for what Saul did, so that you'll ask the Lord to be kind to his people again?”
translation_verse: Kooro bɔɔ Gebeɔn tena la ŋɔ, “Bɔkwaa hɛɛ nyin kɛ ń ɛ tɛ heya ɔ? Bɔkwaa mɛɛ ba wona ɛ ásɛ he berɛ won swee Korowii andɛɛɡa tɛ nɛra baa ɛ o kapɛrɛ nɛra nɔɔ?”

english_verse: They replied, “Saul tried to kill all our people so that none of us would be left in the land of Israel.
translation_verse: Anee ba chaŋo ŋɔ, “Kooro Sɔɔl dɛ nyin ó kpoo yaa, ásɛ ya bini bɛlbwa bɛ ka Israel harɛ nɔ ta.

english_verse: Give us seven of his descendants. We will hang these men near the place where the Lord is worshiped in Gibeah, the hometown of Saul, the Lord's chosen king.” “I'll give them to you,” David said.
translation_verse: Anomanta, lawɛ o naanar banuanɛ baa ɛ baala tɛ yaa yá kpoo ba dɛ́ saɡ ba Korowii sie Gebea waa ɛ Kooro Sɔɔl bwɛɛ nɔ ta.” Asɛ kooro chaŋe ŋɔ, “Mɛɛ lee baa tɛ heya.”

english_verse: David had made a promise to Jonathan with the Lord as his witness, so he spared Jonathan's son Mephibosheth, the grandson of Saul.
translation_verse: Kooro Devid ne Jonatan ŋwɛɛra baa ŋwɛra baɡle dɔŋa Korowii sie nomanta, kooro ta Jonatan bibaa Mɛfebɔsɛt leɛ.

english_verse: turned them over to the Gibeonites, who hanged all seven of them on the mountain near the place where the Lord was worshiped. This happened right at the beginning of the barley harvest. Rizpah Takes Care of the Bodies
translation_verse: Kooro Devid kpɔ ba do Gebeɔn tena nɔn ta ba kpoo ba, dɛ kpɔ ba saɡɛ deŋɡare bɛl ta Korowii sie. Nɛra banuanɛ la bwa sewɔ tɔpebeŋkpoŋ. Awola laanee baa pa mea koma mun, asɛ dɛ kpoo ba.

english_verse: Rizpah spread out some sackcloth on a nearby rock. She wouldn't let the birds land on the bodies during the day, and she kept the wild animals away at night. She stayed there from the beginning of the harvest until it started to rain. The Burial of Saul and His Descendants
translation_verse: Aeya bihaah Rispa, waa ɛ Kooro Sɔɔl sɛno, kpɔ lweyal paɡri tɔ bwe bɛl ta, dɛ so o lɔɡa dɛɛ daah nɛra baa serewa la. Le jaaɡe koma mumpar ka tel kɛŋɔ bwaala aa nɛa la, o ta ɡelɛ jumbii dɔ ba ola di webaŋa, kɛɛ kpɔɡ bini olchɔɡa ba dia jwaana.

english_verse: Earlier the Philistines had killed Saul and Jonathan on Mount Gilboa and had hung their bodies in the town square at Beth-Shan. The people of Jabesh in Gilead had secretly taken the bodies away, but David found out what Saul's wife Rizpah had done, and he went to the leaders of Jabesh to get the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan.
translation_verse: o iro la ka pa Kooro Sɔɔl ne o bibaa Jonatan hoɡa le Jabes Gelead tena be. Dɛ ba ŋwɛa le Bɛt San, bela nɛra yon kaa soŋni bwɛjen la doonyoa. Belaa Filisti tena kpɔ ba saɡɛ ɡɛ saŋ baa kpo Kooro Sɔɔl Gelboa Bwejen ta la.

english_verse: David had their bones taken to the land of Benjamin and buried in a side room in Saul's family burial place. Then he gave orders for the bones of the men who had been hanged to be buried there. It was done, and God answered prayers to bless the land. The Descendants of the Rephaim (
translation_verse: Ba huɡe Kooro Sɔɔl ne o bibaa Jonatan hoɡa la bwebɔɔ baa huɡe Kooro Sɔɔl mɛɛ Kes bini Sela, Bɛnjamen dea harɛ ta. Gɛ Kooro Devid aa do ba laanee ba ɛ. A habɔɔ, Korowii no harɛ la tena wesoŋa. Israel ne Filisti tena laa yoi

english_verse: There was another war, this time in Gath. One of the enemy soldiers was a descendant of the Rephaim. He was as big as a giant and had six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot.
translation_verse: Laa bɛl ɡe chole Gat ja. Dɛ baa bɛl kpeɡo o bwara do kpeɡri kohona. O nɔn bɛlbwa ta, o dɔ nonie anumɛl, o nanie ɡe ɛ anumɛl o nakpale ta. A bwa lɔ fifraanɛ dɛ anaarɛ. O ɛ Rafa naa.

english_verse: One time David got very tired when he and his soldiers were fighting the Philistines.
translation_verse: Laa berɔ chole Filisti ne Israel tena baah. Kooro Devid ne o laa tena leɔ kaa dɛ ka yoo ba. Yoi la bini la, Kooro Devid baa koh dɛ ɡwɛɡre.

english_verse: One of the Philistine warriors was Ishbibenob, who was a descendant of the Rephaim, and he tried to kill David. Ishbibenob was armed with a new sword, and his bronze spearhead alone weighed about three and a half kilograms.
translation_verse: Belaa baa bɛl waa kpeɡa kɛrɛdɛ dɛ ɛ Rafa naa baa yerɔ Esbe Bɛnɔb, ŋɔ wɛɛ kpo Kooro Devidii. Dɛ o kpoŋe ayaawa lampea, o nyoa buni tɔɡre aa ɛ kilore atoro ne fah, dɛ berɛ kpoŋe tokobifale ɡe.

english_verse: But Abishai came to the rescue and killed the Philistine. David's soldiers told him, “We can't let you risk your life in battle anymore! You give light to our nation, and we want that flame to keep burning.”
translation_verse: Asɛ Seruya bibaa Abisae ba dɛ ba lɛ kooro. O baa yo Filisti te la dɛ kpoo. Belaa Kooro laa tena la ŋwɛɛ baɡlo ŋɔ, “N naa kooro, haa ya nɛɛ teŋɛ la laa kpa, ɡɛɛ dɛ́ ɡel hen haa do kɛŋɔ kandea dɛ tɔ ya Israel tena sie nɔ, ba bɛ hen ba kpo, ásɛ Israel kandea dime, ya paŋɛ.”

english_verse: There was another battle with the Philistines at Gob, where Sibbecai from Hushah killed a descendant of the Rephaim named Saph.
translation_verse: Anɔ habɔɔ, ba ne Filisti tena berɔ yo laa Gɔb. Laa la ta la, Sibekai waa le Husa kpo Rafa waa kpeɡa, o bwara do kpeɡri kohona naanar la bini bɛl baa dɛ yerɔ Saf.

english_verse: There was still another battle with the Philistines at Gob. A soldier named Elhanan killed Goliath from Gath, whose spear shaft was like a weaver's beam. Elhanan's father was Jari from Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Ba ne Filisti tena berɔ yo laa bɛl Gɔb ja, anee Jɛɛ bibaa Ɛlhanan waa le Bɛtlɛham kpo Goliat waa le Gat. O lampea nyoa buni tɔɡre kɛŋɔ yasɔɔh kokorowa daa ken.

english_verse: But when he made fun of Israel, David's nephew Jonathan killed him. Jonathan was the son of David's brother Shimei.
translation_verse: O muɡli Israel tena baah, asɛ Simea waa ɛ Kooro Devid dɔɔranar la bini bɛl bibaa Jonatan kpoo.

english_verse: David and his soldiers killed these four men who were descendants of the Rephaim from Gath.
translation_verse: A ɡɛ nɛra banaarɛ nɔɔ Rafa naanar baa lɔ Gat, asɛ Kooro Devid ne o laa tena kpoo ba.

english_verse: You rescued me from enemies who were hateful and too powerful for me.
translation_verse: O lɛɛ mɛ le n dɔma baa kpeɡa nɔn ta, nɛra baa hah mɛ, dɛ do kpeɡri kohona ɡwaa mɛ.

english_verse: David sang a song to the Lord after the Lord had rescued him from his enemies, especially Saul. These are the words to David's song:
translation_verse: Kooro Devid ɡo yel kpɛɛ Korowii ɡɛ saŋ waa lɛo le Kooro Sɔɔl ne o dɔma bwa nɔn ta.

english_verse: I will praise you, Lord, and I will honor you among the nations.
translation_verse: Anomanta, mɛɛ kpɛɛree harɛre nɛra bwa siee, mɛɛ ɡo yelaa kpɛɛ he sɔn la.

english_verse: Our Lord and our God, you are my mighty rock, my fortress, my protector.
translation_verse: O ŋɔ, “N Naa Korowii do kɛŋɔ Bwetal maa chwaa kaa marɛ, ne danjwɛkpeɡ dɛɛ lɛɛ mɛ,

english_verse: You are the rock where I am safe. You are my shield, my powerful weapon, and my place of shelter. You rescue me and keep me safe from violence.
translation_verse: Korowii maa dɛ tomɛ do kɛŋɔ Bwetal maa chwaa kaa marɛ. Onee dɛɛ tɔ mɛ ɡbemɡbe dɛ ɛ n Kpeɡnɛn. Onee n chwa baa pɛl dɛɛ dɔ n nyu, dɛ ɛ n Lɛɛ le nɛra baa dɛ nyin yoi nɔn ta.

english_verse: I praise you, our Lord! I prayed to you, and you rescued me from my enemies.
translation_verse: N wio dɛɛ yerɛ Korowii waa chɛ kpɛɛra kohona, on lɛɛ mɛ le n dɔma nɔn ta.

english_verse: Death, like ocean waves, surrounded me, and I was almost swallowed by its flooding waters.
translation_verse: Seo do kɛŋɔ nehɛma dɛ lɔ baa tɔ n nɛ, a lɔɔ ba tɔ n nɛ kɛŋɔ ne aa sua, mɛɛ ba sewa.

english_verse: Ropes from the world of the dead had coiled around me, and death had set a trap in my path.
translation_verse: A do kɛŋɔ seo aa dɔ ŋwɛɛra dɛ laɡ mɛ kpoŋe, kɛŋɔ lalbɔɔ aa har mɛ bela ken.

english_verse: I was in terrible trouble when I called out to you, but from your temple you heard me and answered my prayer.
translation_verse: N wenaale ta la, n wio yerɛ Korowii, n wio yerɛ Korowii maa dɛ tomɔ ó cha mɛ. O lɔ o Dea bela baa dɛ tomɔ dɛ no n taa, n wii maa dɛ wi la tel o be.

english_verse: Earth shook and shivered! The columns supporting the sky rocked back and forth. You were angry
translation_verse: Harɛ jiɡro jiɡra tenten, asɛ kwaa aa lawɛ nyundua kpoŋe yiiɡi, dɛkalkɛ dɛ Korowii baah diu.

english_verse: and breathed out smoke. Scorching heat and fiery flames spewed from your mouth.
translation_verse: Korowii hwee chuu le o mebɔɔne bini, nii aa dɛ chɔɡ kwa ne hɔla ɛɛ le o nyoa.

english_verse: You opened the heavens like curtains, and you came down with storm clouds under your feet.
translation_verse: O forɔ le nyundua dɛ ba harɛ, asɛ baama biŋere do o naa lɔɡre.

english_verse: You rode on the backs of flying creatures. You appeared with the wind as wings.
translation_verse: O soɡe Kerobim aa ɛ kena kwaa ta ir kaa nyundua, a do kɛŋɔ peu aa dɔ kena dɛ kpɔɔ ir dɛɛ kaa ken.

english_verse: Darkness was your tent! Thunderclouds filled the sky, hiding you from sight.
translation_verse: O kpɔ biro tɔ o te kɛŋɔ yal, baama biŋere aa dɛ nɛ bwaala baro cheme.

english_verse: Fiery coals lit up the sky in front of you.
translation_verse: Bwaala kɔrɔ, dɛ nyɛɡle, asɛ nii chaah o sie.

english_verse: Lord Most High, your voice thundered from the heavens.
translation_verse: Nemenɛ Korowii kɔrɔ le nyundua kɛŋɔ bwaala ken, asɛ nɛra no o taa.

english_verse: You roared at the sea, and its deepest channels could be seen. You snorted, and the earth shook to its foundations.
translation_verse: Korowii baah diu dɛ kah o dɔma aa, mpo vile bwa dɛ chɔ baŋ, baa na kwaa aa lawɛ harɛ kpoŋe.

english_verse: You reached down from heaven, and you lifted me from deep in the ocean.
translation_verse: O ha nɔn le nyundua ba laɡ mɛ kpoŋe, dɛ kpɔ mɛ le vile bini.

english_verse: On the day disaster struck, they came and attacked, but you defended me.
translation_verse: N fa aa lɔ wenaale ta la, ba baa yoo mɛ, kɛ Korowii baa che n habɔɔ.

english_verse: When I was fenced in, you freed and rescued me because you love me.
translation_verse: O cha mɛ dɛ laɡ mɛ le wekpeɡa nyoa, o sie aa dɛ lɛ n nɛɛ nomanta, o lɛɛ mɛ.

english_verse: You are good to me, Lord, because I do right, and you reward me because I am innocent.
translation_verse: Korowii cheɡɛ toɡra n wa aa toɡra ta dɛ cha mɛ, o swee mɛ andɛɛɡa, dɛkalkɛ n di boldɛɛɡe.

english_verse: I do what you want and never turn to do evil.
translation_verse: N dɛ teŋɛ Korowii Mmarare la ta, n ta habɔɔ berɛ kpo Korowii maa dɛ tomɔ la.

english_verse: I keep your laws in mind and never turn away from your teachings.
translation_verse: N dɛ teŋɛ o Mmarare bwa ta, n ta waa waa do mɛ a ta ɡelɛ.

english_verse: I obey you completely and guard against sin.
translation_verse: O jemɔ kɛ wechɔɡe bɛlbwa toole n nɛ, n laa n te kpɔ wechɔɡa ta.

english_verse: You have been good to me because I do right; you have rewarded me for being innocent by your standards.
translation_verse: A waa o che toɡra n waa aa toɡra ta dɛ cha mɛ, o jemɔ kɛ n di boldɛɛɡe.

english_verse: You are always loyal to your loyal people, and you are faithful to the faithful.
translation_verse: N Naa Korowii, he waa dɔ kasinteŋ tɛ nɛn o wa aa dɔ kasinteŋ, ɡɛ haa ɛ nɛndɛɛɡe la, ɡɛɛ hɛɛ nyin nɛndɛɛɡe wa.

english_verse: With all who are sincere you are sincere, but you treat the unfaithful as their deeds deserve.
translation_verse: Gɛ he tea aa toa la, ɡɛɛ hɛɛ baɡlo ɡɛ he tea aa toa wa, kɛ nyubinikpeɡ tena te, he dɛ baɡ ba kɛ he dɔ wejema dɛ bol ba waa dɛɛ pa bole.

english_verse: You rescue the humble, but you look for ways to put down the proud.
translation_verse: He dɛ lɛ nɛra ba wa a pwɛra, kɛ mbarafo tena te, he dɛ ba ba ne harɛ.

english_verse: Our Lord and God, you are my lamp. You turn darkness to light.
translation_verse: N Naa Korowii, henee do kɛ kandea dɛɛ chaah mɛ, henee ɡela biro ber mɛ bɔr waa chaahna.

english_verse: Your way is perfect, Lord, and your word is correct. You are a shield for those who run to you for help.
translation_verse: Korowii maa dɛ tomɔ te, o ŋwɛnɛre toɡrɔ, o waa waa bol bwa ɛ kasinteŋ. Nɛra baa chwaa kaa marɔ la, o dɛ tɔ ba ɡbemɡbe dɛɛ lɛɛ ba.

english_verse: You alone are God! Only you are a mighty rock.
translation_verse: Korowii habɔɔ, nomɛlbwa toole. O ɡbosoo do kɛ Bwetal n chwa kaa marɔ wɛɛ lɛɛ mɛ.

english_verse: You are my strong fortress, and you set me free.
translation_verse: Korowiirii dɛɛ tɛ mɛ bokpeɡa, dɛ ɡel n ŋwɛnɛre bwa do wer tɛ mɛ.

english_verse: You make my feet run as fast as those of a deer, and you help me stand on the mountains.
translation_verse: O ɡelɔ n nakpale do kɛŋɔ chwae kwaa ken, n won bwejena dor cheɡa, n bwara ɛɛ sɔɔh mɛ.

english_verse: You teach my hands to fight and my arms to use a bow of bronze.
translation_verse: O dɛ baɡ mɛ ɡɛ maa yo laa nɔɔra ne, ɡɛ maa ɡure to baa kpɔ ayaawa ɛo dɛ́ yo.

english_verse: You alone are my shield, and by coming to help me, you have made me famous.
translation_verse: N Naa Korowii, henee tɔ mɛ ɡbemɡbe dɛɛ lɛɛ mɛ, he balɔ ba cha mɛ dɛ ɡel n dɔ sɔn.

english_verse: You clear the way for me, and now I won't stumble.
translation_verse: He kwaa ŋwɛnɛ o do paɡri tɛ mɛ, ásɛ n bɛ naa lɔ.

english_verse: I kept chasing my enemies until I caught them and destroyed them.
translation_verse: N ti n dɔma dɛ ka pɔ ba nɛ, maa ba nɛɛ teŋaa ɡel, ka tel kɛŋɔ maa kpoo ba.

english_verse: I destroyed them! I stuck my sword through my enemies, and they were crushed under my feet.
translation_verse: N kpoo ba bil, baa wola won ir, n pɔ ba nɛɛ ba serewe chɔ n sie.

english_verse: You helped me win victories and forced my attackers to fall victim to me.
translation_verse: Hen Korowiirii tɛ mɛ bokpeɡa mɛɛ yo laa, he ɡelɔ n pɔ n dɔma nɛ.

english_verse: You made my enemies run, and I killed them.
translation_verse: He ɡelɔ n dɔma chwa le n sie, n kpoo ba.

english_verse: They cried out for help, but no one saved them; they called out to you, but there was no answer.
translation_verse: Ba wio dɛɛ nyin nɛn ó ba cha ba, kɛ nomɛlbwa ta balɛ dɛ ba lɛɛ ba. Ba wio no hen Korowii, he ta ban chaŋɛ.

english_verse: I ground them to dust, and I squashed them like mud in the streets.
translation_verse: N pɔ ba nɛɛ ba chɔ harɛ kɛŋɔ bomboɡ peu aa taa dɛ kpɔa dɛɛ kaa, n tiɡri ba nɛɛ kɛŋɔ kpechɛɡre ken fɔɡbaahna.

english_verse: You rescued me from my stubborn people and made me the leader of foreign nations, who are now my slaves.
translation_verse: He lɛɛ mɛ le n nɛra baa ɛ deŋnekpeɡ tena nɔn ta, dɛ lee mɛ cheɡ kɛŋɔ harɛre bwa nyu te. Nɛra maa wola ban jemɛ baa do n lɔɡa.

english_verse: They have lost all courage and from their fortresses they come trembling.
translation_verse: Ba bambile chɔɡɔ, dɛ kpɔ bochela le ba dekpeɡa bini dɛɛ ba.

english_verse: You are the living Lord! I will praise you! You are a mighty rock. I will honor you for keeping me safe.
translation_verse: N jemɔ kɛ Korowii lole saŋ bɛlbwa, o chɛ kpɛɛra. N dɛ kpɛɛ Korowii waa do kɛ Bwetal n chwa kaa marɔ wɛɛ lɛɛ mɛ la!

english_verse: You took revenge for me, and you put nations in my power.
translation_verse: Onee ɡela n yo n dɔma dɛɛ pɔ ba nɛ, dɛ lawɛ harɛre nɛra baa do n lɔɡa,

english_verse: You protected me from violent enemies, and you made me much greater than all of them.
translation_verse: dɛ lɛɛ mɛ le n dɔma be. N Naa Korowii, he ɡelɔ n pɔ n dɔma nɛ, dɛ lɛɛ mɛ le naɡrenyine nɔn ta.

english_verse: The Spirit of the Lord has told me what to say.
translation_verse: “Korowii Doma baa so n nɛ, dɛ kpɔ o waa do n nyoa.

english_verse: is like the sunrise on a cloudless day, or like rain that sparkles on the grass.”

english_verse: Bring him back here, and he will take my place as king. He is the one I have chosen to rule Israel and Judah.

english_verse: Benaiah answered, “We will do it, Your Majesty. I pray that the Lord your God will let it happen.
translation_verse: Anee Jehoiada bibaa Bɛnaya ŋɔ, “A ɛ ɡɛ! Korowii n naa kooro aa dɛ tomɔ la sɛh a ta.

english_verse: Zadok, Nathan, and Benaiah left and took along the two groups of David's special bodyguards. Solomon rode on David's mule as they led him to Gihon Spring.
translation_verse: Ate, sɔfo Sadɔk ne Korowii keame Netan ne Jehoiada bibaa Bɛnaya, dɛ nɛra baa dɛ daah kooro la la ka kpɔ Solomɔn so Kooro Devid keeɡo ta, dɛ teŋɛ o nɛɛ kaa o ne Gehɔn.

english_verse: Zadok the priest brought some olive oil from the sacred tent and poured it on Solomon's head to show that he was now king. A trumpet was blown and everyone shouted, “Long live King Solomon!”
translation_verse: Asɛ sɔfo Sadɔk kpɔ nyeɡle bɛl noo aa lɔ o bini le Korowii Dea Cheremibɔr, dɛ ba fuɡe do Solomɔn nyu ta. Ba hoh bɛla la, asɛ nɛra baa teŋɛ o nɛɛ bwa ɛɛ moo kohona ŋɔ, “Korowii tɛ Kooro Solomɔn mkpajaŋ!”

english_verse: Then they played flutes and celebrated as they followed Solomon back to Jerusalem. They made so much noise that the ground shook.
translation_verse: Nɛra la bwa teŋɛ o nɛ dɛɛ hoh kalipere dɛɛ hɛɡre kohona, asɛ harɛ bwa ɛɛ jiɡri kohona.

english_verse: Adonijah and his guests had almost finished eating when they heard the noise. Joab also heard the trumpet and asked, “What's all that noise about in the city?”
translation_verse: Dɛ Adonija ne nɛra waa ta nɔn yer ba baa di kwaa dɛɛ lɛ ba sie la, deno dɛɛ tonɛ dɛ no ɡbɔɡa la. Baa dɛ no bɛla la sii la, Joab bɔɔrɔ ŋɔ, “Gbɔɡa aa dɛ le bwɛjen nɔ ta nɔ munii ɛrɔɔ?”

english_verse: Just then, Jonathan son of Abiathar came running up. “Come in,” Adonijah said. “An important man like you must have some good news.”
translation_verse: O nyoa taa lɔ waa la ta la, dɛ sɔfo Abiata bibaa Jonatan deno ba jo ba be. Asɛ Adonija ŋɔ, “Ba, he ɛ nɛndɛɛɡe, jamɔ he ba amanesoma ne.”

english_verse: Jonathan answered: No, I don't! David has just announced that Solomon will be king.
translation_verse: Jonatan chaŋe ŋɔ, “Akai, ya naa Kooro Devid cheɡ Solomɔn kora ta.

english_verse: Solomon rode David's own mule to Gihon Spring, and Zadok, Nathan, Benaiah, and David's special bodyguards went with him. When they got there, Zadok and Nathan made Solomon king. Then everyone celebrated all the way back to Jerusalem. That's the noise you hear in the city.
translation_verse: asɛ sɔfo Sadɔk ne Korowii keame Netan ka fuɡe noo do o nyu ta dɛ cheɡo kora Gehɔn bule ta, dɛ berɛ baa kaa asɛ bwɛɛ bwa ɛɛ moo ɡɛ la.

english_verse: Solomon is now king.
translation_verse: Hale taraken Solomɔn soɡe kookara la ta.

english_verse: And listen to this! David's officials told him, “We pray that your God will help Solomon to be an even greater king!” David was in his bed at the time, but he bowed
translation_verse: Anɔ la aa jaa ɡee kɛŋɔ, Kooro Devid nomonome ɡe la o be dɛ kaa jaamo ŋɔ, ‘Korowii haa dɛ tomɔ la ɡel Solomɔn sɔn le ɡwaale, ásɛ o kora ɡe do kan ɡwaa he kon!’ Asɛ Kooro Devid ir so o chɔɔbɔr dɛ soŋe ŋɔ,

english_verse: and prayed, “I praise you, Lord God of Israel. You have made my son Solomon king and have let me live to see it.”
translation_verse: ‘Korowii Israel tena aa dɛ tomɔ laanee chɛ kpɛɛra kɛŋɔ waa ɡela n na n bibaa Solomɔn o ba chiɡ n naa ta dɛɛ di kora fini nɔ.’ ”

english_verse: Adonijah's guests shook with fear when they heard this news, and they left as fast as they could.
translation_verse: Belaa nɛra Adonija aa ta nɔn yer ba la ɔmɛ dɛ bwa ir peɡre, bɛlbwa kaa o dem.

english_verse: Someone told Solomon, “Adonijah is afraid of you and is holding onto the corners of the altar. He wants you to promise that you won't kill him.”
translation_verse: Ate, ba ka ŋɔ Kooro Solomɔn be ŋɔ, “Adonija dɛ ɔmɛ, dɛ ka lawɛ kwaa aa paaɡe saraha kon la ta kɛŋɔ nyeɡlare la kpoŋe dɛɛ soŋe kɛŋɔ, ‘Kooro Solomɔn ŋwɛɛ baɡ mɛ fini kɛŋɔ waa men kpo.’ ”

english_verse: Solomon answered, “If Adonijah doesn't cause any trouble, I won't hurt him. But if he does, I'll have him killed.”
translation_verse: Anee Kooro Solomɔn chaŋe ŋɔ, “Dɛ wɛɛ kpɔ o tenee do n lɔɡa aa, wɛɛ dɔ o nyuu. Dɛ ɡɛ laa tenaa, wɛɛ sewɔɔ.”

english_verse: Then he sent someone to the altar to get Adonijah. After Adonijah came and bowed down, Solomon said, “Adonijah, go home.”
translation_verse: Belaa Kooro Solomɔn tomɛ nɛra ba ka lawɛ Adonija le saraha kon la ta dɛ kpɔɔ ba, asɛ o ba ɡuŋi Kooro Solomɔn sie, asɛ o ŋɔ Adonija be ŋɔ, “Kaa he dem.”

english_verse: My son, I will soon die, as everyone must. But I want you to be strong and brave.
translation_verse: “Saŋ telo kɛŋɔ n sewɛ name, anomanta, lawɛ he te dɛ che kiŋkiŋ

english_verse: Do what the Lord your God commands and follow his teachings. Obey everything written in the Law of Moses. Then you will be a success, no matter what you do or where you go.
translation_verse: dɛɛ nyiŋi Korowii haa dɛ tomɔ la waa waa doe a ta la ta kɛrɛdɛ, dɛɛ teŋɛ o Mmarare ne waa aa dɛ baɡle ɡɛ baa chwera do Mosis Tɔn la bini la ta, ásɛ kerekere wobɛlbwa haa dɛ ɛ, ne bobɛlbwa haa la la, a do wer tɛɛ.

english_verse: You and your descendants must always faithfully obey the Lord. If you do, he will keep the solemn promise he made to me that someone from our family will always be king of Israel.
translation_verse: Dɛ he ɛ ɡɛ naa, Korowii ɛɛ teŋɛ nyoa waa baɡ mɛ kɛŋɔ waa ŋɔa ŋɔ, ‘Dɛ he naanar soɡo kɛrɛdɛ ɡɛ aa wera dɛɛ teŋɛ n nɛɛ ba bambile ne ba liire bwa ne naa, banee dɛɛ ba baa di Israel harɛ ta kora la.’ ”

english_verse: Solomon, don't forget what Joab did to me by killing Abner son of Ner and Amasa son of Jether, the two commanders of Israel's army. He killed them as if they were his enemies in a war, but he did it when there was no war. He is guilty, and now it's up to you to punish him
translation_verse: Kooro Devid berɔ ŋɔ, “He ɡbabir na ɡɛ Seruya bibaa Joab aa ɛɛ mɛ dɛ kpo Israel laa sitɔɔla banɛ. Nɛr bibaa Abna ne Jɛta bibaa Amasa. O saahnɔ kpoo ba kɛŋɔ nɛra baa kpoo ba laa ta bɔ kem, ɡɛ saŋ yaa soɡe deŋnesɔɔhna ta, laa yoi aa wola toole kpa ta. O kpɔ ba chale fɔɡɛ o kiriso ne o naŋɡawa, ba seo ɡure o nyu ta.

english_verse: in the way you think best. Whatever you do, don't let him die peacefully in his old age.
translation_verse: Anomanta, he ɡbaɡba nyiŋi dɛ́ na ɡɛ haa tɛr o deŋne he wejema ne, dɛ bɛ ɡel o sewɛ nyumpompoŋ ne bansɔɔhna ta.

english_verse: Be sure to do something about Shimei son of Gera from Bahurim in the territory of Benjamin. He cursed and insulted me the day I went to Mahanaim. But later, when he came to meet me at the Jordan River, I promised that I wouldn't kill him.
translation_verse: Berɛ no, Gɛra bibaa Simei waa le Bɛnjamen dea dɛ le bwɛɛ bɛl baa dɛ yerɔ Bahurim la lɔ bela. Onee taah mɛ kohona awola maa la bobɛl baa dɛ yerɔ Mahanaim la, kɛ a habɔɔ waa baa chem mɛ Jɔɔdan Moo nyoa la, n ŋwɛɛrɔ Korowii sɔn ta baɡlo kɛŋɔ maa on kpo.

english_verse: Now you must punish him. He's an old man, but you're wise enough to know that you must have him killed. David Dies
translation_verse: Kɛ a ta chɛ kɛ he ɡelo o kaa bosɔɔhna ne, he jemɛ waa ɡa. Na ɡɛ háa ɛ ásɛ o sewɛ.” Kooro Devid seo wa

english_verse: Joab's family will always suffer because of what he did, but the Lord will always bless David's family and his kingdom with peace.

english_verse: His son Solomon became king and took control of David's kingdom. Adonijah Is Killed
translation_verse: Kooro Solomɔn soɡe o mɛɛ Devid kora la ta asɛ o kora che kiŋkiŋ. Adonija seo wa

english_verse: One day, Adonijah went to see Bathsheba, Solomon's mother, and she asked, “Is this a friendly visit?” “Yes.
