english_verse: Here's what you should do. First, get rid of those
translation_verse: Ir koranar fifraatoro dɛ banɛ la bwa, dɛ kpɔ laa sitɔɔla chiɡ ba buɡ ta.

english_verse: Then get more soldiers, horses, and chariots, so your army will be as strong as it was before. We'll fight Israel's army on flat land and wipe them out. Benhadad agreed and did what they suggested.
translation_verse: Berɛ nyin laa tena haa paŋa la dɔŋa, dɛ jaɡre ne torɔɡore baa vɔwa pɛl jaɡre la dɔŋa. Ya ne ba cheme harɛpɛɛ ta naa, ya bokpeɡa ɛɛ ɡwaa ba nɛɛ, yá pɔ ba nɛ.” Asɛ kooro sɛh ba be dɛ ɛ ɡɛ.

english_verse: In the spring, Benhadad got his army together, and they marched to the town of Aphek to attack Israel.

english_verse: The prophet went to Ahab and said, “The Syrians think the Lord is a god of the hills and not of the valleys. So he has promised to help you defeat their powerful army. Then you will know that the Lord is in control.”
translation_verse: Belaa Korowii keame la la Israel Kooro Ahab be dɛ ŋɔ Korowii ŋɔ, “Siiria tena dɛ lii kɛŋɔ men Korowii lɔ deŋɡarere ta, n toole harɛre aa chɔa kaa ta nomanta, mɛɛ kpɔ laa tena damanta nɔɔ do he nɔn taa, ásɛ he jemɛ kɛŋɔ menee Korowii.”

english_verse: For seven days the two armies stayed in their camps, facing each other. Then on the seventh day the fighting broke out, and before sunset the Israelites had killed

translation_verse: Ate, bonɔɔna la na kɛŋɔ a ɛ wedɛɛɡa, asɛ dɛ sɛh Israel Kooro waa la ta warane dɛ ŋɔ, “Ɔɔh, he lole Bɛn Hadadee.” Anee Kooro Ahab ŋɔ, “Hé ka kpɔɔ ba!” Kooro Bɛn Hadad aa lea dɛ ba o be la, o ɡelɔ o jo torɔɡo baa vɔwa pɛl jaaɡɔ bini.

And you can have shops in Damascus, just as my father had in Samaria.” Ahab replied, “If you do these things, I'll let you go free.” Then they signed a peace treaty, and Ahab let Benhadad go. A Prophet Condemns Ahab
translation_verse: Kooro Bɛn Hadad ŋɔ Kooro Ahab be ŋɔ, “Mɛɛ berɛ bwɛjena n mɛɛ aa lɛa le he mɛɛ be laanee tɛɛ, ásɛ he ɛ he ɡbaɡba bonadibɔra Damaskɔs, ɡɛ n mɛɛ aa ɛa Samaria la.” Asɛ Kooro Ahab ŋɔ, “Dɛ he ɡelɔ ya fɔwɛ ɡɛ fɔo aa, mɛɛ kpɔe ta he kaa.” Anomanta, o ne o fɔwɛ fɔo asɛ o tao ŋwɛnɛ o kaa. Korowii keame bɛl pwah Kooro Ahab

english_verse: About this time the Lord commanded a prophet to say to a friend, “Hit me!” But the friend refused,
translation_verse: Ate, Korowii do o keamere baa pɛa dɛɛ valɛ la bɛl ŋɔ, ó ŋɔ o dɔŋ be ŋɔ, “Kpɔ he tokobii ŋwɛn mɛ.” Asɛ o vɛh.

english_verse: and the prophet told him, “You disobeyed the Lord, and as soon as you walk away, a lion will kill you.” The friend left, and suddenly a lion killed him.
translation_verse: Anee keame la ŋɔ o dɔŋ la be ŋɔ, “Haa vɛh Korowii waa nomanta, haa den le n be bonɔ dɛɛ kaa la, nyujente ɛɛ kpoe.” Waa dena le bela la, nyujente lawɔ dɛ kpoo.

english_verse: The prophet found someone else and said, “Hit me!” So this man beat him up.
translation_verse: Korowii keame la berɛ na o keame dɔŋ bɛl ɡe dɛ ŋɔ, “Lɔ mɛ!” Asɛ o lɔɔ kohona dɛ doo bol.

english_verse: The prophet left and put a bandage over his face to disguise himself. Then he went and stood beside the road, waiting for Ahab to pass by.
translation_verse: Keame la kpɔ kon vɔwɛ sie dɛ kpɔ o te sɔh, dɛ ka che ŋwɛnɛ ta dɛɛ kpa Israel Kooro Ahab.

english_verse: When Ahab went by, the prophet shouted, “Your Majesty, right in the heat of battle, someone brought a prisoner to me and told me to guard him. He said if the prisoner got away, I would either be killed or forced to pay
translation_verse: Kooro aa ba dɛ kaa la, Korowii keame la yerɔ dɛ ŋɔ, “N naa kooro, he bonɔɔ lɔ laa ta asɛ laa tena la bɛl lawɛ dɔma la bɛl ba tɛ mɛ dɛ ŋɔ, ‘Nyiŋi baa nɔ nɛɛ tɛ mɛ o bɛ chwa, dɛ o chwao waa hɛɛ kpɔ he nyuu charɛ, kɛɛ he bɔ suuɡapoŋa kilore fifraatoro dɛ anaarɛ.

english_verse: But I got busy doing other things, and the prisoner escaped.” Ahab answered, “You will be punished just as you have said.”
translation_verse: Kɛ n sie berɔ do waane ta mɛɛ ɛ asɛ baa la dɔ bɔr chwa.’ ” Anee Kooro Ahab chaŋe ŋɔ, “He ɡbaɡbaa baɡle ɡɛ aa chɛ kɛ ba tɛr he deŋne.”

english_verse: The man quickly tore the bandage off his face, and Ahab saw that he was one of the prophets.
translation_verse: Korowii keame la pur yal waa kpɔa vɔwɛ o siebɔr la, buɡ la ta, Kooro na kɛŋɔ Korowii keamere la bini bɛlee.

english_verse: The prophet said, “The Lord told you to kill Benhadad, but you let him go. Now you will die in his place, and your people will die in place of his people.”
translation_verse: Belaa Korowii keame la ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Waa Korowii aa dɛ bol laanee kɛŋɔ, ‘Haa ɡela baa maa kpɔɔ do he nɔn ta ŋɔ o chɛ kpoe, asɛ he ɡel o dɔ bɔr chwa dɛ dɔ o nyu nomanta, hɛɛ kpɔ he nyuu charɛ o kon, ásɛ he laa tena ɡe kpɔ ba nyuune charɛ o laa tena nyuune.’ ”

english_verse: Ahab went back to Samaria, angry and depressed.
translation_verse: Ate, Kooro Ahab kpɔ sum ne bandia kaa o koodem Samaria.

english_verse: One day, Ahab said, “Naboth, your vineyard is near my palace. Give it to me so I can turn it into a vegetable garden. I'll give you a better vineyard or pay whatever you want for yours.”
translation_verse: Awola bɛl, Kooro Ahab ŋɔ Nabɔt be ŋɔ, “He bodɛɛɡe haa du daa nɔ bɛne n koodem, kpɔ tɛ mɛ ń parɛ papooni baa kpɔa dɛɛ ɛ dɔkpɔɡa dɔr ne kela ne ntoosi dɛ ŋwana. Mɛɛ tɛɛ daa koo waa wera ɡwaalo, dɛ he dɛ nyin ɡe aa, n tɛɛ suuɡa aa chɛ o yoɡ.”

english_verse: Naboth answered, “This vineyard has always been in my family. I won't let you have it.”
translation_verse: Anee Nabɔt ŋɔ, “N naa kooro, n naawa kapɛrɛ koo, asɛ n di, Korowii ɛɛ la ane bojaŋ kɛŋɔ ń kpɔ ya kapɛrɛ kon tɛɛ.”

english_verse: So Ahab went home, angry and depressed because of what Naboth had told him. He lay on his bed, just staring at the wall and refusing to eat a thing.
translation_verse: Ate, Kooro Ahab kpɔ sum ne bandia kaa dem, waa Nabɔt aa bola baɡlo kɛŋɔ “Maa n naawa kapɛrɛ konee kpɔ tɛɛ” la wa. Asɛ bwaawee farɔ o ka chɔ dɛ vɛh kwaa dii.

english_verse: Jezebel his wife came in and asked, “What's wrong? Why won't you eat?”
translation_verse: Kooro haah Jɛsɛbɛl la o be dɛ ka pɛɛro ŋɔ, “Bɔkwa waa he kpɔ sum ne bandia so, haa wola kwaa kwaraa di nɔɔ?”

english_verse: “I asked Naboth to sell me his vineyard or to let me give him a better one,” Ahab replied. “And he told me I couldn't have it.”
translation_verse: Kooro chaŋe o haah ŋɔ, “Nabɔt waa lɔ Jesreel la bee n ŋɔ ó yoɡ o daa koo tɛ mɛ, dɛ ɡɛ laa ɡe aa, ń tɛo bɛl o chiɡ o kon la naa ta. Kɛ o vɛoh ŋɔ waa kpɔ tɛ mɛ.”

english_verse: “Aren't you the king of Israel?” Jezebel asked. “Get out of bed and eat something! Don't worry, I'll get Naboth's vineyard for you.”
translation_verse: Anee Jɛsɛbɛl ŋɔ, “Kenii hɛɛ ba kora dii Israel tena nɛ aa? Ir dɛ ɡel he sie lɛ dɛ di kwa. Mɛɛ lɛ Nabɔt Jesreel te daa koo laanee tɛɛ.”

english_verse: They told the people that it was a day to go without eating, and when they all came together, they seated Naboth at the front.
translation_verse: Ba le tɔpebeŋkpoŋ cheɡ dɛ cheme vɔwɛ nyoa, dɛ yerɛ nɛra cheme dɛ tɛ Nabɔt nomonsobɔr.

english_verse: The two liars came in and sat across from Naboth. Then they accused him of cursing God and the king, so the people dragged Naboth outside and stoned him to death.
translation_verse: Nyosonteŋna banɛ la baa so ba ne o sie chaɡɛ dɔŋa, ba haŋɛ o nyoa nɛra la bwa baah ta kɛŋɔ o taah Korowii ne kooro la. Anomanta, ba lawɔ le bwɛjen la ta dɛ ka foɡro bwea kpo.

english_verse: The leaders of Jezreel sent a message back to Jezebel that said, “Naboth is dead.”
translation_verse: Asɛ ba kpɔ kala tɛ ba ka ŋɔ Jɛsɛbɛl be ŋɔ, “Ba foɡre Nabɔt bwea kpo.”

english_verse: As soon as Jezebel got their message, she told Ahab, “Now you can have the vineyard Naboth refused to sell. He's dead.”
translation_verse: Jɛsɛbɛl aa dena no kɛŋɔ ba foɡre Nabɔt bwea kpo la, o ŋɔ Kooro Ahab be ŋɔ, “Ir dɛ́ ka kpɔ daa koo Nabɔt aa vɛah kɛ wɛɛ yoɡu tɛɛ la. O toole kpa, o sewɔ.”

english_verse: Ahab got up and went to take over the vineyard. Elijah Condemns Ahab
translation_verse: Kooro Ahab aa noa buɡ la ta, o den la Nabɔt daa koo la ta dɛ ka kpɔ ɛ o kon.

english_verse: The Lord said to Elijah the prophet,
translation_verse: Belaa Korowii ŋɔ o keame Elaeja waa le Tisbe be ŋɔ,

english_verse: “King Ahab of Israel is in Naboth's vineyard right now, taking it over.
translation_verse: “La Samaria Israel Kooro Ahab be, o lɔ Nabɔt daa koo ta dɛɛ ba kpɔe berɛ o kon.

english_verse: Go tell him that I say, ‘Ahab, you murdered Naboth and took his property. And so, in the very spot where dogs licked up Naboth's blood, they will lick up your blood.’ ” When Elijah found him,
translation_verse: Ŋɔ o be ŋɔ men Korowii ŋɔ, ‘Ahab, he kpo nɛn dɛ berɛ kpɔ o kwaa di aa? Bela nyootena aa kpɛle Nabɔt chal la, bela tentenee aa ba he ɡe chal kpɛla.’ ”

english_verse: Ahab said, “So, my enemy, you found me at last.” Elijah answered: Yes, I did! Ahab, you have managed to do everything the Lord hates.
translation_verse: Kooro Ahab na Elaeja dɛ ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “N dɔm, he na mɛ.” Elaeja ŋɔ, “Gɛɛ, he ta he nyu dɛ ɛ wechɔɡa Korowii siwi ta.

english_verse: Now you will be punished. You and every man and boy in your family will die, whether slave or free.
translation_verse: Waa Korowii aa dɛ bol laanee kɛŋɔ, ‘Mɛɛ kpɔ wenaalee ba ta he nɛ. Mɛɛ kpo he ne bibaa bɛlbwa waa lɔ he deemii le Israel harɛ ta, yoma ne nɛra baa dɛ di ba nyu bwa.

english_verse: Your whole family will be wiped out, just like the families of King Jeroboam and King Baasha. You've made the Lord very angry by sinning and causing the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Mɛɛ ɛ he demii ɡɛ maa ɛ Nɛbat bibaa Kooro Jɛroboam ne Ahija bibaa Kooro Baasa dem la. He ɡelɔ n baah di dɛ ɡel Israel tena ɛ wechɔɡa dɛ jo n nɛ.’

english_verse: And as for Jezebel, dogs will eat her body there in Jezreel.
translation_verse: Korowii ŋɔ Jɛsɛbɛl ɡe waa ŋɔ, ‘Nyootenaa dɛ́ di o ola bwɛjen Jesreel.’

english_verse: Dogs will also eat the bodies of your relatives who die in town, and vultures will eat the bodies of those who die in the country.
translation_verse: He lole bɛlbwa waa sewɛ bwɛjen la ta la, nyootenaa dɛ́ di o ol. Bɛlbwa ɡe waa ka sewɛ kpɔɡ bini la, jumbii di o ol.”

english_verse: Tell them to put him in prison and to give him nothing but bread and water until I come back safely.”
translation_verse: dɛ́ ka ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, n ŋɔ bá lawɔ do dea, dɛɛ tɛo paanoo ne nee ɡbo ka tel kɛŋɔ maa ba jo sɔnɔnɔɔ.”

english_verse: Ahab asked his officials, “Why haven't we tried to get Ramoth in Gilead back from the Syrians? It belongs to us.”
translation_verse: Kooro Ahab ŋɔ o nomonome be ŋɔ, “Bwɛjen Ramɔt waa lɔ Gelead harɛ ɛ ya kon, ɛrɛɛ yaa wola won ɛ waane dɛ́ berɛ lɛ le Siiria Kooro be nɔ?”

english_verse: Then he asked Jehoshaphat, “Would you go to Ramoth with me and attack the Syrians?” “Just tell me what to do,” Jehoshaphat answered. “My army and horses are at your command.
translation_verse: Asɛ Kooro Ahab bɔɔ Kooro Jehosafat ŋɔ, “Hɛɛ ja n nɛɛ yá ka yo Ramɔt Gelead tena aa?” Kooro Jehosafat ŋɔ, “N sɛh ɡɛ, n ne he bwa ɛ beŋkpoŋ. N nɛra ɛ he nɛra, n jaɡre ɡe ɛ he kwa.”

english_verse: But Jehoshaphat said, “Just to make sure, is there another of the Lord's prophets we can ask?”
translation_verse: Ate, Kooro Jehosafat bɔɔ ŋɔ, “Amɔ Korowii keame bɛlbwa toole ya che o nɛɛ dɛ́ soŋe le Korowii be naa?”

english_verse: “We could ask Micaiah son of Imlah,” Ahab said. “But I hate Micaiah. He always has bad news for me.” “Don't say that!” Jehoshaphat replied.
translation_verse: Anee Kooro Ahab chaŋe ŋɔ, “Korowii keame beŋkpoŋ bɛl lole. Onee Imla bibaa Mikaya. Kɛ n ne waa somɛ, dɛkalkɛ o ta wobɛlbwa nae le Korowii be dɛ tɛ mɛ a ɛ wedɛɛɡa tɛ mɛ bwa, atane wechɔɡa ɡbo.” Kooro Jehosafat ŋɔ, “N naa kooro, bɛ ɡɛ ŋɔ.”

english_verse: Then Ahab sent someone to bring Micaiah as soon as possible.
translation_verse: Asɛ Kooro Ahab yerɛ o nomonome la bini bɛl dɛ ŋɔ, “La ka kpɔ Imla bibaa Mikaya ba taraken.”

english_verse: All this time, Ahab and Jehoshaphat were dressed in their royal robes and were seated on their thrones at the threshing place near the gate of Samaria. They were listening to the prophets tell them what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Dɛ Israel Kooro Ahab ne Juda Kooro Jehosafat do ba koolaala, dɛ so ba kookane ta, pɛla bɛl waa bɛne bwɛjen Samaria doonyoa, asɛ Korowii keamere la bwa che ba sie dɛɛ bol waa baa naa ba be.

english_verse: Zedekiah son of Chenaanah was one of the prophets. He had made some horns out of iron and shouted, “Ahab, the Lord says you will attack the Syrians like a bull with iron horns and wipe them out!”
translation_verse: Korowii keamere la bini bɛlee Kenaana bibaa Sedekia. O kpɔ bune ɛ kwaane a do kɛ nyeɡlare. O ŋɔ Kooro Ahab be ŋɔ, “Waa Korowii aa dɛ bol laanee nɔ. ‘Kwaa nɔɔ hɛɛ ba kpɔe yo Siiria tena, dɛ́ pɔ ba nɛ.’ ”

english_verse: All the prophets agreed that Ahab should attack the Syrians at Ramoth, and they promised that the Lord would help him defeat them.
translation_verse: Dɛ ɡɛ tentenee keamere la bwa bol Korowii waa dɛɛ ŋɔ, “Ka yo Ramɔt Gelead tena, hɛɛ pɔ ba nɛɛ. Korowii ɛɛ ɡeloo he pɔ ba nɛ.”

english_verse: Meanwhile, the messenger who went to get Micaiah whispered, “Micaiah, all the prophets have good news for Ahab. Now go and say the same thing.”
translation_verse: Torome waa laŋa ka ɡaaɡe Mikaya bɔr la ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Korowii keamere la bwa nyoa pɛo ba bol ŋɔ kooro wobɛlbwa chiɡo kɛrɛdɛ. Sɛh dɛ́ ɡel he ne ba waa la ɛ beŋkpoŋ.”

english_verse: Then Micaiah went to Ahab, and Ahab asked, “Micaiah, should I attack the Syrians at Ramoth?” “Yes!” Micaiah answered. “The Lord will help you defeat them.”
translation_verse: Mikaya aa ba Kooro Ahab be la, Kooro pɛɛro ŋɔ, “N ne n dɔŋ Kooro Jehosafat ka yo Ramɔt Gelead tena kɛɛ yá ɡel ɔ?” Mikaya chaŋe ŋɔ, “Hé la ka yoo ba, Korowii ɛɛ ɡeloo hé pɔ ba nɛ.”

english_verse: “Micaiah, I've told you over and over to tell me the truth!” Ahab shouted. “What does the Lord really say?”
translation_verse: Asɛ Kooro Ahab ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Keraŋwɛnɛɛ ń ɡel he ŋwɛɛ kɛŋɔ he bol kasinteŋ Korowii sɔn ta nɔ?”

english_verse: He answered, “In a vision I saw Israelite soldiers walking around in the hills like sheep without a shepherd to guide them. The Lord said, ‘This army has no leader. They should go home and not fight.’ ”
translation_verse: Mikaya ŋɔ, “N na Israel laa tena baa perɛ deŋɡarere ta kɛŋɔ peera aa wola teɡre dɔe ken. Asɛ Korowii ŋɔ, ‘Ba ta sitɔɔ dɔe, ɡel bá berɛ kaa dem deŋnesɔɔhna ne.’ ”

english_verse: Micaiah replied: Listen to this! I also saw the Lord seated on his throne with every creature in heaven gathered around him.
translation_verse: Korowii keame Mikaya berɛ teŋɛ dɛ ŋɔ, “No waa Korowii aa bola. N nao kɛŋɔ Korowii aa soɡe o kookara ta nyundua, o dɔm baa ja o nɛ dɛɛ tomɔ che baro.

english_verse: This is exactly what has happened, Ahab. The Lord made all your prophets lie to you, and he knows you will soon be destroyed.
translation_verse: Korowii keame Mikaya berɛ ŋɔ, “Korowiirii ɡela he keamere la neɡre, o ɡbabirii bol he chɔɡa waa kɛŋɔ a chɛ kɛ hé sewɛ.”

english_verse: Zedekiah walked up to Micaiah and slapped him on the face. Then he asked, “Do you really think the Lord would speak to you and not to me?”
translation_verse: Ate, Kenaana bibaa Korowii keame Sedekia la dɛ ka kpaa Korowii keame Mikaya lwɛɛma dɛ ŋɔ, “Saŋ besoo Korowii Doma ɡel mɛ dɛ ba bol wa he be bwa nɔ?”

english_verse: Ahab shouted, “Arrest Micaiah! Take him to Prince Joash and Governor Amon of Samaria.
translation_verse: Belaa Israel Kooro Ahab ŋɔ o nomonome la bɛl be ŋɔ, “Lawɛ Korowii keame Mikaya kaa Amɔn waa dɛ nyiŋi bwɛjen nɔ ta, ne n bibaa Joas be,

english_verse: However, during the fighting a soldier shot an arrow without even aiming, and it hit Ahab where two pieces of his armor joined. He shouted to his chariot driver, “I've been hit! Get me out of here!”
translation_verse: Siiria laa tena la bɛl ta hɛm o ka yaɡɛ Israel Kooro Ahab kon waa kpɔa tɔ ɡbemɡbe la keŋkeŋ, asɛ dɛ yaɡɛ o bambinyoa dɛ o laa saahna. Asɛ kooro la ŋɔ nɛn waa soɡe o torɔɡo baa vɔwa pɛl jaaɡɔ la be ŋɔ, “Ba do mɛ bol, le n ne laa nɔ ta.”

english_verse: Ahab and Jehoshaphat led their armies to Ramoth in Gilead.
translation_verse: Ate, Israel Kooro Ahab ne Juda Kooro Jehosafat la bwɛjen Ramɔt Gelead dɛ ka yoo ba.

english_verse: Before they went into battle, Ahab said, “Jehoshaphat, I'll disguise myself, but you wear your royal robe.” Then Ahab disguised himself and went into battle.
translation_verse: Israel Kooro Ahab ŋɔ Kooro Jehosafat be ŋɔ, “Mɛɛ beɡre n tenee dɛ́ ka ja laa tena nɔ nɛ, kɛ he te, do he koolaala.” Anomanta, Kooro Ahab beɡre o te dɛ kaa laa la ta.

english_verse: So when they saw Jehoshaphat in his robe, they thought he was Ahab and started to attack him. But when Jehoshaphat shouted out to them,
translation_verse: Laa sitɔɔla la aa na Kooro Jehosafat la, ba liiro ŋɔ Israel kooroo, asɛ ba laa berɛ ŋɔ bá ka yoo. Kɛ waa dɛ dooɡe lɔŋɔre la,

english_verse: they realized he wasn't Ahab, and they left him alone.
translation_verse: mɔɔ ba na kɛŋɔ Israel kooro laa, ba ta on yoi kpa.

english_verse: As the sun was going down, someone in Israel's army shouted to the others, “Retreat! Go back home!”
translation_verse: Wee aa dɛ jo la, takpeɡ le laa tena la baah ta ŋɔ, “Nomɛlbwa berɛ kaa o bwɛɛ ne o harɛ ta!”

english_verse: Ahab's body was taken to Samaria and buried there.
translation_verse: Anomanta, Kooro Ahab sewɔ ba kaa o ne Samaria ka huɡe.

english_verse: Some workers washed his chariot near a spring in Samaria, and prostitutes washed themselves in his blood. Dogs licked Ahab's blood off the ground, just as the Lord had warned.
translation_verse: Ba loo torɔɡo baa vɔwa pɛl jaaɡɔ, o che o bini chal ɛo la Samaria tam bɛl hanjwamanere aa dɛ sɔ nee o ta, asɛ nyootena ka kpɛle o chal la, ɡɛ Korowii aa bol o waa la.

english_verse: Everything else Ahab did while he was king, including the towns he strengthened and the palace he built and furnished with ivory, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Kooro Ahab bwara waa ne o kora ne koodem waa doa dɛ kpɔ bala nyen kwaa o bini ne bwɛjena waa ma danjwɛɛ bara bwa, ba chwera do Israel Koranar Waa Tɔne bini.

english_verse: Ahab died, and his son Ahaziah became king. King Jehoshaphat of Judah (
translation_verse: Kooro Ahab sewɔ ka chɔ o naawa hoɡa ta, asɛ o bibaa Ahasia ba chiɡ o naa ta di kora. Juda Kooro Jehosafat

english_verse: Jehoshaphat son of Asa became king of Judah in Ahab's fourth year as king of Israel.
translation_verse: Kooro Ahab aa di kora Israel harɛ bennaarɛ taa Asa bibaa Jehosafat di kora Juda harɛ.

english_verse: The country of Edom had no king at the time, so a lower official ruled the land.
translation_verse: Dɛ kooro toole Edom harɛ ta, nɛnee Juda kooro le o ka chiɡ o naa ta dɛɛ di kora bela.

english_verse: Jehoshaphat had seagoing ships built to sail to Ophir for gold. But they were wrecked at Ezion-Geber and never sailed.
translation_verse: Kooro Jehosafat kwaa stiimaere asɛ dɛ fee kpɔ la Ofir harɛ ta kaa di suuɡaswɛm bona. Kɛ a kaa paɡre Eseɔn Gɛba a ta wone tel Ofir.

english_verse: Ahaziah son of Ahab offered to let his sailors go with Jehoshaphat's sailors, but Jehoshaphat refused.
translation_verse: Kooro Ahab bibaa Ahasia ŋɔ Kooro Jehosafat be ɡɛ saŋ ŋɔ, “Gel he nɛra ne n nɛra pɛ kpɔ stiimaere la.” Asɛ Kooro Jehosafat vɛh.

english_verse: Jehoshaphat died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Jehoram became king. King Ahaziah of Israel
translation_verse: Kooro Jehosafat sewɔ ka chɔ o naawa hoɡa ta Jerusalam, o naa Kooro Devid Bwɛjen ta. Asɛ o bibaa Jehoram chiɡ o naa ta di kora. Israel Kooro Ahasia

english_verse: Ahaziah son of Ahab became king of Israel in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat's rule in Judah, and he ruled two years from Samaria.
translation_verse: Kooro Jehosafat aa di kora Juda harɛ ta bene fi dɛ anuanɛ taa Kooro Ahab bibaa Ahasia di kora bene anɛ Israel harɛ ta, dɛ so Samaria.

english_verse: Ahaziah disobeyed the Lord, just as his father, his mother, and Jeroboam had done. They all led Israel to sin.
translation_verse: Kooro Ahasia ɛ wechɔɡa dɛ jo Korowii nɛɛ ɡɛ o mɛɛ Kooro Ahab ne o nya Jɛsɛbɛl aa ɛa, dɛ Kooro Jɛroboam waa ɡela Israel tena bwa ɛ wechɔɡa la.

english_verse: Ahaziah worshiped Baal and made the Lord God of Israel very angry, just as his father had done.
translation_verse: O tomɛ voɡ Baal dɛ ɡuŋu, dɛ muɡli Korowii Israel tena aa dɛ tomɔ la baah ɡɛ o mɛɛ aa ɛa la.

english_verse: Soon after King Ahab of Israel died, the country of Moab rebelled against his son King Ahaziah. One day, Ahaziah fell through the wooden slats around the porch on the flat roof of his palace in Samaria, and he was badly injured. So he sent some messengers to the town of Ekron with orders to ask the god Baalzebub if he would get well.
translation_verse: Awola bɛl, Kooro Ahasia le o abrɔsane waa lɔ Samaria saldoa bobɛl waa kpɔ daa sam o koodem bela, dɛ le ba le harɛ dɛɛ we weela. Asɛ o tomɛ toroma Filisti tena bwɛjen bɛl baa dɛ yerɔ Ekron voɡ Baal Sibab ta ŋɔ bá ka voɡɛ kɛ wɛɛ dɔ o nyuu yaa.

english_verse: About the same time, an angel from the Lord sent Elijah the prophet from Tishbe to say to the king's messengers, “Ahaziah has rejected Israel's own God by sending you to ask Baalzebub about his injury.
translation_verse: Kɛ Korowii nyundua torome bɛl ŋɔ Korowii keame Elaeja waa le Tisbe be ŋɔ, ó ka cheme Samaria kooro toroma la dɛ́ bɔɔ ŋɔ, “Korowii Israel tena aa dɛ tomɔ toole kpa, asɛ he berɛ dɛɛ la Ekron voɡ Baal Sibub ta ka bɔɔ le o be nɔ naa?

english_verse: Tell him that because he has done this, he's on his deathbed!” And Elijah did what he was told.
translation_verse: Anomanta, ŋɔ kooro be ŋɔ waa Korowii aa dɛ bol laanee kɛŋɔ, ‘Haa ɡbaŋre dɛ́ ir le bela haa chɔa la, hɛɛ sewɔɔ.’ ” Asɛ Elaeja ɛ ɡɛ Korowii aa doo la.

english_verse: When the messengers returned to Ahaziah, he asked, “Why are you back so soon?”
translation_verse: Asɛ toroma la berɛ laa berɛ ba Kooro Ahasia be, asɛ o bɔɔ ba ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ he den ba warane ken?”

english_verse: “A man met us along the road with a message for you from the Lord,” they answered. “The Lord wants to know why you sent us to ask Baalzebub about your injury and why you don't believe there's a God in Israel. The man also told us that the Lord says you're going to die.”
translation_verse: Ba ŋɔ, “Baa bɛl cheme yaa ŋwɛnɛ ta, dɛ ŋɔ yá berɛ ka ŋɔ kooro waa tomɛ yaa be ŋɔ, waa Korowii aa dɛ bol laanee nɔ, ‘Korowiirii wola toole Israel harɛ ta waa he tomɛ baala ŋɔ, bá la ka bɔɔ le Ekron tena voɡ Baal Sibub ta he weela waa nɔ naa? Anomanta, hɛɛ ka kalaŋ taa, sewaa chɛ kɛŋɔ he sewɛ.’ ”

english_verse: “He was hairy and had a leather belt around his waist,” they answered. “It must be Elijah!” replied Ahaziah.
translation_verse: Ba chaŋe ŋɔ, “Batakaare waa doa la ɛ oltɔn, dɛ berɛ kpɔ oltɔn ɡe vɔwɛ kiriso.” Kooro la ŋɔ, “Tisbe te Elaeja laanee.”

english_verse: Fire has already wiped out the other officers and their soldiers. Please don't let it happen to me.”
translation_verse: Nyiŋi na, ɡɛ nii aa le nyundua dɛ ba fuh laa sitɔɔla banɛ la ne ba laa tena bwa ɡɛ! N poori, na n sum dɛ bɛ ɡel a ba n nɛ.”

english_verse: The angel from the Lord said to Elijah, “Go with him and don't be afraid.” So Elijah got up and went with the officer.
translation_verse: Belaa Korowii nyundua torome bɛl ŋɔ Elaeja be ŋɔ, “Tu he ne o kaa, dɛɛ berɛ ɔma.” Asɛ Elaeja tu ba o ne nomoa la la kooro la be.

english_verse: When Elijah arrived, he told Ahaziah, “The Lord wants to know why you sent messengers to Ekron to ask Baalzebub about your injury. Don't you believe there's a God in Israel? Ahaziah, because you did that, the Lord says you will die.”
translation_verse: Elaeja aa tel bela la, o ŋɔ Kooro Ahasia be ŋɔ, “N naa kooro, waa Korowii aa dɛ bol he be laanee kɛŋɔ, Korowiirii wola toole Israel harɛ ta waa he tomɛ toroma ŋɔ bá la ka bɔɔ le Ekron voɡ Baal Sibub ta he weela nɔ waa naa? A ɡɛ nomanta, haa kalaŋ ta ira ba, sewaa chɛ kɛ he sewɛ.”

english_verse: Ahaziah died, just as the Lord had said. But since Ahaziah had no sons, Joram his brother then became king. This happened in the second year that Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat was king of Judah.
translation_verse: Anomanta, Kooro Ahasia sewɔ ɡɛ Korowii aa cheɡɛ o keame Elaeja nɛɛ dɛ bol la ta. Dɛ Kooro Ahasia ta bibaa dɔe, asɛ o nime Joram chiɡ o naa ta dɛ di Israel kora. Kooro Jehosafat bibaa Kooro Jehoram aa di kora Juda harɛ ta bennɛɛte taa Kooro Joram di kora.

english_verse: Everything else Ahaziah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Waa Kooro Ahasia aa ɛa o kora dii ta bwa la, ba chwera do Israel Koranar Waa Tɔne bini.

english_verse: Not long before the Lord took Elijah up into heaven in a strong wind, Elijah and Elisha were leaving Gilgal.
translation_verse: Saŋ bɛl telo kɛŋɔ dɛ Korowii dɛ ba Elaeja kpɔe dɛ́ kaa nyundua kawulewule ne. Dɛ Elaeja ne o bonɔɔ bɛl baa dɛ yerɔ Elaesa dɛ ba Gelɡal lee dɛ́ kaa.

english_verse: Elijah said to Elisha, “The Lord wants me to go to Bethel, but you must stay here.” Elisha replied, “I swear by the living Lord and by your own life that I will stay with you no matter what!” And he went with Elijah to Bethel.
translation_verse: Baa dɛ kaa la, Elaeja ŋɔ Elaesa be ŋɔ, “So bonɔ, Korowii tom mɛ bwɛɛ bɛl baa dɛ yerɔ Bɛtel.” Anee Elaesa ŋɔ, “N ŋwɛɛ Korowii waa lole saŋ bɛlbwa, asɛ he ɡe do le nɔ kɛŋɔ n ne henee.” Asɛ ba bwa chiɡ ŋwɛnɛ ta kaa Bɛtel.

english_verse: A group of prophets who lived there asked Elisha, “Do you know that today the Lord is going to take away your master?” “Yes, I do,” Elisha answered. “But don't remind me of it.”
translation_verse: Dɛ Korowii keamere bane baa pɛa dɛɛ valɛ lɔ Bɛtel. Ba ba Elaesa be dɛ ba bɔɔro ŋɔ, “He jemɔ kɛŋɔ fini Korowii dɛ ba he dɔɔ kpɔe le he be kaa a ka he ɡbo aa?” Anee o chaŋe ŋɔ, “N jemɔ, hé hel, he bɛ a waa bol.”

english_verse: Elijah then said, “Elisha, now the Lord wants me to go to Jericho, but you must stay here.” Elisha replied, “I swear by the living Lord and by your own life, that I will stay with you no matter what!” And he went with Elijah to Jericho.
translation_verse: Elaeja ŋɔ Elaesa be ja ŋɔ, “Korowii tom mɛ bwɛjen Jeriko, so bonɔ.” Elaesa ŋɔ, “N ŋwɛɛ Korowii waa lole, asɛ he ɡe do le nɔ kɛ n ne henee.” Anomanta, ba kaa Jeriko.

english_verse: A group of prophets who lived there asked Elisha, “Do you know that today the Lord is going to take away your master?” “Yes, I do,” Elisha answered. “But don't remind me of it.”
translation_verse: Korowii keamere baa pɛa dɛɛ valɛ dɛ do Jeriko baa bɔɔ Elaesa ŋɔ, “He jemɔ kɛŋɔ fini Korowii dɛ ba he dɔɔ kpɔe le he be kaa a ka he ɡbo aa?” Elaesa ŋɔ, “N jemɔ, hé hel, he bɛ a waa bol.”

english_verse: Elijah then said to Elisha, “Now the Lord wants me to go to the Jordan River, but you must stay here.” Elisha replied, “I swear by the living Lord and by your own life that I will never leave you!” So the two of them walked on together.
translation_verse: Elaeja berɛ ŋɔ Elaesa be ja ŋɔ, “Korowii tom mɛ Jɔɔdan Moo la ta, kɛ so bonɔ.” Elaesa ŋɔ, “N ŋwɛɛ Korowii waa lole, asɛ he ɡe do le nɔ kɛ n ne henee.” Asɛ ba bwa kaa.

english_verse: Fifty prophets followed Elijah and Elisha from Jericho, then stood at a distance and watched as the two men walked toward the river.
translation_verse: Korowii keamere baa pɛa dɛɛ valɛ fifraanue teŋɔ, dɛ ka jaɡɛ che ba ne ba baah tɛr tama, ba sie chaɡɛ bela Elaeja ne Elaesa aa kaa che Jɔɔdan Moo la nyoa la.

english_verse: When they got there, Elijah took off his coat, then he rolled it up and struck the water with it. At once a path opened up through the river, and the two of them walked across on dry ground.
translation_verse: Asɛ Elaeja foo o batakaare, dɛ laa kpɛwɛ dɛ kpɔ lɔ nee la, asɛ nee la bini pere anɛ, asɛ ba valɛ kpɔ harɛpɛɛ ta le nee la baŋ.

english_verse: After they had reached the other side, Elijah said, “Elisha, the Lord will soon take me away. What can I do for you before that happens?” Elisha answered, “Please give me twice as much of your power as you give the other prophets, so I can be the one who takes your place as their leader.”
translation_verse: Baa le nee la baŋ la, Elaeja ŋɔ Elaesa be ŋɔ, “Korowii ɛɛ ba kpɔ mɛɛ kaa taraken, bɔkwaa hɛɛ nyin kɛ ń ɛ tɛɛ mɔɔ ó ba kpɔ mɛ kaalɔ?” Asɛ Elaesa chaŋe ŋɔ, “Tɛ mɛ he kpeɡri nɔ dɔŋa bele anɛ, ásɛ n chiɡ he naa ta.”

english_verse: “It won't be easy,” Elijah answered. “It can happen only if you see me as I am being taken away.”
translation_verse: Anee Elaeja ŋɔ, “Waa haa dɛ soŋe la kpeɡri kɛŋɔ ń won tɛɛ. Dɛ he na mɛ mɛɛ kaa tenaa, hɛɛ dɔɔ, kɛ dɛ he ta men nae tenaa, haa dɔ.”

english_verse: Elijah and Elisha were walking along and talking, when suddenly there appeared between them a flaming chariot pulled by fiery horses. At once, a strong wind took Elijah up into heaven.
translation_verse: Ba taa bol waa dɛ valɛ dɛɛ kaa la, buɡ la ta, dɛ torɔɡo ne jaɡre baa che Elaesa ne Elaeja baah ta a bwa ɛɛ lawɛ nii, asɛ buɡ la ta, kawulewule den ba kpɔ a ne Elaeja kaa nyundua.

english_verse: Elisha saw this and shouted, “Israel's cavalry and chariots have taken my master away!” After Elijah had gone, Elisha tore his clothes in sorrow.
translation_verse: Elaesa nao dɛ do lɔŋɔ yerɛ Elaeja ŋɔ, “N dɔɔ! N dɔɔ! Nɛn waa cheɡɛ Israel tena habɔɔ! He kaalɔ.” Elaesa ta on nae kpa. O kɛɛ o laala waa doa la bini anɛ, a baɡle kɛŋɔ o loo kuu kohona.

english_verse: Elijah's coat had fallen off, so Elisha picked it up and walked back to the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Dɛ Elaeja yal waa tɔɔ dɛɛ dawɛ o laala ta la leo le, asɛ Elaesa kpɔ dɛ berɛ la ka che Jɔɔdan Moo la nyoa.

english_verse: He struck the water with the coat and wondered, “Will the Lord perform miracles for me as he did for Elijah?” As soon as Elisha did this, a dry path opened up through the water, and he walked across.
translation_verse: O kpɔ Elaeja yal la lɔ nee la dɛ lii ŋɔ, “Leperaa Korowii Elaeja aa tomɔ la dɔɔ?” Waa bera kpɔ lɔ nee la, o bini pero anɛ, asɛ harɛpɛɛ chɔ o valɛ o bini le o baŋ.

english_verse: When the prophets from Jericho saw what happened, they said to each other, “Elisha now has Elijah's power.” They walked over to him, bowed down,
translation_verse: Dɛ Korowii keamere baa pɛa dɛɛ valɛ fifraanue ba le Jeriko la ta cheɡɛ bela nao, asɛ dɛ ŋɔ dɔŋa be ŋɔ, “Elaeja kpeɡri la ba Elaesa nɛ!” Asɛ ba la o be, dɛ ka ɡuŋi o sie,

english_verse: They kept begging until he was embarrassed to say no. He finally agreed, and the prophets sent the men out. They looked three days for Elijah but never found him.
translation_verse: Ba soŋo a ba peo, asɛ o ŋɔ, “Hé tom ba.” Asɛ ba tomɛ baala fifraanue la ba ka ɡaaɡe Elaeja bɔr tɔpera atoro ba ta on nae.

english_verse: They returned to Jericho, and Elisha said, “I told you that you wouldn't find him.” Elisha Makes the Water Pure at Jericho
translation_verse: Asɛ ba laa berɛ ba Jeriko, dɛ Elaesa ta lɔ bela, anee o ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, “N ta he be ŋɔe ŋɔ hé ɡel o bɔr ka ɡaaɡa aa?” Elaesa nyokpowa waa ɛa

english_verse: One day the people of Jericho said, “Elisha, you can see that our city is in a good spot. But the water from our spring is so bad that it even keeps our crops from growing.”
translation_verse: Awola bɛl, bwɛjen Jeriko tena la Elaesa be dɛ ka ŋɔ, “Ya dɔɔ, he ɡbabir nao kɛŋɔ ya bwɛɛ nɔ chɔe wer, kɛ nee yaa dɛ nyɔ aa were, kondikwaa ɡe aa wer do ya harɛ nɔ ta.”

english_verse: He replied, “Put some salt in a new bowl and bring it to me.” They brought him the bowl of salt,
translation_verse: Asɛ Elaesa ŋɔ, “Hé ɛ yar tama do loɡfale ta ba tɛ mɛ.” Asɛ ba ɛ ba tɛo.

english_verse: and he carried it to the spring. He threw the salt into the water and said, “The Lord has made this water pure again. From now on you'll be able to grow crops, and no one will starve.”
translation_verse: Anee o kpɔ la ba bule la ta, dɛ ka fuɡe yar la do o ta dɛ ŋɔ, “Waa Korowii aa dɛ bol laanee kɛŋɔ, ‘N ɡelɔ nee nɔ do wer, harɛ la ɡe ta kwaa ɛɛ do wer nomɛlbwa aa wola sewɛ kpa.’ ”

english_verse: The water has been fine ever since, just as Elisha said. Some Boys Make Fun of Elisha
translation_verse: Nee la wer dɛ ba le fini ɡɛ Elaesa aa ŋɔa o do la.

english_verse: Elisha left and headed toward Bethel. Along the way some boys started making fun of him by shouting, “Go away, baldy! Get out of here!”
translation_verse: Elaesa le Jeriko dɛɛ kaa Bɛtel, waa dɛ kaa la, bechale bane le bwɛɛ la ta dɛ baa ɛo nɛnhɛla ŋɔ, “Le bonɔ, nyuɡbaale te bɛl le!”

english_verse: Elisha turned around and stared at the boys. Then he cursed them in the name of the Lord. At once two bears ran out of the woods and ripped to pieces
translation_verse: Asɛ Elaeja ke nyiŋ ba dɛ taah ba Korowii sɔn ne, asɛ sisirere anɛ le daa ane bini, dɛ ba kpoo bii la bini fifraanaarɛ dɛ banɛ dɛ toɡri ba ola.

english_verse: Elisha went up to Mount Carmel, then returned to Samaria.
translation_verse: Elaesa le bela dɛ teeh kaa Kaamɛl Bwejen doa, dɛ le bela kaa bwɛjen Samaria ta.

english_verse: Joram son of Ahab became king of Israel in Jehoshaphat's eighteenth year as king of Judah. Joram ruled twelve years from Samaria
translation_verse: Kooro Jehosafat aa di kora Juda harɛ ta bene fi dɛ anuatoro taa Kooro Ahab bibaa Kooro Joram di kora Israel harɛ ta. Kooro Joram di kora bene fi dɛ anɛ, dɛ so bwɛjen Samaria.

english_verse: and disobeyed the Lord by doing wrong. He tore down the stone image his father had made to honor Baal, and so he wasn't as sinful as his parents.
translation_verse: Kooro Joram ɛ wechɔɡa dɛ jo Korowii nɛ, kɛ dɛ a ta do kɛ anɔ la o mɛɛ ne o nya Jɛsɛbɛl aa ɛa la. O le voɡ Baal o mɛɛ aa cheɡo dɛɛ tomɔ la ne.

english_verse: But he kept doing the sinful things that Jeroboam son of Nebat had led Israel to do. The Country of Moab Rebels against Israel
translation_verse: Dɛ o teŋɔ dɛɛ ɛ Nɛbat bibaa Kooro Jɛroboam wechɔɡa waa ɛa, dɛ ɡel Israel tena ɛ wechɔɡa dɛ jo Korowii nɛɛ la ane.

english_verse: For many years the country of Moab had been controlled by Israel and was forced to pay taxes to the kings of Israel. King Mesha of Moab raised sheep, so he paid the king of Israel
translation_verse: Dɛ Moab Kooro Mesa dɛ dɛɛ peera. Bena bɛlbwa, o yon kpɔ harɛ la ta kwaa kɛŋɔ pebiiri kaɡboŋa lafa, ne pebala pona kaɡboŋa lafa kaa tɛ Israel Kooro Joram.

english_verse: But soon after the death of Ahab, Mesha rebelled against Israel.
translation_verse: Kɛ Kooro Ahab seo habɔɔ, Moab tena ɛ lwɛmkpeɡ Israel Kooro Joram nɛ.

english_verse: One day, Joram left Samaria and called together Israel's army.
translation_verse: Gɛ saŋ la, Kooro Joram le Samaria, dɛ ka boa Israel laa tena bwa nyoa.

english_verse: He sent this message to King Jehoshaphat of Judah, “The king of Moab has rebelled. Will you go with me to attack him?” “Yes, I will,” Jehoshaphat answered. “I'm on your side, and my soldiers and horses are at your command.
translation_verse: Dɛ tomɛ toroma Juda Kooro Jehosafat be ŋɔ, “Moab kooro ɛ lwɛmkpeɡ n nɛ, hɛɛ ja n nɛɛ ń ka yoo wa aa?” Anee Kooro Jehosafat ŋɔ, “Ɔɔh, n teŋɛ he nɛ, n laa tena ne n jaɡre bwa lɔ he nɔn ta.”

english_verse: But which way should we go?” “We will march through Edom Desert,” Joram replied.
translation_verse: Dɛ berɛ ŋɔ, “Ŋwɛnɛ besoo taa yá kpɔ dɛ́ ka yoo?” Asɛ Kooro Joram ŋɔ, “Yaa kpɔ Edom pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ la taa.”

english_verse: So Joram, Jehoshaphat, and the king of Edom led their troops out. But seven days later, there was no drinking water left for them or their animals.
translation_verse: Ate, Israel Kooro Joram ne Juda Kooro Jehosafat, dɛ Edom kooro kpɔ ba laa tena le. Ba valɔ kpɔ ŋwɛnɛ waa ɡoɡla ta tɔpera anuanɛ, asɛ ba nee ba tonɛ, ane toole nɛra ne ba kondɛɛra nyɔ.

english_verse: Joram cried out, “This is terrible! The Lord must have led us out here to be captured by Moab's army.”
translation_verse: Anee Kooro Joram ŋɔ, “Akwe! Ya na wa. Korowii kpɔ ya koranar batoro nɔ do Moab kooro ne o laa tena nɔn ta!”

english_verse: Jehoshaphat said, “Which of the Lord's prophets is with us? We can find out from him what the Lord wants us to do.” One of Joram's officers answered, “Elisha son of Shaphat is here. He was one of Elijah's closest followers.”
translation_verse: Kooro Jehosafat ŋɔ, “Korowii keame bɛl lɔ bonɔ, ásɛ ya che o nɛɛ bɔɔ le Korowii be naa?” Asɛ Israel Kooro Joram laa nomonome la bɛl ŋɔ, “Safat bibaa Elaesa lɔ bonɔ, dɛ onee dɛɛ cha Elaeja.”

english_verse: Jehoshaphat replied, “He can give us the Lord's message.” The three kings went over to Elisha,
translation_verse: Kooro Jehosafat ŋɔ, “Korowii keame tentenee.” Asɛ koranar batoro la bwa la Elaesa be.

english_verse: and he asked Joram, “Why did you come to me? Go talk to the prophets of the foreign gods your parents worshiped.” “No,” Joram answered. “It was the Lord who led us out here, so that Moab's army could capture us.”
translation_verse: Anee Elaesa ŋɔ Israel Kooro Joram be ŋɔ, “Bɔkwa waa nee he ba dɛɛ nyin ń chae nɔ? La keamere he nya ne he mɛɛ aa la ba be la be.” Kooro Joram ŋɔ, “Akai! Korowiirii yerɛ ya koranar batoro nɔ bonɔ, dɛ kpɔ yaa ba do Moab laa tena nɔn ta.”

english_verse: Elisha said to him, “I serve the Lord All-Powerful, and as surely as he lives, I swear I wouldn't even look at you if I didn't respect King Jehoshaphat.”
translation_verse: Asɛ Elaesa ŋɔ, “N ŋwɛɛ Nemenɛ Korowii waa lole mɛɛ tomɔ kɛŋɔ, dɛ Juda harɛ ta Kooro Jehosafat maa dɛ duuru waa laa aa, n fe aa he siwi taa nyiŋi.”

english_verse: Then Elisha said, “Send for someone who can play the harp.” The harpist began playing, and the Lord gave Elisha this message for Joram:
translation_verse: Dɛ ŋɔ, “Nyin nɛn waa jemɛ janjela lɔe ba tɛ mɛ.” Janjela te la aa dɛ lɔ la, Korowii kpeɡri ba Elaesa nɛ,

english_verse: The Lord says that this dry riverbed will be filled with water.
translation_verse: asɛ Elaesa ŋɔ, “Waa Korowii aa dɛ bol laanee kɛŋɔ, ‘Hé kwi bɔɔne nenabɔɔ nɔ bini bwa.

english_verse: You won't feel any wind or see any rain, but there will be plenty of water for you and your animals.
translation_verse: He nɛra batoro nɔ aa peu kɛɛ bwaalaa na, kɛ nee ɛɛ su nenabɔɔ nɔ bini bwaa, ásɛ he ne he nae ne kondɛɛra bwa dɔ nyɔ.’ ”

english_verse: That simple thing isn't all the Lord is going to do. He will also help you defeat Moab's army.
translation_verse: Elaesa berɔ ŋɔ, “A ɡɛ waa nɔ pwɛre Korowii be, wɛɛ berɔɔ kpɔ Moab laa tena do he nɔn ta he pɔ ba nɛ.

english_verse: You will capture all their walled cities and important towns. You will chop down every good tree and stop up every spring of water, then ruin their fertile fields by covering them with rocks.
translation_verse: Hɛɛ yo bwɛjena baa ma danjwɛkpeɡa bara ne bwɛɛre nɛra bwaa, dɛ́ pɔ ba nɛ, dɛ́ teŋni daa aa dɛ nɔnɛ bwa ta, dɛ́ tɔɔɡe neerare aa dɛ palɛ bwa nyuune. Dɛ kpɔ bwea tɔɔɡe ba harɛdɛɛɡa bwa dɛ́ chɔɡa.”

english_verse: The next morning, while the sacrifice was being offered, water suddenly started flowing from the direction of Edom, and it flooded the land.
translation_verse: Tɔ aa pera chɔɔ ɡɛ saŋ ba yon dɛɛ ɛ sarahare dɛɛ tɛ Korowii la, nee den palɛ le Edom harɛ pera dɛ ba tɔ harɛ la bwa ta.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the people of Moab had heard that the three kings were coming to attack them. They had called together all of their fighting men, from the youngest to the oldest, and these troops were now standing at their border, ready for battle.
translation_verse: Moab tena aa noa kɛŋɔ koranar batoro la dɛ ba bá yoo ba la, ba le baa bɛlbwa waa dɛ ba wona yo, bechale ne nomonome bwa, asɛ ba ka che ba harɛ jwɛh ta nee nyoa.

english_verse: When they got up that morning, the sun was shining across the water, making it look red. The Moabite troops took one look
translation_verse: Baa ira chɔmbibi wee le dɛɛ yaɡɛ nee la sie la, Moab tena baa lɔ ba baŋ bɛl la nao kɛŋɔ nee la aa swɛɛra kɛŋɔ chal ken.

english_verse: and shouted, “Look at that blood! The armies of those kings must have fought and killed each other. Come on, let's go take what's left in their camp.”
translation_verse: Asɛ ba ŋɔ, “Chalee! Koranar batoro la ne ba laa tena ka yoo dɛ kpoo ba te. Hé ba ya ka pa ba laala kɛŋɔ laa ta kwa!”

english_verse: But when they arrived at Israel's camp, the Israelite soldiers came out and attacked them, until they turned and ran away. Israel's army chased them all the way back to Moab, and even there they kept up the attack.
translation_verse: Kɛ Moab tena aa ba bela Israel tena aa soɡa la, Israel tena la yoo ba ba chwa. Israel tena la chwao ti ba dɛɛ kpoo ba.

english_verse: The Israelites destroyed the Moabite towns. They chopped down the good trees and stopped up the springs of water, then covered the fertile fields with rocks. Finally, the only city left standing was Kir-Hareseth, but soldiers armed with slings surrounded and attacked it.
translation_verse: Ba chɔɡ ba bwɛjena, asɛ Israel tena baa chwaa dɛɛ kaa la, bɛlbwa kpɔ vamtor bwe ta harɛdɛɛɡe la ta, ka tel kɛŋɔ waa sua, asɛ nenapale bɛlbwa nyu teŋe, dɛ teŋni daa aa dɛ nɔnɛ ɡe bwa ta. Ba bwɛjen baa dɛ yerɔ Kir Haresɛt ɡboo baa ka, kɛ baala baa kpoŋe vamtore baa bar bwɛjen la dɛ yoo ba.

english_verse: He then grabbed his oldest son who was to be the next king and sacrificed him as an offering on the city wall. The Israelite troops were so horrified that they left the city and went back home.
translation_verse: Asɛ o lawɛ o bibanloɡle waa chiɡ o naa ta dɛ́ di kora la, dɛ kpɔɔ ɛ saraha danjwɛɛ baa maa bar bwɛjen la ta tɛ Moab harɛ voɡ. Israel laa tena la aa na ɡɛ la, ba bambile teŋo kohona ba laa berɛ kaa ba harɛ ta.

english_verse: One day the widow of one of the Lord's prophets said to Elisha, “You know that before my husband died, he was a follower of yours and a worshiper of the Lord. But he owed a man some money, and now that man is on his way to take my two sons as his slaves.”
translation_verse: Awola bɛl, luhaah bɛl o jaa fa aa ɛ Korowii keamere bane baa pɛa dɛɛ valɛ bini bɛl la Elaesa be, dɛ ka wi noo ŋɔ, “Nomoa, n jaa sewɔ. He ɡbabir jemɛ ɡɛ waa tomɛ, ne ɡɛ waa dɛ ɔmɛ Korowii ɡe. Taraken, o di nomɛl kem wɛɛ ba dɛ ba lawɛ n bibaala banɛ yoma bɔ kem.”

english_verse: “Maybe there's something I can do to help,” Elisha said. “What do you have in your house?” “Sir, I have nothing but a small bottle of olive oil.”
translation_verse: Elaesa pɛɛro ŋɔ, “Baɡle kon haa dɛ nyin ń ɛ tɛɛ.” Dɛ berɛ ŋɔ, “Bɔkwaa he dɔ he dem ɔ?” Luhaah la ŋɔ, “He bitolo, n ta komɛlbwa dɔe ka ja ɔleve noo tama ane ɡbo.”

english_verse: Elisha told her, “Ask your neighbors for their empty jars. And after you've borrowed as many as you can,
translation_verse: Elaesa ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “La he bala be dɛ́ ka soŋe viine. Soŋa a warɛ.

english_verse: go home and shut the door behind you and your sons. Then begin filling the jars with oil and set each one aside as you fill it.”
translation_verse: Kaa he dem dɛ́ ka laa ɡbera tɔ he ne he bibaala la nɛ, ásɛ dɛ ka pa mun fuɡe noo le he noo vii bini do viine la bini. A suu waa, he kwaa cheɡ.”

english_verse: The woman left. Later, when she and her sons were back inside their house, the two sons brought her the jars, and she began filling them.
translation_verse: Anomanta, haah la kaa dem dɛ ka laa ɡbera tɔ o ne o bibaala la nɛ ɡɛ Elaesa aa ŋɔ o be la. O bii pa viine tɛo, asɛ o fuɡe noo la dɛɛ do a bini.

english_verse: At last, she said to one of her sons, “Bring me another jar.” “We don't have any more,” he answered, and the oil stopped flowing from the small bottle.
translation_verse: Asɛ viine la bwa su laɡlaɡ ken, o ŋɔ o bie la bɛl be ŋɔ, “Kpɔ vii la bɛl ba.” Bie la ŋɔ, “Vii bɛlbwa toole kpa.” Ate, vii waa fuɡe noo dɛɛ le o bini la noo la nyoa teŋe.

english_verse: After she told Elisha what had happened, he said, “Sell the oil and use part of the money to pay what you owe the man. You and your sons can live on what is left.” Elisha Brings a Rich Woman's Son Back to Life
translation_verse: Haah la berɔ la Korowii keame Elaesa be dɛ ka bol waa aa chiɡa, asɛ o ŋɔ haah la be ŋɔ, “Ka yoɡa dɛ́ kpɔ bɔ he kema, ásɛ he ne he bii di a kar.” Elaesa ne Sunem haah bɛl waa ɛ kondɔɔh wa

english_verse: Once, while Elisha was in the town of Shunem, he met a rich woman who invited him to her home for dinner. After that, whenever he was in Shunem, he would have a meal there with her and her husband.
translation_verse: Awola bɛl, Elaesa la bwɛɛ bɛl baa dɛ yerɔ Sunem ta, dɛ haah bɛl o nɔn bini aa wera lɔ bela. Haah la yerɛ Elaesa la o dem o ne o ka di kwa. Le awola tɔpere dɛɛ kaa la, Elaesa aa kpɔ bwɛɛ la ta baa kaa bwa, ɡɛɛ o la dem bela dɛ ka di kwa.

english_verse: Some time later the woman said to her husband, “I'm sure the man who comes here so often is a prophet of God.
translation_verse: Haah la ŋɔ o jaa be ŋɔ, “N nao kɛŋɔ baa nɔ waa dɛ ba ya be saŋ bɛlbwa nɔ ɛ Korowii keame tenten.

english_verse: Why don't we build him a small room on the flat roof of our house? We can put a bed, a table and chair, and an oil lamp in it. Then whenever he comes, he can stay with us.”
translation_verse: Gel ya ma dejeɡa bɛl ya dem nɔ saldoa, dɛ́ ɛ mpa ne teebur ne kara dɛ kandea cheɡ o bini tɛo, ásɛ o balaa wɛɛ do o bini.” Asɛ o sɛh.

english_verse: The next time Elisha was in Shunem, he stopped at their house and went up to his room to rest.
translation_verse: Awola bɛl, Elaesa berɔ la Sunem dɛ teeh ka jo o dea la bini dɛɛ onɛ.

english_verse: He said to his servant Gehazi, “This woman has been very helpful. Have her come up here to the roof for a moment.” She came, and Elisha told Gehazi to say to her, “You've gone to a lot of trouble for us, and we want to help you. Is there something we can request the king or army commander to do?” The woman answered, “With my relatives nearby, I have everything I need.”
translation_verse: Anee Elaesa ŋɔ Gehasi be ŋɔ, “Ŋɔ haah nɔ be kɛŋɔ, o kaa nyin waa ba dawɛ ya nɛɛ a ɛ waa tɛ yaa. Bɔkwaa yaa ba wona ɛ tɛo wɔ? Yaa won bol o waa tɛo kooro be kɛɛ laa sitɔɔ be naa?” Haah la chaŋe ŋɔ, “N dɔ komɛlbwa maa dɛ nyin, n nɛra maa baa so ba baah ta nɔ.”

english_verse: “Then what can we do for her?” Elisha asked Gehazi. Gehazi replied, “I do know that her husband is old, and that she doesn't have a son.”
translation_verse: Anee Elaesa bɔɔ Gehasi ŋɔ, “Bɔkwaa yaa ba wona ɛ tɛo wɔ?” Gehasi ŋɔ, “Kpelaa, o ta bie dɔe, asɛ o jaa ɡe hwɛɛhrɔ.”

english_verse: “Ask her to come here again,” Elisha told his servant. He called for her, and she came and stood in the doorway of Elisha's room.
translation_verse: Ate, Elaesa ŋɔ Gehasi be ŋɔ, “Ŋɔ ó suuh tel n be.” Asɛ haah la ba, dɛ ba che doonyoa.

english_verse: Elisha said to her, “Next year at this time, you'll be holding your own baby son in your arms.” “You're a man of God,” the woman replied. “Please don't lie to me.”
translation_verse: Elaesa ŋɔ haah la be ŋɔ, “Benanyoa saŋ nɔ dɛ he kpoŋe bibaa.” Haah la ŋɔ, “Akai, n dɔɔ. Korowii keamee hen, bɛ nyosone teŋe tɛ he tolo!”

english_verse: But a few months later, the woman got pregnant. She gave birth to a son, just as Elisha had promised.
translation_verse: Ate, haah la ba kpoŋe tea benanyoa Elaesa aa doo la, dɛ lolɛ bibaa.

english_verse: One day while the boy was still young, he was out in the fields with his father, where the workers were harvesting the crops.
translation_verse: Bie la baa kpeɡ. Awola bɛl, dɛ o mɛɛ ne nɛra dɛ komɛ mea koo ta, asɛ o la o be.

english_verse: Suddenly he shouted, “My head hurts. It hurts a lot!” “Carry him back to his mother,” the father said to his servant.
translation_verse: Kerabeŋkpoŋ bie la den do lɔŋɔ dɛ ŋɔ o mɛɛ be ŋɔ, “N nyu! N nyu dɛ wee mɛ!” Asɛ o mɛɛ ŋɔ o bonɔɔna la bɛl be ŋɔ, “Kpɔɔ ka tɛ o nya.”

english_verse: loaves of bread made from the first barley that was harvested. Elisha said, “Give it to the people so they can eat.”
translation_verse: Bonɔɔ la kpɔɔ ka tɛ o nya, asɛ o lɛo so o nakpale ta, ane ŋɔ a tel webaŋa dɛ bie la sewɔ.

english_verse: She carried him upstairs to Elisha's room and laid him across the bed. Then she walked out and shut the door behind her.
translation_verse: Haah la kpɔ bie la teeh kaa Korowii keame la dea, dɛ kpɔɔ ka bil mpa ta, dɛ laa ɡbera tɔ dɛ ɡelo bela.

english_verse: The woman called to her husband, “I need to see the prophet. Let me use one of the donkeys. Send a servant along with me, and let me leave now, so I can get back quickly.”
translation_verse: O yerɛ o jaa dɛ ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “N poori, ɡel bonɔɔna la bɛl kpɔ keeɡo ba, ásɛ n ɛ warane la Korowii keame Elaesa be dɛ ba taraken.”

english_verse: “Why do you need to see him today?” her husband asked. “It's not the Sabbath or time for the New Moon Festival.” “That's all right,” she answered.
translation_verse: Anee o jaa la chaŋe ŋɔ, “Bɔkwa waa hɛɛ nyin he la o be fini nɔ? Korobifale Tɔpejen kɛɛ Ona Tɔpere laa fini.” O ŋɔ, “Bɛ ɡel a hae.”

english_verse: She saddled the donkey and said to her servant, “Let's go. And don't slow down unless I tell you to.”
translation_verse: Ate, o pa kwaa pa keeɡo la ta dɛ ŋɔ o bonɔɔ la be ŋɔ, “Dɛɛ kaa warawara, nemenɛ n ŋɔ he be ŋɔ hɛɛ kaa tama tama.”

english_verse: She left at once for Mount Carmel to talk with Elisha. When Elisha saw her coming, he said, “Gehazi, look! It's the woman from Shunem.
translation_verse: Anomanta, ba leɔ dɛɛ kaa Korowii keame Elaesa be Kaamɛl Bwejen ta. Korowii keame la aa nao bojaŋ la, o ŋɔ o bonɔɔ Gehasi be ŋɔ, “Nyiŋi na, haah la waa le Sunem laanee dɛɛ ba la.

english_verse: Run and meet her. And ask her if everything is all right with her and her family.” “Everything is fine,” she answered Gehazi.
translation_verse: Chwa ka chemo dɛ́ pɛɛro ŋɔ, ‘He wobɛlbwa wer tɛɛ naa? He jaa ne he bii leaa?’ ” Haah la ŋɔ Gehasi be ŋɔ, “Ya bwa bwara kpeɡri.”

english_verse: But as soon as she got to the top of the mountain, she went over and grabbed Elisha by the feet. Gehazi started toward her to push her away, when Elisha said, “Leave her alone! Don't you see how sad she is? But the Lord hasn't told me why.”
translation_verse: Haah la aa kaa pu Korowii keame la bwe la ta la, o chole Korowii keame la sie, dɛ lawɛ o nakpale kpoŋe. Asɛ Gehasi ŋɔ o ka taɡɔ ta, anee Korowii keame la ŋɔ, “Gelo, o loo kuu kohona. Korowii kpɔ waa aa puu la sɔɔh mɛ.”

english_verse: The woman said, “Sir, I begged you not to get my hopes up, and I didn't even ask you for a son.”
translation_verse: Haah la ŋɔ, “Nomoa, n soŋe bie aa? N ta he be ŋɔe ŋɔ he bɛ men neɡre, dɛ́ ɡel n kpɔ hwɛɡa ta waane ta pɛɛpɛɛ aa?”

english_verse: “Gehazi, get ready and go to her house,” Elisha said. “Take along my walking stick, and when you get there, lay it on the boy's face. Don't stop to talk to anyone, even if they try to talk to you.”
translation_verse: Anee Elaesa ŋɔ Gehasi be ŋɔ, “Gbaa he batakaare dɛ́ vɔwɛ kiriso, dɛ́ kpɔ n daŋɡbala kpoŋe, dɛ́ chwa dɛɛ kaa. He kaa pu nomɛlbwa naa, bɛ waa o be bol. Nomɛlbwa ɡe bol waa he be naa, bɛ on chaŋe. Kpɔ n daŋɡbala la ka bil bie la sie.”

english_verse: But the boy's mother said to Elisha, “I swear by the living Lord and by your own life that I won't leave without you.” So Elisha got up and went with them.
translation_verse: Bie la nya la ŋɔ, “N ŋwɛɛ Korowii waa lole, asɛ he ɡe do le kɛŋɔ maa kaa ɡele.” Anomanta, ba bwa teŋɛ dɔŋa nɛɛ kaa.

english_verse: Gehazi ran on ahead and laid Elisha's walking stick on the boy's face, but the boy didn't move or make a sound. Gehazi ran back to Elisha and said, “The boy didn't wake up.”
translation_verse: Dɛ Gehasi tɔ sie kaa dɛ ka kpɔ daŋɡbala la bil bie la sie, kɛ o ta wobɛlbwa ɛɛ á ba ɛ kɛŋɔ wɛɛ iruu. Anomanta, Gehasi laa berɛ dɛ ka cheme Elaesa dɛ ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Bie la ta ire.”

english_verse: Elisha arrived at the woman's house and went straight to his room, where he saw the boy's body on his bed.
translation_verse: Elaesa tel dem bela dɛ ka jo o dea, dɛ bie la sewɔ chɔ o mpa ta.

english_verse: He walked in, shut the door, and prayed to the Lord.
translation_verse: Asɛ o laa ɡbera tɔ o ne bie la nɛ, dɛ soŋe Korowii.

english_verse: Then he got on the bed and stretched out over the dead body, with his mouth on the boy's mouth, his eyes on his eyes, and his hand on his hands. As he lay there, the boy's body became warm.
translation_verse: O teeh mpa la dɛ ka pi bie la nɛ, dɛ kpɔ o nyoa pi o nyoa ta, o sibie pa o sibie ta, dɛ kpɔ o nɔɔra do o nɔɔra ta. Waa tɛɡra chɔ bie la nɛɛ ɡɛ la, bie la bwara pa mun dɛɛ do wɔrɔbe.

english_verse: Elisha got up and walked back and forth in the room, then he went back and leaned over the boy's body. The boy sneezed seven times and opened his eyes.
translation_verse: Elaesa ir bie la nɛ, dɛ valɛ dea la bini dɛ la dɛɛ ba, dɛ ka teeh mpa la dɛ ka pi o nɛɛ ja. Asɛ bie la chweremi kera anuanɛ dɛ laa sie pili.

english_verse: Elisha called out to Gehazi, “Ask the boy's mother to come here.” Gehazi did, and when she was at the door, Elisha said, “You can take your son.”
translation_verse: Asɛ Elaesa yerɛ Gehasi ŋɔ, “Yerɛ bie la nya la.” Haah la aa bala la, o ŋɔ, “He bie laanee la, kpɔɔ kaa.”

english_verse: She came in and bowed down at Elisha's feet. Then she picked up her son and left. Elisha Makes Some Stew Taste Better
translation_verse: Asɛ o ɡuŋi Elaesa harɛ, dɛ kpɔ o bie dɛ le buse. Nyokpowe-ɛɛla anɛ ane ɡe ja

english_verse: Later, Elisha went back to Gilgal, where there was almost nothing to eat, because the crops had failed. One day while the prophets who lived there were meeting with Elisha, he said to his servant, “Prepare a big pot of stew for these prophets.”
translation_verse: Lɔr baa chole Gelɡal harɛ la bwa ta, asɛ Elaesa berɛ kaa bela. O ne Korowii keamere bane baa pɛa dɛɛ valɛ cheme, asɛ o ŋɔ o bonɔɔ be ŋɔ, “Kpɔ vijen chɔŋɛ nii ta dɛ́ pile dɔr tɛ nɛra nɔ.”

english_verse: One of them went out into the woods to gather some herbs. He found a wild vine and picked as much of its fruit as he could carry, but he didn't know that the fruit was very sour. When he got back, he cut up the fruit and put it in the stew.
translation_verse: Ba bini bɛl iro jo kpɔɡ bini, dɛ ka toɡri papooni ane baa dɛ dia. Waa laŋa la, o kaa na kpɔɡ bini juɡ dɛ pa o nɔna do o yal ta. Dɛ nomɛlbwa aa a konsoo jemɛ, dɛ ba peɡra dɛ pa do vii la ne dɔr la ta.

english_verse: The stew was served, and when the prophets started eating it, they shouted, “Elisha, this stew tastes terrible! We can't eat it.”
translation_verse: Baa doɡ dɔr la, asɛ bɛlbwa dɔ o kwaa ba pa mun dɛɛ di la, ba kpɔ takpeɡ ŋɔ, “Korowii keame, aa somɛ, ya diu yaa serewoo.”

english_verse: “Bring me some flour,” Elisha said. He sprinkled the flour in the stew and said, “Now serve it to them.” And the stew tasted fine. Elisha Feeds One Hundred People
translation_verse: Elaesa ŋɔ, “Hé nyin mendɛɛɡa tɛ mɛ.” Asɛ o kpɔ do vii la bini dɛ ŋɔ, “Kpɔ tɛɛ ba bá di.” Asɛ ba di wobɛlbwa ta ban ɛɛ.

english_verse: So the servant served the bread and grain to the people. They ate and still had some left over, just as the Lord had promised.
translation_verse: Anomanta, bonɔɔ la kpɔɔ ka cheɡ ba sie, o tɛɛ ba ba di ane ka, ɡɛ Korowii aa ŋɔa la.

english_verse: Naaman was the commander of the Syrian army. The Lord had helped him and his troops defeat their enemies, so the king of Syria respected Naaman very much. Naaman was a brave soldier, but he had leprosy.
translation_verse: Dɛ baa bɛl lole baa yerɔ Naaman. Dɛ onee Siiria kooro laa sitɔɔ. Dɛ o ɛ nɛnjen asɛ o dɔɔ kooro ɛɛ duuru kohona. Dɛkalkɛ a cheɡɛ o nɛ Korowii cha ba, dɛ ɡel ba pɔ ba dɔma nɛ. Kɛ dɛ wee lɔ Naaman nɛ.

english_verse: One day while the Syrian troops were raiding Israel, they captured a girl, and she became a servant of Naaman's wife.
translation_verse: Dɛ Siiria laa tena boa nyoa ka yo dɛ lawɛ Israel bitolo bɛl laa ta, o do Naaman haah sie.

english_verse: When Naaman told the king what the girl had said,
translation_verse: Ate, Naaman ka bol kooro be ɡɛ Israel harɛ ta tolo la aa bola la.

english_verse: the king replied, “Go ahead! I will give you a letter to take to the king of Israel.” Naaman left and took along
translation_verse: Kooro la ŋɔ, “Ir, mɛɛ chwerɛ tɔnee tɛɛ he kpɔ ka tɛ Israel kooro.” Ate, Naaman ir kpɔ suuɡapoŋa a tɔɡre aa ɛ kilore lafraatoro fifraanaarɛ, ne suuɡaswɛm kaɡboŋa anumɛl, dɛ yadɛɛɡa bele fi.

english_verse: He also carried the letter to the king of Israel. It said, “I am sending my servant Naaman to you. Would you cure him of his leprosy?”
translation_verse: Waa aa lɔ tɔn Siiria kooro aa chwera ba kpɔ ka tɛ Israel kooro laanee kɛŋɔ, “Menee dɛɛ tomɛ n bonɔɔ Naaman tɔn nɔ ne, kɛŋɔ wee lɔ o nɛ hé chaoh.”

english_verse: Elisha sent someone outside to say to him, “Go wash seven times in the Jordan River. Then you'll be completely cured.”
translation_verse: Elaesa tomɛ o bonɔɔna la bini bɛl o be dɛ ka ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Ir la ka sɔ Jɔɔdan Moo kera anuanɛ, wee la ɛɛ le he nɛɛ he bwara berɛ kwaa kɛrɛdɛ.”

english_verse: When the king of Israel read the letter, he tore his clothes in fear and shouted, “That Syrian king believes I can cure this man of leprosy! Does he think I'm God with power over life and death? He must be trying to pick a fight with me.”
translation_verse: Israel kooro aa cha tɔn la nyoa dɛ kure la, o kɛɛ o batakaare a baɡle kɛ o liire chɔɡɔ, dɛ ŋɔ, “Na Siiria kooro aa dɛ nyin n ne waa ɡɛ! Korowiirii men n dɔ mkpa ne seo kpeɡri, he ŋɔ n chah baa nɔ naa? A ɛ kasinteŋ kɛŋɔ o dɛ nyin mɛ naɡra!”

english_verse: As soon as Elisha the prophet heard what had happened, he sent the Israelite king this message: “Why are you so afraid? Send the man to me, so that he will know there is a prophet in Israel.”
translation_verse: Korowii keame Elaesa aa noa kɛŋɔ Israel kooro laa o batakaare kɛɛ la, o tomɔ ba ka pɛɛro ŋɔ, “Bɔkwa waa bala he laa he batakaare kɛɛ? Tomɛ Naaman ó ba n be, ásɛ n baɡlo kɛŋɔ Korowii keame bɛl lɔ Israel harɛ ta.”

english_verse: Naaman left with his horses and chariots and stopped at the door of Elisha's house.
translation_verse: Naaman kpɔ o jaɡre ne o torɔɡore baa vɔwa pɛl jaɡre, dɛ ir la Elaesa be dɛ ka che o dem doonyoa.

english_verse: But Naaman stormed off, grumbling, “Why couldn't he come out and talk to me? I thought for sure he would stand in front of me and pray to the Lord his God, then wave his hand over my skin and cure me.
translation_verse: Ate, Naaman baah di o laa berɛ dɛɛ naɡre waa ŋɔ, “N te dɛ lii kɛŋɔ wɛɛ leo dɛ́ ba soŋe Korowii waa dɛ tomɔ, dɛ́ kpɔ o nɔn viwe wee la ta dɛ́ chaah mɛ.

english_verse: What about the Abana River or the Pharpar River? Those rivers in Damascus are just as good as any river in Israel. I could have washed in them and been cured.”
translation_verse: Anɔ bwa habɔɔ, bwɛjen Damaskɔs Mojena Abana ne Faapar laa wera Israel harɛ ta neerare bwa ta, ń fee ka sɔ n bwara kwaa raa?” Anomanta, o laa berɛ bandia ne dɛ kaa.

english_verse: His servants went over to him and said, “Sir, if the prophet had told you to do something difficult, you would have done it. So why don't you do what he said? Go wash and be cured.”
translation_verse: Belaa Naaman bonɔɔna suuh tel o jwɛh dɛ ŋɔ, “Nomoa, dɛ wejena anee Korowii keame la ŋɔ he be ŋɔ he ɛ aa, he fe aa sɛh aa? Ɛrɛɛ haa wola won ka sɔ nee la ɡɛ waa bola la, ásɛ dɛ dɔ chaah nɔɔ?”

english_verse: Naaman walked down to the Jordan; he waded out into the water and stooped down in it seven times, just as Elisha had told him. At once, he was cured, and his skin became as smooth as a child's.
translation_verse: Anomanta, Naaman iro dɛ ka jo Jɔɔdan Moo la bini, dɛ sɔ kera anuanɛ ɡɛ Korowii keame la aa ŋɔ o be la, asɛ o bwara berɛ kwaa dɛ do wer kɛrɛdɛ kɛŋɔ bechala bwara ken.

english_verse: Naaman and his officials went back to Elisha. Naaman stood in front of him and announced, “Now I know that the God of Israel is the only God in the whole world. Sir, would you please accept a gift from me?”
translation_verse: Naaman ne o bonɔɔna la bwa berɔ ba Korowii keame Elaesa be, asɛ Naaman ka che o sie dɛ ŋɔ, “N nao kɛŋɔ Korowii bɛlbwa toole harɛ nɔ ta bobɛlbwa ka ja Israel harɛ ta. N dɔɔ, n poori lɛ koŋkɛɛla he bonɔɔ aa ba a ne ba tɛɛ nɔ.”

english_verse: “I am a servant of the living Lord,” Elisha answered, “and I swear that I will not take anything from you.” Naaman kept begging, but Elisha kept refusing.
translation_verse: Belaa Elaesa chaŋe ŋɔ, “N ŋwɛɛ Korowii waa lole mɛɛ tomɔ kɛŋɔ, maa komɛlbwaa lɛ.” Naaman cheɡɛ o nɛɛ nɔ bwa o vɛh.

english_verse: Finally Naaman said, “If you won't accept a gift, then please let me take home as much soil as two mules can pull in a wagon. Sir, from now on I will offer sacrifices only to the Lord.
translation_verse: Ate, Naaman ŋɔ, “Dɛ haa komɛlbwaa lɛ tenaa, amɔ tɛ men he bonɔɔ ŋwɛnɛ n ɛ bonɔ teera keeɡore anɛ aa dɛ ba wona che kaa dem. Maa kwaa kpoo fuh ɛ saraha tɛ voɡ bɛlbwa kpa atane Korowii ɡbo.

english_verse: But I pray that the Lord will forgive me when I go into the temple of the god Rimmon and bow down there with the king of Syria.”
translation_verse: Kɛ kombeŋkpoŋ maa dɛ soŋe Korowii kɛŋɔ, dɛ n ne n dɔɔ kooro kaa jo Siiria harɛ voɡ Remɔn dea dɛ ɡuŋu harɛ naa, ó kpɔ kɛ mɛ.”

english_verse: “Go on home, and don't worry about that,” Elisha replied. Then Naaman left. Elisha Places a Curse on Gehazi After Naaman had gone only a short distance,
translation_verse: Anee Elaesa ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Kpɔ deŋnesɔɔhna kaa.” Asɛ Naaman kaa, waa tel sie tama la,

english_verse: Gehazi said to himself, “Elisha let that Syrian off too easy. He should have taken Naaman's gift. I swear by the living Lord that I will talk to Naaman myself and get something from him.”
translation_verse: Korowii keame Elaesa bonɔɔ Gehasi lii dɛ ŋɔ, “N dɔɔ kpɔ Siiria te Naaman nɔ bwara kɛo, o ta koŋkɛɛla waa ba a ne bɛlbwa lɛɛ. N ŋwɛɛ Korowii waa lole kɛŋɔ mɛɛ chwao tiu dɛ́ ka lɛ komɛl le o be.”

english_verse: So he hurried after Naaman. When Naaman saw Gehazi running after him, he got out of his chariot to meet him. Naaman asked, “Is everything all right?”
translation_verse: Ate, Gehasi chwa tiu, Naaman aa naa kɛŋɔ nomɛl chwao teŋɛ o nɛɛ la, o tuo le torɔɡo la bini dɛɛ chemo, dɛ bɔɔro ŋɔ, “A som aa?”

english_verse: “Yes,” Gehazi answered. “But my master has sent me to tell you about two young prophets from the hills of Ephraim. They came asking for help, and now Elisha wants to know if you would give them
translation_verse: Gehasi ŋɔ, “A som, n dɔɔree tom mɛ he be ŋɔ Korowii keamere baa pɛa dɛɛ valɛ banɛ bane le Efrem deŋɡarere harɛ ta dɛ ba o be taraken. Dɛ he tɛo suuɡapoŋa a tɔɡre aa ɛ kilore fifraatoro dɛ anaarɛ ne yadɛɛɡa bele anɛ.”

english_verse: “Sure,” Naaman replied. “But why don't you take twice that amount of silver?” He convinced Gehazi to take it all, then put the silver in two bags. He handed the bags and the clothes to his two servants, and they carried them for Gehazi.
translation_verse: Ate, Naaman ŋɔ, “Lɛ suuɡapoŋa a tɔɡre aa ɛ kilore fifraanumɛl dɛ anuatoro,” dɛ kpɔ do pure anɛ bini ja yadɛɛɡa bele anɛ ta dɛ tɛ Gehasi o lɛ. Dɛ ɡel o bonɔɔna banɛ kpɔ che tɔ Gehasi sie.

english_verse: When they reached the hill where Gehazi lived, he took the bags from the servants and placed them in his house, then sent the men away. After they had gone,
translation_verse: Ba tel deŋɡare harɛ ta bela Elaesa aa soɡa la, asɛ Gehasi lɛ kwaa la dɛ kpɔ ka bil dea, dɛ ɡel bonɔɔna la laa berɛ kaa.

english_verse: Gehazi went in and stood in front of Elisha, who asked, “Gehazi, where have you been?” “Nowhere, sir,” Gehazi answered.
translation_verse: Ate, Gehasi berɛ la ka che o dɔɔ Elaesa sie. Elaesa bɔɔro ŋɔ, “Leperaa he leɔ?” Gehasi ŋɔ, “N dɔɔ, n ta bobɛlbwa laŋɛ.”

english_verse: Elisha asked, “Don't you know that my spirit was there when Naaman got out of his chariot to talk with you? Gehazi, you have no right to accept money or clothes, olive orchards or vineyards, sheep or cattle, or servants.
translation_verse: Elaesa ŋɔ, “Haa jemɛ kɛŋɔ ɡɛ saŋ Naaman aa le o torɔɡo bini, dɛ ba cheme he ne wɛɛ bol waa la, dɛ n lɔ bela n doma ja he nɛɛ kɛɛ? Saŋ ta tele kɛ he lɛ suuɡa kɛɛ yale ne ɔleve ne daa kooni, ne kooni ne peera, dɛ nae kɛɛ bonɔɔna ne toli.

english_verse: Because of what you've done, Naaman's leprosy will now be on you and your descendants forever!” Suddenly, Gehazi's skin became white with leprosy, and he left.
translation_verse: Gɛ haa ɛa nɔ nomanta, wee a fa aa lɔ Naaman nɛɛ la ɛɛ ba he ne he naanar nɛɛ saŋ bɛlbwa dɛɛ la.” Asɛ Gehasi le Elaesa be kaa, dɛ wee lawɛ o bwa dɛ to kɛŋɔ yabi ken.

english_verse: One day the prophets said to Elisha, “The place where we meet with you is too small.
translation_verse: Awola bɛl, Korowii keamere bane baa pɛa dɛɛ valɛ ŋɔ Elaesa waa ɛ ba sitɔɔ be ŋɔ, “Bela ya ne haa dɛ cheme la aa kanɛ.

english_verse: Why don't we build a new meeting place near the Jordan River? Each of us could get some wood, then we could build it.” “That's a good idea,” Elisha replied, “get started.”
translation_verse: Gel ya kaa Jɔɔdan Moo ta, daa lɔ bela, ya ka teŋe dɛ́ kpɔ kwaa bɔr dɛ́ so bela.” Asɛ o ŋɔ, “Hé kaa.”

english_verse: “Aren't you going with us?” one of the prophets asked. “Yes, I'll go,” Elisha answered,
translation_verse: Ba bini bɛl ŋɔ Elaesa be ŋɔ, “N dɔɔ, n poori ba ja ya nɛɛ ya kaa,” asɛ o sɛh

english_verse: and he left with them. They went to the Jordan River and began chopping down trees.
translation_verse: ba bwa kaa. Baa tel Jɔɔdan Moo ta la, ba pa mun teŋni daa la.

english_verse: “Where did it fall in?” Elisha asked. The prophet pointed to the place, and Elisha cut a stick and threw it into the water at that spot. The ax head floated to the top of the water.
translation_verse: Anee Korowii keame Elaesa ŋɔ, “Leperaa o leo?” Asɛ o baɡlo, Elaesa teŋe daa dɛ kpɔ ta bela, asɛ kpanfɛ la le jaah.

english_verse: “Now get it,” Elisha told him. And the prophet reached in and grabbed it. Elisha Stops an Invasion of the Syrian Army
translation_verse: Elaesa ŋɔ, “Laa kpɔ.” Asɛ baa la ha nɔn, dɛ laa kpɔ. Siiria laa tena nɛɛ pɔe wa

english_verse: Time after time, when the king of Syria was at war against the Israelites, he met with his officers and announced, “I've decided where we will set up camp.”
translation_verse: Dɛ laa chɔ Siiria kooro ne Israel tena baah. Siiria kooro ŋɔ o laa nomonome be, asɛ ba le bobɛl baa kpɔ ba laa tena ka so cheɡ.

english_verse: Each time, Elisha would send this warning to the king of Israel: “Don't go near there. That's where the Syrian troops have set up camp.”
translation_verse: Asɛ Korowii keame Elaesa tomɛ ba ka ŋɔ Israel kooro be ŋɔ, ó nyiŋi kɛrɛdɛ dɛ bɛ ɡel Israel tena la kpɔ bela, dɛkalkɛ Siiria kooro ne o laa tena soɡe bela.

english_verse: The king of Syria was furious when he found out what was happening. He called in his officers and asked, “Which one of you has been telling the king of Israel our plans?”
translation_verse: Siiria kooro baa na waa aa dɛ chiɡ, asɛ o baah di kohona o yerɛ o laa nomonome cheme dɛ bɔɔ ba ŋɔ, “He bini umee kpɔ ya waa kaa taa Israel kooro be nɔ?”

english_verse: “None of us, Your Majesty,” one of them answered. “It's an Israelite named Elisha. He's a prophet, so he can tell his king everything—even what you say in your own room.”
translation_verse: Ba bini bɛl ŋɔ, “N naa kooro, ya bini bɛlbwa laa. Korowii keame Elaesa waa lɔ Israel laanee. Onee dɛɛ no wobɛlbwa haa dɛ bol, dɛ́ ka bol Israel kooro be. Hale waa haa sɔh so he dea dɛ́ bol bwa.”

english_verse: “Find out where he is!” the king ordered. “I'll send soldiers to bring him here.” They learned that Elisha was in the town of Dothan and reported it to the king.
translation_verse: Kooro la ŋɔ, “Hé nyin bela waa lole, mɛɛ ɡeloo ba ka lawɔ ba.” Asɛ ba no kɛŋɔ o lɔ bwɛjen Dotan.

english_verse: He ordered his best troops to go there with horses and chariots. They marched out during the night and surrounded the town.
translation_verse: Belaa kooro tomɛ laa tena baa wara, dɛ tɛɛ ba jaɡre ne kwaa aa do kɛ torɔɡore bela. Ba leɔ jwaana dɛ ka bar bwɛjen la cheme.

english_verse: When Elisha's servant got up the next morning, he saw that Syrian troops had the town surrounded. “Sir, what are we going to do?” he asked.
translation_verse: Tɔ aa pera chɔmbibi la, Korowii keame Elaesa bonɔɔ iro dɛɛ le buse dɛ na kɛŋɔ, laa tena kpɔ jaɡre dɛ kwaa aa do kɛ torɔɡore bar bwɛjen la cheme. Anee o ka ŋɔ o dɔɔ be ŋɔ, “N dɔɔ, akwe! Ya na wa. Ɛrɛɛ yaa ba ɛɛ yɔ?”

english_verse: “Don't be afraid,” Elisha answered. “There are more troops on our side than on theirs.”
translation_verse: O chaŋe ŋɔ, “Dɛɛ berɛ ɔma, ya dɔ laa tena ba warɛ ɡwaa ba kwa.”

english_verse: Then he prayed, “Lord, please help him to see.” And the Lord let the servant see that the hill was covered with fiery horses and flaming chariots all around Elisha.
translation_verse: Belaa Elaesa soŋe Korowii ŋɔ, “N Naa Korowii, pili o sie ó won dɛɛ na.” Asɛ Korowii ɡel bonɔɔ la sie pili, o na kɛŋɔ jaɡre ne kwaa aa do kɛ torɔɡore, ne niirare su deŋɡarere la ta dɛ bar Elaesa.

english_verse: As the Syrian army came closer, Elisha prayed, “Lord, make those soldiers blind!” And the Lord blinded them with a bright light.
translation_verse: Siiria laa tena la aa dɛ tel Elaesa be la, o soŋe ŋɔ, “N Naa Korowii, ɡel baala nɔ nyoŋe, ba bɛ won na bela baa dɛ kaa.” Asɛ a ɛ ɡɛ.

english_verse: Elisha told the enemy troops, “You've taken the wrong road and are in the wrong town. Follow me. I'll lead you to the man you're looking for.” Elisha led them straight to the capital city of Samaria.
translation_verse: Anee Elaesa ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, “He koni ŋwɛnɛ, bwɛjen haa dɛ kaa o ta la laa nɔ. Hé teŋɛ n nɛ, ń la he ne nɛn haa dɛ nyinu la be.” Asɛ o tɔ ba sie dɛ kaa ba ne bwɛjen Samaria.

english_verse: When all the soldiers were inside the city, Elisha prayed, “Lord, now let them see again.” The Lord let them see that they were standing in the middle of Samaria.
translation_verse: Baa dena jo bwɛjen Samaria la, Elaesa soŋe ŋɔ, “N Naa Korowii, ɡel ba berɛ dɛɛ na.” Asɛ Korowii no o wesoŋa dɛ pili ba sie, ba na kɛŋɔ ba cheɡɛ Samaria fɔɡbaah.

english_verse: The king of Israel saw them and asked Elisha, “Should I kill them, sir?”
translation_verse: Israel kooro aa na ba la, o bɔɔ Elaesa ŋɔ, “N dɔɔ, ń kpoo ba kɛɛ?”

english_verse: “No!” Elisha answered. “You didn't capture these troops in battle, so you have no right to kill them. Instead, give them something to eat and drink and let them return to their leader.”
translation_verse: Elaesa ŋɔ, “Akai, he yo nɛra laa dɛ laɡ ba aa, he dɛ kpoo ba aa? Tɛɛ ba kondikwaa ne nee bá nyɔ, dɛ́ berɛ tɛɛ ba ŋwɛnɛ ba kaa ba dɔɔ be.”

english_verse: The king ordered a huge meal to be prepared for Syria's army, and when they finished eating, he let them go. For a while, the Syrian troops stopped invading Israel's territory. King Benhadad of Syria Attacks Samaria
translation_verse: Anomanta, kooro ɡelɔ ba ɛ kondikonjena tɛɛ ba ba di, o tɛɛ ba nee ne sen ba nyɔ. Dɛ ta ba ŋwɛnɛ ba kaa ba dɔɔ be. Le bela dɛɛ kaa la, a biɡro Siiria laa tena ta Israel harɛ ta balɛ dɛ ba lɔ tɔ ba nɛɛ kpa. Laa tena baa kaa chɔ bar bwɛjen Samaria

english_verse: Some time later, King Benhadad of Syria called his entire army together, then they marched to Samaria and attacked.
translation_verse: A habɔɔ la, Siiria Kooro Bɛn Hadad kpɔ o laa tena bwa ba ka yo Israel tena, dɛ ka chɔ bar bwɛjen Samaria tena ɡe.

english_verse: They kept up the attack until there was nothing to eat in the city. In fact, a donkey's head cost
translation_verse: Baa tɔ Samaria tena do la ɡelɔ lɔr chole Samaria, asɛ ba yoɡ keeɡo nyu suuɡapoŋa fifraanuatoro. Dɛ yoɡ kweah bena lakaja del suuɡapoŋa anue.

english_verse: One day as the king of Israel was walking along the top of the city wall, a woman shouted to him, “Please, Your Majesty, help me!”
translation_verse: Awola bɛl, dɛ Israel kooro dɛ valɛ Samaria danjwɛɛ baa maa baro doa, asɛ haah bɛl do lɔŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “N naa kooro, n poori cha mɛ!”

english_verse: “Let the Lord help you!” the king said. “Do you think I have grain or wine to give you?”
translation_verse: O chaŋe ŋɔ, “Dɛ Korowii ta hen chae yaa, bɔkwaa mɛɛ ba wona ɛɔ? N ta mea kɛɛ sen dɔe dɛ́ chae.”

english_verse: Then he asked, “What's the matter anyway?” The woman answered, “Another woman and I were so hungry that we agreed to eat our sons. She said if we ate my son one day, we could eat hers the next day.
translation_verse: Kooro la berɛ bɔɔ haah la ŋɔ, “Bɔkwa waa dɛɛ hae nɔ?” Haah la ŋɔ, “Awola bɛl, n dɔŋ nɔ ŋɔ n be ŋɔ yá lawɛ n bie chwe, ásɛ tɔɔ peraa, yá lawɛ o ɡe kon.”

english_verse: So yesterday we cooked my son and ate him. But today when I went to her house to eat her son, she had hidden him.”
translation_verse: N sɛoh ya daa n kon la chwe, asɛ tɔ aa pera la n la dɛ ka ŋɔ ó ɡel ya kpo o kon la chwe, asɛ o lawɔ sɔh.

english_verse: The king tore off his clothes in sorrow, and since he was on top of the city wall, the people saw that he was wearing sackcloth underneath.
translation_verse: Kooro la aa no ɡɛ haah la aa bola la, o laa o batakaare kɛɛ, a baɡle kɛ a we o nɛ. Kooro la aa dɛ valɛ danjwɛɛ la doa la, nɛra nao kɛŋɔ waa tɔ lweyal do o batakaare lɔɡa, aa baɡle kɛŋɔ o lɔ lwe ta.

english_verse: He said, “I pray that God will punish me terribly, if Elisha's head is still on his shoulders by this time tomorrow.”
translation_verse: A habɔɔ, kooro la ŋwɛɛ ŋɔ, “Dɛ n ta Safat bibaa Elaesa nyu teŋe fini naa, Korowii kpo mɛ!”

english_verse: Then he sent a messenger to Elisha. Elisha was home at the time, and the important leaders of Israel were meeting with him. Even before the king's messenger arrived, Elisha told the leaders, “That murderer is sending someone to cut off my head. When you see him coming, shut the door and don't let him in. I'm sure the king himself will be right behind him.”
translation_verse: Asɛ o tomɛ ŋɔ bá ka yerɛ Elaesa ba, dɛ o lɔ o dem Israel nomonome so o be. Torome la aa wola tele mɔɔ la, Elaesa ŋɔ nomonome la be ŋɔ, “He ta nae kɛŋɔ nɛn waa dɛ kpoo nɛra nɔ aa tomɛ nɛn ŋɔ ó ba kpo mɛ naa? Dɛ torome la balaa, hé laa ɡbera tɔ dɛ bɛ ɡel o dɔ bɔr jo. O dɔɔ kooro nakpale sio teŋɛ o nɛɛ wɛɛ ba.”

english_verse: Before Elisha finished talking, the messenger came up and said, “The Lord has made all these terrible things happen to us. Why should I think he will help us now?”
translation_verse: Elaesa ne ba ta aa dɛ bol waa la, dɛ kooro la dɛ tel o be dɛ ŋɔ, “Korowiirii ɡela wechɔɡa nɔ ba, n berɛ kpa Korowii ka tel saŋ besoo jaɔ?”

english_verse: Elisha answered, “I have a message for you. The Lord promises that tomorrow here in Samaria, you will be able to buy a large sack of flour or two large sacks of barley for almost nothing.”
translation_verse: Korowii keame Elaesa ŋɔ, “Hé no Korowii wa. Waa Korowii aa dɛ bol laanee kɛŋɔ, ‘Kere saŋ nɔ bɔr tenten, lakaja baa do mea o ta Samaria aa yoɡii dɔ, baa yawɔɔ suuɡapoŋ beŋkpoŋii.’ ”

english_verse: The chief officer there with the king replied, “I don't believe it! Even if the Lord sent a rainstorm, it couldn't produce that much grain by tomorrow.” “You will see it happen, but you won't eat any of the food,” Elisha warned him. The Syrian Army Stops Its Attack
translation_verse: Anee nomoa waa dɛ cha kooro ŋɔ Korowii keame la be ŋɔ, “Hale Korowii ɡelɔ bwaala mun pili kohona bɛlbwa kwaraa naa, ɡɛ waa nɔ ɛɛ won maɡre aa?” Elaesa ŋɔ, “Hɛɛ nao kɛŋɔ aa chiɡuu, kɛ kondikwaa la bɛlbwa aa he nyoa jo.” Siiria laa tena kaala wa

english_verse: About the same time, four men with leprosy were just outside the gate of Samaria. They said to each other, “Why should we sit here, waiting to die?
translation_verse: Dɛ baala banaarɛ bane weechɔɡa aa lɔ ba nɛɛ soɡe bwɛjen Samaria doonyoa. Ba ŋɔ dɔŋa be ŋɔ, “Ásɛ ya so bonɔ dɛ́ serewe aa?

english_verse: There's nothing to eat in the city, so we would starve if we went inside. But if we stay out here, we will die for sure. Let's sneak over to the Syrian army camp and surrender. They might kill us, but they might not.”
translation_verse: Dɛ ya jo bwɛɛ nɔ ta naa, lɔr la lɔ bela, yaa serewoo. Ya soɡe bonɔ ɡe aa, yaa serewoo, he den ɡel yá kaa bela Siiria laa tena aa soɡa, dɛ́ kpɔ ya te ka do ba nɔn ta. Dɛ ba ɡel yaa aa, dɛ ya dɔ ya nyu, ba kpoo yaa ɡe aa, ya den serewe.”

english_verse: They said to each other, “This isn't right. Today is a day to celebrate, and we haven't told anyone else what has happened. If we wait until morning, we will be punished. Let's go to the king's palace at once and tell the good news.”
translation_verse: Dɛ ŋɔ dɔŋa be ŋɔ, “Kɛrɛdɛ laa yaa ɛ la, fini ɛ amanesoma tɔpere asɛ ya ɡbo kpɔ so la. Dɛ ya ɡelɔ bɔr chaah a ta naa, yaa dɔ waa. Ya den la kooro dem dɛ́ ka bol a wa.”

english_verse: They went back to Samaria and shouted up to the guards at the gate, “We've just come from the Syrian army camp, and all the soldiers are gone! The tents are empty, and the horses and donkeys are still tied up. We didn't see or hear anybody.”
translation_verse: Asɛ ba la dɛ ka yerɛ nɛra baa dɛ daah bwɛjen la doonyoone ta, dɛ bol ba be ŋɔ, “Ya la bela Siiria laa tena aa baa so la, ba kaalɔ dɛ ɡel ba tɛnte deene a che pɛɛpɛɛ. Ba jaɡre ne keeɡore ta vɔrɔwɔ che, ya ta nɛn nae, ya ta nɛn ɡbɔɡa ɡe noɛ.”

english_verse: The king got out of bed and said to his officers, “I know what those Syrians are doing. They know we're starving, so they're hiding in the fields, hoping we will go out to look for food. When we do, they can capture us and take over our city.”
translation_verse: Anee kooro la ir jwaana la ne dɛ ŋɔ o nomonome be ŋɔ, “Mɛɛ ɡeloo he jemɛ waa Siiria tena aa ɛ yaa. Ba nao kɛŋɔ lɔr chole ya nɛ, anomanta, ba le bela baa soɡa la dɛ ka sɔh kpɔɡ bini, dɛɛ lii kɛŋɔ yaa leo dɛ baa nyin kondikwa, ásɛ ba lawɛ yaa dɛ́ ba jo bwɛjen nɔ ta dɛ́ lɛ dɔɔh.”

english_verse: One of his officers replied, “We have a few horses left—why don't we let some men take five of them and go to the Syrian camp and see what's happening? We're going to die anyway like those who have already died.”
translation_verse: Belaa o nomonome la bɛl ŋɔ, “Nɛra yaa lɔ bwɛjen nɔ ta lɔ bonyɛɡa ta wubwa kɛŋɔ, banɔ la baa serewa la ken. Gel ya tomɛ baala bá kpɔ jaɡre anue aa ka bwɛjen nɔ ta nɔ, dɛ́ la Siiria tena sobɔr bela ka na waa aa chiɡa.”

english_verse: The men rode as far as the Jordan River. All along the way they saw clothes and equipment that the Syrians had thrown away as they escaped. Then they went back to the king and told him what they had seen.
translation_verse: Ba ti ba ka tel Jɔɔdan Moo nyoa, dɛ Siiria tena pa ba yale ne ba laala ta ŋwɛnɛ ta, warane baa dɛ nyin dɛ chwa kaa nomanta. Asɛ toroma la berɛ ba dɛ ba ŋɔ kooro be.

english_verse: At once the people went to the Syrian camp and carried off what was left. They took so much that a large sack of flour and two large sacks of barley sold for almost nothing, just as the Lord had promised.
translation_verse: Ate, nɛra le bwɛjen Samaria ta, dɛ ka kah kwaa aa lɔ bela Siiria tena aa baa so la. Ba pa kwaa kohona, a ɡel ba yoɡ lakaja baa do mea suuɡapoŋ beŋkpoŋ, ɡɛ Korowii aa ŋɔa la.

english_verse: The king of Israel had put his chief officer in charge of the gate, but he died when the people trampled him as they rushed out of the city.
translation_verse: Dɛ Israel kooro kpɔ o laa sitɔɔla la bini bɛl waa dɛ chao ŋɔ wɛɛ nyiŋi bwɛjen la doonyojen la ta, asɛ nɛra aa wura dɛɛ le la, ba tiɡri o nɛ dɛ kpoo. Gɛ Korowii keame Elaesa faa ŋɔ kooro la be ɡɛ saŋ kooro aa la o dem la.

english_verse: Earlier, when the king was at Elisha's house, Elisha had told him that flour or barley would sell for almost nothing.
translation_verse: Gɛ Korowii keame la aa bola la, ɡɛɛ a chiɡ. O ŋɔ, “Kere saŋ nɔ bɔr tenten, lakaja baa do mea o ta Samaria aa yoɡii dɔ, baa yawɔ suuɡapoŋ beŋkpoŋii.”

english_verse: But the officer refused to believe that even the Lord could do that. So Elisha warned him that he would see it happen, but would not eat any of the food.
translation_verse: Dɛ kooro nomoa waa dɛ chao la fa ŋɔ Korowii keame la be ŋɔ, “Hale Korowii ɡelɔ bwaala mun pili kohona bɛlbwa kwaraa naa, ɡɛ waa nɔ ɛɛ won maɡre aa?” Asɛ Korowii keame la fa chaŋo ŋɔ, “Hɛɛ nao kɛŋɔ aa chiɡuu, kɛ kondikwaa la bɛlbwa aa he nyoa jo.”

english_verse: And that's exactly what happened—the officer was trampled to death.
translation_verse: Gɛ waa la tentenee puu, nɛra tiɡri o nɛɛ bwɛjen la doonyojen ta bela o sewɛ.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the king was asking Gehazi the servant of Elisha about the amazing things Elisha had been doing.
