translation_verse: Belaa Ɛsta chaŋo ŋɔ, “N naa kooro, dɛ hɛɛ sɛoh waa, he ne Heeman ba fini dɛ́ ba di kondikonjena maa daala tɛɛ la.”

english_verse: The king said to his servants, “Hurry and get Haman, so we can accept Esther's invitation.” The king and Haman went to Esther's dinner,
translation_verse: Ate, kooro tomɛ o bonɔɔ Heeman be ŋɔ ó ba warane, ásɛ ba la o haah Ɛsta be. Asɛ ba bwa pɛ la ka di kondikonjena la.

english_verse: and while they were drinking wine, the king asked her, “What can I do for you? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom.”
translation_verse: Baa dɛ nyɔ sen la, kooro bɔɔ o haah Ɛsta ja ŋɔ, “Bɔkwaa hɛɛ nyin kɛ ń ɛ tɛɛ nɔ? Hale harɛ maa dɛ di kora o ta nɔ peraa hɛɛ nyin kwaraa naa, mɛɛ tɛɛ.”

english_verse: Esther replied, “Your Majesty, if you really care for me and are willing to do what I want, please come again tomorrow with Haman to the dinner I will prepare for you. At that time I will answer Your Majesty's question.” Haman Plans To Kill Mordecai
translation_verse: Dɛ n waa su he siwi hɛɛ nyin kɛ he cha mɛ naa, kere he ne Heeman ba n be dɛ́ ba di kondikonjena maa dɛ ba daala tɛɛ ja. Gɛ saŋee mɛɛ ba kon maa dɛ nyin baɡla.” Heeman vɔrɔwɔ dɛ́ kpo Mɔdekae

english_verse: Haman was feeling great as he left. But when he saw Mordecai at the palace gate, he noticed that Mordecai did not stand up or show him any respect. This made Haman really angry,
translation_verse: Heeman iro le bela, o sie lɛ kohona. Kɛ waa na Mɔdekae o so koodem doonyoa bela, waa wola ire che dɛ kpɔ duure tɛo o ba kaa la, o baah berɔ di kohona.

english_verse: but he did not say a thing. When Haman got home, he called together his friends and his wife Zeresh
translation_verse: Kɛ ane abwa, o lawɛ bambile dɛ kaa o dem, dɛ ka tomɛ nɛn ŋɔ ó ka yerɛ o daamanar ne o haah Seres tɛo.

english_verse: and started bragging about his great wealth and all his sons. He told them the many ways that the king had honored him and how all the other officials and leaders had to respect him.
translation_verse: Ba bwa aa baa cheme la, o kpɔ o kondɔɔh aa kana ne o bibaala wara baa wara dɛ ta nyoa. Dɛ berɛ baɡle ŋwɛnɛ kooro aa cheɡɛ o ta dɛ tɛo jirima, ne nomonome waa tɛo o ɡwaa o dɔŋa nomonjena ne banɔ la baa dɛ ɛ toma koodem la bwa.

english_verse: Haman added, “That's not all! Besides the king himself, I'm the only person Queen Esther invited for dinner. She has also invited the king and me to dinner tomorrow.
translation_verse: O berɔ ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, “N ɡboo kooro haah yerɛ ka ja kooro nɛɛ ya pɛ di kondikonjena. Kɛ a ɡbo laa, o berɔ dɛɛ yerɛ n ne kooro bwa kere ɡe ja.

english_verse: But none of this makes me happy, as long as I see that Jew Mordecai serving the king.”
translation_verse: Ane abwa, n ta sie na ɡɛ Juu te Mɔdekae aa soɡe koodem doonyoa bela la aa, anɔ bɛlbwa aa n siwi su kpa.”

english_verse: That night the king could not sleep, and he had a servant read him the records of what had happened since he had been king.
translation_verse: Awola tɔpere la jwaana, kooro ta wone chɔ dom. Anomanta, o ɡelɔ ba ba tɔne o kora dii waa aa lɔ a bini la ne bá kure tɛo.

english_verse: the king asked, “What has been done to reward Mordecai for this?” “Nothing, Your Majesty!” the king's servants replied.
translation_verse: Kooro bɔɔro ŋɔ, “Webesoo ń ɛ tɛo ɡɛ waa nɔ ta nɔ? Kembɔr besoo ń tɛo wɔ?” Anee o bonɔɔna la ŋɔ, “He ta wobɛlbwa ɛɛ tɛo.”

english_verse: About this time, Haman came in to ask the king to have Mordecai hanged on the gallows he had built. The king saw him and asked, “Who is that man waiting in front of the throne room?”
translation_verse: O berɔ bɔɔ ŋɔ, “N nomonjena la bane lɔ dem bonɔ naa?” Gɛ saŋ dɛ Heeman ɡe deno ba jo koodem baah bela, dɛ́ ba soŋe ŋwɛnɛ kooro be ŋɔ, bá ka saɡɛ Mɔdekae daa waa pao la ta.

english_verse: The king's servants answered, “Your Majesty, it is Haman.” “Tell him to come in,” the king commanded.
translation_verse: Kooro bonɔɔna la chaŋe kooro ŋɔ, “N naa, Heeman lɔ bonɔ.” Asɛ kooro ŋɔ, “Hé yerɔ ba!”

english_verse: When Haman entered the room, the king asked him, “What should I do for a man I want to honor?” Haman was sure that he was the one the king wanted to honor.
translation_verse: Waa bala la, kooro bɔɔro ŋɔ, “Sɔn besoo ń tɛ nɛn n bambile aa lawɔ, o waa su n siwi ɔ?” Belaa Heeman lii o nyu bini ŋɔ, “Nomɛl lole kooro ɛɛ nyin kɛ ó duuru dɛ ɡwaa mɛ naa?”

english_verse: Tell one of your highest officials to place your robe on this man and lead him through the streets on your horse, while someone shouts, ‘This is how the king honors a man!’ ”
translation_verse: Ásɛ dɛ ɡel he nomonjena tenten la bɛl kpɔ koolaala la do naate, ó so jaaɡɔ la ta, ásɛ nomoa la tɔ o sie, dɛ́ kpɔɔ ɡaaɡe bwɛɛ nɔ fɔɡbaahna, dɛ́ kpɔ takpeɡ dɛɛ ŋɔ, ‘Kenii kooro ɛɛ tɛ ɡɛ nɛn nɔ sɔn.’ ”

english_verse: The king replied, “Hurry and do just what you have said! Don't forget a thing. Get the robe and the horse for Mordecai the Jew, who serves as one of the king's officials!”
translation_verse: Kooro do Heeman ŋɔ, “Ɛ warane ka kpɔ koolaala la ne jaaɡɔ la, dɛ́ ka ɛ ɡɛ haa bola nɔ bwa tɛ Mɔdekae, Juu te la. Bɛ a bini bɛlbwa ɡel. Hɛɛ nao kɛ waa soɡe koodem doonyoa bela.”

english_verse: Haman got the king's robe and put it on Mordecai. He led him through the city on the horse and shouted as he went, “This is how the king honors a man!”
translation_verse: Anomanta, Heeman lɛ koolaala la ne jaaɡɔ la kaa Mɔdekae be, dɛ ka kpɔ laala la doo, asɛ Mɔdekae teeh so jaaɡɔ la ta. Heeman kpɔɔ kpɔ bwɛɛ la fɔɡbaahna, o nyoa che chiŋ wɛɛ ŋɔ, “Hé na ɡɛ kooro aa ɛ nɛn o bambile aa lawɔ kɛ ó tɛo sɔn!”

english_verse: Afterwards, Mordecai returned to his duties in the king's palace, and Haman hurried home, hiding his face in shame.
translation_verse: Baa tona la, Mɔdekae berɔ ka so koodem doonyoa la ta. Heeman ɡe kpɔ sihiih ne baŋaɡola dɛ le bela kaa o dem warane.

english_verse: Haman told his wife and friends what had happened. Then his wife and his advisors said, “If Mordecai is a Jew, this is just the beginning of your troubles! You will end up a ruined man.”
translation_verse: Waa kaa jo dem la, o baɡle waa aa puu la bwa o haah ne o daamanar la be. Asɛ ba jao ŋɔ, “Haa dena pa mun di sihiih Mɔdekae sie nɔ, o lɔɡaa hɛɛ ba doe, ásɛ o pɔ he nɛ, dɛkalkɛŋɔ o ɛ Juu te.”

english_verse: They were still talking, when the king's servants came and quickly took Haman to the dinner that Esther had prepared.
translation_verse: Ba ta aa soɡa dɛɛ bol waa la, kooro bonɔɔna baa fɔɡɛ ba lure la baa kpɔ Heeman kaa kooro haah Ɛsta be kondikonjena waa ɛa ŋɔ bá ba di la mun warane.

english_verse: The king and Haman were dining with Esther
translation_verse: Kooro Sɛksɛs ne Heeman dɛ kooro haah Ɛsta bwa pɛo di kwaa la.

english_verse: and drinking wine during the second dinner, when the king again said, “Esther, what can I do for you? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom!”
translation_verse: Baa dɛ nyɔ sen ba kondikonjena nɛɛtena dii ta la, kooro bɔɔ o haah Ɛsta ja ŋɔ, “Ɛsta, bɔkwaa hɛɛ nyin ɔ? Hale harɛ maa dɛ di kora o ta nɔ peraa hɛɛ nyin kwaraa naa, mɛɛ tɛɛ.”

english_verse: Esther answered, “Your Majesty, if you really care for me and are willing to help, you can save me and my people. That's what I really want,
translation_verse: Anee Ɛsta chaŋe ŋɔ, “N naa kooro, n wesoŋa bwaa kɛŋɔ dɛ n waa su he siwi hɛɛ nyin kɛ he cha mɛ naa, lɛ n nyu dɛ lɛ n nɛra ɡe nyu.

english_verse: because a reward has been promised to anyone who kills my people. Your Majesty, if we were merely going to be sold as slaves, I would not have bothered you.”
translation_verse: Ba yoɡ yaa tɛ ŋɔ bá kpoo yaa, dɛ́ he yaa kwaraa. Dɛ yoɡaa ba yoɡ yaa kɛŋɔ yoma kwaraa naa, n fe ta waane dɔe dɛ́ bol dɛɛ hae.”

english_verse: “Who would dare to do such a thing?” the king asked.
translation_verse: Kooro Sɛksɛs bɔɔ Ɛsta ŋɔ, “Ume baahnee sua o won ɛ ɡɛ waa nɔɔ? Naate sɛ?”

english_verse: Esther replied, “That evil Haman is the one out to get us!” Haman was terrified, as he looked at the king and the queen.
translation_verse: Anee Ɛsta chaŋo ŋɔ, “Nɛnchɔɡe Heeman nɔɔ ya dɔm waa do yaa ɡɛ wahala nɔ ta.” Belaa ɔmee chole Heeman nɛɛ kohona kooro ne o haah Ɛsta sie.

english_verse: The king was so angry that he got up, left his wine, and went out into the palace garden. Haman realized that the king had already decided what to do with him, and he stayed and begged Esther to save his life.
translation_verse: Kooro baah diu kɛrɛdɛ o ir ɡel sen waa dɛ nyɔ la, dɛ le buse ka jo koodem bodɛɛɡe bobɛl baa du daa ane la. Heeman nao kɛŋɔ kooro dɔɔ kpɔ liire ɡɛ waa dɛ ba o deŋne tɛra. Anomanta, o soɡo dɛɛ soŋe kooro haah Ɛsta ŋɔ ó lɛo ta.

english_verse: Just as the king came back into the room, Haman got down on his knees beside Esther, who was lying on the couch. The king shouted, “Now you're even trying to rape my queen here in my own palace!” As soon as the king said this, his servants covered Haman's head.
translation_verse: Kooro aa bera dɛɛ jo koodem la, dɛ Heeman marɛ o haah karajaŋ waa yale o ta la ta, dɛɛ soŋo sibeɡra ne, anee kooro nyɛɡ ŋɔ, “Ei! Baa nɔ dɛ nyin kɛ ó paɡɛ n haah n siwi ta koodem bonɔ kwara!” Kooro nyoa ne chiɡa dɛ o bonɔɔna baa fɔɡɛ ba lure la kpɔ yal bɔle Heeman sie.

english_verse: At once, Haman was hanged on the gallows he had built to hang Mordecai, and the king calmed down.
translation_verse: Gɛɛ a do ba saɡɛ Heeman daa waa paa dɛɛ ba Mɔdekae o ta saɡa la, asɛ kooro baah sɔɔh tama.

english_verse: Before the end of the day, King Xerxes gave Esther everything that had belonged to Haman, the enemy of the Jews. Esther told the king that Mordecai was her cousin. So the king made Mordecai one of his highest officials
translation_verse: Awola tenten baa saɡɛ Heeman la, Kooro Sɛksɛs kpɔ Heeman waa ɛ Juu tena dɔm la dem ne o kondɔɔh te bwa do o haah Ɛsta nɔn ta. Dɛ Ɛsta fa ŋɔ o be ŋɔ Mɔdekae ɛ o lole tenten. Anomanta, le ɡɛ saŋ, Mɔdekae dɔ ŋwɛnɛ kɛ ó jo koodem dɛɛ la kooro sie, saŋ bɛlbwa.

english_verse: and gave him the royal ring that Haman had worn. Then Esther put Mordecai in charge of Haman's property.
translation_verse: Kooro laa o noniseɡ waa kpɔa dɛɛ ɛɡre tɔne ta aa ɛ mmarare o faa kpɔ tɛ Heeman la foo, dɛ kpɔ tɛ Mɔdekae. O haah Ɛsta kpɔ Heeman kondɔɔh la bwa ɡe do Mɔdekae nɔn ta.

english_verse: Once again Esther went to speak to the king. This time she fell down at his feet, crying and begging, “Please stop Haman's evil plan to have the Jews killed!”
translation_verse: Kooro haah Ɛsta berɔ ba kooro sie, dɛ ba ɡuŋu harɛ siniire ne, dɛ soŋo ŋɔ, ó ɡel ba teŋe liichɔɡa Aɡaɡ naa Heeman aa liira kɛ ba kpoo Juu tena bwa la ta.

english_verse: King Xerxes held out the golden scepter to Esther,
translation_verse: Ate, kooro tɛr o suuɡaswɛm daŋɡbala la pa Ɛsta nɛɛ ja, asɛ o ir che o sie.

english_verse: and she got up and said, “Your Majesty, I know that you will do the right thing and that you really love me. Please stop what Haman has planned. He has already sent letters demanding that the Jews in all your provinces be killed,
translation_verse: Belaa Ɛsta ŋɔ, “N naa kooro, dɛ hɛɛ sɛoh, dɛ he sie lɛ n nɛ, n wesoŋa nɔ toɡrɔ aa, ɡel he karakere chwerɛ tɔne kɛŋɔ, Hamedata bibaa Heeman tɔne waa chwera kɛŋɔ, bá kpoo Juu tena baa lɔ he harɛre bwa ta la bɛ toma ɛ kpa.

english_verse: and I can't bear to see my people and my own relatives destroyed.”
translation_verse: Ɛrɛɛ mɛɛ ba wona so nyiŋi, ásɛ wechɔɡa nɔ bwa dɔŋa chiɡ n nɛra Juu tena nɛɔ? Maa won so nyiŋi bá kpoo n dem nɛra.”

english_verse: King Xerxes then said to Esther and Mordecai, “I have already ordered Haman to be hanged and his house given to Esther, because of his evil plans to kill the Jews.
translation_verse: Belaa Kooro Sɛksɛs chaŋe o haah ne Juu te Mɔdekae ŋɔ, “Vɔrɔwa Heeman aa vɔrɔwa ŋɔ bá kpoo Juu tena bwa la nomanta, n kpɔ o kondɔɔh bwa tɛ Ɛsta, dɛ ɡel ba ka saɡɔ.

english_verse: They were written in the name of King Xerxes and sealed with his ring. Then they were taken by messengers who rode the king's finest and fastest horses.
translation_verse: Kooro Sɛksɛs kpeɡri taa Mɔdekae che dɛ ɡel ba chwerɛ tɔne la, asɛ dɛ kpɔ noniseɡ la ɛɡre a ta, dɛ kpɔa tɛ nɛra ba so kooro jaɡre aa won chwae ta, dɛ kpɔ tɔne la ka bɔne tɛ nɛra baa soɡe o harɛre la bwa ta.

english_verse: In these letters the king said: On the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month, the Jews in every city and province will be allowed to get together and defend themselves. They may destroy any army that attacks them, and they may kill all of their enemies, including women and children. They may also take everything that belongs to their enemies. A copy of this law is to be posted in every province and read by everyone.
translation_verse: A chɛ kɛ tɔne la mmarafale la aa lɔ a ta la tel wobol te bɛlbwa tena baa lɔ Kooro Sɛksɛs harɛre la bwa ta la be, ásɛ ba jemɛ a wa, ɡɛ aa ɛ ásɛ Juu tena la won kpɔ ba te kɛrɛdɛ, dɛ́ won yo ba dɔma bɔ kem.

english_verse: Then the king ordered his messengers to take their fastest horses and deliver the law as quickly as possible to every province. When Mordecai left, he was wearing clothes fit for a king. He wore blue and white robes, a large gold crown, and a cape made of fine linen and purple cloth. After the law was announced in Susa, everyone shouted and cheered,
translation_verse: Mɔdekae aa le kooro sie bela dɛ kaa la, dɛ o do laalapoŋa ne laalaburum, dɛ berɛ do batakaare baa kpɔ yapondɛɛɡe ɛo dawɛ kɛŋɔ koolaala ken, dɛ pi suuɡaswɛm ɡbɛrɛdɛɛɡe bɛl. Asɛ Susa bwɛɛ tena la bwa ɡe ɛɛ moo silɛɛ ne.

english_verse: and the Jews were no longer afraid. In fact, they were very happy and felt that they had won a victory.
translation_verse: Dɛ a ɛ silɛɛ ne hɛɡra dɛ tɛ Juu tena la, baa duu ba bobɛlbwa.

english_verse: In every province and city where the law was sent, the Jews had parties and celebrated. Many of the people in the provinces accepted the Jewish religion, because they were now afraid of the Jews.
translation_verse: Harɛ bɛlbwa ne bwɛɛ bɛlbwa ta toroma la aa la mmarafale nɔ ne la, Juu tena baa lɔ bela la bwa sie dɛ lɛ baa hɛɡre, dɛ so di kwaa dɛɛ lɛ ba sie. Nɛra baa wola Juu tena ɛɛ la bini bane ɔmɔ, dɛ kpɔ ba te berɛ Juu tena, dɛkalkɛ ba we-ɛɛla la ɡelɔ ɔmee laɡ ba.

english_verse: The first law that the king had made was to be followed on the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month. This was the very day that the enemies of the Jews had hoped to do away with them. But the Jews turned things around,
translation_verse: Adar korobie tɔpera fi dɛ atoro weeree tɔpere kooro aa do mmara ŋɔ, Júu tena pɛ nyoa dɛ́ yo ba dɔma. Dɛ ba dɔma la dɛ lii kɛ baa won yoo ba dɛ́ pɔ ba nɛ. Kɛ waa la berɔ berɛ. Juu tena la pɛ nyoa yo ba dɔma, dɛ pɔ ba nɛ.

english_verse: and in the cities of every province they came together to attack their enemies. Everyone was afraid of the Jews, and no one could do anything to oppose them.
translation_verse: Juu tena baa lɔ bwɛɛre aa lɔ Kooro Sɛksɛs harɛre ta la bwa chemo kɛ, bá yo ba dɔma baa dɛ ba bá ha ba la. Nɛra la bɛlbwa ta wone puu ba yo, dɛkalkɛ wobobele aa lɔ bela la bwa nɛra dɛ ɔm ba.

english_verse: The leaders of the provinces, the rulers, the governors, and the court officials were afraid of Mordecai and took sides with the Jews.
translation_verse: Hale harɛre la bwa nomonjena ne koranar ne nomonome baa chɔ harɛre nyoo, dɛ nɛra baa dɛ tomɛ kooro la bwa baa che Juu tena la habɔɔ, dɛkalkɛŋɔ ba bwa dɛ ɔmɛ Mɔdekae taeh.

english_verse: Everyone in the provinces knew that the king had promoted him and had given him a lot of power.
translation_verse: Mɔdekae berɛ nomonjen koodem bela, nomɛlbwa no o waa harɛre la bwa ta, asɛ o ta na dɛɛ dɔ kpeɡri saŋ bɛlbwa.

english_verse: The Jews took their swords and did away with their enemies, without showing any mercy.
translation_verse: Juu tena la kpɔ keri dɛ ka kpoo ba dɔma dɛ he ba. Ba ɛɛ ba ɡɛ bwa baa dɛ nyin.

english_verse: Later that day, someone told the king how many people had been killed in Susa.
translation_verse: Awola tenten la, ba baɡle nɛra baa kpoora koobwɛɛ Susa bela la kooro be.

english_verse: Then he told Esther, “Five hundred people, including Haman's ten sons, have been killed in Susa alone. If that many were killed here, what must have happened in the provinces? Is there anything else you want done? Just tell me, and it will be done.”
translation_verse: Kooro Sɛksɛs ŋɔ Ɛsta be ŋɔ, “Koobwɛɛ Susa bonɔ ɡbo, Juu tena la kpoo nɛra lafraanue, dɛ kpo Heeman bibaala fi ja. Dɛ he nyiŋaa, nɛra baŋwɛnɛɛ baa ba kpoora harɛre maa dɛ di kora a ta nɔ ta nɔ?” Dɛ berɛ bɔɔ Ɛsta ja ŋɔ, “Waane lole ń ɛ tɛɛ ja aa? Baɡle kon haa dɛ nyin ásɛ n ɛ tɛɛ.”

english_verse: Esther answered, “Your Majesty, please let the Jews in Susa fight to defend themselves tomorrow, just as they did today. And order the bodies of Haman's ten sons to be hanged in public.”
translation_verse: Belaa Ɛsta chaŋo ŋɔ, “N naa, dɛ hɛɛ sɛoh waa, tɛ Juu tena baa lɔ Susa bonɔ ŋwɛnɛ kere ɡe ba ɛ ɡɛ baa ɛa fini nɔ, dɛ́ kpɔ Heeman bibaala fi la lala la ka saɡɛ daa ta.”

english_verse: King Xerxes did what Esther had requested, and the bodies of Haman's sons were hung in Susa.
translation_verse: Kooro no ɡɛ dɛ ɡel Susa tena no dɛ ɡel ba saɡɛ Heeman bibaala fi la.

english_verse: Then on the fourteenth day of Adar the Jews of the city got together and killed
translation_verse: Adar korobie tɔpera fi dɛ anaarɛ wee la, Juu tena baa lɔ Susa la chemo. Ba kpoo nɛra lafraatoro bwɛɛ la ta ja, kɛ ba ta ba komɛlbwa kpɔe.

english_verse: On the thirteenth day of Adar, the Jews in the provinces had come together to defend themselves. They killed
translation_verse: Adar korobie tɔpera fi dɛ atoro taa waa nɔ chiɡ, asɛ o tɔperafi dɛ anaarɛ ta ba onɛ, dɛ di kwaa dɛ lɛ ba sie, dɛ kpɔ a ɡɛ tɔpere la berɛ ba tɔpejen. Purim Tɔpejen dii

english_verse: On the fifteenth day of the month the Jews in Susa held a holiday and celebrated, after killing their enemies on the thirteenth and the fourteenth.
translation_verse: Juu tena baa lɔ Susa la yoo tɔpera fi dɛ atoro ne fi dɛ anaarɛ la ta. Tɔpera fi dɛ anue wee la, ba ɡel yoi dɛ onɛ, dɛ di kwaa lɛ ba sie.

english_verse: This is why the Jews in the villages now celebrate on the fourteenth day of the month. It is a joyful holiday that they celebrate by feasting and sending gifts of food to each other. The Festival of Purim
translation_verse: A waa Juu tena baa lɔ bwɛjeɡre ta kpɔ a ɡɛ korobie la tɔpera fi dɛ anaarɛ wee la ɛ ba tɔpejen, dɛ di kwa dɛɛ lɛ ba sie, dɛ berɛ dɛɛ kɛ kwaa o ta.

english_verse: Mordecai wrote down everything that had happened. Then he sent letters to the Jews everywhere in the provinces
translation_verse: Mɔdekae chwerɛ waa aa chiɡa la bwa bil. O berɔ chwerɛ tɔne ka tɛ Juu tena baa soɡe Kooro Sɛksɛs harɛre bojaŋa ne bela aa bɛno bwa ta.

english_verse: and told them: Each year you must celebrate on both the fourteenth and the fifteenth of Adar,
translation_verse: O ŋɔ bá kpɔ Adar korobie tɔpera fi dɛ anaarɛ ne fi dɛ anue wee la ɛ tɔpejena dɛɛ dia bena bɛlbwa,

english_verse: the days when we Jews defeated our enemies. Remember this month as a time when our sorrow was turned to joy, and celebration took the place of crying. Celebrate by having parties and by giving to the poor and by sharing gifts of food with each other.
translation_verse: dɛɛ lii tɔpera Juu tena aa lɛ ba te le ba dɔma nɔn ta, ne tɔpera ba suna dii aa ber ba silɛɛ, ba wii ɡe berɛ hɛɡra la. Mɔdekae ŋɔ, dɛ ba dɛ di tɔpera la aa, báa di kondikonjena dɛɛ lɛ ba sie, dɛɛ tɛ dɔŋa ne nyaara bwa kondikwa.

english_verse: They followed Mordecai's instructions and set aside these two days every year as a time of celebration. The Reason for the Festival of Purim
translation_verse: Anomanta, Juu tena la teŋɛ waa Mɔdekae aa chwera tɛɛ ba la ta, dɛɛ di ɡɛ tɔpejena nɔ bena bɛlbwa.

english_verse: Haman was the son of Hammedatha and a descendant of Agag. He hated the Jews so much that he planned to destroy them, but he wanted to find out the best time to do it. So he cast lots.
translation_verse: Gɛ tɔpera nɔ munii kɛŋɔ Hamedata bibaa Heeman waa ɛ Aɡaɡ naa, Juu tena bwa dɔm la, fa aa vɔrɔwa kɛŋɔ bá kpoo Juu tena bwa la. O bil daa dɛ na tɔpere baa kpɔ kpoo ba dɛ́ he ba kwaraa.

english_verse: Esther went to King Xerxes and asked him to save her people. Then the king gave written orders for Haman and his sons to be punished in the same terrible way that Haman had in mind for the Jews. So they were hanged.
translation_verse: Ɛsta aa la Kooro Sɛksɛs be dɛ ŋɔ Heeman vɔrɔwe Juu tena vɔrɔwa dɛ́ fee kpoo ba la, kooro do mmara dɛ ɡel Heeman liichɔɡa waa liira la ɡure o ɡbaɡba nyu ta, asɛ ba saɡɛ o ne o bibaala fi la.

english_verse: Mordecai's letter had said that the Jews must celebrate for two days because of what had happened to them. This time of celebration is called Purim, which is the Hebrew word for the lots that were cast.
translation_verse: Anomanta, dɛ ba dɛ yerɛ ɡɛ tɔpere nɔ Purim, tɔn Mɔdekae aa chwera ne waa aa puu ba la bwa wa.

english_verse: Queen Esther, daughter of Abihail, wanted to give full authority to Mordecai's letter about the Festival of Purim, and with his help she wrote a letter about the feast.
translation_verse: Anomanta, Abihel bihaah Ɛsta waa ɛ kooro haah la kpɔ kpeɡri waa dɔa la, asɛ Juu te Mɔdekae la chao, dɛ chwerɛ o Ɛsta ɡbaɡba tɔn dɛ bol Purim dii la wa, ásɛ a ɡel Mɔdekae tɔn nɛɛte la won ɛ toma kɛrɛdɛ.

english_verse: You and your descendants must always remember to celebrate Purim at the time and in the way that we have said. You must also follow the instructions that we have given you about mourning and going without eating.
translation_verse: dɛ́ berɛ ɡel a ɡɛ Purim tɔpera nɔ che kiŋkiŋ baa dia saŋ la Juu te Mɔdekae ne kooro haah Ɛsta aa doa tɛ ba ne ba naanar kɛŋɔ, ba fa aa cheɡ nyoa vɔwa ne suna dii tɔpera la.

english_verse: These laws about Purim are written by the authority of Queen Esther.
translation_verse: Ɛsta mmara la ɡelɔ ɡɛ baa dɛɛ di Purim tɔpera la che kiŋkiŋ, asɛ ba chwera do tɔn bini.

english_verse: King Xerxes made everyone in his kingdom pay taxes, even those in lands across the sea.
translation_verse: A berɔ ba kɛŋɔ Kooro Sɛksɛs dɛ lɛ nɛra baa lɔ o harɛre ta bwa toɔ, hale dɛ kpoŋe kaa o harɛre aa lɔ mpo nyoa bwa.

english_verse: All the great and famous things that King Xerxes did are written in the record books of the kings of Media and Persia. These records also tell about the honors that the king gave to Mordecai.
translation_verse: Wejena waa ɛa o kora dii saŋ, ne ɡɛ bwa waa ɛ Mɔdekae nomonjen la, ba chwerɔ do Midia ne Pɛɛsea koranar waa tɔne bini.

english_verse: Next to the king himself, Mordecai was the highest official in the kingdom. He was a popular leader of the Jews, because he helped them in many ways and would even speak to the king on their behalf.
translation_verse: Mɔdekae ɛ nomonjen, dɛ Kooro Sɛksɛs toole naa, dɛ onee lole. O ɛ nɛnjen o dɔŋa Juu tena la bwa bini, asɛ baa tɛo jirima dɛɛ nyin o wa, dɛkalkɛŋɔ o nyin kɛrɛdɛ tɛɛ ba, dɛ nyin deŋnesɔɔhna tɛ o naanar bwa.

english_verse: Many years ago, a man named Job lived in the land of Uz. He was a truly good person, who respected God and refused to do evil.
translation_verse: Baa bɛl fa lole, o sɔne Job, dɛ do harɛ bɛl ta baa yerɛ bela Us. Wobɛlbwa toole o nɛ, o waa toɡre. O dɛ tomɛ Korowii, dɛ laa o te dɛɛ kpɔ wechɔɡa ta.

english_verse: the Lord asked, “Satan, where have you been?” Satan replied, “I have been going all over the earth.”
translation_verse: Anee Korowii pɛɛ Bɔnsam ŋɔ, “Leperaa he le dɛ ba nɔ?” O ŋɔ, “Gaaɡaa n do harɛ nɔ ta dɛ ɡaaɡe la dɛɛ ba.”

english_verse: Job's sons took turns having feasts in their homes, and they always invited their three sisters to join in the eating and drinking.
translation_verse: O bibaala la bɛlbwa yon le o tɔpere cheɡ, dɛ́ ɡel ba daa kondikonjena o dem, dɛ́ yerɛ ba nimambihaahna batoro la, bá ka puu ba di kwaa la dɛ́ lɛ ba sie.

english_verse: After each feast, Job would send for his children and perform a ceremony, as a way of asking God to forgive them of any wrongs they may have done. He would get up early the next morning and offer a sacrifice for each of them, just in case they had sinned or silently cursed God. Angels, the Lord, and Satan
translation_verse: Ba di kondikonjena la dɛ bar chiɡ tonaa, ba mɛɛ Job yon ir chɔɔ, dɛ kpo kon ɛ saraha soŋe ba wechɔɡa Korowii be, bɛlbwa nyu ta. O yon lii ŋɔ, “N bii nɔ ken ɛ wechɔɡa, dɛ jo Korowii nɛɛ ba ta jemɛ.” Dɛ waa Job aa dɛ ɛ saŋ bɛlbwa laanee la. Job loɡla daahna dɛ́ na

english_verse: One day, when the angels had gathered around the Lord, and Satan was there with them,
translation_verse: Awola bɛl, nyundua toroma la Korowii be, dɛ Bɔnsam ɡe ja bɛl.

english_verse: Then the Lord asked, “What do you think of my servant Job? No one on earth is like him—he is a truly good person, who respects me and refuses to do evil.”
translation_verse: Korowii ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ he na n bonɔɔ Job waɔ? Nomɛlbwa toole o waa toɡre kɛ on harɛ nɔ ta, wechɔɡe bɛlbwa toole o nɛ, o dɛ tom mɛ, o laa o te dɛɛ kpɔ wechɔɡa ta.”

english_verse: “Why shouldn't he respect you?” Satan remarked.
translation_verse: Ate, Bɔnsam chaŋe ŋɔ, “He dɛ lii kɛŋɔ Job ɛɛ tomɛ pɛɛpɛɛ yaa?

english_verse: “You are like a wall protecting not only him, but his entire family and all his property. You make him successful in whatever he does, and his flocks and herds are everywhere.
translation_verse: He kpɔ nɔn tɔ o ne o dem tena ne komɛlbwa waa dɔa nɛ. Dɛ swee andɛɛɡa tɛo o toma bɛlbwa ta, dɛ ɡel o kondɛɛra ya perɛ harɛ la bwa ta.

english_verse: Try taking away everything he owns, and he will curse you to your face.”
translation_verse: Laa nɔn kpɔ komɛlbwa waa dɔa ta dɛ́ na, wɛɛ taahnee he na.”

english_verse: The Lord replied, “All right, Satan, do what you want with anything that belongs to him, but don't harm Job.” Then Satan left. Job Loses Everything
translation_verse: Anee Korowii ŋɔ Bɔnsam be ŋɔ, “A wer, komɛlbwa waa dɔa la lɔ he nɔn ta, kɛ o te ɡbabir te, bɛ nɔn kpɔ leɡo.” Asɛ Bɔnsam le Korowii be dɛ kaa.

english_verse: Job's sons and daughters were having a feast in the home of his oldest son,
translation_verse: Awola bɛl, Job bibaala ne bihaahna la dɛ di kondikonjena la ane, dɛɛ lɛ ba sie ba dɔɔ nomoa dem,

english_verse: when someone rushed up to Job and said, “While your servants were plowing with your oxen, and your donkeys were nearby eating grass,
translation_verse: belaa torome bɛl kpɔ chwae ba Job be dɛ ba ŋɔ, “Ya kpɔ nae kaa parɛ, asɛ keeɡore ɡe do ya jwɛɛh dɛɛ di,

english_verse: a gang of Sabeans attacked and stole the oxen and donkeys! Your other servants were killed, and I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
translation_verse: asɛ Seba tena ba lɔ jo a bini, dɛ lawa kaa. Ba kpoo n bala la bwa. N ɡboo wona dɔ bɔr chwa, dɛ baa bol he be la!”

english_verse: That servant was still speaking, when a second one came running and said, “God sent down a fire that killed your sheep and your servants. I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
translation_verse: Torome la nyoa taa lɔ waa la ta wɛɛ bol la, dɛ torome la bɛl ɡe balɔ dɛ ba ŋɔ, “Bwaala kɔrɔ jo ya ne kondɛɛra la bini, dɛ fuh a ne n bala la bwa. N ɡboo le a nyoa, asɛ dɛ baa bol he be la.”

english_verse: Before that servant finished speaking, a third one raced up and said, “Three gangs of Chaldeans attacked and stole your camels! All of your other servants were killed, and I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
translation_verse: O ɡe nyoa ta chiɡe, dɛ torome bɛl ɡe balɔ dɛ ba ŋɔ, “Kaldea tena baa kpoŋe dɔmkwaa dɛɛ ŋwɛ bɔne ba bini nɛmbele batoro, dɛ ba lɔ jo ya bini, dɛ lawɛ he nyoɡmare la bwa kaa. Ba kpoo n bala la bwa. N ɡboo wona dɔ bɔr chwa, dɛ baa bol he be la!”

english_verse: That servant was still speaking, when a fourth one dashed up and said, “Your children were having a feast and drinking wine at the home of your oldest son,
translation_verse: Torome la ɡe nyoa ta chiɡe, dɛ bɛl ɡe balɔ dɛ ba ŋɔ, “Dɛ he bibaala ne bihaahna la lɔ ba dɔɔ nomoa la dem, dɛɛ di kondikonjena dɛɛ lɛ ba sie,

english_verse: when suddenly a windstorm from the desert blew the house down, crushing all of your children. I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
translation_verse: asɛ peukpeɡ den ta le pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta dɛ ba lɔ dem la, o bwa ku chole ba nɛɛ ba bwa serewe. N ɡboo wona le a nyoa, dɛ baa bol he be la.”

english_verse: When Job heard this, he tore his clothes and shaved his head because of his great sorrow. He knelt on the ground, then worshiped God
translation_verse: Job aa no ɡɛ la, o ir che dɛ laa o batakaare kɛɛ, a baɡle kɛ o loo kuu, dɛ fonɛ o nyu. Ate, dɛ chɔ kpɔ sie pi harɛ, dɛ jam Korowii,

english_verse: and said: “We bring nothing at birth; we take nothing with us at death. The Lord alone gives and takes. Praise the name of the Lord!”
translation_verse: dɛ ŋɔ, “Ba lol mɛ mumɡbal, mumɡbal nee n berɛ dɛɛ ba kaala. Korowiirii dɛɛ tɛ, onee dɛɛ lɛ. Hé ɡel ya kpɛɛ o sɔn.”

english_verse: In spite of everything, Job did not sin or accuse God of doing wrong.
translation_verse: Waa nɔ bwa ta la, Job ta Korowii nɛɛ nyae a ɛ wechɔɡa tɛo.

english_verse: When the angels gathered around the Lord again, Satan was there with them,
translation_verse: Awola bɛl ɡe ja, nyundua toroma la baa cheme Korowii sie, dɛ Bɔnsam ɡe ja bɛl.

english_verse: and the Lord asked, “Satan, where have you been?” Satan replied, “I have been going all over the earth.”
translation_verse: Anee Korowii pɛɛ Bɔnsam ŋɔ, “Leperaa he le dɛ ba nɔ?” O ŋɔ, “Gaaɡaa n do harɛ nɔ ta dɛ ɡaaɡe la dɛɛ ba.”

english_verse: Then the Lord asked, “What do you think of my servant Job? No one on earth is like him—he is a truly good person, who respects me and refuses to do evil. And he hasn't changed, even though you persuaded me to destroy him for no reason.”
translation_verse: Ate, Korowii ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ he na n bonɔɔ Job waɔ? Nomɛlbwa toole o waa toɡre kɛ on harɛ nɔ ta, wechɔɡe bɛlbwa toole o nɛ, o dɛ tom mɛ, dɛ laa o te dɛɛ kpɔ wechɔɡa ta. He ba n be ŋɔ n tɛɛ ŋwɛnɛ he ka chɔɡo, dɛ o ta waane ɛɛ, kɛ ane a bwa, o waa ta toɡrɔ.”

english_verse: Satan answered, “There's no pain like your own. People will do anything to stay alive.
translation_verse: Bɔnsam chaŋe Korowii ŋɔ, “Nɛn dɛ nyin o nyu aa, wɛɛ won kpɔ kwaa waa dɔa bwa charɛ.

english_verse: Try striking Job's own body with pain, and he will curse you to your face.”
translation_verse: Lɔɔ bil weela ta dɛ́ na, dɛ waa hen taah he na naa.”

english_verse: “All right!” the Lord replied. “Make Job suffer as much as you want, but just don't kill him.”
translation_verse: Belaa Korowii ŋɔ Bɔnsam be ŋɔ, “A wer ɡa, n kpɔɔ do he nɔn ta, kɛ na kɛ haa on kpo.”

english_verse: Satan left and caused painful sores to break out all over Job's body—from head to toe.
translation_verse: Anomanta, Bɔnsam le Korowii be bela dɛ ka kpɔ ŋwɛrchɔɡa ta Job nɛ, le o nyu ta ba ta o napaala ta.

english_verse: Then Job sat on the ash-heap to show his sorrow. And while he was scraping his sores with a broken piece of pottery,
translation_verse: Asɛ Job ka so tɔɔ ta a baɡle kɛ o loo kuu, dɛ kpɔ kaŋli dɛɛ paa ŋwɛra la.

english_verse: his wife asked, “Why do you still trust God? Why don't you curse him and die?”
translation_verse: Job haah ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “He ta lɔ toɡra he wa aa toɡra la ta naa? Taah Korowii dɛ́ sewɛ!”

english_verse: Job replied, “Don't talk like a fool! If we accept blessings from God, we must accept trouble as well.” In all that happened, Job never once said anything against God. Job's Three Friends
translation_verse: Asɛ Job chaŋo ŋɔ, “He dɛ bol ɡɛnewobol. Wedɛɛɡa ɡboo yaa ba dɔe le Korowii be, yaa wola wechɔɡa tenee dɔ aa?” A ɡɛ waa nɔ bwa ta la, o ta waa bolɛ yaɡɛ Korowii bwa. Job daamanar batoro wa

english_verse: Eliphaz from Teman, Bildad from Shuah, and Zophar from Naamah were three of Job's friends, and they heard about his troubles. So they agreed to visit Job and comfort him.
translation_verse: Dɛ Job dɔ daamanar batoro bane. Bɛlee Teman te Elifas, ne Bildad waa le Su harɛ ta, dɛ Sofar o ɡe aa le Naama harɛ ta. Ba no wahala waa dɛ na la, dɛ ka cheme, dɛ bwa sɛh kɛŋɔ baa lao, dɛ́ ka bwɛɛlo.

english_verse: When they came near enough to see Job, they could hardly recognize him. And in their great sorrow, they tore their clothes, then sprinkled dust on their heads and cried bitterly.
translation_verse: O daamanar la aa dɛ ba, dɛ che bojaŋ nao la, ba ta on jemɛ. Ba wio kohona, dɛ laa ba laala kɛɛ, dɛ ɛ tɔɔ do ba nyuune ta, a baɡle kɛ ba loo kuu.

english_verse: For seven days and nights, they sat silently on the ground beside him, because they realized what terrible pain he was in.
translation_verse: Ba ne o soɡe harɛpɛɛ, chɔɔ ne jwaana, tɔpera anuanɛ. Bɛlbwa ta waa o be bolɛ, dɛkalkɛ dɛ ba na ɡɛ o bwara aa dɛ nyɛɡ.

english_verse: Finally, Job cursed the day of his birth
translation_verse: Job ne o daamanar aa soɡa yawanyoa habɔɔ la, o taah nyoa tɔpere baa lolɔ.

english_verse: Blot out the day of my birth and the night when my parents created a son.
translation_verse: “Korowii ɡel tɔpere baa lol mɛ o ta ne jwaana la baa kpoŋe n tea la bɛ ba kpa!

english_verse: Erase that night from the calendar and conceal it with darkness.
translation_verse: Le ɡɛ tɔpere jwaana la le, o bɛ benanyoa bɛlbwa ta ba kpa, a ba ɛ kɛ baa lii o waa.

english_verse: Don't let children be created or joyful shouts be heard ever again in that night.
translation_verse: Bɛ ɡel ba kpoŋe bie tea a ɡɛ jwaana la ta, bɛ ɡel silɛɛ ɡbɔɡa bɛlbwa le o ta.

english_verse: because it let me be born into a world of trouble. Why Didn't I Die at Birth?
translation_verse: Taah awola jwaana baa lol mɛ, n ba dɛ baa na wa, dɛɛ di suna o ta nɔ.

english_verse: Why was I accepted and allowed to nurse at my mother's breast?
translation_verse: Bɔkwaa n nya kpɔ mɛ dawɛ o nakpale ta, kɛɛ dɛ ɔr mɛ elɔ?

english_verse: Now I would be at peace in the silent world below
translation_verse: Dɛ n fe sewɔ ɡɛ saŋ aa, n fe chɔ deŋnesɔɔhna ta, dɛɛ onɛ,

english_verse: with kings and their advisors whose palaces lie in ruins,
translation_verse: n ne koranar ne nomonjena, ba fa aa ma dejena a saŋ la, dɛ so a ta bwa berɛ dimɡbia.

english_verse: and with rulers once rich with silver and gold.
translation_verse: N ne koranar baa kpɔ suuɡaswɛm ne suuɡapoŋa su ba deene dɛ serewe la bwa fe chɔɔ.

english_verse: I wish I had been born dead and then buried, never to see the light of day.
translation_verse: Ɛrɛɛ maa wola doe kɛŋɔ bie baa haro ta dɛ huɡo, kɛɛ bechasɔɔhna waa sewa o ta wee nae bwa nɔ?

english_verse: In the world of the dead, the wicked and the weary rest without a worry. *
translation_verse: Lalbɔɔ binii nyubinikpeɡ tena we-ɛɛla ɛɛ tonɛ, nɛra baa ɛ toma koh la ɡe kaa onɛ.

english_verse: where captives and slaves are free at last. Why Does God Let Me Live?
translation_verse: Nomonjena ne dansaara bwa lɔ bela, bela te, yom toole o dɔɔ lɔɡa kpa.

english_verse: Why does God let me live when life is miserable and so bitter?
translation_verse: Ɛrɛɛ Korowii ɡel nɛra ba bwara aa dɛ nyɛɡ so le nɔɔ? Ɛrɛɛ o tɛ banɔ la baa dɛ di suna mkpa nɔɔ?

english_verse: I keep longing for death more than I would seek a valuable treasure.
translation_verse: Ba pɛla lawɔ kɛ bá sewɛ kɛ baa dɔ, dɛ ɡaaɡe dɛɛ nyinu ɡwaa kondɛɛɡe bɛl waa sɔah,

english_verse: Nothing could make me happier than to be in the grave.
translation_verse: ba sie aa lɛ kɛrɛdɛ, kɛŋɔ ba fe aa sewa ba huɡ ba.

english_verse: Why do I go on living when God has me surrounded, and I can't see the road?
translation_verse: Korowii ɡelɔ baa ba kerekere waa jemɛ, dɛ tɔ ba do bobɛlbwa.

english_verse: Moaning and groaning are my food and drink,
translation_verse: Suna dii ber mɛ kondikwa, maa won ɡel pɛma bwa.

english_verse: and my worst fears have all come true.
translation_verse: Waa maa dɛ ɔma kohona, laanee ba n nɛ.

english_verse: I have no peace or rest— only troubles and worries.
translation_verse: N ta deŋnesɔɔhna dɔe, n ta ona dɔe, atane wenaale ɡbo.”

english_verse: Eliphaz from Teman said:
translation_verse: Belaa Teman te Elifas ŋɔ Job be ŋɔ,

english_verse: Please be patient and listen to what I have to say. *
translation_verse: “Dɛ n bol waa baɡle naa, hɛɛ no n bee yaa? Maa won tɔ nyoa ɡɛ kpa.

english_verse: have guided and encouraged many in need.
translation_verse: He wobol cha nɛra baa nyoɡre Korowii ŋwɛnɛ, dɛ ɡel ba won che ja.

english_verse: But now you feel discouraged when struck by trouble.
translation_verse: He ɡe kwaa bala fini, dɛ kpɔ bambichɔɡa ba ta he nɛɛ la.

english_verse: You respect God and live right, so don't lose hope!
translation_verse: He tomɛ Korowii, wechɔɡa bɛlbwa aa wola toole he nɛ, a chɛ kɛ hɛɛ yarada dɛ dɔ hwɛɡa.

english_verse: In my experience, only those who plant seeds of evil harvest trouble,
translation_verse: N ɡbabir nao kɛŋɔ nɛra baa dɛ vɔrɔwe wechɔɡa vɔrɔwa, ne banɔ la baa dɛ nyin waa la, anee baa dɔ.

english_verse: and then they are swept away by the angry breath of God.
translation_verse: Korowii bandia do kɛŋɔ dompeu, o hwee ta ba nɛɛ ba serewe.

english_verse: They may roar and growl like powerful lions. But when God breaks their teeth,
translation_verse: Nyubinikpeɡ tena do kɛŋɔ nyujentena aa dɛ si, kɛ Korowii sɔɔh a nyoa dɛ kuuɡi a nyena.

english_verse: they starve, and their children are scattered. A Secret Was Told to Me
translation_verse: Nyujente ta ol dɔe lawɛ di aa, o dɛ sewɛ, ásɛ o bii bwa ɡe lɔ peɡre.

english_verse: A secret was told to me in a faint whisper—
translation_verse: Nomɛl sɔɔh ba lɔɡ mɛ waane tamaa ken, aa do ɡɛ la, n ta wone no a bini kɛrɛdɛ.

english_verse: I was overcome by sleep, but disturbed by dreams;
translation_verse: A do kɛŋɔ jwaanen deechɔɡa ken, a chɔɡ n dom,

english_verse: and my hair stood on end, as a wind blew past my face.
translation_verse: Komɛl ɡale n sie ta, asɛ n bwara ɛɛ mɛ nyirr.

english_verse: It stopped and stood still. Then a form appeared— a shapeless form. And from the silence, I heard a voice say,
translation_verse: Kon la cheɡɔ, kɛ n ta wone jemɛ o konsoo. N na o dor o che n sie, asɛ n no taa bɛl o ŋɔ,

english_verse: “No humans are innocent in the eyes of God their Creator.
translation_verse: ‘Nɛwɛnyini waa ɛɛ won toɡre ɡwaa Korowii aa? Nɛn ɛɛ won do ɡoroŋ ɡwaa Korowii waa tao wa aa?

english_verse: He finds fault with his servants and even with his angels.
translation_verse: Dɛ Korowii ta hwɛɡa dɔe o nyundua toroma nɛ, hale o na wechɔɡa ba nɛ aa,

english_verse: Humans are formed from clay and are fragile as moths, so what chance do you have?
translation_verse: he dɛ lii kɛŋɔ wɛɛ dɔ hwɛɡa nɛn waa kpɔ teera mao nɛɛ ya? Wɛɛ won sewɛ warane kɛŋɔ baa dɛ kpo konɡaahle la!

english_verse: Born after daybreak, you die before nightfall and disappear forever.
translation_verse: Hɛɛ nao chɔɔ kɛ jɔmɔra ne tela dɛ o sewɔ dɛ he ta ɡɛ liire.

english_verse: Your tent pegs are pulled up, and you leave this life, having gained no wisdom.”
translation_verse: Baa pa o kondɔɔh bwaa kaa, o sewɛ dɛ o ta wejema bɛlbwa dɔe le Korowii be.’ ”

english_verse: Job, call out for help and see if an angel comes!
translation_verse: Elifas berɔ ŋɔ, “Job yerɛ na, umee dɛ́ chaŋe nɔ? Nyundua torome bɛl lole dɛ́ no he be naa? Akai!

english_verse: Envy and jealousy will kill a stupid fool.
translation_verse: Bandia dɛ kpo ɡɛne, sibeɡra ɡe ɛɛ kpo nɛn waa wola wobɛlbwa jemɛ.

english_verse: I have seen fools take root. But God sends a curse, suddenly uprooting them
translation_verse: N ɡbabir na nɛn waa ɡɛna o soɡa bini do wer, kɛ buɡ la ta, nyotaahna chole o dem.

english_verse: Our suffering isn't caused by the failure of crops;
translation_verse: Teera ta laa wechɔɡa le kɛŋɔ konduuli, a ta laa wenaale le.

english_verse: it's all part of life, like sparks shooting skyward.
translation_verse: Ba lolɛ nɛn aa, dɛ o ne waa, kɛŋɔ nihɛm yon chuɡri dɛɛ kaa nyundua la.

english_verse: Job, if I were you, I would ask God for help.
translation_verse: Kɛ dɛ menee yaa, n fe ɛɛ soŋe Korowiirii, dɛ́ kpɔ n waa bil o sie.

english_verse: His miracles are marvelous, more than we can count.
translation_verse: Wejena haa wola won no a munii Korowii ɛɛ ɛ, nyokpowaa haa wola won kuraa wɛɛ ɛ.

english_verse: God sends showers on earth and waters the fields.
translation_verse: O ɡelɔ bwaala ɛɛ nɛ harɛ ta, dɛ ɡel wɛɛ tel kpɔɡbaah bwa.

english_verse: He protects the sorrowful and lifts up those who have been disgraced. *
translation_verse: Korowii dɛ tɛ nɛŋɡwɛɡra chebɔr, banɔ la baa dɛ wi ɡe dɔ silɛɛ.

english_verse: Darkness is their only companion, hiding their path at noon.
translation_verse: Biro dɛ ba ba nɛɛ webaŋa, baa laɡre bɔr kɛŋɔ jwaana ken.

english_verse: God rescues the needy from the words of the wicked and the fist of the mighty.
translation_verse: Korowii lɛ nɛra dɛɛ le ba seo nyoa, o lɛɛ ba dɛɛ le fiiɡa ta.

english_verse: The poor are filled with hope, and injustice is silenced. Consider Yourself Fortunate
translation_verse: Anomanta, banɔ la aa hiah ba dɔ hwɛɡa, nɛnchɔɡa ta waa dɔe dɛ́ bol kpa.

english_verse: He may cause injury and pain, but he will bandage and heal your cuts and bruises.
translation_verse: Onee dɛɛ do nɛn bol dɛ berɛ dɛɛ vɔrɔwo, dɛɛ do nɛn weela dɛɛ chaoh.

english_verse: God will protect you from harm, no matter how often trouble may strike.
translation_verse: Saŋ bɛlbwa Korowii ɛɛ lɛɛ le wenaale ta.

english_verse: In times of war and famine, God will keep you safe.
translation_verse: Lɔr saŋ wɛɛ lɛɛ le seo nyoa dɛ́ lɛɛ le laa ta.

english_verse: You will be sheltered, without fear of hurtful words or any other weapon.
translation_verse: Wɛɛ lɛɛ le chɔɡa nɛra aa dɛ chɔɡe ta, wekpeɡa dɛ ba he nɛ aa, bɛ ɔmɛ, wɛɛ kpɔ nɔnee tɔ he nɛ.

english_verse: You will laugh at the threat of destruction and famine. And you won't be afraid of wild animals—
translation_verse: Lɔr ne wekpeɡa dɛ ba naa, hɛɛ soo dɛɛ mamɛ, haa kpɔɡ bini olaa ɔmɛ.

english_verse: they will no longer be fierce, and your rocky fields will become friendly.
translation_verse: Koo haa parɛ la, bwea aa o taa do, kpɔɡ bini olchɔɡa aa hen ɡbaa bwa.

english_verse: Your home will be secure, and your sheep will be safe.
translation_verse: Hɛɛ nao kɛŋɔ he dem sɔɔhnɔ kɛrɛdɛ, he kure he kondɔɔh, dɛ́ na kɛŋɔ bɛlbwa ta nyoɡrɛ.

english_verse: You will have more descendants than there are blades of grass on the face of the earth.
translation_verse: Hɛɛ nao ɡe kɛŋɔ he bii warɔ, ásɛ he naanar warɛ kɛŋɔ kpɔɡa ken.

english_verse: You will live a very long life, and your body will be strong until the day you die.
translation_verse: Hɛɛ dɔ mkpajaŋee, he bwara ta do kpeɡri mɔɔ he sewɛ, kɛŋɔ mea yon be kɛrɛdɛ mɔɔ ba koma la.

english_verse: Our experience has proven these things to be true, so listen and learn.
translation_verse: Job, ya ɡbabir nyiŋi ɡɛ waa nɔ, dɛ na kɛŋɔ a ɛ kasinteŋ. Anomanta, kpɔ dɛ ɛ ɡɛ tenten.”

english_verse: It's impossible to weigh my misery and grief!
translation_verse: “Dɛ ba fe kari n wenaale ne n suna maa dɛ di bwa naa,

english_verse: They outweigh the sand along the beach, and that's why I have spoken without thinking first.
translation_verse: a fe ɛɛ do tɔɡree ɡwaa mpo nyoa hɛŋle bwa, a waa he na kɛŋɔ n wobol la bini nyɛɡre la.

english_verse: Do oxen and wild donkeys cry out in distress unless they are hungry?
translation_verse: Keeɡo dɔ kpɔɡa dɛɛ chwe aa, waa si, ɡɛɛ nabal ɡe dɔ kwaa dɛɛ dia aa, waa wola si.

english_verse: What is food without salt? What is more tasteless than the white of an egg?
translation_verse: Yar toole kondikwaa ta naa, a dɛ do som aa? Jahal kompoŋ ɡbo som aa?

english_verse: That's how my food tastes, and my appetite is gone. *
translation_verse: N pɛla aa ɡɛ kondikwaa nɔ dɔ, a dɛ tɛ mɛ weela.

english_verse: Then I would be comforted, knowing that in all of my pain I have never disobeyed God.
translation_verse: Belaa mɛɛ ba bolarawa dɔe n sie lɛ, n weweele aa wola tonɛ bwa ta, á baɡle kɛŋɔ n ta Korowii O Wa Aa Do Goroŋ la waa vɛɛh.

english_verse: I am not strong as stone or bronze,
translation_verse: N bwara kpeɡri kɛŋɔ bwe aa? Kɛɛ n bwadabii do kɛŋɔ ayaawa ɔ?

english_verse: and I have finally reached the end of my rope. My Friends, I Am Desperate
translation_verse: N ta kpeɡri dɔe dɛ́ lɛ n te, bobɛlbwa toole ń kpɔ sie chaɡɛ nɛn cha mɛ.

english_verse: My friends, I am desperate, and you should help me, even if I no longer respect God All-Powerful. *
translation_verse: Dɛ waa pu nɛn aa, a chɛ kɛ o daamanar ɛɛ chao, hale dɛ o vɛh Korowii Waa Ɛ Kpeɡri Bwa Dɔɔ ɔma kwaraa noo.

english_verse: like streams that swell with melting snow,
translation_verse: Dombwea baa ta aa, nenabɔɔne dɛ suuɡi,

english_verse: I am like a caravan, lost in the desert while searching for water.
translation_verse: Nɛra baa soɡe nyoɡmare ta, dɛ valɛ dɛɛ ɡaaɡe nee dɛ nyɔ nyoɡrɔ, ba ɡaaɡɔ dɛ ka serewe pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta.

english_verse: thought they would find water. But they were disappointed,
translation_verse: Ba hwɛɡa kaa tonɛ, nenabɔɔne aa hweehra bini.

english_verse: just as I am with you. Only one look at my suffering, and you run away scared. What Have I Done Wrong?
translation_verse: Hé do kɛ nenabɔɔne la n be, he ta chae bɛlbwa dɔe, he na waane aa ba n nɛ dɛ ɔmɛ dɛ le habɔɔ.

english_verse: What have I done wrong? Show me, and I will keep quiet.
translation_verse: A wer, hé baɡ mɛ n wechɔɡa maa ɛa, mɛɛ tɔ nyoa dɛ́ no he be.

english_verse: The truth is always painful, but your arguments prove nothing.
translation_verse: Kasinteŋ dii dɛ we, kɛ waa haa dɛ bol nɔ ta mun dɔe.

english_verse: Here I am desperate, and you consider my words as worthless as wind.
translation_verse: He dɛ lii ŋɔ n dɛ bol wepuu, ɛrɛɛ hɛɛ chaŋe n waa, kɛŋɔ nɛn waa wola kerekere waa lii nɔɔ?

english_verse: Why, you would sell an orphan or your own neighbor!
translation_verse: Hɛɛ won ta bie bilalbii waa kwara! Dɛ yoɡ he daamanar dɛ́ dɔ suuɡa.

english_verse: Look me straight in the eye; I won't lie to you.
translation_verse: N dɛ soŋe heya, hé nyiŋ mɛ kɛrɛdɛ! Mɛɛ teŋe nyosone he sie yaa?

english_verse: Stop accusing me falsely; my reputation is at stake.
translation_verse: Hé berɛ nyiŋi a bini, dɛ bɛ men bolchɔɡe pa, hé kwaa lii, dɛkalkɛ n waa la wer.

english_verse: I know right from wrong, and I am not telling lies.
translation_verse: Nyosone ane le n nyoa kɛɛ? Maa wedɛɛɡa ne wechɔɡa jemɛ aa?”

english_verse: Why is life so hard? Why do we suffer?
translation_verse: Job berɔ ŋɔ, “Nɛwɛnyini soɡa bini, tomkpeɡaa chɔ le dɛ tɛo, kɛŋɔ paate waa dɛ ɛ toma la.

english_verse: We are slaves in search of shade; we are laborers longing for our wages.
translation_verse: A do kɛŋɔ yom aa nyin chunchule dɛɛ onɛ, kɛɛ paa te aa dɛ kpa o kembɔr la.

english_verse: God has made my days drag on and my nights miserable.
translation_verse: Gɛɛ mɛɛ so korobie bɛlbwa pɛɛpɛɛ, jwaana bɛlbwaa mɛɛ na wa.

english_verse: I pray for night to end, but it stretches out while I toss and turn.
translation_verse: N yon chɔ dɛɛ lii ŋɔ, ‘Bɛweeree bɔr ɛɛ ba chaahna ń irɔ?’ Dɛ chɔ kalaŋ ta, dɛ beɡre ɡɛ naa dɛɛ nyin bɔr chaah.

english_verse: My parched skin is covered with worms, dirt, and sores,
translation_verse: Dudule ne ŋwɛra su n bwadabii bwa, nee ɛɛ le n ŋwɛra ta.

english_verse: and my days are running out quicker than the thread of a fast-moving needle. Don't Forget!
translation_verse: N tɔpera teŋo baa kaa warane kɛŋɔ yasɔɔh aa dɛ ta kokorowa la, a dɛ tonɛ kɛ dɛ n ta hwɛɡa dɔe.

english_verse: I beg you, God, don't forget! My life is just a breath, and trouble lies ahead.
translation_verse: N Naa Korowii, bɛ soh kɛŋɔ me mkpa ka kerabeŋkpoŋ hweera, silɛɛ toole n soɡa bini kpa.

english_verse: I will vanish from sight, and no one, including you, will ever see me again.
translation_verse: Taraken haa na mɛ nɔ, haa men na kpa, hɛɛ baa nyin n bɔree, dɛ n toole.

english_verse: I will disappear in the grave or vanish from sight like a passing cloud.
translation_verse: Gɛ bam aa wola le do saŋ bɛlbwa la, ɡɛɛ nɛn sewaa waa wola ba kpa.

english_verse: Never will I return home; soon I will be forgotten.
translation_verse: Waa berɛ ba so o dem kpa, bela o fa aa soɡa la, baa on na kpa.

english_verse: And so, I cry out to you in agony and distress.
translation_verse: Anomanta, maa nyoa tɔ, mɛɛ che n weweele taa, dɛ́ bol waa sum ne.

english_verse: Am I the sea or a sea monster? Is that why you imprison me?
translation_verse: N ɛ mpo, kɛɛ o bini oljen asɛ hɛɛ do mɛ dɛɛɡɔ aa?

english_verse: but you torture me with terrible dreams. *
translation_verse: bela kwaraa la, he dɛ aah mɛ deera ta, he ɡelɔ mɛɛ na wepila dɛɛ ɔmɛ,

english_verse: Leave me alone and let me die; my life has no meaning.
translation_verse: N soɡa bini pe mɛ, maa nyin kɛ n so le dɛɛ la. Gel mɛ, n soɡa ta mun dɔe.

english_verse: What makes you so concerned about us humans?
translation_verse: Bɔkwaa nɛwɛnyina ɡe ba waa hiaeh nɔ? Ɛrɛɛ hɛɛ dawɛ waa baa dɛ ɛɔ?

english_verse: Why do you test us from sunrise to sunset?
translation_verse: He dɛ nyiŋi ba we-ɛɛla, chɔɔ bɛlbwa dɛɛ daah ba saŋ bɛlbwa.

english_verse: Won't you look away just long enough for me to swallow?
translation_verse: Haa sie laa kpɔ n nɛɛ tama, dɛ́ ɡel n lile nentane kwaraa naa?

english_verse: Why do you watch us so closely? What's it to you, if I sin? Why am I your target and such a heavy burden?
translation_verse: Dɛ n ɛ wechɔɡa kwaraa naa, bɔkwa waa n ɛɛ nɔ? He laa dɛɛ daah nɛra la aa? Ɛrɛɛ he fome siwi pa n nɛɛ nɔɔ? N ɛ bone tɛɛ kɛɛ?

english_verse: Bildad from Shuah said:
translation_verse: Bildad waa le Su la chaŋe Job ŋɔ,

english_verse: How long will you talk and keep saying nothing?
translation_verse: “Saŋ besoo he wobobala nɔ ɛɛ ba tona ɔ? He wobol do kɛŋɔ peukpeɡ, kɛ a ɛ wepuu.

english_verse: He made your children pay for their sins.
translation_verse: He bii ken ɛ Korowii wechɔɡa, a waa o tɛr ba deŋne ɡɛ aa chɛa.

english_verse: and start living right? Then he will decide to rescue and restore you to your place of honor.
translation_verse: dɛ he waa wer dɛ toɡre aa, wɛɛ ba chae dɛ́ berɛ tɛɛ sobɔrdɛɛɡe a ɛɛ kembɔr.

english_verse: Your future will be brighter by far than your past. Our Ancestors Were Wise
translation_verse: Kwaa haa dɔa mumpar la ken aa kanɛ, anɔ la Korowii aa ba tɛɛ a habɔɔ la ɛɛ do kanee kohona.

english_verse: Our ancestors were wise, so learn from them.
translation_verse: Ta sie nyiŋi, saŋ la tena waa bini, dɛ na waa ya naawa aa hwela.

english_verse: Our own time has been short, like a fading shadow, and we know very little.
translation_verse: Ya te aa biɡri, yaa wobɛlbwa jemɛ, ya soɡa bini do kɛŋɔ lileo ken harɛ nɔ ta.

english_verse: and if the water dries up, they die sooner than grass.
translation_verse: Nee la hweehraa, anee tɔ sie dɛɛ hol, kɛ dɛ a ta kpeɡe kɛŋɔ ba kua dɛ́ kpɔ ɛ wobɛlbwa.

english_verse: Such is the hopeless future of all who turn from God
translation_verse: Gɛɛ nɛra baa soh Korowii waa la bwa do, baa vɛh Korowii nomanta, ba ta hwɛɡa dɔe.

english_verse: and trust in something as frail as a spider's web—
translation_verse: Kon baa kpɔ ba hwɛɡa dawɛ o ta, do kɛ ŋwandare yal ken.

english_verse: Sinful people are like plants with spreading roots and plenty of sun and water.
translation_verse: Wechɔɡ-ɛɛra do kɛ kpɔɡa aa kpeɡa dɛ che webaah, ba do kɛŋɔ anɔ la aa moɡa tɔ bodɛɛɡe baa du daa.

english_verse: They wrap their roots tightly around rocks.
translation_verse: A dɛ ta lune bar bwea, ásɛ dɛ lawa kpoŋe kiŋkiŋ.

english_verse: But once they are pulled up, they have no more place;
translation_verse: Kɛ dɛ nomɛl tua le bela aa, nomɛlbwa aa jemɛ kɛŋɔ a fa lɔ bela.

english_verse: their life slips away, and other plants grow there.
translation_verse: Gɛɛ a do, silɛɛ wechɔɡ-ɛɛra aa dɔa laanee, banfalaa yon ba so ba buɡ ta.

english_verse: We know God doesn't reject an innocent person or help a sinner.
translation_verse: Kpelaa, Korowii aa nɛra ba waa aa dɔ kasinteŋ la vɛh bwa, ɡɛɛ waa wola wechɔɡ-ɛɛra ɡe cha.

english_verse: And so, he will make you happy and give you something to smile about.
translation_verse: Wɛɛ ɡeloo he sie lɛ he mamɛ, dɛ́ hɛɡre dɛɛ moo.

english_verse: But your evil enemies will be put to shame and disappear forever.
translation_verse: Wɛɛ ɡeloo sihiih kpo he dɔma, wechɔɡ-ɛɛra deremi ɡe chɔɡ.”

english_verse: What you say is true. No human is innocent in the sight of God.
translation_verse: “Kpelaa, n jemɔ kɛ a ɛ kasinteŋ. Aah ɛrɛɛ nɛwɛnyini ɛɛ ba wona di bole Korowii nɛɔ?

english_verse: Not once in a thousand times could we win our case if we took him to court.
translation_verse: Umee dɛ́ won tɔŋle Korowii ɔ? Wɛɛ won pɛɛ webele kaɡboŋ, nɛn aa won chaŋe a bini beŋkpoŋ kwara.

english_verse: God is wise and powerful— who could possibly oppose him and win?
translation_verse: Korowii dɔ wejema, dɛ do kpeɡri taeh! Umee dɛ́ won ɛ deŋnekpeɡ o nɛ, á chiɡu kɛrɛdɛ nɔ?

english_verse: When God becomes angry, he can move mountains before they even know it.
translation_verse: O huɡri bwejena dɛɛ ta, o baah diu waa, o dɛ chɔɡa.

english_verse: or command the sun and stars to hold back their light.
translation_verse: Wɛɛ won ŋɔ wee bɛ le, jwaana ɡe weweela bɛ won chaah.

english_verse: God alone stretched out the sky, stepped on the sea,
translation_verse: O ɡboo paɡri nyundua bɔle kɛ yal, dɛ berɛ won valɛ mpo nehɛma ta.

english_verse: and set the stars in place— the Big Dipper and Orion, the Pleiades and the stars in the southern sky.
translation_verse: Onee ta weweela bwa soo siwi, ne anɔ la aa lɔ nyundua weekaŋle harɛbɔr.

english_verse: Of all the miracles God works, we cannot understand a one.
translation_verse: O dɛ ɛ wejena nomɛlbwa aa wola won jemɛ a mun, dɛɛ ɛ nyokpowe-ɛɛla aa wola nyoa dɔe.

english_verse: God walks right past me, without making a sound.
translation_verse: Korowii kpɔ n jwɛɛh ba kaa laa, maa on na.

english_verse: And if he grabs something, who can stop him or raise a question?
translation_verse: Dɛ o ŋɔ wɛɛ lɛ komɛlee yaa, umee dɛ́ won tɔɔ ŋwɛnɛ ɔ? Umee dɛ́ won ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, ‘Bɔkwaa hɛɛ ɛ nɔɔ?’

english_verse: When God showed his anger, the servants of the sea monster fell at his feet.
translation_verse: Korowii baah diu waa, o ɡbaɡba aa won o te larawe warane, o dɛ sɔɔh mpo bini oljen ne kwaa aa dɛ chao la nyoa, á do o lɔɡa.

english_verse: How, then, could I possibly argue my case with God? Though I Am Innocent
translation_verse: A do ɡɛ naa, n dɔ waane dɛ chaŋe Korowii aa? N ne waa won cheme.

english_verse: And if God came into court when I called him, he would not hear my case.
translation_verse: Dɛ n fe yerɔ o sɛh n be naa, maa lii kɛŋɔ o fe ɛɛ no n bee.

english_verse: He would strike me with a storm and increase my injuries for no reason at all.
translation_verse: Wɛɛ ɡeloo peuchɔɡe ta dɛ́ lɔ mɛ bil, n bwara foɡri, aa wola mun dɔe.

english_verse: Before I could get my breath, my miseries would multiply.
translation_verse: Waa ɡel ń won hwee ɡba, dɛ́ kpɔ suna dii ta n nɛɛ kohona.

english_verse: God is much stronger than I am, and who would call me into court to give me justice?
translation_verse: Dɛ kpeɡri waa yaa, onee kpeɡa dɛ ɡwaa mɛ! Dɛ kɔɔto ɡee yaa, umee dɛ́ won la o ne nɔ?

english_verse: I am not guilty, but I no longer care what happens to me.
translation_verse: N waa toɡrɔ te, kɛ n waane laa wobɛlbwa aa ba n nɛ. N soɡa bini pe mɛ.

english_verse: What difference does it make? God destroys the innocent along with the guilty.
translation_verse: A bwa beŋkpoŋ, a waa n ŋɔ, ‘Korowii dɛ chɔɡ nɛra ba wa aa toɡra, ne wechɔɡ-ɛɛra bwa la.’

english_verse: When a good person dies a sudden death, God sits back and laughs.
translation_verse: Wekpeɡa piɡro ba seo ne naa, Korowii dɛ mamɛ nɛn wobɛlbwa aa wola toole o nɛ.

english_verse: And who else but God blindfolds the judges, then lets the wicked take over the earth? My Life Is Speeding By
translation_verse: Harɛ bɛl baa do nɛnchɔɡa nɔn ta naa, Korowii dɛ damɛ nɛra baa dɛ di ba waa liire. Dɛ o laa aa, umee dɛ́ won ɛ ɡɛ nɔ?

english_verse: My life is speeding by, without a hope of happiness.
translation_verse: N soɡa bini tɔpera dɛ kaa warawara kɛŋɔ nɛn waa dɛ chwa, silɛɛ bɛlbwa ɡe toole a ta.

english_verse: Each day passes swifter than a sailing ship or an eagle swooping down.
translation_verse: A do kɛŋɔ ɡbera aa chɔŋɛ nee sie dɛɛ kaa warane, kɛɛ kee aa le nyundua, dɛɛ ba ba lawɛ kon di la ken.

english_verse: Sometimes I try to be cheerful and to stop complaining,
translation_verse: Dɛ n ŋɔ mɛɛ soh n weweelee yaa, atane n tɔ nyoa, dɛ́ kwaa n sie do, dɛ mamɛ.

english_verse: but my sufferings frighten me, because I know that God still considers me guilty.
translation_verse: N weweele bwa ta, n dɛ ɔmɛ, n jemɔ kɛ Korowii ɛɛ pa mɛ bolchɔɡee.

english_verse: So what's the use of trying to prove my innocence?
translation_verse: Dɛ n di bolchɔɡe aa, a chɛ kɛŋɔ ń koh ta pɛɛ ja aa?

english_verse: Even if I washed myself with the strongest soap,
translation_verse: Hale n sɔ semina dɛ sarame nɔɔra o ne kwaraa naa,

english_verse: God would throw me into a pit of stinking slime, leaving me disgusting to my clothes.
translation_verse: Korowii ɛɛ taɡ mɛɛ do bɔluŋ doŋa aa lɔ o bini, n bwara laala kwaraa aa men nyin, kɛŋɔ nɛn yon hah o dɔŋ la.

english_verse: God isn't a mere human like me. I can't put him on trial.
translation_verse: O ta nɛn ɛɛ ásɛ n ŋɔ mɛɛ chaŋoo, kɛɛ dɛ́ ŋɔ n ne wɛɛ ka che kɔɔtoo.

english_verse: Who could possibly judge between the two of us?
translation_verse: Kɛ nomɛlbwa toole dɛ́ ba che n ne Korowii baah ta dɛ́ bol ya wa.

english_verse: Can someone snatch away the stick God carries to frighten me?
translation_verse: N Naa Korowii, ɡel n deŋne tɛra, laa ɔmee bɛlbwa kpɔ n nɛ.

english_verse: Then I could speak up without fear of him, but for now, I cannot speak.
translation_verse: N fe ɛɛ bol waa maa wola ɔmɛ, kɛ ɡɛ aa doa taraken nɔ, maa won bol.”

english_verse: I am sick of life! And from my deep despair, I complain to you, my God.
translation_verse: Job berɔ bol Korowii be ŋɔ, “N soɡa bini pe mɛ, mɛɛ bol waa maa wola ɔmɛ. No n tebinichɔɡ waa nɔ.

english_verse: Why do you take such delight in destroying those you created and in smiling on sinners?
translation_verse: A wer he be kɛŋɔ he fiɡ mɛ, dɛ́ vɛh kon he ɡbabir aa tao wa aa? Hɛɛ sɛh waa wechɔɡ-ɛɛra aa dɛ vɔrɔwe taa yaa?

english_verse: Do you look at things the way we humans do?
translation_verse: Nɛn sibie he dɔ dɛɛ nyiŋi waa kɛ nɛwɛnyini aa dɛ nyiŋi naa?

english_verse: Is that why you are so quick to find fault with me?
translation_verse: Dɛ ɡɛɛ a do aa, ɛrɛɛ hɛɛ nyin he na n wechɔɡa dɛɛ nyin he jemɛ wechɔɡa bɛlbwa maa ɛa nɔɔ?

english_verse: You know I am innocent, but who can defend me against you?
translation_verse: He ɡbabir jemɔ kɛŋɔ n ta wechɔɡa ɛɛ, nomɛl aa won lɛɛ mɛ le he nɔn ta.

english_verse: Will you now destroy someone you created?
translation_verse: Men he ɡbabir aa kpɔ nɔɔra ma nɔ, hɛɛ berɔ chɔɡ mɛ naa?

english_verse: Remember that you molded me like a piece of clay. So don't turn me back into dust once again.
translation_verse: Lii kɛŋɔ choh nee he ma mɛ, hɛɛ berɔ chɔɡ mɛ ń berɛ teera aa?

english_verse: As cheese is made from milk, you created my body from a tiny drop.
translation_verse: Hen tɛ n mɛɛ bokpeɡa o lol mɛ, he ɡelɔ n kpeɡ n nya tea bini.

english_verse: Then you tied my bones together with muscles and covered them with flesh and skin.
translation_verse: Henee kpɔ dɛɛhne choŋri n hoɡa, dɛ kpɔ ol ne tɔn bɔla.

english_verse: You, the source of my life, showered me with kindness and watched over me. You Have Not Explained
translation_verse: He nyin mɛ dɛ tɛ mɛ mkpa, dɛ nyiŋi n nɛɛ kɛrɛdɛ n ta do le.

english_verse: but you catch and punish me each time I sin.
translation_verse: Dɛ he dɛ nyiŋi kɛ n fee ɛ wechɔɡa, ásɛ he fe bɛ kpɔ kɛ mɛ.

english_verse: No matter how hard I try, you keep hunting me down like a powerful lion.
translation_verse: N ɛ wedɛɛɡa n baŋa pa kwaraa naa, he dɛ bɛɛ mɛ kɛŋɔ nyujente, dɛɛ aah mɛ dɛ́ do mɛ bol he nyokpowe-ɛɛla ne.

english_verse: You never stop accusing me; you become furious and attack over and over again.
translation_verse: Saŋ bɛlbwaa he kpɔ wefala dɛɛ dawɛ n nɛ, he bandia teŋɛ dɛɛ ɡwaa n nɛ, dɛ na vɔrɔwe wefala dɛ́ ba yoo mɛ.

english_verse: Why did you let me be born? I would rather have died before birth
translation_verse: N Naa Korowii, bɔkwa waa he ɡel ba lol mɛ nɔ? N dɛ nyin kɛ n fe aa sewa, nomɛlbwa bɛ men na.

english_verse: and been carried to the grave without ever breathing.
translation_verse: Dɛ ba ta men lolɛ, n fe den sewɛ tea bini bɔ kɛ baa lol mɛ nɔ.

english_verse: I have only a few days left. Why don't you leave me alone? Let me find some relief, *
translation_verse: N tɔpera aa kaa ta tama kae yaa? Gel mɛ n so dɛ́ lɛ n sie tama,

english_verse: of darkness and despair, the place of no return.
translation_verse: bela ɛ biro ɡbo dɛ do kɛŋɔ harambaŋa o ta mar dɔe, dɛ do saɡasaɡa.”

english_verse: Your words have silenced others and made them ashamed; now it is only right for you to be put to shame.
translation_verse: He dɛ lii kɛŋɔ yaa won chaŋe kɛɛ? He wepuu waa nɔ ɛɛ won tɔ yaa ŋwɛnɛ, ya bɛ won bol wa aa?

english_verse: You claim to be innocent and argue that your beliefs are acceptable to God.
translation_verse: He dɛ bol ŋɔ he waa ɛ kasinteŋ, he ŋɔ he waa toɡrɔ Korowii sie.

english_verse: But I wish God would speak
translation_verse: Gɛ n fe aa dɛ nyin kɛ Korowii fee chaŋe!

english_verse: and let you know that wisdom has many different sides. You would then discover that God has punished you less than you deserve.
translation_verse: Dɛ ɡel he jemɛ kɛ wejema fuuh, waane lole dɛ ɡwaa nɛwɛnyina liire ta. Korowii fe chɛ kɛ ó tɛr he deŋne ɡwaa ken.

english_verse: They are higher than the heavens and deeper than the grave. So what can you do when you know so little,
translation_verse: Korowii wejema la ɡwaa nyundua ne harɛ jaŋne. A bini luŋri ɡwaa lalabwɛ. Hɛɛ won jemɛ ɡɛ naa?

english_verse: and these mysteries outreach the earth and the ocean?
translation_verse: O wejema la kan ɡwaa ɡɛ harɛ nɔ paɡri aa doa, dɛ ɡwaa mpo ɡba.

english_verse: If God puts you in prison or drags you to court, what can you do?
translation_verse: O lawɛ ŋɔ ba bol he waa dɛ́ doe dea aa, umee dɛ́ won tɔɔ ŋwɛnɛ ɔ?

english_verse: God has the wisdom to know when someone is worthless and sinful,
translation_verse: Korowii jemɛ nyosonteŋna wa, o dɛ na ba wechɔɡa we-ɛɛla bwa kɛrɛdɛ.

english_verse: but it's easier to tame a wild donkey than to make a fool wise. Surrender Your Heart to God
translation_verse: Gɛne ne wejema dɔe la, dɛ ba wono dɛɛ kpɔɡ bini ol o berɛ dem kon.

english_verse: Surrender your heart to God, turn to him in prayer,
translation_verse: Job, kpɔ he bambile bwa tɛ Korowii, dɛɛ soŋo.

english_verse: and give up your sins— even those you do in secret.
translation_verse: Gel wechɔɡa ɛɛ, hale wechɔɡa haa ɛa dɛɛ sɔh bwa.

english_verse: Then you won't be ashamed; you will be confident and fearless.
translation_verse: Anee dɛ́ ɡel he ir nyu ne, dɛ́ dɔ hwɛɡa, he che kiŋkiŋ haa wola ɔmɛ.

english_verse: Your troubles will go away like water beneath a bridge,
translation_verse: Hɛɛ soh he wenaale la bwaa kwaraa, kɛŋɔ nee aa pala ba kaa, haa wola an na kpa la.

english_verse: You will rest safe and secure, filled with hope and emptied of worry.
translation_verse: Hɛɛ soo kɛrɛdɛ dɛkalkɛ he dɔ hwɛɡa, Korowii ɛɛ nyiŋi he nɛɛ dɛ́ ɡel he onɛ, ɔmee bɛlbwa aa wola toole.

english_verse: You will sleep without fear and be greatly respected.
translation_verse: Hɛɛ chɔɔ nomɛlbwa aa wola won aahre, nɛra ɡalɡa ba he be, hɛɛ cha ba.

english_verse: But those who are evil will go blind and lose their way. Their only escape is death!
translation_verse: Kɛ wechɔɡ-ɛɛra ɛɛ nao baa a munii no, baa bɔree dɔ dɛ́ chwa kaa. Ba hwɛɡa bwaa kɛŋɔ ba fee sewɛ.”

english_verse: Job said to his friends:
translation_verse: Asɛ Job chaŋe Sofar ŋɔ,

english_verse: But I know as much as you do, and so does everyone else.
translation_verse: Kɛ n dɔ liire kɛ heya, he ta men ɡwaalɛ. Umee lole waa wola ɡɛ waa nɔ jemɔɔ?

english_verse: I have always lived right, and God answered my prayers; now friends make fun of me.
translation_verse: N berɛ akwekwe nɛn n daamanar be, ba dɛ mam mɛ, kɛ n waa toɡrɔ, wechɔɡa bɛlbwa toole n nɛ, Korowii fa no n wesoŋa ka.

english_verse: It's easy to condemn those who are suffering, when you have no troubles.
translation_verse: Nɛn waa lɔ bosɔɔhna ta dɛ mamɛ nɛn waa aa lɔ o nɛ. He nyin waa dɛɛ tɛ nɛn waa dɛ na wa.

english_verse: Robbers and other godless people live safely at home and say, “God is in our hands!” If You Want To Learn
translation_verse: Kɛ ŋwɛɛra ne nɛra baa wola Korowii tomɛ soɡe deŋnesɔɔhna ta, kwaa baa dɛ tomɛ la taa ba kpeɡri do.

english_verse: If you want to learn, then go and ask the wild animals and the birds,
translation_verse: He dɛ nyin waa dɛ hweli aa, he bɔɔ ola ne jumbii á baɡle heyaa wa,

english_verse: Any of them can tell you what the Lord has done.
translation_verse: A ɡɛ kwaa nɔ bwa jemɛ waa Korowii aa ɛa.

english_verse: Every living creature is in the hands of God.
translation_verse: Korowii kontaala bwa nyu lɔ o nɔn ta, hale nɛwɛnyina bwa.

english_verse: We hear with our ears, taste with our tongues,
translation_verse: Gɛ kondikwa aa dɛ do nyondoŋe som, asɛ wobol ɡe ɛɛ do deŋne som la,

english_verse: and gain some wisdom from those who have lived a long time.
translation_verse: ɡɛɛ ya dɔ wejema dɛɛ le nɛra baa biɡra be.

english_verse: But God is the real source of wisdom and strength.
translation_verse: Korowii bee wejema ne kpeɡri, ne nɛra jae dɛ waa mun noe le.

english_verse: No one can rebuild what he destroys, or release those he has imprisoned.
translation_verse: Korowii taɡɛ kon ta aa, nomɛlbwa aa won berɛ kwaaro cheɡ. O do nɛn dea aa, nomɛlbwa aa won leo.

english_verse: just as he rules over liars and those they lie to.
translation_verse: Korowiirii dɔ kpeɡri ne wejema, nɛra baa dɛ neɡre nɛra ne banɔ la baa neɡ ba bwa lɔ o lɔɡa.

english_verse: and makes slaves of kings.
translation_verse: O dɛ lɛ koranar kpeɡri, dɛ́ ɛɛ ba kɛŋɔ yoma.

english_verse: God removes priests and others who have great power—
translation_verse: O dɛ lɛ sɔfore wejema, dɛɛ ba banɔ la baa di kpeɡri biɡri ne harɛ.

english_verse: puts mighty kings to shame, and takes away their power.
translation_verse: O ɡelɔ sihiih ɛɛ kpo nɛnjena, dɛɛ sɔɔh kpeɡnɛra nyoa.

english_verse: God strikes their rulers senseless, then leaves them to roam through barren deserts,
translation_verse: Korowii dɛ lɛ harɛre la nomonome liire, dɛ́ ɡel ba wili do hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta dɛɛ ɡaaɡe.

english_verse: lost in the dark, staggering like someone drunk.
translation_verse: Dɛ do biro ta dɛɛ laɡre, dɛɛ yɛɛɡe kɛŋɔ sennyɔdɛɛra ken.”

english_verse: I know and understand every bit of this.
translation_verse: Job berɔ ŋɔ, “N na ɡɛ waa nɔ bwa, n noɔ, dɛ jemɛ a mun.

english_verse: None of you are smarter than I am; there's nothing you know that I don't.
translation_verse: Waa haa jema la, n ɡe jema, he ta men ɡwaalɛ.

english_verse: you are merely useless doctors, who treat me with lies.
translation_verse: Hé kpɔ nyosone tɔ kasinteŋ ta, hé do kɛŋɔ tɛɛɡa te waa wola won chah weela!

english_verse: The wisest thing you can do is to keep quiet
translation_verse: Hé tɔ nyoa kwaraa naa, dɛ a fe ɛ wejemwa.

english_verse: and not telling the whole truth when you argue his case?
translation_verse: Hɛɛ won ɡel o baŋa pa aa? Hɛɛ won bol o waa tɛo kɔɔto aa?

english_verse: If he took you to court, could you fool him, just as you fool others?
translation_verse: Korowii nyiŋi he bini naa, wɛɛ na wedɛɛɡa anee yaa? Hɛɛ won neɡro ɡɛ haa dɛ neɡre nɛra la kɛɛ?

english_verse: If you were secretly unfair, he would correct you,
translation_verse: Dɛ he ɛ waa dɛ sɔh dɛɛ nyiŋi nɛra sie ta naa, Korowii ɛɛ pa heyaa bolchɔɡee.

english_verse: and his glorious splendor would make you terrified.
translation_verse: O kan waa doa la ɛɛ ɡeloo he jum jah. Aa ɡel ɔmee lawɛ heya aa?

english_verse: Your wisdom and arguments will blow away like dust. Be Quiet While I Speak
translation_verse: He sɛɡla ta mun dɔe, a do kɛŋɔ tɔɔ. Waa haa bola dɛ kpɔ dɛɛ lɛ he te do kɛŋɔ choh aa wola kpeɡe ken.

english_verse: Be quiet while I speak, and we'll see what happens.
translation_verse: Hé tɔ nyoa, dɛ́ tɛ mɛ ŋwɛnɛ ń bol wa, ásɛ waa aa ba n nɛɛ la ba.

english_verse: I will be responsible for what happens to me.
translation_verse: Dɛ wobɛlbwa kwaraa yaa, n sɛoh kɛŋɔ n kpɔ n nyu charɛ seo.

english_verse: God may kill me, but still I will trust him and offer my defense.
translation_verse: Hale dɛ Korowii kpo mɛ naa, n ta dɔ hwɛɡa o be dɛ́ chemo, dɛ́ baɡle kɛŋɔ n ta bolchɔɡe dii.

english_verse: This may be what saves me, because no guilty person would come to his court.
translation_verse: Anee dɛ́ ɡel n dɔ lɛɛ, dɛkalkɛ wechɔɡ-ɛɛ bɛlbwa aa won ba o sie.

english_verse: I have prepared my case well, and I am certain to win.
translation_verse: Maa dɔa lii n waa cheɡ nɔ, n jemɔ kɛ Korowii ɛɛ pa mɛ bolee.

english_verse: If you can prove me guilty, I will give up and die. Job Prays I Ask Only Two Things
translation_verse: Nomɛl lole n ne o won cheme n waa nɔ ta naa? Nɛn lole ɡɛ naa, n fe ɛɛ heloo dɛ́ sewɛ.

english_verse: I ask only two things of you, my God, and I will no longer hide from you—
translation_verse: N Naa Korowii, ɛ webele anɛ nɔ ɡbo tɛ mɛ, ásɛ n won ba he sie.

english_verse: Then speak, and I will reply; or else let me speak, and you reply.
translation_verse: Dɛ he yer mɛ naa mɛɛ chaŋee, kɛɛ n bol wa ásɛ he chaŋ mɛ.

english_verse: Please point out my sins, so I will know them.
translation_verse: Keraŋwɛnɛɛ n ɛ wechɔɡa dɛ koni waa ta nɔ? Gel ń jemɛ waa maa koni a ta.

english_verse: Why have you turned your back and count me your enemy?
translation_verse: Ɛrɛɛ he laa sie kpɔ n nɛ, dɛ kpɔ mɛ berɛ he dɔm nɔɔ?

english_verse: Why do you accuse me of horrible crimes and make me pay for sins I did in my youth?
translation_verse: He chwerɛ n bwara waa aa wola were, hale anɔ la maa ɛa n bonɔɔne saŋ.

english_verse: You have tied my feet down and keep me surrounded;
translation_verse: He do kpɛɛ n nakpale, dɛɛ nyiŋi n vala bini, dɛɛ dawɛ n nabuɡe.

english_verse: I am rotting away like cloth eaten by worms.
translation_verse: Gɛɛ a do, nɛn do kɛ daa waa pɔah, kɛŋɔ yal chao aa dɛ diu ken.”

english_verse: We are flowers that fade and shadows that vanish.
translation_verse: O dɛ kpeɡ warane kɛ kpɔɡa ken, dɛɛ hol warane, tamaa ken dɛ o nyoɡrɔ kɛŋɔ lileo ken.

english_verse: And so, I ask you, God, why pick on me?
translation_verse: N Naa Korowii, hɛɛ nyiŋ mɛɛ dɛ́ na kɛ n lɔ bonɔ, dɛ́ ba bol n waa kɛɛ?

english_verse: There's no way a human can be completely pure.
translation_verse: Nɛn waa kah doŋa la ɛɛ won lolɛ nɛn waa wola doŋa kaeh yaa? Nɛn toole!

english_verse: Our time on earth is brief; the number of our days is already decided by you.
translation_verse: He tɔ sie jemɛ ɡɛ nɛn aa so ka tel, dɛ jemɛ korobie aa lɔ o soɡa la ta. He maɡa ɡɛ bil aa wola charɛ.

english_verse: Why don't you leave us alone and let us find some happiness while we toil and labor? When a Tree Is Chopped Down
translation_verse: Laa sie kpɔ o nɛɛ dɛ́ ta o waa tɛo, dɛ́ ɡel o ɛ o toma ka tel kɛŋɔ waa tonɛ dɛ́ onɛ kɛŋɔ paate.

english_verse: When a tree is chopped down, there is always the hope that it will sprout again.
translation_verse: Hwɛɡa lole dɛ tɛ daa baa teŋo ta, wɛɛ berɔɔ pamɛ dɛ moɡɛ.

english_verse: but at the touch of water, it sprouts once again.
translation_verse: dɛ berɛ dɔ nee tama aa, o berɔ dɛɛ ir dɛ ta kpala kɛŋɔ daa baa chɔɔro ken.

english_verse: Humans are different— we die, and that's the end.
translation_verse: Kɛ dɛ nɛn te sewaa, dɛ a tonɔ, o sewaa, dɛ lee o dɔɔ jaɔ?

english_verse: We are like streams and lakes after the water has gone;
translation_verse: Gɛ neerare yon ɡel pala, ásɛ nenabɔɔne hweeh dɛ́ hol la,

english_verse: we fall into the sleep of death, never to rise again, until the sky disappears.
translation_verse: ɡɛɛ nɛn yon sewɛ, waa wola ir kpa. Nyundua ne harɛ taa lole nɔ, waa won ir kpa.

english_verse: Please hide me, God, deep in the ground— and when you are angry no more, remember to rescue me. Will We Humans Live Again?
translation_verse: N Naa Korowii, n dɛ nyin kɛŋɔ he laɡ mɛ sɔh lalabwɛ, dɛ́ ɡel n do bela ka tel saŋ he bandia nyoa aa sɔɔh, ásɛ he lii n waa tɔpetooro bɛl.

english_verse: Will we humans live again? I would gladly suffer and wait for my time.
translation_verse: Nɛn sewaa, wɛɛ won ir dɛ́ dɔ mkpa ja aa? N fe ɛɛ ɛ tomaa dɛ kpa ka tel kɛŋɔ n wenaale bwa aa ba a jaɡa.

english_verse: My Creator, you would want me; you would call out, and I would answer.
translation_verse: He fe ɛɛ yer mɛɛ, ásɛ n ɡe chaŋe, ásɛ he sie lɛ men haa ta mɛ la nɛ.

english_verse: You would take care of me, but not count my sins—
translation_verse: Kasinteŋ, he fe ɛɛ dɛɛ nyiŋi n vala binii, haa wola n wechɔɡaa nyiŋi.

english_verse: you would put them in a bag, tie it tight, and toss them away.
translation_verse: Hɛɛ kpɔɔ kɛ mɛ haa wola an lii kpa, dɛ́ fee wechɔɡa bɛlbwa maa ɛa.

english_verse: But in the real world, mountains tumble, and rocks crumble;
translation_verse: Gɛɛ, bwejena yon kuuɡi dɛ́ choɡli, ásɛ bwea huɡri le bela aa lole,

english_verse: streams wear away stones and wash away soil. And you destroy our hopes!
translation_verse: ásɛ nee palɛ dɛ́ kpɔ bwea ta dɛɛ kɛɡra, bwaalajen won teera taɡa dɛ́ kaa, ɡɛɛ he won ɡela nɛwɛnyini hwɛɡa ɛɛ ɛ pɛɛpɛɛ.

english_verse: You change the way we look, then send us away, wiped out forever.
translation_verse: He dɛ pɔ o nɛɛ o sewɛ dɛ́ kaa, dɛ́ ɡel o siebɔr beɡre ó kaa.

english_verse: We never live to know if our children are praised or disgraced.
translation_verse: O bibaala dɔ jirima kwaraa naa waa jemɛ, ba di sihiih ɡe aa, waa no.

english_verse: We feel no pain but our own, and when we mourn, it's only for ourselves.
translation_verse: O ɡbosoroo bwadabii wee, ne suna waa dɛ dii wɛɛ na.”

english_verse: Eliphaz from Teman said: *
translation_verse: Belaa Elifas, Teman te la chaŋe ŋɔ,

english_verse: Your words are enough to make others turn from God and lead them to doubt.
translation_verse: Haa Korowii ɔma kpɔe dɛɛ ɛ waane, anomanta, nomɛlbwa aa on soŋe.

english_verse: And your sinful, scheming mind is the source of all you say.
translation_verse: He nyoa wobol dɛ baɡle he da, neɡra lɔ he nyoa wobol ta.

english_verse: I am not here as your judge; your own words are witnesses against you.
translation_verse: He ɡbabir nyoa wobol pae bolchɔɡe, waa aa le he nyoa dɛɛ baɡle ɡɛ.

english_verse: Were you the first human? Are you older than the hills?
translation_verse: Henee nɛn baa tɔ sie lolɛ aa? He lole mɔɔ Korowii ta deŋɡarere aa?

english_verse: Have you ever been present when God's council meets? Do you alone have wisdom?
translation_verse: He no waa Korowii aa vɔrɔwa aa? He ɡboo nɛn haa dɔ wejemaa?

english_verse: We have the benefit of wisdom older than your father.
translation_verse: Banjeni ne nyumpompoŋa tena lɔ ya bini, banɔ la baa ɡwaa he mɛɛ kwara.

english_verse: And you have been offered comforting words from God. Isn't this enough?
translation_verse: Aa were kɛŋɔ Korowii ɡbabir dɛ larawe he bwara aa, he vɛh. Ya sɔɔh bwara dɛ che o naa ta bol waa he be.

english_verse: Your emotions are out of control, making you look fierce;
translation_verse: Ɛrɛɛ he bwaawee ir asɛ he sie beɡre ya nɛɛ,

english_verse: that's why you attack God with everything you say.
translation_verse: he baah di Korowii nɛɛ kohona dɛ ɡel ɡɛ wobochɔɡa nɔ ɛɛ le he nyoa nɔɔ?

english_verse: and neither are angels— not in the sight of God. If God doesn't trust his angels,
translation_verse: Kpelaa, Korowii ta hwɛɡa dɔe tɛ nyundua toroma, ba waa ta toɡrɛ o be,

english_verse: Just listen to what I know, and you will learn
translation_verse: Job, cheɡ deŋne, ń bol waa he be, waa maa naa la, mɛɛ baɡle a binii.

english_verse: Those who gained such insights also gained the land, and they were not influenced by foreign teachings.
translation_verse: Ba naawa ɡboo fa dɔ harɛ la, dɛ nɛŋhɔɔhra toole dɛ ɡel ba laa ba te kpɔ Korowii nɛ.

english_verse: But suffering is in store each day for those who sin.
translation_verse: Nyubinikpeɡ tena baa dɛ fiiɡi ba bala, bwara ɛɛ nyɛɡ baa ba soɡa bini bwaa.

english_verse: Even in times of success, they constantly hear the threat of doom.
translation_verse: Ɔmewa ɛɛ chole ba deŋna taa, ɡɛ saŋ baa ŋɔ ba soɡe deŋnesɔɔhna ta, ŋwɛɛra den lɔ ba tɔ ba nɛ.

english_verse: They scrounge around for food, all the while dreading the approaching darkness.
translation_verse: ásɛ kɔkɔsakire di ba ola. Ba jemɔ kɛ ba seo tɔpere dɛ́ tel.

english_verse: They are overcome with despair, like frightened soldiers facing a fearsome king in battle.
translation_verse: Wekpeɡa ne wenaale ɡelɔ baa ɔmɛ kohona a dawɛ ba nɛɛ kɛŋɔ kooro waa dɛ la ka yoo ba laa,

english_verse: and have attacked him with their weapons.
translation_verse: Ba deŋne kpeɡri dɛ kpɔ kwaa tɔ ba te ɡbemɡbe dɛ ka yo Korowii.

english_verse: They may be rich and fat,
translation_verse: Sodɛɛɡa ɡelɔ ba je faɡra, ba teene do bare.

english_verse: Their property and wealth will shrink and disappear.
translation_verse: Baa nyao, ba kondɔɔh bwa le ba nɔɔra ta, nɛra aa ba kondɔɔh bɛlbwaa na kpa.

english_verse: They won't escape the darkness, and the blazing breath of God will set their future aflame. *
translation_verse: Sewaa chɛ kɛ bá sewɛ. Baa ɛo kɛŋɔ daa nii aa fuh o kpala, peu ta kpɔ o fee kaa ken.

english_verse: They have put their trust in something worthless; now they will become worthless
translation_verse: Ba bɛ ba te neɡre dɛ́ kpɔ ba te dɛɛ dawɛ konsale ta, baa komɛlbwaa dɔ le a ta.

english_verse: like a date palm tree without a leaf.
translation_verse: Ba tɔpere aa tel dɛ ba holɔ, kɛŋɔ daa kpale, baa wola won moɡɛ kpa.

english_verse: Or like vineyards or orchards whose blossoms and unripe fruit drop to the ground.
translation_verse: Baa ɛo kɛŋɔ ɡrepo daa o nɔna aa wola beɛ dɛ lee, kɛɛ ɔleve daa o fee bwa aa leera.

english_verse: Yes, the godless and the greedy will have nothing but flames feasting on their homes,
translation_verse: Nɛra baa wola Korowii tomɛ la aa biirii dɔ, ásɛ nii fuh nɛra baa dɛ nyin kɛ baa yaɡ ba sen la deremi.

english_verse: because they are the parents of trouble and vicious lies.
translation_verse: Gɛ nɛra nɔɔ dɛɛ vɔrɔwe wechɔɡa, neɡra ɡe ɡboo ba bwa saŋ bɛlbwa.”

english_verse: I have often heard this, and it offers no comfort.
translation_verse: “N no waa nɔ dɔŋa bwa ka, he berɔ dɛɛ chwee n ŋwɛr kwara.

english_verse: If I were in your place, it would be easy to criticize or to give advice.
translation_verse: Dɛ he fe do ɡɛ maa doa nɔ, n ɡe do ɡɛ haa doa nɔ naa, n fe ɛɛ bol waa ɡwaa heya he kwaa la berɛ dɔ wesoma.

english_verse: But I would offer hope and comfort instead.
translation_verse: Kɛ n nyoa wobol ɛɛ won tɛ heyaa bokpeɡa, dɛ́ tɛ heyaa bosɔɔhna.

english_verse: If I speak, or if I don't, I hurt all the same. My torment continues.
translation_verse: Wobɛlbwa toole ń bol a cha mɛ, n tɔ nyoa ɡe aa, n weweele nyoa aa sɔɔh.

english_verse: God has worn me down and destroyed my family;
translation_verse: N Naa Korowii, he ɡelɔ n bokpeɡa tonɛ, dɛ kpoo n dem tena bwa.

english_verse: God is my hateful enemy, glaring at me and attacking with his sharp teeth.
translation_verse: He toɡri n bini bandia ne kɛ kpɔɡ bini ol ken. He hah mɛ dɛ fome siwi pa n nɛ.

english_verse: Everyone is against me; they sneer and slap my face.
translation_verse: Nɛra dɛ muɡli n baah ba dɛ warɛ dɛ bar mɛ cheme, dɛɛ kpaa n lwɛrɛme.

english_verse: And God is the one who handed me over to this merciless mob. Everything Was Going Well
translation_verse: Korowii kpɔ mɛ do wechɔɡ-ɛɛra nɔn ta, o taɡ mɛ ta ba bini.

english_verse: Everything was going well, until God grabbed my neck and shook me to pieces. God set me up as the target
translation_verse: N fa soɡe deŋnesɔɔhna ta, Korowii den ba hamɛ n baŋa dɛ taɡ mɛ ta harɛ. O kpɔ mɛ dɛɛ hweli hɛm tae.

english_verse: for his arrows, and without showing mercy, he slashed my stomach open, spilling out my insides.
translation_verse: O ta hɛma le bobɛlbwa dɛɛ yaɡ mɛ, hɛma la yaɡ mɛ dɛɛ vah. O ɡel n teabini kwaa bwa chɔ baŋ, hale o ta n nɛɛ sune tamaa bɛlbwa.

english_verse: and so, in my sorrow I dress in sackcloth and sit in the dust.
