translation_verse: Babelɔn kooro kpoo Kooro Sedekia bibaala o siwi ta Ribla bela, dɛ kpoo Juda nomonjena ɡe bwa,

english_verse: Then his eyes were poked out, and he was put in chains, so he could be dragged off to Babylonia.
translation_verse: dɛ foromi Kooro Sedekia sibie dɛ doo ayaawa jɔɡrɔre, dɛ kpɔɔ kaa Babelɔn harɛ ta.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the Babylonian army had burned the houses in Jerusalem, including the royal palace, and they had broken down the city walls.
translation_verse: Babelɔn tena la fuh koodem la ne nɛra la deene, dɛ kuuɡi Jerusalam danjwɛɛre bwa ɡe.

english_verse: Nebuzaradan, the Babylonian officer in charge of the guards, led away everyone from the city as prisoners, even those who had deserted to Nebuchadnezzar.
translation_verse: Nebusaradan waa chɔ kooro laa tena baa dɛ daahno nyoa, lawɛ nɛra baa kaa dɛ do Jerusalam, dɛ banɔ la baa baa ja o nɛɛ la bwa kaa Babelɔn harɛ ta.

english_verse: Only the poorest people who owned no land were left behind in Judah, and Nebuzaradan gave them fields and vineyards.
translation_verse: Kɛ o ɡel nɛra baa nyaa dɛ do Juda harɛ ta bini bane baa wola komɛlbwa dɔe kwaraa la, asɛ dɛ kpɔ daa kooni ne kooni tɛɛ ba.

english_verse: sent some of their troops to bring me from the courtyard of the royal palace guards. They put me in the care of Gedaliah son of Ahikam and told him to take me to my home. And so I was allowed to stay with the people who remained in Judah. The Lord Promises To Protect Ebedmelech
translation_verse: tomɛ nɛra ŋɔ bá ka kpɔ mɛ le koodem dembaah bela ba. Ba kpɔ mɛ do Ahikam bibaa Gedalia, o ɡe mɛɛ aa ɛ Safan la nɔn ta, ŋɔ ó nyiŋi n nɛɛ kɛrɛdɛ dɛ́ tel n ne n bwɛ. Gɛɛ a do n berɛ ka so n nɛra bini.

english_verse: While I was a prisoner in the courtyard of the palace guard, the Lord told me to say
translation_verse: Gɛ saŋ baa laɡ mɛ do dea dembaah bela baa dɛ daah la, Korowii bol waa men Jeremia be ŋɔ,

english_verse: But because you trusted me, I will protect you from the officials of Judah, and when Judah is struck by disaster, I will rescue you and keep you alive. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Mɛɛ kpɔ nɔnee tɔ he nɛ, baa wola won kpoe. Hɛɛ chwao dɛ lɛ he nyu, dɛkalkɛ he kpɔ he te dawɛ n nɛ. Men Korowiirii bola.’ ”

english_verse: I was led away in chains along with the people of Judah and Jerusalem who were being taken to Babylonia. Nebuzaradan was the officer in charge of the guard, and while we were stopped at Ramah, the Lord caused him to set me free.
translation_verse: Korowii bol waa men Jeremia be, ɡɛ saŋ Nebusaradan waa chɔ kooro laa tena baa dɛ daahno nyoa, aa lee mɛ dea baa do mɛ Rama la. Dɛ ba laɡ mɛ dɛ do mɛ jɔɡrɔre, dɛ kpɔ n ne Jerusalam dɛ Juda tena baa lawɛ yaa laa ta la kaa Babelɔn harɛ ta.

english_verse: Nebuzaradan said: Jeremiah, the Lord your God warned your people that he would bring disaster on this land.
translation_verse: Nebusaradan laɡ mɛ le bokɛre dɛ ŋɔ n be ŋɔ, “Korowii haa dɛ tomɔ la bolɔ ŋɔ wekpeɡa ɛɛ ba he harɛ nɔ taa,

english_verse: But they continued to rebel against him, and now he has punished them just as he threatened.
translation_verse: asɛ taraken dɛ ɛ ɡɛ waa bola la. A ɡɛ waa nɔ bwa balɔ, dɛkalkɛ he ɛ nɛra wechɔɡa dɛ jo Korowii nɛ, dɛ vɛh o waa ta teŋa.

english_verse: Today I am taking the chains off your wrists and setting you free! If you want to, you can come with me to Babylonia, and I will see that you are taken care of. Or if you decide to stay here, you can go wherever you wish.
translation_verse: Kɛ fini, n laa jɔɡrɔre la dɛɛ foo he nɔɔra. Hɛɛ won teŋɛ n nɛɛ kaa Babelɔn ásɛ n nyiŋi he nɛ, dɛ haa nyin ɡe aa, he ɡel. Harɛɛ chɔa kaa la, hɛɛ won kaa bobɛlbwa haa dɛ nyin ka so.”

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar has chosen Gedaliah to rule Judah. You can live near Gedaliah, and he will provide for you, or you can live anywhere else you choose. Nebuzaradan gave me a supply of food, then let me leave.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ men Jeremia aa berɛ n te ŋɔ ń kaa la, Nebusaradan berɛ ŋɔ, “Berɛ kaa Ahikam bibaa Gedalia o nabaa aa ɛ Safan be. Babelɔn kooro leo dɛ kpɔ Juda bwɛɛre do o nɔn ta wɛɛ nyiŋi a ta, ásɛ he ne ó ka so nɛra la bini, kɛɛ dɛ bobɛlbwa ɡee hɛɛ nyin aa, hɛɛ won ka so.” Asɛ Nebusaradan kpɔ kondikwaa ne koŋkɛɛla ane tɛ mɛ n kpɔ kaa.

english_verse: I decided to stay with the people of Judah, and I went to live near Gedaliah in Mizpah. The Harvest Is Brought In
translation_verse: Anomanta, n la Ahikam bibaa Gedalia be Mispa n ne nɛra baa ka harɛ la ta la ka so. Gedalia kpoe wa

english_verse: Gedaliah told them, “There's no need to be afraid of the Babylonians. Everything will be fine, if we live peacefully and obey King Nebuchadnezzar.
translation_verse: Belaa Gedalia ŋwɛɛ ntam baɡ ba ŋɔ, “Hɛɛ berɛ Babelɔn tena nɔ ɔma, hé so bonɔ dɛɛ tomɛ Babelɔn kooro, aa chiɡ heyaa kɛrɛdɛɛ.

english_verse: I will stay here at Mizpah and meet with the Babylonian officials on each of their visits. But you must go back to your towns and bring in the harvest, then store the wine, olive oil, and dried fruit.”
translation_verse: N ɡbabir dɛ ba Mispa soɡa dɛ́ che he naa ta, Babelɔn tena baa dɛɛ ba ya be la sie. Kɛ a chɛ kɛ he boa sen ne daa nɔna ne ɔleve noo nyoa cheɡ, dɛ́ ka so bwɛɛre haa dɛ ba ba so a ta la ta.”

english_verse: One day, Johanan got together with some of the other men who had been army officers, and they came to Mizpah and met with Gedaliah.
translation_verse: Karea bibaa Johanan ne laa nomonome baa peɡra ka do kpɔɡ bini la bwa ba Gedalia be Mispa,

english_verse: They said, “Gedaliah, we came to warn you that King Baalis of Ammon hired Ishmael to murder you!” Gedaliah refused to believe them,
translation_verse: dɛ ba ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Haa jemɛ kɛŋɔ Amɔn Kooro Baalis tomɛ Nɛtanea bibaa Ismael ŋɔ ó ba kpoe naa?” Kɛ Gedalia ta waa la yaradae.

english_verse: so Johanan went to Gedaliah privately and said, “Let me kill Ishmael. No one will find out who did it. There are only a few people left in Judah, but they are depending on you. And if you are murdered, they will be scattered or killed.”
translation_verse: Belaa Karea bibaa Johanan sɔh ka ŋɔ Gedalia be Mispa ŋɔ, “Tɛ mɛ ŋwɛnɛ n sɔh ka kpo Nɛtanea bibaa Ismael, nomɛlbwa aa wola na. Ɛrɛɛ chɛ kɛ o kpoe asɛ Juu tena baa ja he nɛɛ bonɔ nɔ lɔ peɡre dɛ kpɔ sibeɡra ba ta nɛra baa kaa dɛ ta so bela nɛɛ nɔɔ?”

english_verse: Gedaliah answered, “Don't kill Ishmael! What you've said about him can't be true.”
translation_verse: Anee Gedalia chaŋe Johanan ŋɔ, “Bɛ ɡɛ waa nɔ ɛ! Ismael waa haa bola nɔ ta kasinteŋ ɛɛ!”

english_verse: But in the seventh month, Ishmael came to Mizpah with ten of his soldiers. He had been one of the king's officials and was a member of the royal family. Ishmael and his men were invited to eat with Gedaliah.
translation_verse: Korobie anuanɛ ta la, Nɛtanea bibaa Ismael, waa ɛ koobie, dɛ berɛ ɛ kooro nomonome la bini bɛl la, o iro dɛ lawɛ baala fi ja o nɛɛ ba la Ahikam bibaa Gedalia be Mispa. Ismael nabaa sɔne Elisama. Kondikwaa dii saŋ aa tela, ba bwa pɛ so dɛɛ di kwaa la,

english_verse: During the meal, Ishmael and his soldiers killed Gedaliah, the man chosen as ruler of Judah by the king of Babylonia.
translation_verse: belaa Ismael ne baala fi baa jaa la ir kpɔ keri dɛ kpo Gedalia, dɛ onee Babelɔn kooro le ŋɔ wɛɛ nyiŋi harɛ la ta.

english_verse: Then they killed the Jews who were with Gedaliah, and they also killed the Babylonian soldiers who were there.
translation_verse: Ismael berɔ kpoo Juu tena baa ja Gedalia nɛɛ Mispa, dɛ Babelɔn laa tena baa lɔ bela bwa.

english_verse: The next day, the murders had still not been discovered,
translation_verse: Tɔ aa pera, mɔɔ bɛlbwa jemɛ Gedalia kpoe waa la,

english_verse: Ishmael went out the town gate to meet them. He pretended to be weeping, and he asked them to come into Mizpah to meet with Gedaliah, the ruler of Judah.
translation_verse: Anomanta, Ismael leɔ dɛ kpɔ wii ka chem ba, asɛ dɛ ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, “N poo heya, hé ba dɛ́ ba na Gedalia.”

english_verse: But after they were inside the town, Ishmael ordered his soldiers to kill them and throw their bodies into a well.
translation_verse: Baa dena jo bwɛjen la bini la, Ismael ne baala baa ja o nɛɛ la kpoo ba bini fifraanuanɛ, dɛ paa ba ta kɔlɔŋ bɛl bini.

english_verse: He let ten of the men live, because they offered to give him supplies of wheat, barley, olive oil, and honey they had hidden in a field.
translation_verse: Ba bini fi soŋe Ismael ŋɔ, “Bɛ yaa kpoo! Ya dɔ mea ne ɔleve no dɛ tooh a sɔh kpɔɡ bini.” Anomanta, o ɡel ba.

english_verse: The well that he filled with bodies had been dug by King Asa of Judah to store rainwater, because he was afraid that King Baasha of Israel might surround Mizpah and keep the people from getting to their water supply.
translation_verse: Kɔlɔŋ la Ismael aa pa Gedalia ne nɛra waa kpoo ba ka ta o bini la, o ɛ Kooro Asa kɔlɔŋ waa kwiu ɡɛ saŋ Israel Kooro Baasa aa baa yoo laa. Nɛra waa kpoo ba la su kɔlɔŋ la.

english_verse: Nebuzaradan, King Nebuchadnezzar's officer in charge of the guard, had left King Zedekiah's daughters and many other people at Mizpah, and he had put Gedaliah in charge of them. But now Ishmael took them all prisoner and led them toward Ammon, on the other side of the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Ismael lawɛ nɛra baa ka Mispa la bwa, kooro bihaahna ne banɔ la baa jaa dɛ ka bela. Dɛ Nebusaradan waa chɔ kooro laa tena baa dɛ daahno nyoa, le Ahikam bibaa Gedalia o chɔ ba nyoa. Waa laɡ ba la, o ɡale Jɔɔdan Moo dɛ kpɔ sie chaɡɛ Amɔn tena harɛ pera dɛɛ kaa bane.

english_verse: Johanan and the other army officers heard what Ishmael had done.
translation_verse: Karea bibaa Johanan ne laa nomonome la bwa baa ja o nɛɛ la no hiribiwaa Nɛtanea bibaa Ismael aa ɛa la.

english_verse: So they and their troops chased Ishmael and caught up with him at the large pit at Gibeon.
translation_verse: Anomanta, ba kpɔ ba laa tena bwa dɛ́ ka yo Ismael. Ba tiu dɛ ka lawɔ tamjen bɛl waa chɔ Gebeɔn jwɛh.

english_verse: When Ishmael's prisoners saw Johanan and the officers, they were happy
translation_verse: Nɛra Ismael aa laɡ ba dɛɛ kaa aa na Johanan ne o laa tena baa ba la, ba sie lɛo.

english_verse: and turned around and ran toward Johanan.
translation_verse: Ate, ba bwa berɛ chwa le o be, dɛ kaa Karea bibaa Johanan be.

english_verse: But Ishmael and eight of his men escaped and went to Ammon. Johanan Decides To Take the People to Egypt
translation_verse: Kɛ Ismael ne o baala la bini banuatoro chwao le Johanan be, dɛ kaa Amɔn tena be.

english_verse: Johanan and the officers had rescued the women, children, and royal officials that Ishmael had taken prisoner after killing Gedaliah. Johanan led the people from Gibeon
translation_verse: Ismael aa kpo Gedalia habɔɔ la, Johanan ne laa nomonome la bwa baa ja o nɛɛ la tɔ nɛra baa ka Mispa Ismael fe laɡ ba dɛɛ kaa la sie. Haahna ne laa tena, bechale dɛ koodem nomonome baa le Gebeɔn bwa.

english_verse: toward Egypt. They wanted to go there, because they were afraid of what the Babylonians would do when they found out that Ishmael had killed Gedaliah, the ruler appointed by King Nebuchadnezzar. The People Ask Jeremiah To Pray for Them On the way to Egypt, we stopped at the town of Geruth Chimham near Bethlehem.
translation_verse: ɡɛ aa ɛ ásɛ ba won le Babelɔn tena nɔn ta. Dɛ ba dɛ ɔm ba, dɛkalkɛ Ismael kpo Gedalia la Babelɔn kooro aa leo wɛɛ nyiŋi harɛ la ta.

english_verse: Johanan, Jezaniah, the other army officers, and everyone else in the group, came to me
translation_verse: Belaa laa nomonome la bwa, ne Karea bibaa Johanan ne Hosaya bibaa Jesania, dɛ nɛra baa kaa bwa, dɛ́ le bechale nɛɛ ba nomonjena bwa nɛ

english_verse: and said, “Please, Jeremiah, pray to the Lord your God for us. Judah used to have many people, but as you can see, only a few of us are left.
translation_verse: ba men Korowii keame Jeremia be dɛ ba ŋɔ, “Ya dɛ soŋe, no ya wesoŋa nɔ, dɛ́ soŋe Korowii yaa dɛ tomɔ nɔ tɛ ya nɛra yaa ka harɛ nɔ bwa ta nɔ. He ɡbabir nao kɛŋɔ dɛ ya fa warɔ, kɛ taraken te, ya nɛra tamaa kenii kaa.

english_verse: Ask the Lord to tell us where he wants us to go and what he wants us to do.”
translation_verse: Soŋe Korowii yaa dɛ tomɔ la, ó baɡle yaa bela yaa kaa ne ɡɛ yaa ɛ.”

english_verse: “All right,” I answered, “I will pray to the Lord your God, and I will tell you everything he says.”
translation_verse: Anee n chaŋe ŋɔ, “N noɔ, mɛɛ soŋe Korowii yaa dɛ tomɔ ɡɛ haa dɛ soŋe laanee, ásɛ wobɛlbwa waa bol n be la, ń bol he be. Maa wobɛlbwaa kpɔ sɔh heya.”

english_verse: even if it isn't what we want to do. We will obey the Lord so that all will go well for us.”
translation_verse: Dɛ a wer kɛɛ aa were kwaraa naa, yaa teŋɛ Korowii yaa dɛ tomɔ waa taa, o bee ya tomɛ la. Ya dɛ teŋɛ o waa bwa ta naa, ya wobɛlbwa ken ɛɛ won do wer tɛ yaa.” Korowii no Jeremia wesoŋa

english_verse: Ten days later, the Lord gave me an answer for
translation_verse: Tɔpera fi habɔɔ la, Korowii bol waa men Jeremia be ja.

english_verse: Johanan, the officers, and the other people. So I called them together
translation_verse: Anomanta, n yerɛ Karea bibaa Johanan, ne laa nomonome bwa baa ja o nɛɛ la, dɛ nɛra baa jaa bwa,

english_verse: and told them that the Lord God of Israel had said: You asked Jeremiah to pray and find out what you should do.
translation_verse: dɛ ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, “Waa Korowii Israel tena aa dɛ tomɔ, asɛ he tom mɛ ŋɔ ń ka soŋe he waa o be tɛ heya la ŋɔ,

english_verse: I am sorry that I had to punish you, and so I now tell you to stay here in Judah, where I will plant you and build you up, instead of tearing you down and uprooting you.
translation_verse: ‘Dɛ hɛɛ so harɛ nɔ taa yaa, mɛɛ lawɛ heyaa ir maa wola ɡel he chole, dɛ́ kwaa du heya kɛŋɔ da, ásɛ he che kiŋkiŋ maa wola heyaa fuɡri kɛŋɔ dua, dɛkalkɛ wenaale maa kpɔa ba ta he nɛɛ la, ɡelɔ mɛɛ di suna kohona.

english_verse: and I will even force him to have mercy on you and give back your farms.
translation_verse: Mɛɛ dɔ tedomaa tɛ heya, ásɛ dɛ ɡel Babelɔn kooro ɡe dɔ tedoma he nɛ, dɛ́ berɛ ba he ne he harɛ ta ja. Men Korowiirii bola.’

english_verse: But you might keep on saying, “We won't stay here in Judah, and we won't obey the Lord our God.
translation_verse: Kɛ dɛ he ŋɔ, ‘Yaa harɛ nɔ taa so,’ dɛ vɛh waa Korowii haa dɛ tomɔ nɔ nɛɛ teŋa,

english_verse: We are going to Egypt, where there is plenty of food and no danger of war.”
translation_verse: kɛɛ dɛ ŋɔ, ‘Akai, yaa kaalo ka so Ijipt harɛ ta, bela yaa wola laa ne bɛle sii kɛɛ lɔree na naa,’

english_verse: People of Judah, you survived when the Babylonian army attacked. Now you are planning to move to Egypt, and if you do go, this is what will happen.
translation_verse: amɔ hé no waa Koranar Bwa Kooro, Israel tena aa dɛ tomɔ la aa dɛ bol he Juda tena haa kaa la be. ‘Dɛ he siwi beɡre Ijipt harɛ ta kaala dɛ́ ka so bela aa,

english_verse: You are afraid of war, starvation, and disease here in Judah, but they will follow you to Egypt and kill you there. None of you will survive the disasters I will send.
translation_verse: Kasinteŋ, banɔ la bwa ba siwi aa beɡra kɛ bá kaa Ijipt harɛ ta la, laa ne lɔr dɛ weechɔɡaa dɛ́ kpoo ba. Beŋkpoŋ ɡba aa won chwa le wekpeɡa maa kpɔa dɛɛ ba ba nɛɛ la ta.’

english_verse: I, the Lord, was angry with the people of Jerusalem and punished them. And if you go to Egypt, I will be angry and punish you the same way. You will never again see your homeland. People will be horrified at what I do to you, and they will use the name of your city as a curse word. Jeremiah Gives a Warning
translation_verse: Koranar Bwa Kooro, Israel tena aa dɛ tomɔ la ŋɔ, ‘Gɛ maa kpɔ n bandia kohona ba ta nɛra baa lɔ Jerusalam nɛɛ la, ɡɛɛ dɛ he kaa Ijipt harɛ ta naa, mɛɛ ba n bandia kpɔe ba ta he nɛ. Nɛra ɛɛ nao dɛɛ taah heya ba bambile teŋe, dɛɛ mamɛ heya. He siwi aa harɛ nɔ nae ba kpa.’ ”

english_verse: I told the people: You escaped the disaster that struck Judah, but now the Lord warns you to stay away from Egypt.
translation_verse: N berɔ bol ba be ja ŋɔ, “Korowii ŋɔ he Juda tena haa kaa la be ŋɔ he bɛ Ijipt harɛ ta kaa. Anomanta, n dɛ kah heyaa fini ŋɔ,

english_verse: You asked me to pray and find out what the Lord our God wants you to do, and you promised to obey him. But that was a terrible mistake,
translation_verse: he kono kohona, a chɛ kɛ hé sewɛ. He ŋɔ n be ŋɔ ń soŋe Korowii yaa dɛ tomɔ ó nyiŋi he nɛ, dɛ baɡɛ nyoa ŋɔ hɛɛ teŋɛ waa waa do heyaa bwa taa.

english_verse: because now that I have given you the Lord's answer, you refuse to obey him.
translation_verse: Taraken, n bol he be, kɛ he vɛh waa Korowii aa tom mɛ n ba bol he be la bwa.

english_verse: And so, you will die in Egypt from war, hunger, and disease.
translation_verse: Anomanta, hé lii waa nɔ. Laa ne lɔr, dɛ weechɔɡaa dɛ́ kpoo heya, harɛ haa dɛ nyin he ka so o ta la ta.”

english_verse: But Azariah, Johanan and some other arrogant men said to me, “You're lying! The Lord didn't tell you to say that we shouldn't go to Egypt.
translation_verse: Belaa Hosaya bibaa Asaria ne Karea bibaa Johanan, dɛ deŋnekpeɡ baala bane ba ŋɔ n be ŋɔ, “He dɛ teŋe nyosone! Korowii yaa dɛ tomɔ ta hen tomɛ ŋɔ yá ɡel Ijipt laŋa.

english_verse: Baruch son of Neriah must have told you to say that. He wants the Babylonians to capture us, so they can take us away to Babylonia or even kill us.”
translation_verse: Nɛrea bibaa Baruk doe ŋɔ hé kpɔ yaa do Babelɔn tena nɔn ta, ásɛ ba kpoo yaa kɛɛ dɛ́ lawɛ yaa kaa bojaŋ harɛfale ta Babelɔn.”

english_verse: Johanan, the other army officers, and everyone else refused to stay in Judah in spite of the Lord's command.
translation_verse: Anomanta, Johanan kɛɛ laa nomonome la bɛlbwa, dɛ nɛra la bɛlbwa ta waa Korowii aa do ba ta teŋɛ, dɛ ta so Juda harɛ ta bela.

english_verse: So Johanan and the officers led us away toward Egypt. The group that left Judah included those who had been scattered in other countries and who had then come back to live in Judah.
translation_verse: Belaa Johanan ne laa nomonome la kpɔ nomɛlbwa waa kaa dɛ do Juda harɛ ta la kaa Ijipt harɛ ta, ba ne nɛra baa peɡra dɛ ka so harɛfala ta dɛ berɛ ba so Juda harɛ ta la bwa.

english_verse: Baruch and I and others in the group had been staying with Gedaliah, because Nebuzaradan, the Babylonian officer in charge of the guard, had ordered him to take care of the king's daughters and quite a few men, women, and children.
translation_verse: Ba berɔ tɔ baala ne haahna ne bechale, dɛ kooro bihaahna Nebusaradan waa chɔ laa tena baa dɛ daah kooro nyoa sie kaa. Nebusaradanee kpɔ ba do Ahikam bibaa Gedalia, ne men Jeremia maa ɛ Korowii keame, dɛ Nɛrea bibaa Baruk nɔn ta dɛ tɔ ba sie ba kaa.

english_verse: The people disobeyed the Lord and went to Egypt. The group had settled in Tahpanhes,
translation_verse: Anomanta, ba kpɔ deŋnekpeɡ vɛh Korowii waa la, dɛ ka jo Ijipt harɛ, dɛ kpoŋe kaa bwɛjen Tapanes ta.

english_verse: Jeremiah, carry some large stones to the entrance of the government building in Tahpanhes. Bury the stones underneath the brick pavement and be sure the Jews are watching.
translation_verse: “Kpɔ bwekuŋe ane Juu tena la siwi ta, dɛ́ huɡa choh ta bela baa kpɔ berekese ma ŋwɛnɛ ó kaa nyundua, dɛ́ kaa Ijipt kooro koodem waa lɔ Tapanes la doonyoa.

english_verse: Then tell them that I, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, have sent for my servant, Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia. I will bring him here and have him set up his throne and his royal tent over these stones that I told you to bury.
translation_verse: Ásɛ dɛ berɛ ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ men Koranar Bwa Kooro, Israel tena aa dɛ tom mɛ ŋɔ, ‘Mɛɛ kpɔ n bonɔɔ Kooro Nebukadnesa waa ɛ Babelɔn kooroo ba bonɔ, dɛ́ ɡel ó kpɔ o kookara ba cheɡ bwekuŋe haa huɡa nɔ ta. Wɛɛ baŋre o tɛnte deaa ó do kɛŋɔ koodem.

english_verse: He will attack Egypt and kill many of its people; others will die of disease or be dragged away as prisoners.
translation_verse: Wɛɛ ba yo Ijipt tenaa dɛ́ pɔ ba nɛ, ásɛ banɔ la weechɔɡa aa kpoo ba la serewe, banɔ la baa laɡ ba la, bá laɡ ba kaa, ásɛ banɔ la ɡe baa kpoo ba laa ta la, bá kpoo ba.

english_verse: The Lord told me to speak with the Jews who were living in the towns of Migdol, Tahpanhes, and Memphis in northern Egypt, and also to those living in southern Egypt. He told me to tell them:
translation_verse: Korowii bol Israel tena baa lɔ Ijipt bwɛjena Miɡdol ne Tapanes ne Mɛmfes, dɛ banɔ la baa lɔ harɛ la weekaŋle harɛbɔr waa men Jeremia be.

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. You saw how I destroyed Jerusalem and the towns of Judah. They lie empty and in ruins today,
translation_verse: Koranar Bwa Kooro, Israel tena aa dɛ tomɔ la ŋɔ, “He ɡbabir na chɔɡa maa chɔɡ Jerusalam ne Juda bwɛjena la bwa. Hale a bwa berɛ dimɡbia, nomɛlbwa aa wola a ta soɡe,

english_verse: because the people of Judah made me angry by worshiping gods that had never helped them or their ancestors.
translation_verse: dɛkalkɛ nɛra baa lɔ a ta ɛɛ mɛ wechɔɡa dɛ ɡel n baah di. Ba ɛ sarahare tɛ voɡare ane dɛɛ toma, voɡare ba ɡbabir kɛɛ hen kɛɛ he naawa aa wola an tomɛ.

english_verse: Time after time I sent my servants the prophets to tell the people of Judah how much I hated their disgusting sins. The prophets warned them to stop sinning,
translation_verse: Keraŋwɛnɛ bwaa n tomɛ n bonɔɔna baa ɛ n keamere he be, ba bol he be ŋɔ he bɛ wedoŋa aa do ken maa kia nɔ ɛ.

english_verse: Finally, my anger struck like a raging flood, and today Jerusalem and the towns of Judah are nothing but empty ruins.
translation_verse: Anomanta, n kpɔ n bandia ba ta Juda bwɛɛre nɛ, ne Jerusalam fɔɡbaahna, dɛ kpaa nii do a ta. A bwa kuuɡo dɛ berɛ dimɡbeeni dɛ do ɔma, nomɛlbwa aa wola nyin kɛ o nyiŋi, dɛ ba le fini.

english_verse: You have made me angry by worshiping idols and burning incense to other gods after you came here to Egypt. You will die such a disgusting death, that other nations will use the name of Judah as a curse word.
translation_verse: Ɛrɛɛ hɛɛ do mɛ bandia, dɛɛ tomɛ voɡare dɛ ɛ sarahare dɛɛ tɛ voɡare aa lɔ Ijipt harɛ ta bonɔ haa baa so nɔɔ? He dɛ ɛ ɡɛ dɛ́ chɔɡ he te, ásɛ harɛre nɛra bwa ɛɛ nyiŋi he nyubaah, dɛ́ɛ taah heya kɛɛ?

english_verse: When you were living in Jerusalem and Judah, you followed the example of your ancestors in doing evil things, just like your kings and queens.
translation_verse: He deno soh nyubinikpeɡ wa he naawa aa ɛa Juda bwɛɛre ne Jerusalam fɔɡbaahna, ne Juda koranar ne ba haahna, dɛ he ne he haahna ɡe la kɛɛ?

english_verse: Even now, your pride keeps you from respecting me and obeying the laws and teachings I gave you and your ancestors.
translation_verse: Hale ba le fini he ta he te pwɛrɛ mɔɔ. Haa men duu kɛɛ dɛɛ teŋɛ me Mmarare maa kpɔa tɛ he ne he naawa la ta.

english_verse: There were only a few of you left in Judah, and you decided to go to Egypt. But you will die such horrible deaths in war or from starvation, that people of other countries will use the name of Judah as a curse word.
translation_verse: Kɛ Juda tena baa kaa dɛɛ nyin kɛ ba ka so Ijipt harɛ ta la te, mɛɛ chɔɡ ba bwaa. Nomonome ne bechale bwaa dɛɛ ba laa kɛɛ lɔr ta sewa Ijipt harɛ ta. Nɛra ɛɛ nao ba bambile teŋe, dɛ yerɛ ba sɔn dɛɛ taah ba, dɛɛ nyiŋi ba nyubaah.

english_verse: I punished Jerusalem with war, hunger, and disease, and that's how I will punish you.
translation_verse: Mɛɛ tɛr banɔ la baa lɔ Ijipt harɛ la deŋnee, ɡɛ maa kpɔ laa ne lɔr dɛ weechɔɡa chɔɡ Jerusalam tena la.

english_verse: None of you will survive. You may hope to return to Judah someday, but only a very few of you will escape death and be able to go back. The People Refuse To Worship the Lord
translation_verse: Juda tena baa kaa dɛ ba so Ijipt harɛ ta la aa won le a nyoa baa wola serewe. Ba bini bɛlbwa aa won berɛ la Juda harɛ ta, bela baa dɛ nyin kɛ ba berɛ ka so ja la. Ba bwa aa won kaa, atane ba bini tamaa bane.”

english_verse: A large number of Jews from both northern and southern Egypt listened to me as I told them what the Lord had said. Most of the men in the crowd knew that their wives often burned incense to other gods. So they and their wives shouted:
translation_verse: Belaa baala baa jema kɛ ba haahna dɛ fuh konsɔɔhsoma voɡare ane ta, ne haahna baa cheɡɛ bela bwa, dɛ Israel tena baa wara dɛ so Ijipt weekaŋle harɛbɔr ŋɔ men Jeremia be ŋɔ,

english_verse: Jeremiah, what do we care if you speak in the Lord's name? We refuse to listen!
translation_verse: “Ya vɛh waa haa cheɡɛ Korowii sɔn ta dɛ bol ya be la.

english_verse: We have promised to worship the goddess Astarte, the Queen of Heaven, and that is exactly what we are going to do. We will burn incense and offer sacrifices of wine to her, just as we, our ancestors, our kings, and our leaders did when we lived in Jerusalem and the other towns of Judah. We had plenty of food back then. We were well off, and nothing bad ever happened to us.
translation_verse: Yaa ɛ waa yaa ŋɔa yaa ɛo laanee. Yaa ɛ saraharee tɛ ya voɡ waa ɛ Nyundua Haŋkooro la, dɛ́ fuɡe sen ɛ saraha tɛo ɡɛ ya naawa ne koranar dɛ nomonome fa aa dɛ ɛ Juda bwɛɛre ta ne Jerusalam fɔɡbaahna la. A ɡɛ saŋ la, ya dɔ kondikwa kohona asɛ ya wobɛlbwa do wer, wenaale bɛlbwa ta ya nɛɛ balɛ.

english_verse: But since the time we stopped burning incense and offering wine sacrifices to her, we have been dying from war and hunger.
translation_verse: Kɛ le saŋ yaa ɡel daawiile fuih dɛ tɛ Nyundua Haŋkooro, dɛ ɡel sen sarahare ɛɛ dɛ tɛo la, yaa komɛlbwa dɔ kpa, asɛ laa ne lɔr ɛɛ kpoo bane ɡe.”

english_verse: Then the women said, “When we lived in Judah, we worshiped the Queen of Heaven and offered sacrifices of wine and special loaves of bread shaped like her. Our husbands knew what we were doing, and they approved of it.”
translation_verse: Ate, haahna la berɛ ŋɔ, “Ya fuh daawiile dɛ fuɡe sen ɛ saraha tɛ Nyundua Haŋkooro la aa, ya jaranar aa jemɛ kɛŋɔ ya wɔɔ paanoo a mar do kɛŋɔ Nyundua Haŋkooro dɛ fuɡe sen ɛ sarahare ɡe tɛo wa aa?”

english_verse: Don't you think the Lord knew that you and your ancestors, your leaders and kings, and the rest of the people were burning incense to other gods in Jerusalem and everywhere else in Judah?
translation_verse: “He dɛ lii kɛŋɔ sarahare he ne he naawa ne koranar, nomonome ne nɛra baa lɔ harɛ la ta aa ɛa Juda bwɛɛre ta ne Jerusalam fɔɡbaahna la, Korowii aa a waa jemɛ, kɛɛ o soh a waa kɛɛ?

english_verse: And when he could no longer put up with your disgusting sins, he placed a curse on your land and turned it into a desert, as it is today.
translation_verse: Korowii aa wola won so nyiŋi he nyubinikpeɡ we-ɛɛla ne waa waa kia hɛɛ ɛ la, anee ɡela he harɛ la berɛ kon baa taahno, dɛ berɛ dimɡbia nomɛlbwa aa wola o ta soɡe hale ba le fini la.

english_verse: This disaster happened because you worshiped other gods and rebelled against the Lord by refusing to obey him or follow his laws and teachings.
translation_verse: Haa ɛ sarahare dɛɛ tɛ voɡare, haa wola waa Korowii aa do heyaa a ta teŋɛ, dɛ ɛ wechɔɡa jo o nɛɛ la waa wekpeɡa nɔ ba he nɛɛ la.”

english_verse: Then I told the men and their wives, that the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, had said: Here in Egypt you still keep your promises to burn incense and offer sacrifices of wine to the so-called Queen of Heaven.
translation_verse: Koranar Bwa Kooro, Israel tena aa dɛ tomɔ la ŋɔ, ‘He ne he haahna we-ɛɛla dɛ baɡle waa haa ŋwɛɛra dɛ ŋɔ hɛɛ sɛoh fuh daawiile dɛ́ fuɡe sen ɛ sarahare tɛ Nyundua Haŋkooro la.’ Hé teŋɛ he nyobaɡa la ta! Hé ka ɛ ɡɛ haa ŋwɛɛra la!

english_verse: Keep these promises! But let me tell you what will happen. As surely as I am the Lord God, I swear that I will never again accept any promises you make in my name.
translation_verse: He Juu tena haa soɡe Ijipt bwa, hé no waa Korowii aa dɛ bol ŋɔ o ŋwɛɛ o ɡbaɡba sɔn waa kana kɛŋɔ Juu te bɛlbwa waa soɡe Ijipt harɛ ta bobɛlbwa aa won yerɛ o sɔn ŋwɛɛ ŋɔ, ‘N ŋwɛɛ Nemenɛ Korowii waa lole.’ ”

english_verse: Instead of watching over you, I will watch for chances to harm you. Some of you will die in war, and others will starve to death.
translation_verse: Korowii ŋɔ, “N sie lɔ ba be mɛɛ nyin ba dɛ chɔɡ, dɛ ɛɛ ba wedɛɛɡa te laa. Juu tena baa soɡe Ijipt harɛ ta la, laa ne lɔree dɛ́ kpoo ba ka tel kɛŋɔ ba bwa aa serewa.

english_verse: Only a few will escape and return to Judah. Then everyone who went to live in Egypt will know that when I say something will happen, it will—no matter what you say.
translation_verse: Ba bini banɔ la baa dɔ bɔr le Ijipt harɛ ta kaa Juda la ɛɛ do tamaa kenii. Ásɛ Juda tena bwa baa kaa dɛ ba so Ijipt harɛ ta la jemɛ bɛl la o wa aa dɔ kasinteŋ, n waa la kɛɛ ba waa baa dɛ teŋɛ a ta la.

english_verse: And here is how you will know that I will keep my threats to punish you in Egypt.
translation_verse: Anɔɔ ɛ waa dɛ́ baɡle kɛŋɔ bonɔɔ mɛɛ ba he deŋne tɛra, ásɛ he jemɛ kɛŋɔ kaeh maa dɛ kah heya ŋɔ mɛɛ chɔɡ heyaa la ɛ kasinteŋ.”

english_verse: I will hand over King Hophra of Egypt to those who want to kill him, just as I handed Zedekiah over to Nebuchadnezzar, who wanted to kill him.
translation_verse: Waa Korowii aa bera dɛɛ bol laanee kɛŋɔ, “N dɛ ba Ijipt Kooro Hofra lawa tɛ o dɔma baa dɛ nyinu dɛ kpo la, ɡɛ maa kpɔ Juda Kooro Sedekia do Babelɔn Kooro Nebukadnesa waa ɛ o dɔm dɛɛ nyinu dɛ́ kpo nɔn ta la.”

english_verse: In the fourth year that Jehoiakim was king of Judah, Baruch wrote down everything I had told him.
translation_verse: Waa Korowii keame Jeremia aa bol Nɛrea bibaa Baruk be, ɡɛ saŋ Juda Kooro Josia bibaa Jehoiakim aa di kora bene anaarɛ ta la, dɛ Baruk dɛ chwerɛ waa Jeremia aa dɛ bol.

english_verse: Then later, the Lord God of Israel told me to say to Baruch:
translation_verse: A habɔɔ la, Korowii Israel tena aa dɛ tomɔ ŋɔ ń bol Baruk be ŋɔ,

english_verse: You are moaning and blaming me, the Lord, for your troubles and sorrow, and for being so tired that you can't even rest.
translation_verse: “He ŋɔ n be ŋɔ, ‘N bwɛɛlɛ. Korowii kpɔ suna dii ba ja n wenaale ta, n koɔh n hima maa dɛ hime ta, maa onɛ bwa.’ ”

english_verse: But all over the earth I am tearing down what I built and pulling up what I planted.
translation_verse: Belaa Korowii ŋɔ men Jeremia bol Baruk be ŋɔ, “Mɛɛ taɡɛ komɛlbwa maa mao ta harɛ, dɛ́ fuɡri komɛlbwa maa duu ta, harɛ nɔ ta bobɛlbwa.

english_verse: I am bringing disaster everywhere, so don't even think about making any big plans for yourself. However, I promise that wherever you go, I will at least protect you from death. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ɛrɛɛ hɛɛ nyin kɛŋɔ nɛra nyiŋi he nɛɛ kɛrɛdɛ nɔɔ? Bɛ an dɛɛ nyin, dɛkalkɛ n dɛ ba wenaale kpɔe ba ta harɛ nɔ nɛra bwa nɛ. Bobɛlbwa haa chwa kaa la, mɛɛ ɡeloo he dɔ he nyu. Men Korowiirii bola.”

english_verse: The Lord often told me what to say about the different nations of the world. What the Lord Says about Egypt
translation_verse: Waa Korowii aa bol men Korowii keame Jeremia be dɛɛ baɡle harɛre nɛra bwa waa laanee nɔ.

english_verse: In the fourth year that Jehoiakim was king of Judah, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia defeated King Neco of Egypt in a battle at the city of Carchemish near the Euphrates River. And here is what the Lord told me to say about the Egyptian army:
translation_verse: Ijipt harɛ waa tɔ sie. Waa nɔ kaalɔ dɛɛ tɛ Ijipt Kooro Neko ne o laa tena. Onee Babelɔn Kooro Nebukadnesa yo dɛ pɔ o nɛ bwɛjen Kaakɛmes, o bɛne Yufretis Moo nyoa, ɡɛ saŋ Juda Kooro Josia bibaa Jehoiakim aa di kora bene anaarɛ ta.

english_verse: saddle your horses, and polish your spears. Put on your helmets and armor, then take your positions.
translation_verse: Hé kpɔ kwaa darawe jaɡre nɛ, dɛ́ teeh so a ta. Bɛlbwa ka che o chebɔr, dɛ́ kpɔ o ɡbɛrɛ pi. Hé sar he lampeare nyoo dɛ́ kpɔ he laa laala do.

english_verse: You are strong and run fast, but you can't escape. You fall in battle near the Euphrates River.
translation_verse: Laa tena baa ɡbaŋa kwara ta wone chwa le kaa. Ba lɔ naa weekaŋle nyunduabɔr Yufretis Moo ta dɛ choɡli.

english_verse: What nation is this, that rises like the Nile River overflowing its banks?
translation_verse: Harɛ besoo nɛraa ɡɔɔ ba te kɛŋɔ Nael Moo waa sua dɛ bu atɛlɛ nɔɔ?

english_verse: It is Egypt, rising with a roar like a raging river and saying, “I'll flood the earth, destroying cities, and killing everyone in them.”
translation_verse: Ijipt harɛ nɛraa dɛɛ ɡɔɔ ba te kɛŋɔ Nael Moo, kɛŋɔ nee aa sua dɛ bu atɛlɛ ken. O ŋɔ, ‘Mɛɛ suu dɛ́ tɔ harɛ bwa dɛ́ chɔɡ bwɛjena ne a nɛra.’

english_verse: Go ahead, Egypt. Tell your chariots and cavalry to attack and fight hard. Order your troops to march out, with Ethiopians and Libyans carrying shields, and the Lydians armed with bows and arrows.
translation_verse: Jaɡre ne kwaa aa do kɛ torɔɡore ba vɔwɛ dɛɛ pɛla, hé le dɛ́ ka yo. Nɛra haa soɡe jaɡre ta, hé kpɔ sibeɡra le. Banyoola, hé le dɛɛ kaa, Itiopia ne Lebya harɛre baala, hé kpɔ kwaa baa kpɔa dɛɛ tɔ ɡbemɡbe dɛɛ yo laa kpoŋe, ásɛ Lidia baala harɛ ba tori.

english_verse: But the Lord All-Powerful will win this battle and take revenge on his enemies. His sword will eat them and drink their blood until it is full. They will be killed in the north near the Euphrates River, as a sacrifice to the Lord.
translation_verse: Awola tɔpere la ɛ Korowii, Koranar Bwa Kooro Tɔpere, tɔpere waa dɛ ba o dɔma kem bɔe. O tokobii nee wɛɛ ba ba kpoora, dɛ́ nyɔ ba chal sɔɔh nyɔɡre waa dɛ kpoo nyoa. Korowii, Koranar Bwa Kooro ɛɛ kpoo o dɔmaa awola tɔpere, Yufretis Moo nyoa, weekaŋle nyunduabɔr.

english_verse: All nations have heard you weep; you are disgraced, and they know it. Your troops fall to the ground, stumbling over each other. A Warning for Egypt
translation_verse: Harɛre nɛra bwa ɛɛ no he sihiih haa dia waa, bɛlbwa no he wii haa dɛ wi bobɛlbwa. Laa tena ɛɛ lɔ naa dɛ́ laa dɔŋa, dɛ́ bwa choɡli.”

english_verse: When King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia was on his way to attack Egypt, the Lord sent me with a warning for every Egyptian town, but especially for Migdol, Memphis, and Tahpanhes. He said to tell them: Prepare to defend yourselves! Everywhere in your nation, people are dying in war.
translation_verse: “Bol waa nɔ Ijipt bwɛjen Miɡdol ne Mɛmfes, dɛ Tapanes nɛra be ŋɔ, ‘Hé nyin bɔra che dɛɛ kpa, dɛkalkɛ Babelɔn laa tena dɛ ba ba chɔɡ harɛre nɛra baa bar heyaa cheme.’

english_verse: I have struck down your mighty god Apis and chased him away.
translation_verse: Bɔkwa waa bala he voɡjen Apis chole ɔ? Korowiirii taɡɔ o chole.

english_verse: Your soldiers stumble over each other and say, “Get up! The enemy will kill us, unless we can escape to our own land.”
translation_verse: He laa tena ɛɛ teŋɔɔ dɛɛ lɔ na, dɛ́ choɡli dawɛ dɔŋa nɛ. Baa bol dɔŋa bee ŋɔ, ‘Hé ɡel ya ir, dɛ́ berɛ kaa bela yaa lea ne ya nɛra bini, ásɛ ya dɔma bɛ yaa kpoo.’

english_verse: Egypt, I am the true king, the Lord All-Powerful, and as surely as I live, those enemies who attack will tower over you like Mount Tabor among the hills or Mount Carmel by the sea.
translation_verse: N ŋwɛɛrɔ kɛŋɔ men Koranar Bwa Kooro aa lole saŋ bɛlbwa nɔ, menee kooro. Gɛ Tabɔ Bwejen aa jaŋa ɡwaa bwejena bwa asɛ Kaamɛl Bwejen ɡe do jaŋne che mpo nyoa la, ɡɛɛ nɛn waa ba yo heyaa la kpeɡri ɛɛ ba doe.

english_verse: You will be led away captive, so pack a few things to bring with you. Your capital, Memphis, will lie empty and in ruins.
translation_verse: Ijipt tena, hé boa he laala nyoa bá lawɛ heyaa kaa bojaŋ harɛfale ta. Mɛmfes ɛɛ berɛ pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛɛ, dɛ́ berɛ dimɡbia nomɛlbwa aa wola won so o ta.

english_verse: An enemy from the north will attack you, beautiful Egypt, like a fly biting a cow.
translation_verse: Ijipt harɛ do kɛŋɔ nanee waa wera ken, kɛ o dɔm ɛɛ le weekaŋle nyunduabɔree, dɛ́ ba yoo kɛŋɔ batatom aa dɛ domɛ nao ken.

english_verse: The enemy army will go forward like a swarm of locusts. Your troops will feel helpless, like a snake in a forest
translation_verse: Ijipt tena ɛɛ chwao dɛɛ si kɛ harɛkon ken ɡɛ saŋ baa na ba dɔma bala. Kpanfɛre nee ba dɔma ɛɛ ba bala bá yoo ba kɛŋɔ baala baa dɛ teŋe daa,

english_verse: when men with axes start chopping down trees. It can only hiss and try to escape.
translation_verse: dɛɛ chɔɡ kɔrjen la ken. Ba warɔ ɡwaa tontombɛ, baa wola won kur ba.

english_verse: Your people will be disgraced and captured by the enemy from the north.
translation_verse: Sihiih kpo Ijipt tena, ba dɔma le weekaŋle nyunduabɔr ba yoo ba dɛ pɔ ba nɛ.”

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. Soon I will punish the god Amon of Thebes and the other Egyptian gods, the Egyptian kings, the people of Egypt, and everyone who trusts in the Egyptian power.
translation_verse: Koranar Bwa Kooro, Israel tena aa dɛ tomɔ ŋɔ, “N dɛ ba deŋnetɛra ne bala ba ta Tebes tena voɡ Amɔn, ne Ijipt harɛ ne o voɡa dɛ koranar bwa nɛ. N dɛ ba n lawɛ Ijipt kooro ne nɛra baa kpɔ ba te dawɛ o nɛɛ bwa.

english_verse: I will hand them over to King Nebuchadnezzar and his army. But I also promise that Egypt will someday have people living here again, just as it had before. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Will Bring Israel Home The Lord said:
translation_verse: Mɛɛ laɡ baa do nɛra baa dɛ nyin ba dɛ́ kpo nɔn ta. Banee, Babelɔn Kooro Nebukadnesa ne o laa tena. Kɛ a habɔɔ nɛra ɛɛ berɔ ba so Ijipt harɛ ta kɛ saŋ la ja. Men Korowiirii bola.” Korowii ɛɛ lɛ o nɛraa

english_verse: Israel, don't be afraid. Someday I will bring you home from foreign lands. You and your descendants will live in peace and safety, with nothing to fear.
translation_verse: “N nɛra Israel tena, he bɛ ɔmɛ, he bɛ ɡel he bambile chɔɡ. Mɛɛ lɛ heyaa le bojaŋ harɛre taa ba, he naanar baa laɡ ba kaa bojaŋ harɛfala ta bwa. Ásɛ he berɛ dɔ deŋnesɔɔhna ne bosɔɔhna, nomɛlbwa aa wola won aah heyaa kpa.

english_verse: So don't be afraid, even though now you deserve to be punished and have been scattered among other nations. But when I destroy them, I will protect you. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: N nɛra Israel tena, mɛɛ ja he nɛɛ dɛ́ lɛ heya, mɛɛ chɔɡ harɛre nɛra maa lɔ heyaa peɡre ba bini bwaa, kɛ he te, maa den chɔɡ heyaa kwaraa. Mɛɛ tɛr he deŋnee, kɛ aŋwɛnɛ taa mɛɛ ba he deŋne tɛra. Men Korowiirii bola.”

english_verse: Before the king of Egypt attacked the town of Gaza, the Lord told me to say to the Philistines:
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Ijipt kooro aa ka yo Gasa tena la, Korowii bol Filisti tena wa men Korowii keame Jeremia be.

english_verse: When you hear the thunder of horses and chariots, your courage will vanish, and parents will even abandon their own children.
translation_verse: Baa dɛɛ no jaɡre aa dɛ chwa nakpale sii, ne kwaa aa do kɛ torɔɡore kɔbare sii. Mɛɛnanar aa ke nyiŋi ba bii dɛ́ cha ba, dɛkalkɛ ɔmee chole ba nɛɛ kohona, baa wola won ɛ wobɛlbwa.

english_verse: You refugees from Crete, your time has now come, and I will destroy you. None of you will be left to help the cities of Tyre and Sidon.
translation_verse: Filisti tena bwa chɔɡa tɔpere la telo, ba dɔma dɛ ba ba kpoo banɔ la bwa baa kaa, ásɛ nomɛlbwa aa won cha Taaya ne Sidon kpa. Men Korowiirii dɛ́ chɔɡ Filisti tena, ne nɛra ba fa aa soɡe Kret ekwi harɛ ta bwa.

english_verse: The Anakim who survive in Gaza and Ashkelon will mourn for you by shaving their heads and sitting in silence.
translation_verse: Gasa tena dɛ di suna kohona, baa fonɛ ba nyuune á baɡle kɛŋɔ ba dɛ ɛ lwe, ásɛ Askɛlɔn tena hel jeiih ken a wa. Saŋ besoo Filisti tena kabora ɛɛ ba wii ka tel ɔ?

english_verse: You ask how long will I continue to attack you with my sword, then you tell me to put it away and leave you alone.
translation_verse: He yon dɛɛ wi ŋɔ, ‘N Naa Korowii, he kpoŋe he kere, saŋ besoo hé kpɔ kere la kpoo nɛra ka tel ɔ? Kpɔɔ do o tɔɔ bini ó chɔ bela jeih ken.’

english_verse: But how can my sword rest, when I have commanded it to attack Ashkelon and the seacoast?
translation_verse: Korowii aa ŋɔa kere la ka yo Askɛlɔn ne mpo nyoa tena bwa nɔ. Ɛrɛɛ wɛɛ ba wona chɔɔ?”

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, told me to say to the nation of Moab: The town of Nebo is doomed; Kiriathaim will be captured and disgraced, and even its fortress will be left in ruins.
translation_verse: Koranar Bwa Kooro, Israel tena aa dɛ tomɔ bol Moab harɛ wa men Jeremia be ŋɔ, “Nɛbo tena, hé bwɛɛlɛ, dɛkalkɛ he bwɛɛ la dɛ ba chɔɡa. Dɔma yo Kiriataim tena dɛ pɔ ba nɛ, o danjwɛkpeɡ baa maa baro kuuɡo, asɛ sihiih kpo ba.

english_verse: No one honors you, Moab. In Heshbon, enemies make plans to end your life. My sword will leave only silence in your town named “Quiet.”
translation_verse: Moab harɛ nyanyini tonɔ. Dɔma baa yo Hɛsbɔn tena dɛ pɔ ba nɛ, dɛɛ vɔrɔwe kɛ bá ba chɔɡ Moab harɛ. Nɛra haa lɔ bwɛɛ baa dɛ yerɔ Madmen ɡe bwa hel, dɛkalkɛ laa tena ɛɛ ba yoo baa.

english_verse: The people of Horonaim will cry for help, as their town is attacked and destroyed.
translation_verse: Lɔŋɔre dɛ le Horonaim, sibeɡra ne bwɛɛ chɔɡa wii.

english_verse: Moab will be shattered! Your children will sob
translation_verse: Ba chɔɡ Moab harɛ bwa, hɛ́ɛ no bechale wii.

english_verse: and cry on their way up to the town of Luhith; on the road to Horonaim they will tell of disasters.
translation_verse: Hɛ́ɛ no ba wii ɡbɔɡa Luhit ŋwɛnɛ ta, suna wii baa dɛ wi Horonaim ŋwɛnɛ ta.

english_verse: Run for your lives! Head into the desert like a wild donkey.
translation_verse: Ba ŋɔ, ‘Hé ɛ warane, dɛ́ chwa lɛ he nyuune. Hé chwa kɛŋɔ kpɔɡ bini keeɡo waa lɔ pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta ken.’

english_verse: You thought you could be saved by your power and wealth, but you will be captured along with your god Chemosh, his priests, and officials.
translation_verse: Moab harɛ tena, hé kpɔ he te dawɛ he bokpeɡa ne kondɔɔh ta, kɛ ba dɛ ba heyaa yoi dɛ́ pɔ he nɛ, dɛ́ kpɔ voɡ Kemɔs kaa harɛfale ta, o ne o nomonome ne o kerekpoŋra.

english_verse: Not one of your towns will escape destruction. I have told your enemies, “Wipe out the valley and the flatlands of Moab.
translation_verse: Bwɛɛ bɛlbwa aa kae ba dɛ́ le chɔɡa la nyoa, fɛlembɔjena ne deŋɡarere a dor aa chɔa kaa bwa ɛɛ chɔɡoo. Men Korowiirii bola.

english_verse: Spread salt on the ground to kill the crops. Leave its towns in ruins, with no one living there.
translation_verse: Hé paaɡe bwea a che tɛ Moab harɛ, dɛkalkɛ aa biɡri ba chɔɡo. Moab bwɛɛre dɛ ba dimɡbia bera, nomɛlbwa aa belaa so kpa.”

english_verse: I want you to kill the Moabites, and if you let them escape, I will put a curse on you.”
translation_verse: Kórowii taah nomɛlbwa waa wola o toma ɛ bambile bwa ne la! Nomɛlbwa waa kwaa o tokobi cheɡ ŋɔ waa kpɔ kpo nɛn la, Kórowii taahno!

english_verse: Then you will be ashamed, because your god Chemosh cannot save you, just as Bethel could not help the Israelites.
translation_verse: Sihiih ɛɛ kpo Moab tena ba voɡ Kemɔs waa, kɛŋɔ sihiih aa kpo Israel tena voɡ Bɛtel baa kpɔ ba hwɛɡa dawɛ o nɛɛ la.

english_verse: But I am the Lord, the all-powerful King, and I promise that enemies will overpower your towns. Even your best warriors will die in the battle.
translation_verse: Moab harɛ dɛ ba chɔɡa, ásɛ o dɔma lɔ ba tɔ o bwɛɛre ta. Baa kpoo o bonɔndɛɛɡa bwaa, men Koranar Bwa Kooro maa ɛ kooro laanee bola.

english_verse: It won't be long now— disaster will hit Moab!
translation_verse: Moab wenaale telo tonɛ, o chɔɡa dɛ ba bala warane.

english_verse: I will order the nearby nations to mourn for you and say, “Isn't it sad? Moab ruled others, but now its glorious power has been shattered.”
translation_verse: Bwɛɛre haa soɡa baro bwa nɛra hé wi tɛo, hé nɛra haa na o jirima bwa ŋɔ, ‘Hé na ɡɛ kooro faahna waa kpeɡa dɛ dɔ jirima la aa kua.’

english_verse: People in the town of Dibon, you will be honored no more, so have a seat in the dust. Your walls will be torn down when the enemies attack.
translation_verse: Debɔn tena, hé le he soŋnibɔr waa dɔ jirima ba, dɛ́ ba so harɛ bomboɡ ta. Nɛn waa ba chɔɡ Moab la balɔ dɛ́ ba kuuɡi danjwɛjen waa baro la.

english_verse: You people of Aroer, go wait beside the road, and when refugees run by, ask them, “What happened?”
translation_verse: Arowa tena, hé che ŋwɛnɛ nyoa dɛɛ kpa. Hé nyiŋi haahna ne baala baa chwaa dɛɛ kaa, dɛ́ bɔɔ ba waa aa chiɡa.

english_verse: They will answer, “Moab has been defeated! Weep with us in shame. Tell everyone at the Arnon River that Moab is destroyed.”
translation_verse: Sihiih kpo Moab tena, dɛkalkɛ ba harɛ la bwa chɔɡɔ. Hé wi dɛɛ do lɔŋɔre. Hé ɡel Aanɔn Moo nyoa tena no kɛŋɔ ba chɔɡ Moab.

english_verse: I will punish every town that belongs to Moab, but especially Holon, Jahzah, Mephaath,
translation_verse: Bwɛjena aa chɔ deŋɡare doa harɛ waa chɔa kaa ta waa bola dɛ́ pa bole telo, anee Holon ne Jaasa dɛ Mɛfaat,

english_verse: My decision is final— your army will be crushed, and your power broken.
translation_verse: Moab tena kpeɡri bwa tonɔ, baa won yo kpa. Men Korowiirii bola.”

english_verse: People of Moab, you claim to be stronger than I am. Now I will tell other nations to make you drunk and to laugh while you collapse in your own vomit.
translation_verse: Korowii ŋɔ, “Hé tɛ Moab tena sen bá nyɔ dɛɛ kohona, dɛkalkɛ ba ɛ men Korowii deŋnekpeɡ. Hé ɡel ba chɔ dɛɛ ɡbaɡre ba chwɛɛra ta, dɛ́ berɛ akwekwe nɛra.

english_verse: Now you must leave your towns and live like doves in the shelter of cliffs and canyons.
translation_verse: Moab tena, hé chwa le he bwɛɛre ta dɛ́ ka so bwea dor. Hé ka sɔh he kɔne bwebɔɔne nyoo, kɛŋɔ borɔnomare ken.

english_verse: So I will cry and mourn for Moab and its town of Kir-Heres.
translation_verse: Anomanta, n wio dɛɛ tɛ Moab tena, ba ɡbosoro waa mɛɛ wi. N wio dɛɛ tɛ Kir Haresɛt baala.

english_verse: People of Sibmah, you were like a vineyard heavy with grapes, and with branches reaching north to the town of Jazer and west to the Dead Sea. But you have been destroyed, and so I will weep for you, as the people of Jazer weep for the vineyards.
translation_verse: N wio dɛ tɛ Sibma tena dɛ ɡwaa kɛ maa wi tɛ Jasa tena, Bwɛjen Sibma, he do kɛ ɡrepo da, he ta kpala dɛ ɡale Yar Mpo hale dɛ kpoŋe kaa Jasa Mpo nyoa bwa. Kɛ taraken, nɛnchɔɡe baa chɔɡ he bɔwɔb saŋ nɔna ne he ɡrepo nɔna.

english_verse: Harvest celebrations are gone from the orchards and farms of Moab. I have silenced the shouts of people making wine.
translation_verse: Silɛɛ ne hɛɡra bɛlbwa toole Moab harɛpare ondɛɛɡe ne kooni ta kpa. N ɡelɔ sen toole bɔra baa dɛ harama, nɛra toole dɛ́ tiɡri a ta. Baa mooluu, kɛ silɛɛ moola laa.

english_verse: Weeping from Heshbon can be heard as far as Elealeh and Jahaz; cries from Zoar are heard in Horonaim and Eglath-Shelishiyah. And Nimrim Creek has run dry.
translation_verse: Hɛsbɔn ne Eleale tena lɔŋɔre dɛ le, hale aa tel Jahas tena be. A tel Soar tena be, dɛ kpoŋe kaa Horonaim ne Eɡlat Sɛleseya. Hale neerare aa lɔ Nimrim nenabɔɔ bwa hweehrɔ.

english_verse: I will get rid of anyone who burns incense to the gods of Moab or offers sacrifices at their shrines. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Moab harɛ taa mɛɛ ba nɛra baa dɛ ɛ sarahare deŋɡarere dor, dɛɛ fuh daawiile dɛɛ tɛ ba voɡare la kpoora. Men Korowiirii bola.

english_verse: In my heart I moan for Moab, like a funeral song played on a flute. I mourn for the people of the town of Kir-Heres, because their wealth is gone. *
translation_verse: N wio dɛɛ tɛ Moab ne Kir Haresɛt tena, kɛŋɔ baa dɛ hoh kalipe dɛɛ ɡo lweyela ken. Ba kondɔɔh baa dɔa bwa le ba nɔn ta.

english_verse: The people of Moab mourn on the rooftops and in the streets. Men cut off their beards, people shave their heads; they make cuts on their hands and wear sackcloth. And it's all because I, the Lord, have shattered Moab like a jar that no one wants.
translation_verse: Moab saldor ne bɔra baa dɛ cheme bwa, wobɛlbwa toole ka ja wii ta, dɛkalkɛ n chɔɡ o bwa, kɛŋɔ loŋ baa wola nyin kpa la ken. Men Korowiirii bola.

english_verse: Moab lies broken! Listen to its people cry as they turn away in shame. Other nations are horrified at what happened, but still they mock her.
translation_verse: Hé na ɡɛ Moab harɛ bwa aa chɔɡa! Hé na ɡɛ o nɛra aa dɛ wi! Hé na ɡɛ sihiih aa kpo Moab nɛra ba baŋa ɡole! Moab bwa chɔɡɔ, asɛ harɛre nɛra baa soɡa baro bambile teŋe baa mam ba.”

english_verse: Your cities and fortresses will be captured, and your warriors as fearful as women giving birth.
translation_verse: Baa pɔ bwɛjen Kereɔt nɛɛ, dɛ́ chɔɡ ba dekpeɡa bwa. Awola tɔpere la, Moab banyoola ɛɛ ɔmɔɔ kɛŋɔ haah loltea aa lɔɔ ken.

english_verse: You are finished as a nation, because you dared oppose me, the Lord.
translation_verse: Baa chɔɡ Moab harɛ nɛra bwaa, dɛkalkɛ ba vɛh men Korowii.

english_verse: If you are terrified and run, you will fall into a pit; and if you crawl out of the pit, you'll get caught in a trap. The time has come for you to be punished. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Nomɛlbwa koh ɔmee kohona la waa chwa dɛɛ kaa laa, wɛɛ le bɔɔ binii. Bɛlbwa ɡe waa ŋɔ wɛɛ leo la, belii dɛɛ ba o lawa, dɛkalkɛ Moab tena deŋnetɛra saŋ telo ń kpɔ ba ta ba nɛ. Men Korowiirii bola.

english_verse: Near the city of Heshbon, where Sihon once ruled, tired refugees stand in shadows cast by the flames of their burning city. Soon, the towns on other hilltops, where those warlike people live, will also go up in smoke.
translation_verse: Nɛra baa koh laa waa chwa ba bwɛjen Hɛsbɔn wilo, dɛɛ nyin ba nyu, dɛkalkɛ nii le Kooro Sihon koodem dɛ fuh le Hɛsbɔn o fa aa di kora o ta. Nii la fuoh jo ba harɛ jwɛhre bwa ta, hale dɛ ka tel Moab tena baa dɛ nyin yoi kohona la harɛ bwejena dor.

english_verse: People of Moab, you worshiped Chemosh, your god, but now you are done for, and your children are prisoners in a foreign country.
translation_verse: Moab tena, hé bwɛɛlɛ! Nɛra haa dɛ tomɛ voɡ Kemɔs la, he chɔɡɔ. Ba lawɛ he bibaala ne bihaahna bwa kaa bojaŋ harɛfale ta.

english_verse: The Lord has this to say about the nation of Ammon: The people of Israel have plenty of children to inherit their lands. So why have you worshipers of the god Milcom taken over towns and land belonging to the tribe of Gad?
translation_verse: Gɛ Korowii aa bol Amɔn tena waa laanee nɔ. “Baala toole Israel harɛ ta kpa, dɛ́ kpɔ harɛ la ɛ ba kapɛrɛ kon kɛɛ? Ɛrɛɛ nɛra baa dɛ tomɛ voɡ Molɛk berɛ ba lɛ Gad dea harɛ dɛ so o ta nɔɔ?

english_verse: Someday I will send an army to attack you in Rabbah, your capital city. It will be left in ruins, and the surrounding villages will lie in ashes. You took some of Israel's land, but on that day Israel will take yours!
translation_verse: Kɛ tɔpera ane dɛ ba, ásɛ n ɡel nɛra baa lɔ Amɔn harɛ bwɛjen Raba no laa lɔŋɔre. Bwɛjen la ɛɛ paɡroo dɛ́ berɛ dimɡbia, ásɛ o bwɛjeɡre aa baro bwa ɡe fuh. Belaa Israel tena ɛɛ ba banɔ la ba fa aa doŋ ba le ba harɛ ta la doŋa le. Men Korowiirii bola.

english_verse: Cry, people of Heshbon; your town will become a pile of rubble. You will turn here and there, but your path will be blocked. Put on sackcloth and mourn, you citizens of Rabbah, because the idol you worship will be taken to a foreign country, along with its priests and temple officials.
translation_verse: Hɛsbɔn tena, hé do lɔŋɔre bwɛjen Ai chɔɡa wa. Nɛra haa lɔ bwɛjen Raba, hé ɡe wi! Hé kpɔ lweyale tɔ dɛɛ wi, dɛɛ chwa bobɛlbwa yalayala ken, dɛkalkɛ baa kpɔ he voɡ Molɛk ne o kerekpoŋra, dɛ nomonome bwaa kaa bojaŋ harɛfale ta.

english_verse: You rebellious Ammonites trust your wealth and ask, “Who could attack us?” But I warn you not to boast when your strength is fading.
translation_verse: He nɛra he wa aa wola kasinteŋ dɔe, ɛrɛɛ hɛɛ ɛ mbarafo he fɛlembɔjena aa do wer kohona waɔ? He kpɔ he hwɛɡa do he kondɔɔh ta dɛ ŋɔ, ‘Nomɛlbwa aa won ba yo yaa.’ ”

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, will send neighboring nations to strike you with terror. You will be scattered, with no one to care for your refugees.
translation_verse: Korowii, Koranar Bwa Kooro ŋɔ, “Mɛɛ ɡeloo nɛra baa bar heyaa cheme kpɔ ɔmee kohona ba ta he nɛ. Baa doŋi he bwaa le, bɛlbwa aa kae ba dɛ́ boa nɛra baa koh laa waa chwa la nyoa.

english_verse: Yet someday, I will bring your people back home. I, the Lord, have spoken. What the Lord Says about Edom
translation_verse: Kɛ a habɔɔ la, mɛɛ berɔ ɡel Amɔn tena wobɛlbwa berɛ do wer tɛɛ ba. Men Korowiirii bola.” Gɛ Korowii aa bol Edom tena wa

english_verse: I will send disaster to punish you descendants of Esau, so anyone from Dedan had better turn around and run back home.
translation_verse: Bwɛjen Dedan tena, hé laa berɛ dɛ́ chwa! Hé ka sɔh bwebɔɔne aa luŋa bini, n dɛ ba Esɔ naanar chɔɡa, dɛkalkɛ tɔpere telo kɛ ń tɛr ba deŋne.

english_verse: People who harvest grapes leave some for the poor. Thieves who break in at night take only what they want.
translation_verse: Nɛra dɛ chaa ɡrepo nɔna aa, ba dɛ ɡel tama a daa ta. Dɛ ŋwɛɛra balɔ jwaana aa, anɔ la baa dɛ nyin ɡbo laa ba yon kpɔ kaa laa?

english_verse: But I will take everything that belongs to you, people of Edom, and I will uncover every place where you try to hide. Then you will die, and so will your children, relatives, and neighbors.
translation_verse: Mɛɛ laa komɛlbwa Esɔ naanar aa dɔa lɛ ba be, dɛ́ ɡel bela baa sɔah chɔ baŋ, nɛra bwa ɛɛ na baa, baa wola sɔɔhbɔraa dɔ kpa. Ba bii ne lolanar, dɛ ba bala bwa ɛɛ serewoo, ba bini beŋkpoŋ kwara aa wola ka.

english_verse: Even those nations that don't deserve to be punished will have to drink from the cup of my anger. So how can you possibly hope to escape?
translation_verse: Waa Korowii aa dɛ bol laanee nɔ. “Dɛ nɛra baa wola chɛɛ kɛŋɔ ń tɛr ba deŋne nyɔ n danana nee aa, ɛrɛɛ maa wola won tɛr he deŋne ɔ? Haa won le deŋnetɛra la nyoa, a chɛ kɛ hé nyɔ n danana ne.

english_verse: I, the Lord, swear in my own name that your city of Bozrah and all your towns will suffer a horrible fate. They will lie in ruins forever, and people will use the name “Bozrah” as a curse word.
translation_verse: N ŋwɛɛ n ɡbaɡba kɛŋɔ bwɛjen Bosra ɛɛ paɡroo dɛ́ berɛ dimɡbia, ásɛ dɛ berɛ kon nɛra aa na dɛɛ mamɛ, dɛɛ taahno ba bambile teŋe kohona. Bwɛɛre aa baro bwa ɡe ɛɛ chɔɡoo kwaraa saŋ bɛlbwa dɛɛ la. Men Korowiirii bola.”

english_verse: I have sent a messenger to command the nations to prepare for war against you people of Edom.
translation_verse: Men Jeremia no Edom waa le Korowii be o ŋɔ, “N tomɛ torome bɛl harɛre nɛra be ŋɔ, ‘Hé boa he nyoa dɛ́ ir ka yo Edom tena! Hé ir ka yoo ba laa!

english_verse: Your nation will be small, yet hated by other nations.
translation_verse: Mɛɛ ɡeloo he nɛra ɡwɛɡre harɛre nɛra bwa bini, ásɛ ba haeh, dɛɛ nyiŋi he nyubaah.

english_verse: Pride tricks you into thinking that other nations look at you with fear. You live along the cliffs and high in the mountains like the eagles, but I am the Lord, and I will bring you down.
translation_verse: He mbarafo neɡre heya kohona, he dɛ lii kɛ nomɛlbwa dɛ́ ɔmɛ heya, he dɛ neɡre he te. He soɡe bɔɔne bini bwejena dor. A lole kɛ he soŋnibɔr lɔ nyundua, kɛŋɔ kee yon ka sɔh o kɔr nyundujaɡla la, kɛ mɛɛ ɡeloo he le bela le harɛ.’

english_verse: People passing by your country will be shocked and horrified to see a disaster
translation_verse: Edom harɛ dɛ ba kon waa do ɔma bera, ásɛ nɛra baa teŋa baa kaa na, dɛ́ ɔmɛ ba nyoa kpo, o nɛra bola baa do ba wa.

english_verse: as bad as the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah and towns nearby. The towns of Edom will be empty.
translation_verse: Gɛ maa chɔɡ Sodom ne Gomoora ne bwɛɛre aa bara cheme la, ɡɛɛ mɛɛ ba Edom harɛ chɔɡa, ásɛ nomɛlbwa aa won so bela kpa. Men Nemenɛ Korowiirii bola.

english_verse: I, the Lord, will attack you like a lion from the forest, attacking sheep in a meadow along the Jordan. In a moment the flock runs, and the land is empty. Who will I choose to attack you? I will do it myself! No one can force me to fight or chase me away.
translation_verse: Gɛ nyujente yon le Jɔɔdan Moo kɔr bini ba kaa harɛdɛɛɡe ta ka di la, ɡɛɛ men Korowii ɛɛ ba Edom tena doŋa le ba harɛ ta. Ásɛ nomoa maa leo la tɔ ba sie dɛɛ nyiŋi ba nɛ. Umee bá won kpɔ maɡ mɛ nɔ? Nomɛlbwa aa won tɔŋle mɛ. Kooro besoo dɛ́ won che n sie nɔ?

english_verse: The sounds of your destruction will reach the Red Sea and cause the earth to shake.
translation_verse: Edom harɛ baa paɡre tonaa, harɛ ɛɛ jiɡruu ásɛ harɛre nɛra ɛɛ no Edom tena lɔŋɔre, hale dɛ ka le Mposwɛm ta.

english_verse: An enemy will swoop down to attack you, like an eagle spreading its wings and circling over Bozrah. Your warriors will be as fearful as women giving birth. What the Lord Says about Damascus
translation_verse: Hé na, dɔma dɛ́ ba ba yo Bosra tena, kɛŋɔ kee yon le nyundua dɛ́ paɡri kena dɛ́ ba ta jal la ken. Awola tɔpere la, Edom banyoola ɛɛ ɔmɔɔ kohona, kɛŋɔ haah loltea aa lɔɔ la ken.” Gɛ Korowii aa bol Damaskɔs tena wa

english_verse: The Lord says about Damascus: The towns of Hamath and Arpad have heard your bad news. They have lost hope, and worries roll over them like ocean waves.
translation_verse: Korowii bol bwɛjen Damaskɔs tena waa dɛ ŋɔ, “Bwɛjena Hamat ne Aapad tena liire chɔɡɔ, dɛkalkɛ ba ta amanesoma noɛ. Ba bambile dɛ wure kɛŋɔ mpo nehɛma aa taa dɛɛ kaa bobɛlbwa ken.

english_verse: You people of Damascus have lost your courage, and in panic you turn to run, gripped by fear and pain.
translation_verse: Damaskɔs tena ɡwɛɡrɔ, ba kpɔ ɔmee chwa kaa, asɛ bochela ne weweele su ba bwa, kɛŋɔ haah loltea aa lɔɔ la ken.

english_verse: Once I was pleased with your famous city. But now I warn you, “Escape while you still can!”
translation_verse: Ba chwao ɡel bwɛjen o sɔn fa aa lea, bwɛɛ men Korowii sie aa dɛ lɛ o ta kohona.

english_verse: Soon, even your best soldiers will lie dead in your streets. I, the Lord All-Powerful, have spoken.
translation_verse: Awola tɔpere la, Damaskɔs bonɔɔna ɛɛ serewoo chɔ fɔɡbaahna, ásɛ ba kpoo o laa tena bwa. Men Koranar Bwa Kooroo bola.

english_verse: I will set fire to your city walls and burn down the fortresses King Benhadad built. Nebuchadnezzar and the People of the Desert
translation_verse: Mɛɛ do nii Damaskɔs danjwɛɛre taa, ásɛ a fuh Kooro Bɛn Hadad koodem dekpeɡa.” Gɛ Korowii aa bol Keda ne Hasɔ tena wa

english_verse: Here is what the Lord says about the Kedar tribe and the desert villages that were conquered by King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia: Listen, you people of Kedar and the other tribes of the eastern desert. I have told Nebuchadnezzar to attack and destroy you.
translation_verse: Korowii bol Keda dea tena ne Hasɔ harɛre Babelɔn Kooro Nebukadnesa aa yoa dɛ pɔ ba nɛɛ la waa ŋɔ, “Hé ir, dɛ́ ka yo Keda tena, dɛ́ kpoo nɛra baa soɡe pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta wee leebɔr.

english_verse: His fearsome army will surround you, taking your tents and possessions, your sheep and camels.
translation_verse: Hé kpɔ ba tɛnte deene ne a pateesanre, dɛ ba peera bwa kaa, hale ba laala ne nyoɡmare bwa. Ásɛ dɛ ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, ‘Ɔmee kohona bar heyaa cheme!’

english_verse: Run and hide, you people of the desert who live in villages! Nebuchadnezzar has big plans for you.
translation_verse: Hasɔ tena, hé chwa le warane kaa. Hé chwa ka sɔh bwebɔɔne aa luŋa bini. Babelɔn Kooro Nebukadnesa dɛ́ vɔrɔwe he vɔrɔwa.

english_verse: You have no city walls and no neighbors to help, yet you think you're safe— so I told him to attack.
translation_verse: Hé ir ka yo harɛ o nɛra aa dɛ lii kɛ ba soɡe bosɔɔhna ta la. Ba bwɛjen ta doonyojena kɛɛ bune baa kpɔa dɛɛ kara dɔe, komɛlbwa toole dɛɛ tɔ ba ɡbemɡbe.

english_verse: Then your camels and large herds will be yours no longer. People of the Arabian Desert, disaster will strike you from every side, and you will be scattered everywhere on earth.
translation_verse: Baa lawɛ ba nyoɡmare ne kondɛɛra aa wara kɛŋɔ laa ta kwaa kaa. Mɛɛ lɔ nɛra baa lɔ bojaŋa laanee peɡre, dɛ́ kpɔ wenaale ba ta ba nɛɛ le harɛ nɔ ta bobɛlbwa.

english_verse: Only jackals will live where your villages once stood. I, the Lord, have spoken. What the Lord Says about Elam
translation_verse: Bwɛjen Hasɔ ɛɛ berɛ kalampoŋare soŋnibɔree, dɛ́ ɛ pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ saŋ bɛlbwa dɛɛ la. Nomɛlbwa aa wola won so bela kpa. Men Korowiirii bola.” Gɛ Korowii aa bol Elam harɛ wa

english_verse: Not long after Zedekiah became king of Judah, the Lord told me to say: People of Elam, I, the Lord All-Powerful, will kill the archers who make your army strong.
translation_verse: Koranar Bwa Kooro ŋɔ, “Mɛɛ kpoo nɛra baa jemɛ hɛma tae, dɛ ɡel Elam harɛ do kpeɡri la bwaa.

english_verse: Enemies will attack from all directions, and you will be led captive to every nation on earth.
translation_verse: Mɛɛ ɡeloo dɔma le harɛ nɔ ta bobɛlbwa dɛ́ ba yo Elam tena laa, dɛ́ lɔ ba peɡre bobɛlbwa, harɛ bɛlbwa aa ka baa wola belaa do.

english_verse: Your king and his officials will die, and I will rule in their place. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Mɛɛ kpoo ba koranar ne nomonomee, dɛ́ ba cheɡ n kora bela dɛɛ nyiŋi ba nɛ.

english_verse: But I promise that someday I will bring your people back to their land.
translation_verse: Kɛ a habɔɔ la, mɛɛ berɔ ɡel Elam tena wobɛlbwa do wer tɛɛ ba. Men Korowiirii bola.”

english_verse: The Lord told me to say: Announce what will happen and don't leave anything out.
translation_verse: Korowii cheɡɛ men o keame Jeremia nɛɛ dɛ bol Babelɔn harɛ ne nɛra baa lɔ o ta waa ŋɔ,

english_verse: Raise the signal flags; shout so all nations can hear— Babylon will be captured! Marduk, Babylon's god, will be ashamed and terrified, and his idols broken.
translation_verse: “Bol Babelɔn harɛ waa baɡle harɛre nɛra bwa. Ir fraŋkaa, á baɡle waa aa dɛ ba! Bɛ wobɛlbwa kpɔ sɔh, ŋɔ, ‘Babelɔn dɛ́ ba paɡra. Baa paɡre ba voɡ Maadukuu, ásɛ sihiih kpo Babelɔn harɛ voɡa aa ɛ kii kwaa la bwa.’

english_verse: The attack on the Babylonians will come from the north; they and their animals will run, leaving the land empty. Israel and Judah Will Return to Their Land
translation_verse: Harɛ bɛl nɛra ɛɛ le weekaŋle nyunduabɔree, dɛ́ ba yo Babelɔn harɛ tena, ásɛ harɛ la bwa chɔ pɛɛ. Nomɛlbwa aa kae ba dɛ́ so o ta, nɛra ne kondɛɛra bwa dɛ́ ba chwae.”

english_verse: The Lord said: People of Israel and Judah, when these things happen you will weep, and together you will return to your land and worship me, the Lord your God.
translation_verse: Korowii ŋɔ, “Awola tɔpere la telo aa, Israel ne Juda tena bwa ɛɛ pɛo dɛɛ wi, dɛɛ ɡaaɡe men Korowii baa dɛ tom mɛ bɔr.

english_verse: You will ask the way to Zion and then come and join with me in making an agreement you won't break or forget.
translation_verse: Baa bɔɔ Saayɔn ŋwɛnɛ waa, dɛ́ kpɔ sie chaɡɛ bela kaa. Baa kpɔ ba tenee ba pɛl men Korowii, ásɛ n ne ba fɔwɛ fɔo waa do le saŋ bɛlbwa dɛɛ la, baa wola o waa soh bwa.

english_verse: My people, you are lost sheep abandoned in the mountains by their shepherds. You don't even remember your resting place.
translation_verse: N nɛra do kɛŋɔ peera a teɡra aa ɡela a nyoɡre ken, dɛ ɡel a do bwejena dor dɛɛ ɡaaɡe. A lɔ bwejena ne deŋɡarere ta dɛɛ ɡaaɡe, dɛ soh bela aa dɛ chɔ wa.

english_verse: I am your true pastureland, the one who gave hope to your ancestors. But you abandoned me, so when your enemies found you, they felt no guilt as they gobbled you up.
translation_verse: Nomɛlbwa waa ka puu ba la dɛ́ yoo ba. Ba dɔma yon ŋɔ, ‘Ya ta bolchɔɡe dii, dɛkalkɛ ba ɛ wechɔɡa dɛ jo Korowii waa tɛɛ ba kondikwaa la nɛ, Korowii ba naawa fa aa kpɔ ba hwɛɡa bwa do o nɛɛ kohona la.’

english_verse: Escape from Babylonia, my people. Get out of that country! Don't wait for anyone else.
translation_verse: N nɛra Israel tena, hé chwa le Babelɔn harɛ ta, he bɛ ɡel nomɛl ba tɔ he sie, hé tɔ sie le kaa.

english_verse: In the north I am bringing great nations together. They will attack Babylon and capture it. The arrows they shoot are like the best soldiers, always finding their target.
translation_verse: Mɛɛ do harɛre nɛra baa pɛ nyoa dɛ do kpeɡrii le weekaŋle nyunduabɔr, bá bar Babelɔn tena cheme, dɛ́ yoo ba, dɛ́ pɔ ba nɛ. Ba do kɛŋɔ kpaahna baa jemɛ hɛma tae kɛrɛdɛ, baa wola tae dɛɛ kur.

english_verse: Babylonia will be conquered, and its enemies will carry off everything they want. Babylon Will Be Disgraced The Lord said:
translation_verse: Gɛɛ baa ba Babelɔn harɛ tena yoi dɛ́ pa ba laala, ásɛ bɛlbwa dɔ ɡɛ waa dɛ nyin. Men Korowiirii bola.”

english_verse: People of Babylonia, you were glad to rob my people. You had a good time, making more noise than horses and jumping around like calves threshing grain.
translation_verse: Korowii ŋɔ, “Babelɔn harɛ tena, he baa pa n nɛra laala laa ta kaa, asɛ he sie lɛ hɛɛ hɛɡre kɛŋɔ nao waa dɛ tiɡri mea, kɛɛ jaɡ-bala aa dɛ dooɡe lɔŋɔre ken.

english_verse: The city of Babylon was like a mother to you. But it will be disgraced and become nothing but a barren desert.
translation_verse: Kɛ sihiih ɛɛ kpo he bwɛjen Babelɔn tenaa, harɛ baa lolɛ heya o ta la ɛɛ di nchoo. Babelɔn harɛ ɛɛ do jeɡaa harɛre bwa binii, dɛ́ berɛ pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ, dɛ́ hol chɔ, nee kwara aa wola o taa do.

english_verse: My anger will destroy Babylon, and no one will live there. Everyone who passes by will be shocked to see what has happened.
translation_verse: N bandia nomanta, nomɛlbwa aa Babelɔn harɛ ta soɡa ba, wɛɛ berɛ dimɡbiaa, ásɛ nɛra baa teŋa baa kaa na, ba bambile teŋe ba nyoa kpo.

english_verse: Attack from every side! Babylon surrenders! The enemy tears down its walls and towers. I am taking my revenge by doing to Babylon what it did to other cities.
translation_verse: Hé pa mun ka yo bwɛjen Babelɔn tena dɛɛ do laa lɔŋɔre, Babelɔn tena sɛoh dɛ ba ba te ne harɛ, ba dekpeɡa ne danjwɛɛre bwa kuuɡo. A ɛ kembɔr men Korowii aa kpɔa dɛɛ tɛr ba deŋne, bɛlbwa ɡe tɛr ba deŋne bɔ kem. Hé ɛɛ ba ɡɛ tenten baa ɛ ba bala la.

english_verse: There is no one in Babylonia to plant or harvest crops. Even foreigners who lived there have left for their homelands, afraid of the enemy armies.
translation_verse: He bɛ ɡel ba du kwaa harɛ la ta, kɛɛ dɛ komɛ kwa. Hɔɔh bɛlbwa waa soɡe bela ɛɛ ɔmɛ laa tena baa ba yo harɛ la nɛra laanee, ásɛ dɛ bwa berɛ kaa ba harɛre ta.

english_verse: Israel is a flock of sheep scattered by hungry lions. The king of Assyria first gobbled Israel up. Then Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylonia, crunched on Israel's bones.
translation_verse: Israel tena do kɛŋɔ kondɛɛra nyujentena aa chwaa teŋɛ a nɛɛ a peɡre ken. Asiiria koojen do kɛ nyujente dɛ lawɛ Israel tena, asɛ naate waa ka mun paɡre Israel tena hoɡa laanee Babelɔn Kooro Nebukadnesa.”

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, punished the king of Assyria, and I will also punish the king of Babylonia.
translation_verse: Anomanta, Koranar Bwa Kooro, Israel tena aa dɛ tomɔ la ŋɔ, “Mɛɛ tɛr Babelɔn kooro deŋnee, dɛ́ chɔɡ o harɛ ɡe, ɡɛ maa tɛr Asiiria koojen deŋne la.

english_verse: But I will bring Israel back to its own land. The people will be like sheep eating their fill on Mount Carmel and in Bashan, in the hill country of Ephraim and in Gilead.
translation_verse: Kɛ mɛɛ berɔɔ lawɛ Israel tena ba ba harɛ ta, ásɛ ba baa di kondikwaa aa lɔ Kaamɛl Bwejen ne Basan harɛ ta. Baa di kondikwaa ɡɛ bwa baa dɛ nyin Efrem ne Gelead deŋɡarere ta.

english_verse: I will rescue a few people from Israel and Judah. I will forgive them so completely that their sin and guilt will disappear, never to be found. The Lord's Commands to the Enemies of Babylonia
translation_verse: A ɡɛ saŋ ne awola tɔpere la, baa nyiŋi waa aa ɡela Israel tena di bolchɔɡee, kɛ baa bolchɔɡe baa dia bɛlbwaa na, dɛ́ nyiŋi Juda tena ɡe wechɔɡa baa wobɛlbwaa na, dɛkalkɛ mɛɛ kpɔ n nɛra baa kaa la wechɔɡaa kɛ ba.

english_verse: The Lord said: I have told the enemies of Babylonia, “Attack the people of Merathaim and Pekod. Kill them all! Destroy their possessions!”
translation_verse: Hé ir dɛ́ yo Merataim ne Pɛkɔd tena. Hé ti ba, ásɛ dɛ kpoo ba, dɛ́ chɔɡ ba kwaraa. Hé ɛ ɡɛ maa do heyaa bwa. Men Korowiirii bola.

english_verse: Sounds of war and the noise of destruction can be heard.
translation_verse: Laa ɡbɔɡa ɡboo su harɛ la ta bwa, chɔɡa tenten ɡbɔɡaa yaa no!

english_verse: Babylonia was a hammer pounding every country, but now it lies broken. What a shock to the nations of the world!
translation_verse: Na Babelɔn o fa aa do kɛŋɔ hamba, dɛɛ paɡre harɛ nɔ bwa la aa kuuɡa ɡɛ! Na ɡɛ harɛ la bwa aa chɔ pɛɛ, asɛ harɛre nɛra bwa na ba nyoa kpo.

english_verse: Babylonia challenged me, the Lord God All-Powerful, but that nation doesn't know it is caught in a trap that I set.
translation_verse: Babelɔn tena, n harɛ heya bel, he ne ŋɔ he jemɛ dɛ o lawɛ heya, ba nyin he bɔr dɛ lawɛ heya, dɛkalkɛ he vɛh men Korowii waa la noe.

english_verse: I've brought out my weapons, and with them I will put a curse on Babylonia.
translation_verse: Men Korowii pili dea n dɔmkwa aa lɔ o bini, dɛ pa n bandia dɔmkwaa le, dɛkalkɛ men Koranar Bwa Kooro dɔ toma dɛɛ la ka ɛ Babelɔn harɛ ta.

english_verse: Come from far away, you enemies of Babylon! Pile up the grain from its storehouses, and destroy it completely, along with everything else.
translation_verse: Hé le bojaŋa dɛ́ ba yo Babelɔn tena, dɛ́ paɡre deene baa dɛ cheɡ mea a bini, dɛ́ boa a nyoa a daŋɛ, dɛ́ chɔɡa kwaraa he bɛ komɛlbwa ɡel.

english_verse: Kill the soldiers of Babylonia, because the time has come for them to be punished.
translation_verse: Hé kpoo ba laa tena bwa. Babelɔn tena bwɛɛlɛ! Ba deŋnetɛra tɔpere telo.”

english_verse: The Babylonian army destroyed my temple, but soon I will take revenge. Then refugees from Babylon will tell about it in Zion.
translation_verse: Nɛra baa chwaa le Babelɔn harɛ dɛ ba Jerusalam la dɛ bol ŋɔ, Korowii baa dɛ tomɔ la dɛ́ ba ba bɔ Babelɔn tena kem, chɔɡa baa chɔɡ Korowii Dea la wa.

english_verse: Attack Babylon, enemy archers; set up camp around the city, and don't let anyone escape. It challenged me, the holy God, so do to it what it did to other cities. Proud Babylon Will Fall
translation_verse: “Hé yerɛ nɛra baa jemɛ hɛma tae bwa bá ba yo Babelɔn tena. Hé bar bwɛjen la cheme, he bɛ ɡel bɛlbwa dɔ bɔr chwa le. Hé bɔ ba kem ɡɛ ba we-ɛɛla aa doa, ɡɛ baa kpɔa ɛ ba bala la, dɛkalkɛ ba vɛh men Korowii, Israel Nɛŋɡoroŋ la.

english_verse: People of Babylon, I, the Lord, promise that even your best soldiers will lie dead in the streets.
translation_verse: Gɛ nomanta, baa kpoo Babelɔn bonɔɔna fɔɡbaahnaa, ásɛ o laa tena bwa ɡe serewe awola tɔpere. Men Korowiirii bola.

english_verse: Babylon, you should be named, “The Proud One.” But the time has come when I, the Lord All-Powerful, will punish you.
translation_verse: Babelɔn harɛ tena, he ɛ mbarafo, men Korowii, Koranar Bwa Kooro ne he dɔɔ. Dɛkalkɛ he tɔpere telo kɛŋɔ ń tɛr he deŋne.

english_verse: You are proud, but you will stumble and fall, and no one will help you up. I will set your villages on fire, and everything around you will go up in flames.
translation_verse: He harɛ nɛra baa dɛ ɛ mbarafo la ɛɛ lɔ naa dɛ́ chole, nomɛlbwa toole dɛ́ cha heya he ir. Mɛɛ ɡeloo ba fuh he bwɛjena, ásɛ komɛlbwa aa bar heyaa cheme ɡe fuh.”

english_verse: You Babylonians were cruel to Israel and Judah. You took them captive, and now you refuse to let them go.
translation_verse: Waa Koranar Bwa Kooro aa dɛ bol laanee nɔ, “Ba dɛ fiiɡi Israel ne Juda tena. Nɛra baa laɡ ba dɛ tɔ ba ŋwɛnɛ, dɛ ŋɔ baa ɡel ba kaa.

english_verse: But I, the Lord All-Powerful, will rescue and protect them. I will bring peace to their land and trouble to yours.
translation_verse: Kɛ ba Lɛɛ la kpeɡri, o sɔne Koranar Bwa Kooro. Wɛɛ yoo kohona dɛ́ lɛɛ ba, ásɛ ba dɔ bosɔɔhna ba harɛ ta, kɛ Babelɔn tena te, ba bwaraa dɛɛ ba nyɛɡa.”

english_verse: I have declared war on you, your officials, and advisors.
translation_verse: Korowii ŋɔ, “Hé ka yo Babelɔn tena! Hé ka kpoo nɛra baa soɡe Babelɔn, ne ba nomonome, dɛ wejerema bwa!

english_verse: This war will prove that your prophets are liars and fools. And it will frighten your warriors.
translation_verse: Hé ka kpoo keame nyosonteŋna la. Ba ɡɛnɔ kohona! Hé ka kpoo ba banyoola. Ɔmee kohona chole ba nɛ.

english_verse: Then your chariot horses and the foreigners in your army will refuse to go into battle, and the enemy will carry away everything you treasure.
translation_verse: Hé chɔɡ ba jaɡre ne kwaa aa do kɛ torɔɡore la! Hé ka kpoo laa tena baa ba dɛ cha ba la bwa! Hé na ɡɛ baa ɡwɛɡra! Hé chɔɡ deene baa dɛ cheɡ laala a yoɡ aa kpeɡa a bini. Baa paa kɛŋɔ laa ta kwaa kaa.

english_verse: Your rivers and canals will dry up. All of this will happen, because your land is full of idols, and they have made fools of you.
translation_verse: Hwél che ba harɛ ta, ásɛ o neerare bwa hweeh. Voɡa aa lɔ harɛ la ta warɔ, a kpɔ ɔmee kohona ba ta harɛ la nɛra nɛɛ ba ɡɛn.

english_verse: Never again will people live in your land— only desert animals, jackals, and unclean birds.
translation_verse: Pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ olaa dɛ́ ba so Babelɔn harɛ ta, ásɛ kwiure ɡe so bela. Naanar baa ka ba bwa aa belaa ba so kpa saŋ bɛlbwa dɛɛ la.

english_verse: I destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah and the nearby towns, and I will destroy Babylon just as completely. No one will live there again. Babylonia Is Invaded The Lord said:
translation_verse: Gɛ maa chɔɡ Sodom ne Gomoora ne bwɛɛre aa bara cheme la, ɡɛɛ mɛɛ ba Babelɔn harɛ chɔɡa, ásɛ nomɛlbwa aa won so bela kpa. Men Nemenɛ Korowiirii bola.

english_verse: Far to the north, a nation and its allies have been awakened. They are powerful and ready for war.
translation_verse: Hé nyiŋi na! Laa tena le weekaŋle nyunduabɔr dɛɛ ba, harɛ o nɛra aa kana o koranar warɛ kpɔ ba te le harɛ jaɡa dɛɛ ba ba yo laa.

english_verse: Bows and arrows and swords are in their hands. The soldiers are cruel and show no pity. The hoofbeats of their horses echo like ocean waves crashing against the shore. The army has lined up for battle and is coming to attack you, people of Babylonia!
translation_verse: Ba kpoŋe tori ne lampeare, ba nyu bini kpeɡri baa wola nɛn nɛɛ sune. Ba soɡe jaɡre ta a nakpale ɛɛ si kɛŋɔ mpo nehɛma aa dɛ ta ken. Ba kpɔ ba te dɛɛ ba ba yo Babelɔn tena.

english_verse: Ever since your king heard about this army, he has been weak with fear; he twists and turns in pain like a woman giving birth.
translation_verse: Babelɔn kooro no ba wa, ɔmee ɡel o bwara yɔr. Weweele ne bambiteŋa ɡel o ɔmɛ kɛŋɔ haah loltea aa lɔɔ ken.

english_verse: Babylonia, I will attack you like a lion from the forest, attacking sheep in a meadow along the Jordan. In a moment the flock runs, and the land is empty. Who will I choose to attack you? I will do it myself! No one can force me to fight or chase me away.
translation_verse: Gɛ nyujente yon le Jɔɔdan Moo kɔr bini ba kaa harɛdɛɛɡe ta ka di la, ɡɛɛ men Korowii ɛɛ ba Babelɔn tena doŋa le ba harɛ ta. Ásɛ nomoa maa leo la tɔ ba sie dɛɛ nyiŋi ba nɛ. Umee bá won kpɔ maɡ mɛ nɔ? Nomɛlbwa aa won tɔŋle mɛ. Kooro besoo dɛ́ won che n sie nɔ?

english_verse: Listen to my plans for you, people of Babylonia. Your children will be dragged off, and your country destroyed.
translation_verse: Anomanta, hé no bwɛjen Babelɔn vɔrɔwa men Korowii aa dɛ vɔrɔwe wa. Hale ba bii bwa, baa laɡ ba laa taa kaa, ásɛ ɔmee ne bambiteŋa chole ba nɛ.

english_verse: The sounds of your destruction will be heard among the nations, and the earth will shake.
translation_verse: Babelɔn harɛ baa paɡre tonaa, harɛ ɛɛ jiɡruu, ásɛ harɛre nɛra ɛɛ no Babelɔn tena lɔŋɔre.”

english_verse: I, the Lord, am sending a wind to destroy the people of Babylonia and Babylon, its capital.
translation_verse: Waa Korowii aa dɛ bol laanee nɔ, “Mɛɛ ɡeloo peuchɔɡe waa dɛ chɔɡ kwaa ba chɔɡ Babelɔn harɛ ne o nɛra.

english_verse: Foreign soldiers will come from every direction, and when the disaster is over, Babylonia will be empty and worthless.
translation_verse: Mɛɛ tomɛ nɛŋhɔɔhraa ba ba chɔɡ Babelɔn harɛ ne o nɛra kɛŋɔ peu aa ta haahra dɛɛ kaa la ken. Awola tɔpere la, baa le baŋ bɛlbwaa ba yo o nɛra, ásɛ harɛ la chɔ pɛɛ.

english_verse: I will tell these soldiers, “Attack quickly, before the Babylonians can string their bows or put on their armor. Kill their best soldiers and destroy their army!”
translation_verse: He bɛ Babelɔn laa tena ŋwɛnɛ tɛ ba ta hɛma, kɛɛ dɛ́ kpɔ ba laa laala do. He bɛ ba bonɔɔna ɡel, hé kpoo laa tena la bwa kwaraa!

english_verse: Their troops will fall wounded in the streets of Babylon.
translation_verse: Baa do laa tena la bolaa, ásɛ ba serewe chɔ bwɛjena la fɔɡbaahna.

english_verse: Everyone in Israel and Judah is guilty. But I, the Lord All-Powerful, their holy God, have not abandoned them.
translation_verse: Men Korowii, Koranar Bwa Kooro ta n nɛra Israel ne Juda tena vɛɛh. A lole kɛŋɔ ba ɛ wechɔɡa dɛ jo men Israel Nɛŋɡoroŋ la nɛ.

english_verse: Get out of Babylon! Run for your lives! If you stay, you will be killed when I take revenge on the city and punish it for its sins.
translation_verse: Hé chwa le Babelɔn harɛ! Hé chwa lɛ he nyuune! He bɛ Babelɔn tena wechɔɡa waa koh serewe. Saŋ telo kɛ men Korowii bɔ ba kem, mɛɛ tɛr ba deŋnee ɡɛ aa chɛa.

english_verse: Babylon was my golden cup, filled with the wine of my anger. The nations of the world got drunk on this wine and went insane.
translation_verse: Babelɔn fa do kɛŋɔ suuɡaswɛm numol, dɛ do men Korowii nɔn ta, dɛ ɡel harɛre nɛra bwa nyɔ o bini sen, dɛ dɛɛ dɛ bwa ɛɛ we choɡla.

english_verse: But suddenly, Babylon will fall and be destroyed. I, the Lord, told the foreigners who lived there, “Weep for the city! Get medicine for its wounds; maybe they will heal.”
translation_verse: Babelɔn ɛɛ piɡru paɡre dɛ́ chɔɡ. Hé wi dɛɛ tɛ o nɛra! Hé nyin noo aa ɛ tɛɛɡa do ba ŋwɛra ta, a ken ɛɛ ɡeloo bá dɔ bokpeɡa.

english_verse: The foreigners answered, “We have already tried to treat Babylon's wounds, but they would not heal. Come on, let's all go home to our own countries. Nothing is left in Babylonia; everything is destroyed.”
translation_verse: Asɛ nɛŋhɔɔhra baa soɡe bela ŋɔ, ‘Ya takapɔ ŋɔ ya cha ba, kɛ a kaa mun ta. Hé ɡel ya ɡel ba waa tɛɛ ba, ásɛ bɛlbwa berɛ kaa o harɛ ta. Korowii kpɔ o kpeɡri dɛ tɛr ba deŋne dɛ chɔɡ ba kwaraa.’ ”

english_verse: I, the Lord, want Babylon destroyed, because its army destroyed my temple. So, you kings of Media, sharpen your arrows and pick up your shields.
translation_verse: Laa sitɔɔla ŋɔ, “Hé sar hɛma nyoo, dɛ́ kpɔ kwaa haa kpɔ tɔ he te ɡbemɡbe laa ta! Korowii di Midia koranar liire, dɛkalkɛ o dɛ nyin ó chɔɡ Babelɔn harɛ. Korowii koh o Dea la wa dɛɛ nyin ó bɔ ba ba wechɔɡa kem.

english_verse: People of Babylon, you live along the Euphrates River and are surrounded by canals. You are rich, but now the time has come for you to die.
translation_verse: Babelɔn tena, he nɛra haa soɡe neerare aa wara nyoo dɛ dɔ kondɔɔh kohona, he serewa telo.

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, swear by my own life that enemy soldiers will fill your streets like a swarm of locusts. They will shout and celebrate their victory. A Hymn of Praise (Jeremiah
translation_verse: Koranar Bwa Kooro ŋwɛɛ o ɡbaɡba ŋɔ, “Mɛɛ kpɔ laa tena baa wara kɛŋɔ tontombɛɛ bá yo heya, ásɛ dɛ pɔ he nɛɛ dɛɛ moo silɛɛ ne.” Korowii kpɛɛra yel

english_verse: The waters in the heavens roar at his command. He makes clouds appear; he sends the wind from his storehouse and makes lightning flash in the rain.
translation_verse: O bol wa aa, bwaala dɛ nɛ dɛɛ kɔɡre nyundujaɡla, o ɡelɔ baama aa dɛ nɛ bwaala ir dɛɛ le harɛ jaɡa. O ɡelɔ bwaala ɛɛ nɛ dɛɛ nyɛɡle, asɛ dɛ ɡel peu ta le bela waa lole.

english_verse: God used his wisdom and power to create the earth and spread out the heavens.
translation_verse: Korowii cheɡɛ o kpeɡri ta dɛ ta harɛ, o wejema nee o ta harɛ nɔ bwa, dɛ che o liire ta dɛ paɡri nyundua ɡe.

english_verse: People who make idols are stupid! They will be disappointed, because their false gods cannot breathe.
translation_verse: Nomɛlbwa ta liire dɔe, ba ɡɛnɔ, sihiih kpo nɛn waa kpɔ suuɡaswɛm kwaa o voɡare la. Kwaa waa ɛa la bwa ɛ nyosone, a ta hweera dɔe.

english_verse: Idols are merely a joke, and when the time is right, they will be destroyed.
translation_verse: A waa ta tɔnɔ bɛlbwa dɔe, dɛ ɛ kwaa a wa aa dɔ wesoma. A chɔɡa saŋ telo Korowii ba naa, wɛɛ chɔɡ a bwaa.

english_verse: But the Lord, Israel's God, is all-powerful. He created everything, and he chose Israel to be his very own. God's Hammer The Lord said:
translation_verse: Kɛ Korowii Israel tena aa dɛ tomɔ la ta do kɛ ban, dɛkalkɛ onee ta komɛlbwa, dɛ le Israel tena tɛ o te, dɛ kpɔ ba ɛ o kapɛrɛ nɛra. Koranar Bwa Kooroo o sɔn.

english_verse: as well as men and women, young and old,
translation_verse: Henee n kpɔ kpoo haahna ne baala, ne banjeni dɛ bonɔɔna, hale bonɔmbie ne toli bwa.
