english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Korowii ŋɔ men Ɛsekeɛl be ŋɔ,

english_verse: Ezekiel, I hear the people of Israel using the old saying, “Sour grapes eaten by parents leave a sour taste in the mouths of their children.”
translation_verse: “Ɛrɛɛ hɛɛ lii sɛɡla haa dɛ sɛɡle Israel harɛ ta ŋɔ, ‘Nya ne mɛɛ di ɡrepo nɔnnyɛɡa, asɛ ba bii nyena nyɛɡ nɔɔ?’ ”

english_verse: Now tell them that I am the Lord God, and as surely as I live, that saying will no longer be used in Israel.
translation_verse: Nemenɛ Korowii ŋɔ, “N ŋwɛɛrɔ kɛŋɔ n taa lole nɔ, haa ɡɛ sɛɡla nɔɔ sɛɡle Israel harɛ ta kpa.

english_verse: The lives of all people belong to me—parents as well as children. However, only those who sin will be put to death.
translation_verse: Nɛwɛnyina bwa nyu lɔ n nɔn ta, mɛɛ kɛɛ bie bwa nyu lɔ n nɔn ta. Naate waa ɛ wechɔɡa la, naatee dɛ́ sewɛ.

english_verse: Suppose there is a truly good man who always does what is fair and right.
translation_verse: Dɛ nomɛl we-ɛɛla toɡrɔ wɛɛ ɛ waa aa dɔ kasinteŋ o waa do wer,

english_verse: He refuses to eat meat sacrificed to foreign gods at local shrines or to worship Israel's idols. He doesn't have sex with someone else's wife or with a woman having her monthly period.
translation_verse: waa kwaa Israel tena aa kpoora dɛɛ tɛ ba voɡa bwejena dor la di, waa ba voɡa ɡe tomɛ, kɛɛ waa o dɔŋ haah lawɛ dɛɛ chɔ, waa haah waa le dahara nyin,

english_verse: He never cheats or robs anyone and always returns anything taken as security for a loan; he gives food and clothes to the poor
translation_verse: waa nomɛlbwa fiiɡi, o berɛ nomɛlbwa kon waa lɛa cheɡ mɔɔ dɛ kemɔ suuɡa la dɛɛ tɛo. Waa ŋwɛ, lɔr dɛ kpo nɛn aa, o dɛ tɛo kwaa wɛɛ di, nomɛlbwa waa wola yal dɔe la, o dɛ tɛo.

english_verse: and doesn't charge interest when lending money. He refuses to do anything evil; he is fair to everyone
translation_verse: Waa suuɡa kemɛ dɛɛ lɛ a nee dɛɛ ja. Waa wechɔɡa ɛ, o dɛ bol kasinteŋ nɛn ne o dɔŋ baah waa ta.

english_verse: and faithfully obeys my laws and teachings. This man is good, and I promise he will live.
translation_verse: Nɛn waa do ɡɛ nɔɔ dɛɛ teŋɛ me Mmarare ta kɛrɛdɛ. O waa toɡrɔ, wɛɛ dɔ o nyuu kɛrɛdɛ. Men Nemenɛ Korowiirii bola.

english_verse: But suppose this good man has an evil son who is violent and commits sins
translation_verse: Dɛ nɛn o wa aa toɡra dɔ bichɔɡe wɛɛ kpoo nɛra, kɛɛ wɛɛ ɛ a ɡɛ waa nɔ bini bɛlbwa

english_verse: his father never did. He eats meat at local shrines, has sex with someone else's wife,
translation_verse: o mɛɛ aa wola ane ɛɛ ka, kɛ o te ɛɛ di kwaa baa kpoora voɡare ta bwejena dor, dɛ lawɛ o bala haahna dɛɛ chɔ,

english_verse: cheats the poor, and robs people. He keeps what is given to him as security for a loan. He worships idols, does disgusting things,
translation_verse: dɛɛ faah nyaara, dɛɛ ŋwɛ. O kemɛ nɛn suuɡa dɛ lɛ kon cheɡ naate ta kem la ba bɔe yaa. Waa naate kon kpɔe dɛɛ tɛo. O dɛ tomɛ voɡa maa kia la.

english_verse: and charges high interest when lending money. An evil man like that will certainly not live. He is the one who has done these horrible sins, so it's his own fault that he will be put to death.
translation_verse: O kemɛ o dɔŋ suuɡa aa, o dɛ lɛ a nee aa ɡwaa. A chɛ kɛ a ɡɛ nɛn nɔ so harɛ nɔ ta naa? Akai! O dɛ ɛ waa baa kia nɔ bwa, a chɛ kɛŋɔ á ɡure o nyu ta, bá kpoo.

english_verse: But suppose this evil man has a son who sees his father do these things and refuses to act like him.
translation_verse: Dɛ a ɡɛ nɛnchɔɡe nɔ dɔ bie, o na wechɔɡa o mɛɛ aa dɛ ɛ bwa, dɛ ɔmɛ o ta ɡɛ ɛɛ.

english_verse: He doesn't eat meat at local shrines or worship Israel's idols, and he doesn't have sex with someone else's wife.
translation_verse: Waa kwaa Israel tena aa dɛ kpoora dɛɛ tɛ ba voɡa bwejena dor la di, kɛɛ dɛɛ tomɛ voɡa. Waa o dɔŋ haah lawɛ dɛɛ chɔ,

english_verse: He never cheats or robs anyone and doesn't even demand security for a loan. He gives food and clothes to the poor
translation_verse: kɛɛ waa nomɛlbwa fiiɡi, o kemɛ nɛn suuɡa aa waa kon lɛɛ dɛɛ cheɡ o buɡ ta. Waa ŋwɛ, o dɛ tɛ nɛn lɔr aa dɛ kpoo kondikwa, dɛɛ tɔ nɛn waa wola yal dɔe yal.

english_verse: and refuses to do anything evil or to charge interest. And he obeys all my laws and teachings. Such a man will live. His own father sinned, but this good man will not be put to death for the sins of his father.
translation_verse: Waa wechɔɡa ɛ, o kemɛ nɛn suuɡa aa, waa a nee lɛ. O dɛ teŋɛ me Mmarare bwa ta. O mɛɛ wechɔɡa la aa won ɡel o dɔ seo, wɛɛ dɔ o nyuu kɛrɛdɛ.

english_verse: It is his father who will die for cheating and robbing and doing evil.
translation_verse: O mɛɛ te, o ɛɡre o bala dɛ lɛ ba kwa, dɛ ɛ o nɛra wechɔɡa, wɛɛ sewɔɔ.

english_verse: You may wonder why a son isn't punished for the sins of his father. It is because the son does what is right and obeys my laws.
translation_verse: He dɛ bɔɔ ŋɔ, ‘Ɛrɛɛ aa wola chɛɛ kɛŋɔ bie dɔ deŋnetɛra o mɛɛ wechɔɡa waɔ?’ Bie la waa toɡrɔ dɛ do wer, o teŋɛ me Mmarare la ta kɛrɛdɛ ken, anomanta, wɛɛ dɔ o nyuu kɛrɛdɛ.

english_verse: Only those who sin will be put to death. Children won't suffer for the sins of their parents, and parents won't suffer for the sins of their children. Good people will be rewarded for what they do, and evil people will be punished for what they do.
translation_verse: Naate waa dɛ ɛ wechɔɡa laanee dɛɛ sewɛ. Bie ta chɛ kɛ ó na wa o mɛɛ wechɔɡa wa, mɛɛ ɡe ta chɛ kɛ ó na wa o bie wechɔɡa wa. Nomɛlbwa o waa aa toɡra wɛɛ ɛ wedɛɛɡa dɛ́ dɔ andɛɛɡa, nomɛlbwa waa dɛ ɛ wechɔɡa ɡe, wechɔɡaa dɛɛ teŋɛ o nɛ.

english_verse: Suppose wicked people stop sinning and start obeying my laws and doing right. They won't be put to death.
translation_verse: Kɛ dɛ wechɔɡ-ɛɛ ɡel wechɔɡa waa ɛa, dɛɛ teŋɛ me Mmarare bwa ta, dɛɛ ɛ anɔ la aa toɡra dɛ do wer aa, wɛɛ dɔ o nyuu kɛrɛdɛ, waa sewɛ.

english_verse: All their sins will be forgiven, and they will live because they did right.
translation_verse: Mɛɛ kpɔ naate wechɔɡa bwaa kɛo, maa an lii kpa, dɛkalkɛ o waa toɡrɔ. Wɛɛ so lee, waa sewa ba.

english_verse: I, the Lord God, don't like to see wicked people die. I had much rather see them turn back from their sins and live.
translation_verse: He dɛ lii kɛ n sie dɛ lɛ wechɔɡ-ɛɛ seo ta kɛɛ? Akai, n sie aa a ta lɛ. Ó le o wechɔɡa ta, dɛ́ dɔ o nyuu mɛɛ nyin.

english_verse: But when good people start sinning and doing disgusting things, will they live? No! All their good deeds will be forgotten, and they will be put to death because of their sins.
translation_verse: Dɛ nɛn o wa aa toɡra le o wedɛɛɡa ɛɛ ta, dɛ ka ɛ wechɔɡa ne waa maa kia wechɔɡ-ɛɛra ɛɛ ɛa la aa, wɛɛ dɔ o nyuu yaa? Maa o wedɛɛɡa waa ɛa wubwa la bɛlbwaa lii. O kasinteŋ bɛ dɔe ne wechɔɡa waa ɛa la taa wɛɛ ba sewa.

english_verse: You people of Israel accuse me of being unfair! But listen—I'm not unfair; you are!
translation_verse: Kɛ he dɛ bol ŋɔ, men Korowii waa ta toɡrɛ. Israel tena, hé no, he dɛ lii kɛŋɔ men Korowii n waa ta toɡrɛ kɛɛ? He waa laa wola toɡraa?

english_verse: If good people start doing evil, they must be put to death, because they have sinned.
translation_verse: Dɛ nɛn o wa aa toɡra le wedɛɛɡa ɛɛ ta dɛ ka ɛ wechɔɡa aa, wɛɛ sewɔɔ. O wechɔɡa waa ɛa la waa wɛɛ ba sewa.

english_verse: And if wicked people start doing right, they will save themselves from punishment.
translation_verse: Kɛ dɛ wechɔɡ-ɛɛ charɛ o liire le wechɔɡa waa ɛa ta, dɛɛ ɛ anɔ la aa wera dɛ toɡre aa, wɛɛ dɔ o nyuu.

english_verse: They will think about what they've done and stop sinning, and so they won't be put to death.
translation_verse: O na wechɔɡa waa ɛa dɛ le a ta, wɛɛ dɔ o nyuu kɛrɛdɛ, waa wola sewɛ.

english_verse: But you still say that I am unfair. You are the ones who have done wrong and are unfair!
translation_verse: Kɛ he Israel tena dɛ bol ŋɔ, ‘Men Korowii ŋwɛnɛ ta toɡrɛ.’ He ŋwɛnɛree wola toɡrɛ.

english_verse: I will judge each of you for what you've done. So stop sinning, or else you will certainly be punished.
translation_verse: Anomanta, he Israel tena, mɛɛ bol he waa beŋkpoŋa beŋkpoŋaa ɡɛ haa ɛa. Hé charɛ he liire le he wechɔɡa bwa ta, dɛ bɛ naa a ta lɔ. Men Nemenɛ Korowiirii bola.

english_verse: Give up your evil ways and start thinking pure thoughts. And be faithful to me! Do you really want to be put to death for your sins?
translation_verse: Hé laa he te kpɔ wechɔɡa bɛlbwa ta, dɛ́ dɔ bambidɛɛɡe ne liifala dɛɛ teŋɛ n waa ta. Israel tena, ɛrɛɛ hɛɛ nyin kɛ he serewe nɔɔ?

english_verse: I, the Lord God, don't want to see that happen to anyone. So stop sinning and live!
translation_verse: N sie aa lɛ kɛ nomɛlbwa sewɛ. Hé charɛ he liire, ásɛ dɛ dɔ he nyu! Men Nemenɛ Korowiirii bola.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, sing a funeral song for two of Israel's leaders:
translation_verse: Korowii ŋɔ men Ɛsekeɛl be ŋɔ, “Go suna dii yel nɔ tɛ Israel koranar banɛ

english_verse: Your mother was a brave lioness who raised her cubs among lions.
translation_verse: dɛ ŋɔ, ‘Na ɡɛ he nya aa do kɛŋɔ nyujente nee! O dɛɛ o bii nyujentena ambala aa do ɔma baah.

english_verse: She taught one of them to hunt, and he learned to eat people.
translation_verse: O dɛɛ bii la bɛl o kpeɡ, dɛ baɡlo kpaahna, o lawɛ nɛra dɛɛ chwe.

english_verse: When the nations heard of him, they trapped him in a pit, then they used hooks to drag him to Egypt.
translation_verse: Harɛre ta nɛra no o wa, dɛ harɔ bel a bɔɔ bini dɛ lawɔ. Ba doo kwaa kɛŋɔ ɡoŋa dɛ tɛɡro kaa Ijipt harɛ ta.

english_verse: His mother waited for him to return. But soon she lost all hope and raised another cub, who also became fierce.
translation_verse: O nya la nyiŋu ŋwɛnɛ, o hwɛɡa bwa tonɛ. Ate, o berɛ dɛɛ bii la bɛl ja o kpeɡ dɛ do ɔma.

english_verse: He destroyed fortresses and ruined towns; his mighty roar terrified everyone.
translation_verse: O kuuɡi ba dekpeɡa dɛ chɔɡ ba bwɛɛre. O sio waa, dɛ ɔmee kohona chole harɛ la ta nɛra nɛ.

english_verse: Nations plotted to kill him, and people came from all over to spread out a net and catch him in a trap.
translation_verse: Belaa harɛre nɛra pɛ dɛ ba yoo. Nɛra le bobɛlbwa dɛ ta ba asauri baro dɛ lawɔ.

english_verse: They put him in a cage and took him to Babylonia. The lion was locked away, so that his mighty roar would never again be heard on Israel's hills.
translation_verse: Ba kpɔ ɡoŋa lawɔ, dɛ doo buo bini ka tɛ Babelɔn kooro. Ba doo dea, baa o sii no Israel deŋɡarere ta kpa.

english_verse: Your mother was a vine like you, growing near a stream. There was plenty of water, so she was filled with branches and with lots of fruit.
translation_verse: He nya fa do kɛŋɔ ɡrepo daa dɛ che nee nyoa. Nee aa lɔ bela kohona nomanta, o dɔ papooni kɛrɛdɛ dɛ won nɔna ɡe.

english_verse: Her strong branches became symbols of authority, and she was taller than all other trees— everyone could see how strong and healthy she was.
translation_verse: O kpala kpeɡri dɛ do wer kɛ bá kpɔ ɛ kooro daŋɡbala. O kpeɡo tɛr kaa nyundua baama bini, nɛra na ɡɛ waa kpeɡa dɛ dɔ papooni kohona.

english_verse: But in anger, I pulled her up by the roots and threw her to the ground, where the scorching desert wind dried out her fruit. Her strong branches wilted and burned up.
translation_verse: Ba baah di o nɛɛ kohona, dɛ huɡru ɡo. Wee leebɔr peuwɔb tao dɛ ɡel o kpala la ne o nɔna la hol, nii fuh a bwa.

english_verse: Then she was planted in a hot, dry desert,
translation_verse: Taraken, pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ taa ba ka chɔɔro, harɛ waa hola nee aa wola toole o ta.

english_verse: where her stem caught fire, and flames burned her branches and fruit. Not one strong branch is left; she is stripped bare. This funeral song must be sung with sorrow.
translation_verse: Nii le o kpale la bɛl ta dɛ fuh o ne o nɔna la bwa. Daa la kpale bɛlbwa toole dɛ do kpeɡri bá kpɔ ɛ koodaŋɡbala kpa.’ Wii aa chɛ kɛŋɔ bá wi laanee la.”

english_verse: Seven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, some of Israel's leaders came to me on the tenth day of the fifth month. They sat down and asked for a message from the Lord.
translation_verse: Gɛ saŋ baa lawɛ yaa laa ta kaa Babelɔn bene anuanɛ, korobie anue tɔpera fi ta la, Israel nomonome la bane balɔ, dɛ ba so men Ɛsekeɛl sie dɛɛ nyin dɛ́ jemɛ waa aa le Korowii be.

english_verse: Just then, the Lord God said:
translation_verse: Belaa Korowii bol waa n be ŋɔ,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, these leaders have come to find out what I want them to do. As surely as I live, I will not give them an answer of any kind.
translation_verse: “Nɛwɛnyini bie, ŋɔ Israel nomonome la be kɛŋɔ men Nemenɛ Korowii ŋɔ, ‘He balɔ dɛ́ ba bɔɔ dɛ́ na waa aa le n be kɛɛ? N ŋwɛɛrɔ kɛŋɔ maa lole saŋ bɛlbwa nɔ, maa ɡel he pɛɛ mɛ wobɛlbwa. Men Nemenɛ Korowiirii bola.’

english_verse: Are you willing to warn them, Ezekiel? Then remind them of the disgusting sins of their ancestors.
translation_verse: Nɛwɛnyini bie, he dɛ nyin kɛ he pa ba bolchɔɡe kɛɛ? Ate, lii ba ba naawa kii waa baa ɛa la wa

english_verse: Tell them that long ago I, the Lord God, chose Israel to be my own. I appeared to their ancestors in Egypt and made a solemn promise that I would be their God and the God of their descendants.
translation_verse: dɛ́ ŋɔ Israel tena be ŋɔ men Nemenɛ Korowii bolɔ ŋɔ, ‘Awola maa le Israel tena tɛ n te la, n ir nɔn dɛ ŋwɛɛ baɡle Jekɔb naanar, dɛ kpɔ n te baɡ ba Ijipt harɛ ta kɛ menee Korowii baa dɛ tom mɛ la.

english_verse: I swore that I would rescue them from Egypt and lead them to a land I had already chosen. This land was rich with milk and honey and was the most splendid land of all.
translation_verse: N berɔ ŋwɛɛ baɡ ba kɛŋɔ mɛɛ kpɔ baa le Ijipt harɛ ta ba harɛ maa nyina cheɡ ba ta, o ɛ harɛpare ondɛɛɡe ɡwaa harɛre bwa.

english_verse: I told them to get rid of their disgusting idols and not to sin by worshiping the gods of Egypt. I reminded them that I was the Lord their God,
translation_verse: N ŋɔ bá pa ba voɡa maa kia la ta, ba bɛ Ijipt harɛ ta voɡa nɛɛ teŋɛ, dɛ́ kpɔ doŋa kah ba te. Menee Korowii baa dɛ tom mɛ.’

english_verse: but they still rebelled against me. They refused to listen and kept on worshiping their idols and foreign gods. In my anger, I decided to punish the Israelites in Egypt.
translation_verse: Kɛ Israel tena ɛɛ mɛ deŋnekpeɡ, baa n waa no, ba ta voɡa la pae ta, ba ta Ijipt tena voɡare maa kia la ɡe ta leɛ. Anomanta, n ŋɔ mɛɛ kpɔ n bandiaa ba ta ba nɛɛ Ijipt harɛ ta.

english_verse: But that would have made me look like a liar, because I had already promised in front of everyone that I would lead them out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Gɛ aa ɛ ásɛ harɛre baa soɡe a ta nɛra bɛ n sɔnchɔɡe yerɛ ŋɔ n bolɔ ŋɔ, mɛɛ lawɛ Israel tenaa le Ijipt harɛ ta nomanta, n ta ɡɛ ɛɛ.

english_verse: So I brought them out and led them into the desert.
translation_verse: Ate, n tɔ ba sie dɛ le ba ne Ijipt harɛ ta, dɛ ba bane pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta.

english_verse: I gave them my laws and teachings, so they would know how to live right.
translation_verse: N kpɔ n waa tɛɛ ba dɛ baɡ ba me Mmarare, ásɛ nomɛlbwa waa teŋɛ a ta la, ó dɔ mkpa.

english_verse: And I commanded them to respect the Sabbath as a way of showing that they were holy and belonged to me.
translation_verse: N ŋɔ baa di Ona Tɔpera la a ɛ fɔo dɛ́ chɔ n ne ba baah, dɛ́ lii kɛŋɔ men Korowiirii ɛɛ ba ba do ɡoroŋ.

english_verse: But the Israelites rebelled against me in the desert. They refused to obey my laws and teachings, and they treated the Sabbath like any other day. Then in my anger, I decided to destroy the Israelites in the desert once and for all.
translation_verse: Kɛ ane a bwa, ba ɛɛ mɛ deŋnekpeɡ pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta bela. Ba ta n waa ta teŋɛ, dɛ vɛh me Mmarare nomɛlbwa fe aa teŋɛ a ta ásɛ dɛ fe dɔ mkpa la. Ba chɔɡ Ona Tɔpera la. Anomanta, n ŋɔ mɛɛ kpɔ n bandia ba ta ba nɛɛ kohona, dɛ́ chɔɡ ba bwa pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta bela.

english_verse: But that would have disgraced me, because many other nations had seen me bring the Israelites out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Kɛ maa dɛ nyin n sɔndɛɛɡe nomanta, n ɡelɔ ásɛ harɛre ta nɛra baa lɔ bela dɛ na kɛŋɔ, n laɡ ba le Ijipt harɛ ta la bɛ n sɔnchɔɡe yerɛ.

english_verse: Instead, I told them in the desert that I would not lead them into the beautiful, fertile land I had promised.
translation_verse: N berɔ ir nɔn pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta bela, dɛ ŋwɛɛ baɡ ba kɛŋɔ, maa ban kpɔ ba harɛ maa kpɔa tɛɛ ba la ta, harɛpare ondɛɛɡe dɛ ɡwaa harɛ bɛlbwa,

english_verse: I said this because they had not only ignored my laws and teachings, but had disgraced my Sabbath and worshiped idols.
translation_verse: dɛkalkɛŋɔ, ba vɛh me Mmarare, ba ta n waa ta teŋɛ, dɛ chɔɡ Ona Tɔpera la. Ba liire bwa lɔ ba voɡare ta.

english_verse: Yet, I felt sorry for them and could not let them die in the desert.
translation_verse: N na ba sum, n ta ban chɔɡɛ kɛɛ dɛ kpoo ba pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta bela.

english_verse: So I warned the children not to act like their parents or follow their evil ways or worship their idols.
translation_verse: N bol ba bii be pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta bela ŋɔ, ‘Hé nyiŋi kɛrɛdɛ dɛ bɛ he naawa we-ɛɛla kɛɛ mmarare kɛɛ ba voɡa nɛɛ teŋɛ, dɛ́ kpɔ doŋa kah he te.

english_verse: I reminded them that I was the Lord their God and that they should obey my laws and teachings.
translation_verse: Menee Korowii haa dɛ tom mɛ la, hɛɛ teŋɛ n waa ne me Mmarare maa kpɔa tɛ heyaa la ta kɛrɛdɛ.

english_verse: I told them to respect my Sabbath to show that they were my people and that I was the Lord their God.
translation_verse: Hɛ́ɛ di n Ona Tɔpera la, dɛ́ ɡel a do ɡoroŋ, ásɛ a ɛ waa dɛ chɔ n ne he baah ta. Anee dɛ́ ɡel he jemɛ kɛŋɔ menee Korowii haa dɛ tom mɛ la.’

english_verse: But the children also rebelled against me. They refused to obey my laws and teachings, and they treated the Sabbath as any other day. I became angry and decided to punish them in the desert.
translation_verse: Ba bii la ɡe ɛɛ mɛ deŋnekpeɡ. Bɛlbwa ta n waa ne me Mmarare la ta teŋɛ kɛrɛdɛ, a lole kɛŋɔ anee fe dɛ́ ɡel ba dɔ mkpa. Ba chɔɡ n Ona Tɔpera la. Asɛ n ŋɔ mɛɛ kpɔ n bandia kohonaa ba ta ba nɛ pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta bela, dɛ́ tɛr ba deŋne.

english_verse: But I did not. That would have disgraced me in front of the nations that had seen me bring the Israelites out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Ate, n berɛ lawɛ bambile, dɛkalkɛ aa chɔɡ n sɔnee harɛre nɛra baa naa n lawɛ Israel tena le Ijipt harɛ ta, ba siwi ta la.

english_verse: So I solemnly swore that I would scatter the people of Israel across the nations,
translation_verse: N berɔ ir nɔn, dɛ ŋwɛɛ baɡ ba pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta bela kɛŋɔ, mɛɛ lɔ baa peɡre harɛ nɔ ta bwa,

english_verse: because they had disobeyed my laws and ignored my teachings; they had disgraced my Sabbath and worshiped the idols their ancestors had made.
translation_verse: dɛkalkɛ ba vɛh n wa, ne me Mmarare maa kpɔa tɛɛ ba la ta teŋa, dɛ chɔɡ n Ona Tɔpera la, dɛ tomɛ voɡa la tenten ba naawa aa toma la.

english_verse: I gave them laws that bring punishment instead of life,
translation_verse: N ɡelɔ baa ɛ waa aa wola ban cha, dɛ tɛɛ ba mmarare aa wola ɡel ba dɔ mkpa.

english_verse: and I let them offer me unacceptable sacrifices, including their first-born sons. I did this to horrify them and to let them know that I, the Lord, was punishing them.
translation_verse: N ɡelɔ ba kpɔ ba bibanloɡla ɛ sarahare dɛ kah doŋa, n ɛ ɡɛ dɛ kpɔ ɔmee kohona ta ba nɛɛ ba chel, ásɛ ba jemɛ kɛŋɔ menee Korowii.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, tell the people of Israel that their ancestors also rejected and insulted me
translation_verse: Nemenɛ Korowii berɔ ŋɔ men Ɛsekeɛl be ŋɔ “Nɛwɛnyini bie, berɛ ŋɔ Israel tena be kɛŋɔ, anɔ ɡe taa ba naawa ɛɛ mɛ nɛnhɛlwa dɛ le n habɔɔ.

english_verse: by offering sacrifices, incense, and wine to gods on every hill and under every large tree. I was very angry, because they did these things in the land I had given them!
translation_verse: N laɡ ba ba harɛ maa ŋwɛɛra ŋɔ mɛɛ kpɔɔ tɛɛ ba la ta. Ba baa na deŋɡarejaŋa ne dajena aa dɔ papooni kohona dɛ ka ɛ sarahare bela. N baah di daawiile baa fuah a sɔɔh do som, ne sen sarahare baa ɛa tɛ voɡa la ta.

english_verse: I asked them where they went to worship those gods, and they answered, “At the local shrines.” And those places of worship are still called shrines.
translation_verse: Ate, n bɔɔ ba ŋɔ, ‘Bɔkwaa he kaa ɛ deŋɡarejena nɔ ta bela ɔ?’ Ba dɛ yerɛ bela ‘Bama’ ba le fini.

english_verse: by worshiping idols and by sacrificing their own children as offerings. They commit these sins and still think they can ask me for a message. As surely as I am the living Lord God, I will give them no answer.
translation_verse: Ba le fini, he ta lawɛ he bii kaa ɛ sarahare voɡa la ta baa fuuh ba, dɛ kpɔ doŋa dɛɛ kah he te. He ta teŋɔ dɛɛ nyin waa dɛ́ no le n be. N ŋwɛɛrɔ kɛŋɔ Men Nemenɛ Korowii taa lole nɔ, maa ɡel he pɛɛ wobɛlbwa le n be.

english_verse: They may think they can be like other nations and get away with worshiping idols made of wood and stone. But that will never happen! The Lord Promises To Restore Israel The Lord said to the people of Israel:
translation_verse: He ɛ he liire kɛŋɔ he fee do ɡɛ harɛre nɛra bane aa doa, dɛɛ tomɛ voɡa baa kpɔ daa ne bwea ɛa. Aa ɡɛɛ maɡre.

english_verse: As surely as I am the living Lord God, I will rule over you with my powerful arm. You will feel my fierce anger
translation_verse: Men Nemenɛ Korowii, n ŋwɛɛrɔ kɛŋɔ n taa lole nɔ, mɛɛ che n kpeɡri taa dɛ́ ir nɔn tɛr he deŋne n bandia ne,

english_verse: and my power, when I gather you from the places where you are scattered
translation_verse: dɛ́ lawɛ heyaa le harɛre haa peɡra dɛ ka so a ta la ta, dɛ́ berɛ ba he ne.

english_verse: and lead you into a desert surrounded by nations. I will meet you there face to face. Then I will pass judgment on you
translation_verse: Mɛɛ ba he ne pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ harɛre aa baro la taa, n ne he sie ɡba dɔŋa, ń bol he waa dɛ́ tɛr he deŋne.

english_verse: and punish you, just as I punished your ancestors in the desert near Egypt.
translation_verse: Gɛ maa bol he naawa wa dɛ pa ba bole Sinai pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta la, ɡɛɛ mɛɛ ba heyaa ɛɛ. Men Nemenɛ Korowiirii bola.

english_verse: I will force each of you to obey the regulations of our solemn agreement.
translation_verse: Mɛɛ do sie he bee kɛrɛdɛ, ásɛ hɛɛ teŋɛ fɔo waa chɔ n ne he baah ta la.

english_verse: I will separate the sinful rebels from the rest of you, and even though I will bring them from the nations where they live in exile, they won't be allowed to return to Israel. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Mɛɛ lawɛ deŋnekpeɡ tena baa lɔ he bini nɔɔ le bela baa soɡa taraken nɔ. Maa ɡel ba naa tire Israel harɛ. Ásɛ he jemɛ kɛŋɔ menee Korowii.’ ”

english_verse: Go ahead and worship your idols for now, you Israelites, because soon I will no longer let you dishonor me by offering gifts to them. You will have no choice but to obey me!
translation_verse: Nemenɛ Korowii ŋɔ, “Israel tena, hé dɛ nyin kaala ka tomɛ he voɡare aa, hé kaa. Kɛ n dɛ ŋɔ he be ŋɔ a habɔɔ la, hɛɛ baa teŋɛ n waa taa dɛ́ ɡel sarahare ka ɛɛ he voɡare ta, dɛɛ chɔɡ n sɔn waa do ɡoroŋ, dɛɛ duu mɛ.

english_verse: When that day comes, everyone in Israel will worship me on Mount Zion, my holy mountain in Jerusalem. I will once again call you my own, and I will accept your sacred offerings and sacrifices.
translation_verse: Saayɔn Bwejen waa do ɡoroŋ dɛ do Jerusalam la taa he Israel tena la bwa ɛɛ ba men toma. Belaa mɛɛ ba he saraha kwaa aa do ɡoroŋ, ne anɔ la aa le he bambile ta he kpɔ dɛɛ ba ba tɛ mɛ la lɛɛ. Men Korowiirii bola.

english_verse: When I bring you home from the places where you are now scattered, I will be pleased with you, just as I am pleased with the smell of the smoke from your sacrifices. Every nation on earth will see that I am holy,
translation_verse: Mɛɛ lɛ heyaa kɛŋɔ daawiile a sɔɔh aa soma he yon kpɔ ɛ saraha dɛɛ tɛ mɛ la, mɛɛ boa he nyoa le harɛre haa peɡra kaa a ta la, ásɛ harɛre nɛra na kɛŋɔ n do ɡoroŋ.

english_verse: and you will know that I, the Lord, am the one who brought you back to Israel, the land I promised your ancestors.
translation_verse: Maa ba he ne Israel harɛ ta la, anee hɛɛ ba jema kɛŋɔ menee Korowii haa dɛ tom mɛ la, harɛ maa ir nɔn dɛ ŋwɛɛ ŋɔ mɛɛ kpɔɔ tɛ he naawa la.

english_verse: Then you will remember your wicked sins, and you will hate yourselves for doing such horrible things. They have made you unacceptable to me,
translation_verse: Belaa hɛɛ ba we-ɛɛla ne liire aa ɡela he kpɔ he te kah doŋa la nae, ásɛ he hah he ɡbaɡba kɛŋɔ haa ɛ a ɡɛ wedoŋa nɔ la.

english_verse: so you deserve to be punished. But I will treat you in a way that will bring honor to my name, and you will know that I am the Lord God. Fire from the South
translation_verse: N koh n sɔndɛɛɡe waa dɛ ɛ waane aa, hɛɛ jemɔɔ kɛŋɔ menee Korowii, dɛkalkɛ maa heyaa ɛ ɡɛ aa chɛ kɛŋɔ bá ɛ wechɔɡ-ɛɛra. Men Nemenɛ Korowiirii bola dɛɛ baɡle he Israel tena bwa.” Korowii bol weekaŋle harɛbɔr tena chɔɡa wa

english_verse: “Ezekiel, son of man, turn toward the south and warn the forests
translation_verse: “Nɛwɛnyini bie, kpɔ sie pa weekaŋle harɛbɔr dɛ́ bol waa aa dɛ ba kɔr la ta bala.

english_verse: that I, the Lord God, will start a fire that will burn up every tree, whether green or dry. Nothing will be able to put out the blaze of that fire as it spreads to the north and burns everything in its path.
translation_verse: Bol kɔr la be ŋɔ men Nemenɛ Korowii ŋɔ, ‘Cheɡ deŋne dɛ no! N dɛ ba ɡela nii ba fuih, ásɛ dɛ chɔɡ he daa bwa, anɔ la aa hola ne anlwɛɛne bwa. Nomɛlbwa toole dɛ́ won dime nii la. Aa le weekaŋle harɛbɔree dɛ́ fuh ba kaa weekaŋle nyunduabɔr, ásɛ a nyaa nomɛlbwa.

english_verse: Everyone will know that I started it, and that it cannot be stopped.”
translation_verse: Nomɛlbwa ɛɛ nao kɛŋɔ men Korowiirii do nii la, bɛlbwa aa wola won dima bwa.’ ”

english_verse: But I complained, “Lord God, I don't want to do that! People already say I confuse them with my messages.”
translation_verse: Belaa men Ɛsekeɛl ŋɔ, “Nemenɛ Korowii, ba dɛ bol n waa ŋɔ baa waa maa dɛ bol nɔ mun no, a do kɛŋɔ molbie.”

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Korowii bol men Ɛsekeɛl be ŋɔ,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the places in Jerusalem where people worship. Warn everyone in Israel
translation_verse: “Nɛwɛnyini bie, eɡle sie ta Jerusalam tena nɛ, dɛ́ bol ba be ŋɔ, bɔra baa dɛ tom mɛ a ta la aa were. Kah Israel harɛ ta tena ŋɔ,

english_verse: that I am about to punish them. I will pull out my sword and have it ready to kill everyone, whether good or evil.
translation_verse: n ne ba dɔɔ. Mɛɛ pamɛ n keree le o tɔɔ ta, dɛ́ kpoo nɛra ba wa aa toɡra ne wechɔɡ-ɛɛra bwa.

english_verse: Ezekiel, groan in sorrow and despair so that everyone can hear you.
translation_verse: Anomanta, Nɛwɛnyini bie, ɡel he bambile chɔɡ he loo ku kohona hɛɛ hime, ásɛ nɛra bwa nae.

english_verse: When they ask why you are groaning, tell them you have terrifying news that will make them faint and tremble in fear and lose all courage. These things will happen soon. I, the Lord God, make this promise! A Sword Is Ready To Attack Israel
translation_verse: Dɛ ba bɔɔre ŋɔ, ‘Ɛrɛɛ he bambile chɔɡ hɛɛ hime kohona naa’, ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, ‘Waa a taa lɔ sie dɛɛ ba bala waa. Ɔmee ɛɛ lawɛ nomɛlbwa kohonaa ba bwara ɛɛ sa, ba bambile chɔɡ, ba bwara yɔr.’ A dɛ ba bala. Aa bao ɡe. Men Nemenɛ Korowiirii bola.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Jerusalem: I have sharpened my sword to slaughter you; it is shiny and will flash like lightning! Don't celebrate— punishment is coming, because everyone has ignored my warnings.
translation_verse: N saro dɛ́ kpɔ kpo. O dɛ nyɛɡle kɛŋɔ bwaala nyɛɡla ken! Silɛɛ bɛlbwa aa n nɛra nɛɛ doe ba, dɛkalkɛ ba ta kaeh maa kah ba la ne n deŋnetɛra la ɔmɛ.

english_verse: Groan in sorrow, Ezekiel; the sword is drawn against my people and their leaders. They will die! So give up all hope.
translation_verse: Nɛwɛnyini bie, wi dɛɛ dooɡe lɔŋɔre, dɛkalkɛ n nɛra ne Israel koranar waa wɛɛ ba. Wɛɛ kpoo ba ne n nɛra kar bwaa. Kpɔ nɔɔra lɔ bambile á baɡle kɛŋɔ he hwɛɡa tonɔ.

english_verse: I am testing my people, and they can do nothing to stop me. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: N kpɔ ɡɛ waa nɔ daah ba, dɛ́ na kɛŋɔ dɛ ba ta ba liire charaa, ásɛ ɡɛ waa nɔ ba ba nɛ. Men Nemenɛ Korowiirii bola.

english_verse: Ezekiel, warn my people, then celebrate my victory by clapping your hands. My vicious sword will attack again and again, killing my people with every stroke.
translation_verse: Nɛwɛnyini bie, bol waa aa dɛ ba bala n sɔn ta, dɛ́ lɔ kpaŋa sibeɡra ne. Gel kere la ŋwɛnɛ keraanɛ, ó ŋwɛnɛ keraatoro kwara. O ɛ kere waa do ɔma dɛ́ won kpo.

english_verse: They will lose all courage and stumble with fear. My slaughtering sword is waiting at every gate, flashing and ready to kill.
translation_verse: O ɡelɔ ɔmee le n nɛra nɛɛ kohona ba choɡli. N kpɔ kere waa dɛ nyɛɡle kɛŋɔ bwaala la, dɛɛ aah ba ba bwɛjena doonyoo, dɛɛ ba ba kpoora.

english_verse: It will slash right and left, wherever the blade is pointed.
translation_verse: Kere haa nyɛɡa, mɔn ɡal ne diɡ bwa. Mɔn bobɛlbwa haa berɛ!

english_verse: Then I will stop being angry, and I will clap my hands in victory. I, the Lord, have spoken. The King of Babylonia and His Sword
translation_verse: N ɡe ɛɛ lɔ kpaŋaa, ásɛ n bandia la nyoa sɔɔh. Men Korowiirii bola.’ ”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, mark two roads for the king of Babylonia to follow when he comes with his sword. The roads will begin at the same place, but be sure to put up a signpost where the two roads separate and go in different directions.
translation_verse: “Nɛwɛnyini bie, bil ŋwɛnɛre anɛ ásɛ Babelɔn kooro kpɔ o kere kpɔ a ta ba. A ɛ ŋwɛnɛre aa le harɛ beŋkpoŋ ta, dɛ́ pa daa o baɡle bela ŋwɛnɛre anɛ la aa pera kaa.

english_verse: Clearly mark where the two roads lead. One goes to Rabbah, the capital of Ammon, and the other goes to Jerusalem, the fortified capital of Judah.
translation_verse: Ŋwɛnɛ la beŋkpoŋ ɛɛ chaɡle kooro la ŋwɛnɛ waa kpɔ o ta dɛ kaa Amɔn tena bwɛjen Raba la ta, ásɛ bɛl ɡe kaa Juda harɛ, Jerusalam bwɛjen baa ma danjwɛɛ baro la ta.

english_verse: When the Babylonian king stands at that signpost, he will decide which way to go by shaking his arrows, by asking his idols, and by carefully looking at the liver of a sacrificed animal.
translation_verse: Babelɔn kooro cheɡɛ ŋwɛnɛ chɛchɛre la ta, dɛ kpɔ o hɛma bil daa, dɛ́ jemɛ ŋwɛnɛ waa kpɔ o ta. O kpɔ o voɡa bil dɛ kpɔ kondɛɛre waa kpoa pwɛ dɛɛ nyiŋi o ta.

english_verse: His right hand will pull out the arrow marked “Jerusalem.” Then he will immediately give the signal to shout the battle cry, to build dirt ramps up to the top of the city walls, to break down its walls and gates with large wooden poles, and to kill the people.
translation_verse: O kpoŋe hɛm o nɔndiɡ ta dɛɛ ba tae do Jerusalam. A dɛ chaɡle kɛŋɔ o dɛ ba dajaŋa kpɔe ba teɡli doonyojena la ta, dɛ do laa lɔŋɔ, dɛ kwi sɔɔhbɔra bɔɔne, dɛ ma kon baa che o ta dɛ́ jo bwɛɛ la ta dɛ́ kpoo ba.

english_verse: Everyone in Jerusalem had promised to be loyal to Babylonia, and so none of them will believe that this could happen to them. But Babylonia's king will remind them of their sinful ways and warn them of their coming captivity.
translation_verse: Jerusalam tena noɔ waa baa yarada, fɔo ba ne kooro la aa fɔwa la wa. Kɛ aa ɡeloo ba lii ba wechɔɡa baa ɛa, ásɛ ba laɡ ba laa ta.

english_verse: Ezekiel, tell the people of Jerusalem and their ruler that I, the Lord God, am saying: Everything you do is wicked and shows how sinful you are. You are guilty and will be taken away as prisoners.
translation_verse: Anomanta, men Nemenɛ Korowii ŋɔ, ‘He wechɔɡa haa ɛa bwa chɔ baŋ. Nomɛlbwa naa dɛ na ɡɛ haa bera do ɡe bwa. Ba pa heyaa bolchɔɡe wobɛlbwa ta. Baa lawɛ heyaa laa taa dɛ́ kaa he ne.

english_verse: And now, you evil and wicked ruler of Israel, your day of final punishment is almost here.
translation_verse: Kooro haa dɛ nyiŋi Israel nɛɛ dɛ ɛ nyubinikpeɡ te kohona, he tɔpere baa tɛr he deŋne la telo tonɛ.

english_verse: I, the Lord God, command you to take off your royal turban and your crown, because everything will be different. Those who had no power will be put in charge, and those who now rule will become nobodies.
translation_verse: Men Nemenɛ Korowii dɛ ŋɔ he be ŋɔ hé laa he kooɡbɛrɛ la pili dɛ́ laa yal haa kpɔa vɔwɛ nyu la kpɔ. Wobɛlbwa aa ɡɛ aa doa laanee do kpa. Dansaara ɛɛ di koraa, ásɛ koranar berɛ dansaara.

english_verse: I will leave Jerusalem in complete ruins like no one has ever seen until my chosen one comes to punish this city. Judgment against Ammon
translation_verse: Mɛɛ chɔɡ bwɛjen laanee, dɛ́ chɔɡo chɔɡa ɡbaɡba! Kɛ wɛɛ do lee ka tel kɛŋɔ nɛn maa leo ŋɔ ó ba tɛr o bini nɛra deŋne aa ba, mɔɔ ń kpɔɔ do o nɔn ta.’ ”

english_verse: The Lord God said: Ezekiel, son of man, the Ammonites have insulted Israel, so condemn them and tell them I am saying: A sword is drawn, ready to slaughter; it is polished and prepared to kill as fast as lightning.
translation_verse: Anomanta, Nemenɛ Korowii ŋɔ men Ɛsekeɛl be ŋɔ, “Nɛwɛnyini bie, bol waa aa dɛ ba Amɔn tena baa dɛ chɛɡre Israel tena nɛɛ bala dɛ́ ŋɔ, ‘Ba pamɛ kere dɛ́ ba kpoo nɛra. Ba saro, ásɛ o do nyɛɡre dɛɛ nyɛɡle kɛŋɔ bwaala ken.

english_verse: You wicked Ammonites see false visions and believe untrue messages. But your day of punishment is coming soon, and my sword will slaughter you!
translation_verse: Amɔn tena, he wepila haa dɛ naa, ne waa haa ŋɔa aa bao la bwa ɛ nyosone. He ɛ nɛnchɔɡa, he nyu bini kpeɡri. He tɔpere telo, he deŋnetɛra tɔpere la telo tonɛ.

english_verse: Your days to punish others are over, so put your swords away. You will be punished in the land of your birth.
translation_verse: Hé berɛ kpɔ kere la su o tɔɔ ta. Hé berɛ kaa harɛ baa lolɛ o ta he naawa bwɛ, belaa mɛɛ ba he deŋne tɛra.

english_verse: My furious anger will scorch you like fire, and I will hand you over to cruel men who are experts in killing.
translation_verse: Mɛɛ kpɔ n banfuih ba ta he nɛ, dɛ́ kpɔ heyaa do nyubinikpeɡ tena baa won kwaa chɔɡa kohona nɔn ta.

english_verse: You will be burned and will die in your own land. Then you will be forgotten forever. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Niinii mɛɛ ba kpɔe fuh heya. He ɡbaɡba harɛ taa hɛɛ ba serewa, baa wola he waa lii kpa. Men Korowiirii bola.’ ”

english_verse: Some time later, the Lord said:
translation_verse: Korowii bol waa men Ɛsekeɛl be ŋɔ,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, are you ready to condemn Jerusalem? That city is filled with murderers, so remind the people of their sins
translation_verse: “Nɛwɛnyini bie, hɛɛ bol Jerusalam nɛŋkpoa nɛra aa suu nɔ waa yaa? Bol o nɛra we-ɛɛla maa kia la waa ba be.

english_verse: and tell them I am saying: Jerusalem, you have murdered many of your own people and have worshiped idols. You will soon be punished!
translation_verse: Ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, nɛra baa kpoora dɛ teŋɛ voɡa ta, dɛ kpɔ doŋa kah ba te nomanta, ba deŋnetɛra tɔpere dɛ ba.

english_verse: Those crimes have made you guilty, and the idols have made you unacceptable to me. So your final punishment is near. Other nations will laugh at you and make insulting remarks,
translation_verse: Jerusalam tena di bolchɔɡe ba nɛra baa kpoora la wa, dɛ kah doŋa voɡa baa ɛa la wa. Anomanta, ba deŋnetɛra tɔpere telo. A waa n ɡel harɛre ta nɛra ɛɛ mam ba dɛ bwa ɛɛ nyiŋ ba dɛɛ vah la.

english_verse: and people far and near will make fun of your misery.
translation_verse: Harɛre aa bɛna ne anɔ la aa lɔ bojaŋa bwa nɛra dɛ mam ba, ba wesaɡasaɡare la wa.

english_verse: Your own leaders use their power to murder.
translation_verse: Na ɡɛ Israel koranar aa cheɡɛ ba ɡbaɡba kpeɡri ta dɛɛ kpoo nɛra!

english_verse: None of you honor your parents, and you cheat foreigners, orphans, and widows.
translation_verse: Nomɛlbwa toole bwɛjen la ta dɛɛ duu o nya ne o mɛɛ. Ba dɛ faah nɛŋhɔɔhra, baa luhaahna ne bilalbii ɡe waa lii.

english_verse: You show no respect for my sacred places and treat the Sabbath just like any other day.
translation_verse: Ba siwii aa n kwaa aa do ɡoroŋ la su, dɛɛ chɔɡ n Ona Tɔpera.

english_verse: Some of your own people tell lies, so that others will be put to death. Some of you eat meat sacrificed to idols at local shrines, and others never stop doing vulgar things.
translation_verse: Ba bini bane teŋe nyosone dɛ ɡel baa kpoo ba bala, bane ɡe ɛɛ di voɡa kwaa deŋɡarere ta, bane ɛɛ bɔ jwamane.

english_verse: Men have sex with their father's wife or with women who are having their monthly period
translation_verse: Ba bini bane ɡe lawɛ ba mɛɛnanar haahna dɛɛ chɔ. Bane ɡe ɡuɡri haahna ba bwara aa chɔɡa ba ne baa chɔ.

english_verse: or with someone else's wife. Some men even sleep with their own daughter-in-law or half sister.
translation_verse: Bane dɛ bɔ jwamane, bane ɡe lawɛ ba bii haahna, kɛɛ ba nimambii ba ne baa pɛ nya ɡbo, kɛɛ mɛɛ dɛɛ chɔ.

english_verse: Others of you accept money to murder someone. Your own people charge high interest when making a loan to other Israelites, and they get rich by cheating. Worst of all, you have forgotten me, the Lord God.
translation_verse: Ba dɛ yawɛ ba bini bane sen baa kpoo nɛra. Bane ɡe dɛ́ kemɛ ba bala Israel tena suuɡa, dɛ́ chɔŋɛ a nee dɛ́ che a ta ɛ dɔɔhna. Ba soh n waa la kwara. Men Nemenɛ Korowiirii bola.

english_verse: I will shake my fist in anger at your violent crimes.
translation_verse: Mɛɛ lɔ kpaŋa bandia nee dɛ kooɡa ta ba nɛ, ŋwɛɛ ne nɛŋkpoa la wa.

english_verse: When I'm finished with you, your courage will disappear, and you will be so weak that you won't be able to lift your hands. I, the Lord, have spoken and will not change my mind.
translation_verse: Baa wono che n deŋnetɛra nyoa dɛ ta dɔ bokpeɡa awola maa ba tɛr ba deŋne la kɛɛ? N bol wa aa, n dɛ teŋɛ a ta. Men Nemenɛ Korowiirii bola.

english_verse: I will scatter you throughout every nation on earth and put a stop to your sinful ways.
translation_verse: Mɛɛ lɔ baa peɡre harɛre ne bwɛɛre ta, ásɛ dɛ ɡel ba wechɔɡa bwa ba a jaɡa.

english_verse: You will be humiliated in the eyes of other nations. Then you will know that I, the Lord God, have done these things. Jerusalem Must Be Purified
translation_verse: Gɛɛ dɛ ɡel harɛre ne bwɛɛre baa kaa a ta nɛra ɛɛ nyiŋi ba nyubaahna, ba siwi aa ban tɔɡɛ, ásɛ ba jemɛ kɛŋɔ menee Korowii.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, I consider the people of Israel as worthless as the leftover metal in a furnace after silver has been purified.
translation_verse: “Nɛwɛnyini bie, Israel tena waa ta tɔnɔ bɛlbwa dɔe dɛ tɛ mɛ kɛŋɔ ba yon kpɔ suuɡapoŋ do nii ta, dɛ mwɛɛlo asɛ ayaawa ne buni, dɛ kpana yon le a ta kɛ doŋa aa wola tɔnɔ dɔe la. Gɛɛ Israel tena ɛ doŋa tɛ mɛ.

english_verse: So I am going to bring them together in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Anomanta, men Nemenɛ Korowii ŋɔ, ‘Haa wola tɔnɔ bɛlbwa dɔe tɛ mɛ nomanta, Jerusalamee mɛɛ ba he nyoa boara.

english_verse: I will be like a metalworker who collects that metal from the furnace and melts it down. I will collect the Israelites and blow on them with my fiery anger. They will melt inside the city of Jerusalem
translation_verse: Kpela, Jerusalamee mɛɛ ba he nyoa boara, dɛ́ mar nii do he lɔɡa n bandia ne, dɛ́ mwɛɛ heya.

english_verse: like silver in a furnace. Then they will know that I, the Lord, have punished them in my anger. Everyone in Jerusalem Is Guilty
translation_verse: Gɛ baa dɛ mwɛɛ suuɡapoŋ nii ta la, ɡɛɛ mɛɛ ba heyaa mwɛɛla Jerusalam, ásɛ he jemɛ kɛŋɔ men Korowii, n kpɔ n bandia kohona ba he nɛ.’ ”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Israel that their country is full of sin, and that I, the Lord, am furious!
translation_verse: O ŋɔ, “Nɛwɛnyini bie, bol Israel tena be ŋɔ ba wechɔɡa ɡelɔ harɛ la kah doŋa, anomanta, n baah diu mɛɛ ba ba deŋne tɛra.

english_verse: Their leaders are like roaring lions, tearing apart their victims. They put people to death, then steal everything of value. Husbands are killed, and many women are left as widows.

translation_verse: Sɔfore ɡe vɛh me Mmarare ta teŋa. Baa waa aa do ɡoroŋ, ne anɔ la aa wola ɡoroŋ bini peɡri. Baa waa aa wera, ne anɔ la aa wola were ɡe baɡle, dɛ ɡel n Ona Tɔpera ɡe dii, a che a ta Israel tena vɛɛh mɛ.

translation_verse: Ba keamechɔɡa laa sie kpɔ ɡɛ wechɔɡa nɔ ta, kɛŋɔ baa kpɔ fula lɔ dekɔɔh danjwɛ ta, dɛ tɔ o peɡra ta ken. Ba won nyosone teŋa ŋɔ ba na waane wepila ta, dɛɛ baɡle ŋɔ waane ɛɛ bao, dɛɛ neɡre nɛra ŋɔ men Nemenɛ Korowii bee a le, dɛ n laa bol wobɛlbwa.

translation_verse: N nyiŋo kɛŋɔ mɛɛ na nomɛl ba binii ó ba ma Jerusalam danjwɛɛ la bela waa kua la, dɛ́ che ba naa ta, dɛ́ lɛ bwɛɛ la ta, ásɛ n fee ɡel o chɔɡa, kɛ n ta nomɛlbwa nae.

translation_verse: Mɛɛ kpɔ n banfuih ba ta ba nɛɛ kohona, dɛ́ chɔɡ ba, ba waa baa ɛa la wa. Men Nemenɛ Korowiirii bola.”

translation_verse: Korowii bol men Ɛsekeɛl be ŋɔ,

translation_verse: “Nɛwɛnyini bie, bihaahna banɛ bane ba bwa aa le nya beŋkpoŋ waa nɔ.

translation_verse: Ijipt harɛ taa ba so, dɛ le ba toli saŋ kpɔ bannyin dawɛ ba sie ta, dɛɛ bɔ jwamane.

translation_verse: Nomoa la sɔne Ohola, asɛ bechala la ɡe sɔne Oholiba. N haahnaa ban, ba loɡle bibaala ne bihaahna tɛ mɛ. Ohola cheɡɔ tɛ Samaria asɛ Oholiba ɡe che tɛ Jerusalam.

english_verse: So I gave Oholah to the Assyrian lovers she wanted so badly.
translation_verse: Anomanta, n vɛoh tɛ Asiiria baala waa dɛ pɛlɛ ba nɛɛ kohona la.

translation_verse: Ba wur Ohola laala o che mumɡbal, dɛ lawɛ o bibaala ne bihaahna bwa kaa, dɛ kpoo kere ne. A ɛ waa dɛ chɔ le haahna bwa ɛɛ bol o wa.

translation_verse: N nao kɛŋɔ dɛ ɡɛɛ o ɡe do, o da deno doŋ kɛŋɔ o nahaah la.

english_verse: But Oholibah behaved worse than her sister. Oholibah saw images of Babylonian men carved into walls and painted red.
translation_verse: Oholiba ta ɡelɛ a maɡre bela. O na Babelɔn tena fotore baa kpɔ konswɛɛma ɛa a dawɛ danjwɛɛ ta,

translation_verse: ba ɛ banyoola baa vɔwɛ kirisore dɛɛ yo jaɡre ne, dɛ kpɔ yapondɛɛɡa vɔwɛ nyuune.

translation_verse: Waa na ba la, o jwamanwaa la den ir, asɛ o tomɛ toroma ba be Babelɔn harɛ ta.

translation_verse: Bɛlbwa na o we-ɛɛla kɛŋɔ o ɛ hanjwamane. N baah diu n vɛoh ɡɛ maa vɛh o nahaah la.

english_verse: Oholibah didn't stop there, but became even more immoral and acted as she had back in Egypt.
translation_verse: Oholiba ta ɡelɛ a maɡre ɡɛ, o teŋɔ bɔ jwamane ɡɛ o toli saŋ o fa aa lɔ Ijipt harɛ ta la.

english_verse: She eagerly wanted to go to bed with Egyptian men, who were famous for their sexual powers.
translation_verse: Dɛ baala baa won haahna chɔe, ba pena do kɛŋɔ keeɡore kɛɛ jaɡ-bala penaa wɛɛ nyin name.

english_verse: And she longed for the days when she was a young prostitute, when men enjoyed caressing her body. The Lord Will Punish Oholibah
translation_verse: Oholiba, ɡɛɛ a do he lii he toli saŋ haa lɔ Ijipt harɛ ta dɛɛ pɛlɛ baala nɛ. Baala jaɡre he ela a bwa sɔɔh.

translation_verse: Anomanta, men Nemenɛ Korowii dɛ bol hen Oholiba be ŋɔ, ‘Mɛɛ ɡeloo baala ba wa aa pee la baah di he nɛ, dɛ́ le baŋ bɛlbwa, dɛ́ ba bare cheme.

english_verse: I will gather all the handsome young officials and the high-ranking cavalry officers from Babylonia and Assyria, as well as from the Chaldean tribes of Pekod, Shoa, and Koa.
translation_verse: Baala baa le Babelɔn ne Asiiria dɛ Kaldea tena baa lɔ Pɛkɔd ne Soa dɛ Koa bwa ɛɛ ba he bee. Mɛɛ boa laa nomonome baa wera bonɔɔna, ne harɛ la ta nomonjena, ne laa nomonome baa soɡe jaɡre ta dɛɛ yo la bwa nyoaa, ba ba he be.

english_verse: Their large armies will come from the north with chariots and wagons carrying weapons. They will wear shields and helmets and will surround you, and I will let them judge and sentence you according to their own laws.
translation_verse: Baa kpɔ dɔmkwaa le weekaŋle nyunduabɔree, dɛ́ so torɔɡore baa vɔwa pɛl jaɡre, ne anɔ la aa dɔ tɔre baa taɡa kɛ torɔɡo warɛ kohona dɛ́ ba yo. Baa le bobɛlbwaa dɛ́ ba bare, dɛ́ kpɔ kwaa tɔ ba te ɡbemɡbe dɛ́ pi laa ɡbɛrɛre. Mɛɛ kpɔe do ba nɔn ta ásɛ ba tɛr he deŋne.

english_verse: I am angry with you, so I will let them be very cruel. They will cut off your nose and ears; they will kill your children and burn alive anyone in your family who survives.
translation_verse: N baah aa di he nɛɛ kohona nomanta, mɛɛ ɡeloo ba kpɔ bandia doe sibeɡra kohona. Baa teŋe he mee ne deŋnaa ta, dɛ́ lawɛ he bibaala ne bihaahna kaa, dɛ́ fuh banɔ la baa kaa la.

english_verse: I will stop your wickedness and the prostitution you started back in Egypt. You will never want to think about those days again.
translation_verse: Gɛɛ mɛɛ ba he ɛɛ, dɛ́ ba he jwamanwaa haa pa a mun Ijipt harɛ la ne a jaɡa. Haa voɡa la kɛɛ Ijipt harɛ ta wobɛlbwa waa liira ba kpa.’ ”

english_verse: I, the Lord God, am ready to hand you over to those hateful enemies that you find so disgusting.
translation_verse: Nemenɛ Korowii ŋɔ, “N dɛ ba he kpɔe do nɛra ba wa aa pee he hah ba la nɔn ta.

translation_verse: Baa haeh nomanta, baa pa he komɛlbwa haa dɔa bwaa kaa, ásɛ he ka che mumɡbal, nɛra bwa nae kɛŋɔ hanjwamane. He pɛlchɔɡa ne jwamanee

english_verse: have led to this. You were the one determined to have sex with men from other nations and to worship their idols.
translation_verse: ba anɔ bwa ne ba tɛɛ. Harɛre nɛra bwa bee he bɔ jwamane ka tel, dɛ teŋɛ ba voɡare nɛɛ dɛ kah doŋa.

english_verse: You have turned out no better than your older sister, and now you must drink from the cup filled with my anger.
translation_verse: Ŋwɛnɛ he nahaah aa kpɔ o ta laanee he ɡe kpɔ, anomanta, hɛɛ nyɔ o deŋnetɛra nee la anee.”

english_verse: I, the Lord God, gave your sister a large, deep cup filled with my anger. And when you drink from that cup, you will be mocked and insulted.
translation_verse: Nemenɛ Korowii ŋɔ, “Gɛ maa tɛr he nahaah deŋne kohona laanee mɛɛ ba he ɛɛ. Nomɛlbwa ɛɛ mamɛɛ dɛ́ muɡli he baah, dɛkalkɛ deŋnetɛra la kan kohona.

english_verse: You will end up drunk and devastated, because that cup is filled with horror and ruin.
translation_verse: Hɛɛ dɛɛroo kohona dɛɛ di suna. Deŋnetɛra waa do ɔma dɛ chɔɡ he nahaah waa cheɡa tɛ Samaria laanee hɛɛ ba dɔe.

english_verse: But you must drink every drop! Then smash the cup and chew on its broken pieces. Use them to cut your breasts in sorrow. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Hɛɛ nyɔ deŋnetɛra nee la bwa kpɛlɛŋŋ, dɛ́ kpɔ nɔn lɔ ela dɛɛ di suna. Men Nemenɛ Korowiirii bola.

english_verse: You have completely rejected me, and so I promise that you will be punished for the disgusting things you did as a prostitute. The Two Sisters Are Condemned
translation_verse: Kenii men Nemenɛ Korowii ɛɛ bol hen Oholiba be. Haa soh n waa dɛ berɛ habɔɔ kpo mɛ nomanta, hɛɛ dɔ deŋnetɛra he pɛlchɔɡa ne he jwamane la waa.”

english_verse: The Lord said: Ezekiel, son of man, it's time for you to tell Oholah and Oholibah that they are guilty. Remind them of their evil ways!
translation_verse: Korowii ŋɔ n be ŋɔ, “Nɛwɛnyini bie, hɛɛ bol Ohola ne Oholiba waa dɛ́ pa ba bolchɔɡe aa? Di ba kasinteŋ waa maa kia ba ɛ la wa.

translation_verse: Ba bɔ jwamane dɛ kpoo nɛra ɡe ja. Ba le n habɔɔ dɛ kaa tomɛ voɡare, dɛ kpoo bii baa lol ba tɛ mɛ. Ba kpɔ ba ɛ saraha voɡare ta, dɛ fuuh ba.

translation_verse: Awola tenten baa kpɔ ba bii tɛ ba kpoo ba voɡa ta tonɛ la, ba baa jo n Dea dɛ kpɔ doŋa kaoh.

english_verse: They sent messengers to attract men from far away. When those men arrived, the two sisters bathed themselves and put on eye shadow and jewelry.
translation_verse: Ba dɛ tomɛ toroma ba ka yerɛ baala le bojaŋa ba. Ba balaa, ba yon sɔ ne, dɛ́ kpɔ kwaa pe ba siebɔra, dɛ́ kpɔ suuɡaswɛm kwaa do ba baŋa ne ba nɔɔra.

english_verse: They sat on a fancy couch, and in front of them was a table for the olive oil and incense that had belonged to me.
translation_verse: Ba yon so kane aa wera ta, asɛ teebur che ba sie, ba kpɔ daawiile a sɔɔh aa soma, ne ɔleve noo aa ɛ n kwaa la chɔŋɛ o ta.

english_verse: Their room was always filled with a noisy crowd of drunkards brought in from the desert. These men gave the women bracelets and beautiful crowns,
translation_verse: N dɛ no nɛra baa wara dɛ di kwaa dɛɛ lɛ ba sie ɡbɔɡa. Ba ɛ baala baa le ba ne pua hɛŋle ɡbo harɛ ta. Gɛ baala la kpɔ nɔnloɡa do haahna la, dɛ kpɔ haŋkoo-ɡbɛrɛre aa wera pi ba.

translation_verse: Baala la teŋɔ la Ohola ne Oholiba baa ɛ jwamane tena la be, ba ne ba ka chɔ.

translation_verse: Nɛra ba wa aa toɡra ɛɛ tɛr ba deŋnee ba jwamane ne nɛra baa kpoora la waa, dɛkalkɛ ba di bolchɔɡe a ta.”

english_verse: So I, the Lord God, now say to these sisters: I will call together an angry mob that will abuse and rob you.
translation_verse: Nemenɛ Korowii ŋɔ, “Nɛ́nlaa wur ba, dɛ́ ba tɔ ba nɛ, dɛ́ do ba sibeɡra, dɛ́ pa ba laala kaa.

translation_verse: Nɛnlaa ɛɛ foɡ ba bweaa, dɛ́ kpoo ba keri ne. Baa kpoo ba bihaahna ne bibaalaa, dɛ́ fuh ba deene ɡe.

english_verse: I will get rid of sinful prostitution in this country, so that women everywhere will be warned not to act as you have.
translation_verse: Gɛɛ mɛɛ ba ɛɛ, dɛ́ ba jwamane ne a jaɡa harɛ la ta, ásɛ a ja haahna ba bɛ ban hweli.

translation_verse: Mɛɛ tɛr he bwa deŋnee he jwamane ne voɡa haa toma la waa, ásɛ he jemɛ kɛŋɔ menee Nemenɛ Korowii.”

english_verse: Nine years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the tenth day of the tenth month. He said:
translation_verse: Baa lawɛ yaa laa ta kaa Babelɔn bene anuanaarɛ, korobie fi tɔpera fi ta habɔɔ la, Korowii bol waa men Ɛsekeɛl be ŋɔ,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, write down today's date, because the king of Babylonia has just begun attacking the city of Jerusalem.
translation_verse: “Nɛwɛnyini bie, bɔ fini tɔpere nɔ deeti bil, dɛkalkɛŋɔ Babelɔn kooro kpɔ o laa tena dɛɛ ba ba tɔ Jerusalam tena do fini.

english_verse: Then tell my rebellious people: “Pour water in a cooking pot and set it over a fire. *
translation_verse: Kpɔ sɛɡla bol waa chaɡle Israel deŋnekpeɡ tena la be ŋɔ, men Nemenɛ Korowii ŋɔ, ‘Hé ɛ nee do vii bini, dɛ́ kpɔ chɔŋɛ nii ta.

english_verse: Throw in the legs and shoulders of your finest sheep and put in the juicy bones.
translation_verse: Lawɛ pee waa wera dɛ́ chɛwɛ o ola do o bini, hé pa andɛɛɡa la, a vaama ne a hwie. Kpɔ hoɡa bɔra aa wera ɡe ja a ta.

translation_verse: Kpɔ pee ola la bela aa wera kɛrɛdɛ. Mar nii dɛ́ pa ola la do vii la bini, dɛ́ kpɔa chɔŋɛ nii ta.’

english_verse: These words mean that Jerusalem is doomed! The city is filled with murderers and is like an old, rusty pot. The meat is taken out piece by piece, and no one cares what happens to it.
translation_verse: Nemenɛ Korowii ŋɔ, ‘Bwɛjen Jerusalam nɛŋkpoa aa lɔ o ta kohona la bwɛɛlɛ. O do kɛŋɔ vii o bini aa deera ken, o doŋa la aa wola le. Tɔɔ ola baa chɛwa do o bini la beŋkpoŋa beŋkpoŋa le ó chɔ pɛɛ.

english_verse: The people of Jerusalem murdered innocent people in the city and didn't even try to cover up the blood that flowed out on the hard ground.
translation_verse: Ba kpoo nɛra bwɛjen la ta, ba chale chɔ bwea ta, harɛpɛɛ ta laa a chɔ, ásɛ teera tɔ a ta.

english_verse: But I have seen that blood, and it cries out for me to take revenge.
translation_verse: N ɡelɔ chale la chɔ ɡɛ ba ta a ta tɔe, ásɛ n naa n baah di kohona, dɛ́ yoo ba bɔ kem.’

english_verse: I, the Lord God, will punish that city of violence! I will make a huge pile of firewood,
translation_verse: Anomanta, Nemenɛ Korowii ŋɔ, ‘Bwɛjen nɛŋkpoa aa lɔ o ta la bwɛɛlɛ. N ɡe ɛɛ pa damaraa bil a daŋɛ.

translation_verse: Hé pa daa ba ja kohona ásɛ dɛ huuh nii do a ta. Hé daa ola la kɛrɛdɛ, dɛ́ do kwaa a ta a do som, hé fuh hoɡa la.

english_verse: Then set the empty pot over the hot coals until it is red-hot. That will clean the pot and burn off the rust.
translation_verse: Hé kpɔ buni vii ɡbo chɔŋɛ ninhɔla ta, dɛ́ ka tel kɛŋɔ waa bea dɛ swɛɛ, ásɛ doŋa bɛlbwa aa lɔ o bini la fuh, ó berɛ do wer kohona.

english_verse: Jerusalem is so full of sin and evil that I can't get it clean, even though I have tried. It will stay filthy until I let loose my fierce anger against it.
translation_verse: Jerusalam tena, he wedoŋa la ɡelɔ he kah doŋa. N takapɔ kɛŋɔ ń laa he doŋa bwa kpɔ he nɛ, kɛ n ta wone. Aa won le he nɛ, nemenɛ haa na n bandia kohona la bwa mɔɔ.

translation_verse: Wi dɛɛ do he bini. Bɛ wi tɛ lale la, bɛ nakpapɛɛ valɛ, bɛ yal waa vɔwɛ he nyu ta laa kpɔ á baɡle kɛ he dɛ ɛ lwe. Bɛ kon kpɔ tɔ he nyoa, bɛ kondikwaa nɛra baa dɛ ɛ lwe aa dɛ di la ane di.”

english_verse: One morning, I was talking with the people as usual, and by sunset my wife was dead. The next day I did what the Lord had told me,
translation_verse: Men Ɛsekeɛl, n bol waa nɛra la be chɔɔbɔr, asɛ jɔmɔra la n haah sewɛ. Tɔɔ aa pera chɔɔ la, n ɛ ɡɛ Korowii aa do mɛ la.

english_verse: and when people saw me, they asked, “Why aren't you mourning for your wife?”
translation_verse: Belaa nɛra la bɔɔ mɛ ŋɔ, “Haa won baɡle yaa a ɡɛ waa nɔ mun aa?”

english_verse: he is ready to destroy the temple in which you take such pride and which makes you feel so safe. Your children who now live in Jerusalem will be killed.
translation_verse: o dɛ ba o Dea haa dɛ ɛ mbarafo dɛɛ maŋkura he te o waa la chɔɡa. O wer he sie ta hɛɛ nyinu. Wɛɛ ɡeloo ba kpoo he bibaala ne bihaahna haa ɡel ba habɔɔ Jerusalam la laa ta.

english_verse: Then you will do the same things I have done. You will leave your face uncovered and refuse to eat the food that mourners usually eat.
translation_verse: Hé ɛ ɡɛ maa ɛa nɔ. Haa kwaa kpɔ tɔ he nyoo, haa kondikwaa nɛra baa lɔ lwe ta aa dɛ di la ɡee di.

english_verse: You won't take off your turbans and your sandals. You won't cry or mourn, but all day long you will go around groaning because of your sins.
translation_verse: Hɛ́ ɡel yapondɛɛɡa la vɔwɛ he nyuune, hé do naŋɡaware, dɛ bɛ wi, hɛɛ ɡwaŋɔɔ he wechɔɡa nɔ wa, bɛlbwa sɔh dɛɛ wi.

english_verse: I am a warning sign—everything I have done, you will also do. And then you will know the Lord God has made these things happen.
translation_verse: Hé nyiŋi men Ɛsekeɛl dɛ́ kpɔ hweli wa, dɛ́ ɛ ɡɛ maa ɛa la. Anee dɛ́ ɡel he jemɛ kɛ onee Nemenɛ Korowii.”

english_verse: The Lord said, “Ezekiel, I will soon destroy the temple that makes everyone feel proud and safe, and I will take away their children as well.
translation_verse: Korowii ŋɔ, “Nɛwɛnyini bie, mɛɛ chɔɡ n Dea baa dɛ ɛ mbarafo o waa o do wer ba siwi ta, ba sie ɛɛ lɛ o ta laanee. Mɛɛ lawɛ ba bibaala ne ba bihaahna bwa ɡee ja.

english_verse: On that same day, someone will escape from the city and come to tell you what has happened.
translation_verse: Awola tɔpere maa ɛ ɡɛ waa nɔ la, nɛn waa wona le a nyoa la ɛɛ bao, dɛ́ ba bol a waa baɡle.

english_verse: Then you will be able to speak again, and the two of you will talk. You will be a warning sign to the people, and they will know that I am the Lord.”
translation_verse: Awola tɔpere la, mɛɛ ɡeloo he berɛ won waa bola, ásɛ he ne naate bol wa. Gɛɛ aa ba ɛɛ ba nyiŋi dɛ́ kpɔ hweli waa dɛ́ jemɛ kɛŋɔ menee Korowii.”

english_verse: The Lord God said:
translation_verse: Korowii bol waa men Ɛsekeɛl be ŋɔ,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the people of Ammon
translation_verse: “Nɛwɛnyini bie, eɡle sie dɛ kah Amɔn tena, dɛ́ bol waa aa dɛ ba ba nɛɛ bala.

english_verse: and tell them: You celebrated when my temple was destroyed, when Israel was defeated, and when my people were taken away as prisoners.
translation_verse: Ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ bá cheɡ deŋne dɛ́ no waa men Nemenɛ Korowii aa dɛ bol, ‘He sie lɛo kɛŋɔ baa kpɔ doŋa kah n Dea dɛ chɔɡ Israel harɛ bwa, dɛ lawa baa lawɛ Juda tena laa ta kaa bojaŋ harɛfale ta la.

english_verse: Now I am going to let you be conquered by tribes from the eastern desert. They will set up their camps in your land and eat your fruit and drink your milk.
translation_verse: Anomanta, mɛɛ ɡeloo nɛra le wee leebɔr bá yo heya, dɛ́ pɔ he nɛ. Baa baŋre ba tɛnte deene he harɛ taa dɛ́ so, dɛ́ di he daa nɔna, dɛ́ nyɔ he kondɛɛra elne.

english_verse: Your capital city of Rabbah will be nothing but pastureland for camels, and the rest of the country will be pastures for sheep. Then you will know that I am the Lord God.
translation_verse: Mɛɛ ɡeloo bwɛjen Raba berɛ nyoɡmare dibɔr, ásɛ Amɔn harɛ bwa ɡe berɛ peera chɔɔbɔr. Hɛɛ jemɔɔ kɛŋɔ menee Korowii.’

english_verse: You hated Israel so much that you clapped and shouted and celebrated.
translation_verse: Nemenɛ Korowii ŋɔ, ‘He sie lɛo kohona he lɔ kpaŋa dɛ jah dɛɛ hɛɡre, liichɔɡa haa dɔa Israel harɛ chɔɡa wa.

english_verse: And so I will hand you over to enemies who will rob you. I will completely destroy you. There won't be enough of your people left to be a nation ever again, and you will know that I, the Lord, have done these things. Judgment on Moab
translation_verse: Anomanta, n nɔn dawɛ he nɛ ń tɛr he deŋne. Mɛɛ kpɔ heyaa do harɛre nɛra nɔɔra ta kɛŋɔ baa pa laala laa ta kaa ken. Mɛɛ chɔɡ he bwaa kwara, haa wola warɛ dɛ́ tel harɛbir nɛra kpa. Hɛɛ jemɔɔ kɛŋɔ menee Korowii.’ ” Korowii bol Moab tena chɔɡa wa

english_verse: The Lord God said, “The people of Moab thought Judah was no different from any other nation.
translation_verse: Nemenɛ Korowii berɔ ŋɔ, “Moab harɛ tena aa ŋɔa ŋɔ Juda harɛ tena do kɛŋɔ harɛre nɛra aa kaa la nomanta,

english_verse: So I will let Moab's fortress towns along its border be attacked, including Beth-Jeshimoth, Baal-Meon, and Kiriathaim.
translation_verse: mɛɛ ɡeloo nɛra ba yo bwɛjena aa lɔ Moab jwɛh ta dɛ lɛo dɛɛ ta la. Bwɛdɛɛɡa ane kɛŋɔ Bɛt Jɛsemɔt ne Baal Meɔn dɛ Kiriataim bwa jao.

english_verse: The same eastern desert tribes that invade Ammon will invade Moab, and just as Ammon will be forgotten forever,
translation_verse: Mɛɛ kpɔ Moab harɛ ne Amɔn tenaa do nɛra baa le wee leebɔr nɔn ta, ásɛ Amɔn tena sɔn he kwaraa.

english_verse: Moab will be punished. Then the people there will know that I am the Lord.” Judgment on Edom
translation_verse: Mɛɛ tɛr Moab tena deŋnee, ásɛ ba jemɛ kɛŋɔ menee Korowii.” Korowii bol Edom tena chɔɡa wa

english_verse: The Lord God then said, “The people of Edom are guilty of taking revenge on Judah.
translation_verse: Nemenɛ Korowii berɔ ŋɔ, “Edom tena yoi baa kaa yo Juda tena bandia ne, dɛ tɔ ba wel la nomanta, a ɡelɔ ba di bolchɔɡe kohona,

english_verse: So I will punish Edom by killing all its people and livestock. It will be an empty wasteland all the way from Teman to Dedan.
translation_verse: anomanta, men Nemenɛ Korowii ŋɔ, ‘Mɛɛ kpɔ nɔnee dawɛ Edom tena nɛɛ dɛ́ tɛr ba deŋne, ásɛ dɛ kpoo nɛra bwa ne ba kondɛɛra. Mɛɛ ɡeloo harɛ la chɔ pɛɛ le bwɛjen Teman dɛ́ ka le bwɛjen Dedan, ásɛ ba kpoo nɛra laa ta.

english_verse: I will send my own people to take revenge on the Edomites by making them feel my fierce anger. And when I punish them, they will know that I am the Lord God.” Judgment on Philistia
translation_verse: N nɛra Israel tena ɛɛ yo Edom tenaa dɛ́ tɔ n wel. Baa ɡeloo Edom tena na n bandia kohona, dɛ́ jemɛ kɛŋɔ menee tɔ ba wel. Men Nemenɛ Korowiirii bola.’ ” Korowii bol Filisti tena chɔɡa wa

english_verse: The Lord God said, “The cruel Philistines have taken revenge on their enemies over and over and have tried to destroy them.
translation_verse: Nemenɛ Korowii ŋɔ, “Filisti tena aa ɛ Juda tena dɔma biɡri nomanta, ba dɔ liichɔɡa dɛ kpɔ nyubinikpeɡ ka tɔ ba wel Juda tena nɛ, dɛ chɔɡ ba.

english_verse: Now it's my turn to treat the Philistines as my enemies and to kill everyone living in their towns along the seacoast.
translation_verse: Anomanta, n ŋɔ mɛɛ ka yo Filisti tenaa dɛ́ kpoo ba bwa le harɛ la ta. N dɛ ba nɛra baa kaa dɛ so mpo nyoa la bwa chɔɡa.

english_verse: In my fierce anger, I will take revenge on them. And when I punish them, they will know that I am the Lord.”
translation_verse: Mɛɛ kpɔ bandia kohonaa ka tɔ ba nɛɛ dɛ́ tɛr ba deŋne kohona bɔ kem. Ásɛ ba jemɛ kɛŋɔ menee Korowii.”

english_verse: Eleven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the month. He said:
translation_verse: Bene fi dɛ beŋkpoŋ, korobiloɡle tɔpere waa tɔ sie baa lawɛ yaa laa ta kaa bojaŋ harɛfale ta la, Korowii bol waa men Ɛsekeɛl be ŋɔ,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, the people of the city of Tyre have celebrated Jerusalem's defeat by singing, “Jerusalem has fallen! It used to be powerful, a center of trade. Now the city is shattered, and we will take its place.”
translation_verse: “Nɛwɛnyini bie, bwɛjen Taaya tena dɛ do silɛɛ lɔŋɔre ŋɔ, chwaasere, bwɛjen Jerusalam chɔɡɔ! Belaa bonadiire bwa ɛɛ la, waa chɔɡa nɔ, yaa do werii name.

english_verse: Because the people of Tyre have sung that song, I have the following warning for them: I am the Lord God, and I am now your enemy! I will send nations to attack you, like waves crashing against the shore.
translation_verse: Anomanta, Nemenɛ Korowii ŋɔ, ‘Taaya tena, n ne he dɔɔ. Mɛɛ ɡeloo harɛre nɛra wur bá tɔ he nɛɛ kɛŋɔ mpo nehɛma ken dɛ́ yo heya.’

english_verse: They will tear down your city walls and defense towers. I will sweep away the ruins until all that's left of you is a bare rock,
translation_verse: Baa chɔɡ danjwɛɛ waa bar bwɛjen Taaya la bwaa, dɛ́ kuuɡi dejaŋa ɡe bwa. Mɛɛ ɡbaa teɡaŋa ne bwekuŋe bwaa le harɛ la ta, á ka bwetal ɡbo.

english_verse: and that the people who live in your towns along the coast will be killed. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Baa kpoo nɛra baa soɡe bwɛɛre aa lɔ harɛ la ta keri nee, ásɛ Taaya tena jemɛ kɛŋɔ menee Korowii.”

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia is the world's most powerful king, and I will send him to attack you. He will march from the north with a powerful army, including horses and chariots and cavalry troops.
translation_verse: Nemenɛ Korowii ŋɔ, “Mɛɛ ɡeloo Babelɔn Kooro Nebukadnesa waa ɛ koranar bwa koojen bá yo Taaya tena. O ne o laa tena ɛɛ warɔɔ le weekaŋle nyunduabɔr, bane valɛ, bane so jaɡre ne kwaa aa do kɛ torɔɡore baa vɔwa pɛl jaɡre ta, dɛ́ ba yoo ba.

english_verse: First, he will attack your towns along the coast and kill the people who live there. Then he will build dirt ramps up to the top of your city walls and set up rows of shields around you.
translation_verse: Mɛɛ ɡeloo ba kpoo nɛra baa soɡe bwɛɛre aa lɔ Taaya harɛ la ta bwa keri ne. Baa ma teeraa sawɛ ba danjwɛɛ la, dɛ́ che a ta dɛ́ kpɔ kwaa tɔ ɡbemɡbe, dɛ́ yoo ba.

english_verse: He will command some of his troops to use large wooden poles to beat down your walls, while others use iron rods to knock down your watchtowers.
translation_verse: Mɛɛ ɡeloo bá kpɔ dakpeɡa chuɡe ba danjwɛɛre ta, dɛ́ kpɔ dɔmkwaa chɔɡ ba dejaŋa ɡe.

english_verse: He will have so many horses that the dust they stir up will seem like a thick fog. And as his chariots and cavalry approach, even the walls will shake, especially when he proudly enters your ruined city.
translation_verse: Ba dɔma Babelɔn tena la jaɡre ɛɛ warɔɔ, a ɡel tutuɡ bɔle ba nɛ. Kwaa aa dɔ tɔre baa taɡa kɛ torɔɡo, ne anɔ la baa vɔwa pɛl jaɡre kpɔ bwɛjen la doonyoa la ta jo he be naa, a ɡbɔɡa ɛɛ yiiɡi danjwɛɛ laanee.

english_verse: His troops will ride through your streets, killing people left and right, and your strong columns will crumble to the ground.
translation_verse: Baala baa soɡe jaɡre ta la ɛɛ kpɔ jaɡre laanee kpɔ fɔɡbaahna dɛɛ kpoo nɛra keri ne, ásɛ ba pilajena bwa ɡe kuuɡi.

english_verse: The troops will steal your valuable possessions; they will break down your walls, and crush your expensive houses. Then the stones and wood and all the remains will be dumped into the sea.
translation_verse: Dɔma la ɛɛ pa Taaya tena kondɔɔh ne kwaa baa dɛ di a bona bwaa. Baa taɡɛ ba danjwɛɛre bwaa ta, dɛ́ kuuɡi ba dedɛɛɡa ɡe bwa, ásɛ dɛ pa a bwekuŋe ne daa, dɛ teɡuŋe bwa ka ta mpo ta.

english_verse: You will have no reason to sing or play music on harps,
translation_verse: Mɛɛ ɡeloo he yela ne janjela sii bwa ba a jaɡa. Bɛlbwa aa a waa no kpa.

english_verse: because I will turn you into a bare rock where fishermen can dry their nets. And you will never rebuild your city. I, the Lord God, make this promise.
translation_verse: Mɛɛ ɡeloo bwɛjen la bwetal la ɡbo ka, ásɛ nɛra baa dɛ ɛ nee toma la ɛɛ nyenɛ ba dɔɔhne o ta. Baa won kwaa vɔrɔwe bwɛjen Taaya kpa. Men Nemenɛ Korowiirii bola.

english_verse: The people of the nations up and down the coast will shudder when they hear your screams and moans of death.
translation_verse: Men Nemenɛ Korowii berɔ bol bwɛjen Taaya tena waa ŋɔ, ‘Ba yo heyaa dɛ pɔ he nɛɛ tonɛ aa, nɛra baa soɡe mpo nyoa la ɛɛ ɔmɔɔ taeh, lɔŋɔre nɛra baa dɛ kpoo ba la aa dɛ dooɡe la wa.

english_verse: The kings will step down from their thrones, then take off their royal robes and fancy clothes, and sit on the ground, trembling. They will be so shocked at the news of your defeat that they will shake in fear
translation_verse: Koranar baa lɔ mpo nyoa la bwa ɛɛ ir ba kookane taa, dɛ́ foo ba koolaala ne ba laala baa sɔh kwaa dawɛ a taa bil. Baa dɛɛ ɔmɔɔ kohona he wa, dɛ́ so harɛ bochela ne.’

english_verse: and sing this funeral song: “The great city beside the sea is destroyed! Its people once ruled the coast and terrified everyone there.
translation_verse: Baa taa wiilee ŋɔ, ‘Ba chɔɡ bwɛjen o sɔn aa lea la. Ba pa o stiimaere bwa le mpo ta kaa. A ɡɛ nɛra baa soɡe bwɛjen nɔ ta laanee dɛɛ di kpeɡri mpo ta, dɛɛ aah nɛra baa soɡe o nyoa la.

english_verse: But now Tyre is in ruins, and the people on the coast stare at it in horror and tremble in fear.”
translation_verse: Awola bwɛɛ la aa paɡra la, nɛra baa soɡe mpo nyoa ne ekwie ta la ɔmɔ, ba bwara yɔr a wa.’ ”

english_verse: I, the Lord God, will turn you into a ghost-town. The ocean depths will rise over you
translation_verse: Nemenɛ Korowii ŋɔ, “Mɛɛ ɡeloo bwɛjen Taaya chɔ pɛɛ kɛŋɔ bwɛjena aa paɡra nomɛlbwa aa wola toole a ta, dɛ́ kpɔ mpo ba tɔ o ta ó ka vil ta.

english_verse: and carry you down to the world of the dead, where you will join people of ancient times and towns ruined long ago. You will stay there and never again be a city filled with people.
translation_verse: Mɛɛ kpɔ bwɛjen Taayaa ka ja lala bini, o ka pu saŋ la tena baa serewa la. Mɛɛ ɡeloo o ka so bela kɛŋɔ bwɛɛre a fa aa paɡra la, o ne nɛra baa serewa biɡri la so. Waa won ba harɛ nɔ ta weera bini kpa.

english_verse: You will die a horrible death! People will come looking for your city, but it will never be found. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Mɛɛ ɡeloo o chɔɡ kwaraa, o waa tonɛ. Nɛra ɛɛ dɛɛ nyin o bɔree, baa on na kpa bwa. Men Nemenɛ Korowiirii bola.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, sing a funeral song for Tyre,
translation_verse: “Nɛwɛnyini bie, taa wiile tɛ bwɛjen Taaya,

english_verse: the city that is built along the sea and that trades with nations along the coast. Tell the people of Tyre that the following message is from me: Tyre, you brag about your perfect beauty,
translation_verse: ŋɔ bwɛjen waa lɔ mpo nyoa dɛ ɛ bonadibɔr tɛ nɛra baa lɔ mpo nyoa bobɛlbwa be ŋɔ men Nemenɛ Korowii ŋɔ, ‘Bwɛjen Taaya, he ŋɔ he wer ka tonɛ.’

english_verse: and your control of the sea. You are a ship built to perfection.
translation_verse: Mpo nyoa he do. Nɛra baa vɔrɔwe ɡelɔ he do wer kohona kɛŋɔ stiimae.

english_verse: Builders used cypress trees from Mount Hermon to make your planks and a cedar tree from Lebanon for your tall mast.
translation_verse: Hɛmɔn Bwejen taa ba le dakpeɡa ne dɛ ba kwaare. Dɛ le peleme daa ne Lɛbanɔn dɛ ba kwaa dajaŋ yal waa baŋre he ta la ta.

english_verse: Oak trees from Bashan were shaped into oars; pine trees from Cyprus were cut for your deck, which was then decorated with strips of ivory.
translation_verse: Dajenaa ba kpɔ le Basan harɛ ba ɛ he ŋwandaa, dɛ kpɔ dakpeɡa ane ɡe le Saepros, ne bala nyena, dɛ ba kwaa he bini, he do wer.

english_verse: The builders used fancy linen from Egypt for your sails, so everyone could see you. Blue and purple cloth from Cyprus was used to shade your deck.
translation_verse: Ijipt harɛ taa ba kpɔ ŋwɛndɛɛɡe sɔh yapondɛɛɡe waa baŋre he doa dɛɛ kaa he ne la, dɛ berɛ kpɔ ane ɛ he fraŋkaa. Saepros ekwi harɛ taa ba le yaburum ne oŋkɔl waa wera ne, a tɔ he nɛɛ dɛɛ tɛɛ chunchule.

english_verse: Men from Sidon and Arvad did the rowing, and your own skilled workers were the captains.
translation_verse: Bwɛjena Sidon ne Aavad baalaa dɛɛ tawɛ. He ɡbabir nɛra baa dɔ he wejemaa jaa dɛɛ nyiŋi he nɛ.

english_verse: Experienced men from Byblos repaired any damages. Sailors from all over shopped at the stores in your port.
translation_verse: Nɛmbena baa jemɛ stiimaere kwaara kɛrɛdɛ le Beblɔs, dɛ ja ba nɛ. Nɛra baa le bobɛlbwa dɛ kpɔ stiimae dɛɛ kpɔ mpo ta balɔ ba ne hɛɛ di bona.

english_verse: Brave soldiers from Persia, Lydia, and Libya served in your navy, protecting you with shields and helmets, and making you famous.
translation_verse: Pɛɛsea ne Lidia dɛ Put harɛre baalaa ɛ he laa tena. Ba kpɔ kwaa baa kpɔa dɛɛ tɔ ba te ɡbemɡbe, ne buni ɡbɛrɛre saɡɛ he danjwɛɛre ta, dɛ ɡel he dɔ sɔn ne jirima.

english_verse: Your guards came from Arvad and Cilicia, and men from Gamad stood watch in your towers. With their weapons hung on your walls, your beauty was complete.
translation_verse: Bwɛjen Aavad ne Helɛk harɛ baalaa dɛɛ nyiŋi he danjwɛɛre ta, asɛ Gamad baala ɛɛ daah he dejaŋa ta. Ba kpɔ kwaa baa kpɔa dɛɛ tɔ ba te ɡbemɡbe saɡre he danjwɛɛre ta, dɛ ɡel he do wer ka tonɛ.

english_verse: Merchants from southern Spain traded silver, iron, tin, and lead for your products.
translation_verse: He kondɔɔh kohona nomanta, bonadiire le Taases dɛ kpɔ suuɡapoŋa ne bune dɛ kpana, dɛ baa charɛ kwaa he be.

english_verse: The people of Greece, Tubal, and Meshech traded slaves and things made of bronze,
translation_verse: Bonadiire baa le Tubal ne Mɛsɛk dɛ Grik tena harɛre, kpɔ kwaa baa kpɔ ayaawa ɛa ne yoma ba charɛ he laala.

english_verse: You also did business with people from Rhodes, and people from nations along the coast gave you ivory and ebony in exchange for your goods.
translation_verse: He ne baala baa le Roods di bona. He ne nɛra kɛrɛdɛ baa soɡe mpo nyoa ɡe di bona. Ba kpɔ bala nyena ne dadɛɛɡa ba charɛ kwaa he be.

english_verse: Judah and Israel gave you their finest wheat, fancy figs, honey, olive oil, and spices in exchange for your merchandise.
translation_verse: Juda tena ne Israel tena ne he di bona. Ba kpɔ mea ne tohno ne ɔleve no, dɛ konsɔɔhsoma baa dɛ fɔɡla ba charɛ laala he be.

english_verse: The people of Damascus saw what you had to offer and brought you wine from Helbon and wool from Zahar.
translation_verse: Damaskɔs tena ne he di bona kwaa haa dɔa kohona la wa. Ba kpɔ sen le Hɛlbɔn, dɛ pee pona ɡe le Saha ba charɛ laala he be.

english_verse: while people from Arabia and the rulers of Kedar traded lambs, sheep, and goats.
translation_verse: Arab tena ne Keda harɛ ta koranar ne he di bona. Ba kpɔ pebiiri ne pebala dɛ boohna ba charɛ laala he be.

english_verse: Merchants from Sheba and Raamah gave you excellent spices, precious stones, and gold in exchange for your products.
translation_verse: Seeba tena ne Raama tena ne he di bona. Ba kpɔ konsɔɔhsoma bwa soo siwi aa wera kɛrɛdɛ ne bwedɛɛɡa a yoɡ aa kpeɡa, dɛ suuɡaswɛm ba charɛ laala he be.

english_verse: You also did business with merchants from the cities of Haran, Canneh, Eden, Sheba, Asshur, and Chilmad,
translation_verse: Bwɛjena ane baa dɛ yera Haran, ne Kanɛ, ne Eden, ne Seeba, ne Assur dɛ Kelmad ne he di bona. Ba kpɔ laala ba charɛ kwaa he be.

english_verse: and they gave you expensive clothing, purple and embroidered cloth, brightly colored rugs, and strong rope.
translation_verse: Ba yoɡ yadɛɛɡa a yoɡ aa kpeɡa tɛɛ, yakɔle ne kwaa baa sɔah, ne kondɛɛɡa baa kpɔa dɛɛ pa harɛ dea, ne jisedɛɛɡa dɛ ɡboɡbie.

english_verse: Large, seagoing ships carried your goods wherever they needed to go. You were like a ship loaded with heavy cargo
translation_verse: Bwɛjen Taases stiimaeree dɛɛ kpɔ he laala. He do kɛŋɔ stiimae waa lɔ mpo ta dɛɛ che bontɔɡa.

english_verse: and sailing across the sea, but you were wrecked by strong eastern winds.
translation_verse: Dɛ baala baa dɛ tawɛ la, tawɛ kaa mpo baah ta naa, peu ɛɛ tao le wee leebɔr dɛ́ ba paɡre.

english_verse: The shouts of your drowning crew were heard on the shore.
translation_verse: Mpo nyoa harɛ ɛɛ jiɡruu, nɛra baa dɛ nyiŋi stiimae la ta aa dɛɛ wi la.

english_verse: Every ship is deserted; rowers and sailors and captains all stand on shore,
translation_verse: Nɛra baa kpoŋe ŋwandaa la bwa ɛɛ le ba stiimaere binii, ásɛ nɛra baa dɛ nyiŋi a ta bwa le ba che baŋ.

english_verse: mourning for you. They show their sorrow by putting dust on their heads and rolling in ashes;
translation_verse: Baa dooɡe lɔŋɔree dɛ́ wi kohona tɛɛ, dɛ́ kpɔ teera do ba nyuune ta dɛɛ ɡbili tɔɔ ta.

english_verse: they shave their heads and dress in sackcloth as they cry in despair.
translation_verse: Baa koh he waa fonɛ ba nyuune, dɛ́ kpɔ lweyale tɔ. Baa wiu kohona tɛɛ lokua ne.

english_verse: In their grief they sing a funeral song for you: “Tyre, you were greater than all other cities. But now you lie in silence at the bottom of the sea.
translation_verse: Baa wi dɛɛ tɛɛ la, baa taa wiilee tɛɛ ŋɔ, ‘Umee ya kpɔ bwɛjen Taaya maɡɔɔ? Mpo bɔle o ta o hel.’

english_verse: But now you are wrecked in the deep sea, with your cargo and crew scattered everywhere.
translation_verse: Taraken, he paɡrɔ mpo ta, dɛ chɔ vil bini. He laala haa dɛ di a bona ne he toma tena bwa ja he nɛɛ mpo bini.

english_verse: People living along the coast are shocked at the news. Their rulers are horrified, and terror is written across their faces.
translation_verse: Nomɛlbwa waa soɡe mpo nyoa bwara yɔr he wa. Hale ɔmee chole ba koranar nɛɛ kohona. Ba siebɔra nya bena.

english_verse: The merchants of the world can't believe what happened. Your death was gruesome, and you are gone forever.”
translation_verse: Bonadiire baa lɔ harɛre ta dɛ chweere, he paɡrɔ aa wola were, he waa tonɛ kwaraa.”

english_verse: The Lord God said:
translation_verse: Korowii bol waa men Ɛsekeɛl be ŋɔ,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the king of Tyre that I am saying: You are so arrogant that you think you're a god and that the city of Tyre is your throne. You may claim to be a god, though you're nothing but a mere human.
translation_verse: “Nɛwɛnyini bie, bol Taaya kooro be ŋɔ men Nemenɛ Korowii ŋɔ, ‘He dɛ ɡɔɔ he te dɛ ŋɔ he ɛ voɡ, he dɛ so voɡ kara ta mpo bare cheme. Kɛ nɛwɛnyinii hen, he ta voɡ ɛɛ, he dɛ lii kɛ he ne voɡ wejema kɛrɛdɛ.

english_verse: You think you're wiser than Daniel and know everything.
translation_verse: He wejema ɡwaa Danɛl aa? Wobɛlbwa toole he nɛɛ dɛ sɔh aa?

english_verse: Your wisdom has certainly made you rich, because you have storehouses filled with gold and silver.
translation_verse: He cheɡɛ he wejema ta dɛ dɔ kondɔɔh, suuɡaswɛm ne suuɡapoŋa bwa su he be.

english_verse: You're a clever businessman and are extremely wealthy, but your wealth has led to arrogance!
translation_verse: He cheɡɛ he bona dii wejema kohona ta, dɛ dɔ kondɔɔh kohona. He kondɔɔh nomanta, he nyu bini dɛ do he som.

english_verse: You compared yourself to a god, so now I, the Lord God,
translation_verse: Anomanta, he dɛ lii he te wejereme kɛŋɔ voɡ.

english_verse: will make you the victim of cruel enemies. They will destroy all the possessions you've worked so hard to get.
translation_verse: Mɛɛ ɡeloo nɛŋhɔɔhra baa ɛ harɛre nɛra ba nyu bini aa kpeɡa ɡwaa harɛre bwa nɛra ba yoi. Baa pamɛ ba kerii, dɛ́ chɔɡ kwaa haa cheɡɛ he wejema ta dɔ dɛ do wer la.

english_verse: Your enemies will brutally kill you, and the sea will be your only grave.
translation_verse: Baa kpoe dɛ́ kpɔe ta mpo ta kɛŋɔ baa huɡe la ken.

english_verse: When you face your enemies, will you still claim to be a god? They will attack, and you will suffer like any other human.
translation_verse: Hɛɛ won ŋɔ he ɛ voɡ nɛra baa dɛ ba ba kpoe la be naa? Nɛwɛnyinii hen, he ta voɡ ɛɛ nɛra baa kpoe la nɔn ta.

english_verse: Foreigners will kill you, and you will die the death of those who don't worship me. I, the Lord, have spoken. A Funeral Song for the King of Tyre
translation_verse: Hɛɛ sewɔɔ kɛŋɔ nyoate ken, nɛŋhɔɔhra baa wola men tomɛ nɔɔra taa hɛɛ ba sewa. Men Nemenɛ Korowiirii bola.’ ”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, sing a funeral song for the king of Tyre and tell him I am saying: At one time, you were perfect, intelligent, and good-looking.
translation_verse: “Nɛwɛnyini bie, taa Taaya kooro wiile, waa aa dɛ ba o nɛɛ bala la wa, dɛ́ ŋɔ men Nemenɛ Korowii ŋɔ, ‘Henee wera nɛra bwa bini ka tonɛ bá hweli, he dɔ wejema kohona dɛ do wer ka tonɛ.

english_verse: You lived in the garden of Eden and wore jewelry made of brightly colored gems and precious stones. They were all set in gold and were ready for you on the day you were born.
translation_verse: Dɛ he fa lɔ Eden bodɛɛɡe men Korowii aa du daa la, dɛɛ do kwaa aa wera kɛŋɔ, bwedɛɛɡa bwa soo siwi baa dɛ yera rubi, ne topas, ne emirad, ne kresolet, ne onis, ne jasepa, ne safaaya, ne tɛɛkoes dɛ bɛrel. Awola baa tae laanee ba ɛ ɡɛ kwaa nɔ ne suuɡaswɛm kwaa tɛɛ.

english_verse: I appointed a winged creature to guard your home on my holy mountain, where you walked among gems that dazzled like fire.
translation_verse: N le Kerob cheɡ wɛɛ daahne. Dɛ he soɡe n bwejen waa do ɡoroŋ la ta, dɛɛ valɛ bwedɛɛɡa aa dɛ nyɛɡle baah ta.

english_verse: You were truly good from the time of your birth, but later you started doing wicked things.
translation_verse: He waa fa toole n waa bini le awola maa tae mɔɔ he baa ɛ wechɔɡa.

english_verse: You traded with other nations and became more and more cruel and evil. So I forced you to leave my mountain, and the creature that had been your protector now chased you away from the jewels.
translation_verse: He sie fa beɡrɔ hɛɛ di bona, a che a ta he ɛ naɡrenyini, dɛ ɛ wechɔɡa. Asɛ n doŋi le n bwejen waa do ɡoroŋ la ta, dɛ ɡel Kerob la waa dɛ daahne la le he ne bwea aa dɛ nyɛɡle la baah ta.

english_verse: It was your good looks that made you arrogant, and you were so famous that you started acting like a fool. That's why I threw you to the ground and let other kings sneer at you.
translation_verse: He wer haa doa la ɡelɔ he ɛ mbarafo, dɛ chɔɡ he wejema, he nyanyini la wa. Anomanta, n taɡɛ ta harɛ a wa, ásɛ koranar na a ja ba.

english_verse: You have cheated so many other merchants that your places of worship are corrupt. So I set your city on fire and burned it down. Now everyone sees only ashes where your city once stood,
translation_verse: He wechɔɡa ne kasinteŋ bɛ dii he bona dii ta ɡelɔ he kpɔ doŋa kah deene haa dɛ tomɛ a bini. A waa n ɡel nii ba le bwɛjen la ta, dɛ fuh o bwa dɛɛboo. Nomɛlbwa na ɡɛ bwɛjen la aa fuah dɛ berɛ tɔɔ.

english_verse: and the people of other nations are shocked. Your punishment was horrible, and you are gone forever. Judgment on Sidon and Peace for Israel
translation_verse: Harɛre nɛra baa jemɛ bwa bwara yɔr he wa, he chɔɡɔ aa wola were kwara, baa hen na kpa.’ ” Korowii bol bwɛjen Sidon tena chɔɡa wa

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the city of Sidon
translation_verse: “Nɛwɛnyini bie, eɡle sie ta bwɛjen Sidon dɛ́ bol waa aa dɛ ba o ta bala, ŋɔ

english_verse: and tell its people: I, the Lord God, am your enemy! People will praise me when I punish you, and they will see that I am holy.
translation_verse: men Nemenɛ Korowii ŋɔ, ‘Bwɛjen Sidon, n ne he dɔɔ. He nɛɛ mɛɛ ba cheɡa dɔ jirima. He nɛra ɛɛ jemɔɔ kɛŋɔ menee Korowii ɡɛ saŋ maa ba tɛr ba deŋne, dɛ́ baɡle kɛŋɔ n do ɡoroŋ la.

english_verse: I will send deadly diseases to wipe you out, and I will send enemies to invade and surround you. Your people will be killed, and you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Mɛɛ kpɔ weechɔɡaa ba ta he nɛɛ dɛ́ ɡel chal ɛɛ palɛ he fɔɡbaahna. Nɛra ɛɛ serewoo chɔ bobɛlbwa, keri nee baa ba ba kpoora, ásɛ he jemɛ kɛŋɔ menee Korowii.

english_verse: When that happens, the people of Israel will no longer have cruel neighbors that abuse them and make them feel as though they are in a field of thorns and briers. And the Israelites will know that I, the Lord God, have done these things. A Blessing for Israel
translation_verse: Bwɛɛre aa bar Israel cheme, ba ne baa wola somɛ, baa lii ba ne wechɔɡa, dɛ do kɛ jabalnadaŋɛre ne sɔɔhne tɛɛ ba la aa lee do kpa. Baa jemɔɔ kɛŋɔ menee Nemenɛ Korowii.’ ”
