translation_verse: Nɛmbeŋkpoŋii o ta, asɛ a ɡɛ nɛn la lolɛ harɛ bɛlbwa nɛra, asɛ ba ya perɛ harɛ bwa. Waa ta nɛwɛnyini la, o do bɛlbwa tɔpera ne ya dobɔra.

english_verse: God has done all this, so that we will look for him and reach out and find him. He isn't far from any of us,
translation_verse: On saahna ɛa ɡɛ, ásɛ nɛwɛnyini ɛɛ laɡre dɛɛ nyin o bɔr kɛ nyoŋa ken, ásɛ o bɔr nyina bini la, bá nao. Kɛ kasinteŋ, Korowii toole bojaŋ. O ne ya bɛlbwa baah aa jaŋɛ.

english_verse: and he gives us the power to live, to move, and to be who we are. “We are his children,” just as some of your poets have said.
translation_verse: Nomɛl te kompɛɛ, ‘Korowii alaworomɛɛ ya bwa do le, dɛɛ hwee, dɛɛ ɛ ya tomare.’ He nɛra baa dɛ chwerɛ wobobeela la ɡba di ɡɛ waa nɔ danseɛ dɛ ŋɔ, ‘O biirii ya ɡbabir.’

english_verse: Since we are God's children, we must not think that he is like an idol made out of gold or silver or stone. He isn't like anything that humans have thought up and made.
translation_verse: Korowii biirii yan, anomanta, ya bɛ on kpɔ maɡɛ suuɡaswɛm ne suuɡapoŋ ne bwea koŋkwaare nɛwɛnyini ɡbaɡba aa kpɔ ba liire maa la.

english_verse: In the past, God forgave all this because people did not know what they were doing. But now he says that everyone everywhere must turn to him.
translation_verse: Saŋ la nɛwɛnyini fa aa wola Korowii ŋwɛnɛ jemɛ kɛrɛdɛ la, o laa sie kpɔ ba wechɔɡa ta. Kɛ taraken te, o ŋɔ hárɛ ta bobɛlbwa nɛra charɛ ba liire, dɛ́ le ba wechɔɡa ta,

english_verse: He has set a day when he will judge the world's people with fairness. And he has chosen the man Jesus to do the judging for him. God has given proof of this to all of us by raising Jesus from death.
translation_verse: dɛkalkɛŋɔ o do tɔpere waa dɛ ba nɛwɛnyini bwa waa bola kasinteŋ ne la. O le nɛn wɛɛ ba waa la bola. O ir naate seo ta ásɛ nɛra jemɛ kɛŋɔ kpelaa o waa la.”

english_verse: As soon as the people heard Paul say a man had been raised from death, some of them started laughing. Others said, “We will hear you talk about this some other time.”
translation_verse: Pɔɔl aa bol seo ta ira waa la, dɛ ba dɛ mamɔ, asɛ bane ɡe ŋɔ, “Ya dɛ nyin kɛ he bol he waa la yá no ja.”

english_verse: When Paul left the council meeting,
translation_verse: Belaa o le ba bini, dɛ kaa.

english_verse: some of the men put their faith in the Lord and went with Paul. One of them was a council member named Dionysius. A woman named Damaris and several others also put their faith in the Lord.
translation_verse: Nɛra la bane te yarada Yeesu waa la, dɛ ba ja o nɛ. Nɛra baa yaradaa la bini bɛl sɔne Daneseɔs. Dɛ Areɔpaɡos nomonome la bɛlee on. Haah bɛl baa dɛ yerɔ Damaris ne nɛra bane yarada Yeesu waa la.

english_verse: Paul left Athens and went to Corinth,
translation_verse: A habɔɔ la, Pɔɔl le Atens dɛ kaa Kɔrent.

english_verse: where he met Aquila, a Jewish man from Pontus. Not long before this, Aquila had come from Italy with his wife Priscilla, because Emperor Claudius had ordered the Jewish people to leave Rome. Paul went to see Aquila and Priscilla
translation_verse: Belaa o ka na Juu te bɛl, dɛ o sɔne Akwela. Dɛ Pɔntos tee on, asɛ o ka so Rom, dɛ berɛ le bela ba Kɔrent, dɛkalkɛŋɔ dɛ Rom Koojen Klɔdeɔs doŋi Juu tena bwa Rom. Dɛ Akwela haah sɔne Presela. Pɔɔl la ba be dɛ ka na ba,

english_verse: and found out they were tent makers. Paul was also a tent maker, so he stayed with them, and they worked together.
translation_verse: dɛ so ba be dɛ ɛ toma, dɛkalkɛŋɔ dɛ ɡbansaba toma o fa aa dɛ ɛ wubwa laanee baa ɛ.

english_verse: Finally, they turned against him and insulted him. So he shook the dust from his clothes and told them, “Whatever happens to you will be your own fault! I am not to blame. From now on I am going to preach to the Gentiles.”
translation_verse: Dɛ nɛra la dɛ nyin Pɔɔl toma chɔɡa, dɛɛ ɛo nɛnhɛla. Anomanta, o jwii o laala doŋa ta dɛ baɡle kɛ o baɡ ba Korowii waa asɛ ba vɛah, dɛ ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, “Dɛ he nyoɡraa, nɛn laa ɛ heya, he ɡbaɡbaa ɛ he nyu. Le fini dɛɛ kaa, nɛra baa wola Juu tena ɛɛ mɛɛ ba Korowii waa baɡla. Maa he bee ba kpa.”

english_verse: Paul then moved into the house of a man named Titius Justus, who worshiped God and lived next door to the synagogue.
translation_verse: Waa le ba be la, o kaa choɡ baa bɛl waa dɛ tomɛ Korowii ɡɛ Juu tena aa dɛ tomɛ Korowii baa yerɔ Titeɔs Jastos. Dɛ o dem lɔ bela cheremi dea jwɛɛh tenten.

english_verse: Crispus was the leader of the synagogue. He and everyone in his family put their faith in the Lord. Many others in Corinth also heard the message, and all the people who had faith in the Lord were baptized.
translation_verse: Dɛ nomoa waa dɛ nyiŋi cheremi dea la ta la sɔne Krispus. Dɛ o ne o dem tena bwa yarada Yeesu waa la. Kɔrent tena kɛrɛdɛ no Yeesu waa la dɛ yaradaa, asɛ ba sɔ ba Korowii ne.

english_verse: One night, Paul had a vision, and in it the Lord said, “Don't be afraid to keep on preaching. Don't stop!
translation_verse: Awola bɛl, Pɔɔl na wepila ane jwaana. O nao kɛŋɔ Korowii aa dɛ ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Bɛ dɛɛ ɔmɛ, dɛɛ bol n waa la nɛra be. Bɛ nyoa tɔ,

english_verse: I am with you, and you won't be harmed. Many people in this city belong to me.”
translation_verse: dɛkalkɛŋɔ n cheɡɛ he habɔɔ. N nɛra warɛ bwɛjen nɔ ta. Anomanta, mɛɛ che he mun taa, ásɛ nomɛlbwa bɛ won ɛɛ wobɛlbwa.”

english_verse: Paul stayed on in Corinth for a year and a half, teaching God's message to the people.
translation_verse: Anomanta, Pɔɔl soɡe bwɛɛ la ta dɛ baɡle nɛra Korowii waa benanyoa dɛ korobie anumɛl.

english_verse: While Gallio was governor of Achaia, some of the Jewish leaders got together and grabbed Paul. They brought him into court
translation_verse: Gɛ saŋ baa tɛ baa bɛl baa dɛ yerɔ Galio nomonome, asɛ o nyiŋi Akaya harɛ dɛɛ tɛ Rom Koojen laanee Juu tena pɛ nyoa, dɛ lawɛ Pɔɔl la o be.

english_verse: and said, “This man is trying to make our people worship God in a way that is against our Law!”
translation_verse: Baa la o ne la, ba kaa ŋɔ, “Baa nɔ jo ya kii nɛ. O dɛ baɡle nɛra ŋɔ báa tomɛ Korowii ŋwɛnɛ bɛl ta aa wola were.”

english_verse: Even before Paul could speak, Gallio said, “If you were charging this man with a crime or some other wrong, I would have to listen to you.
translation_verse: Pɔɔl te ne ŋɔ o bol waa dɛ Galio ŋɔ Juu tena la be ŋɔ, “Juu tena, dɛ tonchɔɡa anee baa nɔ fe tomɛ nɔ naa, ŋwɛnɛ fe lole kɛ ń lawɛ bambile dɛ́ no he be.

english_verse: But since this concerns only words, names, and your own law, you will have to take care of it yourselves. I refuse to judge such matters.”
translation_verse: Kɛ aa ɛ waa waa bola ne he bwɛɛ tena sɔna ne he bwɛɛ waa ɡbo waa nɔ te, hé ɡbaɡba ka nyiŋi a ta. Maa a ɡɛ waa nɔɔ bol.”

english_verse: Then he sent them out of the court.
translation_verse: Galio doŋ ba o kɔɔto bela.

english_verse: The crowd grabbed Sosthenes, the Jewish leader, and beat him up in front of the court. But none of this mattered to Gallio. Paul Returns to Antioch in Syria
translation_verse: Belaa ba lawɛ cheremi dea nomoa baa dɛ yerɔ Sɔɔstenes la, dɛ lɔɔro Galio kɔɔto dea la sie tenten, kɛ Galio ta ban chaŋɛ kwara. Pɔɔlwa berɔ ba kaa Anteɔk

english_verse: After Paul had stayed for a while with the Lord's followers in Corinth, he told them goodbye and sailed on to Syria with Aquila and Priscilla. But before he left, he had his head shaved at Cenchreae because he had made a promise to God.
translation_verse: A habɔɔ la, Pɔɔl soɡe Kɔrent asɔre tena la be biɡri, asɛ dɛ kal ba dɛ le bela kaa Keŋkrea. Dɛ o baɡɛ nyoa bɛl, anomanta, o fonɛ o nyu mɔɔ dɛ le Keŋkrea, asɛ o ne Akwela ne Presela kpɔ stiimae dɛɛ kaa Siiria harɛ.

english_verse: The three of them arrived in Ephesus, where Paul left Priscilla and Aquila. He then went into the synagogue to talk with the people there.
translation_verse: Ba kaa tel Ɛfesos, asɛ Pɔɔl ɡel ba dɛ te kaa bela cheremi dea, asɛ o ne bela Juu tena kaa bol Korowii wa.

english_verse: They asked him to stay longer, but he refused.
translation_verse: Nɛra la fe ŋɔ ó so ba be tama, kɛ o ta sɛɛh.

english_verse: Paul sailed to Caesarea, where he greeted the church. Then he went on to Antioch.
translation_verse: Waa tel Sisaaria la, o la Jerusalam dɛ ka chɔɔ bela asɔre tena, dɛ le bela kaa Anteɔk.

english_verse: After staying there for a while, he left and visited several places in Galatia and Phrygia. He helped the followers there to become stronger in their faith. Apollos in Ephesus
translation_verse: Waa soɡe bela tama la, o le bela dɛ valɛ Galaasia harɛ ne Frejea harɛ bwɛɛre ta, dɛɛ ja nɛra baa dɛ teŋɛ Yeesu nɛɛ dɛ do bela la, dɛɛ do ba ɡbemba.

english_verse: A Jewish man named Apollos came to Ephesus. Apollos had been born in the city of Alexandria. He was a very good speaker and knew a lot about the Scriptures.
translation_verse: Dɛ Juu te bɛl ɛ bwɛɛ bɛl baa dɛ yerɔ Alɛksandrea la bie, dɛ ba Ɛfesos, asɛ baa yerɔ Apolos. Dɛ o jemɛ wobol taeh, dɛ jemɛ Korowii Tɔn bini waa ɡe kɛrɛdɛ.

english_verse: He also knew much about the Lord's Way, and he spoke about it with great excitement. What he taught about Jesus was right, but all he knew was John's message about baptism.
translation_verse: Ba fa baɡle Apolos Yeesu bwara waa ne o ŋwɛnɛre bwa, asɛ o jema, dɛ ɡe ɛɛ baɡla o bokpeɡa bwa ne. Kɛ, dɛ Jɔn o fa aa dɛ sɔ nɛra Korowii nee la waa waa baɡle nɛra Yeesu waa la ɡboo o no.

english_verse: Apollos started speaking bravely in the synagogue. But when Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him to their home and helped him understand God's Way even better.
translation_verse: O lɔ bambile dɛ baa bol Korowii Waa cheremi dea. Presela ne Akwela no waa waa dɛ bol la, dɛ kpɔɔ la ba dem dɛ ka baɡlo Korowii Waa la kɛrɛdɛ.

english_verse: Apollos decided to travel through Achaia. So the Lord's followers wrote letters, encouraging the followers there to welcome him. After Apollos arrived in Achaia, he was a great help to everyone who had put their faith in the Lord Jesus because of God's gift of undeserved grace.
translation_verse: Belaa Apolos ŋɔ wɛɛ la Akaya harɛ taa. Anomanta, Ɛfesos asɔre tena la doo ɡbemba dɛ chwerɛ Akaya harɛ asɔre tena tɔn ŋɔ ó ba ba be naa, bá nyiŋu kɛrɛdɛ. Waa la bela la, o kaa cha nɛra Korowii aa sune ba nɛɛ dɛ ɡel ba yarada o waa la taeh.

english_verse: He got into fierce arguments with the Jewish people, and in public he used the Scriptures to prove that Jesus is the Messiah.
translation_verse: O wono baɡle Korowii Waa bini bombaah kpeɡri nɛ, Juu te bɛlbwa aa wola wone tɔŋlo, dɛ won baɡle waa Korowii Tɔn bini kɛŋɔ Yeesuu Kristo la waa ɛ nɛwɛnyina bwa Lɛɛ la.

english_verse: While Apollos was in Corinth, Paul traveled across the hill country to Ephesus, where he met some of the Lord's followers.
translation_verse: Apolos aa lɔ Kɔrent la, Pɔɔl kpɔ harɛ la bwe doa bɔr dɛ ka le Ɛfesos. Waa la bela la, o kaa pu nɛra baa dɛ teŋɛ Yeesu nɛɛ la bane bela,

english_verse: He asked them, “When you put your faith in Jesus, were you given the Holy Spirit?” “No!” they answered. “We have never even heard of the Holy Spirit.”
translation_verse: dɛ pɛɛ ba ŋɔ, “Haa kpɔ he te tɛ Yeesu la, Korowii tɛ heyaa o Domadɛɛɡe la aa?” Asɛ ba ŋɔ, “Ɔɔhɔh, ya te ta Korowii Domadɛɛɡe la waa noɛ kwaraa bwa.”

english_verse: Paul replied, “John baptized people so they would turn to God. But he also told them someone else was coming, and they should put their faith in him. Jesus is the one that John was talking about.”
translation_verse: Belaa o ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, “Nɛra baa charɛ ba liire dɛ le ba wechɔɡa ta laanee Jɔn sɔ Korowii ne. Jɔn fa aa dɛ baɡle nɛra waa la, o ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ naate o taa lɔ sie dɛɛ ba bala la baa ba naa, bá yaradao dɛ́ kpɔ ba te tɛo. A ɡɛ saŋ la, Yeesu waa wɛɛ bol la.”

english_verse: After the people heard Paul say this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
translation_verse: Baa no ɡɛ waa nɔ la, ba ɡelɔ ba sɔ ba Korowii nee dɛ baɡle kɛ ba ɛ ya Dɔɔ Yeesu nɛra.

english_verse: Then Paul placed his hands on them. The Holy Spirit was given to them, and they spoke unknown languages and prophesied.
translation_verse: Pɔɔl kpɔ o nɔɔra dawɛ ba nɛ, asɛ Korowii Domadɛɛɡe ba so ba nɛ, asɛ baa bol wobofala, dɛɛ bol Korowii Wa.

english_verse: There were about twelve men in this group.
translation_verse: Dɛ baa tel baala fi dɛ banɛɛ.

english_verse: For three months Paul went to the synagogue and talked bravely with the people about God's kingdom. He tried to win them over,
translation_verse: Pɔɔl di korobie atoro bwa bela, dɛɛ bol Korowii Waa bela tena be bansua ne ba cheremi dea bini. O laɡ ba dɛɛ so, o ne baa bol Korowii Kora la wa. O takapɔ kɛ wɛɛ berɛ ba liiree, ásɛ ba fe teŋɛ o kon ta.

english_verse: but some of them were stubborn and refused to believe. In front of everyone they said terrible things about God's Way. Paul left and took the followers with him to the lecture hall of Tyrannus. He spoke there every day
translation_verse: Ba bini bane deŋne kpeɡri baa waa la yarada kwara, dɛɛ bol Yeesu nɛɛ teŋa la waa aa wola were kwara nɛnlaa la bwa baah ta. Anomanta, Pɔɔl ɡel ba, dɛ lawɛ nɛra baa yarada Yeesu waa la, asɛ tɔpere bɛlbwa o ne ba kaa cheme bobɛl baa dɛ yerɛ bela Teraanɔs Sukuu la ta.

english_verse: for two years, until every Jew and Gentile in Asia had heard the Lord's message. The Sons of Sceva
translation_verse: Gɛ Sukuu la ta laŋa dɛ kaa hweli Korowii waa tɔpere bɛlbwa la, ba ɛ ɡɛ bene anɛ. Anomanta, Juu tena ne Grik tena ɛɛ dɛ do Eesia harɛ ta bela bwaa no Yeesu waa la.

english_verse: God gave Paul the power to work great miracles.
translation_verse: Dɛ Korowii cheɡɛ Pɔɔl nɛɛ dɛɛ ɛ nyokpowaa aa do kpeɡri dɛ berɛ ɡwaa loɡla kwaa la.

english_verse: People even took handkerchiefs and aprons that had touched Paul's body, and they carried them to everyone who was sick. All of the sick people were healed, and the evil spirits went out.
translation_verse: Dɛ nɛra kpɔ dukure ne yakwane waa leɡa dɛɛ la weela tena be, asɛ ba weelare ɛɛ le ba nɛ, asɛ ba bini banɔ la kwaa aa dɛ ir ba nɛɛ la ɡe kwaa la ɛɛ le ba nɛ.

english_verse: Some Jewish men started going around trying to force out evil spirits by using the name of the Lord Jesus. They said to the spirits, “Come out in the name of that same Jesus that Paul preaches about!”
translation_verse: Dɛ Juu tena bane lɔ bela dɛ yon ɡaaɡe dɛɛ doŋi kwaa aa dɛ ir nɛra nɛ. Ba ɡe fe dɛ nyin dɛ kpɔ ya Dɔɔ Yeesu sɔn dɛɛ doŋi a ɡɛ kwaa nɔ dɛ yon dɛɛ kɔɡra ŋɔ, “Yeesu Pɔɔl aa dɛ bol o waa la sɔn ta, hé le kɛ yaa dɛ ŋɔ he be nɔ!”

english_verse: Seven sons of a high priest named Sceva were doing this,
translation_verse: Dɛ Juu tena Sɔfonomoa bɛl baa dɛ yerɔ Skiiva la bibaala banuanɛɛ dɛɛ ɛ ɡɛ.

english_verse: when an evil spirit said to them, “I know Jesus! And I have heard about Paul. But who are you?”
translation_verse: Awola bɛl, baa ŋɔa ba kpɔ Yeesu sɔn doŋi kwaa nomɛl nɛɛ la, a ɡelɔ o ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, “N jemɛ Yeesu, dɛ jemɛ Pɔɔl ɡe. Asɛ he ɡe, heyaa bamewaɔ?”

english_verse: Then the man with the evil spirit jumped on them and beat them up. They ran out of the house, naked and bruised.
translation_verse: Ate, dɛ baa la kwaa aa dɛ ir o nɛɛ la ɡuɡ ba dɛ lɔɔ ba, dɛ a ɔma. O do ba bola, dɛ kɛɛ ba laala dɛ wur ba, asɛ ba chwa le o dem bela.

english_verse: When the Jews and Gentiles in Ephesus heard about this, they were so frightened that they praised the name of the Lord Jesus.
translation_verse: Juu tena ne Grik tena baa lɔ Ɛfesos la bwa no ɡɛ waa nɔ, asɛ ɔmee laɡ ba kɛrɛdɛ. Gɛ waa nɔ aa chiɡa la, bela tena ta Yeesu waa la wesale liire kpa. Ba ɔmɔ kɛrɛdɛ.

english_verse: Many who were followers now started telling everyone about the evil things they had been doing.
translation_verse: Name nɛra baa yaradaa la kɛrɛdɛ le bombaah dɛɛ bol wechɔɡa baa ɛa, dɛɛ sɛh ba chɔɡre.

english_verse: So the Lord's message spread and became even more powerful. The Riot in Ephesus
translation_verse: Gɛ ŋwɛnɛkpeɡ nɔ taa a che Korowii waa la perɛ, dɛ won do kpeɡri kohona.

english_verse: After all this had happened, Paul decided to visit Macedonia and Achaia on his way to Jerusalem. Paul had said, “From there I will go on to Rome.”
translation_verse: Gɛ waa nɔ habɔɔ la, Pɔɔl ɛ o liire kɛŋɔ wɛɛ la Makidoonia harɛ ne Akaya harɛ taa, dɛ ka kaa Jerusalam, dɛ ŋɔ dɛ o la a bwa ta naa, a chɛ kɛ o la Rom ɡba.

english_verse: So he sent his two helpers, Timothy and Erastus, to Macedonia. But he stayed on in Asia for a while.
translation_verse: O tomɛ o bonɔɔna banɛ baa dɛ yer ba Timoti ne Erastos la, asɛ ba tɔ o sie kaa Makidoonia harɛ. Kɛ o te soɡe Eesia harɛ ta tama.

english_verse: At that time there was serious trouble because of the Lord's Way.
translation_verse: A ɡɛ saŋ la, dɛ Ɛfesos tena baa wola asɔre tena ɛɛ la lɛ ɡaeh nɛra baa dɛ teŋɛ ŋwɛnɛfale la ta la nɛ.

english_verse: A silversmith named Demetrius had a business that made silver models of the temple of the goddess Artemis. Those who worked for him earned a lot of money.
translation_verse: Gwine te bɛl lɔ bela baa yerɔ Demetreɔs. O kpɔ suuɡapoŋa dɛɛ kwaa bela voɡ bɛl baa dɛ yerɔ Aatemes la dea chaa, asɛ ɡɛ toma la ɛɛ tɛ o ne o bala tom-ɛɛra tɔnɔ tenten.

english_verse: Demetrius brought together everyone who was in the same business and said: Friends, you know we make a good living at this.
translation_verse: O yerɛ o tom-ɛɛra la bwa ne nɛra o ne baa dɛ ɛ tonsiwi beŋkpoŋ la bwa, dɛ ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, “Yabala, he jemɔ kɛ toma nɔ taa a che ya do wer la.

english_verse: But you have surely seen and heard how this man Paul is upsetting a lot of people, not only in Ephesus, but almost everywhere in Asia. He claims that the gods we humans make are not really gods at all.
translation_verse: Kɛ taraken, he ɡbabir na waa Pɔɔl nɔ aa dɛ ɛ, dɛ no waa waa dɛ bol. Ɛfesos bonɔ ɡbo laa wɛɛ ɛ o waa nɔ. Eesia harɛ kɛrɛdɛ bwaa wɛɛ ɛa. O wono berɛ nɛndamanta bwa liire baa teŋɛ waa waa dɛ baɡle la ta. O waa waa dɛ bol laanee kɛ voɡa nɛwɛnyini ɡbaɡba aa kpɔ nɔn dɛɛ ɛa la ta kasinteŋ dɔe.

english_verse: Everyone will start saying terrible things about our business. They will stop respecting the temple of the goddess Artemis, who is worshiped in Asia and all over the world. Our great goddess will be forgotten!
translation_verse: Waa dɛ ɛ ɡɛ nɔ, n dɛ ɔmɛ kɛŋɔ ya toma nɔ sɔn bɛ ba chɔɡ. Ya toma nɔ ɡbo sɔn laa dɛɛ ba chɔɡa. Ya voɡjen Aatemes dea nɔ nɛra aa dɛ maŋkurao nɔ, baa on komɛlbwa yera ba kpa, ásɛ o sɔn sewɛ, ásɛ dɛ kpo voɡ baa dɛ tomɔ Eesia harɛ ne bobɛlbwa la sɔn kwaraa! Baa on ɔmɛ kpa.”

english_verse: When the workers heard this, they got angry and started shouting, “Great is Artemis, the goddess of the Ephesians!”
translation_verse: Nɛra la aa no ɡɛ waa nɔ la, ba bwaawee iro, asɛ baa dooɡe lɔŋɔre dɛɛ ŋɔ, “Ya Ɛfesos tena voɡ Aatemes nɔ dɔŋ toole!”

english_verse: Soon the whole city was in a riot, and some men grabbed Gaius and Aristarchus, who had come from Macedonia with Paul. Then everyone in the crowd rushed to the place where the town meetings were held.
translation_verse: Ate, dɛ ɡbɔɡa tɔ bwɛjen la bwa, asɛ nɛnlaa la aa dɛ do ɡbɔɡa la lawɛ nɛra bane baa dɛ yer ba Gayos ne Aristakus la. Makidoonia harɛ tenaa ban, asɛ ba ne Pɔɔl ɛɛ valɛ. Nɛra la tɛɡ ba la bela ba bwɛɛ tena aa chema dɛɛ bol waa dɛɛ pa bole la.

english_verse: Paul wanted to go out and speak to the people, but the Lord's followers would not let him.
translation_verse: Pɔɔl fe dɛ nyin nɛra la be bela laŋa, kɛ nɛra baa dɛ teŋɛ Yeesu nɛɛ la ta on ŋwɛnɛ tɛɛ.

english_verse: A few of the local officials were friendly to Paul, and they sent someone to warn him not to go.
translation_verse: Dɛ o daamanaree Eesia harɛ nomonome la bane. Ba tomɛ nɛra ŋɔ bá ka kaoh ŋɔ o bɛ lii kɛŋɔ wɛɛ tire nɛra la baah belaa.

english_verse: Some of the people in the meeting were shouting one thing, and others were shouting something else. Everyone was completely confused, and most of them did not even know why they were there.
translation_verse: Nɛnlaa la kɛrɛdɛ aa jemɛ waa la waa baa cheme bela. Dɛ ba bwa aa wesiwi beŋkpoŋ bol. Bane nyɛɡa tɔɔ ba bol waa chaɡɛ bonɔ, dɛ bane ɡe bol ba kwaa chaɡɛ le. Dɛ ba bwa dɛ bol waa saɡasaɡa ken, asɛ ɡbɔɡa tɔ bela bwa.

english_verse: Several of the Jewish leaders pushed a man named Alexander to the front of the crowd and started telling him what to say. He motioned with his hand and tried to explain what was going on.
translation_verse: Bela Juu tena fe ɡelɔ ba bini bɛl baa dɛ yerɔ Alɛksanda la ir che, dɛ fe tɔh ba nyoa ŋɔ ba laa ba waa la ne. Anee o kpɔ nɔn ɛɡ ba ŋɔ bá tɔ nyoa, ásɛ o fe tɔh o bwɛɛ tena nyoa.

english_verse: But when the crowd saw that he was Jewish, they all shouted for two hours, “Great is Artemis, the goddess of the Ephesians!”
translation_verse: Nɛra la te ne o nae kɛ Juu tee on, dɛ ba pɛo dɛɛ bol kohona ŋɔ, “Ya Ɛfesos tena voɡ Aatemes nɔ dɔŋ toole!” Ba si ɡɛ naaa dɔŋhwere anɛ bwa.

english_verse: Finally, a town official made the crowd be quiet. Then he said: People of Ephesus, who in the world doesn't know that our city is the center for worshiping the great goddess Artemis? Who doesn't know that her image which fell from heaven is right here?
translation_verse: Belaa ba bwɛjen karake nomoa waa chɔ ba nyoa la le dɛ ɡel ba tɔ nyoa. Baa tɔ nyoa la, o ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, “Yabala Ɛfesos tena, nomɛlbwa jemɔ kɛŋɔ ya bwɛɛ nɔɔ dɔ ya voɡjen Aatemes voɡ dea dɛɛ nyiŋi o ta. Yanee dɔ Aatemes bwe la aa le Korowii doa ba le harɛ la ɡe.

english_verse: No one can deny this, and so you should calm down and not do anything foolish.
translation_verse: Tɔŋla toole ɡɛ waa nɔ te ta. Aa do ɡɛ nɔ, a chɛ kɛ he tɔ nyoa dɛɛ nyiŋi. A ta chɛ kɛ he ɛ waane dɛ ba le waa nɛ.

english_verse: You have brought men in here who have not robbed temples or spoken against our goddess.
translation_verse: Nɛra nɔ ta ya voɡ nɔ komɛlbwa ŋwɛɛ, ba ta on sisa wobol ɡe bolɛ. Aah dɛ bala haa ba ba ne bonɔ nɔ mun ɔ?

english_verse: If Demetrius and his workers have a case against these men, we have courts and judges. Let them take their complaints there.
translation_verse: Nomɛl ɛ Demetreɔs ne o bala waane aa, kɔɔto deene lole, nomonome baa dɛ bol waa a ta la ɡe lole. Bá ka samane dɔŋa bela.

english_verse: But if you want to do more than that, the matter will have to be brought before the city council.
translation_verse: Gɛ ɡe laa aa, dɛ waane ta lole naa, tɔɔ la wee bwɛɛ nɔ nomonome aa cheme la, bá kpɔ bil ba sie.

english_verse: We could easily be accused of starting a riot today. There is no excuse for it! We cannot even give a reason for this uproar.
translation_verse: Yaa dɛ do ɡbɔɡa ken nɔ, ya ta kɛrɛdɛ nyiŋaa, baa koh a waa lawɛ yaa. Ba lawɛ yaa ɡe aa, yaa wobɛlbwaa dɔ bol, dɛ́ baɡle ɡbɔɡa nɔ mun.”

english_verse: After saying this, he told the people to leave.
translation_verse: Waa bol waa nɔ ɡɛ la, o ɡelɔ nɛra la peɡre.

english_verse: When the riot was over, Paul sent for the followers and encouraged them. He then told them goodbye and left for Macedonia.
translation_verse: Gbɔɡa la nyoa aa sɔɔhna la, Pɔɔl yerɛ bela asɔre tena la cheme, dɛ do ba ɡbemba, dɛ kal ba, dɛ kaa Makidoonia harɛ.

english_verse: As he traveled from place to place, he encouraged the followers with many messages. Finally, he went to Greece
translation_verse: O kpɔ baah bela bwɛɛre la ta, dɛ bol waa baɡ ba taeh dɛ ja ba, dɛ le bela ba Grik tena harɛ ta.

english_verse: and stayed there for three months. Paul was about to sail to Syria. But some of the Jewish leaders plotted against him, so he decided to return by way of Macedonia.
translation_verse: O di korobie atoro bela mɔɔ dɛ kpɔ o te, dɛ́ fe kpɔ stiimae kaa Siiria harɛ. Waa dɛ kpɔ o te dɛ́ kaa la taa o na kɛŋɔ bela Juu tena dɛ vɔrɔwe dɛ́ lawɔ. Belaa o berɛ laa berɛ kpɔ Makidoonia harɛ dɛ kaa.

english_verse: With him were Sopater, son of Pyrrhus from Berea, and Aristarchus and Secundus from Thessalonica. Gaius from Derbe was also with him, and so were Timothy and the two Asians, Tychicus and Trophimus.
translation_verse: Perɔs bie Sopata waa le Bɛrea la teŋɛ Pɔɔl nɛɛ kaa. Aristakus ne Sɛkondos baa le Tesalonika la ɡe la bɛl. Gɛɛ Gayos waa le Dɛɛbe la, ne Tichikos ne Trɔfemos baa le Eesia harɛ la ɡe la bɛl. Timoti ɡe la bɛl.

english_verse: They went on ahead to Troas and waited for us there.
translation_verse: Gɛ nɛra nɔ tɔ sie dɛ ka so kpa Pɔɔl ne men maa dɛ chwerɛ waa nɔ Troas.

english_verse: After the Festival of Thin Bread, we sailed from Philippi. Five days later we met them in Troas and stayed there for a week. Paul's Last Visit to Troas
translation_verse: Ya tɔpejena yaa dɛ di Paanoo Iisi Aa Wola Toole a ta la ɡarɔ mɔɔ ya che Felepae jo stiimae bini. Yaa le Felepae la, a tɔpera anuee ya ba puu ba Troas. Ya di yawanyoa Troas bela. Pɔɔl berɔ la Troas

english_verse: On the first day of the week we met to break bread together. Paul spoke to the people until midnight because he was leaving the next morning.
translation_verse: Memene wee jɔmɔra ne la, ya asɔre tena la chemo dɛ di kondikwaa ya Dɔɔ aa kpɔa ja yaa ŋɔ yá kpɔ dɛɛ lii o waa la, asɛ Pɔɔl bol Korowii Waa dɛɛ baɡle yaa. Dɛ o fe dɛ nyin kɛŋɔ tɔɔ peraa ó kaa, anomanta, o bol waa ka tel harambaŋa.

english_verse: In the upstairs room where we were meeting, there were a lot of lamps.
translation_verse: Dɛ abrɔsane bɛl doaa ya cheme, asɛ kandere do bela pirim.

english_verse: A young man by the name of Eutychus was sitting on a window sill. While Paul was speaking, the young man got very sleepy. Finally, he went to sleep and fell three floors all the way down to the ground. When they picked him up, he was dead.
translation_verse: Dɛ bonɔɔ bɛl soɡe tokoro ta baa yerɔ Yutikus. Pɔɔl aa bol waa biɡri la, dom lawɛ Yutikus kɛrɛdɛ. Waa dɛ chɔ la, o le tokoro la ta abrɔsane la doa le harɛ. Dɛ ɡɛ dea laanee chɔŋa tooro abrɔsane la deene aa chɔŋra la ta. Baa ɡɔɔro, dɛ o sewɔ.

english_verse: Paul went down and bent over Eutychus. He took him in his arms and said, “Don't worry! He's alive.”
translation_verse: Anee Pɔɔl tu harɛ dɛ ka pi o nɛ, dɛ ɡbaaro pɛl o bambile, o berɛ wee. Asɛ Pɔɔl ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, “He bɛ ɔmɛ, o siwi lole.”

english_verse: After Paul had gone back upstairs, he broke bread, and ate with us. He then spoke until dawn and left.
translation_verse: Asɛ Pɔɔl berɛ deeh abrɔsane la dɛ ka di kwa, asɛ o ne ba bol waa la sie ka tel kɛ tɔ aa pera mɔɔ o kaa.

english_verse: Then the followers took the young man home alive and were very happy. The Voyage from Troas to Miletus
translation_verse: Ate, nɛra la sie lɛo kohona kɛŋɔ bie la aa ira la, dɛ kpɔɔ kaa dem. Pɔɔl le Troas dɛ ba Miletus

english_verse: Paul decided to travel by land to Assos. The rest of us went on ahead by ship, and we were to take him aboard there.
translation_verse: Ya kaa kpɔ ya stiimae la kaa bwɛɛ bɛl baa dɛ yerɔ Asos la ta. Dɛ ya fe dɛ lii kɛ ya ka kpɔ Pɔɔl Asos bela, dɛkalkɛ dɛ ya ne o vɔrɔwɔ asɛ o ŋɔ wɛɛ kpɔ harɛɛ dɛɛ cheme yaa bela.

english_verse: When he met us in Assos, he came aboard, and we sailed on to Mitylene.
translation_verse: Waa baa pu yaa Asos la, ya kpɔɔ ya stiimae la ta, asɛ ya ne o ba Mitiliini.

english_verse: Paul had decided to sail on past Ephesus, because he did not want to spend too much time in Asia. He was in a hurry and wanted to be in Jerusalem in time for Pentecost. Paul Says Goodbye to the Church Leaders of Ephesus
translation_verse: Yaa dɛ ba la, ya ta Ɛfesos cheɡɛ, dɛkalkɛ dɛ Pɔɔl aa nyin kɛ o ba biɡri Eesia harɛ ta. O dɛ nyin kɛ o won tel Jerusalam warane mɔɔ ba Pɛntekɔs Tɔpejen la tel.

english_verse: From Miletus, Paul sent a message for the church leaders at Ephesus to come and meet with him.
translation_verse: Pɔɔl cheɡɛ Maeletus kal Ɛfesos asɔre tena nomonome ŋɔ bá ba o be Maeletus.

english_verse: When they got there, he said: You know everything I did during the time I was with you when I first came to Asia.
translation_verse: Baa bala la, o ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, “Le awola maa ba he be Eesia harɛ bonɔ la ba le fini, he na n da maa kpoŋa bwa.

english_verse: Some of the Jews plotted against me and caused me a lot of sorrow and trouble. But I served the Lord and was humble.
translation_verse: N kpɔ n te kɛ n Dɔɔ Yeesu bonɔɔ dɛɛ ɛ o toma nɔ sipwɛra ne. N koh he nyoɡra haa nyoɡre Korowii ŋwɛnɛ waa dɛ yon dɛɛ wi. Juu tena aa dɛ vɔrɔwe n vɔrɔwa la, a noo mɛ taeh.

english_verse: When I preached in public or taught in your homes, I didn't hold back from telling anything that would help you.
translation_verse: N ta wobɛlbwa kpɔe sɔh heya. Wobɛlbwa aa le tɔnɔ tɛ heyaa la, n ta a ta tɔe. N baɡle nɛra Korowii Waa cheremibɔra, dɛ baɡle o waa he deremi.

english_verse: I don't know what will happen to me in Jerusalem, but I must obey God's Spirit and go there.
translation_verse: Taraken nɔ, Jerusalamee mɛɛ kaa la, dɛkalkɛŋɔ Korowii Domadɛɛɡe kpɔ bela laŋa do n bambile ta maa wola won vɛh. Dɛ waane ɛɛ puu mɛɛ belaa yaa, maa jemɛ.

english_verse: In every city I visit, I am told by the Holy Spirit that I will be put in jail and will be in trouble in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Waa maa jema bwaa kɛŋɔ bwɛjen bɛlbwa ta maa la la, ɡɛɛ Korowii Domadɛɛɡe che nɛra nɛɛ dɛ ŋɔ wahala ne dea chɔe chɔ n sie dɛɛ kpaa mɛ.

english_verse: But I don't care what happens to me, as long as I finish the work the Lord Jesus gave me to do. And this work is to tell the good news about God's gift of undeserved grace.
translation_verse: N waane laa n ɡbaɡba hweera wa. Waa aa swɛɛ n siwi laanee kɛ, ɡɛ maa ɛ dɛ tonɛ toma n Dɔɔ Yeesu aa tɛ mɛ ŋɔ ń ɛ la. N tomaa kɛ ń bol Amanesoma la nɛra be bá jemɛ kɛŋɔ Korowii dɛ sune nɛra nɛɛ dɛɛ nyin ba chae.

english_verse: I have gone from place to place, preaching to you about God's kingdom, but now I know that none of you will ever see me again.
translation_verse: Taraken nɔ, n jemɔ kɛ he nɛra maa valɛ he nɛɛ dɛ bol Korowii Kora nɔ waa he be nɔ, haa men na kpa bwa.

english_verse: I tell you today I am no longer responsible for any of you!
translation_verse: Mɛɛ di heyaa kasinteŋii fini. He bɛlbwa baa nyoɡre Korowii ŋwɛnɛ aa, n laa ɛ waane,

english_verse: I have told you everything God wants you to know.
translation_verse: dɛkalkɛŋɔ n ta waa Korowii aa dɛ nyin la wobɛlbwa kpɔe sɔh heya.

english_verse: Look after yourselves and everyone the Holy Spirit has placed in your care. Be like shepherds to God's church. It is the flock he bought with the blood of his own Son.
translation_verse: Hɛ́ɛ nyiŋi he te kɛrɛdɛ, dɛɛ nyiŋi nɛra Korowii Domadɛɛɡe aa kpɔ ba do he nɔn ta ŋɔ hɛ́ɛ nyiŋi ba nɛɛ la kɛrɛdɛ. Korowii Bie ɡbaɡba chalee o kpɔ yawɛ o nɛra asɛ ba ɛ o kwa, anomanta, hɛ́ɛ nyiŋi ba nɛ.

english_verse: I know that after I am gone, others will come like fierce wolves to attack you.
translation_verse: N jemɔ kɛŋɔ maa dɛ kaa nɔ, nɛnchɔɡa ɛɛ jo he binii kɛŋɔ peteɡre toole naa, ɡboli yon jo peera baah dɛɛ larawa la.

english_verse: Some of your own people will tell lies to win over the Lord's followers.
translation_verse: N jemɔ kɛŋɔ he ɡbaɡba bini bane ɛɛ dɛɛ bol waa aa wola weree, dɛ́ neɡre nɛra ásɛ ba ɡel Yeesu nɛɛ teŋa dɛɛ teŋɛ ba nɛ.

english_verse: Be on your guard! Remember how day and night for three years I kept warning you with tears in my eyes.
translation_verse: A waa n ŋɔ hɛ́ɛ nyiŋi kɛrɛdɛ ŋɔ he bɛ ba soh kɛ n fa aa lɔ he be bene atoro bwa dɛ yon dɛɛ ja heyaa Korowii waa ta tɔpebii te bɛlbwa, dɛ koh he waa dɛɛ wi la.

english_verse: I now place you in God's care. Remember the message about his gift of undeserved grace! This message can help you and give you what belongs to you as God's people.
translation_verse: N kpɔ heyaa do Korowii nɔn ta ásɛ o kpoŋe heya, ásɛ o nɛra nɛɛ suna waa la won do he bambile bini ásɛ he do kpeɡri, dɛ́ won di kapɛrɛsom la waa ɛa cheɡ nɛra waa laa ba doŋa bwa kpɔ ba nɛɛ asɛ ba ɛ o ɡbo nɛra la.

english_verse: I have never wanted anyone's money or clothes.
translation_verse: N sie ta nomɛlbwa suuɡa kɛɛ o yal ta beɡrɛ.

english_verse: You know how I have worked with my own hands to make a living for myself and my friends.
translation_verse: He ɡbabir jemɔ kɛŋɔ ɡɛ saŋ maa lɔ he be la, bɔwɔbee n kwee mɔɔ n ne nɛra baa teŋɛ n nɛɛ la ɛɛ dɔ ya komɛlbwa.

english_verse: After Paul had finished speaking, he knelt down with all of them and prayed.
translation_verse: Pɔɔl aa bol waa tonɛ la, o ɡuŋi harɛ, asɛ o ne ba soŋe Korowii.

english_verse: Everyone cried and hugged and kissed him.
translation_verse: Baa ira la, ba lawɔ ɡbaa ba bambile, dɛ kpɔ wii dɛ kalo.

english_verse: They were especially sad because Paul had told them, “You will never see me again.” Then they went with him to the ship.
translation_verse: Waa la aa ɡela ba loo ku kohona laanee kɛŋɔ waa ŋɔa baa on na kpa bwa la. Baa ɡwao tonɛ la, ba doo ŋwɛnɛ la stiimae la bɔr.

english_verse: After saying goodbye, we sailed straight to Cos. The next day we reached Rhodes and from there sailed on to Patara.
translation_verse: Yaa le ba be la, ya jo stiimae bini dɛ pa sie kaa Kɔs, asɛ tɔ aa pera la, ya la Roods, dɛ ka che bela kaa Patara.

english_verse: We found a ship going to Phoenicia, so we got on board and sailed off.
translation_verse: Belaa ya na kɛŋɔ stiimae bɛl aa ba dɛ kaa Finiisia harɛ ta, asɛ ya jo o bini dɛ kaa,

english_verse: We came within sight of Cyprus and then sailed south of it on to the port of Tyre in Syria, where the ship was going to unload its cargo.
translation_verse: dɛ ba le bobɛl dɛ na ekwi bɛl baa dɛ yerɔ Saepros la, dɛ berɛ pa sie weekaŋle harɛbɔr dɛ ka le Siiria harɛ ta, dɛ ka tu Taaya, dɛkalkɛŋɔ dɛ belaa stiimae la ɛɛ ba bone aa lɔ o bini la ne.

english_verse: But when the week was over, we started on our way again. All the men, together with their wives and children, walked with us from the town to the seashore. We knelt on the beach and prayed.
translation_verse: Ya kaala aa tela la, ya le bela dɛ chiɡ ŋwɛnɛ ta dɛɛ kaa. Ba ne ba haahna ne bii bwaa baa do yaa ŋwɛnɛ dɛ le bwɛɛ la ta, dɛ ka tel nee nyoa, asɛ ya ɡuŋi harɛ nee nyoa bela dɛ soŋe Korowii dɛ kal dɔŋa.

english_verse: Then after saying goodbye to each other, we got into the ship, and they went back home.
translation_verse: Yaa kal dɔŋa tonɛ la, ya jo stiimae bini, asɛ ba kaa dem.

english_verse: We sailed from Tyre to Ptolemais, where we greeted the followers and stayed with them for a day.
translation_verse: Ya le Taaya ba Tɔlemaes dɛ ba chɔɔ bela asɔre tena, dɛ so ba be tɔpebeŋkpoŋ.

english_verse: The next day we went to Caesarea and stayed with Philip, the preacher. He was one of the seven men who helped the apostles,
translation_verse: Tɔ aa pera la, ya le bela dɛ ba Sisaaria, dɛ ba choɡ Felep. Dɛ o ɛ nɛra banuanɛ ba fa aa lee ba Jerusalam ŋɔ báa nyiŋi suuɡa waa ta la bɛl. Dɛ o dɛ ɡaaɡe dɛɛ bol Korowii Wa.

english_verse: We had been in Caesarea for several days, when the prophet Agabus came to us from Judea.
translation_verse: Ya biɡri bela tama, asɛ Korowii keame bɛl baa dɛ yerɔ Aɡabus la le Juda harɛ ba.

english_verse: He took Paul's belt, and with it he tied up his own hands and feet. Then he told us, “The Holy Spirit says that some of the Jewish leaders in Jerusalem will tie up the man who owns this belt. They will also hand him over to the Gentiles.”
translation_verse: Waa ba ya be la, o baa kpɔ Pɔɔl kiriso, dɛ vɔrɔwe o ɡbaɡba nɔɔra ne nakpale dɛ ŋɔ ya be ŋɔ, “Kenii Korowii Domadɛɛɡe ŋɔ, Juu tena ɛɛ vɔrɔwe kiriso nɔ te kenii Jerusalam, dɛ kpɔɔ do nɛra baa wola Juu tena ɛɛ nɔn ta.”

english_verse: After Agabus said this, we and the followers living there begged Paul not to go to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Yaa no ɡɛ waa nɔ la, ya ne asɔre tena baa lɔ bela la soŋe Pɔɔl ŋɔ o bɛ Jerusalam la.

english_verse: But Paul answered, “Why are you crying and breaking my heart? I am not only willing to be put in jail for the Lord Jesus, but I am even willing to die for him in Jerusalem!”
translation_verse: Belaa o ŋɔ, “Ɛrɛɛ hɛɛ wi ken dɛɛ nyin kɛŋɔ he do mɛ bɔhwaah nɔɔ? Baa vɔɡ mɛɛ Jerusalamee yaa, n sɛh ɡɛ. Baa kpo mɛɛ ɡe kwaraa naa, n sɛh ɡɛ. Baa koh n Dɔɔ Yeesu waa dɛ ɛɛ mɛ anɔ bɛlbwa naa, n waane laa. N sɛh ɡɛ waa nɔ wubwa bambile bwa ne.”

english_verse: Since we could not get Paul to change his mind, we gave up and prayed, “Lord, please make us willing to do what you want.”
translation_verse: Ya bol harɛ bini waa nɔ bwa o be, o ta noɛ. Anomanta, ya ɡelo dɛ ŋɔ, “Gɛ Korowii aa dɛ nyin a ɛ la, á ɛ ɡɛ.”

english_verse: Then we got ready to go to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: A habɔɔ la, ya kpɔ ya bone dɛ kaa Jerusalam.

english_verse: Some of the followers from Caesarea went with us and took us to stay in the home of Mnason. He was from Cyprus and had been a follower from the beginning. Paul Visits James
translation_verse: Yeesu habɔteŋra baa le Sisaaria la bane ɡe teŋɛ ya nɛɛ la, dɛ tɔ ya sie la ya ne baa la ya fe aa dɛ ba o dea choɡa la dem. O le Saepros, dɛ ɛ nɛnloɡla baa lɛ Yeesu waa la bɛl, asɛ baa yerɔ Meesan. Pɔɔl kaa tel Jerusalam

english_verse: When we arrived in Jerusalem, the Lord's followers gladly welcomed us.
translation_verse: Yaa ba Jerusalam la, asɔre tena la lɛ yaa silɛɛ ne.

english_verse: Paul went with us to see James the next day, and all the church leaders were present.
translation_verse: Tɔ aa pera la, Pɔɔl kpɔ yaa la Jems be, dɛ asɔre tena nomonome la bwa lɔ bela.

english_verse: Paul greeted them and told how God had used him to help the Gentiles.
translation_verse: Pɔɔl ne ba lea dɔŋa, asɛ o baɡle waa bwa Korowii aa chao o won ɛ nɛra baa wola Juu tena ɛɛ la harɛre ta.

english_verse: Everyone who heard this praised God and said to Paul: My friend, you can see how many tens of thousands of our people have become followers! And all of them are eager to obey the Law of Moses.
translation_verse: Baa no Pɔɔl waa la, ba jam Korowii taeh. Belaa ba ɡe ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Nomoa, taraken nɔ, yaa won jemɛ Juu tena baa yarada ya Dɔɔ Yeesu nɔ nyoa baɡle. Ba warɔ kohona. Ba sie beɡre Mosis Mmara la ɡe ta taeh.

english_verse: But they have been told that you are teaching those who live among the Gentiles to disobey this Law. They claim that you are telling them not to circumcise their sons or to follow our customs.
translation_verse: Gɛ nɛra nɔ bwa noɔ kɛŋɔ haa dɛ ɡaaɡe la, he ka dɛ baɡle Juu tena baa lɔ harɛre aa wola Juu tena harɛre ɛɛ ta la ŋɔ bá ɡel Mosis Mmara la ta teŋa. Hale ba ŋɔ he ŋɔ bá ɡel ba bii pena teŋa, dɛ ŋɔ ba bɛ Juu tena kii te bɛlbwa ta dɛɛ teŋɛ. Mosis Mmara ɡe ta ŋwɛnɛ ɡɛ tɛɛ.

english_verse: What should we do now that our people have heard you are here?
translation_verse: Gɛ nɛra nɔ ɛɛ noo kɛŋɔ he balɔ. Anomanta, ɛrɛɛ hɛɛ ba ɛɛ yɔ?

english_verse: Please do what we ask, because four of our men have made special promises to God.
translation_verse: Yaa baɡlee ɡɛ aa chɛ kɛ he ɛ. Baala banaarɛ bane baɡɛ Korowii nyoa bonɔ.

english_verse: Join with them and prepare yourself for the ceremony that goes with the promises. Pay the cost for their heads to be shaved. Then everyone will learn that the reports about you are not true. They will know you do obey the Law of Moses.
translation_verse: Kpɔ ba la Korowii Dea, ásɛ he ne ba ka pɛ ɛ we-ɛɛla haa dɛ ba ɛɛ, ásɛ dɛ laa doŋa kpɔ he nɛɛ la. He laŋaa, hé bɔ ba kem aa chɛ kɛ ba bɔ waa la ta la tɛɛ ba, ásɛ ba won fonɛ ba nyuune. He ɛ ken aa, nɛra bwa ɛɛ jemɔɔ kɛŋɔ haŋaa ba haŋɛ he nyoa. Baa nao kɛŋɔ he ɡbabir dɛ teŋɛ Mosis Mmara la ta.

english_verse: Some while ago we told the Gentile followers what we think they should do. We instructed them not to eat anything offered to idols. They were told not to eat any meat with blood still in it or the meat of an animal that has been strangled. They were also told not to commit any terrible sexual sins.
translation_verse: Asɛ nɛra baa wola Juu tena ɛɛ dɛ yarada Yeesu waa la ɡe la, ya chwerɛ tɔn ka tɛɛ ba ŋɔ ba bɛ voɡ kwaa ne chal ne ol baa wola o baŋa teŋe o sewɛ la dɛɛ di, dɛ ŋɔ bá laa ba te dɛɛ kpɔ jwamane waa ta.”

english_verse: The next day Paul took the four men with him and got himself ready at the same time they did. Then he went into the temple and told when the final ceremony would take place and when an offering would be made for each of them. Paul Is Arrested
translation_verse: Baa ŋɔ ɡɛ la, Pɔɔl lɛ nɛra banaarɛ la, asɛ tɔ aa pera la, o ne ba ka ɛ we-ɛɛla la ásɛ ba doŋa le ba nɛ. Baa tona la, Pɔɔl kaa jo Korowii Dea bini dɛɛ baɡle tɔpera aa di mɔɔ ba kpoo ba bɛlbwa koŋkwaare, ásɛ ba we-ɛɛla la tonɛ. Dɛ a lɔ tɔpera anuanɛ. Ba lawɛ Pɔɔl Korowii Dea

english_verse: When the period of seven days for the ceremony was almost over, some of the Jewish people from Asia saw Paul in the temple. They got a large crowd together and started attacking him.
translation_verse: Tɔpera anuanɛ la aa ba dɛ tel a jaɡa la, Juu tena bane baa le Eesia harɛ pera la na Pɔɔl Korowii Dea, dɛ bol waa dɛ ir nɛra bwaawee, dɛ lawɔ,

english_verse: They were shouting, “Friends, help us! This man goes around everywhere, saying bad things about our nation and about the Law of Moses and about this temple. He has even brought shame to this holy temple by bringing in Gentiles.”
translation_verse: dɛ kpɔ takpeɡ dɛɛ ŋɔ, “Israel tena, hé ba cha yaa oo! Baa nɔɔ vala dɛɛ bol waa bobɛlbwa dɛɛ yaɡɛ ya Israel tena ne Mosis Mmara ne Korowii Dea nɔ la. Name te kwara doŋaa o kpɔ baa jo ya Korowii Dea nɔ bini. Nɛra baa wola Juu tena ɛɛ, Grik tena baa wola chɛɛ kɛŋɔ ba jo Korowii Dea la, banee o lawɛ baa jo o bini!”

english_verse: Some of them thought that Paul had brought Trophimus from Ephesus into the temple, because they had seen them together in the city.
translation_verse: Dɛ ba na o ne baa bɛl waa le Ɛfesos baa yerɔ Trɔfemos la bwɛjen Jerusalam bela. A waa ba ŋɔ ɡɛ la, dɛkalkɛ dɛ ba dɛ lii kɛŋɔ Pɔɔl jo o ne ba Korowii Dea la bini.

english_verse: The whole city was in an uproar, and the people turned into a mob. They grabbed Paul and dragged him out of the temple. Then suddenly the doors were shut.
translation_verse: Ate, bwɛɛ la tena bwa lɛ ɡaeh, dɛ chwa le bobɛlbwa dɛ lawɛ Pɔɔl, dɛ tuuɡu le Korowii Dea la bini. Buɡ la ta, dɛ ba tɔɔɡe Korowii Dea la ɡbeni bwa.

english_verse: The people were about to kill Paul when the Roman army commander heard that all Jerusalem was starting to riot.
translation_verse: Nɛra la aa cheɡɛ Pɔɔl kpoe naa ta la, nɛra kaa ŋɔ Rom soojanomonjen waa dɛ nyiŋi bela soojare nɛɛ la be ŋɔ Jerusalam tena bwa lɛ ɡaeh.

english_verse: So he quickly took some soldiers and officers and ran to where the crowd had gathered. As soon as the mob saw the commander and soldiers, they stopped beating Paul.
translation_verse: Ate, nomoa la ɡel wobɛlbwa ɛɛ dɛ kpɔ soojanomonome bane baa lɔ o lɔɡa ne soojare bane dɛ chwa la bela baa dɛ lɔɔ Pɔɔl la. Nɛra la aa na nomoa la wɛɛ ba soojare ne la, ba ɡel Pɔɔl lɔɔra.

english_verse: The army commander went over and arrested him and had him bound with two chains. Then he tried to find out who Paul was and what he had done.
translation_verse: Nomoa la baa lawɛ Pɔɔl dɛ ɡel ba doo jɔɡrɔre, dɛ bɔɔ nɛra la ŋɔ, “Nɛn besoo baa nɔɔ? Webesoo o ɛɔ?”

english_verse: Part of the crowd shouted one thing, and part of them shouted something else. But they were making so much noise that the commander could not find out a thing. Then he ordered Paul to be taken into the fortress.
translation_verse: Ate, dɛ ba dɛ nyɛɡ bobɛlbwa, bane ɛɛ bol anɔ, bane ɡee bol ane soo siwi. Baa dɛ do ɡbɔɡa ɡɛ la, o ta wone jemɛ waa la kasinteŋ, dɛ ŋɔ bá lawɛ Pɔɔl ka do soojare dejen bini.

english_verse: As they reached the steps, the crowd became so wild that the soldiers had to lift Paul up and carry him.
translation_verse: Ba dɛ kaa dɛ ka tel dea la sanjol baa cheɡɛ o ta dɛɛ jo o bini la ta, asɛ nɛra la ɛɛ nyin ba kpo Pɔɔl. Anee soojare la lɛo le ba be, dɛ ɡɔɔro dawɛ ba vaama ta.

english_verse: The crowd followed and kept shouting, “Kill him! Kill him!” Paul Speaks to the Crowd
translation_verse: Dɛ nɛra teŋɔ dɛ kpɔ takpeɡ dɛɛ ŋɔ, “Hé kpoo! Hé kpoo!” Pɔɔl bol waa baɡle nɛra pirim

english_verse: When Paul was about to be taken into the fortress, he asked the commander, “Can I say something to you?” “How do you know Greek?” the commander asked.
translation_verse: Soojare la aa dɛ ba Pɔɔl ne dea la bini joe la, o bol waa ba nomonjen la be dɛ ŋɔ, “Nomoa, n dɛ nyin n bol waane he be tama.” Belaa nomoa la ŋɔ, “He dɛ no Grik wobol aa?

english_verse: “No!” Paul replied. “I am a Jew from Tarsus, an important city in Cilicia. Please let me speak to the crowd.”
translation_verse: Anee Pɔɔl ŋɔ, “Juu te e men. Silisia harɛ bwɛjen baa dɛ yerɔ Taasos la biee men. N poori, tɛ mɛ ŋwɛnɛ ń bol waa nɛra nɔ be.”

english_verse: The commander told him he could speak, so Paul stood on the steps and motioned to the people. When they were quiet, he spoke to them in Aramaic:
translation_verse: Waa ŋɔ ɡɛ la, nomoa la tɛo ŋwɛnɛ, asɛ o che dea la sanjol ta dɛ kpɔ nɔn ɛɡɛ nɛra la ŋɔ bá tɔ nyoa. Ba tɔ nyoa surumm ken, asɛ Pɔɔl kpɔ Aram tena wobol dɛɛ bol waa ba be, dɛ ŋɔ.

english_verse: “My friends and leaders of our nation, listen as I explain what happened!”
translation_verse: “N mɛɛwa ne n dɔɔranarwa, hé do deŋna n be ásɛ n bol n kon hé no.”

english_verse: When the crowd heard Paul speak to them in Aramaic, they became even quieter. Then Paul said:
translation_verse: Baa noa kɛŋɔ ba ɡbaɡba wobolee wɛɛ bol ba be la, ba tɔ nyoa jeiih ken, asɛ Pɔɔl ɛɛ bol o wa, dɛ ŋɔ,

english_verse: I am a Jew, born in the city of Tarsus in Cilicia. But I grew up here in Jerusalem where I was a student of Gamaliel and was taught to follow every single law of our ancestors. In fact, I was just as eager to obey God as any of you are today.
translation_verse: “Juu tee men. Silisia harɛ bwɛɛ baa dɛ yerɔ Taasos la taa ba lol mɛ. Kɛ bwɛjen Jerusalam bonɔɔ ba dɛɛ mɛ, asɛ Gamaleɛl chaɡ mɛ kwa, dɛ baɡ mɛ ya naawa kii bwa, asɛ mɛɛ teŋɛ a ta. N sie beɡrɔ mɛɛ tomɛ Korowii ɡɛ he bɛlbwa aa dɛ tomɔ fini nɔ.

english_verse: I made trouble for everyone who followed the Lord's Way, and I even had some of them killed. I had others arrested and put in jail. I didn't care if they were men or women.
translation_verse: Dɛ n fa cheɡɛ nɛra baa teŋɛ ɡɛ ŋwɛnɛfale nɔ ta nɔ nɛɛ dɛɛ nyin ba dɛ́ kpo, dɛ lawɛ ba baala ne haahna bwa do deene.

english_verse: The high priest and all the council members can tell you this is true. They even gave me letters to the Jewish leaders in Damascus, so that I could arrest people there and bring them to Jerusalem to be punished.
translation_verse: Sɔfonomoa ne ya Juu tena nomonome bwa ɛɛ wonoo di danseɛ kɛŋɔ kpelaa n ŋɔ. Banee fa chwerɛ tɔne tɛ mɛ, ásɛ n won kpɔ la yabala Juu tena baa lɔ Damaskɔs la be, ásɛ ba tɛ mɛ ŋwɛnɛ ń won lawɛ ŋwɛnɛfale la tena baa lɔ bela, dɛ́ kpɔ ba ba Jerusalam ásɛ ba ka ɛɛ ba wahala.

english_verse: One day about noon I was getting close to Damascus, when a bright light from heaven suddenly flashed around me.
translation_verse: Maa dɛ la dɛ ka tel Damaskɔs la, kerabeŋkpoŋ dɛ nii le nyundua dɛ chaah n nɛɛ kohona dɛ bar mɛ cheme. Dɛ wee cheɡɛ nyufala.

english_verse: I fell to the ground and heard a voice asking, “Saul, Saul, why are you so cruel to me?”
translation_verse: Belaa n chole harɛ. Maa chola la, n no taa bɛl o ŋɔ n be ŋɔ, ‘Oo, Sɔɔl! Ɛrɛɛ he che n nɛɛ ɡɛ nɔɔ?’

english_verse: “Who are you?” I answered. The Lord replied, “I am Jesus from Nazareth! I am the one you are so cruel to.”
translation_verse: Belaa n ŋɔ, ‘Henee umeo, n Dɔɔ?’ Asɛ o ŋɔ, ‘Menee Yeesu waa le Nasarɛt la. Menee hɛɛ yo la.’

english_verse: Those who were traveling with me saw the light, but did not hear the voice.
translation_verse: Dɛ n ne nɛra banee dɛɛ kaa. Ba na nii la te, kɛ ba ta naate waa dɛ bol waa n be la wobol te noɛ.

english_verse: I asked, “Lord, what do you want me to do?” Then he told me, “Get up and go to Damascus. When you get there, you will be told what to do.”
translation_verse: Belaa n pɛɛro ŋɔ, ‘N Dɔɔ, ɛrɛɛ mɛɛ ba ɛɛ yɔ?’ Asɛ o ŋɔ n be ŋɔ, ‘Ir la Damaskɔs ásɛ Korowii ka baɡle waa waa dɛ nyin kɛ he ɛ.’

english_verse: The light had been so bright that I couldn't see. And the others had to lead me by the hand to Damascus.
translation_verse: Nii la aa chaah n sie kohona la, a ɡelɔ n nyoŋe. Anomanta, nɛra n ne baa dɛ kaa laanee bera laɡ mɛ da dɛ ba n ne Damaskɔs.

english_verse: In that city there was a man named Ananias, who faithfully obeyed the Law of Moses and was well liked by all the Jewish people living there.
translation_verse: Damaskɔs bela la, dɛ baa bɛl lole baa yerɔ Ananias. Dɛ o ɛ nɛn waa dɛ tomɛ Korowii kɛrɛdɛ dɛɛ teŋɛ Mosis Mmara la ɡe ta kɛrɛdɛ, asɛ Juu tena baa lɔ bela la bwa ɛɛ tɛo duure kohona.

english_verse: He came to me and said, “Saul, my friend, you can now see again!” At once I could see.
translation_verse: Ananias baa che n be dɛ ŋɔ, ‘N dɔɔ Sɔɔl, Korowii ɡel he sie pili.’ Buɡ la ta, dɛ n denɔ berɛ dɛɛ na, dɛ nao.

english_verse: Then Ananias told me, “The God that our ancestors worshiped has chosen you to know what he wants done. He has chosen you to see the One Who Obeys God and to hear his voice.
translation_verse: Asɛ o ŋɔ, ‘Korowii ya naawa fa aa dɛ tomɔ la, onee lee tɛ o te ŋɔ hé jemɛ waa waa dɛ nyin, dɛ́ won no o Bidɛɛɡe la ɡbaɡba wobol, dɛ́ nao ɡe.

english_verse: What are you waiting for? Get up! Be baptized, and wash away your sins by praying to the Lord.”
translation_verse: Anomanta, bɛ berɛ so kpa. Gel ba sɔe Korowii ne, ásɛ he yerɛ Yeesu sɔn dɛ́ soŋo ó kpɔ he wechɔɡa kɛɛ.’

english_verse: After this I returned to Jerusalem and went to the temple to pray. There I had a vision
translation_verse: A habɔɔ la, n berɔ kaa Jerusalam. Belaa n kaa soŋe Korowii o Dea bini dɛ na chaahna.

english_verse: of the Lord who said to me, “Hurry and leave Jerusalem! The people won't listen to what you say about me.”
translation_verse: N na n Dɔɔ Yeesu, asɛ o ŋɔ n be ŋɔ, ‘Le Jerusalam warane. N waa nɔ haa dɛ di a danseɛ nɔ, Jerusalam tena aa a noe ba.’

english_verse: I replied, “Lord, they know that in many of our synagogues I arrested and beat people who had faith in you.
translation_verse: Belaa n ŋɔ, ‘N Dɔɔ, ba ɡbabir na ɡɛ n fa aa la cheremi deene bini, dɛ kaa lɔɔ nɛra baa yarada he waa nɔ, dɛɛ do ba deene.

english_verse: Stephen was killed because he spoke for you, and I stood there and cheered them on. I even guarded the clothes of the men who murdered him.”
translation_verse: Gɛ saŋ baa kpo Steeven o fa aa dɛ di he waa nɔ danseɛ la, dɛ n lɔ bela dɛ sɛh ŋɔ o chɛ kpoe. Hale baala la aa dɛ kaa bá ka kpoo dɛ wur ba yale la, men lɛa kpoŋe.’

english_verse: But the Lord told me to go, and he promised to send me far away to the Gentiles.
translation_verse: Anee o ŋɔ n be ŋɔ, ‘Kaa! Mɛɛ ɡeloo he kaa bojaŋ, dɛ́ la nɛra baa wola Juu tena ɛɛ be.’ ”

english_verse: They kept shouting. They waved their clothes around and threw dust into the air. Paul and the Roman Army Commander
translation_verse: Ba baah diu, asɛ baa nyɛɡ, dɛɛ viwe ba yale, dɛ ɛ teera dɛɛ ta nyundua.

english_verse: The Roman commander ordered Paul to be taken into the fortress and beaten with a whip. He did this to find out why the people were screaming at Paul.
translation_verse: Anomanta, soojanomonjen la ɡelɔ ba kpɔ Pɔɔl jo dea. Dɛ o ta wone jemɛ waa aa bala nɛra la ɛɛ nyɛɡ ɡɛ la. Anomanta, o ŋɔ bá lɔɔ Pɔɔl bampɔrɔ ŋwɛɛra ne, dɛ́ ɛo hɔhɔrɔwa ásɛ o fe sɛh chɔɡre dɛ bol kasinteŋ.

english_verse: While the soldiers were tying Paul up to be beaten, he asked the officer standing there, “Is it legal to beat a Roman citizen before he has been tried in court?”
translation_verse: Baa ŋɔa ba lɔɔro la, o pɛɛ ba bini nomoa la ŋɔ, “Ŋwɛnɛ lole kɛŋɔ he lɔɔ Rom te dɛ ba ta o waa bolɛ dɛ́ na wechɔɡa waa ɛa aa?”

english_verse: When the officer heard this, he went to the commander and said, “What are you doing? This man is a Roman citizen!”
translation_verse: Pɔɔl aa ŋɔ ɡɛ la, sooja la kaa ŋɔ ba nomonjen la be ŋɔ, “Dɛɛ do baa nɔ dɛɛɡɔ, dɛ bɛ on wechɔɡa bɛlbwa ɛ. Rom tee on.”

english_verse: The commander went to Paul and asked, “Tell me, are you a Roman citizen?” “Yes,” Paul answered.
translation_verse: Belaa nomoa la ba pɛɛ Pɔɔl ŋɔ, “Rom tee hen aa?” Asɛ Pɔɔl sɛh ŋɔ Rom tee on.

english_verse: The commander then said, “I paid a lot of money to become a Roman citizen.” But Paul replied, “I was born a Roman citizen.”
translation_verse: Anee nomoa la ŋɔ, “Bɛlee n ɡba, kɛ n bɔ kem taeh mɔɔ dɛ won ɛ Rom te nɔ.” Belaa Pɔɔl ŋɔ, “Rom tee lolɛ n te n ɛ Rom te.”

english_verse: The men who were about to beat and question Paul quickly backed off. And the commander himself was frightened when he realized that he had put a Roman citizen in chains. Paul Is Tried by the Council
translation_verse: Buɡ la ta, dɛ nɛra ba fe aa dɛ ba Pɔɔl lɔɔra la le habɔɔ. Nomoa la ɡe aa naa kɛ Rom tee Pɔɔl asɛ o ɡel ba do jɔɡrɔre la, o ɔmɔ. Pɔɔl kaa che Juu tena nomonome sie

english_verse: The next day the commander wanted to know the real reason why the Jewish leaders had brought charges against Paul. So he had Paul's chains removed, and he ordered the chief priests and the whole council to meet. Then he had Paul led in and made him stand in front of them.
translation_verse: Nomoa la dɛ nyin o jemɛ waa la Pɔɔl aa ɛa asɛ Juu tena la baah di o nɛɛ la kɛrɛdɛ. Anomanta, tɔ aa pera la, o ɡelɔ ba le Pɔɔl dea, dɛ ɡel Sɔfonomonome ne Juu tena nomonome baa dɛ bol waa la bwa cheme. Baa chema la, o ɡelɔ Pɔɔl ba che ba sie.

english_verse: Paul looked straight at the council members and said, “My friends, to this day I have served God with a clear conscience!”
translation_verse: Waa baa che nomonome la bwa sie la, o nyiŋ ba, dɛ ŋɔ, “Yabala, n bambile bwa nee n tomɛ Korowii le saŋ la bwa ba le fini. N liire ta men ɛɛ kɛ n ɛ wechɔɡa bwa.”

english_verse: Then Ananias the high priest ordered the men standing beside Paul to hit him on the mouth.
translation_verse: Asɛ Ananias waa ɛ Sɔfonomoa la ŋɔ nɛ́ra baa cheɡɛ Pɔɔl jwɛɛh la kpaa o nyoa ta.

english_verse: Paul turned to the high priest and said, “You whitewashed wall! God will hit you. You sit there to judge me by the Law of Moses. But at the same time you order men to break the Law by hitting me.”
translation_verse: Belaa Pɔɔl ŋɔ, “Korowii ɛɛ lɔe bɔ kem, nɛra sie ta ɡboo he ɛ nɛndɛɛɡe kɛŋɔ dekɔɔh baa lɔɔ fula. Haa chema nɔ, ɡɛ Mmara aa chaɡla laa hɛɛ ba nyiŋa dɛ́ bol n wa aa? Aah dɛ haa ŋɔa bá lɔɔ mɛ nɔ, dɛ Mmara tɛ ŋwɛnɛ ɡɛ naa?”

english_verse: The men standing beside Paul asked, “Don't you know you are insulting God's high priest?”
translation_verse: Anee nɛra baa cheɡɛ Pɔɔl jwɛɛh la ŋɔ, “Hei! Sɔfonomoaa hɛɛ chɛɡre naa?”

english_verse: Paul replied, “Oh! I didn't know he was the high priest. The Scriptures do tell us not to speak evil about a leader of our people.”
translation_verse: Asɛ Pɔɔl ŋɔ, “Yabala, n ta jemɛ kɛ Sɔfonomoaa on. Korowii Tɔn baɡlɔ kɛŋɔ ŋwɛnɛ toole kɛ nomɛlbwa chɛɡɛ nomoa waa dɛ nyiŋi o bwɛɛ tena nɛ.”

english_verse: When Paul saw that some of the council members were Sadducees and others were Pharisees, he shouted, “My friends, I am a Pharisee and the son of a Pharisee. I am on trial simply because I believe that the dead will be raised to life.”
translation_verse: Pɔɔl nyiŋi nɛra baa cheme bela la dɛ na kɛŋɔ bane ɛ Saduki tena, asɛ bane ɡe ɛ Farisii tena. Belaa o kpɔ takpeɡ ŋɔ, “Yabala, Farisii tee men noo! Farisii tena biee men. N dɛ hwɛɡɛ kɛ nɛra ɛɛ ir seo taa. Gɛ hwɛɡa nɔ maa dɔa nɔ waa ba ba n ne ŋɔ hé bol n waa dɛ́ pa bole la!”

english_verse: As soon as Paul said this, the Pharisees and the Sadducees got into a big argument, and the council members started taking sides.
translation_verse: Waa dena ŋɔ ɡɛ la, wetɔŋla chole Saduki tena la ne Farisii tena la baah. Ba nyoa ta berɛ pɛ kpa,

english_verse: The Sadducees do not believe in angels or spirits or that the dead will rise to life. But the Pharisees believe in all of these,
translation_verse: dɛkalkɛ dɛ Farisii tena la te ŋɔ nɛra bwa ɛɛ ba ir seo taa, dɛ ŋɔ lala ɡe lole, dɛ ŋɔ nyundua toroma ɡe lole. Kɛ dɛ Saduki tena la te aa ɡɛ waa nɔ bɛlbwa yarada.

english_verse: and so there was a lot of shouting. Some of the teachers of the Law of Moses were Pharisees. Finally, they became angry and said, “We don't find anything wrong with this man. Maybe a spirit or an angel really did speak to him.”
translation_verse: Ba nyɛɡa la nyoa baa do kpeɡri, asɛ Farisii tena Tɔnjerema la ir che dɛ ŋɔ, “Ya ta wechɔɡa bɛlbwa baa nɔ nɛɛ nae. Bɛl lole komɛl kɛɛ nyundua torome bɛlee bol waa o be!”

english_verse: The argument became fierce, and the commander was afraid that Paul would be pulled apart. So he ordered the soldiers to go in and rescue Paul. Then they took him back into the fortress.
translation_verse: Ba wetɔŋla la nyoa baa do kpeɡri kohona, asɛ ɔmee berɛ lawɛ soojanomonjen la, asɛ wɛɛ lii kɛ baa tɛɡre Pɔɔlee kpo. Anomanta, o ɡelɔ o bechale jo nɛra la baah ta, dɛ lɛ Pɔɔl ba nɔn ta, dɛ kpɔɔ kaa soojare dejen baa doo o bini la ta.

english_verse: That night the Lord stood beside Paul and said, “Don't worry! Just as you have told others about me in Jerusalem, you must also tell about me in Rome.” A Plot To Kill Paul
translation_verse: Awola jwaana ne la, ya Dɔɔ Yeesu baa che Pɔɔl jwɛh dɛ ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Bɛ ɔmɛ. Hɛɛ di danseɛ tɛ mɛ Rom ɡɛ haa dia tɛ mɛ Jerusalam nɔ.” Pɔɔl kpoe vɔrɔwa

english_verse: Then some of them went to the chief priests and the nation's leaders and said, “We have promised God that we would not eat a thing until we have killed Paul.
translation_verse: Ba la Sɔfonomonome ne bwɛɛ nomonome be dɛ ka ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, “Ya ŋwɛɛ ntam ŋɔ dɛ ya ta Pɔɔl kpoe yaa, yaa kwaa di.

english_verse: You and everyone in the council must go to the commander and pretend that you want to find out more about the charges against Paul. Ask for him to be brought before your court. Meanwhile, we will be waiting to kill him before he gets there.”
translation_verse: Anomanta, hé ne Juu tena nomonome baa dɛ bol waa la tomɛ nɛn soojanomonjen la be ŋɔ ó le Pɔɔl tɛ heya, á do kɛŋɔ haa dɛ nyin he kwaa nyiŋi o waa bini kɛrɛdɛ la. Ba dɛ ba o ne naa, waa bonɔɔ tel ya te kpoo.”

english_verse: When Paul's nephew heard about the plot, he went to the fortress and told Paul about it.
translation_verse: Jaah Pɔɔl nimambie bɛl bibaa no ɡɛ waa la. Anomanta, o la soojare dejen baa kpɔ Pɔɔl ka do o bini la ta, dɛ ka ŋɔ o be.

english_verse: So Paul said to one of the army officers, “Take this young man to the commander. He has something to tell him.”
translation_verse: Belaa Pɔɔl yerɛ soojanomonome la bɛl dɛ ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “La bonɔɔ nɔ ne he nomonjen la be. O dɔ waane dɛ bol o be.”

english_verse: The officer took him to the commander and said, “The prisoner named Paul asked me to bring this young man to you, because he has something to tell you.”
translation_verse: Sooja la la o ne ba nomoa la be dɛ ka ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Pɔɔl la baa doo dea laanee yer mɛ dɛ ŋɔ n be ŋɔ ń ba bonɔɔ nɔ ne he be. O dɔ waane dɛ́ bol he be.”

english_verse: The commander took the young man aside and asked him in private, “What do you want to tell me?”
translation_verse: Belaa nomoa la lawɛ bonɔɔ la nɔn dɛ le o ne bokɛre dɛ pɛɛro ŋɔ, “Bɔkwa waa he dɔ dɛɛ nyin he bol n be nɔ?”

english_verse: He answered, “Some men are planning to ask you to bring Paul down to the Jewish council tomorrow. They will claim they want to find out more about him.
translation_verse: Anee bonɔɔ la ŋɔ, “Juu tena vɔrɔwɔ ŋɔ baa ba soŋee ásɛ he kere kpɔ Pɔɔl tɛɛ ba bá la o ne ba nomonome baa dɛ bol waa la sie, á do kɛŋɔ baa dɛ nyin ba ka kwaa nyiŋi o waa bini kɛrɛdɛ la.

english_verse: The commander sent the young man away after saying to him, “Don't let anyone know you told me this.” Paul Is Sent to Felix the Governor
translation_verse: Belaa nomoa la ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Bɛ ɡel nomɛlbwa no kɛŋɔ he bol ɡɛ waa nɔ n be.” O ta bonɔɔ la ŋwɛnɛ o kaa. Ba kpɔ Pɔɔl ka tɛ harɛ nomoa Fɛlekse

english_verse: Get a horse ready for Paul and make sure he gets safely through to Felix the governor.”
translation_verse: Nyin konteehna tɛ Pɔɔl ásɛ o so bɛl ta, dɛ́ la o ne sɔnɔnɔɔ ka tɛ harɛ nomoa Fɛlekse.”

english_verse: Greetings from Claudius Lysias to the Honorable Governor Felix:
translation_verse: Men Klɔdeɔs Lisiasii chwerɛ tɔn nɔ dɛɛ tɛ n nomoa Fɛlekse. He le aa?

english_verse: Some Jews grabbed this man and were about to kill him. But when I found out that he was a Roman citizen, I took some soldiers and rescued him.
translation_verse: Juu tena lawɛ baa nɔ dɛ fe ɛɛ nyin o kpoe, asɛ n ka le ba nɛ, dɛ no kɛ o ɛ Rom te, dɛ kpɔ soojare ka lɛo.

english_verse: I wanted to find out what they had against him. So I brought him before their council
translation_verse: Maa lɛo dɛɛ nyin n jemɛ waa la waa baa dɛ nyin o kpoe la, n kpɔɔ la Juu tena nomonome baa dɛ bol waa dɛɛ pa bole la sie.

english_verse: and learned that the charges concern only their religious laws. This man isn't guilty of anything for which he should die or even be put in jail.
translation_verse: Belaa n na kɛŋɔ ba kii waa ba lawɔ. Waa baa kpɔa dawɔ la ta chɛ kɛŋɔ bá kpoo. A ta chɛ kɛ bá doo dea ɡba.

english_verse: As soon as I learned that there was a plot against him, I sent him to you and told their leaders to bring charges against him in your court.
translation_verse: A habɔɔ la, n berɔ ba no kɛŋɔ ba vɔrɔwe o vɔrɔwa dɛɛ nyin o kpoe, asɛ n ŋɔ a chɛ kɛ ń ba o ne he be buɡ ta. N ŋɔ nɛ́ra o ne baa dɔa la ɡe ba he be, dɛ́ ba baɡle waa la aa lɔ o ne ba baah ta. N jaɡɛ bonɔ.

english_verse: The soldiers obeyed the commander's orders, and that same night they took Paul to the city of Antipatris.
translation_verse: Gɛ nomoa la aa baɡle soojare la, ɡɛɛ ba ɛ. Ba kpɔ Pɔɔl le jwaana dɛ ka tel o ne bwɛɛ bɛl baa dɛ yerɔ Antipatris la.

english_verse: The next day the foot soldiers returned to the fortress and let the soldiers on horseback take him the rest of the way.
translation_verse: Asɛ tɔ aa pera la, ba bini banɔ la baa kpɔ naa ta la berɛ ba Jerusalam, dɛ ɡel konteehna tena la, asɛ ba ne Pɔɔl kaa.

english_verse: When they came to Caesarea, they gave the letter to the governor and handed Paul over to him.
translation_verse: Baa kaa tel Sisaaria dɛ kpɔ tɔn la tɛ nomoa waa dɛ nyiŋi harɛ la ta la, ba kpɔ Pɔɔl ɡe do o nɔn ta.

english_verse: The governor read the letter. Then he asked Paul and found out that he was from Cilicia.
translation_verse: O kure tɔn la, dɛ pɛɛ Pɔɔl harɛ la ta waa lea. Pɔɔl aa ŋɔa Silisiaa o le la,

english_verse: The governor said, “I will listen to your case as soon as the people come to bring their charges against you.” After saying this, he gave orders for Paul to be kept as a prisoner in Herod's palace.
translation_verse: nomoa la ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Nɛra he ne baa dɔa la balaa, mɛɛ bol he waa laanee dɛ́ pa bole.” Dɛ o lɔ Hɛrɔd koodem bɛl ta. O ŋɔ bá kpɔ Pɔɔl do bela, dɛ ŋɔ bá nyiŋu kɛrɛdɛ.

english_verse: Five days later Ananias the high priest, together with some of their leaders and a lawyer named Tertullus, went to the governor to present their case against Paul.
translation_verse: Tɔpera anue aa baa ɡale la, Sɔfonomoa Ananias ne nomonome bane ne mmara jereme bɛl baa dɛ yerɔ Tɛtolɔs la la Sisaaria. Ba la ba harɛ nomoa Fɛlekse be bela baa dɛ ba waa bola la, dɛ ka baɡle waa Pɔɔl aa ɛa ba ne o dɔ la.

english_verse: So Paul was called in, and Tertullus stated the case against him: Honorable Felix, you have brought our people a long period of peace, and because of your concern our nation is much better off.
translation_verse: Ba yerɛ Pɔɔl ba, asɛ Tɛtolɔs den pa mun dɛɛ bɔ nkoro dɛ ŋɔ, “Nomoa, he laworomɛ taraken ya dɔ deŋnesɔɔhna la sie. He wono kpɔ ŋwɛnɛfale ta dɛɛ nyiŋi ya harɛ nɔ, asɛ o do som.

english_verse: All of us are always grateful for what you have done.
translation_verse: Ŋwɛnɛ bɛlbwa ta la, ya ne nɛra baa lɔ bojaŋ bobɛlbwa dɛ jaame kohona.

english_verse: I don't want to bother you, but please be patient with us and listen to me for just a few minutes.
translation_verse: Maa nyin kɛ n kpɔ wobobala lawɛ so biɡri. Kɛ n poori, lawɛ bambile dɛ no ya wetamaa nɔ.

english_verse: When he tried to disgrace the temple, we arrested him. If you question him, you will find out for yourself that our charges are true.
translation_verse: He ɡbabir pɛɛro waa, o ɡbaɡba ɛɛ baɡle waa aa bala ya lawɔ laanee.”

english_verse: The Jewish crowd spoke up and agreed with what Tertullus had said. Paul Defends Himself
translation_verse: Ate, dɛ Juu tena baa lɔ bela la bwa deno pɛ dɛ sɛh ŋɔ kasinteŋii ba nɛn la bola la.

english_verse: The governor motioned for Paul to speak, and he began: I know that you have judged the people of our nation for many years, and I am glad to defend myself in your court.
translation_verse: Belaa ba harɛ nomoa la kpɔ nɔn ɛ Pɔɔl ŋɔ ó bol wa, asɛ Pɔɔl ŋɔ, “Nomoa, n jemɔ kɛŋɔ haa lea di nomonome dɛ bol waa dɛɛ pa bole harɛ nɔ ta biɡro. Anomanta, a som n be kɛ haa dɛ ba n waa nɔ ta nyiŋa nɔ.

english_verse: It was no more than twelve days ago that I went to worship in Jerusalem. You can find this out easily enough.
translation_verse: Maa la Korowii soŋebɔr Jerusalam la, a ta tɔpera fi dɛ anɛ kwaraa ɡwaalɛ. He dɛ nyin hé pɛɛ no.

english_verse: Never once did the Jews find me arguing with anyone in the temple. I didn't cause trouble in the synagogues or in the city itself.
translation_verse: Maa la bela la, n ne nomɛlbwa ta wobɛlbwa tɔŋlɛ. N ta nɛra ɡe doe ŋɔ bá ɛ wobɛlbwa. Korowii Dea oo, cheremi dea oo, bwɛɛ bini noo, n ta nɛra doe a bɛlbwa bini ŋɔ bá ɛ wobɛlbwa.

english_verse: There is no way that they can prove these charges they are now bringing against me.
translation_verse: Ba ta danseɛ bɛlbwa dɔe dɛ́ chaɡle kɛ n ɛ waa nɔ bɛlbwa baa kpɔa dɛɛ daɡ mɛ nɔ.

english_verse: I admit that their leaders think the Lord's Way which I follow is based on wrong beliefs. But I still worship the same God that my ancestors worshiped. And I believe everything written in the Law of Moses and in the Prophets.
translation_verse: Ba waa nɔ bini beŋkpoŋ waa ɛ kasinteŋ laanee kɛ baa ŋɔa ŋɔ ŋwɛnɛ la baa dɛ yerɔ ŋwɛnɛfale la, o taa mɛɛ teŋɛ, dɛ kpɔ o ta dɛɛ tomɛ Korowii ya naawa fa aa dɛ tomɔ la. N dɛ teŋɛ wobɛlbwa aa lɔ Mosis Mmara bini ne Korowii Keamere Tɔne bini la ta.

english_verse: I am just as sure as these people are that God will raise from death everyone, good or evil.
translation_verse: N dɛ hwɛɡɛ kɛŋɔ nɛndɛɛɡa ne nɛnchɔɡa bwa ɛɛ berɔɔ ir seo ta. Nɛra nɔ ɡba dɔ ɡɛ hwɛɡa nɔ.

english_verse: And because I am sure, I try my best to have a clear conscience in whatever I do for God or for people.
translation_verse: N jemɔ kɛŋɔ Korowii ɛɛ ba bol nɛwɛnyina bwa waa dɛ́ pa bole. Anomanta, n dɛ ɛ n wobɛlbwa naa, n dɛ ɛa kɛrɛdɛ dɛ bɛ bolchɔɡe di Korowii ne nɛwɛnyina bwa be.

english_verse: After being away for several years, I returned here to bring gifts for the poor people of my nation and to offer sacrifices.
translation_verse: Nomoa, maa le Jerusalam biɡro, asɛ n la bela ŋɔ ń kpɔ suuɡa ane ka tɛ n bala Juu tena ba soɡa bini aa kpeɡa tɛɛ ba, ásɛ dɛ ɛ n saraha ane.

english_verse: This is what I was doing when I was found going through a ceremony in the temple. I wasn't with a crowd, and there was no uproar.
translation_verse: Baa na mɛ Korowii Dea la, dɛ ɡɛ saraha nɔɔ mɛɛ ɛ. Dɛ n dɔɔ laa n doŋa kpɔ n nɛɛ tonɛ, dɛ fonɛ n nyu tonɛ. Dɛ nɛnlaa bɛlbwa ta n nɛɛ jae a ba ɛ kɛ bá lɛ ɡaeh.

english_verse: Some Jews from Asia were there at that time, and if they have anything to say against me, they should be here now.
translation_verse: Dɛ Juu tena bane baa le Eesia harɛ lɔ bela. Dɛ n ɛɛ ba waane aa, a chɛ kɛ ba ɡbaɡba fe aa lɔ bonɔ dɛ́ fe baɡle.

english_verse: Or ask the ones who are here. They can tell you that they didn't find me guilty of anything when I was tried by their own council.
translation_verse: Gɛ laa ɡe aa, hé ɡel nɛra nɔ baa lɔ bonɔ nɔ baɡle, dɛ ɡɛ saŋ baa laɡ mɛ ka cheme Juu tena nomonome sie la, dɛ ba na n wechɔɡe bɛl aa?

english_verse: The only charge they can bring against me is what I shouted out in court, when I said, “I am on trial today because I believe that the dead will be raised to life!”
translation_verse: Webeŋkpoŋ ɡbo waa n jemɛ. Onee kɛ, awola baa chem mɛ la, n kpɔ takpeɡ ŋɔ, ‘Maa dɛ yarada kɛ nɛra bwa ɛɛ ir seo taa la, a waa he laɡ mɛ cheme bonɔ nɔ.’ ”

english_verse: Felix knew a lot about the Lord's Way. But he brought the trial to an end and said, “I will make my decision after Lysias the commander arrives.”
translation_verse: Dɛ Fɛlekse jemɛ ŋwɛnɛfale la waa taeh. Anomanta, o teŋe wobol la ta, dɛ ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ, “Dɛ soojanomonjen Lisias balaa, mɛɛ nyiŋi he waa nɔ taa.”

english_verse: He then ordered the army officer to keep Paul under guard, but not to lock him up or to stop his friends from helping him. Paul Is Kept under Guard
translation_verse: Waa teŋe waa la ta la, o ŋɔ nomoa waa dɛ nyiŋi Pɔɔl nɛɛ la be ŋɔ ó berɛ kaa Pɔɔl ne dea, dɛ ŋɔ wɛ́ɛ nyiŋu kɛrɛdɛ kɛŋɔ o bɛ on tɔ do dea, asɛ dɛ Pɔɔl daamanar ba o be naa, ó tɛɛ ba ŋwɛnɛ ba baa chao.

english_verse: Several days later Felix and his wife Drusilla, who was Jewish, went to the place where Paul was kept under guard. They sent for Paul and listened while he spoke to them about having faith in Christ Jesus.
translation_verse: Aa baa di tɔpera anɛ la, Fɛlekse ne o haah Drusila ba Sisaaria. Dɛ Juu tee o haah la. Fɛlekse ɡelɔ ba ka yerɛ Pɔɔl, asɛ o baa baɡlo ɡɛ baa teŋɛ Yeesu Kristo nɛɛ dɛ́ yaradao.

english_verse: But Felix was frightened when Paul started talking to them about doing right, about self-control, and about the coming judgment. So he said to Paul, “That's enough for now. You may go. But when I have time I will send for you.”
translation_verse: Pɔɔl aa ba dɛ bol ŋɔ a chɛ kɛ nomɛlbwa ɡel o waa do kaih, dɛ ŋɔ a chɛ kɛ nomɛlbwa ɛɛ nyiŋi o te kɛrɛdɛ wechɔɡa ɛɛ ta, dɛ ŋɔ Korowii ɛɛ ba bol nɛra bwa waa dɛ́ pa bole la, Fɛlekse berɔ ɔmɛ dɛ ŋɔ o be ŋɔ, “Gel mɔɔ. Dɛɛ la. N baa dɔ bɔr ja aa, mɛɛ yerɛɛ.”

english_verse: After this, Felix often sent for Paul and talked with him, because he hoped that Paul would offer him a bribe.
translation_verse: Dɛ o dɛ lii kɛ Pɔɔl ɛɛ tɛo suuɡaa, anomanta, tama dɛ o yerɔ ŋɔ ó ba ásɛ baa bol wa.

english_verse: Two years later Porcius Festus became governor in place of Felix. But since Felix wanted to do the Jewish leaders a favor, he kept Paul in jail.
translation_verse: Bene anɛ baa ɡale, asɛ Fɛlekse le kara ta, asɛ Pɔkeɔs Fɛstɔs ba di kara. Dɛ Fɛlekse dɛ nyin kɛ Juu tena sie lɛ o nɛ, anomanta, o ɡelɔ Pɔɔl ta do dea.

english_verse: Three days after Festus had become governor, he went from Caesarea to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Fɛstɔs ba Sisaaria dɛ ba di tɔpera atoro, dɛ le bela la Jerusalam.

english_verse: There the chief priests and some Jewish leaders told him about their charges against Paul. They also asked Festus
translation_verse: Waa la bela la, Sɔfonomonome ne Juu tena nomonome kpɔ waa ba ne Pɔɔl aa dɔa bil o sie dɛ soŋo ŋɔ

english_verse: if he would be willing to bring Paul to Jerusalem. They begged him to do this because they were planning to attack and kill Paul on the way.
translation_verse: ó cha ba dɛ́ ba Pɔɔl ne Jerusalam ba tɛɛ ba. Dɛ ba dɔɔ vɔrɔwe cheɡ kɛ dɛ ba dɛ ba Pɔɔl ne naa, nɛ́ra ba sɔh ŋwɛnɛ ta dɛ́ kpoo.

english_verse: But Festus told them, “Paul will be kept in Caesarea, and I am soon going there myself.
translation_verse: Belaa Koojen Fɛstɔs ŋɔ Pɔɔl chɔ dea Sisaaria, dɛ ŋɔ aa biɡri o ɡba la Sisaaria bela.

english_verse: If he has done anything wrong, let your leaders go with me and bring charges against him there.”
translation_verse: Kɛ bá ɡel ba nomonome puu la bela, ásɛ dɛ Pɔɔl ɛ waane aa, bá baɡla bela.

english_verse: Festus stayed in Jerusalem for eight or ten more days before going to Caesarea. Then the next day he took his place as judge and had Paul brought into court.
translation_verse: Koojen Fɛstɔs berɔ di tɔpera anuatoro, kɛɛ tɔpera fi ba be Jerusalam mɔɔ dɛ ba Sisaaria. Tɔ aa pera la, o kaa so bela baa dɛ bol waa dɛɛ pa bole la dɛ ŋɔ bá ba Pɔɔl ne.

english_verse: As soon as Paul came in, the leaders from Jerusalem crowded around him and said he was guilty of many serious crimes. But they could not prove anything.
translation_verse: Pɔɔl aa bala la, Juu tena baa le Jerusalam la baa che o jwɛɛh dɛ bol waa aa wola were dawɛ o nɛ. Kɛ ane a bwa, ba ta wone dɔ wobɛlbwa dɛ chaɡle kɛ ba waa la ɛ kasinteŋ.

english_verse: Then Paul spoke in his own defense, “I have not broken the Law of my people. And I have not done anything against either the temple or the Emperor.”
translation_verse: Pɔɔl wono bol waa dɛ baɡle kɛ o ta wechɔɡa ɛɛ. O baɡlɔ kɛ o ta wobɛlbwa ɛɛ dɛ jo Juu tena kii bɛlbwa nɛ, dɛ baɡle kɛ o ta wobɛlbwa ɛɛ dɛ jo ba Korowii Dea kii bɛlbwa nɛ, dɛ ŋɔ o ta Rom Koojen la ɡe nɛɛ joɛ.

english_verse: Festus wanted to please the leaders. So he asked Paul, “Are you willing to go to Jerusalem and be tried by me on these charges?”
translation_verse: Dɛ Koojen Fɛstɔs dɛ nyin kɛŋɔ o kpɔ Juu tena la darame, anomanta, o bɔɔ Pɔɔl ŋɔ, “Hɛɛ la Jerusalamee, ásɛ ba ka bol he waa baa kpɔa dawɛ he nɛɛ nɔ n siwi ta dɛ́ pa bole n ɡe na naa?”

english_verse: Paul replied, “I am on trial in the Emperor's court, and that's where I should be tried. You know very well I have not done anything to harm the Jewish nation.
translation_verse: Belaa Pɔɔl ŋɔ, “Akai! Rom Koojen ɡbaɡba nɛra sie n che taraken nɔ. Bonɔɔ chɛ kɛ ba bol n waa nɔ dɛ́ pa bole. He ɡbabir jemɔ kɛ n ta Israel tena nɔ wechɔɡe bɛlbwa ɛɛ.

english_verse: If I had done something deserving death, I would not ask to escape the death penalty. But I am not guilty of any of these crimes, and no one has the right to hand me over to these people. I now ask to be tried by the Emperor himself.”
translation_verse: Dɛ n fe jo ya kii bɛl nɛɛ asɛ a ɛ kɛ a chɛ kɛ bá kpo mɛ naa, n fe aa won ŋɔ mɛɛ chwa sewee. Kɛ dɛ ba waa baa kpɔa dɛ daɡ mɛ nɔ ta kasinteŋ ɛɛ te naa, nomɛlbwa aa won kpɔ mɛ do ba nɔn ta. N dɛ nyin kɛ he la n ne Rom Koojen Siisa sie, ásɛ o ka bol n waa nɔ dɛ́ pa bole.”

english_verse: After Festus had talked this over with members of his council, he told Paul, “You have asked to be tried by the Emperor, and to the Emperor you will go!” Paul Speaks to Agrippa and Bernice
translation_verse: Belaa Fɛstɔs ne o nomonome le jina. Baa bala la, Fɛstɔs ŋɔ Pɔɔl be ŋɔ, “Dɛ he ŋɔ hɛɛ la Rom Koojen bee ó ka bol waa nɔ dɛ́ pa bole te naa, hɛɛ la o bee.” Pɔɔl kaa che Kooro Aɡrepa ne Bɛnes sie

english_verse: A few days later King Agrippa and Bernice came to Caesarea to visit Festus.
translation_verse: Aa baa ɛ tɔpera anɛ la, kooro bɛl baa dɛ yerɔ Aɡrepa ne haah bɛl baa dɛ yerɔ Bɛnes ba Sisaaria, dɛ ba chɔɔ Fɛstɔs.

english_verse: They had been there for several days, when Festus told the king about the charges against Paul. He said: Felix left a man here in jail,
translation_verse: Baa di Sisaaria tɔpera anɛ la, Fɛstɔs taa Pɔɔl waa la baɡle Kooro Aɡrepa, dɛ ŋɔ, “Fɛlekse fa do a ɡɛ baa nɔ dea, kɛ o ta lole.

english_verse: and when I went to Jerusalem, the chief priests and the Jewish leaders came and asked me to find him guilty.
translation_verse: N la Jerusalam, asɛ Juu tena Sɔfonomonome ne ba bwɛɛ nomonome kaa bol o wa, dɛ kpɔ waa dɛɛ dawɔ, dɛ ŋɔ ń bol o waa dɛ́ pao bolchɔɡe.

english_verse: I told them it isn't the Roman custom to hand a man over to people who are bringing charges against him. He must first have the chance to meet them face to face and to defend himself against their charges.
translation_verse: Baa ŋɔ ɡɛ la, n ŋɔ ba be ŋɔ ya Rom tena te aa ɡɛ ɛ. Ya te bwɛ, dɛ nɛn ne o dɔŋ dɔɔ, dɛ ya ta on ŋwɛnɛ tɛɛ o ne nɛn waa kpɔ waa dawɔ la cheme o bol o kon, o ɡe bol, asɛ a bɔɔ waa, yaa on bolchɔɡe pa ɡɛ.

english_verse: So when they came here with me, I wasted no time. On the very next day I took my place on the judge's bench and ordered him to be brought in.
translation_verse: Anomanta, Juu tena la aa lawɛ dɔŋa ba bonɔ la, n ta hɛlɛ kwaraa. Tɔ aa pera la, n baa so n kara ta bela maa soɡa dɛ bol waa dɛɛ pa bole la, dɛ ɡel ba ba Pɔɔl ne bela.

english_verse: But when the men stood up to make their charges against him, they did not accuse him of any of the crimes that I thought they would.
translation_verse: Dɛ n te dɛ lii kɛŋɔ o ken ɛ wechɔɡa ane kohona. Kɛ nɛra la waa baa kpɔa dɛɛ dawɔ la ta wechɔɡa bɛlbwa ɛɛ.

english_verse: Instead, they argued with him about some of their beliefs and about a dead man named Jesus, who Paul said was alive.
translation_verse: Dɛ ba Korowii toma wa, ne baa bɛl waa sewa baa yerɔ Yeesu la waa baa bol. Ba ŋɔ Pɔɔl te ŋɔ ɡɛ Yeesu la waa sewa la ir seo ta.

english_verse: Since I did not know how to find out the truth about all this, I asked Paul if he would be willing to go to Jerusalem and be put on trial there.
translation_verse: Dɛ maa jemɛ ɡɛ maa ɛ dɛ́ bɔɔ ɡɛ waa nɔ bini, dɛ́ won bola kɛrɛdɛ. Anomanta, n bɔɔ Pɔɔl ŋɔ, ‘Yá la Jerusalam bá ka bol he waa nɔ dɛ́ pa bole bela kɛɛ?’

english_verse: But Paul asked to be kept in jail until the Emperor could decide his case. So I ordered him to be kept here until I could send him to the Emperor.
translation_verse: Maa ŋɔ ɡɛ la, o soŋɔ ŋɔ wɛɛ chɔ dea ka tel kɛ Rom Koojen Siisa ɡbaɡba aa bol o waa la dɛ́ pa bole. A waa n tɔɔ do dea la, ásɛ n baa dɔ ŋwɛnɛ aa, ń ɡel o la bela.”

english_verse: Then Agrippa said to Festus, “I would also like to hear what this man has to say.” Festus answered, “You can hear him tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Belaa Kooro Aɡrepa ŋɔ Fɛstɔs be ŋɔ, “N ɡbaɡba dɛ nyin n na baa nɔ dɛ no o waa nɔ.” Asɛ Fɛstɔs ŋɔ, “Tɔ kere peraa, hɛɛ noo.”

english_verse: The next day Agrippa and Bernice made a big show as they came into the meeting room. High ranking army officers and leading citizens of the town were also there. Festus then ordered Paul to be brought in
translation_verse: Tɔ aa pera la, Kooro Aɡrepa ne Bɛnes do ba koolaala, asɛ ba waa dɔ nyɛl kohona, asɛ ba ne bela bwɛjen soojanomonome ne bela nomonjena ba jo lamu ta. Baa chema la, Fɛstɔs ɡelɔ ba ba Pɔɔl ne.

english_verse: and said: King Agrippa and other guests, look at this man! Every Jew from Jerusalem and Caesarea has come to me, demanding for him to be put to death.
translation_verse: Belaa Fɛstɔs ŋɔ, “Kooro Aɡrepa, ne nɛra haa cheme bonɔ nɔ, n dɛ lii kɛ he bwa na baa nɔ. Juu tena baa lɔ Jerusalam ne banɔ la baa lɔ Sisaaria bonɔ bwa kpɔ bandia dɛɛ nyɛɡ ŋɔ o waa aa were, ŋɔ o do kpoe.

english_verse: I have not found him guilty of any crime deserving death. But because he has asked to be judged by the Emperor, I have decided to send him to Rome.
translation_verse: Kɛ n ta wone na waa waa ɛa a ɛ kɛŋɔ o do kpoe. Anomanta, o ɡbaɡba aa baa ŋɔ yá tɛ ŋwɛnɛ ásɛ Rom Koojen Siisa ɡbaɡba ka bol o waa la dɛ́ pa bole la, n ɛ n liire kɛŋɔ mɛɛ ɡeloo ó la o be.

english_verse: I have to write some facts about this man to the Emperor. So I have brought him before all of you, but especially before you, King Agrippa. After we have talked about his case, I will then have something to write.
translation_verse: Kɛ waa maa baɡla do tɔn bini kɛŋɔ ken ne kenii o ɛ waa n ŋɔ Rom Koojen ɡbaɡba nyiŋi o waa bini la, an kpeɡa tɛ mɛ nɔ. Amɔ a waa n ba o ne he bwa sie, ne Kooro Aɡrepa ɡbaɡba sie, ásɛ he nyiŋi o waa nɔ bini la. Bɛl lole he ken ɛɛ wonoo cha mɛ ń dɔ o waane dɛ́ chwerɛ ka tɛ Rom Koojen,

english_verse: It makes no sense to send a prisoner to the Emperor without stating the charges against him.
translation_verse: dɛkalkɛŋɔ dɛ n la o ne o be dɛ n ta wechɔɡa waa ɛa baɡlaa, a ta maɡrɛ.”

english_verse: King Agrippa, I am glad for this chance to defend myself before you today on all these charges my own people have brought against me.
translation_verse: “Kooro Aɡrepa, n sie lɛo kohona kɛ maa dɛ ba n kon bola he siwi ta, dɛ́ baɡle waa bwa Juu tena aa kpɔa dɛɛ daɡ mɛ nɔ.

english_verse: You know a lot about our religious customs and the beliefs that divide us. So I ask you to listen patiently to me.
translation_verse: N sie lɛo kohona, dɛkalkɛ he jemɛ ya Juu tena nawee waa bwa. Anomanta, n poori, lawɛ bambile dɛ́ no n kon.

english_verse: All the Jews have known me since I was a child. They know what kind of life I have lived in my own country and in Jerusalem. And if they were willing, they could tell you I was a Pharisee, a member of a group that is stricter than any other.
translation_verse: Dɛ ba sɛoh ŋɔ bá bol kasinteŋ aa, ba fe ɛɛ wonoo di danseɛ kɛŋɔ, ya Juu tena Korowii toma ŋwɛnɛ o ta teŋa aa kpeɡa kohona, baa yerɛ o nɛra Farisii tena la, o taa n ɡe ɛɛ teŋɛ.

english_verse: Now I am on trial because I believe the promise God made to our people long ago.
translation_verse: Korowii baɡɛ ya naawa nyoa bɛl. N dɛ hwɛɡɛ ɡɛ nyobaɡa la ta. Gɛ hwɛɡa nɔ waa ba koh laɡ mɛ asɛ n che he sie hɛɛ ba n waa bola la.
